<margin>The Alchemist: why he was appointed. Appointed by God for a purpose.</margin>
But if we compare what is imperfect to our use, for which there is a need, He <note>God</note> appointed the Alchemist <note>Paracelsus uses "Alchemist" here as a metaphor for the internal biological force—later called the "Archeus"—that processes food and separates nutrients from waste.</note> to this end: so that we would not eat as poison the very poison which we take in the form and place of healthy food, but might instead segregate and discern that poison from what is healthy.

Regarding this Alchemist of whom we tell you, pay close attention to our words.

## Chapter III.

<margin>The Alchemist: what kind of craftsman he is.</margin>
**SINCE** every single thing is perfect in itself, yet in relation to others possesses the nature of both poison and health: proceeding in our discourse, we establish that **GOD** has altogether appointed an Alchemist for this being <note>the human being</note>—who eats and uses another thing that yields both destruction and health—who is such a great craftsman that he can properly discern these two from each other, by putting the poison into his pouch and the food into the body. In this way, as we advised above, we wish our foundation to be understood and accepted by you. But take an example of another kind. A lord or prince is perfect in himself, as befits a prince. But a prince cannot be without servants to serve him. Meanwhile, servants are perfect in themselves, but not to the prince; rather, they are both a source of poison (or harm) and profit to him. But to understand the Alchemist of nature, think this way: God granted the prince the knowledge in himself that a prince requires. This very thing teaches him to separate the poison from his servants and to accept the good from them also. If this example does not seem to fit you so well, you will find the foundation of the present matter placed in the teaching according to the doctrine of the Wise, where this is explained. For this is how it is: Man needs to eat and drink. For the body of man, which is the lodging-house of his life, altogether needs food and drink.

<margin>Man, through the consumption of food, acquires diseases and death.</margin>
Thus man is compelled to take within himself both poison, diseases, and death itself, namely through food and drink. Thus this argument could be directed against Him who gave us a body and added food, as if He did so to slaughter us.

<margin>The Creator takes nothing away from the creature.</margin>
But know that the creator takes nothing from the creature, but leaves each its own perfection. And although one thing may be poison to another, the creator can by no means be accused or blamed for that.

## Chapter IV.

<margin>By what power the Alchemist separates poison from the good.</margin>
**FROM** these things you will investigate the creator thus: If all things are perfect in themselves and so arranged by the creator's order that one serves for the preservation of another—as grass feeds the cow, and the cow feeds the man—and therefore the perfection of one thing is both bad and good for another thing that consumes it, and for that reason imperfect; it must be established that the creator, for the sake of a more abundant creation which is more than creation itself, established these things for this cause: because He willed things created under this condition, so that in that which is necessary for another, such power, efficacy, and art should lie hidden, that through this power the poison might be separated from the good for the health of the body and the necessity of nourishment, and that mutual order be preserved.

Example: The peacock devours the snake, the lizard, and the <term>stellio</term> <note>original: "stellionem"; a type of spotted lizard, often associated in folklore with venom or medicinal properties.</note>. These animals are indeed perfect and healthy in themselves; but regarding other animals, all these cited are pure poison, if you except the peacock. Hold this cause for this diversity: its Alchemist is so subtle that no other animal's Alchemist matches it, for it separates poison from good so exquisitely and purely that this food is harmless to the peacock. So it is also true elsewhere, that to every animal its own peculiar nourishment is assigned for preservation, and besides this, a peculiar Alchemist is also given who separates it.

<margin>Peacock.</margin>
<margin>Ostrich.</margin>
<margin>Salamander.</margin>
<margin>Swine.</margin>
To the <term>ostrich</term> <note>original: "struthiocamelus"</note> such an Alchemist is given who separates iron—that is, dross—from nourishment, which would be impossible for any other to perform. To the salamander, for food, fire or the body of fire is given. This has an Alchemist added for the work. For the swine, dung is food, although that is poison; for which reason it is also excluded from the human body by the Alchemist of nature. Yet it is nonetheless nourishment for the swine, because the swine's Alchemist is much more subtle than the human Alchemist. For the swine's Alchemist separates from the dung that nourishment which the human Alchemist could not segregate.

<margin>Swine dung.</margin>
Therefore also swine dung is devoured by no other animal. For there is no Alchemist more subtle or who separates nourishment more exquisitely than the swine's Alchemist. The same is to be understood in the same way for others, which we deliberately omit so the discourse may be shorter.

<margin>The Alchemist established by God's care.</margin>

...so that he might separate from the good that which exists as its opposite, specifically in that body which, by divine decree, takes in something for the maintenance of its life. Now return to what was stated previously: namely, that there are five things which have power over man and to which he is subject. These are the <term>Astral Entity</term> <note>the influence of the stars and atmosphere on health</note>, which we have already discussed, and next, the <term>Entity of Poison</term> <note>the influence of food, drink, and environmental toxins</note>. In this inquiry, we must pass over everything that provides some benefit rather than harm to bodies, as we shall subsequently declare to you.

### CHAPTER VI.

<margin>Whether health can be predicted from the natural entity.</margin> **B**ut first you must know that even in this matter the Astronomers <note>those who practice "medical astrology," claiming all disease comes from the heavens</note> are deluded when, in indicating the ailments of our body, they speak of a "fortunate body" or a "healthy body" based on the stars. Now, if that is not the case, this single cause remains: that the other Entities—of which there are four more—harm the body, and not the stars at all. Therefore, we rightly mock and reject their writings, in which they so generously promise health, yet fail to consider that there are four other Entities just as powerful as the star. But we must play along with them. For what is a cat without a mouse? What is a Prince without a jester? The "Physiomancer" <note>one who predicts health or character based on facial features and physical appearance</note> weaves a plainly similar story, though he will never move us to tears. He promises health and does not think of the four Entities of which he is ignorant. For he prophesies from the "Natural Entity" alone and remains silent about all the rest—which amuses us not a little. It belongs to a man skilled in many things to predict those outcomes which depend on the "course" <note>the trajectory or influence of a specific Entity</note>. For there exist five motions or courses, and yet only one man. He who omits some motions and proceeds only with the rest is truly a vain prophet. To divide, and to speak according to that division—each according to what he has learned, following their judgment and opinion—is greatly to be praised. Thus, the "Pyromantic Entist" <note>An "Entista" is a specialist in one of the five Entities; here, one who judges by the "Entity of Spirit" or fire</note> places his judgment upon spirits. So the "Physiognomic Entist" prophesies from the nature of the man; the "Theological Entist" from the course of God; and the "Astronomical Entist" from the stars. Thus, each is a liar by himself. But they are truthful and just if they agree as one. This we tell you: do not continue to prophesy in this way unless you have first recognized the five Entities of the Entities. Then, at last, we will restrain our laughter.

### CHAPTER VII.

<margin>How the power of the Alchemist behaves in man.</margin> **S**o that you may have a fundamental knowledge of the Alchemist, know now that God has granted to every creature its own substance and the things required for it—not for the sake of its own self-governance, but for the use of those things which it necessarily requires, which are themselves joined with poison. That creature has within its body one who separates the poison from that which is added to the body. This is the Alchemist himself; so called because he employs the chemical art in his operations. He separates the vile from the good; he transmutes the good into a <term>tincture</term> <note>a vitalizing essence or refined nutrient</note>; he tints the body for its life; he governs and disposes his subject within nature; he tints it so that it may turn into blood and flesh. This Alchemist dwells in the ventricle <note>the stomach</note> as if in his own instrument, where he cooks and where he works. Understand it thus: the meat a man eats contains both poison and good within it. Yet in the eating, all things are judged as tested and good. For under the good, poison lies hidden; but under the bad, there is nothing of the good. As soon, therefore, as the food—such as meat—descends into the belly, the Alchemist immediately leaps to it and institutes a separation. That which does not contribute to the health of the body, he deposits in specific places; what he finds to be good, he sets apart for its proper seats. This is the divine order. In this way, the body is preserved from being killed by the poison of what it eats; and that poison is secreted by the Alchemist without any labor from the man himself. And such is the virtue and power of the Alchemist in man.

### CHAPTER VIII.

<margin>Poison and good in every single food. How Essence and Poison differ.</margin> **B**ut understand further that in every single thing which a man takes for his use, there is poison hidden under the good, in this manner. In every single thing, there exists both an <term>essence</term> and a poison. The essence is that...

He critiques doctors who only look at the stars or physical appearance, arguing that health depends on all five "Entities" (Astral, Poison, Natural, Spiritual, and Divine).</summary>

<header>ON THE ENTITY OF POISON.</header>
<sig>B 2</sig>

...that which sustains man. Poison, on the other hand, is that which destroys him and strikes him with diseases. And these things are true in every nourishing substance, in respect to the animal that uses it, with none excluded. Pay attention to these things now, Physicians. If the body consists in nourishment in this way, and cannot do without it but is entirely subject to it, then the body takes in nourishment—just as it finds it—under the appearance of both good and evil; it then delegates the duty of separation to the <term>Alchemist</term> <note>Paracelsus's name for the "Archeus" or the body's innate intelligence that manages digestion and metabolism</note>. Now, if the Alchemist should be weak, such that he is not strong enough to separate the poison from the good according to his perfect industry; and if, furthermore, a united putrefaction <note>the breakdown or rotting of matter</note> arises from the poison and the good together, and finally some form of digestion occurs, then this is the very thing that reveals the diseases of men to us.

<margin>All diseases arise from a putrefied digestion.</margin> For every disease in man born from the <term>Entity of Poison</term> flows from a putrefied digestion, which itself ought to have remained in a balanced state so that the Alchemist would not feel any measure of excess. But when digestion is interrupted, then the Alchemist can by no means remain perfect in his instrument. Thus, it is necessary for corruption to follow, which then stands as the mother of all diseases. And it was proper for you Physicians to observe this most deeply in your minds, rather than being entangled in your own evasions.

<margin>Corruption.</margin> For corruption pollutes the body according to how it exists or becomes. Water that is clear and transparent is ready to be stained by whatever color one pleases. So also the body is like water: corruption is the color. Nor is there any color which does not draw its origin from poison—which exists simultaneously as the sign and indicator of the poison.

### CHAPTER IX.

<margin>Corruption occurs in two ways: Locally.</margin> However, so that you may grasp this more fully, know that Corruption occurs in two ways: *Locally*, and *by way of the Emunctories* <note>the organs or channels, such as pores or kidneys, that carry off waste</note>, in this manner. If, as we have said, it is in the digestion, and the Alchemist fails in the separation due to a fault of deficient digestion, then finally rot is generated in that place, which is poison. For any putrid thing is the poison of that place in which it stays, and thus it becomes the mother of a certain and deadly poison. For rot corrupts that which is good; and if the good is stripped of its strength, then the evil in the good prevails—which nonetheless does not appear otherwise than under the appearance of that good which is subject to the rot. And so this becomes the mother of those diseases which are subject to it.

<margin>By way of the Emunctories.</margin> Now indeed, that which happens *by way of the Emunctories* occurs from a wandering of the expulsive nature in this way: the Alchemist expels poison—each through its appropriate emunctory: for instance, white sulfur through the nostrils, arsenic through the ears, dung through the <term>monoculum</term> <note>original: "monoculum"; refers to the cecum or part of the bowel believed to have a single "eye" or opening</note>, and so with any other poisons, as each has its own peculiar emunctory. If one of these poisons is hindered either by the weakness of nature or by itself and others, then it becomes the mother of the diseases subject to it. Thus universally, in all diseases, two origins are revealed. We will not speak many more words to you here regarding these, but you will read more abundantly about them in the books *On the Origin of Diseases* in particular.

### CHAPTER X.

Furthermore, just as was said above concerning natural Alchemy—how it is situated in every animal because of the necessity of separation which must be established in the stomach—so now attend to a certain brief teaching on how all other diseases can also be explored and tracked down in the aforementioned way. If a man were healthy and well in respect to all the Entities—if, for example, he had a suitable Alchemist who separated properly with convenient instruments, <term>reservoirs</term> <note>original: "referuacula"; internal storage areas for bodily fluids</note>, and emunctories—then it is necessary to know that, besides suitable instruments, many other things also matter here: namely, that the stars must be favorable and all other Entities must be kind.

<margin>Accidents hostile to the Alchemist.</margin> Although these universal matters do not move us much (assuming everything is good and effective), nevertheless many things happen to the body which either break, stain, defile, or obstruct the Instruments, Reservoirs, and Emunctories. For fire is contrary to nature and the body. By its quality, nature, heat, dryness, and other power, it can so corrupt us that the instruments of the Alchemist are violated by its presence; whence he himself afterwards appears weak.

<margin>Diseases from the violation of the Alchemist's instruments.</margin> So also water itself meets our body and Reservoirs in a manner adverse to its nature, substance, and qualities—so vehemently that the instruments are either blocked by it, or perverted, or altered in another way. The same judgment applies to the air and any necessary things, as well as to external accidents, all of which have the power to break apart, change, and render the Reservoirs, Instruments, and Emunctories unfit. For then the Alchemist, weak and dead, becomes unfit for completing his work.

He also notes that external elements like fire, water, and air can damage the body's internal 'instruments,' further disrupting this vital digestive process.</summary>

### CHAPTER XI.

<margin>
How the instruments are corrupted by them.
</margin>
<margin>
From the air.
</margin>
**B**ut it must not escape your notice that through the mouth itself, the **Reservoirs**, **Instruments**, and **Emunctories** <note>the body's excretory organs or waste-clearing channels</note> can also be corrupted—by the air, by food, by drink, and other things of this kind. This happens in the following way: the air we breathe is not without poison, and we are especially vulnerable to it. Regarding the quantity of food and drink, as well as its poor quality—which disagrees with the body's instruments—it must be held that they are violently broken down by those very organs. In such a case, the <term>Alchemist</term> <note>the internal power that governs digestion</note> is clearly disturbed in his operations; then, **Digestion**, **Putrefaction**, and **Corruption** occur. Whatever the poisonous property is of the thing a person consumes, the stomach (and the rest of the body along with it) adopts that same nature. Afterward, this becomes the mother of diseases for that same body. From this, you Physicians ought to understand that a single poison alone—and no more—gives birth to the mother of diseases. For instance, if you eat meat, vegetables, porridge, or spices, and a corruption is generated in the belly from these things, then it is not all the foods together that are the cause of this corruption. Rather, it is only one among them: namely, the poison of either the vegetable, the meat, the porridge, or the spices. You should hold this as a great secret <note>original: "magni arcani"</note>. If you truly recognize which poison is the "mother of diseases," then we shall rightly allow you to be called Physicians. For then you will know for certain which remedy you ought to use, whereas otherwise you were attempting it in error. Let this be your foundation regarding the "mother of all diseases," of which six hundred are numbered.

---

### CHAPTER XII.

**I** will now also share with you a brief instruction on poisons, so that you may grasp which poisons we mean and of what kind they are. We have indicated to you that poison exists in all nourishment. From nourishment, therefore, a certain powerful **Entity** <note>original: "Ens," referring here to the *Ens Veneni* or the influence of poison</note> is led out over our bodies. We previously explained who the Alchemist within us is: the one who separates the poison from the nourishment through his instruments and reservoirs for the benefit of the body. Once this is done, the **Essence** itself passes into the "tincture" <note>the vitalizing part</note> of the body. The poison, however, departs from the body through the emunctories. As long as each of these things is managed in this order, a person remains healthy and vigorous by reason of that Entity. Yet, we have also mentioned hostile accidents that can strike the Entity itself so forcefully that they destroy it, from which the "Mother of Diseases" later arises. Having repeated these things, hear further regarding the kinds of poisons. I believe you know what and how many the emunctories are. By considering these, descend toward the knowledge of poisons. Whatever seeps substantially through the pores of the skin is **dissolved Mercury**.
<margin>
The coagulation of the body's poisons in individual limbs.
</margin>
What is excreted through the nostrils is **white sulphur**. What is ejected through the ears is **Arsenic**. Through the eyes, **sulphur**. Through the bladder, the **dissolution of salt**; through the anus, **putrefied sulphur**. And although your logic might require knowing in what form and species each of these could be tested, our current digression does not permit it. But from the book *On the Philosophy of Human Construction*, you shall draw those foundations which are necessary for a Physician to know, just as you shall find their proper remedies—for many reasons—in the books on putrefactions (the reading of which pertains to you), where they are more copiously handed down. There also, you will find how poison lies hidden within nourishment.

### CHAPTER XIII.

**W**e will place an example before your eyes, from which you may briefly perceive how poison is within nourishment; and how the condition of each thing is perfect in itself, yet in respect to other humans and animals who use it, it is faulty and poisonous. We shall state it thus: the **Ox**, created with his own equipment, is sufficient unto himself for his own needs; his skin for the protection of his flesh, and his emunctories for his Alchemist.
<margin>
How poison is beneath nourishment.
</margin>
But this example does not seem to fit perfectly here. We will give another. The ox was created, for his own necessity, in the form in which he exists; but for man, he was created for nourishment as food. Now pay attention: the ox is half-poison to man. If he had been created solely for the sake of man and not for his own sake as well, then he would need neither horns, nor bones, nor hooves. For in these, no nourishment resides; and what comes from them is not necessary. You see, therefore, that the ox is created exceedingly well for his own sake, and there is nothing in him that he could either lack or have in excess. But now, if he is taken as food for a human, then the human also eats that which is against him and is a poison, even though it was not a poison to the ox itself. This must now be separated from the nature of the human, which his Alchemist performs; there, various poisons are generated without exception. For every poison, by the work of the Alchemist, is driven out into its Emunctories, which are then filled. But whichever of men's Alchemists can perform this...

### TREATISE
### ON THE NATURAL ENTITY.

### CHAPTER I.

**S**ince I have no doubt that you will judge our **Natural Entity** and your own writings quite differently: nevertheless, making light of that very thing, we profess one Natural Entity, which is the third in our Parenthesis, from which all diseases can be generated; and indeed are generated, as often as the Natural Entity falls into that change, as the following chapters will enumerate. First, note what the Natural Entity is. In making its definition, if we do not use the property of the maternal and astral languages, nor even that which you learned from Heinrichmann <note>Jacob Heinrichmann, a famous grammarian of the time; Paracelsus is critiquing traditional academic education</note>: I would like you to be mindful of a certain new law, and also the simplicity of the ancient, obsolete authors. The Natural Entity is this.
<margin>
What is the Natural Entity.
</margin>
You have learned from Astronomy the influences, the firmament, and all the stars, and the planets, and the genius of the heaven, which you have known and examined to the very last penny. Thus this becomes our introduction to the matter: that by the same reasoning as you have learned the element in the sky, a similar constellation, firmament, and something like these is found in man. Nor will we be ashamed of your doctrine, when you call man a <term>Microcosm</term> <note>literally "small world"; the idea that man contains the entire universe within himself</note>.
<margin>
Man is a microcosm, just as the sky has its stars in itself.
</margin>
The name itself is indeed honest: but you have never understood it correctly; and your interpretations are obscure and mere darkness. Value the matter as we explain the Microcosm. Just as the heaven, with all its firmament, constellation, and the rest is fruitful and exists through itself: so man also will be powerfully constellated within himself and for himself. And as the firmament in the heaven is for itself, and thus is governed by no creature: no more is the firmament which is in man ruled by other creatures, but is a powerful and free firmament through itself alone, obeying no command. From this, conclude two creatures: one the heaven and earth; the other, Man.

### CHAPTER II.

**W**e relate it thus. You have learned the motions of the firmament down to the smallest point. Afterward, you also learned the earth with all its births: you have the elements themselves and all substances known. You ought to have understood and explored that same universe in man: that in man himself the firmament is driven by a wondrous motion of the corporeal Planets and stars: which, to be sure, all establish and bring forth their exaltations, conjunctions, oppositions, and other things, as you require according to your capacity: and whatever astronomical doctrine has drawn from deep and abstruse principles, through aspects, through stars, and other things, all those things are a lesson for you for this corporal firmament...

# TREATISE III OF THE PARAMIRUM.

<margin>One ignorant of astronomy never becomes a physician.</margin>
...it was fitting for there to be a firmament. For none of you can become full of <term>Medicine</term><note>Paracelsus views medicine as the culmination of four pillars: Philosophy, Astronomy, Alchemy, and Virtue.</note> if you are empty of Astronomy. Let it be said for this one part: that those things which the firmament encompasses ought to serve as an example and a guide for you toward the bodily firmament. From this, it is right to remember that the earth produces all fruits for this purpose: so that man may live from them and be nourished by them. You ought to believe the same about man: that within him all fruits are generated—whatever the world brings forth, whether large or small, or of any other kind—in this same way. You do not deny that the earth exists for this one end: to bear both fruits and man. The purpose of the body is the same. Thus, from and in the body itself
<margin>Nourishments in the body</margin>
all nourishments emerge which are needed by those things that are within the body. And these are the members of the body. Their growth is the same as that of the fruits of the earth. As the fruits relate to the earth, so the emerging nourishments of the body relate in turn to the members of the body; and so all things emerge within man. We bring these things forward here so that
<margin>The members of the body by nature lack external nourishment.</margin>
you may understand that the members of the body have no need for any external nourishment. For the body itself supplies them with nourishment from within itself. Here you ought also to observe this: that there are only four members which nourish the body; all the others are **Planets**, and they do not require any nourishment, just as the firmament itself does not. For the body is twofold:
<margin>The body is twofold.</margin>
The **Firmamental** and the **Terrestrial**. But I say to you: man consists of two types of creatures, namely the **Nourishers** and the **Nourished** (or the needy).

### CHAPTER III.

<margin>The bodily firmament needs no nourishment.</margin>
As we have now touched upon the fact that something exists in the body which has very little need for external food, so it must be known that this is the firmament of the body. For just as the sky thrives in its own firmament without nourishments, the bodily firmament behaves in the same way. But the body, which corresponds to the earth, provides nourishment from itself to four members. These enjoy that nourishment and have no need for any external thing, because four spirits exist in the body which the body enlivens and nourishes. But as for what is added besides this for the maintenance of the body—this is so that you may find that there is something altogether that sustains and protects the firmament and the earth, and provides that very thing which we find to be within them. But as for our diligence in seeking what form or face that sustainer shows: we boast of nothing in that regard.

Yet take our words as if man himself were also bound by a similar bond, so that he is forced to obtain some nourishment from the outside. But this nourishment relates to the body alone, just as manure relates to a field. By itself, manure does not produce fruit, nor does it increase the seed, nor does it do anything else than enliven the substance of the body and make it prolific, just as manure does for the field. For it contributes nothing else besides this. In a similar way, food contributes to man as if it were his manure. For neither life, nor intellect, nor
<margin>What food provides to man.</margin>
the spirit, nor any other such thing has its beginning from food or drink. Indeed, they are neither improved nor worsened by it. Therefore, food in the body behaves like manure in the field. Manure warms and fattens the field in a secret way. Food does the same for the body in a physical sense, but it does nothing for those things <note>i.e., the spiritual or astral organs</note> that are in the body. Therefore, let this be your introduction to the understanding of the following chapters: so that you may know that we place man within the firmament of his own body and his own earth, and similarly in his own elements, etc., as you will understand from the following reading.

### CHAPTER IV.

We shall take the principle of understanding from the firmament. Concerning which you will first attend to **Creation** and **Destination**: that is, the beginning and the end, and whatever each part is to do in the meantime. We profess this concerning the firmament. Note concerning this, that seven members are situated in the body: which themselves take no nourishment, but consist in themselves after the manner of the **seven Planets**,
<margin>The planets of the body take no nourishment.</margin>
which nourish themselves; neither does one take nourishment or food from another, nor does anything take anything from the stars themselves. Take this as proof: The Planet **Jupiter** is of such a nature that it needs no manure for the maintenance of its body. It was allotted enough provisions at the time of creation. By equal reason, the **liver**
<margin>The Liver.</margin>
also has no need to be "manured" <note>original: "stercoretur"; meaning to be fertilized or fed with waste-producing food</note>; rather, it maintains its substance without any filth. If you persist with an objection and bring up the "digestion" of the liver, we will turn that into a laugh, just as if we were listening to a **German poet** <note>original: "Teutonicum poetam"; likely a jab at contemporary writers who described the world superficially</note> babbling about the blue colors of the mountains, which are actually nothing. How we actually define "cooking" <note>original: "coctionem"; a technical term for digestion</note>, we leave to the **Alchemists** to announce—that is, to the peasant who puts manure in the field. For the seven mentioned members produce no excrement. Just as you have understood this concerning Jupiter and the Liver, so judge likewise...

<margin>Brain.
Heart.
Spleen.
Gall.

Kidneys.</margin>
...the brain is the Moon: the heart is the Sun: the spleen is Saturn: the lung is Mercury: the kidneys are Venus. And just as the higher firmaments display and perform their courses, you should judge the same concerning these lower ones. For if you are to recognize a <term>crisis</term><note>In early medicine, a "crisis" was the turning point of a disease, the moment when the body either begins to overcome the illness or succumbs to it.</note>, it is certainly necessary that you first learn the natural course and motion occurring within the body. If you are ignorant of this, then by Pollux!<note>An ancient Roman oath, similar to "by George!" or "good heavens!"</note> you will in no way be able to arrange natural diseases—that is, those arising from the **Natural Entity**—into a crisis. For the crises of these organs and those of the heavens are twofold: separated from each other by long distances, as you will subsequently understand more clearly.

### CHAPTER V.

<margin>The doctrine for explaining the crisis.</margin>
If, therefore, we share with you the doctrine for investigating the crisis, at least as far as this <term>parenthesis</term><note>Meaning this specific section or transitional argument.</note> is concerned, it is in this manner: When an infant is born, its own firmament and seven members (which suffice for themselves as the seven Planets) are born with it. Indeed, every firmament is born that pertains to and is required for a firmament. For if we speak of a "firmament," we understand a full firmament, by no means an empty one, such as is perfected even in an infant. At its birth, the firmament of this infant adopts its <term>predestination</term><note>Paracelsus uses "predestination" here to mean the biological "warranty" or pre-determined natural lifespan of the body, rather than a purely theological concept.</note>, 
<margin>Predestination.</margin>
that is, how long the Natural Entity ought to run or live. For I suppose that a creation happens at this hour. Then the end of this creation will be near—for instance, in the 30th year. For creation and its own end have this property: nature senses it in advance, and from nature herself she builds how long the Natural Entity shall last and for how many years it shall run its course. If you set a <term>water-clock</term><note>original: "clepsamum." An ancient device for measuring time by the flow of water or sand.</note>, you know as soon as it begins to flow at what point in time it will come to rest. Nature behaves in the same way in a created thing, so that she knows how long the Natural Entity will run. And as it runs for some time, or is destined to run, so according to that time, the Entity of nature and the created thing places all the motions and courses (which are owed to the bodily Planets) into the body itself, so that all of them in total are completed within that time which exists between creation and predestination.

Let this be an example of it: An infant is born at this hour, and according to the Natural Entity is destined to live for 10 hours; thus, surely, its predestination in the created Entity is ordered in such a way. Therefore, the bodily Planets will complete all their hours in their course just as if the infant had proceeded to the 100th year of age. Nor does a centenarian have any other course, although his is slower than that of the infant of one hour, or of an even more concise or shorter time. Thus we wish it to be entirely understood in the Natural Entity what is created and predestined; and it should be observed that other Entities very often break this predestination.

### CHAPTER VI.

Now we declare to you that the celestial firmament was created once, and lasts for an equal time with men themselves. Therefore, it brought forth its course once and its predestination at the same time, nor shall it bear any further offspring. Thus, all its courses are prolonged in such a way that it can wait for its own predestination. But man completes all these courses of his in a single hour if his Natural Entity has been concluded within one hour. Therefore, the change of the Moon 
<margin>The Moon's change is irrelevant.</margin>
has nothing to do with the brain. The reason is that the brain is renewed by the heart many hundreds of thousands of times, while in the meantime the Moon does not receive light from the Sun even once. The brain makes as many new moons and full moons in its predestination as the Moon does in its own. Thus indeed God established and constituted it.

Therefore, an astronomical explanation of a "criticism" or crisis based on the Natural Entity is entirely unskillful. For whatever weakens the body itself through the Natural Entity, it reaches its crisis according to its own motion, and not according to the firmament of the sky. Thus, with respect to the Natural Entity, Saturn has no commerce with the spleen, nor the spleen with Saturn. Count, therefore, from the creation even unto predestination, and bid the sky be the sky of its own firmament. 
<margin>The sky communicates nothing to the infant.</margin>
For the sky does not communicate its created state to the infant, nor the infant to it. Thus, by reason of the Entity, nothing receives anything from the other. If there were anyone who knew the predestination of the sky, he would indeed also know the predestinations of man. But God alone is conscious of predestination—that is, the end.

But, lest we be unmindful of this matter, consider also with me here what the 
<margin>What the exaltations, etc., of the body are.</margin>
exaltations, conjunctions, oppositions, and the like are. Namely, that they do not happen materially, but entirely spiritually. These complete that course through spirit, not by substance itself. For the rapidity of the course or motion of the bodily firmament does not admit this conception in substance. And so the Spirit alone perfects the motions in any member, just like the Planets, for which there is enough time for increase and decrease. Therefore, the world is called the **Long Entity**; but man is the **Short Entity**.
<margin>Long and Short Entity.</margin>

<header>PARAMIRUM, TREATISE III.</header>

<margin>The Heart is the Sun.</margin>
The Heart is the Sun. And just as the Sun works upon the earth and itself: so in like manner the Heart also works upon the body and itself. And although it is not the radiance of the Sun, it is nonetheless the radiance of the body, which the heart requires. For from the heart, a sufficiency of radiance flows forth into the body.

<margin>The Moon is the cerebellum.</margin>
Thus the Moon also likens itself to the brain <note>original: "cerebro"; while the margin specifies "cerebellum" (the small brain), Paracelsus often treats the brain and its sections as lunar.</note>, and the brain to it: but in spirit, not in substance. For this reason, so many <term>accidents</term><note>In early medicine, "accidents" (accidentia) refer to symptoms, external influences, or sudden changes in health rather than injuries.</note> afflict the brain. The Spleen performs its motion in the manner of Saturn, and as often as this planet strives from its creation toward its <term>predestination</term><note>As defined on the previous page, this is the internal "clock" or biological lifespan of an organ.</note>, so often does the spleen also complete its course from birth until death.

<margin>The Spleen is Saturn.</margin>

<margin>The Gall is Mars.</margin>
The Gall <note>The gall bladder or bile.</note> is Mars. But in its substance, it corresponds very little to Mars; this is because every firmament possesses its own character and substance according to the subject toward which it is directed. Thus the gall maintains its own substance, just as Mars does in spirit, and the gall exists in its own spirit just as Mars exists in the air.

<margin>The Kidneys are Venus.</margin>
In the kidneys, a Venus-like nature is inherent, as are its <term>exaltations</term><note>Astrological terms referring to a planet's point of maximum strength or influence.</note>, to a greater or lesser degree, just as with Venus herself, according to the predestination of both. And the work that Venus undertakes is directed toward the production of the fruits of the earth. Likewise, the power of the kidneys regards human fruit <note>Offspring or reproductive potential.</note>, such that Venus herself works nothing in the body, nor kindles anything. For the kidneys perform the duty of this matter, and nothing else besides them. And just as Venus is kindled through the conception of power from the **Great Entity** <note>original: "magno Ente"; referring to the macrocosm or the divine source of nature.</note>, so the kidneys receive their force from human sense and will.

<margin>The Lungs are Mercury.</margin>
The planet Mercury exists as a likeness to the lungs. Each is powerful in its own firmament: nor does one bring anything into the other's domain. And whatever use Mercury provides to the earth, and to the production of which fruits it contributes: the lungs perform this same use within Man.

<margin>The Liver is Jupiter.</margin>
The planet Jupiter is similar to the liver, even according to its substance, so much so that it is found that if the liver were absent, nothing would remain in the whole body: just as Jupiter himself, by his benevolence, softens and tempers all storms. Both also exist with equal motion and equal exercise within their own firmament.

### CHAPTER VIII.

What we have so far set down concerning the **Natural Entity**, namely how it conducts itself in its constellations: so that you may better perceive the foundation of the matter, we shall also examine these same things regarding the stars of the bodies, and then we shall rest. Nevertheless, for a fuller introduction, we shall subsequently bring forward several other things which will provide no small use to this <term>parenthesis</term><note>A specific section or transitional argument in the text.</note> of ours. This will be done in the following chapters, beginning with this principle of knowledge.

<margin>If the spirits of the bodily stars penetrate into other parts, they generate diseases.</margin>
The motion of the **Spirits of the bodily stars** happens from their origin or lineage toward the end of that member, and conversely, back to their lineage, like a reflection toward its center. Let this be an example: The heart diffuses its spirit through the whole body, no differently than the Sun through all the stars and the earth itself. This spirit alone is useful to the body: not those seven members for their own sustenance. The brain alone penetrates to the heart, and from the heart goes back to its own center spiritually. Nor does it touch any other boundary. The liver proceeds with its spirit to the blood alone, and touches nothing besides this. The spleen directs its course into the sides and intestines. The kidneys work their way through the loins and neighboring parts, and through the urinary boundaries. The path of the lung takes place around the chest and throat. The gall undertakes its motion in the stomach and intestines. These things are as indicated: you must know that if any of them should go astray and penetrate into other paths—for instance, if the Spleen enters the paths of the gall—then diseases are necessarily generated. And that is the logic of the other ducts as well. You will understand these things more lucidly and clearly from the book *On the Generation of Diseases*. But let these suffice here. Make a similar judgment concerning the other stars, that they too are found in the body according to the rule of that firmament: which is found to be true concerning the stars of the bodies and the errors of the stars, which nourish and cherish themselves from the reflections they make in their motions.

<margin>The seven lives of man.</margin>
For the exposition of this life, we say that you ought to understand **seven lives**, of which none is the genuine and true life, such as that in which the mind or soul dwells (as is taught concerning the soul and life). Thus, you understand how the other members obtain their life from those seven: namely, each one from its own Planet—that is, in that motion which it possesses as its own.

### CHAPTER IX.

We finished the previous chapter with the seven lives, adding that any given member is cherished by its own peculiar Planet. With that understanding, you should now know that whatever has life from the liver is subject to the liver. Likewise, what lives from the heart is subject to the heart. So it is with all the others. Now, therefore, the **Elements of the body** come to be observed by you. If in this doctrine we introduce a style other than what pleases you, or one that your collected notes are accustomed to: we shall not be greatly disturbed by this.

<margin>Elements in the body.</margin>
From these things, therefore, understand what the Elements in the body

# ON THE NATURAL ENTITY.

<margin>...what things are in the body.</margin>
...they exist in the body. For those things are dominant in the <term>Natural Entity</term><note>Ens naturale: the physical or biological reality of a human being, distinct from spiritual or celestial influences.</note>. For some diseases arise from the stars; others originate from the elements; some emerge from the qualities; certain ones are composed from the humors; and several are created from the complexions—as shall be spoken of hereafter. But so that you may understand the Elements of the body here, dig the matter up from its foundation. Fire <margin>Fire.</margin> receives its origin from motion. For the motion which those elements have essentially pushes out the heat enclosed within them, in this way: The element of fire in the body is invisible, unless it leaps out through a blow or strike to the eyes. For then sparks shine forth, for this reason: because the channels are open in that place; and because the strike was made near the eyes, in which place sparks can be hidden with the greatest difficulty. Thus, just as in this world we have no fire unless it is struck out, in a similar way it lies hidden and stored away in the body. Water <margin>Water.</margin> overflows in the entire body—in all the veins, nervous parts, bones, flesh, and finally in all the limbs. Nor is there any limb of the whole body that does not have water in itself, and just like the earth, it is surrounded and soaked by the same. Air <margin>Air.</margin> is also in the body, from the continuous motion of the limbs, which stirs up winds in the body. And just as the four winds arise in the world, so you should understand the same regarding the bodily winds. Furthermore, earth is that from which <margin>Earth.</margin> nourishment grows. Thus, the four Elements are found in man, no differently than they exist in the world according to their predestinations. Yet it will become more probable to us that the Creator fashioned a free creature out of four Elements which do not originate from other limbs, as the books on the *First Creation* demonstrate.

### CHAPTER X.

<margin>The source of the four complexions.</margin>
**J**ust as it has been handed down so far regarding the motion of the stars—that is, of the firmament itself—and then of the Elements, how they dwell in the living body and substantially consist in themselves, each one in its own power: so we shall explain the remaining annexed things to you with a clear teaching. And so that the Natural Entity may become known fundamentally, we press into your imagination the four <term>complexions</term><note>Complexions: the traditional medical theory of the four "tempers" or balances of bodily fluids (humors) that determine a person's physical state.</note>: Cholera, Blood, Melancholy, and Phlegm. But as we list these, we want no part in that opinion which asserts that they are or come from the stars or elements. None of that is true in the slightest part. In this, however, we will yield to you and prove your argument:

<margin>Explanation of the 4 tastes.</margin>
namely, that they are given into the body as a unique creation; specifically in this way: four tastes exist in the body. There are just as many in the earth: *acidity, sweetness, bitterness, and saltiness.* We bring you such an explanation of these four. Four perfect tastes are in any one subject. Yet in no subject are they as detectable as in man. CHOLERA <margin>Cholera.</margin> takes its principle from bitterness. And anything bitter is hot and dry; yet it does not reach the level of fire. For fire is neither hot nor dry, but it is Fire. Acidity is MELANCHOLY. <margin>Melancholy.</margin> For whatever is acidic exists as cold and dry. And this is understood under the name of Melancholy, yet it pertains nothing to the earth. For there is a great interval or distinction between Earth and Melancholy. PHLEGM <margin>Phlegm.</margin> arises from sweetness. For everything sweet is cold and moist; yet it is not equated to water: for the reason that the relationship between Phlegm and water is the same as that between fire and water. BLOOD is from salt: and whatever is salty <margin>Blood.</margin> is sanguine—that is, hot and moist. And these things are to be noted regarding the 4 complexions as they arise in the body: as they are *Acidity, Sweetness, Bitterness, and Saltiness.* We shall make mention of the rest in the following chapter. Thus, one may pronounce: if salt in a man exceeds the Entity of the complexion, then he is sanguine. If bitterness excels, he is Choleric. If acidity prevails, he is Melancholic. If sweetness predominates, he is Phlegmatic. Thus there are 4 complexions in the body, just as in a certain garden in which grow *bittersweet, polypody, vitriol, and saltpeter.* And all of these can persist in the body, yet in such a way that one alone excels.

### CHAPTER XI.

<margin>Whether complexions determine anything certain about a man.</margin>
**T**he complexions having been indicated, it must be known that besides these, as you suppose, nothing can be pronounced about a man from their essence itself: as if you were to say that a sanguine person is cheerful, or a melancholic one is sad. For this is false. Indeed, what you call properties of nature, we call properties of the *spirits*. Thus determine that nature grants none of these things, such as cheerfulness, learning, and the like. The spirits alone produce those things, not prompted by nature, but from the incorporeal things which are enclosed within the corporeal. Therefore, you ought not use that proverb regarding what is "prompted by nature." For a wise man did not promulgate that. But to the natural...

### TREATISE III ON THE PARAMIRUM.

...the **Natural Entity** remains to be described further; pay attention to the humor. It is exactly the same as the **Liquor of Life** <note>original: *Liquor vitæ*</note>. For from this the liquor, the body lives. 
<margin>Humor or the liquor of life.</margin>
Know this about it: there is a certain humor in the body which sustains and nourishes the entire frame. It is the life of the limbs. This humor is an Entity in its own right, producing metals in the earth, and in man, both goodness and malice. Therefore, accept these things in this way: Man is disposed toward a thousand virtues and just as many malices. This did not flow down to him from the stars, nor from any other star of the firmament: but emerged from that humor alone. Let this be clear from an example: The world contains many metals in itself (that is, many virtues)—in one place worse, in another better. This holds true equally in man. Many virtues are in him: the reason is because his humor is the "mineral" <note>Paracelsus views the body’s internal substances as analogous to ores or minerals found in the earth.</note> of a good nature. Many vices dwell in him; this is the cause which produces many bad metals. And these virtues do not correspond to the habits or intellects of men: but are judged by colors and appearance. For he who is well-colored is of a good mineral. 

<margin>What color portends in man, and whether it testifies regarding the humor.</margin>
He who has a depraved color is of a depraved mineral. But you cannot even affirm this: that a man who resembles a rose is therefore "sanguine" <note>The temperament associated with blood.</note>: or he who represents wax is "choleric" <note>The temperament associated with yellow bile.</note>. On the contrary, you shall pronounce thus: "This man is of a rosy redness; therefore he is rightly solar." For gold is that noble color in roses. The same must be judged concerning those other colors. This we profess to you for this reason: because it is certain that colors testify to you about the humor. From which you can also make a judgment of what nature that humor may be. For many diseases are subject to it, which are in no one else's power.

### *First Section.*

<margin>Four kinds of diseases.</margin>
**T**o the aforementioned demonstrations of the body's motion, add this now: that there are four of those motions in the body: the <term>Firmament</term> <note>The internal "stars" or astrological influences within the human body.</note>, the **Elements**, the **Complexions**, and the **Humors**. Concerning these four, note that all diseases consist within them and arise from them. For according to the **Natural Entity**, all diseases are distributed into four kinds. One kind is from the stars. These are **Chronic** diseases. Another is from the **Elements**. These exist as **peracute** <note>Extremely sharp or sudden-onset diseases.</note> diseases. The third is from the **complexions**. These are **natural** diseases. The fourth is from the **Humors**: which are **staining** diseases <note>original: *morbi tingentes*; diseases that chemically "tint" or transform the body's character.</note>. And as these four kinds of diseases exist: so you must learn to arrange the diseases of the Natural Entity.

### *Second Section.*

Under what name, however, all kinds are specifically designated: we do not explain that in this **Parenthesis** <note>An explanatory interlude or diversion in the text.</note>: but we shall define it more clearly in the book *On the Origin of Diseases*. And just as we have described the Natural Entity to you in eleven distinct chapters: so it is necessary for you to know that the body is only then attacked by its violence if the other entities do not hinder it but look upon it kindly. If you require a more solid foundation for this, you will find more about diseases also in the *Practica*, in which places what is missing can be conveniently repaired from here.

# TEXT OF THE PARENTHESIS UPON THE FOURTH ENTITY, BOOK FOUR, AND PAGOYUS.
## TREATISE ON THE SPIRITUAL ENTITY.
### CHAP. I.

<margin>Spiritual Entity.</margin>
**D**efining the **Spiritual Entity** <note>Ens spirituale: the power of the human spirit or will to cause disease, distinct from physical or celestial causes.</note>, we say that it is a perfect power for violating the entire body and casting it into any diseases whatsoever. Against these things, even if various assaults and various objections can be brought in: we shall nevertheless turn our backs on them all. For those things ought not to move us greatly: since those objections dissolve and tear themselves apart most readily. And the instances themselves ought to be firm: the likes of which, those that are thrown against us, do not yet appear. But as we are about to explain to you what the **Spiritual Entity** is, we urge you to shake off and cast away the style which you call **Theological**. Since not everything called Theology is holy: 

<margin>Not all Theology is holy.</margin>
nor is everything pious that it uses, and likewise not everything is even true which one takes from Theology if he does not understand it. Although this is also established: that Theologians describe this Entity with the greatest labor of all, even if not under the name and text of our fourth <term>pagoyus</term> <note>A Paracelsian term for a specific division or category of medical philosophy.</note>. Add that these same men may deny what we demonstrate here. Meanwhile, where sinews and marrow are lacking, we shall not struggle with them in words. For chatter emerges from an empty mouth. Which, if it had God as its author, we would postpone the loss of our paper and devote ourselves to their writings. One thing, meanwhile, I have with you, and it is this.

<margin>Knowledge of the spiritual Entity is not from the Christian faith.</margin>
Knowledge of this Entity by no means flows from the Christian faith. For us, it is a **Pagoyus**. But neither is it against that faith in which we Christians breathe our last. Hence, therefore...

<meta>This page continues the exploration of the different "Entities" that govern human health. Having previously discussed the Natural Entity, the author now defines the Spiritual Entity (Ens Spirituale). He distinguishes this internal "spirit" from theological concepts like souls or demons, framing it instead as a psychological and physiological force generated by human will.</meta>

-># ON THE NATURAL ENTITY.<-

Know yourselves: you must never think that you should understand this "Entity" among spirits as if you were saying they are all **Evil Demons** <note>original: *Cacodæmones*; a term for malevolent spirits or "bad Genii".</note>. For if you speak that way, you speak unclearly, and your whole discourse is as foolish as that which the devil himself puts forth. Regarding this **Spiritual Entity**, take note that neither the devil, nor any of his effects, nor any conspiracy of his is contained here. For the devil is not a spirit.

<margin>What the spiritual entity is.</margin>
Nor is an angel a spirit. That, rather, is a spirit which is born from our thoughts, without matter, within a living body. That which is born from our death is the **soul**.

## CHAPTER II.

Having established this counsel in the previous chapter—that we should dismiss the wandering dreams and petty opinions of theological sayings—we will now instruct you a second time on how you ought to understand the spirit. We shall make no mention of angels or demons here, as they belong to Philosophy, which is never going to describe our "Entity"; instead, the very mother of **Medicine** herself will be the one who speaks of these things.

<margin>What the spirit is here.</margin>
Therefore, regarding the spirit which our Entity encompasses, what must first be known is this: we propose to you that this spirit stirs up all diseases no less than the other Entities do, without any hindrance.

<margin>The two subjects of disease: Body and Spirit.</margin>
From this, conclude that the subjects of diseases are twofold, into which diseases may invade and be impressed. One subject is matter, that is, the **body**. In this, all diseases lie; in this they dwell, just as the other Entities act upon it. The other subject is not matter, but the **spirit of the body**. This is impalpable and invisible within the body. By itself, it can suffer, bear, and endure all diseases just as the body itself can. And for this reason, it is called the *Spiritual Entity*, because the body has nothing to do with it. From this you see again that the three previously mentioned Entities <note>Likely referring to the Entities of stars, poisons, and nature.</note> regard the body itself. But the two following ones—namely the **Spiritual** and the **Divine** <note>original: *Deale*; referring to the "Ens Deale," the entity relating to God's will or providence.</note>—refer to the spirit. And lest it slip from your memory, consider that when the spirit suffers, the body suffers. Indeed, it manifests itself in the body, yet it does not exist *as* the body.

<margin>Twofold diseases.</margin>
Accept this explanation of the matter: diseases in the universe are twofold: **Material** and **Spiritual**.

<margin>Material.</margin>
Material diseases are those which are "stained" materially, such as those from the first three Entities.

<margin>Spiritual.</margin>
Spiritual diseases are those which are not materially stained, such as the Spiritual and Divine Entities. We shall now pursue the Spiritual ones and explain their nature.

## CHAPTER III.

<margin>To what use the spirit serves.</margin>
Since we have established that there are two subjects, we stabilize that claim on this foundation: it is well known to you that a spirit exists in the body. Now, think: for what purpose does it act and how is it useful? Only for this: that it may **preserve the body**, just as air protects creatures from suffocation. Think the same of the spirit. This spirit in the body is substantial, visible, tangible, and sensible to other spirits. These, in comparison, are kindred to one another, just as one body is to another, in this fashion:

<margin>Mutual knowledge and anger of spirits.</margin>
I have one spirit; another person has one too. There is a mutual knowledge between them, just as there is between me and that person. They use their own language among themselves, just as we do; however, they are not forced by our speech, but speak what they please. From this, understand now that it is possible for these two spirits to nourish enmities and angers between one another, and for one to harm the other, just as one man wounds another. That injury is of the spirit; but the spirit exists in the body. Now, therefore, the body suffers and grows sick, not materially from a material Entity, but from the spirit. Thus, a **spiritual medicine** is required here. Likewise, there are those who pursue each other with a wondrous and unusual love.

<margin>Whence mutual love.</margin>
The cause of this affection does not lie hidden in the body itself, nor does it arise from the body, but it leaps out from the spirits of the two bodies, who come together in that society. These twin spirits can also be kindled with mutual hatreds and persist in that feud.

<margin>Whence mutual hatred.</margin>
To understand this more truly, take note: spirits are not born from **reason**, but from **will** alone.

<margin>Will and reason differ.</margin>
Thus you distinguish **Will** from **Reason** in this way: whatever lives according to its own will, lives in the spirit. But whatever lives according to reason, lives against the spirit. Indeed, reason generates no spirit; only the mind is generated from reason. From the **Will** is born that spirit about which we describe our Entity, setting the soul aside in its own place.

## CHAPTER IV.

Regarding the birth of spirits, take note of these things. It is certain that no spirit exists in infants, for a **perfect will** is not in them. Understand it this way: those who have a perfect will and act from it, generate within themselves a substantial spirit—and a "manufactured" <note>original: *factitium*; implying the spirit is something created through human experience and intent rather than being an innate biological organ.</note> one at that. It is not conferred upon a man or sent into him from heaven; rather, he fashions it for himself.

<margin>How spirits are generated.</margin>
Just as fire is generated from a flint, so also this spirit is generated from the **will**. And whatever the state of the will is, such also is...

It explains that this spirit can suffer "spiritual diseases" and interact with the spirits of others, causing physical illness through non-material means.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the discussion on the Spiritual Entity (Ens Spirituale). The previous page established that this "spirit" is not a demon or an angel, but a force generated by human thoughts and will within a living body. This page explores how these spirits inhabit their own "world" and how they can cause physical disease through mental intent or magical practices.</meta>

-># PARAMIRUM TREATISE III.<-

...it is also a spirit. From this, understand, all you who live by the will, that you possess that spirit of which we speak in this present Entity: which is, as it were, a certain subject into which all diseases are imprinted—specifically those diseases which must be borne by the very person who brought that spirit forth for himself. Now that the birth of spirits is fully recognized, understand further that there are two plainly substantial worlds.

<margin>The spirit world</margin>
One is of corporeal things; the other is of spiritual things. Now, in truth, bodies and spirits are united. For spirits are generated from the body through the will. Nevertheless, spirits preserve their own world just as surely as we do: in which they dwell perpetually and remain substantially, just as we do upon the earth. Among themselves, they mutually exchange and nourish envy, hatred, anger, and the like, without the consent of the bodies. Now, for our purpose, understand that it is permitted for us humans to live with one another as we please; likewise, it is permitted for spirits. For even if bodies harm each other, the spirits do not necessarily violate each other because of it. Conversely, if spirits harm each other—which is allowed to them by right—the body is not materially affected in such a way that we would be forced to do what is not required. However, if spirits do harm one another, then the body of the injured spirit is forced to bear that injury which its spirit received.

### CHAPTER V.

<margin>The spirit inflicts diseases on bodies in two ways: I. II.</margin>
It has already been said that spirits inflict diseases upon bodies. How this happens must be understood in this way. We show you two paths for this. One, of which we spoke before, is this: namely, when spirits harm each other mutually, without the will or consent of humans, driven solely by the stings of envy or other evil emotions. More extensive mention of these is made where we deal with Spirits <note>Paracelsus likely refers here to his other specialized treatises on invisible beings</note>, so there is no need to repeat it here. Yet this knowledge is necessary for the Physician, so that he may understand the matter clearly. Now we will explain to you the second way by which spirits inflict diseases upon us. Initially, we establish this: namely, that through our thoughts, through the senses and the will acting in perfect agreement, a "perfect will" is confirmed within us. Eventually, we agree, desire, and seek to inflict hurt and damage upon another person's body. This determined and confirmed will is the **Mother** <note>original: *Mater*; in Paracelsian philosophy, the "Mother" is the creative source or matrix that gives birth to a specific effect or substance</note> that brings forth the spirit. Take it this way: a thought produces a word; thus, the thought is the mother of speech. So, where there is no thought, there is neither speech nor word. The same occurs regarding the spirit. Just as a word is born, so likewise is the spirit, which takes up its residence according to our will, provided that will is full and perfect.

### CHAPTER VI.

<margin>How spirits inflict damage.</margin>
But regarding these spirits, we must further observe how they inflict damage upon us. If with a full will I strive to harm another, this will in me is a kind of creation in the spirit; my spirit, according to my will, busies itself against the spirit of the one I desire to harm. It acts not against his body, but against the spirit alone, which I then injure. That spirit suffers and is affected within the body, and the damage is felt in the body; it is neither outside the body nor materially inside the body, but the spirit performs all of this. Yet, in the meantime, a free struggle occurs between these two spirits: he who wins takes control. The reason my adversary may succumb is that he did not bring the same heat and intensity of mind as I did. But if, through a "kindling" <note>original: *accenſionem*; a metaphorical firing up of the spirit's energy</note>, his spirit was more fervent in the struggle than mine, then I would fall and he would win. From this account of the struggle initiated by spirits, you ought to understand that through these contests, "vulnerary" <note>original: *vulnerarij*; referring to internal injuries that manifest like physical wounds</note> and similar diseases are produced, which are not initially corporeal. Nevertheless, corporeal diseases are produced by spirits in such a way that, falling according to their own substance, they receive diseases that are perfected and terminated in the body, as is treated more fully in the book *On the Origin of Diseases*.

### CHAPTER VII.

For the sake of clearer understanding, accept a few examples of these things; once we have satisfied you with these, we shall conclude this **Spiritual Entity**. Let the first be this. It is known to you that 

<margin>The power of images fashioned from wax.</margin>
wax images fashioned according to the will of a spirit against another—if they are buried in the earth and weighed down with stones—then that person, for whose harm the image was made, is afflicted with many anxieties in the place where the stones are piled. Nor is he freed until the image is freed and dug up. Then he too is freed from his anxiety. But note further: if a leg is broken on that image, then that fracture affects the person as well. The same is true of pricks, woundings, and the like. Attend to this cause for this matter.

<margin>What Necromancy is capable of.</margin>
You are familiar with **Necromancy** <note>original: *Nigromantia*; here Paracelsus uses the term to describe "image magic" or sympathetic magic rather than just communication with the dead</note>, from which these things take their origin and power. For Necromancy can indeed [produce] faces or images...

<summary>Paracelsus explains that the "Spiritual Entity" exists in a distinct but overlapping world with the physical, where spirits generated by human will can battle and inflict injuries. These spiritual wounds eventually manifest as physical diseases, a process exemplified by the sympathetic magic of wax dolls and necromancy.</summary>

-># ON THE ENTITY OF SPIRITS.<-

...to fashion images, as if a thing were such, though it is not so. But it cannot harm the body at all, unless it happens that another person's spirit is harmed through this spirit.

<margin>Why one wounds oneself with a necromantic tree-trunk.</margin>
Thus a Necromancer <note>original: "Nigromanticus", referring here to a practitioner who manipulates natural spirits or "shadow" forces</note> constructs a tree and plants it in the ground. Whoever strikes or wounds this tree wounds himself. The cause of this is that his own spirit is wounded through the spirit of the tree. That spirit has hands and feet in action just as the body does; if it is struck, it strikes you. For you and your spirit are one thing. But understand it this way: your body does not receive that wound [directly], even if it becomes both palpable and visible to the body. Your spirit causes it, which possesses your limbs and body. Therefore, you should be careful not to apply remedies to the body itself. For that is in vain. Apply the medicine to the spirit, and then the body will also be healthy. For it is the spirit that is wounded, not the body.

### CHAPTER VIII.

<margin>The fashioning of wax images.</margin>
Note this concerning wax images. If I burn with enmity in my will against another, it must be carried out through a medium—that is, through the body. Thus it is possible for my spirit, without the help of the body, to pierce or wound another with my sword <note>referring to a spiritual strike or focused intent</note>, because of my burning desire. So it can also happen that through my will, I may drive the spirit of my adversary into an image; and I can render him distorted or lame in the wax, according to my pleasure. And although many other causes could be brought forward here, the necessity in this Entity <note>the *Ens Spirituale*</note> does not require it. 

<margin>The efficacy of the will.</margin>
For philosophy proposes all these things more clearly. You ought to know and hold this: the operation of the will is of great importance in medicine. For it can happen that he who does not wish himself well, but is full of self-hatred, may feel everything he curses upon himself. For a curse comes from the permission of the spirit, and it can happen in this way that images, through curses, cast people into diseases, such as fevers, epilepsies, apoplexies, and the like, if they are prepared in the manner mentioned. Let this not be a game to you, O Physicians! For you have not understood the efficacy of the will even in the smallest part. 

<margin>The will as the mother of spirits.</margin>
The Will is the Mother <note>original: "Genitrix"</note> of spirits of this kind, with which the rational soul has nothing in common. This kind of operation also occurs in cattle, and much more easily than in humans. For the spirit of a human withdraws and resists much more powerfully than the spirit of cattle. You will find all these things much more clearly explained in the book *On Spirits* and *On the Generation of Spirits*.

### CHAPTER IX.

<margin>Why a thief is forced to return to the place of the theft by the power of characters and is struck down.</margin>
You also have evidence concerning Characters <note>referring here to "characteres" or magical symbols and talismans</note>: namely, that a thief is forced to return to the place from which he fled, and likewise that such a person may be struck down even when many miles away. Note the cause of this, which is the foundation of the Spiritual Entity. If someone fashions a figure similar to a man and paints it on a wall, it is certain that all the punctures, blows, and wounds directed at the image are inflicted upon the very person in whose name the figure was painted—such as a thief. This happens by this power: that the thief's spirit is drawn into that figure by the will of another's spirit, which has forced him into this figure. Here you must also hold that these spirits, not unlike humans, are very combative among themselves. For this reason, whatever you demand to be inflicted upon him who stole your property by theft will indeed happen in reality if you commit it to the fashioned figure. This is because your spirit forced the spirit of the thief into that figure, so that he is now subject to you to bear and suffer whatever you inflict upon him. 

<margin>The honest and the good are not the same.</margin>
However, these things cannot be inflicted in this way upon others who are honest and good. This is because the spirit of a thief is trembling, like a [frightened] man; whereas, on the contrary, the spirit of an honest man, like a male <note>meaning strong, courageous, or proactive in defense</note>, struggles back and defends itself, just as two men would fight among themselves. Now, that a thief is forced to run back to the place of the theft happens because your spirit leads the spirit of the other back to that place where the theft was committed—namely, by your will. And if that spirit is so overcome, then he cannot return there unless he is forced into a certain subject—that is, into an image or figure. But if that is not present, then the operation proceeds to the medium in which he exists. Thus the spirit forces the man to return to the same place. For whatever happens through spirits must necessarily happen under the appearance of the subject in which the spirit dwells (whether it be a figure or an image), so that your spirit might drive the spirit of the other into that subject; or the subject in which the spirit is—that is, the man himself—is forced to run and perform it.

### CHAPTER X.

<margin>Spirits overcome and convict the guilty.</margin>
From the things mentioned, you should observe that spirits overcome and convict the guilty, and also carry out the operations of envy and hatred. Which was indicated to you...
