<header>PARAMIRUM BOOK III: ON THE ORIGIN [OF DISEASES]</header>

# PARAMIRUM BOOK III: ON THE ORIGIN [OF DISEASES]

...that diseases arise and flow from the blood, yet the causes of their generation are explained far differently than they actually exist. Hence, it is inevitable that physicians also hallucinate in their prescriptions and cures. From this, therefore, understand the true nature of tartar, so that you may prevent the error by which many have been given over to death through the sheer recklessness and ignorance of those doctors.

<margin>A twofold consideration of tartar.</margin>
Take note of two paths of tartar: one within its own "stomach" <note>Paracelsus uses "stomach" here to mean any site where the body separates nutrients from waste</note> and the other at its exit. The exit for the blood from the veins is through the skin—that is, through the pores. For the flesh, there is a "stomach" within the flesh itself, and likewise an exit: from the flesh all the way to the bladder. Similarly, the blood has its own proper "stomach" within the blood itself, just as the flesh does. So too with the marrow itself, and its exit from the marrow—that is, into the veins, members, bones, and other cavities. These facts and their private differences must be accurately noted, as must the "tartaric paroxysm" <note>a sudden flare-up or attack caused by these deposits</note> that follows. For he who does not know the paroxysms of tartar is unworthily called a physician. For the tartaric paroxysm and the tartaric "seats" <note>the locations where waste settles</note> teach the physician to recognize diseases which he otherwise cannot heal and would pronounce incurable. Therefore, diligent observation is needed in all anatomy and in the stubborn nature of such diseases, so that what confuses the physician and brings him to shame may finally be discovered.

<margin>Blood, marrow, flesh: the three primary parts of the body.</margin>
To comprehend these things, it must be known that the blood itself, as well as the marrow and the flesh, attracts its own nourishment, cooks it for itself, and removes what is foreign to it.

Now, these three are of great weight and importance, for the largest part of our body depends upon them. It must be especially noted that their digestion is so sharp, and their distillation so subtle, that no *chaos* <note>a Paracelsian term for an undifferentiated or atmospheric state</note> is so clear that these are not even clearer. If they are then led to their separations, their excrement is that which is indeed visible, but nonetheless extremely subtle. <margin>The subtle nourishment of things.</margin> The nourishment of these three, however, is invisible—not like the spirit <note>breath</note> exiting through the mouth and leaving a vapor behind it, which is visible but not tangible. That nourishment in the blood, flesh, and marrow is even more subtle. And whatever coarse thing remains in it (though it be invisible and impalpable), it is rendered even clearer in this "stomach" where the flesh, blood, and marrow reside; and whatever is there that relates to the body is prepared even more subtly. And this is **sweat**. It is visible
<margin>Sweat from [the elements]</margin>

<margin>The elements: why.</margin>
and tangible, even though inside the body it had been so subtle that it resembled and was like a certain *chaos*. We must speak here of this, and not of the nourishment, which is only a spirit that separates its excrement visibly. Likewise, the nourishments of the flesh and marrow are only spirits, without any visibility or tangibility. Yet the excrements are visible, though they are the subtlest of all things found in the whole body.

<margin>The nature of tartar in the blood.</margin>
Concerning the excrement of the blood, know that the tartar within it does not settle into that level of subtlety; instead, it mixes itself in, not unlike tartar in "burning wine" <note>distilled alcohol or brandy</note>. However much it may be distilled or even circulated to the highest degree, it will still retain the tartar within itself. Wine, however subtle it may be or however much it is distilled, still has its hidden tartar within it. It is exactly the same here. Even if the digestions here become extremely subtle, the separation is so fine that it leaves nothing in the nourishment that it does not expel. Therefore, this tartar is subtle and manifold in its essence. For believe this: it is coagulated by the **spirit of salt** <note>a term for acidic or mineral forces that cause solids to precipitate</note>. Then, it is also dissolved by and through that same spirit.

<margin>How tartar affects the members.</margin>
From this, understand that all tartar of the blood, flesh, and marrow consists in two paths: **coagulation** and **resolution** <note>the process of turning into a solid and dissolving back into a liquid</note>. Though it is true that other digestions often return resolved tartar, it does not have a single uniform cause. Rather, it proceeds from the nature of that kind of tartar found in wine (though that should not be understood literally here). It is more that the separation and digestion proceed so sharply, subtly, and swiftly through their **Vulcanian Athanor** <note>original: "Athanar"; an Athanor is an alchemical furnace, here referring to the body's internal heat</note>—together with the **Archeic preparation** <note>pertaining to the Archeus, the "internal alchemist" or vital force that governs metabolism</note>—that one tartar, which was destined for coagulation, is broken and turns into water. And that which turns toward resolution, being ordered in it, proceeds toward coagulation. It is like one who makes water from iron, and from that water iron is made; or like one who wants to make mucilage from seeds, and from that mucilage make seeds again, or something similar. Note in these things that tartar is born from elementary water, whether it comes through food or through drink. Hence it is resolved and coagulated just as has been described. Therefore, it also returns to its **ultimate matter**. <margin>Water is the matrix of things.</margin> For water is the mother and the matrix <note>womb</note> of all such generations. In that state, no further generation of tartar occurs; yet it remains as dung and waste, which cannot be judged as anything other than a dual nature of both tartar and excrement. From this, specific diseases later arise from the blood. Furthermore, keep this in mind: as long as that waste is present, it is subject to nature; nature, of course, attempts to putrefy and expel this evil substance so that it is no longer with her. Yet this expulsion is itself the disease and the "mortification" <note>the localized death or decay of tissue</note> of nature. From this, it is clear that from its putrefaction, one can distinguish what is tartar and what is mere waste. Only then should you seek the operation of the wastes, about which we will say no more for now.

What and where the stomach of the flesh is. 
What the diseases of flesh tartar are.

But learn further regarding the Tartar that is generated in the flesh. Flesh is <term>Sulphur, Salt, and Mercury</term> <note>Paracelsus's "Three Primes": the fundamental chemical principles of all matter</note> coagulated into a soft substance. Its "stomach" is a liquor <note>a vital fluid</note> stored within the flesh. This liquor maintains the flesh in its soft state. Thus, this internal liquor is the stomach of the flesh; it is an incurable matter if it becomes separated. From this, one can see that many diseases arise, especially all those that cause emaciation and "tabes" <note>a wasting away or consumption of the body</note>. For whatever wastes away has its primary origin in the "stomach" of that specific limb. Therefore, if the flesh wastes away, it is certain that this stomach we have mentioned is also wasting—that is, it is failing to digest and failing to nourish. Know, therefore, that tartar is generated here in the flesh when the liquor, which is the nourishment of the flesh, becomes separated. If this separation occurs again—that is, if the waste of the flesh and the specific waste of the nutrients are separated from one another—then tartar is also generated there, just as was said regarding the others. Furthermore, one must also know the places or "seats" where this tartar is produced and lies in wait. Every liquor of the flesh, which is the stomach of the flesh, purges itself through "internal sweat," which then resides in the bladder. This sweat pervades and penetrates those small veins, pores, and orifices, and by this path is finally collected in the bladder as urine. Therefore, in its theory, urine is twofold: one part from the nourishment, and the other from the 

<margin>Where is the location of flesh tartar?</margin>

liquor of the flesh. That which comes from the nourishment indicates its own path and the stomach through which it passes, as far as that is concerned. However, those things that do not participate in it are not seen in the urine of the flesh-liquor. Learn to recognize these through the nature of tartar according to their properties, together with the cure for each kind. He who does this holds more than half of all medicine in his grasp.

<margin>Stones of the bladder and kidneys.</margin>
Regarding this nature and the stones of tartar, keep in mind that they are often found in many regions of the body before they ever reach the region of the kidneys and bladder. More on these in their own chapters.

<margin>What is the stomach of the marrow.</margin>

The tartar of this marrow is not coagulated. For "fatness" <note>the oily or fatty nature of marrow</note> does not cause coagulation; rather, "leanness" <note>a lack of this fatty protection</note> does. Therefore, fatness keeps tartar at bay. This is the greatest preservation to prevent it. If, therefore, the tartar of the marrow does not coagulate and yet is separated, then it is "resolved" <note>dissolved into a liquid state</note>; that is, from it another peculiar liquor is born, which liquor equally [arouses] that paroxysm...

<margin>The double paroxysm of tartaric diseases.</margin>

This is how the disease proceeds in all cases of <term>chiragra</term> <note>original: "chiragricos"; gout of the hand</note>; it forces itself into the same places and seats as their own discharges, and it assists the salt in its work of eroding, corroding, and hollowing out the tissue. ### SIXTH TREATISE

<margin>The generation of stone outside of tartar.</margin>
In addition to these things we have reviewed so far, there are also several other ways stones are generated in man that happen and arise **outside** of tartar. This generation is similar to that which occurs externally. Because man is a <term>Microcosm</term> <note>the "little world"; the idea that the human body reflects the structure and processes of the entire universe</note>, the generations of the exterior world also occur within him according to their differences, as <term>Philosophy</term> <note>here referring to the study of nature and alchemy</note> proves. 

This type of generation occurs in those people who do not receive a "stone" from tartar. In these people, digestion and separation are healthy, and the tartar remains mixed with the excrement, passing away without coming into contact with the **spirit of salt**. 

Since there is yet another kind remaining, similar to the first but not following natural generation, you should know that since there are two generations, there are also two essences present. Tartar has the paroxysm within itself. These others, however, do not have a paroxysm unless it happens that a paroxysm is stirred up from that "neighboring border" where the tartar lies hidden. In that case, those paroxysms should not be attributed to the stone, but to that border, and judged according to it.

<margin>To whom these are familiar.</margin>
Many generations of this kind happen to infants from both natures, as much from birth as from their own specific causes, as is treated individually in their own chapters. I bring these matters up here so that you may realize the same thing happens in infants. For they often turn out to be excessively full of stones, even more severely than the elderly. Yet the cause for them and for the elderly is the same.

<margin>The method of stone generation.</margin>
But now pay attention to natural generation outside of tartar. Generation in matter is twofold. That is, for any stone that is to be produced, it is necessary that it have a "stone-like" first matter. From this it follows that there are two stone-like matters. **One** is in us in the same way as that which is in the "great world" <note>the Macrocosm or the outer universe</note>. The **other** enters into us; that is, if we ingest it—for instance, if we take a certain drink that is of a truly stone-like nature. This is not nutrition, but the very matter of the stone itself. 

These are those two matters from which a stone is produced in man. Now, that which actually produces the stones is the **star** <note>original: "astrum"; the vital or celestial governing force behind a physical process</note> of that element. This star is the fiery **spirit of salt**, which freezes them. This is more properly called <term>congelation</term> <note>freezing or solidifying</note> than coagulation. Concerning these things, consider that it is necessary, above all, to know the four elements in us in which a certain stone-like matter lies hidden: that is, in that "water." 

Now indeed, fire in its spirit of salt, in that element, is the congelation itself. Therefore, the four stars are four fires; that is, a fourfold spirit of fire or spirit of salt. And if a generation is prepared or emerges, its own star is also present, by which it is frozen.

# PARAMIRUM BOOK III: ON ORIGINS

...and it must be understood that we are not speaking of stones found in rivers, mountains, streams, or elsewhere, but rather of **thunderstones**. <note>original: "lapidum tonitrui"; these were objects like meteorites or fossilized belemnites that people in the Renaissance believed were the physical remains of a lightning strike.</note> For this is the manner of generation being discussed here, which occurs in the **Microcosm** <note>The "Little World," meaning the human body as a reflection of the universe.</note> no differently than it does in the heavens.

<margin>How a lightning bolt is born.</margin>
First, however, it is necessary to describe these generations as they occur in the external world. You should know, therefore, that those stones are drawn from the elements by their own stony waters; these are not yet stones, but take the form of dew ascending from its own element into another. This second element is the **ultimate matter** of this element. Thus are the **first matters** of stones in the heaven defined: that is, the quiet world contains this generation of wonderful things within itself. Now, in **Philosophy**, a thing is indeed invisible; yet it becomes visible in the ultimate matter. If, therefore, the spirits of the heavens, generated from salt, govern the sky, they then encounter these generations which are already that matter. Spirit and Time—that is, the force that coagulates—meet with other factors in this coagulation, and they are generated in the manner taught in **Meteorology**. In the meeting of these united elements, a stone is born in heaven, which is then thrust violently downward to the earth. Know that, in likeness to this, these stars and elements also lie hidden within the body itself, no differently than in the heavens. Now indeed, <margin>Man is heaven.</margin> man is heaven; that is, all men together are one heaven, made from a single **limbus**. <note>original: "limbo"; the primordial matter from which all things were created.</note> For this reason, one thing happens to this man, and another to that man. Though divided into his own parts, he is still one heaven—divided, I say, within man. <margin>A stone is formed in man in a single moment.</margin> From this it follows that suddenly, in a single hour, in a single moment, such a stone may be born in a man, specifically by the same reasoning as described above.

<margin>The material of a lightning bolt.</margin>
It would be worthwhile to examine the mechanics of this generation exactly; but this place does not require it, because it is already expected that a physician should be a **Philosopher** and an **Astronomer**. This much is certain: every lightning bolt arises from **salt**, and it is nothing other than salt in its **first matter**. <note>In Paracelsian chemistry, "first matter" is the initial, unformed state of a substance.</note> The spirit of salt congeals itself. The reason it is cast out with such a great crash is because of the salt, which cannot be united with **sulfur**. The salt here turns into stone; the sulfur turns into fire, which is the lightning flash itself. Sulfur burns in the air between earth and heaven. Salt, however, petrifies and is cast down in the form of a stone. Now, the first matters in man are all

spirits, and all the stars, and that "time"—that is, that motion or course. Stones of this kind do not differ much from a thunderstone in their blackness, colors, and other attributes, but only in their hardness. For one may be harder or softer than all other stones. Therefore, if you desire to know the theory of this well, you must first diligently weigh the generation of lightning; and then you will also have knowledge of the matter of the stone itself. There is no need to say much more about it here, because Philosophy at this point makes a man a physician by supplying the knowledge of causes. As for the rest, which pertains to the cure, let the Physician seek it in his own chapters.

<margin>The location of the stone.</margin>

From this middle, the generation proceeds toward the lowest depths. Now, the "middle of heaven," according to the nature of the stars in man, is in the cavity of the **diaphragm**. The "lowest depth" is the earth; thus also the bladder and its region, which lies beneath the kidneys. And just as a lightning bolt falls to the earth, so it also falls into the bladder and kidneys. For there lies the **anatomy** of earth and water; that is, the plain of the lower globe and sphere.

It follows from this: since this region is the plain of the lower sphere, it is also the place forced to sustain this generation, just as it falls and is placed there. It does not, however, fall during coagulation, but while in a liquid state. But coagulation happens so swiftly that it is frozen as soon as it touches the lower plain. Thus, even every lightning bolt only becomes a stone in the region of the lower sphere’s plain, whereas before it was a liquid—that is, the "liquor of the stone." For coagulation begins in a foreign region, not its own. Therefore, know that any such generation is not created where it is found; rather, it is always found in an alien region, not its own. For this <margin>The generation of stones is similar both outside and inside.</margin> reason, sand and stones grow and increase daily, just as **Meteorology** teaches. Now, if there already exists in a person such a dryness—like a **Bolus**, a **Stone**, **Viscous matter**, **Sand**, etc.—and that matter, having been dissolved by water, is unknowingly drunk, then nothing happens in the body other than what happens upon the earth. But if nature does not eject it but retains it, then it is stirred up by the internal dry spirit, just as water is by the air or the sun, and finally it becomes a stone. In many places, however, it is recognized as a "stone of the earth," meaning it is just like those found in the ground.

Furthermore, you <margin>Stone in man from intense cold.</margin> must also know that in a person, a cold, wintry constitution sometimes becomes so powerful that it congeals liquors by that coldness, in the manner of ice; and yet, it may again dissolve and liquefy them. For if there is both summer and winter within a person, then the higher and lower spheres—and whatever bodies belong to them—will also be within that person. From this follows and is proven the coagulation of humidities in the body, which emerge from its parts and which we call **vapors**: their seat is in the blood and in whatever part of the body is moist. Indeed, these vapors are that <margin>What are vapors and where are they?</margin> water which congeals above the earth; perhaps they could not undeservedly be called "humors," though not in the old sense. <note>Paracelsus is distancing himself from the "Four Humors" theory of Galen and Avicenna.</note> If this coagulation is dissolved again, there follow diseases of abscesses, pustules, and the like, which the ancient writers have not yet correctly understood, as will be more clearly handed down in the proper places. Truly, whoever does not know man according to this astral, temporal, and essential nature is unjustly granted the title of **Physician**.

The seat of these stones is not private or peculiar; rather, it occurs in any <margin>The location of stones.</margin> place in the body: certainly in the **emunctories** <note>term: emunctories; organs or passages that carry off waste, such as the kidneys or pores.</note> of the stomach, the bladder, the kidneys, and in the intervening passages. From this it follows that there are many medicines which may resolve and liquefy such stones, and crush them into either a bolus or a fine powder. The reason is that they were such things before. Therefore, the second coagulation is not so strong that it can do anything other than fail to resist the offered medicine that possesses the power of resolving. Yet other stones used as medicine do not provide this; in this matter, many physicians have been deceived, who <margin>A rebuke of physicians.</margin> have attempted to strike out and expel them with **crab's eyes**, and **Jew’s stone**, and **gromwell**, etc. <note>original: "cancrorum oculis" (calcium deposits from crayfish), "lapide Iudaico" (fossilized urchin spines), and "milio solis" (the plant gromwell). These were traditional "lithotriptic" remedies Paracelsus considers ineffective here.</note> But the ignorance of these men has now been sufficiently exposed.

# PARAMIRUM BOOK
## FOURTH.
### *On the Womb.*

**A**lthough we have so far spoken many words regarding the diseases afflicting mankind, all has not yet been perfectly handed down by us. For if we look to the foundation of medicine, then another theory of **Philosophy** and **Astronomy** reveals itself in man beyond what was said above. That theory concerns the **matrix** <note>term: matrix; the womb. Paracelsus views the womb as a "microcosm" within the female body, governed by its own internal "stars."</note>, which pertains to women alone. Since the purpose of this book of ours is none other than to correctly describe the womb with its diseases, just as the other parts have been treated, I would have you know at the beginning that I am speaking of invisible things. For who is there anywhere who has inspected those things in the anatomy of the womb which I am about to propose? And although it is true that nothing particularly conspicuous exists in that place, the whole matter must nonetheless be judged visibly. We see nothing in the air itself, yet we feel it manifest. So it is with the womb. Therefore, what we feel in the air, we ought rightly to "see," as if it were visible. For it is not given to the eyes alone to see, but also to the sense. Nevertheless, all these things must be established according to the nature of **Anatomy**—that is, all things must be deduced from a true and natural foundation and follow one another in turn.

...things ought to be established and defined not according to our opinion or judgment, but in this way: so that by this reasoning, a contemplation of the invisible may be made as if it were visible and truly existing. For it is not only what we see that serves as a foundation, but also what we touch; yet there is a method of demonstration for both. And although the matrix <note>The "Matrix" in Paracelsian medicine refers specifically to the womb, but also more broadly to the feminine generative power and the "soil" in which life is planted.</note> is indeed a very different thing, it is different at least in this regard: that <margin>The matrix is the smallest world.</margin> that which exists as the **smallest world** becomes the matrix. How this happens is within our right and purpose to explain.

<margin>A consideration of the Great, Lesser, and Smallest worlds.</margin> You see, moreover, that the heavens themselves embrace both spheres—the upper and the lower—so that nothing mortal or perishable may cross over and penetrate into the external kingdom that is placed outside this visible heaven. For a mortal thing has no kinship with an immortal one. Thus, the **great world** <note>The Macrocosm or the Universe.</note> is enclosed from the outside so that nothing goes out from it, but everything belonging to it remains within it, and thus enclosed, it persists as one with itself. Such is the nature of the great world.

Now, truly, the **lesser world** is man. <note>The "Microcosm." Paracelsus follows the ancient idea that the human body reflects the structure of the universe.</note> He is likewise covered and enclosed by skin, so that his blood and flesh, and whatever man is, does not exist in the commonality of the great world; that is, so that his internal elements, according to their substance, do not touch the external ones. For if they did, one would be changed and broken by the other. To avoid this, man is covered over with skin. That skin is "man," so that the two worlds may be separated from one another—namely the greater and the lesser, which is to say, the world and man—lest two different and contrary things should flow together and collide. Thus the world remains whole and undistracted in its own dwelling, and there is no one in that house to disturb or violate it. Likewise, man remains in his own dwelling—that is, in his skin—neither letting anything in nor sending anything out from himself, but containing himself in a stable seat, existing as one man within his skin.

But furthermore, it is not only man or the world alone that are so constituted; besides these, there is also another world, the **smallest of all**. This is called the **Matrix**. This too is separate: it has its own vessels, skin, and peculiar bonds, so that it also subsists by itself. This is separated from the "small world" (man). For man is the small world. This other, the woman, is smaller still, existing as the **smallest world**. For she is different from the man, and has her own peculiar anatomy...

---

...as well as her own theory, causes, reasons, and cures. And although she may endure many diseases in common with the man, these must nevertheless be properly distinguished by the physician—that is, discerned from the diseases of the man. For she exists as a different world from the man.

The Matrix is nothing other than a closed world, which has no kinship with the others, and yet is itself a world of its own. For the "World" [the Universe] is and was the first creature. The second world was Man. The third was Woman. Thus, that first world is the **greatest**. The next is the **lesser world**, man. <margin>The smallest world is woman.</margin> The **smallest and last** is woman. Now, the world has its own philosophy and science. So does man. So does woman. In the [Great] world, worms <note>Paracelsus uses "worms" as a general term for parasites or spontaneous life arising from decay/nature.</note> are born; so too in man, and so too in woman. This whole concept must be understood in the sense that these three are one creature, as in Astronomy, Philosophy, and Theory. If the world produces worms, the man and the woman produce the same. For they are not distinguished by their generations. Yet the generation is one thing in the world, another in the man, and another in the woman. From this it follows: because the "form" gives being to one world, it gives the same to the body. Therefore, from the body, a unique **monarchy of medicine** <note>A "monarchy" in this context refers to a sovereign or independent branch of medical knowledge that governs a specific domain.</note> is established: so that there is one monarchy of the world, another of the man, and another of the woman. Thus, there are also <margin>Three Doctors of the three worlds.</margin> **three kinds of Physicians**. One is for the world—this is the one who preserves it and protects it from the injuries of frost, snow, and so on. The second is for the man, who preserves him from harms. The third is for the woman, taking care of her. These three monarchies, even if they are separated from each other, are nevertheless a single thing within the monarchies. For they are not separated from each other by art; rather, art gathers and embraces them all into one.

The beginning of teaching this art is the [Great] World. It contains the four Elements within itself, just as they are situated in its matrix. The middle of these is Man, who embraces the concordances of both of them. The third and final science is Woman. Now, therefore, the Physician is whole and perfect in his theoretical reasonings. Outside of these, what, I ask you, is a Physician? But attend further to this: that the woman herself is a peculiar world. And just as the flesh of man is "earth"—though its reasoning, cause, and physics are different—so it is with woman. And just as blood is the Element of water, so also are the other forms and bodies. Yet it is nothing else besides the Element alone. And, just as man consists of three... <note>Paracelsus is likely about to refer to his "Tria Prima" (Mercury, Sulfur, and Salt), the three substances he believed composed all matter.</note>

He argues that because women constitute their own unique microcosm with a distinct anatomy, medicine must be divided into three specialized "monarchies" or branches of knowledge.</summary>

# ON THE DISEASES OF THE WOMB.

<margin>The elements of the womb are these.</margin>
Mercury, Sulphur, and Salt <note>Known as the *Tria Prima* or Three Primes, these are the fundamental spiritual-physical principles Paracelsus believed made up all matter.</note>: in these three, every world is established. Flesh is salt, Mercury, and Sulphur. The earth itself is also Sulphur, Salt, and Mercury. Blood is Mercury, Sulphur, and Salt. The sea, too, is Mercury, Sulphur, and Salt: and so it follows for all other things. The elements differ among themselves, for they are **matrices** <note>In this context, a "matrix" is a place of origin or a vessel where things are formed.</note>. Therefore, it is necessary to distinguish them. Yet their bodies remain Mercury, Sulphur, and Salt. Now, woman is also something else; yet she is also Mercury, Sulphur, and Salt, no less than the world itself, and no less than man himself. Therefore, hold this as certain: since her body is of that substance, she is also a world. However, she is distinct from the macrocosm <note>The "Great World" or the universe.</note> and distinct from man, just as her *Physica* <note>Natural philosophy or the physical laws governing her nature.</note> is also distinct. Because she is a world, she is similar to man and the macrocosm regarding diseases, but in a different and distinct way. For she has a separate office or function. The *Physica* and the *Theorica* <note>Theory or the scholarly understanding of nature.</note> separate each individual office. Therefore, even if a woman suffers from **dropsy**, **jaundice**, **paralysis**, and **colic** just as a man does, nevertheless the <term>monarchy<gloss>In Paracelsian medicine, the "monarchy" is the sovereign power or governing principle of a specific biological system.</gloss></term> behaves one way toward the man and another toward the woman.

<margin>Diverse Anatomy of man and woman.</margin>
A woman differs from a man not only because she is derived from him—that is, she is taken from his weight—but although she is from man, she is nonetheless distinct from him. Therefore, her **Anatomy**, **Philosophy**, **Theory**, and **Physics** are also different. And yet, she is also similar to the other two worlds. For she is the **smallest and ultimate world**. Therefore, as far as the consideration of the <term>matrix<gloss>The womb, viewed as a foundational biological and spiritual vessel.</gloss></term> teaches you that woman stands apart from man, so far shall you also distinguish her diseases from those of man. You must establish for yourself that what can be produced by the world cannot be produced by man; and similarly, what can be produced by a woman can never be produced by a man. Therefore, because they differ in this, all their diseases will also differ according to the same principle.

Thus, the function of the body shows us that the Philosophy of Medicine must assume a different approach toward women: namely, that their diseases should by no means be compared with those of men, nor should the same judgment be applied even when the signs appear similar. For even if the death of a man and a woman is similar, and even if similar diseases exist in both, the man and the woman must be considered differently by the physician. If you look at death itself and misery, thirst and hunger are the same in both. Yet the thirst of a man is one thing, and that of a woman is another; their hunger is also different. For if a man hungers, the **middle world** <note>The Microcosm, or man.</note> hungers. If a woman hungers, the **ultimate world** hungers. For the ultimate is one thing, and the middle is another. By the same interval and distinction that a mother stands apart from her son, so do these two also stand apart from one another.

<margin>Reprimand of physicians.</margin>
Therefore, we must not care for that error of the ancients who, wandering off in their usual way, make the diseases of men and women identical—claiming there is only one kind of **Paralysis**, one **Apoplexy**, one **Epilepsy**. For this is false. The nature of man is one thing; the nature of woman is another. Wherefore medicine consists in the knowledge of causes and the recognition of the proper cure. If some wish to put forward the erupting menstrual cycles in women as the only distinction between her diseases and those of man, then this distinction is so obvious that it could be found and established even by peasants and the dull-witted. For a peasant believes without a doubt that he is not what a woman is. However, a worthy physician does not perceive it so simply; rather, it is the corrupter of medicine and the deceiver of the sick who judges in such a way. For if a physician pronounces: *"The Apoplexy of a man has this origin: it is born from this or that subject, behaving in such a way, disposed in such a way; but the apoplexy of a woman is raised according to its root from the womb, in her subject disposed and tempered in this or that way"*—unless, I say, he pronounces it definitely like that, he certainly cannot be called a Physician by any right.

<margin>Medicines are either masculine or feminine.</margin>
For there are two types of Medicine upon the earth: of women and of men. For the medicine of the former is one thing, and the medicine of the latter is another. To women, their own remedies are suitable; likewise, to men, their own. He who neglects this distinction possesses no art by which he can fight against dropsy in anyone. For this is the foundation of medicine: that the same thing does not equally suit both creatures—unless perhaps this is affirmed by the mouth rather than proven by work. Why does the whole world think and speak this way: *"This herb is feminine, that one is masculine; this is male, that is female"*? Surely for this reason: because the diseases of each sex are different from time to time. If they were one and the same, why would there be a need for medicine to be divided in nature? It is divided because there are, in fact, two worlds in humanity: one of the woman, the other of the man. Since their diseases are different from each other, it is only fair that the medicine be different as well.

<margin>This reprimand of physicians.</margin>
From this, now understand the deceit and error in which Medicine has been entangled until now. Therefore, draw forth appropriate remedies for men from their medicine, and in turn, draw the proper remedies for women from their own **Anatomy**. Do not deviate even a nail’s breadth from this Anatomy. For its boundary, no one but a fool...

He asserts that because their fundamental principles differ, physicians must use sex-specific medicines and diagnostic criteria rather than treating them with a universal approach.</summary>

...is overstepped: who is rendered the cause and root of all deception by that daring.

<margin>The elements of the world nourish man.</margin>
It is truly right that we discuss these things further. For this matter will pull the ears of our opposing party <note>Referring to the traditional Galenic physicians of Paracelsus's time, whom he frequently criticized.</note> in no light manner. A woman is closer to the world than a man is. A man, however, is more remote from it in **Anatomy**, on account of his office: and that in this way. The world consists of four Elements, just as Philosophy teaches. Moreover, it is the world that provides nourishment for man through its four Elements. Air is not the first food of man. Heaven <note>original: "Cœlum." In Paracelsian thought, this refers to the firmament or the source of astral influences/heat, corresponding to the element of Fire.</note> is the second. Earth is the third. Water is the fourth. Man needs these four foods daily, and cannot live without them. Therefore, man is nourished from them: since in them both all nourishment and whatever else is for use is born. Now, if a human is conceived, they are in the **matrix** <note>the womb</note>. Indeed, the seed of man is the man himself. Hence he also requires that food which a human requires. He does not live in the external world, but lies hidden in the last <note>meaning the internal or most private world</note>. Hence he is also sustained by the internal world, not the external. 

<margin>A fitting comparison of the womb with the world.</margin> 
In this respect, a woman is like the womb of the world, but a man is not so. Therefore, you [as a man] are not a womb. And since that womb is a world in which heaven and earth, air and water are contained—which nourish the human from conception until his breaking out into the [greater] world—woman will now be something entirely different from man. For the nourishment of the fetus is supplied from her, not from the man. But if God created two [beings], and in one of them the world that encloses and contains the seed: then He also divided the **Anatomy**, **Philosophy**, and **Physics** between them, so that man might see from what lofty origins he arose. Therefore, woman is an entirely different subject from man. For her root serves for nourishment. The root of man, however, rests in the man. As far as the pear tree with its nature is distant from the earth, so far apart are man and woman. Man is the seed. Seed belongs to both man and woman. For the seed is his own, and in him: but its bringing forth and propagation is in the woman. A tree produces itself if it is fixed in the earth. Otherwise, it withers within itself. Now, whatever is seed, that grows out from it. Furthermore, the earth brings forth the tree from the seed: by what nature and virtue, or power, is manifest. By that same similarity and virtue, a woman gives birth to an infant, whether it be male or female. 

From this it now follows: if a woman is a field, she will behave exactly like the field of the world, which consists of four Elements. The field is the earth into which seed is cast. So the womb is the earth and a specific receptacle. But from the earth nothing is born unless the three other Elements are joined to it. Namely, water. The woman's water is blood. Here it is necessary for air and fire to be present. These two belong to heaven: <term>Chaos</term> <note>Paracelsus uses "Chaos" here to refer to the atmosphere or the invisible "breath" of the world.</note> and the <term>Stars</term>. And just as we clearly perceive the fruits of the earth to be drawn out and produced for growth by the Sun, Moon, stars, and air: so also nothing can grow in the womb unless the other Elements are present. Therefore, if the matter requires the Elements to be such: know regarding these that you must believe nothing else than that they behave differently than in a man, or what a man has within himself: for they all serve for nourishment. Therefore, because they serve nourishment, they are different from those things that do not serve nourishment. Therefore, man is twofold in the world: one body is the man, and he has one duty; and the other body is the woman's body, and she has another duty; and thus there is also another world: and even another <term>Monarchy</term> <note>A "Monarchy" in this sense refers to a distinct realm of sovereign natural laws or medical principles.</note> in whatever knowledge of things it is lawful to know about them. And just as the nature and condition of the earth and the tree are not one according to their substances and bodies: so by those same limits man stands separated from woman.

<margin>Censure of the physicians.</margin>
From these things, now observe how great an error it is that the diseases of both women and men are identified by one and the same judgment. For similar causes and similar medicines should not be prescribed and defined based on the similarity of symptoms; but the innermost source and cause must be weighed—what each thing is, and how much it differs from the other. 

<margin>The diseases of women are entirely distinct from those of men.</margin> 
This would have been defined by the ancients modestly and wisely if they had considered that woman is indeed subject to all diseases that fall upon men, since she is [taken] from man; but beyond these, they would have designated others so native and proper to women that it is impossible for them to be understood through man. But because they have grouped the diseases of women and men together under one common chapter and under the same treatment, it is evidence that they were led astray because they did not weigh these things in a philosophical examination. Woman, although she was indeed made from man, did not remain a man,

# OF THE DISEASES OF THE WOMB.

...but she was made a woman. Therefore, because she comes from man, yet did not remain a man but was made a woman, it ought to have been added that the diseases of women should by no means be called or understood as masculine, but entirely as feminine, by the highest right. If, therefore, a woman is different from a man, it follows as a matter of course that the diseases of each are also just as different. Moreover, they <note>Referring to traditional physicians who followed the ancient Greek authorities like Galen.</note> ought to have properly observed that divine providence, in all living things, divided **Anatomy** into female and male; and this was not done in vain, but to establish a method, so that from this light of nature, one might see how he ought to conduct himself. But neglecting all these things, the physician omitted the light of nature itself, and trusting in his own fantasy, he reduced medicine to such a state that it happened just as if someone wished to see through a wall to what was happening inside a courtyard. As that is impossible, so too is this. Concerning the method of discovery, a specific book has been written: namely, by what reasoning all arts were discovered; not, to be sure, through such speculations, but through <term>autopsy</term> <note>original: "autopsiam." In this context, it means "seeing for oneself" or firsthand observation rather than a post-mortem exam.</note> and eyewitness experience; not through the sharpness of imagination, but through the brilliance of the light of nature. He who gazes upon a thing with his own eyes is the one who has experienced the thing. He who does not see the thing does not experience it. Thus we also testify to nothing other than what we see, especially in Medicine, in which we see the two Anatomies of the <term>macrocosm</term> <note>original: "magni mundi," meaning the "Great World" or the universe.</note> and of all living things. Thus we also see two of man: one of the male, the other of the female. Since we see this, the handle is extended to us for a deeper investigation: namely, that there is one <term>monarchy</term> <note>original: "monarchia." Paracelsus uses this term to describe the sovereign rule or specific governing nature of a biological realm.</note> of the woman, and another of the man, and they are not the same in both. Beyond all this, the singular cases that afflict women more than men must be understood from her own monarchy, not another's; likewise, those diseases which, besides the common ones, leap upon them, have obtained a certain kinship and affinity with all womanly diseases. This consideration gives birth to an entirely different **Physics**; yet that deceitful crowd of physicians has not even caught the scent of it. How shameful this is, is easy to judge.

<margin>Reprimand of the Physician.</margin>
Therefore, O Physician, wipe the <term>glaucoma</term> <note>Used here metaphorically to mean cataracts or anything that clouds the vision and prevents clear sight of the truth.</note> from your eyes and lay aside that seductive sect. For do you not see what a disgrace you commit in those chapters where you put both man and woman under the same disease? This is so that—as shall be said—you may consider that the fountainhead of all womanly diseases is in women, and not in men. Therefore, their **Physics** also remains distinct from that of men. Furthermore, the Anatomy of women is different from that of men, which itself arises from a different **Physics**. You should by no means think to yourself that the brain, or heart, or liver in a man is the same as it is in a woman; rather, be persuaded of this: a woman's brain is womanly, not masculine; her heart is a womanly heart, not a masculine one. This distinction must always be placed before your eyes. Compare the woman even in external appearance with the man, and you will see what a difference there is between her and the man; and at the same time, take care whether you do not find the female is known as one thing and the male as another. If these things are separate, those things which are more closely related to **Physics** will be much more separate. If, therefore, a woman is something else, she will also rest upon another root. That root is the <term>matrix</term> <note>original: "matrix," meaning the womb or uterus.</note>, which was created for her sake.

<margin>The womb is the root of the woman.</margin>
If the woman was created for the sake of the womb, she shall also be fixed and established upon it; for this reason: because she was created for its sake, and received her name from it. If she was created for the sake of the womb, it will also be necessary that she be made from it, and have at once its nature and condition with and from it. This, therefore, distinguishes the female from the male: that the male grows in the manner of a male, from a masculine nature; the woman, on the contrary, from a womanly nature—that is, from the womb, upon which the male is not placed at all, but the woman is. And if she is from the womb, then all her members, and whatever she contains within herself, will be from the womb, and will be nourished and governed by the same.

<margin>The womb is the cause of all womanly diseases.</margin>
From which it follows that all her diseases are also from it; that is, they are born from the womb along with the root. The distinction lies in this: that all diseases have acquired their condition, nature, and property from the womb; it is not the same for the man, but he consists of a masculine nature. From this you can gather how great a distance separates the paralysis of a woman from the paralysis of a man. For even if both display themselves with similar signs, this does not happen without reason. For is not the woman a human, and is not the man a human also? Indeed. Is it not therefore right that they should agree in similar signs as humans? Yet the **Physics** and the singular condition of the **Monarchy** are reserved.

But is this not a distinction, if a woman is truly called "Matrix" and exists as a Matrix, while this does not apply to a man? Likewise, if all her diseases are of the womb? For she cannot have masculine Elements, since she is a female and a womb.

<header>PARAMIRUM, BOOK IV: ON ORIGINS</header>

## PARAMIRUM, BOOK IV: ON ORIGINS

And although the names of female diseases may indeed agree with those of men, this implies nothing other than that both male and female are called—and indeed are—human beings; yet they are divided by the aforementioned difference. However, it is utterly false to conclude that because they have similar symptoms and because both are human, they are necessarily of one nature and condition. For a distinction must be perpetually maintained: namely, that a woman consists upon the <term>matrix</term> <note>The womb, viewed here not just as an organ but as the formative center of female life.</note>, and she grows and has grown from the same, and that it is her root. Therefore, it is rightly the first thing that must be offered to the Physician for consideration in such diseases. For these diseases spring from the womb itself, not from a masculine power, but rather a "matrical" one. According to these powers, you shall also weigh your <term>Physics</term> <note>Natural philosophy or medical science.</note>, causes, and symptoms; otherwise, whatever you do will be in vain. And just as it is established that a single root thrives from which all diseases in a man spring, so there is also one such root in a woman.

<margin>A Reproof of Physicians.</margin>
Your writings, however, betray that you know nothing of these roots. Otherwise, you would have bitten your own finger before you published such a lie. Now, consider the root of masculine diseases; consider also the root of female diseases; and calculate for yourself how honorably you will stand with your "Physics" and your causes and symptoms? For unless you attribute a private root to women and assign a peculiar one to men—and unless you know that medicine is divided, and that this part must be offered to men and that part to women—you will certainly act not as a physician, but as a deceiver. To earn such a name, you do not need great industry in lying and flattery. For that seems inborn in you, learned with easy effort in the Academies. You will never find this example to be false in <term>Monarchy</term> <note>The sovereign power or "realm" of a specific nature.</note> and Physics. For in the same way that a pear grows from a pear root, and an apple from an apple root <note>original: "pyro... pomo"</note>, and that which has grown returns the flavor of its root: so here too, the disease is not separated from the root, but remains one with that from which it grew. And although the pear may be far from the root, it is truly from the root. The same logic applies to <term>colic</term> <note>Pain in the abdomen; Paracelsus argues here that even abdominal pain in women originates in the womb.</note>. Even if it is far from the <term>matrix</term> <note>womb</note>, it nonetheless flowed and was born from it, just like all other diseases.

<margin>Before woman, there was no disease for man.</margin>
In order that the truth may be dug out from its foundation, one more question must be proposed to you: *do diseases in general—both those of women and men that agree in a certain similarity—arise from men or women?* But the matter must be explained more clearly. No disease was found in man before woman was created. Nor is it established that man, who was created without woman, was ever afflicted with any such diseases as have been propagated from his descendants down to us. From this, one may now understand that since all diseases thereafter first flooded in, all our sicknesses, miseries, and afflictions have gushed forth from woman.

<margin>Human misery comes from woman.</margin>
If, therefore, a lesson concerning the principle and birth of our diseases can be taken much more certainly from the woman than from the man, then it would be more just for us to primarily approach this cause and speak more closely concerning the "first root," and how diseases spring from it. For we do not draw our blood and flesh from our mothers alone; but with these, we also extract all our misery and all diseases from the same source.

<margin>Man's diseases are different from woman's.</margin>
If these things are so established, it follows that a distinction must be seen between the diseases of man and woman; one must weigh by what kinship and familiarity they agree. Thus, it must be determined that a distinct difference is given between them, just as herbs and medicines are distinguished. Certainly, the seed of man remains in the man, as a man. And because he is separate, there will also be a transformation in him by which he is separated from the woman. Just as his form separates him from the woman (by which form he is also separated by nature, so that he becomes and remains a man), so also the woman remains and becomes a woman. Thus must we conclude regarding formation and its dignity. And yet, nothing is taken away from the first root of all diseases by these things. For no other root is found in man than that which was extracted from woman. But by reason of formation, it has been translated into another <term>Physics</term>. The ancient writers of "Physics" forgot this—and not without inconvenience—so that their followers might understand on what flimsy foundations they built most of their works and decided on the truth of things.

Whatever thing grows and is born in another is different from that in which it grows. Now, a man is in a woman no differently than a fish is in the water in which it lives, in which it grows, and without which it cannot live. Now, the fish is indeed "of the water"—that is, it has the nature of water—and yet for all that, it is by no means water. It is, therefore, different from the water.

<margin>A fish is different from water.</margin>
Just as, therefore, water and fish differ from one another, and yet...

<page-num>91</page-num>
<header>ON DISEASES OF THE WOMB.</header>

# ON DISEASES OF THE WOMB.

<margin>Man is brought forth because of the mind.</margin>
<margin>The woman is the field; the man is the seed.</margin>
<margin>A reproof of physicians.</margin>
...yet they are joined as one: so also is the man within the woman. The woman has the nature of the sea. Within her, the human being moves like a fish, yet is separated at birth. This happens so that the human being may know himself and realize whom he resembles—namely, that he is a living creature of the world. But because man possesses a mind, he is brought forth and born into the world; a quality not found in a fish. Now, if different qualities are attributed to the fish than to the water, and different to the water than to the fish, it is therefore right for the physician to observe this comparison: to know that the man is the seed, but the woman is the field. And although the woman herself is also "seed"—even if derived from the man—she by no means remains a "man," but transforms into "woman." At that point, the seed has escaped or surpassed its origin, and she is no longer to be judged according to it. For just as she was once "man" in Adam, once she was handled by the hands of the <term>Plasterer</term> <note>original: "plasta"; refers to God as the shaper or potter of humanity.</note>, she did not remain a man or the rib of Adam. Therefore, it must be determined that it is appropriate for both: that women be placed by the physician into a peculiar "monarchy" and be considered in another, more accurate scrutiny, both in Theory and in <term>Physics</term> <note>Natural science or the study of the body's nature.</note>. For they write wrongly when they say: "this chapter treats of <term>Jaundice</term> <note>original: "Icteritia"</note> common to both men and women." That kind of proof is worthless and trivial, by which we protect and veil our views through others—namely <term>Galen, Avicenna, Rhazes</term> <note>The traditional authorities of medieval and Renaissance medicine, whom Paracelsus famously rejected.</note>, etc. There is no proof to be found in them, nor in you, nor in ourselves. True proof consists in Philosophy, in the foundation of the **light of nature**. All things should be established through this, not through those triflers and word-craftsmen who carry the basis of things located in their own insane brains. Hence, it is inevitable that whoever listens to their voice will be deceived.

<margin>What is the Matrix?</margin>
<margin>Water is the matrix of the world.</margin>
<margin>The Limbus is the seed of the world.</margin>
<margin>Why fornication must be avoided.</margin>
What shall we say of the <term>matrix</term> <note>The womb, but also the primordial "mother-matter" of the universe.</note>, seeing that it is invisible? Since no one sees its "first matter," who can see what existed before themselves? We are all brought forth from the matrix, yet no one has ever seen it. For it existed before man was. and although man proceeds from it and is subsequently born, no one has beheld it. The world itself was founded from a matrix, as was man himself; and so, in a perpetual series, whatever is a Created thing has proceeded entirely from a matrix. For this reason, it is worthwhile to describe what a matrix is. The matrix is that from which man is born and comes forth. Here it is necessary that whatever was founded in the four elements be invisible. For just as the world is the matrix of all burgeoning things, so the matrix in the body must be judged by that same anatomy. Before heaven and earth were founded, the *Spirit of the Lord was moved over the waters*, and was, as it were, sustained by them. This water was the matrix. For in water the heavens and earth were created, and in no other matrix. In this, the Spirit of the Lord was moved—that is, the Spirit of God which is in man, and which all other creatures lack. For the sake of this spirit, so that it would not be alone, man himself was later founded, and within man, the very Spirit of God. Therefore, the Spirit of God enters into man; it is from God, and to God it returns. When, therefore, the world was not yet the world, but water, and the Spirit of the Lord moved over the waters, the water became the world. And thus this is the matrix of the world and of all its creatures. Since, at that time, it was also the matrix of man, God formed man within it—namely, a dwelling place for His Spirit in the flesh. The matrix of that man was the entire world. His seed was the <term>Limbus</term> <note>In Paracelsian thought, the "Limbus" is the primordial "slime" or extract containing the potential for all creation.</note>—the seed, surely, in which the whole world was contained. And these are the beginnings of the first man. Furthermore, man was separated from that matrix, and from him, a specific matrix was founded within himself. That is the matrix of the woman, which henceforth is nothing other than the whole world. And in it, the Spirit of the Lord is moved, which instills and impresses itself into her fruit. In the same way that He moved over the waters, so He is carried by us men over the earth and water. No one has ever seen or sees this Spirit. But it is the Spirit itself which dwells in the matrix of man—that is, of the woman. Therefore, she must not be hindered by <term>fornication</term> <note>original: "scortationem"; Paracelsus suggests that sexual immorality defiles the "dwelling" of the Spirit of God.</note>. For in her is the Spirit of God, which goes forth from God and returns to the same.

<margin>Man is not begotten except in a matrix.</margin>
Now, however, the <term>Limbus</term> does not exist in the woman; yet the Spirit exists. What is the Limbus other than the seed? Just as it was created by God, and from it man was afterwards formed, so God later substituted the "man" for it, so that he himself would now be the Limbus, fashioning a human being for himself according to the likeness originally founded by God. And since it was not fitting for man to create a human from the earth or the Limbus and breathe life into it, God placed under him another matrix, which he should contain within himself, and another Limbus, which he should animate. Thus, man remains within the nature of the world. And just as God enclosed the heaven when He was in heaven and fabricated man in heaven, so it is fitting to know that we cannot beget a human being unless we are occupied in a matrix according to our given power. For God did not bring His whole self forth from His throne, but at least His hand. So also man...

<summary>Paracelsus defines the "Matrix" (womb) not just as an organ, but as a biological "monarchy" analogous to the primordial waters of creation. He argues that women's diseases must be studied uniquely through this lens, rejecting the "insane" reliance on ancient authorities like Galen.</summary>

<header>PARAMIRUM BOOK IV. ON THE ORIGIN.</header>

<margin>
The three matrices of the three worlds.
</margin>
**Man** is not brought forth entirely from his own "leaf" <note>original: "folio"; likely referring to the individual's own biological blueprint or specific nature</note>, but at least provides parts defined and established for this work. Thus, there are *three matrices*. The *First was the Water*, over which the *Spirit of the Lord* was carried. And this was that matrix in which heaven and earth were established. Afterward, heaven and earth were made, and they became the matrix of *Adam*, established by the hand of God the Artificer. Finally, from *Adam* the woman was formed, the matrix of all human beings until the end of the world. What did the first matrix include? The *Kingdom of God*; it surrounded the *Spirit of God*. The world encloses the eternal, surrounding it. The woman is enclosed by her own skin. For whatever is within her is the matrix. Therefore, her body should not be compared with that of men, even if she descended from man. And therefore, she matches him in likeness. For she receives this likeness so that she may be similar to him; yet in many other things, she is separate from him—namely, in substance, condition, nature, and properties. For man suffers as a man; woman suffers as a woman. And both suffer as two creatures beloved by God. Therefore, He demonstrates the same through the double medicine He gave: the masculine, owed to men; and the feminine, attributed to women. For the physician must work from these. For God created the physician, not man. Therefore, the physician is given for the sake of bringing aid, not for speaking lies. He who is strong in this grace is the one the physician helps.

<margin>
What is the Limbus?
</margin>
Furthermore, since the <term>limbus</term> <note>In Paracelsian thought, the *limbus* is the "primordial matter" or the extract of all things in the universe from which man was created.</note> is the first matter of man, it is worth the physician's effort to know what the *limbus* is. For whatever the *limbus* is, that is what **man** is. He who knows the *limbus* knows what **man** is. Such a man is fit to be born a physician. Now, the *limbus* is heaven and earth, the upper and lower spheres, the four elements, and whatever is contained within them. Therefore, man is rightly called a <term>microcosm</term> <note>A "little world"; the idea that the human being contains the entire universe in miniature.</note>, because he is the whole world. Since, therefore, **man** is all these things, the physician must know the upper and lower spheres, with all their elements, substances, natures, and properties. If he has learned these things, he will know the diseases of man with little effort. For he whom God created ought to know more than he who is merely begotten by man. Therefore, within him is the knowledge and reason which proceeds from God, not from man. And let these things be said concerning the seed. But as for what concerns this matter further, you must know that God Himself, without any intermediary, created man from the matrix, and produced him from the matrix, and made him a man.

<margin>
The Limbus in man.
</margin>
But that order and method was not to be kept thereafter; instead, God sowed the *limbus* into man's nature, or recognized it there, so that henceforth the man himself would be the *limbus*—that is, so that he would have his own son. But if he should desire a son, God added the matrix to him: that is, the woman. Thus, henceforth, **man** is begotten from two, not one. He is not established from the matrix itself, but from the man, although he is shaped within the matrix. Therefore, from then on there shall be two, yet they are one: two fleshes, yet one, not two. Understand it thus: both of them together beget the man, not one alone. Therefore, they are two in one, and there is at least one, though they are two. Thus **man** is established from the *limbus*, which is the man; but in the matrix, he is shaped, formed, raised, and gifted with his nature, just as the first **man** was in the Great World, as was said above.

<margin>
Two kinds of diseases in man.
</margin>
Therefore, it is especially necessary that two types of diseases be known hereafter, namely from the cause of the generation of children, as has been understood: one, inherent or coming from the *limbus*; the other, inherent or coming from the *matrix*. And this difference was the reason why I explained this generation to you, so that common errors might be countered. Now, the matrix has indeed been made visible, but its properties and operations are invisible. For he who sees a woman

<margin>
How the matrix is invisible.
</margin>
beholds the man's matrix—that is, the world in which he is born. But what it is that actually fashions the man, no one perceives. For He who once made man according to His likeness still performs the same today. And that is the *Spirit of the Lord*, in that place which is carried over the waters. Now, the Water is the receptacle and storehouse of the seed from which **man** is begotten; that seed is the *limbus*. Now, the matrix is invisible in its operations. That which is invisible suffers nothing. Therefore, we wish to take up no discourse concerning invisible things. But that which is visible is the woman. She consists of three substances:

<margin>
All visible things consist of Sulfur, Salt, and Mercury.
</margin>
*Sulfur, Salt, and Mercury*, just as all other things do. For whatever must be handled palpably must necessarily exist as both visible and tangible. Therefore, she also consists of these three. Now, the first matter of these three is invisible; but the "ultimate matter" <note>The final, physical form of a substance.</note> is visible, which is the whole body of the woman. We must discuss this ultimate matter so that its <term>monarchy</term> <note>Paracelsus uses "monarchy" to describe a self-contained system of nature or a specific realm of medical study.</note> may be found. For in respect to this, all diseases emerge from those three—that is, whatever the ultimate matter of the aforementioned...

<meta>The text cuts off at "of the aforementioned [first]" matter, continuing the discussion of the Tria Prima (Sulfur, Salt, Mercury) in the next page.</meta>

<page-num>93</page-num>
<header>DISEASES OF THE WOMB.</header>

->DISEASES OF THE WOMB.<-

The first matter of its diseases exists from the very first. Therefore, one must first understand that there are three substances that generate those diseases, as they befall a woman—whether knowingly or unknowingly, in the past or present, or even in the future. From this, it must also be gathered that women alone are subject to the external stars in the same manner as men, though in a different physical sense. The bread that is given to us is food for all living things. If a man eats it, it becomes human flesh. If a fish eats it, fish flesh is generated from it. Now, as much as these two types of flesh differ from each other, so too does the theory of such impressions, infections, and so on differ. Therefore, that difference must be duly noted. For since all medicines and herbs possess this distinction, the physician whose knowledge is truth and not a lie will also admit it.

<margin>Reproof of physicians.</margin>
The physician therefore erred who described the womb, situated in the lower abdomen, as the complete and total [organ], and furthermore secluded the woman along with her operations, and outside of those, equated her with the man; and this is a <note>original: "glaucoma"; here used metaphorically for a cataract or a blurring of the vision that causes misunderstanding</note> cataract that is drawn over his eyes. Doubtless he had forgotten that a gateway exists in the world through which God reaches in His hand and works within it according to His will, doing whatever He wishes. He had forgotten that God constituted the woman as a world <note>the "Microcosm" or small world</note> in which man might be formed; and there, man acts in the place of God, who for this reason also has his contact free. This must be understood no differently than how God also reached His hands from His kingdom into the world of heaven and earth, and seizing the <term>limbus</term> <note>the primordial "dust" or extraction from the macrocosm from which Adam was made</note> from it, formed man: so also the man who has intercourse with a woman. If this should seem an obstacle—that God surely took only the limbus, that is, from at least one place, not from all—know that no one has yet understood or known this, except that man is a world, and the limbus is the entire universe. The same reasoning applies to woman: that the whole woman is the womb. For from all her members the field of man is constituted. And just as the earth has need to be sustained by all the elements—that is, all the virtues of the whole world—so also man is formed from the whole body of the woman.

<margin>What is the center of the woman?</margin>
Moreover, the center is that in which the operation takes place. It is also the entrance from every outer surface. And of whatever nature the womb is, the center and the whole body exist of that same nature: namely, the heart, liver, spleen, and whatever is blood and flesh. Now, however, as much as the womb differs from the man, so too are the blood of the man and the woman separated. And although both are indeed red, what is that to the Physician? Peasants consider both to be blood; the physician does not, unless he has been gifted with the veins of peasants.

<margin>Reproof of physicians.</margin>
For at least he thinks himself a physician, when nonetheless he knows his science no better than a peasant. You can achieve nothing with such people. For they cannot be persuaded to believe that some distinction exists between metals, stones, woods, and so on. A similar distinction exists in these as well. For although a human is man and woman, two forms and figures, and even two natures, exist. Therefore, the woman rules a different <term>monarchy</term> <note>Paracelsus uses this term to describe a specific, self-contained system of natural laws or biological domains</note> in diseases both common and unique.

Just as the forces of the sea or Ocean behave, whenever it overflows with its regular tide, so also this monarchy behaves. Now what is the cause of the sea's tide? It is this: that the sea consumes whatever enters into it. For this is its death. 

<margin>The sea is the death of all waters.</margin>
Thus all waters are swallowed and cut off in the sea, and they die within it, just like men upon the earth. But whatever consumes and kills has its own operation by which it breaks down what it receives. Moreover, its operation happens once daily. And just as a man digests the food he eats, and having received it, the stomach, beginning the operation of consumption, is inflated and distended, so also the sea carries out its operation. For in the sea is the death of water; nor does any water ever leave the sea again, but all of it dies within it, just like all things born upon the earth die. Just as the sea has its flows and ebbs, so it must be believed that these things also happen in the woman, for this reason: because she is the mother of children. The sea is the mother of waters. 

<margin>Analogy of the sea's tide and the woman.</margin>
Because the woman is truly a mother, she therefore produces such flows for herself, by whose agitation it happens every month that she is thus purged through the channels given by nature; so that nothing dead remains in her, but is entirely driven out and expelled—which, however, is not similarly observed in the sea.

<margin>What is the menstrual flow?</margin>
Thus, the menstrual flow is the excrement of things flowing together to the womb for the sake of mortification <note>the process of breakdown or "dying" within the body</note>; which are then expelled and cast out. False is the opinion of that physician who imagined from his own brain, 

<margin>Menstruation is not a flower, but excrement.</margin>
*that this menstrual excrement is the flower of the woman, like that of a certain tree.* A worthy physician indeed, who looks upon dung as a flower! The flower of the woman emerges when she has conceived. For in that very hour it breaks forth.

<summary>Paracelsus argues that the entire female body functions as a womb and follows a unique biological "monarchy" analogous to the sea. He rejects the common medical view of menstruation as a "flower," instead defining it as the necessary expulsion of "dead" matter, similar to the tides of the ocean.</summary>
