<margin>Two types of Doctors: Speculative and Experimental.</margin>
Others, however, through personal observation <term>autopsy|In this historical context, the term refers to the act of "seeing for oneself" or direct witness, rather than the modern surgical examination of a corpse.</term>, experience, chemical separations, and alchemical operations, know and touch the thing itself visibly and tangibly, as it is in and through itself. I fear greatly that those who are enclosed only in their books and studies do not attain more knowledge or experience than a man shut in a monastery who only knows the rounds and the ropes of the bells. And just as the knowledge of the latter has no more efficacy than knowing something uncertain and hidden, so too is medicine ineffective and powerless if it judges visible things so invisibly. Everything I have said so far aims to let you know that I reject and discard the description of the generation and cause of Tartar <note>original: "Tartari"</note> <note>In the Paracelsian system, "Tartar" refers to stony or gravel-like deposits in the body, such as kidney stones or gouty crystals, which Paracelsus compared to the hard crust left by wine in a barrel.</note> brought forth by the ancients. For that should not be taught speculatively, but must be explained **Realistically** (just as the matter is in itself), so that everything is known and understood demonstratively. This must be the goal, the reason for Medical Theory: without this demonstration, a Doctor will never penetrate into solid truth.

<margin>Where the types of Tartar are born.</margin>
Since, therefore, the types of Tartars are by no means found in those libraries where writings of invented Theory are kept, it is entirely right that another Library be sought and opened, in which the thing itself is taught demonstratively and the true and genuine species are solidly understood. Indeed, the **entire world** is that Library. Not just one part of it must be read through,

<margin>The World is the Doctor's Library.</margin>
but one must fly through both the Elements themselves and the upper and lower spheres. This must be done not only for this disease, but it is also required for a universal Medical Theory. Pay attention to what properly and entirely belongs here. For this Theory draws its foundation from those things alone which <margin>Knowledge of Tartar from water and earth only.</margin> the earth and water contain: that is, from these two Elements alone proceed the Theory, cause, origin, and description of all Tartar. Not that I am setting limits for the Library here, but rather that I am establishing that paper itself, with its false Theory, does not demonstrate the true origin at all. Rather, the earth and water—as two Elements and twin Wombs <term>Matrices|The source or environment in which something originates or develops; in Paracelsian thought, elements act as "mothers" to specific substances.</term>—are those genuine books and volumes in which the Theory of Tartar is demonstrated abundantly enough. If, therefore, this kind of book is the book of Medicine, I confess indeed that where I leave off, a second, third, fourth, etc., begins, until everything is finished and perfected. That is, if I were to say that I have traveled through Asia and Africa and turned their leaves, I would not be telling the truth. However, I have traversed and known the greatest part of Europe. For who can crawl through and penetrate every corner of the world?

For this reason also, each Nation has been given its own peculiar remedies, which a suitable Doctor must reduce into a fitting Theory. For I am convinced of this: that my recipes <margin>Which remedies are suitable for whom.</margin> may not be particularly fruitful for foreign peoples, just as, conversely, exotic remedies do not suit us. Take it this way. I write indeed for Europe. <margin>Theophrastus writes for Europe.</margin> <note>"Theophrastus" refers to the author, Theophrastus von Hohenheim, better known as Paracelsus.</note> Whether Asia or Africa can enjoy my writings, I doubt. I know this: the remedies of those places are of the very least use to us. For just as each day has its own affliction, so too does each region have its own evil attached. The same lot belongs to every Nation, province, valley, and climate. And just as tomorrow's care awaits its day, so too does its own anxiety occupy every region, nation, and province. In respect of all these things, it is appropriate—indeed, necessary—that everyone be a **Cosmographer and Geographer**, who turns the leaves of his art with his feet and sees with his own eyes <margin>Travel is useful for Doctors.</margin> what is proper and peculiar to each region, and if any other Theory of nations demonstrates itself to Doctors. Therefore, the survey of lands is very much to this purpose: so that it may be known how many species of them...

species

->ON TARTARIC DISEASES<-
<note>original: "TARTAREIS"</note>

...there are species defined by individual regions. If those regions are studied with singular industry, and it is learned what kind of <term>Tartaric bodies|In Paracelsian medicine, "Tartar" refers to stony or chalky precipitates—like kidney stones, gouty deposits, or dental plaque—named after the hard crust found in wine barrels.</term> are found in each: then by the same shortcut, the various kinds of Tartaric species will be discovered and made available. For this reason, it seems advisable to me that every Physician, following this guidance and Method, should experience and describe the Tartaric bodies of his own homeland, and thereafter the specific types of Tartar found there. Indeed, if this were completed by the Physicians of all nations with the same purpose, then at last the **book of Physicians, which is Earth and Water**, could be described and recorded on paper from a most certain foundation and principle. And yet, even in this way, nothing more would be contained than an image painted on cloth; although the original prototype itself would not be present, it could nonetheless be known in a certain way through the icon. For although the entire world can be compressed and drawn into a map, so that its whole character and face can be learned and known even by one who has not physically walked the earth: nevertheless, it is necessary that someone first experienced all those things and impressed them upon the paper according to the measure of his experience. From this idea, other learned men may subsequently draw and take the momentum of their own knowledge. Only then will you have reached, read, and known the true Library of the medical profession, if you have scraped together your learning from the genuine book of nature, and tested your works against it, as if against a <note>The "Lydian stone" is a touchstone used to test the purity of gold; the author suggests nature is the only true test of medical truth.</note>Lydian stone.

<margin>
Travel is necessary for the future Physician.
</margin>

Whoever of the Physicians, therefore, wishes to be a person of upright Theory, must act as a traveler and a wanderer, and turn the leaves of books by surveying the lands—not sitting in his mother’s lap gnawing on figs roasted on a spit, just as those writers until now have hunted their experience no further than they could immediately spring back to their homeland stove. That is to say: they attain all their experience in <note>original: "hypocaustis" – heated rooms or sweat-baths; here used as a metaphor for comfortable, indoor academic life compared to the rigors of field observation.</note>heated parlors. In such a place, however, mere phantasms are learned, destitute of a solid foundation. But you, so that you may primarily understand the Library of the species of Tartar, must know that the species of Tartar in the internal man are to be known entirely from external things; that is, man conceives Tartar from the bodies of both Elements.

<margin>
Man conceives Tartar from the Elements.
</margin>

From this it is also established that whatever Tartaric matter the Elements themselves contain, that same matter enters into man from them. Thus, the external Tartar is truly representative of how the internal Tartar dominates. For the genus is one, the logic is one, the matter is one, and the essence is the same. The name should not be given metaphorically, but essentially, from that essence whose essence it actually is. For no Tartar is invisible on the outside that is not also exhibited visibly: that is, all Tartars become conspicuous externally through the examination of bodies.

<margin>
Tartar must be exhibited demonstratively.
</margin>

From this I can speak demonstratively, not merely speculatively. Therefore, corporal Tartar is nothing other than that which exists in man. Thus, it is not an unequal comparison when one is compared closely with the other. Therefore, use and the reality of the matter require that all species of Tartar, however many there are in the whole world, be known, and that it be understood how many bodies exist in nature, and how many ways their differences exist.

<margin>
The species of internal Tartar must be known from the external species.
</margin>

An example of this consideration is found in wine, in water, in the juices of fruits, herbs, etc. These, clearly, are those bodies in which Tartar is stored, from which it later also enters into man himself. There are various kinds of wine, various kinds of water, various kinds of fruits, herbs, and other foods.

<margin>
Wine, water, etc. are the subjects of Tartar. Composite bodies give composite Tartar.
</margin>

So also there are various kinds of Tartaric diseases in man. To these add those which emerge from composition: that is, if two bodies are joined, another kind of Tartar emerges; if more are joined, yet another. This matter is entirely worthy of the most accurate consideration. For many secrets are stored here. From this also, many obscurities occur in Tartaric diseases. All of which, however, I emphasize here for this purpose: that for that manifold diversity, manifold remedies might also be sought and applied.

<margin>
A specific remedy for every Tartar.
</margin>

For the kind of Tartar from wine requires one kind of medicine, the kind from water another, the kind from fruits and juices another, and finally, the kind from milk and similar foods another. Unless this distinction is diligently observed, no cure can be made safe and secure. For <note>The author repeats the bell metaphor from the previous page to emphasize that specific problems require specific tools.</note>not every rope is fit for ringing every bell. Thus, therefore, the Tartar of a man must be judged according to the Tartar of his region. Likewise, other books cannot supply the Library of Tartars unless they are those whose leaves are turned with the feet, as has been handed down in this chapter. And this is how the Theory of Tartar stands. By this reasoning, the causes of Tartar are found. From these books...

For they sought Tartar where it was not, and where it could not be found. Therefore, it is necessary that we thoroughly investigate and survey the lands, and closely research the diversity of species. For just as the logic of the outer world is evident, the same truth exists in the Tartar of man. But if you are ashamed of travel—to seek anything there where it is readily available—you will certainly never achieve the goal of your purpose.

<margin>The eyes are the teachers of things.</margin>
Indeed, what shame is there in learning those things which the eyes present or experience teaches? Must we not learn almost everything through the discipline of the eyes? For the eyes, which take delight in the experience of things, stand as your most faithful professors. For neither your own fantasies nor speculations can advance you to such dignity that you can rightfully and without <term>sophistry|The use of clever but false arguments, especially by the academic doctors of the time whom Paracelsus frequently criticized.</term> boast of being a Physician—though most Sophists are accustomed to doing this frequently, thinking they have tasted and traversed all the boundaries and limits of the world, the air, and all the Elements.

<margin>A rebuke of Physicians.</margin>
But they do not merely persuade themselves of this rashly; they even dream that they know what God is doing in heaven, what counsel He keeps and meditates upon. For they claim, too confidently, that none of these things is unknown to them. However, no Physician is permitted to trust such a rash persuasion, or to believe anything anywhere of such vain dreams.

### CHAPTER III.

->What the matter of Tartar is, and from whence it arises in those things in which it is uniformly generated.<-

<margin>What the matter of Tartar is like.</margin>
It is **NEXT** for me to explain to you what the matter of Tartar finally is, and how it ought to be known outside in the world: that is, in which bodies it lies, and by what logic it is united there. That Tartaric matter, then, is a natural superfluity, extracted from all <term>coagulated bodies|Solid or thickened substances; in this context, everything from minerals to plants that has taken a fixed form.</term> according to the mode and logic of each concordance, mixed with the seed of that earthly nature which separates from the coagulated bodies. Note here that every body ought to exist by itself, without the mixture of others; namely, let water be only water, wine be wine, without anything else that is not wine. So too, the juices of herbs must be pure, and the juices of leaves must be such that they have nothing else mixed in.

<margin>Pure and impure are in all things.</margin>
But in natural things, it is not so: rather, in all things, the pure and the impure are joined together, like water with mud, or wine with dregs. If, therefore, the pure is separated from the impure, then the water is only water, and the wine is only wine. Now, therefore, know that the impure thing is the Tartar about which I speak and write. But at the same time, note this distinction: that there is a twofold nature of the impure. One regards *Resolution* <note>original: "Resolutionem," referring to the state of remaining dissolved or liquid.</note>; the other *Coagulation* <note>original: "Coagulationem," the process of becoming solid or forming sediment.</note>. That which inclines toward Resolution does not concern Tartar in this place. Nor is anything else handed down about it in this book, except under the guise or form of impure mud within the pure. The other, however, exists as the Tartar of Coagulation.

<margin>Impurity is either of Resolution or of Coagulation.</margin>
And this is that disease of which I treat here, as will be explained more clearly hereafter. But besides these, note also two other things regarding the Tartaric body: namely, *stony mucilage and the Salt of Gems*. These two are the impurity of bodies, and they lean toward the nature of stony coagulation and formation. Furthermore, from Water are born *Gems and stones*; from Earth, *Tartars*.

<margin>All Tartar is either from water or earth.</margin>
For the matter itself teaches that there are two kinds of Tartars: one from the Element of *Water*, the other from the Element of *Earth*, yet both generate Tartar. These things must be understood by you in this way. For the humidity of the earth contains within itself a congenital salt, and moreover a Tartaric nature under the form of viscosity, which separates from coagulated bodies into the earthly humidity—no differently than bark or a fungus, or mistletoe, from the tree itself; all of which are indeed secreted and emerge from the tree, yet they are by no means the tree itself. Just as, therefore, mistletoe or a fungus varies and changes, so likewise from stones some such matter emerges and passes into the liquor of the earth, which liquor later becomes the nourishment of all things being born. If growing things soak up a liquor of this kind, and the <term>Archeus of Nature|An internal "alchemist" or vital force believed to reside in the organs (like the stomach) to separate the nutritious part of food from the waste.</term> does not purge or separate the filth—that is, if it does not separate the Tartar from the liquor, but leaves it together with the nourishment—then that which is left in the growing things is eventually ingested into the human being himself. To understand this more clearly, take further note: in the waters, all kinds of stones are born, both good and bad, which grow from the water just as trees grow from the earth. Now, however...
<margin>Stones from water.</margin>

<margin>What the Dead Head is.</margin>
A certain residue remains through the process, which exists in the likeness of a <term>Dead Head|original: "Caput Mortuum"; an alchemical term for the worthless, inert residue left behind after a chemical reaction or distillation.</term>, and is unfit and incapable of becoming a stone. This residue is mixed into its own matrix—that is, its own Element—and remains within it, existing as the impurity of that Element. In this way, the body itself and the impurity are one mixture; they grow together as one, and are together attracted and drawn in by all growing things. Thus, he who drinks water also drinks the impurity with it. He who drinks wine also drinks the impurity with it. Thus, whatever we consume, the pure and the impure exist within it as a single mixture. Such is the mucilage and salt which, in the manner of the aforementioned examples, come from stones, so that there is a stony mucilage and a <term>salt of gems|A reference to "Sal Gemmae," which refers to rock salt or common salt found in the earth.</term> of a stony nature; yet these are separated from the stones just as bark or a fungus is separated from its tree. For as far as the bark and the fungus are from the tree, though they grow from the same source: so far also are the Tartar and the stone or sand—which are the matter of Tartar in man—removed from herbs. And just as that species of stone and sand behaves within itself, so Tartar is also produced and formed according to its nature, though keeping that distinction which exists between a fungus and wood. Therefore, just as a fungus or bark can by no means be called wood, so neither should Tartar be called or thought of as stone or sand. It shall therefore be called a "superfluous residual mucilage" and a "superfluous residual salt of gems." If these two principal parts are now entangled and begin their operation, then from them is produced that which those <term>sperms|In this context, "spermata" refers to the "seeds" or formative principles of a substance.</term> are able to become.

<margin>Sperm as the cause of generation.</margin>
For all generation is completed by the power of sperms. The seed of any thing, unless it possesses a sperm, does not produce its herb. The matter stands similarly here: just as iron and fire become a nail through the work of a blacksmith. If the fire departs, it leaves the nail, contributing nothing else to it except that it becomes a nail. The same happens with the salt and the mucilage.

<margin>Mucilage is the body of the thing; salt coagulates.</margin>
The salt departs; the mucilage remains and is Tartar. This is the same as saying: Mucilage is that body which salt freezes and coagulates. Once the coagulation is done, let the salt depart, and it crumbles away into excrement. However, no excrement is made from the Tartaric mucilage, but that mass subsists by itself. Thus, a certain conjunction is found, wherein it is necessary for the superfluous sperm to consist perfectly within the salt and mucilage; and moreover, the <term>Archeus|The internal alchemist or vital force that Paracelsus believed resided in the stomach and organs to separate the pure from the impure.</term> must be present in the place and stead of the blacksmith. If any of these three is not perfectly present, the generation of Tartar cannot happen—which is actually better for the sake of health. The reason is that the disease of Tartar is not generated in that way. However, another putrefaction is introduced in its place, which itself acts as a disease. Therefore, you must know that the superfluous sperm of coagulated bodies becomes the Tartar itself, from which the Disease of Tartar is born in the manner described: namely, that the generation of stones occurs in the Element of Water, and the residue does not make stones, but Tartar of a double kind, in <note>original: "Resolutionem, & Coagulationem"</note> *Dissolution* and *Coagulation*.

<margin>What the Element of Water is.</margin>
But furthermore, you must be taught here that not only the sea, or lakes, or rivers, or springs constitute the Element of Water: but any liquor whatever, drawn in by thirst, constitutes the Element of Water.

<margin>What Earth is.</margin>
Conversely, whatever is drawn in by hunger is the Element of Earth. These two Elements are not separated by a divorce, but are united like a husband and wife. Therefore, the Tartar of man degenerates into the nature of the Tartar of the world, and this nature of Tartar falls back again into the nature of stones and those species from which it came—such as sand and gravel—always maintaining that distinction which exists between a fungus or mistletoe and the wood itself. For just as a fungus, even if it grows out of the wood itself, cannot be called wood, but is and is called a fungus: so Tartar itself cannot be called stone, for it is the same as a fungus from stones. Thus, Tartar could also be called the "mistletoe of stones" or "mucilage." Yet these names are not used except before the coagulation of the matter. As soon as it has been coagulated, it retains the name of Tartar, which coagulation occurs after effervescence and digestion. This is the same as saying: it does not exist as Tartar in reality and essence, but as a liquor not yet coagulated, which is finally coagulated after digestion, separation, and boiling. That is, if a growing thing is removed from its matrix, it finally happens that the pure part, by its own nature and effort, shakes off and expels the impure from itself.

<margin>The mode of Tartar's generation.</margin>
When this expulsion and casting out occurs, the Tartaric nature becomes essential, and is coagulated from its first matter into its last, which afterwards becomes and is the Tartar of wine, water, juices, milk, legumes, and so on. And this matter ought to be rightly understood and frequently and diligently ruminated upon by physicians—namely, what kind of nature Tartars have within themselves...

<margin>The difference of Tartar.</margin>
...they have. For the <term>Tartar|In Paracelsian medicine, "Tartar" refers to the stony, solid waste products left behind after digestion, which Paracelsus believed caused diseases like gout, gallstones, and kidney stones.</term> of milk is one thing, and the Tartar of barley is another; the Tartar of meat is one thing, and the Tartar of bread another; the Tartar of wine is one thing, and that of water another. Although in this way not only Tartar is generated, but also dregs—such as the dregs of wine, and so on. Everyone should know, therefore, that these kinds of tartaric dregs grow and break out in man himself, which certain simple Physicians judge and call either <term>Apostemes|An archaic term for an abscess or a swelling filled with pus.</term>, or putrefactions, or resolutions of sperm <note>original: "resolutiones spermatum"; here referring to various bodily discharges thought to be related to reproductive or vital fluids.</note>, and so on; when nonetheless they are nothing other than tartaric dregs, as we indicated in the entrance of this chapter.

<margin>Tartar and dregs are not distinguished.</margin>
And although these kinds of dregs are not coagulated, nor are they Tartars: they nevertheless conspire and agree with one another so that, as if they exist under one origin, they must also be understood and healed by a single cure. From this you can now understand from where a Physician ought to take his foundation for knowing diseases. For whatever is exhibited in these things outwardly <note>i.e., in the natural world outside the human body.</note> is also brought forth inwardly in man. And this is that Medical Theory: this is that Library of Medicine, which has books not covered in dust, nor edible by cockroaches and moths: but the Elements themselves, according to their nature and essence, exist as the volumes of that Library.

<margin>The Elements are the volumes of the Library.</margin>
Therefore, for Medicine, a sound and accurate intellect is required, as well as eyewitness experience. Once possessed of this, then finally the Physician will know what he says and speaks, and he will judge the matter itself not according to his own opinion, or the report of others, or the indication and testimony of read books; but he will proceed securely from the understood science and experience itself. For having been properly instructed by this book—namely, Earth and Water—he will be completely certain that Tartar comes from the stones themselves, and has a stony nature, for which reason it is even likened to stones, yet with almost that distinction which exists between bark and wood, or mistletoe and a tree, or a fungus and the trunk itself.

...and of sands. However, we have defined "superfluous" as that which is not taken up for the generation and matter of stones and sands, but is left behind and separated from the stony and sandy mass, and is afterward cast into the Elements themselves, and mixed with them in the way we have said: and finally, through the Elements or with them, enters into man in the place of food and drink. Where we have also advised that,

<margin>As many kinds of Tartar as are outside, so many are in man.</margin>
as many kinds of Tartar as are found outside in the world, just as many kinds are found inside in man. And although the stones and sands themselves are by no means Tartars: nevertheless, the wood itself is known and discerned from its bark and <term>sap|original: "fugo"; likely a variant or error for "suco" (juice/sap) or "fungo" (fungus).</term>. So it must also be understood here, that through this demonstration all kinds of Tartar are similarly known by the reasoning we have stated. For first, all stones and sands were one body, from which body stones arose through coagulation,

<margin>How the kinds of Tartar are made.</margin>
not otherwise than from the <term>sperm of frogs|A reference to frogspawn; Paracelsus uses this biological analogy to explain how solid matter precipitates out of a liquid "seed."</term>; of which as many grains as there are, so many frogs are made. So it is here also. The grains surely constitute the types and species of stones, each one its own peculiar kind. Now indeed, you ask what becomes of the rest?

<margin>Comparison of the sperm of frogs and of stones.</margin>
That indeed in which the grains—that is, the seeds—lie, is dissolved and becomes watery, and turns into a single mixture with the water. Whence it happens that he who drinks that mixture, frogs are born in him <note>Paracelsus is speaking metaphorically here: drinking the "residue" of the stone-seed leads to the "growth" of tartaric disease in the body, just as drinking frogspawn would lead to frogs.</note>, similar in some degree to true ones, and they are born in him like a fungus in a tree. The birth, or sperm, of stones behaves in the same way. The grains themselves have been led by generation into their final substances and matters. But the rest is resolved into its Element of Water and Liquid. Now therefore understand, that from this remainder the kinds of Tartar are finally born, yet with that distinction which we reviewed before.

<margin>Stones are fixed, and so is their residue.</margin>
Furthermore, regarding the destruction of these, it must be known that the generation of stones exists as something fixed and perpetual, or immortal in itself: that is, in them there is no rust, no moth, but they are fixed and permanent. So also their residue exists as immortal, that is, whatever is made from it has its own temporal immortality in a fixed way. All these things are so explained by this teaching, so that you may know and understand a certain perpetual and incorporated tartaric nature, and that it is joined and united, that is, according to Elemental perpetuity. And this happens for this cause, that

<margin>The generation of Tartar is perpetual.</margin>
this infection proceeds continually and incessantly.

# ON TARTARIC DISEASES

<margin>The perpetual generation of Tartar.</margin>
This is evident from the disease itself and is proven by the facts: not only does <term>Tartar|In Paracelsian medicine, the stony or solid waste from food and drink that the body cannot digest, leading to obstructions like kidney stones or gout.</term> exist as an elemental perpetuity, but its generation is among the very first things to exist and will be among the last. Thus, the generation and the thing generated are joined together in one fixed state. Since man must be sustained by nutrients, and that tartaric nature lies hidden in the nutrients that man requires daily, it follows that man himself will be the first and the last within the four Elements. So too, the disease and whatever it produces remains permanent in that fixed state, which is partially visible in the first union of growing things, though not entirely. This is what I said at the beginning: that bodies naturally separate themselves from their own impurity. Thus, wine casts out its own tartar, and so on; this is visible, but not in every wine. In the same way, it happens in some waters, though not in all waters. The same occurs similarly in fruits, and in all juices and liquids. Since, therefore, it is necessary for man to eat and drink such bodies—which are indeed both nutrients and remedies—it is worthwhile to know by what means these are to be digested and destroyed within one's own body, lest some operation and coagulation happen inside, just as happens outside of man. For example: if wine reaches its perfect digestion, it is clear and pure, having deposited its tartar once, and produces no more of it thereafter. However, if the wine has not yet reached this perfection, it finally achieves it within the human body, and that which it should have accomplished in the vat, it performs in the body instead. Much depends, however, on how his own <term>Archeus|The internal "alchemist" or vital force in the body that separates useful nutrients from waste.</term> separates it.

<margin>The dose and praise of Antimony.</margin>
For here is the one who sends gold seven times through the fire, and who most subtly pours everything through <term>Antimony|In alchemy, antimony was used to purify gold; here, Paracelsus suggests the Archeus uses a similar refining power within the human body.</term> in man, uniquely endowed by God Himself with such arts and so many <term>Magnalia|Great wonders or miraculous works of God in nature.</term>, so that through him such things are perfected in man. But because the Archeus is not always exquisite or perfect in its operation when separating the pure from the impure, disease is always to be expected. Yet this is not lethal in the same manner as other diseases.

<margin>The nature of the body's Archeus.</margin>
According as the Archeus is perfect or imperfect, so too does he proceed to the perfection or imperfection of digestion. For this reason, a greater and more diligent care falls upon the physician to recognize and judge the disease itself. For if the disease is once traced to its true tracks, then it is found to be perfect in the Medical art for healing any species of Tartar: that is, perfect illnesses indicate a perfect cure, just as conversely, imperfect ones show an imperfect cure.

<margin>The tartaric types: Mass of Bolus, Mud, and Tubelech.</margin>
Because I previously indicated the types of Tartars and mentioned their dregs, you must be advised here that, besides stones and sands, other types also remain: such as the <term>Mass of Bolus|A mass of clay-like material.</term>, the **Mass of Mud**, and the <term>Mass of Tubelech|A Paracelsian term for the metallic dregs or slag found in the body.</term>. All these, and many others like them, produce tartaric disease themselves, as was said above. Although these are not stones, they are coagulated earth, such as <term>Armenian Bole|A medicinal red clay.</term>, <term>Hematite|Bloodstone.</term>, *Rotila*, and *Ochre* and <term>Eparita|A liver-colored stone or mineral.</term>, etc. For these are not stones, but coagulated muds. Therefore, the generations of these things also occur in man himself: such as **Hematitic Tartars**, **Eparitic Tartars**, **Rotiline Tartars**, and so on.

<margin>Muddy Tartars are easily dissolved.</margin>
Indeed, Tartars of this kind are more frequently dissolved, and then Physicians boast that they have crushed or dissolved the stone itself—that is, the coagulated Tartar—when they have only pulverized a muddy tartar, which is easy to dissolve. For Tartars of this kind are by no means stony, but only muddy, in which coagulation occurs and later turns into Tartar.

<margin>Muddy Tartars are drawn out daily.</margin>
However, it is resolved and dissolved by its own liquor, so that Tartars of this kind do not persist long in man at all, but are prompted toward excretion daily. There are some, however, which even if they are coagulated, are very easily brought back to a state of resolution. In this way, various types of Tartars are found excreted by men; if these are later dried and coagulated, the nature of that "region" <note>Referring to the specific organ or part of the body.</note> from which that type of tartar was born is revealed in this manner: if the resolved Tartar exits through the bladder and that liquid is led to its own coagulation,

<margin>How a regimen is to be established.</margin>
then it is clearly evident what kind of Tartar produced this muddy or coagulated matter. But if the Physician is not consistent with himself—that is, if he does not understand the proper test or examination of the matter—he will be quite unable to prescribe a suitable and convenient <term>Regimen|A prescribed course of diet and lifestyle.</term> for the sick person, nor to determine what things the patient ought to avoid. For the patient must avoid only that which was revealed in that examination and brought into view.

It details how various "muddy" or "clay-like" deposits (rather than just hard stones) can form in the body and how a physician must analyze these excretions to prescribe a proper diet.</summary>

Thus, the liquors of Tartar beset the neck, in which place they have their vessels and growing power; to speak more of these things here is beyond our purpose. Therefore, open your eyes, you Physicians, and by observing these things, learn and understand them diligently. In their Cosmographies and Geometries, these authors hand down nothing other than how many famous cities there are here and there, how vast the world is, what skins the furriers prepare, and by what method horses are to be mounted. The books of such authors show nothing but dead letters regarding this disease. For what they babble about at great length provides nothing of use to a Physician. Therefore, give your effort to investigating and tracking these things down yourself. In this way, you will be less entangled in errors.

### CHAPTER V.

#### By what means Tartar should be separated from nutrients in the stomach: and that another kind of Tartar is also made and generated in man.

**W**e have spoken so far of the origin and generation of Tartar, showing that it is brought into us with external things—namely, with those things we consume for nourishment. For according to their measure and nature, the tartar conceives its essence internally, so that internal tartars are generated within us according to the nature of external ones. That is, external Tartars enter us with food and drink and finally emerge as "Human Tartars" within us, specifically through the operation of the <term>Archeus|The 'internal alchemist' or vital force that separates waste from nourishment.</term>, in whom the transformation occurs. One nature exists in the transplantation, and another nature exists in the human spirit of coagulation. Thus, a different coagulation also occurs, so that the form, color, and coagulation separate from one another, and the external Tartar breaks down into the internal. Regarding coagulation and formation, therefore, this fundamental principle must be held: it can never happen unless a certain property thrives in the nature of man that promotes this kind of coagulation, or unless something exists in man that similarly assists the transformation. For this cannot happen solely by the 
<margin>Twofold human Spirits are the cause of coagulation.</margin>
external force of the external Tartar; rather, it is necessary that such a work be promoted by twin spirits, born with and implanted in man himself: namely, by the Spirit of Salt 
<margin>Coagulation is the work of the spirit of salt.</margin>
established in the <term>Microcosm|Man, viewed as a miniature reflection of the entire universe.</term>, and by the Archeus of the nature of the microcosm. Concerning these two...

<margin>
Coagulation is the work of the spirit of salt.
</margin>
Note this: the **Spirit of Salt** coagulates all things, even into their predestined form—namely, flesh into flesh, bone into bones, wood into wood, stones into stones, sand into sand, and metals into metals. The exact same principle exists in this matter as well.

<margin>
The separation of the pure is the work of the Archeus.
</margin>
Indeed, the duty of the <term>Archeus|In Paracelsian medicine, the 'internal alchemist' or vital force located in an organ—usually the stomach—that directs digestion and separates nutrients from waste.</term> is to separate the pure from the impure within the <term>Microcosm|The 'small world,' a common Renaissance term for the human body, viewed as a reflection of the greater universe (the Macrocosm).</term>. Therefore, whatever is directed inward by this method, through the power placed in the **Spirit of Salt**, is coagulated into its final body.

<margin>
Coagulation does not occur without the "delight" of the spirit of salt.
</margin>
For just as external things are coagulated and perfected in their own hardening—which can by no means happen without the **Spirit of Salt**—so too in man himself a certain innate nature and property is established which takes up this kind of **Tartaric** generation. If this uptake does not occur, the coagulation of Tartar does not follow; just as it is otherwise known that every spirit in the body enjoys and "delights" in its own particular object. If this "delight" of the spirit of salt with the **Tartar** does not occur, the generation of tartar is likewise finished.

<margin>
How the generation of Tartar occurs.
</margin>
In what manner the generation of Tartar begins in man, understand more precisely from this discourse. In the beginning, **Tartar** is conceived from the outside: once conceived, it is either generated within us, or it is not generated but destroyed. This destruction happens in the following way: the **Archeus** of the stomach is, as it were, the <term>Coryphæus|A leader or conductor, originally the leader of a chorus in ancient Greek drama.</term> and the primary author. Specifically, what we eat and drink, the Archeus must separate in the stomach so that the pure is distinguished from the impure.

<margin>
What the emunctories for the impure are.
</margin>
But that which is not pure—that which is not flesh or blood—is assigned to two <term>emunctories|Organs or passages that carry off waste from the body.</term>: for it is diverted either through the stool or through the urine. Therefore, the first momentum is placed in the powers of the stomach. The duty of these powers is to separate the **Tartar** and the **Nutriment** from one another, and to expel the Tartar through the stool along with the excrement, which ought to be nothing other than dregs and Tartar.

<margin>
Excrement is dregs and tartar.
</margin>
For in the stomach, all the **Tartaric** dregs of food and drink ought to be separated in this way and driven out through the stool. And that which either wants to degenerate into coagulated Tartar, or is naturally fit for it, must furthermore be destroyed and expelled through the urine, so that it does not become entangled and ensnared in the union of the **spirit of salt**.

<margin>
The two expulsive powers that help the Archeus.
</margin>
For as soon as the Matter of coagulated Tartar falls into the dominion of the **spirit of salt** and begins to take hold, the generation of tartar begins on the spot. For this purpose, two powers are ready at hand: the expulsive power of the belly, through the intestines, and the other through the urine. These must be performed and perfected entirely by the **Archeus** of the stomach, in such a way that the final matter of tartar is destroyed in the stomach by it; so that even if the spirit of salt should seize it, it would nonetheless be destroyed and corrupted. Just as a carpenter can make anything he wants out of the wood he picks up, yet if that wood is either burned or rotted, he cannot shape it to his liking; in the same way, if the matter of tartar is destroyed in the stomach (which nature is then able to do, and schemes to do as its duty), no tartar is generated in that man.

<margin>
When and where Tartar adheres.
</margin>
But if it should ever happen otherwise, then the **spirit of salt** has found matter in which it may "delight," until finally, as time passes—if destruction does not happen in the meantime—the tartar is deposited into the intestines from that matter, just like dregs from wine. For the intestines of the body are the reservoir of tartar, and its dregs are the excrement. If, therefore, such a complete separation occurs in a man without the destruction of the matter, that which is dregs and tartar is generated within us. The passages themselves are the vessels or jars to which the dregs and tartar adhere.

<margin>
When Tartar is not formed.
</margin>
However, the **Tartar** ought to be united and joined together with the excrement and driven out through the stool at the same time. If this happens, the spirit of salt does not find anything in this place that it can coagulate into Tartar. For the dregs also take on the properties of tartar, but they do not conceive stone or sand. Once the separation of Tartar and dregs is performed in this way, one part exits and is expelled through the intestines, and the other through the urine. Therefore, to avoid the evils of Tartar, a strong stomach is needed first of all. For in that place, the separation itself is established along with the corruption of the matter. If it does not happen there, then a certain part of the dregs usually adheres to the intestines. Tartar, however, separates itself from the dregs and passes through the urinary paths. With these two kinds of tartar, the **spirit of salt** finally acts as has been said. Thus, enough has been mentioned so far regarding external Tartar: that is, it remains continually the **Tartar of the Elements** until it finally departs from the man again in a broken form. As soon as it is broken, it exists as either excrement or urine.

<margin>
When Tartar belongs to the Elements, and when it becomes the man's.
</margin>
Otherwise, it remains the **Tartar of the Elements** for as long as it takes to fall into the dominion and bonds of the **spirit of salt**, which finally makes it the **Tartar of the Microcosm** out of itself. And at that time, Tartar...

It emphasizes that a strong stomach is the primary defense against these diseases by ensuring waste is expelled as stool or urine rather than adhering to the internal organs.</summary>

The Tartar of the Elements is no longer something external, but belongs to the human being. This has shown enough about what kind of Tartar exists in man, where it comes from, and how it enters the body—namely, with food and drink—and that it must first be separated in the stomach through <term>corruption|In alchemy, 'corruption' refers to the breakdown or fermentation of a substance so that its components can be reorganized or separated.</term>. Next, we must consider how Tartar is to be understood once it has become Human and <term>Microcosmic|Related to the human body as a 'small world' that mirrors the universe.</term>, and so forth. This will be handed down in the following chapters. For now, pay attention so that I may also remind you of another kind of Tartar.

<margin>What innate Tartar is.</margin>
There remains another kind of Tartar which has nothing external about it; that is, this Tartar is implanted and innate, born in man by itself and alone, without the addition of any external help or support.

<margin>In man is everything that is outside of man.</margin>
For just as man is a microcosm, so too does he have Tartar implanted within him, no less than the <term>Greater World|The Macrocosm or the external universe.</term>. For the properties of this whole universe are present in man as well; therefore, this kind of Tartar will also be in him. Nature in man is so constituted that all properties spring up within him, just like herbs and grasses in a field, and all the elements of man work inwardly and incessantly, just as the external operation of the Elements exists perpetually outside. And as springs leap forth from rocks, so it happens likewise in man.

<margin>The meteorology of man.</margin>
Thus, in man, Tartars also <term>coagulate|The process of becoming solid or crusty, like the scale in a tea kettle.</term>, just as in the external world. Everything in man grows, hastens toward its own increase, strives toward its own Elements, and is consumed through the power of the Elements; this means Tartar is no less inside man than outside him. If it is snatched away into the power and dominion of the **Spirit of Salt**, it then coagulates. Indeed, not only does Tartar lie within man, but even stones. Yet these are so consumed and corrupted that they can never be led back <note>original: "reduci," meaning restored to their original state</note>. Tartars, however, are not destroyed in the same way; therefore they can and must be born—excepting, however, this specific Tartar of which we are treating.

<margin>The Sea is the receiver of all waters.</margin>
In this way, all superfluous waters travel to their own Element, which is called the **Sea**. Other earthly things strive toward their own Element, namely **Earth**. Thus fiery things turn to the Element of **Fire**, and airy things to the Element of **Chaos** <note>In Paracelsian thought, "Chaos" often refers to the element of Air or the atmosphere.</note>. In this way, they are consumed outside of their generations and reduced to **Nothing**. Judge all these same things in man likewise: it is necessary for such superfluous generations to be extruded out of him into their own Elements, and yet with such moderation that they are consumed within the man himself. You ought to know, however, that in such generations, Tartar and dregs are united; if this is not consumed by its Element, then the dregs and Tartar remain. That is, they can reach the same end in their own Elements as water finds in the Element of water. If this does not happen, then the **Spirit of Salt** rushes into the stony Tartaric matter and transforms it into Tartar. This Tartar emerges of its own accord, from its own nature, and takes up its substance, body, and form from that man in whom it hides.

<margin>What the subject of innate Tartar is.</margin>
Thus, therefore, another and peculiar species of Tartar is born, opposite to that which is taken in from the outside. That species settles in any <term>urinary blood|Likely referring to the blood found within the renal or urinary system.</term>. For there it has received its habitation, built by nature, and just like wine-lees <note>original: "Tartarum," the crust left by wine</note>, it settles and is separated from the wine.

## CHAPTER VI.

->*Here it is explained and declared how Tartar is derived from men to women, and is conceived by them.*<-

**H**aving perceived these things, you ought furthermore to know how a certain kind of Tartar arises in women.

<margin>Two types of Tartar in women.</margin>
Pay attention, therefore: two kinds of Tartar occur in women; that is, Tartar is generated in them in two ways. One, which is shared with other people, is through food and drink. The other is that they conceive Tartar from men. Regarding the first, enough has been said already. Regarding the other—namely, how it is generated having been conceived from men—we shall hereafter explain more plainly. For in the cure of this, there is need for attentive wisdom and judgment.

<margin>The cause and seat of Tartars are the spermatic vessels.</margin>
Accept the foundation of this matter in this way. First, you must know that this kind of Tartar is generated only in women. This happens by reason of the vessels, which in women differ from those in men. Wherefore there is need of another observation: that Tartar is generated in this way. First, we must speak of the vessels in which the Tartars lie. There exists a great variety of these vessels, as will be handed down in its place hereafter. Nevertheless, it is meanwhile certain and evident that only the vessels of the spermatic region generate this kind of Tartar, and these Tartars, in turn, occupy only the vessels of women. Just as...

<margin>The spermatic vessels and where they are located.</margin>
The spermatic vessels are situated just like those near the kidneys, the bladder, and similar parts. And although the sperm does not lie here alone, the venereal act <note>The "venereal act" refers to sexual intercourse.</note> nonetheless prevails, so that a stirring of all things hidden there occurs. Truly, whatever is contained in the venereal members that serve this act is brought forth and aroused by that stirring; if possible, it is gathered and mixed into the spermatic matter in this manner:

<margin>How sperm and semen differ.</margin>
For sperm is not the entirety of the "seed," but rather a great flood of sorts which, when agitated, overflows. Yet not all of this exists as the "seed" <note>The author distinguishes between the bulk fluid (sperm) and the actual generative principle (semen/seed).</note>. For the seed, in its actual mass, scarcely equals a pea; everything else is superfluity.

<margin>The tiny mass of the seed. What jelly is.</margin>
And with this *jelly* <note>original: "Galreda." This refers to a gelatinous or mucus-like substance.</note> many ailments are mixed, especially those which lie hidden in the members belonging to this act. They penetrate the internal pores or passages so that they associate with those superfluities now flowing out, by which they are also easily taken up and united as if they were a single material. Thus united, they are ejaculated together into those places that receive the sperm, as is customary in that act. Once this is done, the sperm insinuates itself into its own little vessel. Truly, the other outflows likewise turn aside to their own places, which are similar to those from which they flowed. What flowed from the man's bladder goes to the woman's bladder; what came from his kidneys goes to her kidneys. Thus, every single thing is returned to its own seat and receptacle, except that only the foamy superfluity is consumed. But so that you may understand the matter more clearly, note these things further: In women, there is an attractive power; in men, an expulsive power. For this reason, women alone acquire this, never men: because the expulsive force follows the path and impulse of the attractive force.

<margin>The cause of Tartar in women; its retraction where there is expulsion.</margin>
To whatever place a thing is attracted, there it persists. Therefore, the man powerfully expels from himself, through the venereal expulsive power, into the regions of the attractive power which is in women. Now, the expulsive power does not only expel sperm, but indeed any <term>prime matter|The most basic, unformed state of a substance before it takes a specific physical shape.</term> of health and of diseases. Thus it happens that all prime matters come together into one union. Regarding this, hold fast to the fact that <term>Tartar</term> <note>The waste material or stony deposits formed from "unseparated" nutrients.</note> does not penetrate into the woman in its "ultimate matter," but in its "prime matter," before it is coagulated by the spirit of salt and reduced to its final state. The prime matter of the seed proceeds principally. For the operation and power lie in the woman, and she draws the prime matters to herself through the stirring and agitation of the whole body. I have not proposed to describe its force and efficacy here, but only that which is required for knowing <term>Tartar</term>.

***

If it has arrived at the dominion of the attractive power, then every single prime matter is drawn into its own place and directed into the vessel from which it departed, as was said before. In that place, it is perfected and reduced to "ultimate matter." Once the ultimate matter is thus prepared, then the sickness is perfectly present, in the woman as well as in the man. For in this way, two persons become one flesh and one body.

<margin>How man and woman are one flesh.</margin>
Since, therefore, both are one flesh and one body, it is only right that their kidneys and vessels should also be as one in all diseases.

<margin>Why a woman's defect does not flow back to the man.</margin>
Indeed, there is only this one cause as to why it is not conversely and similarly transferred from the woman to the man: because in men, through the venereal act, the attractive power does not operate as it does in women. In this way, judgment must be made concerning <term>Tartar</term> common to women and men: that in its prime matter, it is directed to that place where its vessel is—be it the kidneys or the bladder. For from whatever it flowed out, to that it returns. But if it settles in its own place, then the beginning of generation occurs, and it takes on the spirit of coagulation; from the prime matter, it is prepared into the ultimate matter—that is, into <term>Tartar</term>.

<margin>The potential Tartar of men.</margin>
Therefore, know that the <term>Tartar</term> of men does not exit essentially, corporally, or substantially, but only in the prime matter. <margin>What the distinction is between the Tartars of prime matter.</margin>

The same must also be established regarding human beings. For just as any tree produces something similar to itself, in the same way, human beings are brought forth and generated. And all of this should be understood regarding the **Tartar of the blood** <note>original: "Tartaro cruoris." From these things, it is concluded that many hereditary diseases are abolished in these discords: so that certain diseases are occasionally removed through this contrariety, while others newly succeed in their place, which are divided according to their own nature—much like a mule, which is neither a horse nor a donkey.

<margin>The duty of the Spirit of Separation.</margin>
Hence it also happens that through the external and internal autumn, whatever vessels become full from time to time. Therefore, if liquids of this kind are enclosed in their vessels, then the approaching <term>Spirit of Separation: the innate intelligence or force in the body (called the 'Archeus' by Paracelsus) that sorts nutrients from waste.</term> <note>original: "Spiritus separationis"</note> separates the pure from the impure, nor does it allow the Tartar to remain joined with the liquid, nor does it leave its dregs in the liquid, but separates them all from one another. Thus, a similar operation emerges outside in the wine vessel and inside in the vessel of the body.

Next, however, you must also learn which vessels these are in the body. This chapter is dedicated to explaining this matter. 
<margin>What the vessels of Tartar are.</margin>
<margin>The Stomach.</margin>
The first vessel is the stomach. Its Tartaric diseases demonstrate this, for there the Tartar and dregs either stick or are deposited, no differently than in an external barrel, from which specific diseases are later born.

<margin>2. The Intestines.</margin>
Secondly, the vessels of Tartar are the Intestines, because they contain dregs and hold the annexed or adhering portions of Tartar.

<margin>3. The spaces from the stomach to the neck of the bladder.</margin>
Furthermore, whatever parts extend from the stomach all the way to the neck of the bladder are also counted among the vessels. For wherever urine is either contained or passes, there is a vessel. Although these vessels lying between the neck of the bladder and the stomach are varied and manifold. For in the <term>mesaraic veins: the mesenteric veins, which carry nutrients from the intestines to the liver.</term> <note>original: "venis Mesaraicis"</note> the dregs cause blockages. Afterward, in the regions of the Liver, and from the liver all the way to the Kidneys, and in all the cavities of the whole body, Tartar can adhere. For there is nothing hollow that does not at the same time encompass that liquid which contains Tartar. Although this should also be known: "foreign" Tartar seeks no other vessels than those belonging to the emunctories. However, the Tartar of the Blood, besides the vessels attached to the emunctories, also seeks and devises others outside. But these are of a different kind. For whatever kind each vessel is, the autumn operates in it in such a way, and according to its nature and condition, Tartar and dregs are also generated.

<margin>4. Every single vein.</margin>
Moreover, every single vein of the whole body is a Vessel of Tartar—not indeed of the foreign kind, but of the blood. Nor indeed only the veins: but also the bones and the joints, in which <term>synovia: the lubricating fluid found in the cavities of joints.</term> <note>original: "sinouia"</note> is contained.

<margin>5. Every cavity.</margin>
And to speak summarily: whatever exists as a cavity suitable for collecting liquids is also fit for receiving Tartar, as was said above.

<margin>6. The principal members.</margin>
But even the principal members similarly contain vessels within themselves, such as the lungs, spleen, liver, etc. In these very things, Tartar is also born, just as stones are produced in fungi <note>The author uses "fungis" (mushrooms/fungi) as an analogy for porous organic structures that can develop stony inclusions.</note>. For just as foreign Tartar can be formed in the kidneys and bladder, so the Tartar of the blood can be generated in any cavity. And thus Tartar is also produced in the principal organs.

<margin>A moderate rebuke.</margin>
Wherever, therefore, according to this consideration, such vessels are placed, many and remarkable diseases are born there, which are taken for other things than they are. From this, many errors have also arisen to the certain destruction of the sick, as the daily examples of the <term>Humorists: physicians who followed the ancient Greek theory that health is governed by the balance of four bodily fluids or "humors."</term> <note>original: "Humoristarum"</note> prove.

# CONCERNING TARTARIC DISEASES.

## CHAPTER IX.
### *On the Coagulation of Tartar, and the manner and way in which it occurs.*

<margin>The coagulating spirit is twofold.</margin>
**I**n the preceding chapter, the vessels of Tartar were discussed along with their types—namely, those of the blood and those from foreign sources <note>original: "cruoris scilicet & peregrini"; referring to waste produced by the body itself versus waste from food and drink.</note>. Now, for a fuller understanding, you should know that kinds of Tartar can be produced and can adhere in all the cavities of the body. Whatever happens to foreign Tartar can also happen to the Tartar of the blood. There are two coagulating spirits: one in the foreign Tartar, and the other in the Tartar of the blood. Two points are therefore to be noted regarding these. One coagulates only in the paths to the emunctories <term>emunctory: any organ or duct that allows the body to discharge waste, such as the kidneys or sweat glands.</term>. The other coagulates in the cavities of the whole body, such as in the joints, hinges, pores, ducts, and the more principal organs. That which is coagulated in the waste-paths is found within them; that which is coagulated in the joints and hinges is likewise found there.

<margin>Diverse kinds of Tartars.</margin>
All Tartars are essentially the same, distinguished only by the fact that they are not all formed or colored in the same way or by the same logic. This diversity depends on the variety of the "vessel" <note>In Paracelsian medicine, the "vessel" refers to the specific organ or body part acting as a container.</note> which is conditioned toward this or that form and color, and on the specific kind of coagulating spirit. Furthermore, different Tartars give birth to different pains and illnesses, yet they all exist as Tartar. If it settles in the joints, it is called *Sciatica*, *Arthritis* <note>original: "Arthetica"</note>, *Gout* <note>original: "Podagra"</note>, *Knee-gout* <note>original: "genugra"</note>, and so on. Yet it is simply Tartar of the blood generated in that place, just as another Tartar might be generated in the bladder or kidneys. However, so that you may more clearly understand the manner and logic of coagulation, attend further to these things. Whatever is to be incorporated into the body must be brought there through the process of coagulation.

<margin>The cause of coagulation is the spirit of salt.</margin>
Coagulation is the work of the **spirit of salt**. For in this, the power of coagulation is placed. Thus, all bodies are coagulated into a physical form through the spirit of salt. Note further that the properties and conditions of the spirit of salt are manifold. One coagulates into Wood, another into Gems, another into Herbs, another into Metals, another into Stones or Sand, and so on. The spirit of salt performs all these things; it is the **Hero** <note>The primary agent or "master" of the physical process.</note> of coagulation.

<margin>The various natures of the spirit of salt.</margin>
If this spirit is joined to its subject, it then coagulates that subject into its own physical body. It works in this way in the Macrocosm <term>Macrocosm: the universe at large, which reflects the functions of the human body.</term>; it also works in this way in man, according to the logic of its nature. For it coagulates any body according to the manner of its predestination. In man, however, it finds no subject that can be coagulated into stone, except for Tartar. Other types of "plants" exist in man—namely, Flesh and Blood. And just as every thing receives its body and substance through the spirit of salt, so likewise in man, the *blood, flesh, bones, veins, skin, heart, etc.* are coagulated into that bodily substance through the spirit of salt, just as the order of creation demands.

<margin>The spirit of salt works according to the manner and capability of the subject.</margin>
Only Tartar, however, exists as something foreign and different from the members and body of man. Since it is foreign to the nature of man, nature leads it toward the exit and separates it from the liquid. But if the powers of separation, expulsion, and destruction are strong and potent, no Tartaric disease can be stirred up.

<margin>When Tartar is not produced.</margin>
However, when separation ceases and the expulsive power fails to act, a Tartaric illness must necessarily be induced. Furthermore, regarding other plants and created things, nothing can be generated in man except for Tartar. All other subjects are digested. Learn the manner of this coagulation from the following example. You see how wonderfully nature, through the spirit of salt, coagulates such varied bodies. You see how **Vulcan** <term>Vulcan: in alchemy, the archetypal power of fire or the internal "alchemist" of the body that separates and refines substances.</term> coagulates vitriol <term>vitriol: a sulfate mineral that forms glassy crystals.</term>, salt, and alum from water, with each one obtaining its own peculiar form as its property requires. The same thing happens similarly in the liquors of Tartar, in which the Tartar itself lies, just as vitriol is contained in water in various forms.

<margin>All Tartar is in liquid.</margin>
You must be entirely convinced that Tartar is hidden altogether in Liquid—that is, in water—just as vitriol, salt, or alum is contained in water. And just as Vulcan separates those from water, so Tartar is separated and coagulated through its own innate preparation and coagulation. It is not only vitriols, salts, or alums; even gems themselves in their "first matter" are only waters, liquids, and mucilages, which the innate and inborn art of Vulcan separates and forms.

<margin>Water is the first earth of minerals and stones.</margin>
For just as humans have a skill that is innate and planted within them, the same must be understood of Vulcan and other stones, which are separated from water in a similar way, as the various types of stones teach us. It must be held in a mindful heart, therefore, that in this way everything in the body exists as a **Liquid**. Just as in wine you see everything is liquid and no Tartar appears; so also salt thrown into water exists entirely as a liquid, and not...

It argues that while this force builds the human body, when it acts on waste products (Tartar) that the body fails to expel, it creates painful deposits like gout and kidney stones.</summary>

...nothing is seen except water. However, that separation then disjoins them from one another: and finally, an approaching coagulation brings each thing back specifically into its own body, shaped in the way it was meant to be shaped. The same thing, I say, happens similarly to human Tartars: they are liquid and mixed with other liquids. But since nature leaves nothing unseparated and indistinguishable, it follows that the liquid of Tartar becomes coagulated. And just as if saltpeter <note>original: "sal nitri"</note> is brought into its definite and consistent body, it settles of its own accord at the bottom without being mixed with water: so too Tartar remains as something specific and separated from the liquid. This occurs by the power of predestination.

<margin>Nature is a diligent separator.</margin>
<margin>Providence is the ordained order of fate.</margin>
For it has been so predestined by Providence that every subject is brought back from its "first matter" to its "ultimate matter." <note>In Paracelsian physics, "First Matter" is the raw, unformed substance, while "Ultimate Matter" is the final, perfected form.</note> Indeed, the powers of coagulation are given to the spirit of that predestination, just as sight is given to the eyes, hearing to the ears, and so on. For it was so constituted and ordained by divine Providence that this should be a Metallic body, that an Antimonial body, another the body of "living current" <note>original: "viui currētis"; likely referring to Mercury or "living water."</note>, another the body of wood, and so forth. Thus, in this account, the Body of Tartar is also a certain Created thing, and so ordained by divinity that it is brought to its ultimate matter in that place where it is located, notwithstanding the fact that it is harmful to man. For regarding this, a corresponding Medicine has been set against it in turn. And therefore, this is a certain craft of that smith—namely, the coagulating spirit.

<margin>A Medicine for Tartar is provided by divinity.</margin>
There is no need to write about how that spirit works. For it does not labor visibly, even though its works are visible. In the same way, the wind persists and coagulates mud while it carries away its wateriness (by which coagulation is prevented). The Sun does the same thing, which coagulates the yolk of an egg into *amber* <term>Caraben: from the Arabic 'kahraba,' usually meaning amber; here used to describe the hardening of organic matter into a resinous or stony state.</term> and the white into something translucent. All these same things must be understood similarly regarding the spirit of coagulation. For the day itself teaches that this craft of its is honest and genuine. And yet, an example must nonetheless be drawn from the bosom of nature so that you may see that the spirit must be sought which works in its own art in the same way as a human craftsman or mechanic.

<margin>Amber. The Sun coagulates the yolk into amber.</margin>
Let such an example be as follows. You see saltpeter <note>original: "salem petræ"</note> boiled out of the earth—that is, from the niter of the glass-works or the dung of urine—and through that craft, the saltpeter is reduced into water. If it has been reduced to that, then coagulation goes off into its own operation of its own accord; it granulates and whitens, and thus the saltpeter, without any human help regarding its formation, falls away and is converted into ice <note>The text compares the crystallization of salt into white crystals to the freezing of water into ice.</note>. And although the craftsman himself may contribute somewhat to this, his work is nothing other than gathering homogeneous things together and separating those which are different by filtering. Nor can a man contribute anything else to the generation of saltpeter than to provide for its purification. Once that is performed, the spirit of salt, which is innate to it, leads the saltpeter itself to its own coagulation and formation.

This is something that no industry of any man can accomplish by itself. By a similar logic, a certain *Vulcan* <term>Vulcan: In alchemy, this refers to the internal "alchemist" or transformative fire/spirit within the body that processes substances.</term> is established in the Microcosm <note>The "Microcosm" is the human body, viewed as a miniature version of the entire universe (the Macrocosm).</note> itself, who, like the boiler of saltpeter, prepares and produces that extraction. Once this is done, the spirit of salt adds, as it were, the finishing touch, and perfects and forms the Tartar, just as it grants and illuminates the saltpeter with its own native form.

<margin>The Spirit of salt can; man cannot.</margin>
For in this way, every single thing is brought to its predestined form. And just as no one can see in what way saltpeter is made and generated: so too it is not permitted for anyone to write about the manner of that generation. The same is true regarding the coagulation of Tartar: that art is native to Nature alone, which man himself neither knows nor is able to do. Moreover, the Smith expressing this figure or form is the *Spirit*. And since Spirits are invisible, it seems right that their operations are also invisible.

<margin>How the works of the Spirit and of man differ.</margin>
Who, therefore, could write about their workmanship, since they use neither hammers, nor furnaces, nor molds while they cast, cut, and shape? This much is certain: man himself can also shape many wonderful forms and figures, but they are all conspicuous and visible. But the art of nature is skilled in all these same things no less successfully, yet in the *spirit*, in which the light of nature itself flourishes. In contrast, what man manufactures is tangible and visible. Therefore, his works stand out visibly. Hence it happens that they can be described from the first day until the last—namely, what and how much was performed and labored upon on any given day. So also, by intent inspection, a man's operation can be learned and expressed by another through imitation. But no one knows how to emulate this *Vulcan*. For no one sees or perceives the spirit which he uses in his operations: even if one might look into the work itself...

### CHAPTER X.
#### In what way foods and other things produce Tartar, and how they also induce many pains and paroxysms.

<margin>There are two parts of food: blood and excrement.</margin>
The things said so far regarding the generation of Tartar should be understood at least concerning drink, and how Tartar is produced by it. But because not only drink, but also food is a cause of Tartar: therefore, take note further of the reasoning by which Tartar is generated from foods. Whatever can be consumed as food also produces Tartar from itself. This is to be understood as follows: The food that is taken in, having been subjected to digestion <note>original: "coctione," literally "cooking." Paracelsus viewed the stomach as an alchemical furnace.</note>, is divided into two parts. One part is that which is to become flesh and blood. This is transformed into a liquor familiar to all the parts or members. The other part is excrement. This is expelled from the human being. If it is expelled correctly and quickly, then that food causes no discomfort, nor does it produce any Tartar. But because everything does not always happen according to this established order and manner:

<margin>Hot digestions are the occasion of Tartar.</margin>
therefore it must be held that many digestions exist that are too hot, by which foods are not transformed according to the order of Nature, but are sometimes, as it were, scorched and half-corrupted. For example: If something placed in a pot and moved to the fire is boiled in the proper way, then it is well and purely boiled and cooked. However, if the proper way and order are not observed, it is burned in the pot and crumbles into charcoal.

<margin>Foods are corrupted when the stomach is in a bad state.</margin>
The same thing happens similarly in a human being if a certain <term>dyscrasia</term> <note>An imbalance of the bodily humors or a "bad mixture" of qualities.</note> and unsuitability has occupied the stomach. For it often happens that food degenerates into a certain foul matter which ought to have departed later with the excrement itself, though in actual effect this is not always achieved. This matter then becomes Tartar itself, specifically when the humidity or liquid in which the Tartar lies has departed, leaving the burnt residue behind.

<margin>Burnt residue is the matter of Tartar.</margin>
For this burnt residue becomes the matter of Tartar and is coagulated into its "ultimate matter," which finally exists as true Tartar. Consider some examples of these things. You see cheese, when thrown into boiling and fervent water, cast out a certain material from itself.

<margin>The diverse matter of cheese.</margin>
After this, however, there remains and settles another viscous material, unpleasant to nature itself. But if the water is not too hot, nor boiling, everything appears and exists as one substance; two types of cheese are not made from it, but it remains one, and that one is pleasing and familiar to nature. The same thing happens in the stomach in the same way.

<margin>The <term>Gluten</term> of the stomach is the matter of Tartar.</margin>
If the stomach is too hot while about to "cook" the food, it makes a "double cheese"—that is, it produces two different things: namely, the digested juice, and <term>Gluten</term> <note>A sticky, glue-like substance that Paracelsus identified as the precursor to stones.</note>, which then turns into the matter of Tartar. The truth is the same in milk as well. If it has become warm and turned sour, it is separated into two things: into <term>curd</term> <note>original: "caseamentum"</note> and whey.

<margin>The two parts of milk: whey and curd.</margin>
The whey stands for the excrement: but the curd is the matter of Tartar. Milk experiences the same fate in the stomach. For when acidity attacks, if a separation occurs in the stomach, that separation cannot be without Tartar—namely, Tartar of the stomach or the intestines. For that Tartar becomes like coagulated mud, yet hardened in a Tartaric or stony manner.

<margin>Tartar from spices, into the senses.</margin>
Furthermore, many Tartars are also produced from spices. And such things as these usually stir up great and atrocious pains, produced from the foul constitution of the stomach itself. For the stomach ought to be strong in its own native temperament. If it should happen otherwise, many diseases are thereafter to be expected from it.

<margin>Ash is salt: salt is from the matter of Tartar.</margin>
You ought to know, therefore, that whatever yields ashes can also produce Tartar. For any ash is salt: and any salt of ash is Tartar, and contains the nature of Tartar in itself, whose ultimate matter exists as Tartar itself. However, the whole turning point is placed in this: that the stomach reduces it into <term>Alkali</term> <note>A term used here to describe the caustic or salty residue of calcination.</note>, otherwise there will be no generation of Tartar. Sugar and Honey themselves also, if they reach such a digestion and acidity, produce much Tartar.

With these things understood, a certain error must be revealed to you, arising from the fact that the genuine matter of Tartar has not been properly recognized until now. For what is a wonder...
