->DE MORBIS<-
<note>Latin: "On Diseases"</note>

# ON DISEASES

<margin>Censure of physicians.</margin>
As you will see, even to this day this truth has not been sufficiently recognized, especially by those loud-mouthed physicians who obstinately compete with the ancients while teaching something else entirely on this subject. If the truth itself is rung in their ears, they immediately retreat to the **dead letter** <note>The "dead letter" refers to stagnant, ancient book-learning that Paracelsus believed was useless compared to direct observation and chemical experience.</note>, which is useful only for plundering money. For their entire method of cure and healing is placed in a foolish and lifeless text, which neither the outcome of truth itself nor any experience has ever proven to be stable or certain. To cry out without art and experience is to imitate the ways of the blind, who, when judging colors, shout much more obstinately and rudely than those who see correctly and sharply. For they place all their defense in shouting, and can do nothing else besides this. But so that you may receive an even fuller instruction, take note: many diseases proceed from **Tartar** <term>Tartar: A term Paracelsus used to describe stony or calcified deposits in the body, comparing them to the "tartar" or wine-stone found in wine barrels.</term>, the origin and generation of which is known much more certainly to us than to them. For they have derived these same diseases from the **humors** <note>The "Humors" (blood, phlegm, yellow bile, black bile) were the basis of traditional Galenic medicine, which Paracelsus sought to overthrow.</note>, with great ignorance and to the ruin of the sick.

<margin>How Tartar is born.</margin>
Indeed, I am going to point out some of these diseases to you, starting with the liver. For in its veins and pores, Tartar often coagulates in the manner we have described; just as the vessels of Tartar are located in the channels, pores, and veins. Where these vessels exist, the **spirit of salt** <note>original: "spiritus salis"; in Paracelsian chemistry, this refers to a coagulating or acidic force that causes solids to precipitate out of liquids.</note>—which is necessary for coagulation—also dominates. And **Anatomy** itself has many times revealed that stones are found in these regions, as well as in the lungs and spleen, etc., no differently than in the **Ray-fish** <note>original: "Raia"; Paracelsus often used animal comparisons to show that "stones" were a natural phenomenon.</note> or in sponges, or the "eyes" found in crabs. Furthermore, it is not at all unknown to you how atrocious and cruel paroxysms <note>Sudden attacks or fits of pain.</note> are stirred up by the Tartar of the bladder and kidneys.

<margin>Censure of physicians.</margin>
A similar paroxysm of Tartar also exists in the liver, which many call an **obstruction** <note>original: "oppilationem"</note> or an **abscess** <note>original: "Apostema"</note>, when in fact it is nothing other than Tartar attached there, just as the same thing usually happens in the kidneys and bladder. Yet these Physicians repeatedly take and judge one thing for another, and set up a treatment for an obstruction or an abscess, as if that evil were born from this or that humor; when in truth it is nothing but pure Tartar. It is therefore deeply to be lamented that so many gatherings, assemblies, and deliberations are organized by those Physicians everywhere, when nevertheless all these things are empty, and their counsels are sought and drawn from that which is truly not there. 

<margin>Tartar of the spleen, lung, gall, and veins.</margin>
Similar errors can also be admitted regarding the spleen, as well as in the lungs, the gall, and other similar parts. Even in the blood veins, which are the vessels of Tartar, the Tartar can become granulated. From this, various and acute passions <note>Medical conditions or suffering.</note> can be induced, similar to the ailments of a bladder stone. Yet they consider all of these to be other diseases. You, however, who are worthy Physicians, give your diligent effort to this: that you may carefully recognize and distinguish these types of diseases from others, lest you be entangled in a similar error with the rest and incur certain disgrace among your patients. For this is perpetually true: the arts themselves make the Physician, not the Academies, not the doctor’s cap, nor the ring. For even **fools** <note>original: "moriones"</note> can walk around dressed in such finery and enter into the Medical art. But that is to "enter the house through the roof" <note>A biblical metaphor (Mark 2:4) for entering a place by improper or illegitimate means.</note>.

<margin>How Tartar is generated in the pores of the flesh.</margin>
Furthermore, this must also be known: the very pores of the flesh also become vessels of Tartar, but only of that Tartar which flows in or drips drop by drop. If a certain grain of Tartar coagulates in those pores, paroxysms also emerge, which common Physicians have regarded as other diseases. It is certainly not unworthy of laughter if one hears that these "subtle" Physicists claim they can pull their humors to that place without the help of horses, by mere chatter alone. 

<margin>Censure of physicians.</margin>
In the meantime, let thanks be given to you **Humorists**, because in this way you have betrayed your own stupidity and ignorance. For nothing lies hidden anywhere that will not eventually be brought into the open and under the light. To teach you how these Tartars are brought to this point, apply a teachable mind. Whatever slips out from the stomach is distributed through the whole body, like dew through the whole world. Once distributed in this way, each thing is attracted and collected into its own proper vessel. From that vessel, every limb in which the vessel is located sucks out its own nourishment and food. The remaining surplus either flows into the bladder or is ejected outside the man through sweat, just as rain exudes from the clouds in the sky and distills onto the earth.

<margin>The form given to Tartar according to the nature of the vessel and material.</margin>
Furthermore, if the conjunction of **form** (that is, the spirit of salt) and the **matter** of Tartar are present in that vessel (whether it be in the pores, or the channels of the lungs, or other places), then Tartar is generated according to the condition of its own state and the nature of the vessel, as these are the things by which the form is imprinted. Thus, further on, other diseases are also generated from the tartaric dregs, which...

## CHAPTER XI.

->*A fuller explanation of how cattle become tartaric*<-
->*and instill that tartar into us;*<-
->*with an added warning regarding other*<-
->*kinds of Tartar that occasionally manifest.*<-

<margin>Animals conceive Tartar of the blood.</margin>
**B**ut let us now proceed to continue the explanation of the generation of Tartar as it occurs within cattle themselves. Although my care is not directed toward them, nor did I propose this to myself at the beginning, and although it is not strictly necessary, we shall nonetheless settle this discourse with this discussion to ensure a more certain and fuller understanding of human Tartar. In animals, whether they be terrestrial or aquatic, no "foreign" Tartar is produced <note>Foreign Tartar (Tartarum peregrinum) refers to matter taken in from outside the body, like mineral-rich food or water.</note>, but only **Tartar of the blood**. It does happen, however, that Tartar is sometimes found in the kidneys and bladder of pigs and dogs during an **autopsy** <note>original: "autopsiam" – here meaning direct anatomical observation.</note>. Even if foreign Tartar did not enter these animals nor coagulate within them, it is established from diligent examination that such Tartar was indeed foreign Tartar. Nevertheless, examples of this kind are rare. For animals themselves...

<margin>The spirit of salt is sufficiently coagulated only in humans.</margin>
...do not possess the **coagulated spirit of salt**. In them, only that which their own nature has placed into the Tartar coagulates, and they bring with them a spirit of coagulation that is innate. Otherwise, there is no coagulation within them. Now, regarding the Tartar of the blood, take note further: it happens that tartars of this kind are sometimes born in animals, but this occurs very rarely. The reason for this is that they do not have the **spirit of coagulation** (which leads to the tartaric genus) implanted within them, since that spirit is proper to man, who is composed of all the things and spirits of the entire machine of the world <note>Paracelsus views man as a "Microcosm" containing every element of the "Macrocosm" (the universe).</note>. Thus it follows that all these things also exist within man. In cattle or animals, however, the logic is far different. 
<margin>The logic of man and cattle is different.</margin>
But if something similar is found in animals, it exists outside of nature, and its cause resides in the matter itself, not in the animal. Now, I would like you to know that certain animals are born to receive stones, such as the **Ray** <note>Likely referring to rays or skates; Paracelsus believed certain fish had stony properties.</note>, which is filled with stones. But these stones are by no means Tartars; rather they are ***Duelech*** <term>Duelech: A Paracelsian term for a specific type of stony deposit, distinct from common tartar, often associated with painful urinary stones.</term>, which is a middle ground between Tartar and common stones, and thus a peculiar genus in its own right. Likewise, stones are also born in crabs and other animals. 
<margin>Duelech and stones are something different.</margin>
Observe the cause of these things: there is certainly no wood that lacks its own **Resin**. If that resin is secreted and shaken out of the tree, it is then coagulated by the external wind and the heat of the sun. Just as no wood lacks its own innate resin, neither does any animal. 
<margin>All animals have their own resin.</margin>
Regarding this resin, it must be held that for those animals in which stones are innate, the stones grow from this resin; their primary matter is only Resin, and their ultimate matter is ***Duelech***. The reason stones form from these resins is that such a resin is a particular **Arcanum** <term>Arcanum: A "secret" or powerful internal essence with specific healing or transformative properties.</term>.
<margin>Resin is an Arcanum.</margin>
Hence, it is "signed" <note>Refers to the "Doctrine of Signatures," where the appearance of a substance indicates its medical use.</note> differently than the body itself in which it lies, by which it ought to be recognized. Thus, the bone of a stag’s heart <note>The "os cordis," a small bone found in the hearts of older deer, once prized as a medicine.</note> and the bone of a hare’s foot are directed into a different form and coagulation for this one reason: so that unique powers may be sought within them. Let no one be surprised by these generated things. For you have an example in crabs, 
<margin>Crabs extinguish inflammations and resolve Tartar.</margin>
in which there is a unique and excellent **arcanum** that is much more powerful at extinguishing flaming fires <note>Inflammations or fevers.</note> than other extinguishing substances. Furthermore, they also possess an arcanum particularly suited for **resolving** <note>Dissolving.</note> Tartar. Now indeed, these two things in...

And this is the true separation of the two arcana.

<margin>What is the Art of Signatures?</margin>
And, just as it is established through the **art of signatures** <note>original: "ars signata" - the historical theory that the outward appearance of a plant or mineral (its "signature") indicates its medicinal purpose.</note>, every thing is "signed" according to what it is, what it is made of, and what it belongs to, so that like is always referred to like. Indeed, the *Art of Signatures* demonstrates all these things, which a Physician must be entirely skilled in for the sake of this kind of knowledge. Furthermore, pay attention also to those foods which are not taken from the Elements <note>Paracelsus distinguishes between primary elemental substances and "complex" foods like animal tissue.</note>—that is, concerning meats and fish—and in what way they are naturally Tartaric and can make a human "Tartarous." Even if something has been said about these before, these points must be added for a more fruitful explanation.

<margin>Wild meats are extremely Tartaric.</margin>
All wild meats from animals not raised at home are prone to Tartar, and they produce a difficult and violent Tartar. Moreover, the wilder and less tame the beasts are, the worse, heavier, harder, and more malignant their meat is. Those that live among crags, mountains, and mountain ridges are always worse and more difficult to digest than those that are tamed and raised at home. From these, the Tartars that are born are the most stubbornly and difficultly cured of all, and they produce the sharpest pains. Especially, however, their blood is extremely tartaric. For they consume that Tartaric nature and matter through their drink and food.

<margin>Tartar from wild meat is difficult to cure.</margin>
I will pass over the fact that they exist as such by their own native constitution. Therefore, unless a person has a very temperate and strong stomach, and possesses a vigorous power of **sequestration** <note>The body's ability to separate the pure nutrients from the "impure" waste or tartar.</note> and expulsion, he will hardly escape the onset of tartar, especially and primarily in the bladder, in the kidneys, and other similar vessels. Yet even if the stomach is robust and strong, because it imparts nourishment to the entire body—and the first matter of that tartar lies hidden in the nutrients—the Tartar is separated later in those places to which the nutrients are led, and it settles and remains in its own place. Since it does not remain in the paths to the **emunctories** <note>Anatomical "drainage" points, such as the armpits or groin, where the body was thought to expel waste.</note> like other excrement, the tartar stays behind in the mentioned locations and stirs up paroxysms <note>Sudden attacks or fits of pain.</note>. In this way, cases of <term>Gout</term> <note>original: "Podagrae" - specifically gout of the foot.</note> occur, the paroxysms of which (as with other diseases) are moved by tartar, not as if it were the tartar of the blood, even though it is actually the tartar of food: yet it is

so subtly digested that it penetrates to those places which it ought to nourish; there it is finally separated and resides in that very spot. And these things are to be understood not only regarding wild animals, but even regarding domestic ones, which are themselves also tartaric, such as Capons, Geese, Ducks, and

<margin>Which birds are tartaric.</margin>
similar birds. Similarly, we must teach concerning fish and those animals that live under the water. For these also constantly produce tartars. However, it must first be known by what distinction those tartars are distinguished from other kinds.

<margin>Which fish are tartaric.</margin>
Namely, the primary matter of tartar is in the water. In the water, fish are born and grow. Now, the "seed" of fish in its first matter is united with the first matter of tartar. In this way, by way of nourishment, one is always clothed and heaped into the other. From the separation and the expulsive power, a generation of this sort occurs, just as was said regarding meats: they generate tartar in man. For it happens in clearly the same way with fish as well. Thus, if a man eats fish, and they are properly digested in the stomach, then whatever tartar is in the fish 

<margin>The nature of fish-tartar.</margin>
passes into and is folded into the nourishment. For it has not yet been brought down into its "ultimate matter," but is still fixed in its "first matter." And so the nourishment remains. However, when it has arrived at the regions of its consumption, to which it is attracted and there digested, then finally the Tartar remains there, and the nourishment—from which the tartar was separated—is consumed. So, therefore, in those places, the tartar of gout, **sciatica** <note>original: "fchiaticus" - an older spelling of sciaticus.</note>, **jaw-pain** <note>original: "maxillaris" - tartar deposits or pain in the jaw joints.</note>, etc., is formed. And that is "fish-tartar," which is indeed first digested in man but is not perfected or destroyed. Afterward, from the fish, it is finally brought into its "ultimate matter" within the man, specifically in that place to which the nourishment is seized and changed into blood and flesh. While this happens, the tartar is generated and coagulated, formed according to the logic and condition of its matter. This, therefore, is a peculiar kind of tartar, which is generated only in the "ultimate consumption" <note>The final stage of metabolic processing where food becomes part of the body's tissues.</note> and cannot be separated from the others. Besides the kinds enumerated so far, others also arise from legumes.

<margin>How tartar from legumes is born.</margin>
For all legumes and grains are tartaric. These, however, do not reach the nutrients of the "ultimate consumption," but immediately become tartar. For the "first separation" and the expulsive power are not present. Thus, through the first consumption, the "ultimate" [matter] is immediately...

...be the final matter, just as it was also the final matter in legumes, grains, and fruits. At the very least, there is a need for the separation of Tartar from food. For it is perfect in itself, needing only coagulation, by which the Tartaric mass is led into its own proper form and essence.

<margin>The principle of pearls is drops of blood. Pearly Tartar-stone.</margin>

You know regarding pearls that they have the principle of their birth from a drop of blood, and are subsequently changed into pearls. A similar nature and principle exists even in man, so that sometimes blood-drops are secreted and, like Tartar, are coagulated into a stone. This, however, is not truly Tartar, but similar to Tartar. This kind does not indeed induce pain, but it nevertheless dissolves the parts in which it lies hidden. Moreover, blood-drops of this sort arise from a <term>Vulcanic</term> <note>original: "Vulcanica" - referring to Vulcan, the god of fire; in Paracelsian chemistry, this refers to the transformative heat of digestion or the "internal alchemist" (the Archeus).</note> decoction: just as if, in a hundred-pound weight of some metal, a half-ounce of silver lay hidden and was extracted by "Vulcan" (fire). A mineral nature of this sort also exists in the blood. If it is secreted in this way by mineral separation, it then thrives in its final matter, where it is afterwards transformed into a stone. And by this reasoning, it can retain the name of a "stone" in its generation, so that it is called a "pearly stone" or "pearly sand." The clear proof of this is in Oysters; since man is a <term>microcosm</term> <note>The "small world" - the Renaissance belief that the human body reflects the structure and processes of the entire universe.</note>, he can by no means be excluded from their nature. Beyond this kind of Tartar, yet another remains, which can be recognized by this example: there are many waters in nature which transform peas into stones, or make whetstones out of wood. Those things which do this,

<margin>Another kind of Tartar.</margin>
are also found in some rains. The same can occur no less within the microcosm itself than outside of it. Therefore, for whoever has these properties as part of their constitution, viscous liquors, synovial mucilages, white gluten, and other similar "head-fluxes" <note>Catarrhs or fluids believed to drain from the head into the body.</note> that drip down within a man, are coagulated. For if these properties exert their power upon these fluids, then the viscosities are coagulated into stones, or another similar mass—not exactly like Tartar, nor like <term>Duelech</term> <note>A specific Paracelsian term for a painful stone or calculus formed in the body.</note>, nor like a common stone, but in a certain similar way, though not entirely the same. Truly, just as wooden whetstones and stony peas are formed, so also that viscous matter is transmutated into a "stoniness" by the tinctures implanted in the waters.

<margin>Another kind of Tartar.</margin>
Finally, no one can contradict this fact: that if two different things, such as turpentine and brick, or pitch and marble, are joined or come together in one stomach, they eventually constitute a stone. For similar "simples" <note>Basic, unmixed substances.</note> exist within the body, which, if they are composed and grow together, also constitute Tartar by a similar hardness and coagulation. Although that may not be a complete genus of Tartar, at least Tartar exists in one part of it. Such is the "resin of the microcosm." And all these kinds must be properly known and learned by the Physician, so that he may have discovered and explored what is possible or impossible in man, and by what mode and reason it occurs.

### CHAPTER XII.

->*Explaining that the spirit of salt contains certain properties within itself which stir up the most heavy sufferings.*<-

Hitherto you have learned the origin of Tartar, and what the Tartar of the blood and foreign Tartar are. Indeed, you have sufficiently understood the other enumerated kinds. Now, therefore, take note further of certain properties contained in Tartar, and those hidden ones deeply implanted and sown within Tartar itself. For certain pains will be known from them which cannot be lifted or taken away unless every bit of Tartar is thoroughly removed. Although there are also some paroxysms <note>Sudden attacks or increases in symptoms.</note> which can be eased and mitigated. However, that which is "implanted" cannot be taken away. And this must be noted in every genus and species, especially regarding the aforementioned properties. You shall understand the matter thus:

<margin>Tartar has every matter of salt.</margin>
There is no Tartar that does not contain within itself a certain matter of mineral salt; that is: it is coagulated by salt, whence it also contains the <term>spirit of salt</term> <note>The essential, active essence of salt; in modern terms, this relates to acidic or mineral concentrations.</note>, not only spiritually, but also corporally. And although the corporal part does not coagulate in the least—rather the spirit alone does—nevertheless, the "body" is that in which the spirit lies, and through which it operates. Therefore, its body is either of *Vitriol* <note>Sulfates, often seen as green or blue crystals.</note>, or of alum, or of common salt. Nor do these three give or provide bodies only, but also their own species, such as white vitriol, and plumose alum, or borax, etc.

<margin>Tartar follows the proper property of the sickness.</margin>
Furthermore, not only these species, but also Arsenic-like, Realgar-like <note>Realgar is a bright red arsenic sulfide mineral.</note>, and Niter-like <note>Nitrates/Saltpeter.</note> substances, and those similar to them, whose bodies are mixed with their spirit, and having been taken up with the Tartar into one mass, are coagulated into one. You ought to know, therefore, that Tartar of this sort, which has such mixed species...

## ON DISEASES

Each type of salt has the capacity to produce diseases of its own nature and to mimic the conditions that its particular salt provides: that is, every single species of salt has a peculiar inclination toward a specific disease. For whatever the nature of the salt is, such is the pain contracted from its Tartar. And although these salts nonetheless exist as Tartars, they retain their ancient and innate properties, which are not abolished but remain by inheritance within the Tartar. Thus, diseases become twofold. One kind arises from the condition and nature of the Tartar; the other from the "body" of the spirit of the salt.

<margin>Threefold Tartaric diseases.</margin>
To these, a third category is added from accidents. And these natures in Tartar are threefold; the pains are also threefold. Therefore, Tartaric diseases are also divided into the three aforementioned kinds. Furthermore, take note of this: that

<margin>To every spirit of Tartar its own defined paroxysm.</margin>
every corporal spirit has a natural and defined time for its <term>paroxysm</term> <note>A sudden attack or increase of symptoms, like a fit or a flare-up.</note>. When it attacks, the Tartar displays its pain, and subsequently one paroxysm provokes another. If, therefore, <term>vitriolated salts</term> <note>Salts derived from vitriol (sulfates), which Paracelsus associated with burning and acidity.</note> predominate, then pains are stirred up in the stomach: and first indeed comes *Appetite-pain and Burning* <note>original: "Orexis, Arsuraq;" - Orexis refers to a gnawing, painful hunger or acid reflux; Arsura is a burning sensation.</note>, and from this, the scorching of the stomach. This disease seizes the body immediately if vitriolated Tartar adheres to the stomach, whether that happens in the opening or in the base of it. If that vitriolated substance were to stick and be impacted in another place, such as in the kidneys or the bladder, how heavy would the resulting pain be if the "appetite" and "burning" were to complete their operation? By similar reasoning, it could also stir up *Colic*, if it were to adhere in the same way to the intestines; and yet it is one appetite, one burning, one pain, varying only according to the place in which it sticks. For because the body is one, the pain is also one. The same reasoning 

<margin>What the effects of Aluminous and common salt Tartar are.</margin>
applies to Aluminous Tartar and common salt. For Tartar disposed in this way, as I have taught, does not stir up these acute diseases unless a certain addition is made which bites and rages in such a way. Hence it happens that if this salty Tartar in the stomach is not properly separated, but is drawn unseparated into the vessels, it causes pains that cannot be sufficiently described. For these added bodies do not deviate from their own nature at all, but like <term>corrosives</term>, or even more fiercely and painfully than them, they rage. For these bodies are subtle, and they also have a subtle spirit with them. If this spirit triggers paroxysms, it makes those times extremely troublesome and heavy. For it sometimes happens that the heat or inflammation scarcely extends or spreads to the width of a finger, and yet the pain rages so powerfully that no complaint is enough to testify to it. Otherwise, the rest of the body is free from pain, nor is it extended further than the limit of a finger; nor is anything conspicuous there, nor does any <term>Abscess</term> <note>original: "Apostema" - a swelling or collection of pus.</note> appear, nor any ulcer, nor anything else similar. This one thing is certain: that Tartar lurks there with such a sharp salt that it bites constantly and without end according to the nature of its paroxysm. You ought to know, therefore, that in that very place, only a single grain of Tartar with the sharp property of the spirit of salt lies hidden.

<margin>The cause of Sciatica.</margin>
If a certain grain of this kind falls into the hip, it would be the cause of the sciatic passion. It lies beneath the "girdle" (the waist). If it should eventually coagulate, what sufferer has felt greater torments while he lived? But if the same substance is drawn into other joints, which are themselves also "vessels" of Tartar, the beginning 

<margin>The generation of Arthritis.</margin>
is given to <term>Arthritis</term> <note>original: "Artheticæ" - Paracelsus uses this as a general term for joint diseases caused by Tartar.</note>. And if I knew that your bile would not be stirred up <note>A common idiom meaning "without making you angry."</note>, I would openly declare that Tartar of this spiritual kind falls into the "white gluten" (which itself also exists as a vessel of Tartar). 

<margin>What the movement of dissolved Tartar from place to place does.</margin>
When this happens, the diseases of <term>podagra</term> (foot-gout), <term>genagra</term> (knee-gout), <term>chiragra</term> (hand-gout), and others arise. This must also be held at the same time: that this Tartar does not always coagulate, but in its resolution, it sometimes remains dissolved and moves from one place to another, rushing about in the manner of storms, the ocean, or winds tossed by force. By this likeness, dissolved Tartar in man is also moved through its exercise or the internal operation of nature, 

<margin>What is innate commotion?</margin>
which they call "innate commotion." Accept it with an even mind, then, that I am explaining the reasoning and essence of gout to you here as well, and I have decided to write a specific book about it and its species.

<margin>The "North Star" of Doctors.</margin>
Be more cautious at last, you <term>Humorists</term> <note>Followers of the traditional Galenic theory of the "four humors" (blood, phlegm, yellow bile, black bile). Paracelsus fiercely opposed them.</note>. For he who walks in the light can by no means wander. But you propose a far different origin and generation of gout, sciatica, colic, and "appetite" than what truth itself dictates. Whence you can apply neither suitable nor sufficient remedies to them. This one thing you can subsequently hammer home: that those diseases are incurable. Well done indeed, Doctors! To you, doubtless, thanks are owed, you who have "touched the matter with a needle" <note>An ironic use of a Latin proverb meaning to hit the nail on the head; Paracelsus is being sarcastic.</note>. Regarding the depth of your erudition, your own mouths bear witness.

<margin>The cure of Gout and Colic is the resolution of Tartar.</margin>
You ought to have striven for this: that the Tartar be dissolved and expelled, consumed and separated. In this way, surely, a remedy would have been brought to gout, colic, and the other species. Furthermore...

<margin>The cause of the wasting of limbs.</margin>
I would also have you know that wasting and the consumption of the limbs are induced by Tartar whenever it occupies the nerves—that is, their very roots. <margin>The cause of paralysis and numbness.</margin>
From these blockages, paralysis of the same limb is also induced, or numbness, so that sensation is diminished, or other similar diseases born from the same cause. Meanwhile, the <term>Humorists</term> <note>Followers of traditional Galenic medicine who believed all diseases were caused by an imbalance of the four humors: blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile.</note> chirp on about their humors alone, which are not even present. They comfort themselves with such pleasant trifles—which require neither art nor labor to learn, but which they drink in and devise during dreams behind the stove. It also happens sometimes that this kind of <term>spirit of salt</term> <note>In the chemistry of this era, a corrosive or "sharp" essence derived from minerals.</note> in the Tartar is so sharp and biting that it ruptures or eats away at the veins.

<margin>The cause of bloody urine.</margin>
Bloody urine follows this erosion; once this evil is generated, the torments greatly increase and sharpen. For from the false biting of the salt, the passing of blood arises, which sometimes occurs continuously and is mixed with the urine, so that it is passed with immense agony.

<margin>The cause of disordered urination.</margin>
On the other hand, the nature of Tartar is sometimes such that it stops and withholds the urine. Occasionally, it numbs the urinary passages so that the urine flows out without being felt. These and many similar ailments are stirred up by Tartar, though until now they have all been falsely attributed to other causes. Anyone who wished to describe each of these in order would need much time and a great deal of paper. Since Tartar alone is the cause of these things, it is enough for us to remain within these terms; and yet, in this way, any species of Tartar can be found much more truly.

<margin>Medicine is sighted.</margin>
Even if these things cannot be found immediately, medicine is at hand to seek them out—medicine which, to this end, is "sighted" <note>original: "oculata" - meaning medicine must be based on direct observation and "eyes-on" experience rather than abstract theory.</note> so that it may look for what must be found. You should also know that,

<margin>What the dregs of Tartar do in the urinary tracts.</margin>
the dregs of Tartar are not ejected through the intestines, but enter the urinary tracts and are excreted through them with the urine—sometimes fresh, sometimes foul-smelling and purulent, and at other times in a different manner. For as they occasionally undergo this or that putrefaction, they appear accordingly at their exit. When they are halted or withheld, certain pains are again stirred up, which do not persist without danger and injury. The Physicians have described these very dregs differently than the truth of the matter demonstrates.

<margin>A rebuke of physicians.</margin>
For they say that in such a case, the bladder or kidneys are rotting; yet the dregs of Tartar alone are the cause of these evils, having crept into the urinary tracts. It shows itself exactly as it was when it slipped in. Although it is not always coagulated Tartar that does this: sometimes these kinds of pains and sufferings are also induced by the <term>mucilage</term> <note>A slimy or viscous state of the Tartaric matter before it hardens into stone.</note> of Tartar. Yet those Physicians have handed down nothing of these things, as they have not read truly medical books, but have only tasted "dead letters," which are as sweet and pleasant to them as <term>gentian</term> <note>Paracelsus is being ironic; gentian is famously bitter. He suggests their "sweet" traditional learning is actually useless and unpalatable.</note>.

<margin>The power of material experience.</margin>
The description of the causes of disease must proceed from that which generates the disease itself. And this must be proven through material experience, in reality, according to the thing itself. Thus, the book of Medicine is to investigate the <term>Machine of the World</term> <note>original: "Machinam mundi" - the Macrocosm or the universe as a whole.</note> and afterwards the <term>Microcosm</term> <note>The human being, viewed as a miniature reflection of the universe.</note> itself. For both of these <term>Anatomies</term> <note>Structural analyses of both the world and the body.</note> must be brought together, which are otherwise called <term>Cosmography</term> <note>The mapping of the universe.</note> and <term>Geography</term> <note>The mapping of the earth (or here, the "earth" of the human body).</note>.

<margin>A rebuke of physicians.</margin>
From this, one might not undeservedly wonder why so many Anatomies have been handed down until now, and yet the cause and origin of all the aforementioned diseases—which is Tartar alone—has not yet broken through into discovery. If perhaps something of it did become known, it was poorly obscured and obliterated by a few other names and far-fetched causes. Only that concerning Tartar of the kidneys and bladder was observed, which would have been easy even for a blind man to see. Through the same negligence, they passed over the Tartar of <term>gout</term> <note>original: "podagra" - specifically gout of the foot.</note>. Even if it were coagulated, they did not understand what it was, but called it "nodose gout." Who would not say these names were aptly and suitably given? But even pigs would laugh at this kind of "doctoral" intellect.

### CHAPTER XIII.
### On the formation of Tartar into its own body and figure: and on its signs.

<margin>Differences of Tartar.</margin>
**T**artar has indeed been abundantly reviewed so far: what its essence is, how it coagulates in its vessels, what matter and how many kinds it has, into what it ultimately degenerates, what its ultimate matter is, and what kinds of diseases and ailments arise from it besides the stone and sand of the kidneys or bladder. It follows, therefore, that its differences should now also be handed down...

<margin>
Differences in Tartar.
</margin>
Let us now explain why Tartar is generated and formed in such varied ways: why it is sometimes large or small, round, oblong, sharp, flat, rough, hard, smooth, layered, split, double, triple, quadruple, or in the form of sand or pomegranate seeds, and whatever other shapes and figures may exist. The cause and origin of these are as follows. First, however, you should know that 
<margin>
Potable Tartar adheres to the teeth.
</margin>
its first adhesion is in the teeth. In these, a portion is glued on, one after another, until a thick layer of Tartar is collected; it is deposited and dried on the teeth just as it is in wine casks. This is what we call **Potable Tartar** <note>original: "Tartarus potialis"; Tartar derived from what we drink.</note>. 
<margin>
Edible Tartar begins in the stomach.
</margin>
However, **Edible Tartar** <note>original: "Tartarus Cibalis"; Tartar derived from the food we eat.</note> does not take its beginning in the teeth, but in the stomach. Its formation begins from the fact that it adheres to the walls, not that it merely lingers in the cavity. In this way, it is also similar to the Tartar in a wine vat. It adheres even in the throat, in the opening of the stomach, in the stomach itself, and at the stomach’s base or exit. Although, 
<margin>
Why the stomach conceives Tartar early.
</margin>
since the stomach is like a boiling pot in which everything ingested is mixed together, subdued, and cooked, nothing would easily stick within it unless the stomach were extremely parched and dried out. For when the stomach is in such a state, drawing moisture to itself, the Tartar adheres to the outer tunics <note>The layers or membranes of the organ walls.</note>, and the moisture seeps into the tunic itself. From this, it happens that the Tartar is attached to the tunics just as it is to a vessel. For it is a proven fact that the drier the staves of a wine cask are, the more moisture they attract, and consequently, the more abundantly the Tartar adheres. The same principle exists in human vessels. If they are moister, they collect less Tartar. And this is consequently true of all vessels, if you except the kidneys and the bladder.

<margin>
The reason for Tartar of the kidneys, bladder, and joints.
</margin>
But the joints also have their own peculiar reason. For in the joints, the Tartar is mixed with the "white gluten" <note>synovia; the lubricating fluid in the joints</note>, and in those places, it granulates like peas. Furthermore, if the Tartar is not yet coagulated but still exists in its mass, it is called **Tartaric Gout** <note>original: "Podagra Tartarea"</note> or **Tartaric Arthritis** <note>original: "Arthetica Tartarina"</note>. It can also be called **Tartaric Sciatica**. Furthermore, Tartar also attaches itself to the Mesaraic veins <note>The mesenteric veins which carry nutrients from the digestive tract to the liver.</note> and is called 
<margin>
Mesaraic Tartar.
</margin>
*Mesaraic Tartar*, etc. Now, in truth, gouty Tartar does not adhere in the same way as the Tartar of wine. For that location is somewhat moister. Therefore, it is forced into grains and excites <term>paroxysms</term> <note>Sudden attacks or outbursts of pain.</note> in the <term>synovia</term> <note>Joint fluid.</note>. Regarding the urinary passages, however, keep this in mind: if the cavities 
<margin>
Tartar of the liver.
</margin>
are of a drier nature, then the Tartar attaches itself in the passages near the liver before it reaches the kidneys. Because this adheres like the Tartar of wine, it happens that some of it is again washed away and removed by the urine, and is swept to the exit with the passing urine. This is excreted at the end with pain. This kind of scraping and tearing away of Tartar in the urinary passages is felt from the loins to the exit of the bladder. If this sensation is perceived, the Tartar is truly in motion. It also sometimes stings during its transit, no different than the stings felt from a brisk run. Moreover, these stings are perceived in the side, either right or left—that is, the Tartar is moved by exercise. From here, it is then led down into the kidneys. In them, it is generated in this way: certainly, it cannot adhere easily or readily. For the kidneys are an organ placed in constant motion and agitation more than other parts. Because of this 
<margin>
Why Renal Tartar does not readily adhere.
</margin>
motion, the Tartar cannot readily adhere as it does to the staves of a cask. Furthermore, the kidneys are moist and fatty, which also hinders the adhesion of Tartar. It is necessary, therefore, for it to granulate. And so, in the kidneys, it immediately and continuously takes its form, just as <term>saltpeter</term> <note>original: "sal nitri"; potassium nitrate.</note> takes its form in water. From this are formed grains like sand, some small and some larger, according as the properties and condition of the matter from which they are made might be. And just as a certain order is preserved by nature in the production of all things—so that what ought to be a rock becomes a rock, and what ought to be flint becomes flint—so here too the "maker" shapes the sand, making that which was meant to be sand, and makes it either rough, or large, or tiny. To all these differences, the "former" <note>An internal archeus or creative force that gives shape to matter.</note> approaches and confers its shape, working in the kidneys according to the order of nature. Indeed, whatever 
<margin>
How Tartar of the bladder is made.
</margin>
did not adhere in these parts is glued together in the regions of the bladder: that is, in the neck between the kidneys and the bladder. Regarding that formation, you will note such a process: that the "primary matter" <note>original: "materia prima"; the fundamental substance of the deposit.</note> is collected there and does not leave the spot, but lies there in the appearance of mud or clay until the time of coagulation arrives. For then a stone is made there according to the size of the primary matter, in surely that form or figure which the region in which it is situated provides—which is either flat, or wide, or sharp, etc. The form of the stone itself emerges from the salt itself, just like all other stones. For it emulates the properties of the salt. But enough has now been said about the formation of Tartar, and by what reasoning it is shaped and formed in its various vessels.

<margin>1. The first type of signs of Tartar.</margin>
Furthermore, the signs by which Tartar may be recognized are placed in this: if indeed the urine is not passed naturally and in the accustomed healthy manner and without pain, unless by chance other manifest and evident diseases are also present. Among the signs are also counted: pains of the hip, piercings in the loins <note>the lower back or lumbar region</note>, abnormal appetite <note>original: "orexis"; often referring to a burning or dysfunctional hunger</note>, heartburn, colic following food or drink, from labor or bending the body, from running, from lifting heavy things, easy dislocation of joints and slow recovery, and pain and contraction in those places especially where the vessels are primarily located, such as around the back, the navel, and so on. But let us also come to other signs of Tartar.

<margin>2. The second type of signs. Urine is an uncertain index of Tartar.</margin>
Many busily attempt to judge and recognize Tartar from the urine; yet, a sufficient and fundamental knowledge can by no means be captured through the mere inspection of the eyes. For that Tartar which is secreted with the urine provides very little certain or complete judgment as to where it might have emerged from. And although it may be excreted in two forms—either as sand or as mud—it nevertheless gives us the slightest sign of all. For from this, the malice of the material in the Tartar cannot always be sufficiently or adequately distinguished, at least as much as is necessary for the Physician and the patient. He who wishes to take a sign from the urine, and through that sign recognize the Tartar with all the conditions of its material: let him separate the salt of the urine from the moisture itself.

<margin>The separated salt of urine is a certain index of Tartar.</margin>
<margin>3. The third type of signs.</margin>
Only then will he receive true and genuine knowledge in that salt. For he who separates the urine from the Tartar itself in this way will fully and clearly see and distinguish every property and condition of the Tartar. But whichever Physician does not separate the urine in this manner, he gazes upon it **like a calf at a new gate** <note>a proverbial expression meaning to stare at something in ignorant bewilderment</note>. In this way, therefore, Tartar is to be weighed in the urine, not sought by frequent turning of the eyes at the bottom of the vessel. For just as you see outside, the salt of nitre is made from the nitre of urine, and through this the nature of that nitre is subsequently known: so, before the urine becomes nitre, you ought to know how to extract the salt from its moisture. Then at last the **spirit of salt** <note>an alchemical term for the acidic essence or "active spirit" of the salt</note> will be seen bodily, and truly felt and handled both by eyes and hands. Once this is performed, apply the Philosophical judgment, which befits the Naturalist, the Physician, and the Alchemist. Outside of this path, uroscopy <note>the traditional medical practice of examining urine by sight</note> will profit you nothing at all. Furthermore, now attend to other signs. For there exist certain signs which nature itself brings forth, which testify to us through their pains regarding urgent pathologies. Of this census are ***Podagra*** <note>gout</note>, indicating a Tartar of white glue; pain of the hip, designating Tartar of the sciatica; pain of the joints, betraying **Arthritic** Tartar; pain of the back, the loins, and a fistula under the navel; vomiting, testifying to Tartar of the kidneys and bladder; griping pains, distension, constipation, and thirst, manifesting Tartar of the intestines; appetite and burning of the stomach, revealing Tartar of the stomach. And thus in other diseases also, Tartar is to be assessed and judged through its appropriate and pathognomonic <note>characteristic of a specific disease</note> signs. For it befits a skilled physician to be well-acquainted with all these signs joined with experience.

<margin>A Physician without experience is worth nothing.</margin>
For without experience, a Physician will write nothing of any worth. He must also be skilled in how to distinguish other diseases from Tartaric ones by these signs, or to distinguish Tartaric diseases from one another. For the pains of colic are different from the pains of suffering kidneys. And so it is in all other diseases. For a Physician must be instructed by certain and long-lasting experience, as one who has drawn it not from books, but from the patients themselves. For if he is well-versed in *this* book <note>meaning the "book" of the patient's body</note>, he cannot easily be deceived.

<margin>Patients are the books of Physicians.</margin>
But he who trusts only in the written letter is dead, just as the letter itself is dead. Nor can these two dead things do anything else except kill the patient along with them. If not even an executioner can learn from books how he should skin a dog unless he uses experience as his mistress: how much less, I ask, can a Physician do so?

## CHAPTER XIV.
### On the paroxysm of Tartar, and its natures: namely, Mortal, Chronic, Mild, and Passing.

<margin>4. The fourth type of signs of Tartar.</margin>
Beyond the signs mentioned thus far, many others remain, taken from the **paroxysm** <note>the sudden onset or "attack" of a disease</note> itself, which it is most necessary of all to know and recognize. In this chapter, therefore, we shall primarily describe the paroxysm of Tartar, beginning the matter with such an example. First, you see that when the vineyards and vines are flowering, the wines in the casks begin to bubble up again, and are stirred by a certain agitation.

<margin>Paroxysms are excited at the time of flowering.</margin>
In the same way, all the minerals of the earth and water "flower." If, therefore, those things from which Tartar conceived its spirits and nature are flowering, it follows that the Tartar...

<margin>All things bloom in their own time.</margin>
Tartar <note>The stony, calcified waste Paracelsus believed caused many diseases</note> also rises within a person, stirs itself up, and pours out certain sharp qualities and vapors from within itself. This is now the paroxysm <note>a sudden attack or violent expression of a disease</note> of Tartar. Furthermore, this is not only true regarding wine, but also regarding all fruits and similar things. For whatever kind of these things strives to burst forth—whether it desires to grow green, push out buds, bloom, or send out small branches—it also imparts its own stirrings to the Tartar inside a person. Whatever the nature of that plant, it rouses paroxysms of that same nature. Thus, in this way, the stirrings of Tartar begin. Truly, a paroxysm of this kind does not arise without pain and torment. It is especially fitting for a Physician to know all these things, so that through external things he may see and recognize the internal. The external stirrings are the indicators of the pains themselves, which are well enough known to everyone.

<margin>The Physician must be a Philosopher.</margin>
Therefore, the Physician must be a fundamental Philosopher, so that he knows the "blooming" of Nature, and from this—as if through external alterations—he may judge the paroxysm of Tartar. For just as a tree, or an herb, or a legume pushes forth the power hidden within itself, shakes off its inherent superfluities <note>excess or waste materials</note>, and brings forth a new sprout; so also the Tartar of that same nature acts in the same way, by purging and emitting its own superfluities. Thus, purification <note>original: "Mundificatio"</note> expels; the salts provoke the pain. For just as fire bursts and breaks a pot in which something is powerfully boiling while sealed, so also the boiling invades the Tartar. The vapor of this boiling causes pain and distress in whatever parts it occupies. Furthermore, the paroxysm of Tartar

<margin>From the influence of the heavens.</margin>
is also stirred by the influence of the heavens, namely when the course of the sky sends down contrary rays. Those adverse rays agitate the Tartar into its paroxysm. For it is certain

<margin>Tartar is related to the stars.</margin>
that Tartar has commerce and affinity with the stars. Whence it is also moved by them and driven into a paroxysm. The cause of this matter is that a star is a certain fire, which "cooks" all fruits and

<margin>The Star is the Element of fire.</margin>
created things of the earth. For the Star is the Element of fire. And just as fire burns green wood and, by cooking it, drives and leads it into its own property; so too Tartar is "cooked" into its own mucilage <note>a thick, gluey substance or residue</note>. This is clear from this example: if someone either sits or walks under the rays of the Sun longer than is right, faints and disease-like attacks assault them from this. Another, seized by diseases, is subject to the Moon. He feels the powers and operations of the higher Element. For they move that paroxysm. He who stays in the cold shivers, and after the cold suffers many accidents, such as chills, the numbing of the limbs <note>original: "siderationem"; often referring to a stroke or sudden paralysis attributed to the stars</note>, other diseases, and finally death itself. In the same way, adverse natures also fall upon Tartar, such as immoderate cold or excessive heat, and this happens through the course of the Moon itself. Then, therefore, the paroxysm does not cease until it returns to its

<margin>The Physician must be an astronomer.</margin>
former constitution. Therefore, it is necessary that the Physician be properly skilled in astronomy, and that he be expert in the celestial inclinations which work by penetrating through the very skin. Furthermore, a certain paroxysm is also

<margin>From foods and drinks, either adverse or similar.</margin>
excited by food and drink in this way: if perhaps the nutrients themselves do not agree with the Tartar, from which it happens that it, as it were, leaps out, is driven into a rage, and in that place is tumultuous and rages. Indeed, if Tartar of the same kind is added afterward, then it boils over as if increased by itself, and immediately and greedily attracts the newcomer to itself. Therefore, there are many paroxysms summoned by coagulation alone.

<margin>The paroxysm of coagulation.</margin>
For as often as the Tartar coagulates <note>hardens or thickens</note>, a paroxysm is summoned through that operation. For you ought to know diligently those properties which we will review hereafter. For you may find some who, as soon as they drink sour wine or flat wine, are seized either by a twisting of the belly or a burning of the stomach. Now, truly, those affections occur only from that "contrary" thing which they took in. Just as such things are generated from their own cause, so you ought to think that there are likewise some foods and drinks which, in specific bodies prone to this, have the power to precipitate Tartar into its paroxysm. Just as some drinks produce colic, some produce a dysfunctional appetite <note>original: "orexin"</note>, some loosen the bowels, and some dry out the stomach. Operations of this kind are similar in every species of Tartar. And so that you may thoroughly understand the paroxysm, pay attention: Tartar itself feels and suffers very little pain in itself, but only the vessels which constitute those regions

<margin>Pain is in the vessels of Tartar, not in the Tartar itself.</margin>
of the Tartar. Thus colic occupies only the intestines: a thing which the very reason of the senses teaches. Nevertheless, just as salt placed in a wound provokes torment and pain, so here too the Tartar becomes the cause of pain while it drives out from itself a "spirit of malice," which makes the stomach vomit,

<margin>Tartar is Hellebore-like and Agaric-like.</margin>
because in that Tartar lies hidden a certain nature like Hellebore, Agaric, and Spurge <note>original: "Helleborina," "Agaricalis," "Esularis"; these are all potent plants used as violent laxatives or emetics</note>. For even in itself, Tartar according to its operation...

<margin>4. From external accidents: heat, cold, and sexual activity.</margin>
In its operation it is emetic <note>inducing vomiting</note>, and furthermore, it possesses a combined power to clear blockages and open the pores. If, therefore, something of this kind were lurking within a person and it were expelled, then those other signs would point to other diseases; yet at the same time, they would also be counted in the category of Tartaric signs. There are also several paroxysms <note>sudden attacks of symptoms</note> that are stirred up by other accidents, such as exercise, the sexual act, catching a chill, and similar things. Just as these are observed in patients, they need not be listed at length here.

<margin>5. From an innate property of Tartar.</margin>
It must be known, moreover, that there is a certain property implanted and innate in every single thing: *Commotion, Alteration, Purgation*, and others. This property bursts into action at its appointed time and completes its operation. Just as the kingfisher <note>original: "alcedo"; Paracelsus refers to the lore that the kingfisher molts or undergoes a transformation annually</note> sheds its feathers every year as if it were about to die.

<margin>The commotion of all things.</margin>
In the same way, a stirring is naturally inherent in Tartar itself, by which it undergoes its periodic commotions—not just once a year, but several times. And this logic of "commotion" exists in all things in its own way. Thus, in man, the blood and all the humors <note>bodily fluids</note> in the blood complete operations of this kind. So too, the rooster crows at its own time by the ordinance of nature. This "singing" nature is also present in these Tartaric diseases themselves,

<margin>He teaches that the Physician must be a Philosopher.</margin>
as is clear from Philosophy, in which a Physician must be entirely skilled if he is to recognize the true foundation of diseases. However, since you have now received the doctrine concerning the paroxysm, it seems we must next discuss the nature of Tartar. It is appropriate, therefore, that I begin with the various causes and natures of Tartar.

<margin>The essence or nature of Tartar is fourfold.</margin>
Indeed, one essence is *Mortal*. A second essence in Tartar is *Fixed*; a third *does not cause pain* or is *Painless*, and is a mild Tartar. The fourth essence comes and goes. Thus, *mortal* Tartar is of a peculiar Nature. *Chronic* Tartar is also of a singular nature. The mild Tartar is of another rank and character. So too is the fourth, the *passing* Tartar. And these differences must be known completely. For according to their number, four Methods are also established in Medicine. I emphasize this because I know many Physicians who are capable enough when dealing with "passing" Tartar—though it could be handled with much easier labor—yet, emboldened by this success, they also attempt to remove mild, chronic, and mortal Tartar.

<margin>A rebuke of Physicians.</margin>
It is certainly no small disgrace that they wish to heal anyone, yet they know neither the appropriate Medicine nor the disease itself. I have often noted this kind of ignorance and rashness in the doctors and "Physicians" of Kings, Princes, and cities. But those men, decorated with gold chains and silk robes <note>original: "torquati illi & vndulati"; a jab at the expensive, academic dress of the medical establishment</note>, are not open to any warnings. Indeed, very often these "painted masks" <note>laruae pictae</note> admit no instruction.

<margin>1. Mortal: and why.</margin>
<margin>1. By reason of its poisonous quality. Honey which is lethal.</margin>
From where *mortal* Tartar is birthed, you may learn from this example. You see that by the benefit of art <note>chemistry/alchemy</note>, a thing can be rendered not at all life-threatening. Thus, Honey is harmless by itself. In its "Third Elevation" <note>a high stage of alchemical distillation or refinement</note> it becomes lethal. There are many things in this category which can be led from good to evil. In this way, nature itself does not take a holiday, but is constantly occupied and working in its laboratory, seeking no interval of rest. By this labor, it prepares the "simples" <note>basic medicinal components</note> of metals, bismuths <note>cachimiarum</note>, marcasites <note>pyrite-like minerals</note>, and other minerals. To some things it adds poisons, to others salts, to these corrosives, to those sweets, to others bitters, and so on.

<margin>Nature sometimes wanders astray.</margin>
With these operations of nature so continuous, many errors also frequently occur, so that not everything nature begins succeeds conveniently or according to its wish. From this it happens that poisons are often mixed into the "primary matter" of Tartar, and sometimes corrosive spirits. If these are absorbed by the Tartar, and grow with the person, and live within them, they frequently bring on lethal diseases. This can happen in many ways: especially because the "spirit of salt" <note>term: spiritus salis; an acidic distillation of salt</note> contains three species of salt within itself, which are good and harmless by themselves, but easily changeable into poison and corrosive.

Hence there is a fear that, since Nature itself is the supreme Alchemist among us creatures subject to death, it may prepare that spirit into the greatest wickednesses, which death necessarily follows. For in Tartar are all kinds of poison. Therefore, as this or that species is present, if its operation exerts itself, it expels the poison—which are the "flowers of Tartar" <note>term: flores tartari; the refined or sublimated essence of the waste</note>—and if it invades the regions where life dwells, it is mortal.

<margin>Tartar has all kinds of poison.</margin>
For those fierce and atrocious pains are stirred up solely from the poisonous "flowers" of that Tartar which have exited the Tartar, just like from Arsenical smoke, or anything that operates similarly to it. For all these things are to be understood regarding Tartar as well. And this is *Mortal Tartar*. Another example: Just as poison lurks in a certain metal, and fire expels it, so the Element of fire in the heavens also expels. In the same way...

<summary>Paracelsus explains that Tartar—the metabolic waste causing stones and blockages—has four distinct natures: Mortal, Chronic, Mild, and Passing. He warns that Nature, acting as an internal alchemist, can sometimes "err" and create lethal, corrosive poisons within these deposits that mimic the effects of arsenic.</summary>

<margin>
1. The ratio of magnitudes.

Nature is only preserved in measure.

3. The ratio of multitudes.

4. The ratio for those who live in the waters.
</margin>

...only if something similar exists in Tartar <note>original: "Tartaro"; Paracelsus used this term for stony deposits in the body, comparing them to the tartar crust left by wine in a barrel</note> as well: whatever its nature, it is expelled. Hence follows the accidental symptom of which we spoke. Furthermore, Tartar may even become lethal if it exceeds the boundary of its own magnitude—just as, occasionally, even men step outside the circle of human stature and size. If Tartar becomes such, in whatever vessel <note>The "vessels" of the body, such as veins or organs</note> it may be contained, it will turn out to be mortal. For its magnitude and unsuitability destroys the vessels and leads them to ruin; for Nature cannot bear or sustain these immoderate paroxysms <note>sudden attacks or flare-ups</note>. It also happens that Tartar is harmful when increased by too great a multitude, and by that quantity, it overthrows a shaken Nature. Sometimes the property and condition of human nature is such that it can tolerate no kind of Tartar at all; just as people are found who do not drink wine, or do not eat cheese, etc. In these cases, that Tartar becomes fatal because of that deadly contrariety <note>an elemental or chemical mismatch between the substance and the person's constitution</note>; just as we see elsewhere that destruction, and thus death, is imminent from any opposing force. Then also, if Nature—whether due to weakness or other causes—cannot bear this or that, it becomes a mortal adversary; that is, if Nature herself refuses to be the healer, all diseases are rendered lethal.

<margin>
2. Chronic Tartar and its origin.
</margin>
But now let us proceed, secondly, to **Chronic** Tartar. This is generated from those things that have persisted in their own natures and properties, unchanged, and which have proceeded from fixed materials, remaining indissoluble and whole within the human being, like gold in the fire. For in those materials, the salts are fixed, giving off a fixed spirit, which then itself coagulates into a fixed body. Therefore, where there are fixed generations of this kind, there also arise fixed paroxysms, tending toward death, not toward health; not varying by multiplying the disease, but remaining in one essence.

<margin>
3. Mild Tartar: what kind and from where.
</margin>
Thirdly, you shall recognize **Mild** <note>original: "Mansuetum"</note> Tartar in this way. It does indeed cause some degree of pain, but it stirs up no "passions" <note>violent physical reactions or systemic disturbances</note>. How this can be, learn from this example: you see by what logic the *Stupefactive*, *Narcotic*, *Opiate*, and other *Somniferous* <note>sleep-inducing</note> things grow. Thus, in the varieties of Tartar, properties of this kind are also sometimes found. And just as Nature does not fashion or establish all things according to a single rule and measure, but for the most part delights in variety, so too in this place you shall know that diverse properties and natures of Tartar have been established.

<margin>
Scarring, Acidic, Barberry-like, Pontic, Peppery Tartar.
</margin>
For a Physician should never be so convinced that one disease has only one nature and condition. For example, the plague: for there are as many different natures as there are plagues. This is also true of apples and pears. Apples and pears are indeed individual fruits, yet one is constantly distinct from another. The same logic applies to diseases, and the same logic applies to Tartar itself. Hence, sometimes one finds **Scarring Tartar**, as well as **Acidic**, **Barberry-like**, **Pontic** <note>original: "Ponticus"; likely referring to a bitter or astringent quality associated with "Pontic" herbs like rhubarb</note>, and **Peppery** Tartar. For every single one leads its own paroxysms according to that nature and essence. And just as there are properties in Nature itself, so too are there properties in diseases.

<margin>
4. Passing Tartar: what kind and from where.
</margin>
The fourth is **Passing Tartar**. This is collected daily, and is also secreted daily. The cause is that, by its own innate nature, it has no stable dwelling. Whence it expels and thrusts itself out. And this is the most placid and mildest of all. And it is the bounden duty of Physicians that every single kind of Tartar be reduced and prepared for a similar expulsion.

### CHAPTER XV.
->*On the Order and Regimen which ought to be followed in the case of Tartar.*<-

<margin>
Diet or Regimen is the primary cure.
</margin>
**H**itherto, enough has been said and taught concerning the origin, generation, essence, nature, and causes of Tartar, at least as much as could be demonstrated through the light of nature itself. As for those things which serve for a fuller illustration of each point, let them be sought from the great books of Nature, which are trodden underfoot and read <note>A common Paracelsian metaphor: the "Book of Nature" is the physical world around us</note>. Next, however, being about to turn to the cure which these diseases demand, we shall first undertake an explanation of the Regimen, diet, and order. To this must be prefixed knowledge concerning the Nature and property of the *spirit of coagulation* <note>the invisible force Paracelsus believed caused liquids to turn into solids like stone</note>: which it is necessary to teach so that a regimen of this kind may be established, by which the spirit of coagulation in man may be broken and destroyed. <margin>The diet to be described which must come first.</margin> Afterward, secondly, [we will explain] how Tartar is to be removed and destroyed in all growing things, lest any mass or subject matter be left behind from which the spirits of Tartar might be born and coagulated. Furthermore, if the concordance of those properties can be joined together, so that for the sake of increasing the union, a separation of them may be instituted—just as spouses are separated by divorce so they do not produce children thereafter—once these things are known beforehand, the order...

# ON TARTARIC DISEASES

<margin>Rules and precepts for a proper diet.</margin>
The rule is this: first, care must be taken to ensure that the "spirit of coagulation" <note>In Paracelsian medicine, this is the force that causes substances to harden into stones or deposits</note> loses its power so that it can no longer solidify anything. Second, the person's nourishment, both food and drink, must be purged of **Tartar** <note>original: "Tartaro"; the stony sediment Paracelsus believed caused diseases like gout and kidney stones</note>, and it must be destroyed in such a way that Tartar can never again coagulate from it. Third, the spirit of coagulation and the mass of Tartar must be kept so separate from one another that they never seize or embrace each other again. If a **Regimen** <note>A prescribed way of life or diet</note> is established in this way and in this order, then neither the cause nor the material is left behind from which a disease of this kind could be born or produced.

<margin>One Tartar is granted to each region.</margin>
Thus it will happen that through suitable remedies, Tartar is not only driven out of the body but is also prevented from regenerating by means of a good regimen. This diagnosis, however, must rely on evident and thoroughly tested experience, so that the proof is confirmed by the very testimony of the eyes. For in this way, Tartar is a disease that is visible in a person with the living eyes, and it offers its material to be looked upon visibly and felt by touch. In the same way, external Tartar is also exhibited visibly and tangibly through the art <note>The "art" here refers to alchemy or chemical analysis</note>.

<margin>A Physician must be both a Naturalist and a Philosopher.</margin>
According to these articles, it befits every Physician to prescribe his Regimen solidly and fundamentally for the sake of the cure. Above all, he must know **external Tartar**—what kind of thing it is, how it adheres and sticks together, and whether it lies hidden in food or in drink. He who lacks this knowledge does not know what he is forbidding. If he forbids twenty things when he should only forbid wine, and happens to forbid something harmful by chance, he does so by luck, not by art. It is therefore right, in this case, for the Physician to be a **Naturalist** <note>original: "Physicum"; one who understands the physical nature of the human "microcosm"</note> because of the properties of the human body, and furthermore a **Philosopher** because of the properties of natural things. This ensures that errors and corruptions are not introduced out of ignorance or by chance. For even if very good and excellent remedies are applied to achieve resolution and expulsion, if what was driven out is put back into the person through an error in diet, the Tartar will later grow back more abundantly and firmly.

<margin>Alchemy is necessary for the Physician.</margin>
And it is fitting for a Physician to be "pregnant" with such experience, rather than being proud of **red tunics** or armored and girt with metal plates like the shells of the **Jacobites** <note>A reference to the scallop shells worn by pilgrims of St. James (Santiago); Paracelsus is mocking doctors who care more about their prestigious academic dress and status than actual knowledge</note>. Since these things are required of a Physician, he will especially need **Alchemy**. Through it, one finds what lies within and is hidden in every body. He who does not know all these things "to the fingernail" <note>A Latin idiom meaning "perfectly"</note> has not even touched the beginning or the entrance of Medicine. For the Physician must penetrate so far with accurate investigation that he knows Tartar not only in general, but in every specific type of food and drink in which it hides—what its nature is, what hardness, what form, what property, and what essence it has. And although every single species might present a certain kind of tartar, this caution is nevertheless necessary: that Tartar be extracted in the manner we have described, and the **salt of urine** <note>The crystalline residue left after urine evaporates, used by Paracelsus to diagnose which minerals were depositing in the body</note> be separated by the aforementioned method, so that its grades and qualities may then be judged to see which are suitable or unsuitable for whom.

<margin>The duty of Physicians in prescribing diet and curing Tartar.</margin>
Every Physician who sets out to prescribe a diet professionally and solidly based on the art should turn his mind to these absolutely necessary points. As soon as a Physician approaches a certain region—for he ought to wander through and know all lands—he shall consider most accurately, by seeing with intent eyes and feeling with outstretched hands, if anything exists or flourishes in those places. If he finds a certain Tartaric sickness there, he will diligently and curiously look into and track down from which drink or food that Tartar grew. That is, he will make a judgment from the urine and distinguish what genus and, even more accurately, what species that Tartar is. Thus, he will weigh the nutrients themselves in a certain balance to see which ones correspond with that Tartar, so that through this comparison, the connection between the **internal Tartar** and the **external Tartar** may be found.

<margin>Separated salt of urine: the index of Tartar.</margin>
In this examination, if many types of Tartar are found, they do not all contribute their power to the disease. Therefore, it is necessary that only the "guilty" one be tracked down, and that one alone be pointed out and forbidden in the Regimen. For it happens not infrequently that in a certain region, one legume, or a certain type of grain, or one food or drink, or a single species is found which generates Tartar there and brings it upon the whole population. This must be sought out with the greatest diligence. For if that type, native to that region, is removed and another foreign type is mixed in its place, no more Tartar will be generated in those inhabitants. Let us take an example.

<margin>Tartar species to be judged from urine.</margin>
In this way, once certain Tartars have been found by both genus and species, then those which are at fault must be excluded and forbidden when establishing a natural Regimen.

<margin>Kelheim wine is the cause of many Tartars.</margin>
**Kelheim wine** <note>Wine from the region of Kelheim in Bavaria</note> brings about many Tartaric labors and difficulties. Therefore, he who avoids it and drinks **Neckar wine** <note>Wine from the Neckar river region in Swabia</note> in its place, is [saved] from that disease...

He emphasizes that doctors must look past professional finery to understand the chemical nature of local foods and their interaction with the human body.</summary>
