# ON DISEASES
<lang>Latin</lang>

<margin>
A necessary remedy for him.
</margin>
...he is secure from it. This is also the reason why one should not always remain or be satisfied with what our own land and region produce; rather, whatever is healthy and wholesome should be sought even from foreigners and strangers in such a case. In this way, let one region always extend a hand to another: the Rhine to the Danube, the Danube to the Rhine, Italy to Germany, and Germany to Italy—with each one occasionally supplying that which can serve the benefit and assistance of the other.

<margin>
One region is a medicine to another.
</margin>
Therefore, through this universal example, understand all types of food and drink in a specific sense: that is, one village, city, or spring can always supply and correct the deficiency of another. For not all springs are of one kind, nor are all wines the same. A Physician absolutely requires this kind of experience: so that, while he carries the title, he may also possess the art itself. For he cannot properly forbid this or that unless he substitutes another permitted thing in place of the forbidden one; that is, if he finds "offending matter" in this food, he should also find "non-offending matter" in another food. He shall allow the latter; he shall forbid the former. For one thing is frequently the opposite of another, and there is nothing that does not have some substitute given to it.

<margin>
Good is everywhere opposed to evil.
</margin>
For good and evil exist in every kind of thing. Therefore, a careful examination is needed so that the Physician may know what excels in any given species, lest by chance, while a bad thing is forbidden, a worse one is substituted. As the teachings of books sufficiently demonstrate, this has been the practice of those physicians <margin>Rebuke of Physicians.</margin> whose **Regimen** <term>Regimen: a prescribed system of diet and lifestyle to maintain health</term> and diet were established without any prior examination, but were set down by mere whim. Yet it is a great disgrace to a Physician if he forbids something without knowing why he forbids it, or without knowing what lies hidden within this or that substance. And by such rash whim, diets have been prescribed until now. This is why all Medicine has fallen into contempt and scorn— <margin>Medicine is a demonstration, not an opinion.</margin> because they themselves have publicly fostered these errors with such obstinence until now. For they do not prove or judge anything by sight, by matter, or by reality; instead, they merely bring in their own opinions, which Medicine can in no way tolerate. For Medicine, unlike Logic, does not delight in opinions, but wishes to be established by the truth itself.

<margin>
What a Physician must do to be praised.
</margin>
He who wishes to practice as a Physician in his own country with praise and tranquility must first and foremost thoroughly know the nature and **Tartar** <term>Tartar: the stony, metabolic waste Paracelsus believed caused many diseases</term> of his own homeland, and afterward examine and compare it separately according to every kind of food and drink. For if you live in your land and have inhabited it for some time, yet do not know through a thorough examination of the whole region what is and lies hidden in each individual thing, you are certainly not worthy for the earth to bear you. This is because, beset by lazy ignorance, you have not labored to inquire into those things which you were duty-bound to know. In this way, you bring harm to the citizens of your homeland; to those who supply the nourishment to sustain your life, you return neither gratitude nor any reward. However, if you establish an examination of this kind and track down every necessity, and such Tartaric sicknesses <margin>The examination of Tartar must be made from the salt of urine.</margin> occur to you, then you shall make a judgment from the salt of the urine. You shall compare one thing closely with another, just as one gemstone is compared with another gemstone; and finally, you will follow what is worthy of a Physician in establishing that regimen. For unless the Regimen is properly observed in the cure of Tartar, <margin>Tartaric disease is common to all lands.</margin> all of Medicine is finished. Therefore, it is right for the Physician to be cautious, wherever in the world he may be. For no place anywhere lacks Tartaric sicknesses. Although, I do not remember if I have ever visited any land less subject to Tartaric sicknesses than that which is called *Valtellina* <note>original: "Veldtlinia"; a valley in the Alps, now part of northern Italy</note>. <margin>Valtellina is the least Tartaric of all.</margin> Neither Germany, nor Italy, nor France, nor the East, nor the West in Europe is similar to this place. For among the natives of that region, no **Gout** <term>original: "Podagra"; painful joint inflammation</term>, no colic, no contraction of limbs, nor any stone was ever seen or found, so that I could not help but admire it most greatly. For that region, with all the things that grow there, exists as so healthy that I have not found a healthier one in the entire course of my travels. If by chance other regions similar to this are found, they are not known to me. However, I can hardly believe there are other regions in Europe of the same healthiness.

### CHAPTER XVI.
->*On the preservation against and avoidance of tartaric generation.*<-

<margin>To every disease its own medicine is assigned.</margin>
**A**lthough diseases of various and manifold kinds range everywhere throughout the whole world, there is none among them all for which its own Medicine has not been created and set in opposition by God. Now, however, from the preceding chapters, you know what the generation of **Tartar** is and of what kind. And even if it is sometimes thick, difficult, and strong: on the contrary <note>The text ends with the catchword "econ-" for "econtra" (on the contrary), indicating the argument continues on the next page.</note>

# ON TARTARIC DEPOSITS
<lang>en</lang>

On the other hand, however, nature itself has been given such strong and powerful preservatives that that <term>Tartaric</term><note>Paracelsus used "Tartar" to describe the stony, hard deposits that cause gout, kidney stones, and calcification, comparing them to the crusty "tartar" found in wine barrels.</note> generation can be conveniently countered, so that it is not at all able to dominate at its own whim, but is compelled to yield entirely. But what a human being does not have within their own <term>Archeus</term><note>The "Archeus" is the internal "alchemist" or vital force that governs the body's functions, particularly digestion and separation of nutrients from waste.</note>, they may borrow from the Archeus of nature itself located outside the human. And this is born from the earth. Therefore, take note of the following process of preservatives in this place.

<margin>The ostrich digests iron</margin>
You see that the **ostrich** digests and consumes iron, steel, and copper, as if it were a pear or a nut. 
<margin>The dog digests bone. The blackbird, spiders.</margin>
The **dog** cooks and digests bone no slower than meat. The **blackbird** devours spiders and digests them like hemp seed. 
<margin>The stork, serpents.</margin>
The **stork** gulps down frogs, serpents, and other harmful insects; all of these are good food and nourishment for it. By their example, you ought to know that Medicine was given to man for this purpose: so that his stomach might be strengthened for the *cooking* <note>original: "coctio" - the alchemical and medical term for digestion as a heat-based process</note> of that which he takes in or carries. For example: Tartar is carried into a human. Now, however, it is the office of the stomach to cook, separate, and expel it, just as was said above. If the stomach can do this very little of itself, it must nevertheless be brought to such a state that it is harmed by no poison. Just as the spider does not harm the blackbird, nor the serpent the stork.

<margin>How the human stomach is to be strengthened.</margin>
An attempt must therefore be made to bring the stomach into such a condition that it can digest and consume those Tartars, no less than the ostrich digests iron. For both digestions are possible in the human and in the ostrich. If, therefore, the Physician wishes to prescribe preservation from these Tartaric diseases, he will first reduce the stomach to such a state that it consumes all things that enter into it, not otherwise than fire consumes wood.

<margin>Preservation consists either in the stomach itself, or in removing the Tartar.</margin>
This is done through the rectification, comforting, alteration, and strengthening of the stomach. For it cannot be done in any other way. However, so that you may understand this properly, I will propose to you two modes of preservation. One belongs to the stomach itself, as we said. The other is the removal of external Tartar, so that it is not ingested. Preservation of the stomach itself is procured through *hungry acids* <note>original: "acetosa esurina" - potent acidic substances or mineral waters that stimulate a "hunger" or corrosive power in the stomach.</note>. These are twofold: *Natural* and *Artificial.*

<margin>What a hungry acid is, and how many types.</margin>
A *hungry acid* is a Medicine which by its own nature renders the stomach so famished that it even craves unusual foods. Moreover, what it craves, it thoroughly cooks and digests.

<margin>What a Natural acid is. What an Artificial acid is.</margin>
But so that you may understand *Acid* more fully: know that a **Natural acid** is a spring-fed acid, such as the <term>Acidulae</term><note>Mineral springs believed to have medicinal, acidic properties.</note>. An **Artificial acid** is a vitriolated acid. Thus, in acidity alone consists the power of digesting the things we mentioned. Acidic springs are natural mineral waters, some of which are occasionally superior to others. Artificial acids are made from the minerals of metals and the like. And although it is indeed customary to say *vitriolated acid*, it is nevertheless the vitriol of <term>Venusian copper</term><note>In alchemy, Venus represents the metal copper.</note>. For copper is vitriol. If, therefore, the acidity is extracted from copper, then he who uses it will digest copper. So it happens with all other vitriols of metals. Therefore, if it is said that the ostrich eats all metals, it is to be understood in this way. For in all metals there are vitriolated acids; only gold does not acknowledge vitriol.

<margin>Gold lacks vitriol.</margin>
The ostrich has this kind of *Hungry Acidity* established in its own nature and property, whence it digests even such things. A human, however, does not have it in himself. Yet it can be introduced and carried into him, so that he may similarly digest that which he could never digest through his innate property alone. Therefore, I would further have you know that acidic thermal baths have these kinds of vitriolated natures, though in manifold forms. For as many species of colors as there are, there are also just as many of acidity, nor is there only one species of it. However, one acidic spring, which I proclaim and extol above all those I have known in Europe, I found in **Engadine** at **St. Moritz**, whose source flows most acidic in the month of August.

<margin>The Engadine acidic waters are the most excellent of all for the stomach.</margin>
He who drinks this in the manner of a Medicine attains perfect health; he never knows or incurs any stone, or sand, or gout, or <term>Arthritis</term><note>original: "Artetica" - a general term for joint diseases.</note>. For through it the stomach is so strengthened that it digests Tartar no more sluggishly than the ostrich digests iron or the blackbird a spider. And not Tartar alone, but also other things stirring up diseases in man, the primary matter of which is located in food and drink. These universal primary matters, whatever they may be, are consumed. And just as all wood indiscriminately—crooked, straight, smooth, or knotty—burns in a furnace, so the same happens in those stomachs.

<margin>Spring acidity is twofold: perceptible and imperceptible.</margin>
Moreover, the types of spring acidity are twofold: one is perceived in its acidity; the other is not perceived in it, and yet the property is unique. Concerning this, note that it digests no less than the acid itself. For take a lesson from an example. Fire is not always kindled by fire, such as fire struck from a flint; but sometimes fire burns from no— <note>The text ends mid-sentence as it transitions to the next page.</note>

<summary>Paracelsus explains that Tartaric diseases can be prevented by strengthening the stomach's digestive power ("Archeus") to mimic animals like the ostrich. He identifies specific acidic mineral waters, particularly those from St. Moritz in Engadine, as the most effective "hungry acids" for dissolving stony deposits and ensuring perfect health.</summary>

# ON DISEASES
<meta>catchword: these</meta>

...heat caused by fire, such as comes from the sun, from friction, and so on. And yet there is no less fire here than that struck from a flint. The same logic applies here as well. For if that substance enters the stomach, it produces the same effect as that which <term>acidic remedies</term><note>original: "acetosa" - refers to sour or acidic substances believed to "cut" through heavy deposits like tartar.</note> achieve.

<margin>Hidden acidic sources: what and where they are.</margin>
Furthermore, those *hidden acidic sources* are springs, marked by marvelous natural qualities and gifts, distinguished from other waters in many ways. For the most part, they exist high up in the mountain ridges, in rocks and crags, on snowy peaks far above the earth, the soil, and the mud, found only in sands, rocks, and stones. One of these is the **Rhine** at its source, and the **Elbe**, and almost all waters similar to these, bursting forth from a similar spring-head.

<margin>The origin of the Rhine and the Elbe.</margin>
But as to how they may be more fully understood, I leave that to the Philosophers to teach. For the present passage does not permit a more fertile discussion. It is right, however, for a Physician to be a Naturalist, and to have known such things before he acts as a Physician.

<margin>How illustrious is the workshop of Nature.</margin>
For since nature itself works and perfects these kinds of secrets through its own art—not by human industry—the Physician shall explore these same things within nature itself. He shall investigate what kind and what quality of things she composes, decocts, and prepares; he shall visit her pharmacy, her jars, her boxes, and her vessels throughout the whole world—in mountains, in rocks and crags, in sand, and indeed everywhere. For the workshop of Nature is most ample, and her remedies are also excellent, helpful, and very healthy, yet they are not for sale for any amount of money. For she is not accustomed to heal the sick for a fee, but by offering her medicines. And I recommend this workshop henceforth to all visitors and teachers.

<margin>Acidity is situated in minerals.</margin>
Now, to speak further of artificial acidic remedies, I would have you know that this kind of acidity is situated within the minerals themselves. The art, however, which demonstrates where it is situated, is the **Art of Signatures**. But the art which extracts and draws out that acidity is another; it is called **Alchemy**, which teaches how to separate the acidic from the sweet, and reduces each thing into its own body, minimally mixed. Thus, the artificial acidic remedy is also prepared. But now it is necessary that I explain to you somewhat the process of <unclear>finding</unclear> and the process of *Separating*. And although these things may be considered academic, yet because the current academic curriculum neither knows nor understands this teaching, it is right that it be proposed by me. This shall be done in the following discourse.

<margin>What the Art of Signatures is.</margin>
The <term>Art of Signatures</term><note>A historical theory that plants or minerals that look like a part of the body can treat that body part, or that external traits reveal internal medicinal powers.</note> (or the "Consigned Art") manifests and betrays everything through external signs, whatever is placed within that body. Thus, through external signs and "signatures," one may perceive which is the ore of gold, which of silver, which of copper, and so on. This art is a limb of **Astronomy** itself, and thus provides an entrance to medicine. If we wished to describe here the way in which those signs are found and grasped, this chapter would certainly exceed the length of two books. Let it suffice here that I have explained to you that by the benefit of the Art of Signatures, internal things are known through external signs. Just as the nature of the nettle is known by its burning, or the nature of gentian by its bitterness.

<margin>What Alchemy does.</margin>
As for what pertains to *Separation*, that is the science of **Alchemy**. It teaches how to extract, to gather, and to separate each thing into its own peculiar vessel. Now, the acidities are varied. They are found in metals, in gems, in <term>marcasites</term><note>An old term for various crystallized minerals, often iron pyrites.</note>, in <term>cachymias</term><note>A Paracelsian term for metallic ores that are not yet "perfect" metals.</note>, in <term>chimolea</term><note>A term for various types of clay or earth-like mineral residues.</note>, and so forth. Each genus, however, has its own art and its own method of extraction.

<margin>Acidity in vessels.</margin>
To explain all of these things word for word is beyond the intent of this treatise. Note this here: if copper is broken down and dissolved without a corrosive, you have **vitriol**. From that, prepare the <term>Quintessence</term><note>The "fifth essence" or purest medicinal core of a substance.</note>, the oil, and the liquor of the substance itself. In this way, the acidic remedy of **Venus** <note>In alchemy, Venus represents Copper.</note> is perfected, and thus is the secret in those things of which I have spoken. You ought to do the same with the other metals. However, Venus and **Saturn** <note>In alchemy, Saturn represents Lead.</note> are supreme in their acidic virtues. After them comes **Steel**, and finally **Tin**.

<margin>How copper becomes vitriol.</margin>
<margin>Which metals are more acidic than others.</margin>
In the *Adept* philosophy, **Mercury** is not numbered among the metals. Furthermore, regarding the other minerals—marcasites, cachymias, mountain ores, and chimoleas—it is arranged so that it is necessary first to take away their sulfur and to retain the mercurial liquor and the salt alone. For in that salt exists the *Acidity of Art*; it is extracted and prepared into an *oil*, a liquor, and an *acidic substance*. These, therefore, are the processes and the secrets which, if used, preserve one from **Tartaric diseases**, provided they observe and apply the *dose and quantity* for each, which I leave to the Physician to determine according to the condition of the person.

<margin>The dose must be defined by the Physician.</margin>
If, however, someone has already conceived Tartar within themselves: so that the same may be expelled again through preservatives (as much as can indeed be done), it is necessary to join the order of cure in several points. Thus, washing with added care completes and perfects the cure. So, a medicinal wash combined with care also perfects the preservatives so that they penetrate more exquisitely. Thus, they do not merely cook, boil down, digest, and consume in the stomach, but they also procure this kind of digestion in the entire body. But...

## CHAPTER XVII.

### On the Cure of Tartar in its First Matter, not yet Coagulated, in whatever place of the whole body it exists.

<margin>The cure of the first matter is accomplished by bath and potion.</margin>
As we prepare to discuss the cure, we must first begin with the <term>first matter</term><note>In Paracelsian medicine, "first matter" refers to the initial, fluid stage of a disease before it solidifies into a physical mass like a stone.</note> of Tartar, before it has become coagulated. Let it be known to you that Tartar in its first matter stirs up paroxysms and pains no less than it does in its solidified state. Indeed, various diseases arise from this first matter of Tartar which have, until now, led many astray. But regarding the treatment of this first matter, know that it is perfected by the **Bath** and the **Potion**. The Bath is applied so that the body may grow warm and remain hot, and so that this heat may simultaneously moisten rather than dry it out, whether that Bath be natural or artificial. For the medicine that is to expel the first matter must have external heat and moisture; otherwise, the operation proceeds too slowly. The medicine itself ought to be continually joined and proceed alongside the Bath. It is also fitting that the medicine be of such a kind that both food and drink have the power of a remedy. This is because food and drink are distributed through the entire body and are attracted by all the members under the guise of nourishment. 

<margin>All parts of the body attract nourishment.</margin>
Thus, food and drink pervade the whole body, and no place is inaccessible to them. While the nourishment permeates all the members, it finds and touches whatever is in the body, whether it be good or bad. For this reason, the nourishment is joined most closely to the body's parts. Now, if the nourishment is simultaneously a **Medicine**, then the Medicine reaches the disease wherever it may lurk in any member of the body. A disease cannot be found more conveniently or directly by any directory or index than by nourishment. It is right, therefore, for food and drink to contain a specific medicine against Tartar. 

<margin>Nourishment must be the medicine for Tartar.</margin>
If, therefore, the medicines against the first matter are tartaric, no first matter of Tartar is left in the whole body that is not tracked down, found, and expelled. To ensure that nourishment becomes Medicine, the sick person should be given everything that they crave and desire, whether it be meat, fish, wine, etc., with nothing excluded. 

<margin>Everything should be given to the appetite indiscriminately.</margin>
For the more vehement the appetite, the more eager is the handling of all the body's parts and the more prompt and rapid the drawing-in of the nourishment itself. And although those foods and drinks may be somewhat unhealthy, that should not be a concern. For they are administered for this purpose at least: that they may direct and lead, penetrate, and occupy the site of the Tartar and the pain. 

<margin>Desired nourishments penetrate more quickly.</margin>
Indeed, if they are prepared in the manner we are about to describe, they will become medicine, just as the <term>viper</term><note>original: "Tyrus," referring to viper flesh used in the ancient cure-all medicine called Theriac.</note> is used in **Theriac**. For the viper is not consumed for the purpose of healing by itself, since it is a poison; but only so that it may be a vehicle, penetrating and pervading the body, and simultaneously snatching along with it the other medicinal virtues added to it and entwined through its composition.

<margin>What natural Tartar baths should be like.</margin>
Now, because we said above that the first matter of Tartar is cured by Baths and potions: know that the bath must not consist of sulfur, vitriol, or alum. A Bath—whether it be Natural (such as hot springs) or Artificial—should lack all these species and ingredients. 

<margin>The "Peppery" hot springs are best against Tartar. The Teplitz springs. How artificial baths are to be prepared.</margin>
Of all Baths, the <term>peppery springs</term><note>original: "piperinæ," likely referring to the Pfäfers (Pfeffers) hot springs in Switzerland, known for their heat.</note> are the most excellent and noble; just as the **Teplitz** springs in Bohemia are next to these, located not far from Grauppen toward Brix. Artificial Baths should be prepared from rainwater and snow water, or from dew (which are the best), mixed with other waters. In these are to be boiled: turnip leaves, their peels, or the whole turnips themselves, parsnips, carrot leaves or roots, chamomile, <term>mullein</term><note>original: "tapsus barbatus."</note> (especially its leaves), betony (both purple and white), self-heal, columbine, wild radish, and mugwort. There is no use for other herbs. For what these listed plants do not provide, the remaining ones will produce much more sluggishly. From these, therefore, a bath is to be prepared in the usual manner; it would be superfluous to describe the method more at length.

<margin>The "potion" should include food as well.</margin>
Regarding **Potions**, this must be held: that both food and drink are understood by the single word "potion." The reason for this is that food ought to be reduced into a drinkable form, so that food which is chewed with the teeth does not remain as a solid. For from that solid food, the dregs, Tartar, and bodily excrement must be separated in such a way that only the nourishment remains to be consumed, and this is not left behind with the Tartar and excrement. While this is done, a potion emerges from all those things which were food. Wine is a drink by itself. The separation is done in this way: For nourishment, choose meat. 

<margin>How meat is prepared as medicine.</margin>
But so that meat may become a medicine, let it be prepared thus: Add to it thorny columbine, mistletoe of the oak... <note>original: "viscum quer-," likely "viscum quercinum." The text cuts off here and continues on the next page.</note>

# CHAPTER XVIII.
### On the Cure of Tartar in the form of Tartar and sand, in whatever place of the body it may be.

The Method described in the preceding chapter must also be observed in the Expulsion of *Tartar*, of which this chapter will treat, for this reason: that the first matter of Tartar is always present as well, which must be removed at the same time and by the same operation, lest any new material for coagulation be established. However, the general precept in the cure is such: that every medicine, by its innate power, should be so opposed to Tartar that it dissolves and destroys it to the point that it becomes like a liquid, or a viscous substance, or mucus, and can never be coagulated again. If that destruction has been accomplished, then nature itself expels it. Therefore, in this case, <margin>The dissolution of Tartar is its cure.</margin> one must at least take care that such things are administered which contain <term>Arcana</term> <note>secret or hidden healing powers</note> of this kind. And these are not indeed corrosive, but genuine remedies. For if God created certain things that crush and dissolve iron and stones, and reduce them to liquid: He would also have created the necessary things for the health of man, so that through them the Great Works of God might be known and celebrated. This, therefore, is our task and duty: that we investigate these mysteries of God in Nature, and not grow numb in lazy idleness, but be alert and vigilant when about to practice Medicine, and attend the true and genuine school. The foundation, therefore, of ejecting Tartar is placed in these points: that those...

# ON TARTARIC DISEASES

<margin>The nature of the secrets for dissolving Tartar.</margin> Secrets and mysteries should be applied in which there is the power and efficacy of resolution, dissolution, and destruction. For by this way, the <term>Tartar</term> <note>The stony waste products Paracelsus believed caused many diseases</note> of the whole body is shaken and removed. It grows and is generated in the body in two ways: <margin>The dual form of Tartar.</margin> for it either adheres in the form of a solid crust, or <margin>Tartar and Sand.</margin> in the form of grit, such as the stones that split and tear the tissues. The process of the cure consists first in the regimen; afterward in the bath, in every way we have described. Along with these, remedies must also be administered, morning and evening, as necessity itself demands, applied either more rarely or more frequently.

Furthermore, the preparation of the medicine is such that it must be made from stones and first reduced into a liquor which cannot be turned back into a stone, but is entirely consumed and removed during coagulation. Once these things are performed, the medicine will be prepared and made suitable. Now, no importance is placed on writing long and promised recipes, or huddling many ingredients together in them. The heart of the matter is that what we have spoken of should be well prepared. The aids that have seemed suitable to me are these: **Crab's eyes** <note>original: "Oculi Cancrorum"; small calcium deposits found in the stomachs of crayfish, historically used as antacids</note>, **Jew's stone** <note>original: "lapis Iudaicus"; fossilized spines of sea urchins, traditionally used to treat kidney stones</note>, <margin>Secrets sought from stones.</margin> **Lynx stone** <note>original: "lapis Lyncis"; belemnite fossils</note>, **Lapis Lazuli**, **Sponge stone** <note>original: "lapis spongiæ"; calcified nodules found in sea sponges</note>, **Eagle stone** <note>original: "lapis aquilae"; a hollow geode with a smaller stone inside it</note>, **Ice stone** <note>original: "lapis glaciei"; likely selenite or transparent gypsum</note>, etc. There is no <margin>What the secrets of Tartar are.</margin> need for all of these to be taken together, but each one by itself is sufficient. For it is the preparation that accomplishes the task, and that same preparation integrates and completes the recipe. 

In this regard, it must also be held that for plucking out Tartar by the roots, <margin>Roots, herbs, and seeds remarkable for Tartar.</margin> **roots, herbs, and seeds**, etc., are not strong enough; rather, it is necessary to use similar stones, such as I have reviewed, of which there are many more than I have listed. For in these stones, the power of expelling Tartar is placed. I would wish for you to remember <margin>The Art of Signatures is necessary for medicine.</margin> that the **science of signatures** <note>the belief that the appearance of a natural object provides a clue to its medical use; here, stones are used to treat "stones" in the body</note> demonstrates and proves through a "signature" that these aforementioned stones possess the power to eject Tartar. Therefore, whoever wishes to be a Physician must first know the signature of the Tartar; afterward, he must also grasp the signature of the medicine, so that both signatures are joined into one Anatomy and reduced into one Cosmography. For if you have the signature, you will also have that body in which the mystery that drives out Tartar lies hidden. 

Now, destroy and dissolve that body in this way: Distill the essence of wine <note>alcohol</note> nine times. Afterward, calcine <note>burn to a white ash</note> the fresh <margin>The nature of the mystery's preparation.</margin> stones, and dissolve them in that essence of wine; they will be dissolved just like salt in water. Finally, distill it: and what settles at the bottom, mix that with new essence of wine and sublime it until the whole has risen. Now that body is broken and destroyed, and you can safely use it as a prepared medicine, as I have said. You should by no means worry about separating the liquor from the essence of wine. For the essence provides more benefit when present than when separated. It helps to penetrate, investigate, and direct, and it operates more effectively against the Tartar and the sands of the internal Tartar, which it melts and resolves into a mucilage. 

Although it frequently happens that the Medicine operates quickly, and the Tartar yields its place so hastily that it cannot be dissolved beforehand, but escapes the Medicine and departs before the operation is complete. This process must be carefully watched. By this order and method, all Tartar in the entire body is attacked and expelled, provided the Medicine for its expulsion is sufficiently valid and robust. And although not many recipes are administered, those that are suffice for any kind of Tartar of this sort. For <margin>Any simple remedy is sufficient for Tartar.</margin> any single substance is sufficient by itself. But if a composite must be made, the simple substances are again sufficient from which recipes can be composed and arranged. Therefore, to expand upon this chapter more broadly or profusely is beyond its purpose.

And indeed, that generation can occur in all places of the whole body, wherever there are movements and connections of two members, or the cavities of the muscles and limbs, etc. Wherever, therefore, Tartars of this kind flourish, there also **Arthritis**, **Podagra** <note>gout of the foot</note>, **Chiragra** <note>gout of the hand</note>, **Genugra** <note>gout of the knee</note>, **Sciatica**, and other joint pains are produced, in whatever region of the body it happens, whether in the back and its spine, or in the ribs, etc. Now indeed, Physicians...

# ON DISEASES

They frequently recite a proverbial verse:

> The Doctor knows not how to cure knotty Gout. <note>original: "Neſcit nodoſam Medicus curare Podagram"</note>

Which is, however, clearly foolish and ill-composed. For Gout is not knotty, but "Tartarous." For those grains are grains of <term>Tartar</term> <note>The stony waste products Paracelsus believed caused many diseases</note>: so that it might deservedly be called by the more appropriate name, *Tartarus*. Furthermore, the word *Doctor* [Medicus] in the verse is useless. For those who call themselves Doctors, but are unable to cure Tartar, are by no means Doctors; rather, they are *Roades* <note>A derogatory term Paracelsus used for veterinary doctors or untrained practitioners who lack true medical insight</note>, that is, veterinary doctors, who have not yet ripened, just like wild plums before autumn. Therefore, if I were a poet (which I am least of all), I would correct that verse in this way:

<margin>The proverbial verse about gout is corrected by the author.</margin>
> The Veterinary knows not how to cure Tartaric gout. <note>original: "Neſcit Tartaream Roades curare podagram"</note>

Let him who desires a more elegant one compose it. Furthermore, in this chapter my intention is to teach by what cure Gouty *Tartar* may be expelled. For once that is taken away and removed, the gout also departs. Do not let it seem strange to you that I teach how to cure such a great disease in such a short chapter. The chapter is indeed short, I admit, but it brings more utility and fruit than all the treatises or books ever written and published. As for the fact that I have published another specific treatise on Tartar besides this chapter: it was done to explain the origin and cause of gout more fully. The highest and most harmful thing in Tartar is the "ultimate matter" of gout. Indeed, if you take all the other causes of gout and omit Tartar, you will achieve nothing at all. Therefore, since my intention is to expel Tartar, which holds the first place among the causes: it ought to be joined with the <margin>What the process of his gout treatment is.</margin> other types in this book. Here now is the Method and process: you must not allow a bath, although that might seem suitable because of the Tartar. For it is both harmful and adverse because of other causes and <margin>The bath is harmful to gouty patients.</margin> circumstances concurring in gout. You can, however, observe and maintain the prescribed diet: because there is rarely a gout which does not contain several types of Tartar, besides that which is contained in the joints, articulations, and similar mentioned places. Therefore, the only protection can be expected from the resolution and destruction <margin>Resolution of granular Tartar is the cure for gout.</margin> of granular Tartar, which the *Roades* call "knotty" gout. You will resolve those granules in such a way that they are reduced into the form of honey or thickened sugar; and by that resolution they are consumed, and by that consumption the joints—which were hardened, dislocated, or curved—are again extended, softened, and relaxed, and return to their former nature.

But because more things are required for that dislocation than just the cure of granular <margin>The author's specific book on gout.</margin> Tartar: therefore the rest are handed down in more detail in the published book on *Gout*, and need not be repeated further here. Of the mysteries or <term>arcana</term> <note>Powerful alchemical remedies believed to contain the "inner heart" or essence of a substance</note> which resolve gouty Tartar, five are known and investigated by me. Although any one of these by itself might be sufficient, they can easily allow a composition made from some of them, but not all. Although these five are called "simples," not every simple thing is a species by itself, as in gums: of which although there are many, they are nonetheless *gums*. Following this example, the others should also be judged. These five are <margin>The mysteries of gout are five.</margin> named thus: **Gum**, **Resin**, **Mariyana** <note>A specific alchemical preparation, likely plant-based or a mineral distillate</note>, **Masticatory Oil**, and **Extract of Tereniabin** <note>Persian manna, a sweet substance gathered from plants</note>. These five are superior; in each of them lies the power of resolving all granulated Tartars into a Liquid and "wateriness," which is readily subject to consumption. The preparation of these is such that <margin>What their preparation is like.</margin> they are reduced so strongly into an "elevation" <note>An alchemical process of refining or sublimating a substance to its highest state</note> that after this they can be circulated, and have gone through at least one-seventh of the circulatory cycles. Then at last this composition is granted to you, so that you may compose and join those circulated things, according as the generation of Tartar has appeared and been known to you. With this circulation, anoint the Tartaric limbs and the places of granular Tartar, which the *Roades* call knotty gout. <margin>Granular Tartar yields only to external remedies.</margin> Through this anointing, the granular types of Tartar are resolved, which otherwise cannot be resolved, nor subdued by any other means through medicines, except by those applied from the outside. There is no need to describe the process here of how that anointing should be done. For the method is known to everyone; at least let this be done diligently, so that the grains are resolved and consumed. For just as the Sun or wind dries out water and dissipates it so that nothing remains: so the same thing happens here from these simple secrets. For in them are hidden mysteries that have the power to dissolve gouty tartar, just as the Sun has the power to melt snow. For the coagulation of Gouty Tartar and the <margin>The coagulation of Tartar and ice are the same.</margin> coagulation of water is a uniform hardening, differing in this one thing: that the coagulation of Tartar is caused by heat, while the other [ice] is caused by cold.

It is fitting, therefore, that the **mysteries** <note>In this context, "mysteries" refers to alchemical secrets or "arcana"—remedies that work through hidden spiritual or chemical properties</note> be established in such a way that they resolve through heat what has been coagulated. For the matter is consumed by these secrets and reduced to a liquid which penetrates the body, by which it is eventually consumed so that it no longer appears or is seen anywhere again.

### CHAPTER XX.
### On the Stone of the Bladder and Kidneys.

<margin>The Doctor's duty in preventing the stone.</margin>
To deliver a cure for this affliction—namely, the stone of the bladder and kidneys—is a difficult task and one of great labor. However, whatever I have drawn and learned from the very light of Nature or from experience itself as my teacher, I shall explain here. I would have all physicians warned to communicate a faithful and complete preservation to the inhabitants of the regions over which they are placed, lest by some immense negligence that **Tartar** <note>Paracelsus used "Tartar" to describe stony, calcified deposits in the body, comparing them to the crust left by wine in a barrel</note>, so pernicious and deadly a thing, be produced and grow within a person. For in this chapter, we shall diligently explain in what way <margin>The stone of the kidneys and bladder is a hostile tyrant.</margin> this so-cruel tyrant may be avoided and conquered. I do not deny that the cause of stones and the Tartaric tyrant in man arises even from good food and drink. But there are also other principles of the same, such as a natural inclination and disposition that cause this generation. Whatever the case may be, the Physician ought to know and understand the Nature and condition of the Tartar of his own region, so that he may learn and establish from it both the preventative and expulsive remedies for Tartar, by which it may be expelled daily and not break out into action or be led into its ultimate matter. For this is the duty of brotherhood and Christianity, by which the health of one's neighbor is promoted. It is only just that you give to another the same measure you wish to be given to yourself. If, however, matters have already reached the point where this stone or Tartar has turned **Marbly** or **Flinty**, <margin>What kind of cure for the stone.</margin> it is necessary to hold to this process. A system and order of baths, food, and drink must be maintained as we have prescribed. In this way, one proceeds more cautiously, and if any part of the stone has adhered, it will come away more easily. But so that the stone itself may be attacked and fought, you should know that **Earth-gall** <note>original: "Fel terrae"; likely referring to the herb Lesser Centaury, used here for its perceived ability to break down stones</note>, which <margin>Earth-gall, the mystery of the stone.</margin> signifies the stone, removes it in its own time, though not by a swift cure. Its recipe is as follows:

> ℞ *Oil of Earth-gall althalizai corrected, 2 oz.* <note>Althalizai is a Paracelsian term for a specific alchemical preparation of a plant's "gall" or bitter essence</note>
> *Liquor of Lynx, sponge, Jews' stone, and crabs, 2 oz each.* <note>Liquor of Lynx (Lapis Lyncis) was thought to be fossilized amber or belemnite; Jews' stone (Lapis Iudaicus) is a fossilized sea urchin spine historically used for urinary stones</note>

Mix these and circulate them <note>An alchemical process of continuous distillation or heating in a closed vessel</note> for a month. Provide this for drinking—the more, the better. Collect the urine and freeze or coagulate the sediment into a single mass. Thus you will find the stone and all its quantity or bulk. Rest satisfied in this recipe. For I know of no better one. <margin>The cure for the stone with ulceration.</margin> For the discovery of anything more excellent belongs to experience and divine blessing. He gives His gifts to whom He wills. Nor does God pour out all His gifts in a single day.

Furthermore, some stones sometimes occur with other evils, such as **ulceration**. You shall treat these through oil of Antimony and **Apodeldoch** <note>A complex medical plaster or ointment popularized by Paracelsus for healing wounds and ulcers</note> externally, as well as through Balsam of Hypericum <note>St. John's Wort</note>, which I have described in my *Surgery*. <margin>Apodeldoch as a remedy for the stone with ulceration.</margin> Likewise, use the Balsam of Tartar *Acatiati*; all of which you will use with the most happy success and outcome. Furthermore, you shall take care to preserve the patient afterward in the manner I defined at the beginning of the chapter, lest another stone be reborn in the future and the later pain become more savage than the former. For the gravest evils do not weigh down at the beginning, but eventually, death terminates them. But other arts also remain, such as **sections** <note>original: "sectiones"; refers to lithotomy, the surgical cutting to remove stones</note>. <margin>Cutting for the stone of the bladder.</margin> If these turn out well, who will blame them? Yet a great part of those who <margin>The recklessness of some in cutting for the stone.</margin> handle these matters are sailing for their own private profit; they rarely cut unless they have first taken half the payment. However the cutting succeeds, half the money—or all of it—is already stowed away by them. This is a great indignity in those impostors. For when they see that everything is permitted to everyone with impunity, they all rush to cut indiscriminately, however the dice may fall. If the art does not benefit the sick, it benefits the purse. They hold this to be the sum total of their profession. Such men are mostly bath-keepers, barbers, surgeons, and others like <margin>Medicine, a den of thieves. A rebuke of doctors.</margin> them. Thus, Medicine becomes a **den of thieves**. Indeed, even the Doctors themselves are not so skilled or industrious as to deeply know the matter and the evil itself, although through the signs described by me—which they ought to attend to closely—they might have the time and sufficient instruments for diagnosing these affections. They could easily judge urine in our manner, and not by their own speculations. Yet, having despised all these things, it is enough for them...

<margin>
The nature of modern Medicine.

Therefore, one might most truly say that Medicine today is nothing but imposture, nothing but trifles, nothing but fantasy; since no works are produced by anyone that might withstand a proper trial, or by which the art might be established. And he who considers these things seriously and intimately easily sees with how many impostures and vanities all things are defiled and corrupted. But blessed is he who knows how to select the good from the depraved. Blessed is he who sits in the place of *Sarepta* <note>original: *Sareptæ*. Away with this law or license, that Physicians should owe an answer to no one for a homicide committed! This impunity has already turned every stable-boy into a Physician. Away, too, with this custom: namely, that money is counted out for an art that killed the patient.

## CHAPTER XXI.

### On the stone of the bladder, generated spontaneously by nature from the moisture of the salt of the blood <note>original: *cruoris*, referring to gore or clotted blood</note> or the urine of the blood.

<margin>
Man is preserved by a liquor.
</margin>

<margin>
A Balsam sustains him.
</margin>

<margin>
The subject of the human Balsam is salt.
</margin>

<margin>
The Balsam of the earth.
</margin>

<margin>
The nature of the cure for bladder stones.
</margin>

Now, furthermore, pay attention to the internal **Tartar** <note>Paracelsus’s term for stony deposits or calcifications within the body, named after the hard crust found in wine barrels</note>, which is not generated from external causes or external Tartar: it arises and emerges from the very body in which it lies. Now, it is right that for the sake of the cure, its generation be briefly recounted, so that it may be understood more certainly and easily. 

<margin>
The natural liquor of the body is like the liquor of the earth.
</margin>

It happens in this way: a certain natural liquor is hidden in the body, which imparts its own moisture to the entire body, without which moisture the body cannot live. Let us provide an example. The earth also has this kind of moisture in itself, by which it is sustained and quickened to bring forth fruits, which it otherwise would not bring forth at all. Now, the earth takes this moisture from the water that permeates the earth itself and pervades all its pores on one side; and further also from celestial <term>impressions</term> <note>A Paracelsian term for the influences of the stars and atmosphere on the physical world</note> through rain, dew, etc. 

<margin>
The earth is made fertile by water.
</margin>

By these, the earth is moistened on the outside—that is, on the surface—and the Element of water moistens it below the surface. By these liquors, therefore, the earth is preserved in its essence and vigor, so that it is fit for bearing and begetting fruit. A similar moistening exists in man himself: so much so that his "earth"—that is, flesh and blood, bones and veins—would have no power or ability without that moisture. Therefore, the Element of water is within man, by which he is moistened. To this is added the "meteoric impression," which moistens his surface. 

With these things understood, know that since man exists as flesh and blood, he also has need of a certain peculiar **Balsam** <note>A "Balsam" in this context is an internal preservative force that prevents decay and keeps the body’s "liquors" flowing</note>, by which he is preserved and sustained. This Balsam is placed in the body of salt. Thus man is preserved by salt, as if by a Balsam. Note an example of this: by a similar reason, the earth itself has its Balsam from salt, from which it is preserved. If that salt emits its own excrement, saltpeter emerges from it, and so on. So also in man: if the Balsam gives off its excrement and its "spit-up" waste, then unless the expulsive power is present to cast it out, the "spirit of coagulation" arrives and hardens it into a Tartaric stone. These stones are the hardest of all and excite the most savage pains. 

Therefore, as I have recounted, the cure must be established by this method and order, not by focusing on Tartar as it has been described until now. For this Tartar is unique in Medicine, and its origin is also unique. Therefore, it is also different in the essence and condition of its Medicine. 

<margin>
Where the disease comes from, there comes the cure.
</margin>

And to descend closer to the cure: it must proceed from that from which the disease itself came forth—namely, from the body from which the stone itself was generated. And although I speak here specifically only of the stone of the bladder, I also speak at the same time of all places where Tartar adheres. For just as "foreign" Tartar (from food) seeks its own locations, so similarly the Tartar of the blood <note>original: *cruoris*</note> seeks the same. In this way, the excrement of natural Tartar goes down to the bladder; it descends and is distilled, and gathers in one channel that leads to the bladder. Just as many rains fall from above and flow into one stream and depart with it, the same happens in the body. 

Regarding the cure, you should know that, as we have said, the Medicine arises from that same soil from which the stone itself is born: 

<margin>
The blood is the mystery of the bladder stone.
</margin>

that is, the mystery of the <term>arcanum</term> <note>An *arcanum* is a "secret" or essential remedy that works on the vital spirit of the body to dissolve a disease at its root</note> is located in the blood <note>original: *cruor*</note>, by which this stone is dissolved and reduced to its "first matter." 

<margin>
How the blood is to be prepared.
</margin>

The blood must be immediately coagulated in a glass vial by boiling water. Afterward, it must be excellently calcined in its own manner, and extracted with its own liquid, and made volatile, so that nothing of it that might ascend remains...

<margin>
The syringe, a medical instrument.
</margin>
...let the remainder stay. To this liquid, add half the quantity of the liquid of "hard ice" <note>likely a highly purified or chemically altered water, possibly an acid</note>, and administer it through a syringe. For it is refined to such a degree that it cannot penetrate through drinks, but instead evaporates and ascends rather than descending. Indeed, it is best and most appropriate that you establish a regimen and a bath, as has been described, and furthermore observe the process of "foreign" Tartar <note>Tartar introduced via food or drink</note> in the bladder and kidneys. But that which is injected via the syringe must by no means be neglected. For this is the primary secret <note>original: *arcanum primarium*</note> regarding the Tartaric stone of the native blood <note>original: *cruoris natalis*; referring to stones formed from the body's own vital fluids rather than diet</note>.

<margin>
The second cure of Tartar, namely etc.
</margin>
But furthermore, take note also of another process and order concerning the destruction of every kind of Tartar—whether flint-like, marble-like, etc.—such as are generated in the kidneys and bladder. For whatever substances liquefy gold and dissolve it into a resin <note>Paracelsus used "resin" to describe metals reduced to a thick, oily liquid state</note>, all these same substances also reduce these types of Tartar from their coagulation back into a resinous liquefaction. Even if it seems probable to many that this can only be achieved and obtained through corrosives, I am nevertheless certain that corrosives alone do not reduce gold. For there are certain other simple substances that dissolve gold, which are by no means from the class of corrosives. <margin>Gold is dissolved even without corrosives.</margin> Of this rank is *Manna* extracted from flowers. If this is put into circulation <note>a process of prolonged heating in a sealed vessel</note>, it reduces gold. In the same way, it reduces any tartar, of whatever kind it may be, if it is administered by a syringe. <margin>Circulated, extracted Manna reduces gold.</margin> The whole crux <note>original: *rhombus*; literally "the diamond" or "the turning wheel," here meaning the core of the problem</note> lies in this: that the medicine finds, reaches, and grasps the Tartar. Furthermore, there are also "ashy essences of wine" <note>original: *essentiæ vini Cineratæ*; wine spirits rectified over alkaline ashes</note>, which themselves also dissolve gold into a white oil. And although some of it may be reduced again, not all of it is; yet that solution is sufficient, and it does not coagulate again within the human body. <margin>Ashy essences of wine dissolve gold and Tartar.</margin> Therefore, one must act in a timely manner with the expulsive power, so that it expels the stone while it still remains in a liquid resolution. If indeed any of it coagulates outside the person and is reduced back into its ultimate matter, it matters little. Thus, the cures for Tartar have now been sufficiently handed down and understood, provided the physician is intelligent and skilled, and not merely a scribe of recipes who, by his usual artifice—"Let a drink be made" <note>original: *Fiat Potus*</note>—performs deceptions. There is need for an entirely different foundation and skill than merely writing "Take" <note>original: *Recipe*</note> and "Let it be boiled according to usage."

### CHAPTER XXII.

->A fuller declaration and instruction on the preparation<-
->and administration of those things which are<-
->contained in this little book.<-

<margin>
A critique of the physicians of this century.
</margin>
It would indeed be very easy and simple for us to write and teach, if those were at hand who might read and understand the same. For if you busy yourself with debating the true foundation of medicine with the physicians of this century, you would do much the same as if you were to teach someone to make shoes who knows neither the thread, nor the last <note>the wooden model of a foot used by cobblers</note>, nor even what ink is. Who would debate the art with such a person, who has not even tasted the first principles? So if I say, "Take this, do that," they are then ignorant of what this or that might be that they ought to do. Does this constitute skill and understanding: for the craftsman himself to be ignorant of the tools of his art? Certainly, the matter is no different than if someone should sell himself as a money-changer and yet be unskilled in coinage, or if someone who deals in the trading and selling of horses should not know horses. <margin>It is shameful for a craftsman to be ignorant of his tools.</margin> Yet they are often accustomed to chime in with this: "Write so that you may be understood." Rather, let the disciples themselves learn, so that they may understand! Which of these, I ask, am I writing: the principles themselves, the elements, the foundations? Or those things that follow from them? I speak and write to those who have already attained the principles themselves, not to beginners <note>original: *tyronibus*</note>. If, therefore, they are ignorant of the first apprenticeships <note>original: *tyrocinia*</note>, what can you accomplish with them by explaining the art? To be a Bachelor and understand nothing; to be called a Master and know nothing; to boast of being a Doctor and only have opinions—that is indeed too base and empty. I ask you whether your universal books contain the foundation of medicine or not? If they contain everything, there is no longer any need to learn from the unrefined. If not, it will certainly be necessary for you to learn and hold many more things than how to approach visiting the sick on asses or camels or horses and dromedaries. If all of medicine were contained in your books, the sick would spread no complaints about you.

<margin>
Tartar is twofold: foreign and of the blood.
</margin>
In this book, I have proposed to explain only Tartar, which I have completed with a twofold teaching. The first was concerning "foreign Tartar," as the more common type. The second was concerning "the Tartar of the blood." Although my theory may seem new and foreign, the very writing and context speak clearly upon what foundation, what experience, and what weights of truth I establish and demonstrate my views, according to which I submit both my things and yours to be judged by you.

# ON DISEASES

Nor do I think anyone will be so unskilled and ignorant that they do not understand these matters. For my **Theory** <term>Theorica: the underlying philosophical or scientific principles of a craft</term> is so plain and clear that it could be understood even by a mute person. To this, I have attached the cures, just as the sequence of chapters indicates. Indeed, I am grieved by the lack of learning in you who read these things yet do not understand them, even though they pertain directly to your art. A man should act in a single manner, consistent with his religion and his profession. Truly, how shameful would it be for a **Theologian** if he had not read the **Evangelists**, or was ignorant of whom **David** spoke? What a disgrace it would be for a **Jurist** <note>legal scholar or lawyer</note> if he did not know the power, the will, and the laws of the **Emperor**? What a shame it is for a **Christian** man, who devotes himself to Christianity, yet is ignorant of the **Articles of Faith**? All such men are worthless, fit for nothing. Truly, how can a bird fly if it is deprived of its wings and feathers? How can one be called a **Doctor** who is not equipped with the "wings" by which he might take flight? Even Holy Scripture itself professes: *Faith without works is dead.* <note>original: "Fidem sine operibus mortuā esse"; a reference to James 2:26</note> Is not a name also dead without works? Is a Physician not dead without **Medicine**? Is a master not dead without his art?

<margin>Two things are perpetual in all matters.</margin>
God’s providence has seen to it that two things are perpetually joined and cling together: namely, **Faith** and **works**, the **Teacher** and **doctrine**, the **Physician** and **Medicine**, the **master** and **mastery**. For none of these can subsist by itself without the other, but both perpetually follow and cling to one another. Whence it is also rightly cried out: *Woe to him who is alone. If he falls, who shall lift him up?* <note>original: "Væ illi, qui solus est. Is si ceciderit, quis ipsum eriget?"; a reference to Ecclesiastes 4:10</note> The same applies here: *For woe to the Apostle who performs no signs. Woe to the Physician who lacks Medicine. Woe to the fighter who has no sword. Woe to the Christian who is destitute of works.* Since, therefore, it is the will of God Himself that nothing acts in solitude, but two are perpetually joined: let everyone strive diligently so that he is not found alone. For he who is alone when he falls, remains lying there. And I propose these things to you for this purpose: that you may not remain "singular" in your isolation. For two things make a matter whole, not one; it is double, not simple. In this way, it will happen that we can speak with one another—that is, to read and understand with a genuine sense. I cannot declare this book to you more plainly than by first building the rudiments, principles, and first elements of your religion, profession, and faculty.

<margin>Ignorance of principles is wretched.</margin>
For he who is ignorant of the principles: what can he know of the end, or of those things which follow the principles?

<margin>A certain Galenist’s warning to Theophrastus.</margin>
A certain "Butcher-Doctor" <note>original: "Carnifex Doctor"; a derogatory term for a surgeon or physician who lacks skill or relies on old-fashioned, painful methods</note> sent me a brief and friendly (so he dreams) warning by letter. In it, he explains how reverently and honorably Medicine has been held and cultivated for so many centuries; therefore, he says, it is only fair that I do not translate <note>or "hand down/expose"</note> it so reproachfully, or rashly attack so many outstanding Doctors who have long excelled in art and honors. I, however, remember a certain consul in this or that city who was of the greatest dignity and esteem, and was eagerly showered with the highest honors by everyone—yet who was finally driven to the cross. The same outcome has awaited other leaders. If, therefore, nothing rests in "excelling," but rather in acting honestly: why, I ask, should he not be rebuked who acts out of boastfulness? There is almost no ignorance that is not eventually overturned and exposed. And it would have been more fitting if that "smith" <note>original: "fabrum"; another pejorative for a clumsy or mechanical physician</note> had written to me about *Being* <note>how things actually are</note>, not about *Being Held* <note>how things are perceived or rumored to be</note>. Furthermore, another wrote to me that this smith has good Latin and elegant Greek. But he omitted what was most necessary: namely, that he is a good Physician. Let him be an **Ordinary** <note>original: "Ordinarius"; referring to the "Ordinary" university lectures based on traditional texts like Galen or Avicenna</note> if he likes. Meanwhile, as long as he can be an "Ordinary" on the inside or the outside, blue or green, his letter will remain a dead thing to me until I learn something more certain. I repeat this here so that it may be known from now on: Medicine is not to be taught or learned in the way it has been done until now—not "ordinarily," but **athletically** <note>original: "athleticè"; Paracelsus uses this to mean medicine as a rigorous, practical, and combative struggle with nature, rather than passive classroom study</note>. For here a conflict is waged. Let everyone learn and hold this: the work and the name must be entirely joined and cling together; the whole is by no means divided. And that is enough concerning **Tartar** <term>Tartarus: Paracelsus’s term for metabolic waste that hardens into stones/deposits, similar to the tartar in wine casks</term> for now.

# CONCLUSION

> *And so at last, most Merciful, Gracious, and beloved Lords and friends, those works are finished which I wished to dedicate to you, having compiled them with the greatest diligence and a good and honest spirit: praying with most submissive reverence and entreating that you might deign to receive them with a kind and calm countenance, and to publish them in print for the sake of Christian charity. For unless their publication is procured through your Highnesses and Graces, they will never see the light of day because of the machinations of the **Galenists** <note>followers of the ancient Greek physician Galen, whose teachings Paracelsus sought to overthrow</note>. Firstly, because they know that in this way, their ignorance will be detected.*

*Second, they fear that their profit and kitchen income will henceforth be diminished. Third, because they cannot bear that medicine is becoming known everywhere, even among the common folk, lest anything be taken away from their own private hunting ground in this way. Yet they do not consider that there will nonetheless be certain Medical Doctors, even if every fifth person were to become a Physician. With these things, I most submissively commend and offer myself to you.*

# TO THE NOBLE, MOST FAMOUS
## AND CELEBRATED LORD AUREOLUS
### THEOPHRASTUS HOHENHEIM, DOCTOR OF BOTH MEDICINES,
#### To our singular friend and Lord.

*Noble, Most Famous Lord and beloved friend: let our service and singular favor first be dedicated to you. We have received and read your three books—one on Tartaric diseases <note>diseases involving stones or metabolic deposits</note>, another containing certain responses and defenses, and a third, the Labyrinth—collected by you into one volume and dedicated to this praised province of the Archduchy of Carinthia, in whose particular honor you wrote them; and we have learned the contents within them in long order. Therefore, for that labor and industry of yours, by which many most grave diseases may henceforth be prevented and perfect health recovered (by the help of divine grace), we humanely and zealously give you thanks, especially for that friendly dedication made and exhibited to the said praised province. We have an undoubting hope that this praised province will acknowledge this labor of yours with the affection that is fitting. We ourselves shall also zealously strive for the same. In the meantime, we offer you all the duties of humanity and friendship, intending to labor zealously so that these writings of yours may see the light, printed at the first possible opportunity. This we wished to signify to you by these presents, out of our inclined and friendly affection. Given in Klagenfurt <note>original: "Foro Claudij"</note>, September 2nd, in the year 1538.*

N. N.

->The Nobles of the Archduchy of Carinthia, as many as were present at today’s court assembly.<-

->*The letters were signed with 14 seals.*<-

# FRAGMENTS TO BE APPENDED TO
## THE SECOND VOLUME OF THE MEDICAL WORKS OF THEOPHRASTUS.

### FRAGMENT OF THE "PARAGRANUM" OF THEOPHRASTUS PARACELSUS.

#### The Book of the Four Pillars of Medicine.

->PREFACE.<-

<margin>What Philosophy is and what it teaches.</margin>

That I am a Philosopher, even outside of your "Lyre" <note>meaning outside the standard academic curriculum or "tune"</note>, is indeed right, just, and true. For in this Philosophy consists the knowledge of the whole globule <note>the "globuli" refers to the sphere of the world or the human microcosm</note>, and that through practice. For Philosophy is nothing other than the practice of the globule or sphere. But where is your practice? It remains with Aristotle and Socrates.

<meta>This page continues the philosophical foundation of Paracelsus’s medical theory. It connects to the previous discourse by defining the true Physician not as a degree-holder from traditional universities, but as one who understands the deep, hidden structures of nature (Philosophy), the celestial influences (Astronomy), and the correct preparation of remedies (Alchemy).</meta>

<header>MEDICAL FRAGMENTS</header>

<margin>
The Philosopher is twofold, yet one. Man is twofold, yet belongs to one Philosophy.
</margin>
Philosophy teaches the virtues and properties of the things of earth and water; it demonstrates that which no man has ever seen: namely, earth and water in their true Element. And you say that the elements are known to you, though you do not even know their beginning. How foolish you will be in the end, when you are so ignorant in the first things! Regarding Philosophy, I tell you this: just as the Philosopher is in the earth, so too he is in man. For there is one Philosopher of the earth and another of the water; yet both together are one Philosopher. Similarly, there are also two men <note>Referring to the "outer man" of the flesh and the "inner man" or "essential man."</note>, yet both possess only one Philosophy. And so, the Physician is not yet present, but only that part of Philosophy required for the Physician. Even if you are a practical Philosopher, you are not yet a Physician. <margin>An experimenter is not a Physician.</margin> For every experimenter is a practical philosopher, but not yet a Physician.

<margin>
How Philosophers and Astronomers differ.
</margin>
The same applies to Astronomy. The heavens have their Philosopher; the air has its own as well. These are called Astronomers. Those who deal with earth and water are called Philosophers; yet it is one and the same thing: the Astronomer of the Earth and the Philosopher of the Firmament. Just as there are two Astronomers here who know the properties and virtues of the stars, as well as the Manna of the Air: so also are there two Physicians in man—one who considers his firmament <note>the internal "stars" or governing forces</note>, the other who considers his chaos <note>the atmospheric space or unformed matter within the body</note>. Yet these are not Physicians, but Philosophers and Astronomers of the <term>Microcosm: the human being viewed as a "little world" that perfectly mirrors the vast universe or Macrocosm</term>. Just as they exist in the external elements, so they exist in the internal. Thus there is an Astronomer of the Firmament and a Physical Astronomer, and there is one Astronomy and one Philosophy. The Physician is not yet there; however, the seed from which he grows is present. But you robed and ring-wearing Physicians, from where were you born? From the farts of donkeys and the droppings <note>original: "ficubus," literally "figs," a common euphemism for manure</note> of horses.

<margin>
How the Physician is made from his seed.
</margin>
<margin>
What Alchemy drives at.
</margin>
How does the Physician emerge from that seed? In this way: if the seed—that is, the matter—is present, it must be prepared. But it is prepared by no one except by Alchemy. This is not the art that merely teaches the cooking and preparation that nature established for man's convenience. For example, in St. John's Wort <note>Latin: hypericum</note>, it knows many virtues. As often as there is a different virtue, so too must there be a different preparation. Alchemy itself commands this, as if to say: "For this disease, prepare it this way; for that one, prepare it so." Now, therefore, the Physician arises and shines in Medicine. For he knows the foundation and what cooking and preparation are necessary. <margin>Of the representative Physician.</margin> Why do you shine, you people of Montpellier? You of Leipzig? You of Vienna? <note>These were the great university centers of traditional medicine, which Paracelsus frequently attacked for being too theoretical.</note>

Here, here you will be forced to turn, to learn truly what Philosophy is, what Alchemy is, what preparations nature institutes, and how she instructs her Alchemists. Where do you stand now, you apothecaries and filthy boilers? It is a disgrace and a shame that your practice is nothing but pure fantasy and wickedness, contrary to the whole art of Medicine. Good God! If it finally becomes publicly known what butcheries are hidden in your gilded boxes and solemn decoctions, will there be any limit to your disgrace? Yet the matter must be brought into the light. And even if you were to put twice as many scorpions in my food, that poison will still work within yourselves, not in me; your crafty and lying counsels will overwhelm you and break your own necks, not mine.

From your first published writing until this present moment, not a single one of you has known what a Physician is. But you have all known very well what a Sophist is. And what you know, you try to evade. What you are not, you claim for yourselves. You are not Physicians; you are Sophists. For you yourselves know and testify that you do not treat even a hundred patients except through ignorance, hoping for a good outcome. Thus it is clear to you that all your doctrine, art, doctorate, and books cannot grant you enough skill to give even the slightest judgment with a foundation of truth from a urine sample <note>original: "ex lotio." Uroscopy—diagnosing by looking at urine—was the standard practice of the time, which Paracelsus felt was often used as guesswork.</note>. If you cannot do this and yet you judge, then you are certainly practicing sophistry. See what kind of "kitchen profit" <note>an idiom for income used only to fill one's belly</note> you increase for your teachers with such "honor." Certainly it is no more just or honest than the way harlots pile up the profits of madams. Truly, he is a Physician who has the abundance of aid to bring, and knows how to expel diseases by force—I say nothing of killing. For just as a tree is certainly and undoubtedly felled when an axe is applied, so too a certain Medicine acts upon the sick. If I cannot do that, then say boldly that I am no more skilled a Physician than you. For Medicine is so constituted that it drives out disease not by doubting, but by pressing on with force. God created nothing imperfect or doubtful, as your art is. He is a Physician, thus
