## ON THE POWERS OF THE ORGANS
### BOOK THE FIRST.
#### *On the powers of Spiritual things.*
#### CHAPTER I.
#### ON THE SPIRIT OF LIFE.

<margin>What the spirit of life is and where it is found.</margin>
**T**HE SPIRIT of life is a spirit placed in all the organs of the body, however they may be named separately. In each and every one of these, this *one* spirit dwells, and the power of them all is collectively one.

<margin>The spirit is one in power and kind, but varied by its location.</margin>
It is the highest and most noble seed from which all the organs live. But as it is extended and spread abroad, it exists in different ways according to its various seats. For it is driven by the heart so that it takes on *cardiac* powers, which it does not do in the other organs. Similarly, in the liver, it adopts *hepatic* virtues, which it does not do in other parts. The same likewise happens in the marrow. Even if these powers are either perceptible or imperceptible, the powers of all the organs exist uniformly; they should not be understood otherwise than that the *Cardiac* powers are at least in some way different from the *Bone-related* <note>original: "Ossalibus"; referring to the skeletal system.</note> ones. And yet the powers are one. For the powers that sustain and preserve the bones are no less weak than those which nourish and strengthen the heart. For just as much importance is placed in the bones as in the heart. So, in turn, the powers of the spirit of life in the brain are of no more value than those in the marrow—although from use and necessity, the contrary might rather seem true. And yet the marrow has the same necessity as the brain, and the powers of both 

<margin>The spirit of life is not divided according to the diversity of the parts.</margin>
are similar. The same principle applies to all the other organs. Although some of these may seem worthier than others, nevertheless a single spirit of life remains the governor, virtue, force, and operation of them all.

#### CHAPTER II.

<margin>* The external origin of the spirit of life is simple.</margin>
**T**HE SPIRIT of life has its origin from external causes or generations, not from natural ones according to the flesh. For just as the Generation of other things is twofold, so the generation of the spirit is simple, which is united with the body and its organs, as we have said. This is also the reason why it cannot be strengthened according to its own powers unless the organs themselves are strong and robust. For the stronger, more powerful, and more eager an organ is by nature, the more robustly and vigorously the spirit shines forth from it. Therefore, we should by no means strive to preserve, strengthen, and increase the spirit of life itself, except by this: that we preserve and strengthen the organs—which have arisen from nature—in their primeval integrity and original health. Once that is provided for, the spirit becomes increased and stronger of its own accord. There is one thing, however, that pertains only to the spirit: namely, that it moves in open passages and is cleared of blockages. Regarding this blockage <term>oppilation</term> <note>original: "oppilatione"; a traditional medical term for an obstruction or clogging of the body's internal pathways.</note>, should it ever occur, we shall append a specific small treatise here. Afterward, we shall attach two small books on the organs governing themselves, as will follow in order.

<margin>The health of the organ is the strength of the spirit.</margin>

# ON THE POWERS OF THE ORGANS

<margin>
How the spirit is affected, and in what way by obstruction.
</margin>
...furthermore. It must be known, therefore, that the spirit of life can be so obstructed <note>original: "oppilari"; a common medical term in this era for a blockage or "oppilation" of the body's internal passages.</note> that unless the paths and pores of its passages are opened, it can be suffocated. For the "second generation" <note>In Paracelsian alchemy, the "second generation" refers to the subtle, spiritualized form that matter takes within a living body.</note> is nothing but vapor, and the spirit of life lives within us in the form of a vapor, according to the nature of this second generation, though produced outside of nature. For this reason, from the very beginning, the pores must be opened in the *marrow*, in the *flesh*, in the *veins*, in the *principal organs*, in the *bones*, in the *ligaments*, in the *nerves*, in the *joints*, in the *bladder*, in the *diaphragm*, in the *womb*, and in *all organs*, without exception. For the spirit is situated in the brain just as it is in the flesh, and it pervades the brain through and through; it penetrates both the *pia mater* and the *dura mater* <note>The inner and outer membranes surrounding the brain.</note>, and permeates the heart and its capsule, as well as the gallbladder, the regions of the kidneys, and the center of the bladder; thus, it occupies both what is empty and what is full.

## CHAPTER III.

<margin>
The pathologies that follow the obstruction of the spirit.
</margin>
**W**herever the spirit of life cannot penetrate, a disease is stirred up. For when the spirit itself is obstructed, putrefaction arises, which degenerates into ulceration. For in that place, the spirit dies. That which is dead putrefies and creates an ulcer, according to the nature of the organ in which it is placed. For an ulcer created in the principal organs brings about death. From these obstructions of the spirit of life arise *Fevers*, *Abscesses*, *Pleurisy*, *Jaundice*, *ulcers*, and whatever attacks with a febrile paroxysm <note>A sudden attack or increase in the intensity of symptoms.</note>, such as the plague and similar ailments. The cause is this: the spirit, sensing its own suffocation and death, first shakes the entire body with horror <note>original: "horrore"; referring to the shivering or chills that precede a fever.</note>, while it is, as it were, congealed. Afterward, heat and inflammation grow strong if the spirit is released. I exclude here those fevers which experience paroxysms more than once, such as quotidian, tertian, and quartan fevers <note>Fevers that recur every day, every three days, or every four days.</note>. Thus, if the spirit paroxysms (if I may put it this way) in the brain, it excites phrenitis <note>Delirium or brain inflammation.</note>, Mania, and the like. If in the heart, it induces St. Vitus’s Dance <note>original: "Choream S. Viti"; a disorder characterized by rapid, uncoordinated jerking movements.</note>. For it touches the "veins of joy"; and it often happens that it paroxysms according to the time, the hour, and the year. Canonical practice indicates for what reasons these things happen, namely regarding Fevers and the plague. The spirit of life is subject to celestial influence, just as the body is subject to the earth. For just as the body eats of the earth—and what it eats, it is itself, sustaining its life from the earth—so also the spirit of life eats of the higher influence and is nourished by the Element of Fire, in which the four Elements shine forth. For just as the earth shines forth in the four

How St. Vitus's Dance occurs.
</margin>

<margin>
The spirit of life is nourished by celestial influence.

The spirit of life is preserved by two things.
</margin>
Elements according to its fruits: so here also the influences shine forth. Therefore, two practices must be set forward: First, that the influence be preserved as much as is pleasing and suitable to the spirit. Second, that the body be kept comfortable and fit for the spirit. Following this, the health of the body follows by one path, as far as the spirit is concerned.

## CHAPTER IV.
### On the influence of the spirit of life.

<margin>
Astronomers and Geometers are cited.
</margin>
**F**rom the stars and all the influences of the entire sky, as far as the firmament extends, the power of the spirit of life is stretched out, like an invisible celestial vapor with which it is united, just as cold and heat unite if they constitute a temperate state. But if by chance the "stars of the organs" should wander, corrupt, and paroxysm, then the organ of the body is also broken, and it obstructs the spirit of life, or in that place vitiates and corrupts it. No other remedy can be applied to this evil than to withdraw from that influence and go under another. For the opinion of Astronomers concerning Birth-charts and Ascendants is false and wicked. For example, I was born under Scorpio; but if I submit myself to Aries, I become its offspring, and Scorpio no longer has any dealings with me. Therefore, that ascendant is no longer mine for any longer than I subject myself to it, as I have taught concerning Birth-charts. Thus, one's location must be changed according to the nature of the firmament, and no other ascendant or conjunction should be entered into afterward. Thus, if I had been born under such an alignment that I was destined to be hanged, and that kind of spirit of the firmament were in me (as we know is taught concerning human spirits): if I wished to hinder and break this efficacy, I would let go of that planet and go under another; thus its power is broken. And although that disposition and kind remains with me, the effect does not follow. On the contrary, an honest and noble man often becomes a thief under a bad influence, as is written concerning spirits in the book *On the External Senses of Men*.

<margin>
A change of place changes the influence.
</margin>

## CHAPTER V.
### On obstructions in general.

**T**o clear the obstructions <note>original: "deoppilandum"; to unblock.</note> of the spirit of life in general, it is necessary that the spirit be kept in heat, so that it may be strong and vigorous within itself. The process for this is that it becomes diaphoretic <note>Sweat-inducing.</note>, burns continually in its essence, and lives in full heat. This is managed by this recipe: Take *Saffron, Ginger, and Theriac <note>A famous ancient herbal compound used as a universal antidote.</note>, etc.* Extract the essence of these, etc.

# BOOK TWO.
## On the powers of the internal organs.
### CHAPTER I.
### On the powers of the HEART.

<margin>The sovereignty of the heart.</margin>
**T**he heart demands nothing else except its own strengthening, provided that whatever is adverse and contrary to it is removed. For by itself, the heart is too weak to be able to struggle against and resist all the evils that insult it daily. Therefore, help must be brought to it through administered remedies. For that organ is the primary one, given to man and inserted into his body for this purpose: to keep the body in its stability and vigor. However, if some harm or dissolution of substance occupies a specific organ, the heart was by no means born or ordained to turn that away on its own; rather, that evil must be corrected and removed by the help of Medicine, which is why Medicine itself is seen as a "second heart." For any Physician, a more powerful and diligent care is incumbent upon registering the external heart rather than the internal. For the internal heart is not subject to the Physician, but only the external <note>In Paracelsian thought, the "external heart" refers to the specific medicines and alchemical preparations that correspond to and support the physical organ.</note>. Therefore, if the internal heart should ever have need of the external, it is absolutely necessary that it be applied and conferred to it, as will now be described. Furthermore, a heart medicine should not be taken merely as a simple substance, but rather as a complex one. For it is right for one part to strengthen the Elementary powers, another to inhibit its own putrefaction, and another to turn away other external accidents. Therefore, various powers must be gathered into one in the medicine.

<margin>Medicine as the second or external heart.</margin>
<margin>Heart medicine is made complex.</margin>

> *Recipe <note>original: "R." - the standard medical abbreviation for "take".</note> here: Note the description of potable gold, the matter of pearls, the essence of Saffron, the essence of Lemon Balm, the essence of Celandine, the essence of Mace, etc.*

### CHAPTER II.

<margin>Potable gold is the highest secret of the heart.</margin>
<margin>Description of the golden secret.</margin>
**T**he highest Secret <note>original: "Arcanum"; a term used by Paracelsus to describe a hidden, powerful medicinal virtue or "star" within a substance.</note> for comforting the heart so that it can be harmed by no incident injury, nor its substance crushed, is Potable Gold <note>original: "Aurum potabile"; a legendary alchemical remedy consisting of gold refined into a liquid, drinkable state.</note>, or the Liquor of Gold, and the matter of pearls in the form of an oil, like a balsam. Next is the Essence of Saffron, Mace, and Corals. The description of the gold is such: let the gold be calcined <note>Reduced to a powder through heat.</note> into its own yellowness through the "royal cement" of Hell and Malch <note>These are Paracelsian alchemical terms for specific salts or corrosive agents used in the refining process.</note>. Then let it be separated from its impurity; afterward, let it be mixed with "circulated water" and digested for 24 hours in a moderate fire; then an oil will flow forth which will float upon the water. Collect that, and administer it with "water of life" <note>original: "aqua vitæ"; high-proof distilled alcohol.</note>. None is more excellent than this. You shall proceed similarly with pearls, doing only this: add the "calcination of cheb" <note>A likely shorthand for an alchemical reagent, possibly related to chebula or a specific salt.</note>, and restrain it with distilled vinegar until the corals likewise pass away into a liquor. Take those and resolve them in "burning wine" <note>Alcohol</note> mixed with the "Hell" reagent. If you withdraw the burning wine from the putrefaction, you will have the liquor of coral.

<margin>How the liquor or essence or preparation of Corals is prepared.</margin>
Similarly, for other diseases attacking the heart according to its condition or the elementary humors, the essences of Saffron, Celandine, Mace, Costus <note>original: "Cesti"; an aromatic plant root used in ancient medicine.</note>, and Lemon Balm are suitable. This is the method for preparing them: First, take the best Saffron and cohobate <note><term>cohobation</term>: An alchemical process of repeatedly distilling a liquid off its solid residue to concentrate its power.</note> it in the best water of life, ensuring it does not touch the bottom, using a soft cloth with the Seal of Hermes <note>An airtight, hermetic seal.</note>; you shall do this twelve times, and the saffron will become an oil of the strongest scent. Provide one drop of this in the "wine of life." This medicine is the highest joy of the heart in the elderly, in the infirm, and in those who are melancholic and sad. You shall proceed similarly with Mace, persisting at least 24 times in its cohobation. This essence surpasses saffron in certain powers. Cohobate Celandine, Lemon Balm, and similar herbs in themselves for four days; afterward, separate the pure from the impure by straining. Remove its phlegm <note>The watery, inactive byproduct of distillation.</note>, add "wine of life," and cohobate until it becomes a liquor. Thus you shall work with all herbs intended to preserve the heart and comfort the spirit of life.

<margin>Preparation of essence of Mace. Preparation of essences of Lemon Balm and Celandine.</margin>

### CHAPTER III.
### On the Powers of the Brain.

<margin>There are two brains.</margin>
**J**ust as there are two hearts, so there are also two brains: one external, the other internal. The nature of the internal one is immutable, such that the brain cannot at all purge itself of the fault that is within it. For as it was created, so it remains, and is not changed. But if it should be invaded by certain foreign things—whether that offending matter proceeds from the body or from the spirit of life—that matter must be entirely cast out through the "other brain" which God has placed within herbs. For the organs themselves do not take on a power with which they might fight against the disease to be expelled; rather, they commit the struggle and the removal to the "external brain" while they remain quiet. If the external brain triumphs, the internal recovers. If the former succumbs, the latter feels the loss. Therefore, one must know the external brain against all things that might infest the internal one. Of this kind are the Oil of the Moon <note>Silver was alchemically associated with the Moon (Luna) and thought to treat brain disorders.</note>, Liquor of Sapphire, Musk, and Liquor of Vitriol.

<margin>The organs themselves expel nothing, but medications are the defenses of the Brain.</margin>

### CHAPTER IV.
**T**he brain must be preserved in its own strength, so much so that nothing may inconvenience it...

# ON THE POWERS OF THE ORGANS.

...and let the whole thing be the brain. If at any time a certain weakness falls upon it, then the harm and damages must be averted through an "external brain" <note>In this context, the "external brain" refers to an alchemical remedy that corresponds to the organ's spiritual essence.</note> so that the brain remains whole. Among these brains is the **Liquor of the Moon** <note>original: "Liquor Lunae"; in alchemy, Luna refers to Silver.</note>, which is made in this way: First calcine the silver and cohobate it <note>A process of repeated distillation where the liquid is poured back onto the solid residue.</note> with the **wine of life** <term>vinum vitae: a highly rectified alcohol or brandy used as a solvent</term> for seven days. Thus the Calx of the Moon will be resolved into a viscous liquor. Digest this in a water bath for the space of a month. Then it will be resolved, exhibiting the form of a green liquor. This is the highest substance by which the substance of the brain is nourished, and a new or foreign brain is "inserted." Similar to this is the **Secret Remedy** <note>original: "Arcanum"</note> extracted from **Gilla** <term>Gilla: usually refers to Gilla Theophrasti, an emetic made from white vitriol (zinc sulfate)</term> in this way:

<margin>Preparation and power of the Liquor of the Moon.</margin>
<margin>How Gilla is extracted.</margin>
<margin>Gilla as a remedy for vertigo, mania, etc.</margin>
Distill the Gilla in the wine of life of equal weight. Circulate it until it no longer touches the bottom. Administer it with Falernian wine. It strengthens the brain so powerfully that no vertigo, no phrensy, and no mania can harm it.

The same is also performed by the liquor of **sapphire** and **musk**, prepared in this way: If a sapphire is reduced to a "diamond-like" nature <note>original: "Alcoadamantinam"; likely referring to a state of extreme purity or hardness</note>, and afterward dissolved into its own powder through **Chybur** <term>Chybur: an alchemical term for Sulfur</term>, and to this powder the wine of life is added for six days of cohobation; finally a drinkable liquor comes forth, which heals **St. Vitus’ dance** <note>Sydenham's chorea, a disorder characterized by rapid, uncoordinated jerking movements.</note>, and the madness and delusions of those who would hang themselves or otherwise kill themselves.

<margin>Preparation of Sapphire.</margin>
<margin>The power of sapphire for St. Vitus' dance, insanity, etc.</margin>
<margin>Extraction of Musk.</margin>
<margin>For Scotomia, the falling sickness, mania, etc.</margin>
A similar medicine is extracted from musk. It is boiled in the wine of life within a cloth until it takes the form of a juice, similar to **storax** <note>A fragrant resin.</note>. By this is cured vertigo, **scotomia** <term>scotomia: dizziness accompanied by the darkening of vision</term>, and whatever induces fainting or a spinning sensation, as well as the beginning of the **Falling Sickness** <note>Epilepsy.</note>, Mania, and Phrensy.

### CHAPTER V.
### On the Powers of the Liver.

<margin>The livers are two.</margin>
The liver of the body also has need of a helper in the form of an "external liver." For the liver is not of a combative or military nature such that it can defend itself. Hence these are called "spiritual members." For no spirit goes to war, but only the body. Now, the Liver itself is purely spirit. Its flesh, which bears the name "Liver," is that member of the body in which not so much power resides. Therefore, if the Liver must ever wage war, necessity requires that something else fight for it—namely, a certain "body" which has its own hands and feet, with which it might take up and use weapons against a physical disease. For if the body suffers, it suffers materially. Therefore, its Medicine ought to be of the same kind, so that in this way matter proceeds against matter, and like acts upon its like. It is as follows: Take Essence of **Spodium** <note>Metallic ashes or oxide, often of zinc.</note>. Also, if the liver is failing toward **dropsy** <note>original: "Hyposarcam"; an accumulation of fluid under the skin.</note>, this is its power; if toward **Jaundice** <note>original: "Icteritiam"</note>, its power is that; if toward fevers, its power is this. If toward an **Abscess** <note>original: "Apostema"</note>, this is the power, and so on.

<margin>The principal parts are spiritual members.</margin>

### CHAPTER VI.

<margin>Cheiri, the health of the liver.</margin>
<margin>Preparation of Cheiri.</margin>
<margin>Cheiri for the liver is drunk; it renews the blood.</margin>
For establishing health in the liver, so that it receives no harm or injury, nothing is more excellent or beneficial than **Cheiri** <term>Cheiri: the Wallflower (Cheiranthus cheiri), used in Paracelsian medicine for heart and liver complaints</term>. The preparation is as follows: Cheiri is taken, and its "blackness" is sublimated into "whiteness." This whiteness is drunk with the wine of life. By this drink, the abscess-forming nature and putrefaction of the liver are removed, and all its corruption is corrected, so much so that thereafter it digests well and dispenses blood rightly—not only producing much blood, but also good and praiseworthy blood, unfit for contracting any diseases. It also renews old and exhausted blood, and cleanses it so thoroughly that even leprosy vanishes. The **yellow flower** <note>original: "Anthos luteum"; likely Rosemary or a similar aromatic yellow flower.</note> performs the same if it is resolved through the spirit of the water of life; thus drunk, it heals all the harms and diseases of the liver.

<margin>Preparation and power of the yellow flower.</margin>
<margin>The Liquor Alchahest stands in place of a consumed liver.</margin>
Furthermore, the **Liquor Alchahest** <term>Alchahest: the hypothetical "universal solvent" sought by alchemists, particularly associated with Paracelsus</term> has a great prerogative and efficacy in preserving and strengthening the liver, and especially against dropsy and all its types arising from liver defects. The process for it is that it be resolved from coagulation, and coagulated again into a changed form, just as the process of "coagulating and resolving" teaches. For then, if it has overcome its "like," it becomes a medicine superior to all other medicines of the liver. And indeed, even if the liver itself were broken and dissolved, this liquor stands in the place of the whole liver, just as if it had never been broken or dissolved. Therefore, all you who apply yourselves to Medicine should strive with the greatest zeal to learn how to prepare the **Alchahest**, on account of the averting of many diseases which arise from the liver.

### CHAPTER VII.
### On the Powers of the Spleen.

<margin>The power of the Spleen.</margin>
The spleen is similar to the other members; since it allows the occasion for the breaking of the body no less than the others, it has need of its own "sought-after like." Its malice consists in this: that it generates hardness, incites fevers, putrefactions, obstructions, and many similar things. But the power and industry here consists in this: that the spleen of the body be removed <note>metaphorically, in terms of its diseased state</note>, and an "external spleen" be sent in or inserted.

# BOOK II.

<margin>One lives more comfortably without a spleen.</margin>
For life without a spleen is longer than life with one. Although this cannot be said of the three organs mentioned above <note>Referring to the heart, brain, and liver, which Paracelsus considers essential for survival.</note>, because they are of the highest necessity in the body; yet regarding the spleen, it is true that we can comfortably do without it. Therefore, all medical practice should be directed toward this: that we might live by the benefit of an "external" spleen rather than the internal one, and that we might root out and consume the internal one.

### CHAP. VIII.

<margin>Preparation of Sutratar.</margin>
<margin>Sutratar consumes the spleen.</margin>
For the consuming and taking away of the spleen, **Sutratar** <term>Sutratar: a Paracelsian alchemical remedy, likely a mineral-based preparation</term> is effective. Separate its liquor from it without a corrosive, using a retort over a strong fire, and afterwards extract it five times. Let the whole thing be cohobated <note>A process of repeated distillation where the liquid is poured back onto the solid residue.</note> with the **wine of life** <term>vinum vitae: a highly rectified alcohol or brandy used as a solvent</term> and be administered. This takes away the spleen entirely, leaving not a trace of it, and it even consumes that which the spleen was meant to digest. It protects the entire body from harm. The same power and operation is to be sought in the dregs from which the wine of life was separated.

<margin>Preparation of Casa.</margin>
<margin>Oil of Casa entirely removes the spleen and its pains.</margin>
A similar power is hidden in **Casa** <term>Casa: another specific Paracelsian alchemical substance</term>. Let it be macerated in olive oil, and afterwards mix it with one pound and a quarter of **opopanax** <note>A medicinal gum resin obtained from certain plants, often used in ancient pharmacy.</note>. Distill it through an alembic. This oil, smeared on the region of the spleen, takes away the entire spleen. Used annually, it turns away all pains born from the spleen. If used with a more accurate regimen, it entirely removes and consumes the spleen, and takes away its pains, diseases, and all universal harms.

### CHAP. IX.
->On the Powers of the Kidneys.<-

<margin>The kidneys are to be abolished like the spleen.</margin>
The best strengthening of the kidneys is recognized in those things that "foster" <note>original: "fotis"</note> the kidneys, so that clearly the interior kidneys are abolished and taken away, and rendered similar to the spleen. Only then will the power of the kidneys be whole: when their [natural] operation has been made dead. For by their own operation they produce **stone disease** <note>original: "Lithiasin"</note>, **the stone, sand, and diabetes**, and many other things. If those organs are "dead" <note>Paracelsus means neutralizing the organ's functional ability to create disease, not literal death.</note>—provided this essence is present—none of those diseases remain, but the strength of the body is honest and vigorous, and both old age and youth are healthy. None of those diseases invade which would occur while the organs were alive and surviving.

### CHAP. X.

<margin>The kidneys contribute more to chastity than the testicles.</margin>
<margin>Atrophia deletes the evils of the kidneys.</margin>
So that the Kidneys—which contribute more to chastity than the testicles—may be taken away, it should be known that they can be removed without any harm. Whatever damage might follow their removal pertains in no way to the other passages that pass through the kidneys themselves. For their matter and life remain, but their [pathological] nature and operation are taken away. This is done through **Atrophia** <note>In this context, not the wasting of tissue, but a specific alchemical preparation.</note>. Through distillation in bread, it is reduced into a liquor, and thus drunk. This drink takes away the evil that the kidneys produce.

### CHAP. XI.
->On the Powers of the Gallbladder.<-

<margin>The gallbladder must be removed.</margin>
The highest happiness and virtue of the gallbladder is that it be materially taken away and consumed. In this way, "chimerical" <note>imaginary or unfounded, but here likely meaning complex or shifting</note> sicknesses are not generated, such as Colic, the Iliac passion <note>a painful bowel obstruction</note>, and similar things, as well as contractions, tremors, and other evils of the stomach. For these parts do nothing else than destroy that which the useful members have built up.

<margin>The gallbladder is a superfluous member, of no use.</margin>
Physicians are ignorant of how much the gallbladder profits nothing. For they assign to it great uses and honors, which nevertheless do not exist. For this member is superfluous in Nature, and like a monster. For nothing is made so good and pure that **weeds and tares** <note>original: "zizania & lolium"</note> are not sown into it. Thus the gall also, and other members like it, is the "weed of nature," which has insinuated itself next to the good, not for the conservation of the body, but for its destruction.

### CHAP. XII.

The process for consuming the gallbladder, so that as much of it as is useless is abolished, is as follows: so that all diseases born from the gall are removed, and no anger or sickness is induced by it thereafter. This is obtained through Rhubarb in this way:

<margin>Preparation of Rhubarb.</margin>
<margin>The power to take away the gall.</margin>
Take of Rhubarb and the flowers of **Cheiri** <note>Wallflower (*Cheiranthus cheiri*), often used in early medicine.</note> in equal parts; and, as was said before, extract the liquor of the Cheiri; but from the Rhubarb, extract it in the same way as from **Anthos** <note>Usually refers to Rosemary flowers in alchemical texts.</note>. Combine these two, and add an equal amount of the wine of life. If you administer this, do it first so that anger may cool down, and afterwards if there is any disease present from the gall. Afterwards, a thirst invades. With this, the gall dissipates and departs. Finally, health follows, more comfortable than before.

### CHAP. XIII.
->On the Powers of the Lungs.<-

<margin>The lung is mobile.</margin>
The best virtue of the lung is that it remains in its own matter, and nothing is added to it, but that it lives alone without an adjunct. Now, it is more mobile than all other universal parts, which it has from the force of the **spirit of life** <note>original: "spiritus vitae"</note>. Therefore, reason and experience dictate that this should be compressed and strengthened. This is obtained through those things which make all members healthy. For thus the lung also will be healthy. However, so that it may be able to turn away more excessive "affluxes" <note>fluids or congestions</note> than is right, the following medicine will be handed down. Wherein it must be held likewise that the other members must be preserved healthy, lest an occasion for death be given.

# ABOUT THE THREE

### CHAP. XIV.

<margin>Chibur, as is evident.</margin>
**O**f the medicines beneficial to the lung, none surpasses **Chibur** <term>Chibur: a Paracelsian term for a specific alchemical preparation, likely related to sulfur or a refined mineral essence</term>. Chibur is taken and mixed with double calxes <note>original: "calcibus"; chemically prepared oxides or powders</note> and minerals; it is sublimated three times. Then it is administered to the sick. This wards off all evils of the lung and increases and doubles its strength; indeed, it is a balsam for the lung and the entire chest. Among all the powers of nature, there is none more potent to be found, nor is there anything in which more of the "external lung" <note>An alchemical substitute that performs the organ's function or restores its vital essence</note> is found, except in Chibur, as we have said.
<margin>Chibur is a balsam for the lung.</margin>

### TO THE READER.

**I**t is necessary here once again, benevolent Reader, to forewarn you that these books—as the Author arranged them and intended to write them—were not found with the first two. Perhaps it is because they were not finished by him. This may be conjectured from the original, which was written with a hurried pen, so that it exhibited the appearance of at least a first draft or a collection of fragments <note>original: "Rhapsodiæ"</note>. However, these following Titles, together with the beginning of the Fifth book, were placed here for this reason: because they were found on the same papers with the first two books. This was done so that a sort of handle might be offered to eager students to further pursue the Author's mind more closely. And since there is no slight suspicion that the booklet *On the Three First Essences* is what is inscribed here as the sixth; for that reason, it has been placed here with the others. It is a matter of your fairness, Reader, to enjoy these present things with a content mind, and not to complain with indignation about those that are absent.

#### CHAP. I.

**T**he Elemental Nature which is in us, outside the substance of the organs and the other things we have mentioned, has such interpretations that we also preserve the four Elements within ourselves. This is done in such a way that the Element of Fire does not generate the stone <note>calculus or kidney/bladder stones</note>; or the Element of Earth, types of pustules; or the Element of Water, **dropsy** <term>Hydropisin: an old medical term for edema or swelling caused by fluid accumulation</term>; or the Element of Air, **tympany** <term>Tympanitem: abdominal swelling caused by gas</term>. For in the same way they generate things outwardly, they also do so inwardly. Specifically, Air and Fire are the flesh and skin. The interior parts—that is, those situated in the cavity within the ribs, the skull, and the bones—are subject to the remaining elements, namely Earth and Water. Therefore, the Intestines, the **Womb** <term>Matrix</term>, etc., are the Element of Earth. The remaining members are the Element of Water.

### ON THE THREE FIRST ESSENCES, FROM WHICH that which is generated is composed.

#### CHAP. I.

<margin>Salt, Sulfur, and Mercury constitute all things.</margin>
**E**very single thing that is generated and produced from its Elements is placed into three: into **Salt**, into **Sulfur**, and into **Mercury**. From these three, a conjunction occurs, which [makes up] the body—

<sig>Gg 4</sig>

...constitutes one body and a united essence. What pertains to the body here is not defined, or at least only the internal part of the body is.

<margin>What the power of Salt is.</margin>
Its operation is threefold. One belongs to **Salt**. It acts by purging, cleansing, embalming, and by other means, and it rules over that which falls into decay <note>original: "putredinem"; refers to the breakdown or rotting of organic matter</note>. The second belongs to **Sulfur**. This rules over that which becomes excessive or is dissolved from the other two.
<margin>What the power of Sulfur is.</margin>

<margin>What the power of Mercury is.</margin>
The third belongs to **Mercury**. It carries away that which falls into consumption <note>wasting away or being used up</note>.

Know these things about these Three: what the form of each is. One is **Liquor**, and that belongs to Mercury. One is **Oiliness**, and that belongs to Sulfur. One is **Alkali**, and this is from Salt. Mercury exists without sulfur and salt; Sulfur without Mercury and salt; Salt without Sulfur and Mercury. And in this way, each persists in its own power.

<margin>What a mixed sickness is.</margin>
Regarding the operations found in mixed diseases, it must be known that the separation of things is not perfect, but two are joined in one, as in dropsy <term>dropsy: an old term for edema, or the swelling caused by excess fluid in the body</term> and other similar conditions. For those are "mixed sicknesses" which transcend their own juice and tempered moisture. Thus, Mercury and Sulfur sometimes remove paralysis, because the bodily sulfur also runs together with them, or because there is some injury in the nearest bordering part. Therefore, it must be observed from this that any disease can exist either doubly or triply. That is the "commingling" of disease. In this, the Physician ought to consider, if he takes a certain simple remedy, what its grade is in liquor, in oil, or in salt, and how it matches with the disease of the neighboring injury. According to that grade, the liquor, the salt, and the sulfur ought to be extracted and assigned as needed. And so this brief rule must be held: that one medicine be given for the injury, another for the disease.
<margin>How a mixed sickness is to be treated.</margin>

## CHAP. II.

<margin>Salts purge either through the bowels.</margin>
Others purge, though in various ways. Some through the bowels. Of these there are two types: One is the **salt of the thing**, which digests things for excretion. The other is the **salt of nature**, which expels them. Therefore, without salt, no excretion can happen. From which it follows that common salt aids the salts of nature.
<margin>Vomit</margin>
Certain things purge through **vomiting**. Such a salt is very coarse; if it cannot pass into digestion, it causes a choking sensation higher up in the stomach.
<margin>Sweat</margin>
Some purge through **sweat**. Such is the most subtle salt, which joins with the blood. For those salts meant for dung and vomit do not join with the blood. Therefore, they provoke no sweat; it is only the salt <note>the coarse salt</note> that is excreted.
<margin>Urine</margin>
Certain things purge through **urine**. For all urine is nothing but superfluous salt. Dung is superfluous sulfur. Of the liquor <note>Mercury</note>, however, nothing departs superfluously from the body, but it remains within. Such are all the egestions of the body: phlegm expelled by salt through the nose, ears, eyes, and other passages. And this is understood through the **Archeus** <term>Archeus: the "inner chemist" or vital force that Paracelsus believed governed the functions of the organs</term>, from which those operations take their lead, as will be shown in the final sections.

Now, just as laxative salt comes forth from the Archeus—where one salt purges the stomach because it proceeds from the Archeus of the stomach, and another purges the spleen because it comes from the Archeus of the spleen—so it happens with the brain and the liver, the lung, and other members. For the member of the Archeus moves the member of the **microcosm** <note>The human body as a reflection of the universe</note>.

<margin>What the differences of salts are.</margin>
Know that regarding **Alkali** and salt, it is varied. One is sweet, like cassia, and is a separated salt which in minerals is called **antimony**. Another is sour, like rock salt <note>original: "sal gemmae"</note>. Another is sharp, such as is in ginger. Another is bitter, such as is in rhubarb and colocynth <note>a bitter cucumber used as a purgative</note>. To which it must be known that many Alkalis are birthed, like Harmel <note>Syrian rue</note>; many are extracted, like scammony; many are coagulated, like that of Wormwood. This is to be understood from how it is recognized in salt. Similarly, some purge through sweat alone, some through consumption alone, and so on. For as often as there is a peculiar flavor, so often is there a peculiar operation and expulsion; yet of these there are no more than two: that is, the operation of the thing, and the extinguished operation.

## CHAP. III.

<margin>What the nature of Sulfur is.</margin>
**Sulfur** operates by drying and consuming superfluity. Whether it be from itself or from others, it must be entirely consumed through sulfur, if it is not subject to salts. Thus, for **Dropsy**, the Medicine of salts produced from the Archeus of the Liver works to consume what is putrefied and corrupt. But to remove the disease itself, the power of sulfur is needed, to which diseases of this kind are subject according to their origin. Although not just any sulfur will provide that.
<margin>Kinds of Elements produce kinds of diseases.</margin>
And so it is produced by the nature of the Element, that every single sickness which the nature of the body brings forth has its contrary within the nature of the Element. And this happens both universally and particularly. Therefore, from the kinds of Elements, the very kinds of diseases must be recognized. Thus, one is always... [the next page begins].

<margin>What the nature of Mercury is.</margin>
Similarly, the same judgment applies to Mercury. It takes up that which separates itself from salt and sulfur. From this arise diseases of the ligaments, the arteries, the junctions, the joints, and the like. Therefore, in these diseases, this one thing must be cared for: that the liquor of Mercury be removed. However, the aforementioned ailments ought to be taken away by those things which seem suitable and convenient to anyone, as indicated regarding the specialty of things in nature, and in Philosophy regarding the matter and nature—which are omitted here for the sake of brevity.

### CAP. IV.

<margin>The birthplaces of diseases.</margin>
**I**n this way, the Physician ought to understand three genera of all diseases: One from salt. One from sulfur. One from Mercury. From salt in this way: any "lax" disease is generated from salt, such as flows of the belly, Dysentery <note>original: "Dysenteria"; severe diarrhea with blood</note>, Diarrhea, Lientery <term>lientery: a form of diarrhea where food passes through the body undigested</term>, etc. Moreover, that salt is what lies in its own seat. For every evacuation is caused by salt, whether in the healthy or the sick. That is the salt of nature; this is salt corrupted and resolved. From which it is established that its cure must also be performed through salts: so that the salt may again rectify and separate the resolved salt from the whole. Afterwards follows the sulfurous cure, like a certain confirmation of the operation in the salt. For this dominates it, and it is a specialized sulfur from the power of the Archeus <term>Archeus: the internal "chemist" or vital force that governs the body's functions</term>, etc.

<margin>Which are the Mercurial diseases.</margin>
Furthermore, from Mercury arise all those diseases which occupy the arteries, ligaments, joints, bones, nerves, etc. For in the other parts of the body, the substance of corporal Mercury does not dominate, but only in the exterior members. For Sulfur softens and fosters the interior members, namely, the heart, liver, brain, kidneys, etc. And the diseases of these must be called sulfurous. For in them, the sulfurous substance is located. We shall take an example of this from
<margin>Various kinds of colic from salt.</margin>
Colic. Its cause is salt because of the intestines, in which salt predominates, and it produces many kinds of colic—namely one if it is resolved, another if it is too greatly hardened. For thus it leaps beyond its temperament and fails toward excessive moisture or dryness. Therefore it happens that in the cure of colic, the human salt must be rectified through Elemental salts. For if any salt other than that of sulfur is applied, you should consider that a drowning of the salt, not a cure for the diseases of colic. So likewise, both in
<margin>Like is cured by its own thing, not by any contrary.</margin>
Mercurial and sulfurous diseases, its own thing ought to be applied to each; one should not expend a contrary for a contrary, but accommodate the proper thing to its own innate nature. For cold does not overcome hot, nor hot cold, in innate diseases. The cure proceeds from that which generated the disease and its location.

### CAP. V.

<margin>Division of diseases into branches, shoots, and leaves.</margin>
**T**he genera of diseases are also divided into various branches, and "locusts" <note>original: "locustas"; here used metaphorically to mean shoots or offshoots of a plant</note>, and leaves. Yet there is one cure. For a Mercurial disease is an example, because the Mercurial liquor likewise goes off into many branches, shoots, and leaves. Thus in pustules <note>skin sores or pimples</note>, all kinds are under Mercury. For the disease itself is Mercurial. Some cases of the French Sickness <note>original: "Galli"; referring to Morbus Gallicus or Syphilis</note> are under common Mercury. Certain pustules are under Metallic Mercury; some under Mercury of Ebony-wood <note>original: "Xylohebeno"</note>; some under Mercury of Antimony. The cause is that Mercury departs toward its own shoots, and not out of order. It is necessary, therefore, that the liquors of Mercury be known. For it is that which heals what its own salt dissolves. There is also another thing located within it, namely an "incarnative" <note>flesh-making</note> and "consolidative" <note>healing or closing</note> power (according to the nature of Mercury).
<margin>Mercury is manifold.</margin>
Now, however, it is manifold. In metals, the liquor of Mercury is like metal. In juniper and ebony, it is like wood. In Marcasites, Talcs, and bismuth <note>original: "cachymiis"</note>, it is like a mineral. In Brassatella, Persicaria, and Serpentina <note>various medicinal herbs</note>, it is like a herb. And yet Mercury is one, which exhibits itself so manifoldly. What is said of pustules, the same should be understood of ulcers. Some can find their cure from the Mercury of Persicaria; some from the Mercury of Arsenic; some from the Mercury of Guaiac-wood <note>original: "Xylo Guaiaco"</note>. The Physician therefore ought to know the
<margin>The tree of diseases and things to be known by the Physician.</margin>
tree of diseases and of things. Several of this kind exist. One is the tree of salt. It is twofold: of Rebis <term>Rebis: an alchemical term for a "dual" or "double" matter</term> and of the Element. So also is the tree of sulfur and of Mercury. Therefore let the Physician beware lest he bring two trees into one cure: but let him hold the Rules that Mercury must be given to Mercurial diseases, salt to saline diseases, sulfur to sulfurous diseases—namely to each disease its own appropriate thing, as is fitting. For in the truth of the matter, there exist only three Medicines, just as there are triple diseases.
<margin>Three accounts of disease; only three remedies.</margin>
Therefore those long-winded ramblings and trifles or quibbles of Avicenna, Mesue, and others ought to be cut short and omitted.

### CAP. VI.

**N**ow therefore, after all that has been said so far, so that the Physician may carry with him a brief and easy compendium, he ought to [know] all diseases...

<margin>How a Physician ought to speak.</margin>
The physician must divide or categorize diseases under the names of their respective medicines, just as we began to do with the aforementioned illnesses. And he should be especially careful not to say, "This is Jaundice <note>original: "Icteritia"</note>." For such speech is outside the practice of the art. Indeed, even a peasant knows and is well-versed in that name. Rather, on the contrary, you shall speak thus: "This is the disease of **Leseolus** <term>Leseolus: A Paracelsian term, likely referring to the essence of Celandine, used specifically to treat Jaundice</term>." For in this way, you encompass the cure, the property, the name, the quality, the disposition, and indeed your own art and science in a single word.
<margin>Leseolus cures Jaundice.</margin>
For **Leseolus** cures Jaundice, and it cures nothing else besides this disease. Thus, you have extricated yourself from all errors, and the cure is proven by the fact that in Leseolus there exists the highest transparency of Salt, which colors and shapes more intensely than a molten Topaz. In the same way, Jaundice is likewise (so to speak) a transparency of the "gold-sickness" <note>original: "aurigine," a historical term for Jaundice due to its golden color</note>: and it requires that it be expelled and driven out by its own likeness. Similarly, the Arsenical nature and the Salt that causes Jaundice are like the mother of the Arsenical and the Leseolus—born, however, from two mothers: the Annual and the Elementary <note>Paracelsus divided influences into "Elementary" (from the four elements) and "Annual" (linked to celestial cycles and seasons)</note>.

Therefore, I advise everyone that those three "trees" <note>referring to the three primary sources: Salt, Sulfur, and Mercury</note> be correctly and solidly understood. For he who does not know the seed of these trees is immersed in mere errors. Furthermore, it must be said:
<margin>What the disease of gold is:</margin>
"This is the **disease of gold**"; one should not say it is Leprosy. Nor is its specific type named: which is truly to speak as a Physician, because this name alone sufficiently indicates what cure you should establish for Leprosy. This is much more than if you simply said it was Leprosy.
<margin>What the disease of the tincture is.</margin>
Thus again I say: "This is the **disease of the tincture**." From which the skilled person understands well enough that I have discovered what and of what sort the tincture is, and how it regenerates and makes one young again.
<margin>The Tincture causes rejuvenation.</margin>
Thus I also say: "This is the **disease of vitriol**." Experience proves this, because types of Epilepsy are cured by the oil of vitriol or its spirit. Even if writings everywhere confirm this, since it serves the Theory of my instruction here, what harm is there in repeating it—by what means the Theory ought to be perfected? The reason these things are included in the Theory is a special method from which the former is deduced, and the mysteries of nature which were kept closed by the Alchemical authors. From these, I rightly prove and demonstrate my Theory of both origins: the Elementary in its production and the Annual in its generation, and from there I build the foundation of my Theory.

Furthermore, we also inquire from the Theory:
<margin>What sort of things are incarnatives and from where they come.</margin>
From what virtue do **incarnatives** <term>incarnatives: medicines that promote the growth of new flesh to heal wounds</term> arise? From Mercury alone. It heals wounds over a long time—as if through Mercury in resin—yet more quickly than Mercury in **Mummy** <note>original: "Mumia"; in this context, the vital balsam or essence found in the body, used as a medicine</note>, and again more quickly than Mercury in **Tartar** <note>original: "Tartaro"; the stony sediment often found in wine casks, used alchemically</note>. Likewise also in ulcers: such as certain Cancerous ulcers, **Esthiomenes** <term>esthiomenes: "eating" or corroding skin ulcers</term>, and Erysipelas <note>a bacterial skin infection known as "St. Anthony's Fire"</note>. There are many such Mercurial operations or powers in the Elementaries and Annuals, all found through experience by those who understand in which things Mercury lurks, and in which things others hide. These people also know how to prepare and shape that Mercury—one into a Topaz-like form, another into a **sandal-crocus** <note>original: "crocum sandalinum"; likely a red-orange powder derived from sandalwood</note>, another into a spirit, each into its own "exaltation" <note>the state of a substance at its highest medicinal potency</note> in which it functions best.
<margin>Sandal-crocus.</margin>
And although Mercury is indeed singular, yet if there is a need for it, it wishes to be produced in this way. We testify, therefore, in this place, that the power of "incarnating" (flesh-growing) and consolidating proceeds from Mercury alone, in which no sulfur and no salt exists, but it is extracted and reduced into its pure liquor. You must proceed in exactly the same way with sulfur and salt, and you must know their exaltation, provided you hold the name of Physician and wish to heal your patients with praise. I know well enough that **Porphyry** <note>likely referring to the philosopher Porphyry, representing traditional theoretical learning</note> will be amazed if he hears that **Sapphire** is Mercury, and so is the noble **Jasper**, because he does not see it or feel it with his hands. Even if he has been distinguished by no experience thus far, nor strives to learn anything, I know not what trifles he babbles or dreams about in the meantime.

### CAP. VIII.

<margin>Why Ginger is a Diaphoretic.</margin>
In this way, why is **Ginger** a Diaphoretic <term>diaphoretic: a substance that induces sweating</term>? Because of the Salt from whose body it was made. But that power is of fire, through which generations "boil up" (as is taught in Philosophy); because of this boiling, it clears obstructions and kindles the humors of sulfur, salt, and mercury... <warning>ink stain</warning> just as from the fieriness of Salt it constitutes the second, third, and fourth degree, by which degree the moisture distills out through the pores as drops. Thus, **cleansers** <note>original: "mundificatiua"</note> also cleanse from the power of Salt alone, such as honey and other things.
<margin>Cleansers come from salt.</margin>
From which it also follows that the **Balsam of salt** is located in honey, because of which it does not rot. For the Balsam of salt is the most noble thing that nature has produced.

The **attractive force** <note>the power to draw out toxins or fluids</note> comes from the sulfurous nature or essence, as in gums. These draw by reason of...

<margin>Attraction from sulfur that is not hot.</margin>
...by reason of its sulfurous nature. For Mastic <note>A resin obtained from the mastic tree, used in historical medicine for its binding properties.</note> is a sulfur produced in this way. The same is true for Opopanax, Galbanum, and others. One must not believe this axiom of the Physicians: *It is the nature of the hot to attract*; rather, it should be said: *It is the nature of sulfurs to attract*. This is most true. For hot things only draw when they are in place—that is, where they burn. But that which burns is sulfur, and because it is not fixed, it flies away, which is what Gums do. <margin>Laxatives from sulfurous salt.</margin> Similarly, laxatives also draw from those places in which they do not reside, much like a magnet. The reason why salts also draw is that salt is impressed upon the sulfur and coagulated by the spirit of sulfur. Therefore, it also attracts from more distant places. <margin>Repulsion from Sulfur that is not cold.</margin> In the same way, repulsive medicines <note>Medicines intended to drive "humors" away from a site of inflammation.</note> are also sulfurous, whether they be cold, or green, or scarlet, or in whatever other state they may be. For this is the nature of repulsive sulfur: to go toward the center and to drive before it whatever movable things it seizes. Nor is it true what they say, that *it is the nature of the cold to repel*. To be sure, those simple little men believe they have the fox by the tail, when in fact they have only grabbed its backside. One would have to be a subtle Albertist <term>Albertist: A follower of the scholastic teachings of Albertus Magnus (c. 1200–1280).</term> to want or be able to defend that rule of theirs. But these matters are discussed more broadly in *Philosophy*.

### CHAPTER XI.

<margin>The strengthening power comes from the Archeus of the world.</margin>
**R**EGARDING what we must know about Confortatives <term>Confortatives: Medicines intended to strengthen or "comfort" the internal organs.</term>, the explanation of the **Archeus** <term>Archeus: In Paracelsian thought, the "internal chemist" or vital force that governs the functions of an organ or the body.</term> teaches us. He is similar to a human and lies hidden within the four Elements; that is, one Archeus, but divided into four parts. He is therefore the Great Cosmos <note>The Macrocosm or the universe.</note>, and man is the small cosmos <note>The Microcosm.</note>, and one is similar to the other. From him proceeds the power of strengthening. Thus, what proceeds from the heart of the Archeus is the strengthening of the [human] heart, such as gold, emerald, corals, and the like. What proceeds from the liver of the Archeus strengthens the liver of the lesser cosmos, and so on. Mercury does not provide this kind of strengthening power, nor does sulfur, nor salt. Rather, the "heart of the Elements" provides it, for it flows from this. Within the Elements, there is a force and power that produces a tree from a seed; and it is from the Element itself that the power comes by which a tree stands, is fixed, and is sustained. Likewise, hay and straw are also made to stand by an external strength that the eyes can see. A similar strength exists in animals, by whose benefit they walk, stand, and move. The same applies in the same way to all other products of nature.

Furthermore, there is yet another strength <margin>Nothing subsists without the spirit of nature.</margin> not exposed to the eyes. There is a strength within itself by which that in which it resides remains healthy and strong. This is the **spirit of nature**. Unless a thing possesses this, it perishes. This spirit remains fixed in its body. It likewise strengthens the human being. In this way, therefore, the power of the individual members of the Archeus flows down into the lesser cosmos, specifically through the medium of plants.

### What man is, that is, the flesh of man.

<margin>Where man's mortality comes from.</margin> **T**his is the generation <term>generation: The process of being born or coming into existence.</term> of man. To be sure, he arose from the first matrix, that is, from the Great World <note>The Macrocosm, or the universe as a whole.</note>. That is, the Great World, together with all other creatures through the hand of God's creation, produced and begot man, regarding the nature of his flesh, for mortality. For this reason, man was made earthly and carnal. Indeed, man received this fleeting and fragile flesh from earth and water. Therefore, earth and water are the body of this earthly and animal life, which man received naturally through the creation made by the hand of God. Truly, this animal life in itself is nothing other than Fire and Air. This should be understood in the following way.

<margin>Man consists of four elements.</margin> Man himself, as far as his animal life is concerned, consists of the four Elements. For Water and Earth, from which the body of man is constituted, are the dwelling place and the body of life itself. However, I do not here mean that life which proceeds from the Soul, that is, from the nature of God (for I am acting here as a Physician, not a Theologian), but this life which is animal and fleeting: and which is composed of Fire and Air.

<margin>Twofold life: Animal and celestial.</margin> Thus, therefore, the body, created from earth and water, was made the house of life. From this, it is easily understood how man is gifted with a twofold life, namely the Animal and the sidereal <note>Star-governed; referring to the "astral body" that connects man to the heavens.</note>.

Lest this project of mine—namely, that I am here treating animal and sidereal life—be rebuked by anyone: it is useful for me to describe the Animal body more clearly.

<margin>The body, dead in itself, is made alive by the spirit.</margin> For the animal and sidereal body is one, not double, in this manner. [The body is dead: that is, the body, which is blood and flesh, is always dead. However, the sidereal spirit, from which man has animal life, causes the body to move. From this arises animal life in man. Truly, all these things happen naturally by the property and power of the heavens.

<margin>The reason for the cock-crow.</margin> That the farmyard cock greets both midnight and the day itself with its song, it received this property from the Stars.

---

Now, however, it belongs to me—indeed, to any true and skilled Physician—to know by what reason both the cock and man are thus governed and compelled by the Stars. Heaven governs the life of man: the Elements, however, regulate his body. The body of man is water and earth. His life, however, is fire and air.

<margin>Water and earth are ruled by fire and air.</margin> Thus water and earth are ruled by fire and air. From this principle also, man has diseases and health.

<margin>What the tree of good and evil is.</margin>
<margin>What the image of God in man is.</margin> This is surely the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, from which God forbade Adam and Eve to eat. That is, why God did not want Adam and Eve—and consequently all of us as well—to live according to the nature of this tree; that is, man should not have lived in an animal way at all, according to the condition of the powers of the Elements. Instead, it was right that he should adapt and govern himself according to the will of the divine commandments, against the nature of the Elements. For this purpose, through creation, he also received the image of God. Adam was meant to live in the first paradise according to the integrity of this image, which is the soul itself—and thus all of us were meant to live so. Because that did not happen, we are now deservedly overwhelmed by various diseases and punishments from our Creator on account of our contempt for the divine command.

It seemed right to me to weave in this preface so that I might more conveniently describe the origin of the animal man: which man received his body and image from the Elements themselves, namely, Earth, Water, Air, and Fire.

Having perceived these things, I will now join an argument concerning the likeness of the animal man, how he was fashioned. In this is contained the true, genuine, and solid foundation of this entire Philosophy: so that from here all Physicians, students of the intimate and hidden truth, may understand from which principles and foundations they must philosophize, practice medicine, and write.

Man received this likeness and property. A certain and definite number of these was made by God. <margin>Why man was created after the animals.</margin> <margin>The kingdom exists before the king.</margin> Since, therefore, it is necessary for man to be described truly and accurately according to his animal nature—just as was included in this first chapter concerning the image of man—because he was surely made according to the animals, it can easily be gathered that God willed to create that which is lesser and lowlier than man before man himself. This was so that he who was to rule over the other animals might be a kind of earthly King. For such is the law of Nature, that the Kingdom exists before the King. Note this further, then: the animals themselves have an innate knowledge of both Good and Evil. No less does man himself also have his knowledge infused <note>original: "tinctam" - literally "dyed" or "tinted"; in Paracelsian philosophy, this refers to a quality impressed upon a substance by a higher power</note> with evil and good—infused, I say, from the stars, as far as his earthly nature and condition are concerned.

From this nature, it is right that the supreme and most exquisite investigation of true Philosophy be conducted. In order that this animal condition may be properly and correctly described, this chapter will specifically deal with the <term>tincture: a fundamental quality or spiritual essence that colors or defines a being's nature</term> of the animal man. For man has two tinctures. One regarding his animal nature, from the *Stars*. The other, supernatural, from God. And this will come to be weighed by deep and subtle Philosophy.

<margin>Man has two tinctures.</margin> Concerning the origin and true generation of man, you ought especially to know and philosophize in this way: The origin of the animal man—that is, of the body and the animal life of man—is this: that Holy Scripture (by whose faith you rightly stand) says man was created from the earth, from the <term>limbus: A Paracelsian term for the "great chaos" or the primeval extract of all created things from which man was formed</term>, that is, from a clod of earth. And this is true and correct. For Theology strives for truth and brevity alone, and uses no philosophy of natural things, but the divine word concerning supernatural things. Therefore, I must now discourse philosophically about earthly and natural matters, and not philosophize about the supernatural man. Already, then, man has been taken from the earth, and will become earth again; that is, after death, man will become again what he was before and at first. And this is said of the body and the dwelling of the natural man: namely, that it is composed of earth, water, air, and fire, about which more follows. Meanwhile, no one denies what is said here: that man was certainly produced from these elements. Nor should this matter be called into doubt by anyone. But as for how man was formed from the earth by the hand of God: most people are silent on that point. But I, seeing that for a long enough time now no one anywhere has been willing to lift this stone <note>A metaphor for tackling a difficult and heavy intellectual problem</note>, shall proceed to make this truth plain and accessible to all its lovers.

<margin>The Limbus is the origin of man.</margin> <margin>By what means man arose from the 4 Elements.</margin> <margin>There are four seasons of the year.</margin> And so that I may return to my purpose at the beginning—how man emerged from the four Elements—the matter stands thus: I think it is well known to you that in the Great World, four seasons of the year prevail: Spring, Summer, Autumn, and Winter. These four named seasons, by the help and governance of the Stars, generate and produce whatever God has ordained to be brought forth throughout the world. And concerning these four seasons, there is no one who doubts or raises a dispute. Just as it is established, then, that those four seasons beget and bring forth various and diverse fruits, so also the fruits of the earth ought to be distinguished into four kinds and enumerated according to Philosophy: namely, those of the Elements—Earth, Water, Air, and Fire.

Now, therefore, because I have begun once to discourse on the image of man—that is, on the animal form of the animal man—I cannot help but bring forth and reveal the secrets of these things as well. But before I describe the form and image itself, I am about to explain briefly the matter from which man was composed.

## KABBALAH <note>The author uses "Kabbalah" here to mean "received wisdom" or the hidden spiritual foundations of nature, rather than the specific Jewish mystical tradition.</note>

<margin>Elements arisen from three things.</margin>
**E**arth, Water, Air, and Fire achieve their origin from three things. These three were not created earlier or sooner than Earth, Water, Air, and Fire. These three are and were: Fire, Air, Water, and Earth. <note>While listing four elements, the author argues they are manifestations of three underlying alchemical principles.</note> These three had one mother from which they proceeded.

<margin>Water is the mother of the Elements.</margin>
This Mother was Water. For when the whole world was being established, the Spirit of God was moved upon the Waters.

<margin>"Let it be" is the force of creation.</margin>
For through the word LET IT BE <note>original: "FIAT"</note>, Water was created first of all. And from this thereafter all other creatures were produced, both animate and inanimate. Therefore, by their true and genuine names, these three are called *Sulphur, Mercury, and Salt*.

<margin>All things are born from Sulphur, Mercury, and Salt.</margin>
This therefore is the principle, this the true matter, from which all Animals, and finally man himself, were also fashioned.

<margin>Three seasons are required for generating things.</margin>
Take heed further: for the perfect generation of all things, three seasons are required: namely Spring, Summer, and Autumn. And the generations of all fruits, and of all creatures of the whole world, bear witness to this. By their example, it must be thought that man himself also requires three seasons for his generation, according to the condition of the three aforementioned things or materials: *Sulphur, Mercury, and Salt*. These three acknowledge two Rulers and governors.

<margin>The Moon is the moderator of Salt.</margin>
Salt has the Moon as its moderator. For by her it is ruled and governed. Now truly, Salt is the substance and matter of water, and it is subject to water, as it is even dissolved and liquefied in it. And this is the portion of Autumn and Winter.

<margin>The Sun is the Lord of Sulphur.</margin>
But the Sun is the King and Lord of *Sulphur*. For this is of a fervent and fiery nature. For which reason it is also resolved in fire and the Sun. For the Sun is the Ruler and moderator of Spring and Summer. Now since it has been said that all things—that is, all creatures—either have life in them or do not: it must be known above all that they are all nothing other than *Sulphur, Mercury, and Salt*. Whoever wishes to either read or rightly understand this my Philosophy, let him know that *Sulphur, Mercury, and Salt* are the most certain measure of all things and the true index for any Physician who wishes to extract and track down this Philosophy from its single foundation.

<margin>Salt is the body of Autumn and Winter; Sulphur indeed of Spring and Summer.</margin>
For Salt is the body of Autumn and Winter; Sulphur indeed of Spring and Summer: in which the Sun and Moon perform their operations. You shall understand it in this way: Salt gives form and color to all creatures; but Sulphur gives the body, growth, digestion <note>original: "digestionem"</note>, etc. And these two exist as father and mother, from whom—with the Stars mediating—all creatures are begotten: that is, the Sun and Moon, through Sulphur and Salt, beget Mercury. Now truly, once Mercury is begotten, it has need of daily nourishment for its sustenance, and further always needs Sulphur and Salt for its increase.

<margin>Mercury comes from Salt and Sulphur.</margin>
Furthermore, you must now know that God created and established much and varied Sulphur and Salt in the Earth and Water; that is, every single creature, as many as there are, whether they live or do not live, has its own proper Sulphur and Salt stored within Water and Earth, from which it receives its nourishment.

<margin>Earth and water are full of sulphur and salt.</margin>
For Salt confers flavor and form to all things: Sulphur imparts odor and "digestion" <note>original: "putredinem" – in alchemical terms, this refers to the breakdown of matter to release its essence, often compared to digestion in the stomach.</note> in the stomach to all things, whether they live or do not live. And these things indeed seem strange and unsuitable to the ignorant. But this is not new. For we are usually more intensely amazed by nothing other than that which we do not understand. Now, it is certain that the earth is engaged in perpetual operation and motion—that is, the Sun and Moon labor constantly so that they may abundantly beget, ripen, and produce those three things. For all creatures have need of their own nourishment. For they were created from those three, which they cannot lack for food and sustenance for even a single moment. Thus the stork needs the frog, and the duck needs the same, and many other creatures besides. The swallow requires flies and gnats. The bee requires flowers for honey-making. The bear hunts for honey, and so on. But the more detailed consideration of this belongs to those skilled in such matters. For since these things are common and well-known, they require very little deep scrutiny. From these things it is now clear to you that for generation of this kind, the Macrocosm <note>The "Great World" or the universe at large.</note> has absolute need of its Spring, Summer, and Autumn, so that every creature may be sustained through its own nourishment. Nor shall this change of things be abolished before the consummation of the world. And I wished to preface and explain these things as an introduction to the chapter, so that the following text might become clearer and more lucid. For since we have discussed thus far the fruits and foods of both animate and inanimate beings: it is now following that we begin the explanation of the generation of man. To which, however, it is necessary to prefix the generation of animals from which...

...by which Adam, the first man, received his body.

As soon as a living creature is to be born, it is necessary that first a father and mother exist, from whom that creature may be produced in succession. This father and mother, who contribute to the conception of the fetus, are Salt and Sulphur. Salt with the Moon is the mother. <margin>Sulphur and salt are the seed of all things.</margin> Sulphur with Salt is the father: that is, Sulphur and Salt are the seed of all creatures. <margin>Sun and Moon are the parents.</margin> Sun and Moon are Vulcans <note>In alchemy, "Vulcan" refers to the transformative power of fire or the divine "inner smith" that shapes matter.</note>, that is, father and mother, who drive the seed toward its growth until the fetus, Mercury, is born. Therefore, because Sun and Moon exist as father and mother—which is an astronomical fact—it falls to me to explain astronomically how creatures of every condition are first born through the aforementioned Sun and Moon. What the manner of this birth is, the Great World <note>The Macrocosm, or the universe at large.</note> demonstrates once every year, namely through three distinct seasons of the year, which must be faithfully held and noted. Therefore, I shall begin from the lowest birth and ascend to the highest: that is, I shall start from the smallest living animal, ascending even to the King himself, Man, who is the earthly Lord and King of all animals.

<margin>May renews all things.</margin> You see that once winter has passed (which is the death of all creatures lacking life), through the loveliness of May, all things fit for conceiving life are moved and stirred. For at this time, the entire world is renewed, as it were, and grows young by turning green and blossoming. And if you pay attention, every creature that enjoys life is carried away with a kind of singular joy along with Great Nature. Evidence of this can be gathered from herbs, trees, and all things of the world. Nor is this joy unlike that of a pregnant woman, who with a certain singular vow and inward desire yearns to bring her conceived fetus into the light. Yet it is not brought forth into the vital air <note>original: "auram vitalem"; the breath of life or the open air.</note> until the time (required for perfecting and completing the birth) has passed and finished. Then at last the infant is produced: not unlike a tree pregnant with numerous fruits, weighed down by too much weight, finally laying down and casting off its burden. <margin>All things look toward their end.</margin> For all things are directed toward their end. Wherefore God, the Best and Greatest, has pre-ordained for all creatures their own particular autumn and harvest. For as soon as any creature is perfected, Autumn and Harvest rush in, so that when mature, it may be taken into the winepress, as it were, and into its own receptacle. <margin>Time is the fate of all things.</margin> For a specific resting place and reservoir is predestined by God for every creature. Thus a cage for the bird, a cask for wine, and a granary for the grain. Since, therefore, there is an infinite number and variety of creatures and fruits in the world—and each one has its own particular Autumn, Summer, and May—it is indeed necessary that various times of May exist, as well as various summers and autumns, according to the condition and manner of each creature. There is no reason to speak of Winter here. For it is not to be mixed with these. Since, therefore, as has been said, to every creature its own proper May <note>The author uses the months of May, Summer, and Autumn to represent the alchemical stages of Spring (conception/growth), Summer (maturation), and Autumn (harvest/completion).</note> is given and appointed for conception and birth: it seems right to discuss first and above all else the May of the Great Creature, that is, of the world itself. By this method, the May of the other smaller creatures can thereafter be more easily and conveniently explained and understood. The same should be thought concerning the Summer and Autumn of all creatures.

-> ### *Concerning the May of the Great World.* <-

<margin>Water is the womb of all creatures.</margin> **W**ater—that is, the Element of Water—is the womb <note>original: "matrix"; in alchemy, the "matrix" is the place where generation occurs, like a biological womb.</note> of all creatures. Now, since a womb cannot give birth unless it has first conceived the seed from which the fruit is to be born: it is clearly necessary that some father be provided who, with great pleasure and titillation, pours his seed into the womb. <margin>The womb does not give birth without a man.</margin> The Moon and the Element of Water, therefore, are the womb; but the Sun and the Element of Fire are the father, <margin>Moon and Sun give birth to Mercury.</margin> both bearing the seed and shaking it into the womb so that fruit may be born. Moreover, the seed of the fruits is Mercury. For its maturation, growth, and completion, it has need of sulphur and salt. It follows from this that Water and the Element of Water constantly contain this seed—namely, Mercury—within themselves for the purpose of giving birth to fruit. The crux <note>original: "rhombus", literally a spinning top or diamond shape, but used here idiomatically for the "turning point" or core of the matter.</note> and hinge of the matter turns on the appetite and pleasure of the father, who neither can, nor will, nor should always promote the seed.
