## TRACTATE II.
## ON THE PLAGUE.
->*The manner and process of its becoming.*<-

<margin>Man is earth.</margin> <term>Man</term> <note>The woodcut initial 'H' begins the word 'Homo' (Man)</note> is of the earth, and made from the earth. And just as the earth is a body into which all sorts of seeds are cast—whether they be of herbs, trees, or other growing things that come forth from the earth—so also man is a body into which many and various seeds are thrown. And this is especially to be noted. For whoever wishes to properly understand and distinguish our Philosophy must give diligent labor to this, lest he apply a falsified and impostor-like reasoning and Philosophy. For just as you see various kinds of fruits divided into infinite species, such as cherries, plums, peaches, pears, and so on; so also the various kinds of animals are counted, distributed into a thousand natures: such as birds, fish, and four-legged beasts. And yet, in each and every kind, its own peculiar part of the seed exists for the purpose of feeding man. If these are taken into the man, it is necessary that they be digested in his stomach, dissolved, and putrefied. This kind of dissolution is a corruption, and a reduction of the food into its **ultimate matter**. And this ultimate matter of the food—or rather, the matter from the food—is the first <term>Ens</term> <note>Ens: An entity or "being" in a specific state; here, the fundamental essence of the food ready to be used by the body</note> for the life of the human body, from which the body takes its nourishment. Here now it must be properly and diligently weighed, what it is that the Philosopher says:

> *The corruption of one is the generation of another.* <note>original: *Corruptio vnius est generatio alterius*; a classic principle of alchemy and Aristotelian physics suggesting that for a new form to arise, the old form must break down.</note>

This is the same as saying: if food is digested in the stomach of a man, it departs, separated into three things. <margin>Three things happen in the stomach regarding food.</margin> The first is *Digestion*; the second is *Separation*; the third is the *Generation of the separation*, which is performed by the <term>Archeus</term> <note>Archeus: The "inner alchemist" or vital force that Paracelsus believed directed the functions of the organs</note> in the stomach, and is the reduction of food into <term>sulphur</term>, <term>mercury</term>, and <term>salt</term> <note>The "Three Primes" (Tria Prima): In Paracelsian thought, these are the fundamental components of all matter, representing flammability (sulfur), fluidity/spirit (mercury), and solidity/stability (salt)</note>. You can observe this in the three primary and most common **cleansing-places** <note>original: *emunctoriis*; organs or channels through which the body eliminates waste</note>. <margin>Superfluous things are excreted through the cleansing-places.</margin> For the superfluous part of the salt is separated through the urine; the superfluous part of the sulfur is purged through the intestines. <term>Mercury</term> has no superfluous part but remains with the nourishment. And this indeed—that which is in the salt and sulfur is brought into and joined with the body through and with the seed (that is, with the food)—is easy to understand, since I have written abundantly about it throughout my volumes. Whatever is lacking here, look for in the treatise *On the method of preparing medicines*. There, all necessary things concerning the dung from food and drink will be explained. For it seems superfluous to treat the same matter again. In the same way, as I said, the earth also conceives every cast-off seed, transforms it, digests it, dissolves it, and putrefies it. Yet at this point, you will note a very secret and hidden point of distinction between the putrefaction, digestion, and generation performed in man and in the earth. <margin>The difference that exists between Digestion in man and in the earth.</margin> The difference is of this kind: The earth separates nothing. For it ejects no excrement; rather, it digests, putrefies, generates, and increases by the help and ministry of the stars. However, it lacks the separation of the seed into <term>sulphur</term>, <term>salt</term>, and <term>mercury</term>. For it does not, like man, have need of seed for food; rather, the seed is cast into it so that fruits may be born and multiplied to be food and nourishment for man. And just as the seed of a man is cast into the womb—not so that food may be born from it, but that a man may be made—so also the earth conceives the cast seed not for food, but for the generation of food. For the earth does not at all require that separation into <term>sulphur</term>, <term>salt</term>, and <term>mercury</term>, because it already contains within itself <term>mercury</term>, <term>sulphur</term>, and <term>salt</term> for generation and production. Whence it also does not separate, but its own Archeus increases, generates, and multiplies. Read more about these things in *On the generation of things*, and in...

<summary>Paracelsus explains that human digestion mimics the earth's natural processes, using the internal "Archeus" to break food down into the Three Primes (Salt, Sulfur, and Mercury). He distinguishes man from earth by noting that man must separate waste from nourishment, while the earth acts as a generative womb that requires no such excretion.</summary>

<margin>Man as earth.</margin>
...in my Herbary *on the growing things of nature*. You have also heard above that <term>man</term> <note>The human being as a "terrestrial" entity</note> himself is of the earth, and is the earth itself, regarding the seed which must be conceived, generated, digested, and putrefied no less than in the soil. However, man reduces food in the stomach into its ultimate matter—the final state of food—which becomes <term>sulfur, salt, and Mercury</term> <note>These are the "Three Primes" (Tria Prima), the fundamental building blocks of all matter according to Paracelsian alchemy</note>. From this, the body <margin>Zenextor is Mercury.</margin> receives its nourishment, <term>Mercury</term>, otherwise called <term>zenextor</term> <note>original: *zenextor*; a specific Paracelsian term for the essential or "spiritual" Mercury in the body</note> in Philosophy. And while in the <term>Great World</term> <note>The Macrocosm, or the universe</note> the earth requires ten months for the production of grain and fruit—that is, since in a full year all things sprout from the earth and bear fruit—it seems consistent that man is also owed his own four parts of the year; that is, a complete and peculiar year, which <margin>The hours of the Microcosmic year are 24.</margin> consists of 24 hours, and this is the **Microcosmic year**. Indeed, that birth and that growth are quite headlong, produced and occurring in a 24-hour interval, which in the earth is scarcely generated in ten months. This is the nerve, the hinge of the matter. For because the earth of the <term>Microcosm</term> <note>The "Little World," meaning the human body</note> digests and generates the seed cast into it so quickly, it is for this reason that the signs of the plague, and the plague itself, also arise so quickly. The cause of this rapid generation is that hastened digestion of the Microcosm, which the natural philosopher must understand above all, but much more so the natural physician and the magus. At-<margin>The plague arises in a double seed and by its own impulse.</margin> tend to this: always and at all times when the plague rages, that disease is twofold: that is, it arises from a **double seed**, and moreover has a third within itself, <margin>Otherwise called: Essential.</margin> which is a peculiar principle and disposition arising in man.

One and a natural mode is that of <term>S.S. Nitre</term> <note>original: *S.S. Nitri*; likely referring to "Sal Nitri" or Saltpeter, which Paracelsus viewed as a vital, aerial salt necessary for life and generation</note>, which is the manner by which worms are born, just as I handed down in the first part of my Philosophy concerning the generation of frogs. And yet, I will declare it more broadly here from an abundance of evidence. For the generation of frogs and the generation of the plague in man share one mode and one process of becoming. Judge this from the generation of worms in man, whose own origin is also twofold. For worms are generated by the excessive ingestion of food. They are also generated by the inclination of the heavens. In the same way, the plague is also generated: naturally, from food and drink; non-naturally, from the heavens. This chapter will therefore be explained in the order by which I have established the twofold plague: Natural and non-natural. One <margin>The origin of the plague is threefold.</margin> seed is from food and drink. The other is from the heavens and the stars. The third mode is from the imagination, such as from fear, terror, and the like.

->*On the Natural mode from food and drink, which is the mode of S.S. Nitre*<-

<margin>From where frogs are generated.</margin> **T**he frog is born in the Element of water. This happens in the month of May, which, aided by the ministry and favor of the Stars—namely the Sun and Moon—brings into effect the seed of frogs, which is sulfur, salt, and Mercury. It happens by this reasoning. Sulfur <margin>Sulfur is everywhere.</margin> lies hidden in all places and parts of the earth, and thus everywhere where there is water. It is resolved and dissolved by the heat of the sun. If this now exists in actual practice, it is mixed with the Element of water. Moreover, the Element of water itself desires nothing more greedily than to conceive sulfur thus dissolved. For just as the womb of a woman greedily attracts the sperm of a man to itself, so water also <margin>Water attracts sulfur, and vice versa.</margin> attracts sulfur with desire, for this reason: Water lacks the dryness which is present in sulfur. Therefore, the water is tormented by such a great desire for the sulfur. For the magnet of the water draws the sulfur, which is the attractive power of water. Sulfur, however, lacks moisture; therefore the magnet of sulfur draws the moisture of the water. Indeed, the moisture of the water has the moisture of salt secretly hidden within itself, and sulfur in turn fosters the moisture of fire, nor does it desire anything else than the moisture of salt which is in the water. Sulfur contains the dryness of salt; whence the salt demands dryness from the sulfur. And in this way, the attractive power of both behaves mutually in action. The earth, however, is expulsive, just as the heaven is also of an expulsive nature. <margin>A man desires a woman through imagination, and she in turn desires the man.</margin> Meanwhile, the heaven is also attractive. Similarly, the earth itself also possesses this, because of the power of begetting which exists evidently in the male and female. For the imagination and the attractive power of the man desires and draws the female; in turn, the attractive power of the female desires and draws the male. And this is also the free schoolmaster and the school of my philosophy *On the Generation of all natural things*. Here it must now be noted that the frog itself is similarly generated in the water from the three primes. First from sulfur. Second <margin>Frogs are begotten from the primes.</margin> from salt. If anyone should perhaps ask what becomes of Mercury? Let him know that this matter must be attended to singularly above all things. For from Mercury flows the understanding of all my highest Philosophy concerning the generation of the plague and of all diseases. <margin>No sulfur is devoid of salt, and vice versa.</margin> Let any natural physician know that there is no sulfur which does not have salt within itself.

Although sulfur certainly contains salt, the sulfur part is by far the largest, while the portion of salt is smaller, even minimal. Likewise, in salt, there is a great deal of salt and very little sulfur.

<margin>Whence Mercury originates.</margin>
Therefore, from the "foreign" salt contained in sulfur and from the "stranger" sulfur hidden in salt, <term>Mercury</term> <note>In Paracelsian thought, Mercury represents the fluid, transformative, and "spiritual" principle of matter</note> arises and emerges. Thus, Mercury is a dual, "Hermaphroditic" seed of sulfur and salt; sulfur and salt carry the Mercurial seed like a man and a woman, from which they beget their offspring, Mercury. Now, if sulfur—which is of a dissolved and oily nature—is driven out from the earth by the instinct and operation of salt through the expulsive force of water, then salt is also extracted along with it.

<margin>The little frog is the seed in the sperm of frogs.</margin>
From this, a conjunction of those two occurs, born through the "digestion" of the Sun, and a frog is produced according to the appointed time, just as that sperm is seen in the <term>Macrocosm</term> <note>The "Great World" or the universe at large</note> during the month of May. Its black spots are Mercury, and they are the seed of the whole frog. Now, by a similar understanding, the generation of the plague can also be understood. For as far as the <term>Salt-Nitrum</term> <note>original: *S. S. nitri*; refers to Sal Nitrum or Saltpeter, which Paracelsus believed was a celestial fire-salt vital to life and weather</note> is concerned, the matter is one and the same, whether generated naturally or preternaturally.

<margin>What and of what kind is the generation of the plague.</margin>
And to describe its natural origin, the matter should be judged thus: if the material for the poison is present, the generation of the plague is natural. If, however, the stars outside of man or the imagination operate by chance, the generation is preternatural—and yet, the generation is one and the same. And that plague is already a disease; the way its generation occurs in one part of man has now been explained. Now pay attention to how it may invade a man in another way or by another path.

### *How the plague is generated supernaturally in man, and derived into man through the Basilisk of Heaven and Water, Cabalistically through the number nine.*

<margin>The Sun has an Euestral spirit.</margin>
**A**ll of you "Naturalists" and even you Theologians ought to know that in the Sun there is a certain hidden and concealed <term>Euestral Essence</term> <note>The "Euestrum" is a Paracelsian term for an ethereal or "prophetic" body that links the physical world to the spiritual or astral realms</note> and Spirit; which, by its remarkable and effective knowledge, corresponds with the Euestrum of the animal-man, and even more so with the very regions from which the "first-formed" <note>Referring to the original state of man or the fundamental archetypes of human life</note> is nourished.

<margin>The Euestra of man.</margin>
Hence you lead such a brutal life, with which God himself is angry; He does not want you to drag out such a beast-like existence, or to be infected or poisoned.

<margin>The Macrocosm is the avenger of the crimes of the Microcosm.</margin>
For the "Great Parent" <note>The Macrocosm/Universe</note> has received from God the power of chastising its children, no less than we have been given the license to punish our children when they act wickedly. The matter and condition are exactly the same, and no distinction needs to be maintained, except in this: that the Great Parent, the Macrocosm, does not have hands and feet like a man. For the hands and rods of the heavens are the stars, with which it inflicts diseases upon us. Let everyone diligently learn and note this.

<margin>The duty of the Euestrum.</margin>
All the works of man, both good and evil, are recorded and noted by the Euestrum of the Sun, and are impressed into the Sun, just as a scribe records the debts of his master in a ledger. In the same way, the Sun also has its own Chancellor and Arch-Scribe within itself to record and describe the deeds and institutions of all men.

<margin>Lichtenberger's commentary on the Apocalypse.</margin>
And <term>Lichtenberger</term> <note>Johannes Lichtenberger (c. 1440–1503), a famous German astrologer whose "Prognosticatio" was widely read and influential in the Reformation era</note> seems to have understood this similarly where he commented on the Apocalypse—and especially, as it pertains to this, regarding the first figure of the revelation of the Sun. Indeed, it is not at all convenient for that wicked and sectarian flock to be betrayed and manifested. For the Moon in and under the Sun, with the seven Candlesticks, could be properly considered and weighed here, were it not for the Sectarian and Pharisaical crowd commanding silence. But because the Star of Bethlehem is sought only in Wittenberg, and the Cross of Christ similarly only in Rome, it is for that reason a good thing that the Pearl and the explanation of the Revelation of John lie hidden and buried. For the genuine sense must be sought and extracted from here, where Christ says:

> *There shall be signs in the Sun and the Moon, etc.*

For to eliminate more than this here would be ill-advised. It is a pity, however, that a certain crude and Pharisaical persuasion in the pulpits is valued more in this place than God himself with all his elect, to whom he has revealed the secrets and hidden things of nature. But in their own time, the plague will seize them too. I would have you know, however, that the night is the body in which everything that works evil rejoices and is carried along—such as evil spirits, criminal men, fornicators, adulterers, and others like them.

<margin>Night is the hiding place of evils; the Sun is the torch of night and the betrayer.</margin>
The Sun, however, is the Elixir and the torch and the light opposed to the night. And just as thieves and robbers, and even the spirits themselves, tremble at the Sun and the day, and the Sun turns away from them greatly—so the Sun also carries with it a witness and an indicator of evil works, who on that day is destined to accuse man on account of all the works which he has performed and intended. Because, therefore, the parents—the Sun and the Moon—of their [own]...

# TREATISE II.

<margin>Heaven as the avenger of human deeds.</margin>
Since the Sun and Moon are the observers of their own children <note>In this context, "children" refers to human beings, who Paracelsus believed were the offspring of the celestial bodies in a spiritual and physical sense.</note>, and they clearly see all their crimes and outrages, they report these same deeds to God. It is not absurd to believe that these same parents (namely the Sun and Moon) are entirely stirred up and sent forth to strike and chastise their children because of the accumulation and multiplication of their sins. For the Sun is that force and power which brings forth and ripens the fruits of all creatures, both the bad and the good; moreover, it gives life to all things.

<margin>The Sun gives life and death.</margin>
If this same Sun is provoked and moved to anger, it also has the power to send diseases and to kill utterly. Now, pay close attention to this: just as an offended and provoked father adopts an entirely tyrannical behavior, so too the Sun changes its brightness and its reflection if it is offended and challenged longer than is fair. And just as lashes and blows follow a parent's anger,

<margin>The stars are the ministers of the avenging Sun.</margin>
so too are blows sent out and inflicted by the Sun. The Sun itself delivers such blows, poisons, and diseases to the stars for our punishment. Afterward, the stars pour this received poison down upon us from above.

<margin>The stars are full of poison.</margin>
For there is no star that does not have some hidden <term>Arsenical</term>, <term>Antimonial</term>, and <term>Realgatic</term> <note>Realgatic refers to Realgar, a toxic arsenic sulfide mineral. Paracelsus uses these terms to describe specific "qualities" of poison rather than just the raw minerals.</note> toxicity stored within itself. This poison is transferred into man in the following manner.

<margin>Man has all poisons within himself from birth.</margin>
Man already has the poisons and the matter of all poisons within himself, in his own body, received from the "clod of earth" at his creation. However, there is none of these human poisons that does not have sulfur secretly and latently joined to it. For this reason, man would be overwhelmed by the force of death every day and at every single moment, if God did not mercifully inhibit the ignition of the stars and planets, and break or hinder the infection.

<margin>How man is infected.</margin>
In this way, the sulfur that lies hidden under the skin of man is ignited by the stars; it is secretly inflamed by the power of salt, sulfur, and the Sun, and this happens through the element of water, just as we have said concerning frogs and their generation. Since man cannot survive without food and drink, but requires them by necessity—and the stars have the power to dominate and pour their force into the <term>Mumia</term> <note>Mumia is the Paracelsian term for the vital, protective life-force or "balsam" inherent in all living things.</note> which is in the element of water, acting like a <term>burning mirror</term> <note>original: *speculum igniferum*; a lens or concave mirror used to focus sunlight to start a fire.</note>—then the stars also strike their reflection into the water through the glare of their light, similar to the eyes of a <term>Basilisk</term> <note>The Basilisk was a mythical serpent capable of killing with a single glance. Paracelsus uses this as a metaphor for the deadly "gaze" of the stars.</note>. They secretly infect the fish within it, and simultaneously the herbs, fruits, and whatever is edible to man on the earth. Indeed, something of this sort can be noticed in fish.

<margin>Fish feel the rays of heaven.</margin>
For if the rays of the stars strike the waters, the fish, feeling them, comes out from its hiding places at the bottom—fish that otherwise might not come out or be seen for several years. For if the *Mumia* in the water is infected for the fish, it is the same as if a broth in a kitchen were ruined by too much salt, so that it is not fit for eating.

<margin>Flowers of water.</margin>
This infection occurs through the "flowers of the waters," which are defiled and infected by the gaze of the stars. For every water has its own "flower," no less than the herbs themselves. For whatever contains *Mumia* and nourishment also has its own flowers, and thus it "blooms." You also notice flowers of this kind on the skin of people with a noble <term>complexion</term> <note>In ancient medicine, "complexion" refers to the balance of bodily humors and qualities that determine a person's health and appearance.</note>.

<margin>Who the "people of gold" are.</margin>
For the vivid and lovely color of the face and the outer skin expressly bears witness to this. Such people ought to be called "people of gold." For just as gold assumes <term>Mercury</term> <note>In alchemy, gold and mercury have a famous affinity; mercury is used to "dissolve" or amalgamate gold.</note> most greedily of all things,

<margin>People of gold are infected quickly.</margin>
so people of this kind are also infected and poisoned first of all. And as you see a burning mirror elicit a blister on a man’s skin if it is turned toward him—with its illustrious brightness and the heat of the sun increased—so the stars also imprint poison upon the element of water. This poison similarly excites blisters and tumors in man, just like the mirror. For if their rays, increased by the approach of the Sun, strike the water, they beget a hidden "greenness" within it; then, from the heat of the sun, that sulfur which arises from the *Mumia* of the water is "cooked out" and resolved into the watery moisture, which is mixed so exquisitely with the water that it escapes the sight of man.

<margin>Burning mirror.</margin>
If men now consume this, they conceive tumors and <term>buboes</term> <note>Swollen lymph nodes characteristic of the bubonic plague.</note>. And this itself is also, in some part, from the <term>Salt-Nitrum</term> <note>original: *S. S. nitri*; refers to Sal Nitrum or saltpeter, which Paracelsus viewed as a fiery, celestial catalyst for chemical reactions and disease.</note>, although it is contrary to nature, because it does not happen at all times. Just as we have recounted that the element of water is infected by the "Basilisk-eyes" of the stars,

<margin>Thin-skinned people are most vulnerable.</margin>
so in the same way, men of a thin and delicate complexion are more promptly and easily seized by the "gaze" of the stars through the skin itself, without the infection of drinking water. For that contagion penetrates through the bare skin of a man no more slowly than through the water itself.

<margin>Intemperance disturbs the Mumia of the body.</margin>
Add to this that man himself sometimes lives too intemperately, stuffing himself with excessive food, by which he disposes his own *Mumia* and sulfurous essence in such a way that it easily catches the sparks of fire and the arsenical poison, like tinder. For what else are the Sun, the stars, and fire, but the spirits of Fire and Sulfur?

## ON PESTILENCE

Next, you will also pay attention to digestion <note>In Paracelsian medicine, "digestion" refers to more than just the stomach; it is the alchemical process by which any substance (or even celestial influence) is matured and transformed within the body.</note>. For if the stars are not provoked privately and by chance, but rather through the sins of men along with the indignation of the Sun, then the digestion of the Sun remains tempered, as does that of the stars, according to their innate and proper degree. However, if the "seeds" <note>original: "semina"; Paracelsus viewed diseases as having seeds that grow when conditions are right.</note> provoke and inflame the degree of the Sun through the irritation of human sins, then Fire and the Spirit of Fire dominate what was once tempered. Then Mars, burning white-hot, sets the Sun on fire to create diseases; finally, Scorpio stings, and the other stars bring help and lend their hands to the task.

<margin>The Sun manifests itself in all Elements.</margin>
Thus, the Sun is fourfold: in the Earth, in the Water, in the Air, and in the Firmament. Consequently, it can infect all four Elements. Now, since man himself possesses the power of the four Elements within him, the pestilential infection also occurs in four ways. Thus, there is a plague of Fire, of Air, of Water, and of Earth. Each individual type has the particular signs of its location and its own specific cure. <margin>Each individual Element is fourfold.</margin> For within man there exist four Fires, four Waters, four Airs, and four Earths. Thus, there is Fire by itself (which is the Sun), Fire of Water, Fire of Air, and Fire of Earth. Likewise, there is Water by itself, Water of Fire, Water of Air, and Water of Earth. There is Air by itself, Air of Fire, Air of Earth, and Air of Water. There is Earth by itself, Earth of Air, Earth of Fire, and Earth of Water. Since these matters are Cabalistic <note>Referring to the Kabbalah, though Paracelsus uses the term broadly to mean "hidden spiritual knowledge" or "mystical interpretation."</note> and perhaps difficult for you to grasp, learn to distinguish them in this way: <margin>Individual elements are fourfold by nature.</margin> There is only one Fire. Yet it exerts its power and operation in all four Elements: in the Firmament, the Air, the Water, and the Earth. Similarly, there is only one Air, yet it displays its operation in the Firmament, Air, Water, and Earth. In the same way, there is only one Water. But what was said of the first two should be understood in the same way for Water and Earth. There is a fourfold Water, a fourfold Earth, Air, and Fire. You will find the causes of these things explained more accurately and at greater length in my great Volume on the *Origin of New Diseases*, under the title *Microcosmic Meteors* <note>original: "Microcosmicæ Meteoricæ"; a concept where diseases in the human body (the microcosm) behave like weather patterns, storms, or "meteors" in the sky (the macrocosm).</note>. <margin>A fine examination <note>original: "Pulcrum mamen," likely a typo for "examen."</note>.</margin> For that the Heaven contains the Earth within itself is sufficiently demonstrated by the thunderstone <note>original: "lapis fulminalis"; a reference to meteorites or stones believed to fall during lightning strikes.</note>. So too the Heaven gives waters, though it be entirely made of fire. It also gives forth air and winds, water and earth, and these four

are the Heaven itself. ## TREATISE.

### CHAPTER ONE.

#### Concerning the Pyromantic Plague and its associated signs.

->SIGNS.<-

**I**t attacks with a deep sleep, accompanied by narcotic-like symptoms and strange signs according to the nature of the incidents. For many already have impure blood before the plague strikes. On the skin of these people, many tiny points and small purple or blackish spots break out. These same people also distort their eyes.

->INCIDENTS.<-

These are Spasm, Tetanus, Fever, and Obstruction of the liver.

<margin>What the obstruction of the liver is, or how it happens.</margin>
<margin>Obstruction of the liver is twofold.</margin>
Obstruction <note>original: "oppilatio"; a technical term for a blockage in the body's channels or organs.</note> is a constriction of the pore and the substance, which occurs from a corporeal constriction with the body: and it is of two types, one in the circumference of the region; the other is Elemented from the air according to the body. Regarding the first, it must be noted that every obstruction is a compression of its own region because of the spirit *Yleidus* <note>The "Yleidus" is a Paracelsian term for a specific spiritual force or "gas" within the body that can cause internal changes.</note>, which, when it has no exit, turns into putrefaction within itself, and this happens without any cause from the external region. The second type is the pestilential Aerial type, sometimes causing the plague, sometimes pleurisy, and sometimes preparing a crisis of the liver. These things are to be noted—not the pricking sensations or the wandering pains, but those which are the plague, pleurisy, and crisis, because the signs of "pricking" are merely symptoms of the disease. However, in this place, we are treating the disease itself, not those slight and small signs. But what is the plague? <margin>What the plague is.</margin> The plague is the air of its own region generated from the "first body" and obstructed without exit, consisting of Arsenical and

<margin>The Time of Digestion is either vitriolized or "ogertine," etc.</margin>
Covering matter. Regarding that poison or the places of its mutation, it must be said that it happens through the Digestion of Nature. For some things take two years, some three, some more, and some less, according to any given time. Therefore, those things must be known about the plague which arise from the "digestion" over time—namely: this time is "vitriolized," <note>Linked to vitriol, or iron/copper sulfates, suggesting a corrosive or acidic nature.</note> and this is *prunella* <note>A term for a specific burning fever or throat infection.</note>; another is *ogertine*, <note>original: "ogertum"; an obscure chemical term used by Paracelsus to describe a specific mineral state associated with salt and pleurisy.</note> and this is pleurisy; another is Arsenical, and this is the plague, caused by the Basilisk of the Firmament <note>A metaphorical reference to a deadly celestial influence that "kills with a look," much like the mythical basilisk.</note>; because there lies the foundation of the diseases of this region, and those things which are held concerning the pleurisy of "ogertine" salt. For according to whatever the time of the ogertine salt may be, pleurisy is generated—that is, a pleuritic obstruction. And those obstructions which are Arsenical belong to the plague; those which are "ogartine" belong to pleurisy; and those of vitriol belong to the *prunellae*.

<margin>How many types of Arsenicals there are.</margin>
The plague is a disease separate from the Arsenical *Yleidus*. There are several types of Arsenicals: namely three "ashy" ones, and these three are in the principal members.
<margin>The plague is a simple disease.</margin>
Indeed, the plague is a simple, contagious disease, occurring through the conjunction of the Elements—the Element of Air and another from the Air—through the pores of the blood, or through internal orifices or the higher passages to the exits: and it is a disease of a timed digestion. By the same reasoning, digestion produces separation; and separation produces the disease. Indeed, there is a "time of separation," from which comes this time and that time, which are composed and possess a "dis-composition." This dis-composition proceeds from the first composite according to the **Arlatum** time from the *S.S.* <note>Likely "Sidus Sacrum" or "Spiritus Sanctus" of Mars, referring to a sacred/celestial influence of the planet Mars.</note> of Mars. <margin>What is Arlatum time?</margin> **Arlatum** time is the time for sequestering or setting apart against the order of the *Yliadus* <note>The "Yliadus" (or Yliaster) refers to the chaotic, primordial matter or the foundational life-cycle of a person.</note>: for that *Yliadus* has a period. <margin>The Yliadus has a triple period.</margin> The period is threefold: namely, the first, second, and third ages.

The first age is that of youth, pertaining to one's state without separation. The second is that of disease, and it declines toward the second part of the world, and brings an age contrary to health. The third is the end and brings death. According to this distinction, all minerals and the sequestration of spirits, as well as the beginning of both the healthy and the evil, take their lead. For in these ages, the *Pyronomus*, *Hydronomus*, *Geonomus*, and *Augurineus* <note>These are technical titles for masters of the elements: Fire-ruler, Water-ruler, Earth-ruler, and an Air-diviner/expert.</note> seek their art: from this also flowed that saying, "it is to come." From this, he speaks of those things of which the ancients made no mention and understood very little. The manner of the age is as follows.

->AGE.<-

<margin>Ilech.</margin>
**T**he "Disposed" is the separation through nature by the *Ilech* <note>The "Ilech" is the internal master or the vital force that directs the development of life and the timing of death.</note>; from there flows the time for resolving—namely, of dying—thing by thing.

### INTERNAL CURE.

> **Take:** Unicorn horn, 3 grains. Melons, 10 in number.
> Bone from a stag's heart, 7 drams.
> Musk and Ambergris, 6 grains each.
> Spirit of Vitriol, 1 dram.
> Mumia, <term>Mumia|A medicinal preparation believed to contain the "life force" of a body, often used as a universal panacea in 16th-century medicine.</term> 4 drams.
> Best Theriac, <term>Theriac|An ancient, complex herbal "super-medicine" or antidote containing dozens of ingredients.</term> 4 drams.

Make a mixture. The dose is 1 dram, or up to 1 and a half drams, morning and evening.

### EXTERNAL CURE.

If buboes <note>The characteristic swollen lymph nodes of the plague.</note> are present externally: Take a beetle (scarab), which you shall crush into a fine powder for an ointment. If the sufferer is a man, you shall take a horned beetle; <note>Likely a stag beetle.</note> rub the powder on with warm wine vinegar and cook the mixture for an interval of 24 minutes over live coals. In this, you shall dip and soak a dried frog for 10 minutes. Finally, bind the frog to the swelling or ulcer and renew it every six hours. For women, frogs and beetles without horns are used.

### *Signs from the Air.*

A tossing of the legs to and fro is seen, the forehead becomes white as ceruse (white lead), the mouth turns livid, breathing becomes difficult, and there is a spasm in the neck.

### *The Complications are:*

Paralysis, coughing up of blood, epilepsy, and gout.

### *Cure, if it is in the first stage.*

> **Take:** White Hellebore, 1 dram.
> Purest sublimated Sulfur, 2 ounces.
> Frankincense and Myrrh, half a dram each.
> Spirit of white Vitriol, half a dram.
> Dose: 1 and a half drams in the morning. After midday, add:
> Mumia, 4 drams (otherwise 3 drams).
> Unicorn horn, Stork's blood, 1 dram (otherwise 1 and a half).
> Dose: 2 to 3 drams.

Proceed externally just as was taught for the plague arising from fire. Only avoid this: do not offer wine to these two types of patients (those suffering from the fire-based and air-based plague). Provide good, pure water mixed with rose vinegar.

### *Signs from the Water.*

They are thirsty but refuse to drink; their lips and eyelids swell, purple spots break out on their cheeks, and both feet swell greatly up to the knees.

> **Take:** Water of Henbane, 4 drams.
> Elder and "Jupiter’s Beard" (Houseleek), 2 drams.
> Malmsey wine, 8 ounces.
> Spirit of Vitriol, 3 drams.
> Musk, Ambergris, and Unicorn horn, 1 dram each.
> Best Theriac, 7 ounces.
> Sublimated white Sulfur, 1 and a half drams.
> Oregano flowers, 1 dram.

Mix. The dose is three times a day before noon, from 1 and a half drams up to 2 or 4 drams. In the intervals, provide a little Malmsey wine from time to time, sprinkled with rose vinegar and decocted with foreign Mumia and valerian.

### *For the Tumor.*

Pour over these as much rose vinegar as is sufficient. Boil them until the gums liquefy, then strain. Add 1 dram of camphor and 1 dram of sublimated sulfur. By this first step, all pus is gathered, the poison is drawn out, and the ulcer is healed. You will find nothing better or more useful for both men and women; likewise, you can safely use this in all types of plague. However, in internal treatment, maintain that distinction which I showed above. For nature herself demands this. Take care, moreover, that neither dogs, nor cats, nor birds are present in the same room as these patients.

### Signs from the Earth

When an abscess occurs with the plague—the first sign of the "Earthly" type—it is accompanied by "the thrush," <note>original: "prunella." A term for a sore throat or inflammation of the mouth and tongue.</note> a burning and dryness of the neck and tongue, along with mania.
Take: 4 ounces of the liquid or juice of Roses.
2 drams of purified white Sulfur.
1.5 drams of Spirit of Vitriol. <note>An early name for sulfuric acid, used here in a highly diluted medicinal form.</note>

For external treatment, proceed exactly as was taught regarding the "Aqueous" plague.

Take: 1 part of this composition, and a half-part each of Laurel berry husks and Amber. Always take an amount the size of half a walnut for one room; throw it upon glowing coals, and close the windows and doors. This is the best rectification of the air.

Through that same spirit, dedicated and assigned to the "animal man," she imagines and imprints a deformity or a certain mark upon the fetus, just as she craved or greatly desired absurd things or foods through her imagination—as is also very well known to the public. Yet all of this is also natural and does not exceed the limits of nature in the least, as you will hear in the remaining chapters.

## CHAPTER I.

<margin>The spirits of the imaginative body are fivefold.</margin>

The reason for this is that man received a soul and reason from God in Paradise, unpolluted; but because of the transgression of the divine commandments, he is now subject and liable to this kind of punishment. For otherwise, human reason, if it were regulated and employed according to the pleasure and commandment of God, would be that very chain and bond by which these five spirits are bound and tamed so that they might restrain their imaginations. Whence it also happens that if a man lives too wantonly, he is forced to endure this immense and horrific disease as a form of punishment.

# CONCERNING THE PESTILENCE

<margin>Four types of spirits inhabiting the 4 Elements.</margin>
Once you have read these things, if you have satisfied your desire, you will also rightly understand from where these five spirits in man arise and proceed. For the World, the parent of man himself, contains within itself four Elemental spirits: one kind of which lives in the waters; another in fire, such as the *winged ones* and *Salamanders*; the third in the Air, such as the *Sylvan spirits*; the fourth in the earth, such as *Gnomes, Lemures, Pygmies, Incubi*, and the like. And moreover, there is a fifth kind, of which many thousands exist, as you will learn in my *Philosophy* concerning the soul of the world.

<margin>The spirits of the fifth kind are infinite. What the Flaga spirits are.</margin>
These spirits, which are inserted into the soul of the Macrocosm <note>The "Greater World" or the universe as a whole.</note> or the greater world, are called *Flaga* <note>In Paracelsian thought, these are spiritual influences or "shadows" that can affect the human mind and body.</note>, as Necromancy and Geomancy teach, in which all these things are explained more fully and accurately. Thus, therefore, O noble sons <margin>Who Scayola and Anachmi are.</margin> *Scayola* and *Anachmi* <note>Technical terms used by Paracelsus to describe spiritual or formative forces involved in the creation of man.</note>, in the creation of Adam, these five kinds of spirits arise. Therefore, so that you may more rightly grasp this chapter, it seems necessary to explain it at greater length. For from this consideration is born the wise, attained, and natural Philosophy of Medicine, just as you can know from my work *Paramirum*. To these you will separately add those fifteen treatises which I wrote with singular diligence concerning Medical industry. From those you will fill in what you desire here. There is also another specific treatise on the 5 *Entities* <term>Entia: the five fundamental causes of disease in Paracelsian medicine</term>, which you shall read, as well as a second treatise on the 5 *Spirits*, a third on the 5 *Matters*, a fourth on the 5 *Senses*, and a fifth on *Death and Life*, and on the *logic of incantation*, which occurs in five ways. In the same way, fifteen ways in which diseases arise are indicated: which it is necessary to follow with fifteen cures and their remedies.

<margin>How the Flounder fish is generated.</margin>
Here, however, you must be warned that that fish, which in maritime places is called the *Flounder*, is a certain supernatural animal. It is produced by the movement of the stars, when the excrement of the stars is shaken down into the waters. That excrement is pure sulfur, for which reason it also floats upon the water. From that, through the digestion of time and the sun, the fish is then generated, which is, materially, like a mistake and a Labyrinth of the Stars. But in heaven itself, from the nature and condition of the stars, <margin>Weeds in heaven.</margin> weeds <note>original: "zizania," referring to the biblical "tares" or weeds sown among wheat; here meaning celestial impurities.</note> exist—not materially, but *spiritually*, through the imagination of the soul of the greater world. I mean Comets and wandering stars. And just as the soul of the world "imagines" and gives birth to a monster of its own kind, so man also does the same through imagination. And just as the *Flounder* fish is round like a rose, so the plague of the imagination also has a round form. Therefore, let this first chapter on the plague generated through imagination be concluded with these things.

### CHAPTER II.

<margin>The laziness of the animal-like man.</margin>
This is the sole wish of man: to be able to prolong life for many years. I speak of the man who lives brutally in the manner of the world—which is the character of the vast majority of men. These people are mostly moved by no care for the pursuit of the highest good, which is eternal life. So that God may, to some extent, punish the complacency of these men and bring their vain thoughts into the light, He denies and suspends the protections of Medicine for them. For the hand of God alone is the sole, highest, and most certain preservation from all diseases. For he whom God guards has found a most certain asylum. With these things having been said, I will now explain to you the second foundation of the generation of this disease in this discourse.

<margin>He who does not trust in God trembles. Dread causes continuous fear.</margin>
From the man who does not place his trust in God, nor cares for Him, God also withdraws His protective hand. It is necessary, therefore, that those who do not flee to God at the time of the plague—which is the punisher and avenger of sins—should be seized by great dread and terror. This fear gives birth to a strong imagination of catching the plague. For what reason, you ask? Surely, the fearful man trusts God the least. From this it happens that he thinks nothing more certain to hang over him than disease and death itself, which continually haunt his imagination. In this way, this man, through his own imagination, generates the Basilisk <note>A mythical serpent whose gaze was lethal; here used metaphorically for the internal poison created by fear within the "Microcosm" or the human body.</note> of the Microcosmic firmament within himself. The order and manner of this generation must be judged from the following example. You see that from the neck of an Indian or Calicut cock <note>A Turkey.</note> certain flesh hangs down and droops, which <margin>The <unclear>wattle</unclear> of the turkey varies thus.</margin> is perpetually red. But if the cock is irritated by that agitation or a kind of agony, that same red flesh now turns blue, now green, and assumes other colors—all of which happens to this living animal. In the peacock you also <margin>The peacock, imagining a snake, casts out rays.</margin> observe that if it ever desires a snake for food, it spreads its tail and casts out its "rays" <note>The "eyes" on a peacock's feathers.</note>: by which imagination it generates a snake within its own body and stomach. Just as these twin examples testify to the imagination of animals, so it is certain that a similar and identical operation occurs in man himself, by which he creates his own...

<margin>A man emits seed upon the sight of a woman.</margin>
...generates and rouses poison within itself, as discussed more at length in our *Musalogia* <note>original: *Musalogia*; likely a reference to a specific Paracelsian work on the arts or the influence of the mind.</note>, etc. If it happens naturally that a man, looking quite ardently at a graceful and beautiful woman, is driven to the point that through the lust of the flesh he emits seed of his own accord: why, I ask, can this same thing not also happen in this case? There is no difference in any other way, except that the one concerning the man appears more "natural" because of its more frequent occurrence; meanwhile, the other, because it happens more rarely or more offensively, seems to require a clearer proof. Yet, in the meantime, there is no one who does not know that some people are so constituted that if they happen to see someone else vomiting (as happens often by chance), they are themselves likewise driven to vomit through the image of disgust. Why, then, is there a need for a long and more accurate demonstration of the former point, when the matter can be easily understood? Some might object to me here, as if in this point I were acting like a Heathen or a Pagan. But yet, just as much benefit as a pearl brings when cast before a pig: so much utility will those draw from these writings of mine who find it a matter of shame to learn and investigate the truth itself. Someone might even insist that the example I gave regarding the person vomiting happens naturally through natural sight, whereas the reason for a plague conceived through the imagination is far different. To this, I answer thus: The eyes do indeed see a thing, and they present the appearance of what they see to the mind.

<margin>Imagination comes before sight.</margin>
However, that image is much closer to the soul or the imagination than to the eyes. For unless your thoughts and the spirits of your life existed, your seeing would be nothing. For if you wish to see, that happens entirely by your will. Therefore, the will is first, and the sight is second. In the same way, your thought and imagination exist as the mother of the plague about to be born in yourself, introduced by yourself.

But since I have established this foundation upon which I intend to build my opinion: now the arduous confirmation of my argument will be subjoined. I would wish all physicians to be warned to understand this discourse of mine rightly and clearly, and to intimately weigh and turn over in their minds the <term>Characteristic Art</term> <note>The art of using specific signs, symbols, or "characters" to influence the spiritual or physical world.</note>, through which the imagination is calmed and the plague itself is most easily cured of all. Let there be no other persuasion for you Physicians than that the *Characteristic Art* truly rests and leans upon its own natural and solid foundation.

<margin>The power and certainty of the Characteristic Art.</margin>
For if someone is able to read some pleasant history—such as those of *Melusina*, *Danhauser*, the *Berner*, *Hildebrand* <note>References to popular medieval legends and folk heroes used here to illustrate how stories occupy and soothe the mind.</note>, and the like—for the sake of passing the time and consoling grief: then a cure of that same kind against the imagination will be possible through the characteristic art.

<margin>The ingenuity of Jacob.</margin>
The example of Jacob testifies to this, who placed and presented variegated rods before the sheep when they were watering <note>A reference to Genesis 30, where Jacob influenced the markings of offspring through what the parent animals saw.</note>. Even if this could be believed to be natural, it nevertheless happened in a supernatural way. And by the same reasoning that a mother imprints a mark upon her fetus through imagination: so the same thing happens here as well. And just as stars of a Saturnine and wintry nature freeze and condense water: so it happens with the poison generated along with the plague, so that the buboes <note>The swollen lymph nodes characteristic of the plague.</note> are hard

<margin>Whence comes the hardness of buboes.</margin>
at first, before the abscesses ripen; which hardness is nothing other than the coagulation of the blood.

<margin>Blood is hot and moist.</margin>
For blood is of a hot and moist nature. And since all poison is cold, the coagulation of the blood follows from this. Indeed, just as the Moon, Saturn, and the cold stars freeze water: so in man himself the <term>Microcosmic Moon</term> <note>Paracelsus identifies the brain and the imaginative faculty with the Moon within the "Small World" of the human body.</note>, residing in the brain and existing as the imagination, freezes and infects the blood.

<margin>Imagination is the Moon of the brain.</margin>
<margin>A menstruating woman infects a mirror.</margin>
And by the same reasoning that a woman subject to the menstrual flow contaminates a mirror by her sight alone: so a man likewise infects himself. For a man can bring this effect about unexpectedly, whether knowingly or unknowingly, during sleep and waking alike. And just as a woman born under a malicious ascending star can enchant an infant in the cradle through her sight and words: so it can also very easily happen that one man can inflict this disease upon another through a curse.

Hence the occasion and handle is provided to me to comment in this place also upon something concerning the reason and foundation of incantation. And first, indeed, I shall speak concerning the virtue of <term>Mumia</term> <note>In Paracelsian medicine, "Mumia" refers to the vital force or spiritual essence remaining in a body, often used in sympathetic magic or medicine.</note>. Afterward, concerning the pregnant woman who dies in childbirth.

<margin>A woman's reason is weaker than a man's.</margin>
Regarding women, however, you will first note this: that on account of their simplicity and weakness, they by no means have senses as ready or reason as unhindered for the good as men themselves have. You can take proof of this from the fact that they follow sorcery more eagerly, which men do less. For the <term>Maker of a Thousand Arts</term> <note>original: *Milleartifex*; a traditional epithet for the Devil.</note> can more readily and easily compel them to such things by his deceptions than he can a man. Hence we construct a foundation of this sort: a pregnant woman in the time of plague [is more susceptible than] another...

# ON PESTILENCE

One person dies from another because the poison and malignancy of this disease are undoubtedly contagious. Furthermore, when a woman carries a child in her womb, the infant is very often infected along with the mother. For this reason, singular care must be taken for pregnant women so that they are not left alone; or, if they feel the infection, they must not be rashly abandoned by denying them protection and medicines. In my own time, I have frequently seen this happen with great pity: pregnant women, while the plague was raging, were destitute of all help in the midst of the narrow straits and pains of childbirth. This injustice was afterwards followed by a horrendous epidemic throughout the entire region.

<margin>The imagination of a pregnant woman doubles the evil.</margin>
For if a pregnant woman is about to die in the very tortures of labor, one can easily imagine what thoughts and fantasies she conceives and stirs up at that time. Without a doubt, she meditates and speaks within herself: "Since I and my little one <note>original: "pullo"; literally "chick" or "young," used here tenderly for the unborn child.</note> must die so miserably here, destitute of all human help, I would wish and desire that all people be swept away and slaughtered with me by the same fate." This imprecation is then followed by a "rain"—that is, the doubled poison of this disease. Nor can it be denied here that God Himself redoubles the punishment because humans so foully desert one another in such great distress. Moreover, if power was given even to Satan against *Job* to strike him with the worst ulcers, it is easy to imagine how diligently in this case, too, he will exert his vengeful malice against those inhuman deserters. For he has numerous ready handmaidens for such punishment: young and old witches who are accustomed to travel to the Brocken <note>original: "Bructerum"; referring to the Brocken mountain in Germany, a legendary site for witches' gatherings.</note>.

<margin>The power of the poisoners' curse.</margin>
These very witches are also instigated by Satan so that, when they are about to die, they call down the worst and most ill-omened curses upon the human race. This has been discovered in many ways and in many places.

<margin>The poisoner is exceedingly hostile to pregnant women.</margin>
For since God strikes these witches with the plague in a singular way because of their unworthy sorcery, they, when they feel death at the door, are accustomed to curse their neighbors—especially pregnant women and those in childbed—with an ill omen in this manner.

<margin>The nature of the poisoners' pact with spirits.</margin>
They enter into a covenant and make a bargain with the spirits whom they served and loved while alive, so that they may hide and bury the <term>Mumia</term> <note>In Paracelsian thought, "Mumia" refers to the vital essence or life force remaining in a body after death, which can be manipulated for magic or medicine.</note> of the dead beneath the thresholds of churches, where people must walk over them as they enter and exit. Those spirits, out of hatred for the human race, make that <term>Mumia</term> of the dead bodies even more virulent. Such things have been found and dug up from beneath the thresholds of churches in *Rottweil*, *Wasserburg*, *Passau*, *Eger*, and other places; and the witches themselves, examined under severe torture, confessed that such things were done in this way. We have heard of these same practices from books, or from the kin and associates of the witches themselves.

<margin>A story of witches.</margin>
In *Rottweil*, a certain witch who had been committed to prison often and frequently called out to and summoned her spirit in her sleep, just as a wakeful person calls another. Since other guilty prisoners were also kept confined in the same jail, they reported what they heard to the jail keeper. The matter being judged sufficient for torture, she was put to the question and confessed everything as it was.

<margin>Satan’s trickery.</margin>
For Satan is also the betrayer of his own ministers, so that he may plunge them through this path into despair and the denial of GOD, and graft them into his own kingdom. Such are the works of that old deceiver; these are the wages those hags <note>original: "lamiarum"; refers to witches or malevolent spirits often associated with the kidnapping or harming of children.</note> receive, which they deserve for the worship and love they bestowed upon Satan.

Indeed, we also discovered at *St. Veit* and *Villach* that witches, during the time of the plague, took earth and dust from the mounds of the buried and, by their magical art, prepared it so that they stirred up a most savage and Raging plague, by which many thousands of people were infected and slaughtered. However, the method of preparation must by no means be revealed to them. They had also infected and poisoned the milk and the cattle to such an extent that the livestock themselves fell dead in herds along with the people. To root out these outrages, the magistrate ought to strive diligently to support pious and honest <term>Magi</term> <note>The "Magi" here are not "magicians" in a modern sense, but wise men or practitioners of "Natural Magic" who understand the hidden forces of nature and can counter spiritual poisons.</note> who understand such matters.

<margin>Pious Magi are to be supported by the magistrate.</margin>
I could indeed publish a special treatise about them, so that their arts and machines might be made manifest. But because of the malicious, such things should by no means be spread abroad by pen or quill. For many shameful things could be introduced at the same time, which it is better to keep silent.

Meanwhile, it is right that eyes be turned toward monasteries and brothels on account of detestable fornication and unusual lust. Your care and inspection, O princes and nobles, must be spent here. For in those places, enormous sins are committed which afterwards give a beginning to the plague. For in those dens of vice and colleges, much "seed" <note>likely referring to biological waste or the spiritual essence of lustful acts.</note> is received and collected by spirits, through which the witches afterwards attractively [produce] such...

<margin>Fornication in taverns and monasteries must be abolished.</margin>

By a force of this kind, they prepare a poisonous <term>Mumia</term> <note>Mumia refers to the vital life-force or "balsam" inherent in the human body; Paracelsian medicine taught that this essence could be harvested or, as described here, corrupted into a "contagion" by malicious means.</note> and craft a contagious poison, so that many thousands of people can be infected and contaminated by it. ### On the Magnetic Power of the Mumia in Man.

<margin>The spirit and sidereal body of man are a Magnet.</margin> **T**he **sidereal spirit and body** <note>The "sidereal" or "astral" body was believed to be an intermediate body made of "star-stuff" that connects the physical body to the heavens.</note> is a magnet and of a magnetic nature in man; it is a spirit born from the stars, just as Augury teaches. This kind of spirit and sidereal body has a kinship with the stars. And first, we shall prove this magnetic power of the sidereal body within the elementary <note>Physical or material.</note> body of man by this reasoning: This sidereal body is a spirit in respect to the elementary and earthly man, and it performs spiritual operations. For just as the earthly Magnet is a spirit within its own body and attracts things to itself, so also the body and spirit of the sidereal body in man attract things to themselves. <margin>Lunatics are moved by the new moon.</margin> This is the **Magnet of the Microcosm** <note>The "Microcosm" or "little world" is the human being, viewed as a reflection of the "Macrocosm" or the entire universe.</note>. The sidereal body and spirit attract the virtues of the stars, just as you notice in lunatics at the time of the new moon, when the spirit of the sidereal body and the Magnet of man exerts and brings forth the property of the new Moon. And just as it is that Moon which is attracted through the magnetic virtue of the innate sidereal body and spirit in man, so it also has the property and nature that the precursor of the **Macrocosm's Moon** is felt in man at the time of the new moon; when one is "lunatic," he becomes agitated and fierce. For at that time, the lunatic speaks similarly to one who is drunk from must or wine. There, one clearly notices the correspondences, properties, and agreements of those magnetic virtues which the spirit and sidereal body of man have with the stars themselves. And, what you must carefully note: the Moon of the Macrocosm is a mirror and a body in which the spirit of the sidereal body and the Magnet of man sees during sleep; and from that same source, he takes and brings forth all dreams, however many can happen to a man in sleep. From here, dreams and the things murmured during sleep arise.

<margin>How a fearful person is infected.</margin> Now, therefore, if a man is fearful and full of dread, having stirred up his own imagination and impressed that dread upon himself, the Moon in heaven acts as a body through such a medium, with the stars assisting. If the fearful and dread-filled person gazes at the Moon with a full and perfect imagination, then he gazes into a great poisonous mirror of nature, and in this way, the sidereal spirit and the Magnet of man are infected and poisoned through the stars and the Moon. But you will understand this matter more fully in this way: <margin>How a fearful person infects the eye.</margin> A fearful man turns his eyes in Nature into those of a **Basilisk** <note>A legendary serpent said to kill with its gaze; Paracelsus uses it here to describe how a "poisonous" internal state can be projected outward through the eyes.</note> through his imagination, and he infects the mirror, the Moon, and the stars through himself first. Afterwards, if the Moon has been infected by the imagining man—which happens easily and quickly because of the magnetic force which the sidereal body and spirit share with the stars, the Moon, and the planets of the great nature—then the man himself is also infected by that mirror of the Moon and stars into which he looked. <margin>A menstruating woman is poisonous.</margin> This happens because you see it occur in a natural way as well: a pregnant woman, during her time of menstruation, stains and fouls a mirror with her gaze. For at that time she is poisonous and has the eyes of a Basilisk because of her menstrual and poisonous blood. ## THIRD TREATISE.

*Concerning the Poison of the Planets, that is, concerning poisonous Fire.*

*How Fire is born into the poison of the plague from the seven Planets.*

### CHAPTER ONE.

**E**very created thing naturally desires to return to that which it was before creation. This is the foundation of all our Philosophy. And from our writings, you will easily judge what we are aiming at in this chapter. For we are dealing here with the generation and corruption of the Elements, as well as with the poison that comes forth from that dissolution, concerning which a specific chapter has been established in *On Life and Death*, which is especially necessary for a Physician to know.

<margin>
Elements out of nothing.
</margin>

For the Elements were created out of nothing: whence they also strive toward nothingness again. Let fire be an example for us. Whatever it seizes, it reduces to nothing, although one thing more quickly and easily than another. So in turn water reduces fire to nothing if it touches it, and fire in turn consumes water, and one is perpetually contrary to the other. And yet this happens at least in particular instances.

<margin>
Elements contrary to one another.
</margin>

You shall hold this as the reason why we propose to you the doctrine of corruption and dissolution. For it is no slight defect if he who wishes to be held as a Philosopher does not hold this nerve <note>To "hold the nerve" is a metaphor for grasping the central point or essential strength of a system.</note>. For by this method truth is sought in all matters of Medicine, if the Natural Physician has explored the reason and causes of the corruption of all Elementary things. Therefore, the matter stands thus: just as you see that any iron can be poisoned by poisonous things, so also copper, lead, and tin can be similarly infected. But here you must be forewarned of a slight yet necessary matter. Note this: by the same reasoning that vinegar can be poisoned, so also salt can be infected. And although I do not divulge this very willingly on account of certain malicious persons, nevertheless I cannot altogether hide the secret...

<margin>Salt and vinegar extract Mercury from iron.</margin>
Anyone who cuts meat or bread with this and eats it will not escape the power of the poison. For salt and vinegar extract the <term>Mercury</term> <note>In Paracelsian chemistry, Mercury is one of the "Three Primes" (with Salt and Sulfur) representing the volatile, transformative principle of a substance.</note> from all iron, and in this way they render the iron poisonous. From this it follows that many diseases are inflicted upon man through acidic foods or those cooked with vinegar which infect the knives; because the poison from those knives is eventually ingested into the body. However, Salt and vinegar are not poisons in themselves for this reason: rather, the iron gives off the poison if the salt and vinegar touch it.

<margin>Fish cooked in copper vessels with salt are harmful.</margin>
Likewise, if a tench <note>original: "tinca"; a freshwater fish of the carp family.</note> is boiled with salt in a copper pot: along with that food, something poisonous is also ingested into the body, from which thereafter diseases emerge that are by no means to be trifled with. Not only do men fail to pay attention to this, but they cannot even be persuaded that it happens. Therefore, let this kind of poison from iron and copper be a warning to you.

<margin>What diseases come from Martial Poison.</margin>
For in this way, from <term>Martial Poison</term> <note>original: "Veneno Martiali"; in alchemy, Mars is the planetary correspondence for the metal Iron. Now, if an invading plague finds such poison already previously ingested into the body, then the poison of the plague and the poison of Mars encounter one another. The sick experience for themselves, to their own detriment, what finally results from this. And if you, Natural Physicians, turn your mind to these things, you will find more than Galen himself, or Montagnana, or any others have handed down. Furthermore, lead is also infected by its own peculiar method.

<margin>Sulfur infects lead and tin.</margin>
For if it is rubbed with sulfur, or if a copper pot coated inside with tin is used, and fish are boiled in it with sulfurous water, then the lead or tin becomes poisonous, and the food consumed is extremely dangerous. However, it is hardly possible for the poorer common folk to always avoid and turn away from such infections. Therefore, I do not write such things for them, as they are ignorant of Philosophy; rather, my business is with the physicians, whom I teach so that they may more easily and surely understand, learn, and recognize the <term>Five Essences</term> <note>original: "5. Entia"; Paracelsus's theory that all diseases stem from five possible sources: the stars (Ens Astrale), poisons/nature (Ens Veneni), the mind (Ens Spirituale), fate/magic (Ens Pagoycum), or God (Ens Deale).</note> of diseases. Now, therefore, the fourth treatise follows, handing down the cure for such diseases.

## CHAPTER ONE.
### *On the 5 Essences of all diseases.*

<margin>The Pagoyic Essence etc.</margin>

For otherwise you might omit the <term>Pagoyic Essence</term> <note>original: "Ens Pagoycum"; the influence of sorcery or bewitchment on health.</note> and the <term>Spiritual Essence</term>, and thus despise or pass over the cure for the twin diseases emerging from them. Similarly, a disease from the <term>Divine Essence</term> <note>original: "Ente Deali"; a disease sent directly by God as a trial or punishment.</note> does not fit a spiritual cure in any way: which must be properly understood.

<margin>The rites of witches in enchanting men.</margin>
<margin>Magorista, etc.</margin>
The sorcery is prepared by the witch: she takes a piece of wood and allows a spider to crawl upon it. Afterwards, she places a thread across the spider near the other end, and having brought another piece of wood, she strikes and shakes the spider so that it bursts apart in the middle and pours out its poison. This done, she draws the thread through the spider and allows it to dry. After all these things are performed, she takes wax, or in its absence, freshly baked bread, and from it she fashions a small image of a man or woman, somewhat resembling the person she intends to harm, shaping it with a strong imagination. Once the **little man** <term>homunculus</term> <note>A "little man" or effigy used in sympathetic magic to represent the target of a spell.</note> is formed in the name of the person to be harmed, the witch measures the limb of that man which she intends to harm on that image—whether the image be small or large—using the thread. Having taken the measurement according to the thickness of the limb to be harmed, she cuts the thread. And if it is summer, so that she can obtain either a frog or a toad: she binds the thread around the body of that beast. If the beast afterwards leaps into the water, the man feels heavy pains in that measured limb, in this manner: if the frog crawls into flowing water, the man is never free from pain for a moment in that limb around which the thread was wrapped. But if it be stagnant water or a swamp, then again he is not free from pain. For the vital spirit of that limb, whose measurement was taken, neither rests nor can rest, no less than flowing water is quiet. The cause of this stirred-up pain is this: that the vital spirit of sensation dwells in the blood and is the carrier of blood, never resting in the life of man. Whence that limb of the man cannot be at peace. But whoever you are, whether learned or unlearned, you ought not to wonder at these things, much less doubt that all this happens and occurs naturally. For he who either does not believe or cannot believe this, by that very fact reveals that he does not yet understand the magnetic power of devils and poisons. What use then is the title of "Doctor" to such a fool who has not yet experienced or understood these childish things? But learn more about these matters.

<margin>The needle with which a corpse is sewn into linens.</margin>
She also takes a needle from a funeral <note>original: "acum de funere"; a needle used to sew a shroud, considered to have dark magical properties.</note>, or another, and passes the thread through the eye of the needle; she pierces the eye of a frog with the needle and pulls half the thread through; the other half of the thread she passes through the eye of the little image itself. In this way, the man is blinded and remains blind as long as the witch wishes. But if the frog should die, no mortal can thereafter bring help to that man in whose name the little image was made. Similarly, if she pierces the genital member of the little image, the man is rendered impotent for sexual union. And whatever limb she has measured and cut the measure for: that man remains paralyzed in that limb until death. Thus, whatever she does with that measurement happens naturally to the man himself. Therefore, we ought seriously and ardently to pray to God in our hearts that He lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from all evil. For the punishments which God sends upon men are varied; although such things do not happen by the counsel of God, but by our own merit. For even though God has enough will and power to preserve and deliver man from all evil, He nevertheless often permits such punishments because of our misdeeds, just as it is written, that *He will avenge the iniquities of the parents upon the children unto the third and fourth generation* <note>A reference to Exodus 20:5.</note>. And if you read what God allowed Satan to do to Job, you will without doubt understand these things abundantly. Devils sometimes also possess the whole man, which is more serious. Who anywhere can prevent this except the divine power alone? Therefore, one must cry out to God with a groaning and trembling heart; there is always enough danger at the door.

In like manner, they take also the poison of toads and other beasts, and many such things, which are not to be named more explicitly here. A word to the wise is sufficient. They also take a wax <term>Homunculus</term> <note>A small, artificial human figure used here as a "poppet" or effigy for sympathetic magic.</note>, and bind around its body a fragment or part of a garment polluted with the menses, and to it they add dead <term>Mumia</term> <note>original: "Mumia." In this context, it refers to the concentrated life-force or "balsam" extracted from a corpse, believed to have potent magical and medicinal properties.</note> from some corpse—especially one that died from some abscess <note>Specifically a "pestilential bubo," the swelling associated with the plague.</note>, by which means sheep and pigs often perish. Once that measure or binding is applied—the dimensions of which they took from the limbs of the <term>Homunculus</term>—they tie that part of the polluted garment upon it. Then, in the person whom they have decided to harm, the entire blood in the body is corrupted and, as it were, dies, and the whole of it is filled with ulcers, so that he must finally die. And thus ends the first treatise on incantation. There now follows the second part concerning sorceries, and the execrable arts and works of witches, in this manner.

<margin>Only the Moon fashions the faces of animals.</margin>
Witches take a mirror, set or inserted into wood. They place this into water contained in some vessel, so that the smoothness of the mirror looks toward the sky. Upon this mirror they place a wreath made of bits of a garment polluted with menstrual blood, so that the wreath surrounds and embraces the mirror. They do this for this reason: because they know that a person receives the form of their face from the Moon alone during conception. For because of this formation, it was so ordained by the Creator that all animals should receive the form of their body and face from the Moon. For the Moon alone provides the form and image of the face. And this is known to all women who have reached the proper age. From this, witches also learned that process, though for misuse. Therefore, since a person often looks at the Moon at night, they also infect it more frequently. I speak of witches with the mirror arranged in the said manner. For as soon as the Moon sends down its rays into the water and the mirror, it infects the mirror through the wreath woven from the remains of the menstruated garment. And since the mirror itself also emits a certain reflection and brightness, it likewise infects the Moon. Thus, then, both the Moon and the mirror infect each other, no differently than two people infect each other with their eyes. For if one suffers in the eyes, the other who has looked at the damaged ones is also harmed in their own sight. But if the mirror has now been infected in this way, then the witch keeps it poisoned. Afterwards, if she wishes to enchant some person, she takes a <term>Homunculus</term> previously made of wax, or pitch, or bread, or mud, and places the said wreath upon its head, and directs the brightness from the poisoned mirror toward either the face or another part of the body of the <term>Homunculus</term>, and she curses with the plague that person in whose name the homunculus was made, suddenly and hastily, while the witch is still occupied in her full imagination. And from this curse the person immediately conceives buboes and carbuncles in their body. And this is a "particular" plague <note>A localized or individual case of the plague, as opposed to a general epidemic (a "universal" plague).</note>, such as often seizes a man when the infection is not publicly spreading. But if the witch seeks to infect someone’s eye, looking first into that poisoned mirror, she then takes herself to the places where the person stays whom she wishes to "favor" in this way. This person, as soon as they look into the eyes of the witch, draws the poison from them into their own eyes, and in this way is infected. Therefore, this process is the same as that of other eyes which are naturally in a bad state due to a gaze directed at bleary eyes, from which that contagion and infection flows into the eye of the beholder. But the witch heals her own eyes again with that menstrual cloth from which the wreath was woven. For she lights a hearth, and continually fixes her eyes upon the fire, and binds a bit of the garment infected with menstrual blood to a stone and throws it into the fire: afterwards she catches her own wash or urine, and with it extinguishes the fire.

It also describes a sympathetic ritual involving fire and urine for the witch to cure her own eyes after performing these acts.</summary>
