And the old schools of physicians were ignorant of all these things. For they by no means understood Philosophy herself, the parent of man: about which I have written elsewhere.

## Conjunction.

The conjunction <note>The meeting or joining point.</note> of man and the plague is of this sort. If a man is born, he brings with him the "subject" of all diseases that can be inflicted upon him by the heavens or the elements; that is, the diseases themselves happen from four things. For as many diseases as there are, there are just as many subjects. Now pay attention to what produces disease.

<margin>Foods are the subject of diseases entering from outside.</margin>
External fire does this, entering into a person and separating within the body, such as food, drink, air, and so on. In the food itself, the disease lies hidden; and foods in the body are the "subject" in which diseases thrive and are born. Thus, if fire finds wood, it ignites and burns it. And such is the conjunction of similar things, because like finds its like. Thus man is the "subject," and the disease falling upon him from the outside is like fire to wood, which can burn in the Sun. Just as a color is now made by fire, so the course of the <term>Olympus</term> <note>original: "olympi"; Paracelsus often uses "Olympus" to refer to the heavens or the stars as a functional system.</note> finally becomes fiery in man at its own time.

<margin>All stars are in man.</margin>
For man contains all the stars within himself, just like the firmament and the three remaining parts. Now, if that celestial course passes into a "generation" (such as a disease or something else), then this disease by no means proceeds unless a "subject" is present upon which it can work. Thus, if a sweltering year is imminent, and the Sun glows so fiercely that it scorches and wastes away the trees, and dries up or burns the stalks—nevertheless, it affects none of them except what is "subject" to fire. If such a subject is not present, the heat achieves nothing. There is a similar course in the body, called the "course of heaven," capable of approaching. While it does this, it becomes a disease, whether it be putrefaction or something else. For nothing happens differently than what you see when the heavens, by their motion, rot the mud and fill it with crickets, and make wood full of worms. By a similar reasoning, the bodily course also causes all diseases to be born in the body. That which is healthy remains so if the course seizes nothing from its subject. For such is the origin of all natural diseases which are born in those who are overcome. And this origin is for one part. But the other origin, which is treated here regarding the *plague*, does not behave in the same way: it is a conjunction of the heavens, and it does not arise in the body, but outside it, and yet it terminates in the body and completes its operation. Thus, if someone throws a spear into a body, it does not grow in the body, nor is it the body's matter, nor is it a creature similar to the body; yet the body's disease and death result from it. In this way, the *plague* joins with the body, and its strike is like hail, which strikes one person violently, another more lightly, and misses this one entirely. Thus, therefore, this disease is generated preternaturally, not like other natural diseases.

## BOOK TWO.
### On the Plague.

*What* has been said so far regarding the *plague* looks only at that origin which comes from the *wrath of God*. As long as this persists, the *Physician* has no business with the sick person regarding their health. Nevertheless, trust must be placed in the *mercy of God*, until by His *grace* He grants *Medicine*. From this *grace*, the *Physician* begins, equipped with power and natural remedies at the same time, as this second book explains. For if a man can *repent* of a murder committed or an enemy struck, even though he cannot make the deed undone: how much more can *God repent* of His punished creature? Meanwhile, nothing escapes His hand, by which He can soothe and change the inflicted hardships. Since these things are so, natural secrets must be investigated by us by every right, and the natural use of natural things, as handed down by others, ought to be received and employed: not to go against the origin itself, but rather, if by the permission of God a disease has become "natural," that *experience* (as much as God has bestowed) may be applied, and the punishment and torment itself not be the only focus.

## On the Ignition.

<margin>Lightning strikes the oak most often.</margin>
**J**ust as a spark falls from flint into tinder: so it is here also with the plague. And just as a spark consumes and carries away the tinder: so too does the plague. Now, the flint is the heavens; the tinder is the earth. In the same way, then, that lightning is cast down from heaven into the earth with the greatest speed, so that the crash and the strike happen at once: so in man, too, the fire is forced out. And just as the proverb says—that lightning most often strikes the fir tree, the oak, and men or cattle themselves—so it also strikes its own peculiar places in man: namely, the Ears, the Armpits, and the Groin. What other cause or reason is there for these three locations than that which governs the locations of lightning? Who can investigate this enough? Wherever the Highest sends his lightning, there he designates a place for himself; no one here can emulate or inquire into nature. Nor do these things happen according to the usual order and causes of nature. Therefore, no one will truly know them. For why are the ears struck more than the nose? Why the armpits more than the elbows? Why the groin more than the navel?

<margin>Supernatural things are not grasped by natural judgment.</margin>
For whatever transcends the limits of nature cannot be known by any scrutiny of reason. In this case, both the disease and the location—as we have said—are above nature. Now, if the leaping fire seizes and ignites, first a shivering <note>original: "horror"</note> and then heat takes hold, for these reasons: the spark that ignites instills a coldness because it dissolves the humors and moistens the body. Thus, snow melted and dissolved by the sun produces cold. But if, this being overcome, the heat now begins to dominate, then it strives to dry out the moisture of the body.

<margin>The source of shivering and cold in the plague.</margin>
For this same reason, sweat follows, because the "snow" within the man has been liquified and cannot return again to its form; therefore, it is driven out of the body. And because of this snow, the sweat is appropriate and good. Furthermore,
<margin>A comparison of earthquakes and the plague.</margin>
just as lightning, when it strikes, shakes the earth with its crash and moves houses and courtyards: so here, in this case, the impending earthquake is nothing other than the natural crash of the lightning—invisible in nature. When this strikes, the whole body is lifted and shaken as long as the motion lasts. When the earthquake ceases and returns to the center, the trembling and jolting also cease. And this "earthquake" in man is natural, as is its cause. It is a portion of that earthquake of which Christ made mention in the Gospel <note>A reference to Luke 21:11: "And there shall be great earthquakes in divers places, and famines, and pestilences."</note>. Such is its cause. For every lightning bolt lifts and shakes the earth. As the crash vanishes, the burning follows. That which has been ignited occupies the whole house of the whole man. There, the liver glows and is driven to wrath, and it thirsts. There, the head throbs because of the excessive burning of the brain. There, the heart trembles because the lung does not pour out enough cooling upon it. There, all the parts of the body are afflicted and sob out their suffering. As this burning grows, the strengths of the body flee and slip away, like a mouse from a burning house.

<margin>The twofold eruption of the plague.</margin>
The lightning, however, settles in its usual and known place, and erupts from time to time—just as a mole throws up earth in a field—and so it wraps itself up, as it were, and forces an exit for itself in two ways: either inward or outward. Wherever it finally breaks out, it does not do so without terror and danger. If it turns inward, the signs of death come forward, and a vision of its own mortification is shown to every single limb. For death and destruction attack in various ways. And, as experience testifies, many and abominable signs of death are seen from time to time, which are not at all tolerable to nature. Therefore, having seen these things, be mindful that the plague and the time of punishment are present or pressing, of which it was said: *And there shall be pestilences* <note>original: "Et erunt pestilentiæ."</note>.

### The War Led from Above.

<margin>Crimes do not remain unpunished.</margin>
**F**rom this follows our contention, discord, war, robbery, misery, and the shedding of blood. For there is no son who, having offended his father, is not punished by him. And our "father" is not only our blood, but is also the magistrate <note>The civil authority or government</note>. Therefore, it is no sin to seek peace, security, and tranquility. If it happens otherwise, how—I ask—could crimes pass by so unpunished that the robber is not put on the wheel and the thief not raised on the cross? For if subjects do not obey at all, it is the magistrate's duty to restrain them with punishments. But if they act too remissly, they have a superior father by whom they themselves, along with the rebellious subjects, are punished. That father is the heavens, like the parent of the <term>Limbus</term> <note>In Paracelsian thought, the *Limbus* is the primordial "great chaos" or first matter from which all things were created.</note>, who is the next avenger after the magistrate. But if even he does not perform his duty exquisitely, there remains the first parent of all: GOD. Now, therefore, note that the avenging punishments are diseases. For is it not a disease for someone to be fixed to a wheel or a cross? Indeed it is. Is that not also a plague? Indeed. Thus, the parent punishes some with the noose, others with the plague. For to every parent belongs his own

# BOOK II.

<margin>Heaven, the avenger of crimes.</margin>
...and as the rod is to the magistrate, so is each person’s punishment suited to them. It follows from this that, after human judgment, heaven itself avenges crimes with its own rods <note>The "rod" (ferula) is a recurring metaphor for a tool of discipline or punishment.</note>. Now, truly, heaven punishes no one unless it is provoked and irritated into seeking vengeance. For just as a magistrate punishes no one without cause, so too does heaven. Therefore, the origin of these diseases is within ourselves; heaven sends them upon us because of our wicked deeds, sins, and dishonest lives. For if we devoted ourselves to honesty, patience, and tranquility, none of these things would happen, nor would we know anything of the rod of punishment, but would be entirely free from it. From this same provocation, the *fire of Sodom and Gomorrah* was brought down, which, descending from heaven, consumed them. If they had not brought this punishment upon their own heads, heaven would not have spat fire upon them. Unless men had provoked heaven, it would never have turned into water, nor would the flood have overwhelmed them. For all these things flowed from the evils of men. Heaven is the avenger and punisher closest to us. And whatever is punished in a natural way, attribute that to heaven, as if to our father, the Limbus <term>Limbus: A Paracelsian term referring to the primordial "chaos" or primal matter from which all things were created; here used as the cosmic parent or reservoir of all physical potential</term>, who has the power to punish us. For God, who created us, subjected us to heaven and gave it power over both fire and water, so that it might punish the children produced from its *limbus* in its own way.

<margin>Natural punishments are to be ascribed to heaven.</margin>
For natural death and its precursors—diseases—come forth from it as from our parent. Therefore, it is right for us to remember that God has not exempted us from the rod of this parent, but has subjected us to it entirely. The punishment, therefore, which we stir up against ourselves, is to be referred entirely to this source.

<margin>Diseases are the precursors of death.</margin>

## The Star of Presage.

<margin>Presage is twofold: of Nature and of Wrath.</margin>
A twofold presage is therefore drawn from the stars of heaven and the firmament. One concerns all nature, our own characteristics, diseases, life, and health—just as we said regarding death, because we have risen from the *limbus*.

<margin>As the Limbus is, so is the man.</margin>
For as the *limbus* behaves, so do we inherit its nature. If an Astronomer <term>Astronomer: In this era, the term encompassed both the study of stars (astronomy) and their influence on human life (astrology)</term> knows this, he can rightly judge a newborn infant according to it, and he will not be mistaken. For just as a father, if he procreates while a heaven of anger prevails, generates a son far different than if he had generated him while laughing, so it is with heaven: which is disposed by the nature of the Microcosm <term>Microcosm: The "little world"—the idea that the human body contains all the elements and influences of the entire universe (the Macrocosm)</term> just as they agree with one another. And so, from such a conjunction and nature in action, a presage proceeds even before the infant is brought forth. For from that is estimated the nature, condition, disease, character, complexion, etc. Although this is nearly twofold—that is, if fools produce children <note>original: "libros," though likely a scribal error for "liberos" (children) given the context of generation</note>, heaven dominates them and shapes them to its own nature, which, however, a man can break by dominating heaven in that hour.

Furthermore, there is another kind of presage, when natural events are predicted from the beginning of nature until the end. Here, nothing is presaged concerning the "rod" or disease. For that does not stir, nor can it be counted according to the course of heaven. For who could foresee and predict the anger of a laughing father that is about to erupt a few hours later? Or who could foreknow future accidents? Therefore, this kind of presage is different; it cannot be known with certainty unless every cause is removed and an unshakeable judgment is made regarding the parent alone.

From what, then, does the presage of *Wrath* follow? For there could be no presage of the fire of Sodom while they were still upright. However, it began to be revealed as soon as they devoted themselves to impiety. Signs of the future could be taken from heaven. Likewise, who could have foreknown the flood before men brought it upon their own heads by their newly committed crimes? But as it was already looming, it could be presaged that heaven was its cause.

<margin>The twofold face of heaven for Astronomers.</margin>
Thus, an Astronomer can see two faces in heaven: one natural, the other preternatural. But because it has not been handed down by Astronomers until now that heaven occupies itself with and is incited to shake its rods: it is clear that they had no knowledge of "caused causes" and of those things that happen beyond its nature. But if ever heaven, being offended, proceeded to punishment, they were able to see those signs and announce them to men, adding the manifest causes of that infection from which these things arose and were brought in. And I set these things before you so that you do not perhaps think that the plague is a natural influence, like other natural diseases: but that you might judge it to be a disease of that kind which we ourselves generate in heaven and stir up upon our own heads, in which it then completes its operation.

<margin>Prophetic presages.</margin>
There are, moreover, many presages taken from the causes of diseases. Such things are not placed within the power of nature but transcend its limits, such as prophecies...

...the prophecies. Thus *Asaph* <note>Asaph was a Levite singer and seer mentioned in the Bible, credited with several Psalms.</note> prophesied concerning the desolation of Kingdoms, and thus *David* prophesied concerning the devastation of Arabia. Such things were truly not predicted by human means, but were instilled and foretold by a higher divine power. It was the same as if they were saying: "A time will come when you mortals will irritate heaven, and by your vices and sins you will move it so greatly that it will send upon you hunger, high prices, diseases, and so forth." This prophecy, therefore, is drawn from the cause, not from the immediate face of the heavens. For it speaks of the sins and crimes of the people and exposes them. After these things are predicted and betrayed, punishment follows as a companion—the very "Lerna" <note>A reference to the Lernaean Hydra; here meaning a vast, swampy source of endless evils.</note> of our misery. Indeed, the Prophets themselves wished to say nothing other than something of this sort: "Unless you accumulated sins, no hardships or plagues would fall upon you." By a similar principle, Christ also speaks very often, especially where he says: *signs shall appear in the sun, moon, and stars, etc.* <note>original: "signa fient in Sole, & Luna ac stellis" — a reference to Luke 21:25.</note> not because those things will happen naturally, but because we are going to give heaven a cause to take up those signs, which will subsequently overwhelm us.

<margin>Preternatural signs which the Astronomer should accept.</margin>
Therefore, Christ does not speak as an Astronomer, but as a seer, to whom all causes have long been open. However, once signs of this kind are introduced into heaven, the presage of the Astronomer follows: for when he sees that those things have been established contrary to nature, he can easily predict the destruction and confusion of nature from them. There are many such prophecies issued by Christ and the Prophets which could be known by no Astronomer in those times. For the course of the heavens was still occurring according to nature, nor had it yet received a cause for change. Afterward, however, once the causes were added, the prophecy of Christ was verified. Of this class also are those prophecies which announce wars, hardships, and starvation to the peoples: all of which are by no means diseases in themselves, but are finally introduced in a supernatural way from a given cause. Thus, if coming Prophets—whether good, evil, or false—are announced, all those things were so foreseen and arranged by God before those men were born who were destined to irritate heaven to this end.

<margin>Man creates his own punishment.</margin>
Truly, I discuss these things more broadly and at greater length for this purpose: so that at last you may be better able to know and judge the reason for the plague from what has been said. Nor do I wish anything else to be repeated here except that you know that the cause of the plague flows entirely from us humans; it is first introduced into heaven through us, and afterward it is brought back upon us from heaven (as if from our parent) in the manner of a punishment. Truly, how these things happen or can happen naturally, even if they are called supernatural, is what we shall say next. Thus, this thing—from which all diseases arise—rules over us ourselves, because we gave the cause for it in our "parent" <note>The "parent" here refers to the Limbus or the celestial macrocosm that reacts to human behavior.</note>; just as the following example of a magistrate will explain.

<margin>Heaven is the superior magistrate.</margin>
For I explain these things more copiously so that you may penetrate to the true foundation of the disease and understand how it finally comes to be. Let the example be thus: Just as no punishment is imposed on children by parents if they show themselves to be honest and obedient, so the magistrate does not punish his subjects unless they deserve punishment through rebellion.

<margin>Heaven is the high magistrate.</margin>
Now, truly, there is another magistrate superior both to this earthly magistrate and to all men: namely, heaven itself. You ought not to think of it differently than of the aforementioned inferior magistrate. For the plague is in the place of the wheel, the gallows, or the cross, etc. *Some parts are missing* <note>The Latin "Desunt quaedam" indicates a gap in the original source manuscript or printed text.</note> man is not in it [the plague] itself, but only insofar as the blow falls.

Truly, what I am treating here you ought to accept in exactly the same way as that which was said concerning the death of the nascent Elements. For envy, avarice, and so on, generate <term>bodies of infection</term> <note>Paracelsus viewed sins not just as abstract concepts but as subtle, physical substances or "seeds" that could infect the cosmos.</term> within a person. These bodies are seeds cast into the sun, consuming our Element. They are generated and grow in the sun until their "autumn"—that is, until the time of the breaking out of the plague. Here, however, what we said in the preceding chapter must be repeated: that from anger, a man generates for himself an innate "body" for diseases, which is now evident.

<margin>Envy, guile, avarice, etc., from the heaven of man.</margin>
Now, to speak of the "bodies" of avarice, envy, guile, treachery, and lies, know that all these proceed from the heaven, the planets, the stars, and the signs. And therefore, they are all fit for conceiving "bodies" within a man. For whatever heaven sows and deposits in a man, that becomes a "body" in him. Just as anger proceeds from heaven and its influence, which is thus impressed upon man. Therefore, not only anger is from heaven, but also envy, hatred, fraud, guile, lies, and avarice. If, therefore, they are from heaven, they must also be estimated and judged according to heaven. And this properly pertains to the Physician.

The reason is this: because, if they are from heaven, they return to heaven with their aforementioned Zodiac <note>The "Zodiac" here implies the celestial circuit or the path by which these influences cycle between the micro-cosm (man) and the macro-cosm (heaven).</note>. For nothing penetrates into heaven which did not come from heaven. Therefore, this is the same. Now, truly, anger, envy, hatred, and avarice are not natural motions or courses in man, but they break out and are produced from malice and levity.

For it is not natural for anyone to be envious, fraudulent, or a liar. If he does so, he rouses the "bodies" of his own diseases. However, the natural diseases that are generated within him fall back upon the "parent" of man <note>Likely referring to the macrocosm or the celestial environment</note>, and from there they are derived back into man, just like hail, frost, snow, and so on. However, if it looks at a man, it conceives such a powerful hatred and envy that it creates a physical body for itself out of its own poison, which then infects the man. From the heavens, this power belongs to Saturn. In this way, "Saturn" is also born within us. Certain birds, worms, and other animals perform similar things. <margin>Why the disease of a dog causes harm.</margin> For why is the bite of a rabid dog harmful? Surely because of the dog’s own greed. Because the dog strives to devour everything alone, a physical "body" is collected and conceived in its mouth, which afterwards infects whatever it touches. All these are the volatile bodies of the Planets, and they are joined in this manner. And just as one worm is more poisonous than another, so too is one man, and so on. <margin>The Antichrist is a worm.</margin> The Antichrist is a worm, that is, a Basilisk: and it is well said, for as long as he lives, the Plague is to be expected.

## BOOK TWO.
### SECOND TRACTATE.
#### CHAPTER I.

<margin>Man is twofold: spiritual and earthly</margin> BECAUSE, as we have said, man is twofold—one part consisting of earth and water, and the other part of fire and air—it follows that supernatural diseases take their origin in one part, namely the spiritual, and not the other. Yet this second part is a body just as much as the first, and suffers equally. For every single subject is submitted to both "globules" <note>Referring to the terrestrial and celestial spheres.</note>. Since, therefore, the spirit is the origin of this disease in man, it must be known:

<margin>Appetite fashions a body for itself.</margin> that every appetite, desire, will, and inclination of a man, when conceived in his mind and his <term>phantasia (the creative power of the mind)</term> or imagination, generates a body. Just as you see that anger begets a body for itself—that is, it is born in the body—the same logic applies to envy and other vices. Thus, every single "will" of a man is either envy, hatred, a lie, blasphemy, fraud, or greed. And man generates all these from at least half of himself—that is, they proceed from the celestial half of man. From this it is clear that the things just mentioned adhere to and lie within this "half-man." The logic for this is the same as for food, drink, labor, walking, or any other activity. It is the same for envy, hatred, deceit, perjury, lying, greed, and the rest. Now, if the imagination in a man is so intensified that he desires either good or evil through a powerful "imaging," then that strong imagination begets a "will." <margin>The power of the human imagination.</margin> That will, in turn, creates a body, just as anger does. <margin>How a body may be made from an incorporeal thing.</margin> And that body is what we are speaking of here: that is, it is the "seed of evil" which falls upon us from above. For these things proceed from heaven; therefore they return to heaven—specifically to the "Saturnine" or "Martial" man <note>original: "homo nempe Saturnius, Martius" — referring to people whose temperaments are dominated by the planets Saturn (melancholy/malice) or Mars (aggression/anger).</note>. All these things exist in the "half-microcosm." Now, these exist and move spiritually, so that malice, envy, lies, and deceit are felt; just as the goodness and beneficence of the Sun and Jupiter are felt. Therefore, if a man does not remain in balance, but tips toward either half—leaning toward the upper stars like Saturn, Mars, Mercury, etc.—know that through the spirits of his imagination, he begets a body of that specific virtue or power he is occupied with. His spirit joins itself to it, and they become one body. Note this: that if that spiritual man inclines toward the stars, then he and his envy (or other vice) become a single body. And if it is incorporated like a disease, then that man remains continually and perpetually envious. The same is true on the opposite side: if beneficence is incorporated, he remains perpetually beneficent. For every body generated in this way retains its "disease" to the very end; nor is that disease ever separated from the man once he has pledged his will to his Planet. And these then constitute the "half-man." Now, <margin>Diseases of the imagination are twofold.</margin> these diseases of the imagination are twofold. If they sicken the whole Microcosm—as anger does—a total contraction occurs. But the other part becomes volatile, so that not all the flesh flourishes, but is changed into a volatile spirit. This does not remain in the body, but the spirit of the imagination draws it toward the stars—specifically to that Planet from which it first came. For every single...

# ON THE PLAGUE, WITH ADDITIONS.

The planet is a magnet for those things that are volatile <note>In alchemy, "volatile" refers to substances or spirits that easily evaporate or move; here, it refers to the spiritual aspects of human emotions.</note>; that is, like a magnet, it draws them to itself. In this way, the bodies of spirits and virtues become both corporeal and spiritual. The corporeal remains in the body, while the spiritual is snatched upward toward the heavens by its magnet. This means that within us, the "body" grows out of these virtues. This body is the very first thing to infect the human frame.

<margin>The volatile body of the planets</margin>
Furthermore, a "volatile body" is formed, which is attracted by its corresponding planet. For instance, envy is drawn toward Saturn, while lying is drawn toward Mars, Mercury, and so on. Then, within that planet, the "seed" is formed, as previously mentioned. If these volatile bodies lie within the planets in this way, they become seeds that will fall back upon us, serving as the beginning of the plague and other similar supernatural diseases. For as the origin is supernatural, so too is the disease. Pay attention to how this proceeds into a disease: if Saturn has drawn into itself the will, imagination, and phantasy of its corresponding human, it is then carried away as if with joy; it runs riot because it now possesses more envy and hatred than before. Its nature is like that of a certain worm that seeks to harm and poison all men. Such is the malice of Saturn and Mars; they share the same property, nature, and condition. This malice of the planet generates and transforms its volatile body—received from the <term>Microcosm (the "little world," or man)</term>—into its own will. Now, this planetary will is not good, but purely evil. From this it is clear that the nature of Saturn and Mars portends infection. In this manner, the blows or <term>rods (punishments)</term> are pushed forth in their own time, in their own "autumn." Indeed, God has appointed Saturn in heaven as a pedagogue and executioner, who uses the plague as a rod for discipline.

<margin>Saturn is God’s officer.</margin>
If a man has earned the plague, then his body tends toward that disease. This is the same logic for all other diseases. For whatever a man’s imagination revolves around, that goes into his planet, where the man’s "rod" is subsequently bound. Out of these rods, every single plague is born.

<margin>The plague is the rod of the planets</margin>
Now, you should know that the first plagues are peaceful and mild—meaning they attack quickly, expire suddenly, and do not afflict too severely. However, if the "seed" has already taken root among men, it is finished; the plague gains strength and becomes increasingly more aggravated and bitter. For the nature of the human Microcosm is gradually rendered worse and more malignant. From this, it necessarily follows that the remedies themselves help less and less every day, and a more attentive cure is required.

### CHAPTER II.

<margin>Heaven and earth are subject to human wisdom.</margin>
**H**uman wisdom is so high and arduous that it holds within its power all the stars, the firmament itself, and the entire universe. And just as its force extends to the earth, so it likewise extends to the heavens. Indeed, just as sheep, cows, and other animals are subject to man, so similarly are the Sun, Moon, and all the stars. For the wisdom of each individual governs the heavens. Just as the hand turns and compels the earth, so the interior Microcosm compels the heaven to obedience—no differently than a man either entices a puppy to himself or drives it away. By reason of this power, it happens that men infect and poison their own planets, ascendants, and stars.

<margin>The envious man compels Saturn.</margin>
For the envious man compels and conquers Saturn, directing him to turn his envy toward whatever goal he has established. Thus Mars and Mercury lie, deceive, practice impostures, and the like. This force and power, by which the envious man conquers Saturn and forces him to obey—what else is it but a horse fearing the switch and obeying it? Therefore, when it is a man’s purpose to harm others, to slander them, and to deceive them with tricks, he adopts Saturn and trains him to provide help in this, just as a horse assists a farmer so that a field can be sown. And this "plowing in heaven" is nothing other than a certain commotion intended to sow back into the man that which already lies within him.

<margin>A strong imagination is the cause of fortune and misfortune.</margin>
Thus, both fortune and misfortune emerge for everyone from their own strong imagination, according as each person disposes and orders it. That wisdom is the beginning of <term>Characters (sacred symbols or sigils)</term>. For what is a "character" but a spear, which anyone who holds it in their hand can and knows how to use? Those characters demonstrate the wisdom and strength of men, because by the force of his own wisdom, man makes a blacksmith out of heaven, who is compelled to forge whatever the man wills and commands.

<margin>Heaven is man’s blacksmith.</margin>
From this, you can forge spears for health, for disease, or for death. For there, the "character" is like an herb, naturally created by heaven; just as it is made, so it is found to be certain in its operations—much like a spear, although, etc. <note>original: "Desunt hic quædam" - Some things are missing here.</note>

<margin>What human wisdom, imagination, and will are.</margin>
Human wisdom is the principle of "impression" <note>The act of stamping a spiritual quality onto matter</note>; imagination is the principle and force of "conjunction" <note>The joining of the human spirit with celestial forces</note>. The Will is the dissolution of the body, so that the <term>Tincture (a potent medicinal or spiritual essence)</term> may enter. And whoever wishes to understand how man is joined with heaven beyond what has been mentioned so far, must hold fast to the foundation of incantation, by which that force is achieved. For the matter stands thus. Human wis—

## BOOK II.

<margin>
Human wisdom is the beginning of enchantment.
</margin>
The wisdom with which a man ought to be endowed is not from the earth, nor from the upper spheres, but from the **fifth essence** <note>The "fifth essence" (quinta essentia) is a central concept in alchemy and Paracelsian thought; it refers to the purest, most concentrated spiritual core of a substance, distinct from the four elements of earth, water, air, and fire.</note>. From this, it follows that man may command the stars and compel them to do what he wishes, solely by the strength and power of this wisdom. If a man lives within this wisdom, then she is the mistress of the Stars. This mastery or command is the beginning of *incantation* <note>original: "incantationis". Here, Paracelsus uses "incantation" not as mere sorcery, but as the active application of a wise person's will to the natural world.</note>. This is why men, because of the wisdom of this fifth essence, have called the wise man a **Mage**. For they are rightly called Magi because they have constrained heaven to their will through wax, letters, and words. Hitherto, such works have been called deceptions or 
<margin>
How enchantment and magic differ.
</margin>
incantations. Thus, incantation was also called Magic, yet it is not merely incantation, but the highest wisdom. However, whatever is done by the help of spirits is indeed an incantation. Regarding those incantatory spirits, nothing is taught here; rather, we deal only with natural operations, which are performed by the power of wisdom moderating the heavens, through which all natural things
<margin>
Heaven serves the wise man.
</margin>
are known. Thus, heaven serves wisdom, and the Wise Man or Mage has command over **Saturn, Mercury, and Venus**. I shall leave the longer explanation of this power or dominion for my *Archidoxes* <note>A reference to "Archidoxis Magica," one of Paracelsus's most famous works detailing the use of planetary sigils and talismans.</note>. This wisdom is like a blacksmith: she possesses her own mechanical arts and the very craftsmanship from which fabrication proceeds, so that the wise man can turn and change Saturn into wax to perform Saturnian works, even if it is nothing but wax, or letters and words written upon paper. These things should seem neither strange nor false to anyone. The reason is that
<margin>
Heaven does not rule the wise man.
</margin>
words of wisdom of this kind (to proceed briefly) are the executors. But if a man is not a Mage through the wisdom of the fifth essence, then in turn the stars rule him, and they make of him what they see fit. To this end, they employ Magic, through which—according to their own nature, condition, and character—they shape him: one as honest, another as fraudulent, this man as one type, that man as another. The same thing happens to such a man as happens to a fool: because he is unskilled at taming a horse, he flees from it as if it were his conqueror. Yet industry attacks heaven itself. Half of a man
<margin>
Man is half celestial.
</margin>
is celestial; that is, the virtues of man exist as more powerful than the higher forces. Celestial wisdom itself also governs the earth, yet it is not from the fifth essence. If we are unable to tame the earth, it tames us. Why I propose these things in this way must be understood through their causes. We have the virtues of heaven 

built within us, which are mixed, both good and evil, just as colors are mixed in metals. Now, virtue is not the life of man, but one must live according to the standard of the fifth essence. If, therefore, we have the virtue of the stars hidden within us, heaven also claims a certain portion of us for itself. But if we do not respect equity <note>Refers to spiritual balance and divine justice.</note>, which proceeds from the fifth essence, then heaven is the master over us. Now all these virtues are incorporated and form a single substance within the **Microcosm** <note>The "Microcosm" or "little world" refers to man as a reflection of the entire universe (the Macrocosm).</note>. What becomes of the body that has been formed.

which has become a "body" lies within the man and is "cooked" <note>original: "decoquitur". It is cooked for as long as it takes to bring the matter to the point where the plague is generated from it. For these "bodies" are the seeds of the plague. If this grows strong in a man, the principle of the plague is in that nature. Therefore, the more of those vices there are in a man, the further, more severely, and more often the plagues afflict him. For if we lack true and genuine wisdom, we shall be entirely subjected to the diseases of heaven. And although this chapter might seem to contradict what I said about heaven—that vices ascend to heaven and descend again—there is no actual contradiction. The reason is that we received virtue from heaven at conception. If we use it poorly, we give birth to poisonous bodies within us. These are, as it were, cooked within the man. However, this does not happen in the man who merely walks upon the earth, but in the "half-man" whose spirit dwells among the stars and cooks within them, just as the star in turn cooks within him. His **Will** is the cook among the stars. The operation is performed by fire. The star is the fire of the cook; the virtues are the meat. Such is the cooking. Now, if the father of this cooking does not last until the end but dies away, the turn falls to the son. For through conception, he is the heir to those virtues and they are incorporated into him. For the Will is the cook. **Imagination** is the appetite.

The power of imagination.

Therefore, whatever dealings or states proceed from the imagination—that is, if their imagination has arisen from heaven—

# ON THE PLAGUE, WITH ADDITIONS

...it is then that it achieves the desired success and excels all others. In this way, imaginations have also arisen which have killed and weakened other men. The cause was this: the imagination proceeded from that star, and the star itself conquered and compelled the person to imagine according to its own will. Now, this imagination is **Desire**, **Vulcan**, and **Inspiration** <note>In Paracelsian thought, "Vulcan" refers to the internal "alchemist" of the body or the transformative power of fire, while "Desire" (Cupido) represents the attractive force that pulls celestial influences into the soul.</note>. And so, through that Planet, it is brought into effect. Therefore, not just any presumption could perform an incantation, but only that which is born from a Planet and which the Planet has overcome.

<margin>The wondrous envy of Saturn.</margin>
From this it happens that fortune and misfortune, wealth, poverty, and so on, are sometimes in a state of increase and sometimes in decrease. If **Saturn** <note>Saturn was traditionally associated with melancholy, destruction, and greed; Paracelsus links these planetary "vices" directly to the physical corruption of the plague.</note> conquers and prevails, envy flares up so greatly that it desires to devour, rot, and corrupt everything present, so that they are of no use to anyone. Therefore, Saturn is also the author of all evil diseases. A man who is infected by this is greedy, a liar, deceitful, and dog-like, scraping everything to himself. And this envy later becomes a "body" within the body, which is no longer endowed with any virtue. For it is material. That which has virtues must be the spirit of the body. This body remains with that virtue and turns into poison (if it cannot exercise its virtues in the spirit), just as the nature of the spirit itself is, and through its own Planet, it is changed into a corpse—that is, the **plague**.

<margin>Man and the heavens are one.</margin>
Since man and the heavens are one thing—just as redness is in wine, or whiteness is in snow—they are therefore mixed with one another. And where they collide, they strike. They strike in those places where their subjects lie. Thus, as many virtues as there are, so many are the planets and stars: and so many are the kinds of plague. Yet all are one poison, one corpse, one digestion, one proportion, and one perversity, as has been understood. Now, take note of the distinction between all the animals on earth. For they signify celestial poison, if we allow it to prevail and break out within us. The poisons of worms are from heaven. What these worms have in themselves materially, man has spiritually. Saturn distills this spiritual nature into matter through his **desire** <note>original: "cupidinem".</note>. Now, therefore, man is like the worms, not indeed according to his physical preparation, but because the Planets work it so. Now, if a worm can be prepared with its poison through **Alchemy**, how far, I ask, is its poison stretched? How greatly harmful might it be? So, if heaven also contains poison within itself and prepares it, how much more will that poison be in its own subtlety? Indeed, it falls upon man because it has business with man alone, and not with other things. It seeks to kill man, not other things. Thus, God is often thought to have done such things, which the Planet actually did. For if it touches the body, it is the nature of the Planet, excepting the spirit of incantation.

From this imagination, if there is a "persecution" of the Planets within us, various sects and inclinations of men toward uprightness, religion, and so on, have arisen and continually arise. For one is always drawn in one direction, another in another. But he is a great **Prophet** who can lead men back to the contemplation and imagination of heaven in such a way that they take their root from heaven itself. For such people are occupied by wondrous phantasms; they produce various gestures and behaviors both with their limbs and their faces. All these signs testify that man is imagining celestial things, and heaven establishes and confirms it so.

### Treatise III.

<margin>God is prone to mercy.</margin>
But what are all these things, since I said in the first book that we ought to remember constantly that God is swift and ready for mercy? Therefore, we must strive diligently so that, in the end, His anger may be appeased and softened, and the rest of nature may be commended by Him. And then there will be a place for the **Physician's** science. For example: for one who aims at a certain spot with a direct firearm, if his eyes are not deceived by a faulty sight, the bullet hits that which it was sent toward. The strike of God is similar, though it exists much faster than the other. In the same way, a certain archer can repent of his shot, so that he groans for the other person who has been pierced and slaughtered. A similar affection is much more familiar to God himself, whose creatures and work we are, regardless of what we are like. For if we find that even a magistrate sometimes repents of a hasty process—if he has brought a heavy judgment in too much heat or without circumspection—and so immediately turns around and softens or relaxes the sentence: how much more certainly will this be true of God? Even if His arrows have been shot and are in motion, God is suddenly moved to mercy and pulls back the flying arrow, or makes it so that it does less harm, being mindful of that fatherly promise in which He pledged that He would not hereafter cut off and destroy man in a similar way. What an evident example of this is set before us in **Adam**! For did not God, inflamed with burning anger, [punish him]...

# BOOK II.

<margin>Adam expelled from paradise.</margin>
...set aflame, with a fiery sword, drove Adam out of paradise and cast him headlong into a mournful death, crowded with infinite diseases? And yet, when Adam had scarcely set his first foot outside of paradise, God's mercy immediately overflowed again. In His fatherly generosity, He revealed remedies to Adam, by which not only the stains and plagues of the soul might be softened, but even the diseases of the afflicted body might be uprooted by the herbs at hand, and life might be happily prolonged until its appointed end.

<margin>The physician is founded upon the mercy of God.</margin>
And although God created herbs and medicinal virtues even before man was formed, this should nonetheless be regarded as a sign of His supreme mercy and divine providence. For the manifestation of the powers placed within herbs and created things is an act of pure divine goodness and compassion. The wise physician is founded upon this mercy of God. For he who has known the mercy of God does not reject it, since all our hope and trust are fixed in Him.

<margin>Plague is divine wrath. Medicine is the mercy of God.</margin>
God conducts Himself in the same way regarding the plague. In this, He brings forth His wrath and, at the same time, offers His mercy through the physician to those whom He does not wish to be slaughtered. For the plague is nothing other than divine wrath. Medicine, likewise, is not mere force, power, or justice, but is only mercy. Indeed, if this mercy were taken away, who would live to see tomorrow?

<margin>By what power Christ healed.</margin>
By this same rule, Christ also healed men—not, however, by the help of nature, but by His own power. For He Himself is the mercy from which the powers of all simple medicines proceed. In whatever way medicine is perfected, it is like two-fold fruits coming from a single tree:

<margin>Christ as a twofold Physician.</margin>
so from Christ, a twofold Medicine flows: **Herbs** and **Words** <note>In the Paracelsian tradition, "Herbs" refers to physical, material cures, while "Words" refers to spiritual or semiotic healing, such as prayer or the "Power of the Word."</note>. His Father is the sower. The physician is in His hand, before whom God has set a light kindled in nature, through which he may look into and learn of His mercy. Therefore, the physician is not of himself, nor does he possess art and science of himself. For God distributes knowledge at His own will, imparting much to this man and little to that one, giving to one and taking from another. For the logic of Medicine is not like that of other trades or mechanical arts, which are either received by inheritance or learned with easy labor.

<margin>Medicine is a gift of God, not of Academies.</margin>
It is placed in God’s hand to whom He wishes to grant the gift of Medicine or to whom He wishes to deny it. Therefore, Universities or books are not the foundation of Medicine, but only the mercy of the Lord and His gift. You may include books as well (but only those) which consist of a true foundation and solid experience. All other trades are manifest and operate by visible reason. It is not so with Medicine. It is God Himself whose spirit is not visible. For Medicine is also a spirit <note>Paracelsus often used "spirit" (spiritus) to describe the active, medicinal essence or "arcana" within a physical substance.</note> which works where it wills, not where man wills. For the spirit of mercy and the spirit of man are not one and the same gift.

<margin>The 4 humors are in the body.</margin>
Furthermore, if the plague has now become "natural"—that is, if it has taken on a natural essence—then it follows that it must be understood through natural reason and each species of it must be cured in a suitable manner. This is the cause and manner of the plague: four humors are established in man: **blood** in the veins, **moisture** in the flesh, **mucus** <term>viscus: a sticky or viscous fluid</term> in the nerves, and **fat** in the suet. These four follow a unique process of nature. In addition to these, there are three other things still in man. In whichever of these the plague fixes its foot, its natural essence must be judged and investigated from that source.

<margin>Man is made of Sulfur, Mercury, and Salt.</margin>
These three are **Mercury**, **Sulfur**, and **Salt** <note>These are the "Tria Prima" or Three Primes of Paracelsus. They are not the common chemicals, but philosophical principles: Mercury (fluidity/volatility), Sulfur (combustibility/soul), and Salt (solidity/body).</note>. These three are distributed throughout the entire body. Nor are they separated from one another. If, therefore, the plague seizes someone by natural means, it has its essence either in one of these three, or in two—such as Mercury and Sulfur, Mercury and Salt, or Sulfur and Salt—or in all three together.

<margin>The plague and the constellations.</margin>
Moreover, constellations also exist naturally within man, according to the planets, according to the higher stars, according to the twelve signs, and according to the ascendant. Now, if a plague is birthed in some celestial influx and is led into a man through it, then its natural essence behaves according to that influx, complexion, nature, condition, and property. According to this natural essence, the practice must be entirely established, and the theory or cause must be understood.

<margin>What the plague of time is.</margin>
There are also plagues according to the movement of the disease, the essence of which is known by the season. Of this kind is the plague breaking out at the time of dysentery; the plague invading at the time of Lent <note>original: "quadragesimarum", referring to the forty days of the Lenten season</note> with the movement of pleurisy; and the plague truly attacking with fever, and so on. For just as some diseases are born from the time and with the time, so some species of plague are governed according to it.

How this Theory should be understood will now be discussed in what follows. Let us suppose someone has been pierced by a weapon out of anger. As long as this remains fixed in the wound, Medicine achieves nothing. It is necessary for the wound to be open...

...and free. Now, if God strikes, He may again draw out and pluck away the weapon He thrust with His own hand, so that nature alone remains wounded. But if God does not extract the inflicted weapon, every effort of the Physician is in vain. For this is no wooden arrow that a man might pull out to apply medicine to the remaining wound. Therefore, death looms. To prevent this, the four aforementioned things and paths must be diligently considered: namely, the four <term>Humors</term><note>The four bodily fluids—blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile—thought to determine health and temperament.</note>, the <term>Three First Things</term><note>In Paracelsian medicine, these are Salt, Sulphur, and Mercury, the fundamental principles of all matter.</note>, the constellations, and Time. These four teach the method of healing. For into whichever of these four the blow was struck, the medication must be performed according to its nature and condition.

<margin>The Physician works in vain if the plague is not released by God.</margin>
<margin>The nature of the generation of the plague in punctures.</margin>

In the four Humors, the outcome is as follows. Regarding **Blood**, according to how the vein is established at its origin: if it is struck or seized, it is divided into two paths. One path, if a plague is to come, leads from the outside all the way to the origin of the blood. Where those veins originate in the body, there the plague settles down and, as it were, "pitches its camp." From here, nature expels it through the veins into the skin, which finally occupies the nearest <term>emunctory</term><note>original: "emunctorium." Historical medical term for organs or areas of the body that carry off waste or "corrupt" humors, such as the armpits or groin.</note>. Of these emunctories, as we have said, there are six: three on each side. But if the plague does not penetrate inward to the beginning of the veins, but either halts in the middle of the paths or leaps back again to the ends and boundaries of the veins, <term>abscesses</term><note>original: "apostemata." Swellings or boils.</note> are produced, which some call **Carbuncles**, **Anthraxes**, and similar names. According to philosophical consideration, however, these are the plague itself—either the plague breaking out by name, or the "exodus" of the plague.

<margin>1. In the blood.</margin>
<margin>How abscesses and carbuncles are made.</margin>
<margin>In the juice of the flesh</margin>

If, however, the **juice** or humor in the **flesh** is struck, the plague remains in the place where it fell; the humor is collected in that spot, and once ignited, it blazes through the entire body. For this humor is distributed throughout the whole body and does not lie solely in the veins like blood, which sustains various ignitions. And this particular plague does not have specific and defined places to occupy. It breaks out in the entire body—in the belly, or in any place whatever. Nor does it regard those six locations into which infected blood is discharged.

<margin>2. In the viscous humor</margin>

If the **viscous humor**<note>A sticky or thick bodily fluid.</note> is struck, it goes into the joints, ligaments, and nerves. Wherever it grows strong or predominates, there the plague also settles; its seat is for the most part in the joints. When the plague ends in recovery, great ulcers and holes are made in those joints—deep, painful, and stinking from putrefaction.

<margin>4. In the fat.</margin>

If the **fat** is invaded, the plague occupies the <term>lard</term><note>original: "aruinam." Refers to the hard fat of the body.</note> without much pain, afflicting slowly and almost promising safety. But this death is usually thieving and clandestine, not dreaded by any more serious symptoms. For the body is not very sensitive in ulcers of this kind of fat.

<margin>Fat is insensitive.</margin>

Regarding the **Three First Things**: if the plague strikes **Mercury**, then it departs from the heart. This plague brings a very swift death and is almost hidden and occult; it never comes out to the surface, and is quite terrifying due to the cruel "stings" or palpitations of the heart. If, however, it seizes **Sulphur** distributed through the entire body, then that Sulphur is separated from the other two elements and departs. Thus the whole body catches fire, and the infection ascends to the high head or to the armpits below, in the form and appearance of a tumor or abscess. These, if considered according to their nature, are not truly abscesses, but the plague. This breaks out in many places, either simultaneously or successively, and a heat like a corrosive occupies and harasses the affected place. Afterward, cancers and carbuncles are produced.

<margin>How plague is born in the Three First Things.</margin>

By reason of the **constellation**, the plague tends toward that limb which it regards or aims at. For it is divided according to the manner of the star. To every lightning bolt, there is a leaf that it strikes. When that strikes, then the nature of the plague must be judged according to the condition of that limb. Thus, a plague of the brain is to be judged by the nature of the brain; a plague of the liver, by the nature of the liver. The judgment is similar for the rest.

<margin>How the plague of the constellations occurs.</margin>

According to **Time**, the plague is to be judged thus: **Spring** plagues invade with great putrefaction and febrile heat. Therefore, they must be estimated and considered according to the nature of fevers. Likewise, they follow a <term>pleuritic</term><note>Related to pleurisy, an inflammation of the lungs causing sharp chest pain.</note> nature. For all plagues afflicting in the spring are accompanied by pleuritic symptoms; this very thing must be faithfully observed in administering medicine. If it is done otherwise, no convenient or suitable medicine can be given. **Summer** plagues smack of a <term>choleric</term><note>Related to yellow bile; hot and dry.</note> nature; **Autumn** plagues, a <term>splenetic</term><note>Related to the spleen or black bile; melancholic.</note> nature; **Winter** plagues, a <term>phlegmatic</term><note>Related to phlegm; cold and moist.</note> nature. Whatever coincides with this nature, all remedies must be directed toward it as a sort of target. For by this reasoning, not only the plague but its very essence can be removed. For the plague imitates, as we have said, the condition of the season. And knowledge of the time demonstrates the plague according to its natural essence.

For that blow has infected and poisoned the one struck to such an extent that whatever he looks upon is infected. And just as the Crocodile 
<margin>The Crocodile attacks with its breath.</margin>
poisons whatever it breathes upon with its breath, so some are poisoned by the plague to such an extent that whomever they either breathe upon, or strike with their breath and spirit, they cast into the plague. They are also like serpents, either shedding their old age <note>i.e., shedding their skin, a metaphor for the shedding of infectious material</note> or depositing their poison because of its abundance. For they also infect with their sweat, heat, etc., the places in which they lie or dwell. Whoever approaches or touches these (whether they be beds, clothes, or even the walls of the <term>hypocausts</term><note>Rooms heated from below, common in Central Europe; the warmth was thought to trap the "pestilential air."</note>) is infected without delay. In many, the poison also wanders here and there, and its malice is so intensified that the entire house is infected by their eyes, appearance, heat, sweat, and breath, so that those who enter drink in the poison similarly and are seized by the plague. For those infected in this way, help can conveniently be brought by natural remedies. For they are not wounded "from heaven" <note>referring to the divine or astrological origin mentioned on the previous page</note>, but are seized on earth, etc., as has been said.

<margin>What the accidents of the plague are like.</margin>
This is the reasoning regarding the accidents. Often pestilential sweat is not lethal in itself. However, if that same man is internally putrid and full of ulcers, or has nourished this or that disease within for several years, all these diseases are betrayed and revealed by the assault of the plague. If these diseases were going to be lethal at the time of their own natural end, they now bring death as well: such as <term>pleurisy</term><note>Inflammation of the chest/lungs</note> stirred up by the plague, and <term>Erysipelas</term><note>A painful bacterial skin infection, often called "St. Anthony's Fire."</note>, fevers, <term>Mania</term>, <term>Phrenitis</term><note>Delirium or brain fever</note>, <term>Obstruction</term><note>original: "Oppilatio," referring to blockages in the internal organs</note>, etc. All these diseases vary the condition of the plague. Thus, those held by the plague who become Manic or Phrenetic already had this disposition within themselves, which has now erupted into action. Those who are troubled by fluxes of the belly from the plague were already prone to <term>dysentery</term> before. Likewise, for those women whose menstruation is either provoked or stopped by the plague, all this ends in death or health depending on how the prior and interior 
<margin>The accidents of the plague must be treated along with the plague.</margin>
disease was going to erupt on its own. Therefore, diseases and accidents of the plague of this kind must be attended to no less than the plague itself, and they must be fought with their own specific natural medicines joined with the medicine for the plague.

<margin>The nature of lightning and fire to spread.</margin>
Many of these diseases are also inherent in men by heredity, which must be understood in the course of the plague no differently than the others. For just as lightning is cast down from on high into a house, and sets it on fire and burns it, so the nature and property of fire is such that it spreads itself wider and wider as long as nearby wood or straw is present. Now, however, houses of this kind are not burned by lightning, but only that first one. The others are burned by the fire that penetrates them. Just as it can happen that burning houses are torn down, cast down, and extinguished, and in this way saved, the same is to be noted similarly in the plague. For just as many men often live in one house, so these many are like many contiguous buildings. If, therefore, one man is set on fire by lightning, now the remaining neighbors are also inflamed by the same, and that either with accidents or without them. And just as one flaming log burns up an entire pile of wood, so a single man can infect a whole 
<margin>Sulphur is the ignited wood of the body.</margin>
house, a whole city. Those who are snatched away are like logs pulled out from the pile. For all cannot be pulled out at once. The "wood" is the **Sulphur** <note>One of the "Three First Things" in Paracelsian medicine; it represents the combustible principle in the body.</note> of the body. Therefore, the element of fire has the power to ignite it. 
<margin>Every man is subject to the plague.</margin>
Now every man is subject to the plague. From this, it happens that many often pay the penalty for the infection of one, and thus the diseases become very complicated, from which it is not easy for anyone to extricate himself because of the properties and accidents, where different signs and indications are revealed from time to time in different people. Here, however, a certain hidden and occult contagion often concurs, which regards the very similarity of blood or age: just as we see that the plague more often seizes one family and cuts it off entirely, whether the kinsmen are nearby or 
<margin>Why the plague sometimes destroys an entire family.</margin>
further apart. Here almost the same thing happens as with frost. For this destroys and ruins only what is subject to it, such as flowers, or tender vine-shoots, or something similar. Thus the plague sometimes seizes infants, sometimes parents, sometimes grandparents. Although in this case, not all are usually destroyed. But that plague which is of one blood (I mean those who are of one family, who have one subject, one ascendant, and the same <term>constellation</term><note>The astrological alignment at the time of birth or the current planetary influence.</note>)...

<header>ON THE PLAGUE, WITH ADDITIONS</header>

<margin>Why the plague sometimes attacks only pregnant women: sometimes only infants, etc.</margin>
If the plague strikes the blood, it strikes everyone at once who shares that same nature and blood—unless a different temperament <note>original: "complexio"; referring to the balance of bodily qualities like hot, cold, moist, and dry</note> stands in the way, or some concurring constellation prevents the contagion. Thus, the pestilence often afflicts only pregnant women because their "ascending empire" <note>An astrological term meaning the dominant celestial influence at that stage of life.</note> and dominion has power over them. Often the elderly are specifically struck down, because their constellation, power, and dominion have been infected. So it affects others from time to time. For the powers of the plague in the firmament and constellations seize and afflict: servants, masters, the poor, the wealthy, children, youths, old men, men, women, virgins, and so on. Outside of these celestial powers, nothing is infected or contaminated, unless, as has been said, it happens through communication, contagion, or accidental infection. Because of this, if the plagues of the stars are known and understood, then those who are struck privately <note>i.e., directly by celestial influence</note> can be distinguished from those who are infected through contagion from others.

<margin>The plague often seizes one person more than once.</margin>
Furthermore, it also happens that someone is struck not just once, or in one place, but more often and in different places. For it is not necessary that only one lightning bolt fall; rather, two, three, or more are often thrown out. Nor is only one place set on fire; often several are. And yet there is only one crash, one thunder. These lightning bolts or strikes may rightly be compared to engines of war <note>original: "tormentis bellicis"; referring to artillery or catapults.</note>. And these multiple strikes, following one after another, must be properly attended to and considered in the cure. For a single medicine will not suffice for everyone; rather, as often as there is a new strike, another new medicine is needed. If now, etc. until the end.

<margin>One part of the cure adheres to the plague: another to its accidents.</margin>
<margin>What kind of signs of the plague should be considered.</margin>
*Regarding the doctrine of signs*, you shall observe this instruction. Your cure must look to two things: the *Essence of the Plague* and its *accidents* <note>In early medicine, "accidents" are secondary symptoms or complications that are not the disease itself but result from it.</note>. To know the essence of the plague, pay attention to the nature of the constellation—what the logic and "face" of the heavens are at that horoscope; erect a figure of the sky <note>Create an astrological birth or event chart.</note>, and so, from the property of the firmament and the plagues, search out which plague is at hand, what precise strike it is, and what has wounded the patient. Against that plague, establish the care of the sick. For the nature of that celestial strike is within the patient. Proceed, therefore, fortified by this instruction of the superior nature <note>i.e., the heavens/macrocosm</note>. Now, from the agreement of the patient's signs, you can detect the conjunction of both, so that it may truly be said that this or that sign of the plague teaches that Mars, Leo, etc., has struck.

Furthermore, weigh other signs as well, such as what accident concurs: for instance, deep sleep indicates paralysis; excessive wakefulness, mania; a change in color, an <term>aposteme</term> <note>An internal swelling or abscess.</note>. From these signs, steady yourself and prepare to undergo the cure. In this way, the plague must be known. Whether it truly exists or not, there is no need to write a judgment here. For the matter is plain and evident in itself. But what and what kind of plague it is, how it is constellationed in the sky, or by what accidents it is accompanied, must be discerned from its own specific and peculiar signs. And for this, the <term>Astronomical Physician</term> and the <term>Physical Physician</term> <note>A doctor who combines the study of the stars (astronomy) with the study of nature (physics).</note> are suitable—not at all the trivial and imaginary doctor. For here the whole point lies: that through signs, the medicine is decided against the stars themselves and their accidents. These signs, however, must be entirely compared with the nature of man. Besides these two, one must also consider (so to speak) the very possibility—namely, how much can be achieved or expected here. For this is the first foundation of healing.

<margin>Medicine is of dissimilar things.</margin>
From this it follows that the "Leonists" <note>People whose nature or birth chart is dominated by the sign of Leo.</note> struck by Leo while in the sign of Leo should expect death. The same reasoning applies to the others. This same thing was said: if like falls upon like, death is sown there. For if medicine is to be introduced and applied, it is necessary that nothing similar be present, but rather dissimilar things; not one nature, but different and disagreeing, like a kingdom divided against itself. For the <term>complexion</term>, the accident, and the star are not of one sense: but one is cold, the other hot. Now, if either is contrary, the Physician can hope that the kingdom of that disease will be destroyed, if the other contrary is removed. But if all these three—*Complexion, Accidents, and the Heavens*—are one, who could extinguish the fire in that place? For it will be the same as if fire had caught straw, and someone running up poured burning wine or laurel oil instead of water. For thus everything would be consumed. For they are one with the fire; they easily predominate and grow strong. But if there is something contrary and disagreeing, help can be poured upon them.

<margin>The nature of the subject varies the force of the disease.</margin>
Similar diligence must be applied if the heart, brain, liver, or lungs are struck. For whichever of these is the "subject" <note>The organ being acted upon.</note>; accordingly, the disease is either lethal or less so. For a wound in the leg is not as lethal as a wound in the brain: and a wound in the brain...

It introduces the principle of contraries, arguing that if the patient's nature, the symptoms, and the stars all align (like on like), the disease is fatal.</summary>

<header>BOOK II.</header>
<sig>Oo BOOK</sig>

# BOOK II.

<margin>The gift of Medicine is not given to all.</margin>
...it is safer than a wound of the heart, and so forth. If these things are true and natural in regard to the sword, they will likewise be true in regard to the stars and the superior bodies <note>The "superior bodies" refers to the planets and stars in the heavens, which were believed to influence health on Earth.</note>. For just as this or that place in the body is wounded, so the plague is more or less lethal. However, there is no need to describe and explain every sign here according to the division of the stars and the accidents of elemental nature. Physics and Astronomy teach these things, and they should by no means be confused with this work. For the gift of Medicine is not given to everyone. But he to whom it is given already knows beforehand the constellations, the infections, the powers, and the dominions; likewise the behaviors, properties, essences, and signs of natural diseases. It would be ridiculous for me to teach all these things here and communicate them to such men. For I did not receive this knowledge from them, but from Him who imparted it both to them and to me.

<margin>What the Essence of the Plague is like.</margin>
Regarding the natural essence of the plague, the matter stands thus: if the spiritual strike <note>A "spiritual strike" refers to an attack on the *archeus* or the vital life-force of the body rather than a purely physical injury.</note> has seized the flesh, the same thing happens as with iron. If water is poured upon red-hot iron, then it hisses and whistles, and the heat is extinguished. A similar thing happens in the flesh and nature of man. Just as water can impose its power upon iron, so the firmament <note term="firmament">The heavens or sky, viewed as a source of influential "astral" forces that act upon the physical world.</note> operates similarly upon man. And just as ignited iron is cooled by a great deal of water, so through the multitude of the constellation <note>The combined influence of the stars at a specific moment.</note>, a man is also "cooled"—that is, he fails unto death and passes away, just as the fire of the iron fails because of the water. Such is the power of the superior bodies over us humans.

<margin>How the Accident of the Plague behaves.</margin>
Furthermore, if some "accident" <note term="accident">In medical philosophy, an "accident" is a secondary symptom or a non-essential quality of a disease, such as a rash or a fever, as opposed to the disease's "essence."</note> which lay hidden in a man were also struck at the same time, then that accident of the man ought to be understood similarly to mercury <note>Also called quicksilver. In alchemy, it represents volatility and the spirit.</note>, which can bear neither heat nor anything contrary to it, but at their encounter it leaps, melts, and expires. Buboes <note>Swelling of the lymph nodes, a classic sign of the bubonic plague.</note> and abscesses do the same. They cling to the Essence of Mercury; they are dissolved and operate just like Mercury. For they are not "perfected" things, just as Mercury is not perfected. Thus, every single thing operates according to the mode of its own nature. In this way, Mercury is like an abscess in all metals in which it hides; it ruptures and breaks what is good, and leaves nothing good behind. And just as Mercury in the fire expires from its body and its primary matter, so also life flees from a man through the firmament, with which life at that time has no familiarity or can have none—just as saltpeter cannot coexist with fire, nor Mercury with the same, or anything else similar to this. Thus, life flies away from us like smoke from wood in a fire. Thus, I say, man is drawn out by the firmament. And just as fire is visible, so the firmament exists as an invisible fire. Such is its nature.

<margin>A man snatched from the plague is like a tree dead through winter.</margin>
Those who are liberated and snatched away by the help of a Physician or other protections and rise again: something similar happens to them as happens with trees. For they are dry and dead through the winter—that is, they are held in a slumber—but when summer approaches, they rise again and return to their former vigor. So also the man who lies down struck by the plague lies as if in death—that is, in sleep—just as **CHRIST** said:
> *He sleeps, he is not dead.* <note>original: "Dormit, non mortuus est." A reference to Matthew 9:24 or Mark 5:39 regarding the raising of Jairus's daughter.</note>
This is the same as saying: He who lies down lethally ill is dead, even if he still lives. As long as he lives in death, he is not yet dead, but sleeps. Thus, sleep and death are one thing, like trees in winter. Therefore, whatever is healed is healed in a wondrous way—namely, by divine help—just as the dead were awakened from sleep by Christ. This is the same as if Christ said:
> *Rise, take up your bed, Lazarus, and come forth, etc.* <note>The author here blends two biblical miracles: the healing of the paralytic (Mark 2:11) and the raising of Lazarus (John 11:43).</note>
Because those who are lethally sick have not yet been buried in the earth like Lazarus, many superstitious people are of the persuasion that they rise by their own power, without divine help. However, the faithful and the pious know well enough that these things happen miraculously.

<margin>Twofold Medicines: visible and invisible.</margin>
He has granted us two gifts of Medicine out of singular grace: namely, visible and invisible remedies. Visible Medicine is that which is created <note>Physical herbs, minerals, and compounds.</note>. Invisible Medicine is the word of God. His word created medicine. He who is healed through Medicine is healed through His word.

<margin>Medicine is the word of God, and vice versa.</margin>
He who scorns the word of God scorns Medicine, and vice versa. For God is one, and He is the same. Therefore, if the plague has not merely been struck and dealt a blow but is burning in the limbs, we must by no means despise medicine. For he who says that no medicine can help here denies that God exists. But we must not discourse any further on the theory of the plague. We shall enter into the Practice itself, established from rules leading to experience and the knowledge of experiments. The two following treatises will be designated for this purpose.
