TREATISE II.

...one must stop, so that the wateriness is left behind. For wateriness creates a thickness so that the medicine cannot penetrate. Another test for this is as follows: pour a small amount of it into a tin dish and set it on fire. If it burns so completely that no grease is left behind in the dish, it is good. If grease remains, it must be distilled again, and for as long as it takes until it comes out corrected in this way. Otherwise, unless it is separated thus, it cannot penetrate. However, when it has been corrected in this manner, it immediately penetrates to the principal organ that is suffering, whether it be the liver, heart, brain, etc.; it goes everywhere because it opens the pores, induces sweat, and identifies and expels the harmful matter of the plague, all at once, and it is most excellent.

<margin>What "Cohob" is.</margin>
**Cohob** <note>original: *Cohob*; a Paracelsian term usually meaning redistillation, but here applied to the repetition of a dose</note>, etc.) if someone vomits once, twice, or thrice, and the disease does not yet wish to yield. This is the "cohob" that the physician must observe. For a medicine should not be administered only once: but just as the disease shows itself, so the medicine must be administered in a similar fashion.

<margin>What kind of preventatives are to be given in the plague.</margin>
And preventatives cannot be given in the plague except for those that **deoppilate** <note>remove obstructions or blockages</note>, and those do not allow obstructions to form—that is, so that the plague cannot take root. Water of **self-heal** <note>original: *prunella*; a common herb used for throat and respiratory issues</note> is effective in plague and pleurisy: therefore, let self-heal be given as a drink.
<margin>Zickbaertlin is a great secret remedy in the plague.</margin>
The plums which are called **Zickbaertlin** <note>original: *Zickbaertlin*; likely a regional name for sloes or a specific wild plum variety</note> are a primary preventative: their distilled water contains a great **arcanum** <note>a powerful medical secret or "inner essence"</note> within itself.
Furthermore, where it happens that an **arsenical spirit** <note>Paracelsus associated arsenic with the sharp, burning quality of certain diseases</note> inflames the veins and creates abscesses under the armpits, etc., it is not necessarily the plague; therefore, even if they often suppurate, the patient still frequently dies. In that case, it is not the plague, but an infected abscess from bad matter: thus it is an abscess just like any other abscess that arises here and there in the body. As for **phlebotomy** <note>bloodletting</note>, it cools the blood, but it does not help against the plague.

# CHAPTER III.
## On the Plague.

<margin>What the plague is.</margin>
**T**he **Plague** is a disease separated from the **Arsenical Yleiados** <note>original: *Yleiado Arsenicali*; the "Yleiados" is the Paracelsian term for the primordial "chaos" or raw material of minerals</note>. There are several kinds of arsenical types: namely, three "ashen" ones, and those three are located in the principal organs. For the plague is a simple, contagious disease, occurring through the conjunction of the elements—
<margin>How arsenical things are folded/complex.</margin>
of the element of **Air**; and another from the air, through the pores of the blood, or through the lower orifices, or the higher ones at the exits: and it is a disease of a "digested time." By the same reasoning, digestion causes separation: and separation causes the disease. What is the "time of separation"? Where does this time come from? Things that are composed have a "discomposition" <note>a breaking down or decay</note>. For discomposition proceeds from the first composition according to the **Arlatum time**.
<margin>What Arlatum time is.</margin>
**Arlatum time** <note>a Paracelsian neologism referring to an "allotted" or "destined" duration</note> is the time for sequestering things against the order of the **Yliadus** <note>the vital formative force of nature</note>. For this Yliadus has a period.
<margin>The triple period of the Yliadus.</margin>
The period is three-fold: into the first, second, and third age. The first age is youthful; it pertains to the state without separation. The second age is that of the disease, and it declines toward the second part of the world; it brings an age contrary to health. The third is the end, and it delivers death. According to this distinction, every sequestration of minerals and spirits leads to the beginning of both the healthy and the bad. For in these ages, the **Pyronomus**, **Hydronomus**, **Geonomus**, and **Augurineus** <note>These are Paracelsian names for the spirits or "rectors" of the elements: Fire, Water, Earth, and Air (or celestial influence)</note> seek their art: for from this flowed what they call "that which is to be." From this, he speaks of things that the ancients did not mention; they understood very little of it.
<margin>What "disposition" is.</margin>
The manner of the "age" is thus: **Disposition** is the separation through nature from the **Ilech** <note>the "First Matter" or primordial state of a substance</note>. From this flows the time of "resolving"—namely, the dying of a thing through a thing, matter through matter, nature through nature, body through body, by species, by genera, by similarities, one after another, until the consumption of the primary matter into the **ultimate ENS** <note>the final, purest essence or state of being</note>. When the separation of death begins in the Yliadus, disease follows. For disease follows separation. This continues until all that mineral matter has been consumed; then the disease will appear consumed as well, and no longer known to physicians: thus diseases will perish; thus the "genera of death" decline, even unto the "cure of death"—namely, the final cure established in the Essence. Now the plague, now pleurisy, now other causes of ailments and diseases vanish.

<margin>What the Edelphas is.</margin>
But what should be said of the period of time? Take note, listener: from these things we can know who the **Edelphi** <note>from *Edel* (noble/pure) and *Delphi*; refers to pure or essential mineral spirits</note> are. For we know that "Arsenicum Delphum" can be separated in a seven-year period in one place: we know in another the nature, the matter, and the number. All these things remain hidden to the unskilled in our **Paramira** <note>referring to Paracelsus's major work, the *Opus Paramirum*</note>. For just as a flower, which is a species of the mineral of this tree, falls from another tree, then the fruit, then the herbs, then the locusts, then the dryness, and death follows at the end of regeneration: so too the flowers of the Yliadus—namely, the mineral spirits—will perish, and so will diseases and the deaths caused by diseases. But what is new of the regeneration of "May" <note>likely referring to the alchemical "Spring" or renewal of matter</note>, we do not know.

# ON TARTAR, BOOK II.

## A diaphoretic and resolutive cure for the Plague, of which this is the description.
Take: *Corrected burning wine <note>distilled alcohol or brandy</note>, 10 pounds.*
*Species of Bezoar <note>a stone found in the stomachs of animals, believed to be a universal antidote</note>.*
*The Duke's Stone-breaker <note>original: Lithontripon Ducis; a specific recipe for breaking up stones in the body</note>, half a drachm each.*
*Alexandrian Treacle and select Mithridate <note>two famous, complex ancient poly-pharmaceuticals used against poisons</note>, 1 and a half drachms each.* Let them be mixed.
The dose is from 1 drachm up to 3 drachms by **cohob** <note>original: per Cohob; referring here to repeated doses as discussed on the previous page</note>, according to the nature of the sick person and the judgment of a good physician present.

## Commentaries.
<margin>The plague is an Arsenical disease.</margin>
I have already said recently that the plague is an Arsenical disease, just as **thrush** <note>original: prunella; likely referring to a throat infection or diphtheria here</note> is plumose, and pleurisy is ogertine, etc. This is the matter of **Yliadus** <term>Yliadus: a Paracelsian term for the primordial spiritual force or mineral spirit within the elements</term>, because every Element has within itself a mineral spirit, and that spirit causes all diseases. And if it were not for this—that the mineral spirit causes diseases—why would we use herbs and minerals, or be able to cure diseases? For indeed, herbs are minerals.

<margin>Why humors do not cause diseases.</margin>
If the humors <note>the four bodily fluids: blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile</note> caused diseases, we would not have external humors with which to cure them. Therefore, all things generated from the elements have within them a mineral spirit, which is a poison: just as in the flower, the musk, etc., nothing is so noble that it does not also contain a poison within itself.

<margin>Good and evil in all elemental things.</margin>
For good and evil are joined in all things that the Elements produce. Therefore, those things that are inside the body are sicknesses; those that are outside are medicines.

<margin>Yliadus is the cause of the crisis.</margin>
Yliadus alone creates the **crisis** <note>the turning point of a disease</note>; that is, when the mineral spirit separates itself from the Yliadus, then the crisis begins. Therefore, it behooves the physician to observe when the separation begins, and of which mineral the separation consists, so that he may know how long it will last; it is not for us to judge the crisis simply by time.

<margin>How the plague is inherited.</margin>
In a one-day fever <note>original: ephemerâ</note> there is a sharp salt, and the crisis is on the ninth day; in those nine days it either causes death or moves toward putrefaction. That the plague is inherited is not true, unless it happens that the arsenical spirit, enclosed in the "shell" of a principal organ, ruptures and goes out; then it infects the air as it leaves us, and if that air passes into another, they are infected. External air does not infect, but rather that air which is inside the patient when it breaks the "shell," just as it breaks when Death wins. And if it infects the limbs so that sweat leaves through the pores, that sweat will also infect the air; thus the air within us is infected.

<margin>Inspired air is not the "air of man."</margin>
Furthermore, that air which we draw in and breathe out is not the air within us, but is an external element. But that air within us, which is our own element, passes through every limb. When the **pyronomists** <term>Pyronomist: one who diagnoses or predicts through the study of fire</term> say a plague is coming, they know it because the Yliadus in some external element wants to separate itself; for they see in fire the separation of some mineral spirit, and we do not suffer [until it separates], etc.

## On the Ages.
<margin>The ages and qualities of the Yliadus.</margin>
The first age belongs to the Yliadus as long as it is uncorrupted, even if the man is 70 years old. If he has not been seized by disease, he is in the first age of the Yliadus. But as soon as the Yliadus is infected, then begins the second age. The third age is when it is at the point of death. In the first age, medicine should not be given, because it is not needed; in the third, because it does not help, as it does in the second.

<margin>The ages of minerals are defined.</margin>
Likewise, minerals have three ages, such as Cachimia, Talc, and Marcasites. When they are whole, they are in the first age. When they suffer [change], they are in the second. From this, the **Hydronomist** <note>diviner by water</note> and the **Pyronomist** <note>diviner by fire</note> judge from the elements. If these elements suffer, then the Hydronomist says: if there is an arsenical resolution, then a plague is coming. If it is aluminous, then **thrush** <note>prunella</note> will abound. The same for pleurisy, etc. And therefore those men who abound in the element of water will suffer at that time and have the plague. Other men will not suffer, unless they are infected through the air from another person, but they will not die. Therefore, medicines must also be administered in the water. So too the **Geonomist** <note>diviner by earth</note> judges from the earth, and others from other elements. And the Physician ought to pay attention when the plague comes with nausea and trembling of the heart. Then the Physician shall say that the Element has been directly touched. Where this does not happen, they will not die from the plague; they are cured by themselves.

<margin>Death is twofold.</margin>
Death is twofold: from the Yliadus and from the **Ens** <term>Ens: "Being" or "entity"; here referring to an external or supernatural influence as opposed to the internal elemental spirit</term>. When it comes from the Yliadus, we fight against it; against that which comes from the *Ens*, we cannot. Truly, arsenic in the first age was not separated from the Yliadus; therefore, in the beginning, there was no plague. Afterward, the arsenic was separated, and the plague began, and it still lasts. Therefore, it is still in its second age, and finally it will also separate itself, and the arsenic will resolve itself back into the Yliadus and putrefy; and then will be the final age.

<margin>The plague will eventually cease.</margin>
For by itself the arsenic will finally cease, and the plague will cease. Therefore, the more it rages in any place, the sooner it ceases. And there were many sicknesses in the time of Hippocrates that have ceased today; likewise, pleurisy began late.

<margin>The pleurisy of the ancients is not ours.</margin>
For what they once called pleurisy is not what we have now. The pleurisy of the ancients is pneumonia, not ours; but our pleurisy comes from salt, after that salt has separated itself totally from its Yliadus. It will also come to its third age—that is, it will pass to corruption and cease.

<margin>Thrush is not an ancient disease.</margin>
Likewise, **thrush** <note>prunella</note> did not last long until its salt separated from its Yliadus. It was previously in its first age; now it is in the second age and will last a long time until the third age, because it has hardly been 70 years since thrush appeared, which is a new disease.

<margin>The "French Disease" is new.</margin>
Likewise, the **French Disease** <note>syphilis</note> began when a corrosive salt separated itself from the Yliadus; and now, as long as that disease rages, it is in its second age, and it will not cease until it is resolved and comes to its third age.

<margin>Yliadus is the cause of new diseases.</margin>
Thus Yliadus creates all sicknesses. For as often as something is separated from it, it creates a disease; and when it is universally resolved and putrefies, then it ceases totally, etc. Paralysis, Apoplexy, etc., are not from the Yliadus, but come from the "Elementated" <note>the physical manifestation of elements</note>; they come from the resolution of the liquor of nature, which is the **balsam** <note>the natural preservative essence in the body</note>. All other diseases come from the Yliadus, except those from the "gout" <note>original: gutta; often used for strokes or metabolic dropsy</note>.

<margin>What "Edelph" is.</margin>
He is called an **Edelphus** who prognosticates according to the nature of an element, just like a pyronomist who prognosticates from the element of fire—that is, from the "coals of heaven," etc. They should not be called Astronomers; nothing can be said from the stars [in this way]; they are ignorant of their own name.

# TREATISE II.

**On the Third Age:** A tree that grows expels all minerals from itself every year, such as when it casts off its flowers, and this is **Mercury**. Afterwards, it casts off its husks <note>original: "locustas," likely referring to pods or external coverings</note>, and this is **Sulphur**. Afterwards, it casts off fruit and **Salt**. In this way, the whole <term>Yliadus</term> <note>the vital spiritual and mineral essence that Paracelsus believed governed health and decay</note> is cast off every year, but the Yliadus returns. This does not happen in other things. For those diseases that pass within the Yliadus do not return. If they depart entirely, then comes the final death.

### Cure in the plague.

<margin>Remedies for the plague from water.</margin>
If the plague comes from the element of water, air, fire, or earth—that is, if one of these is suffering—the medicines must be obtained from that specific Element.

#### Medicine for the Plague from the Element of water.
<note>℞ is stylized as a 2 and 4 symbol</note>
<term>℞</term> Of the liquors of elderberry, specifically the flowers.
Wallflower, Anthers <note>the pollen-producing part of a flower</note>, 1 scruple each.
Of the liquors of <term>Cachimia</term> <note>a byproduct of smelting or an "immature" mineral ore</note>, white corals, 2 scruples each.
Liquors of amethyst, 1 and a half scruples. (Alternatively: 3 and a half scruples, or 1 scruple to a half). Reduce to a drink; the dose is from 1 scruple up to 2 and a half scruples.

Where water suffers—that is, the plague is from the element of water—then "burning wine" <note>distilled alcohol or brandy</note> should not be used.

<margin>From earth</margin>
In the third species of plague, that is, from the Earth.
<term>℞</term> Horse-hoof <note>here referring to the plant Nenuphar or Water Lily</note>, 2 ounces.
Harmala <note>Wild Rue</note>, half a scruple. Ambos or Ambostrum <note>specific Paracelsian mineral preparations</note>, 7 ounces. Reduce into liquors. The dose is from 7 grains up to 14.

<margin>From fire.</margin>
In the fourth species, namely Fire.
<term>℞</term> Of the species of Eryngo <note>Sea Holly; it is a small root that grows only in winter, barely the length of a finger joint</note>.
Red corals and <term>Spodium</term> <note>metallic ash or burnt ivory</note>, 1 scruple each. Reduce to a liquor.

<margin>Signs of the plague of earth.</margin>
The signs of the plague of earth—that is, from the element of earth—are abscesses appearing with the pestilence; this is the first sign of Earth. This occurs if the <term>Arsenical</term> spirit in the element of earth resolves itself from the Yliadus. Therefore, use medications from the third group. The sign is from the earth when pimples and abscesses arise. When, however, the legs cannot be kept still but toss back and forth, then it is a sign from the element of Air. When they sleep continually, then it is from Fire. From Water, it is when someone in the pestilence eats but does not want to drink, and the feet swell. According to these signs, the medicines must be administered in proportion to the elements, with each element receiving its own remedy.

## CHAPTER IV.
->Concerning Critical Days.<-

<margin>What a crisis is.</margin>
<margin>What a day of crisis and a critical day are.</margin>
A **Crisis** is the span of time taken from the beginning of a disease until the beginning of death. The first day is called the "day of crisis," and the last day is called the "critical day." The start of the "digested" time <note>when the body begins to process or "cook" the morbid matter</note> is the beginning of the crisis. The resolution of the disease is the final critical day. The "digested time" is that which occurs with the resolutions of species from the Yliadus. The resolution of a species is the consumption and the steady state of the disease. The matter for a crisis proceeds from the "excrements" of the Yliadus. This separation departs into pure Yliadus. Pure Yliadus marks the end of the disease and ailments.

<margin>Which days of these or those dead are critical.</margin>
The Arsenical critical day is the third in acute cases, the fifth in very acute cases, and the seventh in the most acute cases. The critical day for acute Arsenic is at the 24th hour; in very acute cases, at the 15th hour; in the most acute, at the 11th hour. The disease settles immediately, but signs, pains, and causes follow a change rather than an increase, except perhaps in death. A Mercurial crisis occurs on the fourth day; in a subtler case, on the third; in an acute case, on the second. The crisis of resolved Mercury has its critical point on the 13th day; the acute on the 7th; the subtle on the 4th. A Sulphurial crisis has its critical point in the 6th (otherwise 7th) week; in worse cases, in the 2nd week. <term>Ogertina</term> <note>a Paracelsian term for diseases related to metallic or mineral "sweat"</note> have their crisis from the first year to almost the end of the third; in acute cases up to the 4th <term>opposition</term> <note>an astrological measurement representing half a cycle, often lunar</note>; in higher cases, in the 5th opposition. "Separated" diseases have their crisis in the third year; in acute cases in the second; in higher cases in the 7th opposition. **Rock Salt** <note>Sal de gemma</note> has its critical point in the 14th year; in acute cases in the 5th year; in very acute cases in the 13th opposition, as in <term>Ethica</term> <note>Hectic fever or consumption</note>. The critical day for salts, as in **Erysipelas** <note>a skin infection also known as St. Anthony's Fire</note>, is in the 10th or 11th year. (Elsewhere: it later ulcerates, then another crisis begins, which is in the third year; but if it is not healed in the fourth, the disease will then be incurable.) A second will follow, and that in the third or fourth year. Subtler salts have their critical day after the 21st, 27th, or 34th year. Resolved salts have their critical day from the third year up to the sixth or seventh, then up to the twelfth year. **Persian Salts** <note>associated with skin growths or cancers</note> have their critical day from the day of the Crisis until the 22nd opposition. The second critical day is in the 18th opposition. The third critical day is in the 4th opposition. Common external salts have their critical point after the 10th year; in greater cases, after the 18th year; in acute cases, after the 25th year, as in the "dead evil" <note>original: "malo mortuo," a type of gangrenous or leprous skin disease</note>. Reverberated external salts have their critical point in the 2nd year; in acute cases in the 6th; in higher cases in the 12th. Salts of **Gangrene** have their critical point in the 8th opposition; the second in the 14th opposition; the third at the end of the 3rd year. Plumose salts <note>likely referring to Alum</note> have their critical point in the 7th, 9th, or 13th year. Acute external salts have their critical point after the third opposition, the second after the fifth opposition, and they do not have a third.

<margin>Gout and dropsy as species of epilepsy.</margin>
Cancer from hemorrhoids has its critical point in the 7th opposition; after the second crisis in the 6th opposition; after the third crisis in the 4th opposition. **Epilepsy**, along with its species **Gout** <note>Podagra</note> and **Dropsy** <note>Hyposarca</note>, have their critical point at death. Hectic fever from rock salt rarely reaches a critical point at death. Cancer from menstruation has its critical point in the ninth opposition, after the crisis...

->Commutation.<-

<margin>All diseases emerge from the <term>Yliadus</term>.</margin>
<margin>The first disease, etc., of what kind it was.</margin>
<margin>The Crisis, the critical day, and what the "status" is.</margin>
<margin>From where the crisis is to be recognized in individual diseases.</margin>
**A**ll illnesses come from the <term>Yliadus</term> <note>the vital spiritual and mineral essence that Paracelsus believed governed the timing of nature</note>, and the "critical days" prove this. Within the Yliadus is a mineral spirit, and in the Yliadus all things and all simples <note>basic medicinal ingredients</note> consist; some give health, while others give illness. The first disease that came into the world was from corrosive salt, and similar to this is the disease called <term>Ephemera</term> <note>original: "Ephemera," a fever that lasts only one day</note>. The second disease came from vitriolated salt, which descended into the ligaments, and yet did not cause paralysis, etc. So it is with other diseases. However, how diseases reach their "crisis" is known from this: that we may know how long the Salts within the Yliadus maintain their operation. The first day of a disease is the crisis; the last is the critical day. The time in between is the <term>status</term> <note>the peak or steady state of the illness</note>. For the final day leads either to health or to death. But there are many diseases whose final crisis we cannot know, because they end in death. Thus, <term>apoplexy</term> <note>stroke</note> and <term>hyposarca</term> <note>a form of dropsy or edema</note> finish their critical day through death; for when the body is infected, death is present and the final crisis occurs in dying. Therefore, when a disease occurs, such as <term>hydrops</term> <note>dropsy/swelling</note>, we must know which salts are at fault, and afterward how long they remain, and thus judge how long the disease will last. Likewise, in <term>icteritia</term> <note>jaundice</note>, I must consider from which salt it arises. If it comes from <term>Ogertine salt</term> <note>a specific chemical category in Paracelsian medicine</note>, then the crisis is weekly. If it is from sharp Ogertine salt, it may last until the second year. Thus, the Physician ought to know, when he recognizes when a disease begins, so that he can say: "On this day it will be terminated, either for good or for evil." But there are diseases in which we cannot name a limit, such as <term>podagra</term> <note>gout</note> and epilepsy. For their final crisis ends with death. When death is present, then it is the final critical day. Likewise, in the types of fevers, I must consider whether it is from <term>Tartar</term> <note>stony deposits in the body</note>. If it is in the stomach or liver, I can say how long the disease will last, and afterward, the disease either ceases by itself, or the person dies. Other salts, such as the <term>arsenical</term> ones, reach their crisis immediately, such as the plague, <term>prunella</term> <note>a severe throat infection</note>, etc. Therefore, we must first know what disease it is, what mineral is formed there, and how long it carries out its operation. In acute fevers, like the <term>synocho</term> <note>a continuous, non-remitting fever</note>, it arises from a sharp salt and reaches its crisis in seven days. In these seven days, it executes its malice. Afterward, on the seventh day, either signs of death appear, or the disease ceases. And where the critical days are overcome in this way, the person does not die afterward, and the disease does not increase, but there is a "status" between the beginning of the illness and the final critical day—that is, the disease no longer grows, but remains and persists in its vigor. But if the patient remains more and more infirm from then on, then signs of death appear, such as various spots, but it is not the disease itself. Likewise, it does not decline except after the critical day; if that has passed and the patient is still weak, this does not belong to the disease, because the disease passed at the same time as the critical day; rather, it leaves behind weakness, but the disease is no longer present, etc. And as I have said, all illnesses come from salt; and just as the operation of salts and spirits is, so do the diseases reach their crisis. Therefore, in <term>Ethica</term> <note>likely referring to "hectic" or wasting fever</note>, if it is from a salt that is not highly sharpened, it reaches a crisis briefly; if from a higher salt, then longer, etc. Therefore, when such a patient is presented, I must ask when the disease began. If I now know how much time is left until it reaches its crisis—and if I do not have a suitable medicine, and five weeks still remain until the critical day—then I give something for the sake of form until the critical day comes, and afterward it is cured by itself, because the critical day brings liberation. But this is in diseases that do not reach their crisis in death.

<margin>When the "Noli me tangere" disease reaches its crisis.</margin>
For in such cases, medicines must be applied immediately. In external conditions, there is also a critical day; for example, in <term>noli me tangere</term> <note>original: "do not touch me," a name for corrosive skin ulcers or skin cancer</note>, it reaches its crisis in the third year. If it does not reach its crisis in its proper day in the third year, a new crisis—that is, a second crisis—begins, and a new disease starts, such as holes forming, etc. Then it is incurable. So too with <term>Persian fire</term> <note>original: "ignis Persicus," likely shingles or erysipelas</note>; if it first burns, that is the beginning of the disease. When swelling occurs, that is the second crisis; then afterward ulcers come, and that is the third crisis. Afterward, it is inflamed; and if it burns and glows most intensely, then that is the fourth crisis, and it reaches its final crisis on the fourth day, if it is a legitimate one. Then the disease frees itself. If not, then <term>consecration</term> <note>spiritual or ritual healing</note> does not help, but only after the crisis should plasters be applied to remove the scorched and putrefied flesh—likewise for <term>gangrene</term>, the "dead evil" <note>original: "malum mortuum," a necrotic skin condition</note>, etc. If they have persisted to their critical day, they cannot be cured, and attempts are in vain. Cancer, among all diseases in Surgery, reaches its crisis differently.

## CHAPTER FIVE.
### On Pleurisy and Prunella.

<margin>What Pleurisy is.</margin>
<margin>What the signs of Pleurisy are.</margin>
**P**leurisy is a disease enclosed in the principal members; it takes its place in their regions from a <term>Tartaric</term> blockage without resolution, or through resolution. And it is an "aerial passion" <note>an affliction related to the element of air or breath</note> drawn from the body back into the body from Ogertine salt, and from the types of plague and <term>prunella</term>. The signs are: Shaking of the body with cold and heat without multiplicity, discoloration of the face, weakness and restlessness of the limbs, a final rising heat, stabbings in the head and sides, and in the <term>precordia</term> <note>the region over the heart and stomach</note>, and under the thorax; and where the passion or pain is, there is the region of the disease.

<margin>Diet is useless in pleurisy.</margin>
<margin>The cure for pleurisy is twofold.</margin>
Pleurisy has a single <term>paroxysm</term> <note>a sudden attack or fit</note>. Diet is not to be observed in pleurisy; rather, medicine must be applied, and moderation must be kept everywhere. Its cure is twofold, from Tartar and from <term>Syletum</term>. Syletum is a medicine composed of three salts.

### Description of Diatartari.

The dose is from 1 drachm to 1/2 ounce in Malmsey wine, or in Prunella water. Let it be made through <term>Cohobation</term> <note>an alchemical process of repeated distillation</note>.*

### On Prunella.
<term>Prunella</term> <note>original: "Prunella"; an inflammatory condition of the throat or mouth, often called "thrush" or "sloe-fever" because the tongue turns the color of a plum</note> is a primary affliction with its own specific crisis, existing in hot states, taking its origin from vitriolated salts against its proper region and against the shell of the species. It is one of the species of pleurisy and plague, accompanied by vitriolated heats.

### Signs.
It approaches like pleurisy (though the true signs appear at the end of the disease): heat of the throat with redness; then a "Persian heat" <note>original: "calor Persicus"; likely referring to an erysipelas or shingles-like rash</note> with a bluish color mixed with blackness, and a heat like a plum (*prunus*) with abscesses reaching to the tip of the tongue, accompanied by burnt humors.

### Cure.
Begin the cure of Prunella just as you would for the plague.

### Composition of Diaprunella.
Take: 1 pound of Prunella-herb waters.
Half an ounce of pure Laudanum.
Mix and let it be a drink according to the *cohob*, and a gargle with the cleansing of the tongue; it is the ultimate medicine in Prunella.

### Explanation.

<margin>The cause of pleurisy is such.</margin>
<margin>Ogertinum.</margin>
<margin>Pleurisy is not an abscess of the lung.</margin>
**A**nd just as <term>Arsenical salt</term> separated from the <term>Yliadus</term> causes the plague, so <term>Ogertinum</term> <note>a Paracelsian term for a specific corrosive, sharp salt-force that causes internal stinging</note> causes pleurisy in the principal members. The cure is the same for pleurisy of the liver, spleen, heart, and lung. Only the cure for pleurisy in the head is unique and differs from these. The ancients said that pleurisy was an abscess of the lung: but this is not true, because it could not be ripened without danger. For when it turns to pus, if the abscess is in the liver, it leads to death. So too in the heart or spleen: because that pus kills when it invades or seizes with a certain violence. But pleurisy is when the *Ogertine* salt has separated itself from the *Yliadus* and the salt of Tartar. If it is in the regions of the liver, it is pleurisy of the liver; if in the spleen, pleurisy of the spleen. But pleurisy in the brain has its own cure, and produces a fleeing or migratory swelling.

<margin>The peculiar cure for pleurisy of the brain, and what the signs are.</margin>
Signs: if cold and heat seize someone with a shivering—namely, that the coldness comes first, and after the crisis the heat that lasts—this is the sign of pleurisy. Therefore, when the sick say: "First the cold troubled me, but now I am nearly consumed and wasting away from the burning and heat," then it is pleurisy, especially if it shakes the body only once. For if it moves the body twice or more often, it is already a fever, not pleurisy.

*It will cause discoloration.*) because if someone is pale, it turns them red; if they are red, it turns them pale—always by the contrary.

# CHAPTER VI.
## On Dropsy.

<margin>What Dropsy is and its cause.</margin>
**D**ropsy <note>original: "Hydrops"; the accumulation of fluid in the body's tissues or cavities</note> is an affliction in the regions of the liver, arising from an aluminous <term>tartar</term> <note>metabolic deposits or "stones" formed by the body's inability to process certain minerals</note> beneath the "first body," through the breakdown of its own nature, and then through the mineral spirit of that member (one of the seven of the whole body). This follows after the first and second breakdown: that is, from outside or inside, or outside the region through the whole body. Thus also in other principal members, dropsy takes its origin in the manner described.

<margin>How many kinds of dropsy.</margin>
For this reason, there are seven kinds of Dropsy, because there are seven members and seven mineral spirits. For the mineral spirit is a partner with its member, and dropsy exists outside the member, as the chapter on swellings describes, because the species itself is not the disease of dropsy.

<margin>What are the signs of the universal kinds of dropsy.</margin>
### *Signs from the Liver.*
**Pain** in the part, cracks in the lips and tongue, and thirst, long-lasting paroxysms, swelling in the feet, especially on that side, sensitive to the touch.

### *Signs of the Spleen.*
Pain in the part, swelling of the foot on that side, stinging sensations in the area, and other signs without cracking.

### *Signs of the Lungs.*
Asthma and shortness of breath, cough with chest pain, lasting a chronic time; this is the most difficult dropsy of all. Also, foul breath and other signs, except for cracking. Also, equal swelling in the feet, etc.

### *Signs of the Brain.*
Heaviness of the head, catarrh, phlegm, with migraine, and stinging sensations with swellings of the eyelids; also swelling and paleness of the face.

### *Signs of the Gallbladder.*
The color is Citrine <note>lemon-yellow</note>, both of the eyes and the teeth, as in Jaundice, nausea with appetite, bitter vomiting, compression of the chest, hard and rough breath with swellings and wasting of the body.

### *Signs of the Kidneys.*
Excellent thirst, appetite for lust, swelling of the scrotum and testicles, frequent erections, stinging in the spine of the back, members which are numbed, lower parts heavier with swelling in the feet.

### *Signs of the Heart.*
Weakness of all members, swelling of the part, wasting of the members, equal swelling in the feet and knees, yet it does not ascend further, rarely beyond the knees, and other signs except for cracking.

There are also other kinds of dropsy which are mixed, namely from two of the principal members, such as from the liver and kidneys, or from the spleen and heart, or from the lung and gallbladder, etc., as will be clear in the cure.

### Annotations.
<margin>Without aluminous alum, no dropsy occurs.</margin>
Some say that dropsy arises from "fleshy swelling" <note>original: "hyposarca"</note>, others from a "dryness of the liver." But it is none of these: neither can that water from fleshy swelling, nor the "undercooked" matter from the liver, as they say, slip down to the feet. Rather, where there is no <term>aluminous alum</term> <note>the author's term for a specific corrosive, salt-like metabolic waste</note>, there no dropsy is born, whatever the reason for the diet may be. Dropsy occurs in the region of any of the principal organs, but not from the "digestive faculty," since that faculty can generate no disease; rather, it occurs either from nature or accidentally from "resolved <term>tartar</term>" <note>stony metabolic deposits</note>.

<margin>What causes dropsy.</margin>
Indeed, <term>Consumption</term> <note>original: "Phthisis"</note> and <term>Hectic fever</term> <note>original: "Ethica febris"</note> arise from a dry salt, but dropsy arises from an aluminous one, which possesses a most sharp power of penetration. For that which is more subtle is immediately strained through the regions of the liver. Thick and unrefined matter could not achieve this.

<margin>All salts move with the Moon.</margin>
**Oils, etc.** Furthermore, those things which are applied externally easily enter the passages of the body by the aluminous power of a sharp spirit. That salt induces thirst in all members of the whole body, not only in the liver. Accordingly, the root of the body, and the food and drink, correspond to all parts. The salt of alum produces a bluish-gray color. First, when the salt is dissolved, a cindery color appears, then a saffron-yellow one. All Salts have a motion of their own increase in accordance with the **Moon**. Hence, the full moon often threatens death in dropsy, as the salt returns to the region of the liver and finally induces it. An evident sign of this is red urine, which is somewhat thick and also saffron-colored. The older it is, the sharper it becomes. From this, it gathers its power of killing through age; we see this happen when that salt is transmuted into "split alum," by whose violent "bite" the skin is then split and pours out an abundance of saffron-colored water. It is a persistent disease, and it does no good to have drained the water, even if the body is dried out to the utmost: the disease returns, and finally gnaws away at the capsule of the heart, suffocates the spleen, and attacks the other principal organs in a similar way. Therefore, once the salt or the liquid is corrupted, life is over.

->Commentary.<-

<margin>The seat of fevers.</margin>
**CONCERNING** hepatic fevers <note>fevers related to the liver</note>.) Fevers reside in the stomach, the liver, and the kidneys. And just as there is a tertian, or daily, or quartan fever in the stomach, so in a similar way there is one in the liver and kidneys. It arises from the <term>putrefaction</term> <note>the chemical breakdown of waste within the body</note> of **Tartar**, which, when it reaches the point of putrefaction, causes a <term>paroxysm</term> <note>original: "paroxysmus"; a sudden attack or "fit" of fever and chills</note>.

<margin>How a febrile paroxysm occurs.</margin>
For that putrefaction of the Tartar—that is, the "boiling" caused by that decay—ought to penetrate through the pores into the urinary pathways and exit with the urine. When these pathways are blocked, it causes trouble; from this comes the shivering, just like a pot with a lid that, when it boils, must either have its lid fall off or the pot itself will break. So it is in the digestion of putrefied matter: when it boils, it creates a vapor or wind. When that vapor cannot penetrate into the urinary pathways, it causes a paroxysm—that is, it shakes the body and causes shivering. But when the pathways are opened again—that is, when the paroxysm ends and only heat is felt, and the paroxysm does not return—it is a sign of health. Then there is no longer shivering, but only a certain heat. Therefore, the cure for fevers is simply that the pathways be cleared and opened.

<margin>The cure for fevers is opening blockages.</margin>
Therefore, in the regions of the liver, if they are so locked up, and if the pathways through which the matter should go into the urine are obstructed, then the matter boils up. Since it cannot exit, it causes shivering, and the whole body is shaken. The shivering lasts as long as it takes to find an exit and clear the blockage for itself; then it goes to the urine, in which signs can be seen that the regions of the liver are suffering.

<margin>The cause of shivering.</margin>
Note that in a fever, when the paroxysm is about to cease, it must happen simply because the matter finds its own way out and clears the obstruction. It often happens that at least some of the pathways leading to the urine are blocked; then at least a "half-paroxysm" invades. Sometimes there is an "interpolated" paroxysm, which returns once every eight weeks, specifically because the pathways that were previously opened have become obstructed again. Thus, in short, fever comes from obstruction because that "wind" cannot exit; the heat comes after the paroxysm, and the heat opens the pathways. Therefore, every fever eventually cures itself, unless it reaches a "second crisis" <note>a critical turning point in the disease</note>.

<margin>How a half-paroxysm occurs.</margin>
<margin>The cause of febrile cold: an extremely cold putrefaction.</margin>
The cold and the chill come from putrefaction, because all putrefaction is an extremely cold thing. Therefore, while the heat from putrefaction "boils," the substance itself is extremely cold. When a paroxysm is altered—either anticipating the usual time or arriving late—it happens because the putrefied matter is present in double or quadruple amounts, and each has its own "digestion" <note>maturation period</note>; or it happens because the matter has been consumed and there is not as much of it as before; or because the nature of the matter has been cast down.

<margin>What is the cause of fever starting early or late?</margin>
And from this it happens that it ceases, and then later picks up a new paroxysm, just as it often happens that three, four, or five paroxysms come in one day.

<margin>Clearing blockages is the cure for all fevers.</margin>
Therefore, the one cure is the opening of blockages <note>original: "deoppilatio"</note>. A quartan fever is cured just like a tertian, except that in a quartan, the putrefied matter is harder. This applies to all diseases that cause shivering, such as the **sacred fire** <note>original: "ignis facer"; likely Erysipelas or St. Anthony's Fire</note> and others that come from obstruction. Furthermore, shivering often occurs—that is, a shaking that attacks with cold. If we see this, we may not know whether it is the plague, **prunella** <note>a type of inflammatory fever or "slaughter-house fever"</note>, pleurisy, or a quartan or tertian fever. So that the physician can judge this with certainty, you have the signs in the text, etc. The physician must also know how long it is likely to last and when the cure should be applied, because fevers often do not want to be cleared and cured at the beginning, unless the matter has first been totally putrefied.

<margin>A rule to be noted.</margin>
Note: those fevers which shake the body and induce heat and cold at the same time are "mature" and ready to be cured. But when heat comes only after the first paroxysm and the limbs are made heavy, then it is a sign that the matter is not yet "digested" <note>processed by the body's internal heat</note>, and one must wait for a time, such as 6 or 9 days, until the matter is digested. If the shivering and heat attack together, then the cure must be applied.

<margin>No necessity for a diet in fevers.</margin>
There is no need to argue about diet; rather, one must act so that the blockages are opened. Whatever the patient eats does not matter.

# TREATISE III.
<page-num>479</page-num>

<margin>Niter is produced within the body just as it is outside of it.</margin>
**The diabetic suffering.**) Since urine possesses the properties of <term>niter</term> <note>original: "nitri"; saltpeter or potassium nitrate, which Paracelsus viewed as a fundamental mineral force in the body</note>—for it must be considered as such, otherwise what I say about it being a "straining" or "filtration" means nothing—one must understand what urine is when it exits. It contains "split salt," which is to say, a sharp or biting substance like <term>split alum</term> <note>original: "alumen scissum"; likely referring to fibrous or plumose alum, used here to describe mineral crystals that form in the body</note> derived from the urine. And just as a craftsman outside the body boils down niter from urine, the same process occurs within the body. Therefore, when this urinary salt reaches the kidneys, it sticks to them just like <term>Tartar</term> <note>stony mineral deposits</note> sticks to the inside of a wine cask. The "spirit" of that split alum penetrates the kidneys, works its way in, and makes the kidneys <term>fistulous</term> <note>original: "fisticulosos"; porous, full of small holes or pipes</note>.

<margin>All thirst comes from salt.</margin>
For thirst always arises from salt. Thus, this salt makes the kidneys "salty." Those organs which ought to contain moisture pull in humidity through an attractive force, and that attraction is caused by the salt. Where they have humidity, they are satisfied. But in the kidneys, that split alum perpetually seeks out moisture; therefore, the sufferer cannot drink enough. And because the person is always drinking, the kidneys become engorged because they cannot send it all out as urine. The expulsive force cannot expel so much at once; hence, it does not all pass out as urine, but moves to the rest of the limbs. From this, the humor arrives in the feet and they swell. Others call this <term>dropsy</term> <note>original: "hydropisis"; swelling caused by fluid retention</note>, but it is not. Rather, the expulsive force could not drive it out through the urine, so it distilled downward through the pores of the flesh—for every heavy thing moves downward. The feet swell because the expulsive force failed, just as in those who make themselves drunk: the expulsive force cannot expel everything, so the excess moves to another place.

<margin>The remedy for diabetes is a two-day fast.</margin>
The remedy is to fast for two days, so that the expulsive force can catch up and expel the remainder. Therefore, as I said, when the expulsive power cannot expel the fluid, it sends it to the feet and creates a swelling. Then, "old wives" and "market-quacks" <note>original: "vetulæ & circumforanei"; derogatory terms for unlicensed or traveling healers</note> drive the swelling back, and when it returns to the kidneys, death is at hand. The diabetic suffering comes from this: that the spirit of salt sits within the kidneys and renders them salty.

<margin>Signs of diabetes.</margin>
The signs of the diabetic suffering are these: Thirst over a chronic period—that is, if they have daily thirst and later their feet swell, it is diabetes. Likewise, pain in the spine; that pain begins in the <term>nucha</term> <note>the nape of the neck</note>, and stinging sensations arise in the back of the head and travel all the way to the hip bones—this is the beginning of diabetes. Also, equal swelling in both feet; urine that is very saffron-colored and deep red—that is, the urine is reddish on its own, and when you dip a cloth in it and dry it, the cloth is stained saffron-yellow. Likewise, the pulse is fast and there are pains in the <term>ischia</term> <note>the hip/pelvis area</note>, not unlike as if they were being dissolved. When they sit for a while and then stand up, they feel pain until they have walked a little distance; that is a sign of diabetes, provided there is also thirst.

<margin>The cure for diabetes is the mortification of the salt.</margin>
The cure for the diabetic suffering must be achieved through <term>Anodynes</term> <note>pain-relieving or soothing medicines</note>. For the salt and the split alum must be "mortified" <note>original: "mortificari"; to be chemically neutralized or stripped of its biting power</note>, just like Arsenic, which is a great poison on its own, but when injected into ulcers and mixed with oil, it is "rectified." For the oiliness restrains its power.

<margin>Oiliness restrains the sharpness of poisons.</margin>
In this same way, this salt must be restrained. It will not help to cool the kidneys or to offer <term>Juleps</term> <note>sweet medicinal drinks</note> against the thirst, etc. Instead, the salt in the diabetes must be mortified. This is done by applying anodynes externally. For the vapor in Anodynes penetrates and is powerful, not unlike how if you take raw Mercury and hang it over or hold your mouth near it for two hours—even though you do not see any smoke—your teeth will immediately ache and you will produce saliva just from the vapor. In the same way, the diabetic substance cannot leave the kidneys, but there is a vapor of the salt which they feel when you apply the remedy; just as cloves emit their power through their scent, yet when they are dried out they have no smell and then lack power. So also the vapor from the Anodynes passes to the kidneys and extinguishes the thirst, and that split salt or split alum ceases to cause pain, etc.

<margin>Description of the Anodyne.</margin>
### Description of the Anodyne.
Take:
*   Liquors of poppy
*   Henbane, half an ounce each.
*   <term>Loti</term> <note>perhaps "washed" ingredients or a specific herbal wash</note>, 1 ounce.
*   Camphor, 1.5 ounces.
*   Roses, plantain, nightshade, half an ounce each.
*   Bring into a liquid form.

<margin>How the liquor of herbs is to be prepared.</margin>
When I speak of Recipes, I always intend for the pure to be separated from the impure in the ingredients. Therefore, when I speak of poppy, I mean that where the pure has been separated from the impure—that is, the poppy must be prepared, and thus prepared, it gives a liquor. Take the henbane and the poppy with the seed and the herb, and place them in a pot or a jar well-sealed with clay <note>original: "perlutatum"; sealed with 'lute,' a specialized clay used in alchemy to make vessels airtight</note>, and let it boil in a <term>Bain-marie</term> <note>original: "balneo Maris"; a water bath for gentle heating</note> for 2, 3, 4, or 5 days; afterward, strain it through a cloth, and then cook it down until, by evaporating, it reaches the thickness of honey. This is the liquor of poppy, henbane, and the others. In this way, the pure must be separated from the impure.

### Another Description of the Anodyne.
Take:
*   <term>Spernioli</term> <note>original: "Spernioli"; often referring to frog spawn, used in cooling ointments</note>, 3 ounces.
*   Oil of camphor, 1.5 ounces. Make a mixture.
Following the previous liquor, an inunction <note>anointing or rubbing</note> should be performed on the kidneys and the <term>sacrum</term> <note>the bone at the base of the spine</note> morning and evening, continuing for 5 or 6 days; then the thirst ceases. And if swelling is present in the feet after the anointing and the calming of the thirst, then purge the "sinning humor" with the description I gave for dropsy. Such is the second description. Thirdly, after one is cured of the diabetic or uterine condition, then for 1, 2, or 3 months, use the description of <term>diacubebe</term> <note>a preparation made from cubeb, a type of pepper</note>, because the liver and stomach have been chilled by so much drinking. To restore them, the description of diacubebe is effective.

## CHAPTER II.
->On the Milk of the Kidneys.<-

**T**he first essential liquor, placed and separated into this region by the digestive virtue, is the disease of the "milk," and the milk that is produced. This milk is first in the digestion of the kidneys; the second belongs to the blood; the third to the substance of the thing itself. This milk has the nature of milk and undergoes the same separation as milk. From this follows the "rennet" <note>coagulum</note>, the "whey" <note>rustum/serum</note>, sourness, particular coagulation, and serum.

<margin>Ailments of the kidney milk also.</margin>
*The ailments of the milk are these:*
Corrupt discharge <note>sanies</note> of the urine, pus in the urine, oily consumption <note>wasting away</note>, and the urine of "white bleta" <note>original: "bletæ albæ"; an old term for a specific type of white sediment or discharge in urine</note>.

Take:

## Commentaries on the Third Chapter

<margin>Preparation and digestion of food in the body.</margin>
<margin>What the essential liquor is.</margin>
<margin>A whole ox has barely 8 pounds of essential liquor.</margin>
<margin>The nature of kidney digestion.</margin>
<margin>The timing of kidney digestion.</margin>
**O**(N Milk.) The liquids that are generated in the stomach—that is, what is eaten and drunk—are separated in the stomach. The impurity is of <term>sulfur</term> <note>in this context, "sulfur" refers to the combustible, oily part of a substance</note> and passes out through the excrement; the remainder is digested into a liquor, and that liquor retains the color of the food as it was. That liquor passes to the liver, and there it assumes a red color. For the liver takes its nourishment from it, and after it has digested it, it sends the remainder to the kidneys. In the kidneys, it is first white, then red, and there the third nourishment is found. Thus, the "essential liquor" is that from which the limbs are nourished. Indeed, from one pound of what we eat, there is barely half a dram of essential liquor. Thus, in a whole ox, there are barely eight pounds of essential liquor. So, the stomach produces the liquor; then the liver attracts it and separates the pure from the impure, taking its portion and sending the rest to the kidneys. The kidneys then digest it, and the first digestion is white like milk because of the sulfur-quality in the liquor; the second digestion is red. For the third, it separates it and takes its nourishment from there, and the remainder is emitted through the urine. Therefore, observe that in the first digestion, which is white, if the second digestion is not good, then the white digestion remains in the kidneys. For the kidneys have their own time for digesting and operating: three periods of 50 minutes. The first white digestion takes 50 minutes. The second likewise. The third likewise.

<margin>How the "milk" of the kidneys is made.</margin>
<margin>Note: A story from Memmingen.</margin>
And then the expulsive virtue arrives and expels what is impure. If everything is correctly performed and digested, then all is well; if not—that is, if the second digestion is bad and does not do its duty—it still expels. And if it is still in the first digestion and the second has not yet begun, then they urinate, and the urine is expelled like milk, and indeed, it *is* milk. And if, after urination, <term>rennet</term> <note>original: "coagulum"; an enzyme used to curdle milk</note> is thrown into that milk, it curdles, and whey is deposited at the bottom; or if you pour in vinegar, it separates. Whenever you see such a thing in the urine, judge the second digestion to be bad—that is, it was expelled before it was correctly digested, the expulsive virtue having arrived too soon. Therefore it is not pus, but milk, as they say, etc. I saw a beggar who urinated milk for five years; and this so weakened him because of the bad second digestion that he died. And when that physician poured wine or vinegar into that milk, it curdled; and if he let it stand for two or three days, a "flower" or fat would sit upon the top. Thus, it is indeed milk.

### (Ailments of the Milk.)

<margin>What Sanies is. What Pus is.</margin>
<margin>From where pus is urinated.</margin>
That substance is properly called <term>Sanies</term> <note>a thin, greenish-red discharge from a wound</note> when something becoming healthy pours out or produces pus. Sanies is that which flows spontaneously by and from itself. <term>Pus</term> <note>thick, yellowish-white fluid from infection</note> is that which is drawn out by a plaster and found under a plaster. A Physician must most carefully consider what the urine is and what ailments come from it. Just so here: the fact that milk is urinated is due to an imperfect second digestion. Likewise, when the second digestion is good, yet "salt" or "split alum" <note>mineral deposits</note> falls from the limbs into the center; or because the salt of the urine descending from the liver forestalls the second digestion before it can begin—that is, the urine from the liver meets the second digestion too quickly and is separated prematurely—it carries the urine out with it. Then the urine is like milk-whey, and kidney filaments run together (namely, from the curdling). And if that curdled matter is not entirely expelled through urination, it lies in the kidneys and putrefies, and from there pus is urinated. The cure here is to apply urinary remedies so that it is not separated from the liver so prematurely, and so that the spirit does not anticipate the second digestion. From this comes white urine, and often consumption follows.

<margin>From where urinary fat comes.</margin>
<margin>What Nustus is and how it is made.</margin>
The cure is in the text where the test is: take it out and set it on a tablet. If ever urine shows fat, oiliness, or <term>Nustus</term> on top, they say it is from the melting of the kidney fat due to heat. This is true in some diseases, like fevers, where the kidneys melt from the heat. But to know if it is from disease (fevers) or from Nustus, the test is to take it and set it on a tablet. If it remains firm like fat, it is from the fat of the kidneys. If it does not thicken, it is Nustus. Nustus occurs because when the second digestion is weak, the first digestion—like all milk—emits or suspends fat on the surface; and if the second digestion does not take that fat up for processing because of weakness, it later exits with the urine and appears on the surface. This is Nustus: namely, that which the second digestion did not take up. And such urines commonly deposit a white lime at the bottom: and if sand...

# TREATISE III.

<margin>Cure for Nustus.</margin>
### *Cure for Nustus.*

> ℞. 1 ounce of Turpentine washed in rose water. 2 drams of Frankincense lozenges.
> 1 and a half drams of Liquid of Mummy <note>original: "Liquoris Mumiae"; a resinous medicinal preparation</note>. 5 drams of Liquid of Myrrh. Let it be made in the form of a <term>bolus</term> <note>a large, soft medicinal pill</note>. The dose is from 1 to 4 drams, morning and evening.

This medicine is to be administered for as long as it takes until the urine carries no more fat, or until white lime stops settling at the bottom.
<margin>Error regarding bladder stones.</margin>
When people see white sand at the bottom, they claim it is a stone in the bladder; but it is nothing of the sort. When there is oiliness on the surface and white sand at the bottom, it is <term>Nustus</term> <note>an oily or fatty film on the urine, considered by Paracelsians to be "essential liquor" escaping the body</note>.

<margin>Urine of Bleta, how it is to be judged.</margin>
*Bletæ, etc.)* Often urine flows out like a whitish <term>bleta</term> <note>likely referring to chyluria or albuminuria—milky or protein-rich urine</note>, that is, a greenish-white, and if it is held up against wood or a wall, it becomes visible. Generally, urine should not be held up against the sky, for that is deceptive, but against wood or a wall, and yet in a brightly lit place. They [the old doctors] said that this sort of greenish urine comes from indigestion of the stomach; others say from indigestion of the liver. For in such urine there is no <term>hypostasis</term> <note>sediment that settles at the bottom</note> nor <term>ethmoides</term> <note>sieve-like particles</note>; and therefore they say it is from the stomach, even though nothing is lacking in the stomach. It is nothing [of the sort], but the patient is still able to eat, etc. They do not know that the sediment is altered in the kidneys and the liver: if the urine tastes like urine, then it is from the liver. If it has no taste, it is from the kidneys, and that greenish urine takes the Nustus into itself—that is, it contains fat and coagulated matter—but it does not take in the whey of the milk; therefore it has its own greenish color.

It is a certain sign that when urine shines upon the hand like drawn or beaten gold, it comes from the blood. If, however, it is saffron-colored but does not shine, then it is from the liver.

### *Cure for Urine like Bleta.*

> ℞. Half a dram of Radish seed. 2 drams of Mastic.
> Indian leaf. Of the 4 kinds of <term>myrobalans</term> <note>astringent plum-like fruits used as a purgative</note>, 7 drams each.
> Gum Arabic dissolved in a sufficient amount of sage water for incorporation. Let lozenges be made. The dose is from 1 and a half drams to 3 drams, morning and evening.

<margin>What kinds of diseases arise from Bleta urine.</margin>
Wherefore, when such types of urine pass, as I have just recounted, and they persist—that is, they last for a year—they generate four sicknesses: <term>Phthisis</term> <note>wasting of the body; consumption</note>, <term>Ethica</term> <note>hectic fever</note>, <term>Diabetica</term> <note>diabetes</note>, and <term>Hydropisis</term> <note>dropsy or edema</note>. These are not the "true" versions of those diseases, but they are so similar that they are like the daughters of those wild beasts.
<margin>How Phthisis occurs.</margin>
Phthisis arises from this because, when there is coagulated matter in the kidneys and digestion is not present, then the kidneys begin to be consumed because they have no nourishment, the desire for intercourse fails, and pains in the hips set in. From there follows phthisis of the whole body, because when all the principal members do not have and do not receive their nourishment, then the consumption of the whole body follows.
<margin>How Ethica occurs.</margin>
Likewise <term>Ethica</term> <note>a slow, wasting fever</note> arises from the regions of the liver, because blockages occur in the kidneys through those substances, causing tremors—not great ones, but a long-lasting heat, etc.
<margin>How Diabetica occurs.</margin>
And <term>Diabetica</term> <note>diabetes</note> occurs because when nourishment cannot go to the kidneys, they are dried out and thirst is created.
<margin>How Hydropisis occurs.</margin>
<term>Hydropisis</term> <note>dropsy/swelling</note> occurs because when the coagulated matter lies in the kidneys in this way, and the expulsive force cannot push it out, it then descends through the pores of the flesh and causes a tumor <note>here meaning a swelling or edema</note>. But it is not true Dropsy: therefore, where the previous remedies do not help, as in Hectic, Phthisis, or Diabetes, use this medicine to prevent it.

> ℞. 1 dram and 1 scruple of pure Agaric. 3 drams of Poppy seed. Half a dram of Hematite. Magnet and Calamine, 2 scruples each. Let them be mixed with the juice of Lemons or Oranges in the manner of an electuary. The dose is from 4 drams to 2 drams, morning and evening.

That medicine should be administered so that it is used for eight days, and after a year it should be used again, and so on continually. For people should be protected by this medicine against the dropsy that arises from this generation [of matter].

> ℞. Serapinum <note>a gum resin</note> and Laudanum, half a dram each. Galbanum, Lapis Lazuli, and Hermodactyls <note>a type of colchicum used for joint pain</note>, equal parts. Rose conserve in a sufficient quantity for incorporation.

<margin>An aureus weighs 1 dram and 1 scruple.</margin>
The dose is half an <term>aureus</term> <note>a weight based on a gold coin</note>. An aureus weighs 1 dram and 1 scruple. That medicine should be given if there is fear of a swelling of the feet attacking; and after the swelling has ceased, the medicine should also be stopped: and after a year, if it returns, it should be given again. For sometimes it is not a cure for the disease, but a preservation.

## CHAPTER IV.
## On Fevers of the Kidneys.

<margin>Cause of kidney fevers.</margin>
**F**evers originating from the kidneys have their beginning from the dregs of <term>tartar</term> <note>mineral deposits from the body's third stage of digestion</note> of the third separation; and according to the digested time, it creates a paroxysmal hour and a trembling of the whole body according to the nature of the blockage. However, fever from a blockage of the veins is of another kind: namely, that which is called a fever of the veins, such as the fever of the Median, Salvatella, Saphenous, and similar [veins].
<margin>Kidney fever is most dangerous and why.</margin>
Kidney fever is the most dangerous because of the Salt. In the stomach, the separation is coarse. In the liver, it is more subtle. But in the kidneys, it is the most subtle of all. No digestion ceases, except by a <term>narcotic</term> power.

### *Signs.*

<margin>Quartan fever often from the kidneys.</margin>
Stinging pains in the <term>ischia</term> <note>the hip or sciatic region</note> arise from the blockages; from there also come griping pains in the belly, pains of the head and spine, and sometimes the feet swell, the spleen suffers, the urine is entirely red, and it most often happens that a <term>quartan</term> <note>a fever recurring every four days</note> fever arises from the kidneys.

### *Cure.*

Purging should not be done, except by means of <term>arcana</term> <note>secret alchemical or "hidden" remedies</note>. Let all things be done with great care.

*Description for all kidney fevers (whether daily, tertian, or quartan).*
> ℞. 1 dram of <term>Alcoli</term> <note>a fine powder or essence</note> of tortoises. Half a dram of well-ground and calcined Crystal. 1 scruple of Mummy. Make a powder. The dose: the whole amount.

### *Another.*
> ℞. 1 scruple of Liquid of Laudanum. 3 grains of Saffron. (Otherwise: 3 scruples of Saffron, 3 drams of Aloephatic). Make common pills with wormwood water. The dose is 7 grains.

### *Item, another.*
> ℞. Half a dram of Alcoli dissolved from the ashes of wormwood. 1 scruple of Oil of Colcothar <note>iron oxide or calcined vitriol</note>. Mix, and administer all of it before the paroxysm.

### *Explanation of the Fourth Chapter on Kidney Fevers.*

<margin>Kidney fevers are most acute.</margin>
**T**hese fevers, which arise in the Kidneys, also come from putrefied tartar, just as others do in the stomach and liver. But fevers in the kidneys are the most vehement of all, because no member feels more grievous pains than the re- [kidneys]...

<margin>
Why digestion varies in different parts.
</margin>
...when they are afflicted. Therefore, the ailments that fall upon the kidneys are the most acute and severe of all, because if fevers exist in the kidneys, they must arise from putrefaction. That putrefaction is of the most acute sort—it is milder in the liver, and even more mild in the stomach. But in the kidneys, whatever descends to them from the "second digestion" into the "third" <note>In Paracelsian physiology, the first digestion occurs in the stomach, the second in the liver, and the third in the specific organs/kidneys</note> descends through the urine. Therefore, what descends is more refined. Thus, where it is afflicted, it is more acute. For in the stomach, digestion is coarsest; in the liver, it is subtle; in the kidneys, it is most subtle—namely, the urine—and from this, the kidneys take their nourishment and expel the rest. Therefore, if that material putrefies, the spirit is most sharp—namely, when digestion in the kidneys is not completed. This happens due to a "narcotic force": if even a small amount of such force reaches the kidneys, they "fall asleep," digestion within them ceases, and then there are pains in the back, coldness, shivering, and so on. It is a sign that digestion in the kidneys is dormant when nourishment is transmitted from the liver but cannot be processed, and the kidneys lack their own nourishment. When they do not digest, the expulsive faculty arrives and drives the material out. If it does not expel it, then the matter putrefies and becomes dregs <note>original: "soligo"</note> which settle in the region of the kidneys. Then, those things in the renal region also dissolve themselves, because vapor is produced from putrefaction. Since they cannot escape—specifically because that vapor coagulates in the passages <note>original: "potis"</note> and thus causes a blockage—there are then stinging pains in the loins, the private parts, and the head.

<margin>
How a renal paroxysm occurs.
</margin>
Stinging in the hip <note>sciatica</note> arises from blockage: because the vital spirit must pass through everywhere, and when it tries to break through by force, it strikes and stings. When it gets inside the joints, it also irritates. Therefore, there is no worse fever than that in the kidneys and near the intestines. Thus, griping pains, stings, and headaches arise from this: because when digestion does not occur in the kidneys, and the "attractive faculty" <note>the biological force that draws nourishment to an organ</note> has nothing to draw, the kidneys then "ascend" toward the liver <note>a metaphorical way of describing the pull of the organ's needs</note> because they are blocked and yet they have need of drink and moisture. Therefore, through the spine, they pull nourishment from the head—first in the back of the head, then occupying half the head, and sometimes pains occupy the whole head. Because when the attractive faculty of the kidneys pulls the nourishment of the head (the very thing the head should be nourished by), it draws the "flux" <note>flowing humors</note>, and thus the matter in the kidneys is increased by the flux, and the fever increases. Therefore, in <term>Hemicrania</term> <note>migraine; literally "half-head"</note> and every headache, the only cure is that the kidneys be treated first.

<margin>
The kidneys' strong attractive power.
</margin>
Pain is felt in the hip because the kidneys pull forcefully. There is a great attractive power in them. From this, pains of the crown of the head and the back arise. They <note>conventional physicians</note> order people to be scarified <note>to have the skin lightly cut to draw blood or fluids</note> along the spine, and to purge the stomach, and so on. It is for nothing. But in every "cephalic" <note>head-related</note> ailment (I except those arising from the blood), you should always ask whether hip pains are present; if so, the headache is from the kidneys, and it always originates there. It is the same when the region near the head is blocked: then, if there is a clearance in the spleen, it draws from the spleen, and then there is pain in the spleen, and so on.

<margin>
What the sand in urine is like.
</margin>
Furthermore, a Physician should not always say, when a patient says their hip hurts, that it is "sand" <note>gravel</note> or a stone. He should not trust the sign alone, but should look at the urine. If the urine is thin and red, and shows bubbles on the surface, then it is sand. Therefore, he who wishes to consider correctly should first see the uncorrupted urine, and afterward let it "corrupt" <note>sit and settle/ferment</note> so that he can judge it. Likewise, if a burning sensation is felt during urination, it is also sand. But when these signs are absent, and the urine is of a brick-red, pale, or grain-like color, and moreover turbid and confused, then you may say the kidneys are "laboring." One should not consider the <term>hypostasis</term> <note>the sediment at the bottom of a urine sample</note> because that color does not have a hypostasis; but when the urine is like this, it is the beginning of putrefaction, that is, of fevers. Because digestion is failing, the expulsive faculty nonetheless drives the matter out. Sometimes it happens that the urine is good today and not tomorrow, because it is expelled at intervals. But when it collects for a time so that vapors multiply, then digestion begins, and the vapor—or rather the acidity in the putrefaction—produces "alices" <note>spots or small eruptions</note> and stinging of the ligaments; the sick complain of back pain.

<margin>
Most quartan fevers are from the kidneys, not the spleen.
</margin>
When the vapors are too numerous, they fill the region of the liver and block it entirely, and thus the whole body is stirred up, and remains so until the digestion in putrefaction ceases. Every <term>quartan fever</term> <note>a fever that recurs every four days, traditionally associated with the spleen and "black bile"</note> is commonly from the kidneys, not from the spleen, and the paroxysm <note>the sudden onset of symptoms</note> lasts until the digestion ceases and the vapor is expelled. When that vapor exits through the body, heat follows, because it enters the blood. Therefore, if someone gives a good draught of plantain water or Water Lily after the paroxysm, the heat is not felt because the blockage is immediate; but immense back pain follows. Therefore, the paroxysm ceases when the vapor has exited the body, but the putrefaction is still present in the kidneys. Thus, when the crowd <note>the accumulated matter</note> is later processed and digestion occurs, the paroxysm returns again, and so on.

<margin>
Venous fevers: how they occur and are cured.
</margin>
Thereafter, there are fevers that come neither from the stomach, liver, nor kidneys. They are generated thus: when a blockage occurs in some vein, then there is also putrefaction, and it also causes a tremor. In short, they come from blockage and there is a tremor, as in fevers from the kidneys. These fevers are cured by <term>phlebotomy</term> <note>bloodletting</note>, and phlebotomy should be performed where the blockage or fever is in the veins. This should be observed in Anatomy: how it can be that a fever can exist in a vein and not be able to shake the whole body. Thus, regarding fevers in the veins, if a fever is in the <term>salvatella</term> <note>the vein on the back of the hand, near the little finger</note>, do not look at the beginning of the hand but at its root—namely, that the attractive power has drawn from the "tartar" <note>stony metabolic waste</note> that caused the blockage, and so on.

<margin>
Signs of fevers in the veins.
</margin>
The signs of fevers in the veins are stinging sensations in the veins; that is, the patient says after the paroxysm that they feel a stinging in the vein. It is most certain that the fever is in the veins. Often there is a fever in the liver and also in the veins, and a double paroxysm: then there are two fevers, not in one place, but one in the veins—namely, if stings and their putrefactions are present—and it does not stop before the paroxysm. Pierce the vein that feels the stinging, and the patient will feel better.

<margin>
All tremor is from the time of digestion.
</margin>
Note: everything that causes trembling, whether in the plague or otherwise, comes from the "digested time" <note>the specific window of time when the body processes materials</note>. Often the fever stops by itself. For if the putrefaction stops, the fever stops. Often there are also fevers in the spine, and scarification along the spine removes them, especially in a quartan fever at its end. For it often happens that when there is a fever in the kidneys and a headache, and the kidneys have drawn nourishment from the head, even when the putrefaction in the kidneys stops, it is possible that putrefaction remains in those pathways; then scarification along the spine cures it at the end of the quartan fever. It also often happens that all fever ceases, yet on an "evil day" <note>a day when the fever was expected to return</note> they still feel something; then scarification along the spine is effective.

<margin>
Renal fevers are cured neither by purging nor by usual diet.
</margin>
**Cure of fevers in the kidneys.**) Purging through centaury or hellebore is of no use in the kidneys or liver, because it does not serve those parts. But when the problem is in the stomach, then purging helps. Nor is the diet to be concerned with in the kidneys as the Italians prescribe in their regimen. I admit that pork is not good because it generates many humors by which the disease is increased; however, if it is omitted, it does not therefore...
