<margin>Fried meat is as harmful as cabbage, etc.</margin>
...and they are treated accordingly. Thus, pickled cabbage, etc. But if the Physician is skilled, even if the fried <note>original: "fus"</note> meat remains whole within the sick person, it does no harm, because the medicine is more powerful. Nor should the "complexions" <note>The traditional Galenic balance of hot, cold, moist, and dry qualities</note> of medicines be observed, but rather the *arcana* <term>arcana: the secret, essential healing virtues of a substance</term>, which lack a complexion.

# CHAPTER V.
### *On usnea, hail, and stone in the bladder.*

<margin>Usnea and hail are in everyone; stone is not.</margin>
**IT** has been treated above with sufficient abundance what usnea is, what hail is, or what stone is: it is established that usnea is formed from the first separation of tartar, hail from the second, and stone from the third. Hence, it is now appropriate to describe the cures for these diseases once some signs have been presented: first, however, it should be noted that any human being has usnea and hail, but not everyone has the stone.

->Signs<-
Stones move in their own digested time and weaken the area below the navel. Hails bring about pains like a cutting knife.

Usneas <note>In this context, usnea refers to a fine, moss-like or filamentous sediment rather than actual moss</note> affect the spine of the back and the hips.

->Cure.<-
Let the tartar be resolved into a liquid or a powder. Although the stone of the bladder can only be resolved with difficulty or never at all, nevertheless, when it originates from wine or sharp things, it sometimes undergoes resolution. We, therefore, set down this cure for usnea and hail in "sharp tartar."

->*Description of the Oil of Colcothar.*<-
<margin>Description of the oil of colcothar.</margin>
Take of the reddest Colcothar <term>Colcothar: the red oxide of iron remaining after the distillation of vitriol</term>, 10 pounds.
Alcohol of wine, 7 ounces. Let a mixture be made in a vial according to the process of the Retort, with distillation from the first until the fourth day, and the reddest oil will come forth, most burning from the fire. Administer a drop of that oil with radish water (otherwise in good wine) morning and evening, and it is a cure for usnea and hail, but not for the stone.

->*Description of Serpheta.*<-
<margin>Description of Serpheta.</margin>
Take of Scorpions, 1 dram. Of little stones from crabs <note>original: "lapillorum cancrorum," also known as "crab's eyes," which are calcium deposits found in the stomach of crayfish</note>.
Of Columbine root, 2 drams of each.
Of clear Beryl, 1 dram. Let a mixture be made with alcohol of wine and fat.

->*Medicine for the resolution of usnea and hail.*<-
Take of Mead, 1 pound. Of radish roots and Columbine, half a dram of each.
Species of *Lithontipon* <term>Lithontipon: a "stone-breaker" medicine</term>, 1 dram. Let a mixture and decoction be made to the third part; let it be given warm as a drink.

->*Another for hail and usnea.*<-
Radish seed, 1 dram. Cabbage leaves, half a dram. Oriental Saffron, 3 scruples. Make a mixture for a small bag, which should be applied along the penis.

->Another.<-
Distilled Tartar. Fenugreek seed, Psyllium, 2 drams of each.
Prepared Beryl, 7 ounces. Make a powder or compound. The dose is from 2 to 4 drams.

You will note that saxifrage <note>literally "stone-breaker," a plant reputed to dissolve stones</note> breaks the stone easily; but to drive out the fragments is the work of Samson <note>A metaphor for a task requiring immense strength</note>.

->*Laxative for the calculus in the bladder.*<-
Take of the first buds <note>original: "locustarum," referring to the young shoots/buds of the plant, not the insect</note> of Elder, 1 dram.
Mountain Laserwort, 2 drams. Taberseth sugar <note>A high-quality refined sugar</note>, 2 drams.
Cinnamon, Mace, nutmeg, 1 and a half drams of each. Make a powder. Dose from 1 to 3 drams.

->*Addition to the Lozenges of Alkekengi.*<-
Take of Lettuce seed, 1 dram. Distilled Turpentine, half a dram.

->*To the Lozenges of Frankincense.*<-
Take of Mummy <note>A common medicinal preparation made from bitumen or preserved remains</note>, 2 drams. Of red Lac, 2 scruples. Of civet <note>original: "spermate cati"</note>, 2 scruples. These cure by putrefaction; that is, they cleanse. Saxifrage for the stone from bolus <note>A type of medicinal clay</note>.
Take of white Corals, 1 dram. Magnet, half a dram. Hematite to the weight of all. Make a powder. Dose: 1 scruple in white bolus wine.

->*In the cure of the stone from resolved gems.*<-
Take of Citrine stone, 1 dram. Amber of both kinds, 4 drams of each.
Rhubarb, half a scruple. Make a liquor in the manner of an Alcohol. Dose: half a scruple in good wine.

->*Saxifrage in the cure of the stone from mucilaginous mistletoe.*<-
Take of Oak mistletoe, 4 ounces. Quince seed, of bitter peaches, 2 drams of each.
Columbine flowers, 3 scruples. Dragon's blood <term>Dragon's blood: a bright red resin from the Dracaena tree</term>, 2 drams.
Honey of roses, as much as suffices for incorporation. The dose is half a dram.

->*Another for the cure of the hardest calculus.*<-
Take of Liquor of cantharides <note>Spanish Fly</note>, 1 dram. Of Columbine roots, 2 drams.
Agalloch <note>Agarwood</note>, 6 drams. Make a mixture with washed serpentine.

## **Annotations on Chapter Five.**

<margin>Three ailments of the bladder.</margin>
**ON** the stone in the bladder or concerning the bladder.) It should be observed what the ailments in the bladder are. The first is stone; the second, ulceration. The third, putrefaction. First, concerning the calculus, in which the cure is difficult because it is reduced into a liquid with difficulty, but rather into a powder <note>original: "Alcool"</note>.

<margin>Laxatives should not be used for bladder stone.</margin>
But care must be taken: when there is a calculus, the bladder should not be purged or loosened; rather, patients are commonly constipated when they have a calculus. But I will indicate a laxative that is neither mediocre nor troublesome.

->*Laxative for the stone of the bladder.*<-
Take of the first buds of elder, 1 dram. Juniper buds do the same.
Mountain Laserwort, 2 drams. Taberseth sugar, 2 drams.
Cinnamon, Mace, Nutmeg, half a dram of each.

<page-num>484</page-num>
<header>ON TARTAR, BOOK II.</header>

<margin>What the sprouts are.</margin>
...of the powder. The dose is from two to three drams. *Sprouts of Elder* <note>original: "Locustæ Sambuci"; here refers to tender young shoots, not insects</note> are the tender shoots breaking out in May. Let them be dried in the shade and preserved. That laxative does not purge or loosen harshly, but leads nature back to its natural and accustomed seats. Therefore, it is to be used, and one should avoid *Turbith, Senna, Suppositories*, etc. These are to be avoided even if the patient complains of the stomach, because it is the nature of stones that they cause continuous pain in the back, the sciatica, the hip, and so on. But that gentle laxative keeps nature in its proper place, as do the sprouts of *Juniper*, and similar plants.

<margin>How the liquor of saffron is prepared.</margin>
Another symptom is that they cannot urinate. Urine must be provoked so that the kidneys are strengthened, and they expel the blockage and are cleared. Let the clearing be done, and this is achieved by saffron, or the liquor of saffron. When placed in horse dung in a sealed glass, let it putrefy for one month. Afterward, when it is putrefied, add white wine into a pot and let it simmer until a certain thickness remains at the bottom. Give 1, 2, or 3 drops of that in wine; then it drives out the urine. However, when a stone is lodged in the passage, this cannot work, and the matter must be dealt with using instruments. Sometimes, <margin>Why urine is suppressed.</margin> the urine does not flow because of a swelling. At other times, it is because the stone is made of lime <note>original: "calce"; referring to a chalky or calcium-based deposit</note>, which, being arid and dry, attracts moisture from the kidneys like a sponge; a small portion of it flowing causes an intense burning sensation. Whenever this burning is felt, consider it to be a gypsum-like stone, so "calcinated" <note>reduced to powder or lime by heat</note> that it attracts all moisture. Stones of this kind, when cut out and placed in urine, attract and absorb everything like a sponge. In such cases, people use radish seed to stir the urine, but this is not <margin>Saffron draws urine for the exhausted. Cantharides are diuretics.</margin> well done, because it does not treat the true urine: saffron alone does this. Note: Oriental saffron will extinguish the "lime" of the stone.

Another thing that provokes urine is *cantharides* <note>Spanish fly; a beetle used as a potent, though often dangerous, diuretic</note>. But it is not a commendable medicine; it is useful where there is a blockage, for it penetrates deeply. One drop is sufficient, and always add saffron, because it will extinguish the heat of the little stone just as water extinguishes fire. Baths made of turnips are also effective because they extinguish the heat of the stone; once that is extinguished, the urine flows correctly, and there is a cure. If, however, the stone is stuck in the passage, it belongs to surgery; and where the stone is, there is vomiting and perpetual pain, which are treated by baths.

<margin>A cut bladder heals in the middle of the flesh.</margin>
Ulcerations occur because it often happens that the urine breaks through five or six places and flows out. This leads to death, because when the bladder is wounded, it does not accept a cure any more than the lung does. If an incision is made, the flesh growing over it binds together and heals, but the bladder itself does not. Putrefaction occurs when the matter of the stone arises from a "coagulum" <term>coagulum: a curdled or thickened mass of bodily fluid</term> but cannot yet generate a stone; <margin>Lozenges of Alkakengi, etc.</margin> this is putrefaction. This is removed by *Alkakengi lozenges* <note>Winter Cherry</note> and *Frankincense lozenges*.

### Addition to the description of the Alkakengi Lozenges.
Take: *Lettuce seed*, 1 dram. *Distilled turpentine*, half a dram.

### Addition to the Frankincense Lozenges.
<margin>Frankincense lozenges.</margin>
Take: *Mummy* <note>original: "Mumiæ"; a common medicinal preparation of the era made from bitumen or preserved remains</note>, 2 drams. *Red lac* <note>a resin</note>, 2 drams.
*Spermaceti*, 2 scruples.

These remove putrefaction; sometimes they even cure ulcerations, but with difficulty. For in an ulceration, the only goal is that it be cleansed, not that it be closed up. If it were possible for the stone to be shattered, it should be done through the following descriptions. If you apply them and profit nothing in three or four days, stop and try something else. Furthermore, three medicines must often be used for these patients, because many other diseases are often commonly present and coincide with the stone.

### A stone-breaker for a stone made of clay-like earth.
<margin>Excellent stone-breakers.</margin>
Take: *White corals*, 1 dram. *Magnesia*, half a dram.
*Hematite* <note>bloodstone</note>, equal to the weight of the others. Make a powder.
<margin>The use of the stone-breaker.</margin>
*The dose is 1 scruple in good white wine. It must be observed in this medicine that if anyone suffers from the stone, put the powder in half a measure for six days, and give it to be drunk, and stir it whenever you give it. It should also be observed that when you give it to drink, all the discharged urine should be brought to you. If there is powder at the bottom, the medicine is breaking down that stone, and that is good. If you find nothing, the medicine has achieved nothing. The color must also be observed. If the powder is white, it is from the bladder, and that is well.*

### Another stone-breaker for the cure of a stone from a dissolved gem.
<margin>What citrine is.</margin>
Take: *Citrine* <note>yellow quartz</note>, 1 dram (*Citrine is a stone between crystal and beryl, yellow in color*).
*Both types of amber* <note>original: "Carabæ"</note>, 3 drams each. *Rhubarb*, half a scruple.
*(The rhubarb is not here to act as a laxative, but to lead the medicine to the bladder, for it has a secret power over sand and the bladder; and if its laxative force could be removed from it, it would be the best secret remedy for the stone.) Make a liquid in the manner of an alcohol <term>alcohol: here meaning a highly refined or distilled substance</term>. The dose is half a scruple in good wine. I saw, where this medicine was administered, that afterward up to 4 ounces of powder passed through the urine, and the pain ceased. The patient was named Hans Oschlin. But while he was cutting wood, a stone became lodged in the neck of the bladder, which I was therefore forced to remove by surgery. Thus, when the stone is worn down by medicine so that it becomes smaller and sticks in the neck of the bladder, it must afterward be expelled and extracted with instruments.*

### A stone-breaker for the cure of a stone from mucilaginous slime.
<margin>Stone-breaker for a stone from mucilaginous slime.</margin>
Take: *Oak mistletoe*, 4 drams (or 3 drams).
*Quince seeds*, *Bitter peach kernels*, 2 drams each.
*Columbine flowers*, 2 scruples.
*Dragon's blood* <note>a bright red plant resin</note>, 2 drams.
*Honey of roses*, as much as suffices for mixing. The dose is half a dram.

### Another stone-breaker for the cure of the hardest stone.
Take: *Liquor of cantharides*, 1 dram.
*Columbine roots*, 2 drams.
<margin>What Agallia is.</margin>
*Agallia*, 6 drams. Make a mixture with washed turpentine. They take Agallia for Columbine, but it is not: they are stalks or shrubs a span in height, rough with sharp parts, marked by a purple flower at the top. Therefore, those medicines cure, if it is possible, by wearing down the stone. There is a peasant who, by the juice of Agallia, drives out all stones which are then resolved from slime and clay-like earth. But if the stone is from a gem or rock, then it does not drive it out; but from mucilaginous clay, the juice of Agallia drives it so that it exits with the urine like mud. If this mud is slowly cooked, it returns again to its first matter and becomes stone.

## To the Distinguished Patron of Theologians
# D. ERASMUS OF ROTTERDAM
### TO HIS MOST LEARNED AND BEST,
#### THEOPHRASTUS PARACELSUS.

*Woe to me if the sagacious Muse and the medical arts granted by Alstoois <note>likely a reference to a specific medical tradition or inspiration Paracelsus claimed</note> do not speak clearly within me: I am a manifest author of similar judgments. The region of the liver does not lack for medicines, nor do the other two species require laxatives. The medication is a Masterpiece, a secret <term>arcanum</term> <note>a "secret" or "hidden" remedy that contains the essential healing power of a substance</note> rather from a specific strengthening substance and honeyed cleansers, that is, healing agents. For a defect of the liver, there is a second essence which, from the fat of the kidneys, are royal medicines of skilled praise. I know that your little body cannot suffer the <term>Mesuatic</term> <note>referring to Mesue, a medieval medical authority whose use of harsh purgatives Paracelsus despised</note> colocynths, nor anything turbulent, nor even the smallest amount of such a drug. I know myself to be more suited and more skilled in my art, and I know what things may be of value for your little body toward a long, quiet, and healthy life; you do not need evacuations. The third disease is (to speak more plainly) a certain matter or an ulcerated putrefaction, or a phlegm that has arisen, or an accidental binding, whether it be the dregs of urine, or <term>Tartar</term> <note>Paracelsus’s term for stony deposits in the body, analogous to the crust formed in wine barrels</note> in the vessel, or mucus from the remnants of seed, or if it be a viscous or bituminous nourishing humor. It is resolved fat, or whatever of this kind exists, when it is coagulated by the power of salt (in which the force of coagulation resides), just as in flint, or rather in beryl: this generation is similar. I have perceived that these things were not born in you. But whatever I have judged, I have made a judgment concerning a fragmented marble mineral existing in the kidneys themselves, under the name of coagulated things.*

*If, most excellent Erasmus, my specific practice pleases Your Excellency, I shall see to it that you have both a Doctor and Medicine. Farewell.*

->THEOPHRASTUS.<-

## To the Most Skilled Doctor of the Medical Art
# THEOPHRASTUS THE HERMIT,
### ERASMUS OF ROTTERDAM SENDS GREETINGS.

*It is not absurd for a Doctor, through whom God supplies us with the health of the body, to wish for the eternal health of the soul. I marvel whence you know me so deeply, having seen me only once. I recognize your riddles to be most true, not from the medical art, which I never learned, but from my own miserable sensation. In the region of the liver, I have for some time now felt pains, nor could I divine what the source of the evil was. I beheld the fats of the kidneys in my urine several years ago. As for what the third thing is, I do not quite understand, yet it seems probable to me that it is what troubles me, as I said. In these several days, I have no leisure to be cured, nor to be sick, nor to die, so overwhelmed am I by the labors of my studies. If, however, there is anything that can alleviate my ill without the dissolution of the body, I ask that you communicate it. If you are distracted, explain more fully in a few words those things which you noted more than <term>Laconically</term> <note>very briefly or concisely, after the fashion of the Spartans</note>, and prescribe certain other remedies which, when I have leisure, I may take. I cannot promise a reward equal to your art and zeal; certainly, I promise a grateful mind. You have recalled <term>Froben</term> <note>Johann Froben, the famous Basel printer and friend of Erasmus</note> from the underworld, that is, the half of myself: if you restore me also, you will restore both of us in each other. I wish that fortune were such that it might keep you in Basel. These things were written in haste; I fear you may not be able to read them. Fare well.*

->ERASMUS OF ROTTERDAM<-
->by his own hand.<-

# OF AUREOLUS
# PHILIPPI THEOPHRASTI OF
# HOHENHEIM, THE HERMIT
## On Jaundice.
### BOOK ONE.

->*Explained and illustrated by the Author himself in public lectures at the University of Basel.*<-

### BOOKS
### *On Jaundice.*
#### CHAPTER ONE.

<margin>Jaundice is not from nature.</margin>
<margin>From whence Jaundice comes: namely from the composition of three salts.</margin>
<margin>Jaundice is by no means from the bile.</margin>
**J**AUNDICE <note>original: *Icterus* or *Icteritia*</note>, as it is commonly called, by no means takes its origin from nature, but from a composite thing: nor should you think that the yellow <note>original: *citrinum*</note> color is essentially present in nature or the human body, but rather it borrows that color much more from the mixture of a triple salt. It is no different than how food, which is a composite, receives its blackness from three things: namely from pure <term>vitriol</term> <note>iron or copper sulfates, often used in making ink</note>, <term>sal myseum</term> <note>a specific mineral salt in the Paracelsian system, likely related to copper or vitriol-bearing ores</note>, and liquid sulfur. Thus <term>sal entalicum</term> <note>a term used by Paracelsus for a specific purified salt</note>, vitriolated salt, and the liquor of resolved sulfur, when they come together as one, create the beginning of jaundice and a new color.

From this, it is necessary for the Physician to know that these types of defilements and discolorations of the surface of the skin do not come from nature according to local sense <note>meaning they aren't inherent parts of the body's design</note>. For neither the seed itself, nor the first constitution of man, essentially produced such a thing: nor did it assign colors to parts of the human body. Not that I deny that all colors of every kind are contained in the human body: but that they should appear visibly in their own substance as if they were spread out, this we do not admit; rather, we say they are dispersed here and there throughout the entire body, so that in that dispersion none are missing—not unlike when a gray and green color surrounds abscesses. For those also have their color consisting of a mixture of species or accidents <note>temporary qualities rather than essential ones</note>.

Therefore, we boldly reclaim the argument against the opinion of those who credit this disease to the bile <note>original: *felle*—the traditional Galenic view was that jaundice was caused by an overflow of yellow bile</note>, and who, in their published books, do not hesitate to assert that such a poison exists in the bile alone as to render a man discolored. <margin>A threefold defilement of the skin according to the ratio of the three species.</margin> For it is clear enough from what has been said above that neither illnesses nor colors consist of the bile: but much more, the cause of the disease is from the composition of the three species <note>the three chemical principles: Salt, Sulfur, and Mercury</note> which pour color over the body. And this happens according to the subtlety of the color of each, whether the disease be transparent or subtle, black, yellow, or white; and thus it is to be judged of the remaining colors. In sum, therefore, you will observe that colors depend on transmutation, and in this, that transmutation imitates the skills of the <term>Spagyrics</term> <note>alchemists who used chemical extraction and recombination to create medicines</note>. For the process of artificial tinting is the same in both cases, according to the disposition of nature. Furthermore, it must be known from which colors jaundice is made.

<margin>4 Species of Jaundice and what the cause of each is.</margin>
Yellow jaundice consists of vitriol, Entalic salt, and liquid sulfur: Black jaundice from *myseum*, vitriol, and dissolved sulfur: Green jaundice from the six aforementioned: Pale jaundice from *scisso* <note>possibly "cleft" or "split" alum/salt</note>, Mercurial liquors, and white vitriol. Lastly, we believe (and it is within the power of nature) that colors can even be made from a single species through the forces of transmutation. For we know the wonders of nature in her industry and innate skill.

<margin>Remedies for Jaundice.</margin>
In the beginning of Jaundice, when it is Local.
Take: Centaury 4 drams <note>the symbol $\text{ʒ}$ denotes a dram, roughly 3.9 grams</note>. *Oriental Saffron* 1 dram.
*Myrrh* 4 drams (others say half a dram).
*Burning wine* <note>original: *Vin. ardentis*—distilled alcohol or brandy</note> 15 ounces <note>the symbol $\text{℥}$ denotes an ounce</note> (others say 5 ounces).
Reduce into an essence; the dose is from 1 dram to 4 drams. These draw the color to the stomach: But they do not remove the disease.

### Another description.
Take: Juice of celandine <note>original: *chelidoniæ*</note> 1 lb. Juice of wild vine <note>original: *viticellæ*; likely Clematis vitalba</note> 3 lbs.
Juice of St. John's Wort <note>original: *hypericonis*</note> 1/2 lb. Pure water as much as needed.
This is a bath by which the color is drawn out, but the disease is not cured, because the <term>species</term> <note>the underlying substances or "seeds" of the disease</note> are not yet separated.

### Another.

### Explanation of the First Chapter.

<margin>Minerals are not removed by purgings.</margin>
Jaundice comes with trembling and heat: in this state, do not purge the patient, because minerals are not removed by standard purgations <note>Paracelsus argued that common laxatives only moved "humors," not the mineral "salts" he believed caused disease</note>. A discolored body indicates jaundice: where there is a change in color, there is the disease. This is why the medicine must penetrate the body. There is no dye in the gall <note>bile</note>: therefore, it does not produce jaundice.

<margin>Why jaundice is not from the humors.</margin>
The spleen does not dye: therefore black jaundice is not from the spleen. It does not come from <term>choler</term> <note>yellow bile</note>, because that is in the intestines, and no jaundice comes from it. From red comes lemon-yellow, white, and "elephantine" <note>likely referring to the thick skin of leprosy</note>. The cure of jaundice is achieved through those things that separate the colors. Before the jaundice fully appears, the urine is very white and watery, then reddish, and finally lemon-yellow.

First, the sulfur is liquid; second, <term>entalic</term>; third, <term>vitriolized</term>.

<margin>All color is corrosive.</margin>
Every color is corrosive: whatever adheres to the body is dissolved. <term>Entalic salt</term> <note>a specific alchemical salt in Paracelsus's system</note> is sharp in the blood.

Signs of black jaundice: Piercing pains in both sides, leathery urine, after a few days it turns black, and thirdly it becomes completely dark.

<margin>Signs of which jaundice.</margin>
Signs of red jaundice (or Erysipelas): Headache, swelling of the feet, thick red urine.

"Celestial" <note>blue</note> jaundice is rare. Signs: fissures or cracks in the body, grey-green urine, which later becomes watery, then the whole body turns lemon-yellow: finally it turns cyan, and after that, leprosy.

<margin>Centaury and saffron attract color.</margin>
Centaury and oriental saffron: these draw the color to themselves. Regarding the extractions of color in jaundice: <term>Precipitate</term> <note>original: *Præcipitatus*; usually referring to Red Precipitate or mercuric oxide</note> holds the primary place among these, that is, the red powder from metal. But in short, little is gained by purgings. <term>Viticella</term>: it is long like a vine, having a circle of the color of leather. They do not remove the disease: the bath in <note>the town of</note> Göppingen also takes away the colors, but it is not a cure. Take flowers of celandine: this is another description for extracting the color, but not the disease. Then rub it on: it draws out the colors, and saffron-colored scales fall off.

Signs of black jaundice: piercing of the sides, leathery urine, later it tends toward blackness, and at last becomes entirely black.

<margin>The grey-green are leprous.</margin>
Signs of red: headache, swelling of feet, red urine, heat and cold, as in the plague. Signs of the celestial or cyan-colored: cracks in the back or another limb, the urine is grey-blue, later watery, as if cornflowers had been thrown into it. A person of first a grey-blue and then a "celestial" color is very close to leprosy.

# CHAPTER TWO.
## On the Place and Center.

Furthermore, concerning what remains to be said about the salts of Jaundice, you shall observe: that any part of the body can prepare Jaundice in this sense. Often jaundice of the blood occurs—namely when, as has been said, this kind of generation happens only in the blood—and this is most conveniently corrected by bloodletting <note>original: *phlebotomiâ*</note>, leeches, and other remedies of this kind.

<margin>Jaundice of the blood is cured by bloodletting.</margin>
<margin>Jaundice of the flesh is removed by specific properties.</margin>
Similarly, if a part of the flesh is so infested, know that it is a jaundice of the flesh that has been forged, and for that, medicines appropriated to the flesh are required. The same must be thought of the other principal members. For whichever of these shows jaundice, either by signs or by accidental symptoms, the disease is in that same member.

In all these things, "this is the work, this is the labor" <note>a quote from Virgil’s Aeneid</note>: to know exactly both the location and the center of the disease. For if it is a jaundice of the blood, the first thing will be to immediately inquire into its location and center. Surely, since blood abounds throughout the whole body, it must be noted whether all the veins at once, or only some, have contracted the disease, such as by these signs: when a vein is cut, if the blood bursts out with force, tending toward a yellow color, entirely spongy, frothy, and showing bubbles on the surface, with saffron-colored water.

<margin>Signs produced by the jaundice of the blood's concoction.</margin>
Likewise, the suffering person is vexed at the place of origin by stabbings, heaviness, and other troubles of this kind. In the blood of the flesh, the affliction is not difficult to recognize from the color, but when it infests some specific member, such as the heart, there are other signs: namely compression of the chest and stomach, immense pains, and the occurrence of excessive wakefulness. Thus, when neither purgings nor strengthening medicines <note>original: *confortatiua*</note> wish to help the sick person, you may be most persuaded that the disease consists of Jaundice, whether the body turns into discoloration or not. For whenever jaundice lurks singularly in a member, colors do not appear to us, or only rarely; therefore it must be judged from the remaining indicators.

<margin>Of the flesh, as of the heart.</margin>
It happens in a similar way in women: for afflictions of the womb <note>original: *matricis*</note> for the most part arise from jaundice, namely the "precipitation"...

<margin>Of the womb.</margin>

& suffocation of the womb <note>original: *suffocatio matricis*; a historical term for various uterine disorders believed to cause respiratory distress or anxiety</note>, pains in the spine, and in short, all diseases that cannot be countered by the aid of purgings, consist of jaundice—unless certain and apparent signs of <term>Tartar</term> <note>Paracelsus used "Tartar" to describe stony or mineral deposits in the body, like kidney stones or gouty deposits</note> or another disease argue otherwise. It will furthermore be appropriate to carefully observe <margin>Signs of hidden jaundice.</margin> hidden jaundice, which resides in the womb, spleen, liver, and kidneys. For if the persistence of this most wicked disease lies hidden in these members, it is the one and only sign. Meanwhile, various and diverse judgments are imposed upon the Physician, so that he might judge one <margin>Individual signs of jaundice.</margin> disease for another, when the jaundice of a specific major organ is the sole cause. Finally, these signs almost invariably accompany jaundice: weakening of all limbs, compression of the stomach, heaviness of the shoulder blades, back pain (pains of the spine and major limbs), nausea, no desire to eat, lack of sleep, and finally, they end up paralyzed.

<margin>Remedies for jaundice of the Brain.</margin> Description for Jaundice of the brain.
Take: *Flower-heads <note>original: *antherae*; Paracelsus defines this below as the calyx or base of the flower</note> of hermodactyls <note>the "finger of Hermes," a plant often used for joint pain</note>.*

<margin>Of the Heart.</margin> For Jaundice of the heart, where the swelling does not go away, but the pain does.

*Oil of Angelica 4 ounces.* Reduce into the form of an essence; with this you should anoint the injured place.

<margin>Of the spleen and liver.</margin> For Jaundice of the spleen and liver.

<margin>Of the Kidneys.</margin> For Jaundice of the Kidneys.

*Calictae <note>yellow fungi found on juniper bushes</note> 1/2 ounce each.* Let a mixture be made according to the sun <note>exposed to sunlight for extraction</note>; let it be applied to the pain with a cloth moistened with it.

<margin>Of the Lung.</margin> For Jaundice of the lung.

<margin>Of the Gallbladder.</margin> Against Jaundice of the Gallbladder.

### Regarding the second chapter: On Location and Center.

<margin>Jaundice belongs to all parts</margin> **J**aundice is manifold: namely, of the Flesh, Blood, Bones, Marrow, Ligaments, etc., and of all major organs. The color of the face comes from the liver. The precipitation and suffocation of the womb is nothing other than Jaundice of the womb.

Jaundice of the gallbladder burns in the stomach. Jaundice of the liver does not tint the body but has stings in the sides and paleness of the face. Likewise thirst. Jaundice of the kidneys causes pains in the hip, in the spine of the back, and perpetual pains in the sacred bone <note>the sacrum</note>. If a person suffering from <term>Tartar</term> is placed in <margin>A turnip bath takes away the pain of those with tartar.</margin> a bath of turnips, the pain is taken away immediately.

If women have not labored with colic and are contracted <note>suffering spasms</note>, it will be from Jaundice: if they have had back pains and the menstruation ceases. *Jaundice of the heart* also burns in the stomach, and the heart swells and trembles. *Jaundice of the brain*: if it is about to come out as watery, it comes out of the nostrils as lemon-colored. Likewise, if they heal the head, the water becomes lemon-colored. *Jaundice of the lung* causes difficult breathing, and there is a foulness of the mouth, a cough, and spongy spit—sharp and lemon-colored. *Jaundice of the spleen*: the left side hurts, and it cleaves violently during a run. Likewise in a water bath and if they go out, etc. *Jaundice of the blood*: a specific vein sweats, and indeed the sweat is lemon-colored; the blood has yellow spots. *Jaundice of the flesh* tints the body. *Jaundice of the ligaments*: you apply <term>Basilicon</term> <note>a "royal" ointment made of pitch, resin, wax, and oil</note> according to the alignment of the tendons, and they draw it out. *Jaundice of the bones*: the bones are stung internally, and they feel as if a rigid ice is penetrating them; sometimes it penetrates the flesh. *Jaundice of the marrow* is the worst: it is not a "flow from the head" <note>catarrh</note> as they say.

<margin>What a flower-head is.</margin> A *Flower-head* <note>original: *anthera*</note> is any calyx or head in which the flowers are fixed as if to a base. Take: *Flower-heads of Hermodactyls*. Reduce to an essence, dip a cloth in it, and place it on the head (shaved beforehand): if the cloth is dried, it hardens. Afterward, dip it again, or another, and let it be placed upon the head. *For Jaundice of the chest* <note>original: *praecordiis*</note> according to the description, the swelling does not go away, but the pain does. *Oil of Angelica*: <margin>How to make oil of Angelica.</margin> if angelica is distilled by a water bath <note>original: *balneum maris*; a double boiler</note>, its root should be crushed afterward, then the angelica is cooked in it with white wine. Dip a cloth, apply it until the body grows white. <margin>What Calictae are.</margin> *Calictae* are yellow fungi on the Juniper shrub. *For the spleen*: this description is applied where the pain is, with a soaked cloth. *For jaundice of the gallbladder*: provide the drink as long as the pains last; if the sore should break out in the chest, it should still be given.

# ON JAUNDICES.

<margin>Black [jaundice].</margin>
*Liquor of frankincense.*
*Myrrh, of each* 1 dram <note>original: *ʒ j.*; a dram is about 3.9 grams</note>.
*Wine* 3 pounds.
*Rose vinegar* 1 pound. Make a decoction until it is reduced by a quarter. Soak small cloths in it, apply them while warm, and repeat often; the swelling and redness will vanish.

## Cure for the Black [Jaundice].
Take: *Corrected alcohol of wine* 1 ounce <note>original: *℥ j.*; about 28 grams</note>.
*Of the liquor of myrrh.*
*Frankincense, of each* 1 dram.
*Juice of sage,*
*Thyme.*
*Epithyme <note>a parasitic vine also known as dodder</note>, of each* 1 ½ drams. Make a mixture. The dose is from 3 to 5 drams.

### Another.
Take: *Juice of spurge <note>original: *tithymalli* and *esulæ*; plants of the Euphorbia genus known for their milky, purgative sap</note>, of each* 4 grains.
*Frankincense, myrrh, of each* ½ dram.
*Good theriac <note>a famous polypharmaceutical "cure-all" or antidote</note>, as much as is sufficient* for a bolus <note>a large, soft pill</note>. The dose is from 1 to 1 ½ drams before a paroxysm <note>the sudden onset or worsening of symptoms</note> or during a paroxysm.

## Extraction of color from the outside.
Take: *Broom plant.*
*Flower-heads of clematis <note>original: *antheram flammulæ*</note>, of each* ½ dram.
*Silk-waste <note>original: *seii*</note>.*
*Juice of centaury, of each* 3 drams.
*Wine and vinegar, as much as is sufficient* for a decoction.
Proceed as in the case of Red Jaundice.

## Preventative for Red [Jaundice].
Take: *Pure laudanum <note>in Paracelsus's time, this was a secret complex remedy containing various minerals and herbs, not just opium</note>* ½ scruple <note>original: *℈ β.*; a scruple is about 1.3 grams</note>.
*Waters of red corals.*
*Spodium <note>likely zinc oxide or bone ash</note>, of each* ½ dram. *Liquor of myrrh, frankincense, of each* 3 drams.
*Mace, as much as is sufficient.* Form a mass for pills. The dose is 4 grains.

### Another preventative.
Take: *Hepatic aloes, Socotrine aloes, frankincense, mastic <note>a resin from the pistachio tree</note>, of each* 3 drams.
*Alcohol of wine, rose vinegar, liquor of mullein flowers <note>original: *Tapsi*</note>, of each* 2 drams. The dose is from 1 scruple to 1 ½ scruples.

These preserve against the disease for the space of a year if it should recur. Bloodletting must be avoided, because spasms, paralysis, or tetanus may follow.

<margin>Black.</margin>
## Preventative for Black [Jaundice].
Take: *Lapis lazuli. Juice of mountain parsley <note>original: *sileris montani*</note>, of each* 1 dram.
*Prepared laudanum* 4 scruples. *Oil of nutmeg, as much as is sufficient* for incorporation. The dose is from 1 to 3 drams.

### Another.

*Frankincense, myrrh, of each* 1 ½ scruples. *Distilled vinegar* 6 drams. Make a draught to be taken after a paroxysm; it shall be used after the cure.

## General Medicine for Red and Black [Jaundice].
Take: *Badger fat <note>original: *thassorum*; referring to the badger (Taxus/Meles)</note>* 3 scruples. *Flower-heads of saffron* 1 scruple. *Flower-heads of centaury* 1 ½ scruples. *Oil of nutmeg* 2 drams. Make a draught.

## Preventative for both kinds (or general).
Take: *Liquor of myrrh, frankincense, of each* 3 drams. *Extracted laudanum, badger fat, of each* ½ scruple. *Oil of nutmeg, as much as is sufficient* for a bolus. The dose is from 1 to 2 ½ scruples. (Burning of the stomach and pain in the neck are signs of citrine <note>yellow</note> jaundice.)

<margin>Citrine.</margin>
## For Citrine [Jaundice].
Take: *Buds of poplar, pine, and turpentine-resin <note>original: *botin.*</note>, of each* 1 pound. Reduce into a viscous paste with vinegar and wine, of which take 10 ounces. *Flower-heads of saffron, centaury, of each* 2 drams. Mix them over a fire. The dose is 3 drams in celandine water, daily for 6 or 7 days, three times a day, until the color and pain go away.

## Description of Celandine against Citrine Jaundice.
Take: *Celandine with its roots, and flower-heads of Oriental saffron.*
*Flowers of horehound <note>original: *prassii*</note>, of each.* Reduce into a liquor by enclosed distillation. Of this liquor take 4 ounces. *Woodlice <note>original: *asselliorum*; also called sow-bugs or pill-bugs</note>* 10 (otherwise 15) in number. Make a mixture. The dose is a third part over 3 days; if it is not finished, it is a sign of death.

### Another.
Take: *Badger fat* 1 dram. *Select rhubarb* 1 ½ drams. *Egg yolks, 7 in number.* Make a mixture and a plaster to be placed over the area, that is, the pit of the stomach.

<margin>Secrets for jaundice: spider, lizard, horse dung, rhubarb, etc.</margin>
(A spider enclosed [in a container or amulet] cures both fever and jaundice. Likewise, a lizard enclosed in a little bag has the same power. Likewise, horse dung heated in a urinal and worn by the sufferer, which, when enclosed together in a bladder and hung in smoke for 9 days, heals. Corrected rhubarb is a most effective remedy for jaundice. It is corrected in this way: Reduce rhubarb soaked in oil of bitter almonds into a bolus, then distill it in a glass vessel in the sun, and a yellow oil, then a dark one, is expressed. It is also soaked in these waters—horehound, white horehound, and celandine—as above.)

## Concerning Glaucous Jaundice.
(That is, Ash-colored or Sea-green jaundice. In this kind, pustules of various colors appear, along with weariness of the limbs; this is very close to leprosy.)

## Cure.
Take: *Antimony* 1 pound. *Tartar* ½ pound. *Distilled vinegar* 6. Let distillation be made in a <term>Bain-Marie</term> <note>a water bath used for gentle heating</note> for 6 or 7 hours. The dose is 1 to 4 drams once a day; if it does not remove the jaundice, it is leprosy.

## In jaundice of the principal organs.
Take: *Badger fat, woodlice, of each* 3 drams. *Liquor of rhubarb* ½ dram.

# ON THE PARAGRAPHS.
## BOOK ONE.
### ON THE DISSOLVED DISEASE.
### CHAPTER 1. PARAGRAPH 1.

<margin>What the Dissolved Disease is.</margin>
**E**verything that passes through the stomach finished but undigested is the "dissolved disease": and that which descends from the finished to the unfinished state is the *raw and unprepared matter of the dissolved, and the raw from the prepared.*

<margin>The center of the dissolved disease is the stomach.</margin>
The center is the stomach; the exits are through the anus, through vomiting, and the bladder.

<margin>In how many ways the dissolved disease exits.</margin>
In this first paragraph are indicated the ailments that emerge from "dissolution": when something is eaten and drunk, and is dissolved, but is not properly separated by the stomach, and thus exits even through the urine. And then dysentery, lientery, and diarrhea occur, and there is even a "dysentery of the urine," and "lientery of the urine," etc.; and the same for vomiting, etc. Lientery and dysentery are such, etc.

### PARAGRAPH II.
*The disease is called "dissolved" because it is dissolved in its first operation. Dissolution and putrefaction are one and the same passion, generated from good things.*

It should be noted that dissolution is twofold, either through the stomach or through minerals. This happens if the stomach cannot digest, then it is a dissolution of the stomach; or if minerals are dissolved in the body. For everything watery is dissolved.

### PARAGRAPH III.
<margin>The dissolved disease is threefold.</margin>
*The definition of the disease is this: There are three diseases from dissolution, or from the dissolved things of the first kind: Red, White, and Loose.*

<margin>Red.</margin>
That which is digested but not separated comes away red, just as lumps of blood are often excreted through the anus. All these arise from bad digestion in the stomach; nor does the blood flow from any ruptured vein in the body. If someone urinates blood, yet feels no pain in urinating, nor pain in the loins, or hip, or back, nor perceives any other evil except that he voids blood: then that is a "diarrhea of the urine," etc.

<margin>White.</margin>
If the stools or evacuations are white, foamy like lime or chalk, or have a leathery color, and are thin, sticky, and gassy: that is the white dissolved disease; and the stomach is to blame. If white material comes out through vomiting, it is a "diarrhea of vomiting." If the urine is milky, it indicates a "lientery of the urine"; and if it is without any pain, it is diarrhea. A sign in the urine of the Loose type occurs when the <term>Archeus</term> <note>The vital force or "inner chemist" that Paracelsus believed directed the functions of the organs</note> of the stomach is weak, and the stomach does not work as it should.

<margin>Loose.</margin>
If the urine lacks any sediment, and the patient urinates copiously, and the urine appears now white, now red, now turbid, and has no sediment: then a "flux of urine" is present. If, however, many bouts of vomiting occur: that flux is of vomiting. And the white dissolved disease has its own unique cure, for the red and the loose types also have theirs. And every dissolved disease is either through the anus, the urine, or through vomiting.

<margin>The dissolved disease exits in three ways.</margin>
And likewise, there are three diseases through the urine from the dissolved things: namely, urine of blood, milky urine, and watery urine.

<margin>What mandragorated urine is.</margin>
<margin>What digested vomiting is.</margin>
<margin>What frequent vomiting is.</margin>
<margin>What chest vomiting is.</margin>
Mandragorated <note>original: *mandragorata*; refers to a state of numbness or lack of sensation, like the effects of the mandrake plant</note> or watery urine: and likewise three types of "dissolved" diseases through vomiting: digested vomiting, frequent vomiting, and chest vomiting.

Mandragorated urine occurs when someone feels nothing while urinating, and passes much urine at once without the usual tingling sensation that naturally happens to everyone. Digested vomiting occurs when someone, after eating, is forced to vomit an hour or two later, and this happens as often as they eat. Frequent vomiting occurs if one vomits constantly. Chest vomiting occurs when one is compelled to vomit every eight days, or every three healthy days.

A dissolved disease <note>original: *morbus dissolutus*; a condition where the body's substances are "dissolved" or liquefied, leading to excessive discharge like diarrhea or chronic vomiting</note>, whether it exits through urine, stool, or vomit, is a disease. Its center is in the stomach, and it has a single cure.

## PARAGRAPH IV.

<margin>How many and what are the accidents of the dissolved disease.</margin>
*The power and virtue of the dissolved disease are its "accidents" <note>in historical medicine, "accidents" refers to the symptoms or secondary effects of a disease</note>. There are four via the anus: colic, intestinal twisting, sciatica, and pains of the spine. Three via the urine: dysuria, strangury <note>painful or difficult urination</note>, and laxity <note>incontinence</note>. Three via vomiting: bile, liquid, and hiccups.*

<margin>The cause of dissolution.</margin>
The "fall" <note>the failure or collapse of a function</note> is in the stomach, because the <term>Archeitas</term> <note>the *Archeus*, or internal "alchemist" of the body that governs digestion and life force</note> of the stomach is deficient. Food is the cause, because it is coagulated into a watery state; all coagulation from wateriness becomes a dissolution, and this happens through the failure of the stomach. For the <term>Vulcan</term> <note>the internal heat or digestive fire of the stomach</note> of the stomach cannot digest the food that is ingested today, because it is so, for the Vulcan is aluminous. This is the efficient cause of dissolution. This was mentioned above.

<margin>Signs of dissolution.</margin>
If food now exits the stomach undigested, its property will be to produce twisting of the belly. Similarly, it stirs up pains in the spine of the back, just as sciatica pains occur in the dissolved disease.

The accidents in the dissolved disease through urine are dysuria, strangury, and laxity.

But if the dissolved disease is cured in the stomach, the accidents will subside and vanish of their own accord. Therefore, a primary cure in the stomach is absolutely necessary.

<margin>Hiccups from coldness.</margin>
Similarly, in vomiting, the accidents come from the stomach, such as the bitterness of gall, which arises from great dryness of the stomach. Likewise, hiccups come from coldness of the stomach. Therefore, the true disease is only in the stomach.

## PARAGRAPH V.

*The cure for all these is to treat the stomach.*

<margin>By what means the Archeitas of the stomach is strengthened.</margin>
In the treatment, the dissolved disease must be set forth, and the cause and the "fall" must be handled; through the cure, the stomach must be brought to the point where it digests everything eaten and drunk. The <term>Archeitas</term> of the stomach must be strengthened. This strengthening must be procured through <term>spagyric</term> <note>alchemical</note> grades, so that the pure may be separated from the impure. If one must proceed to the cure, those things should be taken which coagulate the dissolution. This is the description:

The Fern is Dill (otherwise Tansy). The Dragon is coal, burning of its own accord, such as is found in the hearths of blacksmiths near the bellows, and in metal mines. These coals are marked with red lines, which they call dragon's blood.

From the liquids of silica to the weight of the whole. The dose is from one <term>aureus</term> <note>a weight equivalent to a gold coin, approx. 4.5 grams</note> up to one and a half.

# THE SECOND BOOK
# OF PARAGRAPHS.
## On the Diseases of Worms.

### PARAGRAPH I.

**T**he generation of worms has three principles. The first is from nutrients. The second is from minerals. The third is from elemented things.

The generation of worms occurs from putrefaction: but <margin>The matter of worms is threefold. 1. Nutrients. Worms are generated in the stomach.</margin> worms are not generated from every kind of putrefaction. Worms are generated from three causes. One cause is from nutrients. If worms are born from nutrients, they are born in the stomach, and putrefaction is not the cause of the generation of the worms. If putrefaction occurs in the stomach and is not expelled by the expulsive power, then worms are born, and the putrefaction is, as it were, a hostel for the worms. Worms are by no means born in the intestines, but they migrate through the stomach to the intestines. For the womb <note>the place of origin or "matrix"</note> of worms is not in the intestines.

<margin>2. Minerals.</margin>
The second cause is from minerals. For it can happen that worms are birthed in the flesh, in the blood, or in the marrow. These do not take their beginning from putrefaction, but are born from minerals.

<margin>3. Ingested sperm. Worms are born in the stomach in men, and in the womb in women.</margin>
There is a third generation of worms from "sperm" <note>reproductive seeds or eggs of animals</note>, either drunk with water or eaten with fish, when the sperm is in a state of "exaltation" <note>an alchemical state of heightened potency</note>. For then it generates worms. If anyone drinks or eats the sperm of frogs, a monstrous Frog is birthed from it. And so it is with other living things. If women drink sperm of this kind, then the womb attracts and takes it in; unlike in men, whose worms are born in their stomachs. If worms are cast out through vomiting, then they did not arise from sperm, but from nutrients. The spotted lizard <margin>The spotted lizard gives birth in six months.</margin> gives birth to its offspring in six months. If its sperm is drunk, and is fostered for that amount of time either in the stomachs of men or the wombs of women, at the appointed time a monster is generated from it, which its own digestion thrusts forward. Since these monsters are not expelled, they seek food, inflate the belly, and infest and afflict the person: and unless they are cast out, they sometimes last for several years. If worms are generated, they do not have an expulsive power, but they seek their food, and the belly swells up because of them.

### PARAGRAPH II.

<margin>What the types of each worm-origin are.</margin>
From the first principle, there are three types: Raw, Chymous <note>related to chyme/partially digested food</note>, and Excremental. From the second principle, five types: of the veins, of the cavities, of the marrow, of the intestines, and of the regions of the limbs. From the third, four types: of Putrefaction, of Wateriness, of Chaos, and of Heat.

<margin>What kinds of worms come from nutrients.</margin>
Concerning the matter or food from which worms are generated when eaten, three things especially must be noted. First, whether they are generated from raw nutrient. If they are not from the raw, but truly from the chymous, small roundworms are born, and they are made from uncooked "ruby" <note>likely a reference to red, undigested food matter</note>; these are white and somewhat long little worms. From excrement, worms like earthworms are generated, yellow in color. These have thin feet and are generated from dung.

If someone discovers worms in one bowel movement, but not in another, it is a sign that the stomach is disposed toward the generation of worms. Those who exhale foul breath—this is a most true sign of worms that are putrefying in the body. These are thin and long. If these begin to be passed out, it is a sign that the worms are putrefying.

<margin>The nature of worms from minerals.</margin> If worms are generated from minerals, they are born in the stomach. Therefore, if mineral matter descends to the stomach and the "matter of worms" <note>the raw materials or biological potential needed for them to grow</note> is present, worms are produced and exit through the bowels. A person suffering from these is consumed <note>wasted away by malnutrition</note>. Furthermore, the worms that are expelled are bloody.

<margin>Thriac, Mandrake, and the Golden Alexandrine expel worms.</margin> If the sick are given thriac <note>original: *theriaca*; a traditional polypharmaceutical ointment or tonic used as an antidote</note> treated with mandrake, or the "Golden Alexandrine" <note>original: *Aurea Alexandrina*; a famous medieval electuary or medicinal paste</note> prepared with cashews <note>original: *Anacardis*; likely the marking nut or cashew</note>, the worms are driven out full of blood and swollen.

Those which are born in the cavities <note>of the body</note> are formed in this way: they are generated between the skin and the flesh, and they cling to a certain specific place where the patient feels pain, heat, and a gnawing sensation. The matter is similar to a whitlow <note>original: *panaritio*; an infection or abscess at the tip of the finger</note>, and it adheres in the same manner. Such patients eat and drink a great deal.

Worms are also easily born in the marrow; they are yellow on the upper part and white on the lower. These are strong and not slimy. This particular disease is incurable. Mineral worms are also generated in the intestines; these are long, do not become entangled or stick together, and are reddish. No other kind is produced in the intestines. Worms are also produced in the anus, which we call pinworms <note>original: *Ascarides*</note>, which cluster in great numbers around the seat. Nothing expels worms from the intestines more violently than colocynth <note>original: *colocynthide*; the bitter apple, a powerful purgative</note>. <margin>Pinworms.</margin> <margin>Colocynth expels worms, etc.</margin> Betony and agaric <note>a type of fungus used in medicine</note> drive out pinworms. Sometimes the stools are mixed, such that fragments of the worms are ejected with them. But if the intestines are purged by means of colocynth, the worms slip out together and are visible in the stools.

<margin>Worms of the brain.</margin> But the regions of the limbs also know their own worms. For instance, through anatomy, a small worm was found in the brain which had bored through the *pia mater* and *dura mater* <note>the delicate and tough membranes surrounding the brain</note>; from this, a frenzy <note>original: *phrenesis*; delirium or brain fever</note> was provoked. Such worms have also been found in the heart through anatomy. Similarly, worms can be born in the region of the spleen and gallbladder. But in the kidneys, on account of the sharpness of the urine, worms can hardly be produced at all. They can, however, also form in the lungs.

From the "third principle," four kinds of worms arise: those of Putrefaction, of Wateriness, of Chaos, and of Heat. These are easily understood from what has already been said.

### PARAGRAPH III.

<margin>The seed of generated things is twofold: of the thing and of the female.</margin> > *Every created thing is created for a second generation: and where there is generation, there is a twofold sperm, namely, of the thing and of the female. From these, it is possible for a monstrous seed to be present in every sperm, or for monstrous matter to be present in the female.*

<margin>Worms are born from sperm, not from putrefaction.</margin> All worms are born from sperm <note>here meaning "seed" or "germinal essence"</note>, not from putrefaction. For any thing whatever is generated from a seed. For from a seed or sperm, another sperm is born, which is a "monstrous sperm" <note>original: *sperma monstruosum*; in this context, "monstrous" means "deviating from the natural form of the parent," referring to spontaneous generation or parasites</note>, from which all putrid worms in wood, and similarly in man, are generated. In nuts, no sperm is left behind, which is why worms are not generated in them. If a woman is not properly purged after giving birth <note>original: *in puerperio*; the period immediately following childbirth</note>, her belly swells again after some time. This happens because of monstrous sperm. From this, a new generation of another disease is indicated. <margin>Why women in childbed swell up.</margin> Women in childbed must therefore be exquisitely purged. For unless they are properly cleansed, this kind of generation occurs. When a man has died, this monstrous sperm breaks out into action: this is why worms are born in a corpse. <margin>Monstrous sperm is in everything, except nuts and peaches.</margin> And since there is sperm in all minerals, it is certain that the same also flourishes in the flesh, specifically when the seeds of minerals descend to the stomach. Thus, children are born from natural seed. Yet all possess monstrous sperm. In nuts, there is no monstrous sperm. Therefore, the kernel of those nuts generates no worms, though the shells do. This is also the case with peaches. However, the grains <note>seeds</note> of fruits have a true and natural sperm; therefore, even if fruits are forbidden to those troubled by worms, the kernels or seeds of the berries should not be forbidden to them.

### PARAGRAPH IV.

> *It should be known from these things that wood exists from sperm, that is, through seed. It is therefore to be known that there are two generations in all seeds: because the first is natural, but the second is monstrous.*

<margin>The generation of a thing is twofold: Natural and monstrous.</margin> Wood, just like other natural things, is from seed. But worms born in wood are from monstrous sperm. Hence, a twofold generation is established: Natural and Monstrous. Furthermore, every sperm in "sensitive" things <note>living beings capable of sensation</note> also has another sperm within itself, which is monstrous, and can procreate something similar to itself. Any single monstrous sperm can turn into a monster, and into "sensitive life" <note>animal life that can feel and move</note>. <margin>All things have monstrous sperm.</margin> And monstrous sperm is in all minerals. Every herb also has monstrous sperm, but not its own seed. Therefore, for those troubled by worms, fruit should indeed be forbidden, but not the kernels or grains. Sperm is also present in meats. If minerals—that is, mineral sperm—descend to the stomach, they degenerate into worms.

### PARAGRAPH V.

> *And it should be noted along with these, that exalted sperm is fixed, and in its own dead time, it passes into a sensitive virtue, and takes a sensitive body from an insensitive body: just as with the elements: because the generation of flies proceeds from the air, of lizards from the earth, of the spider from fire, of serpents from water, and of fleas from minerals.*

Just as natural sperm has life within itself, so also that which is born from the natural but "beyond nature" can produce something sensible from itself: such as the worms generated from dung, wood, and shells. A similar thing happens even in the elements, which possess monstrous sperm no less than natural sperm. Whence each one produces its own kind. For from the air, flies are born; from the earth, lizards; from fire, spiders; and serpents from water. Flies and beetles <note>original: *Machis*; likely a variation of *mucha* or *magis* referring to beetles/flies</note> are all those which are not generated from dung. Flies are born from the element of Air, because in the elements themselves there is also monstrous sperm. Spiders are from the element of fire; that is, the principle of spiders is from the element of fire. From the primitive element of water, serpents are generated.

### PARAGRAPH VI.
Now we turn to those things which pertain to the cure, which are these: internal medicines and external medicines. Both must share a single nature. Furthermore, one must understand the internal kind of worm through the lens of external medicine. It is also necessary to have a most perfect knowledge of the process of poison. Ultimately, every medicine that kills worms is derived from poison. <note>This reflects the Paracelsian principle that "the dose makes the poison" and that substances which are toxic in large amounts can be curative agents when targeted correctly.</note>

<margin>Laxatives do not expel worms. Centaury liquor kills serpents. St. John's Wort [kills] toads, etc.</margin>
In the treatment of worms, one must reason that those things which kill worms externally will also kill them internally. One should not look to purgatives <note>laxatives</note> here. Worms that are born in fruit will kill all the worms of the body that are born from nutrients. For example, let a worm be taken from meat and added to the following composition with colocynth <note><term>colocynth</term>: the bitter apple, a powerful and toxic plant used as a drastic purgative</note> so that the [internal] worms might touch or taste it. If, therefore, external worms die from this, the internal worms will be slaughtered by the same medicine. No laxative kills worms. Medicines that kill serpents externally also kill serpents within the body. And a serpent is slain on the spot by a liquor made from centaury. St. John’s Wort <note>original: *Hypericonis*</note> oil or seed kills toads most effectively of all, as well as star-lizards <note>original: *stelliones*; likely geckos or spotted lizards</note> and common lizards. The seed of Harmel <note><term>Harmel</term>: Syrian Rue (*Peganum harmala*), known for its antimicrobial and hallucinogenic properties</note> kills the spider. Agaric <note>original: *Agaricus*; a wood-decaying fungus used in old medicine</note> kills flies. Therefore, if worms arise from the elements or from nutrients, they must be killed by a medicine derived from nutrients. Those of the air are slaughtered by Agaric. Those of the water by centaury. Toads and star-lizards are slain by a single medicine. Those which are born from minerals must be destroyed by white vitriol <note>zinc sulfate</note>. Likewise, worms produced from lime, from <term>cachimy</term> <note>an alchemical term for metallic ores or bismuth-like residues</note>, or from marcasite <note>iron pyrite</note> are to be killed by Arsenic. The slaughter must be such that the worms actually taste it. Any medicine that kills worms is a poison. And whatever thing is appropriated to a creature by nature must be applied to it. Thus, if a bit of colocynth is given to animals, it is a poison to them. Yet that same thing is healthy for a human in certain diseases. Agaric is health to a human, but exists as a poison to flies. All medicines of this sort are to be offered against worms. Flour made from decayed fir-wood kills worms born from nutrients. Powder from oak wood removes intestinal worms <note>original: *lumbricos*</note>, especially if coals of <term>turbith</term> <note>a medicinal root</note>, agaric, or mountain laserwort <note>original: *filere montano*</note> are added. A potent powder against worms is also made from agaric, which is their specific poison. In the mines near **Schwaz** <note>a major mining town in the Tyrol region</note>, a black mush adheres [to the walls] which powerfully slaughters worms. The dose of this is ten grains. However, it can be mixed with sugar, Gentian, cloves, etc. In copper mines, a black moss clings to the top, which is excellent against worms. Powder of pine also destroys intestinal worms.

### PARAGRAPH II.

Now, those ailments which belong to the types of falling sickness are these: every species of Epilepsy; the suffocation of the womb <note>original: *suffocatio matricis*; a historical diagnosis for seizures or distress believed to be caused by the movement of the uterus</note> outside of its place; Syncope with its various kinds (namely, recurring fainting, and non-recurring syncope), vertigoes, and that sort.

<margin>What Syncope is.</margin>
If the species are to be cured, the treatment for all is one. Syncope is a fainting occurring once. If, however, it happens more often, it becomes true syncope. The suffocations of the womb also stir up the falling sickness. When suffocations induce a falling paroxysm, the treatment for falling sickness must also be established. It also happens that some fall due to prolonged hunger. These also pertain to the treatment for the falling sickness.

### PARAGRAPH III.

There are also many ailments from the categories of falling sickness without an actual fall: such as *tetanus, spasm, facial twitching* (which immediately convulse and stiffen), universal *Apoplexy, contracted paralysis, curvature along the spine of the back,* or particular curvature in the limbs with the species of *synthena* <note><term>synthena</term>: a Paracelsian term for a specific type of muscular contraction or cramp</note> in men and women.

<margin>The cure for spasm is the cure for falling sickness.</margin>
The sign of Syncope is a fainting of the mind, occurring when pains and torments arise in the stomach: when the sick return to themselves from the paroxysm, they recognize people.

Any spasm and tetanus ought to be healed through the treatment for falling sickness. Apoplexy, which happens immediately with a spasm, ought to be treated like the falling sickness. If they distort the eyes and gnash their teeth, and after this a spasm arises: then the apoplexy descends from the falling sickness. If Apoplexy happens from "the drop" <note>original: *gutta*; historically referring to gout or a specific type of stroke/palsy</note>, the sick look at those present with a direct gaze, and they foam, and turn livid. For these are the signs of "the drop," which does not belong here. In paralysis, if the falling sickness is about to attack, it begins from the brain, and a spasm or tetanus invades that side which is to be struck. This paralysis is from the falling sickness, not from the drop.

<margin>Paralysis is either from falling sickness or from the drop.</margin>
However, paralysis from the drop seizes one gradually; foam rises around the mouths of the sick, and they fall asleep, and those limbs which are struck are weighed down and collapse. This paralysis does not look to the treatment of the falling sickness. Any disease which exists with *synthena* pertains to the falling sickness.

<margin>Synthena.</margin>
*Synthena, etc. Spasm, convulsion.* Curvature in the spine of the back happens when the back becomes hunched. It is referred to the falling sickness. One part falls with an epileptic paroxysm. These people slip away immediately, with foam at the mouth, and the paroxysm arises from the brain. Another part exhibits an Apoplectic paroxysm. *Synthena* is Apoplectic when they become foamy and pour water from the mouth.

<margin>Analepsia.</margin>
*Analepsia.* It attacks in such a way that first the nose turns white; afterwards, Analepsia follows.

<margin>Catalepsia.</margin>
*Catalepsia.* If this disease is about to attack, the sick are drowsy for two hours beforehand.

<margin>Epilepsia.</margin>
*Epilepsia.* White foam precedes this by almost two hours.

<margin>Synthena.</margin>

When they are awakened from the paroxysm, they recognize people immediately, and they are more frequently driven into paralysis than syncope.

<margin>Vertigo.</margin>
*Vertigo.* It seizes more often if one looks down from a high place, such as from stairs, etc. The falling sickness follows this, to be healed by the cure for falling sickness. For many, a paroxysm also creeps up when they are carried on the waters, from the shaking and commotion.

<margin>Tetanus</margin>
*Tetanus*, when it convulses all the limbs, is a paralysis from the falling sickness.

<margin>Synthena.</margin>
*Synthena.* It often seizes men and women when their feet are chilled, if they pass through waters, or if they suffer from a flux; a paroxysm of this sort usually returns after eight days. The cure for this is as for an epileptic paroxysm. *Synthena* also occurs in chronic diseases. And then it is fatal. And when patients complain of trembling of the hands and feet, and that frequently, it is fatal. Therefore, this disease must be attacked directly and cured like the falling sickness. In all ailments that exhibit epileptic signs: in these, the cure must be spent first of all on the falling sickness, whatever other disease may happen.

The cause of the whole disease is in the chaos. For the rest of the things that pass into the falling sickness have their part in the chaos. Whoever wishes to understand the true and genuine foundation of the falling sickness: it is necessary for him to consider that four ailments are produced by the four elements. ## PARAGRAPH III.

<margin>The smoke of Mercury induces Apoplexy and epilepsy.</margin>

Sublimated mercury creates an apoplectic paroxysm when under the form of smoke; it also creates an epileptic one. In this paragraph, only the cause should be noted. And as many species of Mercury as there are, so many species of falling sickness exist. And as the disease is, so is the species. The disease is so powerful that it is not felt by those suffering from it, because they sleep. The species of sublimated Mercury is the true species of Analepsy <note>Analepsy: a historical term for a form of epilepsy where the patient remains unconscious or where the seizure is thought to originate in the stomach</note>.

## PARAGRAPH IV.

*I place the likeness of the cause of this disease in the chaos from chalcedony alkali, pontic saffron, or thereniabin <term>thereniabin; a Persian term for medicinal manna or "honey-dew" found on plants</term>. For just as these penetrate what they are placed into and create a new generation, so too the generation of Mercury shows its danger, passes through the limbs, and, following the Ilech <term>Ilech; a Paracelsian term for a vital or astral force that governs the internal movements of the body</term>, results in a paroxysm of the limb.*

Just as saffron and chalcedony tint water, so too do the "pontic" <note>original: *ponticum*; likely referring to a bitter rhubarb or a similar sharp substance</note> and bile make whatever they touch bitter. Similarly, the epileptic paroxysm, which does not come from the brain but from the chaos, moves all the limbs. And this paroxysm is prolonged until the Mercury is consumed. For as it moves toward consumption, the paroxysm upturns the intestines, the stomach, and all internal organs. And this species is the most severe, leading to death. The *Sinthena* <term>Sinthena; a Paracelsian term for a mortal or fatal seizure</term> is deadly.

## PARAGRAPH III.

One must beware of these: where there is corrupt seed, where there is a vitriolic odor, where there is the generation of winds [gas], where there is the provocation of lust, where there is an "essentialized" sharpness.

Those who are held by the falling sickness should diligently abstain from those things whose "seed" <note>original: *sperma*; here used in a botanical sense as the reproductive essence or core of fruits</note> is monstrous, such as apples, pears, etc. They should also avoid things that taste like Vitriol <term>Vitriol; iron or copper sulfates, associated with sharp, acidic properties</term> placed on coals. Spices are harmful; radishes and turnips are harmful. Cumin and fennel are beneficial. All things that stimulate lust should be fled from. Although it is permitted to eat those turnips which are small and sweet.

# ON RESOLVED DISEASES
<note>Resolved diseases refer to conditions where the body's solid components "dissolve" or liquify, leading to swelling or discharge.</note>

...[of raw egg white] <note>Likely referring to the consistency of humors</note>, following the previous examples: on one side gluten, on the other a tenacious liquid throughout the entire body.

<margin>Hypofarca from dissolved alum.</margin>
If alum <note>In this context, "alum" refers to a specific salt-like principle in the body according to Paracelsian chemistry</term> is dissolved, <term>hypofarca; a swelling or accumulation of fluid beneath the skin, similar to edema</term> is produced. For example, if Roche alum is dissolved, it is a "hypofarca of Roche"; the same is to be judged regarding split alum, ice, and niter. If the eyelids swell, this is also a sign of hypofarca. Pits or indentations near the spine, or in the hands and feet, signify the same. Signs of this kind appear 16 or 18 years beforehand. If the color of the face is altered and these pits form, it is a sign of death. In women who have a discharge <note>referring to menstruation or other uterine flow</note>, if that flow is resisted and suppressed, and the spine is marked by pits, this is a sign of hypofarca. In such a case, nothing is more suitable or healthy than to provoke the discharge. For as long as it lasts, the woman remains free from hypofarca.

## PARAGRAPH 4.
*The cause of Resolution is an accidental element: the earthy accident proceeds from its own dissolved matter; the aerial accident from the conjunction of internal elements; the aqueous accident from the vapors of both mixed elements; but the igneous accident from the spirits of its own elements.*

Alum has four "accidents" <note>properties or manifestations</note> according to the four elements, just as it exists in a congealed state in the body. If the earthy element moves and dissolves, it excites no sickness itself, but forces the element of water into a sickness or hypofarca. This must be known for the sake of the cure. Now, if there is a <term>Vndimia; a Paracelsian term for a collection of pathological fluid or a "vintage" of humors</term> of the earth, it comes from Roche alum. It is appropriate, therefore, that the cure proceeds from that same element. Furthermore, if the element of air is similarly mixed in, it generates a hypofarca of the air. If, however, the element of water moves the disease by itself without another element, and dissolves its own salts, it generates a hypofarca of the water. Finally, when the element of fire is similarly joined with the element of water, a hypofarca of fire occurs. These must be diligently known and distinguished for the sake of the cure, so that the reasoning by which it is established may be certain.

## PARAGRAPH 5.

->*The diet for undimia is itself a medicine. If the undimia is dry, it is a useful medicine. If it is humid, it is a sign of ruin.*<-

<margin>What kind of diet for undimia.</margin>
In the observed care, there is a primary need for diet. Beans, lentils, and chickpeas are healthy. Roasted meat is not suitable. For a stomach loosened by humidity is not fit for digestion. Bean-bread is best, eaten during hypofarca. All diuretic herbs are suitable because they extract the humid juice. <term>Lapulus; hops</term> ought to be put into wine and mixed with foods. For it expels the humidities of the stomach while provoking urine.

<margin>The cure for undimia.</margin>
The cure is placed in two things. First, the body must be purged. Afterward, it must be strengthened and comforted with specifics. The process of the cure is this: that it be purged successively with <term>siler montanum; Laserwort, an aromatic mountain herb</term>, which is a powerful purgative in hypofarca if it is boiled in broth, and 3 or 4 ounces of this are swallowed.
<margin>Siler montanum benefits undimia.</margin>
Likewise, laxatives are to be given in wine: for instance, if <term>turpethum; Turpeth, a powerful purgative root from the East Indies</term> is suspended and macerated in wine. Afterward, one must proceed to provoke urine.

This being done, the true cure is finally to be approached. Other things, such as clysters <note>enemas</note>, contribute little. Sometimes sweat is to be provoked with half an ounce of theriac <note>an ancient herbal jam used as a universal antidote</note> and one scruple of euphorbium. Manna, Saffron, <term>Crocus Martis; an oxide of iron</term>, Liquor of corals, <term>Dulcedo Saturni; "Sweetness of Lead," or lead acetate, used historically despite its toxicity</term>, are effective in all species of this disease. In the same way, the large radish boiled in water and prepared into an electuary with honey is very useful. After all these things, the true cure must be begun. In undimia, however, the principal remedy is <term>Diacubebe; a medicinal compound based on cubeb peppers</term>, the compositions of which follow for each individual species.

<margin>Diacubebe is the principal remedy in undimia.</margin>
*Description for the first species, that is, in Vndimia of the Earth.*

<margin>Cure for undimia of the earth.</margin>
Take: 1 ounce of the species of Diacubebe; 1 ounce each of <term>Carabe; yellow amber</term>, plantain seeds, and dill. A sufficient quantity of cleansed sugar. Mix.
The dose is one and a half ounces, morning and evening, in undimia of the earth.

*In the second species, that is, of water from split alum: a description.*

<margin>Of Water.</margin>
Take: 2 and a half ounces of the species of Diacubebe; 3 ounces each of red corals, <term>mumia; powder made from embalmed remains, believed to have great healing power</term>, and dragon's blood <note>a red resin from the Dracaena tree</note>. Let troches <note>medicinal lozenges</note> be made with tragacanth dissolved in endive water.

<margin>Of Air.</margin>
