# THE FIFTH BOOK OF PARAGRAPHS.
## On Dry Diseases or Phthisis.
### PARAGRAPH 1.

<margin>What phthisis is.</margin>
*But if the igneous element departs into its own dryness, it is a certain sign of the consumption of the other elements as well. It should be known, moreover, that this dryness descends from dry fire, with the consumption of the three elements in their bodies.*

**W**asting, or <term>phthisis; a progressive wasting of the body, usually associated with the lungs</term>, otherwise called the "dry disease," is nothing other than a consumption, either of the parts with pain, or of the whole body without paroxysm and pain. First, the congealed matter in the body is dissolved. Afterward, the element of fire consumes the parts of the body and the three remaining elements with its dryness, and within the space of one or two years, it completely exhausts and removes all the body's superfluities. Meanwhile, it assumes nothing from food into the nourishment of the parts. Whence either the whole body is made dry and thinned out.

This disease afflicts either a single limb, several, or the entire body. Nor does this defect consist in the lungs alone; indeed, it is also found in the brain, heart, liver, kidneys, spleen, and other parts, such as the bones, veins, nerves, the fluid of the joints <term>synovia; the lubricating fluid found in the cavities of synovial joints</term>, the marrow, etc. Under one name, however, all species are comprised, which are perceived and distinguished by various signs. A tremor indicates that the heart is being consumed. A cough and the spitting of pus provide a certain indication of a damaged lung. An abundance of urine betrays defects of the liver and kidneys. A cough also arises from an affected liver, and similarly from the kidneys. Inflammation of the joints and pains in the sides argue for a consumption of the spleen and liver. The flesh suffers cavities and fissures <note>cracks or lesions in the skin</note>, which are extremely dangerous in the knees. The nerves are contracted, the blood is dried out, and the joint fluid is painful. And this is the consumption of parts, from which certain specific pains are never separated.

<margin>What universal wasting is.</margin>
Universal wasting <note>original: "Tabes"; a general term for the progressive wasting of the body</note> of the whole body is slower and more tolerable, and it thins the body without great pain. If the skin around the knees breaks or is split, no counsel or cure is of any use.

## PARAGRAPH II.

-> *Therefore, it should be noted in these matters that the dryness of fire causes the reduction of the body because of humidity. The dry and raw part is Death. Humidity itself is the sickness.* <-

<margin>The hidden cause of Phthisis.</margin>
The beginning or cause of this disease <note>referring to Phthisis or pulmonary consumption</note> does not principally come from a blockage or a "moist catarrh" <note>an old medical term for the downward flow of excess humors, like mucus</note>; rather, it occurs from a hidden impression of the heavens. For the "Sun of the microcosm" <note>In Paracelsian thought, the "microcosm" is the human body, and its "Sun" is the internal vital heat or governing principle</note> consumes all humors: whence the body and limbs are dried out. Finally, death follows, either of the limbs or of the entire body.

## THE CURE.

Take: *Stag fat* 10 pounds. *Oil of laurel berries* 6 drams.
*Stag marrow* 1/2 pound (otherwise 5 pounds). *Oil of Angelica to the weight of all ingredients.*
*Juice of Endive, as much as suffices for a decoction.*

Reduce this into an ointment, to be used for the duration of ten weeks. Anoint the entire body twice a day, morning and evening. Then wash in water mixed with boiled vinegar; then the senses are gradually restored.

Once this disease is defeated, it does not return again. In treating it, however, a diet must first be established. Afterward, medicine may be applied. The body must be so moistened that the "Sun of the Microcosm" may find something to consume from time to time. This can be achieved primarily through "arcana" <term>arcana; "secret" or "essential" remedies that Paracelsus believed contained the concentrated power of nature</term>, by which the Physician compels, coerces, and renews the "heaven" from which the diseases arise. The highest secret of this disease is the "liquor of Pearls," which is an Elixir. In food and drink, those things which are suitable should be taken, such as: Licorice, polypody, lentils, raisins, purslane, Lettuce with seeds, both types of radish, red beet, betony, blessed thistle, pine nuts, and all species of mallows. Among things to be taken internally, ground-ivy water with a third part of purslane water helps exceptionally and uniquely in this disease: and if by chance any vein of the body is ruptured, a third part of sowbread <note>original: "cyclaminis"</note> water ought to be added.

Before all other things, however, the composition of "Diacoralla" is held in the highest esteem for wasting. And it is prepared in this way.

## Description of Diacoralla.

The use of this medicine is to be continued until the urine no longer exhibits a spongy foam, which must be restored to its pristine state.

*Native sulfur 1 pound. A Bath.*

**Native sulfur** <note>original: "Sulphur vivum"</note> is sulfur that has not been melted. In this bath, the patient ought to wash for ten weeks (And if it has lasted for eight days, 1 1/2 drams or more of ground amber <note>original: "Carabe"</note> should be added). If the disease is driven out once, it does not return. For those in whom "ragadia" <note>fissures or cracks</note> or splits arise in the knees during the wasting disease, no cure remains for them.

ON LEPROSY

# THE SIXTH BOOK OF PARAGRAPHS.

## On Leprosy.

## CHAPTER I. Declaration of the Disease.

### PARAGRAPH I.

<margin>What leprosy is.</margin>
**L**eprosy is the putrefaction of the elemental body along with its minerals <note>In this context, "minerals" refers to the specific chemical or salt-like substances within the body that provide structure</note>. There are four species of leprosy. There is also mixed leprosy, composite leprosy, and universal leprosy.

<margin>Four species of leprosy.</margin>
Leprosy is nothing other than a degeneration of the body into putrefaction, from which this disease arises. First, however, leprosy arises in the less principal members <note>The peripheral parts of the body, like limbs or skin</note> from the elements. Thus, four species are identified: Earth, Water, Air, and Fire. In the principal members <note>The vital organs</note>, leprosy is produced outside of the "elementated" <note>This refers to the spiritual or archetypal essence of the organs, rather than just their physical matter</note>. Afterward, sometimes a single element putrefies, which is called simple leprosy. Occasionally, two or more putrefy at the same time, from which mixed or composite leprosy arises. If, however, all elements together fall into putrefaction, it becomes universal leprosy, a certain sign of which is if a finger, ear, or nose falls off entirely. If one element putrefies, the others struggle, as it were, so that they themselves are not seized by the putrefaction at the same time. But when two elements are putrefying or infected, the two remaining elements and the "liquor of nature" <note>The natural vitality or fluid that sustains life</note> prevent the whole body from being touched by the same blight. And the minerals of whichever element induce the putrefaction, the death of that same member follows, as it does with the principal members if leprosy takes root in them. Wherever leprosy fixes its center, there arises a great heat, swelling, and numbness. Leprosy of the "earth" first erupts in the face. When leprosy of "water" invades, the feet first swell and cannot bear the cold. The genitals also swell and develop ulcers, which are healed with difficulty. If the leprosy takes root in the element of "air" (or the "chaos"), a foul smell is sensed from the soul <note>original: "animae foetor"; likely referring to the breath or the vital spirit</note>, and the whole body becomes discolored. If it is the element of "fire," phlegmons <note>Painful, spreading inflammations of the skin</note> occupy the whole body with intense heat, which return again after a full year. These types of phlegmonous ulcers are a sign of the beginning of fire-leprosy.

<margin>Which leprosy is simple, composite, universal, particular, etc.</margin>
<margin>Signs of earth-leprosy, air-leprosy, etc.</margin>
<margin>Signs of leprosy in the principal parts: the lungs.</margin>
There remains another species of leprosy that arises in the principal members, not the elements. When leprosy tests the lungs, the minerals of the lungs are infected and the voice becomes hoarse, unless the feet have swollen first. In that case, the leprosy is mixed with water-leprosy.

<margin>The liver, bladder, spleen, and heart.</margin>
If the leprosy is in the liver, thirst vanishes, and the upper skin comes away, yet the crusts do not fall off. Leprosy of the bladder is indicated if pus is continually passed in the urine, and the private parts are eaten away by ulcers that are difficult to cure. If the blood is bluish-gray and sandy, it is to be judged as leprosy of the spleen. Leprosy of the heart reveals itself by a biting pain in the pit of the chest (the sternum) and by ulcers born on the back and around the spine whenever the skin is wounded by blistering or friction; the crusts of these ulcers fall off.

<margin>The kidneys.</margin>
When leprosy takes root in the kidneys, the urine becomes white, the complexion turns pale, the pulse is infrequent and weak, and a toothache sets in, after which the teeth fall out.

<margin>The gall.</margin>
When leprosy emerges from the gall <note>The gallbladder</note>, vomiting begins to plague the patient, sometimes continuing for half a year or longer, and tubercles <note>Small, hard bumps</note> grow on the tongue.

<margin>The brain.</margin>
Leprosy of the brain pours out foul-smelling pus, and the sick speak through their noses even if they do not have a damaged or perforated palate; their forehead and eyes swell, and an itch is excited at the back of the neck.

### PARAGRAPH II.

<margin>Universal signs of leprosy.</margin>
<margin>What Zephena is.</margin>
**Z**ephena <note>A term used by Paracelsus to describe deep, perforating ulcers or specific types of lesions</note> is the first sign in leprosy, as are "points" <note>original: "acumina"; sharp or thinning features</note>; likewise a blue-black color, or a reddish-purple color, or a composite of these with ulceration.

These are the universal signs. *Zephena* is any ulcer or hole in the body; it eventually reaches a certain size. When leprosy afflicts the body, all the emunctories <note>The organs and pores that carry off waste</note> produce their own *Zephena*, and they become round and constricted. By these, the mouth is also contracted, and they speak as if from a hollow space. The ears become red, like the ears of pigs. In healthy people, they form a round circle; in lepers, they form another kind of ring. The penis is twisted in leprosy.

<margin>Leprosy makes all things thinner.</margin>
A "point" <note>original: "acumen"</note> is when something is rendered sharper than it was. Thus, the nose, ears, and fingers have a defined sharpness. All these become sharper and thinner through leprosy. Indeed, the teeth themselves become pointed.

<margin>What the blue-black color is.</margin>
<margin>What the reddish-purple color is.</margin>
The *Lazurius* color is cyan. When the vivid color of the skin degenerates into a leaden blue, it is a sign of leprosy. Nor does this blueness appear more clearly anywhere than in the *zephenas* and the "points." The *Orizeus* color is purple. When this appears, leprosy is imminent. From this color, the cheeks become withered. This purple color exists as a sign of leprosy. If many colors are mixed together, this is also a sign of leprosy. Moreover, all these signs appear even on intact skin. For leprosy is the mother of many different colors.

## CHAPTER II. On the Examination of Lepers.

### PARAGRAPH I.
### On the indications of leprosy from accidents.

**T**he examination of lepers is recognized by these signs. First from "sparkling" urine <note>original: "urina scatea"; urine that appears to have particles or a certain shimmering quality</note>, second from the excrement; this concerns leprosy from "accidents" <note>In early medicine, "accidents" are external causes or symptoms not inherent to the patient's nature</note>, with the first type appearing in the urine, and the second in the stomach regions and parts of the intestines.

<margin>The triple origin of leprosy. Lepers must be observed for three days before examination.</margin>
Those who wish to explore and distinguish those infected by leprosy have need to consider three types of leprosy. One is from Accident. The second is from its own Inborn Nature. And the third is from Chance. Sparkling urine indicates leprosy from accident. However, there are some "preservatives" <note>Medicines or treatments meant to hide or prevent the disease's progress</note> against leprosy which correct it so that it cannot be truly recognized. Therefore, for three days before the examination, the sick person must be shut away so that they do not use these types of preservatives.

<margin>Signs of leprosy from urine.</margin>
Urine that comes out sparkling must be placed in warm water, and a square or disk made of ash-wood should be placed over a glass, and they must be properly sealed. If the urine is distilled in this way and something rough and white appears on the wood (if it is dried), it is a most certain sign of leprosy. And this is leprosy from the urine.

<margin>From the excrement.</margin>
Judgment can be made from the excrement in this way. Let the excrement of the leper be taken and put into water, and let this be stirred well; afterward, let the upper parts be poured off slowly. This must be repeated until almost no excrement remains. If, at last, something like salt remains at the bottom, it completely proves leprosy in the stomach.

### On Leprosy from Chance.

The sign from sweat with coagulation is the first—

### PARAGRAPHS OF BOOK III.

*The second [sign] is from the variety of pustules; the third from the epiglottis and the hair. These are the signs of accidental leprosy.* <note>Accidental leprosy refers to the disease contracted through external circumstances or lifestyle, rather than being innate or hereditary.</note>

<margin>Savin eaten [causes] leprosy; Menstrual blood does the same.</margin>
One contracts accidental leprosy by eating savin <note>original: "sauinam"; a species of juniper traditionally used as an abortifacient and known to be toxic</note>. Indeed, this is a most certain sign of impending leprosy. Likewise, the consumption of menstrual blood induces leprosy. If accidental leprosy is to be recognized through sweat, the patient must sweat in a dry bath. In this bath, if the sweat does not break out in granules like pearls, but rather the entire body sweats evenly, it is a sign of <margin>A sign of leprosy from sweat, etc.</margin> impending leprosy. Furthermore, the sweat dripping from a leper is preserved. If, once cooled, it turns salty, and that salt does not dissolve when thrown into water, it is a certain sign. The same judgment applies to the blood. *From the variety of pustules.* It often happens that small bumps <note>original: "tubercula"</note> grow on the skin. This is not a perfect sign of leprosy. However, if over time those bumps become ulcerated and form crusts, or cause itching, it is a most certain sign of leprosy. If the itching is accompanied by a hoarseness of the voice, or if the sensation of the skin becomes numb, it is a most certain sign of leprosy. Signs are also evident from the epiglottis. The epiglottis <note>original: "Epiglottum"; while this usually refers to the throat, the author here describes a specific medical tool</note> is a <margin>What the epiglottis is. The epiglottis as a test for leprosy.</margin> silver instrument, similar to the tool with which cobblers pull shoes onto feet. This instrument is placed beneath the eyes, and the hairs are drawn across it. If they fall out, it is a sign of leprosy. The same is evidenced by the hair falling out near the ears.

### PARAGRAPH III.
### *On the signs of innate leprosy.*

*Innate signs of leprosy include hollows and the wasting of flesh near the thumb; likewise through orange and azure colors, through vehement lust, and through cold and colors from the outside.*

<margin>Signs of innate leprosy.</margin>
If the cheeks sink and subside in the middle, it is a sign of leprosy. In those whose cheeks are thinner above and thicker below, these also argue for leprosy. In women whose breasts appear harder on top and softer below, and are further conspicuous by the formation of pits, these testify to leprosy. The same is to be judged of men, if their nipples are less fleshy, as are the buttocks. Wasting of the flesh occurs when the flesh situated between the thumb and the index finger is not plump, but has hollows. For this is a sign of leprosy. He who feels vehement hunger or thirst after sexual intercourse is a leper. He who is struck by heat or cold upon the slightest occasion arouses suspicion of leprosy.

## CHAPTER III.
### *On the differences between signs.*

*The first difference proceeds from Alopecia <note>Patchy hair loss</note>, with signs on the face as in "rosy drop" <note>original: "gutta rosacea," modern rosacea</note>, in depraved "stretching" <note>original: "tentigine"; likely referring to abnormal skin tension or priapism</note>, and in an external polyp. The second difference is in itching from the cause of ingested poison. The third difference is from external things, such as from <term>Realgar</term> <note>Red arsenic sulfide, a highly toxic mineral</note> and from external cold and heat. The fourth difference takes its origin from meats, medicines, and from diseases.*

Alopecia, "almonds" <note>swollen glands or tonsils</note> in the neck, and foulness of the face are indeed similar to leprosy, but they do not provide a true judgment of it; likewise other diseases such as rosacea, depraved tension, and external polyps: for even if bumps appear there, they are not to be referred to as leprosy. Those who have swallowed poison feel an itching from it, whether from orpiment <note>arsenic trisulfide</note>, or Salt Ammoniac <note>ammonium chloride</note>, or salt made with urine, or even from menstrual blood, from the blood of hemorrhoids, or from the blood of the left "salvatella" <note>A specific vein on the back of the hand near the ring and little finger</note>. For all these are poisons, not capable of killing, but rendering the body sick and the skin similar to that of lepers, along with wasting. And although the cheeks may sink, or the fingers become thin, or other signs appear, it is by no means leprosy. Leprosy from cold and heat generates leprosy and other diseases, and the hands and feet are cracked. But if it is to be a future leprosy, it is in the lung, and they have a hoarseness of the voice.

*From Heats.* It often happens that bathhouse attendants, as in Meissen and Saxony, are wasted away. Yet this is not leprosy. However, leprosy is sometimes <margin>Bathhouse attendants are mostly wasted.</margin> induced by immense heat. These people are roughened by blisters, and become hoarse, etc. And these are not yet lepers. But if, in addition to those things, they also grow thin in the mentioned places, it is leprosy.

*From Realgar.* Cooks and those who handle metals in kitchens are often infested by a disease from <term>Realgar</term> <note>Arsenic poisoning</note>. Those who melt <margin>Cooks are subject to disease from Realgar.</margin> either realgar, or iron, or lead, or copper, or tin: the vapor exhaling from there inflicts a disease not unlike leprosy upon them, and also makes them hoarse. Thus, those who smelt copper contract a red face; yet it is neither <term>morphea</term> <note>A skin disease causing discolored patches</note> nor leprosy. And whatever is not contagious, so that one can be infected by another, is by no means leprosy. <margin>It is not leprosy unless it has contagion.</margin> If, therefore, the ears of a miner or a smelter of minerals either sink or are twisted, and the flesh within the thumb wastes away, it is a most certain sign of leprosy. The same is to be judged of cooks. Furthermore, it is a property of pork flesh that it breaks out and swells on the face; yet this is not leprosy, except when the signs proceed from <term>Zephena</term> <note>A Paracelsian term for a specific diseased state of the blood or vital spirits</note>. Likewise, if someone becomes hoarse from intercourse, unless the sign of Zephena is present, it is not leprosy. Leprosy also very often emerges from rabies <note>original: "hydrophobia"</note>, from pustules, from alopecia, from morphea, and "touch-me-not" <note>original: "noli me tangere"; a term for corrosive skin ulcers or lupus</note>, and polyps. If these four generate sicknesses and produce hoarseness, and besides this the glands liquefy: then it is leprosy, and a single disease. Thus, from quartan fever <note>a form of malaria</note> itching is born: and those who drink in great heat become hoarse. These, however, are not yet leprosies. But if <margin>A sign of leprosy from quartan fever.</margin> after quartan fever the nostrils sink, this is a sign of impending leprosy. *From blood.* If someone is troubled by a scab on the left side after blood is let from the "salvatella" vein, and hoarseness is not present, leprosy is not recognized from that itching.

# ON LEPROSY.

When a leper is brought for examination, white leprosy is of a different color [than the red]. For whatever the skin of the face is like, such it ought to be in the whole body. If the output of the breath <note>original: "chaos"; in Paracelsian medicine, this refers to the exhaled air or the subtle atmosphere surrounding a person</note> <margin>Form of red leprosy.</margin> stinks, it is a most certain sign of white leprosy. If other stenches break out like roasted onions, and others like arsenic; if that stench is in the urine, just as the breath from the mouth, that matter pertains to the white cure. Indeed, even the excrement smells like the stench exhaled from the mouth. Red leprosy is so called because of the "red cure" [required for it]. If the skin is so ulcerated that holes are left behind, the healing is to be referred to the red cure. If blisters break out on the skin, it shall be referred to the red cure; similarly, if there is a wicked tension <note>original: "tentigo"; likely referring to abnormal skin tension or priapism in a medical context</note>, or if mange <note>original: "alopecia"</note> is imminent, all these things pertain to the red cure.

#### PARAGRAPH II.

<margin>Medicines for the preservation from leprosy.</margin> *The process of leprosy is twofold: The first concerns preservation, and the second concerns the cure of leprosy. Those things which pertain to preservation are these: Extracts of antimony, the essence of blood from the vein of the heart, the liquor of pearls and corals, specifics made from juniper berries, from lemon balm, chicory, and valerian.*

#### PARAGRAPH III.

<margin>Those things which are curative for leprosy.</margin> *Those things which pertain to the cure are these: Minerals of gold, the virtues of manna, and Tereniabin <note>A Persian term for a type of medicinal manna gathered from shrubs</note>, and silver with its various forms.*

->Cure of Red Leprosy from Gold.<-

*Such as potable gold <note>original: "aurum potabile"; gold dissolved in a liquid form, highly prized in alchemy as a universal medicine</note>, liquor of gold, juice of "orizei" <note>unclear; likely a chemical preparation</note>, and the golden liquor. The dose is one grain in good wine, in the morning. All these have power.*

->Cure of White Leprosy from Silver.<-

*Oil of silver, liquor of silver, juice of silver, water of the moon <note>original: "aqua lunae"; "Luna" is the alchemical name for silver</note>. The dose is half a scruple <note>original: "[scrup.] ß"; about 0.6 grams</note> once in a Moon [month]. Likewise, the precipitate of silver and gold from a restored body, then reduced into the "First Matter" <term>First Matter: the primordial, undifferentiated substance from which all metals were thought to originate</term>, and afterwards precipitated, is the highest secret in the cure of leprosy.*

<margin>Leprosy which is incurable.</margin> *The final stage of leprosy produces holes in the hip-bone and pain with the consumption [wasting away] of that part, and this is incurable.*

<margin>Antimony and Manna preserve the balsam of nature.</margin> Those who wish to undertake a cure must preserve the element [of life]. In this preservation, it is necessary to protect the "balsam of nature" <note>the body's internal life-force or natural healing power</note>: and it is fitting to apply those things which can sustain or preserve a cadaver so that it does not putrefy. From this rank is antimony, and the prepared kinds of manna and *tereniabin*. In a similar way, the balsam of nature also preserves. Thus, the essence of wine is a preservative in leprosy, and does not allow putrefaction. The dose of anti- <margin>Dose of Antimony. Dose of human blood.</margin> mony is half a scruple in a week at dawn. The blood ought to come from the vein of the heart. Essences of juniper berries and lemon balm do not allow putrefaction. The dose of human blood is half an ounce, once a month on the second day after the [lunar] opposition. The dose of pearls and corals is four grains every day at dawn. The dose of lemon balm, valerian, and others is from one drachm to an ounce and a half every morning.

<margin>Gold is the cure for red leprosy.</margin> The cure of red leprosy proceeds from gold. And it is the liquor of gold, and potable gold, juice of *orizei*, and the golden liquor. All these have power. The dose is one grain in the morning in good wine.

<margin>Silver is the cure for white leprosy.</margin> In white leprosy there is silver, oil of silver, liquor of silver, juice of silver—that is, the water of silver. This comes from unrefined silver. <margin>Once a moon.</margin> The dose of silver is half a scruple once in a moon—that is, from new moon to new moon.

The "First Matter" of the Sun [Gold] and Moon [Silver] proceeds from a perfected body and is reduced to the First Matter. That Mercury <note>the philosophical or metallic spirit</note> removes hardened leprosy.

The final sign of leprosy is if it reaches the point where they are infested with pain in the hip-bones. The flesh in the hips wastes away and collapses, just as near the thumb. And in that case, neither cure nor preservation is useful.

## CHAPTER ONE.

->The Matter of Gout.<-

### PARAGRAPH I.

<margin>What Gout is and when it occurs.</margin> **G** *out <note>original: "Gutta"; literally "a drop," referring to the belief that the disease was caused by a drop of morbid humor falling into a joint</note> is the <term>Synovia: In this context, not just joint fluid, but the "digestive" fluid of the limbs that provides nutrition to the specific parts of the body</term> of its own part; from whichever part it proceeds, there follows from that part pain and a paroxysm [attack]. Gout is paralysis, and apoplexy, a contraction of the limbs.*

Gout is [found in] any limb that loses its own power within itself. The same thing happens in gonorrhea, in the loss of speech, in the eyes, and in hearing. Moreover, this disease is nothing other than the fact that the limb cannot perform its duty. Otherwise, it has no defect in the stomach or in its nutrients. Paralysis also occurs in the heart <margin>Cause of Gout: separated synovia. All parts that have synovia receive Gout.</margin> and the spleen. The cause is synovia separated from its part. For there is no limb in the body that does not have its own synovia: and similarly in the ligaments. Even the tendons can be infected: and then paralysis is stirred up in the fingers. It happens sometimes that the flesh becomes numb. And that is the paralysis of that limb. Paralysis also occurs in the teeth. And if the teeth fall out from disease, it happens from paralysis. In the heart, paralysis brings on sudden death. And there it is not "gout" which glides in, but the cause is synovia. For Synovia is the "stomach of the limbs." And all nutrients by which the limbs are sustained are digested into synovia.

In the parts of the kidneys, the flesh consists [of it]; in those, the synovia is red. The synovia of the blood is a deep red. The synovia of the brain is an ash-color, and thicker than the white of an egg. The synovia of the spleen is black. The synovia of the gall is yellow and thick. The synovia in the <margin>What the synovia is like in individual parts.</margin> kidneys, liver, heart, and spleen is colored according to the condition of the parts. The synovia of the womb is quite thick and Venereal <note>associated with sexual function or desire</note>, and remarkably slow-moving. The synovia of the marrows is like a head of grain and viscous. Therefore, when paralysis is about to attack, the synovia is changed [separated] from its part. And whichever part is changed, that part is seized by paralysis: which persists as long as the synovia is not yet united again.

### PARAGRAPH II.

<margin>What the power of synovia is.</margin> *Synovia is the nourishment of its own part and the preservation of the retentive and motive power, [derived] from the forces of the digestive power.*

Synovia has an attractive, retentive, and motive power, and the synovia attracts to its own part. Whatever the kidneys attract, the synovia attracts.

<margin>Once synovia is lost, it is not restored to the part.</margin>
It draws away; you do not hold it. The same applies to the other members. An attack <note>original: "paroxysmus"</note> invades according to the nature of the limb. Whatever the logic of the location, such is the condition of the attack. If the synovia <note>In Paracelsian medicine, synovia refers not just to joint fluid, but to a vital, oily "liquor" that nourishes the body’s parts and carries sensation.</note> departs from its place, it cannot return to it again. Therefore, the seed must be united. The "sinning matter" <note>the morbid substance causing the illness</note> cannot be purged; and so the synovia which has been loosened from its place must be taken away and removed as a "sinner."

## PARAGRAPH III.

*From these things it follows that the disease arises from "sequestration" <note>the separation or isolation of fluids</note>, along with the primary generation of pain-relief <note>original: "anodyni"</note> in its part: because once the synovia is separated and left behind, it causes the limb to lose all feeling.*

<margin>Separated synovia causes insensibility.</margin>
If the synovia is separated from its part, it causes insensibility <note>numbness or loss of sensation</note> in that limb. The synovia holds the sensitive quality within itself, not the limb itself. If, therefore, the synovia is withdrawn from the limb, the nutrition and sensitivity of that part are withdrawn. Afterward, that limb is seized by wasting <note>original: "Phthisis"</note> and finally by rot.

## PARAGRAPH IV.
### *On the Accident <note>An "accident" in historical medicine refers to the symptoms or secondary occurrences of a disease.</note>.*

*The fall of the disease comes from coagulation, and thereafter from a congealed loosening <note>original: "resolutione"</note>. For every moist coagulation is a sign of a future loosening, and from this loosening comes the cause of the disease with the sequestration of the two aforementioned things. Therefore, the sign of true Apoplexy <note>a sudden stroke or loss of consciousness</note> is foam and suffocation with contraction. The sign of paralysis is the alteration of the limb and the numbing of the part. In "gonorrhea" <note>here likely referring to a general discharge or "running" of fluids</note> the sign is the matter of the excrement. The signs of other sicknesses are the loss of sense, along with disease according to the Anatomy.*

<margin>Things that coagulate the blood and synovia.</margin>
If the vein is cut in someone who continually eats purslane, the blood will not flow out. If someone is nourished only on cheese and fish for nine or ten days, and is then wounded, he will not bleed. He who constantly eats fat and lard readily incurs "diabetes" and "gonorrhea." Coagulation also happens within us if certain plants are eaten, such as *semperviva* <note>houseleek</note>, that is, *pirula* <note>likely wintergreen</note>, and Jupiter's beard, lettuce, lettuce seed, essences of wine, psyllium <note>flea-wort</note>, and any mucilage. If such things are eaten, synovia is also ingested with them. Thus, when the synovia is consistent, if the blood is stopped with *carniola* <note>likely carnelian or a similar mineral used as a styptic</note>, it coagulates the blood for two days and is finally loosened; but the "sperm of frogs" <note>a common name for frog spawn or a specific botanical/chemical preparation</note> coagulates it for 10 or 20 years. There are also things which, when eaten by us, coagulate the synovia, such as the essence of wine and any mucilage from fenugreek or psyllium. For if the essence of wine is joined to these, it coagulates the synovia even without cold. A "loosening" of the part follows the coagulated synovia. Since the part cannot bear a mixed coagulation for long, the minerals are loosened, and separation happens either more quickly or more slowly. Therefore, that coagulation turns into Apoplexy. If the coagulated brain begins to undergo loosening, Apoplexy is to be feared, the signs of which are snoring <note>original: "stertor"</note>, tremors, and sleep falling upon one with the eyes open. When these signs appear, a sign of future Apoplexy is imminent.

<margin>Signs of future Apoplexy.</margin>
Sometimes a watery discharge <note>original: "ichor"</note> flows from the mouth of those sleeping, and a spasm creeps up so that they are woken by it. The signs of Apoplexy are hiccups, difficulty breathing, whiteness of the nose and yellowness of the face, a sudden onset of the attack, foam at the mouth, and falling, if it arises from the brain, and the stretching of the limbs. When Apoplexy of the lungs infests a person, hiccups, suffocation, the casting out of white foam, and the onset of spasms occur. When Apoplexy of the heart is imminent, the heart trembles and palpitates, a sweat of the body follows, and the sick feel pain in the precordium <note>the region over the heart/stomach</note> after taking food: furthermore, a spasm twitches them, the pulse is swift, repeatedly becoming more rapid by itself. When the Apoplexy finally takes hold, they suddenly collapse and die. Such things happen in the principal members.

<margin>How Paralysis differs from Apoplexy. Signs of paralytics.</margin>
The signs of Paralysis differ from Apoplexy in this: that it attacks no principal member, but seizing some external or more "ignoble" <note>less vital</note> limb, it only loosens that part. Paralysis is preceded by a cold or a "horror" <note>a shivering fit</note> for the space of a year, and a hemorrhage that is not easily stopped. A tremor usually occupies the limb that is to be struck. When the loosening occurs, the attack brings on suffocation. If anyone desires to distinguish whether it is paralysis or Apoplexy: when the patient's mouth is opened, if breath comes out, it is to be judged as Paralysis. If not, it is a sign of Apoplexy, the attack of which falls with a certain terror and with various imaginings, as if they were being invaded and their throats cut by others. The signs in "diabetic gonorrhea" <note>a reference to an excessive flow of fluid</note> are loosening or contracture in the spine; such signs sometimes precede the event by a whole decade, as stated above. It also happens that epilepsy invades, and that is a sign of future Apoplexy. If Apoplexy leaps in during an epileptic attack, they open the patient's mouth and distort the eyes. In paralysis, sometimes another disease concurs: which is a sign that the old disease has departed and this one is new. There are those who complain of numbness <note>original: "stupore"</note> in some limb five or six days beforehand; which is a sign of future paralysis. Sometimes dropsy under the skin <note>original: "hyposarca"</note> coincides at the same point with paralysis; in which case a cure for both must be established.

<margin>The cure of Gutta is either Physical or Surgical.</margin>
The cure is twofold: partly Physical <note>meaning through medicine/internal physics</note>, partly Surgical. In the physical cure, the synovia must be consumed through the application of *arcana* <note>secret chemical remedies</note>, which consume, strengthen, and produce new synovia. Limbs are strengthened by things that are suitable due to their appropriate heat. Such *arcana* include gold, gems, pearls, etc.

# THE EIGHTH BOOK

## On Asthma.
### PARAGRAPH II.

**T**hese are the species of Asthma: *Abscesses <note>original: "apostemata"</note> of the lung, carbuncles <note>original: "Anthraces"</note> of the chest regions, ulcers, a superfluous moisture or dryness of the region or lung, fatness, repletion <note>fullness of humors</note>, and excrements of liquor.*

<margin>Why lung conditions are quickly revealed.</margin>
Many ailments are included under asthma. The division is as such: the lung and the lung region ought not to be obstructed <note>original: "deoppilati"</note>, but should be entirely pure and without carbuncles. And since the lung is always being dilated and constricted, it therefore immediately indicates its own abscess or impediment, which similarly happens very little in the other principal members. For in the gallbladder and others, an abscess can lie hidden for a long time before it is revealed. If, therefore, there are ulcers in the lung, the "opening power" <note>the ability of the medicine to clear passages</note> cannot proceed, and a sign of them is taken from the foul breath. A carbuncle attacks together with a paroxysm and a light chill. If the lung is too moist, it is felt to be heavier, and the sick are always infested by a cough. If there is too much dryness in the lung, it cannot be opened enough again, and a cough molests them, and pain is felt in the ribs from the dryness. If blood is excreted from the lung, it fills the pipes <note>the bronchi/trachea</note> and hinders the breathing-holes of the lung. 
<margin>The cause of Asthma.</margin>
Moreover, when phlegm besieges the pipes, air cannot penetrate, whence asthma arises. However, when the phlegm has dried up in the pipes, a perpetual cough molests. Therefore, the cure ought to be twofold. One which resolves <note>loosens or dissolves</note>, the other which dries out. And those things are to be taken which consume the superfluous phlegm in the lung.

### PARAGRAPH II.

<margin>Signs of Asthma.</margin>
*The signs of Asthma are these: panting, cough, white hawking <note>spitting up phlegm</note>, hoarseness of voice, dryness of the throat, thirst, alteration of the pulse, and compression of the chest.*

When such signs appear, it is certain that the lung is damaged. Moreover, the signs are to be referred to two classes, in this way: if many things are cast back and expectorated, it is necessary to dry; but if less so, to loosen. It often happens that if the lungs of obese people are chilled, they contract a certain harm. Thus, he who is troubled by hoarseness and enters a bath: 
<margin>A bath is harmful to the hoarse.</margin>
whatever happens to him in the bath, he will pay for that harm perpetually. These people also ought not to have a vein cut <note>bloodletting</note>.

## ON THE CURE. §. I.

Take: *Of this sulphur, 1 dram.*
*Oriental saffron, half a scruple. Mastieis <note>mastic resin</note>, 1 dram.*

Mix all these, having been reduced into a powder. The dose is the same as that of the superior sublimated sulphur. A dram of Hyssop can also be added.

The description of the Laudanum above <note>referring to a previous recipe in the book</note> is especially conducive to the lung. This also must be noted, that cold things are harmful when purging the lung.

->On the Resolving Cure. §. II.<-

*The cure for relaxation is this:* <term>Elixir</term> of raw <term>Tartar</term>: Essence of wine, and separated from its flesh <note>its impurities or lees</note> with waters.

In Asthma, a cure of relaxation is appropriate, by which dry things are resolved so that they can more easily be ejected from the lung. Every sweet thing is liquefying. Thus, conserve of roses.

Raw Tartar from white wine is an ingredient for the lung and the lung regions. Elixir, that is, a ferment, if it is reduced into an elixir, and the pure is separated from the impure. 
<margin>What an Elixir is.</margin>
The impurity of Tartar is <term>Alkali</term>. Crush the Tartar, and digest it in alcohol of wine seven or eight times, and prepare it through an <term>Alembic</term> <note>a distilling apparatus</note>, and reduce it into a liquid humor. 
<margin>What Alkali is.</margin>
In this liquor there is no Alkali; finally it ought to be brought down to its own essence. Thus prepared, the lung accepts it, and is cured by it. The dose is from 4 grains up to 7 or 10. And in this way, ulcers of the lung are also to be cured.

It can be taken both internally and applied externally.

# THE NINTH BOOK
# OF THE PARAGRAPHS.
## Concerning Extraneous Fevers.
### PARAGRAPH I.

**Fever is a putrefied heat accompanied by tremors arising from its own obstruction, caused by unseparated matter in closed pores through a constricting force.**

<margin>What a fever is.</margin>
The fevers treated here do not arise from nutrients, and they require their own specific cure. Fever is a heat that does not exist without cold. For any putrefaction gives off heat joined with some degree of cold. Even the blood can induce this kind of cold. <margin>What particular and universal fevers are.</margin> If the "sinning matter" <note>the substance causing the disease</note> sticks in the principal organs, then the paroxysm <note>the acute fit of the fever</note> pervades the whole body. It is "particular" if only a single vein feels the fever. Likewise, there is a universal and particular type arising from the flesh. If the fever occupies the spleen, and the *salvatella* vein <note>a vein on the back of the hand, between the little and ring finger</note> is cut, it removes it. If it is from the heart: cut its own vein. If in the lung, cut the vein of the lung. If in a "quartan" fever <note>a fever recurring every four days</note> white urine is produced, scarification <note>shallow cutting of the skin</note> should be performed at the end of the spine. If the fever is from the kidneys, then the scarification ought to be done below on the feet. And if the fever is not cured by bloodletting <note>phlebotomy</note>, only then should one proceed to the [chemical] cure, and not any sooner. And in these fevers, no purgative should be given. If the fever is about to turn into a [chronic] disease, a "sequestration" <note>a separation of bodily humors</note> occurs. If the fever is in the spleen, it is possible for the entire body to be moved. <margin>Boiling causes the paroxysms. Which fevers come from which causes.</margin> Any putrefying thing passes away at its time of digestion. And the "boiling" produces the putrefaction, which afterwards induces the paroxysm. And it is possible that tertian, quartan, daily, and other fevers originate from the spleen, and from other principal organs such as the heart, kidneys, etc. If it is from sulfur, it is a quartan fever; if from salts, a tertian <note>every three days</note>; if from alum, a daily fever: these have red urine before the paroxysm begins.

### PARAGRAPH II.

**Every material putrefaction creates its own material obstruction from the spirits of salt, with an inborn coagulation, and after coagulation, it turns into tremor through digestion.**

<margin>The duration of the fever is to be known from the "digests."</margin>
Through the "digest" <note>the substances processed or excreted by the body</note> it can be foreknown how long the fever will last. If a daily frequency concurs with a white color, the period will be six weeks, and it will not be cured any sooner. But if it is displayed with a leek-green pain, it will continue for 19, 20, or 21 weeks. If it persists with a cough, it will run until the seventh, eighth, or ninth week. If it afflicts the foot with swellings, it will be terminated at 15 weeks. If it changes the number of paroxysms—for example, if a daily fever becomes a tertian—it will proceed for the space of a year. But if the frequency increases—for example, if a daily fever arises from a quartan—it will last for ten months. However, if the patient's appetite for food and drink persists, it is a sign that the time is being shortened. If the desire for food and drink becomes weak, it inclines more toward a "quartal" <note>a long-term cycle</note>, as was said above.

### PARAGRAPH III.

*A paroxysm which descends from arsenical substances has its own number and digest, and the paroxysm of the first three has an erratic day. And the paroxysm of the blood has its own cure within itself, and its digest.*

It often happens that because of the violence of the paroxysm, blood is poured from the nostrils and comes out with the urine because a vein has ruptured somewhere. <margin>Hemorrhage in a fever is part of the cure.</margin> This is a good sign, and is at the same time the cure of the fever. But if the fever invades in various ways, now later, now earlier, it is "erratic" and a very bad sign; however, under treatment, it is a good sign. If the paroxysm is unequal, let it be considered a bad sign, as one by which an increase of the [morbid] matter is portended.

### OF THE PARAGRAPHS
### BOOK TEN.
#### Concerning internal adversities of the head.
#### PARAGRAPH I.

<margin>The 3 causes of head pain.</margin> **H**eadache proceeds either from the blood, or from resolution <note>the dissolving of solid matter into vapors or fluids</note>, or from obstructions <note>original: "oppilationibus"</note>. Whether the pain is in the left or right part, it comes from these three causes. If from the blood, then the cause is accidental digestion, or an abundance of things, or an error of the three primes <note>Salt, Sulphur, and Mercury; the fundamental chemical principles of all matter according to Paracelsus</note>.
Headaches have three internal causes: blood, resolution, and obstruction. Blood moves the pains of the head either from accidental digestion, or abundance, or an error of the three primes. Every digestion or mobility must have its own rest: because every excess turns into a vice, and even into a disease. Thus, here is a digestion of the blood, when it is moved continually and does not rest, or when too much of it is generated. For then disease is at hand. When Sulphur, Salt, and Mercury err, they immediately produce disease. They also produce disease if they are increased too much. And as soon as the blood is provoked, then the cure begins.

#### PARAGRAPH II.

<margin>The cure for resolution is coagulation.</margin> *THOSE which are from resolutions ascend and descend through fumes. For every smoke or fume is of a narcotic anodyne <note>a pain-relieving substance</note> with an innate stupefaction. However, those proceeding from obstructions—whatever their nature and property, which is from the outside, without an innate nature—such is the disease, and such is its symptom.*
Resolution does not moisten upwards, but evaporates upwards. And this must be coagulated by nightshade <note>original: "solatrum"</note> and houseleek <note>original: "sempervivum"</note>.
Another cause of headache is the resolution of vapors or fumes ascending to the brain, which, by a narcotic anodyne power—by which the sensing spirit is stupefied—falling down again, cause pains. This is frequent in those who have a weak stomach. The third cause is obstruction, which is induced by an error of the three primes. For these produce a disease conforming to their own nature and quality. (Those proceeding...) In these, the obstruction must be cleared.

#### PARAGRAPH III.

*FROM these aforementioned things, in the first species, the part of the side follows: because from anatomy it has this part along with the febrile paroxysm. In the second species, the dry sublimate has a fume in the uppermost cells and parts, with an erratic anodyne paroxysm. In the third species, such as the obstruction is, such are the diseases, namely grave ones, like mania, phrenitis <note>inflammation of the brain</note>, and types of insanity, according to the obstruction of its part through hot or cold, resolved or coagulated.*
All headaches come from those three species: Salt, Sulphur, and Mercury. (Mania, phrenitis.) In these, there is a need to clear the obstruction. A burning fever <note>original: "Causon"</note> is a moist resolution: therefore it must be coagulated with houseleek, nightshade, and purslane <note>original: "portulaca"</note> in the plague.
In the first species, namely of the blood, the right or left part of the head is affected with a febrile paroxysm. A continuous fever <note>original: "Synocha"</note> is a very light headache; a migraine <note>original: "Hemicranea"</note> is the gravest and hardest; for it can extend to a whole year, which finally can even be followed by paralysis. In the second species of resolution, it should be noted that dry fumes, generated and sublimated into the cells of the brain, induce an erratic anodyne paroxysm. If mania coincides, a burning fever is present, nor can they sleep; and those who sleep continually, disease threatens them from the narcotic.

#### PARAGRAPH IV.
-> *Concerning the Cure.* <-

*The cure for the blood is in the cold and the moist narcotic.*
In these diseases, one should neither purge nor digest, but tranquility must be induced, and the pains are to be soothed and lulled to sleep. <margin>What cure is suitable for headache.</margin> If a flow <note>likely a hemorrhage or discharge</note> falls upon a woman after headaches, it is incurable. Similarly, if the menses break out or are stopped with a headache, it is most difficult to cure, and the cure must be begun from the head; afterward, one should turn to the cure of the menses, the cure in the head having been performed first. If dropsy <note>edema or swelling</note> or similar diseases occur with a headache, the cure of the head must always be put first.
The treatment of the first species consists in the cold and the moist narcotic. Narcotics are Liquor of Corals, Rose, Houseleek, Pearls, Darnel <note>original: "Lolium"</note>, and similar things. These are moist narcotics. <margin>Narcotics which bring on headache.</margin>

#### Description for headache in the first species.

<margin>Remedy for the head.</margin> ℞. <note>The symbol for "Recipe" or "Take"</note> Of red Roses, 4 ounces. Of Jupiter’s Beard <note>original: "Barba Iovis," another name for Houseleek</note>, 5 ounces. Let a poultice be made with vinegar or rose water: let all these be applied warm everywhere on the head.

#### Another description.

℞. Of prepared Corals, 1 drachm. Of unperforated Pearls, half a scruple.

# ELEVENTH BOOK
## OF PARAGRAPHS.
### Concerning Pains of the Matrix.
### PARAGRAPH I.

<margin>Two diseases of the womb: Retention and Superfluity.</margin>
The origins of the diseases of the womb <term>Matrix</term> <note>The "Matrix" refers to the uterus, which early modern physicians believed could influence the health of the entire body if it became "corrupted" or "displaced."</note> are not in the womb itself, nor do they arise from it or through it. For every member that depends on others receives harm from those others. For the pains of the womb are Retention and the superfluity of matter.
In the womb, two diseases are to be noted: Retention and Superfluity. The menses is the excrement of the womb. And the womb is nourished by the flesh of man and by all members, not by food and drink. The womb receives its nourishment from all the members once every month, and then it expels its excrements, at which time women feel pains in the back, some feel "gnawings" <note>original: Erosiones</note> in the pit of the stomach, some a headache, and others fatigue before the menses.
<margin>The womb is nourished by all the members.</margin>
Retention does not happen because of the womb, but rather from all parts of the human body, as the womb is nourished by all the members.

### PARAGRAPH II.
The gathering of the disease of Retention or superfluity descends from all parts of the entire body. For the menses in the womb is not the menses itself, but the excrement of the menses. From these things follow conjunction, destruction, alteration, conclusion, the mixing of good and bad matter, discoloration, and the like.
Where women feel pain, there is an obstruction <note>original: oppilatio</note>, such as in the heart, gallbladder, and other principal members. And then the menses must be provoked through the whole body. Conjunction is when the menses comes from all the members, and several sick parts converge. Destruction is when one part breaks and dissolves another. This cannot be observed with such precision; therefore, the menses must be reduced to a temperament <note>a balanced or "tempered" state of the bodily fluids</note>. For then the parts themselves are cured.

### PARAGRAPH III.
### Concerning the Cure.
The cure of the Matrix is twofold: the first is in elixirs; the second is in *orizeo* <note>likely a reference to a specific alchemical preparation or "liquor of gold"</note>. In elixirs, the highest temperament is this: a substance extracted from its essence into "dried alcohol of wine" <note>highly purified, concentrated spirit of wine</note>. In the second cure, the temperament is this: the body, the substance, and its "essentialized" matter without extraction: but rather through transmutations from a solid substance into a drinkable medicine, etc. 
One temperament is found in pearls through extractions in Alcohol. Another temperament is in carnelian <note>original: corniola</note>, and the tempered essence in the "tree of the sea" <note>likely coral</note>. The temperament for pains of the womb is neither hot nor cold, nor ought it to be: and it is neither dissolved, nor a moist coagulate, nor a medicine prepared through "diathesis" <note>disposition or constitutional state</note>. For everything cold and everything hot is an enemy in the illnesses of women. Likewise, everything dry and everything moist is a most wretched poison in menstrual retention and superfluity. Likewise, everything styptic <note>substances that contract tissues to stop bleeding</note>, diaphoretic <note>inducing sweat</note>, harsh, sour, bitter, or sweet is an impediment to the health of women. But the cure of the womb ought to be free from all these aforementioned qualities: because a free temperament possesses its own secret <term>Arcanum</term> <note>An "Arcanum" is a hidden, powerful medicinal essence that acts directly on the life force.</note> and its own judgment.

<margin>Elixir most effective in affections of the womb.</margin>
The description of this temperament for the first cure, the elixirs, is as follows.
Take <note>The symbol ℞ stands for "Recipe," the standard command to begin a prescription.</note> 3 pounds of dried alcohol of wine. 10 drams each of Rosemary flowers <note>original: Fol. Anthos</note>, Mace, and Lavender. 2 ounces each of Cubebs, Cloves, and Cinnamon. Half a dram of Mastic. Half a scruple each of both types of Storax <note>fragrant resins used in perfumes and medicine</note>. 3 drams of Leopard's Bane <note>original: Doronici</note>. Bring this into a "seventh alembic" <note>a type of distilling vessel; "seventh" implies a high degree of refinement</note>. Afterwards, take 20 gold leaves, and 1.5 drams each of unperforated pearls, garnets, and rubies. Bring to digestion for a month. Of this oil, take 3 or 4 drops with Malmsey wine, or Marjoram or Sage water; administer for three or four days, morning and evening. This elixir is a most noble Secret <term>Arcanum</term> for the retention and superfluity of the menses; it dissolves and constricts, and drives away pains of the parts: it removes material suffocation <note>historically called "the rising of the mother," a form of hysteria</note>, and also mineral precipitation.

<margin>The Secret Arcanum of the whole menstrual nature.</margin>
The second description of the liquor of *orizeo* is this.
Take 1 ounce of *orizeo* prepared after the dissolution of honey and salt. 6 ounces each of the liquor of Oranges and Pomegranates. Bring to imbibition <note>soaking or saturation</note>. Afterwards, on a porphyry marble, reduce it into a liquid form. The dose is from 7 or 8 up to 10 or 12 grains in spring water for two or three days. This medicine, from its tempered virtue, dissolves and resolves, constricts and strengthens the womb and the menses of the whole body: outside the womb, it de-obstructs its parts, and releases them from the members...

# TWELFTH BOOK OF PARAGRAPHS.
## On Toothaches.
### PARAGRAPH I.
### On the Cause.

<margin>Where does toothache come from?</margin>

**T**oothaches, along with their accompanying symptoms, are located in the roots of the bone, with the gums and their surrounding regions. There is one external cause of toothache, and another located in the place itself. That which is external descends from the regions of the head; and that which is local is the beginning of a "scabrous" condition or a *panaritium* <note>original: panariti. Usually referring to an infection of the fingertip (a whitlow), Paracelsus uses the term here to describe a localized, festering inflammation or abscess within the tooth or gum.</note>.

<margin>Various causes of toothache.</margin>

Toothache arises from an accident <note>A "casual" or external event, rather than a systemic imbalance.</note>, and the beginning of the disease is in the site of the pain. If the tooth is whole and the gums healthy, the pain descends from the regions of the head. For the pain is carried through the blood of the small veins that are inserted into the gums, and it is nothing but a vice of the blood while the tooth itself remains good. It is impossible for this to be a "flow" from the head. For such a flow would occupy many teeth and invade the entire mouth, from which a quinsy <note>A severe inflammation of the throat.</note> would arise. If it were a different kind of flow, it would also damage the gums. Teeth do not admit disease from their own roots. It can also happen that teeth ache because of ear pain. For the small veins of the ears and teeth are very close together. Just as the *panaritium* and the scabrous ulcer occur in the finger, so too does toothache. By *panaritium*, the "worm" of the fingers, teeth, and ears is understood. The first generation of toothaches occurs when the tooth begins to rot from the sharpness of salt, and it aches continually. Afterward, it proceeds to the generation of a worm, which gnaws the tooth in which it was born with immense pain, feeding upon that which is of its own nature. For every worm eats that from which it is born, just as moths eat clothes. However, if the worm feels the air, it dies.

<margin>Every worm gnaws that from which it originates.</margin>

### PARAGRAPH II.
### On the Cure.

the cure of the teeth is twofold: **Medical** and **Surgical**.

<margin>The medical cure of teeth.</margin>

#### The Medical cure is as follows.
℟. Take half a dram each of Tormentil, Staphisagria <note>Also known as "Lice-bane," used historically to treat parasites and skin issues.</note>, and plantain seed. 
Take half a dram each of the outer root of Henbane and poppy juice. Reduce into a decoction with vinegar. Let it be made into a warm wash.

In the treatment, it must be ensured that an "emunctory" <note>An opening or organ that allows for the drainage of waste or "bad humors."</note> of the blood is created there, such as the one placed here, if it is applied to the teeth. A similar effect is provided by sharp dock, which is otherwise called <term>Oxylapathon</term> <note>From the Greek *oxys* (sharp) and *lapathon* (dock).</note> and <term>Melioca</term>, if it is cut into small discs which, soaked in vinegar, are to be applied to the teeth; or if the root is crushed more coarsely, moistened with vinegar, and applied to the teeth for a quarter of an hour or longer.

<margin>The surgical cure of teeth.</margin>

In surgical care, the "sinning matter" <note>The corrupt substance causing the disease.</note> must be removed. Just as if someone wished to kill a scabrous ulcer or a *panaritium*, they should achieve it through *sperniolum* <note>A term often referring to a preparation of frog spawn or a specific alchemical mucilage used to "cool" and "cleanse" infections.</note>; so too with the worm in the tooth. For if it putrefies, it stinks. In such a case, a gargle should be made of honey and vinegar; if the mouth is rinsed with this, the stench vanishes.

<margin>*Sperniolum* kills the scabrous ulcer.</margin>

# THIRTEENTH & FOURTEENTH BOOKS OF PARAGRAPHS.
## On the Pains of the Ears and Eyes.
### PARAGRAPH I.
### On the Cause.

**T**he pain of the ears comes from the cause of the "fourth emunctory" from the regions of the head, arriving with its own deafness, species, and joints, according to the anatomy of the lower region, along with the regions of the nose and eyes. The occurrence is from an accident and from the location; because it is from an accident, it descends from "aluminous" matter <note>Matter characterized by the properties of alum—likely meaning sharp, astringent, or salty humors.</note>: and that which is from the location arises from its own inborn paroxysm with chronic signs, ringing in the ears, and an abscess with pus and discharge, and its other species.

In the region of the liver is the place where the humors ascend; but this has nothing to do with ear pains. Therefore, it is necessary that the pain comes from an accident or a "fall." All recipes that recommend pouring infusions into the ears are wicked and false. For nothing should be poured into the ears unless the recipe is made from <term>Tutia</term> <note>A crude zinc oxide, used as a medicinal powder or ointment for its drying and healing properties.</note>. Furthermore, no cure handed down by ancient writers for ear pain is useful; they are all erroneous. If the pain comes from the location, it is a pain from aluminous salt.

<margin>Nothing is to be poured into the ears except Tutia.</margin>

# BOOKS OF THE PARAGRAPHS: BOOKS XIII AND XIV

### PARAGRAPH II

<margin>Tridoma</margin>
*The cure for ear pain, firstly through cold opening medicines used for dissolved humors. Secondly through numbing pain-relievers according to the saying of Archelaus, etc., with <term>Tridoma <note>A surgical method or specific composition involving three components, referenced by medieval surgeons.</note></term> according to the process of <note>Albucasis (936–1013) was a famous Arab physician and surgeon from Al-Andalus, known as the father of modern surgery.</note> Albucasis: following the surgical art and the experience of <note>Raymond Lully (c. 1232–1316) was a philosopher and alchemist whose works were highly influential in the Renaissance.</note> Raymond Lully.*

**The first description for ear pains caused by an accident: it is White Sief, made from the power of Tutia with the addition of amber, and is as follows.**

<margin>White Sief for ear pains.</margin>
Take: **Prepared Tutia** <note>Zinc oxide, a mineral used for centuries in eye and ear treatments.</note> without vinegar, half a drachm. **Amber** <note>original: carabae</note>, one drachm. Reduce into a liquid. Then take: Seven and a half ounces of this liquor. **Alcohol of dried wine**, two ounces. Process through the preparation of the <term>water bath <note>original: maris praeparationem; likely referring to a balneum Mariae or a specific alchemical distillation process.</note></term>. Let it become a Sief. This should be applied in the manner of a plaster.

**Description for roughness and inflammation <note>original: panaritio; usually referring to a whitlow or infected swelling.</note> of the ears.**

<margin>Dry Sief for roughness.</margin>
Take: Seeds of **Henbane**, **Poppy**, **Darnel**, and **Black Cumin**, half a drachm of each. **Bull's gall**, half a drachm. **Liquefied camphor**, equal to the weight of all the rest. Reduce into a dry Sief.

**On the conditions of the eyes.**
The logic is similar for pains in the eyes as it is for pains in the ears. Regarding <term>Scotomia <note>A condition involving dark spots or dizziness in the field of vision.</note></term> at the root of the eyes, where a cataract must be considered, the various types of eye conditions should not be set aside. The aforementioned recipes can also be applied and used for the eyes, just as a cataract cannot be removed except by an instrument. Likewise, if a film or "nail" <note>An old term for a pterygium, a fleshy growth on the eye.</note> grows on the eye, it must be pulled out and rooted out by an instrument. Although, eye-washes <note>original: collyria</note> are sometimes useful.

**An eye-wash for Scotomia and all types of eye conditions.**

<margin>Eye-wash for Scotomia.</margin>
Take: **White vitriol**, **split alum**, and **extinguished tutia**, one drachm of each.
**Liquor of Eyebright** <note>original: Euphragiae; a plant traditionally used for vision health.</note>, six ounces. **Ground camphor**, one and a half drachms. Reduce into a liquid substance upon a **porphyry slab** with the separation of the water bath.

Eye-washes ought to be "consuming" <note>Refers to medicines that "eat away" or dissolve excess humors or growths.</note>. For those whose eyes are red from blood, bean flour should be heated and moistened with vinegar, and the resulting steam should be taken into the eyes. For by this, the redness is removed. Furthermore, the less that is poured into the ears or eyes, the more beneficial it is. Eye-washes should not be made from distilled waters and arsenic, etc.

### THE BOOK OF THEOPHRASTUS
## ON EPIDEMICS.
### CHAPTER I.

**THE CAUSE** and origin of epidemic abscesses <note>original: Apostematum</note> is the plague, which is a disease that afflicts a healthy body, remains in a healthy body, and is mixed with nothing impure or unhealthy. Even if the body were perhaps not healthy, but were diseased, putrid, or otherwise faulty: nevertheless, these things do not cause the plague. Rather, it is this alone—that which is healthy—which is the reason the disease comes.

And if a leper is seized by the plague, be certain that some member which is healthy brought the plague upon him, and not the diseased member. Judge the same concerning pustules and any kind of <term>cachexia <note>A state of severe physical wasting and malnutrition associated with chronic illness.</note></term>.

<margin>What the plague is.</margin>
The plague is a disease arising from the four Elements, perfecting its operation in natural bodies, more in some and less in others. But the dominion belongs to one alone.

<margin>The fourfold plague.</margin>
From this emerges the **Star-like plague**, the **Watery plague**, the **Earthly plague**, and the **Chaos-like plague**. And yet four infectors are ready at hand.

<margin>The plague falls from without.</margin>
The plague is an epidemic disease; it is carried from the outside to the inside without any physical sign, by a spiritual means, infecting that which struggles against it—namely the heart, the liver, and the brain. If the plague cannot strike these parts, it strikes those that are neighboring and close to them.
If anyone truly wonders what the plague is...

-># ON EPIDEMICS.<-

## ON EPIDEMICS.

<margin>Plague corresponds with the first three principles.</margin>
Let anyone who wishes to know what the plague is and where it originates attend to this. The plague is the fruit of the four Elements, and it corresponds with <term>Sulphur, Salt, and Mercury <note>The "Tria Prima" or three primary substances that Paracelsus believed made up all material things.</note></term>: however, you must exclude those who contract it from infected persons.

The origin of this "fruit" is as follows: everything corporeal arises from the elements and is drawn from the <term>Great Yliaster <note>original: Yliastro; in Paracelsian philosophy, this refers to the primeval matter or the "star-matter" from which everything is composed.</note></term>. Therefore, the nature of the body emulates that Yliaster and is subject to it. Whatever is corporally united with it becomes contaminated. From this, it follows that whatever is of a fiery nature, <margin>Everything fiery is ignited from the father of the Yliaster in a molar fashion, etc.</margin> being born from the father of the Yliaster, is ignited in a stellar way. That which is of the earth is seized and infected in an earthy way; that of the air, in an airy way; and that of the water, in a watery way. For all bodies are generated from these elements and participate in their nature, health, and disease.

From this comes that force and power, nor can anyone escape the force of the four Elements; whatever they bring about, we conceive within ourselves. First, we arise from them. Second, we exist within them. Third, we are regenerated in them. Fourth, they impart and inflict their own nature upon us. For we are inferior to them—indeed, we are merely their smoke.

Thus, we are produced by them and are not at all separate from them. Hence it happens that we are compelled to suffer because of them. If it were possible to turn this aside, so that we were not born from and composed of the Yliaster but from something else, we could certainly resist that which would harm us. But we do not belong to ourselves at all: we are the smoke of the four Elements.

But as to how it happens that a thing placed outside of us operates within us, even though it has no material influence or substance of its own and performs all such things without a physical body: the reason and cause is this—that our **vital spirit** and the external **Elemental spirit** are one and the same spirit.

<margin>The Vital Spirit must be carefully weighed by physicians.</margin>
This **vital spirit** must be diligently considered by you physicians. For the blindness of your Patrons and Princes has revealed none of these things to you, but has instead drawn a veil and a cataract over them, just as a <term>white spot <note>original: albugo; a medical term for an opaque white spot on the cornea.</note></term> might cover the crystalline humor of the eye.

<margin>Vehement reproach of physicians.</margin>
Weigh this matter carefully. For in this—namely, that the vital spirit gives birth to all diseases—all diseases are understood. But here I speak at least of the plague; elsewhere I speak of others. And I speak of the plague for this primary reason: your authors did not correctly understand the principle of this disease and were utterly ignorant of the plague.

***

For Avicenna says: the plague, etc. Galen says otherwise, etc. How can they prove these things, either by themselves or you with them? For while you consider yourselves exceedingly skilled in Theory and Physics, and yet you do not know the spirit of life—to whom it is related and by what rationale it dwells in the Elements and the body—it becomes clear and plain enough that from your false Theory proceeds an erroneous Practice. Thus, your Theory fits the plague about as well as <note>Likely a reference to a contemporary figure or a proverbial "bad fit," possibly a specific local doctor known for failure.</note> Roland of Halle. Take your **Mithridatium**, bring forth your **Chebulos** and **Turbith** <note>These refer to complex traditional herbal formulas and specific purgative roots like the Myrobalan plum and Turpeth root.</note>, and with them, if you can, dig out the eyes of the Elements themselves! Take your **Theriac** <note>An ancient, complex "universal" antidote containing dozens of ingredients.</note>, and by disputing, conquer the spirit of life outside the body near the fire and burn it. Take all your recipes and hurl them like lightning: and in the end, see if the patient has not escaped healthy and safe without your help.

I do indeed praise experiments themselves. But those men have not at all perceived from whence their powers proceed. On the contrary, they have directed their experience not toward resisting the spirit, but toward conquering it. What do you really want, you physicians of **Montpellier**, **Pavia**, and **Verona**? Of what importance, I ask you, should all your Theory and universal commentaries and trifles about the plague be held? Your foundation collapses through this: that by your own testimony, one plague is not like another, and that which was useful last year achieves nothing in this present one; or what is suitable now will be fruitless next year. This is surely the **Dariadestus Disease** <note>A term likely coined by the author to describe a shifting, unpredictable, or "unconquerable" malady that defies traditional categories.</note>. Answer me, you little scholars, what is this? And do not stumble against a stone.

Philosophy has indeed proceeded conveniently according to your wishes until now. But where Philosophy ends, the Physician finally begins and comes forth. But where were you born and bred as professors? In a cedar tree, I suppose; or rather, in a pine or a fir. And if I knew it wouldn't upset your stomachs, I would state even more clearly that such people are born in oak trunks.

Not everything is insignificant that you Italians judge. But I think you are also **Bolleres** <note>Likely a derogatory term or a reference to "shouters" or "deceivers."</note> who are sent into Germany: and you Germans, too, who are planted or grafted onto Italian plum and cork trees; none of whom is ashamed or reluctant to write Theories about the plague, yet who have not even with the tip of their tongue tasted the Yliaster of Philoso—

# MEDICAL FRAGMENTS
<meta>catchword: white sugar (candi),</meta>

You have tasted just enough philosophy so that <term>Ares <note>original: "Ares." In the author's unique terminology, Ares refers to the specific power within nature that differentiates and gives form to things.</note></term> is silenced. O you gowned men in your reverend robes! What sort of "art" is this, that you prescribe in a time of plague: "Take <term>Diaphenicon <note>A traditional purgative electuary made with dates.</note></term>, take good <term>Theriac <note>A famous ancient "universal" antidote made of dozens of ingredients, including viper flesh and opium.</note></term>," saying that these were useful a year ago, or even ten years ago, and therefore they must be useful now? Truly, those who educated you taught you such things: Galen, Avicenna, and Rhazes. If such men were considered fit to write on diseases and medicines, then even the Riphæan and Hercynian mountains <note>Traditional names for distant or legendary mountain ranges in Northern and Central Europe.</note> would produce plenty of such authors today along with their fir cones.

Remove the dodder <note>A parasitic climbing plant, used here as a metaphor for something choking the truth.</note> from your throats at last, take the cataracts from your rags, and clear the <term>Morion <note>original: "Morionem." This refers to a state of stupor or folly, though the word was also used for the dark mandrake plant.</note></term> from the <term>dura mater <note>The tough outermost membrane surrounding the brain.</note></term>. First establish the Philosopher within yourselves, then plant the Physician. Guard yourselves against being scarred by nettles and <term>Spanish flies <note>original: "cantharides." Toxic beetles used in traditional medicine to cause blistering, which the author here uses as a metaphor for harmful treatments.</note></term>. Strike your "cephalic" <note>Referring to the cephalic vein, commonly used in bloodletting for head-related issues.</note> according to your own training, so that you might be freed from your frenzy, and let neither Madness nor <term>Stentor <note>A Greek herald in the Iliad known for his shout; here perhaps referring to loud, empty boasting.</note></term> occupy you: you breeched Italians, and swollen Frenchmen—or should I say "long-haired"—and even you, the vineyard of Germany.
