## Other Fragments on the Plague follow, collected from his own handwritten notes.

* *Many things are required for this proof. Let them be of this kind: yet in the end, it remains that he has at least a written art. To be sure, those things have been written down which bring us no benefit. That which was going to be useful has been omitted. What, then, can I lose in his writings when no pearl is present? Surely he did not wish to cast them before swine. I was therefore forced and led by these things to care henceforth for no writings—neither Philosophy nor Astronomy, nor experiments, nor Auguries, nor <term>Geomancy <note>Divination by means of lines or geographic features.</note></term>, <term>Necromancy <note>Communication with the dead.</note></term>, or <term>Pyromancy <note>Divination by fire.</note></term>—but to cling to and enslave myself to the **light of nature** alone. For all the monuments of the ancients, as well as those of the moderns, persuade us that we must trust in this alone. Although few colleagues offer themselves here who are skilled in the light of nature, perhaps that which is now green will erupt more fully in the course of time. But put back in its place everything that others have and put forward, Reader. Experience, judge, prove, and do not offer yourself as a slave either to the training of teachers, the information of pharmacists, the experiments of Rhazes, or the theory of Galen. For what good thing, I ask, can you finally read in all of those? Nothing at all. For they themselves are of no value and worth nothing. Here is the reason: if any sick person is cured by you, is the thanks given to you? You yourselves assert that you performed it. But now your Masters are lying. For you performed it from within yourselves; therefore you also assign this honor to yourselves—not to Avicenna, not to Galen, not to Hippocrates. And rightly so. For you do not receive those things from them. Perhaps you learned them from some old woman. Therefore, you do rightly.*

*Look, Reader, this is why I am a diligent exhorter to you. Compare and consider one thing with another, and do not be so headlong to write. Ignore those who do not perform signs <note>Referring to "signs" as evidence of real healing power or miracles.</note>. Do not pay attention to those vain characters of the bath-keepers. For whom do they bear and plant leeks and onions? For all these things are not medicine, but hats woven from straw, which do not hold water at all but let it pass through. Fix your eyes on the true foundation of Medicine, if you are going to do anything honest. But if you are going to do poorly, keep your old ways and follow your <term>freshmen <note>original: "Beanos." A slang term for uninitiated or naive university students.</note></term>, from whom no fewer Canons are chosen than from the learned themselves. How well they do: let the common people be the judge. You judge, prove, assess, read, and delay nothing. If you harbor any particular or customary evils, throw them away with the lice, and show yourself a dedicated student. Farewell.*

What is it that Bruno, Garlandus, Rhazes, Galen, and Anshelmus <note>A list of medieval and ancient medical and philosophical authorities.</note> write? Let those things not move you. No foundation is present; it is a pure and clear lie, whatever they say, etc. The cause of the plague. What it is. The method of forecasting.

# ON THE PLAGUE.

<margin>Sugar, Place. Limbus <note>original: "Limbus." In the author's cosmology, this refers to the primordial "great world" or the reservoir of all created elements.</note>.</margin>
<margin>Signs. Whence the cause.</margin>
<margin>Declaration of the place.</margin>
The reason why it strikes these specific parts: it is like lightning.

### I.
That the region of the ear encompasses the whole grasp of the plague.
That the plague is a wound and a pain of the brain and heart, much like the inflammation of a wound.
**Therefore, no Medicine is of use.** <note>The author argues here that traditional herbal remedies cannot heal what is essentially a spiritual or "astral" wound.</note>

### II.
That anger, envy, gluttony, lust, etc., are the cohort of the planets against the people: therefore come the pustules, therefore the plagues, from Venus and from Mars.
That any prognostication has its origin not from the Planets themselves, but from anger. Therefore, he who knows that envy, anger, and lust are coming, he knows how to prophesy the manner of it, namely, once the generation has occurred in the planets: he is the true Astronomer.
What power is finally assigned to the planets, O you foolish Astronomers, when they do nothing without our merit or cause?
Therefore David and Jesus spoke from the nature of man: the star follows from that same event: the flood, etc. because anger was growing in the times of the New Testament, the stars of the flood were born. And thus Christ speaks of the false Prophets in Matthew 24.
Therefore, this must be judged concerning the plague: that from the anger of the Planets, a constellation of sin rises in the planets; and when it grows to the end and reaches its autumn, it then yields fruit—which is the "fume" of the plague, pustules, famine, pestilence, etc.
Otherwise, no Astronomer can judge such things, unless the Father is angry, regarding the innate rod: he declares this rod. <note>The "rod" refers to divine punishment or a "scourge."</note>

<margin>
I. { It occupies the whole body like rain. But nothing receives it except this part alone: just as a clod of earth receives water, but a rock does not. No other members are infected.
</margin>
<margin>
II. { Just as water seeks the earth, not the rock. Lightning seeks wood. Dew seeks grass. Manna seeks leaves; each has its own parts. Likewise, the plague has its own "earth," etc.; the other part is the rock.
</margin>

The <term>Microcosm <note>The human being viewed as a miniature reflection of the entire universe (the Macrocosm).</note></term> is here, etc.
In short, you ought to attack Mars, and at least overcome him; in this way, you will drive out the plague. Likewise, why use Sapphire from the outside? Because it is the contrary of Mars. Who shall expel Mars, except that which causes an eclipse to him: Medicine and diseases.

---

->**Note on the signs.**<-

From the <term>Limbus</term> comes a fume. The Limbus is the whole of creation, namely the four Elements and all animals. Therefore, at the time when there are many worms, there also is the plague. Likewise, fish, eclipses of the Sun and Moon, are the matter of the plague. The plague grows for many years before it touches anyone: then, through the whole, and everything that is "marked," it smokes; the touch happens wherever it wishes.
And thus very often, those who flee before the appointed time escape: just as a tree that is transplanted into another soil withers, so also the plague withers in the body. For if you wish to know the place, it is thus: the body of man, and that place where he has been, is the "earth" of the plague, like a garden, etc.
In the same year that the plague dominates and is generated, pearls and garnets are also generated in the mountains, and there the minerals overflow.
Why is the plague in these three places <note>Likely referring to the groin, armpits, and neck, where plague buboes typically appear.</note>? Why not in the rest—the brain, ears, etc.? Therefore, where there is an <term>emunctory <note>original: "emunctorium." An organ or part of the body that carries off waste, such as the lymph nodes.</note></term> of sweat, there is the center of the plague in its exiting. Because under the ear, under the armpits, etc., there are certain emunctories for sweat. The pores are not the emunctories of sweat, but these parts are, because there is a twofold sweat: the "fecal" sweat and the "expressed" sweat. In the sweat of dregs is the body of the plague. Therefore, all medicines are made of this kind of sweat. The ears are the emunctory of the brain: the emunctory of the veins, as in their own parts. Likewise, the <term>English Sweat <note>original: "sudor Anglicus." A highly contagious and often fatal disease that broke out in England several times in the 15th and 16th centuries.</note></term> is a sweat of dregs. But I shall discuss this more fully in the <term>Archidoxis <note>One of the author's primary works on the "ancient teachings" of nature and alchemy.</note></term>.

> Why the redness,
> Why the <term>Aposteme <note>An abscess or swelling.</note></term>,
> Why, etc.

Likewise note: six distinct emunctories, separated from one another, a specific Anatomy.
The redness is an <term>Arsenical <note>Refers to a corrosive, burning quality resembling the mineral arsenic.</note></term> sweat; it sets fire to the flesh and the place of the flesh, like a corrosive. Therefore, the Aposteme and the redness differ from Arsenic because of the place, nature, and alteration of the Elements—as fish differs from flesh, or stone from wood—and both are the matter of the structure. So also these minerals differ: man is a corporeal Element, and the earth is a corporeal Element, and thus are their offspring.
1. *A chapter on sweats.*
2. *A chapter on the emunctories of sweats.*
Likewise, how God gives disease...

He links these outbreaks to environmental and mineral phenomena, arguing that the plague must be understood through the relationship between the Microcosm (man) and the Macrocosm (the universe).</summary>

...to everyone according to his acts. The acts are according to their own lust; thus the pustules arise, and thus the plague arises from envy because of "mine and thine" <note>A reference to the sin of greed and private ownership over communal charity.</note>. Likewise, and so it is with others. 
Likewise concerning pleurisy.

Note, the more envious the human race is, the more the fury of the plague tames them. 
Note, envy is the cause of such diseases. The lust of many is the cause of plague; envy is joined with the higher powers; envy kills, poisons, etc.
Note, there is an Arsenical sweat <note>original: "sudor Arsenicalis." In this context, it refers to a sweat that is as toxic and corrosive as arsenic.</note>, that is, a caustic sweat <term>Escharalis</term><note>From "eschar," referring to the dead tissue or "scab" produced by a burn or corrosive substance. It implies a sweat that burns or destroys the skin.</note>: but it is a sweat that putrefies, that is, it strangles, just as smoke strangles cheese. Thus that sweat is like smoke, and whatever it touches, it destroys, so that the poison has no limit. Therefore it putrefies; therefore there must be an opening so that the smoke may exit. The cure is the attraction of a good attractive remedy.

### Another Schedule.

**I**n order that we may rightly understand the nature of the plague, and how it falls upon us from above, we must know the nature of the Basilisk <note>A mythical serpent said to kill with its gaze; used here as a metaphor for the invisible, lethal "rays" of the plague.</note>. As is the nature of this creature, such also is the nature of the Planets which we look upon. The Basilisk is hatched and born against nature, from the most unfit source, beyond all natural operation. So too is the plague generated; it is brought forth from our heart, as if from a hen, an egg is laid which is then hatched by the toads of heaven. In whatever way this animal is born, in that same way is the plague born. Now, truly, this poison remains in those stars, and those stars become and are the Basilisk. That Basilisk retains its own nature. For as soon as it looks upon a person, its nature is so poisonous that the envy within it, etc. For it is entirely Saturn <note>In alchemy and astrology, Saturn is associated with lead, coldness, decay, and the "melancholy" that brings death.</note>, and the select essence of Saturn. That envy is so powerful that whatever it looks upon is immediately infected and poisoned, just as someone is infected by eyes during menstruation <note>A common medieval and Renaissance belief that the gaze of a menstruating woman could tarnish mirrors or cause harm.</note>.

### Another Schedule.

**I**ts sight rushes down headlong and agitated like a bolt of lightning, nor does anyone know where it is being carried. And with whatever speed the eyes are turned toward someone, so swift is its ray. And just as we know that lightning is nothing in the beginning, yet afterwards it grows and is clothed in matter and a body, so similarly there is nothing at first in the eyes of the Basilisk. But like lightning, so this birth happens in the manner of a lightning flash. Once produced, the lightning strikes against men, etc. For it is generated from them. Now truly, lightning is made from sulfur, etc., and it passes into a coagulation of sulfur and salt, from which it also receives its force, its crash, and its thunder, etc.

### Another Fragment.

**T**hus, therefore, volatile bodies are extracted or produced through their own Magnet in their rising, from which they proceed. Afterwards, nothing remains in them except the seed, which awaits its ripening so that it may fall. The Doctors have passed over this through laziness, and they have not understood the origin of this kind of spiritual disease, nor the Magnet of heaven, nor in turn the ripened fruits, nor have they judged the return into the body. Although heaven, on account of the abundance and multitude of such bodies, attracts them spontaneously without digestion or waste; that is, the star of wrath attracts its own wrath, the volatile body, of its own accord. So also the envious star and the beneficent star, which by themselves lead that generation in man to ripeness, all of which ends in the plague, and something similar to this.

<header>ON EPIDEMIIS.</header>

Book One, **CHAPTER I.** *Concerning the volatile body: how the senses, imagination, will, lust, desire, and appetite of the microcosm <note>The human being viewed as a "little world" reflecting the entire universe</note> are changed into a physical body.*

*How that body, thus transformed, becomes a volatile subject to every spirit and movement from above us, because what is light moves upward.*

*How that volatile body retains itself within the physical body, and how the poison becomes most wicked, surpassing other bodies, as the new seed of a new disease—namely the natural one, which is the plague.*

**CHAPTER II.** *How wisdom is the principle of incarnation, and those things are performed by the stars which human wisdom desires, according to the saying of Ptolemy: "The wise man shall rule the stars" <note>original: "Vir sapiens dominabitur astris"</note>; he commands, compels, and orders them.*

*How characters <note>planetary sigils or symbolic diagrams</note> are the instruments of a thing, made from the wisdom of one person into a point and a hammer for everyone who participates in this wisdom; and it is an instrument of this kind.*

*How no incantation acts without a body; the body is volatile, as said above, and that body is taken up with the spirituality of the imagination, and becomes a harmful instrument directed against another person.*

**CHAPTER III.** *What the nature of the Basilisk <note>A mythical serpent said to kill with its gaze; Paracelsus uses it here as a metaphor for the invisible, lethal "rays" of the plague</note> is, as well as an example and visual demonstration of the aforementioned things.*

*How the nature of lightning is an indicator of the Quiver <note>original: "Pharetri"</note> and the Basilisk, for it is similar to the Basilisk.*

*How the conjunction of Olympus and the stars are joined like red wine and white wine, and how the mixed wine is blended in its contrariety—that is, how those two stars are united.*

### Another Schedule.

It is necessary that there be plagues, with nothing prohibiting them. Nor should anyone be persuaded that anything can entirely preserve them. And although some preventatives are indeed given, they are not given to all. For God chooses for Himself whom He wills. Plagues always come in different kinds and species. Therefore, there is no single use for a remedy among the old and the young mixed together.

### FIRST PART OF THE MEDICAL WORKS.

### BOOK I.

# ON TARTARS.

**CHAPTER I.**

<margin>How many types and species of Tartar.</margin>
**T**here are two kinds of Tartar: the kind like frost, and the kind like a gemstone from rock. The frost kind is twofold: *Hail* and *Vine-frost*. The gemstone kind is threefold: *Collected, simple, and divided*. All of these, however, are Alabastrine and Marble, or Elephantine, and Adamantine <note>hard as diamonds</note>, also *Duelech* <term>Duelech</term> <note>A specific Paracelsian term for painful stones, particularly in the kidneys or bladder</note> and Magnet-like: and they have different locations, because there are different types, and many within bodies. Therefore it should be noted: as many locations as there are, so many are the species. The vine-frost of the stomach, the liver, the vessel of the kidneys, and the bladder: also frost...

<meta>This page continues the discussion of "Tartaric" diseases, shifting from the general theory of their origin to specific descriptions of how these stony deposits—which Paracelsus compares to hoarfrost or mud—manifest in different organs such as the stomach, liver, and bladder.</meta>

# MEDICAL FRAGMENTS

...the frost <note>original: "pruina," referring here to a crystalline or stony coating like hoarfrost</note> of the liver, of the stomach, etc. Even hail and gems find a place in the stomach, the liver, and their other parts and dwellings. Likewise, note concerning the "guests": these are foreign, unsuitable sicknesses that do not belong to the main category; they are not the usual diseases and are contained externally.

### CHAPTER II.
<margin>What Frost is:</margin>
**W**hat is "Frost" <note>original: "Prüinum"</note> in the generation of these aforementioned things? The Elemental Womb <note>original: "matrix Elementina," the source of physical elements in the body</note> produced two things: Mud and Mucilage, along with its own "spara" <note>likely referring to a discharge or byproduct</note>, which is both dissolved and coagulated; these are external. The Yliaster <note>The primordial vital force or base matter</note> also gave birth to three things in the nature of the sufferer: a slime of the second generation, a perverse Bitumen <note>a tar-like substance</note> poorly restored and wrongly placed, and a "gluing together" of its own putrefied matter. (We make no mention here of the coagulated, because that matter is moved from the outside and not from within.)

### CHAPTER III.
<margin>The nature of digestion is twofold.</margin>
**B**ut what of our purpose? This: The nature of the Archeus <note>The "internal alchemist" or governing vital force that directs digestion</note> does not dissolve the resolved from the resolved—that is, it does not separate the Mud and the small stone, nor the resolved from the moist. That unique mixture is our food and drink. Furthermore, what then? Nature is twofold in digestion: one side separates the stone from the watery part; the other does not desire it, leaving the stone dissolved in the water and mixed into the meals. If nature consumes these mixed things, all is well. If not, take heed: it harms either the stomach, the intestines, the liver, or the urinary vessels and their common areas. These parts suffer from the indigestion of the Archeus and its failure to separate the "pure Sapphire" from the "unfit Chalcedony" <note>Paracelsus uses gemstone names here to represent the "pure" nutrient vs. the "stony" waste product</note>.

### CHAPTER IV.
**N**ow, if mud or mucilage has been taken in, and if the stomach digests it for the sake of separation, it is well. But if not—if the mud was taken and the remains of that mud or mucilage stay in the stomach, in the floor or the opening—then there follows burning, "orexen" <note>an intense or disordered appetite</note>, compression of the chest, vomiting at dawn, loss of appetite, a roughness of the tongue, and a suffering like that of "prunella" <note>a throat infection or "canker" often associated with fever</note>. But if it does not stay there but passes on to the intestines and does not go through, it will stick under the form of Tartar <note>The stony sediment Paracelsus blames for many ailments</note> or a small stone, causing now constipation, now colic, now back pain, now pain of the hip and sciatica; now it closes the Monocolon <note>The cecum or beginning of the large intestine</note>, now the Longaon <note>The rectum</note>; now the strength of the appetite is halted, and all manner of evils occur. Even blood and "beans" <note>likely referring to bean-shaped deposits or hardened stool</note> will be passed.

### CHAPTER V.
**B**ut if it goes to the liver and is coagulated or "tartarized" there: now comes blockage, now thirst, now a hot vapor, now a piercing pain, now hardness in that part, now a small amount of urine—sometimes red, sometimes reddish-brown—now "wild" urine, now dropsy, now a disorder of the veins. But if it passes through to the kidneys and a drying-out follows there, it is converted into Tartar, and a generation of small stones begins. If it sticks in these regions in many ways, it causes now nausea, now great vomiting, now twisting of the navel, now tumors of the foot and veins, now weakness of the hips; it also causes innumerable and nearly incurable wandering diseases of the kidneys and those parts.

### CHAPTER VI.
**B**ut if it takes hold of the bladder and its parts along with the neck, and the final "pipe" <note>the urethra</note> at its opening, and the moisture has departed, then the generation of salt follows in that place. Then the resolved matter and the watery resolved matter will be coagulated into "Chalcedony." For every muddy or mucilaginous thing that is undigested and unseparated is separated from each other in the bladder. If that muddy, mucilaginous stuff becomes salt, or if a great amount hardens along with the salt, it grows skin by skin into the generation of a stone and calculus. For in this place lies the Archeus of separation and its offspring, which others call Lithiasis <note>The medical term for stone formation</note>, but I truly name "Muddy Tartar."

### CHAPTER VII.
**I**f it was mucilage and not mud, remember that it takes its place everywhere just as mud does. However, if the wateriness and moisture have been separated from it, Tartar is generated—or "Muddy Tartar"—not in one place only, but wherever it is caught and stripped of its moisture. There it gives birth and coagulates; the "Ore" <note>original: "Minera"</note> will appear in dangerous ways. Then follows the Alabastrine kind <note>stones resembling soft alabaster</note>, which is sweet mucilage, and the Marble kind, which is hard and rough, born from mud. This is the generation itself: it is of hail, and of the "moss" of Tartar <note>original: "usneæ Tartari," a term for the growth or crust of the sediment</note>.

### CHAPTER VIII.
->(The Second Treatise)<-
**B**ut whatever comes from the three internal things of the Yliaster—namely, from the slime—takes its local beginning everywhere it is possible for a stone to form. It does not pass through the urinary or fecal pathways, but seeks and holds a foreign place. # ABOUT TARTAR

...[marrow], now in the marrow, and in other putrid parts, and in the juice, and in the emunctory <note>organs that eliminate waste</note> excretions. And the formation of stones, or "Tartarization," is foreign—that is, rare.

### CHAPTER IX.

**B**ut what if it comes from Bitumen <note>a pitch-like or tarry substance</note>? What is Bitumen? It is a kind of "Locust-matter" <note>original: "Locustarum," likely referring to a spreading or invasive quality</note>, a viscous state belonging to the varieties of itching, scabies, and chronic Gout, Hand-gout, and Joint-gout; for nature contains Bitumen. If it should be dried out, nothing remains but Tartar. Every species of Gout is of this Tartar; so too is the "vine-scale" of the teeth <note>original: "vinea dentium," referring to dental tartar or plaque</note> and the coagulated tears of the eyes. It creates hidden signs under the skin of Gout and Stone-disease <note>original: "Lithiasis"</note>. Regarding these diseases, the father-physicians have slept; those who follow do not know how to speak of them.

### CHAPTER X.

**A**nd if the generation comes from putrefactions, it must be noted that wherever it occurs, the matter is neither muddy, nor mucilaginous, nor gemstone-like, nor porous. Rather, it is from the proper substance of that place from which it proceeds—it is possible from all parts. If the liquid putrefies, but the salt does not, the salt will be converted into a congealed mass; the rest settles as dregs according to the nature of salt, placing a center, coagulating, and hardening, and it gives birth to unknown diseases. For whatever reaches the bladder passes into the coagulation of a stone. For in the bladder is the power of salt, in which there is the force of coagulating—sometimes even in the "guest" parts <note>referring to parts of the body where these substances are not native</note>. Note that if this salt is weak in the "spirit of urine," the generation of disease does not follow, but the urine will exit as a dissolved liquid with the dissolved coagulated matter; this too is from the power of nature. This urine undergoes its separation from the outside, and so it is with the "guests."

Now concerning the external generations of the stone from the first to the last. Then the nature of the stone in all its members. Furthermore, concerning the signs. Afterward, concerning the cure.

# THE ELEVENTH BOOK OF PARAGRAPHS.
## Regarding Pains of the Womb.
### PARAGRAPH I.

<margin>Two diseases of the womb: Retention and Excess.</margin>
**T**he origins of the diseases of the womb are not in the womb itself, nor do they come from that womb, or through it. For every member that depends on others receives harm from those others. Indeed, the pains of the womb are *Retention and Excess of matter*.

In the womb, two diseases are to be noted: Retention <note>the holding back of fluids</note> and Excess. The menstruation <note>original: "menstruum"</note> is the excrement of the womb. Now, the womb is nourished by the flesh of the human and by all the limbs, not from food and drink. Once every month, the womb receives its nourishment from all the limbs, and then it expels its excrements; at which time women feel pains in the back, some feel "gnawing" in the upper stomach <note>original: "praecordiorum erosiones"</note>, some a headache, and others a weariness before the period. Retention is not caused by the womb, but rather comes from all parts of the human body, for the womb is nourished by all the members.

<margin>The womb is nourished by all the members.</margin>
### PARAGRAPH II.

**T**he "confluence" of the disease of Retention or Excess descends from all parts of the whole body. For the menstrual fluid in the womb is not "menstruum" [in its essence], but rather the *excrement* of the menstruum. From these things follow conjunction, destruction, alteration, conclusion, the mixing of good and bad things, and discoloration, along with similar effects.

Where women feel pain, there is an obstruction <note>original: "oppilatio"</note>, such as in the heart, the gall, and other principal members. And then the menstruation must be provoked through the whole body. "Conjunction" is when the menstrual matter comes from all the members and several diseased parts run together. "Destruction" is when one part breaks and dissolves another. This cannot be observed perfectly <note>original: "ad unguem," literally "to the fingernail"</note>; therefore, the menstruation must be reduced to a "temperament" <note>a balanced state</note>. For then the parts themselves are cured.

### PARAGRAPH III.
#### Regarding the Cure.

**T**he cure of the Womb is twofold: the first is in elixirs; the second is in the <term>orizeum</term> <note>a Paracelsian term for a specific alchemical preparation, likely involving gold or a "resurrected" substance</note>. In the elixirs, the highest "temperament" is this: a thing extracted from its essence into the <term>alcohol of wine</term> <note>highly distilled spirit or ethanol</note> that has been dried. In the second cure,

the "temperament" is this: the body, both in substance and its "essentialized" matter, without extraction—but rather through transmutations from a non-liquid substance into a drinkable medicine, etc. And one temperament is found in pearls through extractions into "alcohol" <note>here meaning a fine powder</note>. Another temperament is in the carnelian stone, and the tempered essence in the "tree of the sea" <note>likely referring to coral</note>. The temperament for pains of the womb is neither hot nor cold, nor should it be; it is neither dissolved, nor a moist coagulation, nor a medicine prepared through "diathesis" <note>disposition or constitution</note>. For everything cold and everything hot is an enemy in the illnesses of women. Likewise, everything dry and everything moist is the worst poison in menstrual retention and excess. Similarly, everything styptic <note>contracting</note>, diaphoretic <note>sweat-inducing</note>, pungent, harsh, bitter, or sweet is an impediment to the health of women. But the cure of the womb must be absolute and free from all these aforementioned qualities, because a "temperament" possesses a free <term>arcanum</term> <note>a secret, powerful healing essence</note> and its own judgment.

<margin>An elixir is most effective in affections of the womb.</margin>
The description of this temperament based on the first cure, the elixirs, is as follows:

> ℞. Take 3 pounds of dried alcohol of wine. Take 10 ounces each of Rosemary flowers <note>original: "Anthos"</note>, Mace, and Lavender. 2 ounces each of Cubebs, Cloves, and Cinnamon. Half an ounce of Mastic. Half a scruple of each kind of Storax. 3 drams of Leopard's bane <note>original: "Doronici"</note>. Reduce this in a sevenfold <term>Alembic</term> <note>a distillation apparatus</note>. Afterward, take 20 gold leaves, and 1.5 drams each of unperforated pearls, garnets, and rubies. Reduce to "digestion" <note>slow heating</note> for one month. Of this oil, take 3 or 4 drops <note>original: "grana"</note> with Malmsey wine, or with marjoram or sage water, administered for three or four days, morning and evening. This elixir is a most noble Arcanum for the retention and excess of the menses; it dissolves and constricts, and drives away the pains of the parts; it removes material "suffocation" and also mineral "precipitation."

<margin>The Arcanum of the entire menstrual nature.</margin>
The second description of the "orizeum" liquor is this:

> ℞. Take 1 ounce of <term>orizeum</term> prepared after the dissolution of honey and salt. Take 6 ounces each of the liquor of Oranges and Pomegranates. Reduce by soaking. Afterward, reduce into a liquid form upon a porphyry marble. The dose is from 7 or 8 drops up to 10 or 12, in spring water for two or three days. This medicine, out of its tempered virtue, dissolves and resolves, constricts and strengthens the womb and the menstruation of the whole body: outside of the womb, it clears the obstructions of its parts and resolves them from the members...

# THE TWELFTH BOOK OF PARAGRAPHS.
## On Toothaches.

### PARAGRAPH I.
#### On the Cause.

<margin>Where does toothache come from?</margin>
**T**oothaches, along with their associated symptoms, occur in the roots of the bone, with the gums and their surrounding regions. There is one "alien" cause of toothache, and another that is "local." The alien cause descends from the regions of the head: and the local cause is the beginning of a roughness or a <term>whitlow-worm</term> <note>original: "panaritij," usually an infection of the finger, but used here to describe a burrowing pain</note>.

Toothache arises from an occurrence, and the beginning of the disease is in the location of the pain. If the tooth is whole and the gums are healthy, it descends from the regions of the head. For the pain is carried through the blood of the small veins that enter the gums; it is nothing but a defect of the blood, even while the tooth remains good. It is impossible for this to be a "flow" from the head. For such a flow would occupy many teeth and invade the whole mouth, from which a <term>squinancy</term> <note>a severe sore throat or tonsillitis</note> would arise. If there were some other flow, it would also damage the gums. Teeth, in their roots, do not admit any disease on their own. <margin>Various causes of toothache.</margin> It can also happen that teeth ache because of ear pain. For the small veins of the ears and teeth are very close together. Just as the whitlow and roughness happen in the finger, so also does toothache. By "whitlow," we understand the "worm" of the fingers, teeth, and ears. The first generation of toothache is when the tooth begins to rot from the sharpness of salt, and it hurts continuously. Afterward, it moves toward the generation of a worm, which gnaws at the tooth with great pain—the tooth in which it was born—and it feeds upon that which is of its own nature. <margin>Every worm produces that from which it comes.</margin> For every worm eats that from which it is born, just as moths eat clothes. However, if the worm feels the air, it dies.

### PARAGRAPH II.
#### On the Cure.

<margin>The physical cure of teeth.</margin>
**The cure of the teeth is twofold: Physical and Surgical.**

**The Physical cure is as follows.**
Take: Tormentil, Stavesacre <note>a species of larkspur used as a topical emetic or pesticide</note>, and Plantain seeds, 1/2 drachm of each.
Outer root of Henbane <note>original: "Iusquiami"</note>, and poppy juice, 1/2 drachm of each. Reduce these into a decoction with vinegar. Let it be used as a warm mouthwash.

In the treatment, one must ensure that a "cleansing" of the blood occurs there, such as the one placed here, if it is applied to the teeth. A similar effect is provided by sharp dock—which is elsewhere called *Oxylapathon* or *Melioca*—if it is cut into little discs, which, when soaked in vinegar, are to be pressed against the teeth: or if the root is crushed more thickly, moistened with vinegar, and applied to the teeth for a quarter of an hour or longer. <margin>The surgical cure of teeth.</margin> In surgical care, the "sinning matter" <note>the harmful substance causing the disease</note> must be removed. Just as if someone wants to kill a roughness or a whitlow, <margin>Sperniolum kills the roughness.</margin> he will achieve it through <term>sperniolum</term> <note>an alchemical preparation often derived from frog spawn, used for cooling inflammations</note>: so it is with the worm in the tooth. For if it rots, it stinks. In this case, a gargle should be made from honey and vinegar: if the mouth is washed with this, the stench vanishes.

# THE THIRTEENTH & FOURTEENTH BOOKS OF PARAGRAPHS.
## On Pains of the Ears and Eyes.

### PARAGRAPH I.
#### On the Cause.

**T**he pain of the ears arises from the cause of the "fourth emunctory" <note>a drainage point for bodily wastes</note> from the regions of the head, arriving with its own deafness, varieties, and joints, according to the anatomy of the lower region, along with the regions of the nose and eyes. The occurrence is from an accident and from the location; because it is from an accident, it descends from "aluminous" <note>aluminum-based or astringent</note> matter: and that which is from the location comes from its own innate fit <note>original: "paroxysmo"</note> with chronic signs, ringing in the ears, and an abscess with pus and discharge, and its other varieties.

In the region of the liver is the place where humors ascend: but this has nothing to do with ear pains. Therefore, it is necessary that the pain comes from an accident or occurrence. <margin>Nothing should be poured into the ear except Tutty.</margin> All recipes that suggest pouring infusions into the ears are wicked and false. For nothing should be poured into the ears unless the recipe is made from <term>Tutty</term> <note>original: "Tutia," a crude form of zinc oxide collected from furnaces</note>. Furthermore, no cure handed down by ancient writers regarding ear pain is useful; they are all erroneous. If the pain comes from the location, it is a pain from aluminous salt.

### SECTION II.

<margin>Tridoma</margin>

**Treatment for ear pain**, one involving cold opening medicines derived from resolved moisture. <note>original: "Sief," a term derived from Arabic for a dry powder or medicated paste used in eye and ear treatments.</note>

<margin>Dry Sief for roughness</margin>

Take 1/2 dram each of the seeds of Henbane, poppy, darnel, and black cumin. 1/2 dram of bull's gall. Camphor liquefied to the weight of all the others. Reduce into a dry Sief.

**On the affections of the eyes.**
The reasoning is similar to that for ear pain. Regarding <term>Scotomia</term> <note>a condition involving dark spots in the vision or dizziness</note> at the root of the eyes, where a cataract must be considered, the specific types of eye diseases should not be put forward [here]. And the aforementioned recipes can also be used and applied to the eyes, just as [a cataract] cannot be removed except by an instrument. Thus, if a film or "nail" <note>original: "unguis," likely referring to a pterygium, a fleshy growth on the eye</note> grows on the eye, it must be plucked out and rooted out by an instrument. Although eye-washes <note>original: "collyria"</note> are sometimes useful.

<margin>Eye-wash for Scotomia</margin>
**Eye-wash for Scotomia and all types of eye conditions.**

Take 1 dram each of white vitriol, split alum, and extinguished Tutia. 6 ounces of Eyebright liquor. 1 and 1/2 drams of ground camphor. Reduce into a liquid substance over a porphyry stone with the separation of the <term>Water Bath</term>.

Eye-washes ought to be "consumptive" <note>meaning they should wear away or reduce excess humors and growths</note>. However, for those whose eyes are red from blood, bean flour should be heated for them and moistened with vinegar, and then the steam is directed into the eyes; for by this, the redness is removed. Also, the less that is poured into the ears or eyes, the more beneficial it is. Eye-washes should not be made from distilled waters and arsenic, etc.

## THEOPHRASTUS’S
# BOOK ON EPIDEMICS.
### CHAPTER I.

<margin>What the plague is</margin>
**THE CAUSE** and origin of Epidemic Abscesses is the plague, which is a disease that afflicts a healthy body, and remains in a healthy body, and is mixed with nothing impure or unhealthy. Even if the body were perhaps not healthy, but were diseased and putrid, or otherwise faulty: nevertheless, these things do not cause the plague; rather, only that which is healthy is the cause for the disease to arrive.

And if a leper is seized by the plague, be certain and persuaded that some member which is healthy brought the plague upon him, and not the diseased member. Judge the same concerning pustules and any kind of <term>cachexia</term> <note>a state of general ill health and wasting of the body</note>.

<margin>The fourfold plague</margin>
**The plague** is a disease arising from the 4 Elements, completing its work in natural bodies, more in some, less in others. But the dominion belongs to one [element]. From this emerges the Starry plague, the Watery plague, the Earthly plague, and the <term>Chaos-like plague</term> <note>original: "Chaosda," likely referring to the atmosphere or the element of air</note>. And yet four infectors are ready at hand.

<margin>The plague falls from without</margin>
**The plague** is an Epidemic disease, brought inside from the outside, without a bodily sign, by a spiritual means, infecting that which struggles against it, namely the heart, liver, and brain. If the plague cannot strike these parts, it strikes those bordering and close to them.

# ON EPIDEMICS

...it occurs, and from where it arises: let him attend to these things.

<margin>The plague agrees with the three first principles.</margin>
The plague is the fruit of the four Elements, and it agrees with sulfur, salt, and Mercury: except, however, for those who contract it from infected people.

<margin>Everything fiery is ignited in a stellar manner from the father of the Yliaster, etc.</margin>
The origin of this "fruit" is this: that the corporeal proceeds from the elementary, and is drawn from the great <term>Yliaster</term> <note>Paracelsus's term for the primeval, chaotic matter or the universal force of nature from which all things are formed</note>. Therefore, the nature of the body emulates the Yliaster and is subjected to it. Whatever is corporally united to it becomes contaminated. From which it follows that whatever is of a fiery nature, begotten from the father of the Yliaster, is ignited in a stellar way; and what is from the earth is seized and infected in an earthly way; and from the air, in an airy way; and from the water, in a watery way. For all bodies are generated from these, and they participate in their nature, health, and disease.

From this comes that force and power, nor can anyone escape the power of the four Elements. Whatever they work through that power, we conceive. First, we arise from them. Second, we move within them. Third, we are regenerated in them. Fourth, they impart and inflict their own nature upon us. For we are inferior to them; indeed, we are their "smoke."

Thus we are brought forth by them and are not at all separated from them. From this it happens that we are also forced to suffer by them. If therefore this could be averted—so that we were not begotten and composed from the Yliaster, but from other things—we could certainly resist that which would harm us. But we are not our own masters; we are the smoke of the four Elements.

But how it happens that a thing placed outside us operates within us—which nevertheless has no material influence or substance of its own, and performs all such things without a body—the reason and cause is this: that our **vital spirit** and the external **Elemental spirit** are one and the same spirit.

<margin>The vital spirit must be diligently weighed by physicians.</margin>
This vital spirit must be industriously considered by you physicians. For the blindness of your Patrons and Princes <note>referring to the academic and political authorities of the medical world</note> has revealed none of these things to you; instead, it has pulled a web and a cataract over them, just as if a <term>white spot</term> <note>original: "albugo," a medical term for a white opacity of the cornea</note> were drawn over the crystalline humor of the eye.

<margin>Vehement rebuke of physicians.</margin>
Weigh the matter industriously. For in this—namely, that the vital spirit produces all diseases—all diseases are comprised. But here I speak at least of the plague; elsewhere I speak of others. And I speak of the plague for this reason most of all: because your authors have not correctly understood the principle of this disease and were utterly ignorant of the plague.

For **Avicenna** says: "the plague etc." **Galen** says otherwise, etc. How can they prove their claims, either by themselves or you with them? For since you consider yourselves excellently skilled in Theory and Physics, and yet you do not know the spirit of life—to whom it is related and by what reason it dwells in the Elements and the body—it becomes clear and plain enough that from your false Theory proceeds an erroneous Practice. Thus, your Theory fits the plague as well as <term>Roland of Halle</term> <note>original: "Rolandus Halensis," likely a proverbial German reference to a poor fit or a mismatched caricature</note>. Take your **Mithridatium** <note>a complex ancient panacea used as an antidote</note>, bring forth your <term>Chebula myrobalans</term> and <term>Turbith</term> <note>standard purgative plants in medieval medicine</note>, and with those, if you can, dig out the eyes of the Elements themselves! Take your **Theriac**, and by disputing, try to conquer the spirit of life outside the body around the fire and burn it! Take all your recipes and thunder them into the midst: and finally see whether the patient has not escaped healthy and safe without your help.

Indeed, I praise the experiments themselves. But those doctors have not at all perceived the forces from which those experiments proceed. On the contrary, they have framed their "experience" so as not to resist the spirit, but to try to conquer it. What do you finally want for yourselves, you physicians of **Montpellier**, **Pavia**, and **Verona**? Of how much importance, I ask, should your whole Theory and your universal commentaries and trifles regarding the plague be held? Now, however, your foundation collapses because of this: that even by your own testimony, one plague is not similar to another; and that what was useful last year performs nothing in this present year; or what is suitable now will be fruitless in the future year. This is truly the <term>Dariadestus</term> disease <note>a Paracelsian term for a disease that changes its form or "transmutes," making standard cures ineffective</note>. Answer, you little scholars, what is this? And do not strike your foot against a stone.

Philosophy has indeed succeeded conveniently to your wish until now. But where Philosophy ends, there at last the true Physician begins and comes forth. But where were you born and begotten, you "professors"? In a cedar tree, I think; no, in a pine, in a fir. And if I knew that your stomachs would not be turned, I would affirm even more clearly that you were born as <term>oak-blocks</term> <note>original: "quernistales," a neologism implying they are as thick-headed as oak trunks</note> in the woods.

Not all things are small which you Italians judge. But I think you are also <term>Bollers</term> <note>likely "Böller," meaning empty braggarts or noisy blockheads</note> who are sent into Germany: and you Germans also, who are planted or grafted into Italian plums and tubers; none of whom, as a whole, is ashamed or loath to write Theories about the plague, yet you do not even have the Yliaster on the tip of your tongue...

<header>MEDICAL FRAGMENTS</header>

You have tasted just enough philosophy to keep <term>Ares</term> <note>original: "Ares"; likely a reference to the Greek god of war, here personified as the "spirit of nature" or the vital force that drives natural processes in Paracelsian thought</note> silent. O you men of Doctorates in your reverend robes! What kind of art is this, that in the time of plague you prescribe **Recipe:** <term>Electuary of Dates</term> <note>original: "Diapheniconis"; a traditional laxative medicine made from dates</note> and **Recipe:** <term>Good Theriac</term> <note>original: "Theriacæ bonæ"; a famous and ancient "all-in-one" antidote containing dozens of ingredients, including opium and viper flesh</note>, saying that these things were useful a year ago, even a decade ago, and therefore it must be that they are useful now? To be sure, those who educated you—Galen, Avicenna, and Rhazes—taught you such things. If they were truly considered fit to write about diseases and medicines, then even the <term>Rhipean and Hercynian mountains</term> <note>Legendary mountain ranges of the ancient world; the Hercynian forest was a vast, wild woodland in ancient Germany</note> would produce many such men today alongside their fir cones.

Remove, at last, the <term>dodder</term> <note>original: "cuscutam"; a parasitic weed. Here used metaphorically for something choking the physicians' speech or understanding</note> from your throats, and take the cataracts from your eyes, and clear the "fool" out of your <term>dura mater</term> <note>The tough outermost membrane enveloping the brain; the author suggests they are "fools in the brain"</note>. First, establish the Philosopher within yourselves, then plant the Physician, and guard yourselves lest the nettle and the <term>Spanish fly</term> <note>original: "cantharides"; a toxic beetle used in traditional medicine to cause blistering, here used to describe irritation or bad medicine</note> leave scars upon you. Beat your "head-veins" as your education dictates, so that you may be freed from frenzy, lest Madness or <term>Stentor</term> <note>A Greek herald in the Iliad known for his incredibly loud voice; here suggesting a loud-mouthed but empty shouting</note> take hold of you: you breeched Italians, and swollen Frenchmen—or should I say long-haired ones—and even you "proud ones" of Germany.

# *Other Fragments on the Plague follow, collected from his own handwritten notes.*

\* Many things are required for this proof. Let them be of this kind: yet this much remains, that at least he should have the art in writing. To be sure, those things have been written down which bring us no benefit. That which was going to be useful has been omitted. What, therefore, can I lose in his writings when no pearl is present? Surely fortune did not wish to throw them to the swine. I have been forced and led by these things so that henceforth I care for no writings, whether of Philosophy, or Astronomy, or experiments, or Auguries, or <term>Geomancy, Necromancy, or Pyromancy</term> <note>Various forms of divination using the earth, the dead, or fire</note>; instead, I shall cling only to the <term>Light of Nature</term> <note>A central Paracelsian concept: the innate wisdom found in the natural world and the human heart, rather than in books or scholastic tradition</note> and hand myself over to it, just as all the monuments of the ancients and moderns alike persuade us that this alone is to be trusted. Although few colleagues here offer themselves who are skilled in the light of nature. Perhaps, however, that which is now green will burst forth more fully in the course of time. 

But as for all the things the others have and bring forward, put them back in their place, Reader. Experience, judge, prove, and do not offer yourself as a slave—not to the instruction of teachers, nor to the information of pharmacists, nor to the experiments of <term>Rhazes</term> <note>A famous Persian physician (c. 865–925) whose works were standard in medieval medical schools</note>, nor to the theory of <term>Galen</term> <note>The 2nd-century Greek physician whose theories of the four humors dominated medicine for over a millennium</note>. For from all of these, what good thing, I ask, can you finally gather? Not a single thing. For they themselves are worthless and of no account. 

The reason is this: if some sick person is healed by you, is the thanks given to you? And you yourselves assert that you performed it. Now, your Masters are lying. For you performed it from your own self; therefore you also assign this honor to yourself, not to Avicenna, not to Galen, not to Hippocrates. And rightly so! For you did not receive those things from them. Perhaps you learned them from some old woman. Therefore you do rightly.

See, Reader, this is the reason why I am a diligent exhorter to you. Compare and consider one thing with another, and do not be so headlong in writing. Ignore those who do not perform signs <note>i.e., those who cannot perform actual cures</note>. Nor should you pay attention to those vain characters of the bath-keepers. For what do they bring and plant but leeks and onions? For all these things are not medicine, but hats woven from straw, which do not hold water at all but let it pass through. Fix your eyes on the true foundation of Medicine, if you are going to do anything honest. But if you are going to do poorly, keep your old ways and follow your <term>freshmen</term> <note>original: "Beanos"; a term for new university students, often used mockingly to mean naive or uninitiated "know-it-alls"</note>, from whom no fewer Canons are chosen than from the learned themselves. How well the common crowd judges that! You judge, prove, assess, read, and delay nothing. If you nourish any specific or accustomed evils, throw them away with the lice, and show yourself a student. Farewell.

<margin>The cause of the plague. What it is. The method of prognosticating.</margin>
What is it that Bruno, Garlandius, Rhazes, Galen, and Anshelmus write? Let them not move you so. No foundation is present; it is pure, unadulterated lying, whatever they say, etc.

<page-num>513</page-num>
<header>ON THE PLAGUE.</header>

Location. <term>Limbus</term> <note>original: "Limbus"; in Paracelsian philosophy, this refers to the "Great Mystery" or the primal matter from which all things were created—the reservoir of the elements.</note>.
**Signs. From whence the cause.**
Declaration of the place.
The reason why it seeks those specific parts: it is like lightning.

### I.
That the region of the ear is the total containment of the plague.
That the plague is a wound and a pain of the brain and the heart, like the inflammation of a physical wound.
**Therefore, no traditional medicine is of use.**

### II.
That wrath, envy, gluttony, lust, etc., are the cohort of the planets set against the people: therefore come the pustules, and therefore the plagues, arising from Venus or from Mars <note>In medical astrology, specific planets were thought to govern certain sins and their resulting physical ailments.</note>.
That any prognostication [prediction] has its origin not from the planets themselves, but from wrath. Therefore, he who knows that envy, wrath, or lust is about to come, knows how to prophesy about the manner of the disease like a prophet—namely, by observing the generations made in the planets. That man is a true Astronomer.
What power, then, is assigned to the planets, O you foolish Astronomers, since they do nothing without our own merit or cause?
Therefore David and Jesus spoke from the nature of man: the star [of Bethlehem] arose from the same case; the flood, etc., occurred because wrath was growing in the times of the New Testament, because the "stars of the flood" were born. And thus Christ spoke of false prophets in *Matthew 24.*
Therefore, this must be judged concerning the plague: that from the wrath of the planets, a constellation of sin arises in the planets themselves, and when it grows to its end and reaches its "autumn," it then yields its fruit—which is the "smoke" of the plague, the pustules, famine, pestilence, and so on.
Otherwise, no Astronomer can judge such matters, except when the Father is angry, by observing the innate rod of punishment: he declares this rod.

<margin>I.</margin>
It occupies the whole body, just like rain. But nothing receives it except this part alone: just as a clod of earth alone absorbs water, while a rock does not.
No membranes are infected.
Just as water seeks the earth, not the rock.
Lightning seeks wood.
Dew seeks grass.

<margin>II.</margin>
Manna and leaves each have their own specific parts. Likewise, the plague has its own "earth," etc.; the other part is the "rock" [which does not absorb it].
Here is the <term>Microcosm</term> <note>The "Little World"—the human being seen as a reflection of the entire universe (the Macrocosm).</note>, etc.

In summary, you ought to attack Mars <note>The planet associated with heat, iron, and aggression.</note> and overcome him at least; in this way, you will drive out the plague. Likewise, why is the <term>Sapphire</term> used from the outside? Because it is the contrary of Mars. Who will expel Mars, except the one who brings an "eclipse" to him—namely, through medicine and disease?

## Note on the Signs.

The "smoke" comes from the <term>Limbus</term>. The Limbus is the whole of creation, namely the four Elements and all animals. Therefore, in a time when there are many worms, the plague is also there. Likewise fish, eclipses of the Sun and Moon, are the "matter" of the plague. The plague grows for many years before it strikes: then it moves through everything, and everything that is "signed" [destined] smokes; the touch occurs where it wills.
And so, very often, those who flee before the appointed time escape: just as a tree that is transplanted into another soil withers, so does the plague in the body. For if you wish to know the location, it is thus: the body of a man and the place where he happens to be is the "earth" of the plague, like a garden, etc.
In the same year that the plague dominates and is generated, pearls and garnets are also generated in the mountains, and there the minerals overflow.
Why is the plague in these three locations? As for the rest, why is it not in the brain, or the ears, etc.? Therefore, where there is an <term>emunctorium</term> <note>original: "emunctórium"; a term for the body's natural drainage points or organs that filter out waste, such as the lymph nodes.</note> of sweat, there is the center of the plague as it exits—that is, the drainage point, etc., because under the ear, under the armpits, etc., there are certain drainage points for sweat. The pores are not the drainage point for sweat, but these specific parts are, because there is a twofold sweat: <term>stercoral</term> [fecal] sweat and pressed-out sweat. The "body" of the plague is found in the stercoral sweat. Therefore, all medicines are of this kind of sweat. The ears are the drainage point of the brain; the drainage points of the veins are in their own parts. Likewise the <term>English Sweat</term> <note>original: "sudor Anglicus"; a mysterious and highly contagious disease that struck England and later Europe in several outbreaks during the 15th and 16th centuries.</note> is a stercoral sweat. But I shall discuss this more fully in the *Archidoxis* <note>One of Paracelsus's most famous works, "Archidoxis magica," dealing with the occult and chemical secrets of medicine.</note>.

->*Why the redness,*<-
->*Why the abscess,*<-
->*Why, etc.*<-

Item, note: there are six distinct drainage points, segregated from one another, in their proper anatomy.
The redness is <term>Arsenical</term> sweat; it sets fire to the flesh and the location of the flesh, like a corrosive. Therefore, the abscess and the redness differ from pure Arsenic because of the location, nature, and alteration of the Elements—as a fish differs from meat, or a stone from wood, though both are the matter of a structure. In the same way, these minerals differ: man is a corporeal Element, and the earth is a corporeal Element, and thus are their offspring.
1. *Chapter on Sweats.*
2. *Chapter on the Drainage Points of Sweats.*
Likewise, how God gives disease...

...to everyone according to their acts. Acts are according to their desire; thus pustules arise, and thus the plague from envy on account of "mine and thine." Likewise, and so it is for other diseases. Likewise concerning pleurisy.

<note>original: "invidior humana gens... furor pestis domitat eos."</note> Note: The more envious the human race is, the more the fury of the plague subdues them.

Note: Envy is the cause of such diseases. The lust of many is the cause of plague; envy is joined with higher things; envy kills, poisons, etc.

Note: There is an Arsenical sweat, that is, an eschar-forming <note>A sweat that produces a dry crust or scab on the skin, typical of plague sores.</note> one: but there is a sweat which putrefies, that is, it strangles, just as smoke does to cheese. Thus that sweat is like smoke, and whatever it touches, it destroys, as if it were a venom that cannot be contained. Therefore it putrefies; therefore an opening is needed so that the smoke may exit. The cure is the attraction of a good <term>attractive</term> <note>A remedy designed to draw out poisons or "humors" from the body.</note>.

### *Another Schedule.*

**T**o rightly understand the nature of the plague—how it falls upon us from above—we must know the nature of the <term>Basilisk</term> <note>In alchemy and folklore, a serpent-king that kills with its gaze; Paracelsus uses it here to explain how "poisonous" celestial influences can infect a person instantly.</note>. Such as the nature of this creature is, so also is the nature of the Planets which we look toward. The Basilisk is cooked and born against nature, from the most unfit matter, beyond all natural operation. So too is the plague generated, and from our heart—as if from a hen—an egg is laid, which is then hatched by the toads of heaven. In whatever way this animal is produced, in that same way the plague is born. Now indeed this poison remains in those stars, and those stars become and are the Basilisk. That Basilisk retains its nature. For as soon as it looks upon a man, its nature is so poisonous that envy within it, etc. For it is entirely <term>Saturn</term> <note>The planet Saturn was traditionally associated with lead, melancholy, and harmful, restrictive influences.</note>, and a selected essence of Saturn. That envy is so powerful that whatever it looks upon is immediately infected and poisoned, just as one is infected through "menstruous eyes." <note>An early modern belief that a person (traditionally a menstruating woman) could transmit "vapors" or infection through their gaze.</note>

### *Another Schedule.*

**I**ts force rushes headlong and stirred up like lightning, and no one knows where it is carried. And with the same speed that eyes are turned toward someone, so swift is its ray. And just as we know that lightning is nothing in the beginning, yet later grows and is clothed in matter and body, so similarly there is nothing initially in the eyes of the Basilisk. But like lightning, so let this birth be like the birth of lightning. Once it is produced, the lightning strikes men, etc. For it is generated from them. Now indeed lightning is made from <term>sulfur</term>, etc., and passes into a coagulation of sulfur and salt, from which it also receives its impetus, its crash, and its thunder.

### *Another Fragment.*

**T**hus therefore volatile bodies are extracted or produced through their <term>Magnet</term> <note>A spiritual or physical force of attraction that pulls substances toward their source.</note> in their rising, from which they come forth. Afterward, nothing remains in them except the seed, which awaits its maturation so that it may fall. Physicians have carelessly passed over this, and have not understood the origin of this kind of spiritual disease, nor the Magnet of heaven, nor in turn the mature fruits, nor have they judged the return of the disease into the body. Although heaven—on account of the abundance and multitude of such bodies—attracts them voluntarily without digestion and excrement; that is, the "star of wrath" attracts its own wrath, the volatile body, of its own accord. So also the "envious star" and the "beneficent star," which by themselves lead to maturity that generation in man, which all turns into pestilence, and things similar to this.

## CHAPTER I.

<margin>How many genera and species of Tartar.</margin>
**T**here are two genera of Tartar: the genus of Frost, and the genus of the Gemstone from rock. The genus of Frost is twofold: that of Hail and that of the Vine. The genus of the Gemstone is threefold: Collected, Simple, and Divided. All of those, however, are Alabastrine and Marmoreal <note>Like marble.</note>, or Elephantine <note>Like ivory.</note>, and Adamantine <note>Like diamond or hard steel.</note>, also <term>Duelech</term> <note>A specific Paracelsian term for a hard, stony deposit in the body, particularly the bladder.</note> and Magnetic: and they have various locations because the genera are diverse, and there are many within bodies. ...now in the marrow, and in other putrid matters, and in the juice, and in the <term>emunctory</term> <note>Organs or canals that carry off waste, such as the lymph nodes or sweat glands.</note> excretions. And stone-formation or <term>Tartarization</term> <note>Paracelsus's term for the process where the body creates hard, stony deposits, named after the "tartar" crust found in wine barrels.</note> is foreign—that is, rare.

## CHAPTER IX.
**W**hat if it comes from <term>Bitumen</term> <note>Usually a sticky mineral pitch like asphalt; here it refers to a thick, resinous metabolic waste.</note>? What is Bitumen? It is a type of "locust" <note>likely a metaphor for something that swarms or consumes the body</note> of viscosity, from the species of itching, scabies, ancient <term>Podagra</term> <note>Gout of the foot.</note>, <term>Chiragra</term> <note>Gout of the hand.</note>, and arthritis: for it has the nature of Bitumen. But if it is dried out, nothing comes from it except **Tartar**; and every species of Gout is made of this Tartar, as is the "vine" of the teeth <note>dental plaque or calculus</note>, and the coagulated tears of the eyes; it produces hidden signs under the skin of Gout and <term>Lithiasis</term> <note>The formation of stony concretions (stones) in the body.</note>. Regarding these diseases, the "fathers of medicine" <note>Refers to ancient authorities like Galen and Avicenna.</note> have slept, and their successors do not know how to speak of them.

## CHAPTER X.
**A**nd if the generation of these things comes from putrefactions, it must be noted that wherever it takes place, the matter is neither muddy, nor mucous, nor gem-like, nor porous. It is, however, of the specific substance of that place from which it proceeds, which is possible from all parts. But if the liquid putrefies, while the salt does not, the salt will be converted into a congealed mass, and the rest remains with it; following the nature of salt, it establishes a center, coagulates, hardens, and gives birth to unknown diseases. For whatever comes to the bladder passes into the coagulation of a stone. For in the bladder is the power of salt, in which there is a force of coagulating, sometimes even in "guest" parts <note>parts of the body where the substance does not naturally belong</note>. It should be noted that if this salt is weak in the "spirit of urine," the generation of the disease does not follow, but the resolved urine will exit with the resolved coagulate—this too is from the power of nature. This urine undergoes its separation from the outside, and thus it is with the guest parts.

Now concerning the external generations of the "stone" from the first even to the last. Then the nature of the stone in all its members. Furthermore, concerning the signs. Afterward, concerning the cure.

### Another Leaflet.
#### *For Clarification.*

**Tartar** is twofold in its generation: that substantial muddy matter from the gluten of things which is in drinks and in foods. If it is in liquids, its first appearance is as the mud of dregs, and of these stones and materials. If it is in foods, it cannot produce this without liquid.

<margin>The different names of Tartar.</margin>
**Tartar** in milk is called **Cheese**; in the earth **Leffantea** <note>A Paracelsian term for mineral deposits or earthy stones.</note>; in waters **flints**: and there is a difference between these generations and stones.

<margin>The generation of Tartar is twofold.</margin>
The second **Tartar** is in our bodies—in the veins, flesh, intestines, and in other cavities. Therefore it causes constipation and its own generation, as in children and those similar to them. And it must be noted that the generation of Tartar is twofold: from the generation of external things consumed, and secondarily from the generation of its own proper liquid.

<margin>What "Hoarfrost" is.</margin>
The kind called **pruina** <note>original: "pruina," meaning hoarfrost</note> is in the manner of very fine sand, red or white.

<margin>What "Stone-Gems" are.</margin>
**Stone-gems** are granules, like gems that are not transparent, and are round.

<margin>What "Hail" is, etc.</margin>
The **hail** type is when they are not round.
The **vine** type is when it manifests itself by adhering to things.

**Collected** is when there is a plurality.
**Simple** is when the stone is alone.
**Divided** is when both the stone and sand appear.

**Spara** <note>Another Paracelsian term for imperfectly formed matter.</note> is that thing which, not being sufficiently prepared by its nature, is procreated. It is that thing in which there is some "sinning" <note>an impurity or defect</note> element, not separated from the good.

**Resolved** is when it has the substance of water or food within it.

**Coagulated** is when the "sinning" element has been separated from the pure.

# Another Fragment on Tartar.

### Conspectus I. 2.

**T**he nature and variety of things generated from Tartar must be weighed accurately. For the causes of Tartar are undeservedly attributed to other things by some. Therefore, if it is your intention to acquire a true knowledge of tartar, read through and study the following five books, in which is handed down and explained what Tartar is, and what the other thing is in which Tartar is the "father." Although, by the logic of nature, tartar cannot be a father <note>Paracelsus is likely playing with the idea of "generation"—how a waste product like Tartar can "give birth" to a disease state.</note>. In what way does nature contradict dissolution? Just as in nature, what can be the parent of something that is not similar to itself? Therefore, it is necessary that you read and know these five books, to which we here give a beginning, and weigh them with sound judgment. Outside of this, all the labor undertaken by me would be in vain. For whoever is not going to receive this knowledge fully and clearly here, but would rather stand with our adversaries without a foundation: he neither can be called a Physician by right, nor should he be by any logic. For even if those people think they have a full abundance of all things, the greatest wealth of time, and a number of followers and sycophants more crowded than Pompey <note>Gnaeus Pompeius Magnus, the Roman general known for his massive political and military following.</note> himself, and an infinite harvest of friends compared to me: you, however, ought to know that all these things are empty and vain.

<margin>In what things habit changes nature.</margin>
For they resist and struggle against that nature, wishing to restrain it and drive it into snares by "habit": being persuaded, no doubt, that because habit changes nature, it has therefore already changed and tamed itself as well. But you, see the difference. For that proverb concerns at least food and drink; this, however, does not pertain only to food and drink, but is of such importance that nature will never suffer herself to be overwhelmed and outpaced by habit, just as she will not be by the sects of physicians and their innumerable accomplices. Nature surely wishes either to be known and investigated most deeply, or the sick person must perish along with the disease. For this reason, I diligently exhort you to finally desist from your trifles and judge the matter itself from its foundation hereafter: as that very thing which is required and demanded of you by the oath of faithful Physicians.

### Conspectus I. 3.

<margin>Reproof of the Physician.</margin>
**I**s it not permitted for anyone to show the way to another? Why then not here also? Especially since, in such intricate diseases, so many errors and evasions have broken in until now, which you tooth and nail <note>original: *mordicus*</note> nonetheless defend. No doubt, when discussing the origin of fevers, you say they are born from humors, qualities, etc. On the contrary, I boldly assert that unless Tartar exists, no fevers would ever arise.

<margin>Great amounts of Tartar are the cause of fevers.</margin>
Know, therefore, that Quartan <note>A fever that recurs every fourth day, traditionally associated with "black bile."</note> fevers are generated from Tartar-Must <note>original: *Tartaro Musto*. "Must" refers to unfermented wine-juice; here it suggests a raw, active state of the tartarous waste.</note>, and from the same the timing of fevers is also distinguished, just as a Tertian <note>A fever recurring every third day.</note> returns in its own time, and a Quotidian <note>A fever recurring daily.</note> in its own. You assert that one is Melancholy, another is blood, this is phlegm, that is choler, etc. None of these is true. For the cause and origin of those is that Tartar at this time exceeds its own essence, and is changed, and becomes something other than what it is at other times.

<margin>They cause the origin of the humors.</margin>
From which it follows that other fevers arise from there according to the time and similar things. And if a single Tartar were missing: no fever would ever trouble a man at any time. Therefore, neither Melancholy nor anything else similar ought to be considered. For the properties of fevers are designated by the condition of the Tartar. By this standard, even pleurisies and many other diseases, to be handed down hereafter in their own booklets, must be considered. And therefore, because the body is disposed toward disease, it takes this cause from something else, not itself: that is, those diseases do not emerge from the body as if the causes of fevers or pleurisy etc. were hidden within it; rather, they are brought in from the outside with external things, that is, from Tartar.

<margin>All diseases are brought in from the outside.</margin>
From this, a disease is then generated, which you assign either to the blood, or to Melancholy, or to Choler, etc. Just as wood is set on fire by a fire, and the fire is outside and not in the wood, yet the wood catches it: so also the body catches diseases from the outside, so that not the spleen alone is sick, but the whole body. It is therefore permitted for no one to say that a disease is from the spleen or the blood, but it must be said thus: The whole body is set on fire, and all parts likewise. If therefore, by chance, such <term>Apostemes</term> <note>Abscesses, swellings, or inflammatory growths.</note> are produced in the spleen, liver, etc., from the inflammation: you say those are apostemes from which diseases arise. Let the reading of this longer book not weary you. Attend diligently to how fevers and other similar diseases occur; although nothing solid and certain regarding diseases of this kind has been handed down in the books of the ancients, see it at last.

**R**egarding the constitution of these things, therefore, here we shall only treat those diseases which are induced by no other way than an external one, that is, from Tartar. These diseases are surely of such a kind, which with every...

<margin>
Tartar is the cause of disease, not the humors.
