These things are distinguished in every way and by every reason from all other temperaments and humors. And although blood, for instance, may sometimes boil over and be driven into a rage, the reason for this is no different than the reason for wood. For wood never rages unless fire is within it. Furthermore, if the movements and discharges of the bowels are sometimes varied—such as being green, yellow, and so on—these signs and others like them indicate nothing other than that the cause of these things arises from Tartar, and is Tartar itself. Finally, in diseases of the stomach, liver, kidneys, and bladder, many things appear which you attribute to other causes, but which nevertheless ought to be referred to Tartar alone. To this class also belong <term>Orexis</term> <note>An abnormal or excessive appetite.</note>, Gout, Sciatica, <term>Phthisis</term> <note>A wasting disease, usually pulmonary tuberculosis.</note>, Consumption, and similar ailments. Thus, you wander very far astray with those "humors" of yours that you are always chanting about. Should it not truly seem shameful that you occupy yourselves so lazily with these matters, obstinately imitating only your own masks and hairstyles <note>Paracelsus is mocking the academic physicians for caring more about their professional regalia and status than the truth of nature.</note>, and refusing to investigate the truth of things more deeply, or to reason with yourselves whether those fictions of yours actually fit the facts and are held as valid by everyone without distinction?

<margin>
A rebuke of Physicians.
</margin>
From these things, then, judge for yourselves whether the Physicians of Montpellier and Salerno <note>The most prestigious medical universities in the Middle Ages and Renaissance, which Paracelsus famously despised for their reliance on ancient Greek texts.</note>, along with all their followers, are not deservedly rebuked. For so many centuries they have sweated over their books, and yet they have not even made an attempt to see if their authors would stand with honor or fall if subjected to an examination. Instead, they have lazily and indiscriminately accepted all their words as certain, and have so easily and foully rested their case on the testimony of these authors alone. However, I have not determined to ventilate this matter more accurately here in this preface against them. This will be done in the following books, from which you will come to know their character and habits more closely; and you will see with what great darkness you and your authors have, until now, poured over and entangled medical practice in your Academies.

### Chapter I. 
### What Tartar is.

<margin>
The perpetual reciprocity of things coagulated and resolved.
</margin>
**F**urthermore, so that you may more clearly understand what Tartar is, it takes its beginning in this way: All created things proceed from the **coagulated** <note>In Paracelsian chemistry, "coagulation" refers to the process of a substance becoming solid or taking a specific form.</note>; and afterwards, this coagulated thing must pass away into the **Resolved** <note>The "Resolved" refers to a substance being broken down into its liquid or primal components.</note>. From the Resolved, all procreated things now proceed, whether they are in the form of the Resolved or the Coagulated. Furthermore, this coagulated thing can never be so exquisitely resolved that the resolved part does not strive to return to its own coagulation. Thus you see that salt, if it is resolved in water, returns again into its own coagulation. The reason is the same for all other things. Add to this that no coagulated thing is so thoroughly resolved that it does not retain something of its own nature, through which it may be reduced back into its former shape. Therefore, know that this coagulation is from the Three Primes <note>Paracelsus's fundamental elements: Salt, Sulfur, and Mercury.</note>: S.S.M.S., whichever of these it may finally be. Sulphur is never so perfectly resolved that something of coagulation is not left behind and remains attached to it. The same applies to Salt and Mercury. And one must attend diligently to this coagulation and resolution. For one often prevails over the other, from which that which will be discussed next occurs. Therefore, know concerning all things that they proceed from the Three Primes.

<margin>
All things from the coagulated.
</margin>
Truly, that from which they proceed is coagulated, such as a seed, or the earth, or all fruits, and all growing things. For there is nothing that is not coagulated. However, that coagulation is not the one mentioned here, but is above it and existed before it. For fruits are born from that which was resolved, and are coagulated again. From which it follows that in this place such a generation occurs: if it is not digested a second time (just as it was digested from the first resolution into fruits), then finally that which is not so digested becomes the principle of Tartar.

Diseases from the Three Primes.

It exhibits Mercury, which is liquid; it gives oil, which burns; it leaves behind ash, which is Salt, and in its <term>Archeus</term> <note>The internal "alchemist" or vital force of an organ that separates nutrients from waste.</note> it is a sign.

Fire is the separation there.

**FRAGMENTA MEDICA**

Salt. If you truly understood these kinds of separations, you would also recognize how these things exist distinctly within any substance. You see what the element of fire performs and does: it brings forth ashes, oil, and liquid. 
<margin>The Athanor <note>An Athanor was a self-feeding alchemical furnace designed to maintain a constant heat over long periods.</note> works differently than fire.</margin>
Now, on the other hand, you see that the **Athanor** does the same thing differently; it gives three things, yet produces a different **Mercury**, a different **Sulphur**, and a different **Salt**, which are not at all similar to the others. The stomach, in its own operation, provides another form and method. Regarding these things, let me speak so that you may learn and touch upon the beginning. Penetrate to the very foundation, and do not remain stuck in your lies, with which all your texts and commentaries, and all your schools—of **Salerno**, of **Montpellier**, and all the others (for I except none)—are pregnant.

### CHAPTER III.

Since, therefore, those three things <note>The "Three Primes": Mercury, Sulphur, and Salt, which Paracelsus believed were the building blocks of all matter.</note> must be considered by the Physician in this way, and the separation must also be understood—namely, how they are separated—it is my counsel to hand down in this place at least those things which most closely pertain to the Physician. Such things include the **Stomach**, the **Liver**, and the **Kidneys**, all three of which are types of "fire," and they separate those three primary substances from one another. Leaving aside the other two—namely Mercury and Sulphur—I shall here treat only what becomes of **Tartar**. At the start, I state as a conclusion that everything we consume must be consumed within us, just like wood in a fire. Whatever "fifth essence" <note>The <term>Quintessence</term>: the purest, most medicinal part of a substance, separated from its raw, "dead" form.</note> 
<margin>What Tartar is.</margin>
is in food and drink goes into the body and remains fixed there. The remainder, different from that essence, degenerates into **Tartar**, which is the dregs <note>Original Latin: *faex*. Paracelsus compares bodily waste to the sediment found at the bottom of a wine barrel.</note> about which I spoke in the *Paramirum*. That material is also impure, just as the "fifth essence" is pure. Therefore, you should know that this alone is the **Tartar** which produces and induces grave diseases (the causes and names of which I rightly designate); I shall proceed to explain this in the following chapters. While I do this, I will not set sail for any Eloquence or arrogance, but will propose the matter and the necessity itself. The necessity is this: that the Physician understand these diseases.

->*The end of the Third and the beginning of the Fourth chapter are missing here.*<-

<margin>In how many forms Tartar adheres.</margin>
But to continue our proposal concerning **Tartar**, I want you to know that it adheres in two ways: one like **frost**, and the other like a **gemstone**, in this manner. That which adheres in the form of frost is sometimes like a vine on a tree or a rock, in a clod-like or stony form; sometimes it is collected, like the tartar in wine. Likewise, the gemstone-form of Tartar adheres in both ways: although sometimes it is a stone formed like a gem, yet not colored by its own transparency; sometimes it is like simple, solitary garnets. You must attend entirely to these two kinds, and know that the stomach, liver, and kidneys, and whatever is confined to them, produce these things entirely in their separation. You must henceforth learn more attentively how all these things happen, so that you may keep to the method and goal of your practice, and not always take your own dreams for oracles—dreams which can bring honor and commendation neither to **Avicenna** nor to **Hippocrates**. Though these same trifles have occasionally extricated you from the hands of the executioner! The result is that you have quite conveniently established the pillars of your schools from these buffoons and scoundrels.

<margin>Various species of tartar.</margin>

### CHAPTER V.

These two said kinds of Tartar produce various forms and generations. Some are like **Alabaster** and can be cut. Some resemble **Marble** in color, smoothness, and hardness. Others are **Elephantine** <note>Meaning ivory-like or massive.</note>; some are **Adamantine** <note>Diamond-like or incredibly hard.</note>, sharp and cutting; some are like **Duelech** <note>A specific Paracelsian term for a stony deposit, particularly a painful urinary stone.</note> or pumice, rare and porous like sponges. In a similar way, the locations and regions vary, not only in the kidneys, but also in the bladder, liver, and stomach. These things I write should not seem wonderful to you, unless you wish to sell yourselves as professional fools. Wonder will eventually be quite fitting for those people; many of these deposits are also in the intestines, in the cavities, in the joints, in the brain, and in the principal members, and many other places, as will be said hereafter concerning "innate" tartar. By the highest right, therefore, I can speak of the tartar of the intestines. And if I speak of this, I mean **Colic**. Similarly, if I speak of the tartar of the bladder, I indicate that which you call the "cuckoo's stone" <note>Original: *cuculi calculum*. A colloquial or derogatory term for a bladder stone.</note>. So, if I discourse on "resolved salt," I consider it to be that urine <note>Original: *lotium*.</note> which you have not understood since the age of **Apollo**—where it emerges and arises from, what it is called, and what it might be. Meanwhile, I do not speak of diseases and medicines according to your prescriptions, and I do so for a just cause. For as soon as I realized I had been deceived by you, the authority of all of you began to grow worthless to me. Hence...

# CONCERNING TARTAR.

<margin>
Why the author speaks of diseases in a different manner.
</margin>
I also posit another movement, and now I speak of the **hail of the stomach**, the **vine of the liver**, the **frost of the kidneys**, and the **stone in the spleen**. Thus also I say, etc. <note>Paracelsus uses these weather-related and agricultural metaphors to describe various types of calcifications or stony deposits in the internal organs.</note>

->*The sixth chapter and the beginning of the seventh are missing.*<-

<margin>
There are two salts. Urine is a dissolved salt.
</margin>
If, however, these processes do not occur in the manner they ought, something contrary to nature emerges, particularly regarding salt—which is what I am primarily considering in this book—namely this: There are two salts. One of these three <note>referring to the Three Primes: Salt, Sulphur, and Mercury</note> passes into the urine. For urine is merely salt <term>resolved</term> <note>original: *resolutum*; meaning dissolved or liquefied from a solid state</note> from a coagulated state. Now, salt is also innate to sulphur and mercury, and this salt also generates its own opposite. If it is in the sulphur, it follows this path: that is, in the intestines. If it is in the mercury, it performs that generation in the path of mercury. From this, it follows that <term>tartar</term> <note>original: *tartarus*; Paracelsus used this term, originally referring to the stony sediment in wine barrels, to describe all stony deposits in the body like gout, gallstones, and kidney stones</note> is born in the intestines and the pores. The reason is that mercury passes through the pores. If, therefore, it is coagulated in those middle paths before it becomes sweat, then tartar is deposited in those pores. Similarly, it happens in the urine if it is coagulated. Furthermore, the mineral or bodily state behaves in the same way. If the minerals of salt lie in the blood and turn toward coagulation, the generation of tartar has already occurred. If it is in the pores of the bones, in the marrow, or in other places, then the logic is exactly the same. For these parts too are tasked with their own separation and the duty of purging. If this does not happen, then it also turns into something contrary to nature—that is, into tartar—caused by the prevailing coagulation of the salt. By what veil or foundation, then, will you be able to defend any other theory of generation, when tartar is neither known nor understood by you? For you do not even know what it is, except that you constantly babble nonsense about stones in the bladder and sand in the kidneys, and you boastfully sell yourselves as "Doctors," even though you possess no <term>anatomy</term> <note>Paracelsus means chemical "anatomy"—the understanding of what things are made of—rather than just cutting open bodies</note> of these matters, nor of much graver things. From all your metaphysics and sophistry, you cannot define from what man was made, what he is, or what is within him, yet you sing your trifles everywhere and continually. Therefore, in response to my exhortation, now squeeze your nostrils and blow out the fool living inside you; and henceforth learn such things as will enable you to defend yourselves against me.

### CHAP. VIII.

**L**est I skip over anything untouched, one thing remains to be said that weighs upon your heads regarding **First Matter**. As for **Ultimate Matter**, you should know what it is in this way: Nature has within itself the subtle and the thick. The subtle is without harm. The thick is what I am presenting to you: it is that of which I speak. I have spoken of its beginning; this beginning is also in the end. Therefore, **frost** is also an ultimate matter. You ought to know, however, that between these two, a certain middle state exists: that is the **resolved**. <margin>The "resolved" is the middle state of both matters.</margin> From this, the ultimate returns into its first form. This middle state is sometimes <term>mucilage</term> <note>a thick, gluey substance</note>, sometimes <term>viscosity</term> <note>original: *viscus*; a gummy or sticky fluid</note>, sometimes a liquor, and at times like a juice, depending on how the dissolution occurs. From this follow two ultimate matters: the first—

Blood is the dissolved salt of the body.

**N**ow, furthermore, concerning Tartar—what becomes of it and proceeds from it—pay attention in this chapter. The salt of the body, which I call <term>cruor</term> <note>original: *cruor*; usually referring to thick or clotted blood</note>, is pure dissolved salt. In a long sequence, it adheres throughout the entire body until it reaches the bladder. For thus it is constituted. Some exits through sweat. Regarding this internal dissolved salt, it must be held that it also begets Tartar if a mineral liquor also concurs and they pass into one coagulation. This happens because every mineral liquor comes from coagulated matter, and salt is that which coagulates. <margin>Salt coagulates.</margin> Now, if the conjunction of these two occurs, then these types of tartar also emerge similar to the rest. And regarding Minerals, this is the cause or reason: that man consists in and of all minerals; and as many species as exist outside, just as many exist within. From this, the Physician’s knowledge ought to be drawn: that all diseases arise from these. Provide yourselves with proper instruction against these things. For these four minerals will sweep your "humors" aside and drag your foolishness into the light. ## Chapter II.
### White Gluten.

<margin>Gluten from synovia.</margin>
Now, there remains another type of generation, more serious than all others in terms of hardness and pain: namely, this. **Gluten**, which the old surgeons call <term>synovia</term> <note>original: *synouia*; the lubricating fluid found in joint cavities</note>, is slow-moving and viscous, like the white of an egg. If the matter of salt seizes this fluid and mixes with it, it eventually coagulates into a small stone. This generation happens in the following way: the **Gluten** is not actually made from the matter of a "resolved" or dissolved stone; however, it is a viscous and mucilaginous material from which something similar to stones can be generated. These are not "true" stones, in the sense that they should be called such, but rather something halfway between a stone and <term>bitumen</term> <note>original: *Bitumen*; a naturally occurring petroleum or mineral pitch, used here to describe a sticky, resinous substance</note>. Yet, its coagulation and nature are similar to stones. It forms in no other place except where the gluten lies. From this coagulation arises <term>podagra</term> <note>gout of the feet</note>, <term>chiragra</term> <note>gout of the hands</note>, and <term>genugra</term> <note>gout of the knees</note>, if the salt is locally present in those places where the gluten dwells—though this excludes the inflammation that occurs, which we shall discuss in the chapter on Gout. I touch upon this here only so that you may know to judge it as **Tartar**. The same must likewise be understood regarding sperm: if a generation similar to gluten occurs through the "salt of coagulation," stones similar to the others can be generated in those places where sperm is located. Stones of this kind sometimes dissolve on their own. For their generation is not exactly like that of real stones; hence they may be dissolved like mucilage. All these types, however, are distinguished from one another by their own certain signs, to whose differences you must pay close attention.

## Chapter III.

<margin>Diseases from mucilage.</margin>
Furthermore, there are other defects born from **Tartar** which do not degenerate into a stone or "urinary gravel," but rather into mucilage, a clot, or some other kind of pus. Since these too proceed from Tartar, knowledge of them is necessary. For it frequently happens that this Tartar deposits its dregs in the urinary tracts. These dregs repeatedly give birth to many diseases, all of which are mistaken for "the stone." Those afflicted in this way cannot urinate, because these dregs suppress and intercept the urine. Some urinate blood, because the "digestion" <note>metabolic processing</note> exits prematurely on account of the Tartar. Some pass pus because a clot has putrefied; some excrete sperm because the clots and dregs obstruct its paths. Some suffer pain because of the salt in the clot. Others feel nothing or complain that the limb has become "painless" <note>numb</note> because of those narcotic dregs.

Many salts sometimes converge here, as do many <term>vitriols</term> <note>original: *vitriola*; sulfate minerals, often used in alchemy to describe corrosive or metallic salts</note> and many other things which are generated from these dregs of tartar through their own putrefaction. There is neither a set number nor a foresight for these things, as new forms and species are produced daily. In this place, the <term>Archeus of the kidneys</term> <note>original: *Archeus renum*; in Paracelsian thought, the "Archeus" is the internal artisan or vital force that governs the functions of an organ, acting like an internal chemist</note> must also be recognized. What new things he brings forth and generates daily, we leave to the physician to investigate, who will note and weigh his daily works with private industry. But you "veteran" physicians consider all of this as nothing, because it was not prescribed and published by you. O indeed, you fanatic writers and over-confident deceivers! For that day will come when you students will stand with those masters of yours, just like Cuntzius von Hausen, whom the Devil carried off from your midst. <note>A characteristic Paracelsian insult, referencing a contemporary anecdote of a man supposedly taken by the devil to mock his medical rivals.</note>

**There are three species of Tartar:**
1. **Anotron:** is the material of stone, "moss," the ark, etc., according to how it is generated in its potential state.
2. **Mucilage:** is phlegm that descends from food, in the manner of bitumen <note>meaning a thick, sticky, pitch-like substance.</note>.
3. **Nitre:** is the dross produced during digestion—namely, the excrement.

# BOOK FOUR.
## On Nitreous Tartar.

<margin>What kind of sickness is the motion of nitre.</margin>
The **Motion of Nitre** is a sickness that seizes the body with horror or a cold shiver, lasting until a heat or fever rushes in, typically for several hours. When this fades, the disease pauses until a set day, when it returns in a similar cycle. This continues with the same assault until the underlying matter is consumed.

->Declaration of Names.<-

<margin>Whence the disease of nitre is named.</margin>
The **Motion of Nitre** takes its name from its cause. Just as an earthquake <note>original: *terremotus*; literally "earth-motion."</note> shakes the earth, so this "nitre" shakes the body. The Germans name it after this "shaking" or "shuddering," rather than the cold. For by the same principle that an earthquake occurs, this disease achieves its effect, as will be explained hereafter.

<margin>What kind of disease is a Carbuncle.</margin>
A **Carbuncle** <note>A severe, painful cluster of boils or an abscess, often associated with the plague.</note> is an ailment that attacks first with cold, then with heat; and this heat lasts continuously, with no returning cold. The heat continues until it is finished, leading either to health or to death. Furthermore, an abscess <note>original: *Apostema*.</note> follows it, breaking out in whatever part of the body it may be, whether large or small, ripe or unripe.

<margin>Whence the Carbuncle is named.</margin>
The **Carbuncle** receives its name from heat, and the metaphor is drawn from "coals" <note>original: *carbonibus*; the word carbuncle literally means "little coal."</note>. Just as coals pour forth heat and possess a physical body, so in this disease there is a constant and continuous burning; therefore, a "cold-abscess" breaks out, from which, as if from glowing coals, a perpetual heat is eventually poured out.

<margin>What kind of disease is Flammula.</margin>
**Flammula** <note>Literally "Little Flame"; a Paracelsian term for a specific type of burning, delirious fever.</note> is a disease afflicting the sufferer with both cold and heat, though the heat continuously plagues either the head or other members of the body. It has no abscess or ulcer, yet it causes men to become delirious. It ends sometimes in death, sometimes in a long illness, accompanied by intense burning and weighing down into Mania.

<margin>Whence Flammula is named.</margin>
**Flammula** is named from this continuous heat, as if the body were "flaming" with a perpetual burning, an immoderate heat that afflicts the man's head and casts down the body.

---

Three principal diseases are born from Nitre:
1. **Fevers:** the motion of Nitre.
2. **Abscesses:** the Carbuncle.
3. **Flammula:** the Little Flame.

Under the first disease, other illnesses are included:
1. **Under Fever:** Quotidian, Tertian, and Quartan <note>Fevers that recur every day, every third day, or every fourth day.</note>.
2. **Under Carbuncle:** Anthrax, Plague, Quinsy <note>original: *Synäche*; a severe sore throat or inflammation of the neck.</note>, and Saphyrus <note>A Paracelsian term for a sapphire-colored pustule or eruption.</note>.
3. **Under Flammula:** Burning Fever <note>original: *Causson*; from the Greek for "burning heat."</note> and Inflammation <note>original: *Phlegmon*.</note>.

*Fever proceeds from Nitreous Tartar.*
*The Carbuncle comes from Nitre.*
*The "Little Flame" occupies the Nitre-salt.*

# MEDICAL FRAGMENTS

<margin>What nitre is.</margin>
Nitre is the dung and the corpse of a meager thing or of food. <note>In Paracelsian medicine, "nitre" refers to the salty, metabolic waste products left behind after digestion.</note> And it is from this corpse that putrefaction is born. From this putrefaction, all the aforementioned diseases emerge. Therefore, it quite often happens that in a single house, everyone who has eaten of the same food is seized by the same disease or "nitre," not unlike how putrid air or some other poison infects everyone gathered in the same place and strikes them with an abscess.

<margin>Putrid blood is made from nitre.</margin>
All putrid and corrupt blood arises from nitre. And even if it hasn't all completely rotted yet, it nonetheless putrefies quickly and readily if it is exposed to the sun after being drawn from the body. For it is generated first from the putrefaction of the nitre. However, the harm from this is not as great as it would be if the putrefaction were to begin dominated by the heat of the sun.

To speak briefly, all nitres are like dung. If dung is gathered and piled up, it grows hot. If the mass of dung is large, the heat is retained longer. If it is smaller, it cools down more quickly. The same reasoning applies to fevers: If there is much nitre, the paroxysm <note>A sudden attack or increase in the intensity of a disease.</note> lasts longer. If there is little, it ends more seasonably. Salt-nitre behaves in such a way. It forces and collects smoke until it can find an exit or be consumed. As that vanishes, new smoke is gathered again. And this is repeated until the whole is consumed. This is why some fevers extend to two or three years. And indeed this nitre or dung, which stirs up fevers in a person, sometimes putrefies in one day, sometimes in two, and sometimes every hour—thus generating the daily, tertian, and quartan fevers. <note>Historical terms for fevers that recur every day, every third day, or every fourth day.</note> The paroxysm lasts and is prolonged as long as the trapped vapors remain and do not break out; while they are restrained inside, they wander through the individual members, the hands—

<margin>How the cold in fevers occurs.</margin>
—and the feet, and finally, being dispersed, they contaminate and putrefy the veins. From these dissipated and scattered vapors, everything begins to grow cold. For the cold arises from this: that the nitre shakes out its coldness at the beginning so that it may be freed from it. Once this is done, the heat (or the opposite) gains strength, because the blood is constricted, and thus it is generated due to the bad disposition.

<margin>The location of nitre is the blood.</margin>
The location of nitre is in the blood. Therefore, purgations that evacuate the stomach are appropriate in this disease. And there are certain simples <note>Medicines made from a single herb or ingredient.</note> that attract the nitre out of the blood and into the stomach and bladder.

Nitre in a carbuncle <note>A severe, painful cluster of boils.</note> becomes so hardened and dried out that it cannot putrefy any further or more seriously. This is the difference between fevers and carbuncles. For in fevers, the dung remains putrid; in a carbuncle, it dries out so much that it does not move for more than one paroxysm.

## *From the book on Mucilage.*

<margin>Apoplexy is an obstruction of the lungs by mucilage.</margin>
**A**poplexy or "the drop" <note>original: *gutta*; a historical term for a stroke or sudden loss of consciousness.</note> is in the lung: that is, if the respiratory pipes <note>The bronchi and trachea.</note> are filled by mucilage and are, as it were, suffocated. For then the paroxysm invades, such as a spasm, tetanus, etc., all of which arise from the injured power of the vital nature.

Paralysis occurs if mucilage stuffs the passages of the ligaments: for in this way they lose their motive power and their moisture, in whatever place that happens. Therefore, because the loss of motion and the loss of voice happen so suddenly, the beginning is derived from suffocation.

Similarly, judgment must be made regarding Pleurisy, Gout, and Arthritis. Likewise, such Mucilage is also found in wine. However, there is much mucilage in it, and it is called *Isopus* <note>original: *Isopus*; likely referring to the tartar or dregs of wine.</note>, remaining from burnt wine, etc.

A crisis is the space from the beginning of a disease even unto the end of the disease; it has no increase, peak, or decline, but is the disease having been created and existing in its perfected state. The physician must consider this regarding the patient's illness.)

Crisis is the space of time taken from the beginning—

In historical medicine, this was the day the disease was expected to reach its turning point or "crisis."</note> For the crisis takes its origin at the end of the "digested time." The digested time is that period in which the species of the **Yleiadus** are cleansed of their dregs. <note>Yleiadus: A Paracelsian term for the primordial matter or the elemental "spirit" within substances.</note> The dregs are the beginning of diseases, and the start of the crisis—taken from the excrements of the **Yleiadus**—will appear as the pure **Yleiadus** once the excrements are gone.
<margin>The origin of the crisis is the end of digested time.</margin>

<margin>Arsenical days which are critical.</margin>
The "Arsenical" critical day is the 3rd day in acute cases; the 5th day in very acute cases; and the 7th day in extremely acute cases. <note>Paracelsus categorized diseases by chemical properties; "Arsenical" diseases were sharp, burning, and sudden.</note>

The crisis of an acute Arsenic is at 24 hours; of the acute ones, 15.

The "Mercurial" crisis is on the 4th day: in very acute cases on the 3rd; in extremely acute cases at the 18th hour. For acute Mercury, the 13th hour: for acute ones, the 7th. For "Sulphur," the 10th week; in the middle, the 16th week; at the longest, the 13th week.

Dissolved things: 2, 5, 6.

## On Pleurisy, and the Cure of the Planets.

<margin>What pleurisy is.</margin>
**P**leurisy is a disease trapped within the principal organs, taking its place in those regions through a "Tartarean" obstruction—whether generated by dissolved air or by a bodily substance. <note>"Tartarean" refers to the "tartar" or stony grit Paracelsus believed formed in the body like scale in a kettle, causing blockages.</note> It receives its material from the Ogertine salt, along with types of "plague" and "prunella." These are its signs: trembling with alternating cold and heat without plurality, discoloration of the face, weakness of the limbs, a final and ascending heat, and stabbing pains in the head, the sides, the midriff, and the chest.
<margin>Signs of pleurisy.</margin>

<margin>No diet is to be observed in pleurisy. The cure is twofold.</margin>
The location of the stabbing and the punctures indicates the affected organ. No specific diet is to be observed in this disease; rather, medicine is preferred over diet. Its cure is twofold: from Tartar and from Salt-stone. Of the types of Tartar, these are the ones: Take 1 pound of Tartar, 1/2 pound of "water of life" <note>aqua vitae: distilled alcohol or brandy.</note>, and 3 drachms of Juniper berries. Reduce this into a liquid. The dose of this water is 6 drachms to 1 ounce, taken in Malmsey wine or a good wine.

Another: Take 1 pound of this reduction, 4 drachms of select clear Mummy <note>Mumia: a medicinal preparation made from preserved or bituminous remains, used as a panacea.</note> well-ground, and 1/2 ounce each of malt-water and wormwood water. Mix them. The dose is 1 to 2 drachms, morning and evening, or according to the distillation.

Another: Take 6 ounces of this mixture, 1/2 drachm of "stone-water" (which is made of three salts), and 1 drachm each of wormwood and marjoram waters. Mix them; the dose is 1/2 [unit] in good waters or wine.

Another: Take 1 drachm of "Sileti" <note>Possibly a salt from Sile/Silesia.</note>, 1/2 drachm of Tartar. Reduce the mixture with 2 drachms of mummy. The dose is 1 drachm in wine or lemon balm water.

the aforementioned cure is valid for all types of pleurisy, except for pleurisy of the heart, where this description should be administered:

<margin>Remedy for pleurisy of the heart.</margin>
Take 1 drachm of pure Laudanum <note>In Paracelsus's time, "Laudanum" was a secret, potent pill often containing opium, gold, and crushed pearls.</note>, 5 grains of musk, and 6 grains of Camphor. Let pills be made with "spicula" water. The dose is 6 or 7 grains.

Also, a common ointment for types of pleurisy:
<margin>Ointment of marmots against pleurisy.</margin>
Take 1 ounce of marmot fat, 1/2 drachm of sweet almond oil, and 1 drachm each of chamomile oil and rose oil. Mix them; let a soft ointment be made over a fire with a little wax.

## On Prunella.

<margin>What Prunella is.</margin>
**P**runella is a primary suffering with its own "fit" or paroxysm, existing in heats. For it proceeds outside of its region because of the thinness of "vitriolated salt" escaping its shell. <note>Prunella (or "the sloe") was a term for "thrush" or a burning throat infection, likened here to the corrosive nature of vitriol (sulfuric acid/sulfates).</note> It is a species of pleurisy and plague; its heat is a vitriolated heat and a corrosive burning.

<margin>Signs of Prunella.</margin>
The signs appear at the end of the disease: heat of the throat with redness or blackness, a scorched humor and liquid upon the tongue with cracks in the organ, great weakness of the body, thirst, headache, and vehement distress of the chest and the affected part.

<margin>Cure for Prunella.</margin>
Its cure is the same as in the plague. If, however, the plague cure does not remove the disease:
Take 1 pound of "Prunella waters" <note>Likely water distilled from Self-heal (Prunella vulgaris) or a chemical preparation.</note> and 1/2 drachm of pure Laudanum.
Let a gargle be made to cleanse the tongue, and drink a draught of it several times a day. Whatever this description does not expel, other remedies will also be useless.

## On Dropsy.

<margin>What Dropsy is.</margin>
**H**ydrops <note>Dropsy: an old term for edema or swelling caused by fluid retention.</note> is a suffering arising from the regions of the liver, born from an aluminous Tartar beneath the first body. This occurs through the dissolution of its own nature and subsequently through the "mineral spirit" of this organ, which is one of the seven spirits of the whole body. This spirit is dissolved in its parts, and then it is a dropsy of the liver regions throughout the whole body. Thus also in other principal organs, the generation of dropsy occurs in this manner. Furthermore, there are seven types, divided according to the mineral...

### Chapter: On Fevers of the Liver.

<margin>
What a liver fever is.
</margin>
**FEVER** is an obstructed heat, generated from putrefied dregs <note>original: "fæcibus," the metabolic waste or "tartar" within the body's systems.</note> in the regions of the liver. For that obstruction is sometimes in the whole region, and sometimes specifically according to the location. If it is of the whole part, then the swelling is great and long-lasting until it is cleared; the heat travels to the limbs, and after it has been cleared, the body's heat is present. But if it is local, then the tremor quickly turns into heat. That obstruction creates its own blockage, and through the tremor, it breaks and clears—sometimes all obstructions, sometimes only some. If it performs a total clearing, then the fever is easier to bear; if not, it is more severe and is undoubtedly the preparation for the generation of some disease, because the trapped matter causes offense and a change in itself.

One must look into these obstructions: for if the dregs have not been resolved after the tremor, then an increase in these obstructions is to be feared, leading to a long-lasting disease and a future abscess, even locust-like swellings <note>original: "tumorem locustarum," likely referring to the shape or grouping of the swellings.</note> of the body reaching to the center, and stinging pains. For the paroxysm comes from the matter of the dregs, according to its own temporal digestion, until it delivers itself from the obstructions into the total heat, on account of the veins being infected by these spirits exiting after the tremor. Sometimes there is also a fever without obstruction, but without a tremor, when the digestion has an exit: yet there is a small paroxysm with a little heat. This is the smallest species of fever and the most healthful in itself.

<margin>
Signs of liver fever.

It often happens that a first fever, namely of the stomach, is generated; then a second fever follows, namely of the liver.

Fevers composed from the stomach and liver.

## On the region of the KIDNEYS.

<margin>What the region of the kidneys is.</margin>
The region of the Kidneys extends from the first filtrations of the urine down to the final emunctory <note>An organ or canal that carries off waste.</note> of the resolved salt; also, the parts inclining toward the center are of the regions of the Kidneys.

<margin>What the ailments of the kidneys are.</margin>
The ailments of the kidneys are these: Tartar of the urine, or Tartar separated from the spirits of the urine to its own place—namely, the orifice of the kidneys and the bladder; Diabetes; "cheese," or curdled milk. Likewise, ailments involving pus, discharge, and their associated ulcerations.

## On Diabetes.

<margin>What Diabetes is.</margin>
**T**he diabetic passion is a dry urinary salt within the substance of the kidneys. This salt descends from the urine into the middle center of this principal member. This salt is fixed, chronic, and remains until the end of life.

<margin>Signs of Diabetes.</margin>
Its signs: abundant thirst without rest, pains in the spine, swelling of the feet, strong sexual urge <note>original: "coitúſque fortis"; historically, some physicians noted priapism or increased libido in early stages of certain urinary disorders.</note>, and in the end, leading to death.

<margin>Cure of Diabetes.</margin>
Its cure lies in the salt and not in the kidneys themselves, through anodynes <note>Pain-relieving medicines.</note>; otherwise, the salt does not accept a cure.

This is the anodyne: Take one ounce each of the liquor of poppy and henbane; half a dram of darnel, etc.

Likewise another: Take coffee <note>original: "Caphæ"; likely referring to a preparation of coffee or a similar bean, though its use in this era's Latin texts is sometimes debated.</note>, rose water, plantain, and nightshade; the kidneys are thus cured.

Likewise another: Take a mixture, etc.

## On Curdled Milk.

**C**urdled milk <note>original: "Lac cafeato"; referring to a milky or cloudy discharge in the urine resembling curds.</note> receives its matter from the hemorrhoids and the substance [of the kidneys]. The substance of the kidneys receives its own balsam.

The first essential liquor, placed and separated by the digestive power, is milky and is "natural milk." This milk is the first stage in the digestion of the kidneys; blood is the second; the coagulated substance is the third.

Regarding this "milk," however, something must be noted for our present purpose.

Truly, this milk has the nature of milk and undergoes the separation of milk; from this follows the sour, coagulated curd. *Nustum* <margin>What Nustum is.</margin>—which is fat, namely butter—whey, and other dairy-like products <note>The author is using the analogy of milk curdling to explain how fluids in the kidney break down into different waste products.</note>.

The ailments of this "milk" are these: discharge in place of milk, pus in place of *mustum* <note>Unfermented grape juice, here used as a biological analogy.</note>, oily fat floating on the surface (taken for the fat of the kidneys), and the "white beet" <note>original: "bletæ albæ"; likely referring to a pale, thick sediment in the urine.</note> urine.

The cure for discharge, the cure for pus, the cure for fat, the cure for "white beet."

## On Fevers from the Kidneys.

**F**evers from the kidneys have their beginning in the dregs of Tartar due to digestion. Otherwise, where there is no time for digestion, the fever finds its matter. For every obstruction causes a motion of the whole body, and a consequent increase in bodily heat because of vapors passing through all the pores.

The ancients once called this passion "sciatica," others "erratic fever," others the "motion of the stone" or its paroxysm, others the "passage of sand," etc.

## On Fevers in General.

<margin>What fever is.</margin>
**F**ever is a general paroxysmal disease arising from the obstruction of the whole body. There are many kinds of fevers; namely, the simple cause, which is obstruction, whether partial or universal.

*Duelech* <note>A specific Paracelsian term for a painful, stony accretion in the body, particularly the bladder.</note> is a spongy stone.

Received, however, from a lump or a small stone, because the nature of the microcosm <note>The human body, viewed as a miniature reflection of the universe.</note> is the same as that of the mothers [the macrocosmic elements].

<margin>Cruor is salt cast out.</margin>
*Slime* <note>original: "Viscus"</note> of the second generation is the *cruor* <note>Thickened or clotted blood/waste.</note> which descends from salts. For *cruor* is salt that has been carried, that is, rejected, by the first salt. *Perverse bitumen* is a liquor perversely digested, that is, an uncooked liquor which descends under the slime from its own nutriments. *Proper nutriments* are the vital ones. *Congluten* or *conglutinum* is that which, during putrefaction, descends into a colored glue from the proper substance of both bodies—namely, the substantial and the vital.

The liquor of salt sustains the body and is a balsam; when it is lacking, leprosy follows. The substantial body is sustained by the elemental. The vital part has its own proper nutriment. <margin>Diabetes, a disease of the kidneys.</margin>

In Chapter III.

### FOURTH TRACTATE.

<margin>What the "Spara" force is.</margin>
In Chapter I. <term>Spara</term> <gloss>a specific mineralizing force</gloss> is a mineral power from <term>Ilech</term> <gloss>the prime substance of minerals</gloss>, the first substance from the First Being; it is the first part of the four Elements. These elemental parts are the "greater minerals." There are four types of minerals: Essential, Corporeal, Substantial, and Formal. Man is a "Fifth Being" <note>a Quintessence</note>; he is not, as some believe, subject to the heavens, but is stronger than them, even though the same judgment can be made through physiognomy and the stars. A rule of diet should only be prescribed to those who have contracted diseases through intemperance. Urine with lemon-colored pus will provide a judgment of internal tartar. Transparent urine like "burning wine" <note>alcohol or brandy</note> demonstrates an internal and incurable Tartar. There are other signs of internal tartar, such as pressure in the stomach, wasting <note>original: "phthisis"</note>, etc. Natural humors have opposing salts: for example, blood has vitriolated salt, and bile has alum. From these humors, mineral forces, salts, alum, lime, and vitriol, Tartar is made. From pure salt, without the spirits of other salts, internal tartar is born. Phlegm does not enter the veins, but rather dissolved salt. The "Square Physician" <note>original: "Quadratus Medicus"; likely a reference to a perfectly balanced or ideal practitioner</note> finds hailstones in the arms and muscles; wasting (that is, a drying up) is a blockage caused by Tartar. Some, like the Torturer of Vimen <note>historical reference unclear</note>, thought that those suffering from wasting should live in humid places.

<margin>There are four types of minerals.</margin>
<margin>Man is a [quintessential] Being.</margin>
<margin>The Square Physician, etc.</margin>

In Chapter II. Rich deposits of Tartar have their coagulation from the salts of the ore. Salt in this generation is an Elemental and watery "accident," a humoral liquid, and <term>Idestrum</term> <gloss>the spiritual or "star" essence of a substance</gloss>. However, Idestrum does not exist without a compound. The compound is made of minerals through four forms. Idestrum is a humoral, natural, and mineral conjunction.

<margin>Idestrum is not without a compound. What Idestrum is.</margin>
<margin>What Balsam is.</margin>
The stickiness of "glue" <note>original: "gluten"; a viscous biological fluid</note> is a mineral resin, just as turpentine is the resin of its tree. It differs from balsam because it is neither salty, nor bitter, nor sweet. Pain exists in "non-salty glue," but it is caused by a salty humor; however, this saltiness is acidic. Non-salty glue is a "sweet repercussive" against the nutritive liquid, specifically when the "repercussive salt" (which is acidic) coagulates the "sweet glue" of that area, because glue is a nutritive humor. Those things that generate much salt must be observed in the diet, as must those that generate white glue. Glue is found where the ligaments are. Likewise, if glue is poured out from its proper place, it also generates pain. Therefore, an excessive diet can be the cause. If Tartar is in the spine, particularly in the lowest part, it harms everything below it, because the vital spirit cannot defend it; and this spirit is a substance, and not so subtle as some believe. Vomiting, besides indicating Tartar, can also signify gout.

<margin>The 4 centers of disease, and what they are.</margin>
<margin>The locations of the "Sperm."</margin>
<margin>What "Sperm" is.</margin>
In Chapter III. There are four centers: two at the elbows, others at the knees, and the spine has one; thus there are centers of diseases in other parts. The locations of the "Sperm" <note>used here not just for reproductive seed, but for a formative biological "starting liquid"</note> are where the glue is, where the principal members are, where the minerals are, and where the humors and liquids are. For Sperm is the mineral root of the roots of the humors, poured through the whole body. Nothing comes from "crystalline sperm," but Tartar is generated from the "first sperm." All corruption is the generation of a second salt. The seed is in the center of the sperm. The cure for "Diabolical" and "Tartaric" diseases is the same. Putrefied urine is the first sign of leprosy. Urine that tastes like orris root indicates the presence of vitriol, which is bad because it indicates putrefied Tartar; that which tastes like meat broth [indicates] digestion...

<header>COMMENTARIES ON THE BOOKS</header>

...indicates bad digestion, and contains signs of putrefied Tartar and future leprosy.

### FIFTH TREATISE.

<margin>Causes of abolished urination.</margin>
In Chapter I: regarding those who cannot urinate. Their urine and sperm have been converted into pus and discharge <note>original: "faniem"; a thin, greenish or bloody fluid from a wound</note>; there is no expulsive force in either pus or discharge.

<margin>Cause of bloody urination.</margin>
Those who urinate blood are those whose stomach, liver, and kidneys transmit undigested matter along with the "colors of first things" to the bladder. Those who urinate with difficulty experience a burning heat caused by salt and sulfur, since these are made of contrary elements. Those whose expulsive powers—both of the urine and the passages—become numbed will emit urine against their will. Narcotics are scorched substances, and the digestion of innate discharge is either incurable or very difficult to cure. The digestive power of the kidneys is restored only with great difficulty. *Anodynus* <note>Anodyne</note> is a narcotic power.

<margin>What is "Pufta."</margin>
<margin>What cheese consists of.</margin>
In Chapter II: Cheese is composed of Mercurial sulfur, and it receives its coagulation from "salt of the bolus" <note>original: "fale de bolo"; a medicinal clay or earth</note>—that is, from a mineral—and its color and form from mercurial elements. Everything viscous proceeds from white sulfur.

<margin>What is "Agresten."</margin>
Agresten <note>A Paracelsian term for the tartaric acidity found in unripe fruits or mineral salts</note> is a sharp, stony Tartar. Indeed, all sourness proceeds from salts of a vitriolated mineral mixed with alums. "Alkalized Rivers" refers to water drawn through the lime of the earth, and the elements of rainwater. "Lubricated water" is mucilaginous water, such as the separated whey of must, juice, and every concoction like claret, licorice potions, sugar mixtures, or barley-water. "Pontic wines" are those that have flakes and dregs. The origin of a river or water is from the "first Ilech" <note>original: "primo Ilech"; a Paracelsian term for the first unformed state of matter</note>, not in the location of the spring. Boiling is a preparation that occurs without the digestion of the stomach; digestion follows separation, first in the stomach, then the liver, then the kidneys. The power of separation must be strengthened first. Rainwater comes from the element of fire; the sun does not attract it, as some believe.

### On the Second Book.

<margin>Things that produce "Orexis."</margin>
In Chapter I: *Orexis* <note>original: "Orexin"; generally meaning appetite, but here referring to a burning, painful hunger or heartburn</note> is generated by wine, salt-cured meat, wild game, birds, fish, etc. Some feel it in the morning when fasting; others after taking food, and this is from lime; others when going to bed. Some feel a continuous pain, and this happens from the dissolving of Tartar which, sticking even to the throat, generates a violent *orexis*, and the sensation there becomes sharper.

<margin>Things that remove "Orexis."</margin>
<margin>What is "Bread of the Sower."</margin>
Where the pain is not mitigated by clay <note>original: "bolo"</note> or chalk, it is a sign of sharp Tartar. A vapor ascending from the bottom to the throat is cured by "bread of the sower"—that is, St. John's bread <note>Carob</note>—repeated until the pain ceases. If, however, it lurks in the bottom of the stomach near the "cleansing-places" <note>original: "emunctoria"; organs that carry off waste</note>, then chalk or "sealed earth" <note>Terra sigillata; a medicinal clay</note> also removes it. However, observe this: the chalk should not be an adulterated ash-color, but truly white, which is best.

<margin>How "gypsum" and "gypsitum" differ.</margin>
Gypsum differs from *gypsitum*. For the latter calcines, while the former does not. This is due to lime, not the mineral, which brings much lime with it; this is seen in wine which, when poured on a table, leaves a certain stain. Laudanum <note>Paracelsus's specific pain-relieving preparation</note> distilled by descent yields an oil. Remedies should not be used except during paroxysms <note>sudden attacks or fits of pain</note>. Pellitory <note>original: "Pyrethrum"</note> and sow-bread <note>Cyclamen</note>.

<margin>Moisture is extracted from oil by bread.</margin>
Oil is corrected by burnt bread: for if bread is cast into oil, it extracts whatever moisture is within. Since corrosive Tartar can damage the stomach, a cure for this must be kept ready.

<margin>Contraries do not exist together.</margin>
In Chapter II: Abscesses, burnings, weakness, coldness, nausea, "canine appetite" <note>excessive hunger</note>, fainting, and foul vapors are all contained under the term "compression of the stomach." Two contraries cannot stand together; this is understood regarding calcined substances. One limb does not bring its own disease to another. The "noble members" are the gallbladder, lung, heart, and brain. The heart does not tremble, but rather the stomach undergoes a paroxysm during a fever caused by dissolved Tartar.

->*Description of Nectar.*<-

24. Take: Liquor of *vitalicella* <note>possibly Virgin’s Bower or a similar vine</note>, 2 ounces. Redness of *colcothar* <note>iron oxide</note>, 2 ounces. Let a drink be made; the dose is half an ounce in good wine. These are accustomed to stir the urine; if the urine smells of the good drink, repeat the drink once or twice. 4. Take: Juice of *suffus* <note>unclear; likely a botanical juice</note>, 6 ounces. Prepared Laudanum, half an ounce. Oil of nutmeg, half an ounce. Let a mixture be made. It can happen that something is sent into the gallbladder which is thrown back into the stomach through bubbling, and the stomach expels it through vomiting.

<margin>How the air is infected.</margin>
In Chapter III: The "putrefaction of Tartar" is the dregs of Tartar. For those things which do not turn into Tartar pass into dregs, in which the first generation of fever occurs, and the first principle of fevers. The "Air of the body" is an internal element and is perfect. Its infection comes from vapors from the dregs, generated from Tartar, and that generation is the infection of the air; that infection is the cause of a paroxysm. Every paroxysm of fevers is a trembling and a movement of the air. This motion is elementary, just as in the chapter on the motions of the earth. The cleansing of the air has a period: that period is not taken from the fevers, but from the dregs, not according to the nature of the element. For dregs have a periodic digestion—that is, a digestive period. This is in the Chapter on Dregs. Fevers are from the dregs of Tartar. Dregs and Tartar differ in these respects: regarding things that dissolve and things that coagulate. Labor generates heat. A "burning" of Mercurial salt and nature occurs.

<margin>Humors putrefy only in leprosy.</margin>
None of the humors putrefy except in leprosy. In any putrefaction, there is a Mercurial digestive power.

An unequal paroxysm occurs from the unequal digestion of putrefaction: if it comes from salts, it happens in 3, 4, 5, or 6 hours. If from sulfur, in 12 hours. Quotidian <note>daily</note> fevers are from Mercurial salt. Quartan <note>occurring every fourth day</note> fevers are from sulfur. Fever from the stomach makes one sluggish. Foul breath reveals how hard it is. If from Mercury, they do not drink wine. If from sulfur, they vomit undigested food. If from its own salt, they do not vomit, yet *orexis* <note>painful hunger</note> bothers them. Putrefaction does not need digestion, but purging should be applied. Heats and rigors are signs of a long-lasting fever. *Præciatus* is made of three things. Nectar from the corrected and the clear. The clear from the crystalline. The center of the flesh is in the back.

In Chapter IV: Tartaric things are those which descend from spirit coagulated with a dry body. A dry body is a body made from coagulated moisture or dissolved dryness. Bodily gas <note>original: "flatus"</note> is gas generated from periodic cold. Periodic cold is that which is seasonal—either summer or winter—and its cure is periodic, as in the chapter on periodic time. "Regression" is the constriction of a disease against the waste-organ <note>emunctorium</note>, making a return to the first principle. No physician knows where or when digestion occurs in the intestines. Indeed, excrement passes to the *monocolon* <note>rectum/large intestine</note>, but only after the specific nourishment has been saved in the intestines; if these are retained in them, innumerable diseases are born therefrom, especially those of the Tartaric kind. They are also caused by medicine taken wrongly, especially those made from metals.

<header>ON TARTAR.</header>

# ON TARTAR.

It was composed of things not prepared, especially from iron and copper, which can coagulate more quickly. Nature only expels *dung* <term>stercus; metabolic waste or excrement</term>. In treatment, the logic of time must be observed: for winter demands one thing, and summer or autumn another. A sign 
<margin>Vomiting of dung is lethal</margin>
of Tartar lying in the intestines is if one vomits dung; this is lethal, as was proven to us by the death of Duke George of Landshut <note>George the Rich (1455–1503), Duke of Bavaria-Landshut</note>, among many others. Besides this, it is no less evident if the patient excretes only water through the bowels. Those who are troubled by abrasions <note>likely "tenesmus" or painful straining</note> and do not contract in baths are held by the same evil. Likewise, if the navel is anointed and back pain follows, then the Tartar is in the intestines. Piercing pain or hardness in the sides indicates it is in the intestines. Vomiting yellow water does the same, but demonstrates it is hiding in the lower part of the stomach. If it gnaws the intestines like worms, it is a sign of "hail" <note>small, hard stony deposits</note>. Beware, therefore, lest you be deceived and administer those powders that impostors carry around. For worms are born from those very powders. Sour wine retained in the intestines gnaws and stimulates through the Tartar.

## Winter Cure.

Take: 7 ounces of water from wine dregs.
6 ounces of common Tartar.
Half an ounce of Manna <note>a sweet plant resin used as a laxative</note>.
Clarified honey as much as suffices. Make an electuary <note>a medicinal paste mixed with honey or syrup</note> in form: Dose from 3 to 7 drams.

## Another Cure.

<margin>What the use of lemon juice is.</margin>
Take: Mastic, White Behen <note>a root used in tonics</note>, Bezoardic <note>a stone-like mass from an animal's stomach, believed to be an antidote</note>, half an ounce of each. Seeds of dill, caraway, amomum <note>cardamom-like spice</note>, 1 dram of each. Lemon juice as much as suffices for incorporation, make a bolus: dose half an ounce. Lemon juice reduced to the fourth degree of the spagyrists <note>alchemical physicians</note> is a most evident remedy against this Tartar and all others. Orange juice similarly has some effect, but the former is far more excellent.

<margin>Colic and Iliac differ by their location.</margin>
In Chapters V and VI: Colic and the "Iliac passion" <note>bowel obstruction</note> are the same disease, differing only by location: it extends its force from the stomach to the neck. Some have falsely thought this produces cholera, even if it passes with the dung. This is the beginning of "contraction" <note>contractura; a tightening or cramping of the limbs or muscles</note>; hence that disease should rather be named for contraction by no one else. For just as the piercing pains of abscesses are indicators, so is colic an indicator of contraction. Therefore, remedies for contraction should be applied, not for colic. It arises, however, from Tartar, in which there is a styptic <note>contracting or binding</note> and "pontic" <note>sharp or biting</note> force. If this congeals in the intestines, it creates the beginning of the disease in the center—small indeed—but the contraction comes from the styptic power. The vehemence of the pain comes from the pontic power. 
<margin>Retained dung is changed into air.</margin>
Retained dung is changed into "air" <note>gas or vapors</note>. This is not subject to the physician's control, but passes to the stomach, which it offends most severely; then to other parts, and finally is fixed in the ligaments. Because these ligaments are "sweet" <note>in the sense of being moist and vital</note>, they are harmed by the "bitter."

For bitter things turn sweet things into their own nature: 
<margin>The bitter converts the sweet, not vice versa.</margin>
but that which is sweet does not convert the bitter. You have an example in honey and colocynth <note>bitter apple, a potent purgative</note> mixed together. While a spasm extends, and in others a tetanus [stiffens], this [Tartar] contracts. From which it is likely that the voice becomes weak through this contraction, the instruments of the voice being filled with this air. Since, therefore, there is no expulsive force in 
<margin>Baths and anger open the body.</margin>
pontic and styptic things, the dung must be moved by art. Furthermore, those seized by this disease should beware of baths and anger. For these open the passages of the whole body and prepare a way for the "air" [gas].

<margin>What "Pontagium" is.</margin>
"Pontagium" <note>a Paracelsian term for a sharp-styptic quality</note> is that which contains the biting [pontic] with the styptic, such as sweet flag <note>acorus</note> and acacia. Colic occurs in the intestines when the styptic and biting dung has not been changed. Whence contraction can happen from the same. It is cured through the *arcana* <note>secret essences</note> of fatty things, not by boiled herbs, even if these take away some pain. For fat restrains the acid force, just as it checks poison and mitigates corrosives; however, not just any fat should be used. Not the oils of minor things, but of major things should be applied, because minor things have much water. Tartar mixed with oils is ejected upward by vomiting or downward by excrement; it also extracts the smoke <note>vapors</note> that adheres to the intestines. 
<margin>Fats mitigate acids and poisons.</margin>
<margin>Lean people are subject to colic.</margin>
Lean people are subject to colic; fat people more rarely. The fat of the red deer and of slow-moving animals is most select: of the fox, dog, squirrel, and also the badger, which more than others agree with human fat when given as a drink. Fox fat is applied externally. Oils which are numbered among these are such as mastic, and of myrobalans <note>dried plum-like fruits used in medicine</note>, etc.

## Description.

Take: Fat of badger and fox, half a pound of each.
Oil of mastic, 3 ounces.
Oil of spike <note>lavender</note>, 1 ounce.
A little vinegar, make an ointment with dissolution. Vinegar leads to the limbs because it penetrates to the ligaments.
Take: Olive oil, 1 pound.
Laurel oil, 5 ounces.
Resin of *botin* <note>turpentine or larch resin</note>, 4 pounds.
Distill through an alembic in the manner of a Balsam.
The laurel tree is very thick.
<margin>The laurel tree is very thick.</margin>
Under the name "Serpentina" <note>snakeweed or bistort</note> is contained whatever cures wounds. There is a certain species of Serpentina which they call "Bemontina" <note>Bistorta officinalis from Bohemia</note>, with a spotted stem; they prefer that to all others.
Take: *Serpentina Bemantia*, 3 pounds.
Olive oil, 7 pounds.
Poppy oil, 4 ounces.
Oil of spike, half an ounce.
Reduce into a balsam. Also take: *lassa* <note>unclear; likely a fat or resin</note>, 1 pound.
Oil of *Botin*, 2 pounds.
Mastic, half an ounce. Ivy gum, 1 ounce. Gum elemi (others say Ebony), 3 ounces. Take: Reduce into a Balsam.

# ON THE SECOND TREATISE.
## Of the Second Book.

<margin>Description of the region of the liver.</margin>
In Chapter I: The region of the liver is extended in length from the stomach to the kidneys. Its width is from the right side to the middle of the chest, below and above the diaphragm. Therefore, the stomach, liver, and kidneys suffer from nothing except Tartar. The liver is affected by obstruction; this happens both from substance and from "air" [gas], which is emitted from the intestines while still thick. Plague, *prunella* <note>a sore throat or "squinancy" often associated with fever</note>, pleurisy, thirst, dropsy, fevers, and other ailments that induce a livid color are all of the liver. Obstruction occurs, therefore, in the small veins which are scattered through the liver. 
<margin>Prunella is a new disease which he has [described].</margin>
*Prunella* is a new disease; it arises from this air, erupted from the liver, which ascends all the way to the throat and gradually affects it. Pleurisy is air enclosed in one of these members; it is not in the "precordia" <note>the area around the heart</note> as some have thought. Those who are livid suffer from an affection of the liver. The blood is *calcetus* <note>caustic or like lime</note>, so sharp that if dripped on iron, it would generate whiteness and then rust.

<header>COMMENTARY ON THE BOOKS</header>

<margin>Calcified blood brings on the rust of iron.</margin>
...it may generate. The diabetic suffering <term>diabetica passio; often referring to excessive thirst or urination</term> generates thirst in the liver. Prunella <term>a febrile infection of the mouth and throat, similar to thrush or quinsy</term> is in the first degree, thirst in the second, and the plague in the third. Dropsy <note>edema or swelling caused by fluid</note> arises from the liver; abscesses and piercings in the side indicate it, and the liver and legs are split open. Likewise, the lips, which are signs of death. Long-lasting thirst demonstrates a future dropsy. Reddening cheeks on the face and shins, as well as carbuncles, are indicators of future sickness.

In Chapter II. Blockage <note>original: "Oppilatio"</note> in the seven principal members generates either the plague, or pleurisy, or prunella. If any other sicknesses happen, they are accidental. An acute abscess <note>original: "Apostema"</note> does not exceed a space of 9 days. The plague, because of the violence of the disease, does not admit a cure, nor do preventatives have much power, seeing as the plague is both the disease and the sign itself. It is not so, however, in apoplexy.

<margin>Who the Yleiadus is and what its power is.</margin>
The Yleiadus <term>a Paracelsian term for the internal vital spirit or astral force that shapes the body</term> is the interior spirit that gives form to the parts of the entire body. This contains many species of salts, from the breakdown <note>original: "resolutione"</note> of which sicknesses are generated. When Arsenic is broken down, the plague occurs; from Ogertino (or orpiment <note>arsenic trisulfide</note>), pleurisy; from vitriol salt, prunella. Note: Water of prunella with theriac <note>a famous ancient herbal compound used as an antidote</note> is most useful in plague, pleurisy, and prunella. Just as there is good and evil in external minerals, so it is in the human body. These are found in a certain symmetry and proportion. Again, just as gold is affected by Arsenic in minerals, from which comes white Hungarian gold; so in man, the balsam of nature is harmed by others. *Opprimicchiolum* <term>a Paracelsian term for atmospheric vapor or "smoke" from the air</term> is the smoke that rises from the air. Digestion occurs in all things, whether good or bad; and from this, a prognosis of the future plague is received.

<margin>Water of Prunella is most useful in the plague.</margin>
<margin>Opprimicchiolum is smoke and air.</margin>
In Chapter III. The cure in the plague: Diaphoretics <note>medicines that induce sweating</note> and resolvents.

->Description.<-

Take: 10 ounces of corrected burning wine <note>alcohol or aqua vitae</note>.
Half a dram each of the Species of Bezoar <note>an animal-derived stone used as an antidote</note> and the Duke's Stone-breaker <note>original: "Lithontripon ducis"</note>.
One and a half drams each of Theriac and Mithridate <note>celebrated ancient cure-alls and poison antidotes</note>.

<margin>What a medicament given "through cohob" is.</margin>
Let a mixture be made; the dose is from 1 dram to 3 ounces through *cohob* <term>the repetition of a dose or a redistilled medicine</term>, according to the judgment of the Physician—that is, repeat it twice, three times, four times, etc., as it seems fit to the physician, once a week. This potion preserves (when the medicine is given anew, and it is repeated because previously it was either vomited up or otherwise did nothing).

->In the second plague, that is, from Water.<-

Take: 1 dram each of the famous liquids (that is, of wallflower <note>original: "florum cheiri"</note>) and of amber.
2 drams each of the liquids of Cachimia <note>mineral dross or ore</note> and white corals.
3 and a half scruples (otherwise 1 dram and half a scruple) of liquid of Amethyst.
Reduce into a drink. Its dose is from 1 to 3 and a half drams.

->In the third species, that is, from Earth.<-

Half a scruple of Harmel <note>wild rue</note>.
7 drams of Rosemary flowers <note>original: "Anthos"</note> or *antafiri*.
Reduce into liquids. The dose is from 7 to 13 grains.

->In the fourth species, that is, from Fire.<-

Red Corals.
Spodium <note>ash or metallic oxide</note>, 1 dram each. Reduce into a liquid.

<margin>Signs of the plague.</margin>
Signs of the plague from the earth: an abscess with pestilence is the first sign of earth. Movement of the legs—that is, tossing them here and there—is a sign of the element of air.

Unending sleep creeping over one is a sign of the element of fire. One who lies down and is not troubled by thirst (otherwise, if they thirst and do not wish to drink) but only eats, and whose feet swell up, suffers from the element of water.

<margin>The word Yleiadus is derived from Hermes and Archelaus.</margin>
Yleiadus is a word accepted by Hermes <note>Hermes Trismegistus</note> and Archelaus. The external Yleiadus generates health, the internal generates diseases. From this, the crisis now proceeds. A quartan fever can happen in any part of the year. For it is not only an autumn disease. The separation of the spirit in the Yleiadus occurs separately, now in the order of one, now of another. For the leaves are not dissolved in the same or equal measure of time: hence it happens that its crisis has unequal intervals. There are three ages: of health, of disease, and of death. The second age, which occurs when the breakdown of the Yleiadus has happened, alone admits the work of the physician, and it does not have a certain space of time. For as long as the separation lasts, this state remains. Death which comes from the Yleiadus can be hindered by the diligence of the physician; that which comes from the Being <note>original: "Ente"; referring to the Ens, or the fundamental governing force of life</note> cannot be hindered at all.

<margin>Which diseases are new.</margin>
<margin>The plague will not last forever.</margin>
The plague is a new disease, and it will not last forever, but at the end it will be most violent. Pleurisy—this disease was also not known to the ancients; some thought this was pneumonia. Gout <note>original: "Guttae"</note> in its various forms arises from the breakdown of the Balsam; the rest of the diseases from the Yleiadus. Edelphus <note>a Paracelsian term for a prognosticator according to the elements</note>, who gives prognoses according to the nature of the elements, says that nausea with trembling of the heart indicates an infected element. Every element has within itself a spirit from minerals. In the Yleiadus are all the species of nature. In Chapter IV. Arsenical sicknesses are: the plague, internal abscesses (that is, carbuncles), and anthrax. If the disease does not reach its crisis <note>original: "creticat"</note> on the seventh day, it is not from arsenic. In acute arsenic cases, the critical day is in the 24th hour; in acute cases in the 11th hour, in most acute cases in the 12th hour.

<margin>All sicknesses arise from the Yliadus.</margin>
It has already been said quite often that all sicknesses arise from the Yliadus, because this contains all mineral species, all things, and all simples.

In Chapter V. Pleurisy is not an abscess, nor of the lung, nor of others, but it is that which has been broken down by the Yliadus. Ogertine salt <note>orpiment</note> generates this; it brings redness to those who are pale, and on the contrary, paleness to those who are red. After the paroxysm <note>the sudden onset or attack</note>, which is unique, the heat lasts perpetually until the end of the illness. Aqua vitae is made from red wine with melissa <note>lemon balm</note> water. It is added in equal parts and distilled again.

## OTHER ANNOTATIONS ON THE BOOKS OF THEOPHRASTUS VON HOHENHEIM <note>better known as Paracelsus</note> ON TARTAROUS DISEASES; ON BOOK I, TREATISE I.

**W**hat Tartar <note>Paracelsus used "Tartar" to describe stony deposits or "gravel" in the body, like kidney stones or gouty crystals</note> is, how many are its types and conditions, where its locations are, and what is common or uncommon. Likewise regarding frost, hail, and the "guest."

Chapter I. **Stony** <note>original: "Lapilloſus"</note>) that is, a stone made from dissolved matter. **Frost** <note>original: "Pruinam"</note>) A species of sand. **Adamantine** <note>original: "Adamitum"</note>) and most malleable in white. **Alabaster-like**, etc.) it can be split.

Chapter II. **Concerning the Elemental**) From external things. The pure must be separated from the impure in all diets. Wells are harmful. Distilled foods and drinks cause putrefaction.

From the waters of the matrix <note>the environment or "mother" substance</note>, that is, external waters, many fevers arise from the weakness of the stomach and are cured by evacuations.

**Of Pure Sapphires**) liquid.
Leprosy is a lethal putrefaction.

Chapter III. Blood <note>original: "Cruor"</note>
> Of the principal members.
> Of the ligaments.
