> Of the external parts.

**In chaste men**) that is, Eunuchs.
**The cure or difficulty**) and this has a mixture, namely, of the foreign and the substantial. Wherever there is a consumption <note>wasting away</note> of a limb, the physician should judge it to be an obstruction from Tartar.

### ON TREATISE II.

Chapter 1. Tartar is not purged, but resolved <note>dissolved or broken down</note>. Heat is to be mitigated, not purged. Fevers arising from Tartar are affected by the treatment for Tartar. A febrile paroxysm <note>a sudden attack or fit</note> comes from the stomach, which is why the stomach must be purged. **Burning**) sharp in the stomach or its orifice. **Sapphiric Matter**) is the pure separated from the impure.

Chapter 2. "Tympanites" <note>bloating or gas</note> is in the womb and the intestines: here one must take care that the Tartar is loosened, as with the mucilage of fenugreek. (**Not with Hiera Picra <note>a traditional bitter purgative</note> by purging.**) Every hot liquid gives off wind. **Longaon** <note>the rectum</note>) Griping pains from the sharpness of the liquid in the intestines.

<margin>What Colic is.</margin>
Colic is resolved Tartar in the intestines; it is a fixed disease and produces saffron-colored urine. Oil is drunk for colic, as well as sweet wines.

Chapter 3. **Pain of the right side**) from which also comes a cough. **Tumors in the feet**) and around the eyes. **And bluish-gray**) that is, with the color the attractive force always seeks something.

### ON TREATISE III.

Chapter I. The liver separates the ruby <note>the red part of the blood</note> from the crystal <note>the clear part</note>. The red color is from the kidneys; the white is from the bladder. There are **burning things**) burning urine in the penis. In the kidneys, nothing coagulates except from a "bolus" <note>a medicinal mass or lump</note>.

<margin>Crystal is the best medicine for the stone.</margin>
Crystal is an outstanding medicine for the Stone <note>kidney or bladder stones</note>. **Ulcers of the Kidneys**) Mastic, frankincense, myrrh, and Mummy <note>a medicinal substance made from resin and organic matter</note> are the greatest flesh-forming agents.

Chapter II. The first digestion of urine is in the stomach. The second in the liver. The third in the kidneys. Urine is the generation of nitre. Whoever suffers breakdown beneath the "girdle" <note>the waist</note>, it is a sign that the neck of the bladder is constricted.

Chapter III. Stones in the kidneys (alternatively, the bladder) are very hard. Signs of Tartar: Nausea, vomiting, phlegm, pain in the loins, griping of the belly, pains in the feet, pains in the spine, and golden, bright urine. From the third separation, the urine is clear.

### ON TREATISE IV.

Chapter I. Mucilaginous urine below indicates internal Tartar. These patients have perceptible ulcerations, but pus indicates urine; they grow thin gradually.

Colic is resolved Tartar. Thus internal Tartar is not cured by diet, but by the "greenness of salt" <note>a specific alchemical potency</note>. There is a double natural humoral liquid. <margin>What the minerals of the body are.</margin> Minerals in the body are the liquid of salt, of alum, of lime, and of vitriol. Phthisis <note>tuberculosis or wasting</note> is an obstruction made from Tartar, and its cure is through Tartars. Phlegm does not fall into the veins, but rather resolved salt does. "Hailstones" <note>small hard lumps</note> are found in the muscles.

Chapter II. Balsam is neither salty nor sweet, and it preserves most greatly.

**Gluten** <note>the "glue" or synovial fluid of the body</note> is a mineral liquid.

From gluten and sperm comes the hardest Tartar. If it is felt during a new moon, it is from the salt of fire; if the pain is mild, it is from the Air; if more at night, it is from an external cause. It is a repulsive force against the nutritive liquid, because salt is repulsive—that is, acidic—and it coagulates the sweet gluten of that place: because gluten is a nutritive liquid.

Gluten is in the external members, not in the internal ones.

The hardness of Tartar receives its coagulation from the salts of the ore; salt in this generation is an Elemental and watery accident. The liquid of the humors is also the **Idestrum** <note>a Paracelsian term for the formative spiritual-material substance</note>. However, Idestrum does not exist without a composition. It is composed of minerals through four forms.

The tenacity of gluten is a mineral resin: just as turpentine is the resin of its tree. It differs from Balsam because it does not belong to salt. Pain is in gluten that is not salty, but it happens through the salty. This salty thing is acidic; the non-salty is sweet. Tumors are generated from gluten.

Gluten is in all joints; where there is gluten, there also is the place of Tartar. **Gluten**) Synovia <note>the fluid that lubricates joints</note>.

Chapter III. Those who suffer pain after the venereal act are laboring with Tartar from the sperm, and they are mostly sterile. "Sperm" is not the same as seed. The center is where two members end, namely the middle point of two members.

<margin>Sperm is throughout the whole body. What sperm is.</margin>
Sperm is throughout the whole body. These are the locations of sperm: where there is gluten, where there are the more principal members, minerals, humors, and liquids.

For sperm is the mineral root of the roots of the humors. The method of living <note>diet</note> contributes nothing to the sperm, but leisure does: its "emunctorium" <note>cleansing organ or exit point</note> is oil, and there it is called Crystalline sperm.

# ON TARTAR.

One must observe whether a collapse <note>or "slipping"</note> of the intestines occurs in the summer or the winter. Cramps of the belly in autumn reveal a winter condition, while in the spring they reveal a summer condition. A resolving or **Carminative** <note>a medicine that relieves gas or "wind"</note> treatment removes these cramps; **Carminatives** here refer to purgatives made with cumin <note>original: "per diacuminum"</note>. But the cure for the disease is also twofold: the first for winter, the second for summer.

<margin>Lemon juice should be reduced to the fourth spagyric degree.</margin>
*Lemon juice*, if used daily, prevents this kind of Tartar <note>stony deposits</note> in the intestines and dissolves what has already formed, but it should be reduced to the fourth degree of the spagyric art <note>the "spagyric" art is alchemical medicine, involving the separation and recombination of plant or mineral essences</note>.

Chapter V. The secrets <note>original: "arcana"</note> of this cure lie in fats (just as one uses them against poison), oils, and lard, without the addition of water. Oil should be given immediately if someone has eaten something poisonous; let them drink it. If there is a wound, apply butter or oil, but the fats must correspond to the "mummy" <note>original: "mumiæ"; in this context, "mummy" refers to the vital essence or "balsam" of the human body</note>: the "greater" oils are beneficial, but others are not.

<margin>Fatty people are rarely restricted <note>by these conditions</note>.</margin>
Fatty people are rarely afflicted by contractions or fall into colic, unless they are moved by very sharp wine. All those with colic have thin bellies. The fats of the badger and the fox are exceptionally effective; badger fat should be drunk, while fox fat should be used as an ointment. All animals of a fox-like color are beneficial. Badger fat removes "consumption" <note>wasting of the body</note>, as does the fat of dogs and red cats. **Liquor of mummy**) that is, an oil transmuted from the vital essence.

<margin>The power of Iassa against contraction.</margin>
Cooked cabbage is beneficial for women with swollen breasts. Iassa is a herb similar to Royal Comfrey <note>original: "consolidæ Regali"</note>, yet it is not the same. It is effective if a contraction <note>a muscle spasm or tightening</note> arises from anger and behaves like a serpent.

## ON THE SECOND TREATISE

Chapter I. From the wing to the axle <note>likely referring to the area from the armpit to the hip</note> is the region of the liver; if the pain is not fixed in one spot, it arises from the "air" <note>gas or spiritual vapors</note>. Every distance from the stomach to the kidneys is cured by liver medicines. The liver, kidneys, and stomach do not suffer unless from Tartarous diseases. The plague is also a form of "obstruction" <note>original: "oppilatio"</note>. All obstructions on the right side come from Tartar in the liver. A "narcotic" disease, which causes mania and inflames the body, such as *prunella* <note>a feverish condition, often called sloe-thorn fever or cynanche, marked by a parched throat</note>, must be treated with liver remedies. Pleurisy is trapped air. The ailments of the "internal air" must be carefully observed by the Physician. "Limy blood" <note>original: "sanguis calcetus"</note> is sharp blood that turns white. Thirst comes from the liver in the first degree; *prunella* in the second; plague in the third. If the intervening days lack thirst and heat, the fever is from the liver. If diarrhea ceases for an hour without thirst, it is from the liver. In the plague, a crack in the lips or tongues is lethal. Cracks alone can kill the liver. In fevers, if there are piercings in the side and cracks in the lips after a paroxysm <note>the peak of a fever fit</note>, it is lethal. Dropsy <note>fluid swelling</note> usually follows dryness. Red spots on the face or legs and carbuncles are signs of a coming disease. Abscesses <note>original: "apostemata"</note> gather over nine days. **Region of the Liver.**) It is called a "region" because it observes its own specific laws of disease. Obstruction is twofold: in substance, as when veins are clogged with Tartar; and in spirit, that is, in the air or a gap. **For those forming scars**) where the skin separates. Ailments that induce paleness are from the liver, as is whatever is indicated by physiognomy <note>the reading of character or health from facial features</note>. Dropsy exists in the liver, kidneys, and menstrual cycles, etc. If dropsy is in the liver, there will be hardness, piercing pain, or abscesses in the liver. Those who die from a liver ailment have cracks in the liver and the legs; hence in dropsy, if the legs or the testicles in men develop cracks, it is fatal. Red urine in dropsy is fatal. Oger <note>a Paracelsian term for a specific type of disease</note>, plague, *prunella*, pleurisy. Orpiment <note>arsenic trisulfide</note>, Arsenics, and "plumose" <note>likely feathered alum or asbestos</note> share a single origin.

*Yleidus* <note>a mineral spirit that penetrates the whole body</note> is a spirit that enters the entire frame. The liver is enclosed, just like a yolk in an egg.

Chapter II. Obstruction of the Liver. "Hydromancy" <note>divination by water</note> is the true astronomy of water.
*Optimechiolum*) all smoke arising from the air.

Plague from the liver does not produce abscesses except in the regions of the liver and upward, such as under the arms, the chest, and the breasts. All "burning wine" <note>distilled alcohol/spirit</note> contains water which must be removed, and then it will be corrected.

It is removed in this way: if you take a measure, distill it until, if you light a small amount, it is entirely consumed. Let "prunella water" be given frequently to those suffering from the plague if there is an abscess under the arms. "Ash-salt" <note>original: "sal cineritius"</note> is found in pustules. Arsenic tied to the hands causes thirst, inflames, etc. All who die of pleurisy die of Arsenic <note>in a metaphorical or alchemical sense</note>. *Prunella* comes from vitriolated salts. All things must be digested, whether good or bad. There is also a "digestion of time," such as when the plague returns after several years.

Chapter III. On the plague. Ash-salt is in the pustules. ### Chapter VII. ON FEVERS OF THE LIVER.
A fever is like water boiling in a pot, which requires air. It must be expelled through the urine, because the veins of the urine are obstructed; everything putrefied is cold, hence the tremors. Signs of obstruction are seen in the urine collected before the paroxysm <note>the peak of a fever fit</note>. After the paroxysm, the urine indicates signs of de-obstruction. Every fever is eventually cured by itself. In fevers, the medicine should be administered before the paroxysm. *Swelling in the feet*] if the swelling lasts for three weeks, another disease follows, namely either a Migraine, Dropsy, or Jaundice. *Stings*] stings <note>sharp pains</note> do not always occur. Heat after the paroxysm comes from the vapors of the whole body; a paroxysm is said to occur within 24 hours if the urine before the paroxysm shows great obstruction, but after shows de-obstruction—this is a sign of various "digestions" <note>original: "decoctionis"</note>. In daily, three-day, and four-day fevers, the cure is the same; whatever causes tremor arises from obstructions. Thus, de-obstruction is the cure for everything. *White urine*] white urine signifies no digestion, and is without sediment <note>original: "hypostasi"</note>. Let it be collected before or after the paroxysm. *With the fourth beat*] that is, if four healthy pulses occur for every one feverish pulse. In fevers, diet is of no use. But... de-obstruction. A fever with tremor and heat requires swift care. Languid limbs indicate a fever whose cure is still immature. *Description of de-obstruction*] it should always be given before the paroxysm and more often in the 2nd, 3rd, or 4th paroxysms. *Cleansing*] This follows when the heats begin; if the heat lasts a long time into the fourth hour, let it be cleansed again. *Restoration*] after the heat, to be given once at the end of the third paroxysm; if it has not returned in its own time, let it be given then as well.

## IN THE BOOKLET ON JAUNDICE.
In Chapter I: The color of Jaundice is not from bile; for if it were to return into the stomach, it would not stain, but would putrefy immediately when it wanders outside of its own proper place. Nor is bile subtle. Therefore, it cannot penetrate to the eyes. There is also nothing in the body that would take up the tincture of bile. Thus neither can melancholy <note>black bile</note>, which is contained in the spleen, penetrate, because it is thicker; nor is it the cause of black jaundice. Therefore, jaundice does not arise from those humors.

Furthermore, it must be observed that where there is color, there is the disease. If, therefore, the whole body is stained with an alien color...

Jaundice, like ink, is made of three things; even if one simple thing stains it, it contains three within itself. Herbs that provide color are more effective than others that do not stain. In treatment, these three must be separated. Before the onset of Jaundice, the urine is very white, and this is because of liquid sulphur <term>Sulphur: In Paracelsian medicine, one of the three primary substances representing the principle of combustion and growth</term> that has been dissolved; then it turns a dark color because **Entalic salt** <note>a specific Paracelsian mineral salt</note> is dissolved; thirdly, a salt is separated. Take: **Anthera of Oriental Saffron**, **Anthera of Rosemary**, four drams of each (others say six). Four drams of **Angelica oil**. Reduce into an effective form.

### For the Spleen and Liver.
Take: Four drams of **Tamarisk oil**, one dram of **Spikenard oil**. Let a mixture be made.

### For the Kidneys.
<margin>Calieta is a fungus of the juniper tree.</margin>
Take: **Anthera of Spearwort**, of **Juniper**, half a dram of each. **Calieta** (juniper fungus), half a dram. Let a mixture be made for distillation by the sun.

### For the Lungs.
Take: **Rha-pontic** <note>a type of rhubarb</note> of **Iris** (Eryngo), **Elecampane**, as much as suffices. Reduce into a liquor. Let a dose of one dram, or half a scruple <note>℈. ss.</note>, be given in the morning as a drink until the phlegm is improved.

### For the Bile.
Take: **Anthera of Centaury**, of **Greater Celandine**, half a dram of each. **Guaiac wood** prepared to the weight of all. The dose is half a dram.

# COMMENTARIES ON
## THE PARAGRAPHS
## OF THE FIRST BOOK.
## On Dissolved Diseases.

<margin>What a dissolved disease is</margin>
A **dissolved disease** <note>original: "dissolutus morbus"; refers to diseases of flux where the body's contents are "dissolved" and expelled too quickly</note> occurs when excrements are not properly cast down by the expulsive virtue: from this, lientery, dysentery, etc., arise. That which is pure is neglected by the stomach and dissolved. The cause: food, a fall, or the stomach itself; it is dissolved by the stomach, not by salt. Red discharges are contained under the same type: that which is digested in the stomach and separated is red, which is why those things excreted are already red and clotted, occurring through a fault of the stomach. So it is in the urine, where there is redness without any signs of **Tartar** <term>Tartar: In Paracelsian medicine, the stony or gravel-like deposits formed from impurities in the body's "lab" (the stomach/liver)</term>, and in diarrhea and dysentery. Thus, bloody vomiting is called by this name, and the cure for all is the same. But if the excrements are white and foamy, of whatever nature, it happens entirely by a fault of the stomach, just as when it flows simultaneously in the dissolution of urine; so also regarding vomit: Lientery <note>the passage of undigested food</note> is white. But if milky urine is present without signs of Tartar, it is a "lientery of the urine." A loose bowel, when it proceeds from the stomach so that a "fall" <note>likely meaning a sudden failure of function</note> outruns the **Archeity** <term>Archeity or Archeus: The internal "alchemist" or life force that directs the digestion and separation of nutrients from waste</term>, is a dissolved disease. But if there was urine without sediment <note>original: "hypostasi"</note>, of whatever color, it is not urine but a watery, tasteless superfluity; it is a dissolved, loose disease. So also exiting through vomit; vomiting occurs from the digested matter when the food is ejected almost already cooked. Regarding the chest, it occurs through violence.

<margin>The Archeity is located in the salt.</margin>
...infected, it can in no way be driven off by smoke. A time for maturity is established and decreed for all things, as for the plague, the "French disease" <note>syphilis</note>, and all those which arise from the three first principles <note>Sulphur, Salt, and Mercury</note>; it is ascribed neither to autumn, summer, winter, nor spring. The expulsive virtue proceeds from nature itself; that is, it is from those things which, born from minerals in the stomach, are collected, and not from the Archeity. The digestive virtue is not separated from the expulsive. Therefore, digested dung is expelled through **Entalic salt**; in vomiting, by **aluminous salt**; in urine, it is excreted by the **salt of nitre**. Hence, the Archeity is located in the salt. We treat incorrectly with scammony <note>a harsh herbal laxative</note>: medicines should be applied to the limbs, as those things which are clotted in the limbs. Take care not to offend the stomach by constriction. Whatever comes from metals is a "secret" <note>original: "arcanum"; a highly potent chemical remedy</note> in dissolved diseases, likewise those things from minerals such as **Auge**, **Talc**, **Kachimy**, and **Marcasite** <note>various mineral and metallic ores used in alchemical medicine</note>.
<margin>Metals are the secret remedy in dissolved diseases.</margin>

### ON THE SIGNS OF DISSOLVED DISEASE.
->Of life, of trials, and of death.<-

**R**egarding the sign of life, this is to be held: that if, by their own dispositions, the stools should be thickened without griping pain <note>original: "tormine"</note> or nausea, it is the beginning of restoration and good health.

If, however, it should flow into the looseness of the intestines, there are signs of health along with remedies. But if there is a particular tremor or febrile motion with a paralytic fall and a flooding of the eyes, these are wicked signs of death: and if signs of the mouth should concur—ringing in the ears, a deluge of tears, a trembling tongue—it signifies the approach of death. And this is the most certain sign: if there is a hunger of the parts, of the whole, etc.

### OTHER COMMENTARIES.
#### On Dissolved Disease.

<margin>The center of the disease must be observed in all things.</margin>
In all things, the center of the disease must be observed: the "fall," the Archeity of the stomach, and food as the cause, because it is clotted into wateriness. Today's dissolved food does not flow out immediately but can sit inside for three years. A "twisting" <note>cramp</note> is not Colic. The liquor—the cardiac water—is drawn to the stomach in all limbs. Therefore, all medicines are to be applied to the stomach; the cause of the disease is altered there. The Archeity of the stomach must be comforted by those things which are separated from impurity, which have the power of clotting a dissolution. **Dragon** (mountain coal burning by itself, with red lines, from the mountains) is "Dragon’s blood" <note>here distinguishing the mineral Dragon from the plant resin usually called Dragon's Blood</note>. Mustard is not Rocket <note>original: "Eruca"</note>.

<margin>Signs of mineral dysentery.</margin>
Signs of dysentery from minerals: If the patient can eat, it is caused by a fault of neither the stomach, nor the liver, nor the kidneys. What is ejected through vomiting as undigested dregs is not caused by a fault of the stomach. If there is much urine, again it is from minerals; thirst is not a sign. Where there are neither twists nor **Ischuria** <note>retention of urine</note>, etc., it is again mineral: a bloody matter flows, then from the parts and from other limbs it returns to the stomach, and it is the "liquor of the flesh." It is excreted through the bladder by the office of the liver; it clots in the bladder and is thus excreted. When truly it is a dissolution that lasts for a whole year, they have stools in a certain number, and so it happens in the urine and vomiting; it preserves a motion equal in number. When it is resolved to the center, that is, to the stomach, it is converted into that from which it was born. If one excretes white matter, it is a sign of dissolved salt. To excrete blood through sweat is a sign of salt with the substance of resolved flesh, which is not easily to be believed. The cause, the time, etc. As if the air...

*Crude matter of the dissolved:* Lientery, dysentery, diarrhea, and flux of the belly occur through the anus; these also occur in the urine and vomit. *Center:* that is, the true principle of dissolved things. *In the first operation:* that is, in the stomach. The stomach does not take on putrefaction, but the dissolved body does. *Red is contained under the same type:* that is, things digested and separated in the stomach, and then excreted red and clotted. *Red, White, Loose:* that is, fluxes of the stomach of various colors, and that because of the stomach, because it cooks now better, now worse; so also in the urine and vomit. *Red:* whatever is digested but not separated exists as red; nor is it (as they think) the blood of the veins, but a "counterfeit chyme." In the urine, indeed, these things signify diarrhea and dysentery; so also in vomiting. But *White* is "vebolus" <note>possibly a corruption of a technical term</note>, the color and foam of which marks the stomach,
howsoever...

->SCHOLIA ON THE BOOKS.<-

**Mandragorata**) <note>Medicines containing Mandrake</note> because they do not feel it when they urinate; the Stomach is Vulcan, that is, the cook. <note>A classic Paracelsian metaphor: the stomach uses internal "fire" to "cook" or digest food.</note>

**Paragraph III.**) Food is coagulated from wateriness. Food is dissolved by the stomach. **The Cure**) In short: in every care of these things, the stomach must be treated.

A sufficient quantity for incorporation. Unperforated pearls, 2 drachms.

### On Dissolutions arising from Minerals.

**Paragraph I.**) The signs: if the patient is "dissolved" <note>suffering from diarrhea/flux</note> daily and eats yet grows thin; if the matter is separated, the stomach is not harmed at all: likewise the vomiting of undigested matter: if these things also occur in the urine: likewise if there are no pains of the hips or spine, nor twistings [colic], etc. Nevertheless, the bowels flow. Coagulated blood in the stomach later seeks an exit, either through the anus or by vomiting. Salts alone cause either the stool, the vomit, or the urine. **Salt nitre** <note>saltpeter</note> passes through the urine. White vomit signifies a salt resolved without substance: if the urine becomes bloody, the blood is coagulated in the bladder. For those suffering from a "dissolved disease" and having stools on fixed days, it signifies the cause is from minerals: sulfur, salt, or Mercury. Likewise, if this happens on alternating days; if someone sweats blood, the disease is "dissolved." For Salt will be dissolved along with the substance and the flesh.

<margin>Salts cause all bowel movements</margin>
**Paragraph 2. The expelled has the character of its nature.**) Whatever reaches maturity possesses an expulsive power in itself, and this should not be credited to the stomach. However, whatever is not expelled should be digested rather than purged. The cure for mineral dissolution is from "coagulated" things. (For every coagulated thing is an **Arcanum** <term>Arcanum: A secret, powerful remedy that targets the essence of a disease</term> and an essence and essential medicine); that is, let the salts be coagulated, not in the stomach, but in the limbs, and let them not be constricted. **Oil of Mastich**) Mastich <note>original: "Lentiscus"</note> is not tamarisk, as some think, but is mountain-clover: but let the oil be made from the wood, not from the bark. **Scammony** is profitable in dysentery, if it arises from repletion <note>over-fullness</note>.

<margin>Scammony is profitable in lientery from repletion.</margin>
**Scammony** <note>a harsh purgative resin</note> is so vehement that it may trigger lientery <note>passage of undigested food</note> rather than settle it. All things made from metals, whether it be saffron [oxide], or flowers, or gold-leaf, etc., are **Arcana** in dissolved diseases arising from minerals. Likewise whatever is extracted from minerals, **Cachimia** <term>Cachimia: An immature metallic ore or mineral dross</term>, **Talc**, etc.

# PARAGRAPHS OF THE SECOND BOOK.
## On Worms.
## COMMENTARIES.

---

Putrefaction alone does not generate worms: if putrefaction is in the stomach, it generates them here with a "matrix" <note>a womb-like environment</note>, not in the liver, nor in the kidneys: but in women, they are generated in the womb.

<margin>Whence worms come.</margin>
If they come from nutrients, the excrements are cast out by vomiting: the **stellio** <note>a type of spotted lizard or newt</note> is generated in six weeks. Those born from sperm in humans are monsters, and they do not have the expulsive power in themselves like children and other mature things; these remain in men. From raw nutrients come **lumbrici** <note>intestinal roundworms</note> both in the stomach, etc. If during digestion they are born from "ruby" <note>perhaps referring to a red bile/humor</note>, they are long worms, like hairs: if the excrements produce lemon-colored worms, when these die, others are produced by them: a heavy breath indicates them, and these are very many. Others are generated from the veins and minerals, and these are driven to the stomach; these are short and red, and all are expelled by stool; here the man wastes away: **Mandragorated Theriac** <term>Theriac: A complex herbal "cure-all" electuary</term> drives them out, as does a confection of **anacardium** <note>cashew nut</note>.

**In the hollows**) That is, they are formed between the skin and the flesh: worms born from the liquors of the flesh do not return to the stomach: these eat and drink, and primarily occupy the parts of the back; they are very tiny and are distinguished by a vehement heat in that part.

In the marrow, worms with a white back, a bright white belly, and slippery nature are born. In the intestines, and not from putrefaction, they are long; **colocynth** <note>bitter apple</note> and **agaric** <note>a medicinal fungus</note> expel them, torn into tiny parts: for those things purge the intestines, not the stomach.

<margin>Colocynth and agaric are effective.</margin>
<margin>Worms are found in an abscess of the heart. Animals from a human corpse.</margin>
**In regions**) As in the regions of the brain, little worms are born; they affirmed at Vienna that little worms were found during anatomy in an abscess of the heart. All worms are from "sperm" <note>generative seed/fluid</note>. All sperm has a double substance: from one comes the likeness of that to which the sperm belongs; the other also passes into it. But from this latter part, worms and monsters are born. From sperm truly comes the seed; from menstrual sperm, other things like external flesh and pulp are produced; just as in a peach stone, the seed is within and monstrous things are on the outside: from good seed comes a fetus, from putrid seed a monster; as it can happen after birth that a woman's uterus swells from monstrous sperm, from which even monsters can be born. It is possible for animals to be born from a human corpse. Sperm belongs to the sensitive life: whether natural or monstrous. Children abstain from apples and meats. The moth <note>original: "macha"</note> and the beetle do not come from dung. **Lice** come from water, **fleas** from air.

### The Cure of Worms.

The difference between worms need not be observed in their cure: those things which kill worms outside the body also kill those inside. Those purged from nutrients are not led out, but those fruit-worms which are killed in a glass vessel when ingested also kill those within: as if they are baited with colocynth, they die inside and out, and this alone holds the cure. Furthermore, things that kill vipers outside, such as a liquor from **centaury**; or **St. John’s Wort** <note>original: "hypericon"</note> seed kills lizards, toads, and newts; **Harmal** seed <note>Syrian Rue</note> kills spiders, and agaric kills flies. Poison cures worms; newts are killed by hot meats. A powder made from worms in a pine tree kills worms from nutrients: likewise, powder from an oak tree removes roundworms, as do coals from flint and **turbith** <note>a purgative root</note>, and from agaric; likewise, the "copperish vine" <note>vitriol or copper ore</note> found in mines.

If worms originated from sperm <note>original: "spermate"; in this context, the generative "seed" or essence of a thing rather than just reproductive fluid</note> in the stomach, it removes them immediately. If they are in the intestines, it does not work quite so instantly, but the treatment must be repeated several times. # OTHER COMMENTARIES.
### On the Diseases of Worms.

<margin>The generation of worms</margin>
**The generation of worms)** These can come from types of nourishment, and specifically in the stomach—not in the intestines, as some people believe.

<margin>Besides the three types, one comes from sperm.</margin>
**The types of worms are three)** and one is from the outside, that is, from the sperm of living creatures. In men, these grow in the stomach. They can, however, migrate into the liver, and so on. In women, however, they grow in the womb, feeding on the sperm. Swallowed sperm grows there for as long as it does elsewhere, and it becomes a monster; afterward, they cause affliction and infestation, seeking food, and sometimes they last for years. **Concavity** <note>original: "Concauitatis"</note>—that is, where something is born between the skin and the flesh.

**Paragraph I & II.)** From raw matter they are like earthworms: long and thin, coming from chyme <note>partially digested food</note>. From excrement come worms with feet, white and yellow. When worms cause distress at intervals, it is a sign they are in the stomach. For those in whom a foul breath persists even after taking food, it is a sign that the worms have putrefied in the stomach. Without aluminous salt, vomiting does not occur. Theriac mixed with mandrake drives out worms if given to those who are fasting; likewise the "Golden Alexandrian" <note>a famous ancient electuary or medicine</note> made with cashews. Whatever is generated never reaches the stomach. The pain is in a specific spot, like a whitlow <note>an abscess on the finger</note>, but without the ripening of pus. In the marrow, worms grow easily—white on top, yellow, and mucoid—at which point the patient ignores all care. In the intestines, they do not arise from putrefaction; they are long and reddish-pale, and then they appear in the excrement, either torn apart or caught. Nothing drives worms from the intestines as effectively as colocynth <note>bitter apple, a powerful purgative</note>.

<margin>Colocynth powerfully drives out worms.</margin>
**Regions of the limbs)** The principal organs do not suffer from accidental pains, but from their own.

**Double sperm)** Nothing grows without sperm. In the "monstrous fruits" the sperm is monstrous; in the grains of fruits is the true sperm. Sperm is a thing according to nature. Every monstrous sperm can come into sensitive life. Nuts do not have "menstrual" sperm: therefore, the worm is not born in the kernel, but in the shell. Peaches have it, but their kernel does not. If the uterus swells after birth, it will be a new generation. In flesh, there is always sperm. The Macha fly is a winged <term>beetle</term> <note>original: "carabeus"</note>. **Crystal** <note>original: "Crystallus"</note> is white amber.
<margin>What sperm is.</margin>

<margin>The cure for worms</margin>
<margin>Every medicine that kills worms is a poison.</margin>
**The cure for worms)** One should not take precise account of the names of the worms. Those things which kill worms outside of us also cure internal ones. If external worms die upon touching a compound made of colocynth, let it also be given to the person suffering from worms. Eels and snakes die from the liquid of centaury. Likewise, toads, stellions <note>spotted lizards</note>, and lizards die from the seed of St. John's Wort; spiders from harmal seed; and flies from agaric. Every medicine that kills worms is a poison. All purgings are useless for worms unless the worms are killed by them. The powder of various woods cures worms. Powder from pine wood is best for recent worms born from nourishment. Powder from oak wood removes longworms, but only if it adheres to the upper parts. The gall (the oak-apple) grows on oaks. **Against worms from nourishment)** Use for several days; likewise Valeriana and Verbena are effective.

**Another against worms from nourishment)** Let the oil of colcothar <note>original: "colchothar"; the red oxide of iron residue from distilling vitriol</note> be coagulated again, and then it returns to its substance. The dose is 2 or 3 grains; however, mix it with vinegar. **Against worms from sperm)** If the worms are in the stomach, it removes them immediately; if in the intestines, not so instantly; if in the womb, let a pessary be made. With honey and salt. Let it be left until it falls out of its own accord. Let the menses be provoked with pennyroyal and masterwort.

# BOOK THREE, PARAGRAPH.
### On the Falling Sickness.
# COMMENTARIES.

**Species encompassed by one name:** Fainting <note>original: "Syncopis"</note> gathers its attacks at intervals. Fainting happens by chance, and rarely apoplexy, which proceeds from epilepsy. It is observed by these signs: that with eyes turned back, the patient extends their arms. Apoplexy is accompanied by a "drop" <note>likely "gutta," or a stroke/palsy</note>, foam, blackness, and stupor. Paralysis comes from epilepsy; when paralysis comes from a "drop," they stammer. **Synthena** <note>a Paracelsian term for a tightening or contraction</note> contracts, belongs to adults rather than children, and is mortal. **Incarnation of the back.)** An apoplectic fit is without foam and saliva; an epileptic fit is with foam. A sign of *analenta* <note>a type of dizziness</note> is whiteness of the nostrils; sleep precedes *catalentia* <note>catalepsy</note>. The "fright" of epilepsy is white. Fainting is the worst kind; in this, they are awake, they look around, they are insane, yet they have neither spasm nor tetanus <note>rigid tension</note>. It is peculiar to young men at night; when they lie flat on their backs, they are compressed and have a fit. After many years, this transitions into epilepsy. Sometimes epilepsy arises from vertigo contracted in dangerous places. Apoplexy happens with tetanus and spasm; occupying all the limbs, it brings death. *Synthena* happens to women when their feet grow cold or when the white flow of menses occurs. It happens not infrequently in acute illnesses that some limb is affected by a tremor, and that is a sign of death; so it also happens to women when their flow is stopped.

### Regarding Chapter Two.
**Paragraph I.** Man is composed of the three primes <note>Sulfur, Mercury, and Salt</note> and consists of the four elements. Every one of them has its own disease. "Chaos" is the Air, which, dispersed through the whole body, is the cause of the falling sickness <note>epilepsy</note>, from which the spasm is carried; just as the exterior winds are moved by a certain force, so too is this. Leprosy is from the Earth; consumption <note>phthisis</note> is from Fire; dropsy <note>hyposarca</note> is from Water; and "realgar" <note>mineral poison</note> are diseases that flow from minerals. For the Air has its own minerals within the body.

**Paragraph II.** All metals and marcasites <note>iron pyrites</note> are from Water. Air seeks an exit; hence it is credible that those struck by epilepsy are freed by being wounded. Bloodletting should be used for no other reason. Goat meat generates it; goats can be affected by the heat of their feet. Marjoram is beneficial.

# SCHOLIA ON THE BOOKS

Paragraph III. Mercury is the cause from which all species of the falling sickness <note>original: "caduci"; epilepsy</note> arise: The smoke of Mercury causes an epileptic paroxysm, Arsenic causes an apoplectic one, and realgar <note>a دروس arsenic sulfide mineral</note> causes a contraction <note>original: "synthesam"; a Paracelsian term for a convulsive state</note>.

Mercury does not infect the teeth and nails alone.
</margin>
Paragraph VI. Celandine <note>original: "Chelidonium"</note>, a green juice, the matter of the disease, stains the entire body; therefore a limb is moved according to its own internal impulse <note>original: "Ilech"; a Paracelsian term for an internal vital power</note>. A paroxysm of the brain takes away the intellect, hearing, and sight. A turbulence of winds passes through the spleen, lung, heart, and liver; and if it ever goes to the bladder, it raises the marrow, and thus the back and arms. In short, Mercury infects everything except the teeth and nails, in which there is no <term>chaos</term> <note>original: "chaos"; here referring to the unformed, volatile atmospheric matter that Paracelsus believed carried disease</note>: they are released only by the convenience of sleep. When the Mercury is consumed, the paroxysm ceases; then it twists the intestines, ejects saliva through the mouth, and finally they sleep. Catalepsy <note>original: "Catalepha"</note> happens from arsenical Mercury, which is therefore poisonous, so that it becomes fatal, occurring with shivering and twitching of the eyes: then it contracts the mouth and limbs, and afterward induces rigors and colics. In the height of joy the chaos is infected; they drink and eat, and suddenly collapse; with the lungs pressed they breathe with difficulty, and finally they rest, so that they do not even seem to breathe out, lying for four days because of the white arsenic, then they die, just as paralysis arises from the yellow variety. Suffocation of the womb, vertigo, and contraction also come from mercury, but are not fatal: when there is suffocation, mercury flows from the womb and infects the whole body. There are as many diseases as there are species of mercury. Dormice <note>original: "Mussulæ"; likely a variation of *mus* or *musculus*, referring here to rodents</note>—black squirrels—suffer from the falling sickness, but red ones do not: in the beginning, eel is a remedy. In diseases caused by the elements, nourishment takes the place of medicine, as in leprosy, etc. In non-elemental diseases, diet is not to be observed. Wild grapes and wine generate the falling sickness: whey from sheep's milk is beneficial, and grasses also provide nourishment in the falling sickness. Instead of salt, mistletoe <note>original: "visco"</note> should be used, and in this way you will discover whether they suffer from the falling sickness, as they do not require salt. *Bleta* (it is the Beet) and leaves of black hellebore: the rest are not forbidden, provided these are always primary. The oils of the skull and human blood are beneficial; they should abstain from fruits and aromatic spices, and from white turnips: it allows parsnips, cumin, and fennel, which do not generate a windy juice: they should abstain from sex <note>original: "à Venere"</note>.

<margin>
What a Cenigotûm is.
</margin>
A *Cenigotûm* is an instrument with which the skull is perforated, a probe or a surgical plug <note>original: "tenta seu turunda"</note>. Camphor and <term>spodium</term> <note>original: "spodium"; likely zinc oxide or the ash of burnt substances</note> coagulate the air: I would not approve of them in adults. An ointment of Aemilian’s description, a species of *tereniabin* <note>original: "tereniabin"; a Persian term for manna found on plants</note>, prepared manna is useful—the former for women, the latter for men.

<margin>
Manna is dedicated to men, tereniabin to women.
</margin>
Heavenly dew in May, manna, is beneficial if given raw. Dew through a water bath, then through a circular vessel. June dew takes away fainting and contraction. From good human blood.

Goat hooves should be burned with asafetida <note>original: "afsa foetida"; a pungent resin used in medicine</note>: when the smoke is applied, they fall.

In the falling sickness, an exit is prepared through the head in this manner: Let a *zenigotum* <note>a trepan or skull-borer</note> be taken, and the skull perforated as soon as the paroxysm has ceased: afterward let a masterly surgical plug be inserted, and let the patient fall asleep: the hole should not be closed again, but a silver <term>cannula</term> <note>a small tube</note> must be inserted into it, so that it may grow together with the internal parts.

Things that coagulate: Camphor and spodium.

From the elements: manna, and prepared *thereniabin*; if two or three drops are drunk daily with wine, no paroxysm will infest the person.

# OF THE PARAGRAPHS.

<margin>
The squirrel is subject to the falling sickness.
</margin>
The squirrel <note>original: "Musula, sciurus"; likely referring to the black squirrel or a similar rodent</note>, being black, often suffers from the falling sickness <note>original: "morbum caducum"; epilepsy</note>. Its diet becomes its medicine, not its food. In the theory of the elements, food ought to be nourishment.
<margin>
Antidotes for epilepsy: sheep's milk, parsnips, human blood, and human skull. The proper diet for epilepsy.
</margin>
A drink made from wild apples can bring on a seizure. Sheep’s milk is an antidote, as is the parsnip. If you are unsure about the disease, add oak mistletoe <note>original: "viscum quercinum"</note> to a piece of food without salt. If the patient eats it as if it were salted, it is certain that they suffer from this disease. Warm and fresh human blood heals this disease if used as a temporary part of the diet. Likewise, the human skull, if it is prepared and drunk.

Paragraph II. These are the proper nourishments: Oak mistletoe instead of salt, peony seed instead of a confection, roots of pellitory-of-the-wall <note>original: "pyrethri"</note> instead of parsley, and leaves of hellebore instead of chard or Roman cabbage. For those suffering from the "comitial disease" <note>another historical term for epilepsy</note>, these foods make them robust and soothe the illness.

Paragraph III. One must beware of these things: where there is corrupted seed, where there is vitriol <note>sulfuric acid or its salts</note>, where "winds" are generated in the body, where lust is provoked, and where the "essentificated sharpness" <note>a Paracelsian term for a concentrated caustic quality</note> is present. Regarding corrupted seed, avoid fruits. As for the odor of vitriol: throw vitriol into a fire and experience the scent; whatever shares that same smell must be avoided, such as certain growths on the tonsils.

<margin>
All experiments are secrets.

*Experiments are at hand*: they remove the pain, not the disease itself. An *Arcanum* <note>a "secret" or "great mystery"; in Paracelsian medicine, a powerful, hidden curative essence</note> is that which occurs outside the standard rules of medicine and against the balance of the Elements. With *speculation*: this means things created through theoretical insight. Indeed, all experiments are "arcana," but practitioners often do not know the correct dose. The alkali of all medicines are of great importance. Vitriol
<margin>
Vitriol of the brain is the highest secret.
</margin>
is the *highest secret* for the brain. *Hungarian or Roman Vitriol*: Hungarian and Roman copper types do not accept this; others do. Distill it through a retort or by descent. When the receiving vessel becomes milky, you must stop; the liquor will be at the bottom. In the preparation of oil of vitriol, the dose of the phlegm <note>the watery distillate</note> is one dram, always taken before a paroxysm. If the patient has suffered from epilepsy for 20 to 40 years, administer the liquor; the dose is one scruple. The oil should be given to those who have suffered for more than 40 years; the dose is three grains.

*A Device* <note>original: "Ingenium"; here meaning a specialized treatment or surgical method</note>: If the disease can find a way out, the seizure is removed. It seeks an exit in the head;

Various devices for epilepsy. 1. The head must be cut in cases of epilepsy according to Cenigotus.
</margin>
therefore, the head must be cut open. This should be done during a fit. Let the head be cut using the method of Cenigotus <note>likely a reference to a specific surgical authority or technique</note>; then apply a dressing; afterward let them sleep, and thus the skull is opened. Let <term>opodeldoc</term> <note>a traditional soap-based liniment</note> be added, and let the patient wake up naturally. Then insert small silver tubes <note>cannulas</note> and let them fuse with the internal parts. As long as these remain open, the patient does not feel the seizure, or feels it only slightly.

The description by Aemilianus is of great benefit to those composed of elements. Manna—that is, dried dew—if the pure is separated from the impure and taken in wine (a drop every day), it stops the seizure. Likewise "terebiabin," though it is more suitable for women than men.

Human blood against the falling sickness.

## On Undimia or Resolved Diseases.
### COMMENTARIES.

<margin>
Caution and cure for Hyposarca.
</margin>
**I**f <term>Undimia</term> <note>a Paracelsian term for dropsy or edema</note> comes from *Rochus* <note>Alum de Roche; a mineral salt</note>, it is a dropsy that occupies the whole body. Dropsy exists in the bodily regions when that water which breathes through them is coagulated. <term>Hyposarca</term> <note>anasarca; a generalized swelling</note> is nothing but "resolved" <note>dissolved</note> alum; for if that water is boiled and coagulated again, the alum remains at the bottom. If patients swell up, let them be purged with turbith, black hellebore, etc. You shall provoke sweating with half an ounce of theriac and a scruple of euphorbium; provoke vomiting and urination with radish water, chamomile, sage, and mugwort. Undimia or Hyposarca is nothing but resolved alum, the second species of alum; the tops of the feet, hands, and the entire face swell. During the cure, if the body turns white, it is a sign of health, because the "heat" of alum is white. In these wounded patients, the "glue" <note>original: "gluten"; likely lymph or interstitial fluid</note> does not flow. If white menstruation stops while the hip joints swell, it is a sign of future Hyposarca. Therefore, menstruation must be provoked for a cure. If the earthy glue is resolved from a coagulated state, it generates Hyposarca, simply because it resolves water and originates from "Rochus." If the air casts down minerals from itself, its clear part is resolved; this originates from "scissum" <note>split alum</note>. If it comes from the waters, it is like glue, and it is a water-based Hyposarca. If it is from the element of fire, minerals are resolved.

<margin>
Proper diets for Hyposarca.
</margin>
Let the diet be as follows: Moist things are inconvenient for the stomach in this disease, as they supply humidity to all the connected members. Beans and peas are approved, but roasted meat less so. Mugwort cooked with meat, and other things that provoke urine like hops and mountain parsley in a morsel of food. Likewise senna and a little turbith. Also, prepare wine with any of these: <term>diacubebe</term> <note>a cubeb-based remedy</note> for the womb and Hyposarca, saffron of Mars <note>iron oxide</note>, liquor of corals, and "sweetness of lead" <note>sugar of lead/lead acetate</note> are general remedies; water of the larger radish, or the radish itself boiled and reduced with honey into an electuary, is most useful.

## PARAGRAPH OF THE FIFTH BOOK.
### *On Dry Diseases or Phthisis.*
### COMMENTARIES.

<margin>What Phthisis is.</margin>
Phthisis <note>consumption or tuberculosis</note> is a fiery disease, a consumption of the whole body: when the fire has consumed the resolved dry parts, it then consumes the substance of the other elements—such as the coagulated moisture of water, air, and earth—after a resolution into moisture has first occurred, so that the elemental body remains dry. The body is consumed up to half of its weight, and then it dies. From the beginning, it is troubled by "piercings" <note>sharp, stabbing pains</note>; when these cease, consumption follows. At that point, the moisture must be reduced back to its original state. The urine is red or saffron-colored, with a white foam.

<margin>Its Cure.</margin>
Recipe: *Red Corals.* This medicine must be deferred until the urine loses its spongy foam, and the patient ought to be restored to their former weight. There is also an experimental remedy made from the fat of marmots <note>original: "murmentorum"</note>.

<margin>Marmot ointment against phthisis.</margin>
Recipe: *Marmot fat, 5 lbs.*  
*Ox marrow, 1 lb; Yew <note>original: "taxi"</note>, half a lb.*  
*Oil of bitter almonds to the weight of the whole.*  
*Red wine, as much as suffices for decoction.*  
Reduce into the form of an ointment. And this ointment should be used just as other ointments are.

Recipe: Of water and vitriol <note>sulfuric acid or metallic sulfates</note> and a little rock alum. Let the patient bathe until the urine is changed and the spongy foam goes away.

### OTHER COMMENTARIES.
### *On Dry Diseases or Phthisis.*

Phthisis is a consumption without sudden attacks or pains. At first, this disease removes all superfluity for one or two years; it takes nothing away, yet it brings sharp pains in the sides. Fire consumes the parts and the remaining elements, and thus the body is made dry. First, however, it is resolved into moisture: half is dryness, the other half moisture. Hence, in weight also, half the weight is lost, if they are weighed after death.

<margin>Those dead of phthisis are half as light as the living.</margin>
*Licorice, polypody fern, etc.* Always mix these with the food of those laboring under phthisis. The urine is a deep, saturated red with white foam. Let plantain <note>original: "Arnoglossæ"</note>, garlic, etc., be boiled until the pot is full; afterward add:

Recipe: White vitriol, silver pearls, 2 drams <note>ʒ</note> of each.  
Common vitriol, rock alum, half a pound [lb] of each.  
"Living" sulfur (that is, native sulfur that has not been melted), 1 lb.

Use a bath for 10 or 12 weeks, and the urine will change, and the patient will be cured. Crushed and boiled amber <note>original: "carabe"</note>, 1.5 drams, is added.

Caution: Do not use clysters <note>enemas</note> or purgations. Signs: If the skin develops cracks or fissures, it is a sign of an incurable disease, especially if the cracks are around the knees, etc.

## PARAGRAPH OF THE SIXTH BOOK.
### *On Leprosy.*
### COMMENTARIES.

<margin>Which parts leprosy may affect.</margin>
When the element of earth is putrefied in the flesh, one can prolong life for thirty years; it is born from the minerals of Mercury, by which it can also be cured. If the *chaos* <note>here referring to the internal atmosphere or spirit of the body</note> is infected, they have heavy breath and a discoloration of the whole body. If the earth is affected, it appears in the face. If from fire, small blisters [vscula] arise and occupy the throat and gums. Leprosy from water: the feet swell and are extremely cold. Likewise, the private parts swell, and ulcerations follow.

If it stems from the lungs, the voice grows hoarse. If in the liver, the patient is not thirsty, and the skin is rough. If of the bladder, they produce foul-smelling urine, and the penis is affected. If the spleen is affected, there are "piercings" and blood in the water [urine]. If from the heart, there is corrosion and the spine is ulcerated. If from the kidneys, the urine is milky with white fat, and the teeth fall out. If from the gall, they vomit daily, and there are grains like millet on the tongue. If from the brain, there is foul phlegm, the nostrils harden, there are scabs on the back of the head, and the eyes swell. *Zephena* <note>a Paracelsian term for the symmetry of the body's orifices</note>, the symmetry of any emunctory <note>drainage point</note> of the body—namely the mouth, uvula, eyes, and nostrils—because these are contracted in a circle and become round; those that are sharp become sharper, such as the fingers, penis, nose, and the cartilage of the ears. The *Orizeus* color is Venetian or a purplish-blue.

### *On the Examination of Lepers.*

<margin>Urinary signs of leprosy.</margin>
Leprosy is to be divided into three parts. For "scatea" urine <note>likely referring to frothy or bubbling urine</note>, which indicates leprosy caused by an accident, submerge this in a warm place, with the urinal vessel blocked with glue and a disc. Therefore, once the distillation of the urine is done, let the disc be removed; when dried at the fire, it whitens with salt; these signs are found in the urines. Excrement soaked in water and washed with many waters: that which finally remains at the bottom is very heavy and like sand; this indicates leprosy of the stomach. Wild Savin <note>original: "Sabina syluestris," a type of juniper</note> generates leprosy when eaten. Menstrual blood infects both humans and pigs with leprosy. When drops of sweat do not cling like pearls [uniones] but are diffused through the whole body, it is a sign of leprosy. However, [something] must be provoked...

<header>ON TARTAR.</header>

# ON TARTAR <note>In the Paracelsian tradition, "Tartar" refers to stony or sandy deposits formed in the body from metabolic waste, similar to the crusts in a wine barrel.</note>

...moreover, sweat on a dry cloth. If calloused skin becomes ulcerated by its own nature, or if blood is drawn forth by mange or itching, it is a sign of leprosy. If the whole body is covered in mange, accompanied by a hoarseness of the voice or a loss of sensation, it is a mark of a leper. The "epiglottis" <note>likely referring here to a silver probe or instrument used to lift the eyelids, rather than the anatomical throat structure</note> is a silver instrument by which all the eyelids are raised back. If the eyelids fall away, these are signs of leprosy. If blood, when drawn out into a thread, does not dissolve in water, or if the blood is washed away like dung, these are signs of innate leprosy. If the cheeks sink in and are uneven in thickness, it is a sign of leprosy. Likewise, if the breasts are hard in the upper part and soft below, or if the buttocks become soft. If the flesh of the thumb sinks into a contracted hollow, it is a sign of leprosy. If they suffer from thirst and hunger after sexual intercourse, it is a sign of leprosy.

On the differences between signs: Alopecia <term>hair loss</term> produces grains like millet under the tongue, just as leprosy does; one must distinguish it from *Morphoea* <term>blotchy skin discoloration</term>, from *Tentigo* <term>morbid tension or skin eruptions</term>, and from *noli me tangere* <note>literally "touch me not," a historical term for corrosive skin ulcers or facial cancers</note>. Itching sometimes proceeds from the poisons of orpiment <note>arsenic trisulfide</note>, sal ammoniac, or a sun-solution made with urine from menstruation, the blood of hemorrhoids, or the *salvatella* vein <note>a vein on the back of the hand</note> of the left side; these occur with a wasting of the body from cold and heat, and are both a disease and a leprosy, as seen in mules.

If the skin on the front of the hands and feet is covered with mange, accompanied by a hoarse voice, it is a sign of leprosy. If it arises from heat, no matter what sign of wasting invades, it is not leprosy. But if there are scars, a hoarse voice, and hollow eyes, it is leprosy. Those who work with metals and refine them are greatly infected by the "realgar of Vulcan" <note>realgar is an arsenic ore; "Vulcan" refers to the heat of the forge or the alchemy of smelting</note>: just as arsenic generates diseases similar to leprosy, such as *morphea*, etc. "Split salt" <note>likely alum or a specific mineral salt</note> produces polyps, hoarseness, etc. Likewise, Mercury makes one calloused and hoarse. If these "men of Vulcan" <note>smiths and miners</note> are simultaneously deprived of flesh near the thumb and their ears sink, it is leprosy. Cooks contract a certain disease from contraction and fire, which is nevertheless not leprosy. Likewise, pork meat generates such mange in certain places, and <margin>Sexual intercourse produces hoarseness in lepers.</margin> yet it is not leprosy. Intercourse can generate hoarseness, but it is not leprosy unless *cephena* <note>a Paracelsian term for facial distortion or specific leprotic markings</note> is present. The transformation of other diseases can generate leprosy, such as the "French Mange" <note>syphilis</note>, alopecia, or *morphoea*; if these result in hoarseness and swollen tonsils at the same time, it is leprosy. Mange arises from a quartan fever; if the voice becomes hoarse, it is not leprosy unless "rosy drops" <note>acne rosacea</note> or something else follows, and if the upper part of the nose is compressed, it is leprosy. Blood from the *salvatella* vein when the spleen is affected—if the vein is cut, etc.—generates mange with hoarseness on the left side.

### Signs of the White Leprosy.

The skin is an ashen, "lazar-like" color, without mange or swelling; the breath is heavy from "putrefied chaos" <note>in this context, "chaos" refers to the atmospheric air or the internal gases of the body</note>, smelling like arsenic, sulfur, or roasted onions. The urine stinks like the breath, and so does the stool.

### Preservation of Both.

Those things which protect a corpse from decay also preserve one from leprosy. However, they do not restore things that are already putrid. <margin>Balsam, flowers of antimony, etc. preserve against leprosy.</margin> Balsam, flowers of antimony <term>a refined chemical sublimate of antimony</term>, and essence of wine are used. The dose of antimony is about 1 scruple, once a week at dawn. The dose of human blood <note>Renaissance medicine often used preparations of dried or distilled blood</note> is half a dram, once a month, on the second day after the opposition of the moon. The dose of pearls and corals is 4 grains every day at dawn. The dose of lemon balm and valerian is 1 to 1.5 drams every day.

# OTHER COMMENTARIES.
### On Leprosy.

<margin>What leprosy is.</margin> Leprosy is nothing other than a disposition and failure of the body toward putrefaction. For leprosy follows this. The putrefaction of the element of Earth is the putrefaction of the flesh. Indeed, if the flesh begins to rot, the very minerals associated with that element rot with it. Therefore, if the flesh turns toward leprosy, the elements and minerals provide the cause for putrefaction; and if the minerals are dissolved, the path to putrefaction is open, and death takes hold of that affected limb. If, however, the leprosy penetrates to the principal organs, death resides in these three principals: the heart, the stomach, and the liver. If the "coagulation" of the body fails, leprosy is also present; and this leprosy is the most hidden. If the "chaos" <note>the vital air/internal atmosphere</note> is infected, it leads to the death of that limb. A similar thing happens in the element of Fire. And if the leprosy clings to only one element in this way, then the "liquor of nature" <note>vital fluids</note> and the three remaining elements preserve the body. If <margin>The falling off of a finger or the nose is a sign of leprosy of all the elements.</margin> the leprosy is so vehement that a finger, an ear, or the nose falls off, it is a certain sign that all the elements have been seized by leprosy. If, however, only one element falls into leprosy, the other three support it so that the putrefaction does not grow stronger. If two elements are invaded by leprosy, the other two preserve and support the body, etc.

### Signs of Leprosy.

<margin>Signs of which elements are affected by leprosy.</margin> If the leper feels stinging sensations, it is a sign of the leprosy of Water; if he does not feel them, it is of Earth. It indicates Earth if it begins in the extremities, and it indicates "Chaos" <term>Air</term> if the breath of the mouth is heavy and they feel little. From Fire come little "burns" or ulcers that come and go. From Water, the feet swell and cannot endure cold; the groin swells and becomes ulcerated—sometimes it begins from the principal organs.

<margin>Signs of leprosy in which parts.</margin> In the lungs, the sign is a hoarse voice. In the liver, no leprosy infests with thirst, but the skin becomes like the bark of an oak. In the bladder, it is marked by foul-smelling urine. Leprosy of the spleen begins with stinging sensations; their blood becomes sandy, bright, and azure-colored. Leprosy of the heart causes "biting" pains at the mouth of the stomach, and intolerable mange. In the kidneys, it has fatty and milky urine with white "axungia" <term>fatty deposits</term>; a light pulse, and toothaches. Leprosy of the gall bladder begins with temporary vomiting, and "hailstones" <note>likely small bumps or pustules</note> on the tongue. Leprosy of the brain makes people mucousy and foul-smelling; afterward, they speak through their noses, "little ears" <note>likely growths</note> grow on the neck, and the eyes swell.

**Zephena** <note>a term for the outward appearance or "face" of a disease</note> is the mode, form, or circle of any limb, or of the nose, eyes, or mouth. If any of these is altered, it marks leprosy; the ears become round. In men, the *zephena* becomes circular; in swine, it does not become circular but protrudes.

**Sharpness** (*Acumen*): that which shines from the face; the nose becomes sharper than usual, as do the ears and fingers.

**Azure Color** (*Color Lazurius*): this usually comes to those places where there are signs of *zephena*; it is easily detected in the cold if the color turns toward black.

<margin>Savin and consumed menstrual blood cause leprosy.</margin> **Accidental Leprosy**: that which comes from nutrition, such as one who eats savin <note>a toxic species of juniper</note> or menstrual blood; they are easily infected by leprosy. If preventatives for leprosy are taken, leprosy cannot be judged on that day. **The Smoke Test** (*Scatea*): take the soot of smoke, place urine on the fire; it is covered by a disc and distilled up and down; finally the disc turns white and appears covered in salt. **The Stool Test**: pour water over it and stir or shake it until it flows apart; pour it out twice, and a heavy weight will remain at the bottom: leprosy...

...leprosy will then be in the stomach. **As for the sign of sweat**) make the patient sweat, but not in a bath where there is water. If the sweat is like droplets, it is a good sign; if not, then it is not good. If the sweat does not emerge like pearls but is poured out over the whole body at once—that is, it makes the skin soaking wet—it is a sign of leprosy. This is also true if water is poured over the skin, but this can be deceptive: if the sweat coagulates and becomes thick <note>original: "fit l" likely abbreviation for "limus" or "lentus" (thick/muddy)</note> and does not dissolve again, it is a sign of leprosy. **As for the variety of pustules**) when pustules arise on the skin, it is a sign indeed, but a deceptive one. But if they ulcerate themselves, it is true leprosy, or if they form crusts, or spontaneously emit blood through itching. If someone has itching over the whole body along with a hoarseness of the voice, or if the areas are without sensation.

<margin>Use of the epiglottis instrument.</margin>
**From the epiglottis**) <note>Note: In this context, "epiglotto" refers to a silver medical probe or spatula rather than the anatomical structure in the throat.</note> specifically, a silver instrument, similar to the iron tool used by shoemakers. If the eyelids are turned inward and grow that way, the instrument is placed beneath the eyebrows, and hairs are placed upon it and combed, as it were, with the hand; if the hairs fall out, it is leprosy. Likewise, if the hair falls out spontaneously. If the vein of that limb where the leprosy is located is touched, it is discerned in the blood. **Sunkenness**) if the cheeks sink in the middle, it is a sign of leprosy: if the jaws are not uniform or of the same thickness. If the breasts are hard on top but soft below or inside, and hollows form where they were previously more slender. Likewise, the buttocks sink. **Wasting of the flesh**) wasting near the thumb, if cavities are present there as well. **Lust**) if someone is hungry and thirsty after the sexual act, it is a sign of leprosy. **Alopecia**) <term>hair loss</term> this produces pustules on the neck; "rose-drop" <note>original: "gutta rosacea," likely acne rosacea</note> produces spots. **Itching**) those who have tasted poison—namely of orpiment <note>an arsenic mineral</note> and "split salt" <note>likely rock salt or sal gemme</note> taken with wine—also from menstrual blood, from the blood of hemorrhoids, or from the blood of the left *salvatella* <term>a vein on the back of the hand</term>; these are poisons which do not kill the body immediately but bring on disease, such as mange and itching accompanied by the wasting of the body.

**From cold**) This breaks out into rashes <note>original: "rastetas"</note> and causes itching with hoarseness. **From heat**) as is contracted in frequent "Herculean" <note>hot/strong medicinal</note> baths; mange is caused, and if accompanied by hoarseness, the eyes sink. **Realgar**) <note>red arsenic sulfide</note> as occurs in those who are frequently occupied with fire: for whom this disease happens. For the skin is changed by fire, etc.; they are not to be judged as lepers immediately.

<margin>Bavarian pork makes people look like lepers.</margin>
Very salty food also produces ulcers and hoarseness; so too do other metals produce spots. If someone standing near Vulcan <note>the forge or high heat</note> wastes away between the thumb and near the ears, it is a certain sign of leprosy. **From meats**) specifically in Bavaria, those who eat pork; it is not immediately leprosy unless accompanied by *zephena* <note>a Paracelsian term for a film or dimming</note> of the eyes and ears.

**The transformation of diseases**) such as from alopecia, pustules, polyps, etc., or from a quartan fever: for itching follows these, but not the continuation of leprosy. If a spot <note>original: "amygda," literally almond-shape</note> becomes bright and azure, it is leprosy. If after a quartan fever the nose sinks and becomes round, showing a circle. **Blood of the left salvatella**) renders only the left side mangy; if it occurs with hoarseness, it is leprosy, otherwise not. **Red Sigean leprosy**) Alopecia, abscesses, "busones" <note>possibly swellings</note>, and parotid swellings. **From stenches**) such as sulfur or onions. Likewise, if the urine has the stench of the mouth. Likewise the feces.

<margin>Antimony wards off rot. Likewise, etc.</margin>
**Preservation**) it is necessary that the natural balsam <note>the body's innate healing power</note> be comforted; therefore, those things which preserve a corpse are to be used in the preservation of a leper. Antimony allows nothing to rot: so too the essence of wine, etc. The dose of antimony is once a week at dawn.

<margin>essence of wine, human blood, coral.</margin>
The dose of human blood is half an ounce once a month on the second day after the opposition <note>the full moon</note>. The dose of coral is 4 grains every day in the morning. The dose of Melissa <term>lemon balm</term>, etc., is 1 drachm to 1.5 drachms every morning. Gold thins the body. **Cure for the tube**) Potable gold, liquor of gold, "rice juice" <note>possibly a preparation of orpiment or a gold-colored extract</note> from the ore of gold. The dose is 1 grain in the morning in good wine. Raymond Lull was the first to cure leprosy, and later Arnold <note>referring to medieval alchemists Raymond Lull and Arnold of Villanova</note>. In white leprosy: oil of silver, liquor of silver, juice of silver—that is, silver water, which comes from the "lightning" <note>purification process</note> of silver. The dose of silver is half a scruple once a lunar cycle. When lepers feel sciatica and the hips sink, the leprosy is incurable.

### COMMENTARIES.

<margin>What Gout is.</margin>
**G**out, Paralysis, Apoplexy, loss of speech, ringing in the ears, loss of teeth, gonorrhea, and other diseases arise from "anodynes" <note>pain-killing substances that might suppress symptoms rather than cure</note>. Gout belongs to a limb that cannot be master of itself. Apoplexy and paralysis can belong to the heart as well as the liver and other principal members: sometimes all the members have *synophia* <note>a Paracelsian term for the cohesion or fluid-state of the organs</note> at once, and it is nothing other than the place of the member where nutrients are digested; it is like the stomach of that part, or rather a certain mucilage. It is red in the blood, white in the brain—thicker and more tenacious than the white of an egg, with a certain fatness—black in the spleen, citron-yellow in the gall, and similar to those specific organs in the kidneys, heart, liver, and lungs; in the womb it is reddish-purple, tenacious, and thick; in the marrow it is the color of an ear of grain. When these are reduced into one with their member, they become a single part, which is not possible [normally], but that which grows beneath can be united.

<margin>What synophia is and how many kinds.</margin>
*Synouia* <term>joint fluid or vital humor</term>; the retentive virtue is contained here, and others are drawn away. First, coagulation occurs through coagulating agents, such as purslane, which coagulates the blood. Those nourished on cheese and fish yield no blood when wounded.

<margin>Fatty things alone produce diabetes and gonorrhea and stop the blood.</margin>
Fatty things alone, when they take effect, generate diabetes and gonorrhea. Houseleek <note>original: "semperviua"</note>, that is, wintergreen, Jupiter's beard, lettuce, and lettuce seed constrict the "glue" <note>the viscous humors</term>, whereby the blood is stopped. When *synouia* is compressed, carnelian <note>the gemstone</note> stops blood for a period of three days: the "sperm" of frogs stops it for 20 years. The essence of wine finally obtains its power: for even the hottest broth from meats congeals by that essence of wine; a resolution of the parts follows, and then the disease rages.

<margin>Signs of which apoplexy.</margin>
Apoplexy from the brain is accompanied by snoring, trembling, opening of the eyes, the flow of saliva, and spasms during sleep. Another kind belongs to the lungs, and it is swifter than others, intercepting the breath at intervals; the buttocks become sharp and turn pale, with hiccuping, inversion of the eyes, white foam, a vehement pulse, and spasms from the accident. Another belongs to the heart; this is accompanied by trembling and sweat; they feel pain in the chest, and there is sweating of parts, not the whole. Paralysis, a shivering of a part, flow from the nostrils, frequent sleepiness, and numbness of the limbs precede it. Those who are finally seized by the disease and cast into a vehement sleep, sleep for a long time: if their mouths are opened by force and they return their breath, it is paralysis; if not, it is apoplexy. The "falling sickness" <term>epilepsy</term> precedes apoplexy, especially in the elderly; there is also a transition of diseases, such as from fever into paralysis, sometimes together with "hypofarca" <note>likely dropsy or swelling under the flesh</note>, and sometimes epilepsy during an onset.

<margin>Sandalwood prevents gout.</margin>
Sandalwood <note>original: "sandalum"</note> prevents it if taken twice daily, powdered with sugar or in filings. If a limb does not perform its function, it is Gout <term>Gutta: literally "a drop," referring to the belief that "dropping" humors caused joint pain or paralysis</term>; the teeth also fall out. From paralysis, it can even be in the principal limbs. <margin>Synovia is in all limbs.</margin> Synovia <note>original: "Synophia," an early term for the lubricating fluid of the joints and tissues</note> is the "stomach" here, and the cause of the part from which it is nourished. In the bones, arteries, and joints it is white; in the flesh it is red; and in truth, it is nothing other than mucilage. Synovia is in all limbs, both the more principal ones and others. Within the synovia are the bodily faculties; one must not purge in these cases. A defect of synovia causes a lack of sensation. In purslane <note>original: "portulaca"</note> there is a coagulating power. Likewise, if anyone eats cheese and fish for nine days, his throat will not bleed. Likewise, fatness alone reconciles diabetes and gonorrhea <note>Note: here used in the historical sense of a "running" or discharge</note>. <margin>Things that coagulate synovia.</margin> These things coagulate synovia: houseleek—that is, wintergreen <note>original: "pyrola"</note>—Jupiter's beard, lettuce, and lettuce seed. Signs of Apoplexy.</margin> The essence of wine coagulates broth even when it is warm. Apoplexy comes from the brain, heart, and lungs. Signs of future Apoplexy: they snore in their sleep and tremble, and they sometimes sleep with their eyes open; those sleeping have water in their mouth. Apoplexy of the lung sends forth few signs: namely, a tightness of the chest; the nose turns white, the face takes on a new color, the neck swells, a hiccup is present, they emit white foam, and it is incurable. Three grains of mustard seed are the highest preservative against Paralysis when taken daily. *Signs of paralysis*) Paralysis belongs to a specific limb; first, before they come into stiffness or chills, there is frequent hemorrhage, numbness of that limb, and trembling of the joint. There are heats at the end of the spine. *Pains*) these come before gonorrhea. <margin>Epilepsy is a sign of Apoplexy.</margin> Epilepsy is sometimes a sign of Apoplexy. The injured part is opened all the way to the center of the part, then add an attractive <term>attractive: a medicine intended to "draw out" humors or heat</term>. *Ceratum de Minio*) that is, with care and red lead <note>original: "minio"</note> cooked into a wax salve.

<margin>Melissa is against Asthma.</margin>
In Asthma, there come piercings of the sides, and they spit without coughing. *Ulcers*) these cause putrefaction, hence a heavy breath from the mouth, stinking like rotting legs.

### COMMENTARIES.

Fever arises from heat which is mixed with cold things; the matter of the blood is in the whole body, hence the whole body is affected, if it comes from the flesh. If during the time of remission the sick man eats and drinks, something recedes; if he eats less, 13 months. If the hour changes while the erratic period remains, it is a sign of evil. If in the course of treatment the onset comes sooner, it is a good sign. If it is unequal, now mild, now hard, and finally harder, it is a bad sign. The violence of the paroxysm bursts a vein, so that now the nostrils, now the urine, now the mouth brings forth blood; and these things have their own cure: Castoreum, Anacardium, and Pepper, applied to the temples, take away the paroxysm, but they are rendered weaker. The feet swell, and that is a good sign.
*Cure*) Alcohol of dried wine—that is, cleansed of phlegm—which is "burning wine" <note>brandy or distilled spirits</note>.
