# OTHER COMMENTARIES:
## *On Foreign Fevers, that is, those not arising from nourishment.*

Common putrefied heat begins with tremors. If the matter is released from the flesh, the fever is in the whole body. If in the blood, the paroxysm <note>original: "paroxysmus" — an attack or sudden increase in symptoms</note> will be throughout all the blood. The same applies to the principal organs: if it comes from the spleen, bloodletting from the salvatella <note>original: "saluatella" — a specific vein on the back of the hand between the ring and little finger, traditionally bled to treat diseases of the spleen</note> vein removes it. If from the liver, the hepatic vein. If from the heart (*). If in the flesh, use scarification <note>original: "scarificationem" — the practice of making small shallow cuts in the skin</note>. If a quartan fever <note>original: "quartana" — a fever that recurs every fourth day</note> presents with white urine, let a scarification be performed on the spine; if the fever is in the kidneys, scarification on the thigh. If bloodletting and scarifications do not help, then another cure must be applied. All types of fevers can arise even from individual principal organs. Every putrefaction has its own "digested matter" which boils and causes its own paroxysm; the number of paroxysms comes from this digestion. Moreover, the "digested matter" is the sequestered material of the disease. If a quartan fever with a white color lasts 6 weeks. If with a leek-green color, it lasts to 19, 20, or 21 weeks. If it begins with a cough, to 8 or 9 weeks. If with swelling of the feet, it lasts to 15 weeks. If a quartan fever changes into another fever, it will last a year.

<margin>What digested matter is.</margin> If a daily fever should arise from a quartan one, it lasts 16 months; if the patient loathes food, it will last four times longer. If a paroxysm is added within the hours, the fever is erratic. If the paroxysm weakens for a time and then the evil increases anew, it indicates that the "offending matter" is increasing.

<margin>A paroxysm of the blood sometimes bursts the veins.</margin> *Paroxysm of the blood*) A paroxysm of the blood is never so violent as to burst the veins; and if blood exits either through the urine or the nose, it is a good sign. The cure for a "foreign" fever proceeds from gold; another from coral, but a lesser cure exists in silver and pearls. *Description of silver*) Honey consumes silver; the honey is separated from the silver by repeated distillation in a water bath <note>original: "balneo" — referring to a bain-marie or heated bath used in alchemy and pharmacy</note>.

## *On internal conditions of the head.*
### COMMENTARIES.

*Digestion happens*) If the blood falls into a boiling state within itself and does not rest, then sleep must be induced. In the plague, if the sufferers do not sleep, use an anodyne <note>original: "anodyna" — a painkilling medicine</note> coupling. Paralysis can arise from a migraine <note>original: "Hemicranea"</note>. If the labors of the body proceed from the head, the head must be treated first. If a discharge comes from pains in the head, it is incurable. *In a cold state*) Use nightshade <note>original: "solatrum"</note>, crushed. *In a narcotic state*) Use darnel <note>original: "lolium"</note>, liquor of corals, houseleek <note>original: "semperuiua"</note>, rose, or pearl; let it be given externally. <margin>Preparation of corals.</margin> *2. Preparation of corals*) Burn according to this description on the place where the pain itself is; apply it with a cloth and do not remove it as long as the pain remains. *In the second and third species of head diseases*) Obstructions must be cleared and the channels opened.

### COMMENTARIES.

*On Paragraph II.*) If it comes from an abundance of blood, blood should be reduced there. It is not a "flow" from the head, as some think; otherwise, it would not infest only one tooth.

The small veins of the ears and the teeth are continuous.
*2. Bloodroot, lousewort, etc.*) In this recipe, the first three are "opening" medicines <note>original: "aperitiua" — treatments meant to clear blockages in the body's channels</note>; the other three are soothing. Pellitory <note>original: "Pyrethrum"</note> can create a drainage point; onions are opening.

*Surgical Cure*) Worms can be killed with *sperniolo* <note>a chemical or mineral preparation, possibly related to vitriol or a specific salt</note> as in a whitlow <note>original: "panaritio" — an infection of the fingertip, used here as an analogy for the infection in the tooth</note>; afterward, let the decay be removed with a gargle made of vinegar and honey.

# OTHER COMMENTARIES.
## *On afflictions of the teeth.*

<margin>Toothache is not a "flow," etc.</margin> *Toothache* cannot be a phlegmatic flow, nor can it come from the sharpness of salt or "choleric matter," as they say. Rather, its origin is in the place of the pain alone. Otherwise, if it came from the aforementioned sources, it could also cause swellings behind the ears <note>original: "parotidas"</note>. If the tooth and gums are good and <margin>How toothache happens.</margin> pain strikes, it arises from the fertility, goodness, or superfluity of the head—when the head abounds with too much blood and seeks an exit or waste-path. Every tooth has its own small vein; if this becomes overfilled with blood and seeks an exit, which cannot happen because of the hardness of the tooth, then it throbs and stings and sits at the root until it acquires an exit; this is a fault of the blood alone. But from a "purging of the head," not only toothaches would be born, but also parotid swellings and quinsy <note>original: "squinantia" — a severe inflammation of the throat/tonsils</note>, etc. From those stings, a swelling occurs—not because there is so much "offending matter" there, but because the arsenic <note>original: "Arsenicus" — here likely referring to a corrosive or "burning" quality of the humor rather than the pure element</note> is thus inflated by the stings. If the blood breaks through the gums, it raises watery vesicles on the surface of the gums, and the water is separated just as it appears in blood extracted through bloodletting, etc. Therefore, purging should not be used for toothaches, nor even bloodletting, because it is of no use. If, however, the tooth begins to rot by itself, which happens on-site, then it produces a rough scale, not unlike what happens in the fingernails. From that rot, a whitlow or scale is finally born, and it is similar to "Persian fire" <note>original: "ignis Persicus" — a historical term for various skin inflammations like shingles, anthrax, or erysipelas; here describing a burning infection</note>. For if that matter which is here in the tooth were in another limb or finger, a Persian fire would result. The roots of the bones have the greatest sensitivity. Every worm gnaws that in which and from which it was born: such as the worms of wood, of cloth, of the intestines, of the stomach, of the teeth, and of cheese, etc. <margin>Worms gnaw that from which they are born.</margin> It is even possible for a worm to corrode the entire tooth, for its whole power is an abundant sharpness and heat. On account of this, it cannot bear the air, and a great stench follows in the tooth, which is a sign of putrefaction.

*Cure of the teeth*) In the cure, it must be observed that a drainage point <note>original: "emunctorium"</note> be made, either for the blood or its wateriness; once this is done, the pain departs. It often happens that if the root of <margin>A good remedy against toothaches.</margin> bloodroot <note>original: "Tormentillæ"</note>, pellitory, or lousewort <note>original: "staphis agriæ"</note> is placed upon the tooth, the pain ceases, but it does not help everywhere. The above description, however, is effective. For it contains three opening medicines and three soothing ones. The former are bloodroot, lousewort, plantain seed, etc. The soothing ones are vinegar, henbane <note>original: "iusquiami"</note> root, poppy juice, etc. Truly, the "whitlow" of the teeth is similar in its cure to other whitlows.

# ON BOOKS XIII & XIV.
## On Pains of the Ears and Eyes.

<margin>Tinnitus and deafness are not in the place.</margin>
**Pain of the ears**) If the root of the ears came from the brain, tinnitus <note>ringing in the ears</note> and deafness could not arise from it. From the regions of the liver, its vaporous passage goes to the head, wherefore pains of the liver have something in common with pains of the head. But the stomach emits its vapors through its own emunctory <note>an organ or canal that carries off waste</note>, which is the mouth, etc. Tinnitus of the ears is not in the place <note>locally within the ear</note>, but comes from without. If the matter were in the place, it could exit with the excrement. Likewise, deafness is not in the place, but if that same matter were in another limb, it would set it on fire. Roughness or an inflammation <note>original: "Persicum vel paneritium" — terms used here for localized ear infections or inflammatory swellings</note>. Therefore, nothing should be poured into the ears, for it can generate tinnitus, etc. All recipes, unless they are composed of tutty <note>original: "Thutia" — zinc oxide, a mineral used in ointments</note>, do nothing at all for ear pains in general, etc. That excrement arises from a superfluity of good blood and good chyme; if it cannot find an exit, it generates parotid swellings <note>original: "parotidas" — swellings of the glands near the ear</note>, or even other ear pains.

*Cure.* It is necessary to clear the obstructions; the cure must be performed through anodynes <note>pain-relieving medicines</note>.

<margin>Nothing is to be poured into the ears.</margin>
<margin>The tritoma, an instrument for the ears.</margin>
*Take Tutty, etc. let a dry salve <note>original: "Sief" — a term for a dry medicinal powder or paste used in ophthalmology and otology</note> be made*) Let a poultice be made and placed on from the outside, etc. The cure for roughness and inflammation, when it has arisen from the place, is as was said above. The tritoma is an instrument for the ears mentioned by Albucasis <note>a famous 10th-century surgeon</note>: if deafness is present, all cure is in vain. For what nature once takes away, the physician can by no means restore, etc. No medicine is so subtle that it does not have something of tartar <note>in Paracelsian medicine, "tartar" refers to stony or crystalline precipitates that cause disease</note> with it. Wherefore if anything is poured into the ears, the tartar separates itself and sticks to the place, and then the disease becomes worse.

*Take seeds of Henbane, poppy, etc.*) This cure may also be effective for roughness and inflammation of the ears, for it is an anodyne. Whatever is not achieved through tutty must be achieved through an anodyne.

# ON AFFLICTIONS OF THE EYES.

<margin>What a cataract is.</margin>
A cataract, that is, the removal of the eyes or sight, is nothing other than an obstruction, and it can be cleared through instruments and return [to health], if an opening is made through the nape <note>original: "nucha" — here referring to the back of the neck or the spinal passage</note>, so that the nape is separated from the skull, etc. A scotoma <note>dark spots in the vision</note> is only a species of cataract: for if someone correctly distinguishes a cataract, he will also know the remaining species. However, for all species of eye pains, a collyrium <note>eyewash</note> can be given, which is useful in all passions of the eyes: *Take white vitriol <note>zinc sulfate</note>, etc.* You will never remove a scotoma without an instrument. In a scotoma, use the cure for a cataract: cauteries <note>burning tools or substances</note> made of quicklime and ashes should be placed on the back of the head. Both the ears and the eyes should be treated in the nape. Eyewashes should be made of consuming <note>original: "consumptivis" — substances that "eat away" or resolve excess matter</note> materials. Red eyes are to be moistened with bean and barley flour. Caution: Avoid corrosives and distilled substances.

# On *Dissolved Diseases:* from the Author’s Autograph.
## ON DISSOLVED [FLOWS].

**I** indeed say to you, that every flow comes from the dissolution and fusion of the substance of the three primes <note>original: "trium primorum" — the three fundamental substances of Paracelsian alchemy: Salt, Sulfur, and Mercury</note>.

This melting is threefold: one is taken from the flesh of the whole body; another is from the emunctory of the stomach through all the intestines. The third is of nourishment. One is from the exterior parts; it is called the dissolution of the intestines, proceeding from the stomach. The other is bodily, proceeding from minerals.

## DECLARATION.

These things must be declared in this manner. First, concerning the exterior things. If food is taken in, if it offends the stomach—either because of a new condition, or because of moisture, or through a bad concordance—then the separation <note>the vital process of separating useful nutrients from waste</note> fails. For separation wants to take place in heat, which the constitution of the aforementioned things removes. When separation is hindered, there follows the digestion of raw matter, which itself cannot be properly digested. From this emerges white urine—that is, watery, moist, superfluous, undigested, and raw in its primary substance. For everything that is led into the liver lacks both separation and true digestion. Therefore, the urine is also such, the stomach is untimely, and the color and strength turn out similarly. For where separation ceases, there is excess in the excrements.

But the fact that red and white excrements pass occurs by reason of the urine because of its wateriness, which produces no colors other than those mentioned. Whatever matter is at hand, the digestive virtue digests into nourishment, which is like a ruby. But because separation was not performed there, that nourishment is spurious, and the liver does not attract it. Therefore, it is thrust out of the body as it is, and the stool likewise gives forth dissolved nourishment, without form, appearance, or genuine nature, just as any immature thing is constituted.

<margin>Red urine signifies fevers with dysentery.</margin>
But if white matter should go out, the cause is indeed similar: yet it differs in this, that the sulfur is colored into whiteness by this reasoning: because coldness whitens sulfur, just as its nature is.

Furthermore, if other colors should go out, the cause would be that the matter in the stomach degenerates into putrefaction, in which various colors arise according to the time of digestion.

Thickness }
Thinness } all from putrefaction and urine
Wateriness } mixed together.

The fact that it does not smell like other dung is from the untimely digestion of the stomach, which did not proceed according to the order of nature. Therefore, in a dissolution, no other cause is to be understood than that the stomach putrefies, then digestion follows. Now, if digestion is good and separation is lacking, it is Dysentery. But if separation is present and not digestion, it is Lientery <note>a form of diarrhea where food is passed undigested</note>: if both are lacking, Diarrhea is present. But if putrefaction of the stomach matter is present, a flux of the belly occurs with various colors.

Therefore, from these things it must be known that diseases of this kind do not arise from the body, but only from things ingested. But the reason the body wastes away is that it dries itself out; for because it does not have nourishment, it is dried within itself. That it flows for a longer time...

# ANOTHER FRAGMENT
## ON THE DISSOLVED DISEASE
<note>The "dissolved disease" (morbus dissolutus) refers to conditions where the body's solid or stable substances seem to "melt" or "dissolve" into liquid waste, typically covering various types of chronic diarrhea or wasting fluxes.</note>

### PARAGRAPH I.
#### *Definition of the dissolved disease in general.*

<margin>Two types of dissolved diseases.</margin> There are two types of dissolved diseases: Elemental and Mineral. That is to say, the outer type and the type of substance. The first type has its root in the stomach, along with the regions of both the emunctories <note>organs or canals that carry off waste, such as the sweat glands or excretory system</note>, the intestines, and the urinary paths. For every dissolved disease is twofold in itself regarding its species, namely arising from the same matter. But the second type, which is different, has its root in the flesh, descending and gathering in the stomach, and is finally emitted through the emunctories of both paths.

### PARAGRAPH II.
#### *The cause of the first type of disease.*

But pay attention to what the cause of this may be: All things that descend into the stomach require separations and digestions beforehand. If it is not separated and digested, then the **Red Dissolution** <note>original: "Dissolutus Rubeus" — likely referring to bloody flux or dysentery</note> is generated. If it is separated but not digested, this is the cause of the **White Dissolution**. And if it is neither separated nor digested, whether to a greater or lesser degree, then the **Dissolution of the belly** is born. From these <margin>How the Red Dissolution is generated.</margin> causes, various sicknesses appear to exist, though they are from the same cause; for the reason for this plurality is the various and differing nature of man, the various types of Elements, the diverse nature of the Seasons, the putrefactions of the Air, or whether something is present to a greater or lesser degree.

### PARAGRAPH III.
#### *The process of the cause of the dissolved disease.*

Let us return now to the process of the cause of the first type, which is as follows. Everything that exists in a viscous coagulation is dissolved by a superfluous watery quality. Once this is dissolved, it must be noted: if it turns into a dissolution before the separation of the matter, or if it does so before digestion, or if it lacks the expulsive power, it likewise goes into a dissolution after that. From this, it must be most greatly observed that the pure will remain with the impure (the aforementioned cause impeding it) in a viscous mass coagulated by the Watery quality. For from these two, the Dissolution takes its origin. And when the first operations have failed, one waits in vain for the second and third matter. Therefore, the matter and the place are attributed to the stomach, as are the pain, the disease, and the "sin" <note>original: "peccatum" — in a medical context, this often refers to a "fault" or functional error in the organ's natural process</note>.

### PARAGRAPH IV.
#### *The species and variety of the dissolved disease, and concerning monstrous putrefactions.*

Furthermore, we shall speak of those things which are born from the generated disease, such as the urine and the stool. Regarding what pertains to the urine, they are these: Urine that is white, watery, and plentiful, without the substance of urine. The reason is this: because it is not urine, but a superfluity. Indeed, the urine makes its exit mixed with the dregs. But if the superfluity should be tinged with redness, judge the disease to be fatal. For the matter of the stool will adhere to it, and it is without the substance of true urine, just as it lacks good substance.

Regarding the stool, however, it must be known that if it is red, it is a sign of the first dissolution. The reason is that the nourishments are cooked into a raw "Ruby" <note>original: "Rubinum" — a term likely used for a deep red, undigested state of chyme</note>; they will therefore remain in the stomach and appear under a raw, blood-like color. <margin>How the dissolution is to be judged from the stool.</margin> But if it is white, it is a sign of good separation but no digestion, an indication of the second Dissolution; for those things which are separated pass into a white sulfur <note>paracelsian chemistry often used "sulfur" to describe the combustible or oily qualities of substances</note>. But if the beginning of the dissolution was the cause, and those things which are not digested keep their color along with the rest; and if neither of the two were present (that is, neither the generation of the first nor the second), then the Dissolution of the belly is born with various colors—yellowish or others—for it takes its rise from putrefactions.

### PARAGRAPH V.
#### *On the special cause of other diseases.*

The first cooked Red dissolution is raw and mixed, and it is healed with its whole substance in the stomach. But if it emits more stool than food, consider it a long-term bad guardianship <note>original: "custodiam" — referring here to the body's internal management or retention of nutrients</note>. But if parts of the body are consumed, it is a sign of a dire appetite, lacking the matter of nourishment. If it becomes discolored, then that defect creates that cause. Moreover, the second dissolved disease occupies the same place and the aforementioned things. But the third is distinguished from them in this: that its matter putrefies before it exits. This putrefaction is shown in various ways, but it pertains neither to the cure nor to the Theory. Other things which happen occur by chance and do not have a certain indication, such as Twisting of the guts, Nausea, Weakness, Plenitude, swelling of the *Schiza* <note>original: "Schizæ" — possibly referring to a fissure or a specific anatomical part of the lower abdomen</note>, and similar things, which may or may not come.

### PARAGRAPH VI.
#### *On the Signs of the dissolution: of life, health, and death.*

Regarding the sign of life, this must be held: That if the stool should be thickened by its own dispositions, without griping pain or nausea, it is the beginning of restoration and good health. If, however, it should flow into the looseness of the intestines, it is a sign of health with Remedies. But if there is a localized tremor, or a febrile motion with a paralytic collapse, and a flooding of the eyes, these are grave signs; namely, there is hope for safety only with extreme Medicines, otherwise it signifies death. And if a ringing in the ears should concur with the sign of the mouth, a trembling tongue, and floods of tears, it signifies the approach of death. And this is the most certain sign, if hunger of the limbs should concur, and it is the last.

### PARAGRAPH VII.
#### *A declaration of the CURE for the dissolved disease.*

Furthermore,

## PARAGRAPH IX.
### The cause of the mineral dissolved disease.
Now, for the second "dissolved" type, one must attend to the Mineral, which arises from the dissolved salt from the three primes <note>The "Tria Prima" of Paracelsus: Salt, Sulfur, and Mercury</note>. This indeed proceeds from parts of minerals, whether from the whole or a particular place, and it is a dissolution of its own substance, from which follows the ruin of the body—not with violence or speed, but through chronic dissolutions.

<margin>All dissolved things are deposited in the stomach.</margin>
## PARAGRAPH X.
### The process of the dissolved mineral.
Furthermore, after the separation of the Sun <note>Gold or the vital essence</note> from the Three Primes, the matter flows together into one, and again penetrates into its own proper substance; like salt, it corrodes, dissolves, and resolves it, and each thing that is dissolved is placed in the stomach and then removed through the stool. For everything from minerals that passes into the waste of the mineral is driven into the place of waste—that is, into the stomach. Hence the "contrariety" or upset of the stomach takes its origin from an alien guest.

## PARAGRAPH XI.
### Signs of the dissolved mineral disease from Elemental signs.
If it does not observe the crisis according to the Elemental critical days <note>original: "cretico" — referring to the system of 'critical days' in traditional medicine</note>, remember that it is dissolved from a mineral. For the Elemental has its own proper "Cretic" period. The Mineral also has its own innate one, as is perceived regarding the Cretic. But these signs are more certain to the common Physician: Elemental care achieves nothing; the disease exceeds Elemental limits; the patient suffers without acute pains. There is a certain daily number of bowel movements; he fares well in the three digestions; they can sleep; they desire to take food; they have excessive thirst; in other matters of substance, the head is similar to an Elemental disease.

# CHAPTER I. PARAGRAPH I.
## On Worms.

<margin>Worms arise either from tartar or from minerals.</margin>
**W**orms arise and are made from two principles: one exists from the genus of Tartar; the other from minerals. Now, first, that which comes from Tartar lies in the stomach, in the liver, and in the kidneys. That which arises from minerals lies in its own parts.

From these things it should be understood that from the red nutriment, if it comes from the liver into the limbs, then no worms are generated. <margin>What the types of worms are.</margin> For worms are made partly from putrefaction, partly from the nature of spiders, partly from excrement, partly from the chaos <note>the fundamental unformed matter</note> of the body—such as flies, etc.—and partly from sweat—such as lice, etc. Therefore, concerning worms, it must further be known that many things come to be considered here: types, locations, etc. Likewise, there are worms of Earth, Water, Fire, and Air. From these four, derive the generation and cause of each genus, namely of Tartar and of Minerals.

### On Tartar first.
Concerning Tartar in the beginning, recognize four types of worms, and the same in a double generation: namely, if worms are born from rot, it happens according to the four Elements. Similarly, if worms are generated without putrefaction, the same also happens from the four Elements: one is putrefactive, the other is material. Distinguish this well.

### The process of Tartar.
Now, if Tartar is in the body, there is within it "worm-like matter" from which they are produced. Moreover, they are twofold. For the worm-like matter is either with or without putrefaction. Therefore, if the worm-like matter goes into putrefaction, then the cause is [N.]. If it passes into worms without putrefaction, the cause is [N.]. And you shall note these things for the sake of the cure.

# BOOK SIX
# OF THE GREAT MONARCH
## THEOPHRASTUS OF HOHENHEIM.
<note>Paracelsus often styled himself as the "Monarch of Medicine" to assert his dominance over traditional academic authorities.</note>

# FIRST TREATISE ON THE
## CAUSES OF TARTARIC DISEASES.
<note>The term <term>Tartar</term> refers to stony deposits in the body, such as kidney stones or gouty crystals, which Paracelsus compared to the hard "tartar" crust left in wine barrels.</note>

### CHAPTER ONE.

*From whence Tartaric diseases are generated: and this is the*

#### PREFACE.

<margin>God is the creator of experience.</margin>
**B**ut what shall I establish and define here, since my own senses on one hand, and the stubborn disagreement of my predecessors in Medicine on the other, make me doubtful and hesitant? While I consider the possibility of curing <term>lithiasis</term> <note>original: "lithiasis"; stone-forming diseases</note> and <term>podagra</term> <note>original: "podagrae"; gout of the feet</note> within myself: and turn over in my mind the excessive despair of the ancient Chaldeans and Arabs regarding these diseases: to which faction, I ask, should I finally give my support and adherence? Should I follow my own opinion, which has met with such prosperous success everywhere: or should I embrace the prescriptions of the ancients, by adhering to which I could never reach the desired goal? And although a prudent counsel always dictates and persuades us to support certain discoveries (shaking off the ambiguous), the authority of the ancient, highly skilled Physicians cannot help but cause me to approach the publishing of my works—being still of younger years—with some terror and a certain trepidation. For I see that I must diligently attend to this: that while I give my modern views to the public, I do not simply demand the removal of the ancient Authors' decrees; rather, as if by a tug on the ear, I remind them through those same authors to employ more prudence, circumspection, and diligent faith in bringing forth our new writings.

Therefore, while we begin to comment on the "incurable" diseases arising from Tartar, we insist upon a solid foundation and reason, and we shall dismiss all ambiguous treatises, setting before our eyes that most pure and refined
<margin>The Virgin Experience, mother of all arts.</margin>
"Virgin Experience," who, even without a male addition, is the mother and discoverer of all the arts. She alone shall be the authentic and indubitable witness of all our commentaries: for from her alone flows the origin of understanding these diseases. She is the one helper we shall consult and embrace in curing and healing them. Meanwhile, we shall continually keep in our minds, from the first to the last, Him who created this wise and ingenious Virgin Experience, and through Him, we shall gaze upon this image. Since this powerful Virgin Experience, with singular favor, offers and promises herself to be such a helpful assistant to us, under her auspices we shall fearlessly begin our undertaking; and having declined the erroneous wanderings of the ancients, we shall set our sails straight (as they say) to the winds. We shall boast all the more confidently in our foundation because the ancients do not make mention of our experiments by even a single word: just as we shall make none of theirs. Truly, it is a joy to us that by this method, the utter ignorance and lack of skill of one of us will be revealed. Nor can we help but greatly exult over the discovery of this new hope, of which the ancients, as far as can be seen, had no knowledge, but rather entered the doors and sanctuaries of experience like one-eyed men. Meanwhile, we are not so envious as to not
<margin>What the Author's purpose is.</margin>
greatly admire their subtle genius, because with such zeal and affection, mindful of brotherhood and human faith, they labored and spent all their discoveries for the public health and benefit. Therefore, led by their example, let us also rouse our tender years and mind, and briskly establish and compose these six chapters, namely in two treatises: one of which, dealing with causes and origin, is Theoretical; the other, on the cure, is Practical. At the same time, many things are brought forth from experience concerning many of those diseases of people who suffer from and are afflicted by Tartar.

Hither, therefore, turn your attention more swiftly, you Great Lords with <term>chiragra</term> <note>original: "Chiragrici"; gout in the hands</note>, and Princes with foot-gout, and from our writings which we bring forth, learn more closely what the cause is that you are tested and
<margin>A cure for Tartar is possible.</margin>
crushed by these pains much more than the common people. And let this not seem a difficult thing to you, that I offer the possibility of a cure against so many ancient authors and their followers crying out loudly to the contrary. But what we promise you in this preface, receive and believe with full confidence: and persuade your Tartar-afflicted limbs of it, so that they may place and cast a certain hope in these our writings, and fully comply with our precepts and advice.

<header>ON DISEASES FROM TARTAR</header>

...lest they perchance fall sometime into the bloody hands of the imperial executioners. But now, cutting short this preface, let us begin the sixth book of our Medicine and bring forth, without delay, what will be of use to you.

## CHAPTER II.

<margin>The causes of Tartaric diseases are either food or formative nature.</margin>
**T**o those of us about to hand down the cure and healing of Tartaric diseases and gouty affections, it is especially fitting—indeed, necessary—that we recognize the causes and origin of these illnesses. The reasoning behind these causes is twofold: for one cause lies in those things that inflict such diseases upon us from the outside; the other lies in nature itself, which forms the disease in such a way within us. We shall discuss the primary origin in this discourse.

<margin>All food is initially crude.</margin>
Whatever is placed outside our body and then taken into it is formed from three material things <note>The "Tria Prima": Salt, Sulfur, and Mercury, which Paracelsus believed were the building blocks of all matter.</note> and ends in one, as we shall say regarding generations. These three things are, from their very production by nature, crude and coarse, and they are never brought forth without some dregs; rather, they always carry something wild and alien hidden within their substance, from which Tartaric diseases eventually arise. For example, smoke seems inseparable from fire; and yet, it contains within itself a certain substance similar to stones or <term>Tartar</term> <note>original: "Tartaro"; Paracelsus used this term for any stony or crystalline deposit in the body, comparing it to the hard crust found in wine barrels.</note>. This is because it has a light body that is not one with the fire, as we shall establish more explicitly in our writings on transmutations. <margin>Smoke is a cause of tartar.</margin> If this smoke should ever penetrate deep into the body, it is then resolved into water and either excreted through the bladder or it gives birth to other diseases. But if the nature of the smoke is such that it cannot be resolved (as we shall teach concerning the properties of smoke), then it adheres to the boundaries and regions of the stomach, the veins, and the intestines, or other cavities and members of the body, until at last it <unclear>hardens</unclear> <note>original: "coaduletur"; likely a form of "coaguletur," meaning to congeal or harden into a solid.</note>, as will appear more clearly from the following chapters. <margin>Tartaric diseases from smoke.</margin> Thus, one must judge this smoke as something that, by its own varied nature, gives birth to various and diverse Tartaric diseases. For some occur in certain places, <margin>Of Wood.</margin> such as those whose smoke comes from wood; others among those who boil salt, whose smoke is mixed with salty vapor; others among miners, who inhale metallic smoke during the smelting process. <margin>Of Minerals.</margin> And the Tartaric diseases of these people are particularly manifold and almost infinite, for the reason that the inhaled smoke is sometimes from sulfur, sometimes from antimony, sometimes from arsenic, and so on. Similarly, there is a diversity within the metals themselves: thus the smoke of gold is one thing, silver another, mercury another, copper another, lead another, iron another, tin another. But this metallic smoke is particularly harmful to scribes, blacksmiths, and those who master iron with fire, because of the <term>cadmia</term> <note>original: "cadmiam"; a term used for zinc ores or the metallic soot produced in furnaces.</note>. Furthermore, another even more serious kind of Tartaric disease comes from the distillations used by alchemists, goldsmiths, refiners, coin-makers, and the like, and finally by Physicians themselves who occupy themselves with such things. For the various types of these produce various Tartaric diseases. Some are inflicted by sublimations, which are many; for some are produced by the sublimation of mercury, others of sal ammoniac, others of arsenic, realgar, orpiment, etc. <margin>Reverberation.</margin> Some are brought in by the smoke of a <term>reverberatory furnace</term> <note>original: "Reuerberae"; a furnace that reflects heat onto the material being treated.</note>. Here two things concur: one from the wood, the other from the material itself, which is already complex. <margin>Distillation.</margin> So too, a different smoke flows down from distillation, from <term>Strong Waters</term> <note>original: "Aquis fortibus"; nitric acid or other mineral acids used to dissolve metals.</note>, from balsams, from oils, turpentines, and similar things, the subtle vapor of all of which falls and penetrates in various ways. Nay, diseases are even generated from the air, which indeed lacks visible smoke, but nevertheless carries the three primary natures through breathing; from which, afterwards, manifold Tartaric diseases are generated in various ways—through dust and through wind, which, being trapped in the internal parts, becomes coagulated. <margin>Tartaric disease from air.</margin>

<margin>Tartaric disease from nourishment.</margin>
But Tartaric diseases are generated much more frequently and powerfully from nourishment. For there is nothing anywhere that we enjoy that is not, in its origin, something that has a certain coagulation within it. Although this may not appear perfect to our sight, it is nevertheless perfected at last by the body, which is disposed toward it. <margin>Legumes.</margin> Thus, every legume has its own peculiar coagulations, such as beans, peas, lentils, pears, apples, and other similar things. If the coagulation of these were to happen and be prepared before our very eyes (as we shall comment on regarding transmutations), the causes of Tartaric diseases would then be visible to us. <margin>The similar preparation of Art and Nature.</margin> For it must be understood that the same thing happens in the same way within nature itself. A certain peculiar diversity is also stored in meats, which, when ingested, are easily disposed toward Tartaric diseases. <margin>Aromatic meats etc.</margin> But they are formed much more from spices, from which very hard and sharp Tartaric diseases are inflicted. <margin>Wines.</margin> The same judgment must be made concerning wines, beers, honey-waters, and waters, from each of which Tartaric diseases arise. For every single wine produces both Tartar and Tartaric diseases of a dual nature. For one Tartar approaches the nature of wine-tartar; the other is somewhat similar to dregs. <margin>Beers.</margin> So also beer generates a sandy and crumbly Tartar, and thus gout, from the coagulation of the water, hops, and grains from which the beer is prepared. For since each of these has its own separate coagulation, if they are all joined at last, they procreate a peculiar and heavy Tartar, the parent of various diseases. <margin>Waters.</margin> Water itself also generates a singular Tartar, but one of less pain, unless it happens to be aluminous, sulfurous, or vitriolic, etc. <margin>Dairy products. Strong medicines.</margin> A variety of Tartar arises from dairy products. These are tenacious, mucous, acidic, difficult to expel, numerous, and quite thick. By a similar reasoning, a Tartar of peculiar property and nature comes from sharp medicines. Such are those that undergo sublimation, or leave dregs when distilled, or are affected in some other way. <margin>Sugar, Honey.</margin> Sugar itself is also coagulated in the body in many forms, as are honey and other sharp species, which by their heat coagulate whatever is incorporated into them.

Thus, therefore, in many ways and from many things, Tartaric diseases can arise, which surely coagulate themselves in the body, so that a certain residue remains in those places where they were hidden and stored. But this same substance of Nature can also coagulate in every way, without regard for the property of the things ingested, through which (as we have recounted) Tartaric diseases are born, in the form of a coagulation that might be induced because of some other accident. <margin>Coagulation is twofold.</margin> This happens in a twofold generation, namely...

<summary>Paracelsus explains that "Tartaric" diseases like gout and stones are caused by "Tartar"—impure, stony residues found in everything we consume, including food, wine, air, and metallic vapors from mining or alchemy. He argues that the body can fail to process these crude substances, leading them to harden and stick to internal organs and joints.</summary>

<page-num>557</page-num>
-># TRACTATUS I.<-
-><note>Tractate I</note><-

namely of the Assumed <note>Things taken into the body, such as food and drink.</note> and the Internal.

<margin>By reason of the things Assumed and of Nature itself.</margin> But besides this, there is another origin from which Tartaric diseases are born. This, to be sure, flourishes in nature alone, and does not flow from any external thing present at birth. Thus, the Humors, Qualities, complexions, members, bones, arteries, etc., organize and coagulate their own substance out of the perversity and malice of their own nature. <margin>Cruel Tartaric diseases: and they are not cured.</margin> And if Tartaric diseases are the worst of all, they are also, for various reasons, the least able to be cured. For they are fixed into nature itself, just as they are born entirely from it. Since nature itself headstrictly leans toward these, its force and course can by no means be inhibited. For it is not within the power of the Physician to take away and abolish a disposition of nature that is more deeply implanted. For nature itself is directed and inclined not only toward good or evil, but also toward diseases and health. <margin>The Physician cannot abolish Nature.</margin> This innate and implanted disposition of nature can be repealed by no reasoning. One may indeed, in some part, diminish and stop those very outlets from which Tartaric diseases are made; but to change the cause itself is impossible. As long as the body lives and survives, it is compelled to bear and carry around this contamination within itself, unless perchance some <term>Fifth Essence</term> <note>The "Quinta Essentia" was believed by alchemists to be the purest form of a substance, capable of extraordinary healing or transformation.</note> made from gold or similar things is administered, which might, as it were, convert the whole body, restore it, and so renew it that it is rendered similar to a <margin>The Fifth Essence of Gold renews man.</margin> newly born infant. And indeed, we neither credit nor take away from nature or art regarding this renewal; nonetheless, we deem it possible in the manner handed down concerning the Fifth Essence.

Furthermore, since we have thus far discussed the origin and causes of Tartaric diseases: we shall next define more clearly what Tartaric diseases are born from there. We by no means concede that Tartaric diseases emerge only from the dregs and coagulations that exist in all things; for from those same things, other non-Tartaric diseases can also be born. <margin>What Tartaric diseases are and of what kind. 1. 2. 3. 4. 5. 6.</margin> For we call those diseases "Tartaric" which are born in the body like <term>Tartar</term> <note>original: "Tartarus"; a term used to describe stony or crust-like deposits, named after the hard sediment found in wine barrels.</note>. Thus in <term>Podagra</term> <note>Gout of the foot.</note> the Tartar is like a small stone, round, flowing, angular, and conspicuous and sensible in many other ways and forms. It is similar also in <term>Chiragra</term> <note>Gout of the hand.</note>. From this category also are the "little sands" <note>Gravel or small crystals.</note> born in the kidneys and bladder, and in other places. Here also belong the <term>calculi</term> or stones, both loose and fixed, in the bladder and kidneys, in which two places alone they are generated. Afterward, we must also refer to the coagulated things that persist in the intestines and other hollow places into which food and excrement turn. Furthermore, "congelations" are also numbered here, which stick in the pores of the skin, flesh, and bones. Finally, the "hardened" things belong here, which linger in the veins, arteries, and nerves, from which many hidden diseases emerge, produced from concealed causes. For through stones and Tartars of this kind, the nutritional veins are obstructed and blocked, so that they die off from a lack of food. Sometimes even the intestine of the anus or rectum is stuffed, so that death is brought on by filth that blocks and stops the exit of nature. Sometimes the spermatic veins are also blocked, which obstruction is then followed by impotence, the frustration of emission, and many similar things. Then also the Tartars that stick in the skin are subtle and thin, born from sweat, the signs of which are the <term>scabies</term> <note>Itchy skin eruptions or mange.</note>, itching, and stinging of the skin. And so concerning the rest.

Furthermore, we will also explain to you by what reasoning and in what form these kinds of Tartaric diseases are generated, both from things assumed and from nature itself, and for what causes those stones are made. <margin>How Tartar is generated from smoke.</margin> First, regarding Tartaric diseases generated from smoke or vapors, this mode of generation must be held. Whenever smoke and vapor <margin>Tartar is made in two places of the body: either external or internal.</margin> touch the body, it has two ways of "Tartarization": one external, the other internal. That which touches the body from the outside, as for the sake of example, the eyes: this first makes them wet and dripping; afterward, the same smoke is mixed with tears and penetrates the pores of the eyes, and occupies their corners and cavities. At last, when the water is consumed and dried up, there remains in its place the dregs and certain remains of the substance, which would have adhered to other chimneys like soot. Similarly, if the body sweats and also breathes out smoke, a certain mixing occurs which, working its way into the pores, is coagulated there like the former examples and is deposited in the folds of the skin. And this is the reasoning for external things. But if smoke penetrates the interior, then wherever it adheres and attaches itself, there it remains. Thus if it should rush into the stomach, <margin>In the stomach.</margin> the humor of the stomach is mixed with it, and it becomes one mixture. As soon as the humors are consumed, however, sand or stone remains there, grown onto and attached to the region or the linings of the stomach, which afterward becomes the author and cause of many diseases, as will be said hereafter. It also happens that materials of this kind are attracted and drawn out by the liver from the <margin>In the liver and other parts.</margin> stomach; as also by other members. When their humors are consumed, stones and "little sands" are born from the surviving remains in the liver, in the veins, in the intestines, and in the spleen: just as stones are also born in the gall not only of man, but also of cattle, in the manner and way aforesaid.

The same thing should be understood in the same way regarding the kidneys and bladder, and all other remaining members: namely, that Tartar is attracted to those places along with the nutrients themselves; in which, if it sticks and lingers too long, it completes its operation. <term>Podagra</term> is the attraction of this <margin>Podagra: why and how it happens.</margin> coagulation, made with the nutrients toward the joints, in which it stays, and cannot be carried further, because the paths positioned below the joints are not hollow, wherefore the matter of Tartar cannot reside in them. And even if it were carried into the pores and passages, it would still be consumed by the abundant heat of the body, and not in such a way that it could be heaped up in the joints. For where in the <margin>Why more is collected in the joints than in the flesh.</margin> members the heat and virtue are weak: there the matter can be piled up and gathered. Moreover, much more of the humors is consumed in the joints than in the flesh. Therefore, where there is much consumption, there are also more copious remains. The same thing should likewise be understood concerning all foods and the air, namely those things which we assume and breathe in, that they are coagulated within us in those places and limits just as we have reviewed.

But those Tartars which are born from a vice of nature itself, such as some of these that arise in the blood and all the veins, [follow] their own gene[ration]...

Phlegm as it is separated and turns to tartar.

### CHAPTER III.

**S**ince we have so far explained the origin and mode of generation of Tartaric diseases, it is now next that we also explain by what reasoning and manner this Resolution and Coagulation occurs, while it indeed pervades and penetrates the whole body in every direction, and why it does not stop in the nearest seat or immediate neighborhood. Of the primary causes there are two: one is subtlety <note>fineness or thinness of a substance</note>, the other is thickness <note>original: "crassities"; density or coarseness</note>. Understand it this way: Subtlety penetrates the entire body; and the subtler a thing is, the further and wider it overflows. Thickness resides in the immediate vicinity, because it cannot penetrate the veins and pores. But besides these, those causes must also be known through which Tartar is expelled to the outermost and lowest parts. Of these causes there are three: one is from the faculty of the Attractive virtue, which attracts nourishment, together with and in which the Tartar itself is also lured to all members. The second is from the mixture, by which Tartar insinuates itself into the blood and is mixed with it, and finally, withdrawing again at its own time, turns aside into the joints and the skin.

<margin>
Subtlety and thickness are the cause of further penetration.
</margin>

The third cause is that between the materials from which the Tartar is born and the parts of the body, a certain property and familiarity exists, and it moves toward them. Hence, if it reaches the parts, its moisture is consumed, and the remains abound, as we explained a little earlier.

From these three causes proceeds the distribution, made to those parts in which the Tartaric diseases are established. To these a cause is added: that the material sometimes stays behind somewhere and is not carried as far as its property and attraction were going to lead it.

Furthermore, we shall also explain the reasons why one Tartar exists as subtler or thicker than another. This diversity depends on the nature of those things from which the Tartar was born. Thus, the Tartar of common water is much ruder and thicker than that of wine. Hence it happens that the thickness of watery Tartar penetrates very little into the body, while on the contrary, the subtlety of wine Tartar is carried out to the outermost seats. This is the very reason why wine Tartar is distributed deeply through the whole body and produces diseases everywhere, whereas the Tartar of water is accumulated and congealed in at least one place. The same reasoning applies to other foods, drinks, fumes, and all things we have mentioned: in all of them, thickness and subtlety must be similarly estimated. Thus, fumes also uniquely adhere in the inner parts rather than the nearby ones, unless some property happens to cling to the smoke, because of which it is fixed immediately in the first places; or unless it is of such a nature that as soon as it feels another nature, it immediately adheres. So indeed sulfur, since it is not sublimated into more distant parts, does not enter the more distant parts in the body itself, but fixes its Tartar immediately in the stomach. But the smoke that goes to distant parts, such as that of <term>Sal Ammoniac</term> <note>Ammonium chloride, known for its volatility</note> and Mercury: their Tartar wanders more penetratingly to all members in the body itself, and by continuous permeation they flee to the outermost seats of the body, meanwhile leaving their seed everywhere in all the places they have traversed. However, the smoke of Arsenic by no means does this in the same way, but fixes itself collectively in distant places, according to how it is driven and moved. From the weighing of these causes, we understand that some Tartaric diseases arise and are born in only one place; for example, if smoke from <term>Aqua Fortis</term> <note>Nitric acid, literally "strong water"</note> or similar things is attracted into one or another place, and there it is mixed and appropriated to the part, then coagulation and freezing occur simultaneously and collectively in that place alone. As far as the property of foods and nutrients is concerned, that mention seems superfluous here, since they are treated abundantly elsewhere, and especially in the previous chapters.

<margin>
Tartar of water is thicker than that of wine.
</margin>

<margin>
Tartar of wine is more penetrating.
</margin>

<margin>
The Tartar of sulfur does not go to distant parts.

# TREATISE I.

<margin>Appropriation is a defect in the cause of the distribution of nourishment.</margin>
The action follows which we are accustomed to call <term>Tartaric diseases</term> <note>These are ailments Paracelsus believed were caused by "Tartar"—metabolic waste that hardens into stones or crystals, similar to the crusty sediment found in wine barrels.</note>. The reason why this happens through mixing is not merely the mixing that occurs in the stomach—as we have already said regarding the union of nutrients and Tartar—but this same mixing also occurs similarly in that joining outside the stomach. For instance, it occurs within the four <term>complexions</term> <note>The "four complexions" refer to the ancient medical theory of the four humors: sanguine, choleric, melancholic, and phlegmatic.</note> and the four substances of the entire body. Just as we defined this regarding one side of the stomach, we will likewise conclude the ultimate causes of separation, which itself happens through the **appropriation** of the things consumed, which look toward specific parts and limbs. Thus, things that are pleasing and useful to the veins produce diseases in the veins. Things that benefit the stomach deposit Tartar in the stomach. Let this be the judgment for all other limbs as well. However, let us also remember that it can happen that Tartaric diseases are generated in all locations of the body by the force of this appropriation. For whatever we consume benefits the whole body everywhere, and yet a Tartaric disease arises in only one single place.

<margin>A fine objection</margin>
But the cause of this matter is a certain **Resolution** <note>In this context, "Resolution" refers to the body's natural ability to dissolve or break down these stony deposits before they cause harm.</note>, which melts and resolves the Tartar in some places, but not at all in others. For unless that Resolution occurred and was administered by nature within the body, it would surely be necessary for all men everywhere to exist as <term>gouty</term>, <term>hand-gouty</term>, and <term>stone-suffering</term> <note>original: "Podagricos, chiragricos & calculosos"; referring to gout of the feet, gout of the hands, and kidney/bladder stones.</note>.

<margin>Why not all men are Gouty etc.</margin>
From this it is clear that Tartariness arises only in those places where there is no Resolution. Therefore, we now have the cause ready at hand: namely, that Resolution fails equally in an equal limb. For example, if there is no resolution in one joint, there will be none in another similar to it; therefore, the Tartar immediately yields to and adheres to the joints. This is similarly to be understood regarding other parts.

<margin>Why Tartar chiefly adheres to the joints. All such Tartar is of this kind.</margin>
Next, so that you may understand the cause of why Tartar especially remains in the joints and is consumed neither by Nature nor by time, you should turn your mind to this point: all Tartariness is of such a nature. If it is coagulated and granulated, it can be resolved by hot water and digested or changed into a watery liquid and sweated out. Similarly, if it is moist by nature and has not been coagulated by intense dryness, it can be resolved by itself, like <term>calcined Tartar</term> <note>Tartar that has been burned to a white ash; here used to describe deposits "baked" by the body's internal heat.</note>. For saltiness and Tartariness are calcined in the body by the heat of the internal limbs, no differently than by fire. But if the Tartariness remains, the cause is this: it cannot be resolved. For when it is too dry and parched, it therefore comes together and coagulates into a stone, or into many small pebbles, according to how both the property of the Tartar and the mixture of salt behave. Thus, for this reason, it remains as a survivor.

<margin>There are three causes of gouty attacks.</margin>
And from this very cause arise the periods or cycles <note>original: "periodi seu typi"</note> of this disease, by which the pain is felt more or less at one time or another. For it is pleasing to set down this discourse of natural causes. If the air and weather are more humid, then the body itself and all its substance becomes moist, as we teach in our *Philosophy*. Now, therefore, if the body is soaked with such humidity, then by its own nature and property, the Tartar is also moistened and afterward begins to liquefy and resolve. While it is attempting this, it changes its nature, force, and power; it boils up, as it were, and swells and puffs up within itself. From this commotion, the sharpest pains are inflicted upon the tendons; and yet, not all the Tartar is resolved. For the dryness and the property which is not fit for resolution stands in the way to some extent in its own fashion. Hence it happens that hot fomentations <note>Warm, medicinal compresses.</note> sometimes benefit the sick because the heat dries it out again and thus soothes it. Sometimes cold things are useful because they congeal it. Sometimes temperate things help because they restrain both excesses and make it so the Tartar cannot go anywhere worse. Sometimes moist things help because the resolution is continued as far as possible; when this is done, rest is induced. Often dry things also soothe because they take away the humidity and remove the agitation. Frequently, <term>Anodynes</term> <note>Pain-relieving medications.</note> are also beneficial, namely narcotics.

<margin>Influence of the heavens, especially the Moon.</margin>
Furthermore, the <term>paroxysms</term> <note>Sudden attacks or increases in symptoms.</note> are also increased or diminished by influence, either increasing or failing, in this way: if the Moon is waning, the disease is also diminished, and yet pain presses at the same time, namely because the hot or natural virtue is weak while the disease is stronger. But with the Moon waxing, the pains more often stab, because the influx is too great and it boils up in that place. Similarly, one must judge concerning other motions or constitutions of the sky, whether hotter or colder, according to whose proportion the diseases are also intensified, diminished, or varied. Even if all such influences are not known to us, it is easy for us to think that a certain singular force and power dwells above us, which dominates and rules us.

<margin>The higher things moderate us.</margin>
But we let this go for now. Meanwhile, from such influence and from the nature of the Tartar itself, various diseases emerge at different times. Above all, in <term>podagra</term> <note>Gout.</note> various changes occur, in which, on account of different influences, sometimes no remedies help at all or soften the pain; instead, the pain rages and is exacerbated freely according to its own impulse. For there is no disease that we know of that is so strongly governed and affected by the smallest or greatest accidents as this one alone.

<margin>In which causes the alteration of the body [occurs].</margin>
For the change of this disease is specific to any first change of the body. For as soon as the body is altered by food, drink, or exercise, etc., pains of this kind immediately grow and leap forth.

<margin>Gout is the worst of the Tartaric diseases.</margin>
Moreover, these kinds of Tartaric diseases are dissimilar in their change. For some are involved with more grievous pains than others. Hence **Podagra** [gout] exists everywhere. Yet not according to the same form. For from this comes a contraction below the waist <note>original: "infra zonam synthesina"</note>, colic, and death, in a form far different than in gout. The same must be judged regarding congealed and coagulated things. Now, therefore, if there are more Tartaric diseases than one, more than one hardening and form will naturally occur, since there is no doubt that any Tartaric disease has its own peculiar and private form. This is clear from **Lithiasis** [stone disease], in which two things exist: sand and stone. Its form is distinct from gout in that not as much salt is mixed into it as in gout.

<margin>How Lithiasis and gout differ</margin>
But the cause of the diversity is also this: that here no resolution can occur, because the matter turns out either softer or harder; but Lithiasis is perpetually similar to itself...

<margin>How Stone and Sand differ.</margin>

We say the same regarding coagulated and hardened masses in other areas, etc. Although these are not frozen by urine like stone-formation, their solidification has this cause: that surely in the intestines as well, which are the pathways for excrement, there is

For dung has a greater power than urine, according to what is established regarding excrement. In this very same way, these deposits are generated in the other intestines as well, and are coagulated into the form of gout.

### CHAPTER IV.

Since we have so far treated the causes and origin in abundant detail, we shall next explain by which remedies Tartaric diseases are cured. This must be known for two reasons. First, the appropriate remedies must be known so that the evil does not become worse by applying backwards treatments. Second, so that the cure may be established and perfected without any harm. The cure itself must be directed toward two things:

<margin>The dual cure of Tartar.</margin>
either toward gouty stones or toward sands. This is for the reason that we propose two modes of their generation or coagulation: one through the consumption of humors, as in

<margin>Tartar is coagulated either by drying or by the spirit.</margin>
gout and things similar to it; the other through the spirit of urine or dung. For the sake of easier understanding of this distinction, we will also apply the cure to two categories: namely, to the gouty fluxes, and to the stone-forming disease. This is because gouty fluxes are driven out by things of their own kind and appropriated to them, just as, conversely, the stone-forming disease is driven out by

<margin>The cure for gout and stone-formation is different.</margin>
things appropriated to it. For no remedy of one kind expels the Tartar of the other. The gouty cure cannot expel the stone-forming disease for the reason that it was hardened by the spirit of urine or dung. Likewise, the stone-forming remedy cannot cure gouty Tartars for the reason that they work and operate solely upon the spirit of urine and dung. But there are also other reasons for this dual treatment, namely: complexion, nature, etc. These must also be observed because it is sometimes necessary to use

<margin>Specifics to be used in gout and stone-formation.</margin>
**specifics**, because in a "specific form" there lie hidden and secret powers superior to nature itself, as we write in *Beyond Nature*. The necessity of using these arises from the fact that there are many diseases generated outside the order and mode of nature—such as stone and Tartar, etc.—which do not arise from heat or cold, but from another source, namely the "specific form"; that is, just like the specific form in the four complexions. For these, therefore, specifics must be used, endowed with that property, as we teach regarding specifics. For the fact that a stone breaks a stone does not happen from a "complexion" <note>the balance of hot/cold/wet/dry</note>. Likewise, that a bone heals another bone, or flesh heals other flesh, does not come from the condition of nature, but proceeds from a **specific**, which is ordered toward the other. Thus we see that

<margin>Nitric acid breaks all stones by a specific power.</margin>
<term>Nitric acid</term> <note>original: "Aqua fortis," literally 'strong water'</note> does not break all stones by its general nature, but by its specific form.

So also "appropriated" remedies must sometimes be used, because appropriated things are of one nature in their property regarding their perfection, not their complexion. Thus *Lithiasis* (stone-formation) and *Ceuillus* are

<margin>Appropriated things are one.</margin>
generated by one form. Although *Ceuillus* is not produced within the body, it is nevertheless produced from the earth in the likeness of stone-formation, from an earthy Tartar, and is hardened by the spirit of urine that resides in the liquid of the earth, just as we mention in the descriptions of the generations of stones.

<margin>Ceuillus, which is produced in the earth.</margin>
Therefore, **Ceuillus** cures stone-formation through an appropriated nature. <margin>

LUDUS <term>Ludus<gloss>a specific type of medicinal stone, often fossilized shells or sea urchins, believed to have the power to dissolve kidney and bladder stones</gloss></term> cures all stones throughout the whole body.

Through the ignorance and lack of skill regarding these matters, it happens too often that, for want of a genuine remedy, the miserable patient is killed by the Tartaric disease amidst cries of pain. The treatment, however, must be conducted in this way: LUDUS cures all stones arising from Tartar—whether they are frozen, coagulated, in the bladder, or in the kidneys—as well as sands, and similarly all Tartaric stones produced in the entire body, whether known or unknown. For it must be considered that many diseases exist in the body that proceed from Tartaric stones, of which we can have no knowledge, judgment, appearance, or prognosis. Instead, we remain stuck there in uncertainty, not knowing for sure how to escape. The aim of our practice is not merely to apply empirical rules that fit the specific types of stones we have already mentioned; rather, we must produce those recipes which, in general and not in particular, remove all stone-related diseases. For it is by these alone that Tartaric diseases are cleared. Indeed, it is impossible for traditional Physics <note>meaning the natural philosophy or medical science of the time</note> to examine and track down all the locations and regions where stones are born and lie. For this very reason, it is not at all necessary to have knowledge of "directing" medicines, by which remedies are led to the suffering parts, such as the head, the heart, etc. For who could be so clever and perceptive as to investigate exactly where the disease is, and thus be able to send a messenger, as it were, to that very spot? These ideas are vain and should be rejected. Rather, one must see to it that the medicine is directed toward the stone itself, and expels it without the help of directing agents. And this operation occurs simultaneously in all locations, as will be handed down hereafter. This same reasoning must also be held for curing and conquering gouty diseases through similar experience. Thus, let the cure be explained this far. Now, let us continue the text of the practice and set forth the matter itself.

<margin>Description of LUDUS.</margin>
This medicine must be known and understood in two modes: namely, as the *potentive* <note>the "potential" or internal strength</note> and the *acuative* <note>the "sharpening" or activating agent</note>. ### *The potentive is as follows:*

<margin>Ludus is the cure for all stones.</margin>

By this, all the aforementioned diseases from Tartaric stone are removed and cured. Do not let it seem absurd to you that so great a disease can be expelled by this one recipe, so simple and crude, while so many other recipes, so artificially concocted, are discarded and eliminated. Rather, reflect on this: a single splinter of burning wood gives more heat than ten cold logs. The same judgment and distinction must be held regarding this recipe of ours when compared with others, whether they were found by experience or produced by nature.

<margin>Description of the acuative.</margin>
Apply the *acuative* medicament externally, specifically on that place where the disease is felt. If you know the location of the diseases, you shall apply it until they are abolished and consumed: those which consist in the urinary ducts will pass through the urine; those situated in those paths [the intestines] will pass through the dung. The same should similarly be understood for the other emunctories <note>organs or canals that carry off waste, like the pores or tear ducts</note>.

<header>BOOK SEVEN</header>

# THEOPHRASTUS BOMBAST
## OF HOHENHEIM.

### ->*On the Illnesses of the Mentally Ill.*<-

### ->TREATISE I.<-

#### ->CHAPTER I.<-
#### ->*On the Falling Sickness.*<- <note>original: "Morbo Caduco," a historical term for Epilepsy</note>

<margin>All diseases are either of Nature or of Reason</margin>
**A**LL diseases, whatever they may be that afflict man (God's creature), descending from nature itself, either attack the body by weakening its health: or, what is more serious, they assist in crushing and striking down the vigor of the mind and reason. Therefore, when we consider natural diseases—in what ways and how many modes they violently strike and harm our body—utility and the facts of the matter require that we also simultaneously weigh those diseases by whose force our reason and intellect are overcome. We must examine from what origin they flow, since experience itself teaches and demonstrates that these emerge and are stirred up from Nature itself. And even though in this age of ours, the European "vicars of the Gods" <note>likely a satirical reference to religious or academic authorities</note> assign the cause of such diseases to incorporeal creatures and Devils, we are compelled by no necessity of demonstration to agree with them or support them in this instance. For we are carried away toward the opposite opinion by so many proofs given by nature itself, that we are forced to entirely oppose the opinion of those <margin>Illnesses of the mind are wrongly assigned to Devils.</margin> little god-pretenders <note>original: "Deaucalorum," a derogatory term for self-styled experts</note>. We shall teach distinctly about all these things in their own chapters, and we will clearly direct and explain the whole matter according to the manner of nature, which is the sole cause and mother of these things. Furthermore, there are five species of <margin>5 species of madness. Both the healthy and the sick are subject to Epilepsy.</margin> *Amentia* <term>Amentia<gloss>a general term for the deprivation of reason or madness</gloss></term>, or the deprivation of reason, that first present themselves: the first is the **Falling Sickness**, or <term>Epilepsy<gloss>a condition characterized by recurrent seizures</gloss></term>, which pertains not just to one temperament <note>original: "complexionem"</note>, but to none specifically; nor does it touch only one type of person, but all. The healthy, the weak, the young, and the old are all subject to this disease. Yet, this same disease takes nothing away from the strength of the body, nor does it break or destroy its constitution, as will be handed down hereafter. But if this disease sometimes makes people weak or brings on death, it happens for this reason: namely, that its sharpness and vehemence leave behind certain "Remnants" <note>after-effects or secondary damage</note> from which Death then arises, even without the contamination of the body's temperament. There are five <margin>5 types of Epilepsy.</margin> types of this falling sickness numbered, any one of which can produce Epilepsy on its own, and which can be generated promiscuously in all people. The first is in the *Brain*; the second in the *Liver*; the third in the *Heart*; the fourth in the *Intestines*; the fifth in the *Limbs*. Since one is more lethal and dangerous than another, it follows that the first three types occupy the most noble organs, whose <margin>The first paroxysm of epilepsy kills many.</margin> affliction is promptly followed by death. Thus it frequently happens that some are struck down and killed by the very first assault and <term>paroxysm<gloss>a sudden attack or seizure</gloss></term>. The reason for this outcome—since the same does not happen in the other two types—will be explained more plainly hereafter. All five of these types have a similar force of commotion, and an equal and similar deprivation of reason and the senses; yet they are not produced or emergent from one and the same material. For just as the mode of the paroxysms is different, so also the <margin>The matter and epileptic paroxysms differ in different people.</margin> matter itself is dissimilar. Some who are seized vomit and pour out foam, others a copious amount of water; some show eyes fixed and immovably open, others are shaken by frequent jolts and tossings of the body; some lie with a motionless body, some cry out something obscure, others remain entirely silent; some are violently thrown to the ground, and not a few gradually lower and recline themselves. However, one must attend diligently to the signs and reports of the sick. For it is of great <margin>Patients should be questioned about the location of the illness.</margin> importance to know in which place they especially feel the disease before they fall or are cast down from reason—unlike others who can feel no movement of the disease but are suddenly overwhelmed and fall senseless, not noticing the withdrawal of their reason. Their commotion itself is not the cause of these things, but the cause lies in that which *receives* the commotion. Thus the brain receives its commotion much like the intestines do, but the brain is affected more promptly and quickly because it has reason itself located in its region. Hence, because of proximity and nearness, the things mentioned above occur.

Let us proceed next to speak of the Matter from which the falling sickness is generated. It is not present only in man, but in all those things that have life, such as cattle, which fall no less than man himself and are seized by similar forms of paroxysms. Indeed, there are even certain kinds of animals in which this evil flourishes as an entirely hereditary trait, so that there is no individual among them who is not perhaps held by that disease. In this <margin>Weasels, Lions, and certain birds are subject to Epilepsy.</margin> category are **Weasels**, and **Lions**, and many species of birds, in which this evil is never abolished. Furthermore, even growing things [plants], which nevertheless lack sensation, are accustomed to being tried and afflicted by this same disease: not indeed in such a way that they "fall," for they are destitute of sensitive life; but in that <margin>Certain trees are epileptic.</margin> they experience their own paroxysms similarly to animals. For instance, trees may crack and be split apart by them, as we shall hand down in the record concerning the infirmities of trees. These sometimes wither away completely, and after the paroxysm has ended, they sometimes grow again; occasionally they simply die off. Similarly, it should be understood of all other things that have life, that they are equally troubled by this disease and experience its paroxysms: with this distinction, however, according to how much more or less any creature is endowed with sense. But to the investigation of the cause, why those endowed with sense...
