<meta>This page continues Paracelsus’s naturalistic exploration of mental and neurological disorders. Having previously rejected the idea that the "falling sickness" (epilepsy) is caused by demons, he now provides a mechanical and biological explanation for the disease, comparing it to an earthquake within the human body and categorizing it based on the organ where its "root" is planted.</meta>

<page-num>565</page-num>
<header>TREATISE I.</header>

<margin>The causes of the falling sickness <note>original: "caducus," or epilepsy</note> in living men are: 1. Nutrients.</margin>
Since it is granted that living things, though they be deprived of that same <note>referring to the previous discussion of spirit and matter</note>, are nonetheless subject to such a paroxysm <note>a sudden attack or seizure</note>, the following must be noted. No living nature acts or is sustained without the **spirit of life**, in which the life-giving force of all things is established, just as we teach regarding the spirit of life. Thus, in turn, no life exists without nourishment. Therefore, if every living thing labors under this disease, it must also reside within the nourishment. Thus, through nourishment, a "commingling" occurs if it is mixed into the spirit of life.

<margin>2. The boiling of the spirit of life.</margin>
This, therefore, is one cause of this disease. Another cause of the same is the **Boiling** <note>original: "Ebullitio," a bubbling or effervescence</note> of vapors within the spirit of life, and not indeed from other humors or qualities of the body; and it happens in this way: When the spirit of life is altered and cast down from its proper disposition, it then, as it were, effervesces and boils over. This boiling is so incited and violent that it lays waste to and removes all memory along with reason. That paroxysm is similar to that motion by which the entire world is shaken and trembles.

<margin>Epilepsy and earthquakes have the same cause.</margin>
For the cause of this disease corresponds to the causes of an earthquake; in one and the same mode and manner, both the motion of the earth and the falling sickness occur. This disease is generated neither from the order and course of Nature, nor from a weakness of the complexion <note>the balance of humors</note>, nor from any corruption of the humors; rather, it emerges from the same single cause as an earthquake. For an earthquake is also the motion of man himself, and the motion of trees, and the motion of all growing things, which we shall demonstrate in this discourse. We place the cause of earthquakes within our philosophy. Such as that cause is, such is also the falling sickness in the body, in this manner: if the spirit of life boils over from an error of its own property, so that it shakes out and emits smokes and vapors, then the entire body is shaken and trembles by them.

<margin>The spirit of life is the seat of reason.</margin>
But why is this? Namely, because the spirit of life is suffering. While this is suffering, the whole body suffers with it—not in sickness, but in **insanity** <note>original: "Amentiâ," a loss of mind or reason</note>. For reason dwells in the spirit of life; therefore, reason is destroyed and undergoes a "syncope" <note>a temporary loss of consciousness</note> for as long as it takes for the foam or boiling to cool down and be consumed. Indeed, the tossing, the jolting, the trembling, and the foam emerge from there because all the limbs are surely convulsed by a spasm, and their life is afflicted; for which reason they themselves necessarily suffer along with it, etc.

<margin>The five types of epilepsy. Cephalic, how it happens.</margin>
A fivefold difference of this disease must be understood. For one type of Epilepsy is **Cephalic** <note>related to the head</note>, the cause of which is a boiling of the spirit of life occurring in the head alone. Therefore, while this stirs up corruption and foam in the brain, the senses and intellect are intercepted because the dwelling-place of reason is besieged; subsequently, all the limbs are harmed in respect to their connection, because the very "root" of the man is affected. In this case, something happens similar to those earthquakes by which only a single region, not the whole world, is shaken. For here too, the disease consists in the brain alone, inflating everything nearby, just as all neighboring areas tremble from an earthquake. So also, that boiling and effusion which happens in the

<margin>Hepatic epilepsy, if it invades the brain diffusely.</margin>
**liver** <note>original: "hepate"</note> contaminates the spirit of life in the liver. Before it can even be felt, it has already occupied the brain and the entire body with such velocity as wind is carried and stirred rapidly through all things. And just as, if <term>Tartar</term> <note>Paracelsus's term for stony or mineral precipitates in the body</note> falls into a spring of water, even in the smallest mass, it continuously stirs up a powerful boiling; so too is the spirit of life itself swift and fervent.

<margin>Cardiac Epilepsy, how it happens.</margin>
**Cardiac** epilepsy occurs when the spirit of life boils in the capsule of the heart; yet it cannot produce a "poisoned" state (just as an earthquake does not produce infertility), unless by chance a certain superstitious dissolution is induced through the trembling and jolting of the limbs. For from a dissolution of that kind, death can follow, just as a house collapses from an earthquake—not by poison, but by the agitation and concussion.

<margin>Intestinal Epilepsy, how it happens.</margin>
The same is also to be understood in the same way regarding that which takes its origin in the **intestines**. For here the disease has its root from which it is produced, just as a plant emerges from a seed, falls, and is born again. There is a similar root in the spirit of life which produces such a "plant" from which diseases of this kind arise. Now, the location of this root can be anywhere in the whole body: in the head, and thus the disease arises in the head; in the liver, and it arises there; in the capsule of the heart, and it rises there. In the same way, it should also be understood regarding the belly: that the root sometimes lies in the intestines or neighboring places, according to where it is "struck." For wherever it is struck, there it remains and is fixed; it does not change its place or creep wider, because it does not spread multiple roots at once.

<margin>Epilepsy of the limbs, how it happens, namely of the hands and feet. Erratic epilepsy of the body, what it is.</margin>
In a similar way, the same root is sometimes fixed in the limbs, such as the **Hands and feet**, in which places the beginning of the paroxysms is most often detected; rising from there, it is diffused through the whole body with the spirit of life. It also happens that the root is fixed in no certain place, because it is not so substantial or material in itself that it can remain fixed anywhere, but is distributed through the whole body, and afterwards suddenly rushes into the reason.

Furthermore, since we have so far discussed the causes and seats from which Epilepsy emerges, let us now say something further about the spirit of life: by what means it is so infected that a paroxysm now insults the body, now is felt less, and how it happens that no sickness weighs upon the person outside of the paroxysm. Now, the falling sicknesses of this kind are conceived in the mother's womb, where their root is inserted and implanted into the fetuses, which afterwards grows with them as they are brought into the light, in this manner: From the weakness of the seed, or a perverse way of living, or an inordinate diet, the spirit of life in the fetus is produced as being not at all perfect or robust as it ought to be; and thus, from the bad constitution of the parents, the spirit of life in the fetus is contaminated and infected.

<margin>Epilepsy is hereditary, why and how.</margin>
From this foolishness <note>or lack of salt/savor</note>, if the spirit of life in the fetus is perfect, it then expels from itself what is alien and disagreeing. And although it cannot entirely drive that out from the body, it nevertheless continually demands and pushes it away until it seems most convenient. Therefore, in whatever place it is deposited, there it fixes its root. Now, as for the fact that this disease does not show itself immediately and continuously, the cause is this: namely, because the root itself is either not yet strong or large enough to exert its virulence immediately. Instead, it sometimes lasts and grows stronger until it is finally recognized only in the 70th year; many other causes, however, can concur in hindering this, such as the strength of the body, vigorous health, a good and wholesome diet, and such...

<margin>Epilepsy from terror</margin>
...and other things of this kind that are experienced by man. For if we sometimes see epileptics fall because of terror and trembling, then terror itself is by no means the cause of this affliction; rather, the root of this evil was already lurking, implanted in the body beforehand. Terror—which harms the **spirit of life** <note>The "spiritus vitae" was thought to be a subtle substance that animated the body and mediated between soul and flesh</note> and causes it to boil over—acts as a spark that ignites the disease and brings it into action. A seizure <note>original: "paroxysmus"</note> can also be stirred up by joy through a change in the spirit of life, which was already leaning in that direction. Thus, the same can happen through other accidental occurrences.

<margin>Why epilepsy does not afflict continuously.</margin>
As for why the seizure does not last continuously but returns at intervals: this happens by reason of the variety of influence which has the power to disturb, weaken, diminish, or increase the spirit of life. Furthermore, a seizure is sometimes stimulated by the spirit of life alone in this way: if the "root" breaks out and, as it were, sprouts, it triggers a seizure which soon subsides. Later, as soon as it boils up and overflows again, it stirs up another seizure—not unlike how rain now falls, now stops, now returns, and then ceases again. For something similar happens to the spirit of life, which is now rainy, now clear, and frequently varies these cycles according to how it is disposed in one way or another. But for the many things about this disease that ought to be taught and understood, we defer them to the **Second Method on Cure**, where we will teach that it is impossible to cure or pluck this disease out by its root; however, it is possible for it to be blunted and for the growth of the root to be restrained, just as a tree is lopped off while the roots are left unharmed in the earth—at least regarding its matter, though not its nature, as will be more clearly demonstrated.

### CHAPTER II.
## ON MANIA.

<margin>Mania is a deprivation of reason, not of imagination.</margin>
**R**egarding **Mania** <note>In this period, "Mania" referred to a state of frenzied insanity or delirium rather than modern bipolar mania</note>, it must be established that it is an alteration or change of **Reason** alone, and not also of the senses. For just as Reason is entirely absent in these patients, so conversely, their imagination remains strong and obstinate. For Mania almost always attacks with insanity and stirred-up furies, with great restlessness, with all sorts of perverse plotting, and the overturning of things in its path. It is distinguished chiefly by this: that it eventually subsides of its own accord, and the patients become more peaceful and return to their intellect as if by *right of return* <note>original: "postliminio," a legal term for regaining one's status after returning from captivity</note>.

<margin>Difficulties of Mania.</margin>
However, it also happens that Mania more often departs and then returns. Sometimes, that which has departed once does not return again. Some cases are moved according to the phase of the Moon; others are governed by the force of external accidents.

<margin>Two kinds of Mania.</margin>
Thus, there are two kinds of Mania: one that comes upon a healthy body, and another that is raised from other prior diseases. Hence, the causes producing Mania must also be twofold: one from a healthy body, the other from a diseased one. However, for both, there is one "kindling" and the same matter, based on the following reasoning. The matter of Mania is a humor <term>distilled|In Paracelsian medicine, "distillation" refers to the rising and falling of bodily vapors similar to a chemist's still</term> into the brain, which rises and is lifted up and mixed below the **Diaphragm** on one hand; and on the other hand, above the Diaphragm, within the region between the Diaphragm and the throat. For here too a peculiar mixing occurs, and from this, finally, a certain distillation upward into the head takes place. Thus, an internal distillation in the body

<margin>Mania arises from three places.</margin>
happens in two ways, both of which can stir up Mania. Furthermore, in a similar way, distillations can occur in the four external limbs, stirred upward toward the heights according to the path of the ducts and pores. Thus, from these three places alone do Manias arise. Next, however, the differences of Mania must also be recognized. For to each distillation there is attached its own separate nature and property, and for that reason, one exists as worse and more harmful than another. For the Mania that arises from a distillation made below the diaphragm breaks out 

<margin>Signs of mania below the diaphragm.</margin>
with manifest **delirium** and foolishness; the patients are immediately cast down, tempted by nausea and vomiting, while some diarrhea occurs simultaneously. They mutter to themselves and speak various alien things, having no regard for or notice of those standing by, nor even of the place in which they are located.

<margin>Cause.</margin>
The cause of these symptoms is specifically that the lower distillation is produced from **excrement** <note>original: "stercoribus," referring to waste matter in the bowels</note>, the resolution and <term>sublimation|The process of a solid or liquid turning into a gas and rising</term> of which displays the aforementioned signs. The Mania that occurs

<margin>Signs of mania above the diaphragm.</margin>
above the diaphragm is fierce, accompanied by violent compressions of the heart and chest, and dangerous because of dire piercing pains. The cause of all these is that in this seat as well, the matter is resolved and breaks out into the heights; hence, compression is felt most especially in that place where the ascent of the matter occurs. But the distillation that rises from the 

<margin>Signs of the limbs' mania.</margin>
external limbs brings Mania with a certain joy, exultation, and fierce alacrity. For the internal organs feel nothing, nor are they affected by anything except happy and pleasant things, though a frequent mania nevertheless accompanies it. It is not necessary to describe or recount the other signs by which this mania may be distinguished here.

Now indeed, the generations or elevations of Mania exist in two ways: one which is distilled into the head in the form of a **smoky vapor**. This Mania lasts as long as the vapor lasts. The other is distinguished from distillation by the fact that it is **sublimated**, meaning it is frozen in the head and remains coagulated, and is not resolved in the head. For this reason, 

<margin>The double cure of mania.</margin>
two Manias must be considered in the **Cure**: one to be consumed, namely that which arises from distillation; the other to be resolved and consumed, which is generated by sublimation. And although here two elevations of Mania into the head occur, both nevertheless flow from one foundation, if you consider that threefold distinction. Furthermore, while the division of Mania is threefold, they by no means occur in only one way or path. For some distillations and sublimations exist in the blood of the veins of the external limbs alone; others in their ligaments alone. Thus, two kinds of Mania in the external limbs must be recognized: those of the blood and those of the ligaments. For it is possible that, even if Mania arises from the external limbs, it does not occur in the whole limb, but either only in the blood or only in the ligaments. For through this alone it is distilled upward either to the veins or to the ligaments. Although distillation also sometimes travels first to the heart and afterward to the head, and finally along the paths of the veins and arteries. For distillations and sublimations first turn aside to their own principle, and from there they are finally stirred upward. Thus, Mania above the diaphragm is sometimes stirred up by the stomach alone,

It also challenges the traditional Galenic view that mania is caused by an imbalance of the four humors.</meta>

Sometimes mania is stirred up by the stomach alone, as it dissolves its own phlegm or other contained matter; as this eventually creeps into the brain, a similar distillation or **sublimation** <note>In early medicine, "sublimation" referred to the process where bodily substances were heated by internal warmth and rose as vapors, much like in an alchemist's flask</note> can also occur in the liver or the lungs. The same diversity occurs around the intestines, kidneys, etc., because some distillations and sublimations arise from dryer substances, others from the **spirit of urine**, others from the phlegm of the intestines, or whatever else is usually contained in them: any one of these can, by itself, provoke Mania. By this reasoning, many types of Mania can be stirred up, though all are encompassed within the three boundaries previously mentioned. Furthermore, we shall now proceed to review what exactly it is from which Mania arises, how it may be resolved and adapted for distillation and sublimation, and where it is birthed.

<margin>Two types of heat.</margin>
An immoderate, vehement, and great heat exists in two forms: namely, *fiery* <note>original: "igneus"</note> and *putrid* or "putrefying." The cause of that heat is as follows: When the 
<margin>The nature of the reverberation of matter in Mania.</margin>
matter of that place from which the Mania rises is **reverberated** <note>reverberatio: a process of intense heating or reflection of heat, often used in alchemy to break substances down</note> into a **lime** <note>original: "calcem"; referring to "calx," the fine powder or ash left after a substance has been burned or calcined</note>, which is afterwards resolved into an extremely sharp water: then that sharp resolution ignites the **spirit of life**. As long as it touches that spirit, a subtle separation of the fine from the coarse occurs. In this matter, the "subtlety" <note>the refined, vaporous part of a substance</note> is so sharp that nothing remains at the bottom, but everything flies up to the highest point, leaving the coarse dregs at the base. This "reverberation" is caused by a great heat that arises in those places and is inflamed there until such great subtlety emerges. Now, just as this kind of reverberation varies, so too does the resulting Resolution. For one type occurs in the blood, another in the ligaments, and others in the various places we have mentioned. Resolution in the blood happens when the **spirit of salt** <note>a concentrated, sharp essence extracted from minerals or bodily fluids</note> which is in the blood is mixed into one with the spirit of life.

<margin>Why bloodletting sometimes cures Mania.</margin>
As soon as these distilled humors—which are sublimated by the heat of the lower members—strike the chambers of the brain with their subtlety and sharpness, Mania breaks out instantly. Therefore, if it is in the blood alone, then if the true and correct vein is cut, that distilled spirit exits and breathes out. But if the distilled matter is not in the blood but occupies the entire head, then **phlebotomy** <note>the medical practice of bloodletting</note> is of very little use, as will be handed down in the section on cures. In the same way, Mania is sometimes removed by opening the veins of the hands, feet, and fingers, because through that opening a certain kind of cooling and air is introduced, preventing the future heating of the matter within itself and thus prohibiting its ascent. But if this does not always help, or does not help perfectly, it is for this reason: because the matter was not sufficiently cooled, or the distillation was not enough removed. If, however, Mania of this kind lurks in the veins, such an opening does not help, because above all the "center" must be sought, and primary attention must be paid there, as will be taught in the cure. It also happens that the matter of Mania is sometimes sublimated and coagulated in the head. From the putrefaction of this prompt and ready sublimation, either **worms** <note>A common early modern belief was that "worms" or parasites generated from corrupt humors in the brain caused madness or pain</note> are born in the head, or **apostemes** <note>abscesses or swellings</note> due to an excessively hard curdling, or **pus**. While this pus is diffused through the whole head, erosions and "stings" of the head are produced along with sharp pains. Sometimes these resolutions in the head are consumed again until only a tiny surviving drop remains; from this alone, if it lies in a dangerous place, a certain Mania emerges. When the matter is not resolved at all but remains coagulated, it burns and erodes like salt in a wound; from this, reason is shattered and perishes. To put it in a word, the place of Mania's origin can hardly be sufficiently traced and explored, as we are indicating here in a general sense. Thus, sublimation sometimes takes its beginning in the stomach alone—not always in the whole of it, but sometimes in some tiny part. Nevertheless, if medicine is provided and administered to the entire stomach, whatever evil clings anywhere is removed. However, it should be well noted here that this does not happen similarly in the veins. For sublimation can occur in one single vein, sometimes in several, and occasionally in all of them at once. The same judgment applies to the ligaments. Nevertheless, if the evil resides in the liver, lung, or spleen, then the entire organ is treated with a suitable cure.

It must also be noted by us here that there are four **complexions** <note>The "four humors" (blood, phlegm, yellow bile, black bile) which were thought to determine a person's temperament and health</note>, from each of which certain ancients thought Mania could be conjectured. However, we do not yet accept this—for instance, that **Melancholy** 
<margin>Reprimand of physicians.</margin>
is the cause of Mania. For if Melancholy were the cause, then only the melancholic part would suffer. The same would happen if only **cholera** <note>yellow bile</note>, or blood, or phlegm were the cause. Therefore, that opinion of the ancients is not at all true.

<margin>Why mania is not from humors.</margin>
For since Manias are stirred up from three distinct parts of the body, they certainly cannot be generated from a single complexion alone. Nor are they distributed according to the complexions. Furthermore, if Manias arose from complexions, as they claim, then no distillation or sublimation could occur from the external members into the head. For no complexion has such a disposition that it can be reduced to such great subtlety as to drive the head into delirium. Finally, Mania also primarily arises from certain members that are governed by no complexion. If this is true, it will be false that Mania is generated from complexions, as we shall say regarding the complexions. However, it can meanwhile arise from some single place in which Melancholy lives and dominates, such as the spleen; yet this is not by reason of the Melancholy itself, but by reason of the **spirit of life**, which separates itself from the Melancholy in the manner we have described and 
<margin>Mania from the spirit of life alone.</margin>
ascends into the heights. From this it is clear that Mania is incited by the spirit of life alone, ascending upward into the head through distillation and sublimation, as has been said. The same judgment applies to Mania generated from the gall, yet not from the "cholera" contained within it; and so on. We conclude, therefore, that all the spirits of life and the matters from which Mania arises are entirely of one nature, quality, complexion, and essence, etc. One is not hot while another is cold, or this one moist and that one dry; rather, there is one equality among them all. Mania is generated in no other way than that the matter becomes so subtle and sharp that it overwhelms the brain...

It establishes the chemical theory that when the "salt" of the blood or humors is separated by acidity, it hardens into stony matter, leading to conditions like gout and stones in the organs.</meta>

<page-num>558</page-num>
<header>ON DISEASES ARISING FROM TARTAR</header>

<margin>The nature of Tartar, or of the blood which is generated. How blood is separated. Salt is the life of the blood.</margin>
The reason for this is that the <term>salt</term><note>In Paracelsian medicine, Salt is one of the "Three Primes" representing the principle of solidity, structure, and preservation in all matter.</note> hidden in the blood, by its own inherent property, separates itself from the blood. Thus, the saltiness exists on its own, and the blood itself exists separately. Once this divorce and separation has occurred, the blood loses its original integrity and virtue, since its life and goodness are preserved and sustained by the salt. Therefore, when (as has been said) the salt is separated from the blood, it then comes together and coagulates into a certain hardness, like grainy pebbles or gravelly sand. <term>Gout</term><note>original: "Podagricus morbus"; refers specifically to the buildup of crystals in the joints.</note> is a disease of this very kind: one which we have not found described in any previous records, but which we have learned to treat through experience alone, due to its similarity to gout.

<margin>Acidity is the cause of the separation of the blood.</margin>
The cause of this separation is the acidity of the blood.

<margin>Vinegar separates milk.</margin>
Just as milk changes its nature if vinegar is poured into it, separating the substance itself from the whey so that it is no longer milk, a similar thing happens when the blood turns sour, as we have taught.

<margin>How phlegm is separated and becomes tartarous.</margin>
In exactly the same way, through this kind of separation, such stones and <term>Tartars</term><note>Tartar: A term Paracelsus used for metabolic waste products that calcify or harden, named after the "tartar" (potassium bitartrate) found in wine barrels.</note> are generated from <term>phlegm</term><note>One of the four traditional humors, associated here with the lungs and liver.</note> in those places where phlegm settles, such as in the tubes of the lungs, the liver, etc. For phlegm contains within itself "dead salt." If this is separated (just like the milk and blood), then a gout-like disease occurs there as well, just as we defined regarding the blood.

Similarly, from <term>cholera</term><note>Yellow bile; the humor associated with heat and bitterness.</note> in all its specific locations, stones and sand—and thus gout—can be produced for the exact same reasons we have already covered.

<margin>Salt is in all temperaments.</margin>
The same must be understood regarding <term>melancholia</term><note>Black bile; the humor associated with cold and dryness.</note>. For salts exist in all these temperaments. Whenever a certain sourness is mixed into these, wherever they may be in the body, such a separation occurs immediately in the corresponding locations.

<margin>Tartarous diseases occur in the limbs.</margin>
By considering these causes, this kind of Tartarous disease can be produced in all the members of the entire body—such as the liver, the cavity of the brain, the lungs, and the stomach—with none excepted. And likewise, Tartarous diseases can be generated in the humors themselves, as in everything else in which salt is present, as it is moved and driven through the body.

## CHAPTER III.

Now that we have so far explained the origin and mode of generation of Tartarous diseases, it is next for us to explain the reason and manner by which this **Resolution** and **Coagulation** occur as they pervade and penetrate every part of the body, and why they do not simply stay in the immediate or nearest vicinity.

<margin>Subtlety and coarseness are the causes of deeper penetration.</margin>
There are two primary causes: one is **subtlety** <note>subtilitas: fineness, purity, or thinness of a substance.</note>, the other is **coarseness** <note>crassities: thickness or density.</note>. Understand it this way: Subtlety penetrates the entire body; the subtler something is, the further and wider it overflows. Coarseness remains in the immediate vicinity because it cannot penetrate the veins and pores.

<margin>Of Tartar, whether remaining, etc.</margin>
But beyond these, those causes must also be known by which Tartar is expelled to the outermost and lowest parts. There are three of these causes:

<margin>1</margin>
One is from the faculty of the **Attractive power**, which draws in nourishment; with this, and within which, the "Tartar-ness" itself is attracted to all the limbs.

<margin>2</margin>
The second is from the force of **mixing**, by which the Tartar insinuates itself into the blood and is mixed with it, and finally, separating again in its own time, it diverts into the joints and the skin.

<margin>3</margin>
The third cause is that the materials from which the Tartar is born share a certain property and familiarity with specific body parts, and they are drawn toward them. Hence, if it reaches those parts, its fluid is consumed, and the remnants abound, as we explained a little earlier.

From these three causes, distribution proceeds to those parts in which Tartarous diseases are established. To these causes is added the fact that the matter sometimes lingers somewhere and is not carried as far as its properties and attraction would have led it.

<margin>The Tartar of water is coarser than that of wine.</margin>
Furthermore, we will also explain the reasons why one Tartar exists as subtler or coarser than another. This diversity depends on the nature of the things from which the Tartar was generated. Thus, the Tartar of common water is much ruder and coarser than that of wine. Hence it happens that the coarseness of watery Tartar hardly penetrates deeply into the body, while the subtlety of wine Tartar is carried to the outermost seats.

<margin>Wine Tartars are more penetrating.</margin>
This is the very reason why the Tartar of wine is distributed deeply through the whole body and produces diseases everywhere, while the Tartar of water accumulates and freezes in only one place. The same logic applies to other foods, drinks, vapors, and all things we have mentioned; the coarseness and subtlety of all of them must be estimated similarly. Thus, vapors also uniquely stick in the deeper parts rather than the nearby ones, unless some property clings to the vapor that causes it to be fixed in the very first places it reaches; or unless

<margin>Sulfur's Tartar does not go far.</margin>
it is of such a nature that as soon as it senses another nature, it immediately sticks. Thus **Sulfur**, since it is not sublimated to distant parts, does not reach distant parts in the body itself, but fixes its Tartar immediately in the stomach. But the vapor that goes to distant parts—such as that of **Sal Ammoniac** <note>A salt often used in alchemy, known for its ability to sublimate easily.</note> and **Mercury**—the Tartar of these wanders more penetratingly to all members in the body itself. Through continuous permeation, they flee to the outermost seats of the body, leaving their seeds everywhere in all the places they travel through. Yet the vapor of **Arsenic** does not do this; rather, it fixes itself collectively in distant parts according to how it is driven and moved. From the weighing of these causes, we understand that some Tartarous diseases arise and are born in only one place: for example, if vapor from **Aqua Fortis** <note>Nitric acid.</note> or similar things is attracted to just one place, and there it is mixed and appropriated to that part, then coagulation and freezing happen simultaneously and collectively in that single spot. As for the properties of foods and nourishments, mentioning them here seems superfluous, since they are treated abundantly elsewhere, especially in the previous chapters.

Since we said a little earlier that the attraction of Tartar can occur alongside nourishment through the attractive power, we find these causes for that fact: namely, that nourishment and "Tartar-ness" are swallowed together into the stomach and mixed there.

<margin>The cause of Tartarous diseases is the weakness of the stomach's digestive power.</margin>

<margin>Appropriation is a defect in the cause of distributing nourishment.</margin>
An action follows which we are accustomed to call <term>Tartareous diseases</term><note>In Paracelsian medicine, these are "stone" diseases where metabolic waste hardens into solid deposits, named after the "tartar" (potassium bitartrate) that forms crusts in wine barrels.</note>. The reason why this occurs from a mixture is not merely due to the mixing that takes place in the stomach—as we have already said regarding the union of nutrients and Tartar—but this same mixing occurs similarly in that joining together even outside the stomach. Just as we defined the stomach as one part of the four <term>complexions</term><note>The traditional "humors" or temperaments (sanguine, choleric, melancholic, phlegmatic) that governed the body's constitution.</note> and the four substances of the whole body, so we shall also conclude the final causes of separation. This separation occurs through <term>appropriation</term><note>The process where specific organs "claim" or attract the substances they need from the blood; here, the author argues organs also accidentally "appropriate" the toxins meant for them.</note> of the consumed materials, which look toward specific parts and members. Thus, substances pleasing and useful to the veins produce diseases in the veins. Those that benefit the stomach deposit Tartar in the stomach. This same judgment applies to all other members. However, let us remember that it can also happen that Tartareous diseases are generated in all locations of the body from this "mis-appropriation." For whatever we consume benefits the whole body everywhere, and yet a Tartareous disease may arise in only a single place.

<margin>A fair objection</margin>
But the cause of this is a certain <term>Resolution</term><note>original: "Resolutio"; the process of dissolving, melting, or breaking down a solid into a liquid state.</note> which melts and dissolves the Tartar in some places, but not at all in others. Indeed, unless this Resolution occurred and was administered by Nature within the body, it would be necessary for every single human being to be afflicted with <term>gout</term><note>original: "Podagricos" (gout of the feet), "chiragricos" (gout of the hands), and "calculosos" (afflicted with stones/calculi).</note> in the feet, gout in the hands, and stones.

<margin>Why not all men are gouty, etc.</margin>
From this it is clear that "Tartar-ness" arises only in those places where there is no Resolution. We therefore have a ready cause: namely, that Resolution fails equally in a corresponding member. For example, if there is no resolution in one joint, there will be none in its similar counterpart; therefore, the Tartar immediately yields and sticks to the joints. This is to be understood similarly for other parts as well.

<margin>Why Tartar adheres chiefly to the joints. All Tartar is salt.</margin>
Next, so that you may understand the reason why Tartar remains chiefly in the joints and is consumed neither by Nature nor by time, turn your mind to this point: All Tartar-ness is <term>salt</term><note>Salt represents the principle of solidity and crystallization in this medical philosophy.</note>. If it coagulates and becomes grainy, it can be dissolved by warm water, digested or changed into a watery liquid, and sweated out. Similarly, if it is naturally moist and has not been coagulated by intense dryness, it can be dissolved by itself, like <term>calcined</term><note>Burnt to a powder. The author suggests the body's internal heat "burns" the waste into a crust.</note> Tartar. For salt and Tartar-ness are calcined in the body by the heat of the internal members, just as if by fire. But if the Tartar-ness remains, the cause is this: it cannot be dissolved. For since it is too dry and arid, it comes together because of this and coagulates into a stone, or into many small pebbles, depending partly on the property of the Tartar and partly on the mixture of the salt. For this reason, it remains left behind.

<margin>There are three causes of gouty paroxysms.</margin>
From this very cause also arise the periods or "types" of this disease, by which the pain is felt more or less at one time or another. For it is pleasing to set forth this discourse of natural causes.

<margin>Moister air. Various things benefit those with Tartar, for various reasons.</margin>
If the air and the weather are moister, then the body itself and all its substance become moist, as we teach in our *Philosophy*. Now, if the body becomes soaked with such moisture, then by its own nature and property, the salt and Tartar are also moistened, and afterwards begin to liquefy and dissolve. While it is attempting this, it changes its nature, force, and power; it boils up, as it were, and swells and puffs up within itself. From this commotion, the sharpest pains are inflicted upon the tendons; yet not all the Tartar is dissolved. For the dryness and the property which is not fit for resolution stands in the way in its own manner. Hence it happens that sometimes warm <term>fomentations</term><note>Warm, moist medicinal compresses.</note> benefit the sick because heat dries them out again and thus soothes them. Sometimes cold things are convenient because they freeze the matter. Sometimes temperate things help because they restrain both excesses and stop the Tartar so that it cannot boil over further. Occasionally moist things help because the resolution is continued as far as possible, and once completed, rest is induced. Often dry things also soothe because they take away the moisture and remove the agitation. Frequently, <term>Anodynes</term><note>Pain-relieving medications.</note> also do good, namely narcotics.

<margin>Influence of the heavens, especially the Moon.</margin>
Furthermore, the <term>paroxysms</term><note>Sudden attacks or increases in the intensity of symptoms.</note> are either increased or diminished by the influence of the heavens, whether increasing or failing, in this way: if the Moon is waning, the disease is also diminished, and yet pain presses at the same time, because the warm or natural virtue is weak while the disease is stronger. But with a waxing Moon, the pains more often stab, because the influx becomes too great in the place where it boils up. A similar judgment must be made regarding other movements or constitutions of the sky, whether hotter or colder, according to which the diseases are either intensified, diminished, or altered.

<margin>The higher things govern us.</margin>
Even if not all such influences are known to us, it is easy for us to think that a certain singular force and power dwells above us, which dominates and rules us. But we let this pass for now. Meanwhile, from such influence and the nature of the Tartar itself, various diseases emerge at different times. Above all, various changes occur in gout, in which, because of different influences, sometimes no remedies at all help or soften the pain, but it rages and is exacerbated freely according to its own impulse.

<margin>Alteration of the body from any causes.</margin>
For there is no disease that we know of which is so strongly governed and affected by the smallest or greatest accidents as this one. Its change follows even the first change of the body itself. For as soon as the body is altered by food, drink, or exercise, etc., pains of this kind immediately swell and attack.

<margin>Gout is the worst of the Tartareous diseases.</margin>
Moreover, these Tartareous diseases differ in their changes. For some are entangled with more grievous pains than others. From this, <term>Gout</term><note>original: "Podagra".</note> arises everywhere, yet not according to the same form. For from this comes a contraction below the <term>synthena</term><note>A technical term likely referring to the waist or a specific abdominal region in Paracelsian anatomy.</note> zone, colic, and death, in a form far different from that in the feet. The same must be judged regarding different types of coagulations. Now, if there are more Tartareous diseases than one, naturally more than one hardening and form will occur, since there is no doubt that every Tartareous disease has its own peculiar and private form. This is evident from <term>Lithiasis</term><note>The formation of stones in the kidneys or bladder.</note>, in which two things exist: sand and stone. Its form is distinct from gout in that not as much salt is mixed into it as is in gout.

<margin>How Lithiasis and gout differ.</margin>
But the cause of the diversity is also this: that here no resolution can occur by which the matter might turn out either better or harder; but Lithiasis is perpetually similar to itself...

->## ON DISEASES FROM TARTAR.<-

<margin>How stones and gravel differ.</margin>
...it is similar, and does not return to its <term>first matter</term><note>The primordial, unformed state of a substance before it takes a specific physical shape.</note>, but rather expands because it thereafter increases more and more in a similar fashion, hardens, and remains in that state.

<margin>The spirit of urine inclines toward stone and gravel.</margin>
<margin>How stone and sand are coagulated in the kidneys, etc.</margin>
Furthermore, the difference between <term>sand</term><note>Often called "gravel" in modern medical history; small, gritty deposits in the urinary tract.</note> and <term>stone</term><note>original: "calculus"</note> is to be understood in this way: this is <term>Tartar</term> which, by its power and operation, is coagulated into a thin form. If this tartareous nature reaches the regions of the kidneys and the bladder, it is possible for <term>gout</term><note>original: "podagra"; Paracelsus often viewed gout and stones as two versions of the same "tartareous" process.</note> to occur there, because the cause is present. However, that specific character is altered because another <term>complexion</term><note>The physiological temperament or constitution.</note> and another disease are born. This is the <term>spirit of urine</term>, which (as is taught regarding urine) possesses a certain property within itself that inclines toward stony and sandy conditions. Thus, urine is the cause of this disease: not because the stone comes from the substance of the urine itself, but rather from the substance of the "gouty flux," which is nonetheless coagulated by the urine into another form and appearance. This happens in the following order: if the urine catches hold of tartareous matter in the kidneys or bladder, it forces it together because the urine is hot and watery, while the Tartar is viscous and sticky, attracting the spirit of the urine. For this reason, the urine of no one suffering from <term>Lithiasis</term><note>The clinical condition of having stones.</note> is yellow; they are all white. They lack the spirit of urine, by which the deposits are dried out. It is not that the entire volume of urine is dried up by it—as in Gout, where all moisture is consumed—but rather by a certain similarity, just as <term>saltpeter</term><note>original: "Sal petrae"; potassium nitrate, used here as a chemical analogy for how minerals solidify out of liquid.</note> in water is forced into stone and solidified. Let this example not cause you wonder: for saltpeter is born from urine, and there exists a spirit of urine which separates itself within urine from the nature of Tartar; this separation is followed by the hardening of the Tartar and its round shape, as it depends on the property of the salt. Thus, according to the abundance of material, white stones are sometimes formed—though not pure ones—because the saltpeter of the urine has been incorporated with the Tartar. Sometimes they become blue or similar colors, which arises entirely from the property of the urine (as is more clearly taught in the section on urine); sometimes they are red, and these are not from the property of urine, but from the color of the kidneys.

<margin>How sand is coagulated.</margin>
The form of "sand" or gravel is generated because the urine does not possess a spirit powerful enough to incline it toward the nature of a stone; hence it happens that the Tartar simply adheres and becomes granular, just as the nature and property of salt carries it. Therefore, if many small stones are generated, and these are sometimes crushed, tiny, and perceptible, the most powerful cause exists in the property of the kidneys, which have within themselves such a bituminous and viscous nature that the coagulation of the stone is thereby worn down and broken into small pieces.

If, therefore, the gouty flux and Tartar turn to stone and sand in this manner, various signs and manifold pains emerge from it, the description of which does not belong to the theory of the art, but to daily observation.

<margin>The spirit of dung hardens coagulation.</margin>
We say the same also regarding other coagulations and hardenings, etc. Although these are not frozen by urine like Lithiasis, their "freezing" has this cause: namely, that in the intestines, which are the pathways for dung, there is also a certain spirit. This spirit hardens and coagulates similarly to urine, or rather, much more so. Therefore, if Tartar adheres to the intestines in a mixture and is not ejected along with the dung, then the driving <term>spirit of dung</term><note>original: "spiritus stercorum"; the volatile or essential force Paracelsus believed resided in waste matter.</note> forces and coagulates it so that it <meta>catchword: so that it</meta> accumulates and grows larger day by day. For dung has a greater power than urine, according to what is established regarding dung. In this very way, these deposits are generated in other parts of the intestines as well, and are coagulated into a form of gout.

## CHAPTER IV.

<margin>The cure for Tartar is twofold.</margin>
<margin>Tartar is coagulated either by drying or by spirit.</margin>
<margin>The cure for gout and stone disease is different.</margin>
Since we have so far treated the causes and origin in sufficient abundance, we shall next explain by which remedies Tartareous diseases are cured. This must be known for two reasons. First, the appropriate remedies must be known so that the evil does not become worse by applying the wrong ones. Second, so that the cure may be established and perfected without any harm. The cure itself must be directed toward two things: either toward gouty stones and gravel, or intestinal ones. This is because we establish two modes of their generation or coagulation: one through the consumption of humors (as in gout and similar cases), and the other through the spirit of urine or dung. For the sake of easier understanding, we shall apply the cure to two areas according to this distinction: namely, to the gouty fluxes and to stony Lithiasis. This is because gouty fluxes are driven out by things of their own kind and appropriate nature, just as stony deposits are driven out by things appropriate to them. No remedy for one kind of Tartar expels the other. For a gouty cure cannot expel Lithiasis because the latter was hardened by the spirit of urine or dung. Likewise, a stone-cure cannot treat gouty Tartars for the reason that they labor and operate only upon the spirit of urine and dung. But there are also other reasons for this twofold treatment, namely the complexion, nature, etc. These must also be observed because it is sometimes necessary to use <term>Specifics</term><note>Medicines that act directly on a specific disease or organ by a "hidden" power, rather than by balancing humors.</note>, because within a specific form lie hidden and secret powers superior to nature itself, as we write in the book *Beyond Nature*. The necessity of using these arises from the fact that there are many diseases born outside the normal order and mode of nature, just as are stone and Tartar, etc. These do not arise from heat or cold, but from another source, namely the <term>specific form</term>. Therefore, Specifics must be applied to these, endowed with that property, as we teach regarding Specifics. For the fact that "a stone breaks a stone" does not happen because of a complexion. Likewise, that a bone heals another bone, or flesh heals other flesh, does not come from the condition of nature, but proceeds from a Specific, which is ordered toward another.

<margin>Specifics to be used in gout and stone disease.</margin>
<margin>Strong water breaks all stones by a specific power.</margin>
Thus we see that <term>strong water</term><note>original: "aquam fortem"; usually refers to nitric acid or a powerful mineral solvent.</note> by its nature does not break all stones, but does so by its specific form.

<margin>Appropriates are one.</margin>
<margin>Ceuillus which is born in the earth.</margin>
So also "Appropriates" must sometimes be used, because Appropriates are of one nature in their property regarding their perfection, not their complexion. Thus Lithiasis and <term>Ceuillus</term><note>A Paracelsian term for a type of stone found in the earth that was believed to cure stones in the human body through "appropriation" or similarity.</note> are generated in one form. Although Ceuillus is not produced in the body, it is nevertheless produced from the earth in the likeness of Lithiasis, from an earthy Tartar, and is hardened by the spirit of urine which dwells in the liquid of the earth, just as we mention in the generation of stones. Ceuillus, therefore, cures Lithiasis in its appropriate nature. For if these two touch one another, one breaks and diminishes the other, and both are resolved into their first matter and likened to a clod or crumbly sand. For Appropriates, or "proper things," carry within themselves their own destruction...

# SECOND TREATISE.
## CHAPTER I.

<margin>
Tartar remedies either break the stone or consume the salt.
</margin>
**B**ecause in the preceding chapters we have defined the origin of Tartareous diseases: it is our next purpose to complete the cure of them. We shall hand this down in one peculiar treatise in three parts. One will be about Tartareous diseases which are <term>stone</term>. Another, about those which exist as <term>salt</term>. The third will conclude with preservatives. For according to our intention, all remedies for healing Tartareous diseases consist in two things: for some break the stone; others consume and resolve the salt. In this chapter, however, we shall place only that cure which heals the stone, sand, coagulated things, and congealed things, as they grow within the cavities of the body.
In the beginning, however, it must be understood that there is no need to know in which places of the body the stones lie, whether in the bladder, or the kidneys, or the intestines or viscera, etc. Furthermore, it is also not necessary that it be known from where and from what 
<margin>
Remedies for Tartar must be specific.

# ON DISEASES ARISING FROM TARTAR.

<margin>Crab's eyes <note>original: "Oculi cācrorum"; these are small calcium carbonate stones found in the stomachs of crayfish, used in early medicine to treat acidity and stones.</note> expel gravel. It cures stones of the stomach and kidneys.</margin>
<margin>LUDUS cures stones of the entire body.</margin>

Through ignorance and lack of skill in these matters, it happens too often that for want of a genuine remedy, a poor soul is killed by Tartaric disease amidst wretched wailing. However, the medication ought to be performed as follows: **LUDUS** <note>In Paracelsian medicine, "Ludus" refers to a specific mineral or fossilized stone (often a septarian nodule) believed to have the power to dissolve kidney and bladder stones.</note> cures all stones arising from Tartar—those frozen, those coagulated, in the bladder, in the kidneys, and gravel; and similarly all Tartaric stones produced in the entire body, whether known or unknown. For it must be considered that many diseases exist in the body that proceed from Tartaric stones, of which we can have no knowledge, judgment, sign, or prognosis; instead, we remain there in ambiguity, and we have no certainty of where we might end up. The tenor of our practice is this: that one should not merely apply empirical rules which suit the types of stones we have already mentioned piece by piece; rather, those recipes are to be brought forward which, in a general sense and not just in particulars, remove all stony diseases. For only by these are Tartaric diseases taken away. It is impossible, through the study of Physics, to scrutinize and track down every location and region in which stones are birthed and lie. For this very reason, it is not at all necessary to have knowledge of "directors"—those things through which remedies are led to the laboring parts, such as the head, the heart, etc. For who could be so ingenious and perceptive that he could track down exactly where a disease is, and thus send a "messenger" <note>A medicinal agent intended to target a specific organ.</note> to it? These ideas are vain and to be rejected. One must strive for this instead: that the medicine be directed toward the stone itself, and expel it without the help of "directors." This operation occurs simultaneously in all places, as will be handed down hereafter. This same reasoning must also be held in similarly curing and conquering gouty diseases through such experience. Thus, let the cure be explained this far. Now, let us continue the text of the practice and set down the matter itself.

<margin>Description of LUDUS.</margin>
This medicine, therefore, is to be known and understood in two modes: namely, as the *Potent* and the *Sharpener*. And both are to be applied both internally and externally, as will be handed down later in the Regimen.

->The Potent medicine is as follows.<-

<margin>The cure for stones using Ludus.</margin>
Take: Ludus, finely crushed and calcined; from this, cook out the oil by resolution <note>a chemical process of dissolving or breaking down a solid into liquid form</note>, and provide it to be drunk every day and night in the amount of 1 scruple <note>a unit of weight, about 1.3 grams</note> in good wine, for 14 days. By this, all the aforesaid diseases from Tartaric stone are removed and cured. Do not let it seem absurd to you that through this one recipe, so simple and crude, such a great disease can be expelled, while in the meantime so many other recipes, so artfully fashioned, are cast aside and eliminated. Consider this within yourself: that a single splinter of burning wood gives off more heat than ten rocks. For the same judgment and distinction must be held regarding this recipe of ours, if it is compared with others either found through experience or produced by nature.

<margin>Description of the Sharpener.</margin>
Apply the Sharpening medicine externally, specifically in that place where the disease is felt. If you know the location of the diseases, you shall apply it until they are abolished and consumed: through the urine, for those that consist in the urinary ducts; <note>repeated phrase in text: "through the urine, for those that consist in the urinary ducts"</note> through the stool, for those located in those pathways. The same is similarly to be understood for the other "emunctories" <note>organs or canals that carry off waste, like sweat glands or the nose</note>.

Take: Turpentine, Linseed oil, of each an equal amount.
Let them be distilled: let a "cohobation" <note>a process of repeated distillation where the liquid is poured back over the solid remains</note> be made with these:
Take: Crab's eyes, lynx stone <note>original: "lapidis lyncis"; believed to be petrified lynx urine, actually a type of fossil</note>, sponge, oil of Ludus, Jewish stone <note>original: "iudaici"; lapis iudaicus, a fossilized sea urchin spine used for bladder issues</note>, lynx stone, of each 1 and a half drams. Saxifrage, 2 drams. And so on with the others.

<margin>All stones are resolved into water.</margin>
Through this ointment, all stones in the body are resolved and broken down into small pieces, in the manner we described in the Theory. And note regarding these recipes: we do not hold to that method which we set down in the first treatise—namely, that some things expel stones in the form of sand, others as flour, others as a stone, others as a bolus, and others as water. Rather, we have directed our recipes according to this one goal: that all stones be resolved and liquefied into water. Therefore, we omit the rest.

### CHAPTER II.

<margin>Gout is called Tartaric Salt.</margin>
Next, we shall also hand down the method of curing gouty diseases, which are themselves birthed from Tartar. We call this disease *Tartaric Salt*; this is because, like saltpeter, it exists in a granulated, frozen, angular, or sand-like state, and at the same time it stings and is produced in a salty manner.

<margin>The twofold cure for Gout.</margin>
<margin>What the Complete cure is.</margin>
<margin>What the Open cure is.</margin>
The cure for this, therefore, is twofold: *Complete* and *Open*. The Complete cure is that which is done without any injury or opening of the body; namely, so that the Tartaric salt is resolved and consumed from its foundation and roots, through both external and internal remedies. The Open cure is that which is administered by incision, so that the salt is violently extracted, as will be said in what follows. The Complete cure is as follows:

<margin>Remedy for Gout.</margin>
Take: Human bones, scammony, hermodactyls <note>a plant root used traditionally for gout</note>,
Turbith, senna, sugar candy <note>original: "zuccari taberzet"; a high-quality white sugar</note>, of each an equal amount. From these, fashion a powder, of which you shall provide half a dram to be eaten in the morning and evening for one dose.

This powder removes all fluxes and Tartaric diseases from the sick person, in such a way that it resolves the matter, as we said in the first treatise. The power of its operation proceeds from this: that the bones, by their own property, perform miracles, while the other ingredients resolve the matter by their specific power. For just as the "water of wine" <note>alcohol or vinegar</note> resolves the tartar [in a barrel], so these simples <note>medicinal herbs or minerals</note> liquefy the gouty flux.

In the meantime, while these things are being done, you shall proceed to anoint the place of pain twice a day with the following balsam:
Take: Mummy of the gallows <note>original: "Mumia patibuli"; medicine made from the remains of a person who died a violent death, believed to retain "vital spirits"</note>. Distill it, and use it as required. You shall continue this anointing until the end of the healing. For by this, every instance of gout, chiragra <note>gout in the hand</note>, and similar afflictions can be cured, because this is superior to all others.

->The external medicine is as follows.<-

<margin>The open cure for Gout.</margin>
Take: Sublimated mercury, Aqua fortis <note>nitric acid</note>, Arsenic, of each an equal amount. Let a paste be made. Apply this as far as the pain spreads. But if it has occupied the entire limb, make a hole in the place most suitable for it; then apply it to release the "eschar" <note>a piece of dead tissue that falls off from a wound, here caused by the corrosive paste</note>. Afterward, use the "attractive" remedy that follows. In this way, all the flux and Tartaric salt will be extracted, liquefied, and resolved into water. Once all the filth is evacuated, sprinkle powder of "Saffron of Mars" <note>original: "croco Martis"; iron oxide</note> into the hole and close it up. By this art and power, you can extract any gout whatsoever that yields to no other remedies. Nothing can resist this medicine. You shall prepare this "attractive" remedy in this way...

# [THE WORKS OF] THEOPHRASTUS BOMBAST
## OF HOHENHEIM.

### CHAPTER I.
### On the Falling Sickness. <note>original: *Morbo Caduco*, the historical term for epilepsy.</note>

<margin>All diseases belong either to Nature or to Reason.</margin>
**A**LL diseases that afflict man—God's creature—arise from nature itself. They either attack health by weakening the body, or, what is more serious, they take away and shatter the vigor of the mind and reason by overwhelming them. Therefore, when we consider natural diseases—in what ways and how many they violently harm our bodies—it is necessary and useful to also weigh those diseases whose force plunders the power of our reason and intellect. We must seek out from what origin they flow, since experience itself teaches and demonstrates that these diseases emerge and are stirred up by Nature itself. Although in this current age, the "European vicars of the Gods" <margin>Mental illnesses are wrongly attributed to Devils.</margin> <note>Paracelsus is likely critiquing the religious authorities or scholastic physicians of his time who blamed demons for insanity.</note> assign the cause of such diseases to incorporeal creatures and Devils, we are not compelled by any necessity of demonstration to support or agree with them in this case. Indeed, we are pulled in the opposite direction by so many proofs and reasons from nature itself that we are forced to entirely oppose the opinions of these "earthly gods." We shall teach concerning all these matters distinctly in their own chapters, explaining and directing everything clearly according to the way of nature, which is the sole cause and mother of these things. Furthermore, five species of <margin>5 species of madness. Both the healthy and the sick are subject to epilepsy.</margin> madness <note>original: *Amentia*</note> or deprivation of reason first present themselves. The first of these is the Falling Sickness, or Epilepsy. It does not pertain to just one temperament <term>complexio</term> <note>the specific balance of bodily humors</note>, nor indeed to any single one; nor does it affect only one type of person, but all. Those subject to this disease are the healthy, the sick, the young, and the old. Yet, this same disease takes nothing away from the integrity of the body, nor does it break or destroy its constitution, as will be discussed hereafter. But if this disease sometimes makes people weak or brings about death, it is for this reason: the sharpness and vehemence of the attack leaves behind certain "remnants" from which death or the contamination of the temperament eventually arises. <margin>5 types of epilepsy.</margin> Truly, five types of this falling sickness are numbered, any one of which can manifest as Epilepsy, and which can be generated in everyone indiscriminately: the first is in the Brain; the second in the Liver; the third in the Heart; fourth in the Intestines; and fifth in the Limbs. Since one type may be more lethal and dangerous than another, <margin>The first paroxysm of epilepsy may kill many.</margin> it is because the first three types occupy the most "noble" organs <term>membra</term>, whose affliction is promptly followed by death. Thus, it frequently happens that some are struck down and killed by the very first assault or paroxysm <term>paroxysmus</term> <note>a sudden attack or fit</note>. The reason for this outcome—and why the same does not happen in the other two types—will be explained more clearly later. All five of these types have a similar force of commotion and an equal deprivation of reason and senses; however, they are not produced from one single material. Just as the manner of the attacks is diverse, so the material itself <margin>The matter and epileptic paroxysms differ in different people.</margin> exists as dissimilar. For some who are seized erupt and pour out foam, others a great deal of water; some show fixed and immovably open eyes, others are shaken by frequent jolts and tossing of the body. Some lie with the body motionless, while others shout something obscure; some are totally silent. Some are violently thrown to the ground, while not a few sink down and recline gradually. Careful attention must be paid to the signs and <margin>Patients should be questioned about the location of the disease.</margin> reports of the sick. For it is of great importance to know in which place they especially feel the disease before they fall or are failed by their reason, compared to others who can feel no movement of the disease but are suddenly overwhelmed and fall as if out of their minds, not noticing the withdrawal of their reason. The commotion itself is not the cause of these things, but rather the fact that they *undergo* the commotion is the cause. Thus, for example, the brain undergoes its own commotion, just as the intestines do; yet the brain is affected more readily and quickly because it has reason itself located in its region. Hence, because of proximity and closeness, the things mentioned above occur.

Next, let us proceed to speak of the Matter from which the falling sickness is generated. It does not exist only in man, but in all things that have life, such as cattle, which fall no less than man himself and are seized by similar forms of attacks. Though there are certain kinds of animals in which this evil flourishes as something entirely hereditary and so ingrained that no individual among them is healthy or free from the disease. <margin>Weasels, lions, and certain birds are subject to epilepsy.</margin> In this category are Weasels and Lions, and many species of birds, in which this evil is never abolished. Furthermore, even growing things <note>plants</note> which <margin>Certain trees are epileptic.</margin> lack senses are often tested and afflicted by this same disease. Not indeed in such a way that they "fall," for they lack sensitive life, but in that they experience their own paroxysms similar to animals; for instance, trees split and crack apart from them, as we shall describe regarding the infirmities of trees and plants. These sometimes dry up completely, and once the paroxysm has finished, they occasionally grow again; sometimes they simply die. The same should be understood for all other things that have life: that they are equally troubled by this disease and experience its attacks, yet with the distinction of how much or how little sense each creature has been granted. But to the investigation of the cause, why those endowed with sense...

<header>TREATISE I.</header>

<margin>The causes of the falling sickness in all living things are: 1. Nourishment.</margin>
Regarding how living things, whether they are granted [life] or deprived of it, are subjected to such a **paroxysm** <note>A sudden attack or seizure.</note>, the following must be noted. No living nature acts or is sustained without the **spirit of life**, in which the life-giving force of the entire universe is stored, as we teach in our writings on that spirit. Conversely, there is no life without nourishment. Therefore, if every living thing suffers from this disease, the cause must also reside in nourishment. Thus, a commotion occurs through nourishment if it becomes mixed into the spirit of life.

<margin>2. The boiling of the spirit of life.</margin>
This, therefore, is one cause of this disease. Another cause is the **boiling of vapors** within the spirit of life—not actually from other humors or bodily qualities—and it happens in this way: when the spirit of life is altered and cast down from its proper state, it then seethes and boils over, as it were. This boiling is so agitated and violent that it devastates and removes all memory along with reason. This paroxysm is similar to the motion by which the entire world is shaken and trembles. For the cause of this

<margin>Epilepsy and earthquakes have the same cause.</margin>
disease corresponds to an earthquake; in one and the same way and manner, both the motion of the earth and the falling sickness occur. This disease is not generated by the regular order or course of Nature, nor by a weakness of the bodily temperament <note>original: *complexionis*, the balance of the four humors.</note>, nor by any corruption of the humors, but it emerges from the same single cause as an earthquake. For an earthquake is also the motion of man himself, and the motion of trees, and the motion of all created things, as we shall demonstrate in this discourse. We place the cause of earthquakes in our philosophy. Whatever that cause is, such is also the falling sickness in the body: if the spirit of life boils due to an error in its own properties, so that it shakes out and emits fumes and vapors, then the entire body is shaken and trembles from these. But why?

<margin>The spirit of life is the seat of reason.</margin>
Because, obviously, the spirit of life suffers. When this suffers, the entire body suffers with it—not in sickness, but in **madness**. For reason dwells in the spirit of life; because of this, reason is destroyed and "faints" <note>original: *syncopisat*, meaning a temporary loss of consciousness or mental function.</note> for as long as it takes for the foam or the boiling to cool down and be consumed. The tossing, the jolting, the trembling, and the foam emerge from there because all the limbs are convulsed by a spasm, and their life is afflicted; for which cause they also necessarily suffer together, etc.

<margin>Epilepsy is fivefold. Cephalic: what it is.</margin>
A fivefold difference in this disease must be understood. For one type of epilepsy is **Cephalic** <note>Related to the head (Greek: *kephalē*).</note>, the cause of which is the boiling of the spirit of life occurring in the head alone. While this stirs up corruption and foam in the brain, the dwelling-place of reason is besieged, and the senses and intellect are intercepted. Subsequently, all the limbs are harmed due to their connection, because the very "root" of the man is affected. In this case, something happens similar to an earthquake where only a single region, not the whole world, is shaken. For here, too, the disease consists in the brain alone, infesting all nearby parts, just as everything neighboring also trembles from an earthquake. Similarly, the boiling and overflow which

<margin>Hepatic epilepsy very often invades the brain.</margin>
occurs in the liver <note>original: *hepate*</note> contaminates the spirit of life in the liver; and before it can even be felt, it has already immediately occupied the brain and the entire body with such speed as the wind is carried and stirred up rapidly through all things. And just as if **Tartar** <note>In Paracelsian medicine, "tartar" refers to stony precipitates or metabolic waste that causes blockages.</note> falls into "strong water" <note>original: *aquam fortem*, an acid or reactive solvent; here describing a violent chemical reaction.</note>, even in a tiny amount, it immediately stirs up a powerful boiling; so too is the spirit of life itself swift and burning. **Cardiac epilepsy** happens when the spirit

<margin>Cardiac Epilepsy: how it happens.</margin>
of life boils in the capsule of the heart. Yet it cannot poison (just as an earthquake does not produce infertility), unless it happens that through the trembling and jolting of the upper limbs, a certain "dissolution" is induced. From such dissolution, death can follow, just as a house collapses from an earthquake—not because of poison, but from the agitation and shaking. The same thing should be understood in the same way regarding that which takes its origin in the intestines.

<margin>Intestinal Epilepsy: how it happens.</margin>
For here the disease has its root from which it is produced, just as a herb emerges from a seed, falls, and is born again. A similar root exists in the spirit of life, which produces such a "plant" from which these kinds of diseases arise. Moreover, the location of this root can be anywhere in the whole body: in the head, and thus the disease arises in the head; in the liver, and it arises there; in the capsule of the heart, and it rises there. Similarly, it should also be understood regarding the belly, that the root sometimes lies in the intestines or neighboring places, according to where it is sown. For wherever it is sown, there it remains and is fixed; it does not change its location or creep further, because it does not spread more than one root. This same root is similarly fixed sometimes in the limbs, such as the **hands and feet**, in

<margin>Epilepsy of the limbs: how it happens, namely epilepsy of the hands and feet. Wandering epilepsy of the body: what it is.</margin>
which places the beginning of the paroxysm is also frequently detected; rising from there, it is diffused through the whole body along with the spirit of life. It also happens that the root is fixed in no certain place, because it is not so substantial or material in itself that it can remain fixed anywhere; instead, it is distributed through the whole body and suddenly rushes into the reason afterward.

Furthermore, since we have so far discussed the causes and seats from which epilepsy emerges, let us now say something further about the spirit of life: in what way it is infected so that a paroxysm now attacks, now is felt less, and how it happens that no illness weighs upon the person outside of the paroxysm. Diseases of this kind, the falling sickness, are conceived in the **mother's womb**, where their root is inserted and implanted into the fetuses; this root later grows as they are brought into the light of day, for the following reason. Due to the weakness of the sperm, a poor diet, or an unordered lifestyle, the spirit of life in the fetus is produced as something far from perfect and robust; and thus, from the bad constitution of the parents,

<margin>Epilepsy is hereditary: why and how.</margin>
the spirit of life is also contaminated and infected in the fetus. From this assault, if the spirit of life in the fetus is perfect, it then expels what is foreign and unsuitable from itself. And although it cannot entirely drive it out of the body, it nonetheless continuously pushes it away until the whole mass is forced and gathered into a single place. This is deposited in whatever location is subject to the <unclear>expulsive</unclear> power of all the places, and there it fixes its root. The reason this disease does not reveal itself immediately and continuously is because the root itself is either not yet strong or large enough to exert its virulence immediately. Instead, it sometimes lasts and grows stronger until it is barely recognized even in the 70th year. However, many other causes can contribute to this delay, such as the strength of the body, vigorous health, a good and healthy diet, and such things.

<summary>Paracelsus defines epilepsy (the falling sickness) as an internal 'earthquake' caused by the boiling of the spirit of life, which can be rooted in the head, liver, heart, intestines, or limbs. He also explains the disease as a hereditary condition implanted in the womb that may remain dormant for decades depending on a person's health and diet.</summary>
