<meta>This page continues the discussion from page 565 regarding the physical origins of mental disorders. Paracelsus is moving from epilepsy to "Mania" (a general term for madness or delirium), arguing that these conditions are caused by internal alchemical processes—specifically distillation and sublimation—rather than demonic influence or a simple imbalance of the four humors.</meta>

<page-num>567</page-num>
<header>TREATISE I.</header>

# TREATISE I.

Sometimes, mania is raised by the stomach alone as it dissolves its own phlegm or other contained matter; when this finally creeps into the brain, a similar distillation or sublimation occurs. By the same logic, this can also happen in the liver or the lungs. The same variety occurs around the intestines and kidneys, etc., because some distillations and sublimations arise from dregs, others from the spirit of urine, others from the phlegm of the intestines, or whatever else is usually contained in them. Any one of these, by itself, can trigger Mania. For this reason, many types of Mania can be stirred up, yet all are encompassed by the three boundaries already mentioned. Furthermore, we shall now recount what it is from which Mania arises, how it can be resolved, how it is made ready for distillation and sublimation, and where it is birthed.

<margin>Two kinds of heat.</margin>
Immoderate, violent, and great heat exists in two forms: **Fiery**, of course, and putrid or putrefying. The cause of that heat is as follows.

<margin>What kind of reverberation of matter occurs in Mania.</margin>
When the matter of that place from which the Mania rises is reverberated into **lime** <term>calx: the powdery residue left after a substance has been "burned" or oxidized in an alchemical process</term>, which is afterwards resolved into a far more biting water: then that sharp resolution ignites the **humor of life** <note>The fluid that Paracelsus believes carries the vital spirit throughout the body.</note>. As far as it reaches that humor, a separation of the subtle from the coarse occurs. In this matter, however, the "subtlety" is so sharp that nothing remains at the bottom, but everything flies off to the top, leaving the dross at the bottom. This **Reverberation** is caused by the great heat that arises in those places, which are inflamed until such great subtlety emerges. Now, just as this kind of Reverberation varies, so too does the Resolution. For one kind is in the blood, another in the ligaments, and another in the other places we have mentioned. Resolution in the blood occurs when the spirit of salt, which is in the blood, is mixed into one with the spirit of life.

<margin>Why bloodletting sometimes cures Mania.</margin>
As soon as the distilled humors, which are sublimated by the heat of the lower members, strike the cells of the brain with their subtlety and sharpness, Mania breaks out immediately. If, therefore, it is in the blood alone, then if the true and correct vein is cut, that distilled spirit exits and breathes out. But if the distilled matter is not in the blood but occupies the entire head, then **phlebotomy** <term>bloodletting: the surgical withdrawal of blood to cure illness</term> is of very little use, as will be handed down in the section on the cure. In the same way, Mania is sometimes removed by opening the veins of the hands and toes, because through this, a certain "cooling" and air is introduced, hindering the future heating of the matter within itself and thus preventing its ascent. However, if this does not always help perfectly, it is because the matter was not sufficiently cooled or the distillation was not enough removed. If Mania of this kind lurks in the veins, such an opening does not help, because above all, the center must be sought out, and the diversion must be made there first, as will be taught in the section on the cure.

<margin>Worms. Abscesses or pus from the matter of mania.</margin>
It also happens that the matter of Mania is sometimes sublimated and coagulated in the head. From the putrefaction of this ready and rapid sublimation, either worms are born in the head, or abscesses (because of a coagulation that is too hard), or pus. When this pus is diffused through the whole head, gnawing and stinging sensations in the head are produced along with sharp pains. Sometimes these resolutions in the head are consumed again until only a tiny surviving droplet remains; if this alone lies in a dangerous place, a certain Mania emerges from it. But when the matter is not resolved at all but remains coagulated, then the burned quality gnaws like salt in a wound; from this, reason is shattered and perishes. To put it in a word, the place of origin of Mania can hardly be investigated and explored enough, as we are indicating here in a general sense. Thus, the sublimation sometimes takes its beginning in the stomach alone—and not always in the whole stomach, but sometimes in some tiny part of it. Nevertheless, if medicine is provided and administered to the whole stomach, whatever evil sticks anywhere is removed. However, it should be well noted here that this does not happen in a similar way in the veins. For sublimation in a vein can occur sometimes in only one, sometimes in several, and sometimes in all at once. The same judgment applies to the ligaments. Nevertheless, if the evil resides in the liver, lung, or spleen, then whichever of these members it is, it is treated as a whole with a suitable cure.

<margin>A reprimand of Medicine.</margin>
Here we must also note that there exist **four temperaments** <note>original: *complexiones*; the traditional Galenic system of the four humors (Sanguine, Choleric, Melancholic, and Phlegmatic).</note>, from each of which certain ancients thought Mania could be provoked. However, we do not yet grasp how, for example, **Melancholy** <note>Black bile.</note> could be the cause of Mania. For if Melancholy were the cause, then only the melancholic part would suffer. Similarly, it would be the same if either the whole **yellow bile** <note>original: *cholera*.</note>, or the blood, or the phlegm alone were the cause. Therefore, that opinion of the ancients is not at all true.

<margin>Why Mania is not from the humors.</margin>
For since Mania is stirred up from three parts of the body altogether, it certainly cannot be generated from a single temperament. Nor are they distributed according to the temperaments. Furthermore, if Mania arose from the temperaments as those people wish, then no distillation or sublimation could occur from the outer members to the head. For it is the disposition of no temperament that it can be reduced to such great subtlety that the head is driven to delirium by it. Finally, Mania also first arises from certain members that are governed by no temperament. If this is true, it will be false that Mania is generated from the temperaments, as we shall say regarding the temperaments. However, a certain Mania can sometimes arise from a single place where Melancholy dwells and dominates, such as the spleen—but not by reason of the Melancholy itself, but by reason of the **spirit of life**, which separates itself from the Melancholy in the way we have described and ascends to the heights.

<margin>Mania from the spirit of life alone.</margin>
From this it is clear that Mania is stirred up by the spirit of life alone, ascending upwards into the head through distillation and sublimation, as has been said. The same judgment applies to Mania generated from the gallbladder, yet not from the yellow bile contained within it; and so on. We conclude, therefore, that all the spirits of life and the matters from which Mania arises are of one nature, quality, temperament, and essence. One is not hot, another cold, this one moist, and that one dry, but there is one equality of them all. Mania is generated in no other way than that the matter is so subtle and sharp that it overwhelms the brain—

<margin>
What the true causes of Mania are.
</margin>
...shadows [the reason], and in this way cuts off the cells of reason. For by this means a man becomes Maniacal. Furthermore, something must be noted and said regarding the timing of Mania, and the behaviors or gestures of the Maniacs, from which it might be concluded that this disease is born from celestial influence or [elemental] qualities—though this is not at all the case. For it can indeed happen that a disease increases or diminishes alongside an influence; however, in the meantime, the power to increase or decrease is not situated within the influence itself. For we teach regarding human influence that it is a pure lie that influences moderate and govern our bodies in a physical or material sense; rather, the "internal and congenital influence" <note>Paracelsus believed every human contains their own "inner firmament" or internal stars that correspond to the heavens.</note> within us does all of this. Therefore, we also posit concerning Mania that it is produced from human influence, which flourishes no less in us than in the celestial bodies above.

<margin>
Influence has no power over the body.
</margin>
The evidence of gestures and behaviors does not emerge from the qualities <note>The four "qualities" of traditional medicine: hot, cold, moist, and dry.</note>, even if they are thought to be entirely stirred up by them. For if a Maniac mutters to himself, he is not for that reason to be called "Melancholic"; nor is he who busies himself with hitting and striking to be deemed "Choleric." Instead, behaviors and gestures flow from another cause. For if a Melancholic person—one who exists as a natural Melancholic by their very nature—should turn Maniacal, then the "manic matter" ignites and stimulates their old and former behaviors and habits, which they were otherwise accustomed to practice, so that the sick person returns to them in a similar way. The same thing happens in others in the same manner. For Mania is a certain "prompter and discloser" of hidden behaviors and properties which men previously hid and disguised with great effort.

<margin>
Human influence is the cause of Mania.
</margin>
Then, there is also some Mania which does not exhibit the nature familiar to the man, but rather elicits other behaviors contrary and adverse to him. Therefore, pay attention to who reveals himself: since it frequently happens that a man's complexion is set against the Mania and strives to expel it. If this happens, then the man's natural qualities are also revealed, but not those of the disease itself. From all of this, it is established and demonstrated that Mania does not arise from the [humoral] qualities, but only indicates the nature itself as it essentially is—just as we said at the beginning regarding those types produced either from dregs, or the spirit of urine, or other similar things. This is not as if they arise from Melancholy, but because dregs and urine have a certain property similar to Melancholy, yet they do not participate in it even a tiny bit. As for those three points mentioned at the beginning, and whatever else is required to understand Mania: you will find them more clearly expressed in the "Second Method" under the care of Mania.

<margin>
Mania sometimes exhibits behaviors even contrary to nature.
</margin>

### CHAPTER III.
### On the Disease or "Cholera" of Saint Vitus, and similar things.

<margin>
*Chorea lascivia* is the disease of St. Vitus.
</margin>
**I**n this chapter, we shall by no means agree with those who assert that the Saints inflict peculiar diseases, and that names ought to be given to diseases according to them. Furthermore, it is not at all clear from Holy Scripture that this disease is a fatal punishment, even though many declaim deeply on this matter with I-know-not-what "theological" arguments, attributing and imputing the disease more to God than to nature. Indeed, I utterly loathe trifles of that sort, which follow and acknowledge as their teacher nothing but rash opinion—a thing unworthy of man himself, and likewise hateful even to God. Therefore, we shall not rashly change the name itself, which has been taken from the Saint and has testified to the disease until now. In the meantime, however, this disease—for reasons to be stated hereafter—will more rightly be called <term>Chorea lascivia</term> <note>Literally "wanton dance" or "playful dance." Paracelsus is attempting to secularize the condition known as St. Vitus' Dance.</note>.

<margin>
What *Chorea lascivia* is.
</margin>
Meanwhile, let us explode the inconsistent babbling of the Sophists, who chatter much about God whom they do not know, and who everywhere wander away from the prescribed path that leads to the knowledge of Him. The cause of *chorea lascivia*, therefore, is merely an "estimation" and a preconceived imagination, which works in the person who deems and judges it to be "fatal" <note>In this context, "fatal" means destined by fate or divine decree.</note>, and who thus imagines such things for themselves. This kind of estimation and imagination alone is the principle and cause of the present disease or dance. And although a similar affection is found separately even in those people in whom estimation and imagination do not yet flourish, such as in infants and some adults; nevertheless, even in infants, the cause of the affection is imagination—not indeed according to the intellect, but moved through hearing.

<margin>
How infants are seized by the dance.
</margin>
For such things happen to them because of hearing and sight in this way. The sight and hearing of an infant are so strong that they are occupied by the phantasy and imagination of things seen and heard, even unknowingly. Under that phantasy, the reason of the infant is taken away and changed by that "species" <note>In medieval philosophy, a "species" is the sensory image or "likeness" of an object that travels to the mind.</note> which the object presented to them. In the same way, in adults who are not held by any imagination of the work or exercise of the dance itself, yet see or hear those things being done, their own vision and hearing overcome and conquer their reason. But as for the fact that dances and leaping provoke those people to whom no such "species" is presented through sight or hearing, but where such an exultation falls upon them without any occasion: the cause is placed in the <term>venis risuis</term> <note>The "veins of laughter." Paracelsus believed specific veins or vessels were responsible for triggering the physical response of laughter and leaping.</note>, which, being tickled by a subtle spirit, stimulate them to such a dance and leaping.

<margin>
The veins of laughter are the cause of the dance.
</margin>
<margin>
A twofold cause of the dance.
</margin>
Now, furthermore, there are two causes of this disease of the dance: one is <term>Natural</term>, from the <term>veins of laughter</term>; the other is <term>Accidental</term>, from imaginative objects. The principle from the cause of such a dance is as follows. In every man, the <term>veins of laughter</term> are established: if these are struck and emptied, a laughter so persistent seizes the man that he cannot suppress it before the blood is restrained. And if the blood is not stopped, the laughter lasts until death.

<margin>
The so-called veins of laughter bring on perpetual cackling. Why and how laughter [comes] from the veins.
</margin>
And those veins exist as the cause of this disease in such a way. Even if they are not wounded but remain whole: nevertheless, the spirit existing within—from which they have life and are sustained—if it should be altered and changed so that it transgresses its order and motion, it leaps, as it were, and jumps, and the blood itself dances. From this dancing, first comes a tickling, and afterwards laughter follows: from which it finally happens that the spirit in the veins is moved more and more from time to time, and the tickling is continually intensified. For the veins are situated in wanton and ticklish places, and thus from the innermost property of nature, they are disposed and inclined toward laughter.

<margin>
The spirit of life is corrupted.
</margin>
But if anyone should ask the cause why the spirit of life...

He emphasizes the power of the imagination and sensory input (sight and sound) to override human reason and trigger involuntary physical responses.</summary>

# TREATISE I.

<margin>Salt of the blood as the cause of the changed spirit of life.</margin>
...they are corrupted and dissolved, since life itself is as subtle as those very veins, and for this reason, the matter cannot easily be grasped by natural means: let the mind consider this more closely. Just as **burning wine** <note>original: "vinũ ardens"; likely referring to distilled alcohol or "spirit of wine," used here as a metaphor for volatile substances.</note>, enclosed and sealed in some vessel and placed in a warm spot, becomes sharper, subtler, and lighter as time progresses: so too must it be understood regarding the **spirit of life** <note>The vital force that Paracelsus believed animated the body and moved through the vessels.</note> situated in the veins, that through natural heat it is continually refined and sharpened, until a fire invades the blood. The blood then takes on the quality of that fire, just as simple wine mixed with distilled or burning wine changes its original nature and essence. But furthermore, we must diligently consider the cause of the spirit of life in those veins: what exactly is it that harms that spirit, or disposes it to be brought to such subtlety and sharpness? For it did not receive this from its own innate nature and property. Therefore, the cause that refines it and leads the blood to this disease is as follows. In the blood there is a certain **salt** or saltiness, which by its innermost nature has a disposition to fall into acidity, sharpness, or bitterness, according to how other circumstances hold. For whatever is material and corporeal in the body is apt and prone to change, no differently than how wood can either rot, be reduced to ashes, or become charcoal, whether by its own nature or by external accident.
<margin>The spirit of life is not harmed in itself.</margin>
The same must be understood regarding salt: when altered and changed, it renders the spirit of life furious and flaming. This is not because the spirit itself is harmed—since it has no body, it cannot be harmed—but because it dwells in an unsuitable and preternatural lodging, which it plainly recoils from and bears with difficulty. For just as **Camphor** placed in an impure place does not remain, and as **saltpeter** <note>Potassium nitrate, a key ingredient in gunpowder, known for its volatile reaction to fire.</note> does not suffer its opposite in the fire: so here too the same must be understood.

<margin>The manner and generation of the dance from sight and hearing.</margin>
Now, the **dancing mania** <note>original: "chorea"; often referring to St. Vitus' Dance or the dancing manias prevalent in the Middle Ages and Renaissance.</note> that is not produced by this physiological "tickling" is of another and different kind; its cause is placed in sight or hearing, and it is generated in this way. All joy stirred up in a man takes its first principle from the heart. Now, sight and hearing are things that penetrate to the heart. Thus, if I hear someone playing a pipe, and I am moved by the nature of the pipe’s song, I immediately feel and capture delight and joy in the heart itself. This joy is twofold: for at once I contemplate my own pleasure, toward which I am inclined, and furthermore, my sense is directed and constrained toward the **imagination** <note>In Paracelsian psychology, the "imagination" was a powerful force that could physically alter the body's chemistry.</note> of what I see before me. Now, while I impress the song of the pipe upon my nature, a certain delight emerges, by which the joy in the heart overcomes and prevails; and just as I conceive it, so it is impressed upon me, and all other foreign qualities and natures are driven out, so that they succumb and have no further operation. Following this comes a deprivation of the senses, though not of reason itself; yet the force and power of reason is blunted, so that I act according to my conceived imagination or the thing seen before me, and—despising reason—I follow or emulate the impulse of the imagination. My own **consent** <note>original: "consensio"; the willful agreement to give in to the impulse.</note> becomes the cause of that disease. And this happens naturally, so that the 

---

<margin>What the dances of harlots are like.</margin>
consent which a man firms up with a burning vow or a strong desire is perfected according to the conceived imagination, as we shall discuss more extensively and clearly in the section on imaginations. Therefore, the cause is evident and manifest why **harlots** <note>original: "meretrices"; used here to categorize those leading a "dissolute" or "lascivious" life.</note> and wicked people, who take excessive delight in the melodies of the lute, the cittern, and other instruments, are moved away from them with difficulty. Instead, they are carried away by full enticements and, as it were, gorge themselves; snatched away by a solid estimation or imagination, they gape after these things. Being cast into the disease in this way, they continue and insistently urge on the same joy, the same screeching, shouting, song, or dance, or whatever of this sort they were practicing. And this "dance of harlots" of which we speak is not at all "natural" in the sense that it is moved by nature itself as a cause (as we said at the beginning regarding the **laughing veins**); rather, it is a certain accident and consequence, stirred up by foul lewdness and a wicked lust for living, where all reason and sense are exiled. For this reason, they show themselves to be so unbridled, insane, and brutish. Meanwhile, there are many who neither lead nor contemplate that foul and inhuman life so as to be singularly and intimately delighted by it, but rather dance out of a fortuitous chance or without deliberation. 
<margin>Various forms and from where?</margin>
And these people are incited and stimulated by the **laughing veins** <note>original: "venae risuae"; Paracelsus' term for the conduits that trigger involuntary laughter or twitching.</note> in the exact manner we described. Furthermore, there is another dance (as we can testify from our own experience) which involves laughter alone, from which shouting, clamor, and rejoicing are absent; another involves laughter and movement, so that they cannot sit still at all, but are compelled to walk and laugh at the same time. This also arises from the causes mentioned, namely from the laughing veins: yet with this distinction, that the spirit is not greatly changed, or the blood is not entirely changed, so that the paroxysm happens lightly at times and then eases again. But it must also be remembered that various joys burst forth from the heart in this way. If the heart feels a **false spirit**, it can be stimulated by it to laughter, no differently than if the spirit of life of a laughing vein were to strike and beat the heart most violently. For the heart can be affected by joy from a

false spirit, just as the heart is usually burned with sorrow by the **spleen**. For the reason for both is the same. Where, furthermore, this also happens and can occur: that the joy moved by the spirit of life is carried upward into the head, and occupies and possesses it, ruling and compelling it in its own way. These people are not impelled by any violent necessity of "falsification," but are ready and prepared for whatever they are led or applied to; meanwhile, they are neither instructed nor powerful in their senses or reason as is fitting. But other dancers are irrefragably compelled by the force of their disease to dance, cry out, and shout, appearing ridiculous in all those gestures. In this way, therefore, one should understand the cause by which they are incited to the dance, the skipping, and other things similar to these, just as we recounted a little earlier regarding estimation and imagination. ...contain much more within themselves. For in those people, life is set on fire, which seeks and moves so greatly. Meanwhile, even this morbid **chorea** <note>original: "chorea"; referring to the "dancing mania" or St. Vitus' Dance mentioned in previous pages.</note> is an alienation of the reason, specifically because joy predominates and eliminates all other qualities. It is not that it infects or abolishes memory itself, but rather that it suppresses it and constrains it, so that it cannot break through or shine forth because of the obstacle of the disease. Furthermore, as for the timing—why it leaps up alternately, and sometimes lasts longer and sometimes shorter—that happens solely from the abundance of the matter and its disposition. For as that matter is more or less intense, it lasts for a shorter or longer time. However, we shall now put the **finishing touch** <note>original: "colophonem imponemus"; a classical expression meaning to complete or crown a work.</note> to this disease of chorea, nor shall we lead the power of the Gods into contempt; they have full and complete power to send this punishment of disease upon wanton and wild men. Yet, that the natural cause and origin of the disease is removed by this fact is nothing. For this disease can be entirely stirred up from the disposition of nature itself, just as we shall make mention of several such diseases in our book *On the Plague of God* <note>original: "De plaga Dei"</note>. Other matters which seem to belong here will be more fully delivered and explained in the chapter on the cure of **Wanton Chorea** <note>original: "Choreae lasciuae"</note>.

### CHAPTER IV.
### On the Origin of the Suffocation of the Intellect.

<margin>The suffocation of the intellect is triple.</margin>
There are also other deprivations of reason, arising from natural diseases, through which the sense of reason is driven away. There are three such **suffocations** <note>term: "suffocationes" (suffocations); in this context, it refers to a "stifling" of consciousness or a blockage of the mental faculties, rather than literal respiratory choking.</note>: one tests only those who have **intestinal worms** <note>original: "lumbricos"</note> in their bowels; the second arises only in women from the **womb** <note>original: "matrice"; referring to the historical medical belief in "suffocation of the mother" or hysteria.</note>; the third happens to both sexes, arising as much from standing as from sitting and from immoderate food and drink. To these is added a fourth, which weighs upon one only in sleep, and ceases again with sleep. Of these, there are two distinct types: one is with some foreboding and foreknowledge, by which the <margin>Suffocation of the intellect is either with sensation or without.</margin> laboring person feels and knows the evil weighing upon them within; the other attacks with ignorance, so that the sick person is now afflicted and then restored without any sensation or knowledge. Regarding the former, a much more certain and safe understanding can be taken than regarding the latter: for it often happens that these people are stripped of life without any reason or knowledge. This is not because reason itself induces such a death, but because the disease that puts reason to flight similarly strikes down life itself; just as in those who have worms, death itself is sometimes accustomed to weigh upon them during a **paroxysm** <note>term: "paroxysmo"; a sudden attack or increase in the intensity of a disease's symptoms.</note>, as will be taught in our book *On Worms*. So too in women, life is sometimes cut short by the compression of the womb. Sometimes also death rushes in from standing and sitting: because the air or spirit of the heart is suppressed, as our commentaries *On the Destruction of Death* teach. In these diseases, there are many other prognostic signs of good or evil, life or death. For sometimes they fall like **epileptics** <note>original: "epilepticorum instar"</note>, and following their example, they are also convulsed, so that by the similarity of many symptoms they are compared to epileptics. Although this same suffocation of reason does not always fall with such a terror of signs: but sometimes reveals itself with a peaceful sleep and a fall, as we shall say hereafter; sometimes it even seizes with some indication of surviving reason. For there are many such suffocations, and others can emerge from time to time crowded with new and unusual signs. Thus, for example, from worms—born not in one way but variously, and stabling in different places—various paroxysms, and even fiercer ones, can easily be stirred up. The same must be judged as true for other things by a similar judgment. <margin>Two sources of suffocation.</margin> Such a suffocation in a human arises chiefly from two places: from the middle of the body, and from the belly. Furthermore, a third also consists in the head alone, but not from its own nature, but from an accident, such as from a blow or a wound, which are the causes of it and stir it up, as will be declared.

<margin>Suffocation of the intellect happens in two ways.</margin>
First, however, we must understand what and of what kind the generation of suffocation is. Its mode is twofold. One happens through **smoke** <note>original: "fumum"; Paracelsus often used "smoke" or "vapors" to describe metabolic byproducts that affected the brain.</note>, which remains from a paroxysm of **headache** <note>original: "cephalalgiae"</note>, the remnants of which have destroyed the sensitive power of the head. The other is generated by the diversion and withdrawal of air tending toward the heart. And those who are affected in this way feel pains around the **precordia** <note>term: "praecordia"; the region of the body in front of the heart or the upper abdomen.</note>, near the region of the heart. The origin of the smoke, however, is from the stomach, containing a certain matter from which worms either are born or have emerged. If that matter and the worms are ever separated from the excrement, or if they rot; or if some worms devour others, or if they move and agitate this matter (of which there is usually a great abundance) in the stomach: then from that place a certain smoke is carried upward to the head, which overshadows the brain and the **sleep-inducing veins** <note>original: "venas soporiferas"</note> so that men, with the oppression of reason, are cast into sleep, joined with evident snoring and restless, terrifying dreams and powerful oppressions. For any **intellect** can be abolished by way of damaged sleep, just as we teach concerning sleep. For that affection or injury also harms the brain itself, from which a sleepy and sluggish sensation results. And these things are to be understood thus universally concerning worms, which cling either in the stomach itself or its orifice. But the worms of the belly dwell in the intestines. These do not test the head in the way we said regarding the stomach worms, but stir up their paroxysms without smokes and vapors besieging the head. Its generation is such: namely, their exhalation and smoke cannot be carried upward to the head, and that for very many reasons. Nevertheless, the same vapor, by its exhalation and smoking out, strikes the borders of the heart, so much so that the air as well as the nutrients traveling to the heart are infected and contaminated. If the heart is then entangled and affected by these infected things, then it is as if suffocated and strangled in itself, and thus, according to the quantity of the offending matter, death itself can finally be induced—something which can by no means happen in the brain by a similar process. But when that matter has ceased its raging or has burned out, there is a return to health after the fact. And in this way, one paroxysm can follow another. <margin>An affection of the heart is imprinted on the whole body.</margin> For if the heart suffers, the spirits of life of the entire body are affected together with it: from which thereafter spasm, tremor, oppression, tension, agitation, and many similar signs occur, all of which finally result in a certain insensibility of the whole body...

<header>TREATISE I.</header>

<margin>How the womb suffocates.</margin>
...insensibility follows, so that the sick prevail neither in sense nor in intellect. The entire blood, all the humors, and the spirits of the body boil together, not otherwise than if **sulfur and saltpeter** <note>original: "sulphur & salpetræ"; these were the primary ingredients of gunpowder, used here to describe a violent chemical reaction in the body.</note> were ignited together; once this happens, the boiling and agitation do not cease until the opposing force is consumed or life itself is shaken out. A similar explanation must also be given and explained regarding the **womb** <note>original: "matrice"; referring to the medical condition known as "suffocation of the womb" or hysteria.</note>. Although its underlying cause is different, it is nevertheless manifested by the same signs, indications, and behaviors. For if the innate and natural character of the womb is altered and cast into a contrary disposition, a certain compression of the womb arises, by which both sense and intellect are taken away at once. This happens for the reason that the matter of the womb, from which it lives and is nourished, is destroyed within itself, just like **wine that turns sour**. Hence it happens that the womb suffers from a lack of true and genuine nourishment. Its own matter has exceeded the limits of its nature and has become chilled. This coldness contracts and convulses the substance and <margin>The power of cold and acidity.</margin> membranes of the womb like a kind of spasm. For this is the perpetual property and nature of acidity and coldness: by its own power, it inflicts **spasms or pierces** <note>original: "spasmú aut cópunctiones"</note> all the members of the body, if you except the flesh and bones. In the same way, therefore, the coldness of the womb itself triggers a certain spasm, and drives and contracts it as tightly as possible into a single knot or globe. Through this **stiffness and spasm** <note>original: "tetanum spasmúq;"</note>, the other members of the body likewise fall into and are forced into spasms and stiffness, because they are similarly defiled and contaminated by the womb. Therefore, while the intestines and all nearby members are forced together by such a constriction, a noxious vapor breathing out from the womb attacks all the closest members, until finally, when the heart itself is struck and buffeted by it, a **paroxysm** <note>A sudden attack or fit.</note> arises, accompanied by all the signs of the **falling sickness** <note>original: "morbi caduci"; a historical term for epilepsy.</note>. Thus, no member suffers so evidently in sympathy with the womb as the heart itself, with the matter acting as the mediator. Nevertheless, the other members in the meantime are not entirely free from their own symptoms.

<margin>
The third kind of suffocation. Its species are:
1. The Incubus and how it happens.
</margin>
Furthermore, another and third type of suffocation remains, inflicted in many and diverse ways, all related types of which can only be understood and tracked down with difficulty. From this category is that suffocation which seizes those who are sleeping, lying with their bodies on their backs. For by this position, the **water of the heart** <note>original: "cordis aqua"; likely referring to the pericardial fluid.</note> is lowered into the bottom of its capsule, so that the heart is left bare at the top. This arrangement inflicts weakness upon the heart. For if it does not sit, as if floating, in the middle of the water, it then deprives one of intellect and senses, and even crushes the strength and vigor of all the limbs.

<margin>The Galenists are refuted regarding the Incubus.</margin>
Although there are some who say this affection is the **Incubus** <note>A "nightmare" or sleep paralysis, historically attributed to a weight or demon pressing on the chest.</note>, generated by blood flowing to the heart, this is actually nothing. For blood can bring no harm to the heart unless another disease is present, other than the act of lying on one's back, and this is for many reasons. So also others think that blood flows away from the heart, and that from this deprivation the heart lies exposed, and thus sleepers dream that they can move neither hands nor feet; yet even this is not true. For in this case, many reasons can be given why blood can never flow away from the heart in such a way that it causes damage to the heart. From this it is clear that the sole cause of this suffocation is that for those who lie flat on their backs, the circle of the **heart's capsule** <note>original: "capsulæ cordis"; the pericardium.</note> becomes flatter and more pressed than is right, and like a bladder full of water, it swells out wider. When this happens, if the heart is laid bare at the top, or if the membrane of the capsule touches it, then those lying down feel compressions as if from a **great stone placed upon them**. For many things surround the heart which can materially lean upon the heart-capsule of those sleeping on their backs and thus oppress it, which cannot happen to those sleeping on their side or belly; for many reasons which Anatomy explains, and which are by no means to be repeated here. <margin>2. Sleepy suffocations, etc.</margin> Furthermore, other diseases also loom during sleep, taking away reason and inflicting madness, just as happens in the falling sickness. There are two principal causes of these: one is from compression, similar to the incubus; the other is from compression of the brain. Its generation is like this: if the heart is so oppressed that the **spirit of life** <note>original: "spiritus vitæ"; the vital force believed to animate the body.</note> grows hot or catches fire, then it inflames the entire body and rages and raves so powerfully that it besieges the reason and the faculty of sleep, and stirs up and induces trembling and agitation, just like the falling sickness. At the same time, it can also happen that even if the patient rolls onto his belly, the evil does not soften or cease. For what reason? Because, namely, the spirit of life is still in a state of fury and boiling. This disease is never felt in the morning after sleep is finished, and from the paroxysm, a **citrine water** <note>original: "aqua citrina"; a yellowish fluid.</note> usually breaks out. This is undoubtedly what the spirit of life, through its boiling, has drawn out and produced. But it can also sometimes happen that the spirit of life deserts all the members and leaves them as if dead, and withdraws itself to the heart, brain, and liver alone, so that in the other members no surviving life is felt. For just as the power and all the sap of a tree can hide in the root alone, so that the rest of the parts of the tree are dry for a while yet receive life again later, so also the spirit of life can be spread again from the center or root—that is, from the heart—after the boiling of the humors subsides, throughout the entire body, and imbue all parts once more with their former life. We shall make fuller mention of this in the "Cure," in the chapter of the Second Method. It also frequently happens that in sleep an epileptic paroxysm, or suffocation, or some other similar affection of which we have already spoken, seizes the person; however, we deliver nothing separate about them here but leave them with the others. For whatever can happen by day, the same must likewise be believed to happen by night.

<margin>The influence of the heavens moves diseases.</margin>
Here, however, we must also consider the course and movements of the **superior bodies** <note>The stars and planets.</note>, as they have the power of either increasing, generating, or taking away diseases. For we have found that sometimes such paroxysms are stirred up by **celestial influence** <note>original: "influentiâ"; astrological or atmospheric influence.</note> alone, all other causes being absent. The reason for this event is that the spirit is affected according to the condition of the influence, becoming either more cheerful or more turbulent. Moreover, there are also other forms of madness, yet accompanied by no disordered or furious gestures. For if someone should fall while sitting and fall asleep, it happens for this reason: namely, that the matter of this disease, of which we have spoken, does not greatly ignite the spirit of life. Indeed, in the same way we mentioned the heart can be compressed...

<header>ON DISEASES ARISING FROM TARTAR</header>
<note>In Paracelsian medicine, "Tartar" refers to stony or sandy deposits formed in the body—much like the crust in a wine barrel—which he believed caused many obstructions and illnesses.</note>

<margin>How the brain is compressed.</margin>
In a similar way, it can also happen in the head that the <term>sleep-inducing veins</term><note>original: "venæ soporiferæ"; likely referring to the jugular veins or carotid arteries, which ancient medicine believed caused sleep when compressed.</note>, by their own compression, may stifle the brain itself and the reason within the **delicate membrane** <note>original: "pia matre"; the *pia mater* is the innermost layer of the meninges surrounding the brain.</note>, just as the "suffocation of the womb" constricts the womb, from which disease follows. The reason for this is that sleep overflows the entire head and pushes the **spirit of life** into the brain for as long as it takes for that spirit to cool down and flow back into the other limbs. Indeed, this "suffocation" attacks with all those signs, such as spasms and tremors, just as we reviewed concerning the Heart and the Womb. Furthermore, sleep is far more extensively harmed than the heart, and moreover with a more severe injury to the reason. A similar suffocation can also be generated from **excessive indulgence** <note>original: "crapula"; referring to the sickness caused by overeating or heavy drinking.</note>, the explanation for which is the same as that for worms in the stomach. Although it is not caused by the "matter of worms," it happens in this way: <margin>Suffocation from excess.</margin> <margin>The spirit of drinkers under them.</margin> Drinkers, you see, contain within themselves a subtle spirit which, by its very subtlety, harms both sleep and the brain in the manner often described. Then, too, excess generates <term>phlegm</term> in the stomach which, as it rots and joins with the "matter of worms," acts similarly to worms. Meanwhile, the same condition can nonetheless be induced by foods and drinks that do not have such a subtle spirit—such as porridge and water—for the reason that there is a certain impurity in porridge and water which has a specific property for producing diseases of this kind. This property, however, is not in all water and porridge, but only in some. For example: if a certain water has conceived a "worm-bearing poison" or has soaked up the filth of beasts, then it is fit to produce such diseases. So also, if such a poison or excrement lies hidden in porridge, it has the power to produce the disease. Besides what has been said, the intellect is also suffocated by the accidents of **blows** <note>physical trauma</note>: for instance, if a wound has been inflicted on someone's head, from which—at certain times of the year—**Mania**, insanity, and forgetfulness are stirred up. The cause of these things is that an "influence" occurs in the body no less than in the heavens, as is mentioned regarding celestial influences. If, therefore, that time is at hand when the head is naturally affected, then the wound is also touched at the same time, and Mania is moved at that defined period. However, the same is also incited by the poor treatment of a wound, when too much **pus** <note>original: "pus"</note> collects, which boils over and harms the brain, as much by the material itself as by its foul odor. It also happens that even when a wound is quite well healed, a simultaneous injury to the substance of the brain itself can never be entirely cured. From this, it happens that the evil is repeatedly stirred up by a change in weather, by exercise, by food and drink, and other such occasions, which it is beyond our purpose to list individually here, since they will be repeated later in the second method regarding **The Cure**. For now, let these things said regarding the suffocation of the intellect suffice.

### CHAPTER V.
### On the Origin of Madness.

<margin>Hitherto on periodic madness; now on the continuous types.</margin>
Although we have so far devoted four chapters to the treatment of the loss of intellect, those who suffer from this disease are not so affected that they are deprived of intellect continually and perpetually until death; rather, they are shaken by certain periods of paroxysms, so that they alternately lose their reason and then perfectly regain it again, as is clear from the preceding. Consequently, we must next discuss those whose **Madness** <note>original: "Amentia"</note> is constant and continuous, and does not let up regardless of the time. Although even in these cases, unequal times exist, so that now an intensification and now a remission occurs, according as the higher influences twist and govern our <margin>Four types of Madness.</margin> <margin>Who the Lunatics are.</margin> <margin>Who the Insane are.</margin> <margin>Who the Vesani are.</margin> <margin>Who the Melancholics are.</margin> <margin>Who the Possessed are.</margin> lower ones. There are four types of this Madness: the first are called **Lunatics**; the second, the **Insane**; the third, the **Vesani**; the fourth, **Melancholics**. 

*   **Lunatics** are those who receive their entire disease from the Moon, and behave and are moved according to it. 
*   The **Insane** are those who have drawn that evil from their mother's womb, like a hereditary trait, with one person repeatedly transferring the insanity to another. 
*   The **Vesani** are those who are so infected and contaminated by food and drink that they are deprived of reason and sense. 
*   **Melancholics** are those who are driven from reason by a flaw in their innermost nature and are plunged into madness. 

To these four kinds, another kind can in a certain way be added, namely the **possessed**, who are usually occupied by the Devil in various ways—concerning which more is said in the book *On Prophets and Spirits*. But if we weigh the matter itself, those who are included under the four mentioned kinds can by no means be possessed by spirits or devils, as many people babble many things about them. For the Devil and his accomplices enter no home or body that is not, according to its own property, <margin>He enters no healthy body.</margin> fully and entirely governed by reason and intellect. Whence they do not thrust themselves into the four mentioned kinds, since those men, as will be said hereafter, are not at all masters of their own reason. And since they have very little power of their own intellect, they are for that reason not possessed by devils or spirits, but remain free from them by every right and measure. This is the reason why we discuss more things in the said chapter regarding spirits and prophets. 

Although, however, each one of these four kinds of Madness has its own peculiar origin and cause, yet in this one thing they all end and agree: that they abolish or withdraw the reason or intellect. This is not, indeed, in the form and manner we defined above in the first four chapters, but because they do it solitarily and by themselves, with no other sickness, no pain, and no suffering accompanying them, such as happens in the **falling sickness** <note>epilepsy</note>, in **Mania**, in **St. Vitus’ Dance** <note>original: "chorea Lasciua"; a disorder characterized by rapid, uncoordinated jerking movements.</note>, and in the suffocation of the intellect. For those who are affected by these kinds of madness live continuously and <margin>In the mad, a complaint of pain is a sign of death.</margin> solitarily as people without minds. But if it should sometimes happen that some pain concurs with the madness, and the mindless sick complain of it—and by bearing the force of the pain poorly, give some sign or suspicion of reason—then that is a sign that they are not far from death. The cause for this is that the disease becomes so vehement that it more severely harms and infects the spirit of life, which infection brings on death shortly thereafter.

<margin>The power of the stars over man.</margin>
But now we shall next explain concerning the **Lunatics**, from what cause they turn out as such: so that a knowledge of this matter may be pre-conceived before the chapter on the **Cure** in the second method. The higher stars have the power and faculty both of weakening and strengthening our body at the same time. And although this does not happen materially or substantially, they nevertheless incline us spiritually without any sensation, which can be grasped by reason alone. And the same thing happens here which...

<header>TREATISE II.</header>

### TREATISE II.

<margin>The Moon, by drawing from us, harms the reason.</margin>
Just as a magnet draws iron, amber draws straw, or sulfur draws wood, so too is there a certain attractive power in the Moon. This power withdraws reason from a human being by the deprivation of <term>humor</term><note>In ancient and Renaissance medicine, humors were the vital bodily fluids (blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile) believed to govern health and personality.</note> and the strength of the brain. For it is not the case (as many wrongly claim) that the Moon enters into us and works from within. Indeed, the stars have no power or capacity to occupy or besiege us, as some people falsely state. However, we must accept that they may extract from us that which their attractive power is prepared to take. In this way, the Sun absorbs moisture from the earth—not because the Sun is physically present in the earth demanding moisture, as if water were poured onto a fire, but because, standing as if outside, it draws and entices it toward itself by its own power. Similarly, it is not only the Moon that operates within us: indeed, all the other stars prey upon the innate moisture from all the members of our body. Leaving the demonstration of this for now, we shall postpone it until the treatise on *The Stars and Superior Bodies*. Thus, through the attraction of the Moon alone, many men are stripped of their intellect while the humor of the brain is being absorbed. From this, it happens that the entire head is overwhelmed by <term>insanity and madness</term><note>original: "amentia & vesania"</note>.

<margin>Lunatics are created by the Moon.</margin>
<margin>Why lunatics might suffer more severely when the Moon is waning.</margin>
These "lunatics" are ruled by the Moon because the attractive power becomes strongest during the <term>full moon</term><note>original: "plenilunio"</note> and draws more powerfully than at any other time; hence, at that time, men suffer most greatly.

<margin>Why the new and full Moon are strong.</margin>
The new Moon is also strong, because as if through a new conception, it receives new virtues and powers of change; thus, men become more or less insane because of it. Truly, the opinion of those who claim that the Moon makes our limbs weaker because of its own "weakness" is wicked, as if all our strength depended on the Moon. We shall demonstrate that this is false in our work on *Health and Infirmity*. Rather, it is true that the <term>Arch-daedalian</term><note>original: "Archidædala"; referring to the master-craftsman or the supreme shaping force of Nature.</note> nature of the Moon often attracts unevenly, as is known from this phenomenon. It frequently happens that the humor is extracted from the brain even when the Moon is at its smallest appearance and has its weakest drawing power.

<margin>The new Moon draws light humor; the old draws heavy.</margin>
<margin>The Moon draws constantly from the head.</margin>
The cause of this is that the new Moon does not draw the same humor that the older Moon draws. Thus, the new Moon attracts more of the moist and mobile humor than the old one does. The old Moon is harsh and hard; therefore, it attracts a harsh and heavy humor. Similarly, a gentle fire, not being very powerful or strong, does not draw out oils or harder substances, whereas a more vehement fire draws out the heavier and harder things at the same time.

<margin>The rising Sun and the midday Sun draw in different ways.</margin>
The principle of the Sun is the same. For rising at dawn, it draws nothing but <term>dew</term><note>original: "rorem"; Paracelsus viewed dew as a vital, subtle substance falling from the heavens.</note>, as it is the lightest thing. At midday, however, it absorbs even heavier and larger waters. Now, the deprivation of the dew itself is more damaging to its virtue than the drying up of other, thicker humors; the foundation and truth of this matter will be delivered more plainly in the discussion on *Dew*. Although the midday Sun takes away the dew and the subtle substance along with the waters and thicker humors, the specific nature and property of the Moon is not entirely the same. Instead, the new Moon only acts to evacuate the subtle humor of the brain before the old Moon approaches, which finally—after all the subtle parts have been pre-absorbed—attacks and extracts the thick remainder. When the Moon is decreasing, the humor is again accumulated and increased, just like dew during the night, which is consumed again when the Sun rises once more.

If, therefore, we see by chance that more people become <term>lunatics</term><note>original: "Lunaticos"; derived from *Luna* (Moon), reflecting the historical belief that the moon caused periodic insanity.</note> or are more severely exacerbated under a waning Moon than a waxing one, let us consider that this happens because the full Moon had extracted the most humor, and the lack thereof is subsequently felt and grows more intense as the Moon wanes. By a similar logic, it happens that if the midday Sun has evacuated the moisture of the earth, that dryness is only felt toward evening; as the Sun sets, the earth first gapes with rifts and fissures because the moisture was withdrawn earlier, which could by no means happen before noon. In the same way, it can happen to a human being that the operation of the Moon is only revealed near its end or its waning, because of the strength of nature itself. If nature has resisted for a long time until the end, it finally fails, as if it were breathing its last. Another cause of this event can be given: that the Moon draws continually and perpetually. As long as some humor remains in the brain, the Moon draws and entices it. Thus, when it has drawn most significantly at the end, nature is at its most languid until the new Moon returns and ordains new operations, unlike those of the old.

<margin>The cause of insanity is twofold. 1. A defect of the seed.</margin>
But let us proceed to speak now of the Insane who contract this evil from the mother's womb—whether the entire family is subject to insanity, or an insane infant is born from parents who are not. These have a twofold cause: one, if the <term>seed</term><note>original: "sperma"</note> along with its functioning is at fault; the other, that a hereditary vice can be transferred from the father and mother into the offspring. Insanity arises from the seed and its operation in this way: when some defect persists in the matter from which the brain is constituted and composed. For if the matter of a limb is missing during generation, or is present in a faulty state, its genuine and legitimate form, appearance, and nature will also be lacking, as we demonstrate in the first volume of our *Philosophy* concerning human generation. When such a defect is present, a perfect intellect cannot be formed. For a defect of the matter brings imperfection to the reason itself.

<margin>2. The Moon's attraction.</margin>
But there is also a second cause for this kind of insanity, which is the mode of its operation. When the generation and composition of the fetus has been brought to a certain point, if the attractive force of the Moon incites it in the meantime, the reason can be so withdrawn from the fetus that it never thereafter becomes whole and perfect.

<margin>An objection is resolved.</margin>
Although it is true that the Moon draws continually and daily, a reason can be given as to why it does not always make people mad. A certain harmony and mutual consensus is required between the matter and the Moon. For not all the humor of the brain can be extracted by the Moon, but only that which is determined and appropriate, as is taught regarding human generation. When such a concordance exists, the deprivation of reason follows. For then the Moon can entice the reason out of the fetus.

<margin>The Moon draws only appropriate humor.</margin>
Where hereditary insanity exists, since it lies hidden in the brain, it follows that through generation, the infant's brain is also polluted by that vice. For the father's brain generates the child's brain. And for that reason, one adopts the nature of the other, and the same property descends from one to another. Although this does not happen perpetually, the cause then lies in the mixing of the seeds of the man and the woman, where one is from an insane family and the other is not.

<header>ON THE DISEASES OF THE MIND.</header>

<margin>How a completely healthy child may be born from insane parents.</margin>
For the dominance of one seed over the other prevails. In this way, the offspring can be predisposed either toward emptiness of mind or toward intelligence, depending on which parent they received their growth from. And yet, in the meantime, it can also happen that a healthy child endowed with reason is produced by two insane parents: this, however, must be ascribed solely to the strength and excellence of nature, which separates and expels that which is faulty and unfit, just as is more clearly taught in the treatise on human generation.

<margin>Madness brought about by harlots.</margin>
By a similar discourse, we must also discuss those suffering from <term>frenzy</term><note>original: "Vesanis." This refers to a state of raving madness or delirium, often distinguished from chronic insanity.</note> who become such through food and drink, in the following manner. Harlots and prostitutes quite often provide something to be eaten from which the deprivation of the senses and the mind is induced, for many reasons. For <term>frenzy</term><note>original: "Vesania"</note> of this kind sometimes declines and turns toward love, so that the madmen devote their labor and study to women alone. This same affliction sometimes compels them to contemplate wars, which the sick men treat as their only concern while reason, in the meantime, is exiled. Sometimes those in a frenzy climb and run to high places; and in infinite other ways, which we leave to anyone’s observation, they betray their madness. We ought not to wonder that such things can happen because of food. Nor is it right to suspect any cause other than a natural one from their strange gestures. For that food and drink which they have consumed contains within itself the power of such an operation in many ways.

<margin>Four species of frenzy.</margin>
In this place, however, we shall enumerate four of the most powerful species of frenzy stirred up by food and drink, and we shall explain them more fully in the chapter on *The Cure*.

<margin>Love is won by certain simples.</margin>
First, the reason why those who have eaten or drunk something are seized and cast into love for someone is that there exist certain <term>simples</term><note>A "simple" is a medicinal herb or a medicine made of only one ingredient.</note>—which are by no means to be enumerated by us here—that have this power within them. If men give these to women to drink, or women to men, an indissoluble and stubborn love is induced. Even servants sometimes stubbornly dull their masters with something of this kind through snares: once it is consumed, the masters begin to love the servants so obstinately that they mention them as if discussing the State.

<margin>The winning of love happens either Naturally or Magically.</margin>
By similar work, dogs and livestock are also forced into love for those who offer them these medicines. And this happens either Naturally, or through Magic and Incantations. In this way, women sometimes give something to men, by which excess of love they are cast headlong by reason, so that they handle or contemplate nothing else than the love of those women from whom they received the administered <term>drug</term><note>original: "pharmachum." In this period, the word could mean a medicine, a poison, or a magical potion.</note>. But we omit more on this here.

<margin>How martial men are made.</margin>
Regarding the second type, those who are occupied with wars, they have received or eaten something by which they are rendered clearly insane. If they are of a choleric nature, they then turn out to be warriors and <term>Martial men</term><note>Influenced by the planet and god Mars; aggressive or warlike.</note>, and they have consumed nothing else but warlike furies with the thing given to them. The judgment is similar regarding the Melancholic and Phlegmatic types, whose natures are individually betrayed through the drug they have taken.

<margin>Whence climbers and wanderers are made.</margin>
Regarding the third type, those who are climbers of high places, or who crawl into heights, or who run about continually: they do this driven by the power of the thing they ate. For this does not proceed from the man's own nature. If it were permitted to teach more openly about these things, we would hide nothing known to us in this place. For here is hidden a profound secret of Philosophy concerning the nature of those things: about which, however, we are now silent. Finally, even the fourth type can be moved away from their reason and intellect through the property of the aforesaid things, the species of which we shall not review separately here: and since the same things also happen through incantations, we leave the rest to the treatise on incantations, omitting them here.

<margin>Four kinds of Melancholics.</margin>
But according to the first division of this chapter, let us finally also discuss Melancholics. There are four kinds of these: Melancholic, Choleric, Sanguine, and Phlegmatic. If such <term>complexions</term><note>The "complexion" refers to the specific balance of the four humors in an individual, which determined their temperament and health.</note> shatter the reason, it happens for this cause: that they expel their own spirit upward from themselves to the brain, where it is collected in too great a quantity. But we shall not review more concerning these in this place. Let those things be read among the authors who have commented on the complexions.

# THE SECOND METHOD.
## *On the Care of the Sicknesses and Diseases of Madness mentioned above.*
### CHAPTER I.
### *On the Cure of the Falling Sickness.*

->**A**<-s we have taught in the preceding treatise concerning the origin and causes of the <term>falling sickness</term><note>original: "caducus." This is the traditional name for epilepsy, referring to the way a patient falls during a seizure.</note>: in this second treatise, we shall set in order its cure. And do not wonder at the power of the cure for this sickness. For those things which are generated in the body by the reason of the universe: the same cure for them is born similarly in medicine. There are those who have hitherto established this disease as incurable: because they either did not understand the matter intimately, or they deliberately hid the truth itself, which we have also said elsewhere. We, however, shall apply ourselves to the most certain foundation of experience in curing this disease, lest we trust in it rashly.

<margin>The medicine for the falling sickness is twofold: bodily and spiritual. All diseases are twofold.</margin>
Therefore, the medicine for the falling sickness is twofold: one, which is in its own way bodily; the other, which is in its own way spiritual. For we wish ourselves to be understood thus: that the diseases themselves in all men exist as twofold: namely, Material and Spiritual: which we explain more fully in *On the Principles of Health and Sickness*. Now truly, a material medicine is owed to a material disease, just as conversely a spiritual medicine is suitable for a spiritual disease.

<margin>The falling sickness is a spiritual disease.</margin>
These things being established, we now define the falling sickness as a spiritual disease, not a material one; whence no material medicine is suitable for it. Therefore, for this spiritual disease, a spiritual remedy must be applied. Furthermore, there is no spiritual medicine unless it is prepared as such, just as we shall teach hereafter in our *Practice*.

<margin>By how many modes of remedies the falling sickness may be cured.</margin>
We shall first understand the matter in a twofold sense. One, namely, that some medicines are material which cure spiritual diseases, in which the frequent <term>Prescription</term><note>original: "Receptum"</note> excels; although it is indeed material, it nevertheless heals the falling sickness; understand this if the sickness is recent and new.

Take: Camphor, <term>spodium</term><note>Usually bone ash or ivory dust, used for its drying and cooling properties.</note>, <term>unicorn horn</term><note>original: "vnicornu." In the 16th century, this usually referred to the tusk of a narwhal or "fossilized" bones believed to have medicinal powers against poisons and seizures.</note>, etc. Make a powder. Let it be given in a soft-boiled egg, etc. So here is the powder clearly: Take, etc. Thus also this electuary cures any falling sickness whatever. Take, etc. Material medicine operates upon a spiritual disease for this reason: because its faculty is nothing other than the obstruction of the paths through which that disease ascends. Indeed, its operation also comes from great cooling, because it coagulates and, as it were, destroys the matter.

<margin>The remedy for the falling sickness must be general and suitable for all.</margin>

<margin>What sort of remedies for the falling sickness ought to exist.</margin>

First, that the medicine—which must be made subtle and <term>spiritual</term><note>In alchemical terms, "spiritual" refers to a substance that has been refined, distilled, or "volatized" so it can penetrate the body more effectively.</note>—becomes coagulative after its spirituality. Second, that it be incorporated with those things that constrict the veins. Third, that it be specified with appropriate substances. Fourth, that it be taken from such a "simple" <note>An individual medicinal herb or mineral.</note> that possesses a subtle spirit; this spirit should penetrate and pervade the entire body like an Elixir or a certain <term>arcanum</term><note>A "secret" or "great mystery"—a powerful alchemical remedy believed to have universal healing properties.</note>, or no differently than the <term>quintessence</term><note>The "fifth essence," the purest and most concentrated form of a substance.</note> itself. For otherwise, no force or power for restraining the disease will be within it. For it is necessary that the medicine be of a higher degree than the disease. We shall now, therefore, recount the four points individually, noting which simples are referred to each, from which spirituality against the disease can be drawn.

As for the first points:

<margin>1. Coagulants.</margin>
> Coagulants are these: *Camphor, water lily, crystals.*

Besides those enumerated which have the faculty of curing the falling sickness, others are found which are sedatives, whose operation is wonderful if they are mixed with the subtle spiritual substances. These are: *Opium, mandrake.*
*Henbane. Poppy. Darnel, "vua versa."*

<margin>What the restoratives for the falling sickness are.</margin>
These, however, should not be applied as they are in themselves, but according to the use of the preparations in the *Archidoxis* <note>One of Paracelsus’s most famous alchemical works, detailing the preparation of medicines.</note>. For we would not have enough time to describe their individual virtues everywhere. Furthermore, there are also other restorative medicines for the falling sickness which, by their singular and excellent strengthening, assist nature in expelling the disease. They are:

-> *Potable gold. Oil of gold. Reverberated mercury.* <-
-> *Quintessence of gold. Matter of pearls. Solution of corals.* <-
-> *Magistery of Antimony. Extraction of sulfur, etc.* <-

The virtue of these remedies is so outstanding and extraordinary that it can hardly be believed how much power lies hidden elsewhere in all of nature for healing diseases of this kind, which are otherwise incurable. Therefore, one must not despair of remedies, nor should confidence in medicine be cast away. For the one who raised up our enemies [diseases] also created the enemies of those very things; nor is there any disease that can kill a man without any available help. For all diseases are curable, with none excepted; and the defect is in ourselves, who are ignorant of the due remedies, just as we declare what death is in *On Death and Life*. 

<margin>All diseases are curable.</margin>

Furthermore, we shall by no means teach here how the sedatives and restoratives are to be prepared. For these are right and suitable in themselves against this disease, so that they require no correction. Or, if indeed the sedatives require some preparation, they will not demand any other or more accurate one than what will be shown in the Recipes themselves. Moreover, these Recipes of ours are the best of the best, requiring a singular and ingenious Artist <note>An alchemist or skilled pharmacist.</note>, who has not only diligently turned the pages of books and writings, but also has a skillful and ready hand, just as we write in the *Archidoxis* and *On Essences*. Most of the importance is situated in these things; nor can everything be described on paper in such a way as it is shown through experience.

<margin>The subtlety of the Artist is the author of all these things.</margin>

And this is something that has by no means been discovered by regular Physicians, but only by the Artists, who stand as the authors and masters of all subtleties. Nor is it indeed called "Medicine" or "Remedy," but a true *arcanum*, on account of the remarkable and most noble virtue which it hides within itself, which is hidden and not found by everyone. We shall, however, place this *arcanum* here for the cure of the falling sickness, and we shall remain silent about its other virtues. First, however, it must be known that its preparation is various. Just as its preparation is diverse, so too its virtue and faculty are diverse. And understand, not just any such *arcanum* possesses this virtue, but the most powerful force is placed in the preparation and the subtlety of the labor—just as in the "simple" itself. For one is occasionally more excellent than another. 

<margin>Vitriol is the arcanum of the falling sickness.</margin>

This "simple," however, is <term>vitriol</term><note>A sulfate of copper or iron.</note>, either Hungarian, or Cyprian, or Roman, provided that it is peculiarly graded and purified. Let it not, in the meantime, seem absurd or like an imposture to you that we assign such great virtues to vitriol. For in it lies hidden a certain peculiar, golden, secret, and concealed power—not corporeal, but spiritual. This extraordinary and admirable virtue is much more powerful and certain in it than in gold itself, as we demonstrate in *On the Generation of the Salts of the Earth*. This golden spirit of vitriol is refined and separated from the impure, so that only the essence remains, which is likened to potable gold. Its preparation is as follows: **Take of the best vitriol as much [as desired]...**

<margin>The power of vitriol is more excellent than gold.</margin>

### Recipe for the first opening.

<margin>1. A powerful opening.</margin>
Take of fresh Spearwort root or root soaked in vinegar, fresh Spearwort flowers or soaked flowers, 1 ounce. Fat of a Beetle, half a drachm. <term>Spanish Fly</term><note>original: "Cantharidum." Once all are ground and sifted, mix them into an ointment, which is to be applied on a cloth as far as the fingers can reach. If the cloth becomes dry, let it be moistened on the outside with vinegar, so that it remains always damp. Let the plaster sit for 5 or 6 hours: afterwards let it be removed, and the blister broken, and the little skin pulled away, so that the underlying flesh of the place lies bare and exposed. <margin>2. A milder opening.</margin>

Mix these three, and put the mixture into a glass, which you shall place over a light fire until everything is dissolved into the form of water. With this, wash the spaces of the extremities five or six times, and afterwards let them be allowed to dry. Once this is performed, the skin will be removed from the parts like dust from the flesh. These openings are sufficient for scraping away any skin; we have seen them occasionally, with great benefit, strip and excoriate the skin from the flesh. And the blood that flows from this excoriation contributes much to diminishing the Mania. Others have ordered the extremities to be pierced with driven lancets: however, such <term>scarification</term><note>The practice of making small incisions in the skin.</note> is not effective enough for withdrawing the mania; rather, a total opening ought to be established. But if this already mentioned opening pleases you less, use this ulcerating one, which is made in this way:

<margin>3. An ulcerating opening.</margin>
Take of Sublimated Mercury. Pure Arsenic. Aqua Fortis. Equal parts of each. Mix into the form of a <term>cerate</term><note>A wax-based medical plaster.</note>, which you shall bind to the extremities until the sensation is numbed. Afterwards, let it be softened with some fat, so that the <term>eschar</term><note>original: "eschara." A piece of dead tissue or scab produced by a caustic or heat.</note> falls off. Once this is removed, another practice must be established. With the openings made in this way, note that through them the entire flow of Mania with its whole matter ought to be extracted, just as we taught concerning this in the chapter on Mania. This is obtained only through <term>Attractives</term><note>Medicines believed to "draw" or "pull" diseased matter out of the body.</note>, which are placed twice daily on the ulcerated extremities. Through these, every vice is drawn out. Once the extraction is finished, cure the ulceration with the following remedy.

<margin>The Attractive for Mania.</margin>
The Attractive is made as follows:
Take of Galbanum, Opopanax, Serapinum, Bdellium, and Ammoniacum, 1 and a half drachms of each. Dissolve these in vinegar, strain them, and boil to a proper thickness. Afterwards, mix in these species, finely ground and very subtly sifted:
Take of Mastic, half a drachm. Frankincense, 2 drachms. <term>Tutty</term><note>original: "tuth." Zinc oxide.</note>, <term>Amber</term><note>original: "Carabe." Magnet, 4 drachms. Rosin, 2 drachms. Varnish, 5 drachms.
Let all be mixed into a cerate, which you shall apply, and fill the openings of the extremities well, and always

renew the bandage until you feel the alteration of the Mania has taken place. Finally, according to surgical custom, consolidate or cover the skin.
