### CHAPTER I.

## On the Treatment of Vitista, or the Wanton
## Dance, or Levity of Mind.

<margin>Whence Vitista is named.</margin>
Because the cure for **Vitista** <note>Also known as St. Vitus' Dance (chorea); a disorder characterized by rapid, uncoordinated jerking movements.</note> is described and proposed by us, it seems to many to be a rash and plainly impossible thing, persuaded by these reasons: namely, that Vitista took its name from **St. Vitus**, who sends this disease to men in place of a plague or punishment; or that God Himself, in the place of Vitus, inflicts this evil because of men's sins. We do not at all deny that this is somewhat likely; however, we do not believe that such a punishment is one which either God or the Saint inflicts upon us in any other way than by permitting such an **imagination** to be generated in the minds of men through the <term>imprecation</term><note>A curse or a solemn invocation of evil; here, the author suggests the disease is triggered by the patient's own fearful or angry thoughts.</note> of the dance of Vitus. Through this, the disease is subsequently introduced and emerges, which the common people later judge to be a divine punishment, even though the sickness is purely **estimative** or **imaginative** <note>Terms used in medieval psychology to describe illnesses originating in the mind's faculty for forming judgments and internal images.</note>, just as we teach in the chapter on its origin. <margin>Vitista is an imaginative sickness.</margin> Against such estimative or imaginative Vitista, we propose the following cure, and a peculiar one at that. Furthermore, if it takes its origin from **levity of mind** with the consent of the will—an affection called the **wanton dance** or levity of mind—we also teach another and equally singular cure against this. Thirdly, against the **forced dance**, the origin of which is natural, we also apply a natural medicine. <margin>Three species of dance: and as many cures.</margin> To these three distinct species we oppose three distinct cures, each of which must be applied separately to its own disease, nor does one ever work for another.

<margin>The irascible dance, to be cured through the imagination.</margin>
While we first discuss the treatment of the estimative or imaginative dance arising from imprecations, you must note that a certain difference exists between the estimative and the imaginative, because one arises too much from **anger**, and the other from **wantonness**. We therefore call the first **Vitista**, and the other **Lascivious**: their cure is also different, just like their origin. And the cure for Vitista born of anger is as follows. The patient shall fashion an image similar to himself out of wax or resin, and shall obstinately and firmly persuade himself, or think, that all the adjurations or imprecations he has ever made will, by his will, be perfected and fulfilled in this image. In this way: he will think within himself that he curses the image with all those evils, and he will direct and fix all his thoughts and his innermost soul upon that image alone, without any memory of other men. With that most obstinate intention of the mind, he shall finally throw the image into the fire and burn it, so that neither ash nor any soot remains physically surviving from the material of the image. While these things are done in the aforesaid manner, the thoughts proceed and are poured out from the curser into the image so effectively and strongly that nothing can hinder or oppose them. For imprecations are fulfilled in those who make them, not in those against whom they are made or hurled; and this for the reason that the gentleness of others cannot be harmed by the anger of their enemies, as is taught regarding **Images**. Therefore, no such resistance exists in the image either, but it is physically burned so that all these thoughts are taken away from the curser. How these things ought to be understood from their very foundation is taught more fully in the treatises on **Imaginations**, **Incantations**, and **Impressions**. It can also happen that if even the slightest bit of physical ash remains from that image, the patient is not sufficiently cured, but some part of the disease still remains. For this reason, only wax and resin are useful here, as is taught more clearly regarding images and impressions. But let these things said so far regarding the cure of Vitista from anger suffice. Next, we shall also discuss the **wanton and immodest dance** in the following manner.

It is established through use and experience, the mistress of things, that one contrary is driven out by another in a natural way. Since this is done in various and diverse ways, we will also propose our own experience here: how the wanton and intemperate dance may be expelled and conquered, and it happens in this way. <margin>Cure for the wanton dance.</margin> If a dancer, man or woman, begins this dance from an abundance of wantonness and starts to leap (which happens more frequently to women than to men, as they have more estimations and thoughts, and imagine more deeply and effectively, and are more easily conquered and driven out from the strength of their own nature), nothing is more profitable and conducive than that which is adverse to their thoughts and works. <margin>Women are more wanton than men.</margin> For their thoughts are free and wanton, full of levity, and void of all shame, fear, and modesty; these you shall expel thus. Shut them up in a dark and gloomy place; let them be fed for a time on bread and water alone; let them be kept in that filthy place with no affection of mercy. In this way it will happen that through hunger and hardship, they will conceive another nature and other thoughts, so that the wantonness is conquered in them through that abstinence, the luxurious works are put to sleep, the fiercer blood settles, and the spirit of life is calmed and relaxed. The heart is cast from joy into sorrow by the captivity and the filth of the place, and thus the old disease vanishes, and a fresh sadness—accompanied by no joy, no laughter, no dancing or shouting—occupies and governs the mind. When all these things have been performed, let the captives be released from the dark place, and gradually, from day to day, let the former diet be relaxed and better food be provided little by little, and the prison subsequently be made milder and more tolerable, until Melancholy itself is consumed and true reason returns after its exile. This kind of regimen takes away the thoughts as well as the gestures and works of these insane people. But it is mere insanity that some people think these kinds of dances are conquered if the danc- <meta>Catchword: fi saltan- (if dancing...)</meta>

If others are sent in and joined to those already dancing, who dance in the same way and behave just like the sick, singing and jumping about, the patients are actually more incited by this imitation than they are restrained. ### CHAPTER IV.
### *On the Cure of the Suffocation of the Intellect.*

We spoke above in Chapter 4 regarding the origin of the <term>suffocation of the intellect</term><note>A term used to describe a sudden loss of reason, consciousness, or mental clarity, often categorized as a type of stupor or seizure.</note>. Now in this Chapter 4, we will subjoin its cure. Since we have considered three species of the suffocation of the intellect and senses, we will now first arrange the treatment for the first. Since its origin is from worms, we provide such remedies as these:
<margin>Cure for suffocation caused by worms.</margin>

Take **Colocynth** <note>Bitter apple, a powerful purgative.</note>, **Spurge**, **Syrian Rue**, **Black Hellebore**, 1 dram of each.
Half a dram of **Scammony**. 6 drams each of **Polypody** and **Senna**. 3 drams of **Agaric**.
3 pounds each of **clarified honey** and **good wine**. A little **vinegar**.
Let all these be boiled together as a mixture. When sufficiently boiled, let them be strained. Offer as much of this strained liquid to be drunk as seems necessary for the disease to a prudent Physician. Once the operation of this laxative is finished, shortly after, provide another draught in the same way, yet with the moderation of good counsel. This medicine, not only by its own property but also by its specific power, draws out the worms and their nests, so that others do not grow back. This being done, provide those medicines which we placed in the treatise on the "falling sickness" <note>Epilepsy.</note>, observing the same dose. In this way, all paroxysms will be removed and driven away in both the old and the young, nor will Reason ever again be suffocated by worms in any way. Although many other appropriate and specific empirical remedies also belong here, we intentionally omit them. For those have not been confirmed by our own experience, but we grant credit to their inventors. While we do not reject them, we have chosen to set down here only those which we ourselves have frequently found to be useful.

The cure for the other suffocation, arising in women from the womb <note>Historically referred to as "hysteria," where the womb was believed to move or exert pressure, "suffocating" the woman's senses.</note>, is performed in three ways: one consists in ointments, the second in fumigations, and the third in things to be taken internally. Ointments can indeed soothe and pacify the disease by the force of their warmth, but they cannot entirely remove it. Nevertheless, this aid is by no means to be neglected. This is the description of the ointment:
Take **Oil of Mullein**, that is, from the leaves and flowers of mullein, without addition.
**Oil of Dill**, that is, from Dill alone, as above, 1 dram of each.
Half a dram each of **Olive Oil** and **Almond Oil**.
2 drams of **Mastic Balsam**. Mix them all.
With that mixture, anoint the navel and the region over the heart. Furthermore, place this pouch upon the patient’s belly:
Take **Mugwort**, **Chamomile**, and **Beech-ash**, 5 handfuls of each.
If, while persisting with these remedies, you see that the suffocation is not at all becoming milder, but is turning into the falling sickness: then, by means of a funnel, send smoke into the womb from the following things. This alone is sufficient for all suffocations of the womb, even those threatening death.
Take 1 dram of **Horse-knee warts** <note>The horny growths or "chestnuts" found on the inside of a horse's legs, used in folk medicine.</note>.
1 dram of **Asafoetida**. 2 drams of **Goat-hoof horns**. 
Let them be ground finely and mixed into a powder, of which you should use 1 dram, ignited, as is appropriate. This fumigation draws and wards off the suffocation from the heart, frees and clears the head, refreshes the brain, purges the womb, and restores the entire body in a wonderful manner. If, however, this remedy does not perhaps provide full help and liberation: then provide internal medicines. For it frequently happens that through the vehemence of the paroxysms, Nature is so strongly prostrated that, unless aided by honest strengthening agents, it can by no means resist the offending matter...

## CHAPTER V.
->On the Cure for the Loss of Senses in the Mad.<-

<margin>The nature of the cure for Lunatics.</margin>
We shall devote this fifth chapter to teaching the cure for the mad. Since there are four kinds of such people, it seems that four cures must also be established. We will speak first of **Lunatics**. Their cure is based on preventing or anticipating the attraction of the Moon and the Stars. For just as we see roofs constructed against the heat of the Sun so that what is exposed to the Sun does not take harm from it, the same must be understood similarly regarding **Lunatics**, in this manner: First, it must be noted that the power the Moon has over us can be taken away through the specific faculty of a medicine, just as the power of the Sun, the stars, and all other influences that "draw" from our body can be. And understand this again by the example of the Magnet, which has the power to draw all iron and steel.

<margin>A magnet smeared with oil of Mercury or something else does not attract iron.</margin>
For iron that is smeared with Oil of Mercury is attracted by no magnet. Likewise, if a magnet is rubbed with garlic, it never draws iron. By a similar reasoning, one must believe that certain medicines are given which fight against the Moon; others against Mars; others against Jupiter, or Saturn, or all the other stars. Effort must therefore be made to turn away these influences from Lunatics with the aforementioned medicines, administered wisely according to the face or the power of the Moon. The reasoning for the other planets and stars is the same, as is more clearly taught in the books on Influences and the Quintessence.

<margin>The seven metals are in part the seven planets.</margin>
Now, there are seven Planets, and there are just as many metals. Thus, it is established by experience itself that these seven metals within us have power and operation against the Planets. Therefore, whichever Planet is raging in a certain body, the Quintessence of its opposing metal must be applied to it: such as the <term>Quintessence of Gold</term> against the Sun, the <term>Quintessence of Silver</term><note>original: "Lunae," referring to the metal silver associated with the moon.</note> against the Moon, and so on for the others. Here it must also be noted that the Quintessence of Gold works against all the Planets because of the specific and peculiar power it imparts to the heart, from which all things are expelled, as is taught regarding the seven members. And let this interpretation suffice for Lunatics.

<margin>The cure for the Insane as well.</margin>
Secondly, let us also set down the cure for the **Insane**, who have drawn this madness as an inheritance from the mother's womb. This cure consists of two parts. One is the preventative, which must be applied to the father or mother so that they do not infect and contaminate the fetus with a similar blight. The other is the cure for the one who is already insane. The first cure (which should not be called a cure, but rather a preservation or expulsion) is done thus: Parents should not use natural coitus, but "artificial" coitus, and in this way: When they have the appetite for union, that insanity is then ruling them, and the child is created from that state. If it happens during the madness—in which the madness itself leads them—then the child will be insane. If, however, it is not so, and they unite in a state of health, and the union proceeds, then the child is not insane. And thus the treatment follows: that one should not satisfy the natural appetite, nor unite when the appetite arises of its own accord, but should immediately be plunged into cold water, and the urge for union is expelled and extinguished. And when it has been extinguished, it is immediately induced by art; then that union has its fire and incitement through medicines...

# TREATISE II.

...then follows a natural act according to nature, and not according to the mind or the will of insanity. And if coitus is provoked by medicine as often as one wishes, it is ancient and good. And it must be seen in this, that nature itself is not insane, but perfect in itself. If, however, the madness has lasted so long, or if it is a daily insanity, then coitus can take place daily for the reason stated. And even if the first child is not perfectly freed: nevertheless, his offspring are freed from insanity through the said method.

It must also be noted that the insane should be strengthened before coitus by <term>Quintessences</term><note>The "fifth essence" or most purified, potent extract of a substance in alchemy.</note>. For by these, the reproductive members are guarded from what is unsuitable and inconvenient, lest the offspring produced be equally insane.

The second cure pertains to the Insane themselves, and it is as follows: it is impossible for their insanity to be cured and removed unless the <term>complexions</term><note>The balance of the four humors—blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile—which determined a person's temperament.</note> and humors are first thoroughly changed and altered, to such an extent that the newly introduced complexion is sturdier and more powerful than the former one, and through it, the entire old constitution is driven out. This alteration or overthrowing happens in two ways: through **Strengthening agents**, and through **Sedatives**. The Strengthening agents ought to consist solely of Quintessences, such as:

<margin>Strengthening agents.</margin>
> *Quintessence of Gold <note>original: "Quinta Eff. Auri"</note>. Quintessence of Pearls. Quintessence of Silver.*
> *Quintessence of Corals. Quintessence of Antimony. Quintessence of Sulfur.*
> *Quintessence of Mercury. Quintessence of Sapphire. Quintessence of Essences, etc.*

<margin>Sedatives.</margin>
Similarly, the sedatives must consist only of sedative Quintessences, such as:
> *The Great Mitigative, Tempered Anodyne, Purple of the Threads <note>original: "Purpura filorum," a specific alchemical preparation</note>, Dissolved Gem, etc.*

Through these, as has been said, the Insane can and should be restored to themselves, so that they are no longer subject to any madness. For otherwise, the evil can by no means be removed. As for the other things put forward against Insanity, I advise that we skip over them.

<margin>Cure of those with induced madness.</margin>
Thirdly, we shall establish the cure of those **Vesani** <note>Those suffering from "vesania," a type of madness often distinguished from hereditary insanity as being caused by external factors.</note> who are cast into madness by foods and drinks. These are to be helped in this way. First, two paths must be noted: one specific, the other sedative. The specific path is to be held such that a specific Medicine is given for those things which the person consumed; or, that you might better understand, that the Medicine has the power and faculty to "mortify" <note>To kill or neutralize the active properties of a substance.</note> the poison of that madness before it is eaten or ingested. Take it this way: let us suppose someone is rendered insane by eating the brain of a cat. 

<margin>Cat's brain causes madness.</margin>
The Medicine, therefore, ought to be such that it mortifies the brain of a cat—just as there are certain herbs which, when tasted or eaten by cats, kill them, because they are uniquely specified against their brains. If, therefore, insanity was brought upon someone through a cat’s brain, he ought to be cured by herbs of this kind.

<margin>Love fascination through dung.</margin>
So too, if someone has been <term>fascinated</term><note>Under the influence of a spell or "fascination" (fascinatio), often believed to be transmitted through enchanted food or potions.</note> into love by dung: then he shall drive out the love through those things by which dung is expelled. Thus, then, we shall make an end of speaking about specific remedies. For it is not our advice to describe how men are fascinated and harmed; hence it is not right for us to bring forth the contrary remedies <note>Paracelsus implies that teaching the cure might inadvertently teach how to cause the harm.</note>.

Furthermore, the sedatives themselves are also to be taken from Quintessences, which alone—when all others profit nothing—soothe and take away the illness. These sedatives are *Purple Potable Gold, the Opiated Quintessence of the Moon, etc.*

<margin>Poppy-based.</margin>
Even if many things come to be considered here, as was handed down in the Theory: nevertheless, it cannot happen by the nature of common Recipes that a peculiar and perfect Medicine is found for every individual. Therefore, this kind of madness is to be removed by Quintessences alone, mixed with the Quintessences of Opium, Mandrake, Henbane, Poppy, and <term>Darnel</term><note>Lolium temulentum, a weed often found in grain that causes drunkenness or madness when eaten.</note>. There ought also to be Quintessences of Gold, or Silver, and Celandine or similar things, as are handed down separately in the book *On the Quintessence*. Mention of them is also made in the treatise on the greater degrees above the Quintessence. For there is no Medicine there which can either remove or take away foods or drinks fascinated in this way.

<margin>Purgation useless in the insane.</margin>
No one, therefore, should attempt to purge the body and in this way withdraw the poison. For that effort is frustrated, because that madness clings in the **spirit of life**, upon which no purgation acts. Therefore, there is power and a place only for strengthening agents, by which the spirit of life may be animated and invigorated, while the poison is lulled to sleep and blunted.

<margin>Cure of Melancholics.</margin>
Fourthly, there remain the Melancholics, who are foolish by their own nature, in whom there is no evident reason, but their complexions entirely prevail and suppress the intellect, governing it according to their own fashion. In the cure of this Melancholy, two things must be looked to: one is that it be known from which complexion it arose. The other is by what things it may be removed and taken away. The matter is thus: if the complexion be Melancholic, apply contraries. For instance, if the Melancholic man is sad, make him joyful and prone to laughter through remedies. If he laughs too much, cure him through saddening Medicines. Which you shall take in this way: there are some remedies which make a man laugh, and which take away all diseases arising from sadness, and drench the soul in joy. Nor do they only remove the <term>accident</term><note>In medical terms, an "accident" is a secondary symptom or occurrence rather than the primary cause of the disease.</note>, so that laughter is joined with some sadness and the source of the sorrow itself remains; rather, this source is also fundamentally removed. So, in turn, there are certain remedies which bring on sadness, while they blunt immoderate laughter and less-than-wanton joy. When these are turned and changed, the shackles of reason itself are loosened, and reason is raised to its former integrity and excellence. But the cure of this practice also proceeds from Quintessences alone, in which there is a <term>temperament</term><note>A balanced mixture.</note> of such a kind that a violated and downtrodden nature may return to itself and shake off all signs of Melancholy. Remedies of this kind are those which especially soothe Melancholic diseases, and greatly invigorate and clear the mind itself, and strike down all Melancholic madness, and drive sadness from the breast, and make for the intellect a free and unimpeded movement; such as:

> *Potable Gold, Master of Saffron, sharpened Amber, Manna of the sea, Heavy Cordial, Joy of Venus, etc.*

Furthermore, the following things temper and soothe madness mixed with wantonness and too much immoderate joy, and lead nature back to a suitable state, such as:

> *The first Purple Opiate of Filatum, Pure Darnel, etc.*

And although this Melancholy is fourfold, corresponding to the number of the four <term>complexions</term><note>The balance of the four humors—blood, yellow bile, black bile, and phlegm—which dictated a person's physical and mental state.</note>, it is not necessary to assign a separate medicine to every single complexion; the care of two is sufficient. ## CHAPTER V.
## *On Preventatives.*

With the five prior chapters established, let us finally turn to prevention. If we were to labor here to assign a specific remedy for every kind of insanity, the explanation would be far too long and tedious. We shall therefore establish one preventative that may guard a person from the first loss of the senses—namely from the <term>falling sickness</term><note>epilepsy</note>—and similarly from Mania, and likewise from the <term>chorea</term><note>St. Vitus’ Dance, or involuntary dancing/movement disorders</note>, then from <term>suffocation</term><note>Likely referring to 'hysterical suffocation' or a feeling of choking associated with mental distress</note>, and finally from every loss of the senses. Indeed, a universal medicine of this kind can by no means be prepared without the art and benefit of <term>separation</term><note>The alchemical process of isolating the pure essence of a substance from its impurities.</note>, but must be prepared through <term>Quintessences</term><note>The "fifth essence," the most purified and potent extract of a substance.</note> alone, as they possess an extraordinary power for preserving one from such losses of the senses. For to defeat a disease so violent and great, one does not need a weak or light virtue. Consequently, we shall now list these Quintessences. Although sometimes this disease can be averted through milder medicines, both simple and compound, and through a suitable regimen and an appropriate diet, we write nothing of them here because they do not always help everyone, nor are they sufficient. But there is confidence in the Quintessences. These Quintessences are as follows:

Having finished these things, we here give praise and thanks to God forever, and in the name of the holy and indivisible Trinity, we end this book on the Insane: which we have written for the public benefit, for the faithful and unfaithful alike, the good and the bad, the rich and the poor, so that the unjust may be gathered with the just, and the just man may remain just until the final day.
> Amen.

# THE NINTH BOOK OF THE MEDICINES OF THEOPHRASTI <note>Referring to Theophrastus von Hohenheim, better known as Paracelsus (1493–1541).</note> TREATS THE CONTRACTED: AND IS DIVIDED INTO TWO TREATISES, namely Theory and Practice.

## FIRST TREATISE.
### *On the Cause of Contractions from Injury.*

#### CHAPTER I.

<margin>Contraction is fivefold.</margin>
**W**ith eight books having been brought to a close thus far, it now seems necessary to us that the origin of contraction or the <term>resolution of the limbs</term> <note>Likely referring to paralysis or the loss of motor control, where the limb becomes "slack" or "resolved."</note> be explained by us in order. In the beginning, it must be understood what exactly a contraction is. Five types therefore present themselves; all of which harm and contract the limbs, and this either curably or incurably. Every single contraction has a unique origin and principle, and yet they all finally end in one way: namely in "resolution," which is nevertheless entirely different in some places than others, as will be defined in the following chapters. Among all contractions, however, that <margin>Contraction from bodily injury is the worst.</margin> which arises from an injury to the body is the most grave and dangerous: for which reason it is explained before the others. This type arises from external causes, such as from wounds or a fall: both of which may come from the bullets of <term>engines of war</term> <note>original: "tormentorum," referring to early artillery or firearms</note> and the bolts of bows, and other such things. Likewise from a fall come <term>luxations</term> <note>dislocations</note>, fractures, <term>avulsions</term> <note>the tearing away of body parts</note>, etc. From these, a contraction <margin>Contraction therefore happens in two ways.</margin> emerges in two ways. One is through an obstruction <note>original: "oppilationem"</note> made in the flesh, from which nutrients are least able to pass through to the limbs, which because of this become contracted and <term>wasted</term> <note>original: "tabida," referring to atrophy</note>, just as is explained regarding <term>withering</term> <note>original: "aridurâ"</note>. In the other way, it happens through an obstruction or a closing off made in the venous system, because of which arterial nourishment cannot penetrate. In the meantime, however, no natural cause exists for these, but everything happens from external accidents, such as from wounding, bruising, etc., which an obstruction of this kind then follows by this reasoning: When a vein or a ligament is cut and joined back together, if medicines of that kind are not specifically employed which clear and open the nutritional pathways, then a contraction must necessarily follow, because the pores have been altered and the ways of the arteries have been blocked and cut off. More frequently, a contraction also arises from the shortening of the ligaments, or from their unsuitability and uneven knitting together: this happens from a poor application of medicine, as we teach regarding wounds; and yet its cure is also referred to here. The reasoning for the other contraction from a fall is this: namely that the place in which the fall happened—such as the flesh or ligaments—is obstructed, stuffed, and as if suffocated or deadened; because of this deadening, nutrients are cut off so that they cannot reach the extremity of the limb, and thus a "consumption" <note>atrophy or wasting away</note> necessarily follows. These things are explained more clearly in the "Cure": where it is taught by what reasoning every deadened limb ought to be brought back to life, as much in other cases as in this disease of which we treat. All of these things will be more fully understood by everyone from the following types of contractions.

### *On the Generation of Contraction from the Stone.*
#### CHAPTER II.

<margin>Contraction below the belt from the stone.</margin>
**A**nother contraction also presents itself to us here, generated from grit or <term>the stone</term> <note>Referring to "calculus," or kidney/bladder stones, which Paracelsus believed could cause localized "tartaric" blockages elsewhere in the body.</note>. This affects the limbs located below the belt, accompanied by many and sharp pains, from which men sometimes die: sometimes they finally become numb and are deprived of sensation, living in the meantime entirely lame and motionless. This sometimes...

...sometimes it afflicts the belly alone, troublesome with severe griping pains, by which the intestines are <term>loosened</term> <note>original: "resoluuntur"; here referring to a loss of muscular tone or paralysis</note>. And this condition remains invisible. Sometimes it clings to the buttocks and the sacrum, and draws the back into a curvature. <term>Contraction</term> sometimes occurs in the thick muscles above the knees: and then the anus is loosened. More often it also occupies the knees and legs, and at last all the limbs which are below the waist are loosened, and they are loosened either completely and entirely, or partially.

<margin>The manner of the generation of this contraction.</margin>
As for the origin of these contractions—namely, stones in the kidneys and bladder, as well as gravel—it is explained more fully in the book on <term>Lithiasis</term> <note>The medical condition of forming stones in the body.</note> and <term>Gravel</term> <note>original: "Arena"; small mineral deposits or "sand" in the urinary tract.</note>. Here, however, we will also briefly teach the manner by which contraction is induced from stones and gravel. Gravel and stones, then, are dispersed and scattered not only in the kidneys and bladder, and all the cavities of the body (though chiefly and principally in the kidneys and bladder), but also throughout the entire body in every direction.

<margin>How the spirit of life is affected in places where stones are present.</margin>
Now, if such material (whether it is already congealed or merely disposed toward congealing) has settled and been preserved there, then the vital spirit—or the humor of life—needs to flow from the heart, where it arises, into the feet and legs. For it is distributed through the entire body. That part of this spirit which is poured out toward the feet, or is about to flow down to the lower parts, is forced to pass through those regions and places which the gravel and stones have occupied. Therefore, as it passes through these, it is corrupted by the location and is adulterated there through the attraction of humors and through contact with the Gravel and Stone. For from these materials, the spirit of life acquires another nature and property, so deeply impressed upon it that it never lays it down again. This it carries with it and leads down to those places for which it was ordained by nature itself, namely, to the lower parts. If the matter is not abundant, then staying in the hip, it causes a <term>contraction</term> of the back; if it is more abundant, it descends into the muscles of the thigh; if it is very plentiful, it then loosens and contracts both upward and downward.

<margin>Why are not all those with stones made contracted?</margin>
As for the fact that not all people with stones and gravel are always contracted: the reason is that the material of the gravel and stone may be so very compact and congealed, and therefore so very thick, that because of its rigidity it cannot be mixed with the humor and spirit of life at all. Whence it happens that the spirit passes through the bladder and kidneys unhurt and uncontaminated. The same thing also sometimes happens because of a scarcity of material, which is compact in only one place, from which the humor of life cannot be greatly harmed. Thus, it cannot do much damage. Otherwise, if the humor and spirit of life itself drinks in and adopts material of this kind, it loosens and contracts the limbs in this fashion.

<margin>Acidity congeals gravel and stones.</margin>
The materials of Gravel and Stone have certainly grown and been coagulated by acidity and sharpness. If these materials are carried into the ligaments, joints, bones, marrow, and flesh, they then convert these parts into their own nature, block the pathways of nourishment, and cool the ligaments and the marrow in the bones. For that material is nothing other than congealed vinegar, or the subtle <term>Tartar</term> <note>A Paracelsian term for mineral precipitates in the body, named after the crust found in wine barrels.</note> of wine, which does not lay aside its nature and exists more sharply than the humor of life itself. Thus it also corrupts and changes the quality of that humor. This corrupted humor, consequently, also corrupts...

<margin>The acidity of the humor eats away at the parts.</margin>
<margin>Vinegar lacks spirit.</margin>
...that which it ought to nourish. Therefore, through this opposing constitution, quality, or nature, there arises a constipation of the pores, the arteries, and the channels, and a certain kind of "boiling" occurs in the marrow of the bones. From this it happens that, through such an acidic and Tartaric coldness, the corroded limbs cannot be ruled and moved at will. For it is not only coldness that is the cause, but also the acidity and sharpness themselves, which, being present, eat away and erode the ligaments. Furthermore, the same coldness is also putrefactive, lacking spirit, just like vinegar, which is mere dregs, deprived of its spirit. Therefore, this is also nothing but a dead acidity in the limbs, or a cold humor, robbed of its spirit. This is not the case in other things in the same way. For even if they exist as cold and moist, they nevertheless contain within themselves a life-giving spirit, which avoids and turns away that kind of operation made against nature, as we comment regarding acidic things in the book on Stone and Gravel. And this is the manner of the generation and cause of contraction from stones and gravel: which is nothing other than the spirit of life and the humors, contaminated and infected by the property of gravelly and stony things lurking in the lower parts of the body.

### On the Origin of Contraction from colic, pertaining to the hands and feet.
### CHAPTER II.

<margin>Contraction from colic takes various forms.</margin>
**I**t is now next that we also discuss contractions made from colic. Although we do not describe the colic itself here, nor its cause (for that is provided separately in the treatise on <term>Colic</term>), it is our purpose here only to hand down knowledge concerning the contraction from colic that occupies all the limbs. The species of this are various. For one is with Atrophy <note>original: "Aridura"; a wasting away or drying out of the limb.</note>; another with Trembling; another with the limbs extended and stretched out; another with sharp pain; another with insensibility; another with vomiting. Yet of all these evils, the sole cause is colic, as we shall teach hereafter.

<margin>In which parts the spirit of life is stronger.</margin>
The principal cause of the contraction is this: When colic occupying the belly stirs up griping and pains in a profuse condition, then nature in that place where the colic rages demands, as it were, help and aid from the general nature of the body. It draws the humor of life to itself, and plunders and extracts it from the other, less fleshy parts (namely from the arms, feet, and the spine of the back). For in these parts the humor of life clings most lightly and weakly, and therefore it flows toward the pains and gripings of the belly. And since there is not much of it in those parts, it all escapes at the slightest occasion, which by no means happens in the fleshy and muscular parts.

<margin>Contraction from colic is threefold.</margin>
In this way, with the humor flowing toward the pain and deserting its own limbs by reason of its withdrawal, it happens afterward that the pain and the humor are confounded and mixed into one. By that mixing, the humor is "dyed" and infected by the condition of the material stirring up the colic, as is taught concerning colic. Now, with these two thus united, threefold contractions follow: one through the loosening or remission of the disease from itself, when it is dispersed from there through the body into that humor, as far as it reaches. For if the humor has emerged the victor and has subdued the disease, then to its own places...

...returns to its intended place, and carries with it the filth or acidity of the colic—which, like the matter of <term>Gravel</term> <note>Small mineral deposits in the body.</note> and <term>Stones</term> <note>original: "Lithiasis"</note>, is contractive by nature. When this is brought into the natural locations of the vital humor, it attacks the nature of the limbs and causes them to turn acidic; a condition that is subsequently followed by a contraction. However, this does not always happen in this way because sometimes the matter of the colic is too meager to overcome the humor of life, so that no "loosening" <note>original: "resolutio"; refers here to a loss of motor function or paralysis.</note> can be induced. Another type of contraction from colic occurs when the colic is soothed by the protection of remedies, yet not all the "ferment" is consumed. In that case, some amount of the matter remains surviving in the humor, which, when later poured through the body along with the humor, inflicts the disease and contraction in the same way we have already described.

<margin>Baths make those with colic contracted.</margin>
A third type of contraction arises when those afflicted by colic use baths. For if the limbs have grown hot from these, then their heat draws the absent humor back into its natural place. For it is the nature of the humor itself to be carried more readily toward hot places. At that time, therefore, it draws the matter of the colic along with it—matter which had been permitted to join it and, as it were, already inhabited it. If the limbs cool down after the bath, the humor dismisses that same matter from itself; it separates and withdraws from it. Finally, that specific property of colic follows, by which all the joints are loosened and become contracted. Indeed, this contraction often happens while they are still in the bath itself. This arises because of the great quantity of the matter. As soon as the matter senses the body is more porous and thinner than usual—as happens to the limbs, such as the arms and feet, from the heat of the bath—it rushes in all at once. Carrying the acidity of the colic in its company, it loosens and contracts the occupied limbs. For the "sharpness" of colic is nothing other than a burning salt produced by heat and acidity: when this is seized by the ligaments and joints, it creates a contraction there by its inborn property, just as is taught regarding colic. Sometimes it even produces a stretching or tension in the flesh and muscles, just as is the nature of vinegary substances.

<margin>What the contraction from colic is and of what kind.</margin>
In this manner, then, contraction is birthed from colic, which is nothing other than a mutual mixing of the humor of life (as it departs toward the colic) and the colic returning again to the natural limbs, such as the <term>Joints</term> <note>original: "Artus"; referring to the points of connection in the limbs.</note>. This matter, the companion of the humor, remains in the limbs until it is consumed. Through this destruction of the limbs, a "withering" <note>original: "aridura"; a drying out or wasting away of the limb.</note> is induced, because nourishment is driven away and the operation of nature is not free or healthy.

<margin>Withering follows this contraction.</margin>
Furthermore, from a multitude of acidity in the <term>Yellow Bile</term> <note>original: "cholera"; one of the four traditional humors, associated here with sharp, acidic qualities.</note>, a trembling is added to the limbs, though it may be greater or lesser in different people. Moreover, the joints are sometimes contracted because it is the nature of "choleric" acidity to contract.

<margin>Tremor.</margin>
Sometimes the same limbs are extended or stretched out, namely by the strength of the <term>Spirit</term> <note>The vital force or "breath" that was thought to animate the body.</note>, which then fails in the middle of the act of extension while the limb, in the meantime, grows stiff from the disease.

<margin>Contraction.</margin>
<margin>Extension and Collapse.</margin>
Sometimes the limbs collapse and fall downward, deprived of the power and virtue of the humor of life, which has been taken away by the colic. Those limbs which have become numb are as if dead and consumed within themselves, so that they are now stiff and cold and feel nothing: all of which happen from the imbalance of the matter.

Finally, they sometimes retain sensation, which happens by the power and strength of the surviving spirit, which strives to withstand the onset of the attacking disease and to expel the harmful influence from itself.

<margin>Stupor.</margin>
In cases where frequent vomiting occurs, it arises from that colic which has not yet completely penetrated the limbs themselves, but has poured some gall around the stomach, as is more fully taught in the section on colic. Other things which seem necessary to know regarding this type of contraction are annotated more fully in the section on its cure.

## On the nature of contraction born from anger. CHAPTER IV.

<margin>How anger causes contraction.</margin>
Anger or wrath is an unnatural alteration or change of the body, by which a contraction of the whole body—worse than all others—is introduced. For through anger the entire body burns and is inflamed, and the limbs, both internal and external, tremble and throb. These things are familiar only to the wrathful, and this contraction happens especially in this way:

<margin>Bile is the cause of anger.</margin>
The "burning up" or anger of a human being arises chiefly from the <term>Gall</term> <note>original: "fel"; bile produced by the gallbladder, long associated with the emotion of anger.</note>, as is held in the study of bile. Therefore, when anger is stirred, the bile, on account of its acidity and sharpness, strikes a burning heat into the body; this heat kindles a flame specifically in the blood of all the veins. When the blood is made to boil by that commotion, all the veins under the skin begin to "sweat." This sweat turns out to be a salt, in which the blood lives and is sustained in its vigor, as can be seen more extensively in the study of blood. That secreted salt afterwards works its way into the ligaments, tendons, nerves, and flesh, and whatever nearby thing it can seize or touch with its sharpness.

<margin>Salt is the life of the blood.</margin>
Similarly, this same salt also resides in <term>Melancholy</term> <note>original: "Melancholia"; "black bile," the humor associated with earth and coldness, but here described as containing reactive salts.</note> distributed throughout the whole body. As soon as it is stirred by anger, it pours out a sweat that is extremely acidic and sharp. Nor is melancholy stirred to squeeze out its juice by anything other than the powerful boiling of anger. So violent and sharp a thing is anger. By this effervescence, the <term>Yellow Bile</term> <note>original: "cholera"</note> itself is also later set on fire, so that it adds its own bitterness; once joined with the melancholy and the salt of the blood, it creeps and penetrates into the tendons. Afterward, the sharpness of the <term>Phlegm</term> <note>original: "phlegmatis"</note> is also materially dissolved into water. With this water added, the mixture of the four humors just mentioned becomes one substance in the ligaments and joints, similar to how they form substances in other places.

<margin>Anger is a violent thing.</margin>
Now, if anger has squeezed out such sweats and juices from the <term>Four Complexions</term> <note>The four humors or temperaments: blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile.</note> and mixed them into one, and then the anger fades: at that point, the bile returns to its destined place, the heat burns out, and the four mentioned humors remain behind in those places to which they were driven. For they do not flow back, but stay right there in the occupied places. Indeed, they are expelled into all the joints. Therefore, when the anger ceases, the humor of life immediately arrives and mixes with them. By this mixing, a material sharpness and subtlety is bred, which afterward contracts the hands, feet, and all other limbs. And in this case also, all the signs of colic appear, concerning which more can be found in the doctrine on Bile and Colic. The cure for this contraction is therefore quite laborious and...

<margin>Contraction from anger is difficult to cure, especially in women.</margin>

...is [difficult] and arduous, especially in women. For their heat is so fervent and rapid that all the spirit is evacuated and squeezed out of the blood by it; just as in the other <term>complexions</term> <note>The four bodily temperaments: sanguine, choleric, melancholic, and phlegmatic.</note>, everything is infected when driven by <term>cholera</term> <note>Yellow bile, associated with anger and heat.</note>. For this reason, a contraction in women is much more dangerous than in men, frequently leading even to death. To this is added the fact that envy, arising from <term>Melancholy</term> <note>The "black bile" humor, associated here with bitterness and stagnation.</note>, frequently occurs in them. For envy itself ignites and inflames in the manner of bile. Indeed, it is moved by nothing other than the bile [gall] produced by anger. From this it is clear that a contraction can be birthed by envy no less than by anger, just as we have taught elsewhere concerning the complexions. Thus, a contraction occurring from anger is a heat ignited by the external provocation of wrath, which causes such boiling and irritation that the four complexions pour out their own spirits and humors, leaving the physical substance empty. From these humors, then, the ligaments and joints are infected, and when they are so affected, the body contracts. For the "mobile spirit" in this type of ailment is expelled much more swiftly and completely than in any other contraction. This is why its cure is so much more difficult, and the disease is rarely cured entirely—unless by chance the condition is such that the four complexions are not completely squeezed out. In that case, they can still resist in some way and grow again within themselves. If this is not the case, no hope remains for a restoration to health, as we demonstrate more fully in the *Practica*.

### On the Contraction produced by gluttony or drunkenness.
#### CHAPTER I.

<margin>How contraction from wine occurs.</margin>
**F**urthermore, there are certain specific kinds of contractions provoked by wine; these are long-lasting and, because they occupy the limbs deeply, are by nature very difficult to cure. The manner of their generation is generally this: if the wine being drunk possesses the property of a subtle and sharp spirit, then that spirit of the wine unites with the <term>humor of life</term> <note>original: "humor vitæ"; the vital fluid believed to sustain health and movement.</note>. <margin>Wine is pleasing to the humor of life.</margin> Because it is of a noble and excellent nature, the humor of life attracts it, both for the sake of nourishment and because of their similarity. For these reasons, once the mixing has occurred, the next step is for the spirit of the wine to exert its "Quality." This Quality is exceedingly burning and dry, and it contains within itself much of the nature of the <term>Tartar of wine</term> <note>original: "vini Tartari"; Paracelsus viewed "Tartar" as a stony, acidic sediment—like the crust in a wine barrel—that deposits itself in the body's organs and joints.</note>. On account of the subtleness of the wine, the Tartar is dissolved within it to such an extent that nothing, or very little, of it can be seen. While the wine dwells in the humor of life in this manner, over time it exhausts and dries out that humor. The more of it that is drunk, the more it prevails and consumes the humor of life. This continues until nothing of the humor of life remains. Consequently, the limb—now deprived of its nourishment and motion—essentially dies, and its tendons contract according to the drying nature of the wine. Once this happens, a <term>withering</term> <note>original: "aridura"</note> follows, or a certain fattening/swelling, whereby the limb swells due to the thickness of the four humors, even though no vital humor is present. However, this disease is not induced by all wines indiscriminately, because not every wine contains such a subtle and tartaric spirit. From other wines, <term>Gout</term> <note>original: "Podagra"</note> or stones are born, about which more is said in their own treatises. We shall teach more copiously in our *Philosophy* (concerning the variety of growing things and animals) how such things occur both because of the various natures of wine and the diversity of men.

# SECOND TREATISE
# ON THE CURE OF THE
# five kinds of Contractions.

->*On the order and distinction to be observed in practice.*<-

### CHAPTER I.

**J**ust as we have until now established the five kinds of causes for contractions, so in this second treatise we shall provide their cures. In this first chapter, we shall set forth the general order and method according to which all five kinds should be treated together, rather than separately or individually. For the goal for each is one and the same, and the outcome is similar; regarding their beginning and origin, we do not require medicine. For if the disease is driven out from the limbs, and the humor and spirit of life return to their natural state, then those same spirits expel the remaining disease on their own. <margin>What the remedies for contraction should be like.</margin> As the foundation of the cure, therefore, we establish this: the remedies intended to heal a contraction must be "openers" of the pores, "warmers" of the humors, and "moisteners" of the arteries and nerves. Furthermore, care must be taken that the remedies correspond to the disease in the same degree. For if they are weaker, they will be of no use. Nor should there be equality only in the "complexion" (the balance of hot/cold/wet/dry), but also in the "Quality." For not every heat or moisture is useful here, even if it opens, warms, or moistens; rather, there must be a certain inclination from a "specific form" by which the remedies uniquely serve contractions—specifically, just as certain things are directed to the head. For by this art alone can the cure be perfected; if it is attempted by any other counsel, it will never reach the desired end. Furthermore, the cause must be weighed here: that contractions are placed in the highest and final degree of diseases. They are not found in coldness and moisture, nor in heat and dryness, nor in heat and moisture; but rather in the "summit of the humors," meaning that the humors are dead. To these, one must offer a medicine that brings power for their "vivification" (bringing back to life); this flows from the unique property of things and is not present in everything. In the same way, the vital spirit must be recovered and renewed. This itself is only provided by the greatest and most noble <term>comfortatives</term> <note>Strengthening or restorative medicines.</note>, so that the spirit, having been renewed, may be poured violently from the heart into the limbs, where, as it grows, it strikes out and conquers all old infection and the entire poison along with it. If this order and method are observed, remedies may truly provide some help in the healing of a contraction. Now, we must next understand what kind of medicine is suitable for this disease. For here, raw, cooked, or un-separated things [cannot be used] against—

<header>TREATISE II.</header>

<margin>Remedies for contraction should be spiritual.</margin>
...they will bring little benefit, unless the contraction is quite mild, such that it might finally be healed by time itself. It is necessary, therefore, that the remedies be spiritual—which are nothing but "spirits" <note>In alchemical medicine, a "spirit" is a highly refined, volatile substance capable of penetrating deep into the body's tissues.</note> that, through their own subtlety, invigorate the entire body and impart their own properties to the languishing limbs.

<margin>Two types of remedies for contraction.</margin>
There are two kinds of these remedies: one is internal, the other external. Of the internal remedies, there is again a twofold reasoning. For they must either prepare the distorted and changed limbs in the body (if necessary) by purging, heating, or cooling; or they must strengthen those same limbs with powerful restoratives, such as **Potable Gold**, **Oil of Gold**, **Substance of Pearls**, **Essence of Antimony**, the **Secret of Sulfur**, **Water of Life**, **Oil of Vitriol**, **Water of Tartar**, the **Fifth Essence of stones**, of **Corals**, and other similar things.

<margin>Internal [remedies].</margin>
And although we here set down remedies unknown to the ancient Physicians, we nevertheless teach in our book on the **Fifth Essence** <note>Referring to the "Quintessence," the purest and most potent extract of a substance.</note> in what manner and in what form they ought to be prepared. And what is lacking there, we affirm by placing it here: that the remedies we have just named alone are sufficient for any contraction whatsoever, whether born from heat or from cold. This is for the following reason: they strengthen, comfort, and increase the moisture and the spirit of life to such a degree that, having been made stronger, the body effectively expels all diseases. By what power and reasoning this occurs, we omit to explain here, since enough has been handed down concerning these things in the book on the **Fifth Essence**. Let this be taken as certain here: that a power and faculty so potent and noble lies hidden in these medicines that moist things may be cured along with dry ones, and hot things with cold ones, by a single effort. Whence, not without merit, we establish only one single cure for all contractions. And lest our words perhaps be disregarded, we shall discourse specifically on Potable Gold and others here.

<margin>The power and praise of Potable Gold.</margin>
For there is in gold a power and operation so remarkable and admirable that no higher stage can be found for strengthening nature; by it, universal diseases can be cured, especially those which exist in the highest degree—of which order contraction is one.

<margin>Praise of Pearls.</margin>
A similar power and virtue exists in prepared pearls, and much more so in **Antimony**.

<margin>Praise of Antimony.</margin>
For it restores and renews all the powers and faculties in the body wonderfully, just as is taught in the *Restoration of Life* and the *Renewal of Life*. So too the Secret of Sulfur is not inferior, nor is the Water of Life; for with the subtlety of their substance, they carry all virtues through the whole body and increase nature itself. Moreover, Oil of **Vitriol** <note>A sulfate, usually of iron or copper, highly prized in alchemy for its corrosive and transformative properties.</note>, especially if it is prepared in the manner of a Fifth Essence, exerts ineffable and stupendous virtues, as does the Water of Tartar. Deservedly, the wondrous providence of nature ought to be a source of admiration to us, for it has hidden such remarkable properties and gifts so deeply within the substance of things. Virtues no less powerful are also present in Corals and the more precious Gems, and many others, which we mention in the book on the Fifth Essence. Other things which properly belong here will be found in the *Practica* <note>A manual of practical medical application.</note>.

<margin>External [remedies].</margin>
The other mode of practice is performed through external remedies, such as fumigations, Balms, and Secrets. Of this kind are the Balms of Turpentine, Laurel, Olive, Frogs, Fats, and Gums; likewise the Secrets, such as the Compound Secret, the Solid Secret, and the Elemental Secret. Many descriptions of these will be given hereafter. However, we do not yet introduce the process of preparation here. Let that be sought in the treatise on the Fifth Essence. Furthermore, we do not describe the forms and methods of purgings here, for those are presented in the treatise on the ailments of the limbs. We only direct the practice according to the laws of curing, as they seem to fit the disease. Nevertheless, we have included here the dose, the use, and the appropriate form of each remedy. Now, therefore, let us set the mark for further distinction here.

# On Potable Gold, and Oil of Gold, for contracted limbs.
## CHAPTER II.

<margin>What Potable Gold is. What Oil of Gold is.</margin>
Since we have said above that it can in no way happen that contractions are cured except through remedies of the highest degree, such as potable gold and the like (as we teach concerning the higher degrees), therefore those remedies must be handled industriously and according to art, as mention is made in the *Fifth Essence*. A contraction is cured either by Potable Gold, or Oil of Gold, or the Fifth Essence of gold. Potable Gold is when gold, having been made drinkable, is mixed with other spices and liquids. Oil of Gold is if the oil is made from the substance of gold alone, without addition.

<margin>What the Fifth Essence of gold is.</margin>
The Fifth Essence of gold is when the redness is extracted from the gold and separated from its body. For its virtues are located in the color alone, as is demonstrated in the *Fifth Essence*.

<margin>The virtue of gold lies in the color alone. What is the dose?</margin>
The dose of potable gold for one instance is 1 scruple <note>Approximately 1.3 grams.</note>. The dose of Oil of gold is 10 grains. The dose of the Fifth Essence is 3 grains. They are mixed with the best Water of Life, or another subtle water. They are given in the morning, at noon, and in the evening, according to medical custom. The preparation of gold is done without corrosives, and without things that sharpen its virtue in the manner of corrosives.

<margin>The preparation of Potable Gold.</margin>
Make Potable Gold thus. Take: 1 ounce of Gold leaf or powdered gold. Resolve it into a juice with a sufficient quantity of distilled Vinegar. Distill these and separate them from each other repeatedly, until nothing more of the additive can be tasted. Afterward, take 5 ounces of the following Water of Life; mix them, and put them into a pelican <note>An alchemical vessel with two side-tubes that circulate distilled vapors back into the base.</note> for a digestion of one month. Thus you have it prepared. It is not necessary to describe its practice here, for we have interpreted it quite abundantly in the *Fifth Essence*. Although its elaboration and preparation are not exceedingly difficult, there is nothing more excellent than it.

## On the Remedies: *The Substance of Pearls and the Essence of Antimony.*

### CHAPTER III.

<margin>What the substance of pearls is, and how it is made.</margin>
The **Substance** of pearls is their juice, made drinkable and fit to be ingested; it is so strengthening and comforting that among precious things it has no equal. They are reduced into a juice in this way:

> Take: 1 pound of distilled and perfectly purified vinegar.
> Half a pound of circulated Water of Life.
> 4 ounces of Cleaned Pearls. Let them be ground very finely and mixed with the others. Let them be digested in a circulatory vessel <note>A vessel designed for continuous reflux/distillation</note> for one month, and the substance of the pearls will settle at the bottom like a heavy liquid. Once this is done, slowly pour off the other liquids and collect the juice. For one dose, give 5 grains three times a day. And although there are many other ways of preparing this, this method is the best and most useful, just as we teach regarding the Fifth Essence.

Regarding the *Essence of Antimony*, which pervades the body everywhere, we do not place the principles here, because the same was prescribed in the book on the *Fifth Essence*. However, the following Recipe for <term>colic</term> <note>Severe abdominal pain, though here treated as part of the system of bodily "contractions"</note> is as follows:

> Take: Lemon Balm water, Celandine juice, and circulated Water of Life, half a pound of each.
> Let them digest for 12 days, after which a separation should be made via a water bath. Thus you will find the Essence of Antimony. The dose of this is 1 ounce.

## On the Medicines: *Oil of Vitriol, Water of Tartar, and the Fifth Essence of Stones, for Contracted Limbs.*

### CHAPTER V.

<margin>Preparation of Oil of Vitriol.</margin>
**Oil** of Vitriol <note>Sulfuric acid</note>, without any addition, by itself and in its own juice which is within the Vitriol, is an extraordinary medicine. Although not all vitriol is suitable for this, one can choose that which is best and of the highest grade. From this, extract the phlegm or "oiliness" just as you learned in the book on the Fifth Essence. Afterwards, rectify it from the dregs until it becomes a spirit. Of this medicine, provide 3 drops mixed with other waters. You may also add some of the aforementioned Water of Life, and no medicine will be more penetrating than this, <margin>Oil of Vitriol with Water of Life is the most penetrating medicine of all.</margin> which wanders more swiftly and readily through its own substance into all parts of the body. In the same way, Water of Tartar, prepared from crude tartar of wine, provides incredible help, just as we have commented regarding its Fifth Essence. For contractions, it is uniquely prepared thus:

<margin>Preparation of Water of Tartar.</margin>
> Take the best Tartar. Distill it very strongly. Afterwards, rectify it through a pelican as subtly as you can, and pour in an equal part of circulated Water of Life. Of this mixture, provide 10 drops for one dose. There is a peculiar power within Tartar by which it imparts strength to the limbs. For it has the greatest power of penetrating the whole body and is singularly effective in cases of contraction. Likewise, there are other stones whose liquidity has a similar and equal power, such as Corals and Sapphires. Of these, however, we add nothing further, because they are few. Moreover, the operation of both is uncertain. Therefore, we repeat the same regarding the Fifth Essence. We shall now make an end of the strengthening and internal medicines. If it seems we have spoken of them only in passing and briefly: consider that they have been discussed more at length and accurately both in the Treatise on the Fifth Essence and many other places. Therefore, we advise the reader to search in those places.

## On Balms that Heal Contractures.
## CHAPTER VII.

<margin>Balm against contracture.</margin>
Similarly, note must be taken of the **Balms** which cure contracted limbs. The preparation of all these is natural, and there are many types. We shall at least indicate here those which we have found by experience to be singularly helpful. Their use is such that the sick are to be thoroughly anointed with them while warm, three times every day, without skipping any. This is the condition for all Balms.

### The First Balm.
> Take: 2 pounds of distilled Turpentine. 1 pound of distilled Galbanum <note>A bitter aromatic gum resin</note>.
> Half a pound of distilled Ivy gum. Let them be distilled together. Let a Balm be made, separated from the dregs and the phlegm. Use this in the manner prescribed above.

### Another Balm.
> Take: 1 pound each of Turpentine, Laurel oil, Olive oil, and Juniper oil.
> Half a pound each of Mastic, Myrrh, and Frankincense. Distill each separately, like the oils, for one part; and the other three for the second part. Afterward, mix both and distill once more. Use as above.

### Another Balm.
> Take: 1 pound each of Badger fat, Wax, Deer suet, Fox fat, and Marmot fat.
> 2 pounds of Mastic. Half a pound of Frankincense. 1 dram of Euphorbium <note>A caustic resin from the spurge plant</note>.
> Distill in the manner already described first.

### Another Balm.
> Take: 1 pound of Gum Opopanax. 2 pounds of Galbanum. Half a pound of Serapinum <note>A gum resin from a Persian plant</note>.

> Take: however much of this oil there is.
> 3 pounds of distilled Turpentine. Half a pound of Oil of the Philosophers <note>An alchemical oil, often made from distilled bricks or stones</note>.
> 1 pound of distilled Laurel oil. Half a pound each of Mastic and Frankincense.
> 1 pound of Myrrh. Let these be distilled again into a single oil, into which you should then place the following, and expose it to the Sun in a glass vessel for a month:
> Take: 10 ounces of liquid Storax. 20 individual Frogs.

Similarly, you should know that these individual simple ingredients, which are taken into the Balm, are also suitable and useful for use on their own if they are distilled and rectified according to the prescription of the art of **Alchemy**, which is the mistress of preparation.

### Another Balm.
<margin>Alchemy is the mistress of preparation.</margin>

## On the Arcana that Help Contractures.
## CHAPTER VIII.

There are, moreover, other remedies called **Arcana** <note>Secret or powerful alchemical essences</note>, through which contracted limbs are cured no less than by Balms. Their form is a water, prepared without fattiness, yet not at all ineffective for healing. For Arcana of this kind exert a power entirely similar to a Balm. Thus they are quite suitable for curing those with contractures. They are called Arcana because they excel and surpass other waters. There are four kinds of such arcana: the Composite Arcanum, the Solid Arcanum, the Elemental Arcanum, and the Metallic Arcanum. They are prepared by the following artistry.

<margin>What are Arcana?</margin>
<margin>Several formulas for Arcana.</margin>

### The Composite Arcanum is made thus:
> Take: 7 pounds of the best distilled Burning Wine <note>Alcohol</note>.
> 10 drams of Cantharides <note>Spanish Fly, used as a powerful irritant to stimulate blood flow</note>.
> 6 handfuls each of Hemp, Mullein flowers, Chamomile, and St. John's Wort. Crush and mix; let them be digested in the Sun or in warm dung for a month. From there, distill it. Into the distilled water, place the following:
> Take: Half a pound each of the juices of Hemp, Mullein flowers, Chamomile,
> St. John's Wort, Centaury, Betony, and Self-heal.
> 3 and a half drams of Mastic. 5 drams of Frankincense. 3 drams of Mummy <note>A common medicinal ingredient made from preserved organic remains</note>.
> Half a pound each of Earthworms and Frogs.
Let them be distilled in a circulatory vessel for eight days. Afterward, use as you would the Balms.

### The Solid Arcanum is prepared thus:
> Take: The juice of Spearwort <note>Latin: flammula</note> from the roots, herb, and flowers.
> 1 pound each of all the juices of Mullein flowers.
> 2 pounds of the strongest Burning Water. Let them be digested in horse dung for 10 days. Afterward, use as above.

### The Elemental Arcanum is refined thus:
> Take: 2 handfuls each of Celandine, Lemon balm, Wild sage, Mullein flowers,
> Poppy, Centaury, Betony, and St. John's Wort.
> Let them all be thoroughly crushed, and add a little vinegar; let them putrefy. Afterward, let them be most exquisitely pressed out, and placed in a circulatory vessel for 10 days, so they may rise without ceasing. Afterward, use it. It is not unfitting if you add Mastic and similar things to them.

### The Metallic Arcanum.
> Take: Resolved metal; let it be circulated for eight days. Let it be sweetened and used. Here, attention must be paid to the differences between metals: if the disease is from heat, you should take cold metals; if from cold, take hot ones. However, out of all of them, the **Metallic Water made from Gold** is the most noble and excellent for all contractures. Of which we speak here only briefly and in passing, because more has been handed down concerning the **Fifth Essence** <note>The Quintessence, or most purified extract of a substance</note>.

*A conclusion to these remedies against contracted limbs; and an explanation of how and why they have the power to heal diseases of contraction.*

### CHAPTER IX.

<margin>Why are certain contractions cured? Cause 1. Cause 2.</margin>
**T**hus far we have prescribed several medicines for contractures <note>Conditions where limbs are permanently bent, stiffened, or shriveled</note> that were most proven and known to us. If these are prepared in the proper manner and with the required skill, they are sufficient for a cure. There are, however, two primary reasons why some contractures cannot be removed: one is that the spirit of those limbs is utterly extinguished, and the very root of life has been withdrawn. The other is because it is very often fatal <note>In this context, "fatal" refers to "Fatum" or destiny/the predestined end of a condition</note> that they are not cured, as we teach in the book *On Fate*. If either of these occurs, since it escapes our full grasp and foresight, it can only be recognized through the failure of the medicine and the <term>ineffectiveness</term> <note>original: inefficientiam</note> of its power. For no disease is left without its own remedy. And no disease of contraction brings about death simply and absolutely. However, the fact that both Medicine and <margin>No disease lacks its own remedy.</margin> those who use it are often severely troubled by fatal matters, and experience an outcome entirely contrary to the requirements of medicine and the course of nature, should cause us to learn to set aside an overly stubborn confidence and hope in this fragile life. For even if we were to fully possess all harmful things and the powers of all medicines simultaneously, along with the genuine causes of diseases and the proper remedies opposed to them, an impending Fate nevertheless easily shatters this confidence and destroys every firm standing. We cannot withstand this in any way; rather, we find ourselves entirely exposed to these fatal causes, since they make us mortals in our entirety, break our efforts, and overturn our foresight and all our plans, as we have discussed more fully in the book *On Fate*. Nevertheless, meanwhile, since we have received such powerful remedies from God their creator, we must nourish the hope of resisting and struggling against the fates for as long as the will of God permits. Therefore, it is not unjust of us to oppose the highest degrees of disease with the highest powers of medicine, and to strive through these to overcome the difficulties of ill health however we can; just as we set forth in the first prologue to all these books, etc.

### TO THE READER.

**B**enevolent Reader, these present eleven treatises or books written on Dropsy, Wasting, etc., were not finished or entirely perfected by the author as he had intended. For this reason, he even arranged and described the first five diseases twice, and wished to make a single treatise out of both versions, as can be seen from the characters and cross-references moving from one treatise to the other. Yet he did not leave them in a state of completion, but rather as an incomplete draft.

Since, however, no one knows precisely why he repeated the arrangement, it pleased us to transcribe the author's concept here exactly as it was found by us, word for word with nothing changed, in its entirety and in order. As for the fact that you will see the cure for these diseases given so briefly: know that not a single word has been omitted by us. For whatever the Author himself recorded, we have gathered here in full. It seems he wished at least to explain the Theory of these diseases, as the cures themselves are handed down and to be read scattered throughout his other books.
->Johannes Huser.<- <note>The primary editor of Paracelsus's collected works in the late 16th century</note>

### ON THE NAME AND TERM "DROPSY."

**C**oncerning the name and etymology of "Dropsy"—whether it be Latin, Greek, Arabic, or Chaldean—do not let it trouble you, Reader. Here the languages play with one another like cats with mice. It is a trivial and idle thing. You should simply hold onto the name "Water," and add "abundance," or "disease," or whatever you wish: and you will know the disease itself, which is nothing other than an abundance of water. For we are speaking here of water alone; that is, the disease is pure water. However, the term <term>Resolution</term> <note>A term implying a solid substance has dissolved into liquid</note> would fit more aptly. For it is water that has been "resolved." This would serve <margin>Dropsy is a resolved liquor.</margin> to distinguish between true water and this substance. Therefore, its best name is "resolved liquor" or "moist dew."
