# ON DROPSY.

<margin>What are the signs of dropsy?</margin>
## WHAT IS THE DISEASE?
**W**hen the body swells beyond the usual measure of nature, and the feet and hips grow bloated, and the tumor <note>In this context, "tumor" refers to any general swelling or puffiness rather than a cancerous growth</note> occupies the genitals, the heart, and sometimes the eyelids or other similar places: it increases for so long that the spirit of life is suffocated in water, not unlike a man who has fallen into a lake. If, moreover, pressed indentations <note>A reference to "pitting edema," where pressing the skin leaves a lingering dimple</note> remain in those parts, and respiration is suppressed, and a cough with gasping for breath causes exhaustion: all these are the signs of this disease, namely dropsy. Most recently of all, the urine turns more reddish, the skin splits and water flows through the cracks, and an unquenchable thirst causes distress. In some, this evil grows more swiftly, in others more slowly, according to the impression of the heavens: according to whose constitution the sick also die.

## THE CAUSE OF THE DISEASE AND HOW IT COMES TO BE.
<margin>Causes of dropsy.</margin>
**T**hree things must be noted and known here: the power of the heavens, earthly nature, and the Microcosm <note>The "Little World," meaning the human being as a reflection of the entire universe</note>. The Heaven exists as a double artisan: the visible and the invisible. Earthly nature must be known: as that which is nothing without the heaven. The Microcosm is known because it suffers. The Heaven is twofold. The Earth is twofold. But man is simple and one, who in the invisible is the subject that conceives.

### Example.
<margin>The sky is the life of the earth.</margin>
**A**n example for the sake of explanation: The earth is nothing without the impression of the heavens. From the heavens it flourishes and grows green, and brings forth fruit, and lives; that is, the heaven is its life, its disease, and its end. Now indeed there are two earths: one whose example we have proposed here, and the other is man, for whose sake the example was brought forward. For man is an invisible earth, and yet he behaves just like the nature of the earth.

<margin>Man is invisible earth.</margin>
So also the heaven exists as twofold. One serves the earth with its impressions. These are manifest, such as rain, dew, frost, and the like. From these impressions the earth lives. If it is deprived of them, it is dead. If it receives them immoderately and beyond balance, even so its death and the dissolution of what is good follows. Therefore, the earth lives from the heaven, and the heaven disposes it according to its own manner.

<margin>Man is from the earth.</margin>
But there is also a hidden heaven, which sustains man no less than the earth itself. For man was taken from the earth. Whence he exists as an invisible earth. Hence he similarly requires his own nourishment like the earth, and that nourishment is invisible. These are also rains, dew, etc.—impressions of the heaven, just like the visible ones. It is concluded, therefore, that the body of man is like the heaven and the earth, and is constituted in that manner which the next example shall define.

<margin>Dropsy is an inundation of the body.</margin>
By the same reasoning that rain corrupts the earth and renders it wetter than is right, and suffocates it, and dissolves its strength and operation whenever the heaven floods it too much with its impressions and exceeds the convenient temperature and measure: in that same likeness and manner, the heaven of man floods and washes over his own "earth." And this is that dropsy of which we treat in this chapter. Therefore, do not seek other or deeper causes of this disease elsewhere. What has been said is sufficient for you for practice and cure, until the *Paramira* <note>original: "paramira opera"; likely a reference to Paracelsus's *Opus Paramirum*, a foundational text on the causes of disease</note> works are passed down to you.

<margin>The Microcosm consists of 4 elements.</margin>
The Microcosm itself must be understood in this place as consisting of the four elements <note>Earth, Water, Air, and Fire</note>, and it is these same things invisibly. For it was fashioned in the image of Him who created all these things, and yet it remained a creature. Therefore, on one hand, it is the same as the earth, which has need of heaven, air, fire, etc., just like the earth itself: and clearly one and the same logic of the external and internal earth exists on both sides. The same is evident through Resolution <note>The chemical or physical breakdown of a substance into its parts</note>, from which diseases arise whenever measure and temperature <note>Balance of qualities</note> are not observed. Now, therefore, what dropsy is in its origin and anatomy has been sufficiently understood.

## HOW IT IS, OR THE PROCESS OF ITS FORMATION.
<margin>The spirit of life dwells in the center of the body.</margin>
**I**f, therefore, an impression floods the earth of the Microcosm by the aforementioned reasoning: then the water, on account of its weight, sinks downward through the pores of the flesh, and fills all the pores, and mostly also the cavities and the muscles. And as the impressions of the heaven are either strong or weak: so also the inundation increases and becomes heavier, until it ascends to the knees. If the rains of the heaven do not even then abate, the water overflows to the hips, to the private parts, to the pores of the belly, and so continuously to the upper parts. Because the spirit of life <note>The vital force that animates the body</note> is placed in the middle or center of man: therefore it is suffocated there, like a man whom the waves have swept away. Yet the same spirit sometimes struggles and moves the water away from its center: and then the inundation touches the upper parts near the heart, which happens rarely and lasts for a shorter time. For the spirit is violently cast down. And in this way dropsy must be understood by you if you wish to attempt its cure: not that the knowledge of this cause will suffice to make you a Physician, but that through this foundation you may more exactly investigate the rule of treatment. For this too is drawn from two things: From the Philosophy of the earth, which supplies you with the knowledge of the earth from which you then build the Microcosm itself; and from the Astronomy of the heaven, which teaches how you ought to avert the celestial course's impression, just as one averts a stream by draining it. The same also teaches you to know the Microcosm, who and what it is, and what sort of subject you have at hand.

## CONTRARY CASES.
**B**ut if sometimes this kind of watery disease is also produced by a disordered and immoderate way of life <note>Diet and lifestyle</note>: it happens in no other way than as if a thing on the earth were drenched with water, with the celestial rain contributing nothing. For here too the evil arises from water, and its cause is one and the same. Yet the cure of this is easier than the other, and is done with less danger. But if both causes coincide, the disease will become one, and it will be exceedingly dangerous. In the same way, it could be said that the time of the Microcosm or the Macrocosm <note>The "Great World" or the universe at large</note> provides a singular cause for this disease.

## CURE.

<margin>Things to be observed in the cure of dropsy.</margin>
**I**n the Cure, three things must be considered: the heaven, the earth, and the Microcosm. Consider the heaven as an Astronomer, so that you may know the "star of the rain" and its parents <note>The astrological influences causing the fluid imbalance</note>. For once these are known, the specific Medicine is taken from them. Consider the earth—that is, the body—as a Philosopher, namely by what means it has been dissolved, and what the Nature, virtue, and condition of the Microcosm might be. Since there are many peculiar natures of these, which were encompassed generally above, a more accurate consideration belongs to the schools, not to practice. For within these <term>Arcana</term> <note>Powerful "secret" remedies or essential spirits of a substance</note> all are included.

<margin>What the cure for the Heaven is. The Sulphur of metals is the Sun for dropsy.</margin>
Resist the Heaven only through the Element of Fire, which is made from water. And this is the unique Sulphur of Metals. For that Sulphur, whether it be of Metals or minerals, resists these impressions by its strength and <term>arcane</term> nature, and it dries them out. For it is the "Sun" which disperses this "rain" and turns it into air: specifically into that air for which the Sun itself is the master.

<margin>What the cure for the Earth is.</margin>
The influx or entrance into the "earth" <note>The physical flesh</note> through which it is flooded must be taken away. For a cistern that is full and swelling must be emptied; and thus it is subjected to its own "Sun." In the same way, if the earth can no longer soak up fluid, the abundance of humor must be taken away from it, lest it putrefy from that moisture and become incurable. For putrefaction is a dissolution that cannot be restored. The cure for this is carried out through the unique Element of dryness, which is itself fire. In these things, therefore, the cure is placed in this manner: partly because the Crocus dries things out, and partly because the Sulphur, like the Sun, consumes the moisture. Through these two, the cure of any Dropsy is perfectly understood.

# ON WASTING <note>Aridura: A term used in early medicine, particularly by Paracelsus, to describe atrophy, consumption, or the "drying up" of the body or its parts.</note>.

### THE NAME.

**A**lthough the names for Wasting are various—just as its forms are diverse, distinguished by many different symptoms—the things themselves should not be separated by their labels. Instead, they should be understood under a single name, since there is only one primary cause among them all.

### WHAT IT IS.

<margin>What is Wasting?</margin>
**W**asting <note>original: "Aridura"</note> occurs when either the entire body or any of its members, whether internal or external, begins to dry up—that is, it becomes arid. It deviates and fails from its proper proportion in the measure of its flesh, marrow, or blood, or whichever member is wasting away. In whatever part of the body this occurs, the natural weight of that part is diminished, no longer through moderation or fasting, but through another disease-causing agent.

### THE CAUSE.

<margin>The cause and generation of Wasting.</margin>
**U**nderstand the cause of wasting in this way. You see, indeed, that every single body that is upon the earth, and produced from it, has a certain proportion and measure of its own fatness, size, thickness, and the like. This measure and this weight, however, come from the heavens. For the heaven itself confers weight and proportion upon these things through its dew and rain. If the earth possesses the mercy and favor of the heaven, then all those things flourish, gifted with full measure and weight. But if the heaven is more inclement and withdraws its nourishment from growing things, then they are exhausted, they pine away, and they dry up, just like hay. And through this dryness, they lay down their lives. By the same logic, the body of man himself flourishes from its own "earth," much like a cabbage <note>The author uses a humble garden plant to illustrate how humans rely on their environment and "internal soil" for growth.</note>. Hence, he is subject to the same celestial influence <note>original: "impressioni"</note>. If he has a benign heaven, he is of full measure and weight. If not, the encroaching scarcity subtracts measure and weight from him, and the man is diminished in flesh, in blood, in internal or external members—whether in their entirety, in halves, in all parts, or in some. For from whichever part nourishment is withdrawn, that part dries up, either faster or slower, according to the nature of the deficiency. Thus, even a whole man dries up within himself, more and more every day, until every bit of juice is absorbed everywhere, and he becomes like hay or wood. For such is the property and logic of man’s substance, that all his food acts as his "seed." Therefore, just as a garden is rendered joyful and vigorous by seeds, so is man himself. It is not, therefore, food and drink by themselves, but the celestial influence that makes a man fat or lean, and creates a good and fertile "earth" so that he may attain his full measure. If this influence is withdrawn from this fullness, nothing can bloom; instead, food and drink dry up and wither, and that which was once a body likewise wastes away, since it has no access to growth or increase.

<margin>Summer and Winter nourish or consume the man.</margin>
For the human body is similar to the earth itself. The earth that has the Sun or summer is fertile; that which has winter is sterile. Thus, what summer has supplied, winter consumes, until a renewed spring more abundantly pours back what was absorbed by the winter. In the same way, a man is touched by his own "winter," which is sterile in itself and, moreover, feeds upon yesterday's growth. And unless summer followed, all men would waste away and be consumed in the same manner. Meanwhile, as soon as winter has departed, summer succeeds it; and so, by this perpetual alternation, the body is consumed through the winter and renewed through the summer, invigorated, and receives a green and flourishing life.

<margin>Man is subject to the powers of heaven.</margin>
All these things flow from the power and virtue of the heaven. Because man exists as a Microcosm <note>The "Little World"—the idea that the human body reflects the structure and laws of the entire universe (the Macrocosm).</note>, he is absolutely compelled to endure all these alternations. For he is made of the earth: hence he depends on the grace of the heaven. If the heaven withdraws its "summer influence" from him, he then withers according to his mass, is diminished, and is led even unto death. For if you become a winter that gives no hope or sign of a future summer, then even when summer should follow, the winter has not yet disappeared. Whoever is touched by such a fate is now denied life; he eventually dries up and is consumed like hay or wood. That is, his flesh is dried like grass, and his bones, along with the skin drawn over them, are weakened like a lopped tree once all the juice is exhausted; they break and collapse.

### THE PROGRESSION INTO DISEASE.

<margin>Defining the parts of the body geographically. How many kinds of Wasting. A limb endures two kinds of dryness: From itself, and from the internal members.</margin>
**A**ny celestial influence flows into a man in an invisible way; yet afterwards, it becomes both visible and tangible within him. Now, there is a peculiar essence and nature of the brain; another peculiar one of the heart, and so on. This must be understood according to "Geography" and "Cosmography," by which all lands and regions are distributed. Just as rain is missing now from this region, now from that, so too is "rain" denied to this or that member of the body. Hence, Phthisis <note>A general term for wasting or consumption, often associated with the lungs.</note> occupies either one part or several, but not all at once. So also the four external limbs—namely the arms and the feet—have their own primary members among themselves, yet they are also subject to the internal ones. This means two types of wasting can happen to them. Thus, we categorize the wastings of the heart, liver, spleen, lungs, kidneys, etc. Likewise, the wastings of the skin, tendons, synovia <note>In this historical context, a nourishing "gluten" or fluid found in the joints and limbs.</note>, joints, nerves, etc., or a single wasting of the entire body. From these things, conclude that the pains which accompany wasting vary according to the different sensations of the members. For any "mortification" <note>The death or localized dying of tissue.</note> stirs up pain; that of the synovia, however, is the greatest and most exquisite. But if the Wasting is universal, no pains are pressing; rather, the wasting is gentle, peaceful, and without sensation. For every single member has its own peculiar nourishment, and yet it is common to all. Whichever member has this nourishment withdrawn by the heaven is thinned by pining and consumption. For there is one "Sun" in the body which continually and perpetually dries things out and consumes moisture. While this Sun is constantly feeding, and nothing else is put back in the place of what was consumed...

<margin>Wasting of the synovia is exquisitely painful. Universal wasting is painless.</margin>

...is replaced, that is, if the rain is not carried there: then by necessity, a dryness is induced by the power of the sun, and in this way, consumption follows. For the body does not lack its own Sun, nor does it lack its own rain and dew. Both of these, therefore, ought to be in the body. If either one of them is missing, things do not go well, and diseases loom. The Sun of the body is fixed and constant; it does not set, but constantly and without ceasing, it attends to its own operation.

However, the "impressions" <note>Celestial influences or "imprints" from the stars upon the human body.</note> are sometimes hindered, so that they become either greater or lesser, or change their nature. It is right for the Physician to know these things. For he must also be an Astronomer. (Note this: if the heaven cuts off a certain influence from a person so that they are cast into sickness, it happens exactly as if by a sword. But understand this to be a "celestial sword.")

## CONTRARIES <note>Arguments against opposing medical theories.</note>.

<margin>Wasting is not from an obstruction.</margin>
As for the claim made by some that the cause of this kind of wasting is an "oppilation" <note>A blockage or obstruction of the internal passages.</note>: that is a vain and fabricated idea. For even if a fatal obstruction were to block the passage, and that interception were to induce dryness, it would by no means be true Wasting <note>Aridura</note>; it would only be a dryness and consumption caused by an obstruction. For the same thing would happen if the passages were cut off by an inflicted wound, bringing on consumption. These are all merely instances of dryness and should not be referred to as Wasting; they have their own proper chapter under "obstruction" and "wounds," and do not concern this universal or primary disease.

<margin>Why humors are not the cause of wasting.</margin>
Likewise, there is no shortage of people who make the humors of the body the causes of this disease. Yet by this opinion, they only betray that they are entirely ignorant of all Astronomy and the nature of the Microcosm <note>The human being viewed as a miniature reflection of the universe.</note> and its alliances. For humidity does not dry out its own body, but rather cherishes and sustains it. In this disease, however, there is dryness and a lack of humor, born from the drying out and consumption caused by the Sun which the Microcosm has operating within itself. For the Sun absorbs the humidity of the body; humidity does not devour and consume itself.

<margin>Catarrh is not the cause of wasting.</margin>
<margin>The Sun alone causes wasting.</margin>
<margin>The lung is not the cause of wasting.</margin>
Thus, catarrh <note>Drainage of fluid, often from the head.</note> distilling from the head cannot be the cause of this disease. It does not generate Wasting, but only obstruction. Nor has this power been given to catarrh to be able to dry up a limb; for that effect must be ascribed to the Sun alone, or to the Element of Fire. Likewise, Wasting does not flow from the lungs. For nothing can proceed from the lung other than a certain unhealthiness, and certainly not Wasting. In this illness, consumption happens in the same way as in fevers or other diseases; these are indeed types of consumption <note>original: "tabes"</note>, but by no means "Aridura."

Thus it might also be said that Wasting is the useless consumption of the nourishment of the limbs. We could grant this to be true insofar as the disease is understood to be the Sun, and the "nourishment" is the impression of the heaven, not that which enters through the mouth. For the latter is "seed." And thus Wasting will be nothing other than the consumption of the "impression," caused by the Sun of the Microcosm, without the interference of other causes. In this way and respect, the same disease might also be called "Marasmus" <note>A clinical term for severe malnutrition and wasting.</note>, insofar as it is understood. For here, through solar dryings, the "impressions" that sustain the whole body are consumed: which is why they are most rightfully called "Radical" and "Substantial." For they are the root and substance of its very measure.
<margin>What radical impressions are.</margin>

## SIGNS.

If Wasting occupies the heart among the internal members: then a trembling of that side arises. If the lung: it moves a dry cough. If the brain: it excites scotoma <note>Dizziness or blurred vision.</note>. If the liver: it inflicts thirst. If the kidneys: it induces thirst together with a change in the urine. If the spleen: it imparts stings. If the gallbladder: it brings on burning and oppression. If the stomach: it strikes with heaviness. If the flesh: it produces emptiness and cavities. If the ligaments: it generates contraction. If the "gluten" <note>The vital fluid or "glue" that binds the body together.</note>: it architects sharp pains. If the blood: it brings on thinness. But if the Wasting is universal, then by a slow, gentle, and gradual drying, all the members are consumed together and equally.

## PROGNOSTICS.

If it should happen that the cough of the lung softens, and the action of the stomach is not hindered, but meanwhile the malice of the bladder and urine increases, and great thirst and strong hunger weigh upon the patient: these are signs of a desperate evil. However, if those other things hold themselves well, there remains a good hope of restoration. Many signs of this kind were indeed noted by the ancients; yet they meanwhile confused many diseases together and did not stop at the single category of Wasting. Therefore, one should not take everything from them indiscriminately. Let what we have said be enough. The disease is such that it delivers nothing other than consumption and wasting, caused by a "placid Sun," according to the condition of the region subjected to it.

## THE CURE.

<margin>A man who is able to generate a heaven.</margin>
In the Cure of this, the first thing to be done is to supply enough humidity to the Sun of the Microcosm, so that it always and continually has something to act upon and consume: that is, so that when something is used up, fresh supply is immediately poured back in. Now, the heaven can by no means be forced to administer humors continually. For that is not subject to the judgment or will of man. But to Art <note>The art of Medicine or Alchemy.</note> this privilege and power has been given: that it can introduce another "heaven" into a sick man. This is what the Arcana <note>Secret, powerful medicinal essences.</note> primarily serve. For an Arcanum is like a powerful heaven, placed in the hand and judgment of the Physician.

<margin>The Arcanum is the Physician’s heaven.</margin>
<margin>*See below in the additions.</margin>

You see grass break forth so fruitfully with happy growth that all the meadows are clothed from a tiny little root. In the same way, we must bring "water" in this case and place, which may increase and spread in the person like grass in the fields, and thus the heaven itself is placed in our hand.

# ON JAUNDICE OR DISEASES OF TINCTURE.
<margin>What are the species of human colors?</margin>
The names of "tinctured" diseases are various. For they list yellow jaundice <note>original: "Icteritiam citrinam"</note>, black jaundice <note>original: "Icteritiam atram"</note>, and I know not how many others. There is very little need to dispute these matters with great accuracy. It will be enough if the diseases themselves are noted and understood—those which are born from the colors of man, namely: <term>Saffron</term>, green, red, black, <term>Azure</term> <note>original: "Lazurio"</note>, white, and the like. If any color of this kind produces a disease, it is usually called a "tinctured" disease or a disease of "tincture" <note>Referring to a state where the body is "stained" by a diseased spiritual essence</note>.

## WHAT IT IS.
<margin>What are the native colors of the Microcosm?</margin>
As to how this disease is generated—such that a color other than that which is naturally present is induced—know that the natural and genuine colors of the body are white and rosy or purple. These are innate and are called "aerial" colors, either because they are not changed by the air, or because they are imprinted by the Sun (such as the dark color present in Ethiopians). If any other colors of the body are brought forth, different from these, they indicate that a disease lies hidden wherever they are visible. Thus, either the eyes have lost their crystal color, or their transparency is darkened, or the teeth do not whiten, or the mouth is not red, and so on. The same logic of colors applies also to the internal members, such as the flesh and blood, the marrow, and all parts that lose their native and vivid color. It seems necessary to discuss these diseases at greater length. Furthermore, death itself induces other colors, such as livid blues, as if from spilled blood, which are noted in corpses as the intensity of death takes hold. But the consideration of these does not belong to the Physician, since they do nothing for his instruction. For they testify to an impending or already begun destruction of health, but they do not indicate the quality of the disease, which will be dealt with later in its proper place.
<margin>Foreign colors indicate diseases of the parts.</margin>
<margin>Death changes colors.</margin>

<margin>Color is spiritual, not corporeal.</margin>
Therefore, we must discuss the generation of colors separately here. For there is no color in the body that breaks out externally [on its own], but colors are spiritual. It is a spiritual color when the color becomes something other than what it was. Thus, if two spirits meet, they discolor their body. For color is of the spirit. Therefore, two colors mixed together produce a third color. From this, a "tinctured" disease arises. Now, the Azure color <note>original: "Lazurius"</note> arises from the brain and the blood; Saffron and red from the blood; black and purple from the blood and flesh; white from all parts; green from the principal members. Although these colors are not visible in themselves, they become visible through their transformation. The minerals themselves teach us very well what it is that we least see in them—that is, what lies hidden and concealed within them. It is prepared in the same way in man. Just as the craftsman gazes upon these wonders externally, so also the Physician [gazes upon them]...

It is enough that the disease be designated by this name, namely "colic," while other names for it fall out of use.

## WHAT IS IT?

**Colic**, then, is a pain and torment that arises in the belly, accompanied by a contraction of it and a suppression of excrement, along with many other signs felt by the stomach and other members. Finally, if the colic seems to let up, violent diarrhea and troublesome vomiting occur; afterwards, the evil passes into the limbs and joints, where it lingers and contracts the hands and feet more or less, according to how great the disease was and how abundant the matter. Furthermore, it spreads with a certain force and becomes either acute or chronic, according to the nature of its origin. Eventually, there follows a wasting of the body, a change in the voice, and a diminishing of the entire substance.

## THE CAUSE.

<margin>The generation of Colic is the same as that of the winds.</margin>
<margin>The two kinds of winds and a clever comparison between the origin of Man and the world.</margin>
**What** can I say about this, except that the "physicians" <note>The author likely refers to traditional Galenic doctors who follow ancient Greek theories</note> babble much about the causes of colic, even though they have no foundation in true Physics? For the generation of colic is the same as that of the winds blowing in both summer and winter, of which one blows from the north, another from the south, a third from the east, and a fourth from the west. Once these are born, they cross the entire world until they are consumed again. The generation of these winds occurs in four places in the world, equally distributed and packed with their side-winds. By the same logic, man is to be divided as if into four parts of his own world, from which the winds may come forth. If this is not done, the Physician will never be able to know from where the colic arises.

<margin>What is chaos and what is its nature?</margin>
<margin>Obstructions are the cause of colic.</margin>
Now, the heavens are the sphere of all the Elements and stars which they embrace. The skin in man has the same relationship. And just as the four Elements with their bodies exist in the celestial sphere, so it is equally in man. Furthermore, where the Elements have their seat, a certain cavity and emptiness is left, in which man stands, walks, and lives. That vacuum is similarly to be understood in man. For in him—that is, in the hollow in which the <term>chaos</term> <note>In Paracelsian medicine, "chaos" often refers to the air or the atmospheric space between the elements where life and movement happen</note> is located—this disease is fostered. Now, two bodies cannot exist at the same time in one essence; because of this, chaos is not a "body" and does not fill a space, but yields to others, yet never leaves the place empty. Furthermore, as the world's winds have their exit, movement, and finally their consumption, so it is with human winds. However, in man, more things must be considered than in the world. For in him, obstructions sometimes occur by which the exit of the winds is hindered. And this, finally, is the beginning of colic; this is the cause. For no one is without winds, but many are without obstructions. Those who suffer from these obstructions—so that the wind cannot pass through or breathe out—are troubled by colic "twistings." Thus, in the intestines, because of the shape of the organs, whirlwinds are visibly formed, which are driven into a rotation on the outside as well, but through invisible instruments.

<margin>The East wind is the flatus at the end of the stomach.</margin>
Next, we shall speak of the four winds according to the distribution of the world, along with their side-winds (which nevertheless do not have significant power), namely in what way they arise in the same number and from which places they blow. The East, then, is at the end of the stomach where it empties itself; and its wind is <term>Eurus</term> <note>The Greek name for the East wind</note>, which breathes through to the <term>Monoculum</term> <note>Archaic term for the cecum, the beginning of the large intestine</note> outside the colon. This is why the ancients even called this wind "colic," though in another sense. As for the winds that blow in the stomach itself, these are like those that blow on the sea or land. For just as winds are carried through many parts of the world and throw down and shake whatever is in their way, now here, now there, so the same happens in the belly, where many things are blown through and shaken that do not pertain to colic here. To those who claim the intestines are an "elemental body" and conclude from this that there is no vacuum in the belly, we reply: the intestines are something like a "superfluity" which the Great World <note>The Macrocosm/Universe</note> lacks, because the world does not eat as man does. Because man had to eat, he had need of intestines, which the larger world is rightly without. And a Physician ought to know these things much more certainly and accurately than what their Philosophy teaches.

<margin>The West is the Monoculum.</margin>
<margin>The North wind is the back.</margin>
<margin>The South wind is the navel.</margin>
<margin>The 4 cardinal colics.</margin>
<margin>Colic and Iliac are one disease.</margin>
The West comes forth from the regions of the Monoculum, ascends to the colon, and ends near the bottom of the stomach, where it is consumed. For just as the upper wind is consumed in the monoculum, so the lower wind, <term>Zephyrus</term> <note>The West wind</note>, is consumed in the colon. From this are stirred up belching, hiccups, and other similar things. The North wind, <term>Boreas</term>, emerges in the middle region of the spine and extends toward the belly. Opposite the North, near the navel, the South wind, <term>Auster</term>, rises, proceeding toward the back into the regions of the north. From this arrangement, it follows that some remedies cure colic if the navel is anointed; some if the back is smeared; some if they move the bowels; and some if they provoke vomiting. For these colics are cured in no other way than that by which a suitable exit is provided for the winds. Neither Eurus through the stomach, nor Zephyrus through evacuation, nor Auster or Boreas through the two designated <term>emunctories</term> <note>Organs or channels that carry off waste</note> can be emptied and led out; rather, they require to be consumed like a <term>lamp-wick</term> <note>original: "ellychnium"</note>, without a solid body. For this must be noted about colics: that they have no body, but are mere wind. Therefore, we should not seek "bodies" to expel through medicines, nor say that this or that substance is what moved the colic. For the wind, though invisible, is yet palpable, but it has no body. Medicine, therefore, must be so constituted that it does not expel bodies—that is, dung and other similar things. For that is not the true cure of colic. In this way, then, the four cardinal colics with their side-winds are generated. For Colic and <term>Iliac</term> <note>Referring to "Iliac Passion," an older term for severe intestinal obstruction or pain in the lower gut</note> are one and the same wind, except that one is a side-wind; however, the ancients made two different diseases from them, generated from different causes, which does not agree with the truth at all. For all have one origin, one cause; nor do they differ among themselves except by this nature: that one is cold, another hot, one moist, and another dry. And according to this nature and condition, the pains themselves appear in different ways. Read the philosophy of this generation concerning these matters.

<header>->ON COLIC<-</header>

...so that you may hold this as a fully understood summary,
<margin>The body consists of three things.</margin>
I would like you to remember that the body consists entirely of three things: <term>Mercury</term>, <term>Sulfur</term>, and <term>Salt</term> <note>These are the Paracelsian "Three Primes," the fundamental components of all matter, representing volatility, flammability, and stability/solidity.</note>. From this, it follows that if these winds arise—such as the <term>South Wind</term> <note>original: Auster</note> and the <term>West Wind</term> <note>original: Zephyrus</note>—the salt is dissolved in that region of the body where it is contained. Now, the "dissolution of salt" is a separation of the body, such that this or that part yields and brings forth its own salt, which is then dissolved. However, the body itself is not the cause; rather, the salt is separated from the body into excrement and waste. If physicians see this, they persuade themselves it is colic, which is false. They attribute the cause to that bodily filth <note>stool or intestinal waste</note> and think that once the waste is ejected, the colic is removed and mitigated, not considering meanwhile that this is mere excrement and by no means the actual cause.

<margin>Excrement is not the cause of colic.</margin>
Nevertheless, just as dissolved salt in the body is sharp and eroding—biting no differently than salt rubbed into a wound—the same thing happens in the intestines. But this affection is by no means colic; rather, it is a <term>torsion</term> <note>a painful twisting or griping of the bowels</note> afflicted by salt in this manner. For this, purgations are very useful, especially if the cause of the wind was removed beforehand.

The physician should not investigate the excrement itself, but must first investigate the cause of the winds. Once that is consumed, if the "torsion" from the salt remains afterwards, it must be removed by the proper means.

Furthermore, to speak further of the causes of the winds, know that in this place it must be established regarding <term>Meteoric generations</term> <note>Paracelsus compares internal gases to atmospheric weather patterns, believing the same laws of nature apply to both the "Great World" and the "Little World" of the human body.</note> that just as the <term>North Wind</term> <note>original: Septentrio</note> arises from the Northern stars, so the <term>East Wind</term> <note>original: Eurus</note> arises similarly from the East. In exactly the same way, and no other, you should seek and hold the reasons within the man himself. For whatever causes you see in the generation of external winds, you should estimate those same causes in internal ones according to their number, multitude, strength, and whether they are acute or chronic in nature. Thus, colics may be greater or smaller, just as the winds are generated in their own time and fall upon the regions of the body. For as soon as they are generated, they invade the elemental body and either cool it, where colic is present; or moisten it, and colic arises; or dry it, and colic seizes; or inflame it, and colic again follows. For just as the earth is excessively moistened, dried, cooled, and heated, so also is the body. Moreover, because the body is endowed with senses, a certain medicine has been created and appointed for its pains.

<margin>The triple mode of colic.</margin>
Therefore, three "accidents"—that is, three types of diseases—appear through colic. One disease is when the winds rise by themselves and cause a tumult within, like an earthquake or deep caverns, when they cannot be consumed. From this commotion, since the human body is quite sensitive, certain pains are inflicted upon it. A second disease occurs when the <term>Elemental parts</term> <note>the fundamental components of the body</note> become too humid, wet, parched, or dry. For that alteration affects those three things from which man is constituted. Meanwhile, the parts endowed with sense can by no means be free from pain.

<margin>Pain is an affection of the sensing parts.</margin>
The third arises when the salt is dissolved, and also some of the sulfur. For since these are sharp and biting, they cannot exist without pain. Thus there are three modes of pain, and so a triple medicine is owed to them whenever colic proceeds or has proceeded into "exaltation" <note>a state of peak intensity or chemical activation</note>.

<margin>A singular pain exists in the hollow parts.</margin>
All these pains collectively are called <term>tormina</term> <note>griping pains or intestinal cramps</note> or colic. For the nature and condition of the body, where it is hollow and empty, is such that it is infested by "torminous" pains, which do not manifest themselves at all like those which afflict other non-hollow parts. This singular kind of pain must therefore be attributed to the nature and condition of that specific place.

## THE PROCESS

<margin>Man is made of his failing elements.</margin>
Since man is subject to death, and his life is brief and fleeting, barely running for a few years, it can be concluded by certain reasoning that this brevity depends entirely on the fragility of his internal <term>firmament</term> <note>the internal "astronomy" or governing structure of the body</note> and Elements, which too readily admit the force and injury of external things rushing in. If this were not so, he would surely flourish along with the world itself, and would live happily for infinite ages until the "Platonic Year" <note>a cycle of about 25,000 years after which the stars return to their original positions</note>, which will only end together with the Sun, Moon, and all the Elements. But now, since his failing and fleeting lot is too certain:

<margin>The cause of colic is twofold.</margin>
a twofold cause of colic should be noted by you here.

<margin>The first cause explained.</margin>
The first is that the winds thrust themselves in and stir up colic, in the same way that external winds, like the North, West, South, and East winds, fall upon us by their own motion, with us contributing nothing to their stirring. The other is when we ourselves entice those winds, so that they fall upon us even against our will, summoned by our own choice or judgment. And we must now speak of these two modes. When, therefore, the winds rush in by their own motion and accord, their impulses do not have the goal of being useful or comfortable to us, but of shattering and destroying our body. For we, who are subject to death, must endure this entirely. In whatever way death insults us, it must be admitted. In this way, whatever things act for us eventually become our adversaries. Therefore, Medicine was given to us so that such things might be understood. As for the reasoning and manner in which these winds arrive by themselves, I leave that to be investigated by <term>Astronomic Medicine</term>, as well as <term>Meteorology</term>, which inquire into the principles and causes of such "impressions" <note>celestial influences or internal shifts</note>; they teach that these need not be brought up at length here. For this question is more philosophical than medical. Furthermore, to strengthen your knowledge of these things, know that cold and humidity are the causes of the generation of the winds that seize us.

<margin>Cold and humidity are the cause of winds.</margin>
For cold and humidity in the locations and "cardinal points" of the winds stir up a kind of swelling within them. When this swells up like natural winds, they blow through and are stirred up in a man's belly, making an impetus upward and downward. While they invade the pores of the fragile and failing body, by their stirring they dissolve the very substance of the pores, from which triple pains are impressed upon the body.

<margin>The second cause explained.</margin>
Furthermore, there is another stirring up of winds from food and drink. For if we use these too intemperately and gorge ourselves on an immoderate abundance of them, then we excessively moisten that region of the body in which the winds lie. From this, therefore, the winds rise more swiftly and rush in violently with their paroxysms.

<margin>Anger is the mother of colic.</margin>
But anger is also a mother of similar winds. For when anger glows hot, the entire body trembles, and the seat of the <term>incorporeal spirits</term> <note>the vital forces that are not material but govern the body's functions</note> is shaken and scattered, and these move into the place...

He identifies two causes: natural "astronomic" forces and self-inflicted causes like overeating or anger.</summary>

...when they are shaken out as something foreign, where finally, by the heat which boiling anger has stirred up, they are excessively exhausted and dried out. There, the winds—already dry by nature—are dried out most of all; even the more humid winds, like the <term>West Wind</term> <note>original: Zephyrus</note> and the <term>South Wind</term> <note>original: Auster</note>, become drier than is right. The <term>South Wind</term> and the <term>Southeast Wind</term> <note>original: Eurus</note> heat the body too much, while the <term>North Wind</term> <note>original: Septentrio</note> and the West Wind become too sluggish in their coldness. By all these imbalances, they bring on pains and diseases, as we have said.

<margin>Like the East and North Winds.</margin>

<margin>How colic, or subtle wind, breaks out into the joints.</margin>
The nature of wind is so subtle that whenever it drives the body into a "dissolution," the very <term>spirit of salt</term> <note>In Paracelsian chemistry, this refers to the volatile or essential quality of salt, which governs the structural integrity and fluids of the body.</note> also vanishes into wind. Thus, two spirits become one thing, just as one color emerges from two dyes thrown into water. Afterward, if the proper channels or passages are not open, or if the wind is not stopped at the beginning, it then—by its own subtleness—penetrates and breaks through all the pores in every direction until it breaks out into the furthest limbs. Wandering through all the hollows of the joints and connections, it builds a seat for itself within them. And when it has brought the "spirit of salt" along with it as a companion and focus, it produces pains there, seizing and occupying both the <term>synovia</term> <note>The lubricating fluid of the joints.</note> and the spirit of the joint itself. For in whatever place this wind flourishes, it stirs up contraction and spasms, binds the members, destroys their strength, and casts them down no differently than one might tear down a great house. If the mass of the limbs collapses and the joints are stripped of their native strength, they are prostrated by the excessively powerful force of the wind, where they cannot even rise again unless they are supported either by their own nature or by a "blocking" medicine. These pressing pains pierce until the spirit of salt is either consumed along with the wind or drawn away by another path. Whatever has fallen, however, remains down.

### THE SIGNS.

<margin>What is a sign?</margin>
**A**fter these things come their own signs. For what else is a sign but a track left behind by an operation? A house built by an architect is a sign of its maker, from which his art and labor are known. Therefore, the work itself is the sign; so it is here. These winds (or whatever else it may be) render all four limbs contracted. That, therefore, is the first sign. Second, it destroys the virtue of the stomach and casts it into an opposite nature. This is the second sign. Furthermore, it constricts the organs of the voice and the parts near them. That is the third sign. It holds back the bowels and breaks the urine. This is the fourth sign. <note>Note: The "fourth sign" is repeated in the original text.</note> By blowing through the belly up and down, it disturbs and distends it. This is the fifth sign. These are the signs of present colic: that is, signs of that which causes the evil—namely, the flatus, the material of the wind, and similar things. (Just as a house is the sign of the carpenter, and the body of Christ is the house of the sheep; yet not all of us enter this sheepfold.)

### CONTRARIES.

<margin>Why bile is not the cause of colic.</margin>
**B**ecause the waste products are fluid and sharp, it might be said or thought that bile <note>original: fel (gall)</note> produces this disease. Also, because anger is sometimes the cause of it, some people persuade themselves that since anger comes from bile, bile must be the cause of colic. They are used to making much noise about such things. You, however, must be certain that bile is by no means the cause. For it does not emit as much weight from itself as the waste itself contains. Furthermore, bile is a part of the body which—like a bone or any other similar member—does not grow beyond its own proportion and measure. Thus, such a great mass or weight cannot come from it. Moreover, since it is not in the nature of its condition to beget and produce winds, it will be the least likely cause of colic—something many "Humoralists" <note>Followers of the traditional theory of the four humors (blood, phlegm, yellow bile, black bile).</note> claim but do not demonstrate.

There are also many winds that pinch the womb itself, as in "suffocation of the uterus" <note>Historically known as hysteria, often thought to be caused by "vapors" or the movement of the womb.</note>. But whatever name is eventually given to these, the disease itself is nothing but wind, from the number of the four previously mentioned. Now, the womb belongs to women, not men. Therefore, the womb is divided in the same way. However, I am deferring that to its own chapter. Though turnips, and more copious amounts of sour wine, beer, and water, etc., frequently stir up colic. For we are all subject to "dissolution." When it is placed in these things, and if it is then stirred up, like joins to like; and from there—whether 4, 2, or 3 together, depending on the condition of the matter—they arise and enter their "exaltation." For otherwise, no colic occurs that is not born from these four winds.

### DECLARATION.

**T**herefore, there are four types of Colic: *Colic*, which is of the <term>East Wind</term> <note>original: Eurus</note>; *Torsions*, which are of the <term>West Wind</term> <note>original: Zephyrus</note>, in the <term>Cecum</term> <note>original: Monoculo. The "blind" part of the large intestine.</note> (the first is hot and dry; the second is cold and humid, which is why they require contrary remedies); *Griping of the Navel*, which is the <term>South Wind</term> <note>original: Auster</note>, humid and hot; and *Affliction of the Back*, which is the <term>North Wind</term> <note>original: Boreas</note>, which rarely moves far from its region, mostly containing itself there, and is cold.

<margin>The secret for curing Colic:</margin>
Which of these types of colic it is, the signs of the location and the excrement will teach. However, since these signs are often quite obscure and confused, much confidence should not be placed in them. Instead, one should proceed directly in the cure by this method: that the winds themselves be consumed. For this is the one "arcanum" <note>A secret or ultimate medicinal mystery/remedy.</note> of colic. Then, the body should be restored to its native temperature; whether it is drier, more humid, colder, or hotter than is right must be discerned from the waste. For the waste must be observed so that the dissolved salt may be found with its sulfur—which is the very last thing to be done. If, however, the limbs or joints have collapsed, let them be the last priority. For first, all internal parts must be restored to their strength and native constitution. Once that is introduced, power is thereafter granted and returned to the limbs of its own accord. For the base and foundation upon which they lean is fixed within the body.

## ON GOUT OR APOPLEXY.

APOPLEXY contains many diseases within itself, which are designated by many names, such as Apoplexy, Paralysis, <term>Lethargy</term> <note>A state of prolonged unconsciousness or profound drowsiness, then categorized as a specific brain disorder.</note>, etc. There is no need to keep all these names in use. For if names should only proceed from causes, it will be necessary for many of these appellations to fade away. Specific names ought to dictate specific causes. Apoplexy, however, is referred to only a single cause.

### WHAT IS IT?

IF suddenly and all at once a person's health is overthrown, and reason perishes, and the eyes are convulsed, breathing is hard and laborious, a suffocation of the lungs torments them, and the person seethes within themselves like <term>must</term> <note>Unfermented grape juice that bubbles and heats up during fermentation.</note> in a sealed vessel, and their whole body burns; when sensation and mobility are taken away along with reason, speech perishes, the neck swells and bulges, hearing fails, and furthermore, certain outcomes occur: one, namely, if the patient lies in that state for several days without improvement, then death is imminent; another, if the patient recovers himself somewhat, yet speech and talk do not return, or one side is rendered "blasted" <note>original: syderatum; literally "star-struck," a term for sudden paralysis believed to be caused by a malignant planetary influence or "stroke" of lightning.</note> and as if dead, or the mouth is turned distorted, or whatever similar happens, either with a spasm or with <term>tetanus</term> <note>A condition of rigid muscle contraction or stiffening.</note>, etc. If you see these things, say it is Apoplexy: the origin and generation of which is as will now be told.

### THE CAUSE.

<margin>Gout and lightning share one science.</margin>
IT is fitting for you to know that Gout or Apoplexy, in all its nature and property, is similar to heavenly lightning, both according to its generation, its operation, and its marvelous effects. And he who has certain knowledge of heavenly lightning may boldly boast that he is a Physician skilled and conscious of <term>gout</term> <note>original: gutta; while this is the root of the modern word "gout," the author uses it here to describe a sudden "drop" or "strike" of illness, essentially a stroke.</note>. For here, <term>Meteorology</term> <note>original: Meteorica; the study of atmospheric phenomena, here applied to the "weather" inside the human body.</note> and Physics are forced into a single harmony and reason. This is clearly demonstrated by practice and great experience, along with other things drawn from the light of nature itself.

<margin>The marvelous powers of lightning.</margin>
It is surely known to you that lightning strikes, but sometimes breaks nothing: that is, it penetrates a closed and locked chest, yet does not crush it; it melts iron, but does not hurt the man; it breaks the sword, yet does not burn the scabbard. Lightning performs many miracles of this kind.

<margin>The marvelous effects of Gout.</margin>
The nature of gout is also similar. It gathers and melts into one mass either the brain, or the heart, or the lungs, no differently than if they were wax; meanwhile, it hurts no other parts of the body. It strikes and hits from above, from the head to the outer limbs, namely the hands and feet, and inflames and burns whatever is enclosed within the skin, yet does not violate the skin itself. It beats out the speech of the tongue while it burns away the speech (which is a breath) with its seething vapor, yet it does not harm the tongue itself. These are not undeservedly called the great miracles of Nature. But for you, Physician, these things must be well known, and the very light of nature must be intimately examined by you here. For this Philosophy, this Astro-

<margin>The similar nature of lightning and Apoplexy. The marvelous power of lightning.</margin>
-nomy, this Physics, is in this place the truest and most inward Medicine. For the generation of both things is one and entirely similar: one in the external World, the other in the internal. For they differ from each other in this alone, and in nothing else. Now, therefore, if the internal lightning strikes and touches the lung: its vapor suffocates the lung. For the lung suffers nothing else from it than being strangled by an internal state, just as we see the same thing happen outside, that men are suffocated by the vapor of nearby lightning. So if gout strikes the brain, the man dies, not otherwise than if his brain had been broken, crushed, melted, or ground down by external lightning while the skull remained unharmed. For whatever accidents are burned into the brain by external lightning, the exact same things are found in those killed by the other.

By like reason, if internal lightning touches the heart, it strangles and burns it, while its capsule remains whole and the <term>water of the heart</term> <note>The pericardial fluid surrounding the heart.</note> remains safe. For the same thing happens here as elsewhere: namely, if external lightning striking water does not indeed enter it, yet kills the fish living in the water. Those affected in this part have a trembling of the heart, and its strong palpitation, and a wonderful anguish, among other similar accidents of a most seriously injured heart. But if it strikes the liver, it indeed scorches it, but not its walls in the same way. The signs of these must be gathered from the injured places. Therefore, one must know and determine the same not only regarding the strike of these members, but regarding all others universally. Since the strikes of that lightning occur so wonderfully now here, now there, you must be forewarned that in gout many and varied signs appear, and the same are confused: now appearing like the <term>falling sickness</term> <note>original: caduco; epilepsy.</note>, now equal to oppression and strangulation, now exhibiting a spasm that is both contracting and extending. For things of this sort emerge like foam from the nature of those members. What we have said about the superior or primary members—if they are struck in this way, death is not far off, and life is in immediate danger. Besides those, however, the ears, eyes, tongue, and remaining parts are also sometimes struck. The injury to these is not indeed lethal; from it, however, their private life and strength perish, so that not all hope of their restoration is taken away. Nor does gout work here in any way other than how, if lightning strikes, wood is set on fire by it, while straw remains untouched. For the fire in the vapor of lightning is quite marvelous. It does not at all ignite things prepared for burning; but it ignites things that can only be ignited with difficulty. In this way, the members of the body remain unburnt; however, their spirits endure a conflagration. From this it also happens that speech perishes, hearing is dulled, and sight or taste is taken away. Although this also is true: that if either the brain or the heart is about to die, all these nonetheless suffer at once, and their signs show themselves similarly. The same distinction must be held regarding the lung and the liver.

Furthermore, just as you sometimes see lightning [striking] some wall...

The author argues that just as atmospheric lightning can melt a sword without harming the scabbard, internal medical "lightning" can destroy the function of an organ or limb while leaving the surrounding tissue seemingly untouched.</summary>

<margin>How half the side may be paralyzed by the stroke.</margin>
<margin>How both sides may be paralyzed.</margin>
...to seize the very top of something and follow its cracks in a straight line, so that by pulling it apart in every direction, it splits and loosens the wall from top to bottom: so too the stroke <note>original: "gutta"; literally "the drop," a term used for both gout and sudden seizures like apoplexy.</note> sometimes strikes from above into at least one part. Starting its path from there—for example, in the neck—it then diligently follows the continuous track of either the ligaments, the nerves, or the tendons. Whichever tendon it has struck, it also follows that muscle all the way to its end, pushing and driving it precisely toward the hands and feet. And if one of the tendons ends in the arm and another in the feet, then this "lightning" divides itself, and by its forceful path, it paralyzes <note>original: "resoluit"; literally "loosens" or "unravels," the standard term for paralysis in this era.</note> the entire side it has struck. This happens more frequently on the left side than on the right. The reason for this is that the nature of lightning is such that it always more readily strikes the side closer to the heart. But if the lightning—which happens more rarely—is divided above the neck in the back of the head, then that distribution is twofold, occurring on both sides, and both are then injured. This is clearly lethal if it proceeds seriously. However, if the vapor is thin and turns aside into only one part, it would be consumed and the situation would be safer. Therefore, as it strikes, it works in wondrous ways, and its damages and harms cannot be entirely counted. For it burns away or liquefies the fibers of the veins, yet it harms the veins themselves very little. Likewise, it consumes the moisture of the ligaments while their substance remains intact, and vice versa. For all the pores themselves are opened, and the same force travels through all the muscles, pulling and breaking them apart, from which excruciating pains are felt. And who, I ask, could anywhere sufficiently explain in words the works and "loosenings" caused by lightning within a human being? For innumerable things happen, but very few are revealed to us. And although we may not hear the crash and assault of the falling lightning at all, the one who suffers the evil feels it all too exquisitely, as if heaven and earth themselves were colliding. We do not hear the thunder for this reason: we are standing outside that world. Only those who are within it hear it. But every single man is within himself. Thus, each person hears their own "heaven," not another’s. And everyone sustains the impact of their own heaven by themselves. In the same way, those who live outside our world do not feel the disturbances of our firmament. Likewise, we do not hear what happens among them. But these matters belong to the study of Meteorology.

<margin>Injury to a vital organ means death.</margin>
Now, whatever damage and detriment the lightning plots against a man, it completes it suddenly and in the blink of an eye, and whatever it strikes is penetrated. For if it harms a vital organ, it brings death. For who can make a burnt thing as if it were not burnt? Or who can rebuild wood from ashes? So if such a thing happens in the body, death is at hand. But if the injury occurs in other parts that do not govern life itself, then that blow brings only disease, not death. Just as the organs are noble, so either death or disease—be it heavy or light, safe or dangerous—is introduced, just as all these things are providently arranged by God.

### THE PROCESS.

<margin>Nothing acts without a distinct medium. Wood does not burn without air.</margin>
<margin>What the "Middle Heaven" is.</margin>
<margin>Lightning becomes extremely subtle before it is formed.</margin>
**T**his philosophy must be handled skillfully and industriously, lest the meteorological influence be led astray beyond its boundaries. It happens in this way: the conjunctions of the physical stars are the parents of diseases born from influences, of which there are various kinds. From their ranks, this disease also arises from lightning. Now, these conjunctions cannot achieve their effects unless they have a certain concurrent society to which they are joined. For although it is commonly said that conjunctions stir up rain, hail, and every storm, none of these can happen unless the <term>Middle Heaven</term> <note>The atmospheric space or "medium" between the stars and the Earth; in the human body, this refers to the internal environment or "inner air."</note> agrees. Thus, wood and fire, if they are coupled and joined, burn because of the presence of the air as a medium. For unless the consenting air were present, they would not burn at all. The same is true of conjunctions. Unless a fitting and consenting medium is joined with them, they achieve nothing. In the same way, a child is conceived in the mother's womb. But if the seed does not enter the womb, the child is not born. Likewise, unless the seed of a plant is cast into suitable and prepared earth, it will never emerge. So too, lightning will achieve nothing if it does not have its "Medium." Now, the Medium in the heavens is an extremely subtle, distilled moisture which is not produced from the earth, but rather is the very body of the Middle Heaven—just as we say the earth is the body of the ground. So too, between heaven and earth there is a certain body, which is like the soil in which such things are born and produced. Now, so that these things may be related to the <term>Microcosm</term> <note>The "small world"—the human being as a reflection of the great universe (the Macrocosm).</note>, it is right to know that within man himself a similar "Medium Body" or "Middle Heaven" has been established, in which these influences occur. Therefore, if the conjunctions are joined, and that Medium Body is so subtle and fertile that it receives the inseminated conjunction and agrees to its growth, then finally the harvest and autumn of the seeded thing is at hand—namely, so that what we have spoken of may be produced and come to be. Now, the disposition of this operation is such that it reverberates and circulates its body most subtly until its force reaches where it intends. For no lightning exists that, before it was formed, was not much more subtle than anyone can imagine. For it has attained the admirable speed of its onset solely from its most exquisite subtlety.

<margin>The power of heaven can be hindered, but not incited.</margin>
However, there are also some things which promote and bring such effects into being beyond their time—that is, against the natural time. For although nothing can incite or promote the external heaven (though it can be hindered), since it is not situated in our hand or power, man himself is nonetheless fragile within his own "heaven." He should therefore consider this: that his own internal heaven can be both promoted and hindered. For this purpose **Medicine** was created, so that from it we might both be comforted in our miseries and worthily celebrate the immense mercy of God. But so that the causes may be promoted...

# ON APOPLEXY.

<margin>By what means is the middle heaven of man advanced?</margin>
<margin>By what means is it repressed?</margin>
This process has power if a person consumes delicate foods and drinks, which are not expelled by the body but are instead refined and distilled into a state of subtlety. In this way, the "Middle Heaven" <note>In the medical philosophy of Paracelsus, the "Middle Heaven" refers to a specific energetic region within the human body that mirrors the atmosphere of the outer world.</note> of the person is prepared. Since this Middle Heaven is fatty and oily, a boiling and evaporation occur within it, through which any internal "conjunction" <note>A term borrowed from astrology, referring here to the alignment of internal forces.</note> can be nourished and heightened. However, if the body is thinned by abstinence, no such thing happens. For even if some harmful conjunction were hanging over the person, it could easily be hindered or even entirely broken. On the other hand, sadness, joy, terror, and fear promote rather than hinder this process. For these emotions overturn the "heaven" of man and move it out of its ordinary circle and measure; regarding these, read the specific *Theoretical Treatise*. While these events are generated in the Middle Heaven in the manner described, the time it takes for this lightning <note>original: "fulgur"</note> to ignite is only a single, tiny moment. For the internal planet prepares and exalts the body and its "impression" for a long time until it is reduced to an exquisite and supreme subtlety; before it turns into lightning, it has already undergone more than twenty or thirty new generations. A similar thing occurs here as does with urine. When urine is initially too thick, it is forced to undergo many changes in the body. Now this, now that occurs, which had not been there before, and these changes continue until, having cast off all its prior forms, it finally becomes urine, which it was not before. Through so many intermediate alterations, it is finally so refined that it cannot be made any more subtle. For now it becomes Salt, now Alkali, now Nitre, now Spirit, and so forth. The same must be concluded in this proposed case: if excrements are retained in the body and repeatedly refined, they eventually promote that internal conjunction. And as soon as that subtle substance touches the planet in its circulation, nothing else happens than if one were to throw fire into gunpowder <note>original: "puluerem tormentarium"</note>. For the Fire takes the place of the Planet; the powder is the Middle Heaven. The result is that which is produced from those two.

## EXPLANATION.

<margin>The three causes of lightning, etc.</margin>
**T**here are three things that generate lightning: sulfur, salt, and the fire of the firmament. These three produce lightning, as well as thunder and other such things. Thus, that meteorological event is merely sulfur and salt which, through those sulfurous and salt-bearing stars, enters into a conjunction and is ignited by the element of fire, which the heaven contains physically within itself. You should not think of the powers and operations of the internal heaven any differently than you would an artisan who, intending to prepare gunpowder, brings together all the things necessary for it. The heaven does the same. Just as the artisan then adds fire, so too does the heaven—but here it is taken for the preparation and composition of the thunder, lightning, and fire that is present. It is the same in man, who consists of these same things. For he is the <term>microcosm|literally "the lesser world," a concept suggesting that the human body contains all the elements and celestial structures of the entire universe</term>. Thus, Apoplexy arises from those three things mentioned: that is, those three are the matter called Apoplexy, which inflicts that injury and damage. Now, it can happen that this matter is gathered and brought together in a person

within the space of a single year, which otherwise would hardly be collected in ten years or more. For the heaven of the man himself is so placed in the man's hands that he can either extend or contract it according to his own movement. The cause of this is that man is subject to fragility; hence he has a life that is either short or long, healthy or unhealthy.

## CONTRARY VIEWS.

<margin>Why food, drink, and humors are not the causes of Apoplexy.</margin>
**T**his opinion has made many in *Medicine* doubtful and confused, because they thought that food was the material cause of Apoplexy. But how that could be has not yet been sufficiently explained. These people, unmindful of the internal heaven, defined the matter only according to their own opinion. Hence the idea that drunkenness, cold foods, and so on are the causes of apoplexy; yet these have no power as causes except insofar as the heaven permits them, which will be similarly true in countless other cases. For few become apoplectic from drunkenness, but rather from the other causes mentioned above. Because apoplectic patients are usually "full," <note>Referring to "plethora," or an overabundance of fluids/blood in the body according to ancient medicine.</note> they assign the cause to this fullness. In the same way, they make blood itself the cause of apoplexy. This is no more true. For blood is too thick and unfit for the generation of apoplexy. Its generation is of no account, as is that of phlegm <note>original: "phlegmatis"</note>, which is a substance too thick, viscous, and unsuitable. Judge the same regarding the other humors. I will not mention that in explaining the generation of these things, they have brought nothing from the inner secrets of Philosophy to make it clear how apoplexy could eventually be raised from those things. For they always introduce something by which the sense of truth is obscured. And although many such very plausible things can be brought forward to confirm their case, they are all empty and trifling, and such that they fit neither Philosophy, nor Astronomy, nor Theory and Physics.
> (Phlegm is merely the excrement of things contained in the head. But the stroke <note>original: "Gutta"</note> is not an excrement, but a thing most subtle of all, born from the secrets of the firmament. But they, being the kind of physicians they are, do and say such things.)

## THE CURE.

<margin>Apoplexy is an external force of God.</margin>
**W**hat effort or protection remains for us to repress and break such a violent impulse and strong impression? Certainly, if the vital members are touched, the matter should be commended to God alone. For who can resist His power? For the force and power belongs to God when the celestial virtues are moved, as we have already said. But if the vital members are not struck, but only their neighborhood, a counsel that is easy, safe, and prompt can be given. There is a need for two types of medicine. One is a strengthening medicine <note>original: "confortatiua"</note> made from the Essence of minerals—that is, from the highest strengthening agents. For strengtheners of this kind clear the "heaven" and scatter its clouds and mists, turning it from turbid to bright and transparent. Thus the Sun, stirred by the medicine, dries and absorbs the rain it has poured out. A second medicine is needed,
