## ON MANIA.

**M**ania is given many names both by the Latins and by other nations, though it is but a single disease. Since different people have different perceptions, various causes for Mania have been assigned from time to time; however, none of these agree with the experience drawn from the Light of Nature <note>A Paracelsian term referring to the innate wisdom found in the natural world, as opposed to book-learning</note> itself.

### WHAT IS IT?

<margin>Who are the truly manic?</margin>
If a person in possession of their reason is deprived and robbed of it, and does not employ it for those ends for which it was created, but instead raves furiously and is thrown into chaotic turmoil, they are already seized by Mania. Many others are also stripped of their reason, such as the Possessed, Drunks, Fools, and Tyrants. These, however, are not to be referred to this class. For in them, reason is exiled not by a disease, but by other external circumstances. But those we deal with here suffer from true diseases, arising naturally from disease-causing agents.

### THE CAUSE.

<margin>The integrity of reason consists in purity.</margin>
To better understand the explanation of the cause, it must be known that Reason ought to be pure and clean, like the finest wheat in a field, lacking all darnel and weeds. But just as weeds sown among the wheat grow and increase, so too are weeds born in the intellect. If the intellect proceeds to judge matters while oppressed by the overgrowth of weeds—such as vetch and darnel—it loses its way. Thus, Mania is at hand. For the weed has corrupted the wheat itself. Just as we do not touch a dish full of roses and lilies with bare hands if we see even a single bunch of nettles mixed in—because the nettles sting the roses, the lilies, and the hands—so too do the weeds "sting" the reason and cast it down from its true nature. If nettles grow among roses—that is, if wildness grows within reason—then reason becomes inflamed with rage; it becomes like the thorns of the roses, which no one touches, and such a raving reason serves no one, but stings and strikes anyone who seeks to use or enjoy it.

<margin>Lack of moderation breaks all things.</margin>
<margin>The duty of the eye is to see what is appropriate.</margin>
In a natural sense, Mania happens in this way: any thing, if stretched beyond its strength and nature, is broken. Thus, the sight of the eye perishes if directed at the Sun. For every limb has its own destined goal and assigned duty, which cannot be overstepped without damage. Thus, the office of the eye is to see what it can, not what it is unable to reach. Just as the eye is blinded by the splendor of the Sun (which is itself an eye), so too is reason perverted by those things that stand in relation to it as the Sun does to the eye. Since every person has their own defined and ordinary calling, they have also received a measure of reason necessary for its worthy administration. To speculate more deeply than human capacity allows is to break and cast down reason itself. Just as one man receives more strength and vigor than another and has heavier tasks to manage, so is more commanded of one man's reason than another's. Therefore, everyone must know and understand their own limit, and the mind must not be burdened with more or loftier things, lest our reason act against itself, just as our eyes act against the "eyes of heaven" <note>the Sun and stars</note>. But let this suffice regarding reason that is too intensely strained and puffed up.

<margin>To each their own measure of reason.</margin>
<margin>What Elemental Mania is.</margin>
Furthermore, there is another kind of Mania which proceeds from the Elements and shatters our reason, not unlike how you see fire seething and raging in the Element of water, throwing out bubbles, foam, and vapor through its violent boiling. For our reason is a kind of liquid, and thus it is the Element in which fire exercises its power. By what, then, is this element broken? Truly, by Fire alone. If, therefore, that which breaks is fire, then that which is broken must be water. Thus the "body" of our reason is an evaporating water, <margin>What the evaporating Reason is.</margin> whose highest subtlety is a boiling dew. Therefore, when fire is added, operations occur such as those from fire and water. And this boiling is the "dove" <note>original: "columba"; in Paracelsian alchemy, this refers to the spirituous vapor rising during distillation</note> of those who lose their reason or are not in control of it; but the "dove" is the one in control of reason, just as water that boils is no longer under its own power, but under the power of the fire. The supreme art of the Physician, therefore, is to know how to extinguish the fire; once it is extinguished, the boiling itself—the disease—ceases.

<margin>The sky is the unique cause of Mania.</margin>
Many differing opinions arise regarding these people, as if there were not one single cause for this evil, but many, since their behaviors are noted to be quite diverse: one displays sorrow, another hilarity, a third anger, and a fourth something else. Yet there is a single elemental cause for all of them. Understand it thus: <margin>Humors are not the causes of Mania.</margin> there is no nature in man because of which it could be said that this person is Melancholic, that one Choleric, this one Sanguine, or that one Phlegmatic <note>A critique of the traditional "Four Humors" theory of Galenic medicine</note>. For a person does not have such things within themselves. However, it is true and can be said that a person has this "inner sky," this kind of influence, such a constellation or conjunction, and similar things dictated by this Astronomy <note>Paracelsus believed the human body operated like a small universe, or Microcosm, governed by internal "planets"</note>. From these, a person is now joyful, now fickle, and unlike themselves. For the sky contains such things in itself, not as a "nature" like phlegm or bile. The matter is not the same. And the fact that wine may pour joy into a man at one time and sorrow at another comes entirely from the motion and condition of the "inner sky," not from the nature of the Microcosm <note>the human body</note>. Therefore, such people exhibit various behaviors because their internal "sky" is in a state of flux. They mirror this movement, not their own nature. But what Physician can speak or argue about these things if he does not know the sky itself? Thus the Humorists <note>traditional doctors who focused on balancing bodily fluids</note> remain stuck in the shallows.

# ON MANIA.

<margin>What kind of physician there ought to be.</margin>
Beyond these two previously mentioned causes of Mania—namely, an excessive confidence in one's own strength or power, and the operation of the elements—many more causes of Mania could indeed be added and enumerated by others. However, these can find no weight or place either in Philosophy or in <term>Astronomy; used here to mean the study of celestial influences on human health</term> itself, upon which <term>Physics; the study of nature and the physical body</term> is founded. For he alone is a true Physician who earns the praise of being a consummate Astronomer and an accurate Philosopher. The trifles of others are left behind and crushed in the mud. Meanwhile, I shall nevertheless explain one further kind of Mania, which arises from the foods we are given. For just as there are things given to us that make us laugh, grieve, grow angry, or rejoice, so too there exist certain things which, when stirred up, drive out the power of <margin>How wine changes the human mind.</margin> reason. If it is in the nature of wine to entirely change the man who drinks it, and to alter his mind in a wondrous way, exalting it to the highest degree and, as it were, alienating it from itself; so too there will be certain things that exalt a man’s wisdom to such an extent that the brain, on account of that high degree of "sublimity," is corrupted and rendered foolish. For just as a drunkard pours out whatever he knows in a disorganized fashion, so too if a mastery over reason is forced upon it through food and drink, the exact same thing happens as we just said happens with wine. The one who uses this food suffers the same as he who drinks wine and becomes intoxicated. The nature of wine is well enough known to you. Regarding the food, however, which throws the brain into chronic or acute Mania, the cause must next be given, and the secret of nature itself must be brought forth. Although there is no shortage of those who deny that these things can be explained, those who say such things are plainly ignorant of the secrets within objects. For **Lupine seeds** inflict insanity; **Zecharia** <note>original: "Zecharia," possibly referring to a specific herbal preparation or a type of darnel/rye</note> brings about Mania; **Ruffeoli** <note>Likely a reference to a specific plant or compound in the Paracelsian pharmacopeia</note> causes madness; and **Hybellū** <note>Possibly a variant of Hyoscyamus or Henbane</note> generates furies. All these things cast a man down from reason so thoroughly that he does not even know himself; and they do this not by the power of sorcery, nor superstition, nor evil spirits, but out of their own most inward and proper nature, condition, and virtue. The comparison to wine declares this to be so. And even if the wine eventually expels itself <note>i.e., the person sobers up</note>, in many cases this will not happen with these foods; instead, for the most part, people will fall into chronic suffering. However, it is better to be silent and not to publish these things by revealing them. For many causes exist—hardly to be narrated here—regarding what the "secret" of **Hemlock** or similar things might be. But the cause of its specific property, and why it produces insanity, I shall explain to you without difficulty. Although wine indicates many such things, it is better that the <margin>Hemlock is harmful to reason.</margin> reason be added, especially for the sake of the <margin>The pungency of pepper or ginger harms the brain.</margin> cure that follows.

<margin>The brain is intolerant of pain.</margin>
Just as there lies in wine a certain perverse spirit, harmful and hostile to reason, so likewise it must be recognized that in **Hemlock** there is also a hidden spirit, whose virtue and property are no different than **pepper** or **ginger**. If that <term>pungency; original: "ponticitas," referring to a sharp, astringent, or biting quality</term> and bitterness reaches the brain, it becomes insane and furious. For the brain cannot bear that which exists as diverse and foreign to its own nature. Therefore, whatever possesses this "pungency" in its spirit destroys and shatters the brain. However, that which is merely "bodily" in itself does not destroy it, such as ginger and pepper <note>The author distinguishes between the physical spice, which burns the mouth, and the "volatile spirit" of a plant like hemlock, which attacks the mind</note>. Only those things in which the pungency is "airy" <note>volatile or spiritual</note> have the power to incite Mania. So also, <margin>Acidic spirits cause pain in other limbs, but Mania in the brain.</margin> as you see, everything that makes a thing dry, or intends to parch it, moves a person to great pain; so likewise you ought to know that there are some "little brains" <note>original: "cerebella," perhaps referring to the subtle structures of the mind</note> which, in their spirit, burn the brain with a parching dryness. These men are shaken and become Maniacs because the brain cannot endure the pain within it. Therefore you ought to know that Mania is in the brain, and it penetrates the two membranes <note>The meninges: the dura mater and pia mater</note> of the brain. On account of this, they are "spirits." Of these, there are many that only ascend into the brain and weaken and dissolve it, as we have said. To this it must also be known that every disease of the body—whether it be **gout**, **the falling sickness** <note>epilepsy</note>, or **colic**, which are themselves diseases of the spirit—contains within itself this kind of pungency and acidity. Just as it produces diseases in other places, so it does similarly in these. And these paroxysms are paroxysms of Mania, which in other limbs of the body cause only pain, but in the brain they inflict and incite Mania.

Just as spirits of this kind lie hidden in edible things, such as herbs, brains <note>perhaps referring to animal brains used in medicine</note> and other similar things, and bring Mania upon a man; so similar spirits arise in other human diseases. These, striking against the brain, shake and weaken it, and cast it into Mania. When it is disposed in this way, it begins to be subjected to the **Moon** and the **lunar stars**, and finally the heavens draw various things from it according to its nature and condition. This variety and difference does not prove another cause or material, as we have said. This diversity belongs to the **Medical-Astronomers** <note>Physicians who use astrology to diagnose and treat</note> to examine more accurately. Sometimes men are also tested by a similar <margin>Mania from the incitement of the soul.</margin> Mania when they are oppressed by the power of conscience, or who are occupied in a "deeper spirit" (as they call it), or who strike themselves into despair, and others who are similar. For these also, by that very incitement, drive their own brain into Mania. Yet the cause of these is more hidden and obscure, such that a Medical-Astronomer cannot so readily distinguish whether it depends on a foreign spirit or on nature itself. This, however, is more certain than certainty: the Mania of those who strain the subtlety of their own intellect beyond the measure of nature is entirely stirred up from spirits through **fantasies** and deeper meditations lured into the brain, not unlike a dog is lured by the scent of meat. Once those thoughts are introduced into the brain, nature can least of all endure them, just as the eye cannot endure <margin>Visionaries speaking from the spirit.</margin> the Sun, but is blinded by it. For it is certain and true that visionaries <note>original: "phantastæ"</note> of this sort speak through the spirit, not from the man; yet these are not possessed by a malignant spirit. I shall defer the explanation of the cause to the chapter on obsession by greater spirits. The cure for these people is therefore ambiguous. Just as the visionary spirits dwell within them, so must one proceed in the cure. Meanwhile, just as nothing can be achieved toward wisdom with fools, so too nothing—or at least very little—is usually attempted toward health with these "spiritual" men.

### THE PROCESS.
The beginning and manner of this Mania, which arises from a reason that is too intensely strained and burdened, is as follows: namely, these men devote their labor to all manner of foreign speculations,

<margin>What are Myrmidons?</margin>
...and they strive to subjugate or subject all things to their own brain. Such speculations, heaped and collected together in the head, are rightly called **Myrmidons** <note>original: "Myrmidones". In Greek myth, these were "ant-people," but Paracelsus uses the term to describe a swarming, restless multitude of thoughts.</note>. While they are joined together in this way, a certain dissension arises among them, with one constantly rising up against another, and a kind of conflict is engaged: not unlike a crowd of men fighting in a mutual battle; or a dance, as if many people were leaping about; or like a gathering of mourners, as if many were speaking together of sad things—or whatever else of this kind may occur, according to what the rising heavens suggest or what the speculations themselves grasp. For if the heavens, through such "ascendants," invade the <term>phantastic; the faculty of imagination</term>, a fool is immediately prepared and disposed, who acts and breaks out according to how he has been invaded. All these things must be worked out in the brain, which lies beneath them as if defeated, while the **Myrmidons** stand out as victors, and thereafter they drive and push the imagination.

<margin>Maniacs do not feel pain.</margin>
But those who are "set on fire" by the element of fire have a healthy brain that is as moist as dew. Therefore, if that moisture is driven into a boiling state by the Element, reason evaporates and is crushed by the easy effervescence, just as if the head were being squeezed by violent hands. That humidity is nothing but water. While it boils, it acts upon the brain in the same way as a piece of meat placed in a pot. Now, this insanity and **Mania** is so constituted that the sick do not complain of pains. For the crushing of reason is more severe than the pains themselves. Thus, the sick feel pains very little, nor can they complain about them to others; instead, they endure a paroxysm—whether great or small, brief or long—according to the greater or lesser kindling of the fire-Element, or the specific nature of the constellation.

<margin>The spirit of "ponticity" is extremely subtle.</margin>
But those who are driven into Mania by <term>ponticity; <note>original: "ponticitate". A technical term for a sharp, sour, or astringent quality in a substance.</note></term>, etc., their insanity is swift and severe. For the "ponticity" in its spirit is so sharp that it is carried up from the stomach into the head, like a substance moving from a vial into an <term>alembic; a distillation apparatus</term>. It does not merely weaken the head itself, but penetrates the <term>meninges; the membranes enveloping the brain</term> at the same time. And while it seizes the brain, it is similar to the **spirit of wine** <note>alcohol</note>, which intoxicates. They differ only in this: that this spirit is of a different kind than wine. For it is as much superior to the spirit of wine as wine is superior to water—matters which we refer back to Philosophy.

<margin>Spirits may be attracted from more than 1000 miles away.</margin>
For those whose imagination dislocates the brain through faith, their spirits are the most subtle of all. Knowledge of these must be taken from the knowledge of those spirits that hunt the conscience. For they are like dogs that pursue a man. Therefore, while a man meditates on spiritual wisdoms and gapes at the kind of speculation that a spirit can have, then that imagination attracts a spirit from more than 1000 miles away, and unless he stops, it draws that spirit deep into himself. Thus, the spirit now enticed into the man speaks out of his body, according to that spirit's own wisdom, nature, and property, which does not belong to the man himself. And the same spirit, having entered the man, seizes his reason as a dog grips a piece of meat. Now it bites into your brain, and you cry out like a goat caught in the mouth of a wolf, and you bewail your misery. It is good, therefore, for everyone to remain in his own calling. For to take up and defend the callings of others is neither a result of your industry nor of divine grace, but of the impulse of those spirits, which nevertheless eventually bite you—that is, they make you **Maniacal**.

### THE COUNTER-ARGUMENTS.

<margin>An abscess is not the cause of Mania.</margin>
No counter-arguments can be raised here by anyone. For this Mania is too subtle for those who attempt to bring counter-arguments in this place. Even if they were to arm themselves in the same way I do, we would still only be in agreement. It is false that the cause of Mania is what the <term>Humorists; <note>physicians who follow the ancient Greek theory of the four humors (blood, phlegm, yellow bile, black bile)</note></term> claim. For it is ridiculous for them to propose an **abscess** <note>original: "Apostema". A swelling or collection of fluid.</note> as the thing that moves it. They have forgotten the properties of abscesses and the nature of those things which are in the head or the brain. Neither a hot nor a cold abscess is the cause in this case. Blood indeed maintains that process in its Element which we have described, and any smoke or vapor is elevated—which they indeed call an "abscess," but (by your leave) they have never seen it. And even if there were some distinct abscess with which Mania coincided, you should nevertheless be careful not to say that the abscess stirred it up. For the true cause has already been mentioned. Although it may also be true that if abscesses are born either internally or externally, they are born from the same causes from which Mania itself is generated in a natural way. But if Mania follows a formed abscess, judge it this way: that which produced the Mania also gave birth to the precursor abscess. The abscess itself does not bring on the Mania, but is produced equally by the same thing that induced the Mania. This being the case, what use are your trifles now about "red choler" and that ridiculous fantasy about the "cells of the brain"?

<margin>Reproof of the Physicians.</margin>
I believe indeed that your own brain is besieged by **Myrmidons**, while you treat matters that are outside your calling and profession. Whether Mania occurs in the head or elsewhere, whether it happens with sleeplessness or otherwise, it arises entirely from those things which are "above" the brain <note>referring to higher spiritual or elemental influences</note>. Whence they break it even by their own force. But they, besides these things, preach about many other things as well, claiming they inflict Mania. Yet they do not explain in what way they do it. I say nothing of the fact that they offer nothing regarding the other types of Mania. For unless they knew about **Humors** and **Abscesses**, they would have nothing at all to offer in the end. And so, they dispute about blind things with the blind. Furthermore, their theoretical cures correspond to this: they treat abscesses which do not have the force of a cause, and they cite humors which are not present. These and other similar things betray their pure and simple ignorance.

### THE SIGNS.

Those who suddenly degenerate from their nature, manner, and habit, and are changed according to the affections of the mind—you may say these people are falling into mania, especially if they are no longer in control of themselves and pursue men with envy and hatred, strike them, shout, rave, and do many insane things. But that man is also a **Maniac** who, silent and quiet, mutters and sits, yet wanders away from natural reason. And as for their manners and gestures...

## TREATMENT.

<margin>The secrets of Mania must be learned from the helpers of demons.</margin>
Whoever strives to treat this disease through experience should set aside syrups, purgatives, and all the diets prescribed by those traditional authors. Among these, their primary choices are Violets, Roses, Chamomile, Water-lilies, and similar things. This kind of "cure" is familiar to the "helpers of the devils," who pretend that a person is possessed by a Demon, even though they know full well it is otherwise. Meanwhile, they themselves employ other remedies to drive out the Mania, but they hunt for the praise of their craft by claiming they have cast out a demon, when they have merely cured Mania. With these deceits, they lure people in and set sail with their sacrifices <note>original: "sacrificiis suis velificantur". This likely refers to religious offerings or masses performed for a fee</note>, from which they snatch more profit than from Medicine. However, I set aside these "helpers of the devils" here: since our purpose is simply to restore those suffering from Mania to their reason through the method that experience in nature has taught and confirmed. Therefore, in these matters, anyone who affects some skill should learn from those conjurers—not how to drive away demons, but how to cure those with Mania using suitable **secrets** <note>original: "secretis". In this context, it refers to "Arcana" or specific chemical/alchemical preparations</note>.

<margin>Ossiach, a monastery in Carinthia.</margin>
In a certain monastery in Carinthia called **Ossiach** <note>original: "Ossia". Ossiach Abbey was known in the Middle Ages and Renaissance for its "St. Benedict’s Cup," used to treat madness</note>, they display relics with which they "expel Mania," that is, demons. But that is nothing but a remedy. And whatever is beneficial in this case is truly a "sacrament" <note>original: "sacramentum". The author suggests that if a physical object heals, its power is a natural gift from God, not a priestly miracle</note>. For it was not given by God [solely to them]. Therefore, we have said—not without merit—that they have turned their own symbols into Medicines. Thus they also bring help through Crystal. But I leave it to you to consider whether a Crystal is Saint Peter or Saint Nicholas. There are many such monasteries everywhere, whose priests and monks—helpers nonetheless—accomplish their works through Medicine. Indeed, if there were devils in Mania, they would certainly not flee at the words of such "fathers." And if their remedies were the actual bodies of saints, they would surely have flown out of their hands long ago. For Medicine was given to us for this reason: not so that our sins might make it void, but it was placed into the hands of both wicked and upright men alike. However, the power which they claim to possess requires an upright man, just as the Apostles declare.

<margin>Medicine is common to both the upright and the wicked.</margin>
The treatment, therefore, is such:
- Crystal.
- Cauteries <note>The use of heat or caustic substances to sear tissue</note>.
- Actual fires <note>original: "Actualia". Likely referring to "actual cautery" using hot irons</note>.

# ON WORMS.

Although there are many kinds of worms, their names are by no means to be considered here: for it is enough that all of them, universally, are understood under one name. In this respect, there will be only one cause, one Medicine, and one disease. Nor should the species of worms themselves be considered here, but only the cause. For a medicine is found from the cause, not the species. For the species comes from the subject. But the <term>Arcanum; the hidden healing essence</term> is not in the subject, but in the efficient cause, from which every denomination is also taken.

### WHAT IS IT?

If a person sees worms sliding out, or detects other signs and traces of them, it is already a certain indication that they have been generated. 

<margin>The presence of worms is either complete or incomplete.</margin>
For whatever signs appear in those who have worms: if those same signs appear in those who are not yet "wormy," you can nevertheless call both groups "wormy," as the same Medicine benefits both. Although those not yet full of worms might be judged to be jaundiced, dropsical, suffering from colic, or full of abscesses. This error comes from ignorance of a disease that is present, but not yet "perfectly" <note>meaning "fully developed"</note> present. Nevertheless, an incomplete disease must be held and treated entirely as a complete one.

## CAUSE.

<margin>Generation of worms from two things. Worms from seed.</margin>
The causes of the generation of worms are twofold. The first is seed <note>original: "sperma". In this period, it refers generally to reproductive "seed" or biological essence</note>; the other is putrefaction. Regarding the seed, you shall understand it thus: that nothing arises within men from their own seed. Yet, worms are generated in women from it, if the seed turns to rot and is subjected to an "ascending" putrefaction. From this, various generations arise which you could not sufficiently marvel at. For that "heaven" <note>The internal environment of the body</note> has hatched worms, in which the broken seed underwent rot. For just as the "ascendant" of any putrefaction inclines, so does it dispose the worms. Therefore, the judgment of this generation is placed in the hands of the Astronomer, if he is also a Physician. Let these things be said concerning internal and innate seed. Furthermore, we must also speak of external seed and its generation, which (it is shameful to say) occurs from **Gomorrhean union** <note>original: "coniunctione Gomorrhinâ". A reference to "sodomy" or unnatural sexual acts, which Paracelsian theory claimed could generate monsters or parasites</note>.

<margin>How Gomorrhean union generates worms.</margin>
For there is another generation of worms in the womb which the "heavens" themselves do not cause, but the union does. From this, such and such offspring are born, sometimes resembling beasts, sometimes humans resembling beasts, etc. The cause of these is Gomorrhean unions, which everyone should weigh deeply within themselves. For it is absurd to say that the heavens, by themselves, without the seed and matter of such forms, could produce forms of this kind. Therefore, judge and estimate the matter according to this. Nevertheless, we do not deny that it can sometimes happen that such "Gomorrhean" seed might secretly creep into a woman’s places, whereby such things are engendered even without their knowledge. Even if this happens rarely, history teaches that it has occurred, and reason confirms it can still happen.

<margin>Worms arise because seed is ingested.</margin>
In the same way, a worm can slip into the ear or mouth and be enclosed there. If it emits its seed there, a monster is produced from it, because the seed was not placed in its natural vessel. For whatever is not enclosed in its native vessel, from that monsters are generated.

<margin>How monsters are born.</margin>
By similar reasoning, if the seed of insects is left in salads or cooked herbs through the negligence of cooks and is eaten: then, unless the stomach is strong enough to expel it, a worm or a complete monster is born from it. Seeds are hatched by the heat of the body and reach their end. Sometimes such seeds are also drunk with water, and monsters eventually emerge in the body; when they are finally ejected, they resemble external insects. Sometimes they even harm men with their poison, so that they become discolored and swell up, no differently than if they had swallowed the poison of those very worms. From these signs, the evil that was done finally becomes clear. In this way, the seed of fish is also frequently ingested. Unless it were mastered by the stomach, something of the sort...

# ON WORMS.

<margin>Worms from tender flesh.</margin>
Something is born in the body just as it is outside the body from putrefied fish, which degenerates into worms. In the same way, flesh that is too tender or young, and still <term>spermatic; in a raw, seed-like state</term>, generates such a thing as would otherwise be produced by rotting. For whatever happens outside is also produced inside the body through the operation of the stars. Unless our food and nourishment are sufficiently mature and clean, they are entirely subject to this generation. From this, various diseases sometimes follow; not only do worms emerge from them, but also "half-generations," which are often (though erroneously) called fevers, yet they are subject to and yield to the cures for worms. But enough has been said about those things which, being too "spermatic," are consumed prematurely and produce strange generations. Nature itself makes the rest clearer, which I leave for the more experienced to contemplate.

<margin>The heavens as a cause of worms.</margin>
Furthermore, regarding putrefaction, which is the second cause, understand the matter thus: the heavens are the cause of this generation in the following way. Any putrefaction remains putrefaction by itself, and passes away as rot; however, only the heavens lead it into the generation of worms. Although it is commonly (albeit wrongly) said that any rot is the beginning of worms, you should add: *if the heavens so ordain.* For the heavens must be entirely considered here if we are to describe the origin of worms—specifically those which are not generated from natural seed and the accustomed order of nature. For no rot will give rise to worms unless <term>sperma; a generative formative substance</term> is present separately, and the heat is tempered for their generation. It is indeed true that whatever is to turn into worms through rotting requires putrefaction caused by a great and immoderate heat. For any heat exceeding its proper degree stirs up rot in those things whose own temperature is immoderate. All things should be judged and understood according to this example. Indeed, you see that all cheeses become full of little worms under hot stars in the months of August and July, etc., which happens very little at other times of the year. The cause of this is the heavens, which produce those things by their movement. If, therefore, the heavens operate in cheese in this way, they will also operate in the matter enclosed within the <term>Microcosm; the "lesser world," referring to the human body as a reflection of the universe</term>, which, like cheese, lies subject to the operation of the heavens.

<margin>How putrefaction becomes the origin of worms.</margin>
<margin>Heat exceeding its degree is the cause of rot and worms.</margin>
<margin>Life presupposes the heavens.</margin>

More is explained by the Astronomers. Since there are many "ascendants," it follows that many strange worms emerge—common ones, well-known ones, unheard-of ones, daily ones, and so on. Of all these, the heavens are the efficient cause, which operates in the internal world just as in the external world, though in different ways according to the diversity provided by the body. For the sole foundation of this generation is that there are such "constellations" within the Microcosm as well.

<margin>Whence the variety of worms?</margin>
<margin>August and July are causes of worms.</margin>
If, therefore, August and July are hotter, and the matter and subject which may catch fire is present, you can certainly predict that this man can by no means avoid the generation of worms, any more than cheese and similar things can.

<margin>Worms from medicines.</margin>
There are also many generations of this kind from Medicines, from many of which worms are born, both in the body and in wounds—specifically if putrefactive and excessively hot medicines are applied to wounds, which are, as it were, suffocated by them, from which worms eventually come forth. And just as Philosophy gives reasons for these things, understand the same regarding the heavens. For the matter is one, and all are one heaven. However, the principle of this operation is that **salt** is separated from those things which are about to undergo putrefaction.

<margin>The separation of Salt as a cause of rot. Salt is the Balsam of life.</margin>
For Salt is the <term>Balsam; a preservative essence</term> of things to be kept in life. The Salt which the body has united and born within itself is the **Balsam** or **Mumia**. Now, external salt is similar to this. Just as this **Mumia** <note>original: "Mumia". In Paracelsian medicine, this refers to the vital, preservative spirit inherent in living bodies.</note> preserves the living, so salt preserves the dead. But if the Mumia dies, then salt can no longer preserve that thing for long. If, therefore, it cannot preserve it any longer, it follows that the Salt and the Mumia depart.

<margin>Salt keeps rot away. Wormy foods are unhealthy.</margin>
Now, therefore, putrefaction begins; now worms arise. Hence, wormy foods are unhealthy because they lack Mumia and salt, which food ought to have in just accordance and measure. And for this reason, many things rot and turn into worms, both in wounds and internally in the body. Which medicines these are will be defined in their own chapters. Many things drive worms out of a person, even though medicines may have generated them. Therefore, let the matter rest upon your judgment and experience.

<margin>Bread and honey beget worms.</margin>
But the beginning of worms is also often from the composition of natural things. Thus, bread and honey beget worms. Such combinations are also within man himself. And for this reason, the microcosm must be considered, not the "humors" <note>This is a critique of traditional Galenic medicine, which blamed health on the balance of four fluids or humors.</note>. By the same reasoning, any **pus**, whether inside or outside the body, if seized by a putrefactive medicine, degenerates into worms. For there is much rot in the body, which otherwise exits in the form of pus, but which is turned into worms by unsuitable Medicines, just like bread and honey.

<margin>Worms from obstruction.</margin>
In the same way, worms are also generated from suffocation or confinement if an exit for air is not provided. But this happens very little unless the operation of the heavens concurs. Therefore, some worms emerge from obstruction. If this had not occurred, the operation of the heavens would have been in vain.

<margin>Worms from conjunctions.</margin>
Regarding "conjunctions," the matter is easy to understand. For the most common generation of worms is this: if food and a weak stomach coincide and are joined by nature so that the stomach becomes weaker from the heat of August or July, then worms are created. Similarly, if putrid food or putrid and febrile dispositions lurk in the stomach, and the heavens are similarly disposed, worms are also produced. Again, if the heavens are so "exalted" and putrid drink is swallowed, and a disease of <term>dysentery; a severe intestinal infection causing bloody diarrhea</term> has occupied the body, then once more the generation of worms is completed. In the same way, if wounds lurk internally and drink or "milk-bearing" herbs are consumed, the heavens again fulfill their intention. So too with external wounds...

When medicines that encourage putrefaction are applied for three days, that which we have described occurs. The summary concerning worms is therefore this: it requires matter and some specific subject, which is then prepared for the generation of worms by the course of the heavens—which is an excessive heat.

<margin>The heavens as the most skilled shaper.</margin>
## THE PROCESS.

Just as a sculptor fashions a serpent, or a founder casts one, through familiar art and industry: so these "artisans" <note>Referring to the biological forces within the body</note> do not possess that art from themselves, but from the heavens. If they have it from the heavens, then the heavens can also do the same, and indeed more skillfully than a man. If this is true, the heavens must be entirely a sculptor, a founder, and a goldsmith, because they shape such things most masterfully, and display their mastery most elegantly in dung and mud. For who else could draw something of value out of those putrid and useless things?

<margin>The heavens are the father of artisans.</margin>
A man who intends to engrave something requires the finest metals and excellent wood. But the heavens—the parent of those very artisans—takes putrid things and yet constructs living images from them; whereas those things fashioned by men are merely wood, or metal, and colors, and by no means living. These other things, however, are alive. The heavens must therefore be regarded as a most skillful master of the hammer, who knows how to build in secret so that no one sees the worker until the final hand has been laid upon the work. It is a singular delight for the heavens to fashion from putrescence that which is pleasing. From this come the various species and kinds of worms, though these do not pertain to the <term>arcanum; the secret healing essence</term> itself.

<margin>Phlegm is not the cause of worms.</margin>
## CONTRARY VIEWS.

It could be objected here that moisture—specifically <term>phlegm</term>—exists as the mother and the matter of worms. We, however, say the opposite: no phlegm putrefies, and yet putrefaction is necessary for this work. Therefore, that opinion is false. Furthermore, no worm is generated from any physical body unless a physical <term>sperma; generative seed or vital principle</term> is present. For it does not attain life except from matter that has been properly prepared.

<margin>How do worms come from dung?</margin>
Worms are born from dung precisely because dung is not without this seed. And this seed is not only from oil, but is also located in other parts of the body. It is not that the seed of generation is found in man alone, but also in others, from which this or that is produced.

<margin>Beetles from horse dung.</margin>
Horse dung produces beetles: this cannot happen without seed. Yet, it is not the seed of horses, even though it came out of the horse. It befits a physician to know the nature of seeds intimately if he wishes to be considered skilled in this generation. And although there are certainly some foods that breed worms and become their matter without having their own seed, nevertheless that generation by no means happens without seed; rather, it occurs entirely through a seed that, lying hidden in the herbs, subsequently bursts forth into generation.

<margin>No generation without seed.</margin>
Such things never happen without seed. Regarding this seed, there has been a deep silence among both philosophers and physicians until now. However, the <term>astronomer</term> knows what this seed is, for the heavens impart this knowledge to him. Thus, he cries out against <term>Hyle; primordial matter</term> <note>original: "Hylum"</note>, whoever disputes about phlegm and idly declares its nature, or stirs up anxious debate about other similar things.

<margin>Are worms present when symptoms are shown?</margin>
## SIGNS.

The signs of worms are twofold: manifest and occult. Manifest signs are taken from those worms that emerge. Occult signs are not as clear; however, they have been sufficiently handed down and described by others. Many signs were faithfully observed and handed down by the ancients, which we will not discuss at length; instead, we will call the reader back to the foundations themselves. Yet it frequently happens that one cannot sufficiently discern from the signs whether worms are present or not. Thus, certain signs of worms sometimes appear in the intestines when no worms are actually there, which we experience most often in women.

<margin>Gerolea, etc.</margin>
However, you shall investigate the truth itself in this way: Apply <term>Gerolea</term> <note>likely Sanicle or a similar healing herb</note>, or <term>Hypericon</term> <note>St. John's Wort</note>, or finally <term>Centaurea</term> <note>Centaury</note> to the area showing signs. If the symptoms submit to the herbs and do not remain, know undoubtedly that there are worms. Furthermore, if signs of worms occasionally show themselves but the worms are not actually present, let this not trouble you. For if you have properly observed signs of this kind, you should nonetheless proceed with the <term>arcana</term> against worms. For that which removes the worms also removes their nourishment, their nest, and their matter, and the heavens drive away the "seed" of those things, so that the heat of August, the Dog Days, and other similar rising constellations cannot break out into an affliction.

<margin>Where are the locations of worms?</margin>
## EXPLANATION.

At this point, it is right to explain, among other things, the locations of the worms in which they are generated. The locations are wherever the <term>spirit of salt</term> <note>In Paracelsian chemistry, the preservative force that prevents decay</note> is not acidic. Thus, in the eyes, the spirit is sharp.

<margin>Why eyes are not wormy. 1. Ears.</margin>
For the eyes require more <term>Balsam</term> <note>A natural preservative fluid in the body</note> than other members, so that they may be preserved from accidents of this kind. In the ears, however, although salt is indeed purged out, the regions of the ears are nonetheless locations for worms, even though they are very bitter. For bitterness does not hinder the operation of the heavens. If the heavens find the matter, they perform their office, neglecting the other factor.

<margin>2. Teeth. The tooth-worm is the worst.</margin>
The teeth have the most subtle spirit of salt of all. Therefore, a worm is born from it, and it is the worst kind. For its nature is subtle, and it arises from subtle matter. For the sharpness and malice of all worms comes from that spirit of salt.

<margin>3. Stomach. Intestines. 4. Newly formed locations.</margin>
But the stomach itself also provides a place for generating worms; and the intestines provide three. So too do other regions neighboring these. But if a dissolution <note>breakdown of tissue or humors</note> should occur in some other place, a location for worms would be created there where none had been before. Therefore, there are not only destined places for worms, but new ones are created from time to time. For many diseases befall the body, such as Dysentery, Diarrhea, <term>Hemoptysis</term> <note>coughing up blood</note>, Rheum, etc., all of which contribute something to the generation of worms. By the occasion of these diseases, new locations can easily be built and prepared for generating worms—always provided, however, that the heat of the Dog Days and the fervor of July or August prepares them, if joined with the matter and the subject. That heat moves through the matter in various ways, both backward and erratically. For the body is fragile; whence it is forced to endure those courses to which it is subject, even outside their normal order.

## THE CURE.

The cure is twofold: namely, from the "first seed" and from the "second seed." It comes from the specific form; from the smoke of <term>Hyoscyamus</term> <note>Henbane</note>—that is, of Mercury—likewise of Sulfur, and likewise of Salt. Also Hypericon, and Centaurea. Likewise from other similar things. Also note this in children; and note this in pregnant women, lest they conceive [worms], etc.

# ON DIARRHEA.

**D**iarrheas exist in many forms, some Natural and others Unnatural. The Unnatural (which can be healthy) are stirred up either by medicine or by Nature. Many are also provoked by the loosening of nature's own forces, or through the "medicine" of food, or by the season and similar factors. However the diarrhea may happen, there exists both a single disease and a single cause, to which a specific <term>arcanum<note>A "secret" or "essential" remedy in Paracelsian medicine that targets the root cause of a disease rather than just the symptoms.</note></term> must be applied.

### WHAT IS IT?

It is known to every person by their own experience what the mode and pattern of their own nature is in expelling the filth that is produced within a human. Aside from that usual habit, whatever else occurs—whether it be a suppression, an immoderate flow, or some other perversion—know that this disease is Diarrhea. Now, nature has only one familiar way of expelling, and it expels only one thing: the remnants and feces of food. Since the nature of man is fragile and fleeting, that same power does not remain constant, but is very often weakened and changed, now by internal causes, now by external ones, whereby the mode and order of nature are subverted. For in all of nature there is a fixed temperament <note>The balanced proportion of qualities or "humors" in the body.</note>: any excess or defect in this is considered a vice and held to be a disease, which can turn out to be either chronic or acute, and both can end in death.

### CAUSE.

<margin>Expulsion comes from the power of the dung, not the intestines.</margin>
Every diarrhea arises from the stomach and happens through the fault of the stomach. For according as that which is taken in is altered and arranged in the stomach, its expulsive force also exerts itself. For that power is not placed in the nature of the human being himself, but in the <term>dung<note>In this context, the author argues that waste products have an inherent "life" or drive to exit the body, independent of the body's muscular effort.</note></term> which the stomach has produced. For one thing is deposited more quickly or slowly than another, according to the mode of its own nature. The logic of feces is similar to a dog, or any other animal, which exits a stable of its own accord and is not "expelled" by the stable. Thus the dung leads itself out without any added help or aid from nature and the body. However, time also works in a similar way to produce this power—just like a pear, which falls by itself and is not shaken from the tree, but frees itself by an internal motion.

<margin>What is dung?</margin>
Furthermore, dung that withdraws in this manner is nothing other than the "food of the stomach." For nothing can become dung that was not previously food in the stomach. Finally, that becomes dung which had previously existed in the stomach as food. Therefore, we must first discuss the food of the stomach so that the dung, which is later called a disease, may be more certainly understood. The reasoning is as follows.

<margin>Pregnant women devour absurd things.</margin>
You know it happens that pregnant women affected by <term>pica<note>A craving for non-food substances like clay or ash.</note></term> eat and ingest now coals, now clay, now ash, now chalk, and various other absurd things. Now, this is an appetite; it is not a "need." Need seeks only familiar and natural foods. This appetite, however, is immoderate, without use or necessity. And yet, whatever is eaten in this instance becomes food through that appetite. There are many such appetites also in the stomach, from which "preternatural" <note>Beyond the normal course of nature.</note> foods are ingested, which the stomach takes in. Though the human himself also very often, even when such an appetite is not pressing, loads and burdens himself with such foods by a deliberate choice. The same must be concluded regarding this cause.

I am certain that a specific and defined food—and one not yet changed—must be offered to the stomach. And the sum of the medical art is placed in this: that suitable foods be administered to the belly; a matter which has been neglected and omitted by the ancient writers. If this mode and order are not preserved, an operation of the belly follows that is different from what it ought to be, from which the origin of diseases is given. The same must be judged similarly regarding those foods which are swallowed at a person's whim. For the logic of the stools corresponds to the condition of these foods. Now, as has been said, any dung was once food, and proceeds from food which is ingested on the one hand; on the other hand, the stomach takes it in without ingestion. However these things may be, we must discuss the giving and taking of food, as health and sickness seem to be placed within them. Before that is performed, the stomach must first be understood in its taking or "appetite" for its food.

<margin>The foods of the stomach are twofold: Ingested and not ingested.</margin>
<margin>What is hunger?</margin>
Hunger is the appetite for taking in and feeding. These two give birth to the disease of Diarrhea. Regarding what is taken in, know that the stomach contains within itself the power and nature of separating the evil from the good. Now, that which is good brings no harm, but that which is evil does. And to this are referred the various poisons: laxatives, cold, hot, moist, and dry things, likewise styptics <note>Substances that contract tissues or stop bleeding.</note>, diaphoretics <note>Substances that induce sweating.</note>, and other similar things. For there is no food that does not have poison, and is not of a laxative or "elementary" nature. Therefore, the office of the stomach is to separate these things, drive them into dung, and expel them.

<margin>The power of separating in the stomach is remarkable.</margin>
<margin>No food lacks poison.</margin>
<margin>Separation belongs to the stomach; expulsion to the dung.</margin>
The power of expulsion consists in the very act of purging these things. If, however, it happens that the stomach tries to digest more than it was commanded to do by the process of separation—that is, if for the sake of "pleasure" or "delight of the mind" (as they say) it begins to digest the dung—then by that very effort it catches the poison, the laxatives, or the <term>element<note>The raw, non-nutritive components of matter.</note></term> itself which had been separated from the food. From this, then, Diarrhea arises; it is a sign that the stomach is digesting that which it ought not to digest, which causes that "flux."

<margin>How and when does Diarrhea occur?</margin>
This "digestion" is similar to the eating of laxatives or poisons. Therefore, two signs follow: swelling and pressure around the stomach, caused by the poison in the food; then an eruption made above and below, caused by the laxative power contained in the food. For the digestion ought not to have proceeded further; that is, the stomach ought not to have separated the poison, laxative, or element, but should have merely digested the food and left the rest. If it attempts separation even within the <term>Essences and Species<note>In Paracelsian thought, "Essence" refers to the spiritual/medicinal heart of a substance, and "Species" to its specific outward form.</note></term>, it then provides the cause of Diarrhea, according to how that separation is established.

Moreover, it very often also moves an appetite in itself for things which are not ingested; just as if it desired to eat that in which it lies, not unlike a horse that bites its own manger. It happens like this: it draws to itself the humors of its own body, which it "appetites" to eat. Now, by this appetite, it inflicts disease upon the body. For it withdraws from the body its own nourishment. And while it desires to absorb its own blood, it induces yet another disease. For the blood of the body ought not to be food, but an Element of the body, from which...

# ON DIARRHEA.

<margin>Where the variety of stools comes from</margin>
...by which it is sustained. Thus, the stomach often craves the fat of the intestines and all other things existing in the body, such as mucus and fluxes, which it draws to itself like a cupping glass <note>original: "cucurbitula" — a glass vessel used in medical cupping to draw blood or fluids to the surface.</note> draws blood. This is why the stools are sometimes of one kind, sometimes another, and sometimes bloody. Why is this? Because those stools were once blood, and that blood was the food and desire of the stomach. As the food is, so is its excretion. Thus, the excretions are sometimes watery, for the stomach has extracted fluids from the body. This results in the waste retaining the nature of that "food." Similarly, the waste is sometimes the color of clay, because the stomach has drawn the rheums <note>original: "rheumata" — harmful watery discharges or "waste" fluids from the tissues.</note> of the body and flesh into itself as food. Sometimes they are yellow, for it has drawn in bile, which stains them; and so on. Therefore, it is necessary to thoroughly understand the parts of the body—how they appear in their heightened states according to their substance, color, and other traits. One who understands this can judge from the dung what the patient's stomach has "eaten."

<margin>The stomach is like an adulterer.</margin>
Furthermore, it is notable that when such a "stomach-appetite" persists, proper digestion never occurs. For the stomach does not act according to its duty; instead, it wanders and indulges its own desires. In this, it is no different from an adulterer who, while supporting his wife at home, nevertheless chases after a stranger, even though the general matter and reason are the same. In this way, the stomach also wanders and deserts its station. Its own diseases follow this straying. All medicine, therefore, is focused on this: that this appetite be removed and put to sleep. That is, in one way, the appetite for separating the dung into its various types and parts must be taken away; in another, care must be taken that the stomach does not desire to "eat" its own body. Whoever removes this appetite has removed all excessive flows and has properly united nature with the stomach. The constant cause of Diarrhea remains this: that everything a human eats and takes in as food contains within it poison, a laxative, and an "element." <note>In the chemistry of this era, "elements" were the basic building blocks of matter that the body had to extract or "separate" from raw food.</note> However, the stomach has been given the power to separate these things from food and to emit the poison, laxative, and elements out of the body without harm. But if the stomach is seized by the "pleasure" of separation—as if it desires to know what is at hand and to separate each thing individually—then, through that excessive separation, it provides the cause and occasion for Diarrhea. Likewise, for another reason, when it is provoked by the desire to eat its own body, it stirs up diseases in many ways. Therefore, a physician must very carefully and diligently consider the excretions, from which the condition of the stomach is best known. For there is no excretion that does not betray the action and appetite of the stomach.

<margin>Excretions indicate the condition of the stomach.</margin>
Although the stomach can sometimes be led to cause diarrhea by other diseases—not out of its own playfulness, but from the force of another inciting illness—no diarrhea can occur without the stomach's consent. For there are many sufferings everywhere that may drive it and cast it into such an appetite. To understand this, know that the stomach is like a clever and industrious craftsman who strives to express and imitate whatever comes his way or is offered to him, in one way or another. For if unusual, adverse, or inciting things are offered to the stomach, it attempts in many ways to figure out what should be made or fabricated from them. Through these various attempts, various stools are produced. If someone suffers from a fever or jaundice, a portion of these is also offered to the stomach to be "eaten." While the stomach exercises its mastery over these, it applies itself in various ways. It either devours and feeds on it all, or if it does less, it is offended and, as it were, stained. Thus, many things from diseases come to the stomach to be eaten. But when it lacks the appetite to consume everything, certain parts are sometimes left behind, and another disease remains.

<margin>Nature tries to conquer all diseases in the stomach.</margin>
Nature strives to overcome and defeat all diseases that afflict a human within the stomach. You will recognize such stomach-affairs from a single concurring disease. If these are led out, the stomach is well. But if a primary disease were not present, the stomach alone would be at fault; and then the matter stands as we have said.

Since the stomach separates species so miraculously, it produces such varied stools, not all of which can be listed individually. But in general, they are poisonous, laxative, elemental, or stirred up by previous diseases. Therefore, the names of the stools are of very little importance in distinguishing one from another or assigning specific names to each species. For who could track down every species, such as Lientery <note>A form of diarrhea where food passes through the body undigested.</note>, Diarrhea, Dysentery, and so on? One cannot even encompass them through a single cure. For the cure of the stomach is unique: that these types of appetites and "craftsman-like" attempts, by which it brings on Diarrhea, be removed. But Diarrheas are also frequently caused by foods, as has been said, which are not suited to its nature or habit. In this case, they usually last until the stomach learns through many trials by what arts those foods must be handled. For a similar thing happens in infants. Even though they have a stomach, it is not yet fit for taming foods. Therefore, it produces no true excrement. But once it has learned the art of separation through frequent trial and experience, what is taken in no longer causes harm. 

<margin>Habit should not be easily changed.</margin>
Therefore, it is not at all safe to change one's habits. For there are many things that bring a "new discipline" of digestion to the stomach, which are usually not without danger. Thus, fruit, milk, cherries, etc., move the bowels because the stomach is unaccustomed to them and has not yet learned their proper separation. Until it becomes firmly accustomed to them, the Diarrhea does not cease. Just as there is no craftsman who has not learned his art from the first rudiments and principles, so the stomach is constituted to know all the arts of "eating" even poisons and other things, and it applies these to the digestion of food. But it is led to this habit with greater difficulty and only assumes this character through many attempts. From this, you Humorists <note>original: "Humoristæ" — a mocking term for traditional doctors who relied on the ancient theory of the four humors rather than chemical or "alchemical" medicine.</note> should finally learn.

Any sculptor has his tools with him, and in his brain the idea of the image he wishes to carve. That is, the art of carving the image...

### OPPOSING ARGUMENTS.

<margin>Rawness is no longer the cause of diarrhea.</margin>
Some might object that this flow arises from undigested matter <note>original: "cruditatibus" — literally "raw" or "unripe" matter, referring to food that has not been properly "cooked" by the stomach's heat.</note> passing through. But these people fail to notice that the excrement is not raw. Furthermore, raw things do not contain an expulsive force. Add to this that nothing is present from which the stomach can create such a substance and body unless it has first separated it. For Diarrhea occurs *from* the separation, not before it. There are also those who say that external cold or freezing air produces flows of this kind. Yet this can only happen in the way that water extinguishes fire. For by these things, the operations of the stomach are hindered, and yet they turn into dung or excrement, but with a change—just as a craftsman, for example a painter, who paints with bad pigments so that nothing attains its natural color. The Humorists <note>The "Humorists" refers to followers of the traditional Galenic medicine based on the four humors (blood, phlegm, black bile, yellow bile), whom the author is criticizing.</note> could therefore have brought much more against us. But since both the Microcosm <note>term: <term>Microcosm</term> refers to the human being viewed as a miniature reflection of the entire universe.</note> itself and nature are ignorant of those things they babble about, their objections should not be valued highly. For they have described the nature of the stomach very poorly, and its diseases much worse, and they prove by their own accepted views that they err miserably from beginning to end.

### SIGNS.

If you feel compressions, burning, or a craving <note>original: "orexen" — from the Greek for appetite or longing.</note> in the stomach, say that the stomach is suffering in its operation and is being too much refined by a poison. If it acts from above (vomiting), say that it has separated a "Helleboric" nature from the food and allowed this to take control. But if it excretes from below, say that it has pushed a "Laxative" downward. If colic and similar things arise, let them be judged by their own specific symptoms.

### CLARIFICATION.

The species of the "Three Primes" <note>The "Three Primes" (Tria Prima) are Salt, Sulfur, and Mercury—the basic components of all matter in Paracelsian theory.</note> are present in every single thing; through them, all categories are understood, yet they are so subtle in their quantity that it is impossible for them to be measured or seen. For example: <margin>Praise and composition of Roman cabbage.</margin> Roman cabbage <note>likely cauliflower or a specific variety of kale.</note> is the most noble of all edible herbs. But what is Roman cabbage according to its nature? It is surely a thing composed of all species of minerals, fruits, turpentine, and various "degrees." Within it is Arsenic, Mercury, Marcasite, Salt, Sulfur, and all species; in it is Colocynth, Scammony, Turbith, Hellebore, and all styptics and diaphoretics <note>terms: <term>styptics</term> stop bleeding; <term>diaphoretics</term> induce sweating.</note>, all flesh-making things, all cleansers, digestives, and so on. To put it briefly, all species of nature are within it; that is, all universal virtues are stored in this one herb. This is true not only of this herb, but similarly in all other things. This cabbage excels others because it is food; in it, that which is useless is commanded to be separated by the stomach, so that nature may be preserved from harm, just as it is right for a prince to protect his subjects. Therefore, the stomach handles its art so nobly, industriously, and subtly that by its power of separation, it extracts Hellebore so exquisitely that it could hardly be stored in an apothecary's shop without any contamination. <margin>The stomach's wondrous power.</margin> With the same skill, it also extracts Colocynth <note>a powerful purgative fruit.</note> and other similar things. Even if it is not specifically ordered to do so, the stomach cannot take a holiday from its mastery. Man is forced to endure this habit of the stomach, being subject to fragility. <margin>Colocynth from sugar and vice versa. Man is of a fragile lot.</margin> An artisan likewise knows how to extract Colocynth from sugar, and sugar from Colocynth. Could the stomach itself not do this more dexterously? While it performs these miraculous works, we must wait to see what good or what evil it produces. Through these things, God exhibits His miracles to us. Man must bear everything as it falls. For it is entirely his condition that, being frail, he inclines toward all things. Meanwhile, the stomach applies itself to its work, whether for good or for evil.

# ON GOUT.

<margin>Gout is synovia.</margin>
**M**any names are given to Gout <note>original: "Podagra" — traditionally referring to gout in the feet.</note>, yet they are not taken from the cause and nature of the disease itself, but from its location or seat. Therefore, it does not matter which name is used, for it only defines the affected place and provides no other knowledge. The true name of the disease is *synovia* <note>note: while modern "synovia" refers to joint fluid, the author uses it here as a specific name for the "flowing" essence of the disease.</note>. For this is taken from the cause of the disease.

### WHAT IS IT?

<margin>Who should be called gouty.</margin>
Whomever you hear feeling "flows" to the feet or hands, or the hip, or other joints—while the skin remains intact, but with pain, swelling, and spreading redness, along with loss of appetite and a changing state of the limbs—call that person "gouty." Even if the evil is not familiar to just one part but many parts at once, he is nonetheless the same.

->CAUSE<-

<margin>The ancients were ignorant of Philosophy and Astronomy.</margin>
To describe Gout <note>original: "Podagra" — traditionally referring to gout in the foot, but used here as a general term for arthritic pain.</note> briefly, there is a need for a more refined Philosophy and Astronomy than is required in any other disease. Since the Theoretical and Physical foundations of Medicine are established upon these, an error has been admitted until now due to this difficulty, which has meant that until this point no certain cure for gout could be indicated. For who among the ancients anywhere possessed such knowledge in Philosophy and Astronomy that they held even a slight grasp of the doctrine of crises? <note>A "crisis" in early medicine was the turning point of a disease, often thought to be governed by planetary movements.</note> First, therefore, attend to the Essence of Gout in this way. Every disease has its own place where it sits and dwells, as it were. According to this distinction, there is also a different judgment of diseases. For this one occupies the eyes, such as blindness; that one occupies the ears, such as deafness; this one besets the neck, as in quinsy <note>original: "squinantia" — a severe inflammation of the throat or tonsils.</note>; another afflicts the chest, like cancer; another the liver, another the lung, etc. In this way, Gout is a disease <margin>Synovia is the subject of gout.</margin> of the body, building its seat in the synovia <term>synovia</term> <note>While modernly the fluid in joints, here it refers to the specific humor or "glue" of the joints that Paracelsus believes becomes corrupted.</note>. Moreover, in whichever member the synovia is exalted <note>original: "exaltata" — in alchemy and Paracelsian medicine, to be "exalted" means to be raised to a higher state of intensity or activity.</note>, the Gout of that same member is also exalted: nor does Gout occupy any other place besides the synovia.

<margin>What is the material of Gout? A salt liquor.</margin>
Now, the disease is in itself a Liquid, whose nature is no different than a mineral salt or an acidic juice, just as these species are of the genus of salt: *Alums, Vitriols, Salts, Calcinated things, Alkalis*: or of the acidic things: *Vinegar, Berberis juice, Acacia*, and the like. If things of this kind are produced in the Microcosm <term>Microcosm</term> <note>The human being, viewed as a miniature reflection of the entire universe or Macrocosm.</note>, and strike into the Synovia (which is averse to such things): then, according as the nature of the salt exists as sharp, bitter, acidic, or Alkaline, so the synovia is affected, and conceives pain and disease. For there is no agreement between these two. But if they are joined and mixed anywhere, they exist according to how those Liquids and juices are graded or prepared. For some are as if distilled; some as if sublimated; some as if reverberated, or calcinated, or dissolved: or they fall as Liquids, coagulated, resolved, dried out, and whatever else is of this condition.

<margin>The two types of Gout:</margin>
However, the craftsman and preparer of all these is "the year." But what is the year? Summer and Winter, of course. And what are these in Physics? Surely this: Gout has two natures—Summer and Winter. That is, the property of summer is one genus of Gout: <margin>Summer or hot.</margin> while the nature of Winter is the other genus of Gout. Summer is hot, simultaneously humid and dry. Such also is its Gout. As the influence is, so also is the summer. For the days themselves are not "summer," but the sky is. For the sky, constituted in such a way at this time, is summer. Whence it happens that the gout itself is mixedly humid and dry, just as on certain summer days it sometimes rains, and then again heat and dryness fall. <margin>Winter or cold.</margin> By that alternation, the gout is also varied. Winter does the same. Not the days of winter are "winter," but the sky itself, having risen in such a way, will be considered Winter, which is humid and dry. In the same way also its Gout behaves, which is cold, now according to humidity and dryness, it is varied just like summer. Meanwhile, the condition of winter is different from summer. Thus summer also exists differently in its impressions. Therefore, you must work to be upright Astronomers. For thus you will be able to explain the paroxysm <note>A sudden attack or violent increase in symptoms.</note> of gout. The course of the sky is twofold: Winter <note>original: "Brumalis" — relating to the winter solstice.</note> and Summer. <margin>Twofold motion of gout.</margin> Gout also has similar courses. Sometimes, however, it happens that snowy or winter stars rise in summer. Whence during summer a copious snow falls, which in warm places falls in the form of water, and yet it is snow. If there be such a winter during summer: then the gout is winter-like in an opposite season. By equal reasoning, summer stars also frequently rise in winter, so that the summer days are felt to be quite hot. The same thing likewise happens in gout, so that in freezing weather hot paroxysms attack. By the same reasoning, colds sometimes also concur with heat, from the mixed paroxysms of those stars. For if a winter star falls in Summer, it brings on cold: that being digested again, the sun blazes. That is therefore the heat, rushing in after the winter star. Thus cold and heat follow one another in turn, one star rising immediately after another has set. And such is the nature and the mode of occurrence of gout, and of all its connected species.

Furthermore, the impressions of winter are of a peculiar nature: just as those of summer are also peculiar. Summer pours out humid rain and dries the same again. Thus its gout also pours out its liquid and absorbs the same again. Winter places its snow, emits its cold, etc., and coagulates, and leaves the coagulated behind. Its Gout does the same, which congeals its liquid, and from it produces grains and hailstones, <margin>Hailstones are not resolved.</margin> etc. Unless, however, summer follows and resolves the hailstones like snow: then the coagulation remains constantly persistent. But if by such an impression they are crystallized and become stony, they are never thereafter resolved. To this end, the sky brings forth summer, and adds its twofold impressions. For the sky is fervent, and yet it rains; that is, it moistens and cools. Let the Physician be so disposed to himself: for he removes and consumes his own rain. Whence it happens that those gouts remit, and the sick rise up vigorous. But here is another struggle. For winter, if it impresses and coagulates too much, does not recede again, and short summers follow, and the summer stars are not effective. To this gout happens the same thing as to mountains, which are perpetually covered with their own snow.

Only the Astronomer has known the Nature and condition of these diseases and paroxysms. For he who has thoroughly known the sky of Summer, and its stars, and their nature: who has a clear view of the sky of winter, and the force of its stars, and their condition: he can now certainly indicate that such and such a person is gouty, and that such will be his paroxysms, etc. For here the cause of the matter is none other than that there are <margin>They relate to acidic winter and salty summer.</margin> acidic Winters, and the genera of acidic things are species of winter stars: and that salts are summer, and the genera of these are summer stars. Thus, it is surely worthy that Philosophy flows from Astronomy, and both flow together into one. For things...
