# ON GOUT.

<margin>The star Nitiala.</margin>
The subjects of Philosophy and the matters handled by the Astronomer must entirely correspond with one another, just as the salt of vitriol <note>original: "sal vitrioli" — iron(II) sulfate, often used in alchemy and early medicine.</note> corresponds to the star Nitiala <note>A specific star or celestial influence in Paracelsian cosmology.</note>. The same logic applies to all other things. For the very influence that, drawn from the heavens, created salts and minerals in the earth, produces the same things within the Microcosm <term>Microcosm: the "world in miniature," referring to the human body reflecting the universe.</term>. For this Microcosm is itself a world. Within it, the internal heaven must generate everything that the outer world contains. Whichever of these elements predominates and is "exalted" <note>In alchemy, to "exalt" a substance is to raise it to its highest power or most active state.</note> becomes a disease. And just as it is often said that the heaven produced much metal in this place, or many stones in that one, so it is also permitted to say <margin>the heaven produces all things.</margin> that the internal heaven has generated salts here, or acids there, which take command in the hands and feet—much like metals dominate in Saxony and Meissen, or wine in Alsace and Franconia.

<margin>A double heaven: superior and inferior.</margin>
This Philosophy is constant and perpetual in all things: that two heavens exist, the superior and the inferior. Wondrous is the superior heaven, but wondrous too is the inferior one. Just as the upper heaven rules the elements and generates within them the matter found there, drawing forth the character of each region and making from it what it ought to be, so it must be known that the four Elements also exist within man himself, as the Microcosm. <margin>All minerals are within man.</margin> Therefore, in man too, the underlying minerals—all of which are present in him—are produced, though one may be present more or less than another. From this you ought to understand that all men are "exalted" in all things, though by different types: one in this way, another in that. And though one man may not feel Gout, nevertheless its matter is still stored within him. <margin>Why gout affects some and not others.</margin> The heaven has simply drawn forth something else in him, while it has sent Gout into the systems of others. Thus, in those where it produced Gout, it left other diseases aside. It is therefore right for the Physician to act as an Astronomer, so that he may know and distinguish what the heaven is drawing forth in the Microcosm, and what it ultimately intends to exalt. For he must establish his Physics and Theory based on that. If a Physician is ignorant of these things, what is he babbling about regarding the substance, causes, matter, or nature of diseases? He pours out mere sophistry and falls apart with that boastful, ostentatious talk of "the Humors" <note>The traditional Galenic theory that health depends on the balance of four fluids: blood, phlegm, black bile, and yellow bile. Paracelsus rejected this in favor of chemical and celestial causes.</note>.

## THE PROCESS.

It is well known and established among you that it is often said a sorceress <note>original: "phitonissam" — a pythoness or witch.</note> has stirred up hail, thunder, lightning, storms, and the like, which occur in various ways. But many stammer when explaining how these things actually happen. While we are speaking here of Gout, it is necessary that the matter itself be understood without any hesitation. If Gout is to be known as it should be, the situation demands that the force and power of witches also be understood. Let it be far from the Physician to view this as mere superstition. <margin>Witchcrafts are natural actions.</margin> For no one disputes the name. But you should say that it is natural, not supernatural. Do not say the devil performs these things, but affirm that a human accomplishes them. This, however, is not the point. Many arts in Medicine were revealed by the devil and spirits. Who would deny that the same happens with sorceresses? I speak according to nature; as for the rest, I leave it to its own value. <margin>Fire is drawn from Chalcedony.</margin> Just as we strike fire from Chalcedony <note>original: "Cæcedonio" — likely referring to flint or a similar hard stone used to strike sparks.</note> with which we light wood—who would criminalize this work as witchcraft, since it happens in a natural way and depends on us? If, therefore, a certain kind of "iron" (as it were) similarly existed that could manufacture snow and hail, and a suitable subject were provided in place of wood—since thunder is generated in the same way as fire—who, I ask, would not say these things happen by natural reason? Because Magic is now dead, that fire has likewise been extinguished, and the thing itself began to be imputed to witchcraft, though it remains a natural work. What else is lighting a fire but Magic? The other is similar. And it is right to know such things. For God wishes to be known in His works. Nothing, however, should be spent on evil use. Which of these is worse? Or is it not the same thing to burn down a house, a village, or a city, <margin>Raising thunder and burning houses are of one art.</margin> as it is to stir up hail and destroy crops? For there is one Philosophy and one power for both. Or what is it when you offer poison to be drunk and kill a man, which is also itself Magic? One is suppressed, the other is made manifest. And such things must be considered so it may be known that there is no witchcraft here, but mere natural phenomena. Such is the inferior heaven, which gives us fire and likewise gives us cold. It also fashions Gout, not otherwise than if it were lighting sulphur or converting Mercury into snow. <margin>What is gout?</margin> For what else is Gout, but sulphur set on fire, raging in the synovia <term>synovia: the lubricating fluid found in the joints.</term>, derived from the Three Primes <note>The "Three Primes" (Tria Prima) are Salt, Sulphur, and Mercury—the fundamental alchemical building blocks of all matter in Paracelsian thought.</note>? Or the heaven ignites the cold—that is, the Mercury—and it produces hail; and in both, Salt is the concurring factor. Thus, he who makes gout in the Microcosm is like one who brings forth fire from flint and iron and ignites wood; <margin>From Sipha the hags draw fire, Colcita.</margin> or he is like the sorceress who would strike fire from the *Sipha* <note>A Paracelsian term for the "lining" or membrane of the air or heaven.</note> and ignite the natural subject *Colcita* <note>Likely referring to a dense material or "bed" of matter that receives the celestial fire.</note>, from which a storm would arise. By similar reasoning, the "star of Gout" in the body of nature is of either a summer or winter nature, completing its work and subtly and industriously exalting its subject. For more art is required to produce a single disease than all the arts beneath the world have ever possessed. Nature surpasses all arts in her fabrications.

## OPPOSING VIEWS.

<margin>Gout is not "the drop" and why.</margin>
Some drunken Physician might snarl here that Gout is "the drop" <note>original: "guttam" — the traditional term for gout and rheumatism, from the idea of harmful humors "dropping" into the joints.</note>. But if it were a drop, it would not have so much power that it could stir up paroxysms <note>Sudden attacks or fits of pain.</note> and behave in this or that manner. It is therefore worthless to say it is "a drop"; rather, it is necessary that a power be added at the same time by which it exists. From all the writings of those men (mostly hollow and meager), nothing else can be understood by reading them than that "the drop" is like a flint stone, cast down and dead. And just as a flint has no power to stir up paroxysms, so there is no power in "the drop" that proves where it comes from or what it is. Does anyone actually become a Physician because he can say this arises from here or there and degenerates into that? Truly, that is too light and thin. For the patient teaches you this, not you yourself. If that is all you know, you are hardly a Physician at all. The sign that you are a Physician is if you knew the matter even before the

...examine the patient more precisely. You must observe something more sublime than a mere "drop" <note>original: "guttam." The term "gout" comes from the Latin *gutta* (drop), based on the old belief that morbid humors "dropped" into the joints.</note>. For it does not fall as if from a roof, despite your idle talk. Now, what is the point of dividing this matter into species, calling this one *Arthritis*, that one *Sciatica*, another *Chiragra* <note>Gout specifically affecting the hand.</note>, and so on, when you still do not
<margin>Reprimand of physicians.</margin>
know what it is, what it teaches, or why it is in this location rather than another? You talk nonsense about a disease you have not recognized, and you do not explain the matter itself as befits a Doctor. Why do you cite authors and books when they are just like you, and the same ignorance is common to both? For it is ridiculous for anyone to wish to speak of a thing whose principle—namely, Astronomy and Philosophy—he does not know. Your only glory is your Sophistry <term>Sophistry: here used to mean deceptive or overly complex logical arguments that lack practical truth.</term>. That serves as your foundation; therefore, your cure is also sophistical. In your 
<margin>Fortunatus's Purse.</margin>

For just as he found in it whatever he pleased, so you also find everything in your Sophistry—which is to say, both of you find nothing. What is this, I ask, when you say some causes are "primitive," others "antecedent," and others "conjunct" <note>Standard categories of causation in Galenic medicine.</note>, yet you remain ignorant of the very material of which you speak? You do everything backwards: you command them to eat this, avoid that, drink this, or not drink that, yet you do not know the proper method in the slightest degree. Thus you produce Gout now from "cholera" <note>Yellow bile.</note>, now from "phlegm," etc.; and you have the same foundation as the Purgatory of Saint Patrick, or 
<margin>The Purgatories of Brixius and Tundale.</margin>
Tundale <note>References to popular medieval visionary accounts of the afterlife, used here to call medical theories "fables."</note>. Regarding this disease, the signs you put forward belong to no true art. The patients themselves could teach those to you; your brains need not be strained for such things. But you have established such judgments for yourselves so that the logic of the work and the workman would be the same. It is certainly worthy of a hiss of derision when you say that eunuchs, bald men, boys, and women are not afflicted by gout. This is far from the mark. Doubtless, the author believed it because he knew it to be true in his own climate; he then assumed it would necessarily happen similarly in Confluentia <note>Likely Koblenz, Germany.</note> and everywhere else. I omit other nonsense and ravings similar to these. Meanwhile, since their words are not 
<margin>Alexander of Metz.</margin>
the Gospels, and the matter is not one of religious faith, let those books be held in their own place and value—much like the Shirt of *Alexander of Metz* <note>Likely a reference to a supposed holy relic or a superstitious object held in low regard by the author.</note>.

->### SIGNS.<-

Signs are taken from locations. If you know the location of the *synovia* <term>Synovia: Paracelsus's term for the lubricating fluid in the joints; he was among the first to emphasize its role in joint disease.</term>, you will also know the seat of gout. Above all, therefore, seek a knowledge of the *synovia*, and you will then be able to judge gout.
So, if the annual stars move the paroxysms <note>Sudden recurrences or intensifications of symptoms.</note> of time in a human, then you can say that the gout is stirred by the motion of the heavens. It is from this foundation that one must speak of the paroxysm, its nature, temperament, and property; for without Astronomy, you will never understand the matter itself.
Afterward, apply also the signs of experience, as they are presented to you by the sick—not as they happen in one person, but in all; not in one region, but in all: Europe, Africa, etc. Although the monsters in Africa are so terrifying that they barely allow you to leave your mother's lap. There, you physicians grow in peace and tranquility, and you push out worn-out authors like a hen pushes out an egg.

->### DECLARATION.<-

The principle of our diseases, therefore, is taken from external things by which they are governed. First of all, then, external things must be known, not internal ones. For the internal are to be compared to the external. From which it follows that all knowledge of gout must be drawn from the external Elements, the Firmament, etc. And he who lacks knowledge of external things necessarily goes astray regarding the disease.
Furthermore, the "Mechanic" <note>The natural or "laboratorial" process of the body.</note> must be understood, no differently than the cause of fire and hail; and this not in a magical sense, but a natural one; not in spirits, but corporeally. Specifically, a similar logic and conjunction exists in diseases, as the *Archidoxis* <note>One of Paracelsus's most famous works on the "ancient doctrines" of medicine and alchemy.</note> will declare more fully in its proper place.

->## ON THE FALLING SICKNESS.<-

<margin>What is the Falling Sickness?</margin>
**R**egarding the name of the "Falling Sickness" <note>Epilepsy.</note>, it should be known that this disease has been designated by various names by different physicians, according to each one's language, understanding, or opinion. But there is no importance placed in this, since most names were bestowed without an understanding of the cause. Therefore, let the names do nothing except designate the thing. The Germans also call it the disease of Saint Valentine, but undeservedly; which is the same logic for most other names as well. We, however, will retain the name "Falling Sickness" <note>original: "caducus."</note>.

->### WHAT IT IS.<-

If any person, younger or older, suddenly falls without consciousness, or (as happens in youth or the beginning of the disease) with consciousness, and—either senseless or oppressed by a narcotic sleep—trembles, or foams, and grinds his teeth, is convulsed in his limbs, and a spasm distorts the eyes, ears, mouth, neck, feet, and hands, and he is shaken and trembles in his fall like a house from an earthquake: say that this person has been seized by the Falling Sickness. Indeed, all are not attacked in one way. For this one is seized with a certain premonition, that one with another type of paroxysm; this one is seized rarely, another more frequently. In this person, the evil leaps from one limb into the head; in that one, from the stomach, intestines, etc., according to the condition of sex, age, and other factors. You, however, should nevertheless judge this also to be the falling sickness. For if they fall against their will and without reason, and lie as if sleeping or fainting, it is altogether the falling sickness. It is also the falling sickness when a paroxysm is induced by another disease. For some diseases are mutually transformed, just as the 
<margin>The Salar turns into a Salmon.</margin>
Salar turns into a Salmon <note>A metaphor suggesting that while the appearance or "stage" of the disease changes, the underlying nature remains the same. A "salar" is a young trout or salmon.</note>. Yet all these diseases are to be held as one.

->### THE CAUSE.<-

<margin>A stupefying stench is the cause of falling sickness.</margin>
The falling sickness, therefore, is nothing other than a conquering or overpowering of the brain and the reason. For as often as a "foreign stench" <note>A morbid vapor or "aura."</note> is raised into the brain and the cells of reason, it then despoils the person of intellect and prostrates him. However, it is not an odor [in the common sense], but only a "stupefying" one, just as its multiplicity in things...

...having observed various things. This stupefying odor is simultaneously intoxicating and stinging. You see such a thing in herb-paris <note>original: "vua versa," likely *Paris quadrifolia*.</note> and hemlock. Indeed, they rob the reason, since they possess a narcotic power within themselves. And whatever things contain a faculty of this kind produce this disease in the body of the <term>Microcosm: the human being viewed as a miniature reflection of the entire universe</term>, about which I am now speaking. Of this species are also Henbane and the poppy; however, they are not stinging or intoxicating, just as Mandrake or opium are not. But other things, besides being stupefying, also have a stinging and intoxicating power as a companion, such as the sulphur of vitriol <note>An alchemical preparation of sulfuric acid or related compounds believed to have potent medicinal or toxic effects.</note>. Whoever produces or ingests this from the conjunctions of the stars is seized by a paroxysm of the falling sickness, just as are animals that are of this nature, such as weasels, squirrels, and lions. There are many of these <term>Simples: individual medicinal herbs or minerals used as ingredients</term> which, if someone tastes them or inhales their smoke, he is overwhelmed by the said disease. You ought to have an exact knowledge of these "furious" and sleep-inducing simples. For these same things are also within the body.

<margin>
All minerals are in man.
</margin>
<margin>
The diversity of the matter and the ascendant varies the disease.
</margin>
Since man is constituted in such a way that he has the power of the simples within himself, it is necessary that there be such simples from which the falling sickness is made: as if I were to say that the sulphur of vitriol exists in the body. Now it is established that from the <term>Three Primes: the fundamental alchemical principles of Sulphur, Salt, and Mercury</term> from which man is made and composed, he has sulphur, salt, and mercury innate to himself. If this sulphur is exalted by his <term>Ascendant: the specific astrological or vital force governing the person's current state</term>, he is then prepared for the falling sickness. Indeed, this foundation remains unmoved: that just as they are outside, so also inside man himself such minerals are established. Therefore, on the other hand, if the ascendant takes delight in these and is joined there—according to how the conjunction is—so the man falls. Thus, this or that matter is placed in the body. Accordingly, as the ascendant is born, so a similar disease occurs: it resolves, it dissolves, that one burns, this one dries, and so on. In this respect, all diseases are divided from this matter, so that the ascendant causes the disease, yet the body is what we have described. This operation teaches only this: that man contains such simples in himself. And just as something is melted by fire, and he who inhales its smoke falls, so in this case the ascendant is the one who ignites it and stirs up the smoke. If this smoke is raised into the "cells of reason" and into the brain, it stirs up this disease, as is obvious to everyone.

<margin>

</margin>

<margin>

But this same thing must also be understood in this way. The condition and nature of the disease is in the sulphur or that specific species which produces such things, and it is not in the man himself. For it is not the fault of the body. Just as, if the eyes drip from sharp smoke, or if they weep from the juice of onions, it is not the vice or fault of the eyes themselves, but of the smoke and the onions; in the same way, the same thing happens here. Once this matter is consumed, the paroxysm ceases—that is, the eyes are restored to their former integrity. Now, there is nothing here except by the fire of sulphur burning in such a way, for this reason: just as is known in <term>Meteorics: the study of atmospheric phenomena</term>, when "blind" rains and storms arise, the matter of those storms does not emerge in the upper heaven, but in the lower; yet the fire and the "cooker" is in the upper heaven. Whence frequently—indeed, always—when those blind storms are about to arise, smoke is first raised from the earth, which the storm then follows. Therefore, the "igniter" is in the upper heaven, but the matter is in the lower heaven. From these two, the so-called blind storm is made. Just as the matter lies invisibly and imperceptibly in the earth, so it is also in those who stand nearby; though it is not seen, it is no less present than that which is seen. Thus the sulphur of vitriol and its fire are visible; nevertheless, the same logic applies to the others which are not seen. Therefore, just as that kind of matter lies in the earth (which Meteorics teaches), so also in the body, the Microcosm is to be understood and known through <term>Magic: here meaning the hidden spiritual knowledge of nature's inner workings</term>. For without Magic, a man understands his own subject least of all, nor does he have a discovery of what he handles with his hands. Just as the Microcosm has its own species, so its own ascendant is owed to them. Wherefore the ascendant, which moves the "blind storm," must be known. Now if that present ascendant seizes the matter of madness, then it works in it, just as the magical doctrine teaches concerning the blind storm. Here, however, the vapor or smoke is the disease. And because it ascends to the head, it must be determined that the matter is located in many places of the body. From this it happens that sometimes the beginning and origin of the disease is felt in the stomach, and sometimes in the brain itself. And just as the smoke of a blind storm ascends into the sky, so here it ascends into the head. For it cannot escape any higher. If it strikes into the brain—yet according to the quality of the smoke breathing out from this or that simple—so the paroxysm behaves. But if it does not ascend to the brain, then in that limb where it stops, a spasm arises, and fainting, and a fall, etc. These, however, are milder and without the more serious paroxysms. For how many kinds of things or odors are there that make the eyes drip? These paroxysms are moved by just as many species. Yet all of them are species of only one simple lying in the body: namely, of burning sulphur, which carries with it Mercury and Salt, most subtly prepared. That sulphur (which is the principal thing in this disease) has this nature: that wherever its smoke reaches, it numbs and stupefies that limb, and takes away its implanted nature and property for as long as the smoke predominates. And since the head and brain have a more exquisite sense than the other parts, for that reason the species of the paroxysms are more manifest there. For those vapors are manifold, since the stupefying, stinging, and intoxicating things are also manifold.

These things, however, by themselves and simply, do not happen at all; rather, it is necessary for an "ebullition" <note>A boiling up or bubbling.</note> to come which completes them. Then the stars behave like an eclipse, which obscures the Sun and Moon, and so continues its path. Thus it must be known here that the matter lies ready, but the course of the ascendant proceeds either through the middle of the matter itself, or its exterior, or declines near its sides. Whence it now produces more or fewer diseases, according as it passes straight through, or less so. Just as the present course works in the manner of an Eclipse, so also in this case...

# ON THE FALLING SICKNESS.

...by chance, at a single time, moment, or hour, it melts the matter just as if fire were applied. Once this is done, smoke rises upward and continues its gradual ascent until the Eclipse <note>The author uses "Eclipse" as a metaphor for the duration of the seizure, when the light of reason is "blocked."</note> passes. Therefore, as long as the paroxysm <note>A sudden attack or fit; the active stage of the seizure.</note> lasts, the ascending force acts and moves within the matter, whether quickly or briefly. And as often as it enters the matter, so often does the paroxysm begin, which must be predicted by the Physician. It is therefore necessary that he possesses a knowledge of Astronomy. If he does not, he will stare at the disease like a calf at a gate <note>original: "ceu vitulus comædum" (like a calf at a comedian/strange sight), a proverb for looking at something without understanding.</note>.

Sometimes it also happens—indeed quite often—that the ascending influence is not alone but has companions joined to it. For it is very rare for an ascending influence of this condition to be solitary; rather, several are usually folded together and joined, like the "Wagon" <note>The Big Dipper or Ursa Major constellation.</note> in the heavens, which exists as a sevenfold group in its transit. So too there are ascending influences which follow one after another in sequence, and yet they are included under a single name. If, therefore, the ascending influence proceeds accompanied by such a retinue, then 2, 3, 4, 5, or 6 paroxysms follow one another in order, all of which belong to a single motion and day. Sometimes it even happens that such ascending influences follow one another so swiftly that it is believed only one paroxysm has been stirred; however, the multiplicity is recognized by the fact that just as one paroxysm is declining, another immediately begins to build with a new commotion.

<margin>
A physician without Astronomy is nothing.
</margin>
<margin>
The description of Falling Sickness is to be sought from the <term>Cabala: here referring to a natural spiritual science of hidden properties</term>. Falling Sickness from the emotions of the mind.
</margin>

These paths and the nature of the "Eclipses" must be thoroughly investigated by the Physician. For the matter placed within man—namely, the mortified <term>Sulphur: in alchemy, the principle of combustibility and soul</term>—is itself the whole of Philosophy; but the "igniter" is Astronomy. The ignition happens through the ascending influence in the manner described, and that blind smoke or blind storm ascends and builds its impression, perfecting in the head whatever is contained within its nature. This impression is **Magical**, for it receives its matter from the lower Elements and not from itself, and thus it is hidden from our eyes.

However, this Magical operation belongs to the science of the **Cabala**, which proceeds not from spirits or sorcery, but from the natural course of subtle nature. This is not the kind of "knowledge" where men know nothing of their own hidden and secret things; rather, it is true knowledge if the <term>Microcosmic: the human being as a "little world" mirroring the universe</term> man is understood in both ways: namely, manifestly and Magically, visibly and invisibly. For you cannot grasp diseases by any other means unless the Magical art instructs you on their manner, habit, and course, just as is the way of the Cabala. It is therefore useless to describe the falling sickness with many words based on mere opinion, or anatomical speculations, or deductions from "humors" <note>Referring to the traditional Greek medical theory of the four bodily fluids (blood, phlegm, yellow bile, black bile), which the author here rejects.</note> or other things.

Nevertheless, sometimes fear, joy, and terror also stimulate this disease. Since we are subject to fragility, many things are dissolved, separated, and prepared in various places until they are subjected to such a constellation; this would otherwise never happen. And yet, for both this and other types of falling sickness, the sole cause is the presence of Sulphur and the "impression" of the ascending influence upon it, from which two things the paroxysm is induced.

### THE PROCESS.

**I**f, therefore, the vapor of the lower "heaven" has now been raised into the upper firmament—that is, into the head—it becomes visible in that region. While this is happening, vertigo begins and reason is abolished. The more visible this vapor becomes, the more the disease increases, like a cloud which is initially nothing to our sight, yet in a brief moment is so piled up and increased that it shadows the entire sky. As long as such clouds are in the head, the paroxysm has not yet reached its peak.

<margin>
How the tremor of the falling sickness occurs.
</margin>
<margin>
What is an earthquake?
</margin>

But these vapors contain winds and oppositions within themselves, of the same nature as all the <term>Simples: individual medicinal plants or substances</term> used for pain relief, as the specific *Herbal* <note>Likely a reference to a specific botanical text or the author's own book on herbs.</note> teaches regarding this nature. When these generations pass into effect, a kind of sudden storm falls upon the person with incredible persistence and speed, even though the sky is clear and the stars are shining brightly. While the storm attacks in this way—which <term>Meteorology: the study of atmospheric phenomena</term> demonstrates more clearly—then the moisture of the brain is suffocated, along with everything situated in the power of the brain.

And because <term>Sulphur</term> is present together with <term>Nitre: saltpeter, the principle of explosive force</term> and <term>Mercury: the principle of fluidity and spirit</term>, the patient is shaken as if by an earthquake until the ascending influence has passed. It is just as if these three were lying fixed in an **Athanor** <note>A self-feeding alchemical furnace designed to maintain a steady heat.</note> and Vulcan <note>The Roman god of fire, often used to represent the alchemical fire itself.</note> lit the flame. For as long as the fire lasts, the Nitre and Sulphur tremble and shake within the Mercury. That jolting is the paroxysm. Its origin and cause are similar to an earthquake, which is itself nothing other than a mixture of nitre and sulphur. Just as an exit is first given, the paroxysm ends in the "earth" and the "falling sickness" simultaneously. It does not end otherwise, unless it is either consumed by itself or the ascending influence departs. For this reason, it is not unwise to open the head with suitable openings. For if such impressions are not enclosed, the tremor cannot happen. Therefore, a convenient opening is a unique secret, and it is of great importance for proving the cause of this matter.

### THE SIGNS.

**W**hen the operations happen in the said manner, the sulphur reveals itself in the place where it hides. In that same place, the beginning, the exit, and the passage of this "Eclipse" are felt. These are followed by the loss of the brain's faculty (that is, reason), fainting, vertigo, deep sleep, spasms, foaming at the mouth, **Mania**, and other things which are encountered daily. These were sufficiently described by the ancients and need not be repeated here.

But it also sometimes happens that these things or impressions of the head occasionally descend into the lower limbs through the distribution of abundant vapors, so that finally, toward the end of the paroxysm, the whole body becomes full of the impression. Hence it happens that when distributed into the limbs in this way, it operates in them just as it does in the head and its regions. This can also happen because in such bodies there sometimes exist several "places of sulphur." From this arise several transits of ascending influences. Thus it happens that one limb is sometimes moved more violently than another, because a specific ascending influence is passing through that spot as well. And as often as a new commotion occurs after a little rest, a new ascending influence is passing. Therefore, the location and number of the paroxysms must be diligently estimated and judged.

Multiple locations of Sulphur at once.

### CONTRARY OPINIONS.

<margin>The Falling Sickness occurs in proportion to the moon's phases.</margin>
**A**lthough the ancients made certain divisions regarding the location of this disease, one should not consider its seat any differently than what we have already stated. For wherever the <term>Sulphur</term><note>In Paracelsian medicine, Sulphur represents the principle of combustibility and the soul.</note> is stored and the "conjunction" occurs, there too is the disease—whether it happens in one, two, or more places. Therefore, there is no need for distinctions or for bestowing peculiar names upon it. It is not entirely false, as they claim, that the <term>paroxysms</term><note>A sudden attack or violent expression of a disease, such as a seizure.</note> are stirred according to the face of the Moon. However, they did not learn this from a knowledge of the celestial course, but solely from the experience of their eyes and the accounts of the sick. For that reason, their description of these things is too dry and insufficient. The things which <term>Avicenna</term><note>Ibn Sina (c. 980–1037), a Persian physician whose "Canon of Medicine" was the standard textbook in Europe for centuries.</note> writes are vain. For he lacked that foundation upon which alone it is lawful for a Physician to stand. He does bring forth some points, but they are conceived only from opinion. His ignorance of the first principle poured no small darkness over him. Likewise, others propose many causes for this disease. Yet, since they are entirely void of and unskilled in <term>Astronomy</term>, Philosophy, and <term>Meteorology</term><note>In this context, the study of "meteors" or sudden changes in the atmosphere, often linked by Paracelsus to sudden bodily changes.</note>, who would value their fabrications and fantasies so highly? It would be a waste of paper to examine and discuss each of them here.

<margin>Avicenna is criticized.</margin>
<margin>Reproof of doctors.</margin>
Indeed, it is a shameful thing that so many Doctors and Masters, swollen so high with pride and haughtiness, have neither learned nor understood enough to discern a lie from the truth, nor to heal and rescue the sick who lie before them in such a piteous spectacle. And these men, who frequently call me a "buffoon," are they not themselves foul hypocrites? Judge for yourselves which name is more fitting. Meanwhile, however, he who is arrogant in the name of a <term>city physician</term><note>original: "poliatri," a state-appointed or high-ranking town doctor.</note> and boasts of being a regular Reader and Professor—it would be lawful and fitting for him to know those things which are required for these matters. Yet, since these men have partly rotted away in the schools, partly grown calloused in Rhetoric, and partly grown old in poetic trifles, what else could they be capable of or know, except how to paint all men as fools and idiots according to their own whim, just as they paint letters? The very knowledge of the <term>light of nature</term><note>The innate wisdom of the natural world, which Paracelsus believed was the true source of medical knowledge, as opposed to books.</note> constitutes the Physician, if it is joined with experience, of which they themselves are ignorant. And because of their ignorance, it must be endured that those who are skilled in these things are called "experimenters" and "risk-takers" by way of slander. But I say this openly: that concerning this so grave a disease, all of their books are mere Stentorian voices and vanities, intended only for the penny and not directed toward healing. And for this end, they so greatly patronize Avicenna, <term>Galen</term><note>Claudius Galenus (129–c. 216 AD), the Greek physician whose theories of the "four humors" dominated medieval medicine.</note>, and other similar triflers. For the truth—that is, experience sought out and practiced—could never gather such a great harvest for their kitchens with such pleasant leisure. It is a disgrace and a certain crime to claim an arrogant name from mere trifles, and not to earn it by the cure of the sick. And this name is a cloak by which you hide your deceits and dye the faces of the sick <note>original: "fucum facitis," a Latin idiom meaning to deceive or put on a false front.</note>, who are persuaded that the thing and the art are joined entirely with the name. Meanwhile, they are slaughtered by you, or at the very least, left crippled. And as long as the matter is not brought to the point where experience alone is held as the unique foundation of Medicine, Medicine will be nothing but mere wickedness, imposture, and a foul hunting for money. If ever a good and kind hour shines upon them so that they achieve something, through this success all their crimes committed throughout the course of an age are afterwards wiped out and obliterated. But that luck is thrown at you by Satan, so that he may keep you bound in his shackles. It is worthy of every complaint that your consciences have grown so calloused to daring every enormity, while in the meantime you impudently sell your integrity and wisdom to everyone with a lying mouth.

<margin>Galen and Avicenna are noted.</margin>

### DECLARATION.

**I**n the body, the parts of minerals are so fixed that they occasionally both flare up and smoke, yet without the wasting away of the body itself. Therefore, digestives and laxatives contribute nothing to the cure. One element alone is at fault here. Which one it may be matters little. For the sum of every cure ought to be directed toward this: that the <term>Three Primes</term>—namely <term>Sulphur, Mercury, and Salt</term>—remain in a state of moisture, not in a state of oiliness. Once that is provided, the cure is complete. In this, the ancient Physicians are greatly opposed, in whom there is neither mercy, nor faith, nor art. They have only the penny for a heart. While they scrape that together, what does the sublimity of art profit them?

<margin>And the cure of the falling sickness.</margin>

<margin>Twitching is a milder falling sickness; as are heart tremors, the nightmare, ecstasy, etc.</margin>
But this also is true: that from the class of the falling sickness there also exists <term>twitching</term><note>original: "ietigatio," referring to involuntary muscle jerks or myoclonus.</note>, but this is a milder falling sickness, nor is its cause spread as widely. To the same class also belong <term>tremor of the heart</term>, as if residing in the head, and the <term>nightmare</term><note>original: "incubus," traditionally associated with a feeling of being pressed down during sleep.</note> and <term>ecstasy</term>. Concerning these, know that the things which excite the falling sickness outside of its interior course—such as irritation, joy, sorrow, food, drink, etc.—act like a stirred-up tempest, as <term>Magic</term> alone (which is more deeply hidden) teaches more fully. Therefore, the antecedent or primitive cause is nothing at all except <term>Magical Astronomy</term> in all diseases. It is a difficult matter to discourse on external things that generate disease, the explanation of which belongs to the Magi alone. For external things must become internal. If this is to be done, certainly no other faculty than Magic will indicate and expedite the cause. Since that was unknown to those writers, they treated the matter poorly and simultaneously instituted a crippled and erroneous process of cure. For a cure ought to be instituted <term>Magically</term>, not according to their interpretation of degrees, digestion, purging, and so on. Therefore, in Medicine, a double Theory exists: one <term>Physical</term>, the other <term>Magical</term>. But they are blind in the Physical and foolish in the Magical. This at least they do and learn: to be city idiots, courtly flatterers, and moneylenders. That is their Doctorate; that is their Mastership.

<margin>Medical theory is twofold: Magical and Physical.</margin>

**M**any names for fever are circulated, though improperly. For many names testify to many causes, just as it is also clear that many causes and origins are assigned to fevers everywhere, when yet there is only one Theory, Physics, and reason for all of them...

...and the reasoning is established: there are not many. Therefore, those who introduce more names are introducing errors. For error in Medicine is a form of heresy. These people, however, hawk everything as if it were established and indubitable truth. Whence it happens that they experience an outcome similar to that of the truth they claim to possess.

### WHAT IS IT?

**T**hose who complain of some weakness and are troubled by tensions and stretching, yawning, weakness of the stomach and limbs, a distortion of the natural complexion, and at a set time are afflicted by stiffness, trembling, and shaking—which is then suddenly followed by a heat of the body that lasts for a certain time: if these people are afterwards at rest for a while, and the disease returns with the same <term>pattern</term><note>The original uses "typus," referring to the periodic cycle or schedule of a recurring fever.</note> as before, and then rests again: all those who complain of such accidents, I say, judge them to be gripped by fever, regardless of how the <term>paroxysms</term><note>A sudden attack or violent increase in symptoms.</note> vary. For some are additionally burdened by a compression of the stomach, headache, or other accidents. Cold and heat, however, are the primary signs. And although some other diseases also attack with these signs, such as abscesses and the plague—which almost always end in death—I will say nothing of those in this chapter; I speak only of chronic fevers, which are manifest.

### THE CAUSE.

<margin>Man consists of 4 Elements.</margin>
Man is composed of four Elements. And these are subject to the "heaven" that is within the body. These four Elements are four bodies and subjects. Whatever the internal heaven works upon them must be endured. For man is liable to dissolution. As far as this dissolution is concerned, man can to some extent meet and resist it.

<margin>Man has the cause of dissolution within himself, and conservation outside himself.</margin>
For in his hand, in turn, he has received another heaven, which beats back and represses the force of the former. These things are indicated in this way so it may be known that this internal heaven and these bodies generate fever from within themselves. It is not diverse because there are four bodies, but rather it is only one single fever. For in that place, those bodies are one thing. The beginning is not in all of them in one place, although many "roots" spread out from which fevers arise. And yet it is not only the roots that suffer, but all things present suffer together.

<margin>A specific Ascendant rises for each part.</margin>
To understand the <term>matrix</term><note>The source or "womb" where a disease originates.</note> of a fever, attend to this: Every single thing existing as a member in the body has its own proper and peculiar <term>Ascendant</term>.<note>In this context, the "Ascendant" is not just a zodiac sign, but the specific vital/astrological force governing a particular organ or limb.</note> That Ascendant is its own heaven, which serves it alone and not the other members. From this Ascendant (which you might also call a peculiar constellation) this evil arises when some member receives a "dislocated heaven."

<margin>What kind of dislocation of the heaven is it?</margin>
Now, the heaven is dislocated when it is divided into two parts: into cold and heat. Being so constituted, it deserts every duty, neglects its nature and order, and contrives a new motion and order. For according to its power, the same thing happens to the internal heaven as happens to human reason, which fashions one thing today and another tomorrow. And since we and the heaven are one single creature, we therefore also exist as similar things.

<margin>Equal reasoning of the heaven and the intellect.</margin>
Neither is our intellect more than the heaven, nor is the heaven more than our intellect. Thus man sets an order for himself as he wishes. The heaven does the same. Man is premeditated in his reason. The heaven, however, is not premeditated. Yet in both, there is a single power, both premeditated and unpremeditated.

<margin>The heaven is the idea of man, and vice versa.</margin>
Thus we prefigure the heaven, and in turn, the heaven reflects us, while we both fall into wanderings and errors if we place our trust in ourselves. For if it is possible for the heaven to be driven into error, the same can happen to our reason. And so it is conversely. From this, we understand that the nature and cause of all these things is one. We ought to imitate this one nature—which errs less—rather than ourselves. For if we follow ourselves, we will be driven into diseases, just as the heaven is driven when it does not act as it should. For it does not act otherwise than if it possessed reason and said: "I will do this." For it does it so, even if it does not express it in words. Just as a medicine, once taken, performs its work no differently than if it were commanded and ordered, even though it has neither tongue, nor hands, nor movement. <note>The Latin text contains the typo "hbeat" for "habeat" (to have).</note> Yet its force is no less than if it used reason and counsel like a craftsman finishing a work he has begun. Likewise, the nettle and pepper burn, yet no fire or coals are present, even though a fiery force is felt. And this is a **Magical power**. One should understand the "erring heaven" in a similar way.

<margin>The heaven is similar to man's operation.</margin>
The Ascendant maintains this same custom when it approaches its work. For as a laborer proposes to himself what he is to finish that day—or as a carpenter says to himself: "I will work here until I have finished this house; tomorrow I will take up something else, and I will press on with the tasks until I have brought what I started to an end"—so also the Ascendant disposes and orders its tasks for itself, as if it were saying: "Here in this man I have this member, which is mine; now I am the axe which fells the member like a tree, strips it, and shapes it as I wish. I am that craftsman; and like a carpenter, I will build a fever. I will fashion this or that, I will arrange it so that my art and industry are apparent, and it may be known that man's effort against me is nothing, but he must entirely yield to me one way or another." For just as wood is forced to remain motionless as it is placed by the craftsman, so also my will remains fixed; thus I will not desist from the work before I have thoroughly completed it—that is, I will either kill the man or leave him weak and weary. For all the power of the heaven is fulfilled in man.

<margin>What is the mode of fevers?</margin>
If the Ascendant has proposed such a thing for itself to do, then it is itself simultaneously both heat and cold; for in its <term>temperate state</term><note>A balanced mixture of qualities.</note> it has withdrawn into two: into cold and heat, and is divided equally, like day and night. If it has thus divided itself and dissolved its balanced temperature, and arranged each part separately, the matter is no different than if two men were walking, one following the other, of whom one was cold and the other hot. In the same way, the stars follow behind one another, and each attracts its own part.

<margin>How does the cold occur?</margin>
Therefore, if the Ascendant enters not in a state of balance but fractured, it is as cold as winter, and induces cold in its member; from which the entire spirit of the body then suffers, even though...

<margin>
The cause of trembling is cold
</margin>
...if that rising influence does not touch the limb entirely, then the limbs tremble from that cold through a natural operation. For **trembling** <note>original: "Tremor"</note> arises from cold, and from no other cause. However, that cold descends from the "heaven" <note>In this context, "heaven" refers to the internal "astrum" or celestial influence that governs the human microcosm, rather than the literal sky.</note> and not from the bodies themselves. Therefore, its origin must be sought in the "heaven," which is the logic pursued in this place.

<margin>
How heat is produced
</margin>
Furthermore, the heaven brings down its first part, as if a messenger were passing through or a wind were persuading it. Then, following closely in its tracks, comes the hot part of the rising influence, which ignites and burns, impressing its power for as long as it runs and moves. When it has passed through, the heat vanishes. Thus, for this turn, the <term>paroxysm</term> <note>A sudden attack or increase in symptoms.</note> of both cold and heat is finished. Just as is the nature of the heat, so too does it inflame its specific limb. And since all limbs contain within themselves the <term>spirit of life</term> and a shared power of sensation, one limb necessarily suffers along with the other. Just as winter and summer persuade the entire world, so too do these influences pass through the entire body and complete their operation there, each acting according to its condition and nature. Once these have passed in this manner, the disease ceases for the first time, and the body is free. For that which was afflicting the body has now receded, restoring the former strength to its place.

<margin>
The cause of intervals in fever.
</margin>
Meanwhile, such is the trick and nature of the "heaven" that when a person thinks they are now free, it leaps back unexpectedly on the second, third, or fourth day, maintaining its old habit and shaking the body with an entirely similar alternation. One rising influence is prepared to give intervals of a certain length, while another may give more or fewer, according to the specific property it received in its course. For the distinction arises from the number of intervals, from the various rising influences of the heaven, and from the specific and peculiar parts of those influences.

<margin>
Where do the differences in fevers arise?
</margin>
From this it happens that one **fever** <note>original: "febris"</note> belongs to the spleen, another to the stomach, that one to the brain, this one to the blood, another to the liver, some to the kidneys, some to the fluids, and so on. Thus, from the variety of rising influences and the diversity of parts and limbs, different types and natures of fevers are produced. Yet the common cause of all is the rising influence and the part over which it predominates. For as one limb receives a peculiar duty over others, so the signs and <term>premonitory symptoms</term> <note>original: "prodromi," signs that precede the onset of a disease.</note> arrive according to it—namely, a weaker or stronger state, **fainting** <note>original: "syncope"</note>, and whatever else arises from the aforementioned causes. Even if the heaven allows a person a defined interval, great hope of recovery cannot be placed in the daily fever-state. For with the passage of time, by chilling its limb, it weakens it so much that eventually the very substance of the body is dissolved. We see this happen when cold strikes wine or something similar too severely; once spoiled, it does not return to its former goodness but is corrupted and turns into something worse. From this, many accidents emerge which are not the fevers themselves, but something else gendered by the fevers. Thus they keep one name, but do not share the same cause or matter. In the same way, if heat has excessively warmed something, it does not remain in its former integrity. So also the body is shattered in its elements, so that one part turns sour, another bitter, another putrid, and another is changed in some other way. For there are many species, natures, and properties of putrefaction, which need not be discussed at length here, as they are typically taught in Philosophy. And so, up to this point, we have explained sufficiently the accidents generated by fevers.

<margin>
The constant motion of the heaven.
</margin>
Now, the heaven has its own defined course. As long as it lasts, the pain and fever also last. If these are to be turned away, it will be the duty of the subject <note>The patient or the physician acting upon the patient.</note> to resist and struggle against the rising influence more courageously and powerfully. For if this is done, its course is blocked. This is achieved by "closing" the laboring limb, just as someone fleeing the cold shuts themselves in a heated room, or avoiding the heat, hides in a cellar. However, this cannot be obtained otherwise than through the **Magical heaven**, that is, through the heaven of Medicine, which throws up a wall even if no stones are seen, and blocks with boards even if no wood appears. Nevertheless, its passage is hindered so that the rising influence is forced either to pass by or to recede to the side. For just as a person can otherwise avoid being harmed by cold or heat, rain or snow, so medicine exists as a similar craftsman, engineering invisible things to protect the person from evils. But unless it is resisted, the heaven continues its intended work until it either tires out of its own accord, adopts another plan, is led back to its former course, or breaks and dissolves the man himself, which it held as the end of its work.

-> *THE PROCESS.* <-

<margin>
Why a man may be cold on the outside while hot on the inside.
</margin>
In the same way that the sun penetrates glass with its rays and fire goes through an iron furnace without the subjects themselves being broken or destroyed, so also this influence penetrates a man and unites with that which is within him. If it should happen in fevers that at the time of the cold, trembling and chattering of teeth afflict the person, and yet the internal limbs are nonetheless hot, the cause is this: only the spirit of the whole body suffers, while the root is cold. Thus, those who are cold in the winter time have at least cold skin, while the internal parts or those placed beneath the skin are not cold, but hot. For the spirit, which is more powerful than the body, is at least cold and trembles, and shakes the entire body. The matter does not reach the point where the flesh—that is, the physical body itself—is chilled or burned up. But if these parts themselves are seized, death is imminent. Therefore, the order of this influence and constellation is no different than how summer and winter affect a man. Clearly, the influence touches a man in the same way. It is the art of the heaven that it moderates the nature subject to it as it wishes and sees fit.

-> *CONTRADICTIONS.* <-

<margin>
A rebuke of physicians.
</margin>
<margin>
Humors are not the cause of fevers.
</margin>
Paper would hardly suffice us if we wished to wash away the contradictions of the Sophists and the aggressive **town physicians** <note>original: "poliatrorum," referring to established city-physicians, often used disparagingly.</note> here. They all stir up war because they understand nothing and have experienced nothing, but instead hammer home all their mere fantasies. For them, now **yellow bile** <note>original: "cholera"</note>, now blood, now **black bile** <note>original: "melancholia"</note>, etc., is the cause. Yet they have not yet explained the manner or the reason why these things exist. It is not enough if you see a yellow or green discharge to say that its cause is bile; rather, an entirely different discourse will be necessary,

# ON DROPSY.

...since you have not yet made it clear that it arises from <term>cholera</term> <note>original: "cholera"; here referring to yellow bile, one of the four humors of Galenic medicine.</note>. For bile is not the only thing in the body. Nor does this fever bear any resemblance to it. Thus, you cling only to the color and do not search for a more certain foundation—to your great shame. You must explain especially how such bile or phlegm is produced, and so forth. However, you will be quite unable to do this unless you acquire a much greater knowledge than your art has provided thus far. For the "heaven" <note>The "internal heaven" or "astrum," a Paracelsian concept where celestial forces govern biological processes.</note> produces it, which you have not yet recognized; just as you profess a medicine of which you are entirely ignorant. Therefore, Christ threw this morsel at you: *the blind leading the blind, and both falling into the ditch.* 

But because faith is simply granted to you—decrepit schoolmasters, rhetoricians, and poets—you have convinced yourselves that you have no need for a more accurate Philosophy. For something of your "wisdom" is always overflowing, produced by your sweet babbling. But the true art is this: to say what this thing is that produces such change and confusion in the body—and to do so from the foundation itself, not from colors.

It is certainly a "beautiful" brand of Physics that you, bursting forth from dung, speak of colors and put a cap <note>To "put a cap on it" is an idiom for finishing or finalizing a fraudulent claim.</note> on it. That you are "poets" could perhaps be endured. But you are too coarse when you spout such nonsense about fever without any foundation. It is not without reason that various fevers are observed. For there are various <term>ascendants</term> <note>Astrological influences rising at the time of the disease's onset.</note> and many parts. From these come various natures, about which much could be said. Since the "ascendants" belong to the Astronomer and the "parts" to the Philosopher, I commend this matter to those two professions. For it is unworthy to recount here those things which you Physicians ought to have known already. Indeed, your processes, causes, and cures are all perfectly matched: I think no singer ever sang a worse song than the way you compose your Physics and your cures. If by chance you ever stumble upon a favorable heaven, more kind to the sick man than to you, then you produce a single "miracle," which you boast about for the entire following year; thus, through arrogance, you make your arts and sciences seem authentic. And yet, if it were not for the faith of the ignorant, who would value you more than a hollow nut? Likewise, the way you classify daily, tertian, and quartan fevers based on time is mere trickery. For from where do that <term>paroxysm</term> and that matter arise? Puff out your cheeks, I pray, and finally sing out how these things align! For you have not yet touched the matter, but are very far from the mark. Know the "heaven," and you will hit the mark.

->Described and set down in another way by the Author himself, Theophrastus Paracelsus.<-

# ON DROPSY.
### I.

<margin>Dropsy should be called "Resolution."</margin>
**N**ames must be given to all things in such a way that they briefly convey their essence. Regarding "Dropsy" <note>original: "Hydropisis"</note>, however, the names are various and many; yet they do not encompass the cause of the disease itself, except by a certain resemblance—just as peasants can see a certain similarity here to water. From this, the negligence and ignorance of the ancients is clear. These types of "rustic" names were imposed on this disease even in other languages through ignorance, all derived from water. From this, one can understand the sheer rashness and rudeness of languages that are void of Philosophy, Astronomy, and the very light of nature. The genuine name for dropsy is **Resolution**. For the body, which is "resolved" <note>Broken down or dissolved.</note> from a coagulated state into a liquid moisture, is not water, but is "resolved moisture." And this is what dropsy is.

### II.

**T**he signs by which this disease is recognized in the beginning are these: a discoloration of the face, such as occurs in <term>jaundice</term> <note>original: "icteritia"</note>, tightness of the chest and difficulty of breath, indigestion, and great thirst (or none at all). In the middle stage, the signs are: swelling of the ankles and feet, appearing toward night and vanishing in the morning, along with the other aforementioned signs. In the final stage, there is a constancy of the swelling and inflation, sweating, and the persistence of footprints <note>Pitting edema, where pressure from a finger or shoe leaves a lasting indentation in the skin.</note> from the ankles to the knees, and from the knees to the groin. The swelling occupies the belly, the navel, and the private parts; afterward, the skin is pulled apart by cracks, water drips out, and the sick person meanwhile does not return to themselves. Thus comes death—slow and imperceptible.

### III.

**A**lthough other things of this sort happen in many ways—that is, many swellings may occur similarly—nevertheless, they are to be distinguished from dropsy by the sign of Jaundice, a sign which other swellings do not have. So that the Physician may be even more cautious, let him know that dropsies sometimes invade with doubtful signs and cannot be so readily diagnosed until, finally, the end reveals the disease through the cracking of the skin and the flowing out of water. These two signs, therefore, provide evidence of "new dropsy," which in Latin is called **resolved coagulation** <note>original: "coagulatio resoluta"</note>.

# THE CAUSE OF THE DISEASE.

<margin>The division of "growing things."</margin>
**W**e shall say something about the cause in this discourse. The Four Elements are bodies that are not "resolved" when divided. Nothing is handed down here concerning them, but only concerning that which proceeds and grows from an Element—that is, that which is "broken." For example, the earth remains undissolved when divided; but that which grows out of it is subject to a "divided dissolution." So it is also in this case. Now, certain growing things are not dissolved, such as stones, wood, etc. Regarding those, therefore, which are dissolved...

# ON DROPSY.

...is the subject of our discourse: and in these things, the cause of this disease must be sought. Therefore, it follows that any growing thing in the previous example, once coagulated, is not the same thing in its dissolution. That which is dissolved, therefore, classifies the disease. If the dissolution is moist, it is that which is handed down in this chapter. If it is not, it does not belong to this purpose. For wood is dissolved by a divided dissolution. But if it should rot, that is a worthy example to be placed here: for the coagulated becomes moist, which is "Resolution" <note>In alchemy and early medicine, "resolution" refers to a solid substance breaking down into a liquid state.</note>.

<margin>The physicist must consider the heaven in a twofold way.</margin>
A thing that rots is broken by contact. For example: if all earthly things are resolved into moisture, they are resolved by a cause—the heaven itself. Thus, the heaven is the father and progenitor of resolution. This must be understood in two ways by the physicist: the visible and the invisible. That is, it has two bodies, which are nevertheless both only one, comprising that which is seen and that which is not seen. That which is seen is what causes the growing things of the earth to rot. But that which causes a human to rot is not seen; nevertheless, it is one heaven, a single theory.

<margin>Man consists of the Elements.</margin>
Man is placed within the four Elements: for he is fashioned from them. Therefore, if he consists of them, he shall also live from them, and he shall die in them and from them—not from the [external] heaven. For he is not directly present to the heaven. From that which is present to him, he lives, dies, grows old, and falls ill. And to explain these things more correctly, a unique theory is needed, so that the lies of the "Opinionists" <note>original: "Opinistarum"; Paracelsus’s derogatory term for traditional academic physicians who followed Galen and Avicenna based on "opinion" rather than experimental "light of nature."</note> may be uprooted.

<margin>Man requires nourishment.</margin>
<margin>Man is more imperfect than other growing things.</margin>
The four internal Elements which must give fruit to man are sustained by the external ones. We must speak of this sustenance. First of all, man needs to eat and drink so that what was created may remain. For he is more imperfect than other growing things. Just as this food and drink are visible, so, on the other hand, all the other members "eat" invisibly from external sources. For just as the sun draws [moisture] upward from us, so we draw from the sun downward.

<margin>Magnetic force, etc.</margin>
For this is a <term>Magnetic force</term> <note>Paracelsus believed the body acted like a magnet, attracting vital spiritual "food" from the atmosphere and stars.</note>, which is prefigured for us in the Lodestone, so that we may know how visible things attract by an invisible power. In this way, the members of our body are also constituted so that they attract what is suitable for them. For it is not the stomach alone, but every individual member that feeds itself invisibly like a stomach, just as the stomach feeds visibly. The Physician must have full knowledge of this invisible process.

<margin>The food of the earth is dew, etc.</margin>
Dew and rain fall visibly upon the earth. Now, that which falls visibly becomes like the food of the stomach. For the visible things offered to the earth are the cooked food and drink from both heavens, ingested into the stomach of the earth. However, these things do not yet suffice for the knowledge of dissolution. For many things rot and are corrupted even without these causes—a fact which has misled many Physicians. What, then, is it that is dissolved and is simultaneously invisible?

<margin>What and where is the kitchen of heaven?</margin>
It is surely the "kitchen of the heaven": from which our members draw their nourishment by a magnetic force of this kind. And this is the cause of the disease, if it is "cooked" in such a way. For bread is not the only food of man, but the same is sought also from this kitchen, no less than from the bread itself. And in this kitchen is born the plague and diseases similar to it. He who does not know the invisible, and takes the invisible for the visible, has a maimed understanding of the cause. For God is more wonderful in hidden things than in seen or visible things. But these things are too "Astronomical" <note>In this context, "astronomical" refers to the influence of the stars on human health, or medical astrology.</note>: for which reason I commit the rest to that Philosophy. What pertains to this matter has now been sufficiently declared.

### THE MATTER.

<margin>Every Element consists of three things. The solution of Salt is dropsy.</margin>
Every Element consists of three things: in <term>Mercury</term>, <term>Sulphur</term>, and <term>Salt</term> <note>These are the "Tria Prima" or three primary principles of Paracelsian alchemy, representing volatility (Mercury), flammability/soul (Sulphur), and stability/body (Salt).</note>. Thus there are 4 Mercuries, 4 Sulphurs, and 4 Salts. We shall speak of Salt now. If it is liquefied, dropsy occurs. The other two—Sulphur and Mercury—are omitted here. For they do not pertain to this disease. Now then: Salt is the "body of the body," and it occupies the third part of the body of the <term>Microcosm</term> <note>The "Little World," a standard term for the human being as a reflection of the "Macrocosm" or universe.</note>. Salt preserves that body from rot, from stench, and from dissolution. For it is the <term>Balsam</term> <note>The natural preservative fluid or "internal salt" that prevents the body from decaying while alive.</note> which guards the <term>Mummy</term> <note>original: "Mumiam"; the vital life-force or "essential grease" inherent in human tissues that maintains health.</note> of the body.

<margin>The power of Salt. Salt is the Balsam of the Mummy.</margin>
Just as all things in man are subject to dissolution—not by themselves, but through other things—so salt alone has a dissolution leading to this sickness, which comes from the "Celestial <term>Archeitras</term>" <note>From "Archeus," the internal alchemist or vital governor of the body; here the "Celestial Archeitras" is the external cosmic equivalent.</note>, that is, the Kitchen. That is to say: if an influence with a "concordance" touches the Microcosm (which at this time is the subject) and impresses its impression upon it—and that impression happens to be of Venus or Gemini—then the person who is struck at this turn has their salt resolved.

<margin>Dropsy occurs when the salt...</margin>
So now dropsy begins, according to how the influence is graded and exalted in its power. This has dazzled the eyes of many physicians. This "impression" dissolves the salt just as the Sun melts snow. For the powers of the impressions are like the sun, while our bodies are like snow. Thus the superior things play upon the inferior things. And here the foundation for speaking about dropsy is laid: namely, concerning this sun and this snow—that is, the heaven and the salt of the Microcosm—how this solution comes to be.

### THE FABRICATION.

<margin>Zedos, the dropsical star.</margin>
In this manner, therefore, the Sun—that is, the dropsical star <term>Zedos</term> <note>A specific Paracelsian term for a celestial influence or "star" that triggers the melting of bodily salts.</note>—rises and enters into the types of salt, and takes away much or little from them, according to how the salts are disposed, whether tender or soft, etc. That is, according to how the age [of the person], following the nature of that Microcosmic salt prepared for it, has made "snow" of itself in its own time.

<margin>How dropsy occurs.</margin>
If this salt is irradiated by <term>Zedos</term>, a portion of it is eliquated or dissolved. and since man stands upright according to his form, therefore those things sink and glide downward through the pores of the flesh and excite a swelling, according as the regions are more or less filled, from the lowest to the highest, until they reach the region of the heart and the center of life.

<margin>The spirit of Salt penetrates metal.</margin>
Since the spirit of salt is a penetrator of metals, and the subtle spirit of vitriol and alum: it penetrates the region of life through the capsule of the heart, just as the Sun penetrates through glass. This "drenching" <note>original: "pelluminatio"; literally a thorough lighting or soaking through.</note> is death, which the concomitant signs of death indicate. In this way, the spirit of salt strangles the life of man, which is nothing but a rotted thing. For when a flood of water occurs, and life is hidden in the center of man: it happens that the water overwhelms that place and suffocates the life, not unlike how a headlong rush of waves overwhelms and suffocates a house and all its inhabitants.

### CONTRARIES.

<margin>Opinion-mongers.</margin>
Many new things constantly occur to the Opinionists if they take up a meditation on diseases in their unexplored and uncertain Philosophy. The same also...
