This also occurs in cases of dropsy, for which those who laboriously exhaust themselves assign the blame to the liver, to an intemperate diet, and to similar causes. Yet none of these is the cause of dropsy unless the aforementioned "concordance" <note>Paracelsus refers to a "concordance" or alignment between the microcosm (the human body) and the macrocosm (the heavens).</note> also occurs. For outside of that alignment, no dropsy is produced. Indeed, if the causes they smear across full books to assert were true, this disease would certainly be more frequent and common in spotted dogs. Since this is not the case, it is certainly clear that they occupy themselves with empty opinions, which they can easily use to persuade their listeners.

<margin>Reprimand of physicians.</margin>
The point is that nothing here ought to be considered in isolation. For the nature of man behaves in one way and then another. Therefore, in one person nature expels much food, which is good; in another, it is otherwise, for the nature is not "diaphoretic" <note>term: diaphoretic: inducing perspiration or the outward flow of fluids.</note>. Likewise, in one person it excites vomiting, while in another less so, because they do not have a "vomit-prone" nature. And so it goes for the rest. You, therefore, must let Mercury operate according to its own custom and nature. Mercury possesses such industry and property in moving a man that no one among all physicians can sufficiently know or fish it out. Therefore, those who say a patient must be cured through sweats or vomiting are acting foolishly. For they do not look toward the manifold variety of men, nor do they consider that such things should not be the focus in medicine; rather, medicine itself must be entrusted to Theory.

-> **THE CURE.** <-

<margin>In what the cure of dropsy consists.</margin>
**T**he cure consists in Maturation and Re-congealing. Then, it consists in ensuring that the cured person is preserved in that state of congealing. To this end, the science of Astronomy serves first; then, the Philosophy of the earth; and finally, Alchemical preparation, without which nothing can be successfully obtained.

<margin>Rebis, dove dung, chicken dung: how to use them further.</margin>
The nature of "Resolution" <note>Resolution: the process by which a solid (like salt) turns into a liquid, which Paracelsus sees as the root of dropsical swelling.</note> is so constituted that it must be taken from dungs, as much as you see necessary for the resolution. For there is more in **Rebis** <note>original: "Rebis": an alchemical term often meaning a "dual thing," but here referring to a specific prepared substance, likely derived from human excrement in this context.</note> than in **Columbinum** <note>original: "Columbinum": dove or pigeon dung.</note>; similarly, in false dropsies, there is more in **Gallinaceum** <note>original: "Gallinaceum": chicken dung.</note> than in the others. For this reason, cow dung, sheep dung, and others also have their differences. But these must be learned from daily reading, where these things are encountered everywhere.

<margin>What maturation is in dropsy and of what kind?</margin>
Maturation means that the disease has been "resolved" <note>broken down into a fluid state.</note>. For unless it is resolved, it is not taken up by the dropsy-medicine. The method of Maturation, however, is that the thing to be resolved first becomes Mucilage, then a sticky substance, then **Bothin** <note>A Paracelsian term for a specific morbid discharge or abscess-like state.</note>, and so on, passing from one to another until it becomes water. If it has become water, it is then the right time to attack it—that is, when the swelling is at its greatest. As for Re-congealing: if the water has overflowed and the salt is congealed, care must be taken that it is preserved in its congealing until full and perfect drying. For just as **Beryl** <note>original: "Berillus": a gemstone. Paracelsus believed certain gems grew from the "congealing" of liquids like ice.</note> is born from ice if the limit of congealing is reached, so the same must happen here.

<margin>Preparation of Mercury.</margin>
<margin>How Mercury and quicksilver differ.</margin>
The condition of Mercury is that it must be precipitated in its own ore, and the "dead" part separated from it. For in this way, it is not "quicksilver" <note>original: "argentum vivum": literally "living silver," the raw liquid metal.</note>, but truly **Mercury**. For dead is Mercury; living is quicksilver. If, therefore, it has been "mortified" <note>killed or chemically altered to remove its toxic or volatile raw state.</note> according to the prescribed method of preparation, its dose is two grains, following the process taught by the school, which should not be included in the text.

<margin>What re-congealing is in dropsy.</margin>
<margin>Beryl from ice.</margin>
<margin>The resolved is not congealed again.</margin>
That which has been resolved, however, does not take up congealing again—just as melted snow does not become what it was before. If, therefore, salt must return to its congealed state, it must be done according to astronomical instruction. Just as today there is snow which is resolved, but after a year the time for snow arrives again. Therefore, when this term returns or is brought back, dropsy receives its full cure, and not sooner. Even if you had removed all the water, if this time of congealing poured out new salt just as it pours new snow, the cure would certainly be imperfect. Thus, the time of resolution gives the beginning of the cure. But the time of new congealing by the stars is the end of the cure. Thus the time is finished and the cure is perfected according to the natural circuit, which the sphere encompasses through the true motion of heaven, not through the course of imperfect medicine.

<margin>Tincture of Mars dries.</margin>
It is also the use and custom that in the intervening time, the Tincture of Mars <note>Iron-based medicine.</note> is administered as **Anth. SS. S.** <note>Likely "Anthera Solis" or a similar solar-themed chemical preparation.</note>. These are established for the sake of a more exquisite drying. For they dry through evacuation no differently than the Sun dries a washed linen cloth. And this stands as the end and true sign of congealing.

<margin>Hellebore alkali and the Quintessence are useful in dropsy.</margin>
Note here also that many other things perform well in cases of dropsy, such as the Alkali of Hellebore, the Quintessence of Hellebore, and so on. For they contain within them a certain "mercurial power" by which they operate. Yet all these must be led toward the complete cure—that is, toward Precipitated Mercury. For the "experiments" <note>In this context, "experiments" refers to specific tested remedies rather than the modern scientific method.</note> we have mentioned induce no congealing; hence they are nothing but naked aids, unless it should happen that through Mars, Sulphur, etc., a subsequent congealing is found—though this is always found to be ambiguous. Therefore, the "appropriated Arcanum" <note>term: Arcanum: a secret, powerful chemical remedy that targets the essence of a disease.</note> must be chiefly employed here by the physician.

<margin>The cure of dropsy is twofold. External through dungs.</margin>
The cure exists in two parts: one external, which dissolves the mucilaginous matter, and the other internal, which expels. The external remedies are the dungs. And although other things can also be applied, they are not as convenient for assisting the internal medicine, but must be applied only by themselves—which, however, makes the cure weaker. For one medicine should always agree with the other; they should not each act on their own, but all should conspire together as one.

Now, if the nature of the "false rain" or "storm" falling into the Microcosm <note>The human body.</note> through **Euryalean** <note>Referring to the power of the East Wind (Eurus) or a specific elemental force in Paracelsian meteorology.</note> force is such that it resolves the salts of that part into which it distills: it is necessary to know that this impression is an attractive **Realgaric** spirit <note>term: Realgaric: relating to Realgar (arsenic sulfide), which Paracelsus associated with a sharp, corrosive, or poisonous spiritual quality that causes substances to break down.</note>. For it is that spirit which has the power to resolve salt. Just as the Milky Way by its nature produces winters, so also diseases happen from the property of the stated "impressions." The fault lies in the "cooking" of the food—not indeed the visible food, but the corporeal, invisible food which is just as much a body as the visible food, the "ascendant" of which body comes from the Planets...

<margin>Internal through Mercury.</margin>
The medicine which is taken internally is Mercury. For it is powerful and excellent for extracting the resolved salt and restoring the true and genuine salt. To these is added a "comfortative" <note>A strengthening agent.</note> according to the condition of the person, their age, sex, and the quantity and quality of the disease. This will be **Diaphoretic Gold** <note>A medicinal preparation of gold intended to promote sweating and balance.</note>.

<margin>Diaphoretic gold as a strengthening agent for dropsy.</margin>
Concerning the operation of the Medicine, it must be known...

<header>ON DROPSY.</header>

The Moon is the planet where the zodiacal influences come to rest, since they only govern the physical, sensible body.

<margin>The philosophy of humors is worthless. <note>original: Humorũ philofophia nauci est.</note></margin>
Therefore, if the celestial influence falls in such a way, the ancient physicians might rightly say that dropsy is an incurable disease. In any other case, their reasoning lacked all foundation. From this it follows that Medicine must belong entirely to this influence, so that one influence may stand against another within the <term>Three Primes</term> <note>The three fundamental principles of Paracelsian chemistry: Mercury (spirit/liquidity), Sulfur (soul/combustibility), and Salt (body/solidity).</note> on both sides. However, he who strives to purge the humors here will arrive "after the feast" (as they say) <note>meaning: too late</note>; he will let the proper opportunity slip from his hands, and will finally strike his arrow directly against steel. For the "resolution" and coagulation of the body are not caused by humors, but demonstrate their own internal Sovereignty. The "Moon" of Mercury is considered in both influences. For the least of all things is the philosophy of complexions—those which they call hot, cold, moist, dry, or mixed. The greatest of all, however, is that which is above it: namely, the <term>Olympus</term> <note>Paracelsus uses "Olympus" to refer to the celestial or ethereal virtues that influence the human microcosm.</note> of heavenly virtues. These maintain a similar and formless anatomy within their spheres and virtues of exaltation—even the horoscope itself, the day, and the hour with all their ascendants—just like the visible body, but within their own heavenly nature and ethereal course. He who discovers this "heaven" has found the cure for dropsy.

<margin>What is the physician’s heaven?</margin>
For a healthy man is a "heaven," made so by a Physician who does not try to grasp the sky above him in his hands, but rather seeks the drying Sun within the Womb <note>The "Matrix" or internal origin of the disease.</note>, and the fire that meets it within the Sulfur. For the Element creates Suns, and Saffron <note>Often used in Paracelsian alchemy to represent a specific corporeal power or color.</note> gives corporeal operations. However, the overcoming of what has been dissolved is an expulsion performed by Mercury, which precedes the other two principles, just as Lucifer <note>The Morning Star (Venus).</note> precedes the Sun. For Life, placed in the center, perhaps could not endure until this point of parching and drying out if the influence remained in its "exaltation," unless perhaps a path had been built beforehand through preparations. This is done by the Sun alone, without the Mercurial expulsion. Let the judgment for discerning these things rest with you.

<margin>Urine and pulse indicate nothing in dropsy.</margin>
Beyond the signs mentioned above, the Physician should propose no others for himself. For whatever signs of death or life are detected in the urine, the pulse, or similar things, they are to be considered worthless. It is true that when death stands before the doors and the disease grows more seriously powerful, the urine is stained. This is because the Salt, which separates itself from the Mercury and Sulfur, gives a redness. Since this frequently happened, and the "Opinionist" Physicians knew nothing else, they sometimes noticed death following shortly thereafter; they took it as an absolute sign of fatality, which is nevertheless regarded as a sign of life by one who is skilled in medicine.

<margin>The irregularity of the pulse comes from nature's effort, not death.</margin>
So too in dropsy: many predict death from the pulse, which ought to trouble only fools. For it is nature’s laborious effort, not death, that produces the irregularity of the pulse. To this end God created medicine: so that these things might be turned away, and men might not be driven headlong into despair, but might instead learn from it the coarseness and ignorance of [unskilled] Physicians. The greatest sign of death is that which we have spoken of: concerning the "spirit of salt," which penetrates and breaks through the capsule of the heart, just as a wind blows through a wall.

<margin>The cracking of the skin is from the sharpness of salt.</margin>
But even a rupture or a fissure in the body is not, by itself, a sign of death. For that which is split open comes neither from death nor from fullness, but from the sharpness of the salt which eats away by the property of its own nature.

<margin>Nature’s zeal in expelling harmful things.</margin>
Therefore, signs of death ought to be taken from dead things, not from living things—that is, not from the operations of the living. For Nature, everywhere in the body, strives to create exits, paths, and boundaries for the preservation of man. But that which she builds for the benefit and health of man, you say leads to death, when it actually signifies life.

<margin>A diet should not be prescribed in dropsy.</margin>
If I were to wish to prescribe a diet, saying "eat this, or that; drink this, avoid that," I would burn a certain stain into Nature itself. For he who deals and works with <term>Arcana</term> <note>Powerful, hidden healing essences extracted from nature.</note> considers it a shame to command a diet. Prescribing a diet here is not the task of the Physician, but of the patient himself and his own faculties. Medicine and the *Arcanum* take the place of the Physician’s prescribed diet.

<margin>True medicine is free of dung; food is the opposite.</margin>
Conversely, he who clings to diets is weak in his art; he makes medicine out of cabbage, unmindful that dung is made from it. That is, he simply does not taste or understand that Medicine, in itself, contains no dung. That which has dung is food, and is owed to the stomach and to "hungry diseases." In the same way, the consideration of the air and the "six non-natural things" (as they call them) <note>A traditional Galenic concept referring to factors like air, sleep, diet, and exercise that affect health.</note> contributes nothing in this disease. For invisible bodies have no kinship with these things. He who is skilled knows this. But he who is unskilled sews hempen rags onto silks, so that even from this one thing he might seem to be able to know something.

***

## ON ARIDURA.
<note>Aridura: A Paracelsian term for atrophy, consumption, or the wasting away of the limbs and body.</note>

Ignorance of the cause of this and other diseases has given birth to various names, all of which are irrelevant and indicators of the Physicians' ignorance. For there is only one single cause of *Aridura*. However, because the signs are often different—varying and diverse, just as the locations found are diverse—various names were given to this disease by the unskilled based on those signs. By this occasion it also happened that, for the variety of signs, various medicines were subsequently designated, even though the true cause and the disease were not multiple. From this, confusion cannot help but arise, which has followed especially in the case of *Aridura*. Therefore, we shall retain the word *Aridura* in this chapter. If any distinction is needed, the difference should not be sought from the name, but rather should be taken from the location itself. The location separates the cure—that is, it divides the process, the administration, the application, and the other things that must be distinguished.

What *Aridura* actually is, and when it occurs, must be known from external signs through the art of the eyes. For there is another knowledge of the internal kind, unknown to many. The external signs are known both to the patient and to all his family and bystanders, and should be sought from them. For this external evidence is especially necessary for any Physician.

<margin>The external signs are notable.</margin>
For external things testify about internal things; they exist as a kind of fruit from which the tree itself and its nature are known. The fruits of this tree are these: the consumption of the flesh, the increase of the blood <note>likely meaning a perceived thickening or heat in the blood</note>, the wasting away of the calves (*surae*) and the muscles of the arms below and above the elbow, and in the feet, below and above the knees, a dry cough, the alternation of heat and cold, thirst...

<summary>This page concludes Paracelsus's theory on dropsy, rejecting traditional diagnostics like pulse and urine in favor of understanding celestial and chemical influences (salt, mercury, and sulfur), before introducing "Aridura" (wasting disease) as a condition diagnosed through external physical decay.</summary>

...unquenchable thirst, natural hunger, suppression of sweat, urine, and bowel movements. Through this disease, the proportion, measure, weight, and distance of the soft <term>coagulation</term> <note>The process by which bodily fluids are formed into solid tissues like flesh and bone.</note> is consumed—in the flesh, the marrow, and in all members of the external and internal regions (that is, in the hands and feet, and what is contained within them). Sometimes diverse signs also accompany it, such as a powerful cough with much discharge, or a swelling of the veins, or frequent bowel movements. All these are peculiar signs of those members which are more severely afflicted by aridura than the others. Thus, a vehement cough with the excretion of pus indicates that the lungs are being tested by this evil. Copious urination testifies that the <term>tenes</term> <note>Likely referring to the pelvic region or bladder area</note> and liver are troubled. Painful piercings in the sides reveal that the liver and spleen are laboring. Tears of the eyes, vertigo, <term>cardialgia</term> <note>Heartburn or pain in the upper stomach/heart region</note> and so on, indicate the head. And indeed, there are almost as many kinds of these accompanying signs as there are members in the body. However, all these are not properly signs of aridura itself, but only of the members laboring more severely, or of those afflicted by other diseases complicated with aridura, which now break out together through the wasting, having otherwise lain hidden and suppressed for a long time. Here, therefore, diligent caution is needed.

<margin>
Aridura in specific parts stirs up more pain.
The pain of Aridura varies by the nature of the subject. What are the distinctive signs of Aridura?
</margin>

Furthermore, it should be noted that aridura sometimes becomes particular, while only one member—whether internal or external—is afflicted. And the signs of this are much more manifest, such as the aridura of the marrow or of the "glue" <note>synovia or vital binding fluids</note>. For these cause unique pains compared to others because of the peculiar sensitivity flourishing in these humors and others. For one kind of pain exists in the blood, another in the marrow, another in the bones, another in the nerves, another in the flesh, and so on. However, the cause must be sought not from the pain, but from the aridura. Pain, truly, is the index of its own member. You, however, shall observe this distinction: that universal aridura consumes the whole body without pain; particular aridura, however, has pain as its companion. And although there is indeed one cause for both which stirs up all pains, yet here is the distinction between aching and not aching. In the absence of pain, an <term>anodyne</term> <note>pain-killing</note> and numbing cause concurs; this is absent in the presence of pain, as is clear from the knowledge of the cause.

<margin>
How Aridura occurs.
The elements agree with one another.
</margin>

The reasoning of the cause exists as follows. You see, surely, that the earth does not dry itself out as much as the sky does, which provides the Sun and the winds. For the four Elements are so united among themselves that they do not, of course, burden each other. That is, the water, the sea, and the rivers perform similar operations upon the earth entirely as the earth in turn bears itself toward them. In the same way, air and fire also behave toward these same things. The Elements, therefore, can no more inflict diseases upon each other than a house constructed of various and diverse things can hurt itself, if all things contain themselves in their proper place. The earth, therefore, remains in its native temperature because the water itself also preserves the same temperature within itself; and thus similarly also the air and the fire. Therefore, while they remain in their temperature, they enjoy their native strength and do not fail. But as for why it might fail, the sky causes this. Yet the same sky afterwards repairs this defect with rains, dew, and the like.

<margin>
The liquor of the Earth, etc. Aridura is the life of it. <note>original: Aridura ipsius vita.</note>
</margin>

Now, truly, the earth has a certain native liquor, and one proper to itself, so inherent that it is like color adhering to a thing, which cannot be separated from it. Yet you see colors taken away and extracted from bodies, which happens through the fiery Element if it comes forth into its action. This action is the daily exercise in the <term>firmament</term> <note>The sphere of the stars and heavens.</note>, that is, in the <term>ascendant</term> <note>The astrological point rising on the eastern horizon.</note>: just as cloth whitens in the Sun and loses its yellowness; or Saturn is whitened in the Sun and loses its blackness, and so on. Therefore, just as colors are wonderfully taken away and extracted by invisible yet corporeal things, so too is this disposition of the earth affected, so that it loses its liquor extracted through the firmamental force of the Sun and the winds, and not through the Elemental virtue (though the operation is uniform). For fire breaks both bodies and colors. By a similar reasoning, the operation of the firmament also exhausts and breaks this body and its liquid. For where this liquid of the earth does not remain, there its body is broken.

<margin>
Earth's dissolution is the deprivation of liquor.
</margin>

Now furthermore, man himself is earth. For his body, or that which withers, is earth.
Moreover, the earth lives in its liquor, just as it has its defined hardness, so does its wood and its herb. In the same way, multiple types of hardness exist in the
<margin>
Man is earth.

From which it now follows that the element of fire in the <term>Microcosm</term> <note>The human being, viewed as a miniature reflection of the universe.</note> cannot consume the liquid without the dissolution of the body. For if the Elemental fire were kindled and set itself to the consumption of this liquid, then it would destroy its own body no differently than wood; this would then be <term>Persian Fire</term> <note>original: ignis Persicus; historically referring to shingles, anthrax, or erysipelas—a corrosive, burning skin disease.</note> and the like, which we have not set out to treat here. 

<margin>
What is Persian fire?
</margin>
The distinction, therefore, is placed in this: that the active elemental fire finishes and consumes the body itself together with the liquid; but the consumption of the firmament ends only in drying and parching, with the body itself left behind—which is nevertheless the same as if it were dead or dissolved, once that distinction we made has been observed. For the Sun attracts

For just as the blood, flesh, and fat of a man are sustained, increased, or even diminished by food and drink, so also does that liquor sustain the earth, as that which exists as the seed of its power and growth. Therefore, if the earth does not receive this liquor, whatever it has and brings forth withers and perishes. The same is to be judged of the Microcosm also, who is prefigured through the exterior world, because he has a similar nature and reasoning with it. Man, therefore, has his own liquor of his coagulated earth, defined in every part, just as his coagulation requires. For the nature and manner of that coagulation is preserved through its own liquor. Because man is the Microcosm, the operation of the firmament in him is no different than it is outwardly in the earth. If, therefore, the inclination of the influence should bring about an attraction to strip the liquid from the man, [it begins] extracting...

# ON ARIDURA #

...and must be extracted, and if rain is denied: then from the knowledge of Astronomy and Philosophy, boldly affirm that <term>aridura</term> <note>Latin: a withering or wasting of the body; similar to atrophy or consumption.</note> is occurring in the man.

<margin>Knowledge of the Microcosm and macrocosm is very necessary for the Physician.</margin>
For man has need of rain, as the earth itself does; that is, by the invisible rain sustaining the <term>Microcosm</term> <note>The "small world"—the human being seen as a reflection of the entire universe.</note>. And unless the Physician knows the Microcosm so intimately that he can unite it with the heaven, just as the earth is united with it: in this case he will have profited little. For the cure depends entirely upon this knowledge. If indeed the body enjoys this rain and liquor, then the Microcosm remains whole and unharmed, bearing the fruit of health, not of disease. If this is to be achieved, it is necessary to obtain it through such a cure that can compel the heaven and the "rainy stars." For by these stars that liquor is increased and preserved, insofar as it is of use to the earth. And this is the Philosophy of the Stars of the lower heaven, which is placed in the hand of the Physician.

<margin>Causes of Aridura.</margin>
If therefore the sphere were directed in the way already mentioned, so that those things ascending struck each other; it would happen that both the <term>firmament</term> <note>The "heavens" or the driving celestial force within the human body.</note> would not bring forth its rains, and its attractive virtue would meanwhile continue to operate: then necessarily aridura and drying out would threaten the man. For there is (so to speak) a firmament of raining, and a firmament of drying out, and they are two separate things.

<margin>Drying is the death of the superfluous.</margin>
Drying out therefore occurs when the superfluous does not remain, but is separated from the good: which is the death of the superfluous. For example, let us suppose it rains. Now, not all rain is good, but there is scarcely a small amount of good in it. What is not good is dried up by the sun. This drying is to be understood like the stomach, which separates the dung from the good. Meanwhile, when the rain does not fall, the Sun nonetheless dries continually and constantly.

<margin>The power of digestion is constant.</margin>
Similarly also the body: if a man does not eat, the power of digestion continues to work nonetheless. And if it does not have external material to act upon, then by digesting it acts upon itself. That digestion is an operation. In the same way, the Sun also imitates its firmamental operations and continually dries. If rain is present, the Sun subdues it. If not, the power of drying does not cease for that reason, but hunts for liquor everywhere. If that liquor has already vanished, it acts by continuous operation upon what remains, until everything is absorbed and exhausted.

<margin>The Middle Heaven is the Physician’s tool.</margin>
Therefore, that which makes the rain is something else. And this must be entirely attended to in the cure: that we place that heaven in our hands, that is, the <term>Middle Heaven</term> <note>The restorative or balancing influence the physician applies to the patient's internal "atmosphere."</note>, and no other. And although many have carried this heaven in their hands, they could not handle it otherwise than peasants handle a physical globe, while they turn it now up, now down, now forward.

<margin>Peasants are unskilled with the globe.</margin>
For as they understand the matter, they place Jerusalem where Granada lies, and they locate Judea where Naples is placed. Such is their science. To which that of the ancient physicians was not dissimilar. Just as <term>Cosmography</term> <note>The mapping of the earth and the universe.</note> proposes the globe of the earth, so also Astronomy proposes the globe of Medical science. Therefore, the pole must be correctly directed, if you do not wish to wander from the path. For just as a driver moderates the horses drawing the chariot wherever he wishes by his art: so you also must drive, so that you have the reason, knowledge, and power over your sphere, whose stars you wish to use against the upper heaven. For this is the way and the goal you must tread. And just as a driver cannot leap over brambles and mountainous places with his chariot: neither can you do so with yours. Therefore that is the science which proceeds from the <term>light of nature</term> <note>Paracelsus's term for the innate wisdom found by observing the natural world directly.</note>, not from empty speculation, which exists as the sterile part of all science.

<margin>The Firmament gives life to and preserves all things.</margin>
Thus everything is grown and sustained from the Firmament, which Philosophy embraces not only in the Macrocosm, but also in the Microcosm. Therefore, from a defect of the rain itself, and the power of the Astronomical separation made by the Sun, this disease arises. On the other hand, diseases can also arise from excessive and immoderate rain, when the Firmament of the Sun cannot sufficiently dry and separate them. From this, excessive humidity follows, just as immoderate dryness follows from the opposite. This immoderate moistening causes an inflating tumor, but by no means <term>dropsy</term> <note>Edema or swelling caused by excess fluid.</note>. However, it is judged as such by many. Although this kind of swelling brought on by immoderate rain may also admit the cure for dropsy. Yet one must attend diligently so that after its expulsion, aridura does not follow. To avoid this, you must consume the rain exquisitely. If you exceed the degree of consumption, you give the Sun a pretext for consuming the genuine liquor. According to this, therefore, you must moderate the cure. This must be emphasized here: for both too much and too little give birth to diseases.

<margin>Obstruction is not the cause of aridura.</margin>
Furthermore, one thing still remains to be known here, which is fabricated as a cause by our adversaries. These "Opinionists" do not understand what they mean. They object, for instance, that the cause of Aridura is the <term>obstruction</term> <note>Latin: "oppilatio"; a blockage.</note> of the passages or ways, because through this the nourishment of the limbs is prevented from passing. We respond that some aridura happens this way. But we are not speaking of that aridura here. For that aridura is in the same condition as if some limb or ligament or artery, etc., were cut in half, so that the nourishment could not travel to the further parts.

<margin>Consumption and dryness differ.</margin>
This, however, is not consumption, but dryness, and the limb is called dry, not consumed; nor does it have any other Philosophy than obstruction or incision, which are one and the same. See how far the cure which ought to be instituted in a wound or obstruction is from the cure of true consumption. Therefore, they are distant by long intervals.

<margin>What is truly called Aridura?</margin>
For that is not aridura where the transit is precluded because of an obstruction: but it is called aridura where that which ought to pass is missing.

<margin>The Humors are not the cause of aridura.</margin>
By the same reasoning, those <term>Humorists</term> <note>Physicians who believed all disease came from an imbalance of the four bodily fluids: blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile.</note> might object that the cause of this disease descends from the humors. Why this is so is clear. Yet the manifestation of error in this is: that where humors finally are, there also moistening thrives: and where there is moistening, there is no dryness. Here, however, the humors are superfluous. I would indeed greatly hope that a certain distinction be observed in the humors: so that where dryness occurs,

# ON WITHERING #

...let it be removed; where there is humidity, let it be treated in its own way, as much as possible. But to speak fundamentally about humors:
<margin>What is a humor?</margin>
A humor is nothing other than dissolved water, which has left its coagulation and is to be expelled from the body. Thus, it would be called something much different than a "humor," unless perhaps that name were attributed to the body from which it was dissolved—of which there are certainly more than four, not according to temperaments <note>Latin: *complexiones*; the traditional Galenic system of four humors (blood, phlegm, etc.).</note>, but according to natures and properties, which pay very little heed to temperaments. They [the traditional doctors], however, derived them from the Elements. How well they stand with those will be examined in due time, when we investigate this error more thoroughly. For according to how they define them, <term>Marasmus</term> <note>A progressive wasting or emaciation of the body.</note> arises from them, not consumption.
<margin>Causes distinguish diseases, not the eyes. Knowledge is the ruler of the eyes.</margin>
Therefore, diseases ought to be distinguished by their causes, not by appearance. For it is not the role of the eyes to pronounce "this is this, and that is that"; rather, knowledge alone defines what a thing is. The eyes, therefore, ought to proceed from knowledge, not knowledge from the eyes, over which a <term>glaucoma</term> <note>Used here metaphorically to mean a deceptive veil or medical ignorance.</note> is often pulled. They say of Poets that they usually make things up. So too do our "humorists" <note>Physicians who follow the traditional humoral theory.</note> diligently make things up, yet they do not compose verses. They know everything else otherwise. Indeed.

<margin>Particular and universal withering are distinguished by pain.</margin>
Furthermore, <term>aridura</term> <note>A pathological drying or wasting of the body; from the Latin *aridus* (dry).</note> also brings on a sickness in which "Febrile Ascendants" can easily gain and achieve their passage. From this it happens that patients are often tested by febrile paroxysms. We will say nothing of those fevers here. For this is another disease. Its cause is described in the chapter on fevers. Meanwhile, the withering nonetheless continues and grows stronger. And if it has become "particular" <note>Localized to one part of the body.</note>, it is betrayed by pains. In "universal" <note>Affecting the whole body.</note> withering there is no pain. For in this, a numbing quality concurs. 
<margin>Withering is precisely Saturn.</margin>
However, every instance of total withering is placed under the sphere of Saturn, and takes from it its condition, property, duration, nature, and power, and it loses its own sphere, ascendant, and constellation. But because of this, no Physician can say that such a patient is "cold and dry" (for this would be too crude); rather, say that he is Saturnine. Afterward, his nature must be recognized and presented in the condition of earthly bodies, as far as the physical body <note>Latin: *corpus Physicum*</note> is concerned. Their condition is good, and they recover by themselves, whose Saturn has finished or departed. For them, a new heaven arises, from which there is an entry to a long life. Yet Saturn departs from these people with difficulty; instead, he makes and keeps them thin and dry for a long time. For he "cooks" the foods of the beginning. If no account is taken of this in offering help, certainly no other cure is present. For he alone does this—not a humor, not a temperament, or anything similar. Therefore, there are two paths of cure. One consists in giving "rain," administered from the middle heaven, which the upper heaven extracts according to a similar sphere and harmony.
<margin>Why was the Physician created?</margin>
For that God created the Physician is not merely for his person's sake, but so that he might hold the heaven in his hand, which makes the Physician perfect. If that "rainy star" is known, then the Medicine is at hand. 
<margin>The double cure of withering.</margin>
The second path is that Saturn be overcome, and the <term>Microcosm</term> <note>The human being as a reflection of the universe.</note> be snatched from his power and placed into another sphere.

Whichever of these twin cures is applied, it alone suffices for the healing. The first is used by the Astronomer of the lower Olympus; the second by the Astronomer of the upper Olympus. Let every Philosopher, however, be of his own profession, and finally a Physician founded upon it.

<margin>First</margin>
First, the Sun which dries out cannot be removed or taken away, for it is inborn and implanted. Therefore, rain is needed. For the upper heaven cannot be forced or restrained otherwise, unless something similar is replaced from the lower heaven in turn. Thus the Sun of the upper heaven remains, but the rain is of the lower heaven. For it is impossible for this [rain] to be obtained from the upper heaven. Therefore, we must discuss this <term>Arcanum</term> <note>A hidden or secret remedy; a concentrated medicinal power.</note>. 
<margin>Look above at the text on folio 51.</margin> *

<margin>Second</margin>
The other medicine, for raising and lifting the Saturn of man, must be understood such that it is brought about that he is no longer who he was. For by this, man is withdrawn from the sphere of Saturn in this way: that a transplantation of one into another occurs, just as a peach tree into a willow, and similar things. If, therefore, a man is to be transplanted—taken out from under one Planet and subjected to another—then <term>Antimony</term> <note>A mineral used in alchemy and medicine to purge impurities and effect transformation.</note> is suitable for achieving this, which transforms Saturn into Venus. 
<margin>Antimony transmutes Saturn into Venus.</margin>
Through this secret, the man is rendered "Venereal" [belonging to Venus], and he receives another ascendant, which he follows. Therefore, Antimony is the cure in "hectic" <note>Latin: *Ethicâ*, likely a corruption of *Hectica*, referring to wasting fever.</note> disease, which transplants the star of Saturn into Venus. These are the hidden things of the art. And just as <term>Bolus</term> <note>A type of medicinal earth or clay.</note> transplants the star of Mercury into Saturn, 
<margin>Bolus transplants Mercury into Saturn.</margin>
so in the same way all stars in the middle heaven can be transplanted. And although (as usually happens) the root of the removed star remains, the transplantation nevertheless flourishes and persists in that by which the man lives, not in the root. For the fruits rule the roots, not the roots the fruits. Thus, therefore, 6 Planets are implanted into Saturn, 6 into Venus, 6 into Mercury, 6 into Mars, 6 into the Moon. The Sun is not transplanted, since nothing better than it can be born. From this it should be noted that in every incurable disease—if the natural order (namely contraries against contraries) profits nothing—the cure of 
<margin>Transplantation is the cure for incurable disease.</margin>
transplantation ought to be proposed and assumed. This should also be done in true <term>Morphea</term> <note>A skin disease marked by hardened patches.</note>, Leprosy, and similar things. Let us seek an example from nature itself. For if an animal, such as a serpent, has survived past the term of its sphere, death necessarily hangs over it. 
<margin>The term of heaven is the term of life.</margin>
For the term of the heaven is the term of life. But if this animal is transplanted out of its own nature and offers itself to another Planet to which it may be subject, then its life is prolonged. For of all diseases that descend the steps toward death, there is a turning away because the root remains; it is rightly 
<margin>Why it is called transplantation.</margin>
called transplantation. For it is not a "re-greening," but a new planting into an old trunk—whose fruits were adverse to the man—done so that more useful fruits might come forth. The process of this Medicine describes the preparation of these things, such as Antimony and the like. Therefore, to put the same thing twice in the same place is superfluous. Let everyone give labor to the preparation [of medicines] seen in the light and in the workshops. For they burn the place, like nettles.

<header>ON JAUNDICES.</header>

# ON JAUNDICES.

<margin>The name is a naked thing.</margin>
**J**aundices, or "diseases of <term>tincture</term>" <note>In this context, a "tincture" is an alchemical term for a substance that can penetrate and change the color or quality of another body.</note>, take their names from their colors. If the color is lemon-yellow, it is called *Aurigo* <note>original: "Aurigo," from the Latin *aurum* (gold).</note>. If the color is ash-gray, black, green, purple, and so on, the names correspond to the individual colors. However, the genuine name for all of them is *Tincture*. These various colors themselves exist as species, all contained under a single cause. Therefore, the name itself follows a single logic, whether it is given by the Greeks, the Latins, or the Germans. For anyone can give a name; it is not so easy to provide the cause. Furthermore, a name is nothing but a "naked thing" <note>An empty label that describes the appearance but not the essence.</note>. For this reason, the origin of the disease must be rightly and deservedly investigated; once this is known, the name itself can be produced and explained without difficulty.

<margin>What is a disease of tincture?</margin>
A "disease of tincture" occurs when a human being loses their native color, and this is not caused by some other primary disease—that is, if the disease exists by itself. For whether the native color turns to lemon-yellow, saffron, or gold; or into black, or any other color that is beyond nature: it is all referred to as Jaundice. It is true, of course, that natural colors are also changed through <term>dropsy</term> <note>An old term for edema or swelling caused by excess fluid.</note>, contractions, and internal abscesses. In those cases, however, a truly jaundiced color is not present; the distinction between the yellowness of dropsy and that of jaundice lies in the "grade" of the colors. In those with dropsy, the color is like pale straw, but in Jaundice, it is a deeply saturated dye.

<margin>How dyed and non-dyed colors differ.</margin>
Know, therefore, that we are dealing here with "dyed" colors. As far as these colors are poured out, they dye the face, the eyes, the ears, the arms, the nails, the fingers, and so on. Other colors that are not "dyed" do not stain further than the face and mouth, for they do not possess a wider <term>anatomy</term> <note>Here meaning the "structural reach" or path through the body.</note>. Dyed colors, however, can persuade and penetrate wherever the body is open; since they exist as a tincture, they are rightly called "dyed diseases."

<margin>Death is the mother of tinctures.</margin>
Tinctures proceed from the <term>mortification</term> <note>The localized "death" or breakdown of a specific part or substance within the living body.</note> of the body in which the colors are hidden. Just as green, saffron, black, blue, and purple colors are hidden in a seed—which no one sees until the seed dies in the earth and the Sun prepares them and brings them forth, so that what was previously invisible now becomes sensible—

<margin>Colors are united to things.</margin>
so also must it be known here that "seeds" lie hidden in the body—that is, parts exist within which a human being is composed. If one or more of these parts dies, then their death becomes the mother of colors. Now the color breaks out into its anatomy, offering to view that which was not visible before. Just as a green leaf and a yellow flower lie hidden in a black seed, so too in red blood are hidden blue, green, and yellow, which are not visible at all while the body remains whole, but only when it dies.

<margin>Decay is the cause of dyed disease.</margin>
The physician must therefore know that the seeds that constitute the <term>Microcosm</term> <note>The human being viewed as a "miniature world" that mirrors the laws of the universe.</note> ought not to rot, but should remain entirely as seeds. Their putrefaction is the cause of the disease we are discussing here. Let these be examples of this: A blow or a wound inflicted on the body kills that member. It then begins to rot. In this way, putrefaction is the manifestation of the color of that part which was struck. Blood that is drawn by bloodletting loses its color because it dissolves and rots, just like a seed in the earth. By this logic, its color breaks out. Let these examples be given of colors produced in a crude way. Jaundice, however, does not happen in this same way, but by another logic, as will be taught.

<margin>Dead tinctures rise again.</margin>
If, therefore, a dyed disease is a dead body—the body being the mother of that disease—it is next necessary to know what the logic of its generation is. How is that tincture produced in a human being which stains whatever other parts of the body it falls upon? A tincture, however, is more than those colors understood from the previous example. For those colors merely die; but these, having died, rise from death and strive toward a new generation. From this, the color is brought to life. Furthermore, any dead thing (which nevertheless becomes a seed) is subject to the Heavens, provided it lies in the earth—that is, in its Element. But that which does not lie hidden in the earth is not subject to the Heavens (we are speaking of seeds), and it rots and dies. Now, if blood or something else is dissolved in a person's body, it lies within the person and is covered by the skin—that is, it lies in its "earth." From this, therefore, the disease grows, just like a plant from the earth; not the form of the plant itself, but only its colors. Hence it happens that the cutting of that vein and location removes this kind of disease. For it was lying in that very place, as is taught by many in their cures. If, therefore, the body—that is, the blood, marrow, juice, mucus, <term>synovia</term> <note>Joint fluid.</note>, or anything else in the body—is thus dead, then the overhanging Heavens work upon it.

<margin>How the seeds of tincture are diverse.</margin>
Now, the seeds are different from one another. Those which come from the flesh or substance do not turn into any color of tincture, but remain in their places and rot there. From this arise ulcers, which are not dealt with here. But if the "juices" of the body rot, from those are made these tinctures by which the body is colored.

<margin>Tinctures are either substances or juices. How many types of body juices.</margin>
Thus, there exist two "bodies" of dyed diseases: namely, juice and substance. Juice is liquid. Substance is bone, blood, flesh, fat, etc. Furthermore, there are various juices in the body. One is a mucus, another is <term>bitumen</term> <note>A pitch-like or mineral-heavy substance; here referring to thick, dark metabolic waste.</note>, this one is oily, that one is viscous, this one is like this, that one like that. According to the condition of each, the colors are also graded, and they are led by the power of the Heavens into whatever they are inclined toward: this one into Leprosy, that one into <term>Morphea</term> <note>A skin disease causing discolored, hardened patches.</note>, another into <term>Rosacea</term> <note>original: "guttam Rosaceam," a chronic redness of the face.</note>, another into an itch, etc.; to which also belong those things that eat away at the skin, bones, and flesh.

<margin>Tinctures are corrosive.</margin>
Because they are tinctures, they are for that reason also corrosive on account of the power of salt. However, no mention of those [corrosive] diseases is made here. We are treating only of dyed diseases remaining in the body, which themselves nevertheless exist similar to the aforementioned external diseases. For internally, they also eat away and erode the members and ligaments, though they do so hiddenly and invisibly.

<margin>The Artist and the Heavens are similar.</margin>
In the same way that an Artist working in metals transforms them into other colors (and not only in metals, but in other minerals as well), so in this case the Heavens act as the Artist. One and the same art or operation is applied by both. For just as the Artist through <term>Vulcan</term> <note>The Roman god of fire; here used to mean the alchemical furnace or heat.</note>—that is, through the element of fire—cooks those things out;

<margin>The Sun is the Vulcan of the Heavens.</margin>
so the Heavens cook through the Sun, for the Sun is the Vulcan of the Heavens.

### OPPOSING SIGNS.

<margin>
The Physician should be an Astronomer and a Prognosticator.
</margin>

Not a few things must also be recounted here concerning the signs that are brought forth. Indeed, it is right for the Physician to know the signs themselves, but not as the common people are accustomed to; rather, from an Astronomical foundation. For since disease is subject to Astronomical matters—or to Astronomy—it is absolutely necessary to understand them from this source. Although the "tincture" <note>The abnormal coloring of the body in diseases like jaundice.</note> also exhibits signs, these are by no means to be held as the foundation, but they only indicate an operation already performed. The signs of a *future* operation, however, must be taken from Astronomy, without which nothing can be done. For he alone is a true Physician who knows how to indicate future operations. For present ones lie open to the eyes themselves. But those things which strike the eyes ought to have been predicted and prognosticated long ago. For this truly pertains to the Physician. By this reasoning, therefore, if vomiting, tightness of the chest, and other similar signs happen in the limbs, let these not move you to bring in another cause of the disease. For it is brought about by the nature of this or that person, which is inclined toward vomiting, toward tightness, toward fullness, toward contraction, toward flux, toward blockage, etc. In these cases, although various and diverse signs are exhibited, the fault is not of the disease itself, but of the nature and property of the sick person. In the same way, one fire is in wood, another in resin, another in oil, etc., and yet it is one Element of fire. The other difference arises from the body itself. So also in this place. Therefore, those signs contribute to nothing else except to reveal the difference between bodies. But as for what pertains to the Planet of the disease, the ascendant, and the constellation—which in this case are worthy for the Physician to know—that must be sought from Astronomy. Unless this is done, the Physician will easily go astray in Chronic and Acute cases, and in the cause and the cure, so that he knows not what he does. Therefore, you future Physicians, turn toward Astronomy. But if you prefer to be greedy men instead of Physicians, it will ultimately matter nothing what you know of this. Meanwhile, he who does not know the power and art of fire will by no means be able to know and cure these diseases. For whatever is done concerning the disease: he ought to give thanks to God that the matter did not turn out worse. Now to the cure. Since, etc. Seek here until the end of the cure.

### ON COLIC.

<margin>
What is Colic, and what is its cause?
</margin>

When diverse opinions and various sentences concerning Colic were being tossed about everywhere, it happened that different names were also given to it. For the Germans, Latins, Greeks, etc., have their own peculiar names. But no difficulty ought to arise for the Physician concerning the variety of names: rather, one single cause for all of them must be considered. From this cause it also happens that Colic afflicts either more severely or more lightly, and that from the difference of its motion. For sometimes it arises from drink, sometimes from cold, now from here, now from elsewhere. And yet all this variety is comprised under one name, namely Colic or "twisting" <note>original: "torsione"</note>. Concerning which we shall discuss more at length in this chapter.

<margin>
How Colic is defined. What are the signs of Colic?
</margin>

Any Colic is a wind or a whirlwind <term>turbo</term> <note>Paracelsus views colic not just as gas, but as a violent internal vortex similar to a meteorological storm.</note> of the belly, stirred up from wherever—from food or drink, from night travel, from interruption of sleep, from chilling of the feet, or any other change, from a stone in the bladder, from chilling of the belly and obstruction of the bowels, from retention of the menses, etc. For from all these things colic is born, which finally either ends of its own accord, or is removed by remedies, or terminates in Paralysis. Its nature is such: pain and twisting arise in the belly, the intestines are contracted and twisted, appetite is lost, vomiting and belching follow, the urine becomes bloody or otherwise red, body heat accompanies it, and many similar things happen which cannot all be described here. When these appear, the colic intensifies according to the abundance and vehemence of the winds and the resolution of the salt of the intestines. For from these, it becomes either shorter or longer, or milder or more acute. Most often, there follows a loosening of the limbs and contraction, or other accidents, either acute or chronic, sometimes leading to death, according to the nature of the whirlwind. All of which must be more fully known from the following enumeration of causes. For although the disease itself is indeed one, there are many and diverse things which conspire toward its generation. It is important, therefore, to recount here those things which provide the force for some cause, and especially the principal cause itself, which is nothing other than a wind twisting and rolling itself, just as a whirlwind <note>original: "turbo"</note> seizes dust on the surface of the earth, or stirs up a vortex in the waves. It is right, in this place, to abandon all the Theory and explanation of causes handed down by the ancients in their definitions of this disease—which they divided into <term>Ileus</term> <note>A painful intestinal obstruction.</note>, Colic, <term>Tenesmus</term> <note>A distressing, continual urge to evacuate the bowels.</note>, etc.—and to bring forth and extract an entirely different cause, founded in the light of nature itself: namely, that man is similar to the "Great World" <note>The Macrocosm or universe.</note>, and has nothing peculiar to himself. For the reasoning and knowledge of both the world and the human must be one and the same. From this, therefore, it follows that colic is a wind, falling upon the belly from a superior sphere and breathing out into the four parts of the world. Once these have been generated and persist, colic is imminent. The matter ought to be understood in this way: surely it is known to you that four winds blow opposite to each other in the world; and you have learned from Meteorology how it happens that they sometimes breathe, sometimes less, sometimes more violently...

<margin>
What is the cause of Colic?
</margin>

<margin>
Human and world share one logic.
</margin>

<meta>This page continues the transition from the discussion of jaundice to a detailed elemental and philosophical explanation of colic. It frames the human digestive system as a meteorological system where internal winds and chemical dissolutions cause pain.</meta>

<page-num>651</page-num>

-> # ON COLIC <-

When stirred-up whirlwinds break out, they shake everything and cast down trees, occurring more or less in this or that place or time. A generation of this kind also occurs in the human body and is produced in the belly.

<margin>The belly is the chaos of man.</margin>
For the belly is a **chaos**; <note>In this context, "chaos" refers to the Paracelsian concept of the "Great Void" or the atmospheric medium between the elements of heaven and earth. Here, it is the internal space where biological "weather" happens.</note> that is, it is that region or concavity left between the heaven, the earth, and the sea. Therefore, just as winds breathe through this chaos across both land and water, so in the belly these same winds breathe now upward, now downward; the colic follows this flatulence.

<margin>The four parts of the belly and as many types of colic.</margin>
<margin>The navel is the South and the South Wind.</margin>
<margin>The back is the North and the North Wind.</margin>
Now, indeed, there are four parts of the globe or orb of the belly: South, North, East, and West. The South occupies the **navel**; its wind is **AUSTER** <note>The Latin name for the South Wind.</note>. This would be called "Southern Colic" if "colic" were its genuine name. Its breathing is from the navel toward the back. In the back, **BOREAS** <note>The North Wind.</note> flourishes, breathing from there toward the navel. These winds are opposite to each other—namely, one is hot and moist, and the other is cold and dry—and each rouses a colic of its own peculiar nature and condition.

<margin>The stomach is the East, etc. The anus is the West, etc.</margin>
In the upper region, from the base of the stomach, **EURUS** <note>The East Wind.</note> arises and breathes toward the west, namely toward the anus. From the anus emerges **ZEPHYRUS** <note>The West Wind.</note>, blowing toward the region of the East Wind. From this, again, two different types of colic are generated: one hot and dry, the other cold and moist. And these are those four types of colic that exist with their collateral winds.

The beginning and generation of winds are innate by nature. For just as summer and winter arise in their own time, so also the East, West, North, and South winds weigh upon us at their appointed time. And just as they have an ordinary time for their breathing, so they also experience a turn of rest and tranquility.

<margin>The two seasons of the belly.</margin>
Furthermore, two "seasons" of the belly must also be noted and known: namely, Summer and Winter. For in these, the winds weigh upon us either more or less. And thus, colic is either "estival" <note>Summer-like.</note> or "hibernal" <note>Winter-like.</note>. According to how the constellation <note>The internal arrangement of forces or "stars" within the body.</note> is within the human, so he is subjected to that colic. For colic behaves according to the manner of the winds' generation; if they are produced in a "meteoric" fashion <note>Like sudden, violent weather events.</note>, the colic attacks. However, colic experiences two peculiar things compared to external winds: first, that its "constellation" which gives birth to the wind moves through the internal parts; second, that those winds rage with pain, since being enclosed in the abdomen, they have no gate for eruption because of the various bodily objects in their way.

<margin>How man differs from the world in colic.</margin>
And by these two peculiarities especially, man differs from the "greater world" <note>The Macrocosm or the external universe.</note>. Just as winds blow daily in the world, they do similarly in man; however, in the world they are mostly consumed so that they are not greatly felt. Nonetheless, they are produced daily. These ordinary winds do not concern us here. For here we only explain those which are manifest and give birth to diseases, such as storms, hail, frost, and other similar tempests, which, when produced in the belly, rage and spread in the same way as they do in the "chaos" of the world. Because the belly is full of intestines and is moreover endowed with sharp sensation, it is tortured by the trouble and pain of the winds until it either consumes them or drives and shakes them out. Therefore, from whatever part these winds weigh upon the belly, they stir up pain in the manner mentioned above,

<margin>Colic is so named from its location.</margin>
which the ancients called **Colic** and **Iliac**, attending indeed to the reason of the intestines, but not to the reason of **Philosophy** <note>Paracelsus distinguishes between mere anatomical description and the "philosophical" understanding of the chemical/astral causes of disease.</note> itself.

<margin>Man consists of three things.</margin>
Furthermore, observe the accidents of colic in this way. Man is constituted of three things: **Mercury**, **Salt**, and **Sulfur** <note>The Tria Prima: the three fundamental principles of all matter in Paracelsian alchemy.</note>. These are now his blood, flesh, bones, tendons, etc. When the winds blow through, they seize the body itself—that is, the intestines and their regions—just as a strong whirlwind casts down and levels a house, or brings in a rain-cloud or something similar.

<margin>The dissolution of Salt is the cause of colic.</margin>
While these things happen, the wind attacks those three substances and is, as it were, confused and united with them. Through this mixing, the **Salt** is dissolved <note>original: "resoluitur"</note> and flows down into the intestines. When this Salt—biting, sharp, and endowed with various qualities—attacks and twitches the sensitive intestines, the belly is then lanced with pain, just like a wound that is bitten when sprinkled with salt. If, however, the winds do not attack the salt, then they all break out together at once. But where the Salt is dissolved, pain presses instantly, not ceasing until the salt is pacified and subdued. Although pains are also brought in by the West and North winds when they either strike with cold or weaken with vehemence and force, if the dissolved salt concurs with them, much more atrocious and dangerous pains take hold. From these things it is clear that the cure for colic is fourfold, according to the four winds.

<margin>A twofold cure for colic.</margin>
Then also, a peculiar cure is owed to the dissolution of salt if it is separated from the Mercury and Sulfur; just as there is another method if other things occur. For the winds also constipate and loosen, and sometimes they belch upward, and sometimes they fluctuate in their own cavities. The cure is therefore twofold in its kind: one against the winds, the other against the matter which the wind leaves behind. For unless diligent care is spent on the winds themselves and on the dissolved salt, no healing of the colic can be obtained, unless the nature of the **Microcosm** <note>The "Little World," meaning the human body.</note> itself consumes and removes the opposing forces.

<margin>Colic [involves] subtle winds.</margin>
The aforementioned winds—whether they arise of themselves or are produced by humans—are so subtle and thin that they pervade all the muscles and pores of the whole body, just as wind penetrates a wall. By this alteration, the limbs are completely cast down and broken. If dissolved salt concurs with these, its spirit is so exquisitely mixed with the winds that it travels with them to the furthest joints.

<margin>How colic breathes out into the heat <note>Likely referring to the outward limbs/limbs in a state of distress.</note>.</margin>
Thus, once the force of eruption is made, they blow through in a mixture until they have beset the outer limbs nearest by. Once this is done, the pain of the belly itself is also poured out into the limbs. Because the limbs cannot resist this wind and spirit of salt, they collapse just like a house leveled by the wind; a contraction, either more or less grave, follows this "casting down," depending on whether those winds struck lightly or violently. For all these things happen according to the nature of the Microcosm and the condition of the wind.

Therefore, for a conclusion, this must be held (Seek <insert>*</insert> <insert>*</insert>) that the four said winds have their defined complexions, namely immoderate heat, cold, or moisture and dryness, which are then followed by the dissolutions and coagulations of the "three primes" in their Elements; for the balancing of which, subtlety...

The most severe pain is attributed to the "dissolution of Salt," which acts like grit in a wound as it is blown through the body's internal "chaos."</summary>

<meta>This page continues the discussion of internal winds as the cause of colic, transitioning into a deeper philosophical explanation of the relationship between the "Small World" (man) and the "Great World" (the universe). It argues that internal symptoms like colic are governed by an internal "heaven" rather than the distant stars in the sky.</meta>

The utility of penetrating spirits also arises here. For some members are loosened by the cold of Boreas <note>original: "Boreæ"; the North Wind</note>, others by the humidity of Zephyr <note>original: "Zephyri"; the West Wind</note>, others by the dryness of Eurus <note>original: "Euri"; the East Wind</note>, and others by the heat of Auster <note>the South Wind</note>. Therefore, the cure for any contraction or stiffening must be tempered according to these causes—not so much because of the winds themselves, but because of the dissolved **spirit of salt**. <note>In the Paracelsian tradition, "salt" is the chemical principle of stability and physical form. When its "spirit" is out of balance, it causes the body to stiffen or "contract."</note> The sole cure for this is that, just as the only remedy for a collapsed house is to set it upright, so here too the contracted limb must be restored. Thus, there is a specific care for the evacuation of the belly, and likewise a specific care for the uprighting of the limbs.

### OPPOSITES
#### Why ¶. through to the end of the 2nd paragraph.

<margin>q. see above at folio 104.</margin>
<margin>Colic occurs according to the phase of the moon.</margin>
**H**aving premised these things thus far, it is now common knowledge among all sound-minded people that this evil is entirely stirred up and felt in man according to the phase of the moon—whether it be new, full, or waxing. Since this is true, the origin and cause must be thoroughly understood.

<margin>The heaven of man rules the man.</margin>
The cause is this: man also has within himself, just as outside himself, his own peculiar heaven and a similar constellation. From this it happens that he feels the variation of time, not from the external heaven, but from the internal one. For no planet of the sky governs me or you, but only that planet which is in the body. And the Astronomer who judges births from the external planets errs for this reason: those external bodies do nothing in the body of a man; rather, the internal heaven and its planets moderate it. The external heaven exists only as an index or sign of the internal.

<margin>The external heaven does not rule man. The anatomy of the pig and man's heaven are one.</margin>
For man behaves as this coarse and rustic example teaches: the anatomy of a swine or pig is the same as that of a man. So, in turn, the anatomy of man is the same as that of the heaven. Thus, rains and variations of storms also occur within us. What is the cause? It is because the same **matrices** <note>In this context, "matrices" refers to the elemental "wombs" or environments where natural phenomena are generated.</note> exist within us as exist outside. Hence, those who are of one accord and constellation with them feel their impressions. Now that these things are established, the knowledge of colic (so called by the ancients) must be held: that it consists of the winds of the four parts of the world, which, according to their disposition, stir up griping pains and torments. Therefore, we feel the power of the heaven in colic so certainly that we can truly say this man will die in this or that zodiac sign, or in this phase of the moon—not that you should understand the external moon, but the internal one. For it is this internal moon that you feel, and by it you are killed.

<margin>The external heaven does not incline.</margin>
Meanwhile, you observe this too negligently because the internal operation is not felt as immediately as an external wind. Those who have this saying in their mouths—that *the stars incline, but do not compel* <note>original: "Astra inclinent, non necessitent"; a common medieval astrological defense of free will which the author here disputes</note>—think and speak wrongly. For those stars incline nothing, since they are directed only toward the external heaven, which has no commerce with us except by way of "prefiguration" <note>meaning the outer world is a "preview" or map of the inner world</note>. Therefore, nothing in us is inclined by them. Thus, they pointlessly add that it "necessitates nothing." For how could it compel us, if it is not within us?

<margin>The stars of men are the man.</margin>
Man is compelled by his own stars, not by the stars of the world. For the stars of man are the man himself. And what man is, that is a star—not a heavenly one, but an "infernal" one <note>meaning "lower" or earthly, as opposed to the "supernal" sky</note>, whose prefiguration is only shown in passing in the higher heavens. Unless, therefore, the spirit implanted in our reason governs the body, then the heaven which is built into us exercises dominion over us—just like the wind in colic, which is entirely a gust of air and not a "humor." <note>The author is rejecting the traditional "Humoral" theory of Galenic medicine, which blamed diseases on fluids like phlegm or bile.</note> Let us therefore speak of internal things, and not drag in foreign things upon men, nor entertain idle thoughts about them as the **Humorists** <note>term: Humorists; followers of the traditional medical theory of the Four Humors (blood, phlegm, yellow bile, black bile).</note> are accustomed to do.

Thus, the works themselves testify to the facts, just as a painted image provides knowledge of its original subject. By the same logic, a house testifies that it has a master, and what it testifies is that it exists as itself, and is not something else different from itself. In this way, things must be understood properly for what they are, not for something foreign—just as if someone wears a cross, so that from it one may understand that man is of this or that sect or order; but one must rest in the sign itself and say that it is a cloth or rag, sewn or arranged in the form of a cross. For in the same way, the wind of the belly, by the sign it shows—that is, the wind—designates that it *is* wind. We should discuss the wind, therefore, and not other things.

<margin>The Microcosm must be known from the Macrocosm.</margin>
Now, what is wind? This is learned from the origin of the Great World <note>original: "magni mundi"; the Macrocosm</note>, and its causes, mode of generation, and properties. It is demonstrated that man himself is a **Microcosm** <note>term: Microcosm; the "Small World." The belief that a human being is a miniature reflection of the entire universe (the Macrocosm).</note>, consisting of all four creatures of the Elements. Therefore, one must be entirely compared and explained by the other, and Physics itself must be brought to this: that a similar Theory be established in determining the causes of disease, and the cure or medicine itself, which flows from that Theory, must be applied to them. In this way, the signs as they reveal themselves also instruct the Physician on how he ought to conduct himself.

<margin>Man made from the limbus.</margin>
For He who created the Great World finally fashioned man himself out of the **limbus**. <note>term: limbus; in Paracelsian thought, the primordial "extract" or "dust" of all created things used by God to make man.</note> And so, both worlds were established by the same Author. He who placed the winds, the Sun, and the Moon in the external heaven also placed them into man and said: "Let this be." From this, the wonderful goodness of the Almighty Creator shines forth.

<margin>The world testifies of its creator.</margin>
For what, I ask, does the entire world testify or say, except that it belongs to God, its creator? Just as a statue stands as a sign of its sculptor or modeler, so all the creatures of God indicate that they are the works of God. Furthermore, the **Macrocosm** is visible; the **Microcosm** is not, except in the figure of the divine image. For the rest of the things within us lie hidden. In the same way, Christ himself was visible in person, just as the Macrocosm is seen by our eyes. And yet, in turn, He is invisible in another form, being something even beyond what He appears to be. So also man is a world, and it is not seen that he is a world, but he is a *sign* of the world; a sign, however, not made by man, but by Him who made man himself.

<margin>Christ was visible in person.</margin>
Since the matter stands thus, it is a sign that it is the work of God, not of man. The logic of the belly and of colic is the same. The winds are wonderfully present and are a sign that God, not man, made them, just as in the Great World. It would therefore be unworthy for men to turn them into "humors" or to speculate something else about them. For that is not the work of man, but of God. And our mind must be directed entirely toward that work, and the Theory itself must be established from it.
