<header>PARAGRAPH II.</header>

Who indeed do you think baptizes with the Holy Spirit? Surely it is God who does this. If He, therefore, baptizes with the Holy Spirit, and places neither a limit nor a measure upon it, He excludes no one, but looks upon all who are in need. Who, I ask, would dare to think or say that all medicine has already been handed down and poured out, and that those things not yet committed to writing will never be found? For such a thought is born of despair and ignorance of the power of God—the same God who makes the sun, which sets today, rise again for us tomorrow. He is the one who leads the summer, which fades in autumn, back to us in the joyful following spring, and through that season grants us food and drink. And shall we not trust this faithful <term>steward</term> <note>original: "promo"; a household manager or butler, used here as a metaphor for God's provision</note> to similarly provide for us the necessary medicine? For He creates medicine daily, no less than He creates bread, and He commands us to be seriously concerned for this "daily bread." And yet, shall we continue to eat that which was long ago cast out through the bowels? O, you transgressors!

I do not speak this way to boast, as you might suspect. But I do boast in this: that I have known and experienced the truth, and I preach it to both manifest and hidden Christians, whether they dwell among the heathens or among the Christians. You shall not turn this into a crime against me. For what do you think Christ meant by the proposed example of the <margin>What does the example of the Samaritan indicate?</margin> **Samaritan**, who brought aid to the wounded man in Jericho and became his neighbor—rather than the Priest or the Levite? Therefore, medicine is not located within the man whom *man* proposes, but within the one whom *God* proposes. He alone knows and sees through the heart of the Physician; He does not look at the man’s rank, or his dignity and pomp, nor a famous name, nor certificates and seals. Instead, He directs His mind toward the man’s **mercy**, to which alone He <margin>Medicine is given only to the merciful.</margin> grants and bestows Medicine. For who, after all, discovered Medicine—at least as much of it as has flowed down to us? Certainly not the wicked, but the **blessed**, whom God has chosen, not man. And in this we ought to boast: that we have received Medicine from the <margin>Medicine was discovered by the blessed.</margin> elect, not from the <term>sophists</term> <note>A derogatory term for university-trained scholars who prioritize logic and rhetoric over practical experience and divine truth</note> of the Academies. From those elect, we continually obtain what is lacking. For if "the care of tomorrow is to be left to itself," what else is the labor performed before now but a sign of the tomorrow that has already passed? So also let the successor be anxious for his own future day, and ask God for the bread of that day, so that he might be able to prevent the diseases of the sick. For **charity** teaches all these things.

But everything I have said so far aims at this: that it may be known that a Physician must seek an entirely different foundation, and that his art and experience must be learned from a source far different than has been visited until now. Therefore, since I am here treating specifically of the <term>falling sickness</term> <note>original: "morbo caduco"; epilepsy</note>, you shall attend to me seriously and diligently—not for the sake of my profit, but for the sake of the health of the sick. For a Physician ought to be so equipped that he presents himself as a helper in all urgent diseases. This is not done by inspecting <term>foul urine</term> <note>original: "faedo inspiciendo lotio"; uroscopy was a standard diagnostic tool of the time, which Paracelsian medicine often rejected as fraudulent</note> and prophesying from it in the manner of a <margin>By what means medicine should be established.</margin> soothsayer, nor by merely touching the pulse, nor by guessing, nor by administering a mash of oats or barley water, or preserves, or laxatives. (For these things neither make a Physician nor prove him, since they are the proper business of <term>old wives</term> <note>original: "vetularum"; a common dismissive term for folk healers or unlearned women</note>). Rather, a Physician proves himself by establishing a practice outside of these vanities, through those medicines in which the <term>secrets</term> <note>original: "arcana"; the hidden healing powers within natural substances</note> lie hidden, demonstrating the praise of the Physician and the glory of God. For God is not celebrated through the inspection of urine or the touch of a pulse, but through these "arcana." Thus, at the final judgment of Physicians, the Physician conscious of his own integrity may say: *You, Judge, taught me thus, not man; I have finished Your work, not mine; I have labored from You, not from myself.* Therefore, let us be inclined toward mercy, which is the mother of charity; thus all things necessary shall be added to us according to the desire of our hearts. For the arts of medicine are now asleep. Unless we rouse them, they will never wake up of their own accord. We must labor with every effort to wake them.

## PARAGRAPH II.

**R**egarding this deadly and terrible falling sickness, this must be held above all: why God afflicts us through it and so miserably tortures us. Concerning this question, various men bring forth various ideas, each holding to the tradition of his own profession. Meanwhile, not everything is drawn from the foundation of truth. No one can explain this cause more rightly than the Physician. Now, if someone says that God reminds us through this disease of who we are and what sort of evils we are subject to—that is wide of the mark. For it belongs to no one to speak of these things unless he has come forth born from Medicine. A lawyer might bring forth another cause: namely, that this is a deserved punishment inflicted by God on those whom the Emperor does not subject to punishment. But this is not agreeable to the truth either. Others may pretend other reasons, yet all of these are mere opinions and the dreams of idle and ignorant men. The "Naturalists" also take it upon themselves to judge this—partly Philosophers, partly Physicians—who nevertheless themselves produce nothing but impertinent things far removed from the truth. For this reason, what should finally be felt regarding this disease is worthy of consideration above all else. Meanwhile, no faith is to be given to the other professors of any faculty—Jurisprudence, Poetry, History, Philosophy, etc.—nor even to the Physicians of whom I spoke a little while ago. For all of these are seducers and corrupters of genuine Medicine and truth, who have already despaired of God’s creatures. I exhort you again, you who wish to be worthy Physicians, to hold fast to the truth itself with your teeth, and following a legitimate method, to pity the sad lot of these sick people more deeply. Led by mercy rather than the desire for profit, perform your duty skillfully from now on.

Therefore, so that you may understand the cause of this disease more exactly, you shall reflect within yourselves with a mindful soul that <margin>What is the cause of the falling sickness?</margin> **man is a smaller world**, and because of this, he contains within himself everything that the great world encompasses. Now, therefore, the external world is the mirror, the theory, and the anatomy of man himself; thus, through the external world, everything <margin>Man. The Microcosm.</margin> belonging to man may be known. For the excellence and eminence of man's creation, which a Physician must know, cannot be sufficiently investigated from the man himself. Therefore, in describing this disease, the Physician shall set before himself the Nature of the **great world** and explain it. Once that is accurately and sufficiently declared, it will also be clear and established that the same is found and seen in man. While I consider this method of investigation, I cannot help but condemn all the little books written about this disease, both by the moderns and the ancients...

Having dismissed the humoral theory, he now begins a detailed comparison between meteorological phenomena (thunder and earthquakes) and the "falling sickness" (epilepsy).</meta>

<page-num>664</page-num>
# ON THE FALLING SICKNESS.

<margin>By what reasoning diseases are to be known</margin>Nothing has ever been written or published by the ancients regarding how diseases are to be recognized that contains any truth. For they possess nothing drawn from the foundation of nature, from which all knowledge of disease must flow. Therefore, no one should find fault with my criticism of them, since they have known neither the principles of medicine nor its methods in the slightest degree. Anyone who examines the books written by them with more diligence will testify to this along with me. Meanwhile, little care should be given if you offend those whose books are filled with every kind of imposture.

<margin>Diseases are of two kinds</margin>The world must therefore be considered entirely according to its four Elements, not according to "complexions": not according to the virtues and operations of temperaments, but of the Elements. For diseases are twofold: those from the Elements, and those from the complexions. As far as the falling sickness is concerned, let us look at the Elements themselves. But before we provide that, let the humors—about which unskilled doctors babble—be cast far away and exploded; otherwise, you will be entirely unable to penetrate into the intimate knowledge of this disease. For many errors have emerged from those four humors, as is more clearly demonstrated in other books. Therefore, having shaken off that dizziness, know that the <term>Great World</term> <note>The Macrocosm, or the universe as a whole, which mirrors the human body.</note> is divided into two parts: <margin>The two parts of the World.</margin> into *heaven* and *earth*. Under the name of heaven, understand two Elements: <term>Fire</term> and <term>Air</term>. Likewise, under earth understand two: namely <term>Earth</term> and <term>Water</term>. And in these is contained the cause for treating diseases.

<margin>The nature of any Element is twofold. Which fruits belong to which Elements.</margin>Know, moreover, that from any Element there are two things, or two natures: one is its *Fruit*; the other is its *Impression*. Fruit behaves in this way: the fruits of the earth are all herbs, trees, and grasses. The fruits of water are metals, stones, and flints. The fruits of air are <margin>Manna and Terebinthin are two different things.</margin> Dew, Manna, and <term>Terebinthin</term> <note>In this context, a resinous or balsamic substance thought to fall from the sky, distinct from the tree resin.</note> (which are two, not one). The fruits of fire are rain, snow, and frost. These are the fruits of the four Elements, about which we shall say nothing in this place, as the falling sickness is generated from none of them. And although the causes of these diseases can indeed be investigated from the fruits (if we speak medically), the proof nevertheless falls to the other part, which must be considered in this way. You see, surely, that heaven produces <margin>What is thunder?</margin> thunder from its element. However, thunder is not the fruit of heaven; rather, its fruit is rain, <margin>Thunder and the fire of the falling sickness</margin> which is generated from it. Here, therefore, thunder must be considered, not rain. From the rain, one knows that medicine is a fruit of that Element. But thunder provides the knowledge of the cause of the <margin>Thunder is the anatomy of the falling sickness</margin> falling sickness. For it can be known naturally beforehand when thunder is about to strike. And he who has the science of predicting thunder can likewise predict (just as you do with nativities and judgments) whether a man is about to fall from that disease or not. And he who <margin>The Elements prefigure the whole man.</margin> knows this, is the one to be heard when discussing the disease. For this is truer than truth itself: that the external Elements prefigure the whole man. Therefore, he who has known the Elements well will also know man well. Thus, I rightly reproach the astronomer who, boasting of himself, forgets the "Elementary Anatomy" of diseases. For the physician who does not know the world is not a physician at all, but is pure, unadulterated error and a trifler. Once these things are correctly understood, know that thunder itself—that is, the matter of thunder—is this very disease. Furthermore, so that you may know the matter more clearly, you must know that the <margin>Thunder is made of three things.</margin> cause of thunder is threefold: <term>Mercury</term>, <term>Sulphur</term>, and <term>Salt</term>. <note>The "Tria Prima" or three primary substances of Paracelsian alchemy, representing volatility, flammability, and stability.</note> These three are the bodies of thunder. These are similarly present within man. For man is composed of sulphur, salt, and mercury. These are his <margin>Man consists of sulphur, etc.</margin> body. But setting these three bodies aside for a moment, we must speak of their effect or operation. I have described thunder in my *Meteorica* <note>A reference to the author's work on meteorological phenomena.</note>, which must be read by every physician entering the art. As for the effect, these three produce that *impetus* [force]. This impetus resides in the body as if it were hidden, enclosed by a certain bark or an overlying skin. As long as the body remains intact, the thunder <margin>How thunder is made.</margin> does not break out. But if the Mercury, Sulphur, and Salt reach maturation, then a paroxysm of thunder attacks, which violently shakes and bursts through the "bark" in which it lies. In this way, thunder, and that which birthed the thunder, is present. You are already <margin>Comparison of thunder and the falling sickness</margin> familiar with the custom and reasoning of thunder. The judgment is entirely the same regarding the falling sickness in all its parts, as far as the matter and the body of Mercury, Sulphur, and Salt are concerned. Just as thunder is involved and enclosed, like wind in a bladder, so too must we think about the generation of the falling sickness, which is produced by the Element of fire. For the same cause of the falling sickness exists. From these things, you can now gather what I moved in the entrance of this paragraph: namely, what the cause of this divine affliction is. There is no other cause for it than that man is a <term>Microcosm</term> <note>The "Small World," the idea that the human body is a miniature reflection of the universe.</note>, and so he necessarily suffers the same things that usually happen in the greater world. Therefore, the falling sickness in man <margin>The falling sickness is thunder.</margin> is thunder; which is even proven by the cure for it. For by whatever reasoning thunder is consumed, by that same reasoning the falling sickness must also be consumed.

However, it is not enough for this to be demonstrated only in the Element of fire: <margin>Thunder and the falling sickness of the earth</margin> but the same must also be known concerning the earth. To explain this more conveniently: you must know that the earth has its own Star no less than the Element of fire does. For that which is an Element is also <margin>Elements do not live without a Star.</margin> a Star. For without a "star," the Elements cannot live or flourish. (This is found in *On the Generations and Properties of Things*.) To speak of the Star of the earth, it must be noted that all celestial operations flourish within it. <margin>The Star of the earth, etc.</margin> For the Star is hidden away, while the bodies are clearly open to view. We will treat nothing of bodies here, for a discourse on them contributes nothing to this disease; but we speak of stars. At this point, take for yourself the example of an <margin>What is an earthquake</margin> earthquake. My adversaries say this happens because of wind enclosed in the cataracts of the earth around waters. They pile up this matter with many explanations or interpretations added. Yet their opinion is nothing; it fights against all Philosophy. What the truth of this is will be explained in its own place separately in the book *On the Stars*. As far as this matter is concerned, it is like this: An earthquake arises from the "star" of the earth in plainly the same way and reasoning as thunder in the heaven. They differ only in operation and appearance, insofar as the Elementary form contains them. Therefore, an earthquake must be considered as coming not from the sea, not from the wind, etc., but from the earth itself. I am an exhorter to you, that if by chance those books of mine come into your hands, you read and unroll them. Now at this point,

# PARAGRAPH II.

<margin>How an earthquake occurs.</margin> Now, to discuss this example more clearly, it must be understood that the Star of the Earth, through its own Mercury, Sulfur, and Salt—not unlike what happens in fire—first builds for itself an "egg," that is, a crust and a shell, in which the aforementioned matter lies and matures, just as thunder matures in the heavens. However, once the maturation is perfected, its destruction or bursting begins with a "terrestrial thunder." This thunder tosses and shakes the earth (read my *Meteors*). From this, it happens that the Astronomer can predict the time of an earthquake to the very hour. For it arises from a natural cause, not from wind, whose entry or exit is known or explored by no one. Thus, there is another more recent type of falling sickness <note>original: "morbus Caducus," commonly known as epilepsy.</note> which arises from the Star of the Earth, just as the Astronomical Physician demonstrates. For just as there are four Elements, so there are also four diseases. For in man there are four Stars, since he is a <term>Microcosm</term> <note>The "minor world" or "small world"; the idea that the human body reflects the structure of the entire universe.</note>.

<margin>How thunder and falling sickness are cured.</margin> Since, therefore, the falling sickness must be understood through the four Elements, we shall also weigh the example and manner of the third falling sickness, which arises from the Element of water. Just as mention was previously made of the Stars of the four Elements, so it must be repeated here that there is also a star in the Water, which has the same conjunctions as fire, as well as Planets and other stars. For from stars <margin>Who the Hydromancers, Astronomers, and Geomancers are.</margin> of this kind came the Hydromancers, just as Astronomers came from fire. Certainly, these are natural Doctors and forecasters. In the same way, <term>Geomancy</term> <note>Divination or study of the earth.</note> was born from the stars of the earth. These arts, however, were afterward adulterated and sank into augury or sorcery. Regarding these perverse arts, I prescribe this rule for you: do not believe their initial principles, but do believe their process. For in a natural way, the births and judgments of natural things are carried out. Similarly, from the stars of the Air, natural Astronomy flowed down, which was subsequently transformed into "beryls and nails" <note>A reference to scrying or divination using crystals and polished surfaces.</note>; this was called <margin>What is Necromancy?</margin> <term>Necromancy</term> <note>Paracelsus here uses the term to refer to a natural science of the air/spirit rather than communication with the dead.</note> by the ancients. I indicate these things in this place so that you may know that the four Elements have four Stars. Furthermore, the four stars have four types of Astronomers, yet the Astronomy remains one and the same. From <margin>4 species of Falling Sickness.</margin> these stars, therefore, a fourfold *falling sickness* arises, namely from their conjunctions, just as I recounted regarding thunder.

<margin>What is Lorindus? and how is it made?</margin> Moreover, to speak of water here, know that **Lorindus** <note>A Paracelsian term for a specific acoustic or seismic sound in water, likened to aquatic thunder.</note> is a noise or a whispering of the water, specifically in quiet ponds or lakes, accompanied by a certain movement and trembling. That *Lorindus* is the thunder of the water, produced from sulfur, mercury, and salt through the preparation and conjunction of the aquatic star. For as soon as the astral operation begins, a closed shell or bladder is immediately present there, in which this thunder matures, as has been handed down. From this, *Lorindus* bursts forth with its signs. Indeed, this <margin>Why Lorindus is more frequent in winter.</margin> thunder is more frequent in winter than in summer. For such is the nature of the Star of the Element of water. Similarly, the thunder of the earth is not moved according to the reasoning of the star of fire, but according to the proper condition of the earth itself. From here, therefore, come the <margin>This must be known through Geomancy, Hydromancy, etc.</margin> Geomancers—not from the geomancy of "points," <note>Referring to traditional geomantic divination using random marks on the ground.</note> but from the Astronomy of the earth. From here come the Hydromancers—not sorcerers from water, but the Astronomers of water. I propose all these things at greater length to this end: so that through the external things of the world, you might know man himself through *Geomancy*, *Hydromancy*, *Pyromancy*, and *Necromancy*. For those who now wish to be called Astronomers are skilled in these: that is, those who know how to explain the movements of the sky from the very foundation of the light of nature. For <margin>The fourfold Astronomical Physician.</margin> the light of Nature follows in such a way that the Physician must be a fourfold Astronomer, who knows how to gather and bring into the Microcosm those things that exist in the Macrocosm; otherwise, nothing can be known from the foundation itself.

The third example of the falling sickness has thus far been explained, the cause of which is understood to be that man is a Microcosm, subject to all those things which happen in the Macrocosm. After this, it must be handed down that <margin>Thunder and falling sickness of the air.</margin> there is also a certain thunder in the air, born from the Aerial star, which has a great affinity with the thunder of fire. The difference is that it does not occur with rain, but happens with clear air and a bright sky, conspicuous with flashes and other similar things, but not falling with lightning-bolts, hail, or rain. It very often arises at night, and sometimes even in winter, etc., as there are many such laws concerning the stars. This thunder also belongs to Mercury, Sulfur, and Salt, according to the condition of the Element of air; it fashions for itself a house or receptacle like a shell or a nut covered in a husk. For just as you see in all things that nothing is produced without its own house and tunic, so the same must be thought of the stars. Thus the cherry has its skin, the pear has its own, etc. Following their example, let the Physician know that these things of which I treat are likewise enclosed in their own skin. And the thunder of the air is excluded, like an embryo from the afterbirth <note>original: "fecundina," the placenta or fetal membranes.</note>, about which more is said elsewhere.

In this way, therefore, you ought to recognize the falling sickness and seriously weigh the magnitude of the pain: namely, that the *falling sickness* <margin>What is falling sickness?</margin> is a disease born from the stars of the Microcosm by no other reasoning than how we taught the four thunders are generated in the four Elements. But if anything here seems superstitious to you: come, set before yourself the great and small worlds, recognize what each is, and compare them between themselves, maintaining the legitimate ascent in all things. Then it will become known and plain to you just <margin>The ancient physicians are rebuked.</margin> how many errors the ancient writers have introduced, while by prescribing other causes for disease, they obscured the cure itself and shut off health from the sick. From these things, the method of healing must also be understood. For whatever dissolves thunder also dissolves this disease. How that may be done, seek from the [section on] curing. However, so that I may describe this disease fully and entirely in this place, the order and process to be held within it will be handed down next. From which it will be clear how thunder and the falling sickness are one thing, with one cause, essence, and matter for both, as has already been partially handed down before.

The contrariety of Mercury, Sulfur, and Salt <margin>The cause of thunder is contrariety.</margin> is the cause of thunder, as is taught in the *Meteorics*. Now in this there is also a preparation through the operation of Mars, and many other things, not unlike as if someone were to prepare "Persian fire" <note>Likely a reference to Greek fire or an incendiary chemical compound.</note> by art. For the arts of men are the natures of the Planets and Stars. Nor in the arts...

# ON FALLING SICKNESS
<header>ON FALLING SICKNESS</header>

<margin>All arts are in the Planets.</margin> ...anything is found which is not similarly found in the nature of the Planets. For the Nature of these provides us with the arts. Whence every art is deservedly ascribed to its own Planet, and one thing is considered one matter; differing only in this: as the <term>Microcosm</term> <note>The "minor world" or human being.</note> differs from the <term>Macrocosm</term> <note>The "greater world" or the universe.</note>, as is taught more plainly elsewhere. Here, as far as the knowledge of the falling sickness is concerned, you must strive to know the Nature, cause, and essence of Thunder, according to the prescription of my *Meteors* <note>Referring to Paracelsus's work *Liber Meteorum*.</note>. From those writings, learn now that the body is one in both places—one nature, one essence—except that the secrets of each world differ in form and manifestation, while remaining always one thing and one essence. For just as heaven and earth were created from nothing, and yet arranged into the three things so often mentioned—namely <term>Mercury, Sulfur, and Salt</term> <note>In Paracelsian thought, these are the "Tria Prima" or three primary substances that make up all matter.</note>—so in these three are all the Planets and all the stars; and not only those, but also all bodies that are born and arise from them. Now if the great world is this, and these three matters (as proposed) can be denied by no one, then certainly, since man is constituted from the great world, <margin>Man has all things of the world.</margin> he will have within himself all things that the great world has. In this way, man is nothing but Mercury, Sulfur, and Salt. Moreover, where these three are, there also is the star. And each one is fourfold. And thus in the great and small world there is one body, differing only by the judgment of the eyes.

I study to be brief here in every way, so that I do not make you weary in reading our Philosophy, and so that I am not the cause of delaying the cure for falling sickness. To satisfy the skeptics here in some way (though I shall not finish everything here, but complete most of it in the book *On Generations*), pay attention: they demand that only their eyes and ears be filled—that is, they require to hear thunder with their ears and see lightning, flashing, and clouds with their eyes. For only then do they think it safe to believe. Surely their intellect is so weak and faint that they do not even understand what is seen and heard. To what end, therefore, will it serve to satisfy their eyes and ears? But lest these words of mine be discussed as an excuse or a complication, I will proceed as briefly as I can to describe the process of falling sickness hereafter, as the logic of the Microcosm demands. If any things necessary to the matter seem to be lacking here, they will be supplied in our *Meteorological* books, as well as in the book *On the Generations of the Great and Small World*, where each thing will be delivered in its own separate place in a long series of words.

<margin>How is falling sickness generated?</margin> I will omit the nature and condition of the stars here, concerning which I trust you are already certain. I speak at least of the Generation. But I do not treat the matters themselves here, such as sulfur, mercury, and salt. Since these are described in the *Philosophy*, they would be explained by me here quite idly. Regarding Generation, however, pay attention thus: If the bodies themselves are present and the conjunctions of the Stars concur, first of all a change in the weather occurs. So also in a future thunderclap, you observe first that the weather changes and the air becomes more sweltering, so that birds and flies feel this change. Likewise, in the body when a <term>paroxysm</term> <note>A sudden attack or seizure, here referring to an epileptic fit.</note> is invading, the precursor of the sickness is a change of reason. For any "storm" changes and weakens the animal reason. Birds and cattle betray that change in the air with their cry and fury—such as hens and flies, which plague men with more aggressive bites. In the same way, a man perceives his own assault beforehand, and he is changed entirely within himself, cast down from his previous nature. <margin>What are the precursors of thunder and falling sickness?</margin> Thus the beginning and precursor of the paroxysm in the Falling Sickness corresponds in most respects to the generation of thunder. For what is said in this place about "fiery thunder" is offered only as an example, because the same thing happens in the same way in others, with only a difference of form and the particular Nature of the Elements intervening. Just as you see that from such a beginning clouds gather (which yet are not part of the true matter), so also in man clouds arise before the eyes, dizziness and darkening of vision occur, and a deep sleep. All these proceed from that cloud which induces drowsiness and heaviness of the soul. Therefore, if there is one name in both places, there is also one matter for both, and one logic exists. A wind follows these preceding things, leaving nothing in its place, moving and disturbing everything in its path. A similar wind also seizes the body, so disturbing and agitating the man that he can remain quiet in no place, but is tossed to and fro. This tossing is to be learned and known from the wind alone. Even if it is not visible in the Microcosm, it is clearly felt from the internal agitation, while the belly and neck are inflated and filled with wind, according to the condition of each part. I hope that by these things you will be moved to look upon such sick people with intent eyes, and not shrink from the sight of them; namely, so that you may more certainly witness the truth of my words and learn the healing more easily. Let your heart not be so hard, but be moved by mercy toward the sick, since you are called entirely to this duty. Have pity on the afflicted ones themselves, and do not hold the matter in contempt, but judge the truth of my writings and the health of the sick deeply and inwardly. But to return to the purpose: if winds of this sort blow in every direction, then at last the horrendous crash of thunder resounds, by which you see heaven and earth moved. In the same way, in man, once the "thunder-bladder" <note>A theoretical vessel within the body where the "storm" of the disease builds up before exploding into a seizure.</note> is ruptured, the whole body is shaken and tossed, so that all the internal parts tremble—just as the earth is shaken by external thunder—until the matter is consumed. This thunder is the cause of the <term>spasm</term>. For what else is a spasm in this disease than a violent eruption and a strongly enclosed wind? It convulses, extends, and makes rigid all the limbs. And just as lightning flashes occur with thunder, so the eyes of the sick also flash, so that mere flames appear before the eyes. And as a rain shower follows thunder, so <term>foam</term> <note>The frothing at the mouth typical of a grand mal seizure.</note> follows the tossing of the sick person. And these things must be diligently considered by you Physicians concerning this disease, so that you may be drawn into worthy compassion and not despise my teaching. Go to the sick, look at them, and see how aptly all things match which have been said by me thus far. Do not accuse me of arrogance; for no worthy and honest Physician will testify that of me. To whom, indeed, even one drop of faithful blood...

### SECTION III.

<margin>He wrote the enlarged *Archidoxes* with singular care.</margin>
If there is even a drop within someone that wishes well for the sick, let him read my works on the *Generation of Heaven and Earth*, as well as *The Microcosm* and the **Archidoxes** <note>These are titles of major treatises by Paracelsus; *Archidoxes* (The Supreme Teachings) is one of his most influential medical works</note>, which I have written with singular care. In those many volumes, I have handed down things that I here—wishing to avoid your boredom or offense—scarcely encompass in a few tight pages.

<margin>What is lightning?</margin>
But let us proceed. It is surely known to you that thunder is sometimes followed by hail, lightning, and so on. We have found that the same happens similarly in man. Lightning is a body composed of Mercury, Sulfur, and Salt; this is what is taught regarding its generation. In a person with the falling sickness <note>original: "caduco," referring to an epileptic</note>, it happens in this way: if the "star" has produced its disease, then it has no other peculiar place than that which the *Planets* have in their motion. Therefore, where the place of the star falls, the center and root of the disease are established in that very spot. 

However, if it turns into lightning, then its matter becomes compressed without a physical body. It is as if a man were able to take a great deal of air or wind and shove it together, forcing it into a single eggshell—which is what thunder can achieve—then that invisible wind would be made compact. This kind of compaction breaks through walls, pervades all pores, and scatters everything. A similar compaction occurs in the body, which bursts forth from the center or root into one place, seizing whatever passage it follows. From this, it happens that the limbs are wrenched and broken by this disease, and are so struck that they are contracted and then dissolved. All these things occur within the enclosed skin. For just as thunder cannot strike outside the shells of the four Elements, but performs its entire force within its own shell, so in the *Microcosm* <note>The human being</note> itself, the thunder remains within the shell or skin, like the thunder of fire. 

If, however, the paroxysm <note>A sudden attack or fit</note> has finally ended, as we have reviewed part by part so far, a serene sky follows, just as after the thunder of fire. And just as you see the earth soaked and the roads made muddy after that thunder, so that some time is needed until they return to their previous state; so also in man, the reason, the limbs, the body, the senses, sight, hearing, and so on, rest for a while, until the *Sun of the Microcosm* <note>The internal life-force or vital spirit</note> restores the change that fell upon him and returns the man to his original state. Furthermore, as I have proposed this example to you, so you ought to compare the whole man to the greater world. Since man was created from it, he must necessarily have its likeness. Just as one region feels thunder more frequently than another, the same must be understood regarding man. For one is struck by this disease more or less than another. And although I may seem to have discussed these things sufficiently until now, it will nevertheless be necessary, because of the crowd that hinders the health of the sick at every moment, that I attempt a discussion of the cure itself. For the cure sweeps away and removes all these things. Therefore, attend to this diligently when that chapter is reached.

### SECTION III.

<margin>Signs of a paroxysm. FIRE.</margin>
<margin>Fire is a most vehement thing.</margin>
The signs of the falling sickness are evident in themselves. Therefore, in this place, I will at least review the signs of the Stars—that is, from which Star the disease proceeds. Concerning this, it should be clear to you that only the degrees of this disease come into consideration. For these stir the paroxysm. It receives its strength from its stars. The most grave, greatest, and most intense paroxysms are ascribed to Fire. For fire is the most vehement of all things, and the most atrocious pains are inflicted by it. Therefore, one must look here for the highest degree of pain.

<margin>EARTH.</margin>
Next, attribute the pain closest to the most grave to the Earthly star. For that is the second cause of pain.

<margin>WATER.</margin>
From here, turn to the third pain, which is in the middle between the two highest and the one lowest. Attribute this to the Element of *Water* and its Star.

<margin>AIR.</margin>
The lightest paroxysm of all is judged to belong to Air. In this way, the distinction must be made. Indeed, signs cannot be taken from anywhere else than from the multitude of pains.

Now, indeed, a gradation very often occurs: namely, an intensification from the minimum to the maximum, and conversely, a remission from the maximum to the minimum. This is a change from one *Element* to another. For it frequently happens that two, three, or sometimes all the Elements suffer together. Moreover, paroxysms are sometimes entangled and mixed among themselves. Then, the change is often such that today a paroxysm of fire weighs upon the patient, tomorrow one of water, etc.; these are signs of a grave and long-lasting residence of the diseases in all the stars. The use of such signs taken from the pains is that they make the way of the cure readier for us, as will be handed down in its proper place. Many other things could also be handed down here concerning the conditions of the paroxysms and their appearances; however, we will omit them in this place as they are manifest and conspicuous. For it is superfluous for a *Physician to explain to a Physician* what the eyes themselves witness and declare. Let each person see and hear what is obvious. For if the Physician's business is reduced to the point where he only wishes to be supported by the writings of others, nothing can be expected from him that leads to the health of the sick. These things are therefore placed within the experience of any Physician.

<margin>From where is the time of the falling sickness to be known?</margin>
The time of the beginning of the falling sickness must be sought from the four Astronomers, so that the Astronomer judges his part, the *Geomancer* <note>One who practices divination by means of the earth or geographical features</note> his part, and others theirs. For from these, it is understood what prognostications are to be made concerning the time and hour of the paroxysm.

<margin>Let the Physician be a fourfold Astronomer.</margin>
I would therefore propose that the Physician treat not just of the Stars, but of diseases and what is required for them. Let these things concerning the causes and signs of this disease suffice for now.

<margin>In what does the cure of the falling sickness consist?</margin>
There remains the care of the limbs. For we cannot resist the Stars themselves in any other way than by removing the "subject" upon which they act. Therefore, he who is about to cure this disease is compelled to obtain it through that subject. For who can take away the brightness of the Sun? Who can break *Mars*? Who knows how to rule *Saturn*? Who knows how to tame *Venus*? No one. And just as we are unable to change the state and face of the Moon (for whether she be new, full, or old, it must be borne by us entirely as it is), so much less are we able to break the stars here.

# CONCERNING THE FALLING SICKNESS.

Further care is therefore placed in this: that we know how to withdraw the bodies from the stars. These bodies are **Microcosmic** <note>In Paracelsus's view, the "Microcosm" is the human being, who contains within themselves a miniature version of the entire universe (the Macrocosm), including internal "stars" or governing forces.</note>.

<margin>Metals and stones from water.</margin>
It has already been said in various places and many times that metals, stones, and similar things are born from the Element of Water. But what do we contribute to this work? Not even the slightest bit. Indeed, those things grow even without our labor. From a clearly similar power, the diseases of the stars grow as well. Now, if any aversion <note>Meaning a prevention or turning-away of the disease.</note> could be made, it would surely be made in one just as much as in the other. For if you could prevent stones and metals from being born, you could also prevent diseases from being born from the stars. But if you cannot do the former, you will be much less able to do the latter. Truly, just as you see crops and grasses grow and become physical bodies, so too are diseases **incorporated** <note>Given a physical form within the body.</note>. But as soon as that incorporation has occurred, no healing will be of use. Therefore, the sense and reason here is twofold:

<margin>The cure of the falling sickness is twofold.</margin>
Namely, the **Cure of Incorporation** and the **Cure of the Harvest**. If any care is applied in the meantime, it is hardly a true cure, since it does not penetrate the root itself, but only deals with the established trunks. In a perfect cure, one must invade not the surroundings, but the "harvest" or the very beginning of the disease itself. We must firmly believe, therefore, that these whole bodies must be removed and separated from the stars—just as if one were to remove a weed from a garden so it does not grow, or as if one were to remove the bodies of minerals from the hand of the "Star of Water" and thus prohibit the minerals from growing. For unless a Physician knows the autumn and the harvest of a disease as well as a vine-dresser knows his vineyard, or a farmer knows his field, he will certainly provide not even the smallest utility in the cure. And upon this point the entire momentum is placed—something which the ancients never considered, even in their dreams. For Physicians of that sort <note>original: "Huius enim farinæ Medici," literally "Doctors of that flour/brand."</note> look only to their own profit, not to that of the sick; nor do they weigh the dignity of their calling with equal experience. They think everything is well cured as long as they can establish their opinions from books (whether those opinions are good or harmful), and as long as they know how to inspect much urine and pile up frequent prescriptions, however the matter otherwise falls or fits.

The principle of the cure ought to be this: that we divide the bodies of the star, and assign to each star its own body, and to each body its own star. Before this can be done, it is necessary to know how the star matches with the bodies in a disease, specifically in this way: Every seed must begin its growth in the genuine motion and course of the star. If it happens otherwise, it is a perversion of the growth.

<margin>How astral diseases are made.</margin>
Unless the star matches the seed with a similar position, and the nature of both is one, that which ought to have happened will not happen at all. From this source arise **astral diseases**, such as the **Falling Sickness** <note>original: "Caducus," referring to epilepsy.</note>. But regarding conception, note this: it can happen in no way unless there is one concordance of all things. And unless the four "stars" stand in their own "springtime," no conception will occur.

<margin>As it is fit for sowing.</margin>
For from the concordance of both, the offspring is conceived. Moreover, the conception will proceed properly if the laws remain correctly in their star—that is, if the sowing was not done in winter or in a rainy time, but found according to the **Astronomical** custom, which is comfortable and fit for all things to be produced. Furthermore, it must also be known that the stars concur in all diseases; and those which are astral diseases mix themselves and grow up together until the time of their maturation.

<margin>The nature of the maturation of diseases.</margin>
The maturation of these things is similar to metals. For they do not fall down like pears, but lie and rest in their place like stones. Although—if the **paroxysm** <note>A sudden attack or seizure.</note> is to be explained—this generation is like a tree from which the paroxysms proceed, not unlike the **saffron** <note>original: "crocus."</note>, which is plucked today and another is reborn tomorrow.

<margin>Saffron grows daily.</margin>
For every paroxysm, and every saffron flower, exists as one reason and science regarding its origin and generation.

In this way, if the body has grown, or if the body has taken on growth having been "sown" with the disease, then in the cure it must be entirely provided for that this "tree" be exempt from the power of the star, so that its operation never again passes into nature. This is obtained by ensuring that each one remains without its own dissolution, separated in a single conjunction. For here, no disease from the star grows separately unless the bodies and the stars constitute it together and at the same time, from a conjunction that is either convenient or inconvenient. Thus you see entirely that, unless oil and water are joined and fitted in a fire, no hissing or motion emerges. Both, therefore—namely the oil and the water—must be together, nor can we be without them.

<margin>Oil and water joined together stir up a hissing in the fire.</margin>
Yet we must take care with all zeal lest they come together or be joined in the operation of the star. For as the fire is, such is the star. But if oil and water are joined, then the reason is the same on both sides: that there is the beginning of the produced astral disease. For it is settled and certain that if, at conception, the heaven coincides with the **Red** and with the **Lion** <note>Likely referring to the astrological sign Leo and the "Red" (Mars or the alchemical Red King).</note>, and at the same time the impression of **Aquarius** inserts itself, then in that same place the beginning of the falling sickness emerges, breaking out and bringing itself forth from the course of its own horoscope, which the concordance of the four stars established.

<margin>Egyptian Days, etc.</margin>
In turn, it must not be forgotten that I should explain or bring to you the **Egyptian Days** <note>Traditionally, "Egyptian Days" (dies Aegyptiaci) were specific days of the month considered unlucky or dangerous for medical procedures, though Paracelsus interprets them astronomically here.</note> (I do not speak here magically, but as an Astronomer).

<margin>The knowledge of Egyptian days is adulterated today.</margin>
We have no knowledge of them from the art of the ancient Egyptian writers. Yet if we had it, it would certainly be evident that they correctly understood the four stars. However much we know of the Egyptian days, we know at least from the testimonies and their own indications that they secretly knew and understood this matter. Yet that art, from a sound sense, was afterwards turned and transmuted into a magical and deceptive nature, so that today it is not safe to trust it. For it is not such as it ought to be. God, however, looked to this: that we have no knowledge of that kind of concordance, nor do we greatly desire to have it. Therefore, in place of this, He established **Medicine** for us. If we observed conception according to the prescription of the ancients and those primates of astronomical things, then we would be afflicted by no diseases. But since we are begotten in **fornication** <note>original: "scortatione." Paracelsus suggests that humans conceive based on lust rather than waiting for the proper astrological timing, which he believes leads to disease.</note>, we are therefore subjected to all miseries.

<margin>Men today are begotten by fornication.</margin>
Lust and lewdness moderate conception today, not the mature time...

### SECTION III.

<margin>Where the cure of the falling sickness is placed.</margin>
...mature and selected. But if the distance <note>Likely referring to the duration or progression of the disease over time.</note> must be deeply and truly considered, its first foundation must be placed entirely in conception; then, the second in the dominion of the Star. But so that I do not overstep the boundaries of the proposed text, you must understand the beginning of the falling sickness, as far as the cure is concerned, in the following way: namely, that the bodies must be separated from one another. Now indeed, if two bodies are involved in this kind of effect and operation, it is impossible for them to be separated by hand; that is, it can in no way happen that either one is placed in its own proper place apart from the other. For who can take oil and water out of a fire? No one, I think. Just as none of us can perform this, it is no less impossible to separate and divide bodies in a <term>Vulcanic</term> <note>Referring to Vulcan, the god of fire; in alchemy, this refers to the use of fire and the furnace to transform matter.</note> operation. Therefore, I would have you understand me such that water can be separated from any oil through the **Athanar** alone, and not by hands. I am speaking of <term>spagyric</term> <note>The alchemical process of separating and recombining the constituents of a substance to create a medicine.</note> secrets, not of manual crafts. More on this matter hereafter.

<margin>The Athanar separates water from oil.</margin>
<margin>The Asylum: The Doctor and students are eternal.</margin>
<margin>The Fire of the Lion separates mixed astral bodies.</margin>
The hinge of the matter therefore turns on this: knowing how two mixed bodies can be separated, yet without the help of hands. For what hand can endure the fire? By that same reasoning, one must proceed with the Stars in the body. This must be perfected through its own proper fire, that is, through the Element of fire, which expels from itself what does not belong to that place. For you see that the separation of all things is done by and through fire. If, therefore, it must be entirely perfected through fire, then the fire suitable for those astral diseases is the **Fire of the Lion** <note>original: "ignis Leonis"; a term for a specific high degree of heat or a potent alchemical preparation.</note>. For it must be noted that the aforementioned concordance is fixed on both sides. Therefore, one should not attempt to separate what is fixed from what is fixed, but rather that the fixed be entirely separated from the fixed, and that one fixed thing becomes volatile, yet without being broken or otherwise separated, except so that it remains in its own **Anatomy**. For if the spirit slips away and collapses in the Anatomy, and does not hold its place: then, as has been said, you know the cause of the disease. Now, separation does not happen such that dross is produced from one and gold from the other, but rather so that nothing is corrupted, nothing is burned, and each thing is led to its own convenient place. I speak of a separation of such a kind that like is led to its like, and that spirits and bodies consist in one and the same likeness. If this is done, know that nothing else happens than that nothing is broken through this kind of Vulcanic **Athanar** <note>An alchemical furnace designed to provide a constant, even heat over long periods.</note>; yet it is not done likewise through wood, fire, or a brick furnace. Understand the matter as it has been handed down from before. I ask, however, that you be not ashamed to learn what you do not know. That will be much more honorable than remaining asses and geese by not learning, etc.

<margin>God is the creator of the arts.</margin>
...concedes. For by birth you are feminine <note>In this context, Paracelsus uses "feminine" pejoratively to imply weakness, gossip, or a tendency to corrupt rather than create; it is a common rhetorical flourish in his polemics.</note>, you who turn everything for the worse, not the better, for those who do not pay tribute to your finery. But as far as the invention of the arts is concerned, what do I feel about how they are obtained? I shall enumerate it next. You judge what sort of man I am in these things, whether honest or wicked. The origin of the arts is this: that they descend from one to another even down to me and to you; and what has not yet been manifested, that shall yet be manifested hereafter. For the Master and teacher of Medicine lives until the very last day, as do his disciples. But you create "Masters," and you do not remember that you yourselves are still novices, and your fathers are more foul than any dung, though you are all swollen with the "Most Blessed" <note>A sarcastic jab at the high titles of university doctors of his time.</note>. Therefore, attend to how Medicine reaches us, by which we complete a cure. First: which man can give an account of who learned the art of tilling the field, the vineyard, or of making cheese and butter, etc.? Certainly no one, except he who points his finger toward his Master. This master will point again to his own master, and so on consequently until the first. But whom will the very first of all point to? No one else but He who created man himself. He also created man's knowledge. For what would men have anywhere, unless they labored? For the mandate was promulgated once: *In the sweat of your brow you shall live.* <note>Genesis 3:19</note> This is indeed like a certain new creation. For God had said, *Let there be,* and everything was made. But the art was not made, nor the **Light of Nature**. However, when Adam was cast out of paradise, God created for him the **Light of Nature** <note>original: "lumen naturae"; the internal intellectual and spiritual capacity of humans to understand the world and the properties of things through observation and divine inspiration.</note>, when He commanded that he should live from the labors of his hands. He also created for Eve her own light, when He said, *in pain you shall bring forth children.* There, then, they were made plainly human and earthly creatures, who before had been as if Angelic. From this, Eve learned to raise children: hence the cradle, hence nursing were invented. For just as creatures were made through the Word: so through the same Word, the Light was also made, which was necessary for man. And so his intellect is no less necessary than the body itself. Therefore the inner man followed in a second creation, after he had departed from paradise.

<margin>The Light of Nature: when and by whom was it created?</margin>
<margin>Athanar etc.</margin>
<margin>Theophrastus's exculpation.</margin>
Furthermore, to satisfy many thoughts, I shall finally treat here of the arts by completing the cure: so that from this, the cause and origin of the disease may be more clearly understood. From this you will know by what sequence the arts proceed in these diseases, so that you do not later dare to claim that the Devil speaks out of Theophrastus, or that he brings forth such things from Necromancy or Astroth, etc.; or that he is full of incantations and a supreme Magician. Although you might not be lying that Theophrastus knows such things, and is wiser than all of you in them. Nevertheless, all that you babble about, he does not grant and...

<margin>Adam received the arts from an Angel.</margin>
Nothing further, therefore, is to be known than this: namely, how we received all our members from the first creation; and afterwards, how well all things were made? But the notice or knowledge which was necessary for man did not yet flourish in Adam. He received it, however, when he was cast out of paradise, from an Angel. But he did not receive everything; rather, he and his sons, in their succession, made use of the **Light of Nature** to learn what is in all things and to bring forth what is hidden and concealed in them. Therefore, at one and the same time, the whole man was made in respect to the body; but not in respect to the arts. And indeed all arts were given to him—not known and perceived, but to be known by learning. We shall discourse more on this: how we learn, namely, what we already know. For there is no peasant who does not know all arts in his light: which he himself, however, darkens so that it does not shine. How that light may be brought forth; attend further here, at least as much as is required for knowing this disease.

# ON THE FALLING SICKNESS #

<margin>The internal garden of the arts.</margin>
Indeed, a herb does not grow in gardens unless it is sown or planted. If this is not done, nothing grows. Yet, that which we sow is nothing other than earth. We entrust it to the earth, and from the earth, we pull it out again. It is the same with the "art" <note>In this context, "art" refers to specialized knowledge or medical skill.</note> that is instilled and driven into us. This is demonstrated by the one who teaches me. He possesses it from the **Light of Nature** <note>original: "lumen naturae"; the Paracelsian concept that all true knowledge of the physical world is a divine gift revealed through the observation of nature itself.</note>. I have it from the same source, no less. Nevertheless, it must be poured in and driven forward. Yet it often happens that many herbs grow which were not sown, and these are often the best. Likewise, there are many "teachable natures" <note>Referring to people with innate talent.</note> that are not "sown" by teachers, yet they are more sublime than those who are. Such is the power of the earth, and such is the Light of Nature, that neither side ever ceases or rests. In the meantime, simply take account and care of your own garden. For the "internal man" has been made with great skill. If he acts diligently with the "external man" and they share their mutual work, then he will certainly learn from himself what no one could have taught him—so much so, that he will be an object of wonder to everyone. This is how the arts of natural works take their beginning.

<margin>
Plantain restrains the menses.
Scarcely seven arts.
</margin>
Now, who revealed to the Physician that the **plantain** <note>a common herb, *Plantago major*</note> stops the **menses** <note>menstrual flow</note>, when such a thing is not visible in the plant? Who persuaded him of its use? Only the Creator, of course. He gave the Physician this knowledge so that he might learn—and yet, he may not even know *how* he learns it—and thus he learns from the power of fruitful creation, which is itself the Light of Nature. Furthermore, how is this knowledge recognized and made manifest? Truly, there are seven ways by which we emerge as craftsmen.

<margin>1. Through spirits and angels.</margin>
The first of these is this: as happens quite often and as the secrets themselves show, spirits and angels have taught or continue to teach the arts. Their teaching was no different than how a Master instills in a boy what was already within him. In this way, they made the art manifest. This frequently happens to people in times of great necessity.

<margin>2. Through the counsel of men.</margin>
Secondly, a man has often given fit and suitable advice to another man, which the giver himself did not even understand. For in this case, the Light of Nature worked effectively in the other person, and whether it turned out well or poorly was noted down. For **Leviathan** <note>Used here metaphorically for the devil or a spirit of chaos and distraction.</note> is never at rest, but constantly throws his evil into our midst.

<margin>3. Through accidental experience.</margin>
Thirdly, many arts have been revealed to us through accidental experience, specifically when someone tried something based on their own opinion and it happened to succeed. Thus the Light of Nature prepared it and led the sick person to it, even though they had previously neglected it and considered it worthless. In this way, nature finally produced it from her own Light.

<margin>4. Through sorts of divination.</margin>
Fourthly, many Magi attained the arts, such as the Nigromancers, Necromancers, Pyromancers, Geomancers (I do not mean astral Pyromancy or Geomancy, but those who deal in **sortilege** <note>divination by drawing lots</note>), and Hydromancers. All of these have revealed many arts through the art of divination; not indeed by the power of the craft they supposed, but because the Light of Nature revealed it to them, albeit through trickery and deceit, by the power of their own desire. For the Light of Nature plays with man in this way. If the arts had performed this by their own virtue, the same thing would surely still succeed today for many lazy people. For one cannot obtain the arts in this way without a powerful faith, directed and focused upon the Light with a fiery desire. However, many eventually fell away into mere fortune-telling.

<margin>5. Through chiromancy.</margin>
Fifthly, many arts were produced through **Chiromancy**, specifically when the chiromancy of the hands, and the chiromancy of herbs or wood, made a person skillful and artistic. It was not without merit that Chiromancy was held in such high dignity among the ancients. Although today we use it only for fortune-telling, the ancients practiced it to track down the arts. I will not reject this Chiromancy either, but will hold it entirely as an inventor of the arts.

<margin>
6. Through Physiognomy. What is Physiognomy?
Archelaic secrets, etc.
</margin>
Sixthly, many arts were discovered through **Physiognomy**. Physiognomy is the art that indicates the essences hidden within, not only in man, but also in growing things; in all of them, the internal things are known through the external. In this way, almost all the **Archelaic secrets** <note>From "Archeus," the vital internal force that Paracelsus believed governed the functions of life and the growth of minerals and plants.</note> were discovered.

<margin>7. Through form.</margin>
Seventhly, arts were explored through **form**, when one form indicated another, so that like responded to like—cancer to a crab, form to form, etc.—just as the **serpentine** <note>A stone or plant resembling a snake.</note> is used for the venom of snakes, and many similar things.

There are also more inventions of the arts of this kind, such as those made through Astronomy, through Philosophy, and through the science of herbs and natural things, about all of which I shall establish a special little book, from which you will be able to understand everything more easily and clearly.

<margin>Praise for Alchemy.</margin>
I also attribute a great deal to experience, by which someone proposes something to themselves, as in **Alchemies**, where many unheard-of and scarcely believable things are produced. From these, a fruitful science and distinguished experience in the Light of Nature is gathered. And I would dare to swear that this experience has produced the highest and most subtle foundation in Medicine. For without it, who will ever be a Physician, or know or understand anything?

Now, consider carefully among yourselves whether I am writing something new, from what source I write it, and from where I take it. For I do not take it from your books—which, along with you, I would send straight to **Vulcan** <note>The god of fire; he means he would burn the traditional medical textbooks.</note>. And judge at last whether I should not be permitted to write, even if you snarl at me worse than a dog.

But let me break off here and return to describing the falling sickness. I believe its cause, origin, and signs have been handed down accurately enough, so that now only the method of curing remains to be proposed, so that we may finally bring what we have begun to its conclusion. To all of you in general, whether you act as Physicians or read these works of mine: I ask you earnestly not to pass judgment on me too hastily, but to suspend it entirely until you have seen the faithfulness of this treatment. Do not let the great crowd of those who oppose me be a stumbling block to you. Think on this: one **millstone** <note>original: "lapidem molarem"</note> brings more utility than all the rocks hidden in the mountains. For just as it is the condition and duty of a millstone never to rest, but to always rotate and turn the mill, so it is right for medicine to be practiced continually.

He rejects traditional textbooks in favor of active, practical investigation, comparing the true physician to a tireless millstone.</summary>

<header>SECTION IV.</header>

A rock hidden in a mountain is indeed a stone; but whom does it benefit? It stands there without use, without motion. However, the **Light of Nature** <note>original: "Lumen naturae"; the innate wisdom provided by God through the observation of the natural world.</note> must be stirred up repeatedly, and this mill must never rest. Otherwise, it will fail and die.

### SECTION IV.

<margin>Where the Light of Nature perishes.</margin>
**I**n the distribution of care, it seems right that I should follow the progression of the arts, just as we have handed down the history of discoveries. For the sake of greater clarity, we will establish the order such that "Canonical" care <note>Standard or traditional medical practice based on established rules.</note> comes first, and then the **Arcana** <note>original: "arcana"; secret, powerful remedies that act through their spiritual essence rather than physical qualities.</note> shall follow, each one according to its own process as they have reached us. Although I will not bring forward everything belonging to this profession here, I nonetheless entrust these matters to the experience of others no less than to my own. Nothing is omitted here, not even the smallest letter required for this subject. Moreover, other books have been compiled by us elsewhere, in which the "Anatomy of the Falling Sickness" <note>The "Falling Sickness" (original: "Caducus") is the historical term for epilepsy.</note> is treated separately and specifically. One may compare the reading of those books with these. For I am not accustomed to saying or treating the same thing twice. In the book on **Phlebotomy** <note>Bloodletting.</note>, you will find the order in which the cutting of a vein ought to be performed for this disease. Likewise, in the method of <term>pharmatidi</term> <note>original: "pharmatidi"; a term derived from Greek referring to the use of purgative drugs.</note> you will find some purifications useful for the falling sickness. All of these I omit here, and I simply propose the proper process of care. The rest, depending on the variety of circumstances, ought to be either employed or excluded, which we leave to the judgment of any skilled Physician.
<margin>Dual care for the falling sickness.</margin>

<margin>Canonical Care.</margin>
First, regarding **Canonical care**, the rule states that "cold is driven out by hot, and hot by cold." But this rule will not be valid here, nor will it be of use in this disease. For its cause is neither heat, nor cold, nor moisture, nor dryness; rather, it is the mixing of bodies that are adverse to one another that must be considered—not complexions, nor qualities, nor humors. You see, of course, that this contrariety or conflict is greatest if two "Marses" <note>In Paracelsian thought, "Mars" refers to a specific iron-like or forceful spiritual quality in minerals or the body.</note>, who are of one nature, oppose each other, or even two "Saturns," in the manner we have described. This kind of contrariety is what you must know and approach, not "hot" or "cold." <margin>Why does water crackle when thrown into hot butter?</margin> If water is poured into boiling butter, what is the cause of that hissing and crackling? It is certainly not a "quality," nor a "complexion," nor a "humor," but the body itself. For those two bodies cannot exist together under the action of fire. And this action is exactly what must be discussed regarding the cure of the Falling Sickness. Therefore, Canonical care, as it is commonly understood, will have no place here.

Furthermore, my adversaries also prescribe purges, syrups, and "comforting" medicines. They call this "regular care." Now, after the cure is completed, let you all judge whether it should be called regular or irregular. To me, it seems entirely irregular; for it benefits and helps nothing. Therefore, those processes provide either nothing or the very minimum of benefit. Although they might mix the "care of arcana" into that other method, if anything is achieved through them, they credit the "Recipe," which actually hinders more than it helps. <margin>In what does the composition consist?</margin> For the basis of the composition of Recipes consists in the arcana. They, however, place all their power in laxatives and **colocynth** <note>A powerful and often harsh bitter purgative derived from a desert vine.</note>. What kind of foundation this is, I leave to all of you to judge.

As for what constitutes a "Canonical" medicament or a "Regular" remedy, I believe that cannot be investigated by any other reasoning than that which we shall propose hereafter. For it is right to hold to that process which we have drawn from the very foundations, despising all the recipes of those <note>Paracelsus uses the crude term "Cacatilium," a play on words suggesting "toilet-doctors" or those who focus only on excretion.</note> "Privy-Doctors," who attempt to accomplish everything by purging, without considering that "dung" is not the cause of the problem. If dung were truly the cause, then they would undoubtedly be the "Regulars" and "Canons" in that matter.

<margin>What Canonical care is.</margin>
Since any care that heals the sick is "Canonical," while that which does not heal can be called neither "Canonical" nor "Regular," we shall first take up that Canonical medicine which has been handed down through the teaching of either "spirits" (as you might call them) or "angels." In this, as far as my art instructs me, I see nothing superstitious involved. For whatever this is, it has been handed down through the **similitude** <note>The principle of "Like cures Like" or finding signatures in nature that match the disease.</note> of that which was in nature. And it is my firm opinion that **Chiromancy, Physiognomy, Anatomy, Necromancy, and Astronomy**, etc., emerged chiefly for this purpose: so that through them we might penetrate into the art itself—one person in this way, another in that, but all through God. Now, either an Angel or a spirit seems to me quite suitable to instruct me as a Master in natural things. <margin>Spirits know all natural things.</margin> For what is there anywhere in Nature that escapes them, or that they do not know? A man must certainly learn from someone who knows the matter, rather than from someone who does not. <margin>By whom the Physician is taught.</margin> For we are made expert and wise by the expert; conversely, we are made ignorant by the ignorant. God alone can make a Physician. Many things can teach a Physician. No man despises or rejects what God bestows. For is there any man who can teach us, or who knows herbs of his own accord? It is necessary that this knowledge flows from others, who are something more than mere men. It is of the highest interest to Physicians that they learn the certain and established truth. From such teachers, no Physician was ever taught anything false. Yet many "false physicians" have broken in with these truths, contaminating the teaching of the legitimate Master and placing Medicine upon pillars of lies.

<margin>Oak mistletoe: medicine for the falling sickness.</margin>
For example, a certain Art was first taken from <term>visco quercino</term> <note>original: "visco quercino"; Mistletoe that grows specifically on oak trees, traditionally considered more potent than other varieties.</note>, which is a medicine for the Falling Sickness—provided we have a "falling" disease that labors in the same way as the one for whom that remedy was revealed. However, physicians have neglected this and forgotten the signs of the disease, introducing errors so that the "faith"—that is, the **Arcanum** existing within the mistletoe—was obliterated. Now, I have identified four types of Falling Sickness. We will follow this division here, not observing the numbered series here, but mentioning in the section on Arcana which remedy works for which type. <margin>For which falling sickness and which age oak mistletoe is useful.</margin> Note here concerning mistletoe that it is useful in the "watery" falling sickness, or that which is born from the Stars of the Element of Water. It is specifically beneficial in [certain] behaviors and separates the "falling conjunction" of Venus and the Moon, and the Moon and Saturn, and Saturn and Venus. Its process is as follows...
