<header>### ON THE FALLING SICKNESS</header>

<margin>What is the great Ylech?</margin>
...possesses. Take mistletoe <note>original: "viscum"; historically used for its perceived neurological effects</note> gathered under the ascending signs of its creation, and give it crushed in a drink at the weight of half an ounce, up to the third degree; repeat a second and third time, and the patient will be healed. You might marvel at the simplicity and brevity of this medicine for a disease so long and grave. But what do you think of the hour and the time—what do they provide? These very things were indicated and revealed to the sick, but they were not committed to observation. The medicine itself was noted, but the **Ascendant** <note>The specific zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon, believed to influence the potency of the herb.</note> was not. Truly, should I not laugh when I see so many schools and academies laboring over mistletoe and yet achieving nothing? Away with those Doctors! For they have not once considered the Ascendant itself, which I call the **Great Ylech** <note>original: "Ylech"; a Paracelsian term referring to a primordial or vital force, often linked to astrological influence.</note>, without whose knowledge a physician is entirely ignorant. Therefore, they have fluttered about fruitlessly in the arts, like a hornet in a boot. Is it any wonder you can heal no one, when you are completely ignorant of the **Ylech**? Who, then, raised you to the status of the Doctorate?

<margin>Titiofonis's cure for the falling sickness.</margin>
Another art was also revealed in the time of Titiofonis, suggesting that the patient drink the blood of a decapitated man. When this was done, the patient recovered. What else can you conclude from this, other than the truth of the art, by the reasoning that at that time a concordance of the Stars was achieved? For unless the stars are conquered and overcome, none of these things will happen.

<margin>Human blood as a cure for the falling sickness.</margin>
But you physicians provide blood to be drunk without a foresight of the Stars; with this remedy, you kill more than you heal. Its process consists in this: that during the conjunctions of Leo, Taurus, Aries, Scorpio, as well as Mars, Jupiter, Mercury, and the Sun, you administer it warm and quickly—specifically to those falling-sickness patients who carry the exaltation of those Stars. This is for the reason that the Stars remain entirely within the blood until it cools. Therefore, you shall judge the blood with mature judgment, lest it be infected by the Stars. If it is infected, let it not be drunk; but let healthy blood be drunk. Once swallowed, nothing else happens except that the Stars are renewed in the sick man, and the healthy overcomes the sick in all diseases, if it is administered in its own **Ylech**. And these are the **Arcana** <note>Secret or "essential" medicines that work through spiritual rather than physical qualities.</note> from the Stars, about which more writings are found in the manner of "Preparations," which I wish to indicate in passing to the reader.

<margin>Spirits possess countless arts.</margin>
With these things brought forward, it seems timely to close the arts that were produced and manifested through the "invisible mouth." I attribute this to those Authors: that they held countless arts of this kind within their grasp. For they have full knowledge of the Stars, and of those who rule the Stars, whose use we require. Therefore, physicians, learn, learn!

<margin>The invention of arts from these dreams.</margin>
Just as arts were produced through spirits or Angels—both evil (as you wish) and good—which only a physician can judge, so in the same way arts were found and produced through dreams. This happened when men invoked the Gods for these things, or, as some wish, even the divine ones, or, as it seems to others, the one and only God. Through sleep, they were made masters of their petition, and through dreams, health was offered to them—that is, a suitable medicine by which they might be restored to health.

<margin>The power of the Light of Nature.</margin>
This happens not only to Christians, but also to Turks, Heathens, Saracens, Jews, Mamluks, Persians, Egyptians, and the like. I can hardly believe that these revelations descended from heaven, since there is only one God. Yet I maintain that the **Light of Nature** <note>original: "Lumen Naturae"; the innate wisdom provided to all humans through the observation of the natural world.</note> handed these things down to its disciples. Although nature lacks speech, it prefigures things through sleep by the power of the Word, through which God established the inner man in the Light of Nature. For they are taught by this power. Meanwhile, they err in this: that they took others as Masters who were not truly such.

<margin>The human skull as a remedy for the falling sickness.</margin>
Since the Light of Nature confers such good knowledge upon us, it is right that I indicate in this place a medicine taken from the skull, which is administered to falling-sickness patients in this way. This bone of the head is the very center. If it is drunk, the man becomes healthy. But its process is far different than those fictitious physicians have established. For they filed down all skulls and gave them to be drunk, in which they held to their old, worthless customs.

<margin>What is the shape of the skull-bone?</margin>
<margin>The stars of the skull are not in everyone.</margin>
This small bone of the "cross-bearer" <note>original: "crucigeri"; likely referring to the sutural or "Wormian" bones in the skull that can form cross-like shapes.</note> (it is a type of coin-like shape) does not exceed the width of a coin, and is angular, located behind the fissure; it is not found in all skulls, but only in some. For the Stars cleave it, not bodies or birth. Let filings of this small bone be drunk only for one occasion: as much as there is of it, at the beginning of a paroxysm <note>A sudden attack or seizure.</note>, under the **exaltation of the Moon**. Thus, the first draft will help immediately. For experience itself testifies that by this, the "conjunction" of the disease is separated so that no further meeting occurs on either side.

<margin>The Light of Nature is the most skillful Master, but to unwise children.</margin>
You might rightly call this Light of Nature the most skillful Mistress of all. For what man could have known or found this by himself?

Furthermore, it also happens that advice is sometimes given by those who neither know the matter themselves nor have experienced it. This also happens through the Light of Nature, urging men repeatedly so that they cannot contain the secrets, but are compelled to reveal them entirely. Just as a flower in the field bursts forth from the earth, not for its own benefit, but to be food for the cattle: so for that same end, Nature herself pushes out her secrets, which are thereafter found to be reliable.

<margin>Peony seed as a remedy for the falling sickness.</margin>
In this way, the seeds of the Peony were first advised and recommended because they were beautiful and cleverly colored, so that they might be put to wondrous use. And nature reveals such things in many ways while things are administered and offered, either due to rarity, or costliness, or fame, in which other virtues are then discovered to be hidden at the same time. Therefore, great honor and esteem should be given to the Peony seed—not as the ancients used it, but if it is applied by a legitimate process. For its power is to pacify and restrain the stars, lest they be carried away into a paroxysm, while an "exaltation" is fabricated from the earthly stars, Saturn and the Moon, and partly Jupiter himself, and frequently in many other diseases of the falling sickness. For blessed is the **Spagyric** <note>An alchemist-physician who uses the "Spagyric art" to separate, purify, and recombine the essential virtues of plants and minerals.</note> who can harmonize the Stars of the Peony to the Stars of the earth, and administer them in their own exaltation. And...

# PARAGRAPH VI.

<margin>Arts discovered through experience.</margin>
The correction of this disease is based on this: that the medicine be drunk according to the prescribed alignment <note>original: "coniunctionis"; referring to the conjunction of planets</note>, and administered in such a way that the patient's internal "Star" does not withdraw or waste away within the body, but rather that the Peony <note>A plant long associated with healing the "falling sickness."</note> always remains the **Governess**, protecting the healthy body.

<margin>Antimony as a remedy for the falling sickness.</margin>
But experience also brings forth medicines. Thus, **Antimony** <note>A metallic element that Paracelsian physicians believed had powerful purgative and curative properties when "purified."</note> has been prepared through the transmutation of things and reduced to such a state that it passes into sweetness. This substance, when licked by infants, healed a certain child who happened to be among their number and suffered from the falling sickness. Now, who would discourage the use of Antimony, or not love it vehemently, seeing how its power has since wonderfully benefited so many cases? Is this discovery not worth more than the entire doctrine of Avicenna? <note>Ibn Sina, a foundational Persian physician whose traditional theories Paracelsus often rejected.</note> Furthermore, such a potent power and **Secret** <note>original: "Arcanum"; a deep hidden virtue in nature.</note> lies hidden in Antimony that it removes even the most violent paroxysm—that is, the "fiery" fit. Who would despise such a discovery? Who would reject it simply because it is not contained in the books and the "Galenic lyre"? <note>A mocking reference to the traditional followers of Galen, the ancient Greek physician.</note> Yet all of them, if compared to this Secret, are worth nothing at all. The preparation of this, described as the "White Flowers of Antimony," is found in the section on preparations. Therefore, it would be idle to repeat it here, especially since it is well enough known to all skilled practitioners. Its order is this: nine grains should be given before the paroxysm; in the middle of the paroxysm, eighteen grains should be placed in the mouth by whatever means possible; and after one hour of sleep, another nine grains. This should be repeated as often as necessary until the third paroxysm, which will be the last.

<margin>Galen is eluded.</margin>
<margin>Arts discovered through Nigromancy, etc.</margin>
Furthermore, arts have also been found through **Nigromancy** and **Necromancy** <note>In this context, these terms often refer to "black arts" or intuitive methods used to uncover hidden properties in nature, rather than strictly "evil" magic.</note> that are healthful for the falling sickness—namely, those involving Gold and Corals. Others were found through **Pyromantic** <note>Divination by fire or light.</note> lot-casting, involving Crystals, fingernails, and visions; others through literary **Geomancy** <note>Divination using earth or patterns; here, perhaps referring to the study of signs and markers.</note>, with compasses, leaden images, wax, rods, candles, and so on, just as the lot-casters explain. In this way, the art of the **Vulture's Gall** <note>The bile of a vulture, used in folk medicine.</note> was discovered through Pyromancy. Both, however, involve lot-casting. In the meantime, the **Light of Nature** has proven this art, not by the power of a potent craft, but by the faithfulness of the discoverer. The preparation of this art is as follows.

<margin>Vulture's Gall discovered through Pyromancy.</margin>

## ON CORALS.

<margin>Preparation of Corals for the falling sickness.</margin>
According to the method of Necromancy, the way to use Corals is to grind them as finely as possible and mix them with **Alcohol of Wine** <note>original: "Alcool vini"; highly distilled or pure spirit of wine.</note> until all redness leaves their body. Digest this until it liquefies. The dose is half a scruple <note>symbol: ℈ β; about 0.6 grams.</note> every morning, until the fourth conjunction and movement of the stars.

These two remedies are suitable for those with the falling sickness if they are "exalted" in Leo, the Sun, and Mars; they especially regard the fiery complexion of the Stars. And although even here the stars are not proposed according to their specific motion, nevertheless, daily administration overcomes the daily nature of the Stars. By the power of these secrets, it also expels the nature of the stars so that they fall silent in their motion and do not stir up the disease at all.

<margin>Arts from Pyromancy.</margin>
Many such arts have been brought forth from Pyromancy, which were discovered and administered through lot-casting, such as through Beryls, Crystals, and other things, as the profession teaches. Indeed, such arts are innumerable. Among these, some are quite excellent and distinguished, such as **Unicorn** <note>Usually referring to narwhal tusk or "fossilized" bone, believed to have immense detoxifying powers.</note>, which is excellently prepared by itself, but one must still attend to the stars—that they are positioned in the element of Water and exalted in the watery signs. No other signs need be observed there except the beginning of the "shaking" or the <term>Lorindi</term> <note>A Paracelsian term for the onset or aura of an epileptic seizure.</note>. Then, administer the Unicorn at a weight of 15 grains, nine times or more, as the watery stars occur.

<margin>Unicorn as a remedy for the falling sickness.</margin>
The nature of all these secrets and arts is such that they are applied either simply or alone, without the mixing of "Recipes." For those teachers who pass down these things are dealing with the highest secrets; they do not babble like common men about Recipes without a foundation of knowledge. And although this virtue does not lie in the Unicorn alone, but in many other things as well, it nevertheless seemed right to the masters of Pyromancy that this one should be revealed here, because all things are brought forth from the same fountain of doctrine, differing only in the knowledge of the specific things.

## ON GOLD.

<margin>Preparation of Gold against the falling sickness.</margin>
The preparation of gold according to the discovery of Nigromancy is this: purify it through Antimony to its highest refinement and reduce it into thin sheets. Cover these in "cement" <note>A mixture used in refining or alchemical heating.</note> with sheets of **Saturn** <note>The alchemical name for Lead.</note> for a space of fourteen hours. Afterward, let a separation be made, and let a digestion be set up in a suitable furnace for about twenty days in "burning wine" <note>Strong distilled alcohol.</note> that has been properly purified. Let it be separated very gently in a **Bath of Mary** <note>A gentle water bath (bain-marie) used for slow heating.</note>, and keep the liquor. The dose is one scruple six times, one hour before the paroxysm; and during the paroxysms themselves, half a scruple in the morning and evening likewise, until the sixth paroxysm has passed. Although Nigromancy does not indicate the exaltation of the stars in this specific place, it is still observed in that it is ordered to be given at the start of the paroxysm. For all medicines that are thus related to the paroxysm take their origin from the stars. Although many physicians do not understand this and explain it in other ways, the disease itself and its cause nevertheless teach that the stars are moved, and not the bodies.

<margin>Arts from Geomancy</margin>
With the same fertility, **Geomancy** has also produced many arts, namely **Camphor**, **Mummy** <note>original: "Mumia"; a medicinal substance made from resin or sometimes actual mummified remains, used as a panacea.</note>, **Spodium** <note>Metallic ash or residue.</note>, and others like them. In administering these, no other method is required except that they be given as they are in themselves. Regarding these, let it be known to the Physician that our **Archimagi** <note>High masters or "Great Mages" of the alchemical and medical arts.</note>, who profess these Secrets to their disciples through this art, reveal them only according to the level of understanding the disciple has in such matters. If he is refined and skillful, then more excellent and ancient secrets are shared with him. If not, then lesser and more common ones, lest he receive secrets he cannot understand. These Geomancers, therefore, discovered arts concerning Camphor, Mummy, and Spodium only because they were not more learned. Thus, the spirit of Geomancy did not suggest greater secrets to them. And yet, there is one inspiration for all, according to the condition of the Stars, as we have said, not in respect to the physical body.

<margin>Camphor, Mummy, and Spodium as remedies for the falling sickness.</margin>
<margin>Secrets which are given to greater or lesser degrees.</margin>
To this class also belong those Secrets which are suited only for infants, or only for adults, just as some are for women and some for virgins. For when Secrets were sought for infants alone, only those were found. Therefore, one should not inquire more deeply into them than as...

# CONCERNING THE FALLING SICKNESS

## CONCERNING THE FALLING SICKNESS

<margin>Plantain. Chiromancy is the discoverer of many arts.</margin>
...just as they have been given. The Sophist Doctors <note>False scholars who prioritize rhetoric over truth.</note> do not understand this, as they constantly seek more from a thing than it actually contains. The reason for their failed efforts is that they are ignorant of the origin and the ultimate goal of the medical art.
One of the **secrets** <note>original: "arcanis"; hidden healing virtues</note> discovered through **Chiromancy** <note>Usually palm-reading, but for Paracelsus, it is the "art of signs" used to read the lines and textures of plants and minerals.</note> is the **Plantain**. Indeed, this same art is the discoverer of many other arts as well. Let no physician boast of himself if he cannot discover true arts, but instead wears himself out only with "pictures" <note>Outward appearances without understanding internal power.</note>. For who would celebrate a doctor who does not know how to prove his own art? But I will not be unmindful of you in my books; I will lead you into schools much more famous than those of your "red Doctors" <note>A reference to the red robes worn by university-trained doctors.</note>, who are nothing but mere **novices** <note>original: "Beani"; a derogatory term for uninitiated or clumsy students.</note>. For he is a novice who seeks his art in a state of turmoil and runs about like one who has lost all five senses except for four.

<margin>Arts derived from Chiromancy.</margin>
To explain these **secrets** derived from Chiromancy—which does not flow from spirits or sorcery, but arises from nature itself and Natural discovery—one must know that the chiromancy of the plantain and the chiromancy of the "falling air" <note>One of the four elemental types of epilepsy.</note> are of one and the same formation. Therefore, the whole plantain, with its leaves and roots, must be given during the rise of the **Ascendant** <note>The astrological sign rising on the eastern horizon.</note>. If you repeat this three times, you will feel no paroxysm <note>A sudden attack or fit.</note> thereafter. For that Ascendant is the very likeness of this chiromancy. What do you "Recipe-mongers" and "Syrup-drinkers" <note>Paracelsus's mocking names for traditional physicians who relied on complex, ineffective mixtures.</note> think of these secrets? If you would only spend your effort on knowing Nature, then you would know from her external face what lies hidden within her. But how can you discover arts when you are so unskilled? If your Avicenna, Galen, and Vigo, etc., are wrapped up in the Devil’s backside, where, I ask you, will your arts eventually break out? They will all go to hell.

<margin>Plantain as a remedy for the falling sickness.</margin>
Many "simples" <note>Medicines made from a single herb.</note> are taken from chiromancy, though they cannot all be recorded here because of their great number. There are more in my *Herbal*, where I define all these things with a richer explanation. For it is of no small importance that these things be narrated clearly and lucidly, so that the principle is maintained: how the arts descend to us, and in what sense and manner they ought to be understood, so that even unskilled doctors can grasp them—who otherwise speak and judge like blind men talking about colors.

<margin>Which arts come from Physiognomy.</margin>
**Physiognomy** <note>The art of judging character or qualities from physical features; here, applied to plants and diseases.</note> also teaches us about the medicine of men. For from Physiognomy, diseases are identified—the physiognomy of herbs, and so on. In this way, we are taught to match like with like. It is absolutely necessary that we be taught from elsewhere, for our Universities profess nothing of the truth.

<margin>Swallow, poppy, crystal, manna. Four classes of remedies for the falling sickness.</margin>
Thus, for the "falling sickness" of Fire, the **secret** is the **Swallow** <note>original: "Hirundinis"; parts of the swallow were used in folk medicine for epilepsy.</note>; in the falling sickness of Earth, the **Poppy**; in the falling sickness of Water, the **Crystal**; in the falling sickness of Air, **Manna** <note>original: "Tereniabin"; a Persian term for the sugary exudate of certain plants.</note>. These must be administered according to the ascending degrees, from 10 up to 60 or 70, for the beginning of the Ascendants.

Regarding these revelations of **secrets** through natural discovery, it must be held that great protection should be placed in them. For Nature teaches you nothing of evil or fraud. Just as she produced one human similar to another, so she has made and will make the medicine itself similar to the disease. And here lies the art that the physician seeks—not in <margin>Brunschwig.</margin> **Brunschwig** <note>Hieronymus Brunschwig, a famous surgeon and distiller whose methods Paracelsus often critiqued.</note>, not in Serapion, etc. For even Dioscorides himself is compelled to be a disciple of Nature. Unless you follow her, you will by no means be physicians, but mere wandering vagabonds.

<margin>Arts from Anatomy.</margin>
Similarly, arts have also flowed from **Anatomy**, when form is joined to form, indicating that to which the hidden or concealed virtue beneath the form leads. This is most evident in **Acorus** <note>Sweet Flag, a medicinal plant.</note>, whose anatomy is similar to the falling sickness of the elements of Water and Air, not only in form but also in color, nature, and behavior. <margin>Acorus as a remedy for the falling sickness of Water and Air.</margin> You should know, therefore, that Acorus must be administered—not preserved, and not dissolved in its anatomy—according to the logic of its **star** <note>original: "pro ratione sui astri"; its astrological signature.</note>. For the form goads and warns all physicians to learn to prepare recipes in such a way that if a foot is missing from the anatomy, a foot is replaced; if an eye is lacking, an eye is restored; if a tooth is absent, a tooth is inserted; and so with all members, until the human being becomes whole. For a human is healed by a whole human <note>i.e., a "whole" or complete medicine.</note>, and not by one that is mutilated or dissolved. For as long as Medicine does not invisibly possess the whole **Microcosm** <note>The "small world"—the human body as a reflection of the universe.</note> in its Anatomy, health remains crippled and medicine imperfect. Therefore, a recipe is not made whole by Sage, Lavender, or Marjoram, but by the "members" <note>The functional parts of the medicine that correspond to the body.</note>, which have never been considered or explained in the Universities. The leaders of those schools deal in mere cobbler's work, applying heat to cold and constrictives to laxatives <note>The Galenic method of "curing by contraries," which Paracelsus rejected.</note>; through such trifles, no one can ever penetrate to a solid knowledge of Medicine.

<margin>Arts from Astronomy.</margin>
Furthermore, **Astronomy**—the knowledge of the heavens and the other three elements—also teaches and hands down the knowledge of all diseases. Once the disease is known, it is easy to judge that what the star gave must be taken away again by the star. From this arises the art of bloodletting. Since I have explained this in its own specific books, I will not touch upon it here. Any physician who is ignorant of the Stars is not a physician, but a "tempter" <note>One who experiments blindly on patients.</note>. Now, there is no crime more shameful than to experiment in matters concerning body and life. And this is what Christ taught us to pray: that we be not led into temptation. For what else is "tempting" but acting imprudently and uncertainly, thereby harming the body and life? Whatever we do, we must do with full understanding. For it is not pleasing to God that we walk in ignorance and vanity. Nor will that serve as an excuse for us. We must pray, therefore, that the punishment of "temptation" does not overwhelm us. For it is the doctor’s duty not to "tempt," but to *know*. Masters are available everywhere from whom a physician may be taught. These are not to be sought in the Universities. For those who act there are nothing but "privileged fools" who have obtained seals and privileges, and having taken an oath, have taken care that they should never be made any more learned.

<margin>Arts from Philosophy. Philosophy is the mother of all sciences.</margin>
All sciences flow from **Philosophy**. For the aforementioned arts constitute the whole of Philosophy, which is discovered through them. It does not proceed from opinion or fantasy, but from proven and scientific Masters, whom neither Aristotle, nor Pliny, nor Dioscorides, etc., ever knew or possessed. With these men, therefore, a worthy physician does not easily...

<header>PARAGRAPH 4.</header>

# PARAGRAPH 4.

...may easily contribute. For it is necessary that any Physician be led astray who wishes to follow those who have never learned. For who has known the truth or any art without a Master? No one. We know the truth of our soul from God; otherwise, nothing of it would be certain to us. In the same way, we have drawn the truth of Philosophy from nature, which she taught us without idle fantasies. For to speculate too much is the same as to trifle or to pray too much <note>Paracelsus argues that practical observation of nature is more "holy" than empty theorizing or religious performance without action.</note>. And just as Christ exhibited himself in person to the eyes of men, so also in nature we have "personal" Masters, from whom Philosophers must be born—not by seeing nothing, but by seeing everything. For sight and touch bear witness to the truth. However, many trifles and prayers obtain nothing. Therefore, I earnestly urge you not to hold Philosophy in the least contempt, but to claim full possession of it for yourselves. Thus it will happen that you reach the genuine foundation of Medicine.

<margin>Arts from **Alchemy** <note>original: "Alchimia"</note>.</margin>
Now indeed, **Alchemy** has brought many distinguished and sublime **secrets** <note>original: "arcana"; hidden healing virtues</note> to light: not specifically sought after, and yet found. Therefore, let Alchemy be great and venerable to anyone. There are many of these secrets in **Tartar**, in **Juniper**, in **Melissa**, in **Tincture**, in **Vitriol**, in **Salt**, in **Alum**, in the **Moon** <note>Silver</note>, and in the **Sun** <note>Gold</note>: which are, however, omitted here for the sake of avoiding wordiness. Yet, from all those known to me, I have selected a single one concerning vitriol, which I am about to explain to you. By this, I believe I shall accomplish more than if I were to set forth all the others in a long series.

<margin>Vitriol is the secret for the **falling sickness** <note>Epilepsy; original: "caduci"</note>.</margin>
In vitriol there is a secret concerning the falling sickness; however, it benefits few. The error arises from this: that those challenged, while they strive to improve things, usually make them worse, forgetful that they are fools. In this way, they have also "corrected" vitriol itself and poured away its secret, reducing the matter so that **oil of vitriol** <note>Sulfuric acid</note> is used, even though that secret required for the falling sickness is not present in the oil. Meanwhile—as is characteristic of these **Stentors** <note>Loud-voiced boasters, named after the Greek herald Stentor</note>—they have prevailed with their shouting so that the oil is preferred and extolled, which is nevertheless least useful for the falling sickness. I wish to be understood correctly.

<margin>The **volatility** of vitriol, not the oil, cures the falling sickness.</margin>
This, however, is true: that the **volatility** <note>The subtle, vaporous essence that rises during distillation</note> of vitriol cures the falling sickness even in adults, not the oil. What they pour away, they do not know. Thus they deceive the art and betray their own fraud. Indeed, in the oil itself, without the volatility, no healing operation has ever been observed. Meanwhile, they do not blush at their lies. You, however, must strive with all zeal to devote yourselves to the truth in all your arts. And since your purpose is entirely to bring help to the sick, I ask that you do it from certain skill. Correct nothing, lest you make it worse. Take up what is good in the meantime, until you find something better. But for the sake of investigating the better, do not let the good perish or be forgotten. Let each thing be held in its own place and value. If something better is given, remove the old. If not, hold fast to it.

<margin>How the oil of vitriol may be made **volatile**.</margin>
Regarding vitriol, what I think should be pointed out is this: that you should urge and confine its volatile part to the highest degree, and purify it a third time with a great fire, gradually increased and then stepped down. Thus the oil will be reduced into volatility. This is undoubtedly that volatile part which you must not allow to perish. In this is the power of healing the falling sickness. It is administered according to the **stars** and their **exaltations** <note>Astrological positions where a planet's healing influence is magnified</note>. Despair of nothing. Persevere and press on.

<margin>Only **volatile** things command the stars.</margin>
For only volatile things command the stars. But discard the oil, unless it be volatile or has the volatile within it. It becomes more powerful and useful according to its strengths if it is processed in a **pelican** <note>A specialized alchemical vessel for circular distillation</note> or a retort for its **month** <note>A "philosophical month," usually a period of 40 days of heat</note>.

Now, review what we have handed down so far regarding the cause and cure of the falling sickness of the first kind. Next, by the favor of divine grace, we shall also treat the second kind. I lovingly urge you again and again not to despise anything. Let it not offend you that I receive no public salary or stipend for teaching and professing. Nor let my detractors, who rush at me in a pack, frighten you. These are biting gnats, who will soon reveal their own foolishness <note>original: "morionem"; a fool or a jester's cap</note>. There are many other secrets in this disease which I do not mention here. But if you move me by your zeal, love, and diligent reading, I will suppress none of them, but will hereafter publish an entire book from which you can take a full taste of everything. I would have included those things here as well, since I hope you will read all this with great desire and affection, but a certain **goose** <note>Likely a punning reference to a rival or a specific printer blocking his work</note> intercepts the press from me, devouring the oats alone. They think, no doubt, that if they deny me the press, they have already exhausted everything else. And yet, in their own time, the roses also will be brought forth.

It is a confession to myself that nothing is produced before its time. Haste contributes nothing to the delivery of the offspring. If indeed something could be ripened by hurrying, their own **ass-heads** <note>A common Paracelsian insult for university doctors</note> would certainly have been sufficiently exposed to everyone by me long ago.

The introduction of this treatise was so established that I might turn you Physicians toward mercy, since I have seen that a sack of money outweighs or overpowers everything with you. In that [mercenary] practice, no other art is hidden than that which squeezes money from men through trifles. By such an art, nothing is provided for the sick; moreover, Medicine itself is obscured and contaminated by such Doctors. Therefore, even now for the last time, I call you back to mercy. For thus charity will drive you to the **light of nature**, to **Chiromancy** <note>Reading the "signs" or lines of nature</note>, to **Geomancy** <note>Divination/study of earth-signatures</note>, etc., so that you become skilled and expert in them. Thus it will happen that you come forth shining and conspicuous with even more arts than has been done so far. If indeed this so deadly and miserable disease does not turn you toward mercy, then surely nothing else anywhere will ever be able to compel you toward charity. Along with this, I have also handed down not a few things to you concerning the true **Doctor of Medicine**, so that you might finally depart from those ancient fanatics. For in this explanation, you will find a singular foundation by which your stupidity can be judged—even if you cover it up as best you can with **red hats** <note>The doctoral caps worn by university graduates</note>. Never cease from reading my writings, but proceed strenuously in unrolling them; then you will finally know both yourselves and me sincerely. By this labor of yours, you will obtain from me that I, in turn, will also diligently read through your writings.

<header>PREFACE. ON THE FALLING SICKNESS</header>

# BOOK TWO.
->Indeed.<-
## ON THE FALLING SICKNESS OF THE WOMB.

In that various and manifold abundance of books which are written about Medicine and circulated everywhere, Reader, this ought to be your perpetual rule for reading: that all your reading should look toward utility and be directed toward the health of the sick. Since, however, it belongs to you, Reader, to judge all things, it is especially necessary that you have certain knowledge and understanding of those **Recipes**, as well as the **Theories** and **Practices** in which you are engaged, so that you are able to judge whether an author is truthful or a liar. If you are not equipped with this judgment, what do you think you will draw from reading such things? Surely nothing but what is depraved. For you place your faith in things that you have not yet tested to see if they are true or false. Now, the first thing of all is that you have the truth itself known to you, and that you read nothing outside of it. If you do not do this, you will become entirely like those Doctors who seek their food and clothing by lying, opining, and divining. Therefore, I not undeservedly advise that you have within yourself a certain and indubitable knowledge of Medicine before you turn aside to read the writings and books of the faculties <note>Paracelsus refers to university faculties, which he often criticized for teaching theory without practical natural knowledge</note>. 

For it is known to you that this opinion is on everyone's lips: that a "promoted Master" <note>A university graduate holding a Master's degree</note> is more fit for learning Medicine than another who is not a Master. You yourself admit the same, looking toward the intellect or aptitude for more easily grasping medicine. Now, however, in the **seven liberal arts** <note>The medieval curriculum: grammar, logic, rhetoric, arithmetic, geometry, music, and astronomy</note> there is no protection or foundation from which you can form a more correct judgment concerning medicine. For they do not teach you anything other than how not to offend the author himself, and how to agree with him, whether he speaks truths or lies. If, therefore, the foundation for judging Medicine is not contained in the seven liberal arts, you shall certainly learn something else entirely before you enter into medicine, and you will see to it that you are a **Master in Philosophy and Astronomy**. If you are a Master in these, then this profession lies open to you on a full hinge, and you can bring forth judgment from yourself as to whether an author proposes true or false things. 

So that you may be present and equipped with such protection, Reader, I commend this book of mine on the **falling sickness** <term>Falling sickness: The historical term for epilepsy, so called because the patient falls during a seizure.</term> to your reading, and I ask that you do not judge me according to the other authors of the liberal arts, but lead me to the fire (as they say) where gold and silver are tested, to receive a trial. Indeed, I also lectured or professed on the Falling Sickness at Basel: but I did so according to the listeners I had obtained. If such listeners had fallen to my lot, my other Lectures would also have been different. Therefore, let these and other listeners rightly recognize my presence here, and let them not lightly esteem that which concerns the danger of life. A Physician must not seek the profits of the kitchen, but the praise of Medicine itself, and the glory and honor of God: and likewise it must also be considered, etc.

# ON THE FALLING SICKNESS OF THE WOMB, A DISEASE PECULIAR TO WOMEN.
## By Theophrastus von Hohenheim, Doctor of both Medicines.

### PARAGRAPH I.

<margin>Division of this book.</margin>
I have indeed already published a small book on the falling sickness. That was a general treatise, containing all types of this visitation. In addition to those, however, there is a certain peculiar type, which is similar to the previous ones neither in its cause nor its cure, and therefore it ought not to be referred to them. This type is the falling sickness of women, arising from the **womb** <note>original: "utero"</note>. Regarding this, a peculiar book is not undeservedly established, in two parts. The first will deal with the distinction between the falling sickness of the womb and other falling sicknesses outside the womb. The second will hand down the cure, with all the requirements owed to this explanation.

Since, therefore, I must write again in this place, I am once more compelled to warn you Physicians to seriously and soberly weigh this disease of which I treat, and to seek knowledge of it from the true and most ancient Masters, not from the crumbs that have been gathered from everywhere by the **Sophists** <note>Paracelsus used "Sophist" as a slur for academic doctors who relied on logic rather than observation</note>. Taste of the true banquet: thus you will depart satisfied. For no one will become satisfied by crumbs. Therefore, let it be your desire to learn not in the Academies, but in nature itself, just as I have sufficiently shown before, who the Physician must learn from and where. Think, therefore, how great a loss of time it is that you wear away your age in those spacious commentaries of Jacobus de Partibus,

<margin>Reproof of Physicians.</margin>
Gentilis, Trusianus, Hugo, Mesue, Azaronius, Avicenna, Galen, Rhazes, Montagnana, and others, whose wars and works are remembered not without disgrace? 

<margin>Reproof of Rhetoricians.</margin>
And what is this, that you study with such fervor the trifles of Rhetoric, which nevertheless do not make a Physician, but destroy him? And what are you hunting for in your **Logic** and **Dialectic**, which are not only adverse to the Physician himself but also forcibly suppress and darken the **light of nature**? 

<margin>Reproof of Logicians.</margin>
For nature does not give those things, but a black genius <note>A malevolent or false guiding spirit</note> who, conspicuous in your eyes, triumphs over those fanatical studies. Therefore, do not spend precious time on those vanities hereafter. 

<margin>Reproof of Poets.</margin>
And what does it finally matter if you excel Virgil himself in fine letters? Answer me, and say: are the entire works of Virgil to be compared to a single Physician, if he knows even a single "fall" <note>Likely a pun on the "falling sickness" or a clinical case</note>? Judge, I pray, which of these is a more worthy governor of the body? And what will you be in the end if you become pure Lucans, pure Ovids, pure Horaces? When distress presses, to whom, I ask, can you be of use other than to yourselves with your womanish chattering? I would indeed dare to swear to you that even the worst verse from the books of **Macer** <note>Aemilius Macer, a Roman poet whose works on the virtues of herbs were highly valued by Paracelsus for their practical natural knowledge</note>, the least of all poets, is much nobler than all the poets and even Homer himself. For who would be such a mushroom or a blockhead who, when detained by some disease, would not [give] his entire poem, his Greek...

<header>OF THE WOMB</header>

...then, would he exchange his Hebrew <note>Possibly a reference to ancient biblical wisdom or a specific scholar, suggesting that spiritual or ancient health is more valuable than worldly status</note> for even the smallest knowledge or restoration of his health? Do you really think that both Virgil and Horace themselves did not repent before their deaths for the papers smeared with their own foolishness? But what would a Physician have to repent for? Not a thing. For he has spent his age in the <term>arcana</term> <note>Hidden secrets or powerful medicinal mysteries of nature</note>; he lived for God and nature like a singular Monarch of the terrestrial light.

<margin>The Physician is heart and work, not word.</margin>
To what end does all our sagacity, prudence, reason, and wisdom serve, if we do not bestow it upon our neighbor who is needy and pressed by necessities? Who among those who have fallen ever cried out, "Save me, Juvenal!" <note>Juvenal was a Roman satirist; Paracelsus is saying that poetry cannot save a dying man</note>? Instead, everyone cries out, "Save me, Hippocrates!" For God destined this duty to him. The physician lives in nature and is the craftsman of the <term>light of nature</term> <note>The innate wisdom and biological laws found in the physical world, accessible through observation rather than just scripture</note>. What is your Terence with his character Davus? To trifle, to flatter, to fawn—these are the works of leisure. But to bring help, to be useful, to assist—these are the duties of the heart. The Physician grows in the heart; he proceeds from God, and thus he is a member of the household of the light of nature and experience. Therefore, I wish for you to learn this: if trouble and affliction press upon your neighbor, you should have not only the soul to help him, but also the resources. You should not just turn your backs and pass by, as the Scribes and Levites do—to whom the poets and all those who hold their own mouths as God and their own opinions as heaven are likened.

<margin>The Physician is a Samaritan, not a Levite.</margin>
Nothing can be obtained from such people. However, with the Samaritan—that is, with the one skilled in nature—there is knowledge and help. From this, understand that there is nowhere anything from which more faith and distinguished help is expected than from the Physician. Into his hands, finally, all the prayers of everyone fall, while all history and law fade away; use and outcomes prove this. Truly, the poet does not grant this. For as long as he flourishes like a leaf, his "club" <note>original: "claua" - likely a reference to a poet's staff or badge of office</note> is more decorated than others. This same vanity is familiar to <term>poetasters</term> <note>Insignificant or inferior poets</note>.

<margin>What is the duty of the Physician?</margin>
I ask and entreat all of you Physicians to be moved to mercy by the fact that the sick have been committed to you by God, so that you may diligently attend to their care and account. For you yourselves can easily judge that God did not appoint the Physician to destroy, but to heal; not to despair, but to succor everyone, everywhere, and fearlessly. To what end was hope given to us, if not so that we might do more than what seems possible to be done? If, therefore, you find that nothing profitable or healing can be extracted by you from books, then certainly you will know—by the judgment of your own conscience—that far other and more things must be considered and investigated than those which have been written. For Medicine has not been brought to its final goal or limits even at this very moment; rather, more and greater things can be learned and known continually.

<margin>Medicine has not yet reached its final goal.</margin>
<margin>Seekers of ancient medicine?</margin>
Furthermore, there has been a grave error regarding this "falling" <note>The "falling sickness" or epilepsy</note> condition up to now, both as to the knowledge of its cause and the understanding of its cure. Although this error is an abomination, and so very manifest, it is nevertheless a cause for grief that there are those who do not shrink from further veiling it and protecting it with their patronage. They act as if our entire salvation were written down in those papers with a few printed letters, and as if we lived entirely deprived of the other secrets and mysteries of nature. Only those who are lazy and rest satisfied with prescriptions and preconceived opinions cast this stumbling block; they do not look further to see whether those things are healing or harmful.

<margin>Medicine which nourishes.</margin>
Concerning the causes, know that they have not yet been sufficiently considered and investigated as they ought to be. Likewise, the system of **Recipes** is mere confusion—a great detriment to the art introduced by writers—where no respect is given to complexions, nor secrets, nor anatomy, nor form, nor limbs. Thus, these recipes are by no means composed according to the order of nature. You must be possessed of a very stubborn blindness if you allow yourselves to be informed in no part. What true reason and method should finally be held in these matters, so that you might at last throw away that "ancient lyre"? <note>A metaphor for outdated, repetitive medical theories</note> Shall I say what the cause of this is? It is because you are not **Astronomers**. Thus, one of your wings is clipped. You are also not **Philosophers**. Therefore, the other wing also fails. I remain silent on the fact that you are not skilled in other related arts. Thus, naked of all feathers, you think it enough if you can only read or write down **Recipes**, and send what you have written to the apothecary shop. Is that truly a monument worthy of a Doctor? This error is far too fertile, and could be revealed and made manifest in a long discourse. In the place where I shall hand down the method of composing, I shall fill many more volumes on these things. Yet I cannot help but touch upon the madness of your **Theory** and **Practice** here as well; in both of these, not even a tiny bit has been spent on actual deeds, even though they are placed in the highest rank by everyone. Therefore, pay attention to me, you who establish these things. If you follow me, you will stand with the highest honor, and thus you will finally bind yourselves anew and throw yourselves into the fire of your own accord.

<margin>Theophrastus burned the medical books.</margin>
In your madness, you charge me with a crime because I burned that "culinary author" in the fire of Vulcan <note>Paracelsus famously burned the books of traditional authorities like Galen and Avicenna in a public bonfire, comparing their complicated recipes to mere kitchen-cooking</note>. But what sort of abomination is that? If he belongs to the kitchen, he shall also belong to the funeral pyre. Fix your eyes upon me, and strive to do what you see me doing. Learn from me the knowledge of the causes of diseases and the composition of **Recipes**. And so, hereafter, you will be immune to the usual mockery of the peasants. For I can easily imagine that you now have the same mind that I once had. As long as I used your remedies, I suffered the same as you. Truly, it is excruciating and insanely frustrating if a peasant mocks a Doctor. And yet, unless the Doctor seeks out a greater and more sublime knowledge for himself, he does not suffer an injustice, but pays the entirely just penalty for what he deserves.

<margin>What kind of physician one ought to be and be considered:</margin>
Therefore, let our firm opinion stand, so that we may now proceed to write down the cause and practice of the aforementioned "falling" condition: not indeed according to the rule of the ancients, but according to the tenor and base of the Physician's foundation, which consists in these primary parts: **Astronomy** and **Philosophy**. These will be explained in such a discourse that the physician may be a complete anatomy of the greater world <note>The Macrocosm</note>, and that the Cosmographer is not neglected, but entirely joined with the aforementioned professions to form the physician. For all natural arts and sciences arise and remain in the Physician. For if they all separated themselves from one another and fell apart—so that the Cosmographer discussed his purpose separately, and likewise the Astronomer, the Philosopher, the Physiognomist, and the Chiromancer <note>Palm reader</note>—medicine would fall.

<margin>The Physician is the center of the arts.</margin>
...might diverge; nevertheless, they must all meet and flow together again if a Physician wishes or ought to move forward. For just as many roads lead to Rome, all of which converge in Rome: so also all roads, that is, the arts, are joined in the Physician. Indeed, he cannot be entangled in confusion, since he is the center and the point of the circle into which all lines depart and tend. From this, therefore, you should understand that I forge my practice and theory from all the arts in such a way that the Cosmographer, the Astrologer, the Philosopher, the Geomancer <note>A practitioner of divination by means of signs from the earth</note>, and finally all students of nature are compelled to praise me. For the physician is born from their very arts: which he, in turn, exalts and illuminates. Therefore, the Physician to be sought is one who is whole, not a mere part of one, but possessing all things required to constitute a whole. For now, however, be content with this brief treatise. For I shall not make an end of writing here: but I shall bring forth many more books indeed.

## PARAGRAPH II.

<margin>The Falling Sickness of the womb is badly called "suffocation of the womb."</margin>
<margin>Signs of the Falling Sickness of the uterus.</margin>
<margin>Falling Sickness of the uterus is a women's disease. What is a virgin?</margin>
*Let us now proceed to weave together the description of the "falling sickness" <note>original: "morbi caduci"; traditionally referring to epilepsy, but here applied to uterine disorders</note>, which is familiar only to women, and was called "Suffocation of the womb" <note>original: "Suffocatio matricis"; a common medieval diagnosis for "hysteria"</note> and other unsuitable names by the Ancients. For where an error is committed regarding the cause, there an error is also made in the naming and declaration of the disease. In this place, it shall be designated as the **Falling Sickness of the Womb**: specifically because it resides in the womb alone, and is revealed by the same symptoms as the falling sickness <note>epilepsy</note>, namely the extension of the limbs, spasm, convulsion, foaming at the mouth, and other similar signs. A specific book must be written about this, because it differs from other types of falling sickness in its subject, paroxysm <note>the sudden onset of symptoms</note>, form, essence, species, person, and the like. Since, however, it is also of a <term>Microcosmic</term> <note>The concept that the human body is a "little world" reflecting the "Macrocosm" or the great universe</note> nature, and in all things conspires toward a common cause (as was said regarding the falling sickness): its condition and quality shall now be explained more explicitly in what follows. This disease pertains only to women, not to men, nor to virgins themselves. For virgins are those whose wombs are devoid of conception, and have neither been provoked nor handled <note>original: "palpatae"; likely implying sexual activity or physical examination</note> for this purpose. Those who are otherwise all belong to this category. And although it happens more rarely to virgins, it does occur sometimes in them due to their own fault in certain diseases, just as we shall subsequently recount many works and causes.*

<margin>All shelled things are included.</margin>
In the beginning, I will teach about the Womb, its essence, and its property, which is as follows. Just as you see the heaven and the earth enclosed in their own "shell" <note>original: "testa"; referring to the outer limits of the universe</note>: so also is the womb enclosed, along with everything it contains, which possesses the four Elements in itself—to say nothing of the types of animals and humans. An empty and void womb, in which a fetus is not contained, is in all ways similar to the heaven and the earth in which there were no living or sensible things. And just as the Sun, Moon, Trees, Herbs, the North wind and the South wind, Metals, and <term>Cachimiæ</term> <note>A Paracelsian term for mineral ores or the "essence" of metals</note> nonetheless came forth with all their operations even without man: so the Womb is the same in relation to the human.

<margin>The womb contains all the stars within itself.</margin>
Clearly, in the same way, the womb also contains its own stars and their bodies within itself. Since, therefore, man is from the world, and the world—that is, the Microcosmic world—ought to be: then he takes it from the womb. For just as man was first created from the four parts of the world;

<margin>Life is one, both inside and outside the Womb.</margin>
<margin>The womb is a lesser world.</margin>
so was he likewise to be created perpetually. Since the Creator creates only once and afterwards desists: so here also He made the heavens and the earth, and formed it into the womb, in which man is conceived, generated, and nourished, no differently than he is outside the womb once he has come forth into the air. Thus, it is one and the same thing: to live in the womb, and to live outside of it. The fetus in the womb lives in the firmament of the Womb. The fetus outside the womb lives in the external firmament. Thus, therefore, the womb is a lesser world <note>a microcosm</note>, having in itself every condition and nature of the heavens and the earth.

Since, then, such is the stated condition of the womb: it will necessarily also be subject to thunder, and earthquakes, and winds, and all <term>Lorindis</term> <note>A Paracelsian term for elemental or spiritual storms/disturbances within the body</note>: with this distinction at least, that here there are two Microcosms, the Womb and the human. The human is himself a Microcosm: therefore he has all Elemental operations within himself. Likewise also in the womb.

<margin>How the womb of the world and of the human differ.</margin>
Furthermore, the difference is this. By the same ratio that the World and the Human are distant from each other: so also the Womb and the Human differ. For just as Adam was conceived and born in the world, which was the womb of his own self in which he lay: so now that womb is more, but it is implanted and innate in the female, yet preserving all the natures and properties of that womb in which the generated Adam lay.

<margin>The specific Microcosmic nature.</margin>
Now indeed, man is a lesser world, and contains the nature of the womb—that is, of the great and small world—within himself, and thus all the things and operations of natural bodies. But beyond these two worlds, man also has the operation of the senses and of reason. For herbs indeed have virtues: but they operate without reason and senses. Nettles sting; fire burns, but without intellect. Man wounds, slays, etc., but with reason. Therefore, here too there is some difference. Whatever the firmaments operate, that is similar to a tree which grows. But the firmament of man is otherwise similar to the Elementals, except that he perfects his works through reason, not through mere impulse.

<margin>A double operation: without and with sense.</margin>
For in all things there is one operation: but this happens under a double appearance: one is with sense, the other without sense. If cattle are thirsty, they go to the cistern and drink until they are satisfied: this happens through their own sense and intellect. But a tree in a field also drinks, yet without sense: in place of sense, it has a force attracting moisture, which an animal is compelled to pursue and seek. Where, therefore, such a force exists, reason is not present. Where reason is, that force is banished. Now apply this to the womb.

<margin>1. The cause of the Falling Sickness is thunder.</margin>
Even if these things I have brought forward do not seem to contribute to the disease I proposed: nevertheless, because a Physician must grow out of Philosophy, the matter serves to help you understand one thing from another, and (as I have handed down concerning the Falling Sickness in other books) to estimate the cause of thunder even from this to some extent, and to adapt it to our matter or purpose. But that the matter may become even clearer: I shall now begin to explain the causes themselves, so that once they are known, you may penetrate to the true principles, without the knowledge of which you will by no means be able to properly establish the practice itself.

<margin>The stars of the uterus bring forth fourfold things.</margin>
Now, the stars of the womb that contribute to this disease are as follows. First, it must be known that the star of fire gives thunder; the star of the earth gives the earthquake; the star...

# PARAGRAPH I.

<margin>
The stars of the womb bring forth fourfold things.

The Star <note>In Paracelsus’s system, a "Star" is not just a celestial body, but an internal vital force or "virtue" that governs biological functions</note> of Air brings forth a crash; the Star of Water, a bellowing. These same things happen in the matrix <note>the womb</note> itself in this way. Take an example for yourselves, which must first be known. You see, surely, that nothing happens on earth that does not proceed from a certain reason, such as eating, drinking, working, and the like. Now, where does this reason come from? From the stars. For the stars themselves possess this same reason. And although they do not speak, they perform their tasks just like a human. And no less than man himself, they are also craftsmen. For whatever man does, the heaven does the same. Yet heaven does not do it as if it were learning from man; rather, man learns from the heaven. For all these things proceed from the heaven, and of all these things, heaven is the Teacher and Master. Heaven is the Carpenter <note>original: "Tignarius"</note>, and hews out the work; it is the smith who hammers. So also is man on earth. And let no one be surprised that heaven works such wondrous things. For it is equipped with all crafts and has within itself all kinds of artisans. From this it happens that many wonders occur to us on earth: and such power is to be understood not only from the heaven, but also from the other three Elements, through their own stars.

One operation of heaven and man.

Heaven possesses all craftsmen.

<margin>
The process of paroxysms.

In accordance with these principles, now also recognize the process of paroxysms <note>sudden attacks or fits</note> in the matrix. Indeed, not only in the matrix, but also in the "great falling sickness" <note>original: "magno caduco"; referring to epilepsy</note>, paroxysms are hammered out and manufactured through this kind of conjunction. Now, this conjunction should not be understood differently than if a smith, a hammer, fire, and an anvil come together and hammer iron: or if a Carpenter, an axe, and wood were present, and a house were built. The reasoning for understanding this present conjunction is similar. And in the same order, by the same art, and in the same way a house is prepared, manufactured, and erected: in the same way, the same must be understood concerning the stars.

<margin>
A conjunction is necessary for the manufacture.
</margin>

<margin>
The mixed nature of the Three Primes.
</margin>
Furthermore, take note that the three primes—Sulphur, Mercury, and Salt—are variously disposed and prepared. In some bodies they are sensible to the eyes, in some to the ears, in some to the voice, in some to reason. The astral bodies in which they lie do this, so that some see this operation, as in lightning and flashing; others feel or touch it, yet neither hear nor see it, as in an earthquake; some hear it, as in the Lorindus <note>a Paracelsian term for a specific sensory or meteorological phenomenon often linked to thunder</note>; some feel it by touch, as in the Air. This nature is also present in the matrix itself, but in such a way that sensitivity is most powerful, and visibility is very close, by which the disease is manifested. For not much is perceived by the ears, but more by reason. Now indeed, since, as you have heard, the Matrix is a Microcosm <note>a "little world" that reflects the structures of the universe</note>, made according to the nature of the other Microcosm and the Microcosm itself: then its operation in these things is such that conjunctions manufacture such a disease. Truly, the knowledge of the cause of the conjunction is different, namely this. In man lie all diseases, and whatever is good or evil. For he is born in the hour of concord, and not outside of it. For there, all the stars must be present at the conception. And when they produce good and evil: one is manifest, the other less so, and thus one rather outweighs the other, and rarely—indeed, hardly ever—are both in balance. Now, however, the stars predominate so that a man becomes wrathful, savage, etc.; sometimes the mild and gentle predominate, with the wrathful ones yielding. From this it happens that a man cannot be without anger, nor without gentleness, even if he is most savage. For his heaven has no less of the soft and gentle within itself than the wrathful, even if the latter prevails. And this is the cause of the variety of natures or dispositions in man, so that one and the same person is now mild, now wrathful, now good, now evil, as long as he lives according to that constitution which he received at his conception.

<margin>
Conjunction manufactures the falling sickness.
</margin>
<margin>
Man has all diseases within himself, etc.
</margin>
<margin>
The stars of conception live together.
</margin>
<margin>
Whence the variety of man's disposition?
</margin>

<margin>
Man is disposed toward all diseases.
</margin>
The reasoning is exactly the same in diseases. For there, either health or sickness prevails, this or that habit, just as the over-weight <note>preponderance or "superpondium"</note> falls. From this it is clear that man is exposed to all diseases—that is, he is disposed to conceive all diseases. And unless the heaven were such, man himself would be undisposed to those diseases. Just as all astral nature—namely goodness, malice, wrath, gentleness, etc.—dwells in man: so also the dispositions of all diseases are within him, not indeed as actualities yet, but according as the weight of the stars has instilled them. For in such diseases, the body provides a Physician for itself, and has its own arcana <note>secret healing powers or essential virtues</note> with it. Thus, therefore, from an unequal weight, a disease of that nature which outweighed the others is brought in. Now, that which outweighs toward the falling sickness <note>original: "morbum caducum"</note> is "thunder," and it is the Star of "earthquake," and the other two. Thus, therefore, man carries about a disease innate to himself, which is easy for you to understand if you review the Astronomy of the four Elements more accurately.

<margin>
Whence the falling sickness of the matrix?

<margin>
The second cause of the falling sickness: the reason that rules the stars.
</margin>
But besides this cause, another must also be related, which brings on the falling sickness even outside of that innate disposition of which we spoke. For even if the heaven itself is pure, equal, and clear, and does not at all verge or decline toward disease—that is, toward heat and paroxysms—it is nevertheless subject to reason, which governs the stars. Just as it is known to you that, if the heaven incites or inclines toward theft, reason resists and opposes it. For in the heaven and the stars are Robbers, Thieves, traitors, etc.; nor is any man so upright and noble that all these evils are not within him, just like that robber who will be placed on the wheel <note>a form of execution</note> tomorrow. Just as reason moderates the Star: so it also gives a cause and beginning to disease in this way, because reason and the stars in man are the subtlest of all things, and cohere with one another, just like the Sun and its brilliance. Now, if joy or sorrow strikes the reason, exceeding its natural degree and concord: immediately the growing and ascending Star is set on fire, no differently than if a hand struck fire from a flint into sulfur or some other tinder.

<margin>
Reason sets the growing Star on fire.
</margin>

The third cause of the falling sickness: nourishment.
</margin>
<margin>
Food is a Star.

For if a man eats, he eats a Star. This Star is now an arcanum, both health and disease. In these there is a distinction: here there are good foods, there bad; here poison, there sour, there sweet, and the like. Just as you see this diversity in the earthly Elements, and their stars, and all other similar things: so here also there are different Natures from the stars, as you see, by this reasoning. # ON THE FALLING SICKNESS OF THE WOMB.

...one falls into dropsy. In that state there is Jaundice; in the other Apoplexy; in that one a fever, etc.

The same principle holds true for the stars. This star arranges its species in such a way that whoever eats retains the food in a similar species, and this is because of the stars themselves. If the human element predominates, the Star itself predominates. By this predominance, it increases one part and adds to its weight based on what the person eats or drinks. Thus, this disease is also at hand, because the stars are increased in their exaltations <note>In astrology and alchemy, an "exaltation" is a state where a planet or force reaches its highest potency</note>. And so the paroxysm is prolonged. Thus, one must also judge by reason that something is added to the person, whereby the star is increased in its effect. This is now a concordant conjunction. This conjunction is a multiplication and a predominance according to the condition of that star which is affected. For <margin>The highest Star in man, etc.</margin> a Star is established in our reason—and that the highest one—for the sake of which man was created.

Open your ears to hear of this star, all you Professors in every Faculty! For from this, it can be known with what reason anyone operates, whether from the reason of the Elemental Stars, or from the reason of etc. And certainly, you Physicians ought to know that the cause of all diseases is situated here. Therefore, act as Astronomers <note>The author uses "Astronomer" here to mean someone who understands the internal "stars" or spiritual forces of the body, rather than just the sky</note>: and you will know how to establish regimens in all things. Meanwhile, that opinion of yours is donkey-like and contrary. For Cholera does not cause this, nor Melancholy, nor the blood, etc. This is mere "Bean-ism" <note>original: "Beanismus"—a term referring to "Beani," or greenhorn students; essentially calling their knowledge "freshman-level" or foolish</note>. Rather, it should be said thus: To this <margin>Every disease is a star.</margin> star give nothing, to that one do not offer, etc. But what is every star? Nothing but a peculiar disease. If you have known the disease of a man, you have also known the same star. You will recognize this same thing in food, in drink, and similarly in reason. According to these things, therefore, decree the Regimen, the diet, and the order. Otherwise, you act as impostors in all things.

But these things suffice for a fuller explanation of the Falling Sickness of the Womb proper to women. These points also serve to more clearly understand the first book on the Falling Sickness. For this page proves and elucidates that one. Justly, therefore, things which are of one matter are brought together into one volume. But how (which I omit here) this concordance and conjunction produce a mutual predominance until either health or disease <margin>Grass and the cow give milk.</margin> is generated—since that pertains to Philosophy—will be defined separately in its own books. To be sure, grass and the cow, both joined, bring forth milk. Now, the grass does not make milk, nor does the cow give it; but in nature there lies hidden a certain "Mechanical Star" which produces the milk, as we have said. If a man can paint—this star—or can make that white: the heaven can do the very same. For the heaven (that is, the star) and man <margin>Mechanical.</margin> are both "Mechanicals" <note>Here, "Mechanical" refers to a craftsman or one who performs a specific art or function</note>. What a "Mechanical" is will be handed down in the Philosophy. But I ask you, Physicians, to finally overturn your trifles and look further than your "humors" <note>The traditional medical theory that health is governed by four fluids: blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile</note>. In these matters, you are mere fools. For every humor, just as you describe it, is mere mud and dung. Thus, you are dealing with mere dung and excrement. From dung, <margin>Physicians are beetles.</margin> what else is born but a Beetle? O stinking Beetles! Nor are you worth a single hair more than horse dung. And whatever arises from this, that is what you are. But you, Theologians and Lawyers,

<margin>Reproof of Physicians.</margin> and all others who stand sublime in the Star of wisdom, I diligently exhort you to weigh this matter a little more deeply than those Physicians themselves, and to punish them with a worthy penalty, because they do not fix their eyes more sharply on these matters. For it happens to be very painful for them to depart from their "urinary and fecal money" <note>Money earned from analyzing excrement and urine</note>. Although it smells heavily, they nevertheless live sweetly off it. And if my admonition is of no concern to them, let your reproof find its place. For take note of the spirit with which I instill these things: not out of arrogance, as they pretend. For pride never gave birth to any learned man or any art; but it has destroyed and cut them off in every age. And it was altogether fair that men as honorable as they wish to seem should have treated this Falling Sickness of the Womb a little more accurately than to <margin>Suffocation of the womb accurately treated.</margin> thrust forward a few small chapters on the *Suffocation of the Womb* <note>original: "Suffocatione Matricis"—a common historical diagnosis where the womb was thought to move upward and "choke" the woman</note>. In which matter they have the same character as a thief just about to be hanged. For he would swear with formal words that he was honest, if only men would believe it.

For man and the stars of heaven are one thing, one nature: which is also the judgment of the rest. In him, therefore, are all creatures.
