<meta>This page continues the discussion of the "falling sickness" (epilepsy) of the womb. Having established that the womb acts as a microcosm within the woman, Paracelsus now argues that its diseases must be understood through the laws of the Greater World (the Macrocosm), specifically comparing uterine epilepsy to the phenomenon of thunder.</meta>

-># ON THE FALLING SICKNESS OF THE WOMB.<-

<margin>All are one.</margin>
<margin>The senses give the theory; the eyes give the practice.</margin>
How then does man imagine, hold, or propose? For in the same way that the Macrocosm <note>The "Great World" or the universe at large.</note> and man differ from each other, even though they are one, so also do man and the womb differ from each other. Therefore, those reasons by which a man is recognized in his diseases are not the same as the reasons for the womb itself. For anything considered in itself behaves differently, and yet everything is nothing other than the world, the orb, the four elements, the star, the heaven, and the earth; yet in such a way that each has its own peculiar possession, not one shared by all. Although this is also true: that thunder is a "falling sickness" <note>original: *caducus*; usually refers to epilepsy. Paracelsus views epilepsy as an internal atmospheric disturbance similar to lightning.</note>, and the falling sickness is thunder, and thus the falling sickness of the womb is also thunder. From this it is concluded that there is altogether one **Theory** and cause for understanding these three worlds in this regard: but it is not the same in the signs, nor in those three—**Mercury, Sulfur, and Salt** <note>The *Tria Prima*, the three primary substances Paracelsus believed made up all matter.</note>—according to the judgment of the eyes. The senses provide that. For the internal sense comprehends the Theory, but the eyes comprehend the Practice. In Theory, the reason is one. Although the Theories are three, there are three Practices in the eyes. I speak of these so that you may consider them. For in this way, you will find those things you write about these diseases to be false—namely, concerning the "precipitation" of the womb, "suffocation," and the like—where you have equated it to the Microcosm <note>The "Little World," meaning the human body.</note>, when Medicine and the force of the disease do not indicate that. The womb is *another* world and requires *another* Physician. But what does "another Physician" mean, except that another process should be established, and not the same cure as in the Microcosm? Rather, just as it is in the Microcosm, so it is in the womb. Yet the star of the secret essence <note>original: *astrum arcani*; the "star" or spiritual virtue of a remedy.</note> is different: there is one in the womb, and one in the Microcosm. So also in the world of medicine there are two stars: one in the womb, and one in the Microcosm. You are therefore hallucinating when you do not recognize the star of the womb in the world and instead apply the star of the Microcosm in place of the star of the womb. But learn!

<margin>The cure for the falling sickness: what kind should it be?</margin>
Regarding the Falling Sickness of the Womb, let this be held: that every process and order which its Philosophy and Astronomy prescribes must be taken from the thunder of the four elements, and must be accommodated to the prescription of Astronomical Philosophy; meanwhile, the eyes should by no means be stuck in only one mode of practice. For, to understand the matter more plainly by an example, imagine for yourselves as if stones had the length of wood and grew in the manner of wood, and in the same way clay also grew. Now, if a singular house had to be built from each of these three separately, then one art—that is, one **Geometry**—would be required for this. And although three different things lie before your eyes, from each of which must be made that which is made from the other, yet it is necessary that it be done through a single art, but through three ways or modes. This "way" is the Practice. That which deals with wood fabricates its part, and the work succeeds well. That which handles stones raises walls, and the work similarly succeeds for it, and it finally reaches the goal of its purpose. That which is occupied with clay also successfully completes its work by obtaining a house. Here, therefore, is one art and one comprehension of the art; but there are three workmen or Masters. The carpenter handles wood; the stonemason, stones; the potter, clay. Unless a similar science is observed in these matters as well, so that the Physician knows what ought to be applied where—what, I ask, will he finally apply or administer? For here three worlds meet, distinguished by triple buildings, each of which wants to maintain its own reason and seeks nothing else. Therefore, estimate and apply your Theory and Practice to these things, lest by reckless Recipes you perhaps burden your pharmacists. For truly, I can testify to this: that all of you together have not yet learned to compose even the smallest suitable Recipe for the falling sickness, even if you are too arrogantly persuaded that you alone reign in this art. But since your dealings are with the "mutes" <note>Refers to patients who cannot speak or argue back against a doctor's authority.</note>, it is not difficult for you; since they can do nothing but nod, and cannot speak against you.

### PARAGRAPH 11.

<margin>Man is known from the natural things of the world.</margin>
In such a lengthy description of this falling sickness belonging only to women, I ask you, Readers, do not be weary that I bring in matter sought so far afield from Philosophy and Astronomy. For those two grant the entire Theory and knowledge of the matter. Nor do I teach you this only here, but also everywhere else where I treat the causes of diseases: that before all things you should drink in the knowledge of the natural things of the Great World, and then also of the Lesser World. For who will know the Lesser World <term>Microcosm</term> without the Great? No one at all. Moreover, what kind of Physician is he who does not understand the Great World <term>Macrocosm</term>? For from where else will he take the knowledge of man himself, whose recognition is so difficult and profound? Therefore, for the sake of this comprehension—even if this specific falling sickness is not so frequent—it would nonetheless be fair that even if only one single disease reigned in the entire world, the Physician should have an exact and intimate knowledge of it, even if it afflicted only one man out of all people. For so great is the nobility of man that his care has been commanded to the Physician by God with a most heavy threat. It is right, therefore, that the Physician’s science be great and arduous, so that he remains ignorant of nothing in caring for the necessities of the body.

<margin>The knowledge of the historian is twofold.</margin>
<margin>The argument of this paragraph.</margin>
<margin>That the theory of diseases may be known from histories.</margin>
Furthermore, I would like you to know that here in my Great Theory, I will proceed as I have begun. I will not yet cease from writing about natural Philosophy and Astronomy. For these things prefigure the whole for man and offer it to be known. For it is evident to you that even in a Historian, such knowledge is required that he knows how to set down a twofold description: one **Theoretical**, the other **Practical**. His Theoretical knowledge is such that he first knows and understands all deeds and acts, triumphs, etc., from Astronomy, and according to this he then describes the man and leads him into his Practice. And he who rightly follows this example also understands the Theory of Medicine, as well as the Practice which is suitable for the sick. Therefore, let it not be a distraction to you that I complete this fourth paragraph from such things. For the falling sickness of the womb is not known even from women themselves, but entirely from Astronomy and Philosophy. For this reason, we introduce here a comparison from Histories. For in the same way these must be understood, so similarly the Theory of diseases must also be known; where you will find...

## SECTION IV.

<margin>The historian of Alexander the Great is no Astronomer.</margin>
You will find here a Theory of the Microcosm <note>The "Little World," meaning the human being as a reflection of the universe.</note> which is solely practice, and not theory. To put the matter as briefly as possible: who can describe the deeds, triumphs, and praises of Alexander the Great if he is ignorant and unskilled in the heavens? Only he who has a certain knowledge of the heavens can do this. For if Alexander is described, what else is written about him but the Practice? For he himself does not provide the Theory. Indeed, he is the achiever and the executor of those things which the Theory encompasses. But who can fully inform or understand the Practice who is not first a Theorist? Alexander is the Practice; the Heaven is the Theory. For Alexander is also in the heaven, having preceded the man himself; he was born from that heaven, and he merely completed the practice and operation of it on the earth. Therefore, it is right that the Historian should first describe the father of this son—not the father who was the husband of his mother, but the father whom the son's mother never knew <note>Paracelsus refers to the "astral father," or the specific arrangement of stars that "sired" Alexander's destiny.</note>. In this way, he will rightly write the Theory, and afterward, he will complete the works of the Theory, which is the Practice. However, so that you may understand the matter more briefly and clearly: know that there is a diversity here in man, such that a matter or business is managed either from the stars or from God.

<margin>Human actions come either from God or from heaven.</margin>
If it is from God, then that Theory does not proceed from the heaven but must be taken from God, such as in describing *Peter, Paul, Andrew, Solomon, David, Jeremiah, John the Baptist*, and whoever else among the number of the Saints are like them. In this case, the <term>Law</term> <note>original: *Ius*; here referring to Divine Law or the governing principle of a life.</note> is fulfilled, of which God is the practitioner. Thus the praise of Peter, Paul, Samson, etc., is not their own, but God's. It proceeded from God; therefore, the Theory must also be drawn from God. Thus, who is to describe these men correctly and truly if he is not skilled in the Theory of God? No one, in the end. For the doer or achiever on earth is credited to his God. Furthermore, the heaven is likewise assigned in place of God for those who operate by its influence. Thus, who will know how to describe Alexander the Great? He who does not know his Star and his Astral birth. No one at all. For it is quite inconsistent and unsuitable for someone to merely join Theory and Practice within a man and outside of him without knowledge of that which operates within him. Alexander indeed did not work of himself, nor for himself, nor by himself; the heaven rather provided it, not only in him, but also in Julius Caesar, in Augustus, and others like them. It is therefore the duty of the Historian to know the generation of the father <note>the celestial cause</note> who is the executor and fulfiller of the Astronomical Theory. In this way, he will surely have explored what he can and should praise and commend from *Leo, Cancer, Saturn, Venus, Mars, Jupiter*, etc., and likewise he will know how much and how far it is right to either praise or blame that deed.

<margin>All the deeds of men belong to the heaven.</margin>
For all deeds belong to the heaven, not to the man. Therefore, the heaven, not the man, ought to be described. If, then, the heaven or the star precedes all these things, and that is the Theory itself: how, I ask, can a Physician take the description of that disease from the frailty of a woman? For she did not give birth to or create her own disease; rather, that which is greater than her—namely, the star—did this. In this way, and no other, both are understood under a single Theory.

For as long as the triumphs of Caesar and a disease are not reduced to a single Theory, nothing can be written concerning the Practice. And pay diligent attention to this example. For the matter stands no other way. Earthly deeds happen in heaven before they are designated on earth; they are in the same manner as when someone dreams of that which happens tomorrow. For in this way the heaven runs ahead and performs all the works which the man afterward completes on earth. For here, in both places, there is one star, and the master of the Star indicates through his work what the star performed yesterday in heaven. Thus the Astronomer indicates today what will happen tomorrow; so it is the man who performs the Practice of the Astronomer, who through his own work indicates the past movement of the heaven. The Astronomer is he who indicates the movement itself after the heaven has moved. Just as Alexander is in the star and afterward also on earth: so it is right for you to know that every man is designated and fashioned in the stars from his birth until his death. This book of description is the Theory of which I speak. Outside of this book, what is all our writing on earth?

<margin>All men are described in the stars.</margin>
Not that I praise those who live and conduct themselves according to this book; rather, I blame and reproach them entirely. For they become mere false Prophets, false Kings, and false Rulers. For all these things ought to come from God, not from this book. Hence I cannot praise them. Nevertheless, I point these things out so that it may be known what it is finally appropriate for naturalists to write: namely, that all these things must be considered by the Physician, and he must be entirely skilled in them. The sum of my argument, for the sake of which I introduced this example, is this: that in a similar way, the falling sickness <note>epilepsy</note> also exists in heaven, just like the man who suffers from the falling sickness. For that man is the one who afterward carries what the heaven played out within him; that is, what his image in heaven does, he does as well.

<margin>Diseases are in the heaven.</margin>
Now indeed, Reason is the Mistress of wars, quarrels, etc., so that she herself is the Medicine against the heaven. Just so, herbs are the Medicines against disease. Now, therefore, there is one cause and one Medicine on both sides. For here the reason is revealed why God created the Medical art: namely, to prevent what the heaven does when it is not beneficial or healthy for man.

<margin>Reason is the Medicine against the heaven.</margin>
For this use He also granted reason. Thus, the Physician is ordained for the one; Reason for the other. Now, which of these is worthy of praise: the medicine of herbs, or of reason, or both, or he who uses no medicine? Surely he is to be praised who applies medicine, and he who is healed. He who suffers the disease is not to be praised, since he pleases neither God nor the world. This is the cause: because God wants Medicine to be practiced. For this reason, He has need of the Physician’s actions. Moreover, he is healthy and rightly cured who applies medicine to his own reason against the disease which his image and star produced in the heaven. And he is healthy whom the heaven made sick, but who grew well again through herbs. These things are truly worthy of praise.

Therefore, regarding the woman (lest I wander too far from my purpose), know that in the same way, her womb has its own preludes, which she is compelled to bear and suffer—that is, what the star inflicts upon her. Understand this in such a way that the womb is a peculiar and distinct world, as much as...

# ON THE FALLING SICKNESS OF THE WOMB

<margin>The womb described in heaven</margin>
As far as the womb is concerned, it is just as we have understood. The reason I explain it more clearly here is so that what is said—and from what foundation and theory it is said—might be easily understood. For because a woman's womb, its name, its length, its habits and nature, and its health and sickness are all described in the "book of the stars," <note>Paracelsus refers to the "Liber Astronomicus," the idea that the blueprint for human organs exists in the celestial realm.</note> it is right that all those things be considered there, and that the true Theory be sought in that place. Truly, no one will learn anything from the physical womb itself, because it is hidden and concealed within the body. For what benefit does a hidden thing offer a physician? No one lights a torch and then hides it; rather, one lights it so that it may give off light and people may walk by it. If the womb is indeed a light, it is certainly a hidden one. Who can see by it?

<margin>The light of the womb is in the stars.</margin>
Now, in truth, the womb does not lack its own light. However, that light shines from the stars, not in the body. We ought to see, walk, and learn by means of the stars. External things are the knowledge of internal things. Otherwise, what need would there be for Medicine? What need for a Physician? If these things did not exist, what would ultimately be left for us? Nothing but another life. But since health, evil, good, diseases, the sick, and all things lie in the stars and are derived from the stars into us, all such [traditional] physicians are nothing but smoke. We all possess reason and medicine, which we ought to use. If these are not employed, do not persuade yourselves of anything other than this: just as a soldier, a merchant, or any other person in their fortune or misfortune is nothing more than a "falling" patient <note>The term "caducus" refers to "falling," as in epilepsy or the "falling sickness," which Paracelsus connects here to a lack of alignment with one's astral destiny.</note> (for they err in Medicine because they wish to operate out of reason rather than from the stars), so too the sick person who lies down from disease and lacks medicine is in error.

<margin>The things for which Reason is the Medicine</margin>
<margin>Diseases which herbs do not cure.</margin>
Now, the medicine of herbs cannot heal a person in a way that provides fortune or misfortune regarding their struggles, greed, envy, and so on. Instead, the medicine for all of these must be **reason**. Conversely, reason cannot heal one who is oppressed by the falling sickness <note>original: "caducus"</note>; it is necessary that this be done through herbs.

<margin>The herbal "reason" is not within man like the moral "reason."</margin>
I would have you know, therefore, that my purpose is to treat further the medicine of natural growing things and to weave this material together. Thus, what the Theory of the stars indicates may be removed through a natural operation—that is, through "herbal reason" or through the secrets <term>arcana</term> <note>Paracelsus uses "arcana" to mean the concentrated, essential healing power within a natural substance.</note> of the herbs themselves. For this "reason" or power over diseases is not within a man in the same way that the reason of morals and virtues is. For one pertains to the soul, the other to the body.

Furthermore, so that the practice on earth (which you might also call Theory) may be correctly described and nothing necessary omitted, it is first necessary to describe the paroxysm <note>A sudden attack or fit, typical of the "falling sickness" or hysteria.</note> and afterward the cure. The description of the paroxysm proceeds from various complex gestures, from the actions of the stars, and from the actions of the patient. Thus, two things are composed and understood as one. This conjunction also gives signs of the womb: which astral element reigns—fire, earth, air, or water? Even if you have these, you at least have knowledge of the star, but not yet of the "father." <note>The "astral father" refers to the specific celestial cause or origin of the condition.</note> And for what other reason am I more indignant than that the "Humoral Physicians" <note>Physicians who followed the traditional Greek system of the four humors (blood, phlegm, yellow bile, black bile).</note> call the element of fire a "humor," not realizing that it is not the element itself, but its star that operates? If you have the star in the aforementioned way, but not yet the father, then seek what conjunction is there, what it is, and how it is positioned in the star so that it operates in such a way in that disease. 

<margin>Humors are never to be considered.</margin>
<margin>What is Power?</margin>
If through reason you have also found the "father," you cannot and should not say, "this is Melancholy, that is Choler, this is Blood, that is Phlegm." For none of these are to be considered. Just as a painter who paints white or black is not distressed in the slightest about what is in the pigment—whether it be choler or phlegm—but attacks and handles the pigment itself directly, so here too nothing else should be considered except **power** <note>original: "potentia"</note>. Power is that which acts or is acted upon with strength. In phlegm, choler, blood, and melancholy, there is no strength placed. This strength must be sought in Leo, in Mars, etc. Here the cause of the disease must be sought.

<margin>Where to seek knowledge of the Father.</margin>
<margin>What Humoralist Physicians are like.</margin>
And with these things, the Theory—the one from which it is fitting for a physician to proceed—has been treated briefly but sufficiently. If you now know what that Theory is, it follows that you must also know how and in what way it should be recognized. That, however, will henceforth be more Philosophical and Astronomical than Medical. For this reason, I stop at this declaration and commit the matter to those two professions: Astronomy and Philosophy. From this, you see it is entirely necessary that a Physician be by no means ignorant of Philosophy and Astronomy. For the knowledge of a man proceeds from the knowledge of the parent, who is found through these two professions. The physician who finds this parent already knows which stars, which constellation, which impression and influence cause the disease: who the "man in heaven" is, not only by name but by life, habits, gestures, body, and figure—I except only the soul. To this end, the Physician will travel through those regions and track down his diseases; only then will he arrive, not unhappily, at the desired shore of Theory and practice. And since without this experience nothing is ever whole, and yet no physician dares to travel in this way—most preferring to perish and be suffocated in those humors of theirs—who, I ask, would dare seek their health from such idle people? No one who is wise. For whoever places their foundation in these humors, their errors and fantasies are measured, nor do they know how to assert the truth with any probability; thus they exercise mere wickedness and Pharisaical works. <note>He compares traditional doctors to the Pharisees of the New Testament—legalistic and focused on outward forms rather than inner truth.</note>

### PARAGRAPH V.

<margin>The woman has a double world.</margin>
Therefore, you women yourselves, pay attention to the nature of your diseases. Of these, I propose only one here, but it is the most serious and dangerous for you. I do not describe it merely as a doctor, but I also warn you of other necessary things: so that you may understand from me that you carry around a **double Microcosm**: namely, a body similar to the bodies of men, and the "world of human generation," <note>Referring to the reproductive system as a complete "world" or "cosmos" unto itself.</note> concerning which world and its paroxysm I am beginning this treatise. For this book treats the Disease of women, by the force of which they fall and are thrown down, are placed outside of their reason, are convulsed, and suffer other similar things. It treats the signs, order, and essence of this disease. Therefore, turn your mind to it, for the signs will teach you what I am writing about, which is expressed more clearly through a variety of names...

# PARAGRAPH 5

<margin>Names are ambiguous.</margin> I do not wish for a variety of terms, for names are often ambiguous and deceptive. It cannot be otherwise: whoever does not truly recognize a disease will surely give it a false name. In this discussion, I shake off and reject the authority and protection of all the ancient writers; I will use nothing from them to defend or demonstrate my points. Although they may seem to hold the right path, their deception is more than miserable. Even when they see they are merely guessing, they nevertheless stubbornly cling to their opinions, preferring to be totally deluded in their medical practice rather than to truly understand.

<margin>Comparison of the womb and the Sun.</margin> The <term>Matrix</term> <note>original: "Matrix," usually translated as "womb," but for Paracelsus, it refers to the entire creative and functional system of the female reproductive power.</note> behaves in the body just like the Sun. The Sun is a single mass and a single body in the sphere, occupying the smallest space of the earth and sky. Likewise, the womb in the entire <term>Microcosm</term> <note>The human being viewed as a "miniature world" that mirrors the structure of the universe.</note> occupies no more space than the Sun occupies in its own geometry, relative to the size of the four elements.

<margin>What the Sun is in the universe.</margin> Furthermore, the Sun exists in the whole world, within all the elements. And although its physical body is not present everywhere, the Sun is nevertheless present. For the Sun is not merely a body. That which *is* the Sun is within the body—just as a person is thought to be their physical body, though they are not. <margin>What a human is. Sight is the sun of man.</margin> A human being is that which is *not* the body. What is the Sun? What is sight? It is not a body, but something more than a body. Thus, the "Sun" of humans is their sight—not the tongue, nor the eyes. For these physical parts are merely a corpse. Understand the same concerning women. <margin>What the womb is and what it consists of.</margin> The <term>pudendum</term> <note>The external female genitalia.</note> or womb is the woman herself; by the same logic, flax is not the light, but the flame is the light. And just as the light clings to the flax, so does the Sun: that is, the body is the flax, and the radiance is the Sun. The womb behaves similarly. For the body is not the womb, even if it is called by that name.

<margin>The center gives the name to things.</margin> For the center demonstrates the truth of the thing. All things should be named according to their center. Therefore, the womb remains "the womb" according to its center; however, in a physical dissection, it is not the womb, but merely flesh. It is fitting, therefore, that in describing a disease of the womb, I should also explain its "anatomy" for the sake of understanding its <term>paroxysm</term>. <note>A sudden attack or fit, like a seizure.</note>

<margin>The womb is the human being, and is throughout the whole body.</margin> It must be noted that the womb lies throughout the whole body of the woman, and it is the human being. For it has no other nature than that of a human. How could a human be generated from something that is not human? For just as a father and mother produce one like themselves, so too there is something like the womb in its own anatomy—and it is more than its mere physical structure. <margin>The fetus has traces of the womb.</margin> The reason is that within the "anatomy" of the womb, if a defect occurs in any of its members, that same mark appears in the member of the fetus. Thus, nothing is actually located in the physical limbs of the father or mother; rather, all influence is placed in the members of the womb. If the womb suffers from a deformity, the infant will exhibit that same deformity entirely. Since the womb occupies the whole body, just as the Sun occupies the sky, earth, sea, and air, it is right that we understand its anatomy as we understand a shadow or a spirit, which enters after the manner and custom of a man, yet has no physical body. <margin>What kind of bodies radiance and the moon are.</margin> The radiance of the Sun is a body; light is a body. These bodies are not tangible, yet they are corporeal. <margin>What is mortal.</margin> For nothing is fleeting or mortal that does not have a body. Death exists only in the body. Because that [spiritual] part in us is not tangible, I say that there are two bodies, as far as our judgment is concerned. It is necessary, therefore, that we recognize and understand the anatomy of these impalpable bodies. Once that is done, the Physician will have described the Microcosm of the womb, of which I shall provide a brief anatomy. I will deliver a full and more extensive anatomy of the womb in its proper place.

<margin>Anatomy regards the works; it is taken by reason; the sun is fourfold.</margin> For this brief description of the womb's anatomy, you will note four distributions into the four Elements. For you see the Sun is not simple in its operation, but fourfold. Anatomy is determined by its operation, not by what the eyes or hands can see. The Sun works in the heavens. It is in Mars, in Aries, in the Galaxy, and in all the stars; these cannot flourish without its radiance—not because the radiance exists, but because that radiance is a "body," and the operation is within that body. Therefore, they have need of it. Who can do anything without operation? Next, it also works in the air. <margin>Where Manna and Tereniabin come from.</margin> Neither <term>Manna</term> nor <term>Tereniabin</term> <note>original: "Tereniabin," a type of medicinal manna or honey-like dew found on plants, used in traditional pharmacy.</note> are produced if the corporeal radiance of the Sun does not work. In creatures subject to death, all operations occur bodily—just as in a human, whose body is compelled to labor and work, yet that physical body is not the "human." Then, it works similarly in the earth. If the Sun were not bodily present in the earth, nothing would be produced. Finally, it works in the sea. Without it, no fish would remain alive, and so on. Now, just as the parts of the earth are manifold, so too are the "bodies" of the Sun. Thus, a human falls into four anatomies, and yet his body is one. <margin>The anatomy of man is fourfold because of his four parts.</margin> There are four because the body is divided into four parts: into Earth, which is flesh; into Water, which is blood; into Air, which is the <term>chaos</term> <note>In Paracelsian thought, "chaos" often refers to the atmospheric air or the space between heaven and earth.</note>; and into Fire, that is, into the degrees of heat.

<margin>There are four falling sicknesses of the womb: blood, flesh, chaos, fire.</margin> According to these, there are four "falling sicknesses" of the womb: of Earth, Air, Fire, and Water. Recognize these four types from the Anatomy, the description of which is as follows. If the Womb suffers from the "falling sickness" and it spreads from the center into these parts: then if it falls into the water, the fit is in the blood. If it falls into the earth, the fit is in the flesh. If into the air, it is in the chaos of the body. If into the "complexions," it is in the fire. Each type of falling sickness has paroxysms like those we described in the first book. Each is revealed by those signs. Now, it must be known that all things are "one human" in the entire Anatomy, which lies wherever the form has its magnitude. The transition of the disease is no wider than the reach of the Anatomy. From there, it invades the whole body of the member into which it falls. If it twists the eyes, that happens from the Anatomy of the Womb, which twists the eyes, the mouth, the limbs, and everything. The tangible body is not the thing affected; rather, the Anatomy of the Womb is affected. Just as pears force their way and burst out of hard wood, so the womb forces all its members, especially those it holds in a diseased state. Therefore, the spasm of the womb's "falling sickness" is not of the physical body, but of the womb itself. Yet it drives the limb in which it resides to bend and curve itself as the condition dictates. Just as fire masters wood, so the Microcosm of the womb masters the human Microcosm.

<margin>How the paroxysms of the falling sickness occur.</margin> But what are these things that cause the paroxysm? Or how is it stirred up? This cannot be understood in any other way than as a carpenter works with his wood...

# ON THE FALLING SICKNESS OF THE WOMB
<note>original: "De Caduco Matricis." While "Caducus" refers to epilepsy (the "falling sickness"), it also carries an astrological double-meaning referring to "cadent" or falling planetary positions.</note>

...nor can a house be built without one. For within us there is also a carpenter, who, like a master craftsman, gives birth to and produces diseases. Now the craftsman is Mars, now Jupiter, now Taurus, now Scorpio. These are the artisans of the falling sickness: these are the ones who forge within the Microcosm of the Womb and occupy its Anatomy for their own work. Truly, how many hundreds of these craftsmen are there, whom no one knows except the Astronomer? No one except the Philosopher? This matter seems incredible to the Sophistic Physicians <note>Paracelsus's derogatory term for traditional Galenic doctors who relied on logic rather than observation and alchemy.</note>, whose art is perpetually occupied with dung, catarrhs, and the humors of the body. Truly, these things are not to be sought in dung, nor in rheum, nor in humors, but in the Planets and signs. In these <margin>The artisans of the falling sickness are not to be sought in dung.</margin> those craftsmen dwell. I beg you, do not take or divine the causes, origin, nature, essence, property, knowledge, and cure from urine, from dung, or from the pulse; but rather recognize these same things from the Planets and the celestial craftsmen. For every single disease is a work, proceeded from and completed by its own craftsman. Turn your eyes toward this, and judge what it is or is not. For such is the nature and condition of the Microcosm <note>The human being as a "little world" mirroring the universe.</note> that it carries the necessary wood and stones to whatever craftsman is in the star. <margin>The twin sciences of the Physician.</margin> Whence it follows that two sciences are required in a Physician: the first, so that the craftsman's wood does not grow; the second, so that the wood may be shattered or worn away for him.

Furthermore, someone might wonder in these matters what place it is where the anvil lies for forging this work. Answer me this: where does that craftsman sit who forges Roses, Lilies, etc.? Where does he have his workshop? What house does he possess? None. Likewise, there are none in man; and yet the craftsman has a place. These are the Architects, who are likened to Mechanical workers, but are nonetheless divided into their own tribes. It serves no purpose to ask in what place they work, or how <margin>The sensitive spirit suffers in the falling sickness.</margin> they conduct themselves in their workshops. It is enough to know this concerning the place: that the falling Planet has its possession in the Anatomy of the sensitive spirit <note>The "spiritus sensitivus" is the subtle medium that carries sensation and movement through the body.</note>, and through its roots, it falls into the sensitive spirit no differently than the Sun penetrates through glass. And the paroxysm <note>A sudden attack or seizure.</note> is manifested in the body—that is, in the flesh—just as the heat of the glass arises from the sun. For so also here, the spirit-disease is in the body, that is, in the flesh. Furthermore, what is the cause that such a spirit throws the body into such a great paroxysm? For it must be noted that the eyes and ears suffer much because of the Anatomy of the heart, which appears no differently than if it were the Anatomy of the ears and eyes, when nevertheless that Anatomy has not been invaded, but the others are moved together only by the commotion of the heart. And because of this, this art and medicine is local, just like a sign of the true members to their native place. In women, an ailment is everything; in men, the same is a light matter. For this reason, those ailments must be considered in women which in men are a light matter and not an ailment.

# PARAGRAPH 6

<margin>The falling sickness of women and the hidden diseases it may stir up.</margin>
Many diseases of the <term>Microcosm</term> <note>the human body, viewed as a miniature reflection of the entire universe</note> are stirred up and brought to light in women at the same time, which previously lay hidden within them. In this category are apoplexy, sudden death, paralysis, spasms, fever, jaundice, and <term>dropsy</term> <note>swelling caused by excess fluid, known today as edema</note>. Let no one be persuaded that such diseases either arise from the nature of the falling sickness itself, or that they *are* the falling sickness. For the falling sickness does not contain fever, apoplexy, or jaundice within itself. However, if these diseases erupt alongside the seizure, it is because the falling sickness has at least agitated and brought forth those conditions from pre-existing matter. And although heat, foaming at the mouth, and suffocation might happen to coincide outside of this matter, it must be understood that all these things emerge from the narrowing of nature and the violent agitation that arises from the striking of all the limbs. These symptoms end when the <term>paroxysm</term> <note>the fit or seizure itself</note> ends and do not typically lead to death. In these accidents of the "Falling Sickness of the Womb," the Physician must be exceptionally prudent, so that he can distinguish them correctly and skillfully assign each symptom to its proper cause.

But now that the nature and condition of the seizure have been sufficiently explained, I would next like you to understand the signs of which <term>Element</term> <note>the four building blocks of the universe: Fire, Air, Water, and Earth</note> any particular falling sickness belongs to, and in which <term>Anatomy</term> <note>not just physical organs, but the inner essential structure and spiritual blueprint</note> it is found. For to understand the cure itself, these signs—which I have proposed are twofold—are absolutely necessary. <margin>Twofold signs of the falling sickness.</margin> For some signs refer to the Element itself, while others pertain to the Anatomy. Every cure must be established in two ways: according to the Element and according to the Anatomy. I will pass over those other things previously proposed regarding the falling sickness which are stirred up by the seizure itself, for which specific experience and canonical care must be maintained, with this distinction: the cure for the falling sickness itself must always take precedence. Furthermore, pay attention to that cure which contains its own <term>Theory</term> within it—which is to say, the <term>Practice</term> that affects the entire body. <margin>Theory flowing from practice is the most certain.</margin>
For who, I ask, would not consider and accept that Theory as true and right which flows from and is confirmed by Practice alone? <margin>The practice of things...</margin>

Who will understand or interpret voices or words unless he is a speaker? For a mute person cannot, nor can a deaf person. To know is true practice.</margin> In this way, our reason is also mute and blind in recognizing those things it ought to handle, unless it is informed more deeply through Practice, not through "trying" <note>original: "tentationem"; mere trial and error</note>. Because you are ignorant of this, stay away from Medicine; otherwise, you will be operating in a den of thieves.

<margin>The Melancholic Hare and the Choleric Ram.</margin>
It must be said that what is beneficial for people of this kind must not be directed toward the <term>Microcosm</term> <note>the human being as a "small world" mirroring the universe</note> of the person, but specifically toward the microcosm of the <term>matrix</term> <note>the womb</note>. The ancients—whether writers or doctors—established their medical regimen according to the judgment of their own will, based on the outward appearance of things presented to their eyes. Thus, they claimed the hare was Melancholic and the ram was Choleric. In this way, they built their art and science solely from the forms or species that met their eyes, and from this, they prescribed a regimen for this "falling sickness." However, you should neither accept this nor consider it true in any part. For this seizure is neither from the outward form nor *within* the form that their eyes behold. Therefore, the regimen is not located in a form visible to the eyes. Just as the disease of the womb was hidden from them, so too its cure and regimen remain concealed from them. I will not list their entire foolishness here; rather, as much as seems necessary, I will provide you with the opportunity to recognize their errors, lest you be accidentally deceived by them—something they have attempted until now through their Pharisaic and hypocritical crowds.

<margin>Like is pleasing to like.</margin>
For "like" does not wage war against "like"; instead, one frequently protects the other, without regard for whether the cause is good or bad. Rather, read the writings of both sides and act as fair judges, lest you be deceived by any partiality.

Regarding the establishment of a Regimen, accept these two modes. One regards the <term>complexion</term> <note>the internal temperament or "astral" quality of a substance</note>; the other regards the <term>arcana</term> <note>the secret, powerful healing essences within nature</note>. The first pertains to the nutrition of the womb's microcosm. For the womb is nourished by the complexion, not by physical bodies. The second belongs to the arcana, which run alongside foods, just as Salt accompanies all things. After these two, learn further about the regimen and the care of that regimen in this manner. (Note that there is no discussion of the actual *cure* here yet.)

<margin>What "Complexion" is.</margin>
Complexions nourish the microcosm of the womb. What is a complexion? It is that which has no physical body, yet possesses a quality. It is not that "quality" itself is the regimen in this context, but rather that it indicates the <term>anatomy</term> <note>the internal functional structure, both spiritual and physical</note> of the womb's microcosm. For the limbs are nourished by all things, not just one. Furthermore, they do not take in more than they can digest, or more than they need or is suitable for them.

<margin>Complexion is a star.</margin>
Now, in truth, the "complexion" is a "star" <note>an internal spiritual influence or "astrum"</note> that no one sees, much like the scent of Musk that breathes out, which no one sees. If the scent has breathed out, its complexion has vanished. For the complexion is not a body. That which does not depart via scent vanishes by another path. In this way, complexions are changed through their "virtue" during preparation: one scent becomes another, one taste becomes another, flavors change, and the complexion changes. If these qualities lay fixed in the physical bodies, they could not be changed. But they do not consist in physical bodies; therefore, they are transformed and pass into that transmutation. Thus, if a regimen is to be employed, the complexions and arcana must be brought into harmony, as these are what should be esteemed and held as the regimen.

The regimen, then, exists without a body; it is the sole essence of things. It does not look at "cold" or "hot" <note>a critique of Galenic medicine, which balanced the four humors</note>, but at the "anatomy"—that is, at the "Medium" of those things, so that the whole man might be balanced in the regimen. For what is this practice where you treat an obstruction in the liver, or phlegm in the lungs, or strengthening in the brain? Those who do such things are "prevaricators" <note>liars or evaders of the truth</note>, not Physicians. For such a system fights against the entire order of Medicine. All members in the body ought to be subject to this regimen, which is not based on cooling, heating, spitting, or "comforting," but on the Virtue which is the *Medium*. That virtue refers to and contains the whole body, as is taught elsewhere regarding this art of establishing a regimen, which I omit here for the sake of brevity.

<margin>Regimen is the whole anatomy.</margin>
Since, therefore, the regimen must be the "whole anatomy," you ought to know that any single "simple" <note>a medicinal herb or single ingredient</note> occupies the whole and entire anatomy. Furthermore, know that it is not the physical body of the medicine, but the *complexion*—in which strength flourishes or is hidden—that constitutes the regimen. From this it follows that the physical bodies of foods or drinks, whether they be hot, cold, moist, or dry, are not to be considered. Rather, one must see what they become in their *transformation*.

<margin>Transmutation is the principle of regimen.</margin>
For things do not remain the same inside the body as they are outside. Therefore, just because you find this or that to be "hot" or "cold" on the plate, it will not necessarily be so within the "anatomy." Do not care or believe that lettuce is "cold," nor purslane; nor that balm or basil are "hot." Instead, labor to know what they are like in their *transmutation*—what becomes of them. And from this final state, define the regimen.

<margin>Two worlds regarding regimen.</margin>
For since there are two worlds—the womb [of the woman] and again the womb [of nature], namely women and herbs—there will also be two Microcosms under one anatomy.

Why, then, do you ordain and offer "coolants" and "heaters" etc., in this falling sickness, when they do not help, but actually harm? What is the cause? This, surely: because you are ignorant of the "double bodies." This is why you make the disease worse. Meanwhile, it is enough for your excuse if you can pretend that the patient himself hindered the success, even though you are safely the author of that evil. Therefore, so that you may correctly grasp the meaning, I repeat and command that you weigh that complexion which is the *ultimate* one. Such is the anatomy of both Microcosmic natures: of the womb in the woman, and of the womb in the external elements. From these things follows the regimen and order, as I have written in a specific book on the subject. For foods are not only to be judged, but also tested, lest they fall into contempt. Because of you triflers, I am forced to describe elsewhere what I would have preferred to embrace in this very discourse for the health and safety of the sick. Nevertheless, so that you may better understand that little book, pay attention to this brief information about the difference in complexions in which this regimen consists—as well as about arcana and other similar things—as much as is needed here for the falling sickness of the womb. Although these things are handed down in brief "universal" terms, they should not be neglected by you on that account. I hope you will not do so because of those people...

Seek more information in other books.

# PARAGRAPH VIII.

<margin>Who the true Master of Medicine is.</margin>
**B**ut so that, setting these things aside, we may finally cross over to the practice that remains: it will indeed be appropriate that I do not follow the style of the ancients, or their opinions, but rather give my support to the truth itself. For no science is founded upon imagining and speculating. While I undertake to do this, I will never be able to rightly turn aside toward "authorities," but it will be necessary that I seize support from authority itself <note>Here he distinguishes between human "authorities" (like Galen or Avicenna) and the supreme authority of Nature and God</note>. In this, I shall not bring forth fantasy, nor speculation, nor wisdom for the sake of **sophistical** <note>arguments that sound clever but are actually false or misleading</note> subtleties; rather, I shall demonstrate the whole matter from that source from which it is lawful for me and any other Physician to take proofs. For our "divorce" <note>The split between Paracelsus's followers and the traditional medical establishment</note> is in this: that some follow the doctrines of "heads" <note>human intellect/leaders</note>, while others, on the contrary, embrace the doctrines of "roots" <note>the foundations of nature</note>. Or rather, some recognize Physicians as their Masters, while others recognize **Nature herself**—among whose number I profess myself to be. For what could a man teach me that he himself is ignorant of? What is not situated within himself? For Medicine is not founded in man. And although one man may indeed teach another something, yet even he must have been taught by nature; otherwise, his doctrine will be worthless. If, therefore, he has drawn from nature—since she still lives today—he will for that reason still be a fellow-disciple with me, and I with him. Yet we differ again in this: that he makes other disciples and professes himself a Master, while I make myself a disciple of Nature and constitute her the Master of my colleagues and teachers.

<margin>Medicine consists in two things.</margin>
But lest you become too timid while I command you to recognize my Master, and thus, moved by the instigation of the Doctors who oppose me, you abandon me: now a definition or conclusion shall follow in that manner which is customary in Medicine. This is so that you may know how to cure the sick person from every handed-down foundation and theory—which cure concludes and perfects the knowledge of any Physician. All these things being predefined, I would first have you know that Medicine consists entirely of two things: one is **regimen**, the other are **arcana** <note>term: Arcana. In this context, it refers to the secret, powerful "essences" or "souls" of substances that act as specific remedies, as opposed to the general diet or lifestyle</note>. The distinction between these two operations is this: that which consists in regimen is the daily, compelled course of the stars. That which consists in arcana is a unique poison, infused at a single time, which comes further from heaven and the stars.

From these things, now discern the arcana of foods and the arcana of Medi-

<margin>medicines, and how they differ from each other.</margin>
-cine from each other in this way. That which is to be administered with its body is food or drink. That which is administered without its body is Medicine. Therefore, errors are committed in this way: Medicines that are offered with their bodies, like food and drink to satisfy the requirements of hunger, ought to be administered as foods, not as Medicine. And Medicine must be given at its own hour, according to the rule of the ascendants and the disease, not for hunger or thirst.

<margin>When cumin is food, etc.</margin>
Cumin is food in cases of "windiness" <note>gas or bloating</note>, not a Medicine; therefore it ought to be administered as a food. Similarly, many spices and similar herbs are very effective and provide much benefit in various diseases for this reason: that those diseases are so managed or passed over in their stars. For **Cumin** is the enemy of **Boreas** <note>The North Wind, representing cold/dry influences</note> and breaks its star.

<margin>From what things prescriptions for diseases should be taken.</margin>
From this it is concluded that the knowledge of regimen must be taken from those things which do not allow themselves to be separated from their bodies. For these bodies, and the bodies of the body, contribute their confluence and concordance on both sides. Therefore, in these things there is only "regimen," and not also "Medicine." And whatever recovers because of this, recovers from the regimen by that power of which we have spoken. From this, therefore, learn to order the regimen as is fitting, lest you perhaps deviate from this order, which erroneous Physicians have done until now.

<margin>The diversity of regions in diet must be carefully considered.</margin>
Thus, I would also be hallucinating if I wrote down a fixed regimen in the manner that has been observed until now by the ancients and continued for a long time. You ought to understand it this way: if I established a regimen, for example, for a fourth part of Germany, I could not extend it wider or further. For the region of that fourth part—its sky, its confluence, the influence of heaven and earth—would be the reason why the stated regimen could not be extended wider than it was defined. For from that earth in which the "falling" <note>the seizure or sickness</note> originated, the person wishes to be fed and given drink from the same. Therefore, if I set a region before me and rightly consider its sky, earth, all its degrees, essences, properties, etc., comprised here: then I shall have described neither Europe, nor Germany, nor Italy, much less other parts, namely Asia and Africa. Wherefore I have only pre-figured a summary regimen of its Theory. The rest belongs to the Physician, so that from these things he may further direct his diet according to the reason of that climate—and not of the climate alone, but also of the **ascendant** of the entire region. For a different arrangement and diet ought not to bring blame upon the Physician. For the great constellation, the confluence, and the property of regions, parts, lands, and waters compel it so. For in these, from time to time, other and different properties, essences, and natures (and whatever else must be considered here) fall between.

For just as the womb suffers from that disease, so it must be known that its Medicine is in a similar form according to the anatomical distribution...

# ON THE FALLING SICKNESS OF THE WOMB.

...distribution be given again. Whence this opinion of mine is not unjust, in which I say that the Physician, for the sake of finding arts and composing **Prescriptions**, has need of a daily teacher <note>By "daily teacher," Paracelsus refers to Nature itself and the experience of observing patients every day</note>. For who is there that knows anything of the art without this "inventress," anatomy? No one. <margin>The Physician is like a hunting dog in tracking down hidden secrets.</margin> For the Physician is like a hunting dog: who, once he has perceived the scent of a wild beast, follows it with a continuous tracking until at last he falls upon the beast itself. <margin>Hidden secrets are like wild beasts.</margin> And let this example serve you, so that, just as the dog holds the prey in his nose, so you may hold the **arcanum** <note>arcanum: a hidden, powerful medicinal essence or "secret" within a natural substance</note> in your eyes, and know it exquisitely through a similar formation of Anatomy, so that it cannot slip away from you. For you ought to arrange Prescriptions through this tracking alone, and follow nothing else than what that scent indicates. For just as a wild beast may outrun the dog, it nevertheless leaves behind such a scent that the dog can follow the entire path by its guidance; similarly do the hidden secrets of nature behave, which precede all diseases. If the Physician proves himself a diligent dog, he will easily fall upon their tracks, so that herbs, stones, seeds, and so on will be met with, and will present and offer themselves according to the nature of the **paroxysm** <note>paroxysm: a sudden attack or violent expression of a disease, such as a fit or seizure</note>, the rising signs, and the entire constellation of the stars as well as of bodies. For in the falling sickness, you have a manifest movement of the heavens, so that you can readily explain it like Astronomers and Philosophers. Thus, according to these things, you will find the entire course of heaven and earth—that is, of all the stars—within the things of nature, because they rise or fall together with the paroxysm. And this Anatomy is equal. Therefore, not only the paroxysm of men, but also the paroxysm of growing things <note>i.e., the cycles and "fits" of plants and minerals</note> must be known, and thus at last like must be matched to like. However, although I do not fully describe everything here, but leave the greatest part to the book *On the Method of Composing*, nevertheless I touch upon these things at least in passing, so that you are not deceived by the Prescriptions of the ancient Writers. For those things oppose the inventress of all Medicine and of every art, and they hallucinate gravely both in anatomy and in other matters; so much so that their writings seem to be from a certain fanatical brain, who indeed claimed much knowledge for himself, but had very little of it, and hardly once even heard in passing anything about the true inventress of the arts.

Thus, therefore, the inventress of Prescriptions teaches that the falling sickness of the womb should be taken away through the Medicine which she indicates and shows. For within her is the force and power of the composition of Prescriptions, not within men. Therefore, know this now from all things: that the same womb prefigures itself in many ways, now with the **Granagranae**. And although <margin>Verrista etc. Granagranae etc. for the womb.</margin> this form can only be reduced to the form of anatomy with pain and difficulty, it is nevertheless a form. For although the appearance may be twofold, the star is nevertheless similar in both, and the bodies are similar to the body as it becomes in disease. <margin>Whence Verrista originates.</margin> **Verrista** <note>Verrista and Granagranae are specific Paracelsian terms for medicines or pathological conditions; Verrista likely refers to a preparation related to "verruca" (warts/growths) and Granagranae to grain-like medicinal extracts</note> descends from that blood, and is natural. And from that which it grows and exists, from the same it is given to the womb. The same also happens with the Granagranae: if the paroxysms rise vehemently, then they lead the ultimate body of the womb into a similar form. Therefore, even if the womb is not as it exists in [standard] anatomy, you should not care about that. <margin>The anatomy of the womb is different when sick.</margin> For the womb of a healthy woman does not have the "anatomy" of the falling sickness; but if she becomes sick, then it brings forth that anatomy, similar to the Medicine, just as has been said. The order of the process of this Medicine has been explained enough so far, and this place does not allow for it to be drawn out further. In the book *On the Virtues of Simples*, both this and many other things will be handed down more explicitly.

<margin>Note: paragraph starts with a decorated initial 'I'</margin>
**I**t also happens with the **Granagranae**. If the paroxysms are increased more vehemently, they cause the final body of the womb to become like the Granagranae. And therefore, even if a womb such as exists in [diseased] anatomy is not found in nature [ordinarily], you should care nothing for that. For nothing is given to a healthy womb; but just as the womb itself forces the disease into a form, so you should follow the tracks of its form. For eventually the womb returns to this point: that it is reduced to such a bodily **Physiognomy**, **Chiromancy**, etc. <note>Paracelsus believed the "lines" and "features" of organs could be read like a palm (chiromancy) or a face (physiognomy) to diagnose disease</note> Therefore, I rightly draw you into this art. For in this alone does the Physician stand. But if you do not know this, whatever you attempt is in vain. Therefore, let what has been said here suffice, until, God willing, I name the **simples** <note>simples: individual herbs or minerals used as medicines</note> and the **arcana** themselves, and reveal them in their proper places.

### CONCLUSION OF THE LAST BOOK.

<margin>Note: paragraph starts with a decorated initial 'S'</margin>
> *Thus, therefore, the book of the suffocation or precipitation of the womb—which I therefore call the "falling sickness" of the same—is finished. For the falling sickness and the disease of the womb do not differ in cause, origin, and essence, but are one thing, and are contained in one. But how the difference occurs by reason of the bodies, you may know from the present [work]. Indeed, if this Philosophy and Astronomy seem too arduous and difficult to the ignorant, nevertheless they cannot be handed down in any other way, except finally in the cure, concerning **Verrista** and **Granagranae**. For these two are the highest **arcana** that can be applied in this disease, which are preferred above all other things of nature. Indeed, there are many processes here and there. <margin>Verrista and Grana are the highest secrets in the falling sickness.</margin> Concerning which we judge in the book on simples, and we do not speak further here. For experience itself manifests it. What is manifest in nature through itself is not fitting to be explained and taught. For from such [teaching] Physicians become lazy, thick, and ignorant: who have all their protection in books alone, and consult them alone concerning the truth. But this knowledge ought not to flow from the letter, but from use, experience, and ocular information, etc. For this teaches true practice. Therefore, I attempt nothing peculiar in practice here. For what is manifest must not be written down, but proved through use. If that is not done, nothing good can either be hoped for or sought from those Physicians. I wish this brief practice, therefore, to be free from blame; concerning which enough has been handed down regarding the things in which this virtue is situated, etc. Let everyone betake himself to use and ocular experience. Without which all arts perish and bring harm. Know the simples rightly and diligently: then transfer them to use and experience, by persisting for a long time, not by snoring behind the furnace, or by [mere] persuasion, which is the proper custom of the Academies.*

# CERTAIN MEDICAL FRAGMENTS FOLLOW,
# pertaining to the fourth volume of the works of Theophrastus. <note>Theophrastus: referring to Paracelsus, whose full name was Philippus Aureolus Theophrastus Bombastus von Hohenheim.</note>

## TO THE READER.

<margin>Theophrastus taught at Basel.</margin>
**A**lthough I know well, Reader, that these works of mine will not be greatly approved by my adversaries, as they seem entirely erroneous and disordered to them: nevertheless, they will not even find or obtain what they seek. For these are the ones who, with all their accomplices, are entangled in manifest error—something that would be too laborious to demonstrate at length here. If we publish our *Paramirum* <note>The *Paramirum* is one of Paracelsus's most important medical works, focusing on the five "entities" or causes of disease.</note> it will provide a full and clear teaching on Theory and other matters they desire to know. And though these things will not be approved by everyone, those who do approve will find their effort well spent. For my method of teaching about various diseases is clear from the individual chapters, at least as far as it applies to practical use. Indeed, the people at Basel heard me, but they did not receive my work as they ought to have. The arrogance of the students stands in the way of their own progress. For they waste away and die among those medical books which they seek out and collect from everywhere without judgment or wisdom. It is a pity they do not see how little utility they gain from reading them. And everywhere many new books fly forth and are published by them, yet the authors have never tested what they write through any experience. Although this is not without shame, they do not value the matter highly. They describe diseases from head to heel. They force and pile into this order every disease known to medicine, whether known to them or not. For they think it a disgrace to omit anything. And for the ignorant, they often paint over such things with "colors" <note>Metaphorical "colors" or rhetorical flourishes used to hide a lack of actual knowledge.</note> in which the danger to the body and to life itself is often clearly present. And this was the reason why, after first diligently unrolling and following the books of those authors, I later made an open divorce and departed from them. Nor was I the only one, but many <margin>Why Theophrastus broke away from the ancient physicians.</margin> others did as well. It was only right that the truth be dug out from far different principles and works, and that ancient things should not be accepted indiscriminately as Gospels, for they were never sold as Gospels. Experience itself is the mistress and proof of things. He who follows and preserves experience will detect many errors and lies of the ancient physicians. Although those things might seem too sweet and pleasing to the moderns. I wish indeed that a right conscience would so moderate everyone that, with a sober and sincere affection, both my writings and those of the ancients might be weighed and judged. But the old schoolmasters and apothecaries suffer themselves to be called back to the true school only with great difficulty. Farewell.

---

### Fragment on Dropsy. <note>Dropsy: known today as edema, the painful swelling of soft tissues due to the accumulation of excess fluid.</note>
### CHAPTER I.

**F**irst, it must be known that dropsy is nothing other than a superfluous moisture of the body, contained anywhere within it. That moisture clings in the pores of the flesh and the cavities of the muscles; and finally, it occupies the pores of the skin after it has filled all the cavities and muscles. It is revealed by no other signs than swelling, the marks left behind by pressure <note>This refers to "pitting edema," where a finger press leaves a lasting indentation in the skin.</note>, and the compression of the heart, etc. Whether something is shown above the heart or not is all the same. For what is below is the same as what is above, and vice versa. It makes no difference in the cure. In practice, do not let the liver or spleen, etc., distract you, but look only to the moisture.

<margin>The nature of the cure for dropsy.</margin>
Furthermore, in the cure of dropsy, consider three things: *Heaven, Earth, and the Moon*—that is, Astronomy, Philosophy, and the Microcosm <note>Microcosm: the "small world," a term used to describe the human body as a reflection of the entire universe (the Macrocosm).</note>. The Earth is the subject; Heaven is the effect. The Microcosm is the patient.

<margin>Mercury in the cure of dropsy.</margin>
Therefore, above all, labor to remove the water; afterward, apply yourself to tempering Nature and strengthening her. For one without the other is death. The expulsion must be instituted through **Mercury**. For in it alone resides the power of purging the water. The drying must be done through the **Element of Fire**. For those things by which moisture is properly and truly dried out, their description is as follows:
1. *Preparation of Mercury.*
2. *Preparation of Sulphur.*

### EXPULSION.

**T**he power and quality of **Mercury** is such a medical secret <term>arcanum: a hidden, powerful medicinal essence or "secret" within a natural substance</term> that it leads out the moisture of this disease to an exact weight. For Colocynth, Hermodactyl, Turbith <note>Colocynth (bitter apple), Hermodactyl (meadow saffron), and Turbith (root of a morning glory) were traditional, often violent, herbal purgatives.</note>, etc., do not provide this. They have no entry into the pores in which that exceeding moisture lies. Nor can any other spirit besides the spirit of Mercury penetrate those places. The rest of the medicines, therefore, weaken the intestines too much by emptying them, taking the good with the bad.

### FIRE.

**T**herefore the "Fire" is Iron Saffron <note>original: "Crocus Martis," an early name for iron oxides used in medicine.</note>, Sulphur, etc., which are able to penetrate to those places where the moisture is stored. But they ought to be sublimated and reverberated <note>Sublimation and reverberation: alchemical processes involving heating a substance to purify it or change its state.</note>. For in this way, after the separation of the other three Elements, they become Fire.

---

# FRAGMENTS OF MEDICINE.

<margin>
3. On the cure, etc.
4. Interpretation.
</margin>

### *Explanation.*

**J**ust as the sky pushes out grasses and leaves from the earth, which the sky brings forth by its rains: so also the sky contains within itself an invisible rain. This rain is the cause of dropsy <note>original: "hydropisis". A condition characterized by an excess of watery fluid collecting in the cavities or tissues of the body.</note>. The earth is the body. For just as rain acts upon the earth, so in the same way it acts within a human being, as has been said. Therefore, first of all, the human body must be understood. Once that is known, one should then also know its "seed" and understand whether that which falls from the sky above into the body is too much or too little, and whether the earth—that is, the body—can attract all of it to itself, or whether it is far too little. For an abundant supply of rain results in dropsy. However, a moisture that is less than what is right results in wasting <note>original: "aridura". A historical term for the drying out or wasting away of a limb or the whole body.</note>. This chapter, however, deals with dropsy. The law of temperament in a human is such that the sky gives equal and fitting impressions, as much as is required for the constitution of the body. From an abundance of rains, dropsy arises.

### *Opposing Views.*

**H**e who drinks too much, and indulges in excessive drinking, does not bring dropsy upon himself in any other way than a farmer floods his meadow with too much overflow; and to this irrigation, the rain of the sky is added, by both of which the meadow or field is excessively moistened and suffocated. But the "sky" <note>In Paracelsian thought, "sky" or "heaven" refers to the astral or atmospheric influences that act upon the internal organs of the human "microcosm."</note> is the dropsy, not the water that was drunk. This is demonstrated by the increase of the disease. Therefore, it arises from the sky, not from the earth.

### *Symptoms.*

## *Fragment on Wasting (Aridura).*

**W**asting <term>Aridura<gloss>A disease involving the progressive drying out or atrophy of the body's tissues.</gloss></term> in its beginning sometimes attacks one limb, sometimes several, and occasionally all of them, occupying the whole body so that the blood, liver, heart, veins, and all other parts waste away; I exclude only the bones, cartilages, and ligaments, etc. These parts are dried out just as grass withers in a field. For just as you see grass, deprived of its moisture, become parched and dry: so similarly the same thing happens to the body. Indeed, a body that has its proper moisture is fat, solid, and vigorous.

Now, a body that lacks its moisture receives it from the "sky," not from itself. It is indeed made of earth according to the physical body: but it does not live from the earth, but from the sky. Therefore, the sky moistens it. What a person eats is the "seed" of his body, which grows continually within the person. This growth comes from the nourishment given by the sky. If, however, moisture is withdrawn by the impression of the sky, the person withers and dries up. Many stars and many parts within a human cause the wasting to occupy now this limb, now that one, now one, now several, now all. This is the sum of it: to whatever part of the body a rain more meager than is right is given, that part is afflicted by wasting.

### *Cure.*

With distilled and sublimated things, that is, with liquid silver <note>original: "aqua argenti", likely referring to mercury or a specific alchemical preparation of silver.</note>.

### *Explanation.*

Why winter causes a paroxysm <note>A sudden attack or violent expression of a disease.</note> of fever. Likewise, Saturn <note>The planet Saturn was traditionally associated with coldness, dryness, and chronic diseases.</note> causes it. Likewise, unequal rain—cold and snowy rain—stirs up new pains.

### *Signs.*

Why there is a cough: because of dryness, etc.
Why there is shortness of breath: because dryness extinguishes the parts of the body.

---

## *Another Note on Wasting.*

**O**bserve how the grass grows: In the same way, water must be brought so that growth may occur. "Water" is the Arcanum <note>A secret or "inner" medicinal power.</note> or the "sky" in Medicine. That which sows the water is the "seed of Pearls," not the Margarites <note>Paracelsus distinguishes between different medicinal preparations of pearls here.</note>. This generates milk in the breasts of women. For what else is that but rain and dew growing in a state of wasting <note>original: "Marasmo", referring to marasmus or severe malnutrition/wasting.</note>, in which the Sun of the Microcosm <note>The "internal sun" or vital heat of the human being.</note> rejoices. Regarding its preparation, I will conclude thus: resolve it into an Elixir, so that it may be a ferment. For the body provides the rest of what is needed. The dose is for the time of sowing, that is, in Spring and Autumn. What else is this than the rising and setting of the Sun?

## *Fragment on Diseases of Tincture.*

**A**ll colors lie hidden and concealed. It is Art <note>Referring to the "art" of Alchemy or Chemistry.</note> that brings them forth. Therefore, the Archeus <note>The internal "alchemist" or vital force that directs the functions of the body.</note> is there, who creates the tinctures. He then emits and pours them out as far as the body extends or its anatomy reaches.

### *Cure.*

It is a washing away, like a color being washed from a cloth by water.
Likewise, the washing away of diseases that take on color, which take on dregs.

### *Opposing Views.*

Just as color is made from many things—that is, ink from two things, etc.—so types of this kind are also in the body. If these are joined together: from them such diseases arise.

### *Conclusion.*

If my theory is not approved by you, at least let my practice please you, which will confer more utility upon you than all the ancient writers combined.

---

## *On Colic.*

**B**ut I say that Colic is the "primary matter" of the generation of winds <note>Gas or flatulence.</note>. If the winds are made, they are sent forth with their own property. Not only is dung generated, but wind is consumed within it.
> Such as concerning ***Thunder of the belly.***
> Such as concerning ***rain without wind.***
Now it must be noted: what is the generation of winds?

---

## *On Paralysis and Apoplexy.*

**B**ut I say that Paralysis occurs, etc. Paralysis is called "Autumn" or the "obstruction of the vintage."
For if the body ought to gather its vintage, nothing is present. In this body—that is, in the Microcosmic vintage <note>The internal "harvesting" of nutrients and spirits.</note>—the spirits tread the fruits of the body and store them in their cask. The "cask" is the free body. If it is too hot and does not ferment or foam properly, then it rises up and throws or pushes the "lid" upward toward the heart, lungs, brain, etc. And just as a cask that is opened behaves, so also does a human: for he must not admit air. But air enters if the cask bursts itself. This bursting is nothing other than excessive heat created in the body, if the cask has fermented too hotly and the hoops were not tightly joined.

# MEDICAL FRAGMENTS.

## On Mania.

The heavens, therefore, produce a multitude of the insane <note>original: "Amentium", referring to those without mind or reason</note>, all of whom cannot be described. For even those whom the heavens make wise are fools. Indeed, the wisdom of this world is nothing but foolishness. However, since you do not exercise your medical practice for these types, we shall remain silent about them here. Regarding the others, however, who fall under the scope of Medicine, take note of this: Just as they are broken by natural things, so they are cured again by natural Medicines.

That which drives away Madness <note>original: "Amentiam"</note> has a two-fold logic: one from the stars of the blood, and the other from the administration of things that exceed the intellect. Those arising from the blood are influenced by the stars of the blood, which prevail. Those arising from administration are like nettle seed sown among cabbage, or like mustard, which moves the entire brain. For things of this sort affect the brain. It is often said that this or that person became manic <note>original: "maniacum"</note> during a certain disease. And this is rightly said, for in such a case the conjunction of the stars coincides. They also say: "This or that person eats this," which is also not poorly said. For there are certain things that overwhelm the brain, where one of two things dissolves the other. Likewise, they say a person is insane <note>original: "amentem"</note> due to intense meditation or excessive study. This is not wrongly determined, for the brain ought not to be driven or stretched beyond its powers. For its excessive tension is the dissolution of its properties and gifts.

That which dissolves the brain is either too exalted in its temperament <note>original: "complexione"</note>, or it encounters the brain in too subtle a form, or it is a body that itself possesses reason or intellect. That which has too much temperament is from the stars. That which is too subtle exists from the property of Nature. That which is from the intellect has another conjunction. As far as temperament is concerned: excessive heat, cold, or moisture, etc. Fire causes Mania <note>A state of intense excitement or "madness" in the medical theory of the time</note>, as does the brain of a cat, likewise Hemlock <note>original: "Cicuta"</note>, and likewise Galita <note>likely a reference to a specific mineral or stone used in alchemy</note>.

## Another on Mania.

The heavens are unique to reason. For as many stars as there are in the sky, so many thoughts and inconsistencies are in a human being. If, therefore, the sky errs within itself, the human also errs. The modes and types of this error are various and cannot all be told. For the variety of the stars creates this variety in the human. Thus also fools are to be recognized, and the many manias in humans, which exist as both simple and varied forms. But regarding these fools or Maniacs, what other reasons do you seek to scrutinize? Think and weigh what a human being is, and rest there—that is, in the heavens.
