## Another Fragment on Mania.

Wandering stars of memory, prudence, wisdom, and knowledge.
Likewise, if nettles emerge among wisdom, then they burn it out, etc., and create a "hot" cause.
Likewise, if the Water-lily <note>original: "Nenuphar"</note> appears, it creates a "cold" cause.
Likewise, if Mars, if Saturn, etc.

## Conclusion of the Book.

Now indeed, see what experience contributes. A few years ago I did not yet know what I know now. Therefore, only now do I write what I ought to have written long ago. For those things of which I have found a proof, I treat and hand down. Concerning other things not yet discovered by me, I am ashamed to write. How do I seem to you?

## The Cure.

In these matters, the <term>Cure of Offia</term> <note>original: "Cura Offiae". This likely refers to a specific alchemical preparation or a "morsel" (offa) used as a carrier for medicine</note> must be maintained. Likewise, where demons are conjured, such trifles are employed. They do not hold this in the intellect, and so it remains. And from these, recipes are taken—not from Violet flowers, Water-lily, Roses, etc. These things must be learned from Monks and conjurers, etc.

---

## On Worms.

Although worms are indeed manifold, there is nonetheless at least one name and one cause for all of them. Their diversity is produced by the matter from which they are generated. Whatever this matter may be, it requires at least one medicine, which is general for all worms.

### What?
If worms, etc.

### The Cause.
<margin>The cause of worms is twofold.</margin>
The cause of worms is twofold: decay <note>original: "putredo"</note> and seed <note>original: "sperma"</note>. The logic of the "seed" is this: If a certain seed of worms, etc., enters the body and is not digested, then it is changed by natural heat into worms, or a "monster" of worms. Why? Because it is not in its proper place, that is, in the Womb <note>original: "Matrice"</note>. Therefore, it becomes a monster, just as a human generates <term>Gnomes</term> <note>Earth elementals in Paracelsian philosophy</note>, or likewise <term>Giants</term>, etc.

<margin>Cheeses made in August are prone to decay.</margin>
The other cause is decay. Any decay produces worms if it aligns itself according to the heavens and the Moon; otherwise, not at all. Thus, cheeses that are made in August and July all rot. There are other similar months in the year. Therefore, the generation of worms is a "heavenly decay."

Similarly, worms are generated from great heat. Thus, in summer you see many things rot from the more abundant heat. If, therefore, August, June, the dog days <note>the hottest days of summer</note>, etc., dominate in the body, then parts of the body will decay, from which worms are then produced. For such is the nature of the entire <term>Microcosm</term> <note>the human being viewed as a miniature reflection of the universe</note> and its parts.

---

## ON THE LOCATION.

Concerning the place where they are generated, you should know that worms arise only where decay can exist.

How Nature’s daily purging works.

-> ## *Chapter on the Falling Sickness.* <-

**N**othing should be taken away from sleep, etc. That is, sleep when you wish, not according to day or night. Day and night are established for the herbs and the grass, not for you. You should keep watch, etc., when there is need, etc.

If a salmon can be made from a trout <note>original: "salare", a term for a young trout or small salmonid</note>... it will also be possible for one sickness to be produced from another in a man; that is, the falling sickness <note>original: "caducus", referring to epilepsy</note> from a tremor, or from the falling sickness, etc., which is a unique philosophy.

Squirrels, etc., also suffer from the falling sickness. Why? Because they surely participate in the same nature.

A stench also rouses the falling sickness, yet not just any: but only Sulphur, Mercury, and Salt have this power.

There is a fixed fire which does not burn unless it has fire. As long as the fire lasts, it is a Persian fire <note>Persian fire: traditionally used for shingles or anthrax, here used by Paracelsus to describe a specific kind of internal "burning" or inflammation</note>. Smoke from Saltpeter, Sulphur, and Mercury causes one to fall, shaking the brain with a flaming heat.

<margin>Fire is Mars—burning so long until it passes. Example: just as an Eclipse passes across the Sun, so Mars [passes] this fire in the manner of an Eclipse.</margin>

Its place is in many members of the body, nor can it be known everywhere: namely in the stomach, blood, veins, here, there, and everywhere, etc. But if it blazes up from the fire, then penetrating in every direction, it reaches the brain through certain channels and causes madness. The same likewise begins in the brain itself.

In the same way there leap in the tremor of the heart, the nightmare <note>original: "incubus, succubus", referring to sensations of pressure or terror during sleep</note>, and twitching: although the brain is not occupied by the generation of these, because it does not have enough vapors, and because of the smallness of the obstructions, it remains in its place.

When the generation is imminent, a paroxysm <term>Paroxysm: A sudden attack or violent expression of a disease, such as a seizure</term> arises. This is either equal or unequal. And these are true Astronomical subtleties, leading to the knowledge of those things. Whereby a sound Astronomer is one who does not consider the hypocrisy of the weather, but the conjunctions of diseases. And for this reason was the Astronomer created.

# MEDICAL FRAGMENTS.

-> Cordial Greetings from Theophrastus. <note>The Latin "S. P. D." (Salutem Plurimam Dicit) is a traditional formal greeting meaning "Sends many greetings."</note> <-

Is there anyone anywhere who can assert with truth that experience ends with himself? No one. Thus, truly, no one could say that experience was completed in the ancient authors. It is therefore fair that what has no end should be continually investigated further. Such is also the fate of Medicine, which has not yet reached its limits. For who would praise that foundation upon which predecessors have stood until now, when that which is highest in it has not yet been understood or indicated? I speak of properties. <note>In Paracelsian medicine, "properties" refers to the specific hidden virtues or "essences" of a substance that give it healing power.</note> For who would not believe me that, until now, mere rubbish has been sold in the apothecaries' shops? If we examine the matter to the quick, Hippocrates was certainly the most diligent and exquisite preparer. <margin>Hippocrates was the sharpest preparer.</margin> Avicenna, however, was opposed to him. For what, in the end, does he or his followers provide? And is it not worthy of laughter that so many physicians have bypassed Astronomy, when Medicine is of no consequence without it? I remain silent on the fact that they held no distinction of climates, or Cosmography, or Geography; nor did they distinguish the past time from the present or the future. And who would not judge these things to be absolutely necessary? And should a physician—I meant to say a Physician—terrify Theophrastus when he is neither a Cosmographer, nor a Geographer, nor an Astronomer, nor a Philosopher? That will certainly never happen. Nor can he be forced to praise those who lack the columns of Medicine. And how, I ask, will these men, with their one-eyed and limping gait, overtake Theophrastus? Or is it truly fair and decent that medicine be killed in the very process of preparation? And that the skilled be placed behind the unskilled because of favor, influence, and kinship? Truly, how awkward is that Prescription: *Take Turbith, senna, etc., let them be, etc., against gout,* if you compare it with this: *Take the Essence of Gold.* Or should dung, in which there are neither elements, nor secrets <term>Arcana: Paracelsus's term for the "hidden" or "celestial" curative powers within natural substances</term>, nor virtues or properties, be separated and held in high regard?

Therefore, all these things considered give me firm hope that the fathers and elders who wish to emerge as Physicians from the schools will not be so seriously cast down and trampled. Nor do I doubt that the use of the shops and these remedies or prescriptions suits them better than this art which is so subtle. For they have not advanced their learning any further; and as much of it as they have, they defend. But there is a need for a foundation far different from this one which those fathers defend. For their art is merely idle, which they now learn one after another with great study. There is very little experience in it; nor does their arrogance allow them to learn more exquisite things, etc.

---

### CHAPTER I.

Now, indeed, beyond their own experience, those men chatter about nothing. Why, then, should my own experience not be granted to me and be free? For what else is Medicine but experience? And this is as familiar to me as it is to them. And who can make the experience of another person certain? No one, indeed. Why then, you followers, do you lean upon them or upon me? Rather, let everyone lean upon his own art and experience. For the knowledge of any matter is through experience. Therefore, let everyone apply himself: my experience profits me, not you. But if I grant you something from my experience, then it is right that you also experience the same thing yourself; and thus you will become like me. Other things are lacking.

---

### -> Concerning the Womb. <-

To what end does the reading of ancient writers lead? You truly wish to cure all the diseases of women individually, and to produce milk, to stir or restrain the menses, to make them fertile, etc. Do this one thing: reduce the womb to its proper balance, strength, virtue, and temperament—that is, to its own being. If you do this, what else will be missing? Nothing: thus everything will be ready.

It is certainly true that there are restorations, provocations, relaxations, etc. But what are those to you? Many superstitions also spread. But to what end are all these? Do not do that. One God, one Medicine.

Who can observe all necessary things if we deal with the matter point by point? Not in this way—not by the ounce, but by the pound. <note>Paracelsus is arguing for looking at the "whole" essence of the cure rather than small, specific dosages of ineffective ingredients.</note> That is, seek one way, not many roundabout paths.

---

# PREFACE.

-> Of Doctor Theophrastus on gouty diseases and others related to these. <-

Through my many travels across the borders of Europe, I have learned and recognized that in this our century, gout <term>Podagra: A term for gout, specifically affecting the foot, but used here as a general term for metabolic joint pain</term> has become much more common than it was from the beginning of the world. This is gathered from the books themselves, which hand down very little concerning gout. Furthermore, that gout was infrequent is testified by the fact that the ancients did not labor much over curing it. For it usually happens that by more frequent visits and occurrences of a disease, more and readier remedies are found than for those that are not frequent, but rare. Finally, present-day gouts, if compared to the ancient ones, are no different than black is from white. For today's gouts exist as so difficult, stubborn, and rebellious, that the ancient ones compared to these are like child's play; they afflicted more slowly, did not stab as severely, ceased quickly, and were easily tamed by light remedies. All these things have now climbed to the highest degree, nor have they remained in their former place or manner, but today they have even invaded those members which in previous ages were least subjected to them.

<margin>The occasion on which Theophrastus broke away from the ancient physicians:</margin> But for this reason, it is also necessary that these same diseases be considered far more accurately by modern Physicians than was practiced by ancient Physicians. For it is otherwise known to us that all diseases begin gradually, and with time they subsequently become stronger and more increased. For just as an entire garden is sown from one seed, so also through human propagation, pains also subsequently become stronger and increase. And just as a growing tree is at first more compact, then is spread and expanded with branches that are subsequently wider and more numerous: so gout also is extended in the body, subsequently dilating itself more with its branches, and driving its roots deeper. For by seeding itself, it grows continually and is subsequently spread wider. I cannot remain silent here about my old opinion concerning gout, in which I so stubbornly agreed with the writings and traditions of the ancients that all their words were like the Gospel to me;

<note>original catchword: "fuerint" (were)</note>

# MEDICAL FRAGMENTS.

...there were those by whom I could never be persuaded that better things could be found anywhere. But at that time, I was unwise and did not realize that this entire opinion was built upon sand. However, after I had more diligently unrolled their writings, I learned through the process of time that no remedy is handed down in them which is sufficient for curing this disease. Therefore, I withdrew from their decrees and applied my mind to a more certain experience. When I had progressed so far in knowledge, I already knew that the degrees of medicines could altogether heal <term>podagra [gout]</term>, which the recipes of other Physicians could not. The necessity then fell upon me to find these degrees through <term>Alchemy [the art of refining and purifying substances]</term>. Truly, this taught me to remove and separate those things which would dull the degree and hold it as if bound. There, "like" was continually drawn out from "like," and experience itself taught me that gout is cured not by coldness, nor heat, nor moisture, nor dryness <note>Paracelsus is rejecting the traditional "humoral" theory which claimed diseases were caused by an imbalance of these four qualities.</note>, but by the <term>arcanum [the hidden, essential healing power]</term> of its virtue.

<margin>Magic is the discoverer of the cure and the causes.</margin>

Furthermore, <term>Magic [the study of nature's hidden forces]</term> itself—which is the teacher in the light of nature—teaches this arcanum and its virtues. Through this, I learned and recognized where the virtues lay hidden, and how the pure ought to be separated from the impure. Having found this, I then voluntarily said farewell to the books and trifles of the ancients, whose entire wisdom flowed from the Universities.

However, what I indicate here should be understood only regarding the discovery of the Medicine. Furthermore, the investigation of the causes likewise became known to me through Magic, in such a way that the stars and the four other Elements were understood, rather than the "complexions" <note>Original: "complexiones," referring to the four temperaments (sanguine, phlegmatic, etc.) of traditional medicine.</note>. For to contract the whole matter into one sum: gout arises solely from external essences. It descends from the external into its subjects. For it has sown and gathered itself into its subjects so that it subsequently propagates itself as a hereditary condition, as will be more clearly defined in its own chapters.

While I was everywhere inquiring into these things and seriously investigating them, as my experience advanced, I reached such a point of knowledge that, if both the sick man and the Physician accept this foundation of mine, both will perceive a happy outcome. But it pleases me further to recount something of my own status and perhaps my former lot. Whenever I undertook the cure of gout and had a great number of sick people ready, it happened that, being many times deceived by unskilled pharmacists, I was least able to experience the hoped-for operation in the medicines. For besides the fact that they quite clearly mixed in one thing for another <note>Original: "Quid pro Quo," a pharmaceutical term for substituting one drug for another, often used disparagingly here.</note> from time to time, they furthermore prepared the remedies or medications so filthily and wickedly that, unless God had turned away His singular hand, the sick could by no means have used them without harm. I remain silent on the fact that, with an added eulogy, they increased the price of the remedies so impudently that the matter lacked all moderation. Therefore, I made my desertion from them. In this way, <term>Empirics [unlicensed practitioners]</term>, Surgeons, Barbers, Alchemists, etc., then came to me of their own accord, all of them eagerly offering me every service of kindness and respect, so that they seemed not only to revere me as the most learned of all, but also moved me to no small joy by their arrival. Yet none of them—not even the most honest of them all—remained honorable for more than three months. Rather, they had all imbibed the poison of malice from the very beginning, seeking through their tricks to learn the art from me by deceit, and once it was perceived, they ungratefully drove out or expelled their teacher. For they had already persuaded my patients that they were willing to accept one part of the fee, while three parts were being paid to me, and yet they claimed they could complete the whole cure just as quickly. To this, not a few patients easily assented, having no regard for equity or honesty. After these, I subsequently also admitted several Doctors into my teaching. But just as red is brighter than black, so did these men prove to be worse than the others—flattering in front, biting behind. Thus, to bring the matter to a sum, I never found any colleague who did not mislead me along with the sick themselves. But they all flew away too early, before the virtue had yet been found; and thus they could not restrain their malice until the end. Therefore, they attained nothing of perfection, but only this: that they are able to deceive people.

However, I earnestly exhort all who profess their name among my disciples not to consider themselves perfect. For they have not reached the end of the discipline.

But so that the true principle and end of the art itself may be known, I have proposed to write this book as a testimony for my own people, as a genuine Physician, and against others, as deceivers and impostors. I have resolved to treat gout, both its causes and its cure, with a perfect and accurate discourse, so that from this the ignorance of the ancient writers might be open to anyone. For whatever the Universities profess, teach, or declaim about gout, it lacks all foundation and is directed and prepared only for the purpose of wiping away money <note>i.e., extorting money from the patient.</note>.

It is a just grief to me in all my writings that, from all the Universities of both Germany and Italy, no Physician or pharmacist has yet come forward who has found out in the least what Virtue is,

<margin>What Virtue is.</margin>

even though they have read about its principle in Hippocrates. The cause of this ignorance is that they simply do not understand the pure and the impure; what, therefore, can they know of the rest of the foundation? It would therefore have been much more convenient and honorable if they had introduced a local school (as they call it) in Deventer <note>A city in the Netherlands; Paracelsus implies a smaller, practical school would be better than a prestigious, useless Academy.</note>, rather than founding a University for the Faculty of Medicine. But however those things may be, something will eventually come forth and emerge, since the seed has once been sown for those who will devote my labor to the singular benefit of the sick. Next, therefore, follows the treatment of this book, distinguished into its parts and chapters. There are two treatises: one on Causes; the other on the Cure. The chapters of the first treatise will be those which are now handed down. So also the chapters of the second treatise.

# TREATISE I.

# MEDICAL FRAGMENTS.

For those people teach the composition of recipes, not us. Since, therefore, there is a need for those ancient things to be known, I will henceforth thoroughly shape my recipes according to their prescription, and I will similarly weigh and prove the medicines of other physicians according to their standard.

## The arrangement of the Books on Gout follows.

**BOOK ONE**, *on the common origin of all things.*
*Treats the prologue. The Person of the Disease.*
*The origin of the arts. The <term>Limbo [the primordial "great reservoir" of matter]</term>.*
*The <term>Mechanic [the force that shapes or manufactures disease]</term>.*

**BOOK TWO**, *treats the knowledge of composing recipes, and the nature of the disease through Anatomy, Chiromancy, and Physiognomy.*

*Prologue. The origin of diseases. The declaration of the disease.*
*The Mechanic. The Limbo.*

I. Those arts teach the origin of all diseases, they describe the birth and the process, and they are the contents of the first book, namely:
1. *Prologue, in which he treats errors and external characteristics.*
2. *The Origin, in which he treats the causes of the disease from a single source.*
3. *On the Limbo, where he treats how things are one.*
4. *Mechanics, where he treats how diseases are manufactured.*
5. *Signs of diseases, where the first knowledge of the disease is declared.*

II. Those arts teach how to recognize the disease, of what kind it is, and for that same kind recipes and a single concordance must be made <note>original: "F. Recepta," likely meaning "Fiat Recepta" or "Make the recipes."</note>.
1. *Prologue.*
2. *<term>Physiognomy [judging nature from outward appearance]</term>.*
3. *<term>Anatomy [here, the inner structure and "signatures" of a thing, not just dissection]</term>.*
4. *<term>Chiromancy [reading the "lines" or signs of the body, like palmistry]</term>.*
5. *Conclusion.*

III. Those teach the natures and mutations, and the return and departure toward one another, what can be cured and what cannot be cured.
1. *Prologue.*
2. *<term>Pyromancy [diagnosis through the element of fire and heat]</term>.*
3. *<term>Geomancy [diagnosis through the element of earth and minerals]</term>.*
4. *<term>Hydromancy [diagnosis through the element of water and fluids]</term>.*
5. *<term>Necromancy [here, the study of the "dead" or sidereal body, rather than conjuring spirits]</term>.*
6. *Conclusion.*

IV. The Cure
- 1. Of the Male.
- Therefore all *Anatomy, Astronomy, Hydromancy, Pyromancy, Chiromancy, Geomancy, Physiognomy, and Necromancy* are double things in the World. 
  - That is, they are twofold:
    - *Anatomy.*
    - *Pyromancy.*
    - *Chiromancy.*
    - *Physiognomy.*
- 2. Of the Female.

## Fragment on the Falling Sickness <note>original: "de Caduco," referring to epilepsy.</note>

It is more a suffering of the person themselves than a suffering of all the Elements. Why is that? Why does it happen to man in such a way? Because, unless divine grace protects our reason, whatever we do or apply will be of no use. When divine help is withdrawn, we all tremble and shake, and every effort of ours is accidental, lacking reason, sight, and hearing. Therefore, by looking into our misery, men should not swell with pride, but as if struck down, we ought to practice the humility of our hearts even in a state of health, and declare mutual mercy toward others with sincere affection. Since, therefore, the relief of our neighbor is placed in these things: the rationale of the physician’s duty seems to consist in two things, namely in help for the poor and in diligence. For the Physician can bestow nothing else upon the poor man but help, and that through the duty of charity. 

However, there are many ways of knowing and learning the doctrine of help. Some seize upon this by speculating and dreaming; others seek it by introducing examples; others hunt for it by investigating nature; others inquire by other modes; but all of these do so wrongly. The fundamental rationale for knowing help is placed outside of all those things. Therefore, students of Medicine labor in vain among them. Let them all consider with what empty results they continue to tread this path, and how few people such a study of theirs benefits. Rather, consider this: that the composition of help can be known or thoroughly investigated by no one. 

Let the whole hinge turn on this one thing: You see, surely, that God created iron for the sake of houses, not houses for the sake of iron; but so that by this, stones and wood might be fashioned. But who will investigate what that thing is in the iron which cuts? No one. Who will explain the cause of why iron cuts wood, but likewise does not cut Marble? No one, I think. So, in turn, no one shall know why Medicine performs this or that in this or that disease? Who will give the cause why an axe cuts wood, but not also stones? No one. So, similarly, these operations also lie hidden and concealed in nature. And since we must speak of Medicine, I would have you know that no other foundation is given in it than experience itself, through which the blacksmith and the carpenter know that such power issues from the iron, and that iron is suited to wood. For whatever the suitability of iron and wood is, that same thing is also the unity of Medicine and disease.

Furthermore (although no deeper Theory is required here), this must be known regarding those with the falling sickness: that God encloses all things within natural limits, and disposes the universe according to a natural course. Meanwhile, however, no one can assert that this disease exists naturally, or emerged from a natural cause. Nevertheless, while it happens and is presented naturally, it must be met with a natural remedy. For because God inflicts diseases not in one way, but by various paths, there are also various paths of medicine: which for that reason are proposed in many modes. Not, indeed, that we should establish a single Theory for all of them, and "play on one string" (as they say) by inquiring into the causes and origins of diseases; but that we should consider that the same path exists entirely within medicine as well. **[Text missing]**

<header>MEDICAL FRAGMENTS.</header>
<meta>catchword NOBILIS</meta>

### *Another Fragment on the Falling Sickness.*

Thus, with an entirely similar crash, this disease also attacks, no differently than thunder, lightning, and so on; like an earthquake, which prostrates everything near that place; or like the <term>Lorindus [a Paracelsian term for a meteorological spirit or phenomenon associated with water and storms]</term>, which cries out the mutation of its water; or like <term>Manna [here referring to an atmospheric excretion]</term>, which belongs to its own air, etc. Therefore, since man is like the world, and no less than it, he preserves the complete <term>idea [form or essence]</term> of the world itself: for this reason, he is also forced to endure a similar *Lorindus*, or earthquake, and lightning, and chaos. For the cause lies in this: that just as man is a <term>lesser world [microcosm]</term>, so he also contains all the things of the world within himself. Hence there are so many parts in man: from which the cause of possessed men is also drawn. For the Devil lives in the world: wherefore he also lives in man. And just as various and manifold worms exist and are born inside man, so they also exist outside in the world: and in both cases the reasoning and nature of their division is the same.

Therefore, since whatever is outside man is also inside man, and what is in man is also outside man, it must be known that the four aforementioned things—thunder, etc.—are counted as the part of fire; the earthquake for the part of earth; the *Lorindus* for the part of water; the <note>original: "thronum," likely referring to a specific Paracelsian atmospheric phenomenon or "throne"</note> throne for the part of air: and yet all are one <term>falling sickness [epilepsy]</term>, and are divided according to these species. It would please me to investigate this division or diversity. But I have very often exhorted Physicians to act as Philosophers and Astronomers, rather than showing themselves to be triflers or dreamers, so that they might be able to draw a more certain knowledge of diseases. For whatever those men have ever published about this disease is a mere lie. How serious, however, do you think it is to build a lie in medicine about some disease, through which those sick people are led astray and mocked? Yet that has been done not rarely until now. Open your eyes at last, and learn that the knowledge of Medicine is not so easy as you persuade yourselves. Meanwhile, those are rotten trifles which are trumpeted about regarding the <term>humors [the four bodily fluids of traditional Galenic medicine, which Paracelsus rejected]</term>, which bring nothing but the deception and neglect of both the sick and the diseases themselves.

->End of the Fourth Volume.<-

Paracelsus concludes with a sharp critique of traditional physicians who rely on the theory of humors rather than observing the "astronomy" of the human body.</summary>

<page-num>704</page-num>
<header>PREFACE.</header>

# THEOPHRASTUS BOMBAST
## OF HOHENHEIM, HERMIT,
### ->Doctor and Professor of both branches of Medicine<-
<note>The "both branches" refers to Physic (internal medicine) and Surgery, which were often treated as separate professions in the Renaissance.</note>
### ->To the Students of the Medical Art, Greetings.<-

*Since alone among all disciplines Medicine, as if some divine gift, is praised under the title of necessity by the testimony of both sacred and secular writers—and yet very few doctors today practice it successfully—it seemed right to recall it to the former praise of its authority. We shall purge it, which some have left in a state of barbarian filth, of its most serious errors. We are not bound to the precepts of the ancients, but only to those which we have discovered partly by the indication of the nature of the thing, and partly by our own struggle <note>original: "noſtro Marte", literally "by our own Mars," a classical idiom meaning by one's own effort or strength</note>, and have proven through long use and experience of things. For who does not know that most doctors in this age have failed most foully, even to the greatest peril of the sick? This is because they have adhered too anxiously to the sayings of Hippocrates, Galen, and Avicenna <note>Hippocrates and Galen were the ancient Greek foundations of medicine; Avicenna was the medieval Persian authority. Paracelsus famously burned their books in public.</note>, as if these had flowed like oracles from the tripod of Apollo <note>A reference to the Delphic Oracle of Apollo, implying the texts were treated as unquestionable divine truths</note>, from which it was not permitted to depart by a finger’s breadth. From these authors, indeed, the most splendid "doctors"—if it please the gods—are born, but not physicians.*

*It is not a title, nor eloquence, nor skill in languages, nor the reading of many books (although these are no small ornament) that is to be required in a physician, but the highest knowledge of things and mysteries, which alone easily takes the place of all others. It is indeed the duty of a Rhetorician to be able to speak eloquently and to persuade, and to draw the judge to his own opinion: but it is the duty of a Physician to have known the types of ailments, the causes, and the <term>symptoms</term> <note>original: "συμπτώματα" (symptomata). At this time, medical terminology was often still written in Greek characters within Latin texts.</note>, and to apply medicines to them with sagacity and industry, and to heal all according to each one’s nature and reason.*

*Furthermore, to depict my method of teaching in few words: Regarding myself, having been invited by a large salary from the lords of Basel, I publicly interpret for two hours daily books of both active and investigative Medicine, of Physics, and of Surgery—of which I myself am the author—with the greatest diligence and to the great benefit of my listeners. I do not, however, beg these from Hippocrates or Galen or anyone else, as others do, but have attained them through the highest doctrine of things, experience, and labor. Therefore, if I am to prove anything, experiments and reason support me in the place of authors.*

*Wherefore, excellent readers, if the mysteries of this Apolline art delight anyone, if love and desire take hold of him, and he wishes to learn thoroughly whatever belongs to this discipline in a very short space of time, let him betake himself immediately to us at BASEL; and he will find far other and greater things than I can describe in a few words. But so that our purpose may be more clearly known to students, it does not grieve us to add, by way of example, that in the system of complexions and humors <note>This refers to the "Four Humors" theory (blood, phlegm, yellow bile, black bile) which dominated medicine for 1,500 years; Paracelsus rejected this in favor of chemical principles.</note>, we by no means imitate the ancients, who surely attribute all illnesses falsely to them. Hence it happens that none, or certainly very few of the doctors today, have exactly known the diseases, causes, and critical days. Finally, let these things shown as if through a lattice suffice; I allow you to judge rashly of these things only after you have first heard THEOPHRASTUS. Farewell, and look with favor upon this our attempt to restore medicine. Given at Basel on the Nones of June, in the year 1527.*

->**PHILIP**<-

He outlines his plan to teach his own medical and surgical discoveries, focusing on the "mysteries" of nature rather than ancient humoral theory.</summary>

## PHILIP
# THEOPHRASTUS

## OF HOHENHEIM:

### OF THE SWABIANS
#### From the Assembly of Nobles

# ON METALLIC DISEASES,
## OR MINERAL DISEASES, AND OTHERS
## RELATED TO THESE.
# THREE BOOKS.

->By the supreme Philosopher and Physician, Philip Theo-<-
->phrastus of Hohenheim.<-

# CHAPTER I OF THE FIRST TREATISE.

<margin>A single theory for Asthma and the metallic affliction.</margin>
**A**s we are about to describe metallic diseases, it is necessary above all else to explain, at least in part, that old and long-known disease of the lung called **Asthma**, and what its origin might be. For from that same theory, the origin of the <term>metallic affliction</term> <note>original: "luis metallicae". While "lues" often means plague, in Paracelsus it refers to a chronic disease or "taint" specific to a substance.</note> will also be recognized. These two diseases do not differ in reality, except in their "Element" and location; otherwise, they occur by one and the same process. Now, Asthma is a disease of the lungs and similar parts subject to the same infection. Such also is the metallic affliction. Therefore, for this purpose, the first treatise of the first book contains a description of Asthma and the causes from which it arises, which is covered briefly as far as the subject necessarily requires. Afterward, in the second treatise, the generation of metallic disease is proposed. This knowledge is followed by the third treatise on the nature and essence of the external and internal body together—specifically, how this disease is produced. Finally, in the fourth treatise, the cure of the metallic affliction is handed down, in which all necessary parts are enumerated.

<margin>What is Asthma?</margin>
<margin>Who are liable to Asthma and the metallic affliction?</margin>
This mineral or metallic disease or affliction is that which is incurred by miners, smelters, and diggers, and those who are occupied in any way with metals, whether washing or smelting them—such as silver, gold, salts, alum, sulfur, vitriol, lead, copper, iron, and mercury. For whoever labors in these metals is seized by Asthma, by a wasting of the body <note>original: "tabe corporis", often referring to consumption or tuberculosis.</note>, and by an abscess of the stomach <note>original: "vomicâ stomachi"</note>; they are called <term>arosi</term> <note>original: "arosi". A term likely derived from "erosio" (erosion), describing those "eaten away" or corroded by metallic vapors.</note>, or those infected by the mineral affliction. Regarding these diseases, nothing at all is found in the writings of the ancients <note>Paracelsus famously rejected the authority of ancient Greek and Roman physicians like Galen, especially regarding diseases they never encountered, such as those in German mines.</note>. Hence, the cure for them has not been known until this day. Since a man cannot be the inventor of the generation of these diseases unless, relying on the <term>light of nature</term> <note>The "Light of Nature" (Lumen Naturae) is a central Paracelsian concept meaning the innate wisdom found through observing the natural world rather than reading old books.</note>, he examines their consideration a little more deeply, it will be our task to investigate their cause and origin in the four following treatises. By what name this disease truly ought to be called has not yet been declared or handed down by others before us from the foundations of nature. And although they may pretend that the nature and quality of this disease can be proven by reasons that are not obscure, yet all those reasons, when compared to true Philosophy, are found to be quite ridiculous. Therefore, you ought to know that its origin and generation are exactly as shall be handed down. For the generation of the metallic affliction testifies to the error committed by the ancients in their understanding of Asthma.

# CHAPTER II.
### On the Generation and Origin of Asthma.

<margin>The lung is contaminated by air alone.</margin>
You will recognize the proposed disease in this way: if you consider that **air** is that body from which the lung contracts its blemish. For the lung is contaminated by nothing else, in reality or in evil, except the corporeal air. For it is drawn in by the lung; and even if someone drinks, and harm is brought to the lung by that drink, that harm is not from the drink itself, but from the air contained within that drink. For that air is drawn in by the lung and is there consumed or "digested." 

<margin>Each Element has its own peculiar stomach.</margin>
For every Element has its own proper stomach in the body, and within that stomach, its native Element must be consumed. By this reasoning, the lung consumes the air. And just as the stomach digests its food, turning part of it into nourishment for the body and thrusting the remains out of the body, the same must be judged concerning the air: one part of it is digested and consumed, the other is excreted in the form of waste. For the logic and judgment regarding air and food are the same. Just as diseases can be inflicted by food, so can they no less be inflicted by the air. There is no need to bring the matter further, except to declare the **Chaos** properly and accurately, because only the Element is to be considered here, in this manner. It is known and explored 

<margin>What is Chaos</margin>
<margin>Air alone inflicts diseases on the lung.</margin>
by everyone that **Chaos** exists between heaven and earth, and that all diseases [of] the lung...

...pertains to the lung, producing its fever, abscess, <term>phthisis</term> <note>A historical term for pulmonary tuberculosis or any progressive wasting of the lungs.</note>, blockage, cough, and shortness of breath, along with similar outward appearances. For it is necessary that the human lung be nourished by that <term>Chaos</term> <note>In Paracelsian philosophy, "Chaos" refers to the atmosphere or the invisible medium between heaven and earth through which vital influences and "vapors" travel.</note>. Now indeed, this chaos is governed by the power of the stars.

<margin>The air is ruled by the stars.</margin>
Therefore, just as the stars dominate the air, so is the air itself disposed. And as the chaos is disposed, so it impresses its force upon the lung.

<margin>There are various differences in the air.</margin>
And this is now the foundation from which a Physician must recognize diseases of the lung: namely, that they are brought in by the force of the stars, just as another disease is inflicted by food. For those things that make a man sick are no fewer in species within the chaos than are counted among foods; nor are the "excrements" of the air—whether good or bad—any less significant than those of the foods themselves. And just as food can be defiled or adulterated, so too can the chaos be contaminated. Therefore, since it is taught by this example that the chaos—standing between heaven and earth—is no less a food for the lung than the fruits of the earth are food for the stomach, it must now be understood why similar fruits are produced above the earth for those who dwell between the earth and the sky: such a chaos also exists within the earth to nourish the lungs of those who live in the mountains or the mines.

<margin>How Asthmatic and metallic diseases differ.</margin>
And just as those who live above the earth are made asthmatic by their chaos, so likewise do those who are subjected to the subterranean chaos in the mountains become asthmatic. The difference in names, therefore, arises from the different elements: those who are affected while living above the earth are said to have **Asthmatic** diseases, and those who suffer while living below the earth are said to have **Metallic** diseases. Because of this difference, it is rightly and deservedly seen that two separate books should be written. For the upper heaven with its stars "cooks" the air that lies between it and the earth. In the same way, the minerals of the earth are also "heavens and stars," which govern their own chaos no less than the external heaven rules its own.

<margin>Arsenic destroys man.</margin>
And just as you see that Arsenic kills a man, in exactly the same way certain stars also kill him through the introduction of the chaos. We must discuss these stars further—specifically, how they impress diseases upon the lung, insofar as it is possible for the air to infect its own "stomach" <note>Paracelsus views the lung as a second stomach that "digests" air.</note>.

<margin>God's providence in preserving the human race.</margin>
<margin>Asthma is brought to the lung in three ways.</margin>
...a plague is prepared, which enters through the <term>rough artery</term> <note>original: "arteriam asperam," a historical term for the trachea or windpipe.</note>, and from there extends further into its own anatomy, just as a bird flies to its nest. And if God had not willed from the very beginning of the world for man to be preserved and to leave children behind him, who, I ask, would have remained safe and alive? Thus, it must also be held concerning Asthma that it is produced by the force of the stars through the "boiling over" of their properties, which adheres to the lung in three ways: first, like **Mercury** and sublimated smoke, which coagulates itself; second, like the **spirit of salt**, which passes from a dissolved state into coagulation; and third, like **Sulfur**, which is dashed and struck against the walls or sides by "reverberation" <note>The "Tria Prima" (Mercury, Sulfur, Salt) are Paracelsus’s three primary components of all matter. Here he uses them to describe different types of chemical deposits in the lungs.</note>.

<margin>The lung is turned into a barrel by Tartar.</margin>
The same thing happens here as in a new and clean wine barrel, which lacks any bodily or tangible crust until it is filled at harvest time. For if this barrel is emptied again after a year has passed and the wine is poured out, then these three species—Mercury, Sulfur, and Salt, which constitute **Tartar**—are found clinging to it everywhere. Therefore, just as something lies hidden in the wine that is not initially perceived to be there, so likewise there is a "body" in the chaos that clings to the lung just as it does to a vessel. It "bituminizes" <note>Becomes sticky or tar-like.</note> with its own viscosity like a mucilage, where finally coagulation—which is the matter of Asthma—follows.

### CHAPTER III.

<margin>The heaven changes the chaos.</margin>
<margin>Natural chaos</margin>
In order that you may understand the foundation and reason for all asthma as briefly as possible, know that the Heaven is the Element of Fire, and its elemental motion brings forth the chaos that we are describing here. For just as water boils from fire, so the chaos is that which is "cooked out" by the element of heaven. And just as boiling meat deposits its essence into the water, so the stars, like meat, pour their essence into the chaos. Furthermore, just as that broth of meat serves as nourishment for man, so the chaos of which we speak is nourishment for man. And just as the broth is digested in the stomach, having slipped down through its own passages, so too the chaos is digested in the lung, having slipped through its own throat. And just as things thrown into water confer either health or sickness upon a man by their property, so the stars, which are placed in the chaos, make men either healthy or sick like a broth. For this is the broth in which...

### CHAPTER IV.

<margin>On the union of Asthma and metallic disease.</margin>
Having mentioned these things, I am by no means about to describe the species of Asthma themselves; rather, what we have said so far serves to instruct us that, according to the manner of the heaven and the chaos, the same thing likewise happens within the earth. Even those who are instructed in the Philosophy of the earth will know how to provide an explanation of Asthma—that is, the origin and causes of metallic disease—while they explain the species and generation of Asthma. For in this way, one is often declared through the other. He who is affected with the knowledge of earthly disease will also have the same knowledge regarding the firmament. And conversely, he who truly and rightly describes the diseases of the firmament will also rightly explain earthly diseases. He who errs concerning earthly things will also hallucinate concerning heavenly ones.

<margin>What the duty of the Physician is.</margin>
For a Physician ought to be so skilled in the <term>light of nature</term> <note>A Paracelsian term for the innate wisdom found in the natural world, accessible through observation rather than just books.</note> that he knows not only the seven stars <note>The seven planets of classical astronomy.</note>, but all the stars that the heaven encompasses. If he knows these, he will not stop there, but will also inquire and track down the same things regarding the earth, just as he does for the other two elements in his Astronomy and Philosophy. Now, therefore, according to this rule, it must be known: that just as the chaos has its own generation, so the earth is the "heaven" of this generation.

<margin>Minerals of the earth are the firmament of heaven.</margin>
For the minerals that lie in the earth are the "firmament of heaven." From this Element of earth arises a fire that stirs up the chaos of the earth, similar to that which exists between heaven and earth. That chaos, moreover, passes into the "broth" of its own minerals, just as the external chaos is the broth of the stars. Therefore, those men who seek and build their dwellings under the earth must nourish their lungs from that chaos which exists within the earth. Now indeed, whatever is parboiled or boiled down in that chaos, its mineral impression is the **Tartar of the lungs**, which I call "metallic disease" here.

<margin>Tartar of the lungs.</margin>
Moreover, the method of generating both diseases is the process of one...

# SECOND TREATISE.
## On the Origin and Generation of the Metallic Disease.
### CHAPTER I.

<margin>One theory for Asthma and Metallic diseases.</margin>
**F**or the understanding of the second treatise, in which the cause and origin of metallic diseases will be discussed: first of all, there is a need for knowledge of those things which are proven by the evidence and testimony of the eyes themselves—namely, that they are the cause of coughing, gasping, and asthma, along with other related symptoms. For according to this knowledge, the <term>Theory</term> <note>In historical medicine, "theory" refers to the underlying rational principles of a disease's nature.</note> is drawn for both asthma and the metallic disease alike. For just as those things must be understood which clearly appear to generate asthma, so under the guidance of true Philosophy, similar things are also discovered in the "influence," as we taught in the first treatise. 
<margin>Mist is a cause of Asthma, etc.</margin> 
For you see that in the external chaos between heaven and earth, mists are generated in many ways, which provoke asthma, coughing, and gasping. Here our experience is to recognize and believe that the mist is the cause of these evils. Therefore, just as a mist arises from the firmament, a similar mist also occurs in the mountains, from which metallic diseases can be generated much more readily and powerfully than from the external chaos or its own mist. 
<margin>The mineral is the cause of the terrestrial mist, just as the Galaxy is the cause in the air. The disease is not curable.</margin> 
To those inquiring into the cause of this mist, it is clear that it is produced from the sphere of the <term>Galaxa</term> <note>Original: "Galaxae." Refers to the Milky Way or a specific celestial vapor that Paracelsus believed influenced the weather and health.</note>. This efficient cause is likewise present within the earth. Therefore, a <term>Mineral</term> <note>Original: "Minera." Referring to the ore or the spirit of the metal in the earth.</note> is now the cause of that mist; the knowledge of which grants the reason and science of its cure, just as the knowledge of fire provides the knowledge of that by which fire ought to be extinguished. For by this process, all diseases which are subject to cure must be recognized. Hence, death is "incurable" only because the "heaven" of its specific constellation has not yet been discovered. What we have said about mists should also be understood equally regarding rain, frost, and winter ice—that asthma is also produced from them. All these things must now be considered again within the mountains.

### CHAPTER II.

<margin>Various causes of Asthma:</margin>
**F**urthermore, asthma is also generated by cold and heat. Thus, a very hot lung, if it is suddenly quenched by cold, is cast into asthma. The same happens also from sour and sweet drinks. Therefore, just as a sudden chilling of the lung, or acidity and sweetness, bring forth asthma, it must also be understood regarding those working in the mountains: their lungs grow hot from their labors. If the coldness of the neighboring chaos follows this heat, then when the labor stops, the lung is struck by sudden cold. Even if that cold is hardly felt outwardly, it nevertheless dwells essentially in the earthiness of the mountains and goes into action, no differently than if it were entered into the body by drinking. 
<margin>The acidity of the earth.</margin> 
The same must likewise be judged regarding acidity. For as you know, the acidity or <term>stypticity</term> <note>A quality that shrinks or constricts body tissues.</note> of the wild plum is enclosed within its skin; so too the acidity of the mountains is constricted in the earth, covered by the surface. Men who build their dwellings in the mountains absorb and inhale this acidity. Moreover, one acidity comes from <term>vitriols</term> <note>Sulfate minerals, often corrosive or metallic in taste.</note>, another from alums, just as can be understood regarding wild and rustic plums. When, therefore, a conjunction of these things can occur—so that acidity and similar things in the chaos of the earth are drawn in by a greedy and hot lung—it is then entirely damaged. 
<margin>Various appetites of the lung.</margin> 
For as an appetite goads one person to eat chalk, another to drink vinegar, etc., so this diversity is also found in the lung. And through this appetite, the lung attracts now Alum, now Vitriol, now Saltpeter, etc. While the lung strives to satisfy this craving, it suffers nearly the same as a sick person whose desire turns toward the worse. By the same reasoning, acidity also stabs the lung with its sharpness, a condition which asthma can follow. 
<margin>The sweetness of the earth, etc.</margin> 
What we say of acids must likewise be judged for sweets. For sweetness is also enclosed in the mountains, just as it is restrained outwardly in <term>Ribes</term> <note>Currants or similar tart-sweet berries.</note>. Thus, when we walk in the mountains, it happens no differently than if we were eating that sweetness. For the things of the earth are "eaten" just as the sweetness in currants is, with this distinction: that the mountain sweetness is also taken in through the chaos. There, after the appetite has deceived the lung, the sweetness subsequently inflicts the metallic disease, the cause of which outcome is described more plainly elsewhere.

### CHAPTER III.

<margin>Fatness as a cause of hoarseness. Varieties of fatness.</margin>
**A**mong the external causes which inflict hoarseness, fatness is not the least. For when the lung delights itself in fatty things, it is forced to undergo damages that are well known. Moreover, there exist many types of fats which we eat—from oil, from meat, from fish—both visible and invisible. Hence it happens that multiple types of asthma are found, since one man is hoarse from this fat...

And just as the visible ones can bring certain harm: so too can the invisible ones. ## CHAPTER IV.

<margin>
Mercury of the chaos is the cause of darkness.
</margin>
**N**ow, just as the sole cause of these things is that sulfur lurks in the chaos, harming the lung for the stated reason: so similarly in the same chaos, Mercurial smoke is also mixed in, which gives the chaos its thickness and takes away its transparency. This smoke flies into a person no differently than a swift exhalation from ascending Mercurial <term>Arsenic</term> <note>In Paracelsian chemistry, arsenic is often considered a "species" of mercury or a closely related "smoke."</note>. For any vapor of this kind inflicts a notable and perpetual hoarseness. Such a vapor also lies in the chaos, besides which another is often generated in addition. For as sulfur lurks in the chaos of the world, to which a flash is also added, from which a double damage is recognized: so it must also be understood that in the earth there is one fixed Mercury, like Arsenic, which is perpetual; and another "incident" Mercury resulting from the daily constellation. For minerals are like stars in the firmament. Therefore, recognize which mineral occupies that region. That then is the "influence": as if <term>cachimia</term> <note>An immature or base metallic ore.</note> were present, then sulfur is generated from that cachimia. For just as we are accustomed to say that this region is situated under [the zodiac sign of] Virgo—or just as the astronomer knows which star hangs over anyone's head—so too the earthly philosopher considers and understands what inclines or gives the "constellation" in any mountain.

<margin>
Mercury is twofold.
</margin>
<margin>
Minerals are the stars of the earth.
</margin>
<margin>
The influence of the chaos is to be determined from the dominant mineral.
</margin>

<margin>
Various kinds and species of sulfur.
</margin>
For this earth bears its <term>marcasite</term> <note>A term for various metallic sulfides like pyrite.</note>, while that one bears antimony. And whatever that region contains, it gives to this chaos of which we have spoken. But just as the astronomer says, "this star gives the influence," so in turn the philosopher says, "in this earth the covering thrives." From this the influences arise. Instructed by this knowledge, the Physician says: "this metallic disease is a Resin, born from the chaos, in which the star and mineral of the covering have been concocted." From these things it is clear that it is entirely necessary that all species of minerals be properly known according to their properties. For there is sulfur of marcasites, white and red; of <term>talc</term>, yellow, red, and black; of cachimia, purple and black; there is sulfur of <term>Ochre</term>; sulfur of <term>Cinnabar</term>; sulfur of <term>Bismuth</term>; sulfur of Marcasite; sulfur of Marble; sulfur of <term>Duelech</term> <note>A Paracelsian term for a calculus or stone formed in the body.</note>; sulfur of Amethyst; and many other similar ones, which cannot all be listed here. But just as you have now heard about the kinds of sulfur, so you also have the mercury of copper, of lead, of zinc, of arsenic, and the like. Finally, the same logic applies to salt as to sulfur and mercury. For there is salt of vitriol, of alum, of <term>ental</term> <note>Likely related to dentalium or sea-shells used in medicine.</note>, of saltpeter, of common salt, of rock salt, and many others. This Salt, Sulfur, and Mercury are the spirits which constitute the chaos itself, disposed and affected according to the nature of the region.

<margin>
Kinds of mercury.

Kinds of salt.

## CHAPTER V.

<margin>
Mercury gives soot; Sulfur gives resin; Salt gives tartar.
</margin>
**N**ote therefore regarding this spirit, that Mercury gives soot. For just as sublimation <note>The process of heating a substance to turn it into vapor that then deposits as a solid.</note> exhibits the "ultimate matter," so also does this spirit. Therefore its disease is dry and arid. But the spirit of sulfur gives its resin, while the spirit of salt produces its <term>tartar</term> <note>Stony or calcified deposits in the body, which Paracelsus believed caused many diseases.</note>. And these are the three highest genera of metallic diseases. Furthermore, although "marcasite" may be the only name used, just like "cachimia," nonetheless their kind should not be understood as only one. For the variation of the earth also changes those minerals themselves, just as you see regions change according to their forms. And although sometimes a certain herb, such as an onion, has only one name, nevertheless, as often as there is a new region, its form is new, and yet it is still an onion. If therefore in this place the form is different and varies, it must also be known concerning that other property: that the same thing in Nature is changed in one way or another by the earthly power, namely into the property of a certain part of that region of the earth. Whence it happens that the medicine of such earth is safer and more useful than a foreign or strange one. For as much must be attributed to minerals as is attributed to the sky which governs the stars. For heaven and earth are two similar heavens: and the Mineral and the Star are good, similar stars. He who is skilled in one also understands the other. Therefore the Physician takes his beginning from Astronomy and defines it in Philosophy. For Astronomy teaches him about the constellation of the firmament and the mineral, while Philosophy bestows the property upon him: both of which are concluded through the cure. Because man is the Microcosm, he must therefore be led into the knowledge of external things: such as new moons,

The Physician begins from astronomy and finishes in philosophy.

<margin>Moonwort follows the course of the Moon.</margin>
One should seek out exaltations <note>In alchemy and astrology, "exaltation" refers to a state of heightened power or refinement.</note> and similar qualities not only in the planets, but also in the "terrestrial star." For if the **Moonwort** <note>original: *Lunaria*; a plant believed to be influenced by the moon, often used in alchemical experiments.</note> displays itself according to the course of the moon, this is certainly proof that many such "moons" exist on earth: just as other known things exist in which the celestial course is clearly noted and observed by a manifest example.

Let us now conclude this treatise, having taught how metallic diseases are generated from those three minerals—that is, from their spirits, which hide in the <term>chaos</term> <note>The vaporous or atmospheric medium surrounding minerals.</note> and emerge from the mines like a voice coming out of a mouth.

# THIRD TREATISE
### On the signs and the Nature of the external and internal body joined together, and how disease is produced.

### CHAPTER I.

<margin>
Oppositions in all natural things. The Crocodile kills a man with its breath. The fragility of man.
</margin>
<margin>
The Devil of men.
</margin>
<margin>
Poisons are the enemies of bodies.
</margin>
<margin>
The utility of Vulcan. Alchemy is the death of things.
</margin>
<margin>
Evil is mixed with good everywhere.
</margin>

**I**n this treatise, we must propose and discuss the operation of this disease: how it is birthed or made. And since man is entirely established in a fragility of life, such that he can be killed and destroyed by many things—which, if he be ignorant of them, he cannot avoid—it is necessary that these things be thoroughly recounted. This must be done by the Physician alone, for this is his specific duty. For he was created by God for this purpose: to recognize lethal power and to declare how it opposes Nature, and how one thing continually fights with another, just as animals on earth encounter and battle one another. Nor is there any less opposition and hostility among insensate things. For by the same logic that a Crocodile destroys and strangles a man with its breath, so too do the metallic fumes of those minerals kill us. But since God created both good and evil, which cannot exist together and yet are found within the same thing, a mandate was given to the Physician to reveal to fragile and mortal man his enemy, who lies in wait for his life and health, so that man may guard himself in time. For just as the doctrine proceeds from God through which we recognize the Devil—the most bitter enemy of souls—namely through the Prophets and Apostles; so too through the "light of nature" has God revealed the enemy of the body. He has taught what is poison, what is malignant, and what is healthy for man, so that he may prolong his life for many years. Therefore, lest the poison which is mixed with the useful should cut short the life of man, God gave the Physician the power and faculty to understand both the good and the evil in a single thing. To the Physician, God also added **Vulcan** <note>In Paracelsian terms, "Vulcan" refers to the art of fire or alchemy, used to refine and separate substances.</note>, by whose help and industry the evil might be separated from the good. The art of Vulcan is similar to death, by which the eternal and the mortal are separated from each other. For this reason, that art should rightly be called the "death of things." For whatever is useless is separated from that which is good. We must rightly and necessarily teach these things: since without this fear of enemies, we could neither eat, nor drink, nor breathe the air in or out, nor act securely in summer or winter. Instead, we would bring forth poisons from our very gardens alongside our food. Furthermore, for the conveniences of human life, we cannot do without gold, silver, iron, tin, copper, lead, mercury, and other metals. And yet, when we handle these, we handle the very enemies of our life and health. Thus, nothing is so fit or suitable for our use that it does not also carry our enemy within its bosom. Since so much importance is placed on the knowledge of natural things—which man cannot know of himself, but for which purpose the Physician was established by God—it is entirely fitting that the Physician knows how to bring forth the good from the secrets of the light of Nature, to separate the evil gathered with the good, and to apply the useful for the benefit of the body. And just as the Devil is driven out of a man, so the Physician must expel diseases through tested medicines; he must drive out evil with evil, and retain good with good.

<margin>
The excellence and authority of the Physician.
</margin>

### CHAPTER II.

<margin>
Both Medicine and poison are in the Three First Principles.
</margin>
<margin>
The Rose refreshes, yet causes fainting.
</margin>
<margin>
The spirits of metals cause longer diseases than their solid bodies.
</margin>
<margin>
Realgar dries out the lungs.
</margin>

**T**herefore, the conclusion stands: for the knowledge of metallic diseases, it is absolutely required to explain those things from which they are produced, as was previously understood. Just as in these three—**Mercury, Sulfur, and Salt** <note>The *tria prima*, or three primary chemical principles in Paracelsian thought.</note>—medicine is offered to us, so in the same things poisons are also present. Both exist in one thing. Through the "death" of the substance, we find that which is useful to us; that very thing was previously with the part that inflicted evil upon us. Let us take an example. A miner seeks silver until he finds it. Once he has it, he holds the metal. While he seeks and handles the ore, he falls into disease. Now, being afflicted by the disease, if he separates the metal he dug up from the silver, he finds in that which is discarded the very thing that made him sick. But in that same separation, he also finds that which can heal him. It should be known, therefore, that the "soot" <note>The byproduct or residue of smelting.</note> which leaves the ore has the power of poison within it, which is separated from the silver during smelting. For if a rose can refresh us with its scent while simultaneously causing us to faint—while the body of the rose itself remains unharmed—a completely similar power can exhale from the aforementioned things and be cast into a man. And although the solid body of that poison does not enter him, its exhaling power and malice inflicts a similar sickness. Thus, diseases endure in a man for a long time which would have been shorter if the solid body itself were present or had entered him. For example: from the ingestion of **arsenic**, a swift and violent death looms. But if the body of it is not ingested, and only the spirit <note>The vapor or gas.</note> is inhaled, then the disease is prolonged from an hour into a year. What the solid body completes in ten hours, the spirit executes in ten years. And yet, from the spirit, such a violent and cruel death does not attack as that which attacks from the ingested body. Here it must also be noted that he who wishes to have certain knowledge of metallic diseases must know the swift disease and death of the solid body, along with all its signs and properties. From those signs, when rightly estimated, one can judge the disease: what species it is, or from which metallic body that spirit emerged. The understanding of signs is taught by such an example: the ingestion of **Realgar** <note>A toxic arsenic sulfide mineral.</note> makes the lungs dry; from this drying out follows a change of the spirit...

It explains how the vapors or "spirits" of metals like arsenic (Realgar) cause slow, chronic diseases compared to the rapid death caused by ingesting the solid material.</summary>

<header>ON METALLIC DISEASES</header>

<margin>Signs of ingested Realgar.</margin>
The symptoms include a struggle for breath and difficulty in breathing, a discoloration of the face, and fissures or cracks in the liver. There is an immoderate thirst and an erosion of the stomach linings, such that they peel away like bark from a branch. Furthermore, there is a compression of the midriff, difficult and heavy digestion, immoderate heat, palpitation of the heart, and tremors in all the limbs. Finally, <term>prunella</term> <note>A historical term for a severe inflammation of the mouth and throat, often accompanied by a brownish coating on the tongue.</note> and its accompanying "frenzy" appear. Just as the diseases of this poison show themselves suddenly when the substance is taken into the body, so too can the "spirit" of <term>Realgar</term> <note>Red arsenic sulfide.</note> persist for many days and years with these same signs and illnesses, eventually followed by these same symptoms. Miners infected in this way are thrown into all manner of "celestial" diseases <note>Diseases influenced by external or atmospheric conditions.</note> by any slight occasion or change in the weather, such as fevers, wasting of the body, manias, and <term>prunella</term>.

<margin>Infected miners easily incur other diseases.</margin>

## CHAPTER III.

<margin>Realgar encompasses arsenicals and all "coverings."</margin>
Since we have already spoken of the operation of the poison—that is, which diseases are induced by it—it now seems appropriate to add the signs taken from the bodies themselves, as mentioned before. The number of these is so great that they cannot all be recounted individually due to their multitude. In this category, I would like it to be understood that under the name **Realgar**, all <term>arsenicals</term> and all <term>orpiments</term> <note>original: *operimentituma*; yellow arsenic sulfide, often called "auripigmentum."</note> are included and understood. Whoever has the age and leisure to test every species in bodily infections through long practice will know how to distinguish and divide these "spirits" more certainly. Although the treatment is concluded under the heading of **Realgar**, it is because the <term>Arcana</term> <note>The secret, essential healing virtues of a substance.</note> are proposed there. If the cure were to be established more specifically, it would be appropriate to define and explain everything by its species, as the <term>Humorists</term> <note>Followers of the traditional medical theory of the Four Humors (blood, phlegm, yellow bile, black bile).</note> are accustomed to doing. Just as various species of **Realgar** are understood, so under **Antimony** are included all <term>Marcasites</term>, <term>Cachimias</term>, <term>Talcs</term>, <term>Ochres</term> <note>original: *Ogerta*.</note>, and other similar things. Thus, if the poison of **Antimony** is taken in, a harsh and dry cough arises, along with piercing pains in the sides, headaches, constipation or dryness of the bowels, abscesses of the spleen, burning of the blood, <term>scabies</term> <note>General term for itchy or crusty skin eruptions.</note> and foulness of the dried skin, and yellow jaundice. Where these signs appear, they indicate that the spirit of **Antimony** has slipped in from the aforementioned minerals.

<margin>What Antimony encompasses. Signs of ingested Antimony.</margin>

<margin>What Alkali encompasses.</margin>
Furthermore, it should also be known that under the name of **Alkali**, many minerals transmit their spirits into man in the form of poison. Yet the category is completed under the name of **Alkali**, whose death-bringing force reveals itself through difficult breathing, foul breath, excessive spitting, intense heat and appetite, diarrhea, frequent colic and twisting of the belly, drying out of the lungs and stomach, cracking of the liver and spleen, melting of the kidneys, acrid urine, and erosion of the kidney region, with the expulsion of impurities, blood, and waste. For whatever other diseases cling to the members of the body, these it brings forth and makes manifest. To **Alkali** are referred the species of blue and white <term>vitriol</term> <note>Sulfate minerals.</note>, as well as three species of <term>alum</term>—rock, split, and feathery—and species of salt: common, gem, flint, and whatever others are related to these. From the recorded signs, the distinctions of the minerals must be judged, and one must see which it is. For **Realgar** proceeds from gold, silver, iron, copper, tin, etc.; and so does **Antimony** from gold, silver, iron, etc.

<margin>Signs of ingested mineral Alkali.</margin>

<margin>Minerals of different regions.</margin>
Likewise, **Alkali** follows that same distinction. This must be properly recognized in their physical forms for the sake of the cure.

To this end, the nature of the region also contributes, according to which different things are produced from time to time. In these simple substances, the eyes themselves reveal a great diversity. For the Hungarian and Styrian regions yield results differently according to their own signs, and yet they are ultimately enclosed by similar metals. So too the "glasses" <note>Probably referring to vitriols or glassy mineral ores.</note> of the mountain-dwellers of **Etschland** and **Innsbruck** are different when compared with the mines of **Meissen**. The same must be judged similarly for the rest. They even differ in other places closer than those we have named, such as **Rautriss**, **Gastein**, **Linzgau**, and **Kanggau**. Indeed, they often differ even in two mine shafts very close to each other. All these things must be sought from experience itself, without which no knowledge of such diseases can be grasped. It is especially useful that all bodies, as they are found in their specific forms, be looked into and known by their actual effects: namely, by what means they exert their poison and malice. For **Marcasitic sulfur** drives away sleep; on the contrary, **Vitriolated sulfur** instills a sleep even unto death. In the same way, salts are contrary to one another, as are **Mercurials**; all of which I entrust to the experience of each person.

<margin>Hungary. Styria. Etschland. Innsbruck. Rautriss. Gastein. Linzgau. Kanggau.</margin>

<margin>Marcasite sulfur takes away sleep; vitriolated sulfur increases it.</margin>

## CHAPTER IV.

<margin>General arcana, not special, and specifically from those things that birthed the disease.</margin>
Although there are many enemies—indeed, their number can hardly be known by a physician—it is not necessary to weigh them all. For he who would follow these things one by one would introduce too many errors into practice. For practice is such that it arises from the secret power (<term>Arcanum</term>) that is contrary to diseases. Now, understand the <term>Arcanum</term> in this way: You know that many arsenical things and the like proceed from gold. He who wishes to compare every species with its disease in medicine departs from the <term>Arcanum</term>, inclines toward error, and walks a difficult path. But he who sets before himself "good against evil" tends toward the <term>Arcanum</term>. For the "good" cures the "evil" that was once joined with it. For example: that which causes the disease of jaundice, that very same thing cures the disease of jaundice, namely because in that thing there is both good and evil. From the evil, jaundice arises. But if the "good" is separated from that very "evil," it will be the <term>Arcanum</term> against jaundice. It receives the name <term>Arcanum</term> because various plagues arise from that evil. He who wants to consider every jaundice separately does not know what an <term>Arcanum</term> is. For the <term>Arcanum</term> cures all those species. If a physician wants to seek a particular diet and medicine for every specific disease, that search will be too long for the patient. From this order of cure arises **Laudanum** <note>In Paracelsian medicine, this refers to a "most praiseworthy" remedy (from Latin *laudare*, to praise), usually a highly refined mineral essence, rather than the opium tincture of later centuries.</note>—that is, a "perfected matter"—which is just as if a pearl were extracted, and that pearl cured the disease born from its own "evil." For the medicine that must cure paralysis must flow from the very same thing that birthed the paralysis. Thus one proceeds according to the <term>Arcanum</term>, and the consideration of the many species of that disease is removed. Thus also are understood the <term>Arcana</term> of minerals: namely, that gold itself is the medicine for all those diseases which its diggers contract.

<margin>What an Arcanum is.</margin>

<margin>Medicine and disease from the same source.</margin>

<margin>Gold is a general secret remedy.</margin>
Thus <term>Saturn</term> <note>The alchemical name for lead.</note> also possesses within itself its own <term>arcanum</term> <note>A "secret" or essential healing principle within a substance.</note> against diseases arising from lead, and so it follows for the others, so that we may always have a medicine at hand <margin>Incurable diseases.</margin> against the diseases of the things we handle.
