### CHAPTER II.

<margin>Others say 365. How many days and parts in a year.</margin>
<margin>The year is twofold: the year of minerals.</margin>
<margin>The year of minerals lasts for only one year.</margin>
<margin>A beautiful speculation.</margin>
<margin>Surface things belong only to the ground.</margin>
<margin>The seeds of metals are not implanted by themselves.</margin>
**I**t is known to you that the year is divided into 364 days along with the minutes attached to them, and that it is half summer and half winter. In this form, one year follows another until the end of the world, so that summer and winter always and continually succeed one another. For thus the world was created, and this is its order; and this is the world that man sees. Now, however, within the earth itself there is another world, having its own <term>constellations: the inner astrological forces that govern the growth of minerals</term>, its own dwellings, and its household, so that it is a peculiar world unto itself, of which you know. You should know, however, that in that world of the earth there is only one year, which began on the first day of creation and still lasts today. From this it follows that, according to this "year," the things that are in the earth grow (for whatever is born on the surface of the earth does not belong beneath the earth). Understand it this way: the seed of metals was scattered into the earth—not the metals themselves—and these manifest at the time of their harvest and vintage, one after another, early or late, according to the oridnance of divine providence. Just as we have violets now, then thyme, then roses, cherries, pears, nuts, grapes, and so on, until the year is finished; yet all are born in the same year, even if one comes forth later than another. So it happens here also: now gold "flowers" in one region, in another silver, in another iron, in another lead. This one has passed, that one is present, another is yet to come; that is, the Spring of this one is finished, the Summer of another, the May of another, the July of another. For those who lived at the beginning of the world obtained their gold and silver with the violets of Spring; those who lived after them obtained silver and gold with the clover and spearwort <note>original: "flammula"</note>, and so on, from the first to the last, the time of this "year" is distributed. Thus, whatever has fallen is not born again; it is finished, for no year repeats itself within the earth. And just as plenty of apples, grass, grain, etc., grow upon the earth, so also man is provided for with metals. Yet with this difference: that this metal was born in the time of violets, another in the time of the cornflower, a third in the time of cherries, pears, grain, grapes, etc. This is according to the time of this earthly year, whose months, in a long sequence, encompass many thousands of years.

### CHAPTER III.

<margin>The nature of summer and winter in the earth's year.</margin>
<margin>Summer stars and winter stars.</margin>
<margin>The Sun chiefly creates summer.</margin>
**S**ince, therefore, there is only one year in the world of the earth, the distribution of which is as previously stated, it is necessary that this year also has its own summer and its own winter. Summer upon the earth is perceptible heat, and similarly winter is perceptible cold; yet both of these cannot be touched, but are part of the <term>chaos: the atmospheric air or "middle space" between heaven and earth</term>. In the world of the earth, however, both exist palpably and essentially—neither hot nor cold—but like the Sun and Moon, and that in a hidden manner. Note, therefore, the explanation of external summer and winter, which are as follows: In the heavens is a multitude of stars that produce summer, among which the Sun is the prince; yet the Sun by himself and alone produces no summer, but only when joined with his multitude. Likewise, winter is composed of its own army of stars, which have their exaltation after the dominion of the summer stars. Therefore, summer is a collection of stars, as is winter, so ordered that they follow one another. Now, note in turn: the summer of the earth is a heap of minerals that have a summer-like nature within them. Similarly, there is a pile of ores that have the nature of winter. Thus, in the mines there is winter and summer, not according to days, months, and seasons, but just as they are placed next to each other—like a mountain bearing snow and a valley having flowering gardens. So here, summer and winter are placed side by side, as is evident in their ripening.
<margin>Winter and summer exist together in the mines.</margin>
For if by chance they were opened at the time of their creation, then the summer in its nature would be found to be similar to the external summer, and the winter in its nature similar to the external winter, so that their properties, qualities, and natures would agree. From this agreement, the philosophy of Physics and Astronomy arises and follows.

### CHAPTER IV.

<margin>Mercury is the Moon and the mineral winter of the earth.</margin>
<margin>What the genuine name for quicksilver is.</margin>
<margin>Mercury is called Mercury because it is as versatile as the planet Mercury. Quicksilver is the Moon. Lead is Mercury. Silver is Saturn.</margin>
**A**nd so there is a year in the earth, and summer and winter are distinct, lying hidden in their bodies and not manifesting as they do in the external world, where they were created so that their force and nature might proceed from them. In the earthly world, however, summer and winter remain locked away, emitting nothing perceptible, neither heat nor cold. Those forces of cold or heat that proceed from them remain hidden, but other properties break forth. Just as you see in the Moon, which emits a hidden nature that can weaken a person, besides the fact that it rules over cold along with its stars. So it also happens in this winter of the earth, which is indeed nothing other than <term>Mercury: quicksilver</term> itself, which in all its properties is the "Moon of the earth," with all necessary qualities. In this are situated winter, the winter stars, the winter ores, and everything belonging here. It is right, therefore, to treat this nature of quicksilver, so that you may know what its force and power are, which certainly could not be sufficiently understood from what came before. The name is indeed commonly used, so that quicksilver is called "Mercury," as it falls under the planet Mercury, just as gold falls under the Sun. But this name was not imposed upon it according to its nature; it is a foolish and false philosophical arrangement. For quicksilver, according to its nature, ought rather to be called "Moon," "Winter," "Snow," "Cold," or "Ice." And yet, because it is not solidified <note>original: "coagulatum"</note> but is an open metal and the <term>first matter: the fundamental substance from which all other things are made</term> of all metals, let its name remain. But in this place, let it be understood as the Moon and as winter. Silver, however, ought to be called Saturn; and lead ought to be called Mercury. The stars themselves and the nature of these things prove this naming and distribution, as experience testifies—their own properties, essence, and quality—without which it is not permitted to work or speak at all.

### CHAPTER V.

<margin>What quicksilver is.</margin>
**S**ince we have therefore indicated regarding quicksilver what it is—namely, the Planet of the earth, and the Moon, etc., as the Astronomy of the earth also demonstrates—know therefore that man is subject to this Planet, just as you know that the Moon has power over man, and how winter and the winter stars that make winter affect a person when they are exalted. For in this way, it is also to be understood concerning the lower planets, namely those of the earth, that similarly in...

<header>BOOK III.</header>

<margin>Mercury (quicksilver) operates in us like the moon of the sky; we cannot flee the latter, but we can avoid the former.</margin>
<margin>The difference between the moon of the sky and the moon of the earth.</margin>
...thrice in their own regions they imprint their power and influence, but not in humans. For they <note>Referring to other metals like lead or iron</note> are compact, coagulated, frozen, and hardened. Therefore, the impressions that lie hidden within them cannot emerge, and in this way, man is safe from their influence. However, because <term>Mercury (quicksilver)</term>—which is the "moon of the earth"—is open and not compact or hardened, lunar influences proceed from it just as they do from the moon in the sky, except that the coldness is not felt by the senses. Since, therefore, Mercury exerts its influence upon man just like the upper moon, observe (as has been said) the nature and property of the upper moon and what it is. Truly, we endure the moon of the sky in a certain measure and manner, neither more nor less, according to its course and property. Such also is the moon of the earth <note>Paracelsus refers to Mercury as the terrestrial counterpart to the celestial Moon</note>, but we can either do without this one entirely, or have it in abundance or in small amounts. Thus, according to how much of it is present near us, its influence is to be expected. This, then, is the reason why we write about those who are harmed by the "moon of the earth" while they live near it, work with it, dwell around it, or touch it—things which cannot happen with the upper moon. We must, therefore, speak of "lunar diseases" as far as I have discovered through experience. For if it were possible for a man to live on the celestial moon, to touch it and handle it as we do the earthly moon, similar diseases would be found on the upper moon as are found in Mercury.

## TREATISE III.
### How two contraries, Mercury and man, can exist together.

### I.

<margin>Man is a microcosm; therefore, he is subject and liable to the entire nature of things.</margin>
<margin>Man was made from the <term>limbus: the primordial "clay" or chaotic matter from which the universe was fashioned</term>.</margin>
<margin>The limbus dominates continually within man.</margin>
**I**n order to satisfy our purpose, it is necessary to know the opposition between Mercury and man—why these two are mutually repugnant to each other, and yet man can neither harm nor destroy either the Moon or Mercury. For those things always remain unharmed in their essence by man. Man, therefore, is the cause of this interaction because he was made from the <term>limbus</term>, and this primordial matter encompassed all elements and their essences. If the limbus was such, and man was made from it, it follows that the limbus is man’s parent; consequently, the son is compelled to fear the father, and the father has command over the son. From this it happens that we can be suffocated or infected by the stars and the elements, falling into their nature and essence. For just as a son cannot say, "My blood is not from my father and mother," neither can we say that we can live without the elements. And just as a son is born of father and mother and retains whatever he received during generation until death, so we must recognize that we are from our father, the *limbus*, who indeed reigns in us without end, just as in an embryo in the mother’s womb. For we humans, however grown we are, are all still always in the <term>matrix: the "womb" of the natural world</term>, and whatever is placed in the womb is forced to sustain itself from that which the womb supplies. Thus all the elements surround us, and we walk and live in the midst of them, like young chicks in an eggshell. We are no less tender and soft, so that all the "blows" penetrate us and take effect—which blows are of the planets and the *limbus*, which is the seed. The sky and the earth are the womb, yet both are one thing. Man is the smallest part, and yet he is all these things.

## CHAPTER II.

<margin>Opposition is not by reason of the element itself, but a property within that same element.</margin>
<margin>Opposites do not endure each other at the same time.</margin>
<margin>How lightning, etc., is made.</margin>
<margin>How sulfur and saltpeter are contraries.</margin>
**H**ere it must also be known that two contrary elements cannot stand together without mutual injury. For summer must yield to winter. Now, however, nature is so established that it does not contain contraries within itself; that is, opposites do not harmonize in the course of nature, but like with like. For greenness does not harm a cold herb, nor does yellowness or redness harm a hot one. Every element, without regard for the others, remains in its own essence and state without opposition. Therefore, it is not true what is said—that thunder, lightning, snow, etc., come from contrary things. For the thunderbolt, the flash, and that fire descend from the virtue of their own element and from their own proper nature, not from opposition. Look at gunpowder: sulfur and <term>saltpeter</term> are of one and the same element <note>In Paracelsian chemistry, they are both considered "earthly" or "mineral" in nature</note>, and yet there is an opposition in them. This opposition is a property of nature which is thought to be a contrariety—not of the element itself, but of "liquidity." For the "liquor" of sulfur and the "liquor" of saltpeter cannot be as one, solely by reason of their liquidity and not because of their element. This is also how it is in the generation of a thunderbolt. Just as a man and a woman both have a warm temperament—they are of the same nature, property, and quality regarding blood, flesh, bones, etc.—the reason they cannot be as one or be combined, but rather flee from each other <note>Likely referring to the physical separation of the sexes or specific biological tensions in Paracelsian theory</note>, is not the nature of the element, but a nature behaving like a liquidity, which is placed in form and application. This "application" is that contrary which must be considered. From such application, the planets also become malevolent and contrary, and similar things, which I commend to other books, etc.

## CHAPTER III.

<margin>The conjunction of man and Mercury is a disease.</margin>
<margin>A woman is no colder than a man.</margin>
<margin>The <term>tincture: a subtle, transforming spiritual or physical quality</term> causes the elements to infect man.</margin>
**H**ow two contraries cannot exist in their element without mutual destruction, note this. Man is of a hot nature, in which quality one human is like another, both male and female. The claim that "this one is cold" and "that one is hot" is erroneous and false. A woman also has the heat of a man, nor is she found to be colder. Since, therefore, man is of a hot nature, while the Moon <note>Mercury</note> is cold, then those two are contraries. But why should man care about the cold of the Moon? Not at all, because they are not joined and coupled into the same thing. Therefore, they cannot destroy each other. The injury in this case is that a certain "tincture" occurs here; it is not that the element itself is present, but it operates in man through a tincture—just as if someone [put] poison into water...

### CHAPTER IV.

<margin>
Mercury behaves like winter in man.
</margin>
Since therefore living Mercury is winter itself, it also behaves like winter. Winter does not expel heat from the human body, but makes it difficult for it, and repels it so that it is unwilling to bear it. When, therefore, someone perishes from cold, the cause is not that heat has left them. For it still hides in their center and gathers into one compaction. Death comes from this: that the heat has too much inflamed the heart. For when the heat yields and gives place and entry to the cold, the heart is strangled, and thus two different elements, hot and cold, are mixed and become one, just as if wine and water were confounded. But just as oil and water are separate, so also cold is present. This is also how it is with the <term>earthly Moon</term> <note>original: "Luna terrena", referring to Mercury</note>, which has no sensible cold, but the signs of cold are sensibly present. Because of this, quicksilver produces tremors, grinding of teeth, and the like. If it were not earthly winter, it would not produce these things. For every tremor is an influence impressed as if from the celestial stars; and although heat joined with heat brings tremor, just as coldness does, that is not said in a metallic or earthly way. Let those causes remain in their place. But here my purpose is only to describe earthly mineral diseases, born from their alliances, which indeed requires nothing else than that Mercury be described in the way we have done. For Mercury is the earthly moon and earthly winter, and thus has two impressions in man: one as the Moon, if man makes himself subject to it; the other as winter, and the winter stars whose nature it has. How all these things are to be understood most fully need not be described here. As much as was necessary to demonstrate the origin of this disease has been said enough. After this, therefore, nothing else is proposed to us than how that disease is cured.

## TRACTATE IV.
->On the diseases which quicksilver generates in man.<-

### CHAPTER I.

<margin>
Every frost is a disease unto death. The cold of mercury drives the heat of man so that it burns the principal organs, which will also experience their own natural diseases.
</margin>
Before we rightly instruct you concerning the cure, know that the winter which lies hidden in quicksilver generates a unique disease, namely tremor without sensible shivering, as was said, which indeed you must understand in this way. Every frost is a disease unto death, for overcoming cold drives all heat inward, and in this way overcomes the heart and other members, which it affects with stiffness. But heat cannot flee from the center or yield elsewhere. Therefore it scorches the heart, and similarly the lung, liver, stomach, and brain. For when they tremble, then the heat has retreated into that center of its own, in which the degree becomes excessive, and from the abundance and surplus of heat, the temperament is corrupted, whence fire is born, which devours everything, operating from the nature of its element. From this now arises <term>rot</term> <note>original: "putredo"</note> of the lung, liver, stomach, brain, kidneys, intestines, and other similar diseases so many that they can hardly all be enumerated. Indeed, even the marrow itself dries up in the bones: the veins and nerves of the bones, likewise the blood, are scorched; similarly the flesh itself under the skin, the cartilages, and whatever is in man. There also occur other accidental diseases, which indeed are of the nature and property of any member, such as in the lung: difficulty breathing, cough, panting, abscesses, rots, and <term>consumption</term> <note>original: "phthisis"</note>; in the brain: <term>mania</term>, <term>frenzy</term> <note>original: "phrenesis"</note>, <term>headache</term> <note>original: "cephælalgiia"</note>, <term>catarrhs</term>, toothaches, paralysis, apoplexy, the <term>falling sickness</term> <note>epilepsy</note>, and the like. Thus it is to be understood of all others which are affected here, which there is no need to list, since it is very well known to all physicians what kind of diseases are born and arise from such an infection.

<margin>
Tremor and other diseases proper to the LUNG and BRAIN.
</margin>

### CHAPTER II.

<margin>
Mercury in man marks its new moons, quadratures, and full moons.
</margin>
But concerning the diseases which quicksilver produces by reason of its cold, in those who make themselves subject to it and take it in externally as an impression—that is, as a scent from a rose—let enough be said. Let us speak further of those diseases which it brings as the Moon, in which indeed there is the new moon, the <term>quadrature</term> <note>a phase where the moon is 90 degrees from the sun, such as a first or last quarter moon</note>, and the full moon. As its waxing is, such also is its waning. It has indeed another action also from the birth of Adam even to the middle age of the human race, or of the world; which middle being completed—namely, at the half duration of the world—its full moon is present, after which it decreases and its other part follows. He who does not understand the reason of this Moon speaks unworthily of the age of the world or of the last day. For it is necessary here also to consider the full moon and the quadratures. Furthermore, you know how the new moon behaves toward man, according to the doctrine of the upper heaven; similarly how it is affected while it waxes until the first quadrature, from the quadrature until the full moon, from the full moon to the latter quadrature, and from this until the loss of its light. Just as, therefore, you know these things from astronomical experience, so also even if you had no <term>ephemerides</term> <note>tables of astronomical positions</note> at all, but at least made judgment from <term>lunatic diseases</term> <note>diseases affected by the moon's cycles</note>, you would altogether know...

...you would know how the Moon behaves, from those signs of the Sun which become known to you in the sick. ## CHAPTER III.

<margin>
Mercury, like the Moon, leaves its impressions not only on the brain, but on all the limbs.
Is the brain dedicated to the Moon?
Reason increases and decreases according to the Moon.
What the lunar diseases are: 1. Of the head.
Lunar diseases of individual members.
2. Of the joints.
3. Of the liver.
4. Of the kidneys.
</margin>
**S**ince therefore the Moon of <term>quicksilver</term> <note>original: "argenti vivi"</note> generates diseases of "impression" in men, know some of their signs. In this way, it is commonly said that the brain is the organ of the Moon in man; that is, the brain is the Moon of the <term>microcosm</term> <note>the human being as a "little world" reflecting the universe</note>, and reigns within it. Know, therefore, that you should by no means cling to this opinion. For the Moon leaves its impression on all members, not just on one; the brain also exists in man just like any other member. However, the reason the brain is chiefly considered a "lunatic" organ by the common people is because of "lunatic" disease <note>epilepsy or mental illness associated with moon phases</note>. For when the brain suffers from that, the suffering is chiefly perceived in the reason. For reason increases or decreases according to the Moon. Since it is perceived so sensibly, and especially by the common folk, it is for this reason that the Moon and the brain are said to correspond to each other. It must be known, therefore, that such signs shine forth in all other members just as they do in reason, and not only in the brain. The lunar diseases are <term>mania</term>, <term>dog bites</term> <note>rabies</note>, <term>Saint Vitus’ Dance</term> <note>a disorder characterized by rapid, uncoordinated jerking movements</note>, <term>Epilepsy</term>, and many other similar chronic diseases, when they are exasperated and attack with fatal accidents. And these diseases belong to the brain. But the lunar diseases belonging to the joints are paralysis, the "drop" <note>gout</note>, arthritis, <term>podagra</term> <note>gout specifically in the foot</note> and its species, along with convulsions, fluxes, <term>distillations</term> <note>leaking of bodily humors</note>, and their types. In the liver, there are fevers, <term>jaundice</term> <note>original: "icterus"</note>, and the like. In the kidneys, the "diabetic suffering"; and so with the other members. I have brought these up because quicksilver dominates and presides over the same diseases as the celestial Moon itself—according to its <term>exaltation</term> <note>an astrological position of strength</note>—namely, consumption, dropsy, hectic quartan fever, etc. However, the foundation from which these things are more fully understood proceeds from "First Astronomy," about which there is no need to write here. Yet to the learned and expert, enough has been said: that here one must think of the *terrestrial* Moon <note>mercury</note> and not the *celestial* one in the knowledge of diseases and the undertaking of their cure.

<margin>
The Moon of Mercury is perpetual.
Mercury is a perpetual winter.
Living Mercury cannot be digested by man.
The celestial Moon assists.
Mercury taken inside the body.
</margin>
For Mercury is an entirely perpetual moon, in which there is no death until the final day, whether it enters a man or not; and at the same time it is a permanent and fixed winter, whose snow no sun can melt, nor is its ice unlocked. Since these things are so, it is necessary that it be treated with greater understanding, since it is manifest that man cannot digest or concoct it. For all metals of Mercury are "cooked" <note>processed by the body</note>, but quicksilver is not; neither man nor even the ostrich can digest it. In short, quicksilver remains "living," and does not die, and if you place it within the body, the man will have the Moon within himself, and along with it all the properties of the Moon. Indeed, it even happens that the Moon above associates itself with its like <note>the mercury inside the body</note>, and together with it, it opens its purpose all the more eagerly, and thus the diseases are doubled. For whatever the Moon can work in all diseases, quicksilver can also do: and from this come the errors in the most difficult diseases which arise from this application. For unless this Moon of quicksilver is cast down, all the diseases of that man are incurable. For true and genuine Medicine <note>original: "Physica"</note> consists in these things being known and performed.

## CHAPTER II.

<margin>
Magical Fires, etc.
Spirits can do all things spiritually which man does naturally.
Incorporeal spirits.
Spirits can make fire, horses, men, etc.
</margin>
**N**ow, if "Magical fires" and similar "impressions" are seen outwardly, the same are also discovered in the mountains. Their cause and origin is as follows. If the spirit of any man is similar in genius and nature: then that same spirit can also express and imitate all the works of that man—that is, a spirit can plow, cut wood, and perform all human works, no less skillfully than the man himself. The difference, however, lies in this: that the spirit does not cut natural wood, nor perform natural handiwork, etc., but performs and is capable of it in *supernatural* things, in which wood and handiworks are held in their own way, just as ours are. They are surely spirits, who possess nothing corporeal; therefore their fields and wood are also such. But man, since he is natural, also uses natural instruments and subjects. Therefore, just as a man can draw natural fire from natural things, so spirits can also make spiritual fire from supernatural things, such as they themselves are. For man makes corporeal fire because his subjects are corporeal. From which it now follows that spirits can generate roses, horses, men, flowers, etc., but still like themselves: spiritual, not corporal. For both their region and their things are spiritual, just as the world's region and things are corporal. Thus also fly dragons and other similar forms, which nevertheless are not natural. Thus also "impressions" and similar things are raised.

## CHAPTER IV.

<margin>Mercury acts like the moon inside the body.</margin>
**J**ust as it has been said concerning external diseases, which quicksilver can bring about through the "impression" of smoke and hidden vapor, so know that it works similarly even in those who take it into the body, as in medicine. Wherefore it would be right that doctors who administer Mercurial medicines through ointments, fumigations, <term>precipitate</term> <note>a solid substance separated from a solution</note>, corrosive waters, and the like, should become somewhat better skilled in Mercury, lest they fall into impostures. ## CHAPTER III.

<margin>What lightning is. A burning mirror, etc. Sulfurous soot within the earth... by what it is ignited.</margin>
In addition, it now remains for you to know that in the mountains, thunder, lightning, and flashes are produced in a natural way; which we shall define briefly with a <term>meteoric</term> <note>referring to phenomena of the atmosphere and earth, not just falling stars</note> explanation. A flash from the clouds is <term>sulfurous soot</term> <note>original: "fuligo sulphurea"</note>, burning or ignited of itself, just as a fire is lit by a <term>burning mirror</term> <note>original: "speculo ignifero"; a lens or concave mirror used to concentrate sunlight</note>, which is clear from the foundations of meteorics. Sulfurous soot of this kind is also stored in the mountains, emerging from <term>earthly stars</term> <note>Paracelsus believed minerals were influenced by "stars" within the earth</note>, and this soot can be ignited by the air. Otherwise, that fire remains dormant and dead. If sulfurous soots exist in some mountain, then they are similar to sulfurous smoke raised in a <term>sublimatory</term> <note>a vessel used in alchemy to heat a substance until it becomes vapor and then solidifies again</note>. However, since that smoke cannot be caught by any fire, it does not flame or burn. But if indeed candles, torches, and lamps are carried into the mines by the miners, and their fire catches the smokes, then they burn just as if fire had burst into a sublimatory with air. Since that is nothing other than smoke, it burns away in a brief moment, the essence of which is like a lightning flash. For all things that burn in this way—whether they are in the firmament of the earth or above it—consist of sulfur. For the same reason, it also happens that sulfurs of this kind produce sulfurous stones, which stones, through that ignition, conceive a fixed flame; and they burn for as long as the fixed sulfur remains, whether it be earthly, or stony, or <term>marcasitic</term>, or <term>talcic</term>, or <term>bismuthic</term>. For where these minerals are not smelted and are fixed in their composition, the same thing happens to them as to a heap of coals, which is entirely ignited and consumed by a single coal. In the same way, the vapors in the caverns, passages, channels, and cavities of the mountains behave here also; once caught by a flame, they burn until all the soot has been consumed and burned away.

You, however, kind Reader, take these in good part, and do not be of an unfair mind regarding those things which have perished and cannot be shared with you.*

### On the Cure of diseases from quicksilver.

## CHAPTER VI.

Thus enough has been said about preservatives and conservatives: for those things which preserve also conserve, and vice versa. Furthermore, we must speak of the cure by which <term>quicksilver</term> <note>mercury</note> is expelled from the body before the medicine and cure may begin. If this is to be done, it is necessary for the quicksilver to be <term>vivified</term> <note>made "living" or active/mobile</note>; for while it is not "living," it cannot be separated from the body. Therefore, the most important thing is that it be vivified; and then, how it may be expelled from the body. The process, however, is as follows. I pose a case: you have a patient who carries in himself a certain weight of quicksilver, and it is "living." It will therefore give its signs: the teeth are very black, the limbs are weak and stiff, and there is a wandering <term>flux</term> <note>a flow of humors or discharge</note> staying in no certain place, showing itself first in the joints and nodes. These are the signs of quicksilver, which usually has a fixed place, as if a hard <term>aposteme</term> <note>an abscess or swelling</note> were hiding there. <margin>Signs of living and dead Mercury in the body.</margin> But if the quicksilver is not "living," it shows its signs according to the Moon in a hardness of the shin; it also brings tinted urine and foul-smelling breath: in this way, both types of Mercury are recognized and detected.

## CHAPTER VII.

<margin>Locations of living Mercury in man.</margin>
Now indeed it becomes us to speak of the exit of quicksilver: next we shall say how that which is not "living" may be made "living," so that it becomes fit for exit. Note therefore regarding the exit of Mercury, that any Mercury places itself in the cavities of the nodes and joints, in this way: namely, if it tends downwards through the spine of the back and the regions of the hips, it falls into the knees or into the <term>sockets</term> <note>original: "acetabula"</note> of the joints through the neighboring ligaments. Just as quicksilver, if it is placed in a trench of water, always tends downward until it finds a seat and a <term>cataract</term> <note>here meaning a basin, drain, or collection point</note> in which to settle. So also the knees are "cataracts," and similarly the joints of the nodes and the hips, and the joints of the spine: even sometimes it collects itself in the ligaments themselves, and often in the very soles of the feet, as far as it can fall. Thus it also fixes its seat in the arms, in the "cataracts" of the shoulders, the elbows, and further in the <term>wrists</term> <note>original: "rastetis"</note>, also in the back of the head, in the cavity of the eyes, so that the inner corners of the eyes cast it out. Often it also occupies the nostrils; often it falls through the throat into the stomach and exits through the bowels. Where it is positioned must be learned from signs and certain experience.

Afterward, heal the place with a gummed plaster until it knits together.

### CHAPTER IX.

<margin>How "dead mercury" may be revived.</margin>
If you wish to make <term>dead mercury</term> <note>mercury that has settled or become inactive within the patient's body, causing chronic poisoning</note> "live" again, so that it can be led out of the body by the aforementioned method, proceed as follows. First of all, prepare a strong bath from mucilaginous herbs, the tips of fir trees or juniper shrubs, and even fresh fir cones, decocted in water. Let the patient wash in this, adjusted for their person and strength, as hot as they can bear. Indeed, they may also use the thermal springs at <term>Pfäfers</term> <note>original: "Piperinis"</note>, <term>Plombières</term> <note>original: "Plumbariis"</note>, <term>Gastein</term>, <term>Teplitz</term> <note>original: "Dopplizenfib"</note>, <term>Aachen</term> <note>original: "Aquifgranẽfib"</note>, <term>Ems</term>, <term>Göppingen</term>, or artificial baths made from sulfur and similar things. When the patient leaves the bath, let them be rubbed with the juice of <term>spearwort</term> <note>original: "flammulae"</note> or oil of pepper; after which, a sweat should be induced in whatever way possible, using <term>theriac</term>, <term>mithridate</term> <note>famous ancient poly-pharmaceutical "cure-alls" and antitoxins</note>, and so on. This should be done continually, without regard for the pain. For in the midst of this, the <term>quicksilver</term> <note>original: "argentum vivum"; mercury</note> revives. After you have found from certain experience that the mercury is "living," proceed as directed above. And since it often happens that the pain does not stop, move toward the center; recognize it and proceed. For mercury administered in the form of medicine is often so strongly "mortified" <note>chemically altered to be inactive</note> that it is revived with difficulty; though "pustule-doctors" <note>a derogatory term for doctors who only treated the skin symptoms of syphilis</note> may pride themselves on this as an art, I consider it a great foolishness.

### CHAPTER XII.

<margin>Secrets against diseases of the principal organs.</margin>
Other accidental diseases also rage in the principal organs without the presence of other great diseases—such as violent and singular pain of the stomach, pain in the sides, spleen, or liver, as well as the most burning headache, and pain of the kidneys and back. These cannot be brought under the disorderly rules of common <term>Recipes</term>, but must be entrusted to those great <term>Arcana</term> <note>secret, powerful chemical remedies</note>, such as <term>Laudanum</term> <note>Paracelsus's specific opium-based preparation</note>, <term>Materia perlata</term> <note>essence of pearls</note>, and the like. ### CHAPTER XIII.

<margin>On afflictions of the teeth from Mercury.</margin>
There still remain several afflictions of the teeth with many accompanying symptoms, such as pain, rot, loosening, falling out, and violent stinging and torments, and the tossing of <term>fluxions</term> <note>excessive discharge of fluids</note>. Finally, place <term>plantain</term>, salt, <term>comfrey</term>, and <term>serpentine</term> into distilled and prepared alum water, and wash the teeth with that water twice daily; thus the rot of the teeth will cease. As for the wobbling of the teeth, what is better than oil of <term>Crocus Martis</term> if they are anointed with it? Regarding the falling out of teeth, nothing else removes the mercurial force better than oil of nutmeg. The spirit of urine produces its Bolus in two ways. First, because everything we eat and drink provides urine. This begins in the stomach and is perfected in the kidneys. However, the Bolus generated in the stomach is more subtle than that generated in the middle of the kidneys; it flies upward in the stomach, attaching itself to the sides, the opening, and the base. This is worse than the first, because it coagulates itself, whereas the former only becomes mud-like with little pain.

From that body, Tartar and Stone-disease <note>original: "Lithiasis"</note> are generated in this manner: When this matter divorces itself from the spirit, and the spirit (being exceedingly subtle and clear) withdraws from the matter, then by creeping along the sides of the organs, the matter itself is coagulated. The spirit vanishes, and its "body" <note>the solid residue</note> remains. In this case, therefore, it is not healthy to retain urine longer than is right. Furthermore, if the spirit is so subtle, it often departs before nature seeks an exit. It is therefore right for every Physician to know that Tartar and Stone-disease arise from the spirit of urine; this urine is made from food and drink, not indeed from their own nature, but from the nature of the spirit in the urine, according as it is or becomes volatile. The same must be judged concerning sand and stone.

This spirit is tinged with a two-fold color: red and white. For colors separate every single body within the spirits. Therefore, the red body seeks its own place; the white body seeks another place. Moreover, the first digestion is lighter than the second. Hence, it will not produce stones. The second digestion is harder and thicker, whence it brings forth stones and sand, and exhibits a two-fold work of its body. For sand is generated for this reason: that the spirit departs from its body sooner than it should, and the salt coagulates into sand and a certain kind of "muddiness," because sand is in some way equal to the first digestion. Stone of the kidneys and bladder is the worst of all; though stone of the kidney is worse than stone of the bladder. Thus, in every place, the first is best and the last is worst. For the first body is mud-like; the second is "bolar" <note>clay-like or clumping</note> and lies in the stomach; the third is sandy and lies in the kidneys; the fourth is stony and lies in the urinary passages, the kidneys, the bladder, and their paths. From these things many people die, yet [the stones] are not found when they are dissected <note>Paracelsus implies here that some of these "stones" are spiritual or salt-based and may dissolve or vanish after death</note>.

## THE GENERATION OF GOUT.

1. The spirit of urine is the craftsman <note>original: "opifex"</note> that generates the stone and its various types, just as it generates gout. Therefore, those who say that gout is a "flux" <note>original: "fluxum"; referring to the traditional humoral theory that gout was caused by a "dropping" of excess phlegm into the joints</note> are notably mistaken; for it is nothing other than **Tartarous matter** <term>Tartareitas: the Paracelsian concept of metabolic waste that hardens like the crust in a wine barrel</term>, located in salt. It is far from the truth to suggest that a "flux" could generate small stones. For these are generated solely from the salt contained in the urine.

2. Regarding these matters, it should be noted that in the foods which are eaten and become blood, no spirit of salt is contained—and much less in the meats offered at the table. Therefore, only the spirit of urine is to be considered in the process of coagulation, not a flux or catarrh. For that spirit itself is the disease and the cause of the disease.

3. As for why the spirit of urine extends to that specific place, and to the extremities and fingers, the cause is this: the humors, which are drawn from food into the body by the "attractive virtue" <note>the biological force believed to pull nutrients to specific organs</note>, sometimes simultaneously pull the mixed-in spirit of urine along with them. Now, nothing is so pure or whole that it does not contain something immoderate within itself. The same is true in these attractive virtues; hence they are either too hot, or they attract more than is fair, and by adopting the spirit of urine, they carry it through the body.

4. It follows from this: if the spirit of urine penetrates to those regions where it finds no place to pass through, it then sticks there and coagulates according to the nature of its condition. As for why it is different there than in the liver, the reason is that different humors are mixed with it there. Thus, the generation of gout occurs only in the cavities. For where these are absent, the spirit of urine cannot be digested <note>here meaning "processed" or "broken down"</note>. Where it can be digested, there "boli" or "gouts" are generated—provided, of course, that the spirit expires and evaporates, leaving the solid body behind.

**Boli.**

Similarly, it should be known that the commotion of small stones and sand, etc., also happens in one of several ways. **Gouts.**

Here it must be noted that the motions of the Bolus and Gout occur according to the Elements; that is, just as those elements behave and move in the earth and in a shell, so they also move in the body. Since they descend from the elements themselves, they move according to the manner of those elements. For when the "first mover" <note>original: "mobili primo"</note> is moved, the second and final mover is also moved.

</margin>

Every overabundance of food and drink becomes a cause of this disease for the following reason: Within food and drink, a spirit is contained that is strong and powerful in its life and vigor, which is volatile. If this spirit is taken into the body and the limbs—namely the head—it then tests its strength and exerts itself against nature. For external nature struggles, as it were, with internal nature; they are two contraries, not indeed in substance, but in spirit. If this external spirit emerges as the victor, it then dissolves itself into a boiling state. By the force of this boiling, whatever is in its path is seized and dissolved—such as the body itself, which is reduced to a liquid. This liquid is what falls and brings about the injury.

<margin>
From this condition or nature, many other diseases are born which are named in the Practical branch of medicine.
</margin>

The spirit of nourishment is Narcotic. It provokes a sleep that is not natural if it is driven in too forcefully. For just as natural sleep has its own progression in a human, so it is in nourishment with its own spirit. If that spirit enters the body, being infused too densely and copiously, it makes people lazy and sleepy. From the multitude of this Narcotic faculty, sleep is stirred as if through a shadow; but along with this comes another sleep, which is a disease in the body. For sleep should not be felt in the limbs, but only in the back of the head <note>original: "occipitio"</note>.

<margin>
These four are the principal or "prize" diseases of the head, under which all others are understood.
</margin>

This spirit frequently increases in the body to such an extent that it damages the "root" from which the entire body is produced. Just as it goes out from the root, so it tends back toward the root. Moreover, the more it is permitted by a decaying body (or its decay), the more and more readily it wins out. It causes whatever it has dissolved to be converted into a disease of the whole body. This external spirit exists without the internal spirit; it inflicts an alien and Narcotic force upon the body, which exceeds the limits of Nature.

This kind of Narcotic condition arises from the spirit of the **Three Firsts** <term>trium primorum: the three Paracelsian principles of Salt, Sulfur, and Mercury</term>, which flourishes in nature and has the power of stupor. For the **Salt of Vitriol** <term>Sal Vitrioli: a chemical salt often associated by Paracelsians with neurological or "contracting" effects</term> is innate to it. From this mixture, the Narcotic-dissolving spirit arises, and from these two it takes on double powers: namely, a numbing spirit and the power to dissolve substance and the body.

# TABLE IV.

### THE GENERATION OF CONTRACTURES.
<note>original: "Contractorum" — referring to ailments where limbs are stiffened, drawn together, or cramped.</note>

In all explanations of contracture and tremor, it must be known that the spirit of contracture and tremor is similar to the spirit of **Mercury** <term>Mercury: in this context, one of the three "Prime Principles" of alchemy, representing volatility and the spirituous state</term>. This is to say, a most subtle nature of **Sulfur** <term>Sulfur: the alchemical principle of inflammability and oily substance</term> concurs with the spirit of **Salt** <term>Salt: the alchemical principle of stability and solidification</term>, which is never without the spirit of Mercury. This spirit works somewhat more than the other two: for wherever there is a tremor, the spirit of Mercury is present more abundantly than the rest.

<margin>
In these two diseases—namely, contracture and tremor—one must first understand the Philosophy: that is, that wine is nothing other than sulfur, salt, and Mercury. Therefore, whatever fault wine commits must be attributed to these three.
</margin>

<margin>
In the same way that Mercury, salt, and sulfur show themselves externally in their physical matter, so too does the spirit show itself in the form of wine—namely, the spirit of Colic and Gall <note>original: "Fellis"</note>. It is therefore the duty of the Physician to compare the spirit of the three first Elements with their respective bodies.
</margin>

> The spirit of Contracture and Tremor is without substance or physicality; it is a pure and naked spirit, entangled in no body. It is a vapor from the salt that resides in wine, which the Nature of salt has stirred up and deposited into the limbs.

---

<margin>** Of Wine</margin> The kind produced from wine is as follows. If the spirit of wine evaporates, and the wine is too strong, subtle, penetrating, and dry in its essence, and contains little substance in terms of physicality: then, if that wine travels further than it should and enters the external limbs, it excites a paroxysm <note>a sudden attack or fit</note>, namely **Tremor**. Or, it consumes the humors <note>the bodily fluids</note> in which the **motive spirit** <term>motive spirit: the vital force that enables the body to move</term> lies; this spirit can then no longer move itself but lies as if dead. The limbs therefore lie as if dead, and in the progress of time, the spirit is so dried out that the ligaments, veins, and tendons are contracted, and they pull the limbs closed along with them.

<margin>❡ Of Food</margin> Regarding food, it should be held that although it does not generate contracture and tremor, it nevertheless confirms and strengthens them. If adverse foods are ingested, then whatever the spirit of wine has abandoned or added, the "blood" of the food finishes and perfects. It assists the wine in its passage, consuming and drying out the body's humors, and finally taking away the motive spirit.

<margin>):( Of Anger</margin> This is similarly like wine in overcoming the natural humors in which the motive spirit lies. Its operation is such: if anger seethes in a person, it is nothing other than the **gall** <note>the bile</note> attracting all the humors in the entire body to itself, so that while the anger lasts, the gall and the humors occupy one place in a single mass. In this way, once the conjunction of the gall and humors has occurred, the bile (as it were) gives body to the humors and drives them into a fury. Afterward, when the anger ceases, the humors are poured back into their limbs, dragging the gall itself along with them. They possess a spirit similar to the spirit of wine for the consumption of nature, where the movement of salt is found, etc.

<margin>♏︎ Of Colic</margin> Likewise, if colic afflicts the body through external or internal accidents, without the aforementioned cause and origin—that is: through the spirit of its own wind—it consumes, dries out, and performs similar actions. For its matter excites griping pains and piercings in the belly, and moreover, a certain force or strength is inflicted upon the intestines of the belly by medicines, whether external or internal. Then the offending matter becomes a subtle spirit, which, moving itself outside the body, rushes into the limbs. While it occupies them, it has an operation entirely similar to those mentioned above and causes contractures, but not many tremors, because it dries out and consumes the humors too quickly and overthrows the motive power.

<header>THE GENERATION OF CONTRACTURES.</header>

Regarding **tremor** and **contracture** <note>original: "contracturâ" — a condition where muscles permanently shorten or joints stiffen</note> in this category, it must be understood that nowhere in the limbs can Nature be more easily corrupted by its own goodness than in the liquids and the brain. This happens because wine is not the least among the best things a human can consume. The same is true of the noblest and best-prepared foods. If these are brought into the body, their subtlety exceeds and overcomes the strength of Nature. Therefore, when the spirit <note>original: "spiritus" — referring here to the volatile essence of wine or food, similar to alcohol</note> has occupied its place and dominates there, it operates according to its own nature: that is, it consumes Nature and perfects its own properties. It works no less or more lightly in the ligaments and arteries than it does in the brain, namely, when it makes men drunk. The difference lies in this one thing: the brain may overcome that spirit, whereas the limbs can do so very little. Therefore, by its delay and congestion, it induces contracture and tremor. For everything external that dominates the body overcomes and dissolves nature, disposing it toward its own likeness. That is to say, a disease is introduced into the body to the destruction of health by nothing more readily than by the very best food or drink.

Therefore, this whole matter must be understood: that <term>Contracture</term> and <term>Tremors</term> are nothing other than the subtle spirit of wine and food, of bile, and of the "winds" of colic. If this spirit erupts to the external limbs, it then pervades the veins, tendons, and whatever is in its path. However, it cannot work the same way inside the body because of the excessive abundance of heat there. Furthermore, the internal subject is not as susceptible as the external limbs, which contain many tendons and similar structures. Among the causes, however, there is this difference: no contracture afflicts more gently and mildly than that which comes from food and wine. But that which attacks from anger and colic stirs up grave and atrocious pains in the body.

***

***

§ The origin of these diseases is twofold, but the end result is only one. Therefore, they are reduced to a single Theory. Their origin is partly from the Elements. Thus, according to the nature of the Elements, the disease also infests externally, just as their infections are poured into bodily things. In this case, the body does not "sin" <note>original: "peccat" — in a medical sense, meaning to fail or malfunction</note>, but only external things do. No cause of these diseases resides within the body itself, but only in the impressions of the Elements. For this reason, we will not theorize further here regarding the "fixed" falling sicknesses. Those which are attributed to the elements manifest as paroxysms in the "cells" <note>original: "cellulis" — likely referring to the ventricles or cavities of the brain.</note>.

So also do the non-fixed ones end in the cells. These find their origin in the body, not from the Elements—that is, the body's own nature acts with the force of an Element. But because the nature here is not truly Elemental, the paroxysms do not become exactly like the Elements. In the same way, it reaches its end; for this kind of operation of nature toward evil is not durable. For in the body itself, nothing is durable as it is in the Elements.

<margin>§ Conditions etc.</margin>

1. For these to occur, it must be known that the four external Elements give four "impressions," from which arise four types of <term>Analentia</term>, four of <term>Catalentia</term>, and four of <term>Epilentia</term>; and likewise as many <term>Syncopes</term>, <term>Manias</term>, and <term>Phreneses</term>. Therefore, their species must be properly known because of the impressions of these four Elements.
2. The reason for the matter is this: namely, that the incorporeal Elements—substances without a body—are the souls of the external, bodily Elements. From this, the body attracts the nature of external things to itself, according to how they are disposed or arranged. Thus the elemental soul exists within the physical body, participating in the Elements and their operations.
3. Now, if these impressions are moved, then the substance of the elemental soul in the body boils up and becomes volatile; it ascends to the heights and penetrates the cells of the brain. While the spirit of these elements lies in that path and place, the "Lord of the cell" <note>likely referring to the conscious mind or the vital faculty governing the brain's cavities</note> suffers entirely. While he suffers, the predicted diseases are generated, whether they be fixed or non-fixed.
4. Furthermore, they are generated according to the time, hour, and day of that impression of either kind, and they moderate the physical body, which consists in this <term>Yliado</term> <note>original: "Yliado" or Yliaster — a Paracelsian term for the primeval matter or the internal vital chaos from which life and health are governed</note> according to the nature and hour of its paroxysm. That they are moved in this way comes from their Elemental nature and condition. Woe, however, to that man who is generated in that <term>Yliado</term>!

<header>THE GENERATION OF FALLING DISEASES.</header>

<margin>The conditions of the types of diseases among the falling sicknesses:</margin>
In <term>Epilepsy</term> <note>original: "Epilentia" — the "falling sickness," historically used to describe seizures and various loss-of-consciousness events</note>, three species are counted. One occupies the head; the second, the belly; the third, the limbs. That which besieges the head is born from the impressions of two elements, namely fire and air. That which occupies the body and limbs is from earth and water. Those types that afflict more strongly and severely, or last longer, are from the element of fire, provided the limbs feel nothing. If, however, they retain sensation and the seizure occurs mildly, they are made from air. Those originating from the body are from earth. Those from the limbs are watery.

They occupy their specific place in the body for this reason: their spirit and soul, which adheres to the elements themselves along with the bodily substance, has its own peculiar place in the body. For just as the elements are fourfold, so there are also four parts in the physical body similar to the external elements. They are defined in such a way that they do not remain in their own seats, but since they exist as spiritual entities, they ascend into the center of the spirit. This spirit resides in the brain, just as life has its center in the heart. Therefore, while it creeps into its center, that spirit is drawn over the body of the brain and casts it down. From this follow paroxysms <note>sudden attacks or fits</note> according to the nature of their element.

The body, which also attempts something similar within itself, stirs up <term>Syncopy</term> <note>fainting or loss of consciousness</note> in place of <term>Analentia</term> <note>a Paracelsian term for a type of epilepsy originating in the stomach or a state of restorative seizure</note>, and moves toward <term>Phrenesis</term> <note>delirium or "frenzy," often associated with brain inflammation</note> in place of epilepsy. It gives no fixed place because the location of the disease does not remain stable but becomes volatile and is carried upward into the head, deserting its own proper place, which is then not returned to because it is not fixed. Thus, syncopy occurs in four ways, just as there are four parts of the physical elemental body; likewise, there is a fourfold <term>Mania</term> and phrenesis.

If syncopy ascends, it sometimes takes away all the senses. This type is from the elements of air and fire. Sometimes it does not overpower the senses, yet meanwhile the spirit of the ligaments is moved and, as if dead, moves nothing of the body. This is from the elements of earth and water. From these things, it can be understood that diseases of this kind are easily united with the external elements and readily overcome the elemental spirit, so that it falls into a fixed disease; however, sometimes both elements concur at the same time.

Mania, which is joined with dancing and cheerfulness, arises from the two upper elements, namely fire and air. That which exhibits itself with furies is born from the two lower elements. Yet dancing and cheerfulness are common to both kinds, though under a double appearance.

Phrenesis is also itself twofold: the mild and peaceful kind is from air and earth, as well as from water. The furious kind, however, arises from fire.

The causes of these must therefore be diligently weighed in treatment, so that the "fixed" and "non-fixed" may be properly distinguished from one another. For that which is fixed in the body does not have "sinning matter" <note>original: "materiam peccantem" — a traditional medical term for the corrupt humors or substances causing a disease</note>. That which is not fixed has sinning matter in the body. For there are only two ways in treatment: no fewer, etc.

# TABLE VI.
## THE GENERATION OF DROPSY.

<margin>From unnatural watery generations, seven diseases arise, such as:</margin>
<margin>The generation of these is as follows: If Nature wanders in her operations and does something other than what she ought, then these diseases occur. In this way arises:</margin>

- **Tympanites** <note>a condition where the abdomen is distended by gas, named after a drum or "tympanum"</note>, which is wind, born from the generative nature of air in the body. For the body, besides the air drawn from outside, requires another additional and internal air of its own, by which the physical limbs of the inner element are sustained. When Nature wanders in her operations, then a sort of "miscarriage" is generated from it, which is called Tympanites; or other swellings, specifically where there are cavities, such as in the joints, the bladder, etc. Thus, there is one Tympanites of the joints, another of the belly, and another of the intestines, which is more clearly demonstrated through treatment.

- **Dropsy** <note>original: "Hydrops" — edema or the accumulation of excess watery fluid in the tissues</note> arises from the matrix <note>the "womb" or originating place</note> that generates humors, fluxes, and other things related to these. If this humor proceeds from a bad generation, then from it comes a certain slimy water, occupying all the places and regions to which that humor belongs. Because it is slimy, it is not absorbed by the flesh; rather, it putrefies and dissolves the flesh and increases in the manner of slime. For any unnatural thing grows continually, and much more abundantly than a genuine and natural one; the reason for this is that every dissolution increases in its own generation. This slimy water is heavy and foul, subsisting lower in the man and afterwards gradually ascending upward as it is more and more accumulated.

- **Ascites** <note>original: "Asclites" — specifically abdominal dropsy</note> is a dropsy of the belly, collecting itself in the manner of a general dropsy, except that it is generated particularly and is a localized dropsy. Thus, it can occupy only the foot, or another separate place or limb; meanwhile, it does not differ from general dropsy in its cause and generation.

- **Spongia** <note>literally "sponge" — likely referring to a soft, porous tumor or a specific type of fluid-filled swelling</note> is a humor born from a corrupt change of that which ought to have become flesh or blood. If Nature wanders in the alteration of this, and the end...

...and if it does not reach its intended end, then something similar to slime results both inside and outside the body, such as swellings, corns, fleshy hernias, and warts. Something similar also occasionally arises in wounds, in which nature is unable to return to its accustomed order or operation. Therefore, through this dissolution of that which ought to have become flesh and blood, a "sponge" <note>original: "spongia" — a term for a porous, soft tumor or morbid growth</note> is born, clinging around the wound like a vine or a sponge. And these exist in many forms in the body and become large, such as <term>struma</term> <note>a swelling of the neck or thyroid gland, often called scrofula</note> and similar things, which are aberrations of nature, occurring in that which ought to have become flesh and blood.

<margin>Hernia</margin>
A hernia is a failure <note>original: "abortus" — used here to mean a "miscarriage" or failure of a natural process to develop correctly</note> of the humor that ought to sustain oil and things related to it. It arises, however, from the matrix <note>the "mother" or source-site</note> of that humor. And just as nourishment behaves in oil, so in those cases, the failures are divided. One humor is <term>oseous</term> <note>original: "osei" — likely a Paracelsian technical term related to the "bony" or "salt-like" firm humor</note>, which produces a humoral hernia. Another is the flesh of the oseous, from which the oseous receives its own flesh; from this arises a fleshy hernia. Another is "windy" <note>flatulent or gaseous</note>. For the "wind" is that which sustains the oil in its operation. Indeed, nothing exists without air.

<margin>Tumor</margin>
A tumor is a collection occurring in all places, and that either universally or particularly. This ought to be understood in this way: if a tumor proceeds from universal matter, then it occupies the entire body. If, however, it is made from particular matter, then it occupies a single location. This, as we have already said, exists in three types: of humor, of flesh, and of winds. If it arises from an external cause, then this external cause moves that tumor in its first <term>paroxysm</term> <note>a sudden attack or fit of symptoms</note>. Unless it happens that the paroxysm transcends its limit, so that no paralysis, epilepsy, or "stabbing pain" follows: then external things move the generation of internal things, so that one of the aforementioned diseases necessarily follows—either a hernia or, most especially, a "sponge," according as nature finds an exit and is coagulated by the generative power in the skin. For in this way, "sponges" are born hanging externally from the skin.

<margin>Humpback</margin>
A humpback <note>original: "Gibbus"</note> is itself also a failure of nature. This, however, is born only in the substance of its own body, while the <term>growing power</term> <note>original: "virtus crescitiva" — the vital force responsible for physical growth</note> goes astray. For those true members—the back and the bones—which ought to grow: these are dissolved by nature due to a defect of the growing power, so that it is nothing but a spasm of the growing power.

</insert>

*   **Twisting of the mouth.** <note>original: "Tortura oris" — likely referring to Bell's palsy or facial paralysis</note>
*   **Epilepsy.**
*   **Apoplexy.** <note>a sudden loss of consciousness, similar to a stroke</note>
*   **Syncope.** <note>fainting or sudden loss of blood pressure</note>
*   **Suffocation of the womb.** <note>original: "Suffocatione matricis" — a historical term for "hysteria" or uterine spasms believed to cause respiratory distress</note>
*   **Colic.**
*   **Poisons.**
*   **Others, etc.**

---

<margin>Natural</margin>
> The natural type behaves as was said regarding the spasm of the body that produces humpback and curvature. Furthermore, a natural type also exists which induces Tetanus and spasm in the spine, ligaments, or arteries. Its origin is from natural matter—that is, where the powers of extension and retention reside—and then, where nature has been depraved, she corrupts the limb. Nevertheless, it remains "natural" <note>meaning it arises from the body's own developmental processes rather than external injury</note>.

<margin>Preternatural</margin>
> The <term>preternatural</term> <note>occurring outside the normal course of nature; often caused by external accidents or injuries</note> type occurs when the natural order is broken; for example, if the expansive growth-spirit ought to be present, but is then broken by external actions. Where the "spirit of healing" overcomes and drives out the rectifying spirit <note>the force that maintains the correct shape</note> that ought to be present, it is succeeded by an expansive spirit that stretches the limb. For many dissolutions of this kind happen in the mother's womb, caused by human factors rather than external ones; sometimes they also occur if the progress of nature is hindered, so that they cannot become perfect due to diseases or similar causes.

---

Therefore, as a conclusion, it must be held that confusion arises from nothing more than if Tetanus is mistaken for a spasm, or conversely, a spasm for Tetanus. The same occurs in the placement of the "spirits" when they are transposed in the matter by the <term>Archeus</term> <note>the internal "master chemist" or vital force that directs the functions of the organs</note>. From this, many monsters are born in various ways and appearances, as discussed in "The Generations of Animals," etc.

Moreover, if nature becomes monstrous even in the growth-power—which ought to extend or retain—then even if that power remains in its proper place, it nonetheless produces a monster according to its own form: that is, either excessive straightness, or curvature, or deformity, contrary to nature. Those things which become long or small are produced by the "generative power," about which more is said elsewhere.

### THE GENERATION OF WORMS AND ABSCESSES.

<margin>From the corruption of substances—the physical things of Nature—there are generally two types of putrefaction.</margin>

*   Putrefaction in the place of a thing properly dissolved.
*   Putrefaction in the place of a thing properly congealed.

<margin>From this, diseases arise, namely:</margin>

<margin>For there are two operations in any putrefaction, as has been said.</margin>

*   **Worms** / **Fluxes** <note>original: "Fluxus" — abnormal discharges or flows of fluid from the body</note> } And both have similar locations, such as }
    *   In the ears, fluxes occur and worms are born.

    *   In the lungs, abscesses and hardness are generated.
    *   In the spleen, abscesses and hardness are born.

<margin>They have one origin, yet not one effect, nor one <term>Yliadum</term> <note>original: "Yliadum" — a Paracelsian term for the basic elemental matter or the chaotic force from which physical forms and diseases emerge</note>.</margin>

And wherever there are fluxes, there also worms are produced; and where there is hardness, there also are the locations of abscesses. And vice versa: where there are abscesses, there also are fluxes and worms; and where there are worms and fluxes, there also are abscesses and hardness, in whatever place of the body it occurs, such as:

        *   In the skin.

This corruption occurs if the <term>salt of nature</term> <note>original: "sal naturae" — in Paracelsian thought, Salt is the principle of stability and physical substance; its dissolution leads to the decay of the body</note> is dissolved. For at that time, if that limb cannot be preserved, the salt withdraws and deserts that limb—whether it be a specific part or the whole body—and seeks its own exit. Therefore, when a suitable emunctory is available, the salt departs, provided that nature is strong. If not, it remains in its place. And if the salt is hard, then it coagulates and creates an abscess until a time convenient for expulsion. If, however, it departs, then some part of it remains and produces ulcerations. For the salt erodes the flesh and cartilage and produces worms. But if it putrefies, it creates fistulas in the veins where it lies. If it is carried outside the body, it operates according to its own malice and brings forth these diseases, namely:

# THE GENERATION OF WORMS AND ABSCESSES.

<margin>Namely, all ulcerous discharges in the physical body, such as:</margin>

**Internal Discharges:**

*   **Fistulae:** If the salt of the body <note>Paracelsus views "Salt" as the principle of solidity and preservation; when it corrupts, it becomes corrosive.</note> penetrates and takes bodily form—much like saltpeter <note>original: "nitrum"</note> seeps through a location—it creates a harmful matter. Then, rotting within itself, it creates a cavity and a small ulcer in the skin because it cannot endure the air, or at least so that it might leak out. If these burst internally, it is lethal; it is simply salt that has been corrupted in its internal power.
*   **Discharges:** If a flow <note>original: "Fluxus"</note> arises from this, it can cause a "flux of the belly" <note>diarrhea</note>, or the matter of <term>sanies</term> <note>a thin, greenish-yellow discharge from a wound, often mixed with blood</note> wherever it lies in the body. It can also produce worms, as indicated in their treatment. If it lies in the parts of the ear, ear-discharges occur, and even worms of the ear. If it lies in the gums, the teeth become rotten. If in the eyes, it causes bleary-eyedness <note>original: "lippitudo"</note> and other similar abscesses, stirred up with other filth; these pains may be annual, or sometimes daily.
*   **Abscesses:** But that which is so hard that it is not dissolved into liquid, but instead coagulates again, proceeds to grow steadily in its size and ripening <note>original: "maturatione"</note>, wherever it may be located. This is a "coagulated liquor" formed from the body's salts and sulfurs.

**External Discharges:**

*   **Unnatural Abscesses:** If the matter finds no place within the body and nature expels it, then (if it is of the essence of an Abscess) it first infects the skin and raises a swelling that ripens quickly. For the air and external influences, which are absent inside the body, ripen it beyond the natural power of the body. If it bursts, the pain ceases at once. Unless the discharge is drawn out by medicine, it does not have the true nature of an <term>Aposteme</term> <note>an old medical term for a deep-seated abscess or swelling filled with purulent matter</note>. This is what is said regarding abscesses arising from the body's own nature.
*   **Discharges of Jupiter <note>original symbol: ♃; in alchemy, this refers to Tin or the Liver</note>:** If, however, it is not an abscess by nature but a "flux," and it finds its own <term>emunctorium</term> <note>an organ or duct that carries off waste; here, a self-made exit point</note>—that is, it erodes the skin and forces an exit for itself—this happens in many ways. The reason is that "Salt" is manifold, and its dissolutions are also manifold. Thus, the discharges are manifold, resulting in various ulcers that flow in different ways. The treatment of ulcers teaches this; there is no need to describe them more at length here. These openings have no nature other than that of flowing.

---

<margin>☿ Discharges <note>original symbol: ☿; Mercury</note></margin>
<margin>What is Kholerus?</margin>
**Kholerus:** If the discharge becomes dried out with a great deal of salt, creating its own outlet, then *Kholerus*, *Eschar* <note>a dry scab or slough formed by corrosive action</note>, and similar ulcers arise. These are worst around the chest because of the "matter of milk" found there in both men and women, which is entirely dissolved into this diseased matter. Wherever it appears—be it in the feet, the eyes (such as *Noli me tangere* <note>original: "touch me not," a historical name for corrosive skin cancers of the face</note>), or on the back, belly, neck, or chest—whether it be *Lupus* <note>literally "the wolf," referring to skin lesions that "devour" the flesh</note> or something else, it is nothing but "corporated salt" which Nature has dissolved, expelled from herself, and deposited into the skin. There are many kinds of such ulcers and forms in both men and women, which cannot be listed here in this Theoretical section without causing boredom.

->TABLE IX.<-

# THE GENERATION OF FEVERS.

<margin>There are generally 3 types of Fevers.</margin>
<margin>They take their cause and principle as follows.</margin>

1.  **Opiatic:** This fever arises from the boiling of the "paroxysmal spirit." The sole cause is that the raging spirits are set on fire by the accidents of the external Elements. These are divided in turn by the "reversion of the Elements" and act like opiates. Thus, they received their name from the very thing that heals them.
2.  **Centaurean:** This fever is a superfluity in the body, born from the humors. It is their "excrement" <note>original: "stercus," meaning dross or waste</note> which collects over time. If this waste needs to be ejected but cannot exit, it stirs up paroxysms in the feverish spirits. Therefore, those things that consume the humors' waste also remove these fevers; the name and the disease are one and the same <note>referring to the herb Centaury, used to purge the body</note>.
3.  **Errant:** The generation of this fever occurs if the feverish spirits wander <note>original: "errant"</note> and are snatched away outside of their proper matter. They are agitated against their natural motion and order, moved by the dissolution of their location and matter, and by external accidents.
