<header>THE GENERATION OF FEVERS.</header>

<margin>4. Litteristum.</margin>
> This fever is contrary to nature—that is, it is beyond the powers of nature. It is a commotion similar to a fever, yet it is not a fever in itself, and it must be cured only through <term>Litteristum</term> <note>a Paracelsian term likely referring to a specific chemical or spiritual remedy for non-natural diseases</note>, not by natural means.

<margin>5. Albugineum.</margin>
> This fever has no part in common with the four previously mentioned, but fixes its seat in the center of the humors, from which it is repelled by the <term>Albugineous</term> <note>original: "Albugineum"; referring to a clear, egg-white-like humor</note> humor.

### I.
In order to understand fevers—what their nature and properties are—you must first know that fevers and earthquakes come from a single <term>Archeus</term> <note>the "internal chemist" or vital force that directs the functions of an organism</note>, and they produce their effect at their appointed time. The foundation of its essence is as follows.

<margin>II. What is Neastron.</margin>
<term>Neastron</term> <note>a Paracelsian term for a sudden atmospheric or internal agitation</note> is a commotion of the Elements and of things made from Elements; it is an agitation produced in all those things that descend from the Elements. The division occurs in "locusts" <note>likely a metaphor for sudden, swarming outbreaks of disease</note>. Wherever it falls, there it will exert itself.

<margin>III. The fourfold Neastron.</margin>
A certain part in the body adheres to the <term>Neastron</term> of fire, some to air, some to water, and some to earth. According to this, the Physician ought to know when a <term>paroxysm</term> <note>the sudden onset or intensification of symptoms</note> occurs, or when it lessens. For these are recognized within their own Elements.

### IV.
For there is a congenital nature which resides in the <term>Yliadus</term> <note>original: "Yliado"; the primordial matter or vital force of the world</note>. And by the same reason that other <term>Neastra</term> break out and reveal themselves, this one does so as well; nor does it leave the body so long as that Element holds it. It is a disease existing in opposition within the Elements and within the body.

### V.
How this happens in the Elements is a matter of philosophy. But as to how it happens in the body, it must be known that from the power of the "temperature" <note>the balance of qualities</note> within the four Elements of the body, destructions occur. For example: in the power of the internal air, an <term>oppilation</term> <note>a blockage or obstruction</note> in the passages causes paroxysms if it is dissolved. In the power of fire, if it cannot boil according to its nature and becomes "constipated" <note>crowded or thickened</note>, it is compared in its effect to internal air. In the power of water, if it cannot penetrate the pores of the body. In the power of earth, if it produces a fever for itself during its "flowering" <note>its period of peak activity</note> according to its nature.

<margin>VI.</margin>
These things must be understood correctly in this way: The Element of earth generates its own fruits; so also in the body, at the same time. Fire generates its own stars; so also in the body. Water permeates the body; Air blows through the body. As it is outside, so it is also inside. Therefore, these fevers are to be recognized according to the external Elements, because they occur similarly within the body.

<margin>VII.</margin>
The hour and its generation weigh upon it when the exit or eruption occurs. This happens according to the nature of its Element. For instance, for Earth there are 4 points; for Fire, 3; for Air, 2; for Water, 1. If this point vanishes, then the exhalation and the expulsive power are present, which—on account of the obstruction—cannot ascend to the summit. And then the hour of the paroxysm begins.

<margin>VIII.</margin>
For the expulsive force in these generations is so great that if it cannot exit through the open places or pores, it attempts to break through by force. Philosophy teaches more fully whence the paroxysm and the movement of the sick person arise.

<margin>IX.</margin>
They are far from the truth, those things you read about "humors" in the books of the ancients—namely <note>Paracelsus famously rejected the classical "Four Humors" theory of Galen and Avicenna.</note> Avicenna, Galen, etc. He who wishes to be a true and genuine Physician should read through the *Practica*: and he will find that there are five kinds of fevers: four from the Elements, as has been said, and one that emerges from the four mentioned. How these particular fevers are to be understood must be taken from their own chapters, where what a Daily <note>original: "Diaria"</note>, Quotidian, Tertian, or Quartan fever is, is specifically indicated.

* Of Blood

* Of Air
* Of Fire

**Each kind has 3 powers in the "sinning" matter <note>the material cause of the disease</note>; namely:**
* Blocked <note>original: "Oppilatum"</note>
* Putrefied <note>original: "Putrefactum"</note>
* Superfluous <note>original: "Superfluuum"</note>

**From blood in this way: \***
**From earth: ☞**
**From air in this way: ¶**
**From fire: ):(**

---

<margin>\*</margin>
**Blocked:** This is when the blood cannot have its own path and course, and it is a blockage in the veins from a defect of the blood, such as when it congeals or similar.
**Putrefied:** This is when the humor of the three principles <note>Salt, Sulfur, and Mercury</note>, once separation has occurred, falls into decay. This putrefaction is in the place where the pain is.
**Superfluous:** This is when blood abounds in the body beyond what is due, and increases its powers beyond its proper weight; and this superfluity is the generation of Fevers.

<margin>☞</margin>
**Blocked:** The generation from earth is thus: if the earthy humor in us, which is innate and fixed in the members, cannot stand freely as a vital force, it is the generation of an earthy fever.
**Putrefied:** And if that humor does not exist as an Element, but transforms itself out of its own nature, yet without corruption: that is the generation of an earthy fever made from the putrefaction of its own Element.
**Superfluous:** And if that earthy humor is "elemented" <note>given material form</note> and is taken as an Element in this member: when it appears and exists beyond its degree, then it is the generation of earthy fevers from a superfluous element.

<margin>¶</margin>
**Blocked:** And if the air in us, which exists like a "chaos" <note>the atmosphere or space between things</note>, is blocked and has no return, it is the generation of this fever.
**Putrefied:** But if it is turned into putrefaction, like external air: now it is a generation of fever from the putrefaction of air—namely, the internal air.
**Superfluous:** But if it over-abounds into "winds" <note>gas or vapors</note> as it were, and beyond its due, this is the generation of fever from superfluity.

<margin>):(</margin>
**Blocked:** And if the fire that blows around within us cannot have its own "suffumigation" <note>the venting of smoke or vapors</note>, this is the generation of fever from the blockage of fire.
**Putrefied:** And if the body of fire putrefies by its own power within itself, this is the generation of fever from the putrefaction of fire.
**Superfluous:** And if it abounds beyond its fiery Element, now it is a fever from the Element of fire, on account of a superfluity of fiery heat.

# SPECIFIC PRACTICE ON LITHIASIS.

# BY THEOPHRASTUS HOHEN-
# HEIM.

<note>Theophrastus von Hohenheim is the birth name of the famous physician Paracelsus (1493–1541).</note>

->CHAPTERS<-
->1. *On Lithiasis in the stomach.*<-
->2. *On Lithiasis in the Veins.*<-
->3. *On Lithiasis in the Pipes.* <note>original: "Arundinibus"; Paracelsus uses this term for the long, tubular bones or any reed-like structure in the body.</note><-
->4. *On Lithiasis in the Small Tubes.*<-
->5. *On calculous Lithiasis.*<-
->6. *On Lithiasis in the cavity.*<-

---

### CHAPTER I.
### *On Lithiasis in the Stomach.*

<margin>Tartar from wine which is produced in man.</margin>
If the spirit of wine is separated from its corporality and passes through to the liver: then it leaves behind a "body" which contains within itself Tartar <note>original: "Tartarum"; referring to the stony sediment found in wine casks, which Paracelsus believed caused many human diseases</note>, which is thick, hard, and sharp. This Tartar then attaches itself to the walls of the stomach, persisting there and establishing a permanent place for itself; from this, several diseases of the stomach arise, namely <term>Orexis</term> <note>a disorder of appetite or an acidic stomach condition</note>, the mode of whose generation is this. If the Tartar sticks in the opening or the bottom of the stomach, and while not yet fully hardened it feels some moisture, then it becomes acidic, and a certain sharp and violent spirit is distilled upward through the opening. This is only calmed by those things in which the "spirits of salt" are neutralized,
<margin>The cause of Orexis.</margin>
<margin>Saffron, opium, and the like cure it.</margin>
such as <term>crocus</term> <note>saffron</note>, opium, and similar substances. But if it should block the veins leading from the stomach, it takes away the appetite and hinders the passage of nourishment, which is then followed by <term>Phthisis</term> <note>a general term for wasting or consumption</note>, wasting, <term>Hectic</term> <note>original: "Ethica"; a slow, consuming fever</note>, and a species of diabetes. It also excites pains in the stomach—that is, it stirs up compression, burning, fissures, and ulcerations in the <term>precordia</term> <note>the region of the stomach and heart</note>. For all these things proceed from the sharpness and nature of the Tartar: which, if it should calcine itself <note>burn itself into a dry powder</note>, then renders the diseases four times more violent than they otherwise ought to be.

->THE CURE.<-

First, the Tartar must be removed from the stomach. Then a preventative must be established so that it is not born again. This is done in the following way.
Take: Essence of <term>cantharides</term> <note>Spanish fly, used here in a medicinal preparation</note>, 1 dram.
Of <term>Precipitated Mercury</term> <note>a chemical preparation of mercury</note>, 1/2 scruple.
Long pepper.
Cardamom, of each 1/2 dram.
Cinnamon.
Cloves.
Nutmeg, of each 2 drams.
Mix and make a powder. The dose is 1/2 dram for one dose. This purgation releases and peels the tartar from the stomach, and it opens that which is enclosed within it, reducing it back to its original nature. To one thus prepared, a strengthening remedy such as this must be offered: Take Opium 1/2 dram.
Galangal 1/2 dram. Make a <term>tragea</term> <note>a medicinal powder or confection</note> for use.

---

### CHAPTER II.
### *On Lithiasis in the Veins.*

In the same way, Tartar is also generated in the veins; that is: When the spirit of wine is converted into nourishment and is not separated from the tartar which it carries with it, then it enters the veins of the body, and the blood and the "treasure of life" become joined with the spirit of the food, which itself also contains Tartar. Then, therefore, if the Tartar lying in the veins separates itself from the blood in its usual manner and takes on a substance like Tartar, it comes together into globules or "hailstones," and either blocks the veins or clings to the walls of the veins, just as also happens in other cavities. If it settles in those parts, it causes stabbings, abscesses, inflammations, and many similar diseases—that is, it causes the blood to rot by closing its paths so that it cannot pass through; it also stirs up "strokes" and localized wasting in that member, and adds many other diseases descending from the blood, as they will be more certainly recognized through experience.

->*THE CURE*<-

In the beginning, such medicine ought to be applied which may enter into the veins and resolve the Tartar within them. This is done through the spirit of tartar and salt alone, which passes through the body into the veins and resolves it into water. Therefore, those veins must be cut <note>bloodletting</note> so that this blood may flow out. And if the blood has been coagulated by the power of the Tartar, or dried out, or hardened, or burned, then it must be resolved by the <term>essence of salt</term>, which alone has the power and authority to resolve that blood, to renew it in its fragility, and to lead it back to its original state.
<margin>The power of the Spirit or Essence of salt.</margin>

---

### CHAPTER III.
### *On Lithiasis in the Pipes.*

Similarly, Tartar is also produced in the marrow, which clings to the inside of the "pipes" <note>the hollow shafts of the long bones</note>, just as it does elsewhere in the flesh, etc. This Tartar also comes from the nourishment of the marrow and separates from the substance. From this arise intense stabbings, heavy "strokes," and other pains of the marrow, according to whether the Tartar has adhered more or less in this or that bone. But because of the heat of the "pipes," it is felt least of all unless the person is an adult, or weak, cold, asthmatic, wasted away, or affected by some other similar evil. For in this case, the disease is felt more, just as it is in infants.

->*THE CURE.*<-

<margin>Ointment of tears, Essence of pearls and gold.</margin>
Its cure must be established through the "Ointment of Tears" <note>likely a resinous or distilled balm</note>, with which the limb must be anointed; nothing else should be taken internally unless it be the essence of pearls or gold, which penetrate into the nourishment of the marrow. Here the tartar is resolved and vanishes, and it goes away into the bones, in which it is consumed.

->THERE FOLLOW<-

# SOME USEFUL MEDICAL ADVICE, WHICH Theophrastus Paracelsus communicated to certain patients. Although the recipes themselves are not always handed down or appended in every instance, other teachings are provided in the meantime which should by no means be despised. Furthermore, it is clear from these how Theophrastus maintained his method of curing, even while employing common medicines, etc.

## ADVICE I.

->*To strengthen the brain and stomach, for the avoidance of fluxes and other diseases: written to the learned man, Master Adam Reusner, Senior, secretary in Mindelheim.* <note>Adam Reusner (c. 1494–1582) was a German mystic, hymn-writer, and secretary to the military leader Georg von Frundsberg; he was a close associate of Paracelsus.</note><-

The brain and stomach especially ought to be strengthened and comforted, lest they continue further in their mischief. For from the brain you will be afflicted by <term>Arthetica</term> <note>a general term for joint pain or gout</note>, vertigo, pleurisy, and paralysis; from the stomach, <term>Phthisis</term> <note>consumption or tuberculosis</note>, <term>Hydrops</term> <note>dropsy or edema</note>, fever, and dysentery. As far as food is concerned, you shall beware of spices, strong and noble wine, wine seasoned with herbs, garlic, mustard, vinegar, and fish; and this with the greatest care, especially regarding cooked foods.

Abstinence in this case is healthful, provided that neither hunger nor thirst causes torment; let a daily custom be observed at defined and fixed hours.

The cutting of a vein <note>bloodletting</note> or purging is harmful: for it leads you toward paralysis, to headache, and to dropsy.

To wash in hot springs is bad. For by these, <term>fluxes</term> <note>the flow of "humors" or morbid fluids</note> are excessively stirred up into the head by loosening and softening the nerves: from which a fall into gout is more likely. By these, all the limbs of the body are also rendered more sluggish.

<margin>A.</margin> For the head, a potion is to be made from the following things, from which one should drink twice every day, at dawn and towards night, for a month. Through this potion the brain will be restored to itself and reduced to a suitable temperament.

<margin>B.</margin> For strengthening the stomach, always after ingesting food, morning and evening, you shall take as much of this electuary as equals half a walnut.

After taking the electuary, you shall eat nothing more. Use it for a period of two months.

But if, on account of descending fluxes, it should perhaps be necessary to loosen the bowels, you shall take two drachms of tender elder leaves with an equal weight of sugar in the morning. Through this, the fluxes that have fallen into the stomach are removed, with no other ingredients added. And this laxative is free from all harm. However, let it be used only once in the year, namely in May.

This regimen will be sufficient for you for six whole years. When these have elapsed, further advice and aid regarding the state of the diseases must be sought.

<margin>A.</margin> ->*Potion for the brain.*<-

Take: Root of Avens <note>original: "Radix Caryophyllata"; a common herb also called Clove-root</note>.
Sweet Flag <note>original: "Acorus"</note>, half a pound of each.
Elderflowers. Marjoram, one pound of each.
Eyebright, two handfuls.

Let all be placed in a wine cask holding thirty measures. When they have been macerated for eight days, you shall drink of the wine, as we have said. If a smaller quantity of wine must be prepared, a smaller weight of the ingredients should also be taken.

<margin>B.</margin> ->*Electuary for the stomach.*<-

Take one pound of juniper berries. Let them be cooked in water for two hours: afterwards, let the decoction be strained through a cloth and pressed out, so that the skins and seeds are separated. To that which is pressed through the cloth, add an equal weight of sugar. Let it be mixed, and by pounding them together, let these spices be worked in:

Take: Ginger, 1 ounce. Sweet Flag, 2 ounces.
Mace, 2 drachms. Cubebs, 1 drachm.

Let all the mixed ingredients be received in a glass vessel which, being exquisitely sealed, should stand in the sun for one month. Use this according to the prescribed rule. It will do no small amount for strengthening the stomach.

---

## TO THE READER.

> *Theophrastus gave this preceding advice to Adam Reusner, who was at that time acting as the public secretary of Mindelheim, in the year 1535. He promised at the same time that if he used these two prescribed remedies in the defined order and manner, he would have no need of any other physician’s advice for six whole years. Since the aforementioned Reusner (who recounted this outcome in person to the excellent Master Michael Toxites <note>a physician and editor of Paracelsus's works</note> of blessed memory at Memmingen some years ago, when he gave him the opportunity to transcribe this advice) had previously always lived weak and subject to fluxes, and after the use of these remedies subsequently always enjoyed comfortable health and extended a peaceful old age beyond 70 years: I could not fail to mention or add these things here, lest by chance this advice be despised by anyone.*
>
> *Theophrastus wrote the two following pieces of advice to the noble and excellent Master Francis Boner, a Pole living in Kraków, who in that century showed himself to be a Maecenas <note>a generous patron</note> and protector of all learned men. From this, one may divine how great the authority of Theophrastus was among the great men of the land, since his advice was sought and requested from such great distances.*

### ADVICE II. ON HERNIA
#### *To Lord Franciscus Bonerus, a Pole.*

THEOPHRASTUS HOHENHEIM, called Paracelsus, Doctor of Liberal Arts and of both branches of Medicine <note>Referring to the traditional division of "Physic" (internal medicine) and Surgery.</note>, to the most noble and excellent Lord Franciscus Bonerus
->sends many greetings.<-

Most noble and distinguished Lord: I have received, read, and reread the letters written to me by Your Excellency. As far as the medicines used and the dangers endured by Your Excellency are concerned, I have understood them fully. At the same time, I have become more fully aware of the lack of skill in the Physicians and Surgeons who did not understand the matter at the beginning. This first failure of the Physicians is by no means slight—that they did not recognize the disease at the outset; for signs and prognostications of diseases precede them, just as the rising of the heavens precedes the birth of a child.

A child, while still under the fear of a father, can be bent and corrected. But if he has grown up, he often obeys neither father nor executioner. In exactly the same way, all diseases can be cured in the beginning; yet, when they have subsequently gained strength through delay, they can be cured only with the greatest difficulty.

I mention these things here so it may be known that the same has happened to Your Excellency regarding the pain in the scrotum or private parts, since the disease has now degenerated into a <term>fleshy hernia</term> <note>original: "Herniam carnosam"; a term used for a firm, fleshy swelling or tumor in the scrotum, often distinguished from a simple intestinal rupture.</note>, which at first had only been a <term>Napta</term> <note>A Paracelsian term for a soft, fatty, or mucous-like tumor.</note>. That has now become almost incurable, since a certain kind of <term>Elephantia</term> <note>original: "Elephantie"; here referring to a thickening or hardening of the skin and tissue resembling elephantiasis, rather than the specific modern tropical disease.</note> has emerged. Whence it does not seem to me that much progress will be made by our advice.

For this disease cannot be cured according to the advice of the Krakow Physicians. Indeed, it would be a mark of madness to decree advice for a hopeless evil. And I am not slightly grieved that Your Excellency sent a messenger to me across such great distances between places—namely from Krakow to Salzburg—both because of the expenses incurred in vain, and because the Krakow Physicians did not warn you of this damage beforehand.

### ADVICE III.

I have indeed read by what means the disease gained strength, and that the Physicians gave advice without a proper knowledge of the matter. For they drew their remedies and regimen from "cold" things, even though diseases of this kind are nourished by the cold. The same judgment must be made concerning the fact that they attempted to treat Your Excellency by applying Narcotics and Stupefactions, all of which must be judged contrary to a true cure. I shudder, therefore, at the repetition of those things which Your Excellency wrote to me; it is so unworthy that those pieces of advice were given, as I said, without any reason or understanding. For it is truer than truth that Narcotics, Stupefactions, and Cooling agents—which usually consist of the fourth degree <note>In traditional medicine, medicines were graded by "intensity" from 1 to 4; the fourth degree was the most potent and dangerous.</note>—can achieve nothing in the aforementioned diseases. For this reason, even the Physicians who were first consulted about this evil judged the disease incurable.

And yet, although this disease is now near its end and is thus considered incurable, it nevertheless seems to me that it can still be treated; this is because it is not always necessary for a Physician to know or understand the disease itself to a hair's breadth, but it is enough to have known its chief cause and foundation. For it is possible for us to know things that are invisible and enclosed. We know, understand, and possess something in this matter, even if we lack the sight of it itself.

I have given a suitable name to this disease, and according to my understanding, I have designated a cure for it, however brief, as follows:

Seek out somewhere a man who has skill in the art of distilling. Offer him the following Prescription to be prepared.

| Ingredients | Quantity |
| :--- | :--- |
| **♃** <note>The symbol for "Recipe" or "Take".</note> **Opopanax, Serapinum,** | |
| **Ammoniacum, Galbanum** | 1 ounce of each |
| **Oil of the Philosophers** <note>original: "Olei Philosophorum"; a chemically prepared oil, often distilled from bricks or minerals.</note> | as much as suffices |

Let the gums, as is the custom, be dissolved in rose vinegar, and boiled down again, and with the aforementioned oil let them be reduced into the form of a plaster.

Apply this plaster to the entire Hernia for three or four weeks; in a suitable place, an <term>Aposteme</term> <note>an abscess or gathering of purulent matter</note> will eventually collect, which will break by itself and be resolved under this plaster. Once the abscess is open, a "drawing" plaster made of Gums and Colophony <note>a type of resin</note> ought to be applied, many forms of which are found described in my books. In this way, the matter will truly be resolved and expelled. Here, however, I exclude that evil which is fixed in the body and verges toward elephantiasis. Nevertheless, even if it is already a species of elephantiasis, let it still be expelled and the disease diminished.

Furthermore, preventatives against this fixed disease should not be taken internally. For this evil is increased by its contrary, and it relapses into its former state.

In this way, I have defined and established the cure for Your Excellency’s disease, although I have seen neither the person nor the disease more closely than what I understood from Your Excellency’s letters. If the matter is as described, Your Excellency wrote correctly. If not, it is not correctly written. I believe the letters, which were composed according to the custom of Physicians. It matters little, however, if someone perhaps wonders at this unheard-of order of mine. Let Your Excellency see to it that the prescribed plaster is prepared by someone skilled; then a happy success will not be lacking. I have received the gift sent by Your Excellency. With these words, I commend us to God. Given at Salzburg, August 5, in the year 1541.

### ADVICE IV.
#### On Spots or white films of the eyes, given to the Excellent Lord Francis Bonerus for his son.

Most esteemed Lord, I have read the note regarding your son's disease. I judge that this defect of the eyes arose from a certain congenital flux. And thus, there is fear that a more serious evil may emerge from this defect.

It would therefore be advisable, first, for this youth to devote himself to abstinence, and to strive for a selection of suitable foods, and to use a common and well-tested way of living.

As for the sight, my advice is that in the beginning of October, one drop of **oil of the philosophers** (which is "brick oil," a corrected oil, a common oil, twice distilled, as those skilled in chemistry know) be dropped into the eyes morning and evening. This oil removes and consumes spots, clouds, and all defects of the eyes.

### DOCTOR THEOPHRASTUS HOHENHEIM’S
#### explanation of how he treated the Noble Lord, Lord Johann in Leipnick and Moravian Kromau, High Hereditary Marshal of the Kingdom of Bohemia, etc. In the year 1537.

## An attached regimen and order, which Your Lordship ought to follow hereafter.

When Your Lordship <note>original: "Dominatio vestra," a formal address for a nobleman.</note> summoned and sent for me through Lord John of Lottiz Efferdingen, he described Your Lordship's present illness to me. However, because he was unskilled in medicine, he was unable to accurately explain the disease as I later observed it in person. For when I arrived, I recognized a different disease than the one described to me in my absence. If I had known at the very beginning that the condition was as I later saw it—a body so utterly consumed, wasted away, and brought low by various medicines—I certainly would never have undertaken the care of it. In that time, I could have far more easily cured other diseases that fortune might have brought my way from elsewhere. Nevertheless, since these things happened by fate, I cannot deny that I have labored for three whole weeks in investigating this disease, until I could understand it thoroughly from its very foundation. For this reason, no small amount of time has passed. And yet, the matter could not have been hurried more than it was. The truth of this is plain to see. I shall certainly be more careful to avoid undergoing such a risk again. But if that delay in treatment was a burden to Your Lordship, you will easily be able to judge, even if I remain silent, that the matter could not have been finished in a shorter time. Now, however, I will recount to Your Lordship in order what has been achieved by me regarding your afflicted health. For although I have already spoken several times before about the cause and nature of the disease, it seemed untimely to speak too hastily about it.

I found the disease to be of this nature: First, I found the <term>matter of quartan fever</term> <note>A form of malaria where the fever recurs every fourth day; in humoral medicine, it was associated with "black bile" in the spleen.</note>, which had been excessively congested in Your Lordship's spleen. If this had not been drawn out, it would undoubtedly have stirred up a quartan fever, which then, with nothing to stop it, would have been followed by <term>dropsy</term> <note>Edema or swelling caused by excess fluid; often seen as a final stage of organ failure.</note>. Second, I found an overflow of bile into the stomach, such that the bile and the stomach had cast off all their natural constitution and powers, producing pain in the <term>precordia</term> <note>The region of the body over the heart or stomach.</note> as well as other more serious symptoms, already too well known to Your Lordship. The source of these symptoms could never be recognized or removed by any previous physician, but instead was continually accumulated more abundantly. This increase would have been followed by a <term>colic</term> <note>Severe abdominal pain.</note> and a paralytic loss of function in the hands and feet, just as signs of these had already revealed themselves around the navel. Third, congested and collected matter remained stuck in the intestines, which produced winds and flatulence and drove them toward the private parts. Fourth, there was an obstruction in the liver, which changed the urine and added stinging pains in those parts. But Your Lordship does not need to be warned at greater length about these four internal diseases, which you yourself have felt and experienced only too truly. This, then, was the general state of the internal diseases.

As for the external limbs—namely the hands, arms, and feet—first, that <term>podagra</term> <note>Gout, specifically when it affects the joints of the foot.</note> afflicted you, which Your Lordship has suffered for a long time. Then, a general <term>arthritis</term> <note>original: "Arthetica," referring to wandering joint and nerve pain.</note> twitched throughout all the nerves, ligaments, and tendons, by which most parts were strangely weakened and brought low. Third, a paralytic flux occupied the left side, which is why it was more sluggish and numb than the right. These are the diseases I detected in Your Lordship’s body. How I treated them, I will now recount.

In the beginning, I set out to draw out the <term>saburra</term> <note>An old medical term for the "dregs" or accumulated undigested matter in the stomach and intestines.</note> and filth of the body through broths, which I administered and repeated for Your Lordship for some time. To these we also added purging pills for the same purpose. I then applied an ointment for the belly and the left side of the body, with a warm bag placed over it, to remove the matter of the quartan fever and the bile and the obstruction of the liver. Although we persisted with these for some time, we did not yet achieve what was desired. Therefore, I attempted to draw out that foul matter through the upper channels using **gilded pills**, in the use of which we spent several days. By these and the other aforementioned remedies, all the internal diseases were conquered and utterly expelled.

Furthermore, I also prepared a distilled potion, which Your Lordship drank several times with <term>theriac</term> <note>A famous ancient medical "cure-all" and antidote made of dozens of ingredients.</note>, for this purpose: so that all the internal parts might be thoroughly searched, and no hidden abscess might remain. We also added **wormwood wine**, by the use of which, as well as the previously named drink, all the diseases were pulled out from their foundation.

For the external diseases, we applied this care: Against the paralysis, gout, arthritis, and catarrh, etc., that wine was provided which Your Lordship was to drink daily, so that the origin of the evil in the head (where it emerged from the root) might be restrained and subdued. This being done, we applied three ointments: one for arthritis, the second for gout, and the third for paralytic fluxes. When Your Lordship was anointed with these for some time, as is well known, the arthritis was removed at its foundation, along with the progression of the paralysis and gout.

However, to more fully inform Your Lordship about the internal diseases—as to how they stand at this very moment—I boldly assert that nothing of them remains anymore. And the purging of the kidneys, performed several times through the urine, will be visible.

Regarding external matters, the gout will indeed show itself in some way, but more mildly. For since no more "matter" remains, what is left will be consumed through exercise. I cannot deny that small grains of sand <note>Kidney or bladder stones/gravel.</note> also trouble Your Lordship. But these do not have a fixed essence; rather, they are moving toward the exit. Therefore, my advice is that their expulsion be promoted.

The weakness of the body and stomach arises from this cause: that because of the long illness, the body is excessively thinned and consumed. And it is impossible for that weakness to be removed by given medicines, as it will be removed and pass away of its own accord through the progress of time and a suitable diet. Nor is there any doubt that Your Lordship will return to your former strength and old integrity of power. But if Your Lordship does not keep to this order, nature itself will not be strengthened, but the weakness will increase and become more long-lasting. For he who is exhausted by too much walking dispels his weariness by resting, and returns to himself. If he does not rest, he will become more and more exhausted; no other medicine will help more than rest and the cessation of walking. By the same reasoning, Your Lordship must believe that through the following order, the weariness, infirmity, and weakness (which are not diseases in themselves) may be removed and settled.

Your Lordship should also reflect on the various and diverse medicines, contrary to one another, sought so far from different physicians and used by Your Lordship for a long...

...remedies used for too long. For every doctor has followed his own path, but no one has grasped the true nature of the matter in its entirety. Furthermore, excessively long and continuous bed rest has worn down the strength of the body and weakened the power of the limbs. This is by no means the least cause of your present infirmity. However, the following newly established program of exercise and walking will conveniently correct and restore this.

It is also possible that remedies were prescribed to Your Lordship <note>original: "Do. V." (Dominationi Vestrae), a formal address for a nobleman.</note> against obesity which cast down the body’s strength too severely. Medicines of this kind, by their own power, absorb all the vitality in the bones and limbs; sometimes they wear down the body so forcefully that the sick are afterwards forced to lie in bed forever, unable to move forward at all. Your Lordship should therefore avoid their use from now on.

Finally, without a doubt, the remedies themselves were not given at the proper time, but were administered at unseasonable and unfavorable hours. When this happens, the internal nature of the body is provoked as if by a kind of internal war, so that nothing follows except mere infirmity and weakness.

### The following is the order or Regimen <note>original: "Dieta," referring to a total lifestyle and nutritional plan, not just food restrictions.</note> which Your Lordship must use from now on, so that you may enjoy your desired health in the future.

**I**t was right and proper that during the time I stayed here, I should have observed Your Lordship’s usual food and drink. From those things I could have gathered much regarding Your Lordship’s <term>complexion</term> <note>The specific balance of "humors" (bodily fluids) that determined a person's physical and mental health.</note>, habits, nature, and characteristics; this is the reason why all princes and lords like to have their doctors with them. However, since this was not done by Your Lordship, I was able to penetrate the knowledge of your nature only more slowly. As much as I have been able to learn from others so far, Your Lordship’s natural constitution is good: specifically, a <term>sanguine</term> <note>A temperament dominated by blood, associated with a ruddy, cheerful, and active disposition.</note> temperament united with an excellent balance of phlegm. 

Even though your nature was such, many things converged to destroy that goodness: among other things, a rather delicate upbringing, followed by heavier foods that were harmful to that constitution. In this category are also included lying down too late, prolonged sleep, and premature <term>Venus</term> <note>A euphemism for sexual activity.</note>, which was also too frequent before the necessary strength was added to the body. Exercises were also lacking, by which the body might become solid and robust. Indeed, the health of youth depends in no small part on this: that they abstain from women until their 24th year and exercise the body constantly and daily. If this is not done, it follows that nature could not overcome that which a regular exercise routine otherwise shakes out of the body. Furthermore, Your Lordship was raised in poor air, so that you contracted a nature that is not particularly strong or vigorous. Once immoderate sleep, food, and drink were added to this, that disease crept in which Your Lordship has endured for so long. Now that this has been removed, it will be necessary hereafter for the old order to be changed, and for you to live more innocently in a "new world and new sky." I shall now explain the reasoning and method of this change in a convenient sequence.

**First**, you shall never stay awake past nine o'clock in the evening; nor shall you remain in bed past six o'clock in the morning. You shall sit, stand, walk, ride a horse, travel by carriage, and devise various exercises. You shall not sleep during the day, but shall carefully avoid a midday nap, specifically to prevent <term>paralytic flow</term> <note>A contemporary medical term for the "settling" of harmful humors that was believed to cause paralysis or strokes.</note>.

**Second**, Your Lordship shall begin lunch before 11 o'clock and dinner at half-past five in the evening; you shall keep this custom in both summer and winter. If a heavy thirst presses you in the intervening time, you may take one draught, but no more. Let the food not be beef, but something more delicate and younger, of whatever kind; I except pork and goat meat, as well as waterfowl, which are to be studiously avoided. Most other things are permitted to Your Lordship.

Foods should not be seasoned with pungent spices, as the <term>gall</term> <note>Bile; the doctor warns that hot spices "burn" the bile, leading to digestive and temperamental issues.</note> may be inflamed and scorched. However, Saffron, Cinnamon, and Mace are suitable; besides these, none. Let all foods be well-seasoned with salt. For salt both promotes digestion and produces good blood.

For drink, use old wine, not particularly strong, but mild and pure, whether it be red or yellow. Beer should be drunk only later, or rather never, unless a powder of nutmeg is first soaked into toasted bread and added to it.

Every 14 days, you shall use a dry bath <note>Likely a sauna-like heat treatment without water immersion.</note> for six months; afterwards, the body may be washed. Also, every month, <term>scarification</term> <note>A process of making small superficial cuts in the skin, often used with cupping to draw out "bad" blood or fluids.</note> shall be performed on the shoulders with two cupping glasses applied. Four times every year, scarification shall also be performed along the spine with four small cupping glasses. This shall be done first in autumn, second in winter, third in spring, and fourth in summer—specifically during the waning moon, or when it is most convenient for Your Lordship.

Twice a year, <term>phlebotomy</term> <note>Bloodletting.</note> shall be performed on the feet: in the month of May in the veins of the ankle, and in autumn in the veins on the back of the toes, when the signs of **Aries** or **Libra** are shining <note>Medieval medicine timed treatments like bloodletting to the zodiac; Aries rules the head, but Libra and the waning moon were often chosen for balancing the whole system.</note> and the moon is waning.

Your Lordship shall studiously avoid fish and crabs, in whatever way they are cooked or prepared. However, Gudgeons, small Pike, Grayling, and Gilt-head are permitted, though you should eat them rarely and in small quantities. Abstain from fatty foods, fried foods, and all seasonal fruits.

And this diet must be held and continued assiduously and diligently.

---

### The Medicines which Your Lordship must use hereafter now follow.

**S**ince diseases arise easily from any cause, my advice is that the opportunity for disease be blocked for Your Lordship in two primary ways. First, to ward off both internal and external diseases, this is the principal foundation: that Your Lordship refrain from the embrace of women for a full year, or at least during summer and winter. If it happens otherwise, it will newly overthrow all Your Lordship's strength and so trample your nature with fresh damage that the invading diseases will be such as would never have fallen upon you otherwise.

In the future, therefore, only a few medicines need be known, such as the wine which I have prepared for Your Lordship, and an ointment for the hands and feet. Beyond these, nothing. Something must also be spent on the "sands" <note>This likely refers to a treatment for kidney stones or "gravel," a common ailment of the era.</note>, although that need not be observed so scrupulously in private. Through these two noted observances, Your Lordship will be sufficiently and safely equipped for preservation and will not need many others.

Your Lordship should not be surprised that I place all protective power in these two things. For they are sufficient and will work well. I will record the recipes for how they are to be prepared, along with the proper instructions.

I hope that Your Lordship is satisfied with these things. If Your Lordship has also suffered from other even more serious evils until now...

regarding matters not yet revealed to me, should you suffer from them, if you inform me of them, God willing, I shall provide everything required to remedy them. Once a gracious dismissal is obtained, I have decided to move forward. As for how Vienna seems disposed toward me: I stayed there for some time. Meanwhile, through my humble services, I have remained closely connected to Your Lordship <note>original: "D. V." (Dominationi Vestrae)</note>.

### ANOTHER CONSULTATION.

->*Your Lordship shall henceforth observe the following Regimen and diet to prevent*<-
->*Gout, Paralysis, and Pleurisy—that is, an Abscess in the chest. For no other*<-
->*diseases shall weigh upon you from now on.*<-

<margin>
Year 1536.
March 24.
</margin>

**F**irst, great care must be taken that Your Lordship <note>original: "N.V." (Nobilitas Vestra)</note> does not take any purgative that causes more than 6 or 7 bowel movements. Such evacuative medicines should be used no more than twice a year, unless a singular necessity demands it. Even then, no "digestives" or drinks made of syrups should be taken beforehand. For by medicines of this kind, the natural strengths are excessively destroyed, the marrow and parts of the body are afflicted, back pains are stirred up, the kidneys are worn away, the male seed <note>The OCR reads "feminis," but the medical context strongly suggests "semenis" (seed/semen), referring to a loss of reproductive vitality.</note> is dried up, coldness and weakness are brought into the stomach, the liver is scorched with thirst, and the foundation for future dropsy <note>term: dropsy <gloss>an old term for edema or swelling caused by excess fluid</gloss></note> is laid. This is especially true if those purgatives are made from Agaric, Spurge, Hermodactyls, and Turpeth <note>A group of harsh botanical laxatives common in the 16th century.</note>—unless, perhaps, they are mixed with a *Tragea* <note>term: Tragea <gloss>a medicinal powder, often mixed with sugar or spices</gloss></note> which includes burnt reed. In this way, neither Turpeth nor Hermodactyls cause any harm, provided they do not move the bowels more than twice beyond the usual amount. Indeed, this must be diligently observed everywhere: that you take no medicine which moves the bowels more than six times, of whatever kind it may be.

Diligently avoid all hot thermal baths made of sulfur and similar substances. In your case, the baths of Pfäfers <note>original: "Piperinae"</note> and Wildbad <note>original: "Ferinae"</note> are the most suitable of all; however, Your Lordship should not use them until you have been lightly purged beforehand and have had a vein in your foot bled. While bathing, one must strive for abstinence in food and drink, and in sexual matters, which should either be entirely omitted or engaged in most sparingly. And lest any constipation occurs, always have some laxative ready at hand to move the bowels once or twice; the formula for this is noted on the schedule.

Regarding food and drink, a moderate path must be held, so that all excess is cut away; nothing should ever be eaten or drunk except when prompted by hunger or thirst. Let the drink be simple and of one kind. Red wine is more healthful than white. Nevertheless, light white wines are also beneficial. Avoid wines mixed with sage or spices. Beer is not harmful. Avoid mead <note>original: "Melicratum"</note>, gas-forming foods like fruit, and drinking after dinner. Devote yourself to all kinds of exercise, such as riding and walking. Avoid intense activities of the head and brain, serious thoughts, writing, and the like. For these of themselves harm the stomach, stir up "fluxions" <note>term: fluxions <gloss>morbid discharges of fluid thought to flow from the brain to other parts of the body</gloss></note> of the head, excite gouty humors, and provide an occasion for paralysis and vertigo. Fish is also harmful, although it is less damaging if toasted. Fish and meat should not be eaten together. Avoid solid and tough meat, such as pork; avoid freshwater baths as well. Dry baths are suitable, made from Chamomile, Sage, Rosemary, Lovage, Oregano, etc. Avoid the bleeding of the head veins; the disturbance of the others causes no harm. Once a year, the vein corresponding to the lung should be bled in the arm; likewise, bleed the veins that empty the spleen and liver in the little fingers of both hands. For in these, the benefit is not to be despised. Scarification <note>term: scarification <gloss>a method of bloodletting involving small shallow cuts on the skin, often used with cupping</gloss></note> should be continued according to custom and not omitted. If at any time the air is foggy or rainy, or if there is an unfavorable astrological aspect—such as in Pisces, Gemini, or during a new moon—you must avoid with vigilant study all the things we have already prohibited. For such conditions of the air powerfully move and change the body. Therefore, these precepts must be diligently observed.

#### Regarding the order and prevention of an Abscess in the chest or lungs.

**E**very year, for ten or twelve days after the Feast of the Nativity of Christ, one shall drink a draft of the following medicine morning and evening, persisting for four consecutive days. If this is done, Your Lordship will be safe and secure from every such abscess <note>term: abscess <gloss>here referring to an internal collection of fluid or "pleurisy"</gloss></note> in that year—especially if, after the drink, you bleed the lung vein whenever it seems most convenient. This is the description of the recipe:
> ℞ Take: Linctus of fox lung <note>A traditional "sympathetic" remedy: using the lungs of a fox (an animal known for long-windedness) to treat human lung ailments.</note>
> Prepared and tested, 1 ounce each.
> Syrup of Horehound,
> Hyssop,
> Licorice, 1.5 ounces each.
> Waters of Blessed Thistle,
> Endive,
> Speedwell, 2 ounces each.
> Licorice juice, 3 drams.
> Sugar candy, 0.5 ounce. Mix them.

This potion is to be divided into eight or ten parts, for four or five days. Meanwhile, one must abstain from fried foods, eggs, and fatty foods. In this way, those things from which abscesses are born will be entirely consumed, with the superfluities being cast out through coughing. If, however, a very strong cough should happen to occur, which is a sign of an abscess, the same potion should be taken for ten days. In that time, every abscess will be driven out without harm; no more profitable advice can be given to Your Lordship regarding abscesses.

#### Regarding the order and prevention of Paralysis.

**I** have warned above against immoderate purgations. For the nature of Your Lordship can easily be cast into Paralysis by such purges. And although gouty "fluxes" are somewhat removed by them, Paralysis is nevertheless invited by the softening and weakening of the nerves. Therefore, one must strive for the drying of the fluxes and the consumption of humidities through those recipes which I first decreed for Your Lordship, marked with the sign **W**. The more frequently that drink is consumed, the more healthful it is. As for the mass described on the schedule, Your Lordship should obtain it from the Apothecary. From this, you shall swallow one pill every week, whenever it is convenient. This shall be done once every week without fail and never interrupted. Let the pill be the size of a pea.

#### For the Gouty Flux.

**T**he vein of the knee-pit or the ankle is to be bled twice a year, once in summer and once in winter; this shall never be neglected. And since Your Lordship has become so accustomed to purgations that you cannot stop them entirely, I advise that they be conducted henceforth...

### *Advice for the Spouse of Your Lordship.*

The use of the Hot Springs in the coming month of May is the safest and most immediate medicine for her. However, as often as she enters the bath, she shall drink two spoonfuls of the following blended waters. During the time of the bath, she shall observe a distinction in foods. She shall avoid heavy and dense foods, whether prepared from fish or meat; she shall abstain from twice-cooked foods, or those cooked with wine, unless this wine is good and not flat. Vinegar is harmful in all foods. She shall flee from almonds and things made from them. After she has risen from bed in the morning, she shall enter the bath one hour or an hour and a half later, not immediately after finishing sleep. Having left the bath, she shall only dine after an hour. Two hours after eating, she shall enter the bath again, as much as she is able to tolerate. She shall drink mild, tempered wine—white, not red. The waters which ought to be mixed are these: Lemon balm and Pennyroyal, ten spoonfuls of each; twenty spoonfuls of red Mugwort; six spoonfuls each of Speedwell, Blessed Thistle, and Endive. Let them be mixed and well-preserved in a glass vessel so they do not evaporate.

### *Advice for the Maiden Anna.*

She shall also wash in the manner prescribed and shall strive for a similar diet. Furthermore, it would be beneficial if she would taste a little of the medicine written below in the mornings and evenings. These are tablets, of which one is to be swallowed at each time. By the use of these, her monthly courses <note>original: "menses"</note> will be stirred; once these are moved and restored to their former state, it is most advisable that she marry at the first opportunity.

Take: One dram <term>ʒ j</term> of the species of Diasatyrion <note>A traditional tonic made from orchids, often used to stimulate the reproductive system.</note>.
Four scruples <term>℈ iiij</term> of Oriental Saffron.
As much as is sufficient of Savin juice.
One ounce <term>℥ j</term> of fine sugar.
Let them be mixed. Make tablets without fire, and let them be dried in the shade.

## Preparation of Aromatic Wine, white and red, for both summer and winter, by Theophrastus <note>Theophrastus von Hohenheim, known as Paracelsus.</note>
This serves to prevent all "fluxes" <note>Abnormal discharges or flows of humors, such as diarrhea or catarrh.</note>. Its use is one draught in the morning and evening. Red is suitable in summer, white in winter.

<margin>Winter Wine.</margin>
### Winter Wine.
Take: *A stertinum <note>A specific unit of measure or type of container</note> of white wine must. 2 pounds of Acorus <note>Sweet flag</note>. 3 pounds of Herb Bennet <note>Caryophyllatæ</note>. 1 pound of Rhapontic <note>False rhubarb</note>. 1 ounce of Angelica. 1 and a half drachms each of Burnet, Tormentil, and Dittany. Half a pound of Ginger. 2 drachms each of Galangal and Zedoary. 2 and a half drachms of Cinnamon. 5 handfuls of Juniper berries.*
Let all be enclosed in a small bag and suspended in the wine, or placed at the bottom. Pour the must over it. Skim the froth above the bag. As often as you drink from it, fill the vessel up again.

## To the Noble and Valiant man, Jacob Tollinger, Master of Accounts for His Imperial Majesty in Aufsee <note>Likely Altaussee in Austria</note>, Lord: and my singular friend.
Greetings and my services to you, noble Lord Tollinger, etc. I received your letters, in which you ask that I explain the manner in which you should use the pills sent recently with Sixtus. For a reply, therefore, accept these few words. If you feel a "flux" beginning to move, take two pills every morning, as well as before bed. This must be continued for ten days. When these are finished, perform the customary bloodletting. By these means, the flux will be prevented, etc. But if the flux is too strong and headlong, such that it might scorn the aforementioned pills: in their place, I will describe two recipes.

My advice, therefore, is that you pour 8 measures <note>original: "cantharos"</note> of wine into a clean vessel. Into which, throw *half a pound or a pound of Herb Bennet, half a pound of Ginger, and 1 drachm of Cubebs.* Let all stand and soak in the vessel. When, therefore, the constitution of the air is more humid and damp, threatening the danger of fluxes, let one draught of this wine be drunk in the morning on an empty stomach, especially when the Moon is full or new, so that the good wine does not go to waste, etc.

If you should perhaps have need of more medicines at some time, I will communicate them gladly and of my own accord, if you remind me. Greet your wife and daughter dutifully from me. May the Grace of God be with us. Done at Schober, the 15th day of April, the year 1541.

Here I send together two recipes for pills, which you will take care to have prepared when you wish. The second recipe contains stronger pills.
*Pills ordered for the aforementioned Lord Jacob Tollinger by Theophrastus.*

### First Recipe.
Take: *1 drachm each of Aloephangine pills, Cocchia pills, and Arabic pills. 1 scruple of Diagridium <note>A preparation of Scammony, a potent laxative.</note>.*
Mix with sage water. Make into 9 pills per drachm.

### Second Recipe.
Take: *2 drachms of Hepatic Aloe. 1 drachm of Elaterium <note>A juice from the squirting cucumber, used as a purgative.</note>. Half a drachm of Troches of Alhandal <note>Colocynth or bitter apple</note>. 1 drachm of Sagapenum <note>A gum resin.</note>.*
Let them be powdered and mixed into the Sagapenum, dissolved with sage water. Make into 12 pills per drachm.

### Which Theophrastus prescribed for a certain person in Affections of the lungs.
> I place your regimen in three parts. The first is that you maintain the **Iliastrum** <note>A Paracelsian term for the vital essence or the specific "star" or life-force of an organ—here, the lungs.</note> of the lung in its own essence. For otherwise, it will stir up hectic fever and pneumonia in you.
> I also advise that you take diligent account of the ligaments and arteries. For these threaten you with desertion <note>Wasting away or failure of function.</note>.
> Finally, avoid fats, eggs, wine, and fish. Things that come from fresh animals are beneficial.
> Let your foods be mixed with Medicine of Cabbage and Scabious: let salt be tempered by half with Succotrine Aloe: let bread be mixed with an anti-obstruction remedy <note>original: "obstructio," possibly a specific herb or medicinal preparation for clearing blockages</note> in a proportion of a twentieth part.
> It would be very beneficial to avoid anger, and whatever other properties of the bile there are. Imagination <note>original: "phantasia"</note> must also be conquered: for from it is generated trembling of the heart, which is more harmful than all other evils.

### Another Regimen by Theophrastus.
The use of the powder contained in the small box is for pain in the back, for small sands <note>kidney stones/gravel</note>, and for the summoning of urine. The manner of use is as such: as often as the Moon wanes, for five days after its last quadrant, half a drachm of the powder ought to be taken, put into one measure of aromatic wine. This mixture shall be drunk morning and evening, so that in five days the whole measure is drunk up.

### *Explanation of how the oils are to be used.*

This oil, contained in the glass bottle to which a label inscribed with the word **Balsam** <note>original: "Balzimon"</note> is attached, ought to be used in this way against paralysis, against spasms, and other similar diseases.

If it is used against a spasm, it must be heated in a tin dish over coals immediately at the first onset of the attack; with this, the neck should be anointed in the amount of one or two hazelnuts. And the convulsion will cease. Moreover, as often as the malady returns, the anointing must be repeated. It also greatly benefits the <term>paroxysms</term> <note>Sudden attacks or fits.</note> of those with the "falling sickness" <note>original: "caducorum"; a historical term for epilepsy.</note>.

Against paralysis, the use is as follows. In preventing and forestalling it, it is necessary that once every month, two or three warm drops be dripped onto the middle of the crown of the head, where the "cross" is formed <note>Referring to the sutures of the skull or the fontanelle.</note>, and afterwards the area should be rubbed. The best time for this anointing, however, is at the beginning of the signs of **Pisces** or **Aquarius**, during the waning moon.

If paralysis has already occurred, the patient must be anointed on the back of the crown three times daily, and a small amount of the oil should be rubbed into the nostrils and the pulse points near the thumb. And even though a better condition may appear, one must by no means stop, but must continue by anointing the crown twice daily. Furthermore, the healthy limb should be washed with very hot lavender water or water of <term>Spikenard</term> <note>An aromatic essential oil from a Himalayan plant.</note>, while the injured and affected limb should be anointed once daily with the aforementioned **Balsam** while very hot. But if human sensation or reason returns, the lavender water should be omitted, but the anointing with balsam must be continued until the stricken limb returns to its former state.

That water in the glass, on whose attached label is written "**Diaphoretic for acute cases**" <note>original: "Diaphoreticum in peracutis"; a medicine that induces sweating.</note>, is useful and very suitable for all internal abscesses <note>original: "apostematis"</note> of the lungs, liver, spleen, and chest, and it even works greatly against the plague. The method of use is this:

As soon as the disease is felt and is known to be present by its signs, one spoonful of the aforementioned water must be drunk warm; the patient shall then take to his bed and sweat thoroughly. In this way, all the aforementioned internal abscesses will be dissipated and expelled through sweat and urine, unless they tend toward death or the medicine was administered too late.

Likewise, if signs of the dangerous plague are shown, that dose is to be drunk once more, if by chance the first draft is not sufficient for expelling the poison.

Careful attention, however, must be paid to abstinence, especially in food: where one must also avoid wine, heavy water, harsh air, and cold.

But if a good **Theriac** <note>original: "Theriaca"; a famous "universal" herbal jam or electuary used as an antidote to poison and plague.</note> is at hand, one drachm of it should be skillfully mixed with the stated dose of water and drunk in the manner we have described. But if the plague breaks out externally <note>i.e., as a bubo or sore.</note>, it must be opened and healed with a suitable plaster, such as the one I have frequently sent to you in part with Sixtus. Through this, the poison is extracted from the root, nor does the ulcer close up before the proper time, which the medicines of common surgeons are accustomed to do. The plaster must be renewed and changed every 12 hours.

Furthermore, Noble Sir <note>original: "N. V."; likely *Nobilitati Vestrae*.</note>, I have ordered a triple purgation for three potential future diseases. One has the form of **burning wine** <note>original: "vini ardentis"; distilled spirits or brandy.</note>; the second of **pills**; the third of an **electuary** <note>A medicinal paste made with honey or syrup.</note>. The burning wine is to be used thus: If a <term>catarrh</term> <note>Excessive buildup of mucus.</note> should fall into the chest, causing pains in the sides, difficult breathing, great thirst, loss of appetite, and foul breath: half a spoonful of this wine is to be drunk today, and tomorrow the same amount again. But if one spoonful is sufficient and works vigorously, the second should be skipped, and the purgation taken; otherwise nothing, unless the aforementioned warning signs appear—no matter what zodiac sign the moon is in, though I except **Aries** and **Leo**.

The purgation in the form of an electuary is to be taken if vomiting of the stomach urges, and back pains begin, and the bowels are obstructed, causing colic, and the urine is changed. The dose of the electuary to be taken should be 3 drachms, which is to be swallowed in the morning. When you have endured a fast of three hours, you may eat afterwards. If, however, it has not worked enough by the 12th hour, 4 more drachms should be swallowed with wine or by itself after taking food. Thus it will happen that those occurring diseases are conquered. And if by chance some fever were also imminent, it would be conquered in this same way.

The method for using the pills is this: If some "filth" <note>Impurities or morbid humors.</note> has collected internally in the body, whether in the chest or intestines, etc., it will be expelled if three pills are swallowed toward nightfall, and this is continued for three or four days. This may be repeated as often as such congested filth appears during the year. And as necessity seems to demand, it is enough if the prescribed dose is taken for two nights, or even just one.

In addition, I grant two other medicines to Your Lordship <note>original: "N.T."; likely *Nobilitati Tuae*.</note>, with instructions on how they ought to be used.

Furthermore, I have prepared a certain peculiar kind of pill which will be especially beneficial to Your Lordship. And my advice would be that these be used first of all, and the others reserved for future cases.

I have also sent separately in another glass an oil with which the others may be mixed, but especially that which works for paralysis. If help is needed for others, I will send it if I am notified. Likewise, if colic twists the belly, let the oil which Your Noble Sir sent to me in a glass be taken and warmed. Let several drops of it be dripped into the middle of the navel, and furthermore, let wool soaked in that oil be applied very hot to the navel; let this use be repeated four or five times, and thus the evil will cease.

Secondly, if anyone is obstructed and is <unclear>unable</unclear> to take medicines from above, nor can bear the "Elements" <note>Possibly referring to harsh elemental medicines or primary humors.</note>, concerning this ointment, which [must be] sought from the pharmacy—

->### Another Regimen by Paracelsus.<-

My advice regarding your disease is this: that you use preventatives as long as you can, namely a laxative powder and bloodlettings. For you are wonderfully prone to <term>fluxes</term> of the head and an abundance of blood. This purging and bloodletting ought to be done four times every year, as the following explanation will show.

From that prescription described in the schedule and marked with the letter **L**, when the moon is waning in the primary purgative signs, you shall take 2 drachms <note>original: "ʒ ij."</note> on toasted bread for two or three days in the morning on an empty stomach, and you shall fast for at least two hours: in this way, the bowels will be gently moved. The same should be done similarly on the second day: and the dose may be either increased or decreased, depending on whether the first worked too strongly or too weakly. The third day shall be regulated in the same way. This should be done at the beginning of Spring, Summer, Autumn, and Winter, if the signs are included in the waning moon.

Regarding <term>phlebotomy</term> <note>bloodletting</note>, you shall conduct yourself as follows. After the aforementioned purging has been completed, at the next following new moon, at the very first point of the new moon, you shall cut the right <term>salvatella vein</term> <note>a vein on the back of the hand near the ring and little finger</note> and extract enough blood. After the second purging, you shall bleed the left salvatella. After the third purging, the inner vein of the right calf: after the fourth purging, you shall cut the inner vein of the left calf, and thus you will lead nature into a habit.

An order of this kind preserves one from <term>gout</term> <note>original: "podagram"</note> and blunts its malice and force. If, however, a more certain protection is desired, I have described another powder in a separate schedule, marked with the letter **X**, which you shall use in the intervening time, after the purging and bloodletting have been performed. Its use is 1 drachm taken morning and evening on toasted bread throughout the entire year. By this powder, gout is prevented and warded off, so that it cannot afflict you for the entire following year.

I have also composed another prescription, marked with the letter **W**, which you shall hang in wine, and drink two drafts of it daily at the table.

---

By these, the fluxes in the head will be consumed, and I would wish them consumed in the joints as well, wherever they lie. In the schedule, there is also described an ointment marked with the letter **S**, with which the hands and feet are to be anointed three days after the purging, which anointing ought to be continued for four days. The anointing should be done in the evening, upon going to bed, in a warm place.

If you maintain this order, you will be secure from the infestation of gout. This is my advice regarding preservation. As for food and drink, you yourself know their moderation. Above all, you shall avoid four things: strong wine that tests the head; deceptive and luxurious foods; anger; and women. The greater the abstinence from these, the healthier it will be.

# THEOPHRASTUS PARACELSUS THE GERMAN,
->### supreme philosopher and physician, his explanation of the first section of the Aphorisms of Hippocrates, as well as the first six of the second section and the last nine of the fourth section.<-

->### Also another Explanation of the first Aphorism.<-
->### First Section, First Aphorism.<-

> *Life is short, art long, opportunity fleeting, experiment perilous, judgment difficult: but it is not enough for the physician to have done his duty, unless the patient also does his, and the attendants theirs, and external things are properly arranged.*

<margin>What was the age of Methuselah?</margin>
That our life is short, no one can deny, even if it is written of certain people that they lived a very long time: namely, Methuselah 900 years; but it is not proven that these were <term>Milesian years</term> <note>Solar years of 365 days, attributed to the calculations of Thales of Miletus.</note>, but perhaps shorter periods from sunrise to sunset. For the royal Prophet David says: "our age is eighty years, the rest is labor and misery." This saying speaks of Milesian years, and it can reach ninety: David himself testifies only to eighty Milesian years, not to 900.

<margin>The year of Thales of Miletus was 365 days: see aphorism 14. What of Anaximenes?</margin>
If, therefore, the life of men is only 80 years, it is certainly a short number, which certain birds far exceed, though they are of less value than man. But just as the Moon, if it lasted longer, would achieve nothing good, yet can complete all good things in one month and then be renewed: so also man has his limit, which he does not exceed.

<margin>Physicians note the prolongation of human life by years.</margin>
And although medicine was created for the length of our life, so that we might reach eighty years, and furthermore even the years of labor and misery: nevertheless, if the physician cannot drive away the diseases that bring us death, it is necessary that our life be short, quite apart from the fact that we ourselves shorten our own lives.

<margin>What was the age of Christ?</margin>
<margin>What is human life?</margin>
Christ also reached the 32nd year of his age, as far as I have understood, which was certainly a short time: therefore no life can be long among us; it is utterly denied to us. For we are dust, smoke, nothing else but a shadow passing daily, and a bubble on the water. Our life, therefore, is short if it be compared with others. Gold and silver remain even until the final fire, as do minerals,

stones, salts, etc. Man, however, does not endure; he has the shortest limit of all and no certain time of death—indeed, he ought to expect that end every day. For that which attacks man secretly spares other creatures.

<margin>A Physician should be an Astronomer.</margin>
The physician should be an astronomer <note>In the 16th century, "Astronomy" included what we now call Astrology—the study of how celestial bodies influence human health.</note>, lest he neglect time so blindly and reveal his own ignorance. For if time can bring forth and perfect rains, roses, flowers, and other things from beginning to end with nothing to stop it: it will likewise finish diseases according to its own will. Since time can do these things, the physician must certainly consider them, so that he knows what is possible and what is impossible, and understands what he must do. This prevents the art which God created from being blamed, and prevents the patient from faring worse—something God by no means desires. Time is sharp <note>original: "Tempus acutum"; a translation of the Greek "kairos" or "fleeting opportunity."</note>: for every hour it brings something new, just as a man’s thoughts change from hour to hour throughout the twelve hours of the day. No one can know them except for one alone <note>referring to God</note>; likewise, time always brings something new. Who can perceive its intended sharpness and secret counsel? Therefore, the Physician should not attribute too much to himself. For he has a master superior to him, namely Time, which plays with the Physician like a cat with a mouse.

<margin>The power of Time.</margin>
<margin>Time rules the Physician.</margin>

->*But art is long.*<-

<margin>Why the Medical Art is long.</margin>
It is true that the Art is long in this way: it began at the start of the world and has been sought until my own time, and yet no end has been found. Disease is fast, but art is slow, and thus the patient is neglected. For physicians have not yet reached the end of the art, and the tools they have are so slow that the disease overcomes the art with its speed. Therefore, Hippocrates rightly complains about this, for the same thing happened to his own patients.

<margin>What the Medical Art consists of.</margin>
The medical art consists of Philosophy, Astronomy, Alchemy, and Physics <note>These are Paracelsus's famous "Four Pillars" of medicine: the study of nature, the stars, chemistry, and the physical body.</note>: it can therefore rightly be said that the art is long. For much time is required to learn and investigate these four columns of medicine. And just as there is no flight without wings, so it is in medicine. Before the wings grow, much time slips away until the art is perfected. For the sick person, the art is long because they are cured slowly by it. However, "art" and "medicine" differ. Art is slow, namely so that we may recognize diseases and their remedies. Medicine, however, is fast: the cause [of its perceived slowness] lies in the errors and meanderings of medical practice. But to tell the truth, the art is brief, but learning it is long. It is worth noting that errors existed even in the time of Hippocrates. Hence he says, "art is long," meaning that more is applied than is necessary. Art is short: the knowledge of the true physician demonstrates this. But erroneous art is long: for those who investigate it never reach any certain end. Therefore, what Hippocrates said in this place, he did not say without cause. For the investigation was with him, but the gift of the "end" <note>the final, perfect knowledge of the art</note> was not granted to him. Therefore, Hippocrates died before the art was finished. Art is long, but life is short. But where the gift of the "end" is found, there art is short; and life is long, if compared to the art.

<margin>How Art and Medicine differ. The Medical Art is full of meanderings for those who [do not] have the gift of truth, and do not dwell in medical meanderings. What kind of man Hippocrates was among Physicians.</margin>

->*Time is sharp.*<-

<margin>What influence is. How great the power of influence is.</margin>
Just as time afflicts a naked man, now in winter, burning him with cold, now in summer, with heat; so time brings now rains, now snows, now moisture, now dryness; it makes the air now calm, now windy. Similarly, this "influence" <note>referring to astral or environmental forces</note> works inside a man. For influence is time, and time gives birth. Influence, moreover, has manifold power in its rays and impressions, as Hippocrates—being a skilled astronomer—well knew and considered: namely, that the interior is ruled by the exterior. Therefore, "time is sharp." For it gives birth to all diseases, all symptoms, and all adversities. This saying therefore means that the physician must be an astronomer and observe the time, so that he may know how it rules and will rule, and through what means. It is not enough to contemplate today, but also tomorrow, and all those to come after it, from the beginning to the end, so that from the time, the physician may gather what he must do.

->*Experiment is deceptive.*<-

<margin>Why experience is deceptive. The nature of women is more favorable. What experience is.</margin>
Hippocrates says that experience can be deceptive, as if he were saying: do not trust your experience too much. For it is just the same in the Physician's hand as a woman’s heart is in the hand of a lover, who believes he has it, but often does not. For no trust is to be placed in a woman, and likewise none in experiments <note>This comparison reflects common 16th-century gender prejudices used as metaphors for uncertainty.</note>. This is the opinion of Hippocrates. Nevertheless, the art and the help of the sick come from experience. It must not be false, but rather certain and practiced. For both it and the Physician were created by God. But if medicine were deceptive, this would not recommend Medicine; rather, it would diminish its reputation, and thus medicine would be turned into nothingness, which is far from the truth. Just as a wife ought to live faithfully with her husband in marriage: so also medicine ought to be joined to the physician by a marital bond of faith. Then it is not at all deceptive. But what confirms a marriage? And what is marriage? Nothing but the knowledge of the heart—this is the beginning and the end. So also the physician and Medicine ought to know each other. Then no deceptions will be in them. But where there is no understanding, there is trickery and falsehood on both sides. In the time of Hippocrates, it was not so in medicine: indeed, colocynth <note>a powerful, often toxic purgative made from a type of bitter cucumber</note> was given to all horses; it helped one and destroyed the other. Therefore, it was called deceptive by him: the cause is that mutual knowledge between the two was lacking. Indeed, they acted like "pustule-doctors" <note>likely a derogatory term for quacks who treat only surface symptoms like skin sores</note>, who anoint everyone with the same ointment. Hippocrates speaks here of such trickery. This is how medicine was in the beginning: it had no theory, but only experience—to loosen this, to constrict that—but how and why, that was unknown. Therefore one was saved, another destroyed. But now, since medicine has theory, it is no longer so; indeed, science is present and experiment is no longer deceptive but true. This is accomplished by medical theory, which rests on the four pillars: Philosophy, Astronomy, Alchemy, and Physics.

<margin>What kind of marriage exists between Medicine and the Physician. What marriage is.</margin>

<margin>Experience without reason is worth nothing.</margin>

->*Judgment is difficult.*<-

Hippocrates' opinion is this: Since he said life is short, so that a physician cannot be perfected in his art so quickly...
