### Annotations on the final clinical type.

**The Eyes)** When they sink into depth, that is, when they collapse into themselves, it is a sign of death. For when death comes from the brain, it is dissolved into a crystalline liquid, and that is death.

**Azure)** It should be noted that these colors appear more quickly than the sinking into the depth. Moreover, Azure is the color that silver gives when it is resolved into its first and proper color—that is, azure—just as the "oryzeus" color <note>original: "orizeus"; likely referring to a golden or rice-like yellow</note> is a purplish-yellow.

**The Pores)** When the skin becomes rough and falls into a depth—that is, a hollow—it is a sign of death.

**Tenesmus)** <term>Tenesmus: A distressing and continual urge to evacuate the bowels.</term> When the anus wishes to go out with force. By its harshness, it becomes rough and sharp.

**Ceruse color)** White like ceruse <note>Ceruse: a white lead pigment; here indicating a deathly, unnatural pallor</note>, a sign of death.

**In reverberation)** If they become rough, as if they were scraped or filed with a file, which quite often happens. If this occurs three weeks before death, it is a sign of death.

**With discolored roots)** Such as those of the nails, hairs, soles, and teeth; if these are discolored, whatever color they may be, it is a sign of death.

Likewise, if the forehead takes on a white color.

**The Hairs)** When they are turned back—that is, they become inverted—it is a sign of death.

**Ocher)** The color of the body <note>original: "Ogrum"; likely referring to a sallow or ocher-like skin tone</note>.

**In shriveling)** <note>original: "acatia"</note> That is, a wrinkling. A contraction, which is a tension.

**Colors)** When these members alone are colored and the neighboring parts are not, they mostly descend into a reddish-purple.

**Monis)** The buttocks.

**Summary of all signs.** In the eyes, one must observe whether they fall into depth or not; if they do, the case is already desperate, especially if the pulse is also erratic.

Next, when the nose becomes sharp and turns white at the tip, it is a sign of death.

**The Mouth** if it is opened, that is, if yawning occurs.

**The Teeth** become spaced out and appear long.

**The Flesh** of the gums turns black.

**The Skin** becomes an ash color, or a yellowish-blue.

However, the greatest despair is when it tends toward redness, especially in the face and jaws.

**The Air)** That is, the breath; if it stinks, or if it is accompanied by color, it is a sign of death.

**Speech** when it begins to stutter, it is dangerous; or when one cannot utter complete words but rushes through them.

**The Smoke of the breath)** When they draw breath from deep within.

# ANOTHER SHORT TREATISE
## ON URINES, TRANSCRIBED
### from the original manuscript of Theophrastus.

->*To his dearest listeners.*<-

->Th. B. H. Doctor and Physician. <note>Theophrastus Bombastus von Hohenheim, the birth name of Paracelsus.</note><-

## On Urines.

<margin>Urine is the index of the constitution of the members.</margin>
**WHATEVER** is brought into or imparted to the body from its members is shown by the urine in such a way that the faults and affections of the body can be clearly discerned from it. It is the duty of the physician, therefore, before all things, to acquire for himself a knowledge of the members—what they are and which they are. At the same time, he shall consider that every single member has its own **Yliadum** <term>Yliadum: In Paracelsian philosophy, this is the fundamental vital essence or spiritual matter that gives a specific organ its form and power.</term> which is potent in its own form and essence.
<margin>The Yliadum is in all members.</margin>
Once these things are known beforehand, he will easily recognize the faults of the member's **Yliadum**. But as to what its accidents and symptoms may be, the sick man indicates those. Let the physician, however, rest his case on the cause, the location, and the specific property.

<margin>What must be observed in examining urine.</margin>
2 Therefore, he who is about to inspect the urine should observe three things or think upon three things. First, that there are some diseases whose magnitude and malice—as well as their thickness, region, location, and beginning—can be recognized through their chaos <note>Chaos: used here to mean the medium or the surrounding atmosphere/substance of the disease</note> by means of color.

2 The second is more subtle than what can be seen by the eyes in the urine. These are the tartaric diseases <term>Tartaric diseases: Illnesses caused by the "salt" or metabolic deposits in the body, such as stones or gout.</term>. If you wish to see and know these in the urine at all, you must set aside the first rule and do this: coagulate the urine and separate it into its types. Only then will the diseases become known to you.
<margin>Urine is equivocal.</margin>
3 The third, different from the others, is this: it sometimes happens that the two aforementioned rules regarding urine cannot indicate the man's diseases. In that case, the urine is "equivocal" <note>Ambiguous or misleading</note>, which indicates a poison or a coagulated tartar; these two do not enter the urine, or they are mixed with it but separated from it. 
And from these three rules, the urine is especially to be judged. He who does not know these knows nothing. And he who judges by any other way acts as a fortune-teller and a trifler. For if a disease does not appear in the urine, then it is either a poison or a separated tartar, which are two diseases that do not imprint their traces upon the urine.

## CHAPTER I.

**First**, the colors in the urine must be noted. But before all things, healthy urine—of men as well as women, of the old and the young—must be known. Afterwards, the urine of those same people when they are sick.

# ON JUDGMENT

<margin>
Urine is of two kinds.
</margin>
...and so it is collected and unified from all parts into a single manner. If this urine is "solitary" <note>meaning urine produced by the body's internal state alone</note>, the Physician will discern health from it. But besides this, another kind of urine must be noted: that which travels from the stomach through the liver into the kidneys, and from there into the bladder. From this latter kind, diseases are judged that arise from food, revealing their nature and specific properties.

Therefore, for this consideration, two kinds of urine must be inspected: internal and external. Regarding these, the specific diseases belonging to each must be correctly distinguished—which ones are subject to which kind of urine—so that one does not wander blindly in delivering a judgment. For internal urine gives evidence of a disease of nature from the 
<margin>
What is internal urine.
What is external urine.
</margin>
<term>Yliadus: A Paracelsian term referring to the spiritual or elemental essence of the body’s internal nature.</term> External urine gives evidence of diseases falling upon the body from the outside, but specifically through the "tincture" <note>the color or quality imparted by what is consumed</note>. Thus, urine should be collected before fasting and during the fast itself. In this way, you possess a twin judgment.

Now, concerning external urine, the judgment is that you observe the three aforementioned rules; likewise for internal urine, which must be observed in the same way: first according to the colors and what is contained within them; second, its coagulation and separation, and what arises from these; and finally, its "equivocal" nature. We shall hand down instructions on these matters in what follows.

### CHAPTER I.

### On the colors of healthy external urine: or on the colors of a healthy external state in the urine.

As far as external urine is concerned: the first is that of the healthy. From its condition and power, it must first be known whether the stomach digests well or poorly. For this shines forth from the urine: if it digests well, its "salt" is in that place and state where it ought to be. If not, the opposite is true.

### ON EXTERNAL URINE.

<margin>
The source of separated and digested urine.
</margin>
Regarding external urine, note that things taken in or ingested are first separated, and then digested. From these processes, such urine is produced. If indeed those things are correctly separated by the <term>Archeus: The "inner chemist" or vital force that governs the body's functions.</term>, then "separated urine" is produced. If they are correctly digested, the urine comes out "digested." In the same way, if the expulsive power drives it out correctly, the urine comes out "perfect" with its signs. If all these things are done correctly, the urine will also be "correct" as far as the stomach is concerned. If, however, there is indigestion, you shall make your judgment from this.

### We shall know it in this way.

<margin>
How separation is estimated.
How color in urine is to be estimated.
</margin>
Separation must certainly be recognized from healthy urine in this way: healthy urine in its separation, digestion, and expulsion ought to behave correctly in the stomach. These three consist in the colors as follows: if it is correctly separated, the <term>Spirit of Sulfur: Representing the combustible, oily, and vital qualities in Paracelsian medicine.</term> exhibits a golden color, that is, the color of a Ruby or of distilled oil. When this color appears, separation in the stomach is happening correctly regarding the Spirit of Sulfur. Now, however, if that color is changed and becomes another, then the Spirit of Sulfur is lacking or not present; therefore the colors of Salt and Mercury emerge, which should by no means predominate. But let us proceed to the Salt. If the urine deposits a <term>Hypostasis: The sediment or suspended matter that settles at the bottom of a urine sample.</term>, 
<margin>
What the sediment (hypostasis) of urine signifies.
</margin>
the Salt is correctly separated. For Salt is mixed with the sediment. If the sediment is lacking, the separation of Salt in the stomach is lacking. Similarly, if there is a heavy "base" or dregs at the bottom of the urine, the <term>Mercury: Representing the volatile, fluid, and vaporous qualities in the body.</term> is correctly separated. If not, its separation has not occurred.

And let these words suffice concerning separation regarding the stomach.

As for digestion, you shall note these things.

<margin>
How digestion is judged from urine.
</margin>
If the urine is thick, fatty, or thin, the Spirit of Sulfur is not digested. If it has a broken or scattered sediment, or is thinner or thicker than normal, etc., the Salt is not digested. If the base or dregs be thin, light, etc., the Mercury is not digested.

<margin>
How expulsion is to be judged.
</margin>
Regarding expulsion, if there is a moderate balance of the urine according to the three mentioned signs, then it is a healthy expulsion. If not, expulsion is lacking, and it is expelled more sluggishly than is right. For these three signs consist only in a proper measure of moderation.

By signs of this kind in the urine, you ought to know what external thing taken into the stomach is doing, or what is happening around it. Once that is known, you know the health of the stomach. If, however, no sickness is noted: for the signs of disease are different.

### The condition of the Liver.

<margin>
How the Three Primes behave in the liver.
</margin>
The same likewise happens in the liver, yet with this reasoning: that the three mentioned signs are altered there. For in Sulfur, transparent colors are innate. If those are not present, and the "Ruby" <note>deep red</note> is ready at hand, then the Mercury is correctly separated from the Sulfur. The liver, however, lets go of the Spirit of Sulfur. Thus, if the sediment has a peculiar color, separation would similarly be lacking in the Salt. Likewise, if the heavy dregs are discolored, separation in the liver does not occur.

This is the reasoning for digestion: If the color is intact, without thickness, the Sulfur is correctly digested. If not, poorly. Similarly, if the sediment is round, the Salt is correctly digested. If otherwise, poorly. Likewise, if the base is clear and heavy, the Mercury is correctly digested. If not, poorly. The same is true of expulsion, according to how the measure behaves in the aforementioned signs. For if nothing, or not much, is lost from it, the expulsion is strong and correct.

### The condition of the Kidneys.

<margin>
How the Three Primes behave in the kidneys.
</margin>
The judgment regarding the kidneys is also the same. If the color of the urine is "specular" <note>mirror-like or highly reflective</note>, let the Sulfur be judged as correctly separated in that place. And if the sediment has its own distinct colors in its substance, the Salt is correctly separated. The same is true of digestion. If the color in the "circle" <note>the upper rim or meniscus of the urine</note> is Ruby-colored, the Sulfur is correctly separated. If the sediment is pointed or sharp, the Salt is correctly separated. If the base is thin, the Mercury is correctly separated. Furthermore, if the urine in the circle is transparent, the Sulfur is correctly digested in the kidneys. If the sediment is porous, the Salt is correctly digested. If the base is transparent from the bottom to the top, the Mercury is correctly digested. Expulsion is estimated by quantity.

### Summary on Healthy Urine.

If the best signs appear in the urine, such that the color is transparent at the sides, the sediment is porous and compressed, and the base is clear from top to bottom: then separation, digestion, and expulsion are in the best condition and are free from fault.

### Note.

It also frequently happens that the urine sometimes fails in one area—either digestion, separation, or expulsion—and that either in the stomach...

## TREATISE II.

<margin>
The principal diseases recognized from urine.
</margin>
Furthermore, if any of the aforementioned qualities are different from what has been handed down concerning healthy urine, it must then be considered with merit. For from this, all diseases that arise from external things are known. Here, one must simultaneously observe the region and place in which they reside. Afterward, the nature, property, essence, and condition of the disease itself must be understood. This too is known from the urine, as are life and death themselves.

### On Recognizing Tartar from External Urine.

<margin>
How Tartar is to be known from urine.
</margin>
**A**ny tartaric urine <note>In Paracelsian medicine, "Tartar" refers to stony or sandy deposits that "precipitate" in the body, much like tartar in a wine barrel, causing stones, gout, or blockages.</note> cannot be perfectly recognized by colors alone. For those colors belong to the first treatise. Fundamental knowledge, however, is situated in distillations and coagulations. Once these are performed, Tartar is readily displayed. Tartar is recognized in this way: if the urine is separated—that is, if it falls away from its proper proportion and appearance—Tartar is revealed. This happens in the following way: through particular separation into sand, grains, or a total liquid—that is, granular urine, liquid urine, and <term>Alkalized urine</term> <note>original: "Alkolita"; a Paracelsian term for urine affected by the digestive salts of the stomach</note>. These three urines display Tartar. The location is known thus: Alkalized urine belongs to the stomach; Liquid belongs to the liver (it is a separation of the kidneys and liver); Granular belongs to the kidneys.

Three species of Tartaric urine. To which part Alkalized, Liquid, and Granular urines belong.

# OF JUDGMENTS

<margin>The urine of gore as a certain indicator</margin>
Urine also exhibits foam, and so on. The same is to be judged regarding the other organs as well. For in this case, all the organs are able to pour their own gore <note>original: "cruorem"; here referring to the vital, internal essence or "clotted" component of the blood</note> into the center according to the design of nature. If we were to lack this "urine of gore," we would be unable to distinguish any disease of these organs from the other types of urine. It is evident, therefore, that it is entirely appropriate for the urine to be collected alone and through a period of abstinence. In this way, it will happen that the fault of whatever organ may be is thoroughly recognized, as will be passed down hereafter.

Before all things, however, one must know what this "gore" is; just as one must also inquire about the other type of urine. This shall be done in the following discourse.

<margin>What is the urine of gore? All urine is dissolved salt.</margin>
Every urine is **Resolved Salt**, arising from the salts of the "Three Primes" <note>The "Three Primes" (Tria Prima) are Salt, Sulfur, and Mercury—the fundamental building blocks of matter in Paracelsian alchemy.</note>, which discharge themselves into the bladder by way of purging. For there is no other moisture in the whole body looking for an exit except that which emerges from resolved salt: which itself also arises in part from the blood. Therefore, if the blood is sick, its "gore" comes out sick. If the flesh is sick, it is similar, and so on. The same is also true for the rest. And all urines are as one, except that which arises from fat and marrow, which is a liquid floating upon the urine, as will be treated in its own proper chapter.

<margin>What is the urine of fat and marrow?</margin>
Furthermore, the gore in its own body or substance is similar to its own organ; that is, the "resolution" <note>The process by which solid or complex matter breaks down into liquid form.</note> is not equal, but as many organs as there are, so many are the resolutions. Each resolution, therefore, remains separate from the others, which must be diligently observed.

<margin>Resolution is manifold.</margin>
Thus, urine is also the indicator of **Local Anatomy**, and is called the **Microcosmic Anatomy** indicator—that is, just as every organ lies in the body, so also its liquor of salt or resolved salt lies in the same place without mixing. From these things, now pay attention to the **Tartar** of the urine. For it can seize other parts. From which it follows that, in this case, the urine does not indicate the location. It indicates the disease, certainly, but not the location. For the **Tincture** <note>In this context, "tincture" refers to the specific medicinal or vital color/essence extracted from a substance.</note> of the salts discolors the differences.

<margin>What is the nature of the Tartar of urine, etc.</margin>
Therefore, with this caution, the urine must be exactly inspected so that the organ may be thoroughly known, and by what fault it is held. For every organ has its own peculiar sign in the urine, which pertains to it alone. For every organ also has its own peculiar disease, which is recognized through that sign. It happens, however, that four or six diseases may cling to a single organ, all of which, as far as the sign is concerned, are accepted as one disease. Thus, for example, in the brain there is **Mania**,

<margin>Certain organs have both their own peculiar sign and disease.</margin>
**phrenesis** <note>delirium or brain fever</note>, headaches, **Hemicrania** <note>migraine</note>, and so on, all of which have only one sign. The distinction, however, by which they may be recognized from one another, is not very difficult, and will be handed down in its proper place. Similarly, this must also be known concerning all the organs.

In the urine, moreover, both the density and the transparency and clarity of every organ must be diligently and curiously considered. Afterward, even its colors, all of which are contained in the urine. Yet the smallness and subtlety of the location of that transparency is seen with difficulty. Nevertheless, the locations and the good colors must be entirely known.

<margin>All colors in the urine</margin>
Thus, the decoloration of that place from which any urine proceeds will easily appear. The difference in the **Womb** and the breasts, and the singular nature of the woman herself, must also be maintained. For these too have their private places, for which they must be recognized. These, however, are to be judged from the interior urine alone, without the mixing of the exterior. For the exterior obscures and adulterates it. For this reason, a general treatise will follow elsewhere, which must be read entirely. For it is directed toward all mixed urines, or to the common signs that exist in urine.

<margin>Which colors of which parts appear in urine.</margin>
First, therefore, it must be understood regarding colors that every organ in its own region pours out its own colors: namely, the **brain** white, the **spleen** ashen-gray: the **Kidneys, heart, liver, lungs, and the sides** (with discretion of colors, however); the **blood** a transparent redness; the **marrow** a fatty thing or fat, which floats by its own nature. Therefore, it cannot remain in its own place or region. Likewise, the **flesh** does not have one color throughout the whole body. The **ligaments** have nothing; they are not **humors**; these things, however, are explained more fully in the book written about excrements.

Therefore, the colors in the urine <note>original: "lotio", literally "wash" but used as a synonym for urine</note> are to be recognized from these colors of the organs. For if the color is "cardial" <note>of the heart</note>, then the tincture proceeds from the heart. If "hepatic," it proceeds from the liver, and so on for the others. And if whiteness, from the brain, etc.; except for the urines concerning excrement, which have their own as has been said.

<margin>The tincture of every organ must be observed.</margin>
From these colors, therefore, the judgment must be directed to whatever organ. Thus, the disease will be correctly and entirely established, and the same will be properly healed. Give your effort diligently to this, therefore, so that you may know the tincture of every organ. And judge any organ from that color, or pronounce upon its disease. Hereafter, we will set forth the tincture of every organ.

# ON URINES.
->GREETINGS TO THE READER.<-

*There now follow, dear Reader, certain other observations on these same books regarding Urines, Pulses, and Medical Physiognomy. These are twofold, having been recorded and written down in various ways by different students of Paracelsus while he was lecturing. This is a common occurrence in Academies: one student might note something more copiously, while another more succinctly, and so on. Even though these following sections agree in some places with the preceding ones, there are nevertheless many things here which were not contained in the earlier parts; indeed, many things are spoken of here more clearly and openly which were previously stated more briefly and obscurely.*

*Since all these notes could not be forced into a single book without a significant alteration of the words (which I have taken special care to avoid in this edition), I believed I would be doing something far more pleasing and useful for young students if these were published separately. For those things which are sought out with a bit more labor through a studious comparison of these observations—and gathered together in the mind—will stick more firmly in the memory. Let everyone, therefore, use these with fruitfulness according to their own industry, etc.*

# ON JUDGMENTS OF URINES AND PULSES:
->LIKEWISE,<-
### ON MEDICAL PHYSIOGNOMY, OTHER
->*certain Annotations.*<-

### On the First Treatise of the First Book.

<margin>Urine is threefold. Three excrements of food. What sign gout shows in urine. What diseases the urine of blood-essence indicates. What signs are in the urine of tartar and blood-essence. The urine of Tartar is twofold.</margin>
## CHAPTER I.

**I**T MUST be noted above all whether the urine is "exterior," or of "blood-essence" <note>original: "cruoris"; referring to the internal vital essence or "gore" of the blood rather than just liquid blood</note>, or a mixture of both. For it is threefold: namely, from food and drink. For there is a triple excrement from this: stool, urine, and sweat. The second urine is from the resolution of the body's natural salt, etc., and it has its own peculiar signs. The third is a mixture of both, etc. Furthermore, only those things that arise in the stomach, liver, and kidneys—indeed, from food and drink—can be judged from the "exterior" urine; therefore, epilepsy, etc., cannot. But only <term>Tartar</term> <note>In Paracelsian medicine, "Tartar" refers to stony or gravel-like deposits that precipitate from bodily fluids, causing various diseases.</note>, its putrefaction, and similar things can be judged from urine that is not of the blood-essence. <term>Gout</term> <note>original: "Podagra"</note> can only be recognized from the exterior urine; if it has much foam, the patient drank much toward nightfall. The urine of blood-essence shows only natural diseases, such as the "falling disease" <note>original: "morbum caducum"; epilepsy</note>, otherwise nothing: neither diabetes, nor Tartar, etc.
It is the urine of Tartar when the circle of the urine <note>The "circle" or "ring" refers to the uppermost edge of the urine in the glass flask (urinal).</note> is of a leaden color, etc. But if the circle is more reddish, the urine is of the blood-essence itself. And if two similar circles are joined, it is a mixed urine. It is wrongly said by some that leprosy is present when a lead-colored circle floats on top of the urine; for the person has simply drunk too much. When the urine has nothing but a leaden circle, it is only exterior urine. You can say nothing about the head, nor likewise about the rest, etc. A red circle indicates urine of the blood-essence universally.

<margin>What the stench of stool signifies. What the tincture of sulfur notes. Sediment. The bottom. What color in urine notes. Porous, healthy, white, and deceptive sediment.</margin>
## CHAPTER II.

The urine of Tartar is twofold: healthy and unhealthy, just as with the others. <term>Sulfur</term> <note>One of the Three Primes; here associated with the combustible and coloring principles of the body.</note> lies beneath the stomach, for that is what creates stool. But the "tincture" (color) of that Sulfur remains and descends to the liver, and it is this alone which tints the urine. And the more the stool stinks, the better the "separation" <note>The alchemical process by which the body extracts nutrients and expels waste.</note>. Where the tincture of sulfur is, there is healthy urine.
The <term>Hypostasis</term> <note>The sediment that floats or remains suspended in the middle of the urine flask.</note> in the urine demonstrates the <term>Salt</term> <note>The Prime representing stability and the physical "balsam" of the body.</note>. The <term>Fundus</term> <note>The heavy sediment at the very bottom of the flask.</note> demonstrates the <term>Mercury</term> <note>The Prime representing the fluid and volatile essence.</note>; the color or tincture is from the sulfur. If the hypostasis comes out azure-colored, the matter of the salt is well-off. If the Mercury is well separated, the bottom of the urine is thicker than the rest of the urine. If the urine is clearly transparent, the stomach is well-off and the sulfur is well separated. Judge the hypostasis the same way, even if it is a little less transparent, and judge the bottom likewise.
The expulsive force is in the things themselves, even external things (not in our body); when, specifically, the Separation and digestion have been completed everywhere, then the excrement of each member departs of its own accord.
Transparent yet pale urine indicates a person's over-indulgence. The hypostasis ought to be porous if it is healthy, even if it is continuous in itself. A white hypostasis is a sign of deceptive urine; therefore, nothing should be judged from it.

<margin>The sediment and the boy. The sediment which the Womb peculiarly has. The sediment in which the menses are defined. Which sediment is natural. Sediment is scarce in the elderly and differs. What foam that vanishes quickly indicates. What bubbles in urine note. Twofold diseases from food.</margin>
## ON CHAPTER III.

A perfect partitioning between the parts shows a perfect digestion. A pointed or "peaked" hypostasis means the expulsive power is well-off.
The hypostasis of virgins is more subtle than that of boys, and they have, as it were, two sediments, because the <term>Matrix</term> <note>The womb.</note> has its own peculiar sediment (which is not so in men); it is a sign of fertility. In the elderly, the Sulfur does not differ from the urine of the young if it is healthy, despite what those others say. In women, when the menstruation has ceased, the lower sediment also departs. And the hypostasis ought to be white and almost leaden, even if it is compared to a healthy hypostasis.
Some hypostasis ought to be of a celestial color by itself, and in old age it becomes scarcer and thinner.
The urine of an old man has four parts; that of a youth has three, specifically in relation to the hypostasis.

## ON CHAPTER IIII.

Two colors reflecting and shining back into the hand indicate a good separation in the kidneys. When the urine is moved, if the foam vanishes quickly, the urine is perfect and healthy, and vice-versa.
Perfect separation, digestion, and expulsion must be present in healthy urine.
Bubbles appearing in the hypostasis after the urine is shaken show, with certainty, that it belongs to a woman.

# SECOND TREATISE,
### On unhealthy urines, specifically regarding Alcolitis.

## CHAPTER I.
### On the Definition of urines.

**F**URTHERMORE, those things which pertain to the second Treatise are concerning unhealthy "exterior" urine. In these, we treat diseases born from things taken through the mouth, which is from the "elementals." From these, two illnesses descend: of <term>Tartar</term> and of <term>Ruby</term> <note>likely referring to a "Rubinus" or red-colored crystalline pathology.</note>. The following chapters declare what pertains to Tartar and what pertains to Ruby.
The first is about Tartar, and there are three types or species of Tartar-urines.
The first is concerning coagulated Tartar, and it is <term>Alcolita</term> urine. <note>A Paracelsian term (derived from "Alkali") for a specific type of metabolic or salty deposit in the urine.</note> "Alcolita" is a term accepted among us only, and it is taken from the thing itself. In alcolita urine, all diseases of this kind are contained.

<header>ON JUDGMENTS OF URINES</header>

<margin>How many types of Tartar in urine. Which diseases are the Alcolitae urines. What is scatea urine. What is a nutricolous member. What tremulous urine signifies.</margin> of this; Vine-shoots, Hail, Frost, Lump, Pebble, Mucilage, and the others which I have written about under Tartar.

The second urine is **scatea** <note>original: 'scatea', likely referring to a gushing or bubbling quality</note>. *Scatea* was unknown among the ancients, but is in use among us. *Scatea* or *scata* urine provides evidence of resolved Tartar, that is, of putrefactions, liquids, and dissolved substances, and of all these similar diseases existing in the **Nutricola**. A nutricolous member <note>An organ specifically responsible for the processing and distribution of nourishment.</note> is one in which the separation, digestion, and expulsion of the produced elements is concocted.

The third urine, which is **tremulous**, declares tartaric obstructions. The name *tremulous* is taken from its form and was hidden from the ancients: it makes manifest the plague, pleurisy, acute or chronic fever, abscesses, blockages, and other various types whose origin and birth descend from or through obstructions and turn into disease. Now for those which belong to the **Rubinus** <note>The vital red essence or "nourishing blood" within the body's systems.</note>.

<margin>How many types of Rubinus in urine. What is the facula of urine. What is the formula of urine.</margin> Nevertheless, the Rubinus contains two urines, namely the **facula** <note>original: 'facula', usually meaning a small torch, but here derived from 'faex' (dregs)</note> and the **formula**. *Facula* is derived from dregs and is spagyric <note>Referring to the alchemical process of separating and recombining substances.</note>. *Formula* is a technical name taken from its primary form. The *faecula* of urine treats these diseases:

Those arising after separation, digestion, and expulsion, and it stands for a putrefied Rubinus, or one segregated into specific types. The *formula* of urine shows the Rubinus without segregation, along with its primary species in its diseases.

### ->On CHAPTER I of the Second Treatise<-
### ->COMMENTARIES.<-

<margin>Which urine is to be examined for diagnosis.</margin> Urine collected immediately after taking food indicates nothing certain. After the fourth hour it is better, but not yet perfect. The third [collection] is superior. However, the fourth urine is finally good and true for making a judgment. But be careful not to separate the urine; collect it all. For if the true and untrue urine are collected together at the same time, the urine may be watery and foamy, which you should ignore. These things are said concerning the exterior urine, etc.

<margin>When the urine of gore is to be collected.</margin> When the **urine of gore** <note>original: 'urina cruoris', referring to urine containing blood-essence or vital sediment.</note> is to be collected, the patient should eat or drink nothing the day before, unless perhaps it is entirely dry; then collect it the following day early in the morning, but before the seventh hour. From this urine, even the "falling disease" <note>Epilepsy.</note> can be judged, etc.

Mixed urine consists of both.

<margin>What is Rubinus. What is Alcolita urine.</margin> **Rubinus** is that which provides nourishment to the limbs, digested by the stomach and sent to the liver; it is so named from its red color.

**Alcolita** urine is merely excrement; from this alone is Tartar identified. Sometimes it appears like hail, sometimes like vine-shoots, sometimes like frost, sometimes like wool or plucked lint, and sometimes it is entirely dissolved. If it stands for a little while, it leaves a mucilage at the bottom, which is a sign of a Stone in the Bladder.

The property of Tartar is that it dissolves only in heat; in cold, however, it coagulates. In *alcolita* urine, you should care for neither the color, nor the milkiness, etc.

<margin>What scatum signifies.</margin> **Scatum** is a sign of the stench of urine: from this, the putrefaction of these three members is identified. Under this is also categorized the taste of the urine. Among the Spagyrics <note>Alchemists or chemical physicians.</note>, until the *scatum* is removed from the substances to be prepared, the pure is not separated from the impure.

**Tremulous** urine—that is, fermenting or boiling as if step by step—is a sign of obstruction.

**Faecula** urine—that is, corrupt, named from dregs (*faeces*)—signifies Rubinus lying in the liver, not yet attracted by the limbs. **Formula** urine is *ogra* <note>An alchemical term for a specific type of sediment or essence.</note>; it signifies Rubinus exiting with the urine.

## CHAPTER II.
->On Alcolita Urine.<-

<margin>How many parts and signs of Alcola.</margin> **A**lcola has three parts: the Stomach, the Liver, and the Kidneys with their regions. Likewise, it has three signs to be judged: **Hypostasis** <note>The sediment at the bottom.</note>, which signifies tartar of the stomach; **Divulsion** <note>Clouds or fragments suspended in the middle.</note>, which signifies tartar in the liver; and **Sediment**, which signifies tartar in the kidneys.

Alcola is threefold: in *hypostasis*, it signifies tartar of the stomach and appetite <note>original: 'orexen', from the Greek for appetite.</note>, compression, and burning; in *divulsion*, it signifies tartar of the liver—namely, piercings, thirst, and compression; in *sediment*, it signifies tartar in the kidneys—hail, vine-shoots, frost, stone, etc.

Alcolita urine has three parts: { *Stomach. / Liver. / Kidneys.* }

Likewise, three signs: { *Hypostasis — for the Stomach / Divulsion — for the Liver. / Sediment — for the Kidneys.* }

<margin>Likewise</margin>
*   *Hypostasis* has one sign, namely Alcola in the hypostasis, and it signifies: { *Appetite / Burning / Compression* }
*   *Divulsion* has one sign, namely alcola separated with the hypostasis, and it signifies: { *Tartar of the Liver / Piercing / Weakness, etc.* }
*   *Sediment* has one sign, namely dispersed alcola, and it signifies Tartar in the kidneys.

## CHAPTER III.
->On the Form of Alcola in Particular.<-

<margin>The form of Alcola is threefold.</margin>
*   **Resolved** { *White, milky like whey. Watery. Signifies stone and pebble.* / *Red, reddish, lemon-colored, saffron, tinted. Signifies sand and marble.* }
*   **Sandy.** { *White, mealy, bran-like. Signifies stone from pebbles with a lump.* / *Red, lemon-colored. Signifies form and matter as it appears.* }
*   **Mucilaginous** { *Bituminous, viscous. Signifies unconcocted tartar, or many other things.* }

<margin>The accidents from Alcola are these</margin>
*   *Blood*: signifies an injury from Tartar in another part.
*   *Pus*: signifies ulceration according to the location.
*   *Gore*: signifies putrefaction according to the location.
*   *Restriction*: signifies an obstruction of the blood.

<margin>Signs</margin>
*   **Extraneous**, and they are two: { *Involuntary emission: signifies the entry of Tartar.* / *Drop-by-drop burning: signifies the sharpness of Tartar.* }
*   **From experience**: namely two: { *Spirit* / *Salt* } of Urine { *signifies: Impossible cure, except with the prior signs.* }

### SCHOLIA.

<margin>What porous hypostasis signifies.</margin> **A** notably porous **hypostasis** signifies Tartar in the stomach, especially if filaments are seen in the pores—that is, Alcola. If it should also be red, it signifies vehement pain, just as in other locations and urines.

<header>ON URINES.</header>
<meta>Catchword: Of the Intestines.</meta>

Whoever has Tartar <note>In Paracelsian medicine, "Tartar" refers to stony or calcified deposits in the body, similar to the scale found in wine casks.</note> in the liver almost always has cold hands; pains in the sciatica, shoulder blades, and hips signify "sand" (fine sediment) in the kidneys.

Hail or marble-like deposits are a red formation found in the kidneys. If the urine turns white, it is a sign of a stone forming.

If urine stands for some time and a sediment forms at the bottom that is tough, mucilaginous, and looks like white sand, it signifies that Tartar is attempting to coagulate into a stone.

<margin>What white urine denotes.</margin>
White urine that contains "types of Bertold" <note>original: 'species Bertoldi'; likely referring to a specific particulate appearance named after a medical authority or case.</note>, appearing like phlegm, is a sign of Tartar. If the urine is golden, it originates from the sperm.

<margin>What bloody urine denotes. How pus and discharge differ.</margin>
Bloody urine signifies that Tartar has eroded a small vein. If there are clots of blood, it signifies that it has coagulated.

Pus and discharge <note>original: 'sanies', a thin, greenish or bloody discharge from a wound.</note> differ. Discharge is what exits through plasters, on its own, daily; but "pus" refers to the foul stench itself.

The involuntary discharge of urine signifies the entry of Tartar through the pores.

Dripping urine: if white, it turns into a stone; if red, it turns into a "bolus" <note>A large pill or mass.</note> or sand.

Distill the urine, and you are said to have extracted the "spirit" when it is placed into cold water; it will return a "split salt" <note>original: 'sal scisum'.</note>.

The salt of urine is Tartar, as seen in the residues of the urinal.

## CHAPTER IV.
### On Gushing Urine, that is, on putrefactions.

**The stench of urine consists of three things:**
*   **Sulfur**, which has three factors: { *Pitch, Oil, Its own self* } — Sulfur is the offending matter of these three.
*   **Mercury**, which has three flavors: { *Urea-like, Meaty, Herbal* } — Mercury is the offending matter of these three.
*   **Salt**, with three odors, namely: { *Raw salt, Arsenic, and Spirits of Vitriol* } — Salt is the offending matter of these three.

<margin>Stinking urine denotes rot. Putrefaction is of two kinds.</margin>
The stench of urine designates putrefaction within the body of that person. This putrefaction is of two kinds: either of the body itself, or of the urine only.

White, stinking urine is a putrefaction of the urine; however, when accompanied by other colors, it designates a putrefaction of the body itself.

If the stench of the urine is like dung, it also comes from "pitch," which is to say, Sulfur.

"Its own self" means like sulfur.

"Meaty" means like meat broth, and such people (arising from Mercury, in whatever way) usually decline toward leprosy, especially in "blood-essence" urine. "Herbal" refers to the smell of hay.

### ON THE LOCATION.

**Urine** { *Pale* (is of the Stomach), *Red* (is of the Liver), *Saffron* (is of the Kidneys), *Cloudy* (is of all Three) }

## CHAPTER V.
### On Tremulous Urine, that is, on obstructions.

**Locations** { *Stomach, Liver, Kidneys* } — **The urine is clear, transparent, and without contents.**

### Signs of Obstruction.

**Symptoms in Tremulous Urine** { *Thick and red* (leads to death if without contents), *Bright, Moderate.* }

<margin>How pale and milky urine differ.</margin>
Pale and milky urine differ. For pale urine verges toward yellow, and these patients have foul-smelling breath.

If the disease arises from Sulfur, the course of cure should be made with frankincense, myrrh, and mastic. If from Mercury, through distilled turpentine, centaury, and "Oil of the Philosophers." If from salts, the cure is made from vitriolated substances.

"Without contents" means like distilled water, entirely clear, yet colored.

The stench of raw salt is tested by throwing the salt onto live coals. Test for Arsenic and Vitriol in the same way.

If the obstruction is in the stomach, the urine is foamy and designates a fever. Similarly, if it is red, the obstruction is in the liver; if saffron and foamy, it is in the Kidneys.

If the urine is entirely without foam, it designates a mortal plague. Every obstruction occurs with heat.

### On Dreggy Urine, that is, having feces.

Corrupt urine signifies corrupt nourishment—that is, the "Rubinus" <note>The vital red nourishing principle of the body.</note>—and Phthisis <note>Consumption or tuberculosis.</note> and Hectic fever usually follow if it corrupts within five hours.

The "formula" <note>The visual pattern or appearance.</note> of the urine is similar to the washings of meat, and it designates that Dysentery and diarrhea will follow.

<header>800 NOTES ON THE BOOKS</header>

-> *Of the Intestines, the Flanks, the Colon, the Rectum <note>original: 'Long. Monoec.', likely referring to the monocolon or rectum</note>, Cartilage (that is, of both the bladder and the veins), the Skin, and the Blood.* <-

<margin>What are called minerals.</margin>
"Minerals" are defined here as all those things which contain and sustain the body itself. Therefore, the "urine of the blood-essence" <note>original: 'urina cruoris'. In this context, 'cruor' refers to the vital, internal blood rather than shed blood.</note> is that which does not come from food or drink, but only from the waste products of the body itself, etc.

<margin>What the urine of the blood-essence is.</margin>
The substance of this urine does not have a "hypostasis" <note>A medical term for sediment that settles at the bottom of a urine sample.</note> or sediment. Every organ provides blood-essence, colored in no other way than the organ is itself. However, when an organ becomes weakened, this "mineral" color is corrupted. For when the urine of the blood-essence is healthy, it looks like gold leaf.

<margin>What the color of the brain is.</margin>
The brain has its own color, which is white and mucilaginous, yet not milky; it is called *cerebella* <note>Referring here to a brain-like discharge or appearance</note>, and it always carries with it a white foam that clings to the upper circular part of the vessel. From this, you shall judge the diseases of the brain.

<margin>What the color of the lungs is.</margin>
The color of the lungs is brick-red, or liver-colored, with foam. You should also note the quantity in such urines, and from this you shall judge asthma, pneumonia, cough, etc.—in short, any pulmonary disease.

<margin>What the color of the bile is.</margin>
The urine of the gallbladder, when viewed against the light, appears yellow; but when placed against something white, it appears green, with foam that possesses the same color as the urine itself. If it lacks foam, it is a sign of jaundice <note>original: 'Ictericia'</note>.

<margin>What the color of the liver is.</margin>
The urine of the liver's blood-essence is colored no differently than the lungs, but it has no foam and is a little darker.

<margin>What the color of the spleen is.</margin>
The color of the spleen is dark, like "Saffron of Mars" <note>original: 'crocus Martis', an alchemical term for iron oxide (rust), which is reddish-brown</note>, with small granules clinging to the ring <note>The 'ring' or 'circle' refers to the meniscus or the line where the urine touches the glass.</note>.

<margin>What the color of the kidneys is.</margin>
The urine of the kidneys is colored like the liver, but is more transparent and oilier, for it has a fatty foam like [*]

<margin>What the color of the flesh is.</margin>
The urine of the flesh, etc., is like the washings of meat; at such times, patients waste away in their whole body, for there is a general dissolution, yet without pain in any specific organ.

<margin>What the color of fat is.</margin>
The urine of fat is pale; however, exclude the fat of the kidneys. Such patients suffer many "strikes" <note>original: 'Ictus', likely referring to sudden spasms or sharp pains</note> here and there, almost like colic, but it is not true colic.

<margin>What the color of the ligaments is.</margin>
The color of the ligaments is white, more transparent than that of the brain, and it has foam and a white ring at the bottom. It is a sign of either gout in the feet, the hands, or the knees <note>original: 'Podagræ, Chiragræ, Genugræ'</note>, etc.

<margin>What the color of the intestines is.</margin>
The urine of the intestines is like distilled water, with a moderate amount of foam usually floating in the middle; it indicates colic, or even dysentery, diarrhea, or "lientery" <note>A form of diarrhea where food is passed undigested.</note>.

<margin>What the color of cartilage and skin are.</margin>
The urine of cartilage is entirely lead-colored; and for this condition, it produces large bubbles <note>original: 'ampullas'</note> instead of foam.
The urine of the skin is like that of cartilage, but without foam; it is a sign of approaching leprosy, for at that point the skin is not being dissolved.

<margin>What the color of the blood is.</margin>
The urine of the blood is brick-colored, but at the bottom it is four times thicker than the upper part of the urine, and it signifies a deficiency of blood. Sometimes it appears sky-blue, green, saffron, white, or black. You will especially note a deficiency of blood if it has a water-like layer on top, so that it seems almost able to be separated.

<margin>Mucus and urine.</margin>
Mucus makes the urine look like that of the brain, but with the mucus at the bottom. It is a sign of sweating when the urine is thinner but has a ring that is excessively watery compared to the norm.
"Fugilis" <note>original: 'Fugilis', often referring to earwax or an ear discharge in early medicine.</note>, appearing as saffron-colored things on top of the urine, signifies pains of the brain and ears.
Tears appear like the urine of the brain, but with small bubbles on top.
Dung causes red urine and a small white foam; it signifies constipation.
Urine, if it is not healthy in itself, changes almost to a whitish color, yet it is not "broken" <note>Referring to the consistency or the 'breaking' of the humors.</note>.

## CHAPTER II.
-> The order of substances is threefold, that is: <-

<note>The following section organizes medical prognosis by comparing the clarity of the urine against the affected organ system.</note>

**Thick**
**And this according to the organ.**
**Clear**
**Transparent**
<margin>There are seven divisions of the organs.</margin>

1. { Lungs, Liver, Kidneys } { **Thick**: healthy; **Clear**: bad; **Transparent**: death.
2. { Brain, Spleen } { **Thick**: average; **Clear**: Good; **Transparent**: best.
3. { Gallbladder } { **Thick**: death; **Clear**: curable; **Transparent**: good.
4. { Cartilage, Intestines, Ligaments, Skin, Flesh } { **Thick**: good; **Clear**: distress; **Transparent**: toward a crisis.
5. { Fat, Blood } { **Thick**: Chronic; **Clear**: deceptive; **Transparent**: incurable.
6. { Mucus (Phlegm), Tears, Urine, Sweat and Pus } { **Thick**: bad; **Clear**: good; **Transparent**: health.
7. { Earwax, Dung } { **Thick**: critical; **Clear**: interval <note>A period of uncertainty or waiting.</note>; **Transparent**: health.

<margin>Three substances of urine.</margin>
There are three "substances" (consistencies) of urine: Thick, which cannot be seen through; Clear, which can be seen through but only a little; and Transparent, which is entirely see-through.
When "and others" is placed in this figure, remember the previous lesson; for example, by "cartilage" you must also understand the bladder.
"Of the interval" means it is doubtful, for the "critical day" <note>The day a disease is expected to take a turn for better or worse.</note> can be delayed there.

<margin>What granules denote.</margin>
If the granules in the foam are small, it tends toward paralysis.
If the bubbles of the foam descend below the ring, as it were, the paralysis has fallen or is being resolved; the foam then becomes white.

<margin>What bubbles denote.</margin>
If the foam remains continuously for up to five hours, it signifies phlegm of the lungs.
If there is a white ring inside the foam, like the foam itself, it is apoplexy <note>A stroke or sudden loss of consciousness.</note>.
If the foam has large blisters, the body is plethoric <note>Overfull of fluids or blood.</note> and obese.
But if even one single bubble persists, it is a sign of "phthisis" <note>A wasting disease, usually pulmonary tuberculosis.</note>.

## CHAPTER III.

<margin>What 'Content' is. Bubbles and foam differ.</margin>
The "Content" is said to be not what is *in* the urine, but what is *on top* of the urine, such as the ring, foam, or bubbles. Now, a "bubble" is that which does not touch the glass, but there are three (more or less) bubbles in the middle; however, foam touches the glass. This is how they differ.

<margin>What foam denotes.</margin>
If the foam is saffron-colored, it is the beginning of jaundice.
If the foam is hollow—that is, above the ring of the glass—and is white, while the ring is black, it is a sign of death. Likewise, when the foam sinks to the bottom, there is a trembling of the heart or a "nightmare" <note>original: 'incubus', often interpreted as a heavy pressure on the chest during sleep or a cardiac symptom.</note>.

<margin>What a bubble denotes.</margin>
Where there is a bubble, there the disease has a great deal of "windiness" (gas), and it usually also signifies the beginning of colic, or in women, a displacement of the womb <note>original: 'præcipitationem matricis'</note>.
You will also see a fault of the head here if the bubbles touch the foam.
If a bubble is colored other than watery—such as saffron—it is jaundice; if green, it is the "falling sickness" <note>original: 'morbus caducus', or epilepsy</note>; if red, it turns into a "synocha" or "causon" <note>Two types of acute, burning fevers.</note>. In this case, you shall not care about the color of the urine itself.

<margin>What filaments denote.</margin>
If the ring has filaments, it signifies a chronic disease. In women, however, it is a sign of pregnancy or a "mola" <note>A 'molar pregnancy' or a non-viable mass in the uterus.</note>.

<margin>What the ring denotes.</margin>
If the ring is colored like a rainbow <note>original: 'Iris'</note>, the worst kind of falling sickness is present.
If a ring falls below another ring, it signifies leprosy, and often the "leonine" type <note>A form of leprosy that makes the face look lion-like.</note>.
A wide ring, having granules within it, is a sign of a most complete apoplexy.

<header>ON URINE.</header>

A green ring indicates Jaundice <term>Icteritia; a yellowing of the skin and eyes</term> that is fatal and incurable. 
In the "suffocation of the womb" <note>original: 'suffocatione Matricis'. A historical term for a condition where the uterus was believed to put pressure on other organs, causing respiratory or emotional distress.</note>, it also signifies impending death.

A sky-blue ring occurs only in women and signifies a putrefaction of the womb; that putrefaction eventually leads to leprosy.

A half-circle signifies paralysis on one side of the body.

If a ring and foam are present at the same time and are of the same color, they signify a chronic and incurable disease of any kind.

If, in otherwise healthy-looking urine, bubbles and foam are stuck together with the ring, it signifies a defect of the midriff <term>praecordia; the area of the body around the heart and diaphragm</term>, though not specifically in the lungs.

A ring of a substance thicker than the urine and red signifies a "lethargic disease" <note>Referring here to Lethargy, a clinical state of sleepiness or coma-like stupor</note> that is either currently present or coming.

A clear ring with thick urine indicates Dropsy <term>Hydropisin; an old term for edema or swelling caused by fluid retention</term>.

If the ring spreads out from the foam or bubbles and then dissolves again, it signifies *Hyposarca* <note>original: 'Hyposarcam'. A specific type of dropsy where fluid collects under the flesh.</note>, which is the worst form of Dropsy.

A foamy ring in the middle of the urine in women signifies pregnancy; if it is colored, it signifies some defect or suffering of the womb or even of the child.

When lepers urinate, they have an azure bubble; this signifies confirmed leprosy, and also indicates *Alopecia* <note>Loss of hair, often associated in early medicine with internal corruption.</note>.

Those who have St. Vitus' Dance <note>original: 'S. Viti morbum'. A disorder characterized by rapid, uncoordinated jerking movements.</note> have saffron-colored urine, but they have a ring that is purple below and saffron above; this lasts only as long as they are experiencing a paroxysm <note>A sudden attack or violent expression of a disease.</note>.

What is said here regarding "rings" should not be understood as the common or lead-colored ring, but as a peculiar and singular ring.

# BOOK TWO
## TREATISE II
### On Mixed Urine.

**ON** mixed urine (that is, urine composed of the external, the mineral, and the blood-essence).

Red in mixed urine—that is, with a transparent red: if it is bright, it is somewhat red; if it is thick, it is extremely red. These show a disease currently present in the body, not a future one. This red color here indicates heat.

This red color is fatal in cases of dropsy.

Red urine that is clear at first and later becomes dark is still a sign of recovery; but if it becomes thin, it is a sign of death.

Foam and bubbles here signify only the upper part of the body, that is, the area above the diaphragm.

If the sediment in the urine is white, it signifies an excessive menstrual flow; if it is red, it signifies a constriction.

If the sediment sinks to the bottom and is neither precisely white nor black, it signifies pain in the hips <term>Schiae; sciatica or hip-joint pain</term>.

White urine signifies a "cold" disease; if it is transparent, it is a good sign; if bright, better; if thick, it is most healthy and best. You shall judge as described above.

However, if the urine is neither perfectly red nor perfectly white, yet has no other color, it is a most certain sign of death. Likewise, if such urine has a "cloud" <note>original: 'nebulam'. A suspension of particles or haze within the fluid.</note> above it, life is at an end.

Transparent green signifies pain of the spleen. A cloud floating on top signifies death; green urine also signifies quartan fever <note>A fever where paroxysms occur every fourth day, often associated with malaria.</note>.

Citrine-yellow urine with a thick cloud above it is a certain sign of death. Black urine with a cloud is a sign of death. However, if it is black without a cloud, the patient has an abscess <term>apostema</term> that is about to break.

Violet color (that is, azure): if it comes from a sick person, it leads to death; if from a healthy person, to leprosy. If it is bright in chronic diseases, it is a sign of health; in acute diseases, it is a sign of death. But if it is thick and violet, it can be a sign of health, unless perhaps it points to leprosy.

Transparent darkness signifies death; other types of dark urine do not.

If all the pulses of the entire body are similar to one another, it is a good sign; if otherwise, it is a bad sign.

If the eyes sink in, it is a bad sign, for it signifies death. Likewise, sharp nostrils and a gaping mouth are signs of death.

Ashen or dark skin is a certain sign of death. So too if the skin turns to a redness of the cheeks, it also signifies death.

"Air"—that is, a foul odor emanating from the patient—signifies death.

Stuttering speech or rushing words signifies death.

Breath drawn from deep within signifies death.

---

## ON THE PULSE.

**T**HE pulse appears in four locations, etc. A hard, slow, and thick pulse, like that found in peasants, is a sign of "Tartar" <note>In Paracelsian medicine, 'Tartar' refers to stony or gravel-like waste products that calcify in the body.</note>, even if the person feels no pain. When a vein is cut, the blood is always grainy. When a patient has such a pulse, one should not despair, because it arises only from Tartar.

A "subtle" pulse comes from minerals, and that pulse is the best; you can best explore this using cold water.

A pulse that is hotter than the rest of the skin signifies the man's disease. Or when the pulse overflows with heat, etc., it is some disease. If a cloth soaked in distilled water is placed over the pulse, and if it dries faster at the site of the pulse than on the surrounding parts, there is a violent disease in the blood.

A pulse restricted on both sides: if it rests, it is well; if it moves again in either of those two places, it is a disease.

If four fingers are placed upon the pulse and it strikes less, yet feels hotter than natural heat, the person is healthy.

A hard pulse indicates Tartar; if it becomes soft in an acute disease, it is a sign of the "resolution" or breaking down of the Tartar, and therefore bloodletting <term>phlebotomandum</term> should be performed.

If the pulse is harder in one place and softer in another, it is a bad sign, because a violent disease is present.

For a constricted pulse: place the elbow in cold water; if it keeps its color (namely azure) and also its motion, it is well. If one of these fails, it is bad; if both fail, it signifies death. If the arms are tied and the pulse is similar on both sides, it is well; if otherwise, bad.

All other pulses should be similar in motion to the pulse of the hands.

The pulse of the head is the last of all pulses to go in death. For the pulses of the temples, the sides of the neck, the hands, and finally the feet follow an order. The pulse of the foot is the first of all to die.

When the motion of the pulse can be seen visually, it is either a very good or a very bad sign. A strong and swift pulse signifies an abundance of the element of fire, if heat is present at the same time. If heat is not present, it signifies coldness.

### On the Pulse in "Gutta" <note>The 'Gutta' or 'Drop' usually refers to gout or apoplectic strokes.</note>.

In a person with apoplexy, a strong pulse is bad; the stronger it is, the worse. When the pulse of the neck has small nodules in such a patient, it is a sign of death. Likewise, if it is felt in the neck and not in the hands, it signifies death; conversely, if it moves in the hands and not in the neck, it signifies life.

In the "falling sickness" <note>Epilepsy.</note>, if the pulse continues to move after a paroxysm while they sleep, it is well; if the pulse also "sleeps," it is a bad sign.

#### In wasting diseases, Lientery <note>A form of diarrhea where food is passed undigested.</note>, etc.

If the pulse remains the same, but some other sign of death appears, do not concern yourself further with the pulse. For it can continue to beat even after death.

An "elemented" pulse in the flanks signifies pregnancy in women. A pulse in the flanks belongs only to women, and specifically to the womb. A trembling pulse in the male organ <note>original: 'priapo'</note> is a sign of sterility.

---

### On the Pulses and their Motion.

The pulse has four "Powers":
*   **Of Tartar** { Rounded, Hard, Coarse, Subtle
*   **Of Mineral** { Constricted, Obscure
*   **Of Disease**, namely { and it has two demonstrations: { Tartaric, Mineral, of Tartar, of Mineral.
*   **Of Health** { And it has two meanings: { Equal, Moderate.

Likely a Paracelsian term for a specific golden-red hue.</note> is a deep red, and it is the primary color of gold, properly speaking. A wasting navel is a sign of death, just as in the eyes. ### ON HEALTHY URINE
### CHAPTER I.

<margin>Nostrils.</margin>
Sharp and lead-colored nostrils are a sign of death; death also comes from the brain in this case. So it is also in *Tenesmus* <term>Tenesmus; a distressing but ineffective urge to evacuate the bowels or bladder</term> when it tries to exit by itself. In the ears, it is a sign when the cartilages turn to a wax-like color. In the mouth, when it pales to a wax-like color, it is likewise a sign of death. Judge the same regarding the womb.

<margin>Cheeks.</margin>
When the cheeks turn purple, it is all over. Judge the same regarding the belly. One should judge similarly in other cases. In *Acatias* <note>original: 'Acatias'. This refers to a shriveling or contraction of the skin.</note>, that is, when it is wrinkled or contracted, just as the mouth is contracted from eating plums.

**U**RINE is "exterior" when it is expelled from food. For all digested food seeks the emunctory <term>emunctory; an organ or canal that carries off waste, such as the skin, kidneys, or bowels</term>, either through feces or through urine. "Blood-based" urine is that which is expelled by nature, not by food or drink. "Mixed" is when both are mingled, and then it has a double ring of different colors in the upper part.

### On CHAPTER II.

<margin>Teeth.</margin>
Rough teeth, worn down as if by a file, are a sign of future death. Therefore, depart cautiously. Judge the same for other signs. For even if death does not follow immediately, it follows certainly.

**E**xterior urine indicates the passions of the liver, stomach, and kidneys, not of the head or other members.

Urine is divided into parts. { The upper part } { Sulphur is well separated when it is clear. }
{ The Hypostasis } which indicates { The condition of Salt, which is well separated. } <term>Hypostasis; the sediment that settles at the bottom of a urine sample</term>
{ The lower part. } { The state of Mercury, which is well separated when it is clear at the bottom yet more turbulent. }

### ON THE SECOND TREATISE OF THE FIRST BOOK.
->Annotations.<-

If the urine is clear, it signifies healthy digestion and the matter of salt being well-digested. If the sediment in the urine is "lazuria" <note>original: 'lazuria'. A sky-blue or azure color.</note>, it is a sign of the matter of salt being well-digested.

Sulphurous urine is a sign of health.

A sub-purplish color is the nature and color of Mercury. At the bottom of the urine, Mercury is more turbulent than the Sulphur in the upper part. This is a sign of Mercury being well-digested.

<margin>What "alcolized" urine denotes.</margin>
**A**lcolita ) "Alcolized" urine <note>In this context, 'alcolita' or 'alcolifata' refers to urine containing dissolved mineral matter or "Tartar" that has been broken down.</note> demonstrates diseases of the stomach, kidneys, and liver; and such urine is generated from excrements. Urine is "alcolifata" when the Tartar <term>Tartar; the stony or gravelly deposits Paracelsus believed caused many diseases, named after the crust in wine barrels</term> of the stomach, kidneys, or liver is dissolved; and this urine has sand at the bottom. Sometimes this sand is hidden, and then the urine is filamentous, like wool. If there is mucus in the bottom of the urine, it is a sign of a stone in the bladder. If the urine stinks for six hours in the urinal and is sandy, it is alcolized urine, in which the tint and sediment are not to be regarded.

But these are signs of concoction <term>concoction; the "cooking" or ripening of humors by the body's natural heat</term>. ) If the sediment in the exterior urine is white, the urine is deceptive. This happens from drunkenness, when the stomach is weighed down beyond its custom with food or drink that it cannot digest.

The urine of a youth is divided into 3 parts; that of an old man into 4.

### On CHAPTER III.

<margin>What "scatea" urine denotes.</margin>
Scatea ) *Scatum* is the stench of urine. By this, the putrefaction of the stomach, liver, and kidneys is known. Only through this stench is putrefaction known; when the urine is sharp to the taste, it is a sign of the same thing.

<margin>Signs of digestion and rawness in urine.</margin>
**V**ery clear urine is a sign of good digestion in the liver. For the stomach does not perfectly color the urine.

If the urine lacks sediment, it is a sign of rawness and bad digestion in the liver and kidneys. When the urine is neither clear nor has sediment, it is a sign of a cold liver. If the sediment is dispersed, it is a sign of such salt not being well-digested in the liver.

<margin>What "tremulous" urine denotes.</margin>
Tremula ) Urine is "tremulous" when, once set aside, it continually seethes or bubbles; this is a sign that there are obstructions of Tartar in the liver, kidneys, or meseraics <term>meseraics; the mesenteric veins or vessels of the abdomen</term>. Through this urine, obstructions of Tartar are recognized.

<margin>What "fecula" urine denotes.</margin>
Vrina Fœcula. ) This is when urine turns to putrefaction—that is, it is corrupted—and by this, a defect of the attractive virtue in the limbs is recognized.

<margin>What the sediment indicates.</margin>
Vrina Formula. ) This is when the urine comes out like a ruby and resembles "ogrum" <note>original: 'ogrum'. Likely a term for a specific type of gore or dark fluid.</note> or blood; then it is "formula" urine, by which healthy urine is distinguished.

<margin>A sign of fertility in urine.</margin>
The sediment in the urine of a virgin or a woman not advanced in years is more delicate. But the urine of a youth or a man and of healthy people has a sediment deep in the Mercury parts, etc., which is a sign of a fruitful woman.

### NOTE.
If the sediment is missing, it is a sign of either a menstrual defect or childbirth. The sediment in young women is of a sky-blue color, but in older women, it is lesser.

If the sediment is "alcolized" or perforated with holes, and in those holes there are flakes like wool, it is a sign of Tartar in the stomach or an appetite disorder.

If the sediment of the urine is wider at the bottom than in the upper part, it is a sign that the expulsive virtue is failing.

If the sediment is redder than the urine, it indicates great pains in the stomach.

If the sediment is dispersed, it is a sign of a defect in the liver; and if the urine is red, the sick suffer thirst and have cold hands.

### On CHAPTER IIII.
->On the Urine of the Kidneys.<-

If the sediment is torn apart, it is a sign of Tartar in the stomach.

If the urine is torn apart in the dregs, it is a sign that Tartar is descending to the bladder.

<margin>How a woman's urine is distinguished from a man's.</margin>
**I**f the bottom cannot be clearly seen in the urine, or if it is dispersed, it is a sign of poor separation in the kidneys.

If the urine has "hailstones" <note>referring to small white particles</note>, there is pain in the kidneys; and if the urine is white with sand, it is a most certain sign that a stone is being generated.

If the urine is shaken, and if all things do not soon settle at the bottom as they ought, it is not healthy urine. If a woman's urine is shaken, it creates bubbles or vesicles in the middle, which are a sign that the urine is female.

If it is cloudy in the dregs without filaments, then Tartar is in the kidneys; and if the urine is reddish-brown, it indicates greater pains, and they suffer pains in the "ischia" <note>the hip/pelvic region</note>, in the loins, and in the thigh; and if there is also sand at the bottom, then they have pains in the pit of the chest.

### On CHAPTER II.

**Alcola** <note>A Paracelsian term for fatty or cloudy sediments in the urine.</note> **has parts in the** { **Stomach**, **Liver**, **Kidneys** } with their respective regions.

**Three signs are to be judged:** { **Hypostasis** <note>The sediment that settles at the bottom.</note>, **Divulsion** <note>Cloudy fragments suspended in the middle of the liquid.</note>, **Sediment** } these signify Tartar <note>The stony, calcified deposits Paracelsus believed caused many diseases, named after the hard crust in wine barrels.</note> { **In the stomach**, **In the Liver**, **In the Kidneys.** }

**Alcola is threefold:** { **In Hypostasis, where it signifies: Tartar of the Stomach, Appetite** <note>original: 'Orexen'; Greek for a sharp or unnatural hunger</note>, **Compression, Burning.** }
{ **In Divulsion: Tartar of the Liver, Sharp stinging pains, Thirst, Compression.** }
{ **In Sediment: Tartar in the Kidneys, Hail-like particles, Sticky matter, Frost-like particles, Stone.** }

Most often, Tartar is not recognized by these three signs in the urine; when this happens, it is healthy urine mixed with unhealthy urine, and the healthy and unhealthy urine stand separated in the urinal <note>The glass vessel used to examine urine, also called a matula.</note>, one above the other. And if the lower, unhealthy urine is white, it is a sign that Tartar is being formed into a stone. If it is milky, it also indicates the generation of a stone. If, however, it is like whey <note>original: 'aqua casei'; literally 'cheese water'.</note>, it is also a sign of a stone. If the urine is red, it is a sign of a red stone.

# ON THE SECOND TRACTATE OF THE FIRST BOOK:
## OBSERVATIONS.

### On CHAPTER I.
->Concerning unhealthy urine.<-

**ALCOLITA** <note>A variation of 'Alcola', referring to the presence of these sediments.</note> therefore refers to urine containing certain very finely dissolved particles, and other sticky substances at the bottom, which demonstrate that Tartar is present in the bladder. **Scatea** is named from *scatea* <note>original: 'scatea', related to the Greek 'skatos'</note>, meaning dung or excrement. Similarly, **Faecula** <note>Dregs or lees.</note> is named from the dregs of corrupt urine. **Formula** refers to a mixture of a ruby-colored substance and urine; it is either dark orange or reddish.

### On CHAPTER II.
->Concerning Alcolita.<-

**Parts of Alcolita:** { **Stomach**, **Liver**, **Kidneys** } With their regions.
**Signs:** { **Hypostasis**, **Divulsion**, **Sediment** } of Tartar { **of the Stomach**, **of the Liver**, **of the Kidneys** }
**Alcola in:** { **Hypostasis**, signifies tartar, appetite, compression, burning;
{ **Divulsion**: sharp pain, thirst, compression:
{ **Sediment**, tartar, hail-like, sticky, frost-like, stone.

But so that these things may be more clearly known, we will combine some of them. For instance, when white urine appears with **Sand**, it indicates a stone in the bladder.
However, a **perforated hypostasis** <note>Sediment that appears to have holes or gaps in it.</note>, in which Alcola (that is, filaments) are contained, signifies compressions and burning sensations.
**Divulsion of the hypostasis**, in which there are both holes and Alcola, signifies pain in the right side: If these are red, it indicates the severity of the disease, which is accompanied by thirst or coldness of the hands.
**Hypostasis which seeks the bottom** is an indication of pain located between the liver and kidneys.
Something **dense lurking at the bottom** signifies a long-lasting disease: If it is red, it signifies a more violent one; if in a pit-like shape, it signifies compressions, vomiting, and a poor condition of the stomach.

### Toward CHAPTER III.
->On the form of Alcola.<-

**Sand and marble** ) a red stone, or sand-like deposits.
**Mucilaginous form** ) signifies Tartar not yet fully formed, or several deposits.
Accompanying symptoms: thick pus, watery discharge.

**Signs:** { **External.** ) that is, known through the fields <note>Possibly referring to symptoms observable outside of laboratory tests, like physical exertion.</note> { **Involuntary emission**, **Burning, etc.** }
{ **From experience:** { **Spirit of urine.** **Salt of urine.** } these signify, namely, an impossible cure when found with the previous signs. }

**Involuntary emission:** ) happens when Tartar is dissolved and passes through the pores.
**Spirit of urine:** ) is extracted through distillation; place that which has distilled into cold water, and it produces an icicle-like form similar to saltpeter.
**Salt of urine:** ) is born daily in the urinal; this is not curable here unless the superior signs are present.

### CHAPTER IV. ON SCATEA <note>Foul-smelling urine.</note>.

**The stench of urine exists in either:** { **Sulphur**: having the stenches of { **Dung**, **Burnt Pitch**, **Very Rancid Oil**, **Orris Root** } Sulphur is the offending matter, leaning toward leprosy. }
{ **Mercury**: stenches of { **Flesh**, that is frankincense <note>original: 'thuru'; likely referring to the heavy, sweet smell of incense.</note>, **Fresh Hay** } Mercury is the offending matter. }
{ **Salt**: with the stench of { **Raw salt**, **Arsenic**, **Spirits** } Salt is the offending matter. }
