...the manner of prescribing requires: then also that I describe the digestive virtues. Furthermore, since an error has occurred where judgments were established based on the colors of the waste <note>original: "stercorum"</note> without considering their origin, many fallacies have been introduced. For no color arising from putrefaction <note>The breakdown or "rotting" of substances within the body.</note> signifies anything of truth unless it comes from its own specific place. For this reason, the waste retains the color of that place and region; for instance, the waste of the brain retains its whiteness and blue color. If, however, the waste of a place putrefies, then the place itself putrefies with those colors, and so on. In the gall <note>The bile or gallbladder.</note> there is greenness and yellowness: whatever putrefies from it also clings to these colors. This is to be understood in the same way for all parts. Yet, a change of this kind happens: as often as a disease falls into putrefaction, the colors are changed. Waste that ought to be tinted with redness becomes black and purple-red <note>original: "phoenicea"</note>, which are falsely called melancholy <note>Traditionally, "melancholy" was the "black bile" humor; Paracelsus argues these colors actually come from blood, not a specific humor.</note>. These colors arise from the blood: how then can they be melancholy? Therefore, judgment based on these colors is deceptive. In the same way, when a putrefied thing ought to be white and blue, the efficacy of that disease changes it into an ash-gray color <term>leucophaea</term> <note>A pale, dusty, or ash-colored hue.</note>, <margin>Ash-gray color, etc. No one knows what phlegm is.</margin> which they judge to be phlegm—and yet no man knows what phlegm actually is! Thus also the remaining colors are changed in putrefactions. For this reason, one must not immediately judge by colors, because these judgments are all false. Indeed, colors are so changed into different essences that no one can recognize their true mother of origin. But just as deceptions occur with colors, so they do with the substance itself. For diseases produce putrefactions in such various ways that no one can say, "this is yolk-colored cholera <note>Yellow bile.</note>, and so its cure will be such." For the digestive virtue is affected in one way or another to change the substance. Whence it follows that a cure should not be taken from yolk-colored bile, but from the signs of digestion. It does not even matter what color the waste is. The sum of the cure, therefore, is held in the judgments of digestion, not of the waste. Both the substance and the color declare nothing else than that the diseases are in the region of digestion; but what the diseases actually are is not signified. Until the Physician has been well instructed in these, he can establish nothing rightly in those things which pertain to the body. Since, therefore, the parents of man are the heaven and the earth, from which he was finally created: learn the infant from the parents, and practice anatomy on the parents—dissect them, not children. When you have known the heaven and the earth, you will have full knowledge of the whole of human nature. Whence I can say, not without merit, that they all err and are deceived who cast their foundation of learning in the child, and not rather in that from which he is born. I am not speaking here of those children whose parents also exist as children, but of the father and mother of Adam and Eve. And let the image not offend or hinder you. For it so seemed good to God that man should be born in such an image. Therefore, one does not become a physician from the image, but from that course and flow which is within the image—that is, the whole heaven and the whole earth. From those, the physician is born and nourished.

->Preface.<-

<margin>
The ancients' method of purging was erroneous.
</margin>
**S**ince purgations <note>Medicines used to cleanse the body of humors, usually laxatives or emetics.</note> have until now been as much a hindrance as a help to many, it has pleased me to compose this treatise about them. For it is of no small importance that this doubtful outcome of purgations be properly considered according to its causes; it cannot help but emerge from a bad foundation or prove a doubtful and ambiguous doctrine. For if the matter were truly understood, certainly no one would purge except when necessary. And where there was no need for purging, they would abstain from it. Therefore, it is my purpose to ventilate the uncertain doctrine of the Physicians here, and to teach that they have used no certain method of purging, but have lived in mere ambiguities...

He begins a new book critiquing the traditional, often harmful, use of purgative medicines.</summary>

<page-num>819</page-num>
<header>PREFACE.</header>

# PREFACE.

...they have blindly clung to ambiguities. For it is not the part of a Physician to decree purgations <note>The medical process of cleansing the body of "bad humors," usually through laxatives or emetics.</note> with a doubtful outcome, or to commit the operation to blind fortune. Indeed, this is clear evidence of an uncertain art. Therefore, it seems that diligent effort must be given so that, the old lyre having been cast aside, a fuller and more certain knowledge may henceforth be held. For the ancient Physicians did not apply themselves to the gathering of experience with a very great zeal for honesty and integrity, which they nevertheless ought to have done. And their rashness is so much to be grieved, because in administering medicines, they understand the reason and method of them much less than peasants know the method of sowing seeds. For if a doubtful physician hopes for a good outcome, he acts wickedly. If he cites the authorities of writers, he offers up trifles. If he says, "who can see through the intact skin?" then he betrays his own folly. If he claims to know the disease but says remedies are lacking, or if he cries out that nature is so malignant that it cannot be resisted: then he certainly betrays by these things that he is in no way a Physician. Therefore, since the entire foundation of truth is placed in Knowing, not in Opining <note>Paracelsus distinguishes between "Scientia" (proven knowledge) and "Opinio" (mere guesswork or theoretical belief).</note>, knowledge and experience are absolutely necessary for the Physician—namely, that a purgation is a Cure and not a preparation. For preparation is one thing, purgation another, digestion another, and a purgative yet another. Moreover, the name of "purgation" was given because nothing is purged other than that which is stained and polluted. To this also looks the entire foundation of my teaching: namely, what it is to pollute and what it is to purge, not according to opinion. For the industry of the Physician is occupied not in opining, but in knowing. For since Medicine was created by God, it must certainly lack any defect. For if God created the arts of weaving and pottery to be certain in their own experience, then surely the same will be entirely true regarding Medicine, which is of far greater importance. Truly, the reason why Physicians neglected experience was the work of the Sophists <note>Paracelsus used "Sophists" as a derogatory term for university-trained doctors who relied on ancient Greek texts rather than chemical experiments.</note>, with whom all Medicine swarms, who handle Medicine no differently than a butcher handles a pig. Therefore, for reasons by no means trivial, I dedicate and compose this treatise for you, N. N. <note>A placeholder for a name, likely a patron or colleague.</note> For you love justice and worship truth exceedingly. Therefore, to join truth to truth and the just to the just is very laudable both for me and for other Physicians, and especially for you. Farewell.

Reprimand of ancient medicine.
</margin>
<margin>
It is the physician's job to know, not to guess.
Purgation is a cure, not a preparation.
What is a purged thing.
Medicine is thought to be created by God.

## BOOK ONE.
## TREATISE I.

<margin>
What it is to be stained?
</margin>
**S**ince everything that eats produces waste <note>original: "stercus"</note>, I must discuss this matter more at length. Truly, the nature and division of waste in things from the insensible to the sensible must be known. First, however, it must be known what is "stained" or "polluted." That which is polluted is that which does not belong to nature, but is outside of it. But how does the polluted or the filthy enter? You see how mud or dung found in the streets, produced by rain and earth, etc., are carried into the stoves <note>original: "hypocasta," referring to the heating systems of houses.</note>. Similar are the operations in the body, similar to the generations of rain, etc.

<margin>
All creatures eat.
</margin>
Furthermore, all creatures eat and drink, nor is there any thing, whether sensible or insensible, that does not eat. That which eats also defecates and produces waste, of whatever order it may be.

<margin>
Stones eat. How do the Diamond and Magnet eat?
</margin>
Stones eat and drink: for if they did not do this, their body would not remain. The Diamond eats obscurely. The Magnet <note>The lodestone.</note>, however, eats manifestly. For what else does the Magnet testify to us by its eating, than the manifest power of attracting and eating? In the same way, stones and all gems eat, nor is anything sustained without food.

<margin>
Epicurus
</margin>
Now, if the Physician knows how to offer to each thing its own food, no differently than he does for himself, he will certainly make a very gifted medicine, so that it becomes, as it were, fat and stronger, like a fat Epicurus <note>Paracelsus uses the philosopher Epicurus as a symbol of someone well-fed and vigorous.</note>, whom food and drink continually cheered and made eager to perform his duties.

<margin>
Grass is the food of cattle; rain is the food of grass.
</margin>
Otherwise, grass is given to cattle for food: but for grass, the food is the earth and rain. Just as it might seem a wonder to the grass, if it knew it was to be the food of a cow, and furthermore milk and cheese; so in turn it would seem a wonder to the cattle if they knew they were to be the food of men. And yet, meanwhile, you all wonder greatly at this: that stones eat and drink, when nevertheless they, no less than man, the beast,

<margin>
Why stones are nourished.
</margin>
and the grasses, cannot be sustained without food. For since all things live, all things will also need food and drink.

<margin>
What are the foods of each creature?
</margin>
**W**hat each thing chooses for food by the ordination of the creator is one of the "magnalia" <note>Great wonders or mysteries</note> of God. What, for instance, feeds stones? The mineral chaos <note>original: "Chaos mineralis"; the basic elemental substance from which minerals are formed.</note>. What nourishes grass? Mineral liquor. What feeds man? Vegetative flesh. Who cooks all things? God. Afterward, man prepares them. Man is subject to preparation, and yet he is not. But grass and stone necessarily lie in their own liquor, nor can they ever leave their own kitchen. Man, however, can do this: for which use he received hands and feet, which the others lack; because of this defect, food is even offered or placed before them of its own accord. For just as cattle are compelled to follow the manger, so on the contrary, the manger in which the material food is stored is compelled to follow insensible things. Therefore, just as the hungry veins of the body attract from the mouth, stomach, and liver whatever nourishment is present, or as a piglet sucks from its mother: so also stones attract their own nutriment, since they lie right next to it.

<margin>
Sensible creatures follow their food; insensible ones the opposite.
</margin>

<margin>
Where there is food, there is waste.
</margin>
While these things happen, waste is certainly everywhere that food is gathered. The veins attract what is good, and the same veins leave the waste behind. Since this is useless, it is driven out from that place. For the "place" in all things, both sensible and insensible, contains within itself a separative power <note>original: "virtutem separatiuatam"</note> by which waste is expelled.

<margin>
Separative power is in all things.
</margin>

<margin>
Usnea is the waste of its subject.
</margin>
But for a fuller knowledge of this question of what waste is, it is further asked: is "usnea" <note>A type of moss or lichen that grows on rocks or trees.</note> a growing thing, or waste? It is answered: it is the waste of that which it grows upon. So it might also be asked whether the mucus found upon stones is mucus from the water or from the stones? For it is the waste of stones. If it were from the water, it would also be applied to other things in the same place, no less than to the stones themselves. Here there is no escape. Stones, therefore, lie in their own kitchen and pantry, from whose abundance they eat and grow, like a man increasing and becoming fat. Truly, the excrement left over from the nourishment is driven out from the stone, and nothing impure remains within it.

<margin>
Stones have their nourishment with them.
</margin>

This universal process of eating and excreting forms the basis for his theory of purgation and health.</summary>

<meta>This page continues from the previous discussion on the necessity of certain knowledge in medicine, moving from a general critique of "opinion-based" medicine to a specific study of waste products (stercus) as the key to understanding disease and purging.</meta>

<page-num>820</page-num>
<header>FRAGMENTS</header>

The same is true in the same way in other things as well: that all things similarly eat, drink, and defecate or discharge. Now, therefore, we shall begin the second treatise, for the sake of which we first established [the previous points], namely to speak about **human waste** <note>original: "stercre hominis." While "stercus" usually means dung or excrement, Paracelsus uses it here as a technical term for any byproduct or waste material left over after the body extracts nourishment.</note> in particular, and we shall omit the rest. For these [other types of waste] belong neither to Medicine nor to our primary purpose. Nevertheless, all these things which serve to weigh the secrets of nature ought to be properly understood by the Physician, just as they are specifically handed down in that branch of Philosophy. Here, however, I treat this waste—that is, the method of purging—so that you may diligently weigh the origin and causes of waste. For in this knowledge much importance is placed for destroying the opinions of the ancients, and for establishing more certainly those things which will be handed down hereafter.

### TREATISE II.

<margin>What is waste?</margin>
Since, therefore, I must treat the subject of waste and where its locations thrive: before all else, it is right to know, **What is waste?** Waste is that which is left behind from the nourishment of the body and is expelled: that is, waste is that which, mixed with food and drink, cannot become nourishment.

<margin>How many kinds of waste.</margin>
It must now be known how many kinds of these there are. One is in the mouth; the second in the stomach; the third in the urine; the fourth in sweat, and so on.

<margin>How many digestions there are.</margin>
Since all these are types of waste, it must consequently be known that there are as many separations in the body as there are types of waste.

<margin>The Hermits lived by the chewing of food alone.</margin>
The first is in the mouth: for it is possible for food held in the mouth to be digested there no less than in the stomach. Indeed, by this reasoning many **Hermits** sustained their lives, swallowing nothing at all, and yet prolonging their lives in a natural way. For mastication <note>The act of chewing.</note>, and the time given for digesting food in the mouth, change food into nourishment; and no less is drawn from mastication than from the boluses <note>Chewed morsels of food.</note> of the stomach and the rest.

<margin>1. Waste of the mouth</margin>
In this way, what remains in the mouth becomes natural waste and is attached to the teeth, etc. <note>Paracelsus is referring to dental tartar or plaque as a "waste product" of oral digestion.</note> From this follows a peculiar regimen for a long life. Thus, whatever is digested in the mouth renders men healthy and long-lived. For such was life in the desert. Note the region of the mouth, likewise of the tongue, and abstinence.

Regarding this waste of the mouth, however, nothing is treated here, as it is accustomed to be washed away. The brain is fed from the mouth.

<margin>2. Waste of the intestines.</margin>
Furthermore, if from here it is sent away into the stomach and leaves the region of the mouth: then the stomach becomes the digester, which prepares and forms the waste, and sends it further into the intestines. And it is about this waste, therefore, that we must chiefly discourse. For it is found in that place where colics, ileus <note>A painful intestinal obstruction.</note>, constipation, and laxity are born. Regarding this origin of diseases generated from waste, therefore, it must be held in what manner they are to be brought into the method of purging.

<margin>3. Waste of the liver.</margin>
Besides this, another digestion is also counted, the location of which no one knows, and yet it is ascribed—less than truly—to the liver. Through this, **urine** is produced. From there diseases are generated, except for those which <term>tartar</term> <note>In Paracelsian medicine, "tartar" refers to stony or calcified deposits (like kidney stones or gouty deposits) formed when the body's "internal alchemist" fails to separate waste properly.</note> generates. These diseases are to be drawn out by purgations, according as their own nature shall teach.

<margin>4. Waste of the blood.</margin>
Afterward, the nourishment goes into the blood: and from the blood is generated the internal mucus of the lungs and chest. This is waste from the blood, generated in that place and separated by nature from its own emunctories <note>Organs or canals that carry off waste, like pores or ducts.</note> into the external regions and ligaments, etc., just as from the stomach into the intestines. And these mucous diseases are similar to those excremental diseases in the intestines, and to the urinary diseases in the bladder.

<margin>How many wastes of specific parts, etc. Of the nose. Of the ears.</margin>
Furthermore, there is a certain "waste-disease" from the brain, which is the mucus of the nose, born from the digestion of the brain. For in this, that which is separated exits through the nostrils. Whence a "mucid" disease arises, after the manner of the others.

Another digestion also occurs in the location of the ears, which separates itself from the fat of the ears and produces the diseases of ear-filth <note>Earwax.</note>, just like the other wastes.

<margin>Of the eyes</margin>
In the same way, the eyes also have their own peculiar digestion and separation. Their waste, however, is led out through the eyes by weeping, though they have no expulsive power of their own. For whatever is moved from resolution and flow, or from abscesses and tears, produces the singular "waste-diseases" of the eyes.

<margin>Of the throat, etc.</margin>
So also the region of the Throat, Larynx, etc., has its own sputum, produced from its own peculiar digestion and separation. For since there is a peculiar digestion and separation, there will also be a peculiar emunctory, which is the mouth, for foamy salt, etc. These are the diseases of that waste.

Therefore, if you Physicians attend to these things, why do you babble nonsense about waste? There are surely as many wastes as there are digestions: and conversely, as many digestions as there are wastes, etc. But you—what do you prattle about <term>choler</term> <note>Yellow bile, one of the four traditional "humors" of Greek medicine.</note>, claiming it is evacuated through the ears? Where on earth did you learn that? Likewise, you say <term>phlegm</term> flows out for you through the nostrils, etc. Trifles! These are surely your frauds and impostures with which you deafen the unwary.

Stop speaking of "humors" henceforth. Speak rather of **salts**. Thus it will finally be out in the open that you are professing the truth. For the truth is that seven digestions are found in the body. For that many wastes occur. Moreover, there is no waste without digestion: just as there is no digestion without separation.

<margin>Seven digestions and wastes.</margin>
But what, finally, do you idly babble about "choler" in the ears, and about "melancholy" in the anus? Now you blame "leek-green" choler, now "egg-yolk" choler, and many similar trifles, all of which are nevertheless built upon shifting sand.

<margin>Humors are nothing.</margin>
What waste truly is, learn that from the following treatise, in which you will dig out the truth itself and see the vanity of your "humors." For what you propose regarding the method of medicating are mere deceptions and impostures, which testify all too certainly to your blindness and the darkness of your minds.

Thus, therefore, we have so far enumerated how many kinds of waste there are in man. Now, the following treatise will teach by what means each one is generated.

### TREATISE III.

<margin>What the digestion of the stomach is. A peculiar digestion and separation is in all members.</margin>
The **first digestion** of the stomach is not digestion, but a preparation for the digestions of the particular members: and it is the separation of crude waste, that is, of common waste.

Every member has its own digestion and separation proper to itself, an emunctory, excre...

-># THE METHOD OF PREPARING MEDICINES<-

...waste, and the six illnesses associated with these wastes.

Just as waste materials are formed in the mouth, in the stomach, in the urine, in the mucus, and so on, there are also childhood diseases, diseases of the lungs, and likewise diseases of the mucus—that is, of the nose.

<margin>
        Colors.
Note: { Diversities.
        Location.
</margin>
Where does this diversity come from? It comes from the **location**: the location must be carefully observed. Look at the heavens and see what happens there—that is, where it is hot, where it is cold, and so forth. Therefore, wherever health varies, illness also varies, not only in its outward form, but invisibly within the stomach, and likewise in those other locations.

<margin>
The digestion of the body is marvelous and manifold.
</margin>
It is truly worthwhile to speak of the power of **digestion**, and how marvelous it is that it changes so many times within the body. Just as digestion is not uniform, so too <term>Medicine</term><note>Here referring to the medicament or the treatment itself.</note> is not a simple thing. For just as the powers of digestion are divided in various ways, it is proper that medicines themselves be divided in various ways—not according to the <term>humors</term><note>The four bodily fluids (blood, yellow bile, black bile, and phlegm) central to ancient Greek medicine, which Paracelsus frequently challenged.</note>, but according to these very powers of digestion. From this, the indication for <term>laxation</term><note>The process of loosening or purging the bowels.</note> is derived. Indeed, the purging of "choler" or "phlegm" and so on is a mere imposture. Just as there are wonders in the earth, so there are wonders in man. Consider how much mucus and excrement differ from one another, or how much urine differs from sweat, and so on.

<margin>
The humors are a fiction.
</margin>
All these differences emerge solely from the nature of the <term>Microcosm</term><note>The "small world"—the human being, viewed as a reflection of the entire universe (the Macrocosm).</note>, so that man is similar to the greater world. This allows their diversity to be compared, and ensures that man has internal "bodies" upon which the heavens can leave their impression. For every operation of the heavens, there are corresponding locations in man. A physician must know man and divide him according to the parts of the heavens, not according to the **fantastic anatomy of corpses**, which demonstrates nothing of any substance in medicine. Rather, the heavens, the earth, the air, and the water fully teach what exists within man. But you have learned none of these things; instead, through your arrogance, you have separated yourselves from the learned, like <note>original: "canicidæ"</note> **dog-killers** from honest men. No matter how such people practice their "art," they think they should never have to face criticism from anyone.

<margin>
The anatomy of corpses is erroneous.
</margin>
Furthermore, one should observe an example taken from medicine to understand digestions and how they differ from one another, so that the waste products of any disease may be recognized and it may be understood how the power of digestion passes into its final matter. That is to say: while all these things are indeed "waste," they are more noble or less noble depending on their location, and so it is in other cases as well.

Now, in the stomach it is another matter, and so on.
Furthermore, what is the operation, or what does the first experience take away from the **phlegm**? Phlegm is mucus, which generates "arthritic passion"—that is, pain in the feet and hands, sciatica, and so on. Why is this? Because it falls into unsuitable places. In those places, it becomes "contrary" or foreign. If it is contrary, then there is disease. It is therefore specific: in gout it acts one way, in paralysis another, as is contained in my books, and so with the rest.

<margin>What is phlegm?</margin>
In these matters, you will note that the purging of mucus is useful only so that the mucus itself is removed. If, therefore, it is a disease of the mucus, the purge helps. If not, it does harm.

Now, what is the "anatomy" of mucus? Where does it fall in paralysis? Where in gout? Where in sciatica, or in pains of the teeth and ears?

***

Furthermore, what becomes of mucus if it rots? What if it hardens? It becomes this or that. This is how all the various types of waste are divided.

Thus ends the first book, from which you ought to know what should be purged and what should not.

Now follows the process: when, and in which sign of the heavens and the body, and so forth. Likewise how, and where, and by what means, and so on.

Also, what the power of laxation is, from where it comes, and from what cause.

## BOOK TWO.
### TREATISE I.

But to open the method of preparing medicines even more clearly, you should know it is right that from the knowledge of waste, the diseases born from them may be known. And not only the diseases produced by the wastes themselves, but also those which the wastes have set in motion. For the causes of "excremental" diseases are twofold: one is the waste itself; the other is its "accidents" <note>In philosophy/medicine, "accidents" are secondary qualities or symptoms that are not part of the essential nature of a thing.</note>.

<margin>
Diseases from waste are of two types.
</margin>
The disease which waste contains within itself from digestion is a **poison** within that waste. Because it is a poison, it is also a cause of disease. And so, in the manner of a poison, the "anatomies" of the <term>emunctories</term><note>Organs or canals that carry off waste, such as sweat glands or kidneys.</note> in a healthy body are infected and inflamed. These will be discussed hereafter.

Thus there are diseases in the body that are not the waste products themselves, but true diseases which frequently poison the waste itself, so that the waste exceeds its own nature and limit, and thus becomes the cause of a new disease. The cause is such: namely, for every disease, there is a fresh infection, and a new and different medicine is required. Moreover, the operation of these poisons is varied: for sometimes the poison is <term>Saturnine</term><note>Related to the planet Saturn; in alchemy/medicine, often associated with lead, coldness, or chronic, heavy conditions.</note>, sometimes it is like that of scorpions, now this kind, now another.

<margin>
Poisons are subject to the heavens. All secret essences come from the heavens.
</margin>
The heavens rule every poison; this is why they are capable of sudden action. For all <term>Arcana</term><note>The "secrets" or vital healing essences of substances.</note> come from the heavens. Since poison is an *arcanum*, it is from the heavens, as is the poison of scorpions, and so on.

Since it is produced from disease, its operation upon such a disease is marvelous. Even if it is not exactly like the disease, the cause is nevertheless present, so that the waste is made to resemble the man from whom it is expelled. And although it is not the same, it is similar to him, and a "monster."

Just as a sick man is similar to a healthy one, so these things are assimilated to each other in this case: that is, the poison always adds something to the disease that produced it and from which it was born.

You shall judge that disease, therefore, according to the difference in its location, its essence, and the poison of the disease. This is where the Method of Preparing Medicines belongs, which must be understood. For waste is the material and the subject of the medicinal method. Therefore, it must be understood in every case before a medicine is prescribed. For this treatise deals only with those diseases which are addressed through the method of purging and which pertain to waste.

As for the second cause—namely, if other diseases lurk in the body and infect the waste—it should be known that if the waste "conceives" an infection from external or foreign regions, the resulting diseases are not so grave...

### TRACTATE III.

<margin>
Nature is second to the Physician. Humors are fictions.
</margin>

**B**efore we finish the treatise on purging, understand its method in this way. Since medicine divides itself so significantly in its operation, that is a sign of division in the object itself: specifically, as many kinds of medicines as there are, so many are the diseases; or, as many species of remedy, so many species of waste.

Now, if medicine proves that its specific waste is found so often in the body, it follows that "like must be joined to like," since the experience of nature itself shows that we must proceed according to this rule. Nature does not follow our invented systems at all. Therefore, the things spread about the types of diseases—yellow bile, phlegm, melancholy, blood, etc.—are lies. For if these <term>humors</term><note>The four bodily fluids of ancient medicine: blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile.</note> existed in the body according to your chatter, it would necessarily follow that a healthy body would be divided in the same way. For example: in this herb there is "leek-green bile"; in that one, "egg-yolk bile"; this one is "sanguine"; that one "melancholic"; this one "salty phlegm."

But all these things are vain, and nature cannot be divided in this way—much less a human being. For whatever the logic of a human is, the same logic must apply to all herbs, roots, seeds, and so on. Therefore, you have categorized nature poorly, which proves that for so many centuries you have understood the condition and property of nature from <term>Avicenna</term><note>Persian polymath (980–1037), author of "The Canon of Medicine."</note>, <term>Galen</term><note>Greek physician (129–216 AD) whose theories dominated Western medicine for 1,500 years.</note>, and <term>Hippocrates</term><note>Ancient Greek physician traditionally regarded as the father of medicine.</note>, yet you have established your practice on a doubtful foundation.

Are you not ashamed that you are so poorly equipped by medicine? From what foundation, finally, did you dig up that much-repeated yellow bile, phlegm, melancholy, and blood? Surely from a rotten latrine, and a poorly [trained] physician...

<margin>
The logic of man is the same as the logic of all growing things.
</margin>

<page-num>823</page-num>
<header>ON THE METHOD OF ADMINISTERING MEDICINE.</header>

...badly spent. For that division <note>The traditional Galenic division of the four humors: blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile.</note> can in no way be sustained, since it lacks a solid foundation and miserably conflicts with both genuine science and experience; nor can it endure any more exact proof. Indeed, your very works show more than enough that you are practicing mere trifles and deceptions.

<margin>Man must be examined according to nature.</margin>
Since nature does not tolerate such a division in external things, she will tolerate it much less in man, who is composed of them. For man ought to be compared to external nature, not the other way around. Why then do you fail to evaluate or learn about man from this perspective?

<margin>Matter and time teach the nature of waste. Waste is one, though varied. From where the substance of waste comes.</margin>
But so that you may see where the genuine foundation is placed: I ask you to consider within yourselves from where time and from where matter proceed. In this way, you have simultaneously discovered from what <term>waste</term><note>Latin: "stercus." The author uses this term broadly for excrement and bodily by-products.</note> emerges, which you shall judge thus: Waste is simple or of one kind, not double. For it is simple, being that which is separated in any digestion. But as for why it varies in substance, quantity, dryness, thinness, colors, sharpness, etc., that must be traced deeper, in this manner.

Substance proceeds from the substance of food. As the food is, so too is the substance. If this is not produced according to the nature of the substance of food and drink, then there is disease in the food. Thus nutrition fails and wanders from the food, no less than the waste itself. So, waste decays with the food like waste that has not achieved its perfection. You babble that this is <term>cholera</term><note>Yellow bile. The author is mocking the traditional view that digestive issues are caused by an excess of this humor.</note>, etc. Nonsense. It is not bile: it is the digestion of an imperfect substance, which is colored in many colors.

<margin>From where the colors of waste come.</margin>
In the same way, waste is colored by incidental things, such as by bile, by which it is also made sharp. However, such a thing is not the waste itself, but something that is added; it is not waste, yet it tints the waste. Meanwhile, you call that "cholera," which it nevertheless is not.

<margin>The sharpness of waste is from the influence of the heavens.</margin>
But let these things be said regarding matter. Concerning time, it must likewise be understood that the heavens, by their influence, change the waste—so that at one time it is yellow, at another sharp (which is from Mars); now black and earthy, which is from Saturn, and so on.

If, therefore, the heavens perform these things, where do you finally stand with your fabricated Four Humors? At the <term>pillory</term><note>Latin: "palum numellarium." A post used for punishing criminals; the author suggests the traditional doctors deserve public shame for their errors.</note>, where the <term>Ringleria</term><note>Likely a derogatory reference to followers of a specific rival or traditional school of thought.</note> has also worn away its honor. By this you betray that you have thus far acted neither as Physicians nor as other good men, flowing as you do with mere infamies.

<margin>Putrefaction is a new generation in quality. The dryness of waste comes from heat.</margin>
The heavens beget colors, corruptions, and the digestions of nourishment, of nature, etc. And <term>putrefaction</term><note>The natural process of decay or breakdown during digestion.</note> produces one color after another. For every putrefaction is a new generation of taste—in sweetness, in acidity, in sharpness, etc. To you, however, these are yellow bile, phlegm, etc.; and that which is black, you call "burnt melancholy" <note>Latin: "Melancholiam adustam." In traditional medicine, this was thought to be a highly toxic, "overcooked" form of black bile.</note>, and so forth.

Likewise, there is heat, which dries things out. For the motion of the body is now of one kind, now another, just like the Sun in Summer. It also produces all colors by scorching, etc.

Furthermore, it also happens that bodies are dissolved and liquefied from the whole. This body you call "phlegmatic," though it is actually flesh. Furthermore, there is the putrefaction of blood.

How easy a province you have maintained in asserting your four humors and complexions! But you, on the contrary, must seriously know that you ought not to point out either bile or melancholy in the blood. For those things are mere slanders.

**On the division of these things, how they vary in urine, waste, sweat, mucus, etc.**

<margin>What the efficient cause of urine is.</margin>
The cause of urine is that all the humors of the members of the entire body flow together: in the nose as the mucus of the whole body, etc.

Hold to these things, therefore: there are four operations in all things—that is, four bodies, which are nothing in themselves, but in which something is stored.

As many colors as proceed from what is good, just as many proceed from putrefaction. Among these, therefore, and the genuine colors, a distinction must be recognized—namely, that red may be produced from green, green from white, green from black, etc.

<margin>Putrefaction indicates nothing certain.</margin>
Therefore, nothing is to be judged from colors. For putrefaction indicates nothing certain, as it can be changed into anything. For the heavens, time, matter, and place—all these can alter it. Whichever physician makes a judgment based on putrefaction is in error.

Know therefore in this place that nothing else is to be considered but the putrefaction of the waste: not indeed in the waste, but outside of it—that is, the decay happens with the waste and is born with it. For the generation of waste begins in the nature of the digestive faculty, and with it simultaneously begins the nature of the disease, which moderates the waste so that it decays in the body. What putrefies externally has nothing to do with the body. For decay happens in various ways in this place due to the occurrence of winds, etc.

<margin>Which colors of waste are to be judged. All colors are in foods.</margin>
The colors, therefore, must be further judged for the knowledge of the generation of waste: where the places and <term>emunctories</term><note>Organs or pores that carry off waste or secretions from the body.</note> must be known, which it enters.

Now indeed, its colors come from that matter from which the waste emerges. For in edible things all colors are stored: blood-red, azure, red, yellow in the gall; black and white in the spleen and brain. And so all colors are found complicated and mixed in the body from edible things. When, therefore, all colors lie hidden in the body—that is, in the body of the food—it must be known that when the food and the waste are separated from each other, the colors themselves are also separated.

<margin>Nutriment in food is the best. Waste is the worst.</margin>
The best thing in the body is the nutriment; the worst is the waste. So, similarly, the best colors remain in the body, while the worst are diverted into the waste.

While, therefore, all things are separated from useless colors, the <term>Hepatic</term><note>Liver-like or liver-colored.</note> color remains in the useless body. For all things have within them waste and nourishment; so also good and bad colors. But when the good colors are separated from those things, then one color remains. However, that color is not of the essence or of the colors; but in the same way that the devil is an [fallen] Angel, so too is that color. This is the color of waste.

Furthermore, if this color is not a bad or "waste-like" color, but it happens to be a good color, it must be known in this place that this color is not the waste itself, but that <insert>nourishment</insert> is exiting along with it.

<header>FRAGMENTS</header>

<margin>
The nourishment itself sometimes exits with the waste.
</margin>
...nourishment. Therefore, whatever color exits here: that is the type of nourishment passing out from the body.

You should not say, therefore, that if it comes out yellow, <term>cholera</term><note>In this context, "cholera" refers to "yellow bile," one of the four humors of ancient medicine, rather than the modern infectious disease.</note> is passing out; rather, you shall affirm that the nourishment itself is exiting along with the waste. If this is to be considered, it follows that medicine should seek to treat the nourishment itself, not cholera or phlegm. For if you speak of cholera, you are certainly speaking of nourishment. Why then do you name it cholera, when there is nothing in the body called "cholera," except that which makes your brain <term>fanatical</term><note>Meaning delusional or driven by wild imagination.</note>?

<margin>
There is no cholera in the body. Colors bear witness to the defects of the body.
</margin>
Colors testify to the defects of the body, which is to say, which digestion is faulty: for one is <term>dysentery</term><note>Bloody diarrhea.</note>, another is <term>lientery</term><note>A form of diarrhea where food is passed undigested.</note>, etc., a flux, etc.; similarly, there is seasonal alteration, such as yellow in the summer and <note>original: "(*)"</note> in the winter.

In the same way, a great quantity of food and other immoderation tints the waste, so that the substance is carried away, etc.

I bring all these points here so that you may recognize wastes, and not be "suffocated" or overwhelmed by them, but proceed by learning constantly and continually to know how and what you ought to purge.

To this also contributes the knowledge of <term>alteration</term><note>Transformation of matter during digestion.</note>, occurring not only in the waste exited through the anus, but in the whole body, wherever it may lie.

<margin>
The ureters. Urine contains many types of waste.
</margin>
Furthermore, as we speak next of the <term>ureters</term><note>The tubes leading from the kidneys to the bladder.</note>: pay attention. Many colors are contained in the urine: for many wastes meet there, just as they do in the stool. For in both places, there is a different expulsion. For there are different <term>emunctoria</term><note>Organs or passages that carry off waste, such as sweat glands, kidneys, or the bowels.</note> of the urine which come together; others of the stool which come together; others of the blood; others of phlegm and mucus. For the waste that is discharged through the anus is not one single thing, but is gathered from many. So too, the waste of the others is not just one thing. For there are many emunctoria that meet: likewise saliva, likewise mucus.

In the case of urine, therefore, diligent work must be given to its inspection, lest the "number" <note>The proper balance or full measure.</note> of perfect urine decreases, nor the "number" of the perfect emunctorium fails. However, since it is not my purpose here to teach on urine, I defer this matter to the books on the judgment of urines, stools, and other excrements.

<margin>
Colors indicate the method of administering medicine.
</margin>
If you who are about to give medicines are ignorant of these colors—what they are and from where they arise—then you will not even be able to seek out their locations or remove the colors. For medicine must be directed according to the generation within the digestions, not according to "cholera," etc. It is shameful that you do not feel the slightest bit of shame for those four fictions when you say: "These things purge and digest cholera because they make the stool yellow; those things purge excremental phlegm because they lead out mucus; these things purge the blood, etc., because they are subtle and do not cause many bowel movements." But those things which lead out green or lead-colored stool, you say "purge melancholy." In truth, if <term>melancholy</term><note>Black bile, the humor associated with sadness and the earth element.</note> were a <term>fool</term><note>original: "morio." A professional jester or a person of low intelligence; the author is mocking the logic of his rivals.</note>, you would have certainly guessed the matter.

Rather, recognize colors in their own digestions: in this way you will also know the emunctoria and their wastes. But those things which you have used in practice and custom until now were mere absurdities, as witnessed not only by your writings, but also by your erroneous method of purging, etc., which teaches nothing other than this: that you are utterly ignorant of what you are purging or treating at last.

# BOOK THREE.

<margin>
Cleansing organs are nearly infinite.
</margin>
**J**ust as it is necessary above all else to enumerate the errors usually committed in any matter, so in turn it is fitting to hand down the true order that ought to be kept. Regarding these things, therefore, learn further the order of purging.

If, therefore, you are mindful of the things said above: divide medicine according to the locations, which are the Heart, the Liver, the Kidneys, and many others, all of which in their specific kinds neither I nor others know. In the meantime, however, one must not desist from the purpose, but eager progress must be made continually in knowing the truth, etc.

## TREATISE II.

**T**he summary of my proposed argument is this: that in purging, the waste which has been created ought to be expelled, not that something new should be created. Since this is the chief point: therein lies the error of the digestive power. For that is where they are made.

### A small note in the fifth volume, pertaining to the book on Metallic Diseases.

<margin>
What is Mercury? The Earth is a unique world. Mercury is Winter. Sulphur is Summer.
</margin>
**I**n order that it may be clear to you that Mercury is half of the earth's time—that is, half in the firmament—it must be held that the earth is a unique world which has its own peculiar star. Its star is the mineral or ore. Now, Mercury is ore. Thus, it is the star of time, which is to say, it is the winter of the earth. For as you see, the Sun is summer, and it is a star, constituting a part of Winter together with other stars. In the same way, there are stars that exist as Winter, namely the <term>Milky Way</term><note>original: "Galaxa."</note>; as long as it lasts, so long do winter and cold flourish, etc. In this way it should be known that similarly, summer also occurs in the earth, whose stars are similar to the Sun, just as the stars of Winter are similar to the Milky Way. Those stars are two parts: Mercury is one part, that is, Winter; the other part is sulphur in the mountains.

<margin>
Winter stars flourish from Mercury; summer ones from sulphur.
</margin>
For these things, therefore, one must think of Winter as being half the Mineral, and the other half as being Summer: the half part is Mercury, of which I speak here. For the division is made such that summer and winter touch each other; yet they are divided just as they follow one another upon the earth. All the stars of Winter live in Mercury, and all the stars of Summer in sulphur, and they remain thus continually next to each other. Such, then, is the nature of the earth's star. Having accepted these things, know further that Winter lies hidden in Mercury: from which nature or property it also generates tremors and rigors, which are characteristic of Winter.

<header>THE METHOD OF MEDICINING.</header>

<margin>A multitude of those in error does not provide protection for the error.</margin>
...of others. Rather, think of it this way: the errors of those whose nonsense chaste and sincere Medicine can least endure ought to be proven by the very number of those clinging to them. He who knows the truth of a cure is a Theorist, and thus is Theory itself. For Theory is occupied with the cure, not in the brain, nor in the senses and opinion. Although the Ancients produced their works with such pomp and abundance, they are nonetheless of no weight, since no Physician can emerge from the foundation they intentionally laid. <margin>From truth comes nothing but truth.</margin> Therefore, that which does not lead to truth should by no means be considered as truth or as a foundation.

**Errata A.** The world indeed lies wide open, but in it, those skilled in things are not often found. Many indeed step forward with affectation, but there is no use for arrogance. Many dream of many things, but everything is outside the foundation. Here, the true foundation alone lies open. <margin>Two natures.</margin> Many experiments are indeed available, yet none are in their proper order. This man knows this; another knows that. But what is the help itself? None. It is only accidental trial and error.

Therefore, so that we may all tread the right path—which is the chief thing in practice and in which the foundation of every cure consists—let us hold to this above all else. Since I have handed these things down more prolifically and wordily in other books and volumes, I now embrace the same here in a brief compendium, which it is entirely right for you to accept as my settled experience. For the foundation that I have intimately explored, I communicate to you. Let those noisy ones mourn under the kingdom of the <term>Babylonian whore</term><note>A common Reformation-era polemic used by Paracelsus to describe the academic medical establishment, comparing them to the corrupt biblical city.</note>; who would care for their bellowing? <margin>Diseases are either punishments or natural. Two kinds of Physicians.</margin> Diseases are of two kinds: punishments and natural. So also are there two kinds of Physicians: the genuine and the counterfeit.

### *A Letter written by Theophrastus to a certain person.*

> ***D**istinguished Doctor, it is no wonder that a Physician greets a Physician, for truly a traveler seeks his fellow traveler, and many other foreigners make their acquaintance with me. For license is given to all honorable men to greet one another in turn, among kin and strangers alike; and you ask most excellently, both in words and letters, that I return as soon as possible. But I do not cease to go about my affairs, nor does time snatch the hour, nor Venus <note>original: "Venus" — here referring to physical pleasure or distractions</note>, but continuous labor—now in these things, now in others—just as I began. I write what pleases me to write, and what the stars and the earth command; I have dared to write more deeply than those Physicists and to have it printed. As soon, therefore, as the <term>Esthiomenos</term><note>original: "Esthiomenum" — a gnawing or "eating" ulcer, such as lupus or gangrene.</note> becomes sweet and the <term>Anthrax</term><note>original: "Anthrax" — a severe, coal-like carbuncle or boil.</note> of the field becomes manageable, I shall take care to return to Nuremberg, especially so that I may show my person to yours and enjoy the good kindnesses you have shown me. Although the earth did not grant me a fixed place (or, the earth did not give me fixed feet), nor did my parent beget an immobile Theophrastus—for which reason my fatherland is granted to few, and I am very difficult to hold. Farewell, and in whatever things of this sort I can gratify you, you shall find me ready. Again, farewell, and love your Physician-Prophet.*

# THEOPHRASTUS HOHENHEIM
## On the Origin of Diseases and Health.
# On Health and Sickness.

### CHAPTER I. ( Here, Astronomy.

<margin>Man, created whole, is affected by the world.</margin>
**I**n the beginning, man was created healthy, fixed, and whole. But as soon as he entered the world, two contrary things met one another, by which he was corrupted. For the external, which is <term>falling</term><note>original: "caducum" — meaning perishable or subject to decay.</note>, and the internal, which is whole, could by no means agree in one. From this it follows that man, according to his creation, exists as healthy; but the world is death, which weakens and kills him.

<margin>The 4 winds of the world, tempting man. Man and the Elements are one.</margin>
There are four winds in the world which destroy man. These are the four Elements, which conspire both universally and individually to destroy his safety. This happens for this reason: that man and the four Elements are one thing. For he emerged from them. In Paradise, he was indeed healthy. But cast out into the world, he began to be tried by diseases.

<margin>Which diseases arose at which times of the world.</margin>
In the year from the beginning of the world <note>Paracelsus uses mystical or idiosyncratic dating systems here.</note>, the first febrile disease arose; in 1123, the <term>falling sickness</term><note>original: "morbus caducus" — epilepsy.</note> arose; in the year 1523, the disease [of ...] arose; in the year 5556, the disease of pustules, leprosy, etc., arose.

<margin>In the beginning of the world, the sky was in balance. Where leprosy came from.</margin>
All these things happened because the conjunctions of the Elements were so disposed. For at first, the firmament revolved as if in the balance of all things. Afterward, the sky was dissolved, and from the error of the Scales and the Earth, leprosy was born. From the error of Scorpio and Fire, the plague. Now, hereafter, diseases will come (namely N.N.N.N.), that is, new <term>phlegmons</term><note>Inflammations.</note>, new <term>Erysipelas</term><note>A bacterial skin infection.</note>, and biting herpes. In the same way, fever will be changed when the year 1563 is numbered. Afterward, leprosy will change and utterly die out; and all sicknesses will immediately reach a <term>crisis</term><note>original: "creticabunt" — a medical term for the turning point of a disease.</note>, except for the new ones, like Rheuma, which will never die; and since those were the first drops of the end of disease, these are now the second drops.

If, therefore, they are generated Astronomically, they further operate Philosophically. It must be known, however, that <term>Influence</term><note>The astrological power or "flowing in" of celestial forces.</note> carries out or moderates all these things. For it attracts all operations toward evil or toward good from the rest of the Elements. Hence, through Influence, a progression is made into man, according to how the operation behaves.

### CHAPTER II. ( Here, Philosophy.

<margin>All diseases arise from the three primals.</margin>
**A**ll diseases arise from the three primals, that is, the earthly ones, and similar things from the four complexions. From <term>Sulphur</term> so many diseases; from <term>Salt</term> so many; from <term>Mercury</term> so many. Now follows the cure from these three. Thus humors are made, thus qualities are made—that is: from this we mourn, from this we laugh, from this we weep. This is an affection of the mind, not of nature. Nature does not weep, but the inner man weeps.

<margin>Man is twofold: of Nature and of Mind.</margin>
In this way, those two men must be compared and understood mutually: one of nature, the other of the mind. In nature there is no death, but only in the mind. Whence one must pay attention to which sicknesses...

### ON EXCREMENT.

<margin>What excrement is. Excrement is twofold.</margin>
**E**xcrement is the putrefied body of internal bodies, or of external ones entering into the internal parts. The external kind is natural, healthy, and good. For whatever we eat must first putrefy <note>In this context, putrefaction refers to the natural breakdown or "fermentation" of food during digestion</note>, so that it may approach the nature of generation. Indeed, a grain does not produce fruit in a field unless it putrefies. Likewise, food and drink provide no blood or flesh unless they first putrefy.

<margin>What the nature of putrefaction is.</margin>
However, the excrement that emerges from within is unhealthy, and thus it is a disease, and it produces diseases in many ways. For in that body from which that excrement comes, there is no seed for blood or flesh; rather, it behaves like the wood of a tree. For this reason, that excrement is another thing, different from the kind just mentioned, which is healthy and natural. This one, however, behaves in the opposite way.

<margin>Every putrefaction has its own peculiar character.</margin>
But that from which excrement comes is such: every single putrefaction produces its own stench, and its peculiar form and property. Thus, for example, if grain sown in a field putrefies, it is far different in its form and stench than if it were "sown" in the stomach—that is, eaten. For in the stomach, human excrement is made, and in the earth, the ferment of the earth; yet both are one thing, differing in this one respect: that the excrement of animals is separated and removed from its essence. However, that in the field putrefies in the earth and is consumed, so that such a separation does not occur, because the expulsive or separative power is not present.

<margin>The stench of excrement comes from the heat of the animal, both in species and in the individual.</margin>
Excrement acquires its stench from the nature of the heat of that animal in this way: any excrement is produced by heat. Therefore, as many heats as there are, so many stenches. Thus, there is one for man, one for the horse, one for the ox, etc. And conversely, as many men as there are, so many differences of stench among them. The same is also to be judged regarding oxen, cows, and horses. Hence it follows that the nature and difference of the stench in excrement depends on the character of the internal heat.

<margin>Whence come the form and color of excrement.</margin>
Similarly, the substance, form, color, etc., of excrement emerge from the seed—that is, from food and drink. According to their nature, it is colored, shaped, and thickened. For no such nature resides in the stomach, unless perhaps the stomach itself strives toward putrefaction through heat, and yet does not reach true putrefaction. Then it remains half-formed or malformed in its own proper form and species, more or less, as it happens. If this occurs, the excrement receives neither its genuine stench nor its proper form, but a disease is born there, or Diarrhea <term>Diarrhea: from the Greek for "flowing through," here described as a failure of the digestive "heat"</term>, whenever such ingested matter penetrates the stomach more abundantly or sparingly, more or less often, according to the condition of the heat that is altered in the stomach.

Therefore, that diarrhea is to be understood from the food in the manner described. But what other diseases arise from there in the other region of the liver? Seek that from that little book in which only excrement is treated. The summary is this: from that excrement arises a kind of colic in the belly, by obstruction, or excessive flow, or winds, or worms. Pay attention to the manner in which these emerge from that excrement.

<margin>Why worms and insects are created from corrupted excrement.</margin>
The food itself, through the corrupt heat of the body, can reduce excrement to such a state that worms are generated from it. Thus, if horse dung has this disposition from food, such that signs of a bad color appear, then beetles are produced from that dung. The same reasoning applies to the dung of other livestock.

A similar disposition can also occur in the human body, so that from the corruption of heat and the nature of food and drink, such generations occur, which are common in the places and regions where this retention happens.

<margin>Winds which are made from putrefaction.</margin>
In the same way, winds <note>gastrointestinal gas</note> are generated from such putrefaction. For you see that any putrid smoke pours forth vapor from itself. From this vapor, winds are generated if it is kept trapped. It follows that if the excrement in the body is not disposed as it should be, or if it putrefies much more than its nature requires, or undergoes a false putrefaction, it will flow out on the slightest occasion. From this "smoke" come the winds of the belly, whose names are various and diverse, though most are ineptly and inconveniently applied to them.

In the same way, if that putrefaction turns into dryness—that is, if the moisture joined to the excrement is consumed, or if the body attracts that moisture by its own dryness—then constipation begins, flourishing in the intestines until that heat is consumed. From this constipation follows colic, born from the acrimony <note>sharpness or irritation</note> lurking in the dry excrement. These conditions have also been given various names, all of them unsuitable. For nothing is present here except the falsity of excrement.

<margin>Excrement is affected in various ways by foods.</margin>
Thus, various affections arise from food and heat. So if gold is eaten, it is produced in the stomach in this way. In the same way also in the intestines, etc. So too iron, tin, etc. Likewise stone, Sapphire, Garnet, Ruby. Likewise poorly cooked food. Likewise drink. Likewise mixed Tartar <term>Tartar: in Paracelsian medicine, the stony or gravel-like waste that precipitates from food and causes stones or blockages</term>, etc. From all these things, various results are produced, born in the intestines, which must be especially well known to the Physician.

<margin>What the effects of putrid heat are.</margin>
<margin>Diarrhea, Dysentery, Flux, etc.</margin>
Moreover, the excrement that comes from the substance of the body is generated if the body's heat is putrid. Just as you see certain motions in the heavens outside arranged so that they rot the fruit on trees, or nuts in their shells, or chestnuts, etc., so also putrid heats exist in the body which rot the blood in the veins, leading to Diarrhea; or they rot the blood in the flesh and its substance, leading to Dysentery; or the humors, leading to a flux of the belly, etc.

Whenever any liquid substantial part goes...

->Prologue to the whole Anatomy.<-

<margin>Everything to be observed in Anatomy.</margin>
In any Anatomy, these three things must be considered entirely: Substance, Matter, and Form—specifically, how one agrees and fits with the other. But as to how one passes into the other, or how all things touch each other mutually: other writers have described this in terms of location <note>original: "localiter"; referring to traditional descriptive anatomy which focuses on the position of organs.</note>, and they have not spent their labor badly, as far as the locations are concerned.

*Substance is from without,*
*Form is from within.*
*Matter is in both.*

Every physical Anatomy of the eyes is twofold: namely
* **Intact.** This concerns the whole body according to true anatomy, well and rightly composed, without hindrance, but as a complete whole.
* **Corrupted:** This is the kind which treats the physical body according to a corrupted anatomy of the eyes—namely, when the whole has been corrupted. It is the corruption of the whole.

The composition of the eyes consists of three things, namely:
* **Substance.** This is that which has both form and Matter within itself, and is therefore called substance. But in this section, substance is taken in a different sense, that is, according to the anatomy of the eyes.
> <note>Note to the right of brace:</note> This is composed in its three parts through the whole, and the Substance makes the whole. (The shape of a cross and both eyes were to be depicted here.)
* **Matter** is that which has substance and form. It is taken in this section differently, that is, only for the sake of the composition of the matters—which or what they are, from where they come, and what the matter of the eyes is.
> <margin>How so? Respond.</margin>
> <note>Note to the right of brace:</note> These have the matter of seeing, but not the sight itself. These matters are: <term>Sulphur, Mercury, Salt</term> <note>The "Tria Prima" or three primary principles of Paracelsian alchemy, representing soul/fire, spirit/fluidity, and body/solidity.</note>.
* **Form.** This is that which has matter and substance, and is a living thing, but in this place it differs for this reason: that the roundness of the eyes works in this spirit toward perfection.
> <note>Note to the right of brace:</note> In these is the roundness, and it makes the eye. Vision is the reflection of the circle, etc. In one it is open, here closed; but the latter is intrinsic, the former extrinsic.

### SUBSTANTIA <note>Substance</note>

<margin>Comparison of the tree and the eye. The root of the eye is in the forehead.</margin>
Substance. You see how the creator established for the tree its root, then the trunk, afterwards the branches, finally the flowers, and lastly the fruits; from which the whole tree is finally joined together. Now take note: here the root is in the forehead: and it is twofold. For the eyes are Twins <note>original: "Gemelli"; likely referring to the paired nature of the eyes and perhaps the sign of Gemini.</note>. And though the kind is one in generation, there are nevertheless two offspring. For this reason, two cells or chambers were established, which intersect each other in the manner of a cross <note>A description of the optic chiasm, where the optic nerves cross.</note>, so that the right eye has its root on the left side, and the left on the right, and they constitute a circle on a pedestal. For no cross is without a center. Therefore, the cross provides the center. And he who has no center is held by a defect of the eyes, so that he sees squint-eyed. The eyes are a composite thing, like a circle or a ring. <margin>No cross without a center.</margin> The cross is called the medium (which any composite has) consisting in a circle, and having no other union. From here, however, it is divided from the center upward into the root, and downward into the trunks, which are two, and are Twins.

<margin>What the composition of the eyes is like. What the flower, fruit, bark, wood, etc. of the eyes are.</margin>
The eyes are Twins, that is, two fruits or offspring, bound in the form of a cross by reason of the center, which any whole composition—that is, an <term>Integrastrum</term> <note>A Paracelsian term for a complete elementary whole or a nearly-perfect body.</note>—ought to have. They consist in the center, and look downward with the trunk and upward with the root. These trunks do not send out branches, but only give fruits—that is, they give flowers, or matter, and they give fruits—that is, sight. The flower is white, the fruit is crimson; both of them give from themselves the bark, that is, the tunics <note>The membranes or layers of the eye.</note>. The wood is that which lies between the tunics and the root. The marrow is that in which sight flourishes, which is the substance. The declaration follows.

### MATERIA <note>Matter</note>

<margin>How the eye relates to the three first principles.</margin>
Matter, however, consists of three: Sulphur, Mercury, and Salt. <term>Sulphur</term> is the flower and fruit, in all colors, according to the manner of resolution, outside the seeing body. The seeing body is <term>Mercury</term>, in which sight lies, perfect, without other matters. <term>Salt</term> in both is the coagulation, which reduces these parts into one form, that is, it completes its Essence. The declaration follows.

### FORMA <note>Form</note>

<margin>Why the form of the eyes is cruciform. Comparison of the eyes and the Sun.</margin>
Form is cruciform for this reason: because the center gives birth to Twins. Just as this falls, so the Twins are generated. Afterwards, each Twin goes out into its own form or roundness for this reason: because the eyes fill the place of the Sun in the body as if in a <term>Microcosm</term> <note>The "Little World"—the human being seen as a reflection of the Macrocosm or Universe.</note>. And just as the Sun provides a torch for heaven and earth, and for its own body (which are the four elements), so the eyes likewise give a torch to their own body. They differ from the Sun in this, however: that the ray is not sensitive <note>The sun's light is not a sensing organ in the same way the eye is.</note>. For our sight produces nothing in its own body. But the Sun is the eye of its own body, thus working and shining interiorly. The eyes, truly, shine as much as is necessary for the body.
The declaration follows. Roundness creates the reflex: as in its Declaration.

->Declaration of Roundness<-

<margin>The Sun is the eye of the four Elements.</margin>
Pay attention, indeed, to how sight is made in the eye. You see, surely, that the four Elements are one thing, of which the eye is the Sun. The others have ophthalmia and <term>scotoma</term> <note>Dizziness or blurred vision with dark spots.</note>, and are enumerated in the book *On the Diseases of the Eyes* in the <term>Archeus Elementatus</term> <note>The "Elemented Archeus"—the internal vital force or "alchemist" of the body that governs the elements.</note>. Therefore, just as the Sun makes an image, and without it the World cannot stand, so man is also a microcosm, and cannot subsist without eyes. Now, indeed, very often the Microcosm is blind; but the World is not. Receive it thus: There is one eye in the World. In Man, there are many <note>Possibly referring to the many individuals/eyes within the "greater man" or the spiritual eyes.</note>, all of whom it is not necessary to see and work. For such is the Divine power, and God’s counsel regarding man. Just as in the mother's womb, He can take away the eyes of a man...
<margin>How great is the necessity of the Sun and the eye. God's power is infinite.</margin>

<summary>This page concludes a discussion on bodily putrefaction and introduces a Paracelsian anatomical treatise on the eye, which uses alchemical principles (Sulphur, Mercury, Salt) and the Microcosm metaphor to explain vision. The author describes the eyes as "Twins" rooted in the forehead, intersecting like a cross (the optic chiasm) and acting as the Sun of the human body.</summary>
<keywords>Anatomy, Eye, Substance, Matter, Form, Microcosm, Sulphur, Mercury, Salt, Twins, Cruciform, Paracelsus, Optic Chiasm, Vision</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the "Anatomy of the Eyes" from page 827, moving from the philosophical basis of sight to the specific alchemical composition of the eye and the causes of its diseases.</meta>

<page-num>828</page-num>
<header>FRAGMENTS ON THE ANATOMY OF THE EYES</header>

<margin>The eye is round, just as in the anatomy of man. How great a necessity.</margin>
...witness: thus he can even strike his own eye out for the world. But he never did this. The eye is round, and so it ought to be. For the external anatomy is like the internal, and the internal in its form is like the external. For anatomy is established in this: that the anatomy of the world <note>The Macrocosm</note> and the Microcosm <note>the human being</note> are one thing. Nor must only the anatomy of man be known, but also that of the Archeus <term>Archeus: the internal "chemist" or vital force that governs the body's functions according to Paracelsian theory</term> itself. For both constitute a single anatomy, which the anatomy of the Archeus of both worlds teaches. In these anatomies, all diseases of the eyes are also contained.

<margin>The Moon is an injured eye</margin>
For the Moon is an eye, but an injured one, namely with a scotoma <note>a dark spot or blind area in the visual field</note> where the redness is separated from the whiteness. Now, if the Microcosm suffers from scotoma, then the Whiteness is separated from the Redness, and the scotoma lies within the Redness. The same further applies to Ophthalmia <note>inflammation of the eye</note>:

<margin>Xelses stars etc. Dladus stars etc.</margin>
The star Xelses flickers upwards, not downwards. The star Dladus has a cataract <note>a clouding of the lens</note> placed before it. That star is indeed seen, but it does not shine. But those stars which have a spot or a "nail" <note>original: "unguem"; likely referring to a pterygium, a wedge-shaped growth on the eye</note>: we see these not at all. Thus, anatomy must be established around the eyes in man just as in the Archeus. Note: concerning Earth, Water, and Fire.

### Explanation of the Matter.

Now indeed you see how subtly the Sulphur <term>Sulphur: In alchemy, one of the 'Three Primes' (Tria Prima), representing the principle of soul and combustibility</term> is dissolved in the stars, which are branches of the eye, and the Sun is the center. If also here the Salt-Sulphur <note>original: "SS"; likely referring to a specific alchemical grade of Salt and Sulphur</note> of the eyes from the three primes is more subtle than all flowers, then the sulphur is most noble.

<margin>What the nature of the sulphur of the eyes is; Sulphur is the flower of the eyes.</margin>
This Salt-Sulphur is distilled and purified, and it is of the most subtle matter of the eyes; it is this which produces the Ruby in the Element of Water; it is this which makes the Galaxa <note>likely referring to the Milky Way or a milky stone</note> in the Element of Fire; which produces the garnet in the Earth; which scatters and throws crosses into the Air. This, I say, is the most noble Salt-Sulphur, which constitutes the center and the trunk.

<margin>Mercury is the fruit of the eye.</margin>
Now in turn, their fruit is Mercury <term>Mercury: One of the 'Three Primes', representing the principle of spirit and fluidity</term>, which in its three parts remains pure and clear according to its nature, and sublimes itself. For it is not of the power of dissolution, but of sublimation. First of all, it goes from the outside into the center and leaves its greenness outside; it retains its lividity and all its other innate colors. Furthermore, that which is most subtle in the whole circle, it forces into the center. This most subtle thing is that from which the transparent parts of the "whiteness" <note>albedo</note> are made in the four Elements:

<margin>What the transparent things of the Elements are.</margin>
Beryl, Camphor, Manna, Peach. Now indeed, that we may investigate to the highest degree, the matter and being of the Sun is equal in the world, towards the world, that is, the Microcosm. So that what is the eye in the Microcosm, that must be called the eye in the Macrocosm. Now indeed they also have a most subtle spirit in coagulation, and a clarity towards the red, and that most perceptively of all.

...from sulphur, a subtle clear redness; from Mercury, a subtle transparency; from salt, a subtle spirit. The veins in which the sulphur lies are the rinds of the three primes. Nor are there any other rinds more subtle. For because of the subtlety of their three primes, they are dissolved. Furthermore, they adhere even to the crystal <note>the lens of the eye</note> so subtly that no rind has ever adhered to its body so exquisitely. What is similar to this? Or who from all the rinds is so united to its body as this one alone? Certainly no fir tree, no balsam, no alder; no cypress or boxwood. No skin beneath the Element of Water is so subtle, no Diamond, no carbuncle. In the air, no Solna, no tereniabin <note>tereniabin: likely a corruption of "taranjabin," a type of medicinal manna</note>. Only the Element of Fire with its Sun is a single Sun; but here there are Twins.

<margin>Solna etc.</margin>
What is in the Sun that is not also in the eye, from all the Archeic *Ares* <note>Ares: the principle of differentiation and individualization</note> with Nymph-like and celestial virtues? Just as the Sun gives light to its eye, so the eyes give light to their Elements. And both are Element and Elemented.

->End of the Whole section.<-

# IT FOLLOWS:
## The Practice of the Anatomy of Each Thing, that is, Concerning the Corrupted.

From the things cited above, now arrange your discourse in this way. No thing was ever so whole that it would not eventually be corrupted. I must explain this corruption, and accurately so. For here I begin to become a Physician, that is, an Oculist. Do not be ashamed of this, since it is spagyric <term>Spagyric: alchemical medicine involving the separation and recombination of natural elements</term>. The anatomy of the whole eye has been described to you; furthermore, it is necessary to know the corruption of the eyes, which happens according to three things: namely, Substance, Matter, and Form, as the anatomy teaches.

<margin>Diseases which arise from the SUBSTANCE of the eyes.</margin>
From the substance, these diseases of the eyes arise: Ophthalmia, blindness; for this reason, because the substance has wandered in its composition, so that the joining was made erroneously. It happens in this way: the root, which ought to give birth to Twins, runs out on both sides, that is, mixed together, and they become Squint-eyed <note>original: "Strabi"; strabismus</note>, etc. Likewise, if the center is coagulated by the spirit of salt, then the generation is false, and it produces blindness. And these things are said concerning those born with it. Otherwise, no diseases arise from nature. Likewise, ophthalmia is manifold; seek it in the explanation.

From the matter arise cataracts, scotoma, etc., if it be dissolved, etc.

From the form, no diseases arise except the consumption of the eyes, if they waste away in form, or swell up and go out from their center. Note that this loosening from consumption or tumor also makes boys squint-eyed who were not born so.

On this matter, the author had not written more in these pages.

<margin>The most subtle substance of the eyes.</margin>
To see the Substance, how subtly it is constituted. It has the three primes in their most subtle state. A...

->End of the Fragments of Volume V.<-

<summary>This index page outlines Paracelsian medical philosophy, emphasizing that diseases (like gout or the "falling sickness") arise from internal "bodies" and minerals (sulfur, mercury, salt) rather than traditional humors. It also frames God as the ultimate source of medicine and wisdom, whose providence directs the healing arts.</summary>

<note>This leaf is a flyleaf, an empty sheet of paper found at the very beginning or end of a book. It contains no handwritten or printed text, but it shows heavy "foxing"—the characteristic brownish spots caused by the aging of the paper and environmental moisture over centuries.</note>

<note>There is a faint, large-scale embossed pattern or watermark in the center of the paper. In early modern bookmaking, these marks were used by papermakers as a signature to identify the quality and origin of their paper. Though now faded, such marks are vital for historians to date and locate the production of manuscripts.</note>
